name: Vanilla Layer Cake Recipe
note: This vanilla cake recipe is made in one bowl, and is super moist! One batch makes 3, 8-inch cake layers, and is frosted with vanilla buttercream frosting.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup egg whites from a carton or about 7 egg whites, room temp (240g)
ingredients.name: egg whites from a carton or about 7 egg whites, room temp (240g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 Tbsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (12g)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (12g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup heavy cream or whipping cream (60g)
ingredients.name: heavy cream or whipping cream (60g)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Line four 7" or three 8" round cake pans with parchment rounds and grease with non-stick baking spray or homemade cake pan release.
Mix 3 cups all-purpose flour, 3 cups sugar, 2 1/2 tsp baking powder, and 1 tsp salt together in a stand mixer with a paddle attachment or hand mixer until fully combined.
Mix in 1 cup of room temperature, unsalted butter slowly into the dry ingredients on a low speed. Continue to mix until no large chunks of butter remain and the mixture looks like moist sand.
Pour in 1 cup of egg whites and mix on low until just incorporated. Mix in 1 1/2 cups of buttermilk in two installments at a low speed.

Add in 2 Tbsp of vegetable oil and 2 tsp of vanilla extract and mix at a low speed until fully incorporated. If you plan to color your cake layers, add in the gel food coloring with the oil and vanilla.

Scrape down the sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula, then beat on a medium speed for about a minute to make sure everything is properly mixed together. This also helps lighten the texture of the cake layers a bit.
Divide the batter evenly between your prepared pans. I like to use a scale to make sure each pan has the same amount of batter and will bake up to the same height.
Bake for 33-35 minutes or until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Let the pans cool for 10 minutes, then run a small offset spatula around the perimeter of the pan to separate the cake from the pan.
Place the cake layers into the freezer for 30 minutes to accelerate the cooling process. Once the layers are fully cooled, carefully flip the pans and remove the layers.
Use a serrated knife to level the tops of the layers right before you plan to assemble your cake, or you can wrap and freeze them if you're making them in advance.

If you make these cake layers in advance and freeze them, let them thaw for about 20 minutes before making your cake. The cake layers should still be slightly cold to the touch, which will make it easier to assemble your cake.
While the cake layers bake and cool, make the vanilla buttercream frosting.
Beat 2 cups of unsalted butter on a medium speed for 30 seconds with a paddle attachment until smooth.
Mix in 1 Tbsp of vanilla extract and 1/2 tsp salt on a low speed.

Slowly mix in 7 cups of powdered sugar on a low speed. Add 1/4 cup of heavy cream halfway through to make the frosting easier to mix. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl with a rubber spatula to make sure everything is properly mixed together.
Continue to mix on a low speed for a few minutes until the desired consistency is reached.
If the frosting is too thick, add additional cream (1 Tbsp at a time). If the frosting is too thin, add more powdered sugar (a quarter of a cup at a time).
If you plan to color the buttercream, add in the gel food coloring once the frosting is fully made and beat on low until it reaches the desired color.
Stack and frost cake layers on a greaseproof cake board using a dab of frosting to help stick the first cake layer to the board.
Add an even layer of buttercream between each cake layer with a large offset spatula.

Once the cake layers are stacked, add a thin coat of frosting around the cake that fully covers the layers. Smooth using a bench scraper, then chill the cake in the fridge (30 minutes) or freezer (10 minutes) until the frosting is firm to the touch.

Next, add a second, thicker layer of frosting to the cake and smooth it using a bench scraper. If you're struggling to get smooth sides on your cake, I share all my tips and tricks in this smooth cake tutorial. Then, decorate as desired and enjoy!

name: Spicy Chicken Stir-Fry With Celery and Peanuts
note: This one-skillet recipe is fast and furious—ideal for those nights when you have 10 minutes to stand at the stove, tops. The cooking technique is in the tradition of Chinese stir-fry, in which proteins and vegetables are chopped small so that they cook quickly over high heat, then bound together with a cornstarch-thickened sauce. If you have a wok, now's the time to use it, though a cast-iron skillet will also do the trick. The wildcard ingredient is Medjool dates. They may not be a common stir-fry ingredient, but their jammy sweetness is a welcome surprise between bites of crunchy celery, salty peanuts, and spicy chicken.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tsp. plus ¼ cup soy sauce
ingredients.name: soy sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ tsp. kosher salt, plus more
ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ cups cilantro leaves with tender stems, divided
ingredients.name: cilantro leaves with tender stems

preparationSteps: Whisk together 2 tsp. soy sauce, 1½ tsp. cornstarch, ½ tsp. sugar, and ½ tsp. salt in a medium bowl; set marinade aside. Cut 1 lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs into ½" pieces. Transfer to bowl with reserved marinade and toss to evenly coat. (The cornstarch will tenderize the chicken and lock in its juices.) Set chicken aside.

Whisk 3 Tbsp. sambal oelek, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, remaining ¼ cup soy sauce, 1 tsp. cornstarch, 1 tsp. sugar, and ¼ cup water in a small bowl or measuring glass. (Here, the cornstarch serves the role of thickening agent.) Set sauce aside.

Using the side of your chef’s knife, lightly smash 4 garlic cloves, then peel and finely chop. Finely chop one 2" piece ginger (skins and all unless they scare you!) Combine garlic and ginger in a small bowl.

Trim roots from 6 scallions, then slice crosswise into ½" pieces. If there are any leaves attached to 4 celery stalks, remove and coarsely chop them; set side for serving. Cut stalks in half lengthwise, then crosswise into ½"-thick pieces. Tear open 4 oz. dates and remove pits; discard. Cut flesh into ½” pieces. Combine scallions, celery, and dates in a medium bowl.
Coarsely chop 1 cup cilantro leaves with tender stems. Reserve remaining ½ cup cilantro leaves with tender stems unchopped for serving.
Head over to the stove with all of your prep work (gathering it all on one baking sheet will make this easy!). This stir-fry comes together fast, so you want to be sure to have it all at the ready.

Combine ⅓ cup vegetable oil and ¾ cup roasted, salted peanuts in a large cast-iron skillet. Set skillet over medium heat and cook nuts, stirring often to encourage even toasting, until they are a few shades darker and fragrant, 5–7 minutes. Remove skillet from heat and, using a slotted spoon so you leave the oil behind, transfer nuts to a small bowl or plate.
Set skillet with oil over medium-high heat. Cook garlic and ginger, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until very fragrant but not yet browned, about 30 seconds.

Add reserved chicken and cook, stirring to break it apart, until it is no longer pink on the outsides, about 3 minutes . At this point, it will still be slightly undercooked inside, but it will cook a few more minutes with the remaining vegetables.

Add scallions, celery, and dates and cook, stirring often, until scallions are bright green and slightly softened, about 2 minutes. The celery should still be quite crisp and crunchy (taste as you go!).

Give reserved sauce a good stir to be sure cornstarch is incorporated (it loves to settle at the bottom), then add to skillet. Cook, stirring often, until sauce thickens and turns glossy and chicken and vegetables are evenly coated, about 2 minutes.

Remove skillet from heat and stir in fried peanuts and chopped cilantro. Taste stir-fry and add a little more salt if you think it needs it. Serve straight out of the skillet or transfer to a shallow bowl. Scatter reserved celery leaves (if you have them) and cilantro leaves over. Serve with rice alongside.

name: Tandoori-Style Baked Chicken: Bold, Flavorful & Effortlessly Delicious
note: Use Moji's Tandoori Chicken recipe and one masala packet to prepare a hassle-free, mouth-watering marinated baked chicken. Infused with Moji’s signature garam masala, this blend delivers a punch of flavor with just the right amount of heat. Perfect for an easy yet authentic Indian meal, serve alongside one of Moji’s spiced vegetables and basmati rice for a complete, satisfying feast!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 chicken thighs preferably bone-in, skin on, (approx. 3 lbs.)
ingredients.name: chicken thighs preferably bone-in, skin on, (approx. 3 lbs.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packet Moji Masala Tandoori-Style Chicken Masala
ingredients.name: Moji Masala Tandoori-Style Chicken Masala

preparationSteps: Puncture each piece of chicken with a fork a couple of times to allow the marinade to penetrate.
In a medium-to-large mixing bowl blend the olive oil and tomato paste.  Add the contents of the masala packet and mix until you have a smooth even paste.

Add the chicken to the marinade piece by piece to coat evenly, ensuring the mixture gets under the skin (your hands are the best tools in the kitchen for this).  Cover and refrigerate for up to 48 hours.

Preheat oven to 450 degrees. Line baking sheet with foil and grease with oil.  Lay pieces touching side by side (the chicken stays juiciest when laid out without spacing).  If using boneless, skinless, roll them in as if there were a bone so the thighs don't dry out.  Cover loosely with a piece of foil.

Bake for 25 minutes, then remove cover and cook for about 20-25 more minutes, or until chicken is fully cooked with a nice slightly dark coat.  The marinade should be dried out on top, but the chicken still juicy.  If you use a meat thermometer, it should register close to 200 degrees.  (Despite the high temperature, the marinade helps retain moisture, so the chicken does not dry out.  Magic!)
use 3 lbs of chicken tenderloins (boneless, skinless);
use 3/4 cup of olive oil
cover and cook at 425 until chicken reaches an internal temp of 165 degrees
remove foil and broil for 1-2 minutes so the coating is no longer wet

name: Funfetti Layer Cake
note: This delicious funfetti layer cake recipe is made from scratch and is so easy to make. It's tender, moist, and packed with sprinkles!!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature (226g)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature (226g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup carton egg whites or 7 large egg whites, room temperature (240g)
ingredients.name: egg whites or 7 large egg whites, room temperature (240g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (8g)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (8g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2/3 cup rainbow jimmies or long strand sprinkles (115g)
ingredients.name: rainbow jimmies or long strand sprinkles (115g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups (4 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature (454g or 1 lb.)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature (454g or 1 lb.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 Tbsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (12g)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (12g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 7 cups powdered sugar (904g or a 2 lb. bag)
ingredients.name: powdered sugar (904g or a 2 lb. bag)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup heavy whipping cream, room temperature (60g)
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream, room temperature (60g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup rainbow jimmies or long strand sprinkles - to be mixed in once the cake is filled and crumb coated (85g)
ingredients.name: rainbow jimmies or long strand sprinkles - to be mixed in once the cake is filled and crumb coated (85g)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Grease then line four 7-inch or three 8-inch cake pans with nonstick spray and parchment paper rounds. Set aside.  You can also use this recipe to make 4, 6-inch cake layers but the bake time will be a few minutes longer. If you don't have enough cake pans, the batter can sit at room temperature for a few hours. Bake as many layers as you can at a time.
Mix 3 cups all-purpose flour, 3 cups sugar, 2 1/2 tsp baking powder, and 1 tsp salt together in a stand mixer with a paddle attachment or hand mixer until fully combined.
Mix in 1 cup of room temperature, unsalted butter slowly into the dry ingredients on a low speed. Continue to mix until no large chunks of butter remain, and the mixture looks like moist sand.
Pour in 1 cup of egg whites and mix on low until just incorporated. Mix in 1 1/2 cups of buttermilk in two installments on a low speed.

Add in 2 Tbsp of vegetable oil, 2 tsp of vanilla extract, and 1 1/2 tsp almond extract and mix at a low speed until fully incorporated. If you want to color these cake layers, add the gel food coloring during this step.

Scrape down the sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula, then beat on a medium speed for about a minute to make sure everything is properly mixed together. This also helps lighten the texture of the cake layers a bit.
Fold 2/3 cup of sprinkles into the cake batter using a rubber spatula and mix until they're evenly distributed.

Divide the batter evenly between the prepared cake pans. I like to use a scale to weigh each pan and make sure they have the same amount of batter. This ensures that the layers bake evenly and end up being the same height.

Bake for 34-36 minutes or until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs. Let the pans cool for 10 minutes, then run an offset spatula around the perimeter of the pan to separate the cake from the pan.
Place the cake pans into the freezer for 45 minutes to accelerate the cooling process. Once the layers are fully cooled, carefully flip the pans, and remove the layers from the pans.

These layers bake up pretty flat, so leveling them is optional! If you want to level them, use a serrated knife to level the top of each cake layer. I also like to trim the sides of the cake layers to remove any sprinkles that have caramelized and make them easier to frost. If you make these in advance, wrap and freeze them at this point.
While the cake layers bake and cool, make the vanilla buttercream frosting. Beat 2 cups of unsalted butter on a medium speed for 30 seconds with a paddle attachment until smooth.
Mix in 1 Tbsp of vanilla extract and 1/2 tsp salt on a low speed.

Slowly add in 7 cups of powdered sugar while mixing slowly on the lowest setting. Halfway through add 1/4 cup of heavy cream or milk to make it easier to mix. I like to place a kitchen towel over my mixer to contain any powdered sugar clouds.

Continue to mix on a low speed for a few minutes until the desired consistency is reached. If the frosting seems too thick, add additional cream (1 Tbsp at a time). If the frosting is too thin, add more powdered sugar (a quarter of a cup at a time).
Wait to add in the sprinkles until you've filled and crumb-coated the cake. Cover the buttercream flush with plastic wrap to prevent crusting, then set aside.
Stack and frost cake layers on a greaseproof cake board or flat plate using a dab of frosting to help stick the first cake layer to the board.

Spread an even layer of buttercream on top of each cake layer with a large offset spatula. If desired, add a couple of spoonfuls of sprinkles on top of the frosting. Repeat with the remaining cake layers.
Flip the top cake layer upside-down to make it easier to frost.
Once all the layers are stacked, gently press down on top of the cake with both of your hands to help them settle and to press out any trapped air between the cake layers.

Spread a thin coat of frosting around the cake to fully cover the cake layers. Smooth using a bench scraper, then chill the cake in the fridge (30 minutes) or freezer (10 minutes) until the frosting is firm to the touch.
While the cake chills, fold ½ cup of rainbow sprinkles to the remaining buttercream.
Use the sprinkle buttercream to add a second layer of frosting to the cake with the remaining buttercream. Smooth using a large offset spatula and bench scraper.

Then decorate as desired and enjoy! I added some pink white chocolate ganache drips around the cake and used the remaining buttercream to pipe some buttercream dollops in a ring around the top of the cake.

If you want to pipe a border around this cake, be mindful of the sprinkles in the buttercream. They can get stuck in the groves of frosting tips. I recommend using a large, round piping tip if you use one.

name: White Chocolate Ganache Macaron Filling
note: This white chocolate ganache filling for macarons is the best! It's silky-smooth, rich, and absolutely delicious.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 210 g finely chopped white chocolate or white chocolate chips (1 1/4 cups)
ingredients.name: finely chopped white chocolate or white chocolate chips (1 1/4 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 95 g heavy whipping cream, room temperature (1/3 cup + 1 Tbsp)
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream, room temperature (1/3 cup + 1 Tbsp)

preparationSteps: White Chocolate Ganache
The white chocolate ganache filling needs about 2 hours to set, so I recommend making it first! It can also be made up to a week in advance. I usually make it the night before.
Place 210g of white chocolate in a medium-sized bowl and set aside.

Pour 95g heavy cream into a heat-proof bowl and heat in 15-second intervals in the microwave until it just begins to bubble (this usually takes me about a minute). If you don't have a microwave, heat the cream over medium-high heat in a saucepan until it starts to bubble and steam.
Pour the heavy cream over the white chocolate. Make sure all the white chocolate is submerged beneath the cream. Let the mixture sit for a couple of minutes.

Use an immersion blender or a spoon to mix the ganache until the mixture has come together and is smooth. Press a piece of plastic wrap flush against the ganache and place the bowl in the fridge to chill.
When you're ready to use this ganache, place it in a piping bag fit with a large round piping tip. It should be thick enough to scoop into the piping bag and hold its shape.
Pipe a thick dollop of white chocolate ganache on one macaron shell.  Gently press a second shell on top of the ganache to create a sandwich.
Place the finished macarons in an airtight container and chill in the fridge overnight, then enjoy! Store any leftover macarons in the fridge.

preparationSteps: Place 2 chicken breasts on a cutting board and slice in half horizontally into 4 cutlets. Pat the chicken dry and sprinkle both sides with 1½ teaspoons Italian seasoning and ¼ teaspoon salt.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Arrange the chicken in the pan in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until browned on the underside and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part registers 160°F, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean cutting board; do not wipe the pan clean.

Reduce heat to medium-low and add the remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Add chopped shallot, minced garlic, 2 teaspoons rosemary and ¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper; cook, stirring constantly, until the shallot is softened, 1 to 2 minutes. Add 1½ cups orzo; cook, stirring often, until lightly toasted, about 1 minute.

Add 3 cups broth, ½ cup cream and the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, stirring and scraping up any browned bits; bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is tender, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat and gradually stir in spinach until just wilted, about 2 minutes. Stir in ½ cup Parmesan, 2 teaspoons lemon zest and 2 tablespoons lemon juice. Spread into an even layer.

Slice the chicken cutlets. Arrange the sliced chicken on top of the orzo mixture in a single layer. Cover the skillet and let stand until the chicken is warmed through, about 3 minutes. Garnish with lemon zest and/or basil, if desired.

name: turkey pesto focaccia sandwiches
note:
How do I pack/transport these? If you’re taking your meal on the go, you can wrap the individual sandwiches in parchment paper (or reusable wax paper like this) to keep them assembled, then stick the individually wrapped sandwiches in a sealable plastic bag. I usually use a couple gallon-sized Ziplocs, filling each with a few individually wrapped sandwiches. You can then pack the bags in a cooler over ice. Food safety wise: meat, cheese, and dairy dishes like this must be eaten within 2 hours (or even 1 if it’s super hot outside, like in the high 80s/90s) once they’re out of the cooler/fridge.

I want extra credit: Tie your parchment-wrapped sandwiches with this twine and it’ll feel like you spent $15/sandwich at an artisan deli.

Any side ideas? Chips! If you want to add a side salad to the mix, I highly recommend this arugula and fig salad. Or, if you’re feeling ambitious, the rainbow chicken chop sans chicken would be an excellent addition to your picnic. If you’re going for ease, just grab a bagged salad kit!

Prep ahead/love your leftovers: You can make these up to a day ahead of time. The arugula might wilt a little if you prep it that far in advance (rather than only a few hours), but no prob at all, it’ll still be excellent. Same math applies to leftovers!

Cooking for a crowd: This recipe is very easy to double or triple.

What does “chunky-smooth” pesto mean? It’s easier to show than tell — scroll back up to the first photo at the very top of this email/post and look at the pesto. That’s the consistency we’re aiming for!

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the homemade pesto and use store-bought instead. I love Gotham Greens’ — Costco makes a great one, too.

Riff: Make an Italian sandwich! Swap in mozzarella slices + prosciutto and/or salami, use all basil for the pesto, sliced fresh basil instead of arugula on top of the sandwich, and add a balsamic glaze drizzle!

Vegetarian: Roasted sliced mushrooms or eggplant would be delicious used in place of turkey. Or plant-based deli slices. Or crispy tempeh (cut into big strips instead of cubes) could also be great. Or… have you made the vegan beach sandwiches yet?!

Dairy-free: If you can’t do dairy, swap the Parm out for a DF Parm like Violife, or 1/4 cup of nutritional yeast. Another good option would be to swap the Parm out for 1/2 cup of a plain dairy-free yogurt. This would give you a delicious creamy pesto sauce. For the cheese slices, you can use any dairy-free cheese slice substitute. Or just omit if you’re not into DF cheese!

Nut-free: If you can’t eat nuts, swap the pistachios out for roasted pepitas, sunflower seeds, or hemp seeds.

Gluten-free: Use your favorite GF bread. You may only be able to find a sliced sandwich bread and that’s fine!

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and pepper to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and pepper to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large focaccia loaf, sliced in half horizontally
ingredients.name: large focaccia loaf, sliced in half horizontally

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) jar sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil, drained (with a little of the oil reserved before draining)
ingredients.name: sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil, drained (with a little of the oil reserved before draining)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1/3 cup mayo (it’s your call how much you spread on there!)
ingredients.name: mayo (it’s your call how much you spread on there!)

preparationSteps: Make the pesto first — it gets better as it sits. Throw 1 cup arugula, 1 cup basil, 1/2 cup roasted pistachios, 1/2 cup grated Parm, 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, and 2 tablespoons lemon juice into a food processor or blender. Blend until chunky-smooth. Season with kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste. If your arugula is very peppery tasting, you can add more basil and/or Parm to balance it out, if needed.
Slice 1 large focaccia loaf in half horizontally, right through the middle. You want two giant pieces that are going to become the top and bottom.

Lay the bottom piece of focaccia cut-side up on a baking sheet. Spread the pistachio pesto all over it. Layer on 1 pound of thinly sliced turkey, folding it upon itself as you add each slice to build height (AKA, don’t just lay the slices flat, fold each slice in half as you add it to the sandwich). Lay 10 Havarti slices over the turkey.

Top with 2 to 3 cups arugula, piled high! Squeeze the juice from 1 lemon over all of the arugula and season it with a little kosher salt and black pepper. Drizzle a TINY bit of the oil from the jar of sun-dried tomatoes over top.

Spread 1/4 to 1/3 cup mayo onto the cut side of the empty piece of focaccia. Drain then finely chop 8 ounces sun-dried tomatoes and spread them over the mayo,  kinda smooshing them into it to hack together a little sun-dried tomato mayo. Sprinkle all over with a pinch of flaky sea salt (or kosher salt) and a grind or 2 of freshly cracked black pepper. Place the top half of the focaccia mayo-side down on top of your sandwich.

Press it down gently with your hands. It’ll be great as is, but, if you have time, put another baking sheet on top and weigh it down with something heavy like a stack of cookbooks or a big pot. Let it sit for about 10 minutes.
If eating at home and not on a beach/lake/boat, remove the weighted baking sheet and bake the sandwiches in the oven at 375°F for 10 to 15 minutes, until toasty and warm.

Cut into individual sandwiches with a sharp serrated knife. I usually go for 6 to 8 pieces depending on the size of the focaccia. Press firmly down while you saw back and forth or else everything will slide around.

name: grilled pickle-brined chicken sandwiches and zucchini
note:
But I hate pickles, Caro: Do this instead: Mix 1/4 cup of salt into 3/4 cup of water that is as warm as your sink will go. Stir until the salt dissolves. Add 1/4 cup of ice to cool it down, then add the chicken and marinate for 30 minutes at room temp or up to 24 hours in the fridge. This is a basic brine! Next, instead of pickle mayo, you’re going to make a spicy mayo by stirring together 2 tablespoons of mayo and 2 teaspoons of your fave hot sauce per person. Season with salt.

I don’t have a grill: Preheat the broiler to high. Place the zucchini on a foil-lined baking sheet on the bottom rack of the oven. Throw the chicken on a large foil-lined baking sheet and broil on the top rack for 6 to 7 minutes. Check in on the zucchini when you flip the chicken — it should be getting tender but won’t get a ton of color. Take the chicken out, then broil the buns for 30 seconds to 1 minute but SIT ON YOUR BUTT AND WATCH! Buns burn quickly. Return the zucchini to the TOP rack for a quick broil if needed to get a bit of color on it.

Want to make a fancier grilled zucchini side dish? Add lots of chopped herbs like basil or cilantro, a sprinkle of cheese like feta, cotija, or Parmesan, and a sprinkle of toasted chopped nuts. This is seriously my favorite summer side dish!

Whole30 it / I don’t do carbs: Use dill instead of bread-and-butter pickles if you want sugar-free. Omit the bun and don’t thinly slice your iceberg — instead use big pieces of lettuce as your “bun.”

Vegetarian: OK this is a fun one — you’re going to make grilled veggie sandwiches! Make the zucchini and squash as directed (including the balsamic), and add one more veggie. Bell peppers, or fennel, or onions! Throw those on a bun with the spicy mayo from the “but I hate pickles” note above. Yum, right?

Make ahead: Brine the chicken, make the mayo, and cut the zucchini planks up to 24 hours in advance. Just don’t toss the zucchini with salt until you’re ready to grill, or they’ll let off too much liquid and get limp.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Grab a rotisserie chicken. Slice it up. Throw some pickles on your sando since the chicken didn’t get the pickle marinade!

Special ingredient: You all bought balsamic for last week’s recipe, so use that for the zucchini drizzle if you have it! Lemon juice works too.

preparationSteps: Place the chicken thighs in a large ziplock bag or bowl. Add enough pickle brine (aka just the liquid from the pickle jar) to cover the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, or marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes. I highly suggest a longer marinade on this one if you have time!

To make the pickle mayo: Chop up a big handful of pickles and stir them into some mayo (about 2 tablespoons mayo per person). You want the pickle mayo to be thick and chunky. Season with a tiny pinch of salt and pepper. (You can make this as far as 2 days in advance!)

Cut the zucchini and/or yellow squash into planks. To do that: Cut the zucchini in half widthwise (like through the middle), set the zucchini halves so they’re standing up on their cut sides, then slice them into thin planks. Toss the planks in a bowl with just enough neutral cooking oil to lightly coat them (about 1/2 teaspoon per whole zucchini). Season with salt and pepper — about 1/8 teaspoon salt per whole zucchini, plus a pinch of pepper.
Preheat the grill to 450°F.

While it’s preheating, open the buns and grill them cut-side down with the lid open until they’re lightly toasted. Don’t take your eyes off of them! They burn quickly. Once toasted, place the buns on a platter.
When the grill is hot, clean it with your grill brush. (When your grill is dirty, it loses its nonstick coating, so your food will stick. It’s also just gross — and a hazard.)

Wad up a paper towel and soak it in a neutral cooking oil. It should be saturated but not dripping (so wring it out if you have to). Grab the (saturated-but-not-dripping!) paper towel with tongs and rub it all over the grill grates.

Next, grab the zucchini planks with your tongs and add them the grill. Grill them for 2 to 4 minutes per side, until almost melting-ly tender and charred. I like my zucchini to be incredibly soft — it’s so tasty this way. Transfer to a platter and drizzle immediately with balsamic vinegar or lemon juice. Taste and add more salt and pepper as needed.
Remove the chicken thighs from the brine, shaking them as dry as you can. Add the chicken to the grill and cook for 5 minutes per side, or until at least 165°F internally.

Meanwhile, stir 1 tablespoon of pickle mayo into every 1/4 cup of iceberg lettuce. So, if you’re making sandwiches for 4 people, stir 4 tablespoons pickle mayo into 1 cup of lettuce. If needed, add the tiniest splash of pickle brine/juice to loosen it up and help you coat the lettuce.
Take the chicken off the grill and allow it to rest and cool down for 5 minutes.

When you’re ready to eat, smear the remaining pickle mayo on the tops and bottoms of the buns. Add the lettuce to the bottom bun, place a chicken thigh or two on top, and throw the lid on. DEVOUR IMMEDIATELY!
servings: Serves however many you want to feed

name: tortilla scramble
note:
Cooking for 4: If you use a large skillet, this recipe can easily be doubled!

Garnish: If I had them on hand, I’d top my scramble with hot sauce and some chopped fresh cilantro too. Yum!

Must have meat: As always with vegetarian meals you see here, this meal is totally filling and balanced without the meat. But, if you want, you could cook some ground sausage in the pan along with the onions and peppers, or top the scramble with bacon crumbles (cook the chopped bacon in the pan first, transfer it to a paper towel, but use the bacon grease as your cooking oil).

Prep ahead: To make this meal come together even faster, you can pre-slice or chop any vegetables — except the avocado — up to a day in advance, and store them separately in the fridge in airtight containers.

Love your leftovers: If you’re planning to save some of your scramble for leftovers (it will last in the fridge for up to 4 days), be sure to store the fried tortillas, scallions, and cheese separately so they don’t get soggy in the fridge. To reheat in the microwave, put the scramble in a microwave-safe bowl and top it with a damp paper towel. Microwave in short increments (like 15 seconds) and check each time to avoid over-cooking the eggs. Once it’s warm, top with the crispy tortillas, crumbled cheese, and chopped scallions.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Omit the cheese or swap it for a plant-based alternative, if avoiding dairy. This meal is gluten-free as written.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces queso fresco or Cotija cheese, crumbed (1 cup crumbled)
ingredients.name: queso fresco or Cotija cheese, crumbed (1 cup crumbled)

preparationSteps: Line a plate with towels. Stack 4 tortillas, cut them in half, then cut into 1/2-inch-wide strips. Trim, peel, and slice 1 medium onion.
Put 1/3 cup vegetable oil in a medium skillet over medium heat.
Core, seed, and slice 2 poblano chiles.

When the oil is hot (to test, toss in a bit of tortilla; it will sizzle), add the tortilla strips. Cook, stirring constantly until they are golden brown and crisp, 1 or 2 minutes. Transfer the strips to the towels with a slotted spoon and sprinkle with salt.

Raise the heat to medium-high. Add the sliced onion and poblano chiles to the skillet, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until they soften and begin to brown, 5 to 10 minutes.
Core and chop 1 medium tomato.
Halve and pit 1 avocado, scoop out the flesh, and chop.
Trim and chop 2 scallions.
Crack 4 eggs into a medium bowl, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and whisk or beat with a fork until smooth.
Crumble 4 ounces queso fresco (it should yield 1 cup).
Add the eggs to the skillet and cook, stirring frequently and scraping the sides until they begin to curdle, 3 to 5 minutes.

Add the tomato and tortilla strips and stir gently. If some parts of the eggs are drying out, remove the skillet from the heat and continue stirring until the cooking slows down a bit then return to the heat.
The eggs are done when they’re creamy, soft, and still a bit runny, just another minute or two. Scatter the avocado, scallions, and crumbled cheese over the top and serve.

name: sunshine curry with cilantro-lime rice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 yellow summer squash, thinly sliced into rounds
ingredients.name: yellow summer squash

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch cubes
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons coconut oil (or any neutral oil, such as avocado)
ingredients.name: coconut oil (or any neutral oil, such as avocado)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces cherry or Sun Gold tomatoes
ingredients.name: cherry or Sun Gold tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 tablespoons yellow, green, or red curry paste (SEE NOTES for important heat-level intel)
ingredients.name: yellow, green, or red curry paste (SEE NOTES for important heat-level intel)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch grated fresh ginger or 1 teaspoon ground ginger
ingredients.name: grated fresh ginger or 1 teaspoon ground ginger

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup chicken stock (or my preference: 1 teaspoon chicken Better than Bouillon plus 1/2 cup water)
ingredients.name: chicken stock (or my preference: 1 teaspoon chicken Better than Bouillon plus 1/2 cup water)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fish sauce or soy sauce (preferably fish sauce)
ingredients.name: fish sauce or soy sauce (preferably fish sauce)

preparationSteps: As always, start your rice first! Rinse 1 1/2 cups white rice (I put it in the pot, cover it with water, swish it around with my hand, then carefully dump out the water and repeat until the water runs clear). Add 2 1/2 cups water, bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat when it’s finished and let it continue to steam with the lid on.
Now we’ve got some chopping to do!

Cut 1 small red onion into 1/2-inch chunks. Thinly slice 1 squash and 1 zucchini into rounds. Thinly slice 1 red bell pepper. Mince 4 garlic cloves. Cut 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes.

Warm 3 tablespoons coconut oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add everything you just chopped plus 10 ounces cherry tomatoes and 2 teaspoons kosher salt to the pan and cook, stirring often, until the chicken is starting to cook on the outside and the veggies are beginning to soften.

Stir in 2 tablespoons yellow curry paste (or 3 if you want it to be spicy), 2 teaspoons ground coriander, and 1 teaspoon ground ginger until they coat the veggies. Then stir in 1 can coconut milk, 1/2 cup chicken stock, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, and 1 tablespoon brown sugar. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 10 minutes. Cut the kernels off of 2 ears of corn and stir them into the pot. for the final 5 minutes of cooking.
Now back to the rice! Use a microplane to zest in the zest of 1 lime straight into the pot, then add the juice of that lime, 1 tablespoon butter, and a 3-finger pinch of salt.

Chop up enough cilantro leaves and tender stems to get 3/4 cup chopped (this does not need to be truly measured — eyeball it). Stir 1/4 cup of the cilantro into the rice and 1/4 cup into the curry. Stir the juice of 1 lime into the curry as well.

Taste the curry. Does it need more acidity? Add more lime if you have it, or a splash of vinegar. Want it to be saltier? More fish sauce or soy sauce! More flavor generally? Add some more curry paste (and Better than Bouillon, if you used it). Keep playing with it until it’s your perfect curry.
Serve the curry over rice, garnish with cilantro, and drizzle with chili crisp.

name: moroccan pork tenderloin and carrots with whipped pistachio feta and dita fries
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: Dip: Your whipped pistachio feta will last in the fridge for 5 or so days (eat it with veggies, crackers, as a spread on a sandwich, with grilled chicken the next night, whatever!!!). Pork: Thinly slice leftovers and use for sandwiches! Or finely chop, reheat in a hot skillet with a little oil, and make tacos with the leftover dip, chili crisp, and some pickled red onions. Pita fries: Snack on them!! Toast them up in the oven if they get stale.

Dip: Your whipped pistachio feta will last in the fridge for 5 or so days (eat it with veggies, crackers, as a spread on a sandwich, with grilled chicken the next night, whatever!!!).

Pork: Thinly slice leftovers and use for sandwiches! Or finely chop, reheat in a hot skillet with a little oil, and make tacos with the leftover dip, chili crisp, and some pickled red onions.

Pita fries: Snack on them!! Toast them up in the oven if they get stale.

I can only find a 5/6/7 ounce block of feta! That’s fine, carry on with the recipe as written. Will still be delish. Add more salt if needed since you’re missing a little salty feta.

I don’t own a food processor and my blender isn’t very good: If you’re worried your blender can’t handle pistachios, soak them for an hour before you blend them with the other ingredients.

Prep ahead: You can make the whipped feta days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. You can also prep the pork and carrots on the sheet pan in the morning, wrap the sheet pan tightly with plastic, and keep it in the fridge until it’s time to cook dinner! The pita fries can also be cooked days ahead of time — let them cool completely then store at room temp in an airtight bag.

Vegetarian: Roast 2 cans of chickpeas (or any white bean) along with your carrots. Drain, rinse, and pat them dry then mix them on the sheet pan with the carrots, oil, and seasonings as written. They’ll be delish!

Halve it: The pork and carrots and the pita fries are both easy to halve if you are cooking for 1 or 2 and don’t want leftovers. I’d go ahead and make the whole batch of whipped feta though so you aren’t left with half a block of cheese — it’d also be harder for your blender/food processor to mix. See the “leftovers are a good thing” note for what to do with your extra dip.

Gimme some greens: You’ll find instructions for a simple arugula salad in the recipe! I just want to note that if you love lemon and are also making the salad, pick up a second lemon at the store — you might want to add more juice to the whipped feta and/or the arugula salad and I don’t want you to run out!

I don’t wanna measure all those spices: You could buy Ras El Hanout, a Moroccan spice blend that contains these spices and others! Or skip the Moroccan vibes and use a great everyday spice blend that you love. You’d use a heaping tablespoon of it for your pork and carrots. Or, just do like I do when I’m not developing a recipe, and don’t measure anything — eyeball it!

Feeding kids: My kids loved the dip and pita chips (I called it green hummus). My pickiest eaters didn’t go for the meat and carrots — my least picky did! You could keep the spices off of one of the tenderloins and just season it with salt and pepper if you’re worried about the spices throwing your kids off!

Dairy-free: VioLife DF feta is SO GOOD if you can find it. Use that and a DF plain yogurt to make something very similar to the original sauce. Another option would be to trade the pistachio feta for a dairy-free tzatziki or a store-bought hummus like Little Sesame or Ithaca. Any of these will add a delicious saucy element!

Nut/seed-free: Omit the pistachios — the whipped feta will still be delicious without it. Or, use pepitas or sunflower seeds instead. I like the idea of pepitas here.

Gluten-free: Buy gluten-free pita.

ingredients.name: Sheet-pan Moroccan pork tenderloin and carrots:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 bunches (1 1/2-ish pounds) small carrots, greens removed, halved lengthwise
ingredients.name: small carrots, greens removed, halved lengthwise

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional if you want some greens: 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper
ingredients.name: Optional if you want some greens: 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 to 4 pita, cut into 1/2-inch thick strips
ingredients.name: pita

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, throw some of that in there too)
ingredients.name: packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, throw some of that in there too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup toasted pistachios (shelled — AKA, without the shells)
ingredients.name: toasted pistachios (shelled — AKA, without the shells)

preparationSteps: Position one oven rack in the center of the oven and one above it. Preheat oven to 400°F.

Remove the stems from 2 bunches of small carrots then cut them in half lengthwise. If you’re using big standard grocery store carrots, you’ll need to cut them in half (or into quarters if they’re really fat!) lengthwise and in half widthwise. Your goal is for them all to be about even size. Place the carrots on your largest rimmed sheet pan. Add 2 pork tenderloins, 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric, 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Use your hands to toss to coat everything evenly in oil and spices.
Roast on the center rack for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pork tenderloin reaches an internal temperature of 130°F.

Right after you put the pork and carrots in the oven, prep your pita fries: Cut 3 or 4 pita in half, then into 1/2-inch thick strips. Toss on a second sheet pan with 3 or 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon dried dill, 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and the zest of 1/2 lemon. Add the sheet pan to the oven so the pita fries can bake with the pork and carrots for 10 to 15 minutes, until golden brown and toasted on the outside, but still chewy and soft on the inside. Ideally you’ll position the sheet pans side by side on the center rack. If they can’t fit, put the pita on the rack above the pork and carrots.

Once the pork has reached 130°F (and you’ve removed the pita fries from the oven), switch the oven to Broil on High and broil the pork and carrots (still on the center rack) for 3 to 5 minutes, until everything gets nice and browned and the pork reaches 140°F.

Transfer the pork to a cutting board to rest (the internal temp will continue rising to 145°F as it sits). If your carrots are not fork tender at this point (fork tender means you can easily cut through them with a fork), continue broiling them on the center rack of the oven for a few more minutes (this ensures that they’re not too close to the heat — we want them to brown but not burn). Keep a close eye on them — they can go from being nicely browned to burnt quickly!
While the pork and pita are roasting…

Make the whipped pistachio feta: In a food processor (ideal) or a blender, blend 1 block of feta cheese (I cut it into quarters before I add it), 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (and a little dill, mint, or basil if you have it), 3/4 cup toasted pistachios, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup plain yogurt, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and the juice of 1/2 lemon together until chunky smooth. If you’re using a blender, you can use the tamp (if yours has one!) or a spoon to push and scrape the feta down as needed. Taste. I needed to add about 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt at this point, but this will totally depend on how salty your feta and pistachios are. I love lemon flavor, so I also wound up adding the juice from the other half of the lemon.

If you want some greens (I did, and it was excellent): Toss 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper in a serving bowl. Thinly sliced radishes, apple, or snap peas would also be excellent here if you have some!
Slice your pork 1/4-inch thick and serve it with lots of whipped pistachio feta, carrots, salad (if you made one), and pita fries!!

name: chicken chili verde burgers with lime butter corn
note:
Make ahead: Combine the burger mixture — or even form the patties, if you have a container that can store them in the fridge! — and refrigerate covered for up to 48 hours.

Freezer-friendly: If you have leftover burgers, freeze them! Go ahead and cook them now as it’ll make reheating easier. Store them wrapped individually in plastic or foil and in an airtight bag. Thaw them reheat on the stove, in the microwave, or on the grill.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. This is a v simple recipe — did you notice that it’s NO CHOP if you skip the cilantro or buy it pre-minced?! — but feel free to skip the salsa verde mayo and just use regular mayo any/or ketchup or any other condiment you love to simplify your life even more.

Vegetarian: Use 1 pound of Impossible Burger or another plant-based meat!

Make it into meatballs: Make 8 to 10 meatballs with the same mixture. Bake at 425°F for 10 to 15 minutes or until 165°F internally.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Swap in your fave df shredded cheddar and plant-based butter. For a gluten-free meal, buy or make gluten-free breadcrumbs (or omit) and use gluten-free bread as your bun. Alternately, you could chop the sides off of a head of iceberg lettuce and make a lettuce bun! Or serve your burger over salad.

Feeding kids: Be sure that you’re buying a mild salsa verde if feeding spice-averse kiddos!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, plus more to toast the buns with
ingredients.name: mayonnaise, plus more to toast the buns with

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded cheddar cheese, divided (I give you permission to buy pre-shredded)
ingredients.name: shredded cheddar cheese, divided (I give you permission to buy pre-shredded)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup panko or plain breadcrumbs (you can literally blend up a slice of bread and use that)
ingredients.name: panko or plain breadcrumbs (you can literally blend up a slice of bread and use that)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 English muffins (or your fave burger bun, but I love English muffins for burgers!)
ingredients.name: English muffins (or your fave burger bun, but I love English muffins for burgers!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: cilantro for garnish, lettuce, tomato, thinly sliced onion, pickled red onions
ingredients.name: Optional: cilantro for garnish, lettuce, tomato, thinly sliced onion, pickled red onions

preparationSteps: Drain the 12-ounce jar of salsa verde over the sink — we want to get as much liquid out as possible while reserving the chunky part! If you don’t own a strainer, you can pour the salsa into a colander lined with paper towels or a very thin towel, then squeeze the liquid out.

To make your salsa verde mayo: Add 3 tablespoons of the drained salsa verde to a small mixing bowl. Stir in 1/3 cup mayonnaise, the juice of 1/2 a lime, and a pinch of salt. Add 2 tablespoons minced cilantro if you bought it (it was optional!). Throw in the fridge (covered) until you’re ready to eat.

Add the rest of the salsa verde to a large bowl along with 1 pound ground chicken, 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese, 1 large egg, 1/3 cup breadcrumbs, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Mix until combined.

Divide the burger meat into 4 chunks and form each into a 1-inch-thick patty. Refrigerate the patties for at least 10 minutes before cooking. (This isn’t totally necessary if you’re tight on time, but will help them stay together and be easier to flip.)
Spray 4 ears of corn with cooking spray.

To grill burgers + corn: Preheat the grill to 450°F. Clean the grill grates very well. Spray the tops of the burgers with cooking spray and place them on the grill, sprayed side down. Add the 4 ears of corn as well. Close the lid and cook for 4 minutes. Spray the tops of the burgers carefully (don’t spray the flames with oil — bad plan!) and flip them over. Once flipped, sprinkle each patty with some of the remaining shredded cheddar (as much as desired!). Turn the corn. Cover and cook for an additional 4 minutes. Meanwhile, smear a light layer of mayo on the cut sides of 4 English muffins. Remove the burgers and corn and quickly toast your English muffins on the grate for about 1 minute with the grill lid open. Watch them CLOSELY! They like to burn.

To bake: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Place the patties and 4 ears of corn on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until cooked through. About halfway through cooking, flip the burgers and sprinkle each patty with as much of the remaining shredded cheddar as desired. FYI, the burgers will look FUNKY — lots of liquid will ooze out. Don’t worry, that’s normal! Remove from the oven. On a separate baking sheet, place 4 English muffins — each smeared with a light layer of mayo on the cut side — cut sides up, and broil on high for 1 to 2 minutes. Sit on your butt and watch them closely. Again, bread BURNS QUICKLY!

To pan-fry: Heat your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for several minutes. Add 1 tablespoon cooking oil and swirl to coat the pan. Cook the burgers for 3 minutes per side (you can probably only cook 1 or 2 at a time… hence why baking is an easier option!). After you’ve flipped them, sprinkle each patty with as much of the remaining shredded cheddar as desired. Meanwhile, broil 4 ears of corn, sprayed with cooking spray, on each side for 2 to 3 minutes. Then broil the English muffins following the “to bake” instructions above.

Once cooked, rub the corn with 1 tablespoon butter and the cut side of the remaining lime half, squeezing it as you rub it all over the corn. Sprinkle with salt. Garnish with chopped cilantro if you feel like it.
Smear the salsa verde mayo on both sides of the toasted buns. Add a burger patty, avocado slices, and whatever other toppings you’re into.
Enjoy your burgers and corn!

name: summer tomato galette
note:
Level up: Make this sun-dried tomato and basil mayo and use that instead of regular mayo. Do not blend it until completely smooth — it should be chunky! A few people tried to blend it for too long and caused the mayo to break, so don’t do that :)

Must have meat: Grilled chicken would be a perfect summery addition to this meal. Try my balsamic basil grilled chicken (which is part of the same recipe as that sun-dried tomato and basil mayo) or this one: the most perfect grilled chicken.

Prep ahead: You can make the dough up to a day before you plan to bake your galette. Once you’ve rolled it into a ball, wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, and store it in the fridge. When you’re ready to cook dinner, remove it from the fridge and let it come to room temp for about 20 minutes. From there, pick the recipe back up where you left off!

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. Like I said in the intro: Go with pre-made dough! See the “pie crust” substitution below for my store-bought recs.

Leftovers are a great thing: Wrap your leftover galette tightly and refrigerate it for up to 3 days. It’s delicious cold or warmed up in the microwave.

Dairy-free: Use plant-based butter, skip the goat cheese, and use vegan ricotta in lieu of both the mayonnaise and Cheddar cheese. (Mayo doesn’t have dairy, but you don’t need both if you’re using df ricotta as the cheese-like base.)

Gluten-free: A gluten-free all-purpose flour alternative like Cup4Cup or Bob’s Red Mill 1 to 1 Baking Flour

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound of the ripest, most delicious tomatoes you can find (such as heirlooms or Early Girls)
ingredients.name: of the ripest, most delicious tomatoes you can find (such as heirlooms or Early Girls)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 stick (8 tablespoons) very cold unsalted butter, cut into tiny pieces
ingredients.name: very cold unsalted butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup ice water (I like to fill up a glass measuring cup to the 1/4 cup mark, then add a handful of ice cubes. Then just use caution when pouring that you don’t add more than 1/4 cup of water since some will melt)
ingredients.name: ice water (I like to fill up a glass measuring cup to the 1/4 cup mark, then add a handful of ice cubes. Then just use caution when pouring that you don’t add more than 1/4 cup of water since some will melt)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon lemon pepper (or: 1/4 teaspoon regular pepper and the zest of 1/2 lemon)
ingredients.name: lemon pepper (or: 1/4 teaspoon regular pepper and the zest of 1/2 lemon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packed cup shredded sharp Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: packed cup shredded sharp Cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh basil leaves
ingredients.name: thinly sliced fresh basil leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces crumbled goat cheese (or just more shredded Cheddar, or grated Parm, or really any cheese)
ingredients.name: crumbled goat cheese (or just more shredded Cheddar, or grated Parm, or really any cheese)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Cooking spray, or a whisked egg yolk, or melted butter, or milk
ingredients.name: Cooking spray, or a whisked egg yolk, or melted butter, or milk
The simplest, most delicious side salad:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar (ideally a nice thick one, or even a balsamic glaze)
ingredients.name: balsamic vinegar (ideally a nice thick one, or even a balsamic glaze)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Slice 1 pound tomatoes 1/4-inch thick and place them on a paper towel-lined baking sheet. Sprinkle generously with kosher salt and set aside.
Now let’s make the pie crust! In a large bowl, stir together 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.

Use a chef’s knife to quarter 1 stick of butter, lengthwise, into 4 long pieces, then thinly slice the butter into tons of tiny little pieces. Toss the butter pieces into the bowl of flour and use your fingers to pinch the little pieces of butter until they’re all combined into the flour mixture in little flaky pieces.

Drizzle 1/4 cup ice water over the flour mixture and use a fork to stir it in. Use your hands to try to pinch everything together into a big dough ball. If it’s still too dry to stick together, add a tiny bit more water.

Sprinkle flour over a clean surface (I just use the kitchen counter) and dump the dough out onto the surface. Sprinkle flour over top too. Use the heel of your hand to finish blending the dough together, then gather it into a ball and place it on a sheet of parchment paper. Place another piece of parchment paper over top and use a rolling pin (or wine bottle) to spread the dough into a 12-inch wide circle. Nothing about this needs to be perfect — the edges will be shaggy and uneven, you might make an oval instead of a circle, all good!

Remove the top sheet of parchment paper. Spread 1/4 cup mayo over the crust, leaving a 1 1/2-inch-ish border. Over the mayo, sprinkle a pinch of salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon lemon pepper, and 1 cup shredded sharp Cheddar cheese.

Use clean paper towels to dry any excess moisture off of the tomatoes, then layer them over the cheese, leaving the 1 1/2-inch border. You’ll shingle them on — you want them to overlap by about 1/2 of each tomato.
Fold the dough over the tomatoes to form a crimped crust.

Sprinkle 2 ounces crumbled goat cheese over top. Spray the crust with cooking spray (or brush with melted butter, or egg yolk, or milk). This will help it take on a nice pretty brown color versus remaining beige!

Transfer the galette (still on the bottom sheet of parchment paper) to a baking sheet (either a new one or the same one you used for the tomatoes — but be sure it’s completely dry!) and bake for 45 to 50 minutes on the center rack in the oven, until the crust is a nice light golden-brown color.
Let the galette rest for at least 5 minutes. Top with 3 tablespoons thinly sliced basil.

While it’s resting, in a large bowl toss 4 packed cups arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon balsamic, and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Taste and add more balsamic or seasonings as desired.
Slice the galette however you please and serve it with the side salad!

name: asparagus grandma pizza + prosciutto salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces mascarpone (cream cheese works if you can’t find it!)
ingredients.name: mascarpone (cream cheese works if you can’t find it!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1 lemon (the same lemon you zested for the pizza!)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1 lemon (the same lemon you zested for the pizza!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: As much Parm as you want
ingredients.name: As much Parm as you want

preparationSteps: Rub 2 tablespoons unsalted butter all over a half sheet pan, then plop your 1 pound pizza dough ball right in the middle. Flip it around to coat it in butter. Cover the pan with plastic wrap and leave at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, but ideally 2 to 3 hours.
Preheat oven to 450°F.

Use your fingers to “dimple” the pizza crust out to fit the entire pan by pressing all 10 fingers into the dough ball and pushing outwards over and over. If your fingers are sticking to the dough, just rub them in the butter on the pan to grease ‘em up.

One by one, hold each asparagus by its tough end and use a vegetable peeler to peel it into skinny pieces. When it gets too hard to keep peeling, just use a knife to thinly slice it. Admittedly: this takes a few minutes. Feeling lazy? Just slice the asparagus on the diagonal as thinly as you can. It won’t be as pretty, but it will still taste delicious!

Add the asparagus strips to a large bowl and drizzle with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil. Use a microplane to grate in 4 garlic cloves and the zest of 1 lemon, and add 1/2 teaspoon salt, a pinch of nutmeg, and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Stir so everything’s evenly coated.

Use a spoon to dollop 8 ounces mascarpone all over the pizza dough. Don’t worry about spreading it out, it’ll melt! Scatter the asparagus across the entire pizza, all the way to the edges. Don’t wash the bowl — you’ll need it to make the salad and do not need to wash it out between uses. Sprinkle 4 ounces grated Gruyère (or more, or less, do your thing) over top.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the crust is golden-brown and pulling away from the edges.
Meanwhile, lay 3 ounces prosciutto in an even layer across a serving platter (like, cover the whole plate with a layer of prosciutto!).

To the already oily bowl, add 5 ounces arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice from the zested lemon, and a big pinch of both salt and pepper. Use the vegetable peeler to shave as much Parm as you want into the bowl. Toss. Taste. Add more oil, lemon, salt, pepp, whatever, until it’s delish.
Mound the arugula on top of the prosciutto. Chop 1/4 cup almonds and scatter them over top.
Transfer the pizza to a cutting board and cut into big squares.
Serve immediately! Enjoy your springy pizza night!

name: sheet-pan miso maple mustard chicken, sweet potato, & brussels
note:
Save time: If your store sells it, buy pre-cubed sweet potato or butternut squash.

Feeding kids: Add a different sauce to their plate if it’ll get them to eat the chicken. Ketchup, BBQ, ranch… whatever it takes! If they love fries, you could swap the sweet potato cubes out for TJ’s butternut zig zags.

Love your leftovers/meal prep: These leftovers make a 10/10 lunch. Store them in an airtight container in the fridge. See the “bowl” section in the “do your thing” note in the intro.

Prep ahead: Pre chop/cube your veggies earlier in the day or even the day before and store them in the fridge in an airtight container. If it’ll fit in your fridge, you can even prep the whole sheet pan ahead of time, wrap it tightly with plastic wrap, then just throw it in the oven when you’re ready to cook! You might have to go the two half sheet pan route for that though unless you have a really big fridge.

Vegetarian: Chickpeas!! Drain, rinse, and dry 1 or 2 cans of chickpeas and use those in place of the chicken. Since you’re not getting fat from the chicken, add another tablespoon of oil to the sheet pan.

Gimme some cheese: Goat cheese, crumbled feta, shredded white cheddar, grated Parm — any would be a delicious addition to this.

Gimme some greens: Add a handful of mixed greens, arugula, or some lacinato kale (that you’ve sprinkled with salt and massaged/squeezed a few times to soften) to your bowls.

Gimme a grain: Add cooked farro, brown rice, or quinoa!

DF/GF: For DF, swap the yogurt for a plain DF yogurt or mayo. If you need to avoid gluten, check your miso paste to make sure there are no added grains. The brand Miso Master is gluten-free!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 pounds bone-in skin-on chicken (use whatever cut of chicken your fam likes, I used 4 leg quarters!)
ingredients.name: bone-in skin-on chicken (use whatever cut of chicken your fam likes, I used 4 leg quarters!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large (3/4-pound to 1-pound) sweet potato, peeled (or not! but I like to peel mine) and 1 1/2-inch cubed
ingredients.name: and 1 1/2-inch cubed
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (3/4-pound to 1-pound) sweet potato, peeled (or not! but I like to peel mine)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound Brussels sprouts, ends trimmed (only if they look grubby! no need to if not), and halved
ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts, ends trimmed (only if they look grubby! no need to if not), and halved

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1/2 lemon, plus more to taste (use the lemon you zested for the chicken + veggies!)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1/2 lemon, plus more to taste (use the lemon you zested for the chicken + veggies!)

preparationSteps: Position an oven rack in the center of the oven. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 2 to 3 pounds of bone-in skin-on chicken on the baking sheet. Peel (or don’t, but I do!) and cut 1 large sweet potato into 1 1/2-inch cubes and add it to the baking sheet. Trim (only if the root ends look grubby — if they don’t, you don’t have to worry about it) and halve 1 pound Brussels sprouts and add them to the baking sheet.

Right on top of everything, add 3 tablespoons EVOO, 3 tablespoons miso paste, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, the zest from 1 lemon (use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to zest it), 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper.
Now GET IN THERE with your hands and smoosh and toss until all the chicken and veggies are evenly coated with all the ingredients!!!

Spread everything out into an even layer — it’s OK if everything is smooshed tightly, but it shouldn’t be overlapping. If it is, grab another baking sheet, line it with parchment paper, and transfer half of the chicken and veggies over there. The chicken should be skin-side up, and the Brussels should be cut-side down (to ensure crispiness all around).

Roast on the center rack in the oven for 35 to 40 minutes, draining off the accumulated liquid from the sheet pan at the halfway mark (just bring the pan to the sink and tilt it to drain off excess liquid), until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are very tender. If the chicken skin starts to burn (start peeking at it at the 30 minute mark), simply cover the baking sheet loosely with aluminum foil and keep roasting. I didn't need to do this but all ovens are different!

While the sheet pan is in the oven, make your miso yogurt: In a medium bowl, stir together all the ingredients (1/3 cup plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons miso paste, the juice of half the zested lemon, 2 teaspoons maple syrup, and a pinch of salt). Taste and adjust seasonings if needed until it’s perfect. If it’s too sweet, add a bit more lemon juice. If it’s too tart, add more syrup. If it’s dull tasting, add a little more miso or salt.
Serve the chicken and veggies drizzled with miso yogurt. DIG IN!

name: cacio e pepe primavera
note:
Must have meat: Grill some chicken to go alongside this or buy a rotisserie chicken and shred up about 2 cups and stir that in. For the grilled chicken: Marinate a few boneless, skinless chicken breasts in 3 tablespoons of Worcestershire, the juice and zest of 1 lemon, 3 grated garlic cloves, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Marinate it for at least 4 hours — and up to 24 hours — in the fridge. Grill for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until 160°F internally. Thinly slice and serve with the pasta. Don’t serve it as a big chicken breast — serve it sliced!

Dairy-free: You can make an equally delicious garlic and olive oil pasta primavera, but it won’t be a one-pot sitch (or as creamy obviously). While your noodles and veggies are boiling, add 1/2 cup EVOO to a large skillet over medium-low heat and throw in a bunch of finely sliced garlic cloves (like 5-6) and few shakes of red pepper flakes. Cook until the garlic turns a nice golden brown being careful it doesn’t burn, then take it off the heat. Once the noodles and veggies are drained (reserve 1 cup pasta water!), add them into the skillet of garlicky oil. Mix, adding lots of chopped fresh parsley, lemon juice and zest, salt and pepper, and some df Parm if you like it! Mix in some reserved cooking water to make it a little saucier if needed.

Gluten-free: Use a gluten-free noodle alternative like Banza.

To make a more traditional Cacio e Pepe: Ditch the veggies and lemon. Use spaghetti instead of orecchiette. Cut the Parm by 1/2 cup. Use a bit less cold water when making the paste. Done!

Make ahead: You can make this whole meal ahead of time and reheat it on the stove just before you eat! Just be sure to hang onto the reserved cooking water and read my note in the directions above for how to best reheat it. Warning: the veggies won’t be as bright green and beautiful when you reheat it.

Leftovers are a great thing: Make the entire batch even if you’re only serving two. Freeze individual (or double) portions in quart Ziplocs, and have a microwaveable pasta party at your fingertips on a night when you don’t feel like cooking! I always microwave frozen food in 45-second increments until warmed through.

Add some leafy greens: Toss in 4 big handfuls of spinach when you add the pasta to the cheese. It’ll wilt right in!

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of water (at least 8 cups) to a boil. Add 1 tablespoon salt.
Boil 1 pound orecchiette pasta for 3 minutes less than the package says. For instance: orecchiette cooks for 11 minutes, so you’d set your timer for 8 minutes.
When your timer goes off, add 1 chopped bunch of asparagus and 2 cups frozen peas to the pot with the pasta and cook for an additional 3 minutes, or until the pasta and asparagus are tender.

While the pasta is cooking, add 1 1/2 cups grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese and 1 1/2 cups grated Pecorino Romano cheese to a large serving bowl. Stir in 1/2 cup cold water, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon black pepper, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and the zest and juice of 1 lemon.
SAVE 1 CUP OF THE PASTA COOKING WATER by dunking a measuring cup or  mug or anything into the water and scooping it out!

Once you’ve reserved 1 cup of pasta water (yes, it’s worth repeating), drain the pasta and vegetables. Do not rinse them! Immediately add the hot pasta and vegetables to the bowl of cheese. I like to use two spoons here to really get in there quickly and toss everything together. It will look clumpy at first, but don’t worry! Just carry on and soon it will melt into a smooth creamy sauce. Add a bit of the pasta cooking water if needed to thin the sauce. It should be creamy and clinging to the pasta — not at all watery or not thick and clumping together.
Serve immediately, garnished with any or all of the following: thinly sliced fresh basil, a drizzle of EVOO, a sprinkle of Parm, flaky salt, more pepper, and/or red pepper flakes if desired!

name: one-pan coconut curry chicken with roasted vegetables and lime
note:
Leftovers: I recommend storing the vegetables, chicken, and extra sauce separately for optimum leftovers. The sauce will harden in the refrigerator - that’s normal (remember how hard the coconut cream was when it was cold in the can?).

Speaking of leftovers: make curried chicken salad with the leftover chicken. Shred leftover meat until you get at least 2 cups. Stir in 1/4 cup mayo (or Greek yogurt), 1 teaspoon curry powder, the juice of 1 lime, 1 chopped celery stalk, 2 tablespoons of raisins (or whatever dried fruit you have), 1 small chopped apple, a handful of chopped cilantro, and a pinch of salt. Season to taste. Add more mayo if needed.

When’s the last time you sharpened your knives? If you can’t remember, it’s time. Butchering the chicken will be a lot easier if you aren’t using dull knives!

Add greens to your meal: tear up several cups of spinach or kale, and stir it into the hot vegetables once everything is finished cooking. It’ll wilt in the residual heat!

Pressed for time? Grab 2 to 3 pounds of pre-chopped butternut squash at the store, and use that instead of chopping your own sweet potatoes and carrots.

Veggie subs: any root vegetable is great here. Any winter squash, potatoes, parnsips (they don’t float my boat but some people love ‘em), fennel (now that we all love fennel), golden beets (red beets will make the curry sauce a freaky color), cabbage (halve it, then cut each half into 3 large wedges), cauliflower, kohlrabi, rutabaga…

Fish sauce sub: I really want you to use fish sauce, but 1 tablespoon of soy sauce is a great swap.

Cilantro sub: hey cilantro haters. I see you, but I don’t understand you. Chop up a bunch of basil and use that instead!

Curry powder sub: equal parts red or yellow curry paste, or just use more cumin and turmeric.

Coconut cream sub: you can use a can of coconut milk instead, but I forbid you from purchasing “low-fat coconut milk”. It’s just coconut milk that’s been watered down! Why are you paying for canned water?

Whole chicken sub: Listen, yes, you can swap in other cuts of chicken, but I really don’t want you to! I want you to roast this chicken whole, because the curry sauce depends on the chicken fat dripping down onto the vegetables and mingling with the coconut milk. BUT IF YOU MUST KNOW, follow the below directions but use your meat thermometer to guide you!Bone-in skin-on chicken thighs or chicken quarters (aka the legs and thighs attached) will cook the same way as the whole chicken.  Boneless skinless chicken thighs: add along with the coconut milk and fish sauce, after the vegetables have been roasting for 20 minutes, then roast for another 15 to 20. Bone-in skin-on chicken breasts: same as the boneless skinless chicken thighs. Boneless skinless chicken breasts: add along with the coconut milk and fish sauce, after the vegetables have been roasting for 30 minutes, then roast for another 12 to 15 minutes. But, if I may intrude: why not roast the chicken as the recipe is written, then pull the bones and skin off of the breasts if you have a picky kid/spouse?

Bone-in skin-on chicken thighs or chicken quarters (aka the legs and thighs attached) will cook the same way as the whole chicken.

Boneless skinless chicken thighs: add along with the coconut milk and fish sauce, after the vegetables have been roasting for 20 minutes, then roast for another 15 to 20.

Bone-in skin-on chicken breasts: same as the boneless skinless chicken thighs.

Boneless skinless chicken breasts: add along with the coconut milk and fish sauce, after the vegetables have been roasting for 30 minutes, then roast for another 12 to 15 minutes. But, if I may intrude: why not roast the chicken as the recipe is written, then pull the bones and skin off of the breasts if you have a picky kid/spouse?

Cut your 3 to 4 pound whole chicken out of it’s plastic wrapping over the sink so that it’s juices don’t spill all over your counter, then pat the chicken dry with a paper towel, throw away the giblets (guts that are wrapped in a little baggy) if your chicken came with them, and transfer the chicken to a plastic cutting board, breast-side down. Use sharp kitchen shears or a chef’s knife to cut along each side of the spine and remove it from the chicken.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups red wine (whatever kind you like to drink)
ingredients.name: red wine (whatever kind you like to drink)

preparationSteps: Add 2 cups red wine, 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tablespoon garlic powder, 1 tablespoon dried oregano, and 1 tablespoon black pepper to a large ziplock or bowl and stir to combine.

Trim the fat (the hard white stuff) off of 1 tri-tip roast. It doesn’t have to be perfect, but there’s usually a large fatty piece on one side of the roast, and we want to trim as much of that off as possible. (Fat on meat usually = good, but this is too much.) Add the tri-tip to the marinade and marinate for up to 24 hours, but 4 at the bare minimum.

When you’re ready to cook, preheat the oven to 350°F. Bring 4 tablespoons of butter to room temperature. If you follow me on IG you know my tip — stick half a stick of (wrapped) butter in the waistline of your pants to bring it to room temp quickly.
Shake off as much marinade from the tri-tip as possible, then pat it completely dry.

Warm 2 tablespoons oil in your largest oven-proof skillet (such as a cast iron or stainless steel) over medium-high heat. When it starts to smoke, add the tri-tip and cook until a nice golden-brown crust forms, 4 to 6 minutes.
Flip, then smoosh the room-temperature butter onto the top (seared) side of the tri-tip.

Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 11 minutes per pound to cook it to medium (which is better than medium-rare when cooking tri-tip). So, if you purchased a 3 1/2 pound tri-tip and cut off 1/2 pound of fat, 3x11 = 33 minutes of roast time. It should reach between 140 and 145°F internally.
Remove the tri-tip from the oven and let it rest in the skillet. Tilt the skillet to the side and use a large spoon to spoon the pan juices over top of the tri-tip.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then slice against the grain.
