name: roasted mushrooms
note:
Tri-tip swaps: Beef tenderloin or any steak would work instead of tri-tip cooked the same way. Cook those to medium-rare (unless you prefer otherwise), AKA to 135°F internally. A roast chicken would be great instead of beef (and using the same marinade)! It will need about 60 to 90 minutes of cook time at 350°F (it depends on the size of the bird), or until the thickest part of the thigh registers 165°F. You won’t do the sear in the skillet, but can instead top the chicken with little pats (pieces) of butter. Scallops would also be delish! Grab 1.5 to 2 pounds fresh jumbo scallops (10 to 20 scallops per pound) — NOT bay scallops, which are small and rubbery and yucky IMO. Marinate them as written. Warm your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for at least 3 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon cooking oil and swirl to coat the pan. Let the oil heat up for at least 30 seconds. Place the scallops in the skillet at least 1 inch apart. You will have to cook in a few batches! Use a spatula to press them firmly down into the skillet to ensure a nice sear. Cook until golden-brown, for 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook on the second side for 1 minute, then add 2 tablespoons butter to the pan. Tilt the skillet to the side and use a large spoon to spoon the melted butter all over the scallops. Cook for 2 additional minutes once you’ve added the butter. Remove the skillet from the heat. Repeat with remaining scallops.

Beef tenderloin or any steak would work instead of tri-tip cooked the same way. Cook those to medium-rare (unless you prefer otherwise), AKA to 135°F internally.

A roast chicken would be great instead of beef (and using the same marinade)! It will need about 60 to 90 minutes of cook time at 350°F (it depends on the size of the bird), or until the thickest part of the thigh registers 165°F. You won’t do the sear in the skillet, but can instead top the chicken with little pats (pieces) of butter.

Scallops would also be delish! Grab 1.5 to 2 pounds fresh jumbo scallops (10 to 20 scallops per pound) — NOT bay scallops, which are small and rubbery and yucky IMO. Marinate them as written. Warm your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for at least 3 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon cooking oil and swirl to coat the pan. Let the oil heat up for at least 30 seconds. Place the scallops in the skillet at least 1 inch apart. You will have to cook in a few batches! Use a spatula to press them firmly down into the skillet to ensure a nice sear. Cook until golden-brown, for 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook on the second side for 1 minute, then add 2 tablespoons butter to the pan. Tilt the skillet to the side and use a large spoon to spoon the melted butter all over the scallops. Cook for 2 additional minutes once you’ve added the butter. Remove the skillet from the heat. Repeat with remaining scallops.

Cook the meat in a slow cooker: Prep and marinate the meat as written. This is a meat that’d benefit from a quick sear in a skillet before it goes into the slow cooker! Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Take the meat out of the marinade, pat it dry, and sear it for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Add it to the slow cooker, pour the marinade in around it, add softened butter on top, cover, and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or high for 3 to 4 (until it reaches 140 and 145°F internally). Let it rest for at least 10 minutes before you slice it.

Or, cook the risotto in a slow cooker: Grease the inside of the slow cooker pot with cooking spray, butter, or oil. Add 5 cups of warmed stock the pot plus the rice and stir to combine. Cover and cook on low for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring once about halfway through. Check it! If the risotto isn’t quite done yet, keep it cooking until it is. When it’s cooked, stir in the extra cup of stock and the rest of the ingredients and adjust seasonings as needed.

Dairy-free: Use DF Boursin (it’s a thing!), DF butter, DF Parm (or omit), and omit the burrata for those who can’t eat it. If you can find VioLife DF feta, that would be delish crumbled over the carrots.

Gluten-free: Swap soy sauce out for tamari or coconut aminos. Risotto is gluten-free but double check that the stock you’re using is too. Better Than Bouillon is gluten-free, but is made in a factory that is not gluten-free certified.

Vegetarian: If the whole group is vegetarian, omit the tri-tip and double the boursin risotto and mushrooms to make it the star of the meal. If just one or two of the diners don’t eat meat, you may want to double one of the veggie sides to ensure they get their fill!

Prep ahead: See the “plan of attack” section above for a timeline of what to prep ahead and when!

Veggie subs: Swap the carrots for thinly sliced cauliflower or delicata squash or cubed butternut squash. If you don’t like mushrooms, just omit that side and double the carrots, or swap in another family fave veggie side dish!

Love your leftovers: Make tri-tip sliders! Get a pack of King’s Hawaiian rolls, cut them in half, spread mayo and Dijon on one side, pepper jelly on the other side, add a layer of thinly sliced tri-tip, lots of cheese (whatever you have! cheddar, provolone, havarti, pepperjack…), close. Brush melted butter over the tops of the buns. Bake on 325°F for 10-15 minutes or until the cheese is melty. Yum. Store any other leftovers in airtight containers in the fridge and let people pick on them throughout the week!

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Toss 2 pounds sliced mushrooms, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 1/4 teaspoons garlic powder, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to your largest rimmed baking sheet and toss to evenly coat.
Roast for 40 minutes.
If you are cooking the tri-tip at the same time, stir several spoonfuls of those pan juices into the mushrooms at the end.
Transfer to a platter and sprinkle with a little chopped parsley.

name: sheet-pan summer corn pizza
note:
Must have meat: Mild Italian sausage would be delish! Crumble and cook in a medium-high skillet until cooked through. Drain off the grease then add it to the pizza at the same time as everything else.

Get more greens: In case you skipped the intro, a simple arugula side salad would be delightful alongside this recipe. Mix a bowl of arugula with a big squirt of fresh lemon juice, a healthy drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add some pepitas if you have them in your pantry and want to give your gut health an extra boost!

Make ahead: You can prep the veggies and Parm earlier in the day. Halve the tomatoes, grate the garlic, shuck and de-kernel the corn, slice the basil, grate the Parmesan — store it all in the fridge until it’s go time. Don’t pull the dough out more than two hours beforehand though!

Gluten-free: Google gluten-free pizza crust — there are a lot of easy recipes out there to DIY some gf dough! You could also use a cauliflower crust (but if you’re  doing dairy-free too, check the ingredient list as many pre-made cauli crusts contain Parmesan).

Dairy-free: Use df cream cheese brought to room temperature in place of the mascarpone and your favorite vegan mozzarella and Parm.

Can I use my pizza stone? Yep! Just preheat it in the oven then take it out, add the dough, and build the pizza on the stone. Don't try to build the whole pizza elsewhere then transfer it — that rarely works.

More pizza ideas, plz! Maybe you’re reading this in the dead of winter and delicious fresh corn and cherry tomatoes aren’t an option. Or maybe you don’t dig corn or cherry tomatoes. Or maybe you just successfully made this bomb homemade pizza and are officially on a kick. Whatever the case, I have some more pizza recipes for you here! And if you have my cookbook, Just Married, head to pages 168-169 for two cast-iron pizzas you’ll love (my sausage and honey and arugula pesto pizza insalata!).

preparationSteps: About an hour before you plan to eat dinner, grease an 18-by-13-inch half baking sheet with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Place the 1 pound pizza dough ball onto the baking sheet and cover it with plastic wrap for 30 minutes to 1 hour at room temperature.
While the dough is proofing (aka resting and rising at room temperature), halve 2 pints of cherry tomatoes and grate or mince 4 garlic cloves.
Preheat oven to 500°F.

Turn the dough ball over so that it is coated in oil, then use your fingers to press the dough out toward the corners of the sheet-pan. If it isn’t perfectly stretching to fill the entire pan, no worries — it doesn’t need to. Just press it out as best you can.

Spread 8 ounces mascarpone over the pizza. Scatter 2 pints of halved cherry tomatoes and 4 minced garlic cloves over top and season with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cover with 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese and the kernels from 2 ears of corn.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pizza dough is firm and the cheese is melted.
Scatter 1/2 cup thinly sliced basil leaves, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and a pinch of red pepper flakes over top. Take a bite — you might want to season with more salt at this point.
Cut your pizza into slices (I like lots of small squares) and dig in!

name: good luck soup
note:
Don’t mess with tradition: I hear you! If you love Hoppin’ John, make that on January 1st and make this today!

One more note about Hoppin’ John: There’s SO much important heritage, history, and tradition behind this classic collards, black-eyed peas, and ham dish. It’s a gorgeous and significant meal, and how it fits within the African-American diaspora absolutely merits exploring. I learned so much today reading this and this.

What do I serve this with? By itself!!! if you want a grain, serve it over microwavable frozen rice (or, ya know, cook some from scratch) or with a piece of naan or pita (or cornbread!!!).

Wait, you wash your collards after you chop them? YES! Molly thought we should flag this because it sounds more efficient than spinning big clunky leaves dry (and it is). I chop my dark leafy greens then wash and spin them dry in a salad spinner.

Tell me more about yellow curry paste: We’re using yellow curry paste, which isn’t as widely available as red and green curry pastes can be. Order it today on Amazon — I love Mae Ploy and Mike’s Organic. Last time we cooked with yellow curry paste, you all shared where you had luck finding it in the comments section. HMart, World Market, Safeway, Whole Foods, and neighborhood Asian markets are safe bets, but if you can’t find yellow curry paste, you can swap it for red or green curry paste! Green curry paste is the spiciest kind, so use just 1 tablespoon if making that swap. Red is next up, but heat level varies drastically by brand. Thai Kitchen is pretty mild but Mae Ploy is very spicy, so start with just 1 tablespoon and stir in more as needed. Yellow curry paste is quite sweet and mild, so the 3 tablespoons I call for here shouldn’t bother even the biggest spice wimps, but if you have ULTRA wimps, use only 2 tablespoons.

Freezer-friendly: Yes, you can freeze this meal if you have leftovers! Also yes, the sweet potatoes might get a little mushy after their trip through the freezer, but I don’t mind it. Let your curry cool then freeze it in an airtight container or Ziploc bag for up to 6 months. Thaw it in the fridge overnight then reheat on the stovetop, adding more stock if needed to loosen things up!

Prep ahead: This is a great make-ahead meal! Make the soup up to two days in advance and store it in the pot you cooked it in with its lid on in the fridge (or in an airtight container). Reheat on the stovetop over medium heat, adding more stock if needed. Or, if you don’t want to cook the whole thing, you can pre-chop your veggies up to two days in advance and store them in the fridge. Pancetta croutons can also be prepped ahead and stored in the fridge. Reheat them until warm in a 325°F oven or in a skillet over medium heat, adding a little extra oil or butter if needed to get them nice and crispy again.

Vegetarian: Skip the pancetta and just make croutons! Add 2 tablespoons butter to the pan in place of the pancetta fat then proceed with the recipe as written. Also use vegan fish sauce, miso, or extra soy sauce in place of fish sauce.

Gluten-free: Use coconut aminos, shoyu, or tamari instead of soy sauce, and use your favorite gluten-free bread for the croutons.

Dairy-free: Already is — just be sure to use DF butter or oil if needed for the croutons.

preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Cook 1 finely chopped onion until softened, about 3 minutes. Add 3 tablespoons yellow curry paste and 1 heaping teaspoon ground turmeric and continue cooking, stirring, until the paste starts to stick to the bottom of the pot.

Stir in 2 cans drained black-eyed peas, 1 pound peeled and cubed sweet potatoes, 2 cans coconut milk, and 2 cups vegetable stock. Use your spoon to scrape up any bits that are stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Raise the heat to high and bring it to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer (small bubbles!) and cook *uncovered* for 20 to 25 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, roughly chop and wash 1 large bunch of collard greens. You want pieces that are about 1 inch in size — long pieces are not as enjoyable to eat because they hang off your spoon!

Stir in the collards, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, the juice of 1 lime, and a squirt of sriracha if you like a little heat. *Cover* the pot and cook for 4 minutes to help the collards wilt. If you don’t have a lid for your pot, you can use a sheet pan!
Stir and taste. Does it need more salt? Add more soy sauce or fish sauce! Feel like it’s a bit too rich? Add more lime juice. Want a brothier soup? More stock.
Serve your soup topped with pancetta croutons. Enjoy a bowl on January 1st so that you can enjoy good luck, wealth, and progress all year long!!!

name: bee-sting pizza insalata

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16 ounce — aka 1 pound) fresh pizza dough ball
ingredients.name: fresh pizza dough ball

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14 ounce) can diced or whole tomatoes, drained
ingredients.name: diced or whole tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 Serrano pepper, thinly sliced (spice wimps, omit this)
ingredients.name: Serrano pepper, thinly sliced (spice wimps, omit this)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups (6 ounces) shredded mozzarella cheese, divided
ingredients.name: shredded mozzarella cheese

preparationSteps: Drizzle a 12-inch cast iron skillet (see above for more pan options) with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil. Plop a 1 pound pizza dough ball down right in the center of the pan and flip it around to coat it in oil. Cover the ball tightly with plastic wrap (here’s a visual) and leave it at room temperature for at least 30 minutes but up to 2 hours (the longer it sits, the better).

Meanwhile, place a rack on the bottom rung of the oven and preheat your oven to 475°F (or the hottest it will go) and make the pizza sauce. For the sauce, drain 1 (14 ounce) can tomatoes, then pour them into a blender along with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Blend until smooth. Set aside.
Thinly slice 1 Serrano pepper and set aside.

When the dough has been out for (at least) 30 minutes, uncover it and discard the plastic wrap. Use your fingers to “dimple” the pizza dough out until it fills the entire skillet. Sprinkle 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese over the crust, all the way to the edges. Spoon the sauce “dollop” style (aka no need to spread it into a layer) over the cheese. You won’t use all of the sauce! Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese over the sauce.
Cover the pizza with 4 ounces soppressata and as much thinly sliced Serrano pepper as you’d like (I use the whole thing).

Bake the pizza on the bottom rack for 17 to 20 minutes, until the bottom of the crust is golden-brown (use a spatula to lift it up and take a peek). If the bottom looks good but the top needs more time, transfer the pizza to the top rack of the oven for a few minutes to get brown on top.

Remove the pizza from the oven and place it on the stovetop to cool. Run a spatula around the edges of the pizza to detach it from the skillet. Let it cool for a few minutes, then use a spatula to slide it onto a cutting board.

While it’s cooling down, toss 1 1/2 cups arugula, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, and a big pinch of salt in a large bowl until evenly coated. Use a vegetable peeler the shave in a handful of Parmesan ribbons. Toss gently.
Drizzle the pizza with 2 tablespoons honey, then scatter the arugula over top. Cut into slices. Enjoy immediately!

name: short ribs and grits
note:
Vegetarian: You’re going to do a delicious braised vegetable situation. Get 3 pounds of Yukon Gold potatoes, halve them, and sear them cut-side-down just like we sear the ribs. Then proceed with the recipe, but also add 1 can of drained chickpeas. Do the rest of the recipe the exact same — the potatoes will be insanely creamy and delicious!

Gluten-free: It’s already gluten-free!

Dairy-free: Use Mykonos dairy-free butter and instead of the Cheddar cheese, stir in 8 ounces of dairy-free cream cheese.

Leftovers are a good thing: To reheat the grits, add them to a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water or milk and stir until creamy. When putting leftover short ribs away, throw the bone away and just store the meat. You can shred the meat and reheat it in a skillet, or just throw it in the microwave. Throw 1/2 cup of shredded short ribs and a bag of shredded Brussels sprouts in a skillet together and saute until the Brussels are tender for an insane Brussels sprouts hash situation.

Prep ahead: Short ribs are actually even better when they’re made a day in advance. Cook them, let them cool right in the sauce, and refrigerate the entire pot. When you’re ready to eat, just throw them in a 350°F oven for 30 minutes or until warmed through.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (or 1 chipotle pepper from a can, seeds removed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups grits (ideally you’ll be able to find stone-ground corn grits, but I know these are regionally specific. You might only be able to find quick-cooking grits, or you might only be able to find polenta. Any ground corn situation works!)
ingredients.name: grits (ideally you’ll be able to find stone-ground corn grits, but I know these are regionally specific. You might only be able to find quick-cooking grits, or you might only be able to find polenta. Any ground corn situation works!)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Season 4 pounds of short ribs with 2 teaspoons salt and 1 1/2 teaspoons pepper. Yes, that’ll seem like a ton of salt and pepper — trust the process. Season the ribs as early as you can — up to two days in advance. But if you have to do it right before cooking, that’s cool too!

Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot (preferably a cast iron Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Sear ribs until deep golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. You will probably have to do this in batches since they won’t all fit in your pot at once. Grab a wadded up paper towel with your tongs and soak up all of the excess grease in the pot.

Now add all of the other short rib ingredients to the pot: 3 cups beef broth, 1 small can of diced tomatoes, 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, 1 chopped yellow onion, 2 chopped carrots, 2 chopped celery stalks, 6 garlic cloves, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.
Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then turn off the heat. Nestle the seared short ribs into the braising liquid, bone-side-up. Cover the pot, transfer it to the oven, and cook for 3 hours.
After 3 hours, remove the lid from the pot and turn the heat up to 450°F. Cook for 30 more minutes to thicken the sauce up.
Depending on the type of grits you buy, they might take up to 2 hours to cook, or they might only take 30 minutes! Time your grits appropriately!

To make your grits: follow package instructions to cook the grits in water. All brands and types require different amounts of water and different times, so I won’t even try to guess. Just follow the package instructions! When the grits are cooked (they should be tender and creamy with a tiny bit of chew), stir in 8 ounces shredded white Cheddar cheese and 4 tablespoons butter. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper to start, then add more to taste.

Ladle about 1/2 cup grits into each bowl. Use tongs to place 2 short ribs on top of each bowl. The bone might slip right out — no problem if this happens! Just throw the bone away. If there are any leftover short ribs, place them on a separate plate so that we can blend the braising liquid into a sauce.

Use a ladle to skim any fat off the top of the braising liquid. Blend braising liquid using an immersion blender, or if you don’t have an immersion blender, use a ladle to scoop several cups into a blender and blend it there.
Taste the sauce and season it with more salt, black pepper and red pepper flakes as desired.
Ladle sauce over the ribs. Garnish with parsley. DIG IN and prepare for compliments!

name: healthy (or less healthy!) corn chowder
note:
Vegetarian: Skip the bacon!

DF/GF: To omit dairy, use coconut milk instead of heavy cream and skip the cheese or use your favorite plant-based cheddar alternative. To avoid gluten, just double check that your stock doesn’t contain any!

Make it a Southwestern chicken corn chowder: Stir in 1 1/2 tablespoons taco seasoning and 1 chopped red bell pepper along with the onion. Add 2 cups shredded cooked chicken and a 4-ounce can of green chilis when you stir in the cheese at the end. The cheese will be very good in this version. I’d use heavy cream and def include the bacon too :)

Make it Thai shrimp corn chowder: Skip the bacon. Stir in 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder and 1/2 teaspoon ginger powder along with the cayenne. Stir in 1 pound peeled shrimp, cut into bite-sized pieces, after you pour the blended soup back into the pot. Cook over medium-heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 1/3 cup chopped cilantro, the juice of 1 lime, and 1 tablespoon soy sauce (or 1 teaspoon fish sauce) at the very end.

Make ahead + love your leftovers: This is a great meal to cook over the weekend and reheat on a busy weeknight! I speak from experience when I say these leftovers are delicious for days when stored in the fridge. You could also freeze all or a portion of your chowder in airtight Ziploc bags. To do so, let it cool completely, pour it in the bag(s) then lay it flat on a sheet pan small enough to to fit in your freezer. Once it’s frozen, remove it from the sheet pan: It’ll be flat and easy to store! If you’re planning to freeze your soup, I’d suggest going with coconut milk over heavy cream as the soup will keep its consistency better.

preparationSteps: In a large heavy-bottomed pot (preferably a Dutch oven), cook 8 chopped strips of bacon over medium-high heat until crisp, 4 to 6 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the bacon to a paper towel-lined plate to drain, leaving the bacon grease behind.
Turn the heat down to medium and add 1 medium chopped yellow onion, 3 minced garlic cloves, and 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring frequently.

Add 1 large chopped Yukon gold potato, the kernels from 6 ears of corn, the corn cobs (the ones that you cut the corn off of — they are full of flavor for our soup!), and 3 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable stock. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low, cover, and cook for 30 minutes.
Discard the corn cobs.

Stir in 1 can full-fat coconut milk (OR 1 1/4 cups heavy cream), then use a ladle to transfer half of the soup to a blender. Or use an immersion blender and only blend half! Blend until smooth. If it is too thick and can’t blend properly, add a bit more stock. Hold the lid of the blender on with a dish towel so that the steam doesn’t make the lid pop off and explode hot soup all over you!

Pour the blended portion of the soup back into the pot along with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. If the soup is still too thick, add a bit more stock until it reaches a consistency you like. If the soup is too thin, continue simmering it over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until it reaches a consistency you like.
If you want a more decadent soup, allow the soup to cool for 5 minutes, then stir in 2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese. Delish!
Taste and adjust seasoning as desired.
Ladle into 4 bowls. Garnish with the crispy cooked bacon and thinly sliced green onion and/or chopped green herbs. Dig in!

name: one-pan roast chicken with goat cheese-mashed squash
note:
Vegetarian: Roast the squash solo for 30 minutes, then add 2 cans of chickpeas that have been drained, rinsed, and dried, then tossed with 2 tablespoons oil, 1 tablespoon minced rosemary, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 3/4 teaspoon salt for another 30 minutes.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Check that IG video I mentioned up top. You can skip the homemade chicken and opt for a rotisserie chicken instead (the video will show you how to make it fancy). Cook the goat cheese-mashed squash (it’ll need to roast for an hour).

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It’s already gf. For dairy free, use df cream cheese in place of the goat cheese in the mash, and df butter for the chicken.

Make ahead: The chicken will be best straight out of the oven, so you’ll want to time this one right so that it finishes right at dinner time.

What to do with leftovers: Leftover cooked chicken will stay good in the fridge for four days, BUT it’s only safe to reheat it once (so, you can’t reheat all your leftover chicken, eat half, then reheat THOSE leftovers the next day). To store leftover chicken: let it cool completely then stow it in an airtight container. I like to go ahead and shred any chicken to throw into dishes for lunch or dinner. Here are some recipe ideas for using up any extra you have (they’re not all written with chicken but it’d make for a delicious sub or addition!). Lastly: You can freeze cooked chicken. ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5- to 6-pound) whole chicken (sometimes called a “roasting chicken”)
ingredients.name: whole chicken (sometimes called a “roasting chicken”)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar or lemon juice (or any vinegar really)
ingredients.name: balsamic vinegar or lemon juice (or any vinegar really)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional if you want greens: 1 (8- to 9-ounce) bag spinach
ingredients.name: Optional if you want greens: 1 bag spinach

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place the whole chicken on the baking sheet and pat it dry with paper towels or a clean dish towel. Remove and discard any giblets from the cavity of the chicken. Season the inside of the chicken with big pinches of salt and pepper, then stuff it with 1 bunch fresh rosemary, 1 quartered lemon, and 2 halved garlic bulbs (it doesn’t matter if it falls apart — just stuff the bulbs and skin all inside).

In a small bowl, melt 3 tablespoons butter (I do this in the microwave, but you can throw it in a skillet if you don’t have one) and stir in 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Brush or use your hands to rub it all over the chicken skin.

Turn the chicken so that the breasts are facing up (check out the photo at the top of the newsletter). If you have kitchen twine, use it to tie the legs together. Tuck the wings under the chicken so that they’re tight against the breasts. This will help the chicken roast more evenly.

Place the acorn squash on the same baking sheet. No need to cut it or add any oil, just place it beside the chicken. Cut the top off of the third garlic bulb to expose the cloves. Drizzle it with olive oil and wrap in aluminum foil. Place it on the baking sheet as well.

Roast for 1 1/2 hours, or until a meat thermometer stuck into the meatiest part of the breast and thigh registers 160°F (or until the juices run clear when you cut between a leg and a thigh, if you don’t have a meat thermometer).
Let everything cool down for 10 minutes.

Cut the acorn squash in half. Scoop out and discard the seeds, then scoop the flesh into a bowl. Squeeze the roasted garlic into the bowl along with 3 big spoonfuls of the chicken drippings from the pan, 2 ounces goat cheese, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Mash! Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. You might want it saltier, tangier (more vinegar!), or creamier (more butter or cheese!).
Carve up the chicken (discarding the elements you stuffed it with) and serve over mashed acorn squash.
Want some greens? Scoop 2 tablespoons of chicken drippings into a nonstick skillet. Warm over medium heat. Add 6 cups of spinach and a pinch of salt and toss until wilted.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup freshly chopped flat leaf parsley
ingredients.name: freshly chopped flat leaf parsley

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 to 8 big slices of good bread (a whole grain, seedy situation would be great here)
ingredients.name: big slices of good bread (a whole grain, seedy situation would be great here)

preparationSteps: Cut 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes and season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Set aside.

Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch heavy-bottomed vessel (see the tools note above) over medium-high heat for several minutes, then add 4 ounces diced pancetta and cook until just crisp, 3 to 4 minutes. Add 1 1/2 pounds sliced mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, for an additional 12 to 15 minutes or until all of the moisture from the mushrooms has evaporated and they have browned.

Season with a hefty pinch of salt and pepper and stir in 4 minced garlic cloves and 1 tablespoon thyme leaves and cook for an additional minute. If at any point the pan looks dry, just add a little more oil. Stir in 1 tablespoon flour for the last 30 seconds. Everything will look weird and goopy — you’re right on track!

Stir in 2 cups white wine, the 1 1/2 pounds of cubed chicken, and 1 cup frozen pearl onions. Bring to a boil over high heat for 1 minute, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook *covered* for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in 2 big handfuls of spinach, 1 cup heavy cream, and another hefty pinch of salt and black pepper and simmer *uncovered* for 5 more minutes, until the spinach is wilted.

While your coq au vin is simmering, make your salty olive oil bread. To do so, coat 4 to 8 slices of bread (just depending on how much you want!) with a nice coating of extra-virgin olive oil. A really fun thing to do is to grill your bread — just turn the flames to medium-high and grill for a minute or two per side, uncovered, until nice grill marks emerge. Don’t leave the grill! You’ll burn the bread! When you take the bread off the grill, sprinkle each piece lightly with some flaky sea salt.

If you can’t grill right now, broil it in the oven for 1 to 2 minutes per side, again, not leaving the oven’s side because, if you do, you’ll forget and your bread will burst into flames and it’ll really put a damper on your evening.

After the spinach has wilted into your coq au vin, stir in 1/3 cup finely chopped parsley and 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Taste and add more salt and pepper as needed. Serve right away alongside your crispy bread!

name: 15-minute veggie peanut noods
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: I am setting you up for leftover success with the extra peanut sauce here! This stuff will be good in the fridge for up to a month. Next week, make a big pot of white rice, grill up some chicken, dumpster dive for raw crunchy veggies like cucumbers and bell peppers and make rice bowls with lots of peanut sauce on top. Need more direction? Try my Thai Basil Beef Bowls — you’ve already made the sauce! Or, ya know, just make another batch of these noodles!

Carb-phobic: swap in zucchini noodles (throw them in a really hot skillet with a bit of oil and cook for 2 minutes, then toss in the sauce) or cooked spaghetti squash (stir together over medium heat with the sauce).

Make ahead: Make the sauce up to a month in advance, but cook the ramen and veg right before dinnertime for best results. You can totally cook the noodles and veg up to 1 day in advance if needed, but keep the sauce and noodles separate in the fridge, then combine them in a skillet with a splash of water over medium heat to rewarm.

Must have meat: Grab a rotisserie chicken, shred up 2 cups of meat, toss it in. You’ll need to use some of the reserved sauce to coat everything. Or, make the 30-minute pork in a huge skillet, and add the noodles and sauce right to the skillet. Or, crispy tofu!

Gluten-free/soy allergy: Use tamari, coconut aminos, or shoyu, depending on what you can tolerate. Just taste and adjust seasoning if needed. For the noodles, try using a gluten-free spaghetti. There are some gluten-free ramen brands out there too!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 to 10 ounces fresh or dried ramen noodles (3 Maruchan packets)
ingredients.name: fresh or dried ramen noodles (3 Maruchan packets)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon sriracha, plus 1-2 tablespoons more, if desired
ingredients.name: sriracha, plus 1-2 tablespoons more, if desired

ingredients.rawIngredient: Dumpster dive for optional toppings: thinly sliced scallions, chopped cilantro, more sriracha, chopped toasted peanuts or almonds, sesame seeds, raw grated carrot…
ingredients.name: Dumpster dive for optional toppings: thinly sliced scallions, chopped cilantro, more sriracha, chopped toasted peanuts or almonds, sesame seeds, raw grated carrot…

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat. Stir in 2 tablespoons kosher salt.

Break 3 to 4 cups broccoli florets into even 1-inch pieces. I’m not even putting a cutting board and chef’s knife on this tools list because you can just pull them apart with your hands, making this a NO-CHOP recipe!

Add the broccoli and 8 to 10 ounces ramen to the boiling water and cook for 2 minutes. Add 1 cup frozen shelled edamame and cook for 1 additional minute. Test the ramen and broccoli for doneness — the ramen should still have a bit of chew to it, the broccoli should be tender.
Reserve 1/4 cup cooking water (you can use a coffee mug and just scoop it up until it’s halfway full) then drain the noodles and vegetables in a colander. Shake to get ALL of the water out.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup peanut butter, 1/3 cup soy sauce, 3 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon sriracha and 1 tablespoon honey. It’s going to seem very difficult to stir together but I promise it’ll come together eventually — just keep stirring! If your nut butter is really dry, it will be easier to mix it together in a blender. Adjust seasoning to taste. Seriously! Taste it! Need more salt? Soy sauce! Need more heat? Sriracha! Not creamy enough? More peanut butter!

Add the noodles back to the pot along with half of the peanut sauce and a splash (about 2 tablespoons) water. Stir to combine over low heat. Do you like your noods hella saucy? Add more sauce until it’s right for you. If they get too thick, add another tiny splash of water. Keep adding sauce and water until your noods are perfectly saucy to your liking. One of my testers used half of the sauce, the other used the whole thing!
Save any leftover sauce in a tupperware for up to 1 month, and see the notes below for ideas on how to use it (other than just making these noodles again).
Divide noodles between bowls and top with nuts and herbs if you have ‘em.
Questions? I get back to all comments ASAP! Please comment when you make it!
