name: sheet-pan chili crisp salmon and snap peas
note:
Love your leftovers: The chili crisp mayo will keep for weeks (roast some baby potatoes and serve them with chili crisp mayo, trust me), while leftover salmon, veggies, and rice will be good for up to 4 days. Just pack everything up in airtight containers and refrigerate. Reheat the salmon in the oven at 400°F for 5 minutes so it gets nice and crispy again.

What kind of salmon do I like? If you like buttery, fatty salmon, then you, like me, like farmed Atlantic salmon. Here’s the truth: it is not as good for you. Wild salmon is a lot more nutritious. But wild salmon is a lot leaner, and a lot fishier tasting. I simply do not like it. I’ve tried. I’m a Costco farmed Atlantic salmon gal.

Prep ahead: You can basically do everything ahead aside from cooking the salmon and snap peas. Make the rice, stir together the chili crisp panko mixture, toss the snap peas in chili oil and salt, and prepare the chili crisp mayo and store them all in separate airtight containers in the refrigerator. Press the panko mixture into the salmon and spread the prepped snap peas out on the parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet while the oven preheats and rewarm the rice in the microwave while everything cooks.

Vegetarian/Vegan: Replace the salmon with tofu! Place a cube of extra-firm tofu between two clean towels and put something heavy on top (like a cast-iron skillet) for 15 minutes to drain excess water. Slice the block into 1/2 inch-thick planks. Season and marinate them just like the salmon, add the tempura topping, and bake until the tofu and panko breading are firm and crispy, roughly 20 to 25 minutes. To make it vegan, replace the mayonnaise with vegan mayo.

Gluten-free: Swap in gluten-free breadcrumbs.

Dairy-free: It already is!

Peanut allergy: Some jars of chili crisp contain peanuts and/or peanut oil, such as Red Clay’s version. So be sure to seek out a chili crisp that doesn’t contain them, if needed, like the versions from Trader Joe’s or Fly By Jing.

Spice averse: If you can handle some spice but not too, too much, keep the crunchy stuff from the chili crisp in the recipe but replace the chili oil with olive oil or a mild-tasting oil like avocado or canola oil. If you’re super spice averse, though, leave the chili crisp out entirely (both crunchy stuff and oil) and just use sesame oil, olive oil or a neutral oil for the salmon and snap peas.

Feeding kids: If they’re sensitive to spice, follow the suggestions above!

Cooking for 1 or 2: This recipe is super easy to halve. And if you’re cooking for 1, you’ll have leftovers to look forward to for lunch or dinner tomorrow! If you don’t like leftover fish, only cook as many filets as you need, but keep the pound of snap peas. They’re so good.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions, stem removed, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions, stem removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken bone broth or stock (or, like me, use a big scoop of Better than Bouillon plus 2 1/2 cups water)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken bone broth or stock (or, like me, use a big scoop of Better than Bouillon plus 2 1/2 cups water)
For the salmon and snap peas:

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 jar chili crisp (you don’t need an entire jar)
ingredients.name: chili crisp (you don’t need an entire jar)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Take the chili crisp out of the fridge, if it’s in there, so that the oil can re-liquify (it hardens in the fridge). If you need to speed this up, stick it in the waistband of your pants, your body heat will heat it right up a la our favorite butter trick).

As always, start your rice first! Rinse 1 1/2 cups white rice (I put it in the pot, cover it with water, swish it around with my hand, then carefully dump out the water and repeat until the water runs clear). In a small pot or saucepan, warm 1 tablespoon sesame oil over medium-high heat. Thinly slice 1 bunch scallions (discard the root end) and cook until very tender, about 4 minutes. Add the rinsed rice and stir to coat in oil for about 1 minute. Add 2 1/2 cups chicken stock and a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat when it’s finished and let it continue to steam with the lid on until dinner time.

Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Place 4 salmon filets on one side, about 1 inch apart from each other, and pat dry with a paper towel. Season generously all over (about 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper per filet but you do not need to measure) with salt and pepper.

In a small bowl, combine 1 cup panko breadcrumbs with 1 tablespoon of the crunchy stuff that’s in the jar of chili crisp + 1 tablespoon of the oil from the jar of chili crisp, and a little sprinkle of salt. Stir until the breadcrumbs are coated. Divide between the salmon filets and press down to make them stick.

On the other half of the baking sheet, toss together 1 pound snap peas, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, and big sprinkle of salt until the snap peas are evenly coated. Spread evenly. If you have some sesame seeds, sprinkle them on the snap peas, but I’m not writing this into the ingredient list because it’s simply not necessary.

Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon easily flakes when you prod at it with a fork and the panko is golden-brown. I like to use a meat thermometer here—the filets should be 135°F for medium or 125° for medium-rare. If your panko isn’t nicely golden but your salmon is cooked through, you can turn on the broiler to crisp them up, but turn on the oven light, sit on your butt, and watch closely the entire time! They’ll burn quickly. Don’t ruin dinner!

While the baking sheet is in the oven, cut 1 lime into 6 wedges, then stir together 1/2 cup mayo and 1 tablespoon of the crunchy stuff that’s in the jar of chili crisp, the juice from 1 lime wedge (about 1 teaspoon), and a tiny pinch of salt.
Serve bowls with rice, salmon, snap peas, and chili crisp mayo, and a lime wedge for squeezing over everything.

name: poppy seed rolls
note:
Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be good for 3 to 4 days stored in airtight containers in the fridge. Here are delicious ways to use them up:Dice up ham and add it to the pastaAdd sliced ham to poppy seed rollsToss any leftover roasted veggies with greens, feta, pistachios, and dressing for a roasted veg salad. You could add diced ham if you have it. If you have a ton of leftover ham, you can freeze it! Wrap the sliced ham in plastic wrap or foil, then place it in a freezer-safe bag or container. Use within 2 months.

Dice up ham and add it to the pasta

Add sliced ham to poppy seed rolls

Toss any leftover roasted veggies with greens, feta, pistachios, and dressing for a roasted veg salad. You could add diced ham if you have it.

If you have a ton of leftover ham, you can freeze it! Wrap the sliced ham in plastic wrap or foil, then place it in a freezer-safe bag or container. Use within 2 months.

I have a frozen pre-cooked ham: Remove the ham from the freezer and place it in the refrigerator for 24-36 hours to ensure it’s thawed before you bake it.

Got a cocktail rec? Strawberry lemon margs! Or salty minty dogs!

Vegetarian: To make this meal vegetarian, swap the ham out for a frittata! If you have my book, turn to page 131 for frittata ideas. Or use the vegetarian note in this recipe.

Dairy free: Omit the Parm from the cheese board and the goat cheese from the salad (or swap it with a DF cheese alternative like dairy-free Parm). Use DF Boursin and Parm (or omit the Parm) from the pasta. Use plant-based butter sticks for the rolls and cake, and use DF sour cream for the sweet cream.

Gluten free: Make sure your granola’s gluten free. Use a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour for the cake. Use GF rolls and GF pasta.

Nut free: Swap the pistachios out for pepitas or just omit. Pay attention that your granola is nut free!

Feeding a bigger crowd/prep ahead/special ingredient/I just need a weeknight meal: Go back up and read the intro sections!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons granulated sugar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon (ideally an organic Meyer lemon), zested, 1/2 of it juiced
ingredients.name: lemon (ideally an organic Meyer lemon), zested, 1/2 of it juiced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound (aka 16 ounces, aka 1 standard clamshell container) of strawberries, de-stemmed and halved (or quartered if your strawberries are big)
ingredients.name: (aka 16 ounces, aka 1 standard clamshell container) of strawberries, de-stemmed and halved (or quartered if your strawberries are big)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Add 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter to a 10-inch (well seasoned!) cast-iron or nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook until browned, swirling the skillet occasionally. Let cool for 10 minutes (put it in the fridge to expedite).

Stir in 3/4 cup granulated sugar and the zest of 1 lemon for 30 full seconds. Add 2 large eggs (just crack them right into the skillet!). Add 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and a tiny pinch of kosher salt in a pile and use your fingers to mix the dry ingredients together. Now stir to combine them with the rest of the ingredients.

Smooth out the top of the mixture. Wipe/clean off the sides of the skillet (you can use your finger but, I’m just warning you, once you taste this cake batter your life will never be the same). Add 1 pound de-stemmed and halved/quartered strawberries on top with the cut sides facing down (see the pic for a visual). Sprinkle 1 tablespoon granulated sugar and the juice of 1/2 lemon over top.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center of the cake (don’t poke near a strawberry) comes out clean and the top and edges have turned golden.
While it’s baking, make your sweet cream by mixing together 1 cup of sour cream and 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar.
Slice the cake and serve with a big dollop of the sweet cream!
servings: Makes 12 rolls, easily doubled if needed

name: saucy chicken and cabbage satay bowls
note:
What do I cook this in/my store only sells 16-ounce bags/I want more veg: First things first: If your biggest skillet is 10 inches, you shouldn’t use a skillet to cook this meal (it’d overflow!). Use a deep pot, braiser, or Dutch oven instead. If you own a large 12- or 14-inch skillet, you can use that! But a few notes on cabbage and pan size, because bagged coleslaw/cabbage sizes vary a lot from store to store: A 12-inch skillet can hold 20 ounces of cabbage max without overflowing as you stir. So if you came home with two 12-ounce bags (rather than 10-ounce bags), use a pot instead to make stirring easier! A 14-inch skillet can hold more like 24-26 ounces of cabbage without overflowing. This is what I developed this recipe in, but I know a lot of you don’t have a skillet this big!If your store only sells 16-ounce bags of coleslaw/cabbage, you can decide whether you use one or two bags (or somewhere in between!). Love a lot of veg? Use both! Either way will taste delicious. If you’re going with two bags, definitely use a deep pot to prevent overflow, and know that it’ll take longer to cook down and release its liquid than if you cooked one bag. It’d also be a littles less saucy, but equally delicious. Regardless, the cabbage will look like a LOT when you add it to the skillet. It’ll shrink a ton as it cooks!

A 12-inch skillet can hold 20 ounces of cabbage max without overflowing as you stir. So if you came home with two 12-ounce bags (rather than 10-ounce bags), use a pot instead to make stirring easier!

A 14-inch skillet can hold more like 24-26 ounces of cabbage without overflowing. This is what I developed this recipe in, but I know a lot of you don’t have a skillet this big!

If your store only sells 16-ounce bags of coleslaw/cabbage, you can decide whether you use one or two bags (or somewhere in between!). Love a lot of veg? Use both! Either way will taste delicious. If you’re going with two bags, definitely use a deep pot to prevent overflow, and know that it’ll take longer to cook down and release its liquid than if you cooked one bag. It’d also be a littles less saucy, but equally delicious.

Regardless, the cabbage will look like a LOT when you add it to the skillet. It’ll shrink a ton as it cooks!

Double it/halve it: Add rice or another grain to stretch this meal or make it more filling. This is an easy recipe to double if you’re feeding a crowd or want leftovers to eat for lunches or to freeze. You could also easily halve it if you’re cooking for 1 (though I always encourage you to make the whole recipe and freeze half for future you!).

What kind of rice? Any cooked rice or grain you love! Frozen microwaveable rice is always a go-to here at What to Cook, or you can cook a pot of jasmine or brown rice, or some quinoa or couscous.

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be fab for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container, or frozen for 3 to 6 months in an airtight ziplock bag or freezer-safe container. You could serve it over rice or as lettuce wraps or as is. I think leftovers are good warmed in the microwave or a skillet, or even cold straight out of the fridge.

Prep ahead: If you’re looking to chip away at this recipe throughout the day, you can finely chop your mushrooms and cilantro and thinly slice your scallions ahead of time. Store them in airtight containers in the fridge. This is also a great recipe to cook from start to finish earlier in the day, then reheat in a skillet over medium heat when it’s time for dinner. Add a few splashes of water to make it saucy again if reheating.

Feeding kids/spice wimps: The sriracha in the recipe isn’t enough to add potent spice to the dish, but feel free to omit it just in case.

Vegetarian: Use a block of extra-firm tofu instead of chicken! Gently squeeze the whole block of tofu over the kitchen sink to get excess moisture out. Also pour out the liquid from the container. Use your hands to break off pieces of the tofu and squeeze them (again, over the sink), letting them crumble as you do, then place the crumbles in the container the tofu came in. Repeat until it’s all crumbled and as dry as possible. Add the crumbled tofu in a thin layer to the empty half of the skillet after you cook the veggies and let it cook untouched for 3-4 minutes, until golden on the bottom. Stir and repeat until it’s looking golden all around (add more oil to the skillet if needed), then mix it with the veggies and proceed with the recipe as written. See fish sauce subs below!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: It’s already dairy free. If avoiding gluten, swap the soy sauce out for coconut aminos or tamari.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons sesame oil or any neutral cooking oil (such as avocado), divided
ingredients.name: sesame oil or any neutral cooking oil (such as avocado)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (10- to 12-ounce) bags coleslaw mix or shredded cabbage (see notes if your store only sells 16-ounce bags!)
ingredients.name: coleslaw mix or shredded cabbage (see notes if your store only sells 16-ounce bags!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) container sliced mushrooms (any kind), finely chopped
ingredients.name: sliced mushrooms (any kind)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions, roots trimmed off and discarded, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions, roots trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2/3 of a can of coconut milk (if it has hardened on top, use a spoon to scoop the hardened part into the skillet — it’ll melt down quickly)
ingredients.name: of a can of coconut milk (if it has hardened on top, use a spoon to scoop the hardened part into the skillet — it’ll melt down quickly)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch cilantro, leaves and stems, finely chopped (about 1 packed cup)
ingredients.name: cilantro, leaves and stems, finely chopped (about 1 packed cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, grated on a microplane or minced (or 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger, grated on a microplane or minced (or 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 garlic cloves, grated on a microplane or minced (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, grated on a microplane or minced (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce (or 2 tablespoons if using regular soy sauce)
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce (or 2 tablespoons if using regular soy sauce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons rice vinegar or the juice of 1/2 lime
ingredients.name: rice vinegar or the juice of 1/2 lime

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: sesame seeds, chopped peanuts, or everything bagel seasoning for garnish, and/or rice for serving
ingredients.name: Optional: sesame seeds, chopped peanuts, or everything bagel seasoning for garnish, and/or rice for serving

preparationSteps: In your largest skillet (or a large pot), warm 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high heat. Add 2 bags coleslaw mix, 8 ounces chopped mushrooms, and 1 thinly sliced bunch of scallions (both the white and green parts) and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the cabbage and mushrooms are just beginning to soften. Scooch everything over to one half of the skillet. Warm the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in the other empty half of the skillet and add 1 pound ground chicken. Let the chicken cook for 2 to 3 minutes undisturbed, then start flipping and stirring it, using a spatula to break the chicken up into tiny pieces as it cooks — no big chunks allowed. Continue stirring the cabbage occasionally as you cook the chicken.

Once the chicken is cooked through (after about 8 to 10 minutes), stir it together with the cabbage. If there is still liquid in the skillet, crank the heat up to high and keep stirring until it’s all evaporated.

Reduce the heat back down to medium-high, season everything with a big pinch of kosher salt, then stir in the remaining ingredients: 2/3 of a can of coconut milk, 1 bunch finely chopped fresh cilantro, a grated 1-inch piece of ginger, 2 grated garlic cloves (I use a microplane to grate my ginger and garlic directly into the skillet), 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon creamy peanut butter, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 1 tablespoon sriracha, 2 teaspoons rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon honey, 3/4 teaspoon curry powder, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin.

Cook on medium-high for 3 to 5 minutes, until the liquid has thickened and is clinging to the chicken and vegetables. If it’s still really liquidy after 5 minutes, crank the heat up to high, stir frequently, and it’ll thicken up quickly. As always, taste and adjust seasonings until it’s perfect (you could add a pinch or two more salt if the flavors need to pop more, some lime juice or more vinegar for extra tang, honey for more sweetness, sriracha for spice, etc.!).
Serve over rice, if you’d like, or just by itself! Garnish with sriracha, peanuts, and sesame seeds to make it look less like beige slop, but either way, who cares, it’s delicious!
servings: Serves 2-3 if served on its own, or 4 if served with rice

name: twice baked delicata squash
note:
I don’t like squash skin. Delicata squash skins are entirely edible, but if you’re not into it, you can actually just discard the skins, leave the filling in the skillet, smooth it out, sprinkle it with cheese, and bake it right in the skillet. Scoop it out and serve it like a casserole — plop it in a bowl and enjoy!

Feeding kids: Remember team, branding is everything! Perhaps your kids will go for “sausage boats?” If they’re casserole lovers, see the “I don’t like squash skin” note above.

Bulk up the salad: Add candied nuts or any roasted nut, apple (I know there’s already apple in the squash but it would be great raw and crisp in the salad), pomegranate seeds, and/or more shredded white Cheddar cuz why not?

Bump up the protein: Add a can of rinsed and dried cannellini beans to the sheet pan along with the kale. Yum.

OK but what if I want to make this a side dish? This would be a delightful holiday side. I would make it this exact same way, but cut the squash halves in half after they’ve finished twice-baking so they’re more “side” portions.

Add something sweet: Raisins, dates, or another dried fruit would give the filling a nice pop of sweetness, if you have them and and would be into that!

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be great for up to 3 days. I wouldn’t freeze the assembled stuffed squash as the squash would get mushy. But the filling would freeze so well! The warmed kale salad is best right of the oven, so only cook as much as you plan to eat for this meal.

Prep ahead: You can prep the whole recipe through the step when you assemble the stuffed squash up to a day ahead. Store the stuffed squash covered in the fridge until you’re ready to bake. Bake them for 20 minutes instead of 10 so they’re warmed all the way through. If the cheese is scorching on top with the added bake time. Cover them all with foil while they finish cooking.

Vegetarian: Grate 8 ounces of tempeh on the largest hole of a box grater. Cook it in a skillet in a little oil and all of the same seasonings I mention in the “you can make lean ground meat taste like sausage” section above the recipe. Or, use a vegan ground “sausage.”

Dairy-free: Use a DF cheese if you’re into it, or just skip the cheese! It’d be delicious without it.

Gluten-free: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs like these or cooked rice.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 delicata squash, halved (try to buy squash that are as uniform in size as possible)
ingredients.name: delicata squash, halved (try to buy squash that are as uniform in size as possible)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of garlic (AKA the entire bulb!)
ingredients.name: of garlic (AKA the entire bulb!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound Jimmy Dean sage sausage (or any ground sausage, but if you have the choice, that’s the one)
ingredients.name: Jimmy Dean sage sausage (or any ground sausage, but if you have the choice, that’s the one)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces chopped, washed kale (store-bought in a bag)
ingredients.name: chopped, washed kale (store-bought in a bag)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Trim the tiniest bit off of both ends of 4 delicata squash to remove the root end and the stem. Trim the top off of 1 head of garlic (see minute 6:55 of the video above for a demo!) so that the tops of all of the cloves are exposed.

Cut the squash in half vertically, then use a spoon to scoop out (and discard) the seeds. Place the squash halves on the sheet pan skin-side down, along with the head of garlic. Drizzle the insides of the squash and the exposed garlic cloves with extra-virgin olive oil. Season everything with kosher salt (about a teaspoon total between all 8 squash halves plus another pinch for the garlic) and freshly cracked black pepper.
Flip the squash cut-side down on the baking sheet. Wrap the garlic head in aluminum foil — just tightly smoosh some foil around it.
Roast for 30 to 40 minutes, until the squash and garlic are very tender. Check at the 30 minute mark — if the squash is still hard, keep roasting! You want it to be squishy when you push down on it.

Meanwhile, prepare the filling. Add 1 pound ground sausage to a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, using a spatula to break the sausage up into tiny crumbles, until it’s brown all over, 6 to 8 minutes. While it’s cooking, grate 1 apple using the largest hole of a box grater, and add it into the skillet along with 1/2 cup panko. Stir to combine everything and continue crumbling the meat. Once the sausage is cooked through, remove the skillet from heat.
Grate 8 ounces of white cheddar cheese on the largest hole of the box grater (it’s OK if it’s covered in apple guts, no need to wash it) and set it aside.

Once the squash and garlic are out of the oven and cool enough to handle, squeeze the roasted garlic directly into the sausage mixture. Use a spoon to carefully scrape as much of the squash flesh out as possible without ripping the skins. You don’t need to get all of the squash out! The skins are thin and will rip easily if you try to scrape them down completely. Even if the skins rip, don’t stress — when the filling is in there you can squeeze everything back together. Add the scooped-out flesh and half of the shredded cheese to the skillet and stir to combine. Use your spatula to break up large chunks of garlic and squash so it’s all well incorporated. Taste and add more salt and/or pepper if needed. I add about 1/2 teaspoon of salt here!
Scoop the filling back into the now-empty squash skins. Add the remaining cheese on top. Bake for 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melty.

Right after you put the stuffed squash in the oven, line a second baking sheet with parchment paper. Dump 10 ounces of chopped kale (or however much you want to eat for this meal) onto the baking sheet. Drizzle the kale with 2 tablespoons EVOO, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, and a big pinch of salt (about 1/2 teaspoon). Use your hands to lightly massage the kale to make sure it’s evenly coated. Add the baking sheet to the oven with the squash and let it cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until crispy on the edges but still tender on the bottom.
Remove both pans from the oven and plate a stuffed squash (or 2 if you’re really hungry!) with a side of warmed kale salad. ENJOY!

name: farro fattoush
note:
Is it safe to eat the farro when it’s been cooked with raw chicken?!?!?!?! Yes.

What’s a “low bowl”? I love eating salads — and almost any other meal — out of a low, or shallow, “coupe” or “entree” bowl like the ones pictured. I also love these and these.

Farro note: Farro comes in a few types: pearled, semi-pearled, and whole, AKA unpearled. You can use whatever farro you have or can find at the store — they just have different cook times, so read the instructions on the bag to see how long yours will take to cook. If you’re new to farro, you are cooking it until it’s tender yet chewy (similar in texture to pasta cooked al dente).

Tomato note: If you plan to meal prep this salad and eat it for more than 48 hours, I recommend omitting the tomatoes — they get mushy IMO. You can always add them to the individual bowls.

Why are my leftovers watery? Adding salt to veg makes them release their liquid! You can pour off any excess liquid that collects at the bottom of your container, or just shake the container to toss the liquids back into the salad.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Swap the farro out for microwaveable brown rice or quinoa (or any grain) and shred a rotisserie chicken rather than cooking it from scratch.

Prep ahead: If you want to prep some elements of this meal earlier in the day or the day before to make cooking it even easier, pre-chop your veg and store it in an airtight container in the fridge.

Love your leftovers: Like I said in the intro, this is a good-all-week situation! Just store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. If you want, you can brighten up each day’s serving with a new garnish of fresh green herbs and a squirt of lemon. I highly recommend the daily brighten up! A drizzle of balsamic glaze would also be delightful.

Feeding kids: This is a meal that I’d deconstruct for my boys. So before you mix and toss everything in the bowl, pull the individual elements out for their plates: a little pile of chopped chicken (with ketchup or BBQ sauce, if that’d get them to eat it!), a pile of whatever vegetables they like (with ranch, if that’d get them to eat it!), and a pile of farro (aka “fat rice”).

Vegetarian: Just skip the chicken! If you have some, use veggie stock instead of water (or add a spoonful of Better than Bouillon to the water) when cooking the farro to add some extra flavor. You can also add another can of beans (I’d do one can chickpea, one can cannellini!) for extra protein.

Tomato allergy: Add 3 thinly sliced and chopped radishes, 1 extra red bell pepper, and 1 green bell pepper in place of the tomatoes.

Dairy-free: There are great dairy-free feta brands! I like Miyoko’s. Or just omit the feta. You could add avocado for some richness and/or chopped Castelvetrano olives for a briny note.

Gluten-free: Use brown rice instead of farro. It’ll take roughly 45 minutes to cook — check the bag to see exactly how long, but ignore the water measurements and instructions, you can absolutely boil brown rice in a big pot of water, like we’re doing here! Just remember to pull the chicken out after 15 or 20 minutes.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 large lemon (preferably organic since we’re zesting it)
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 large lemon (preferably organic since we’re zesting it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 orange OR yellow bell pepper, finely chopped
ingredients.name: orange OR yellow bell pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 English cucumber, seeds removed, finely chopped
ingredients.name: English cucumber, seeds removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 heaping cup fresh dill, finely chopped
ingredients.name: heaping cup fresh dill

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 heaping cup fresh parsley or cilantro, finely chopped
ingredients.name: heaping cup fresh parsley or cilantro

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved (see notes if you plan to meal prep this recipe!)
ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes, halved (see notes if you plan to meal prep this recipe!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 7 to 8 ounces feta (buy a block, not pre-crumbled, if possible)
ingredients.name: feta (buy a block, not pre-crumbled, if possible)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional for crunch (add as a topping to individual bowls, if desired): crumbled pita chips, chopped roasted pistachios or almonds, any sort of crouton
ingredients.name: Optional for crunch (add as a topping to individual bowls, if desired): crumbled pita chips, chopped roasted pistachios or almonds, any sort of crouton

preparationSteps: Bring a medium pot of salted water to a boil. Add 1/2 cup farro and 1 pound  boneless skinless chicken breasts. The chicken will take 12 to 20 minutes to reach 165°F internally (which is when you should pull it out of the pot), and the farro will take between 20 and 45 minutes to fully cook depending on the type of farro you have (see notes below the recipe for more on this). Just pull the chicken out of the pot when it’s fully cooked and keep cooking the farro until it’s tender.
While those cook, get chopping!

Mince 1 large shallot and 1 large garlic clove. Add them to a large serving bowl along with 3/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/3 cup red wine vinegar, the zest and juice of 1 large lemon, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, and 2 teaspoons kosher salt. Whisk everything together until smooth.

In a colander, drain and rinse 1 can chickpeas (keep the colander out! we’re going to use it for the farro in a bit). Add the chickpeas to the serving bowl and smash them lightly (this helps the chickpeas absorb the dressing because dry chickpeas suck). Stir them into the dressing.

You’re about to finely chop all your produce — as you’re chopping, keep adding them to the large serving bowl. Don’t let them pile up on your cutting board! That will make things less efficient and more annoying for you.

Finely chop 1 red bell pepper, 1 orange or yellow bell pepper, 1 English cucumber (cut the cucumber in half vertically, remove the seeds with a spoon — this is important because they’re so watery! — cut each half in half, then dice), 1 heaping cup fresh dill, and 1 heaping cup fresh parsley (or cilantro). Halve 1 pint cherry tomatoes, if using.
Shred or chop the cooked chicken and drain the farro when it becomes ready.

Add everything to the bowl and toss to coat in dressing. Taste, then stir in lots of kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper (probably at least 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper) until it’s delicious. Use your hands to crumble 8 ounces feta over top. Option to drizzle olive oil, sprinkle flaky salt, and grind black pepper on top, if you want to make it look restaurant-y.
Serve in low bowls and top with a crunchy thing, if desired!

name: sheet-pan sausage, sweet potatoes, and apples
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Opt for pre-cubed sweet potatoes, and pre-cubed butternut squash in lieu of the carrots to save time and avoid having to chop anything. You can even buy pre-sliced apples at many stores if you need a total shortcut!

YUM… but I’m super hungry: Make the meal even heartier by serving it over brown rice or farro instead of spinach.

WTC recipe collabs: So speaking of farro… This would be amazing served atop my roasted asparagus farro-tto (remember that guy from back in March?) minus the asparagus. Another WTC recipe combo idea: Skip the fancy chicken fingers and serve this dish atop the greatest kale salad.

Make ahead: Wash and cube your veggies up to a day in advance and store them in the fridge. You can go ahead and mix up the “marinade” sauce too, again stored in fridge. Mix them all up on your sheet-pan when it’s time to cook.

Vegetarian: Opt for plant-based sausage. Slice it and add it to the pan when you add the apples.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Done and done! (Obviously just don’t add the optional cheese I mention if df, or farro if gf.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds sweet potatoes, scrubbed and 1-inch cubed (peeling is optional)
ingredients.name: sweet potatoes, scrubbed and 1-inch cubed (peeling is optional)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large carrots, scrubbed and 1/2-inch sliced on the bias (no need to peel if you scrub them clean!)
ingredients.name: large carrots, scrubbed and 1/2-inch sliced on the bias (no need to peel if you scrub them clean!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound sweet or hot Italian sausages (the uncooked kind — see below for directions on how to cook pre-cooked chicken sausages)
ingredients.name: sweet or hot Italian sausages (the uncooked kind — see below for directions on how to cook pre-cooked chicken sausages)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red apple (such as Honeycrisp or Pink Lady), cut into 1/2-inch wedges
ingredients.name: red apple (such as Honeycrisp or Pink Lady)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon, cut into wedges for serving
ingredients.name: lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: a tiny bit of cheese like grated parmesan or crumbled goat cheese or feta
ingredients.name: Optional: a tiny bit of cheese like grated parmesan or crumbled goat cheese or feta

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a rimmed sheet-pan with parchment paper.

On the sheet-pan, toss everything except the apples and spinach (so that’s 1 1/2 pounds of cubed sweet potatoes, 2 sliced carrots, 1 pound of uncooked sausages, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon miso paste, 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper).
The miso will be kind of clumpy and difficult to combine — just get in there with your hands and smoosh and smash it until it’s all evenly combined. You can do it!
Now prick each sausage 3 times with the prongs of the fork. This will ensure they don’t explode!
Roast for 20 minutes.
Remove the sheet-pan from the oven, transfer the sausages to a cutting board, and cut into 5 or 6 pieces, on the bias (AKA on a diagonal — not straight across into circles).
Add 2 cut-up apples and the cut sausages back to the sheet-pan and toss thoroughly to coat everything in all of those juices that have collected in the pan.
Return the sheet-pan to the oven and roast for an additional 15 to 20 minutes. Check the sweet potatoes and carrots at the 15 minute mark — when they can be easily pierced with a fork, they’re ready!
Sprinkle with any fresh herb you have, if you have some. Taste the vegetables and season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the sausage and veggie mixture over top of a big plate full of spinach. Drizzle with your best extra-virgin olive oil and squeeze lemon juice over top. If you want, throw some cheese on there.

name: pork chops with apples and polenta

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large apples (such as Granny Smith or Honeycrisp, or both!), 1/2-inch sliced
ingredients.name: large apples (such as Granny Smith or Honeycrisp, or both!), 1/2-inch sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: a pinch of cinnamon and garam masala or cumin
ingredients.name: Optional: a pinch of cinnamon and garam masala or cumin

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup instant polenta (check the bag before you buy it — you want the kind that takes about 5 minutes to cook)
ingredients.name: instant polenta (check the bag before you buy it — you want the kind that takes about 5 minutes to cook)

preparationSteps: Season 4 pork chops generously (as in, way more than you think!) with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Heat a 12-inch skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high heat for several minutes. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and warm for 30 seconds. Turn on your oven vent — things are about to get smoky! I also crack open a door to help vent the smoke.

Cook the pork chops for 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until an instant thermometer registers 135°F. If the sides look pink, use tongs to hold them up and sear each side for 30 seconds. Transfer pork chops to a plate and reduce skillet heat to medium.
Now you’ll get the polenta going at the same time that you cook the apples and onions.

Warm 2 cups whole milk in a pot over medium-high heat. When the milk starts to bubble, whisk in 1 cup instant polenta and cook until the polenta is soft and thick, about 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in 1/3 cup parmesan, 1 tablespoon thyme leaves, 1 tablespoon butter, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper. If it gets too thick, just stir in a bit of milk to loosen it up. Add more salt and pepper to taste, if desired.

To the skillet over medium heat, add the second tablespoon of olive oil, 1 sliced onion, 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves, and 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves. Season with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until the onions are soft but not totally shapeless. Add 2 sliced apples and cook for 4 to 5 more minutes, until they are soft and warm, but not mushy.

Remove skillet from heat and stir in 2 tablespoons unsalted butter and 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar until incorporated. Taste. I love the simplicity of this chutney-inspired concoction, but sometimes I’m in the mood for more of a bold flavor and I’ll add a big pinch of cinnamon and garam masala. Maybe a little cumin too if I’m feeling wild.
Slice the pork chops into 1/2 inch-thick slices and serve over polenta, with the apples and onions served over top.

name: early dismissal pot roast

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (3-pound) boneless chuck roast or bottom round
ingredients.name: boneless chuck roast or bottom round

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large bulb fennel, halved and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: large bulb fennel

ingredients.rawIngredient: Herby Horseradish Cream (recipe follows), for serving
ingredients.name: Herby Horseradish Cream (recipe follows), for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Season 1 (3-pound) boneless chuck roast or bottom round all over with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. When the oil is shimmering, add the meat and cook until nicely browned all over, about 6 minutes on each large side and 2 minutes on each small side. Transfer the roast to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and add 4 ounces cubed pancetta. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the pancetta is crispy, about 4 minutes.

Meanwhile, roughly chop 2 of the carrots, 2 celery stalks, and 1 large white onion. Add the veggies, along with 8 garlic cloves, to a food processor and pulse about 8 times to finely chop the ingredients. Add the veggies to the pot and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until a thick, paste-like mixture forms, 10 to 12 minutes. (The veggies will release a lot of liquid at first and then dry out.) Stir in 1 tablespoon tomato paste and cook until it darkens to a deep red, about 2 minutes. Stir in 1/2 cup red wine and 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes and season with salt and pepper. Add 1 thinly sliced fennel bulb, 1 pound of peeled pearl onions, and 8 ounces sliced cremini mushrooms. Cut the remaining 2 carrots into 1-inch pieces and add them to the pot. Stir to coat everything in the tomato sauce and bring to a simmer.
When the sauce begins to simmer, use tongs to nestle the seared roast into the center of the pot. (You might have to move some veggies out of the way to make room, but everything should fit snugly.)
Gather 2 parsley, 2 rosemary, and 2 sage sprigs into a bundle, wrap it a few times with a piece of kitchen twine, and tie it tightly. Drop the bundle into the tomato sauce and cover the pot.

Roast for 3 to 4 hours, until the meat is fall-apart tender. Make the Herby Horseradish Cream (recipe below) while it’s roasting. Remove from the oven and use tongs to roughly break up the meat into large pieces. Serve from the pot with the horseradish cream alongside.

name: herby horseradish cream
preparationSteps: In a medium bowl, combine 1 (16-ounce) container sour cream, 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley, 1/4 cup chopped fresh basil, 1/4 cup prepared horseradish, and a large pinch of kosher salt.
Whisk to mix well. Cover tightly with cling wrap and refrigerate until ready to serve, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: one-pot pantry pasta
note:
Riff options:Taco pasta: Stir in 1 tablespoon taco seasoning and things like corn, beans, and diced red bell pepper.Bolognese: Stir in 1 diced celery stalk and 1 diced carrot along with the onion. Use 1 (14 ounce) can of tomato sauce instead of ketchup/tomato paste.Beef stroganoff pasta: Add 8 ounces sliced mushrooms along with the beef. Instead of cheese, stir in 1 cup sour cream and 1 tablespoon dijon mustard at the end.

Taco pasta: Stir in 1 tablespoon taco seasoning and things like corn, beans, and diced red bell pepper.

Bolognese: Stir in 1 diced celery stalk and 1 diced carrot along with the onion. Use 1 (14 ounce) can of tomato sauce instead of ketchup/tomato paste.

Beef stroganoff pasta: Add 8 ounces sliced mushrooms along with the beef. Instead of cheese, stir in 1 cup sour cream and 1 tablespoon dijon mustard at the end.

Vegetarian: Use 1 1/2 pounds thinly sliced or diced mushrooms instead of 1 pound ground beef. Cook them (along with the other veggies) until all liquid has evaporated. If you hate mushrooms, skip them and up the cauliflower to 2 cups and add a thinly sliced red bell pepper or two.

Wanna make it a bit healthier?: Use 3 1/4 cups broth and 1 cup milk, use less cheese, and stir in several handfuls of spinach at the very end, when you add the cheese. You could also stir in spinach and skip the other tweaks, if you just want to add some nutrient-rich greens.

Make ahead/love your leftovers: You can prep this whole thing a day or two ahead of time — store it in the fridge with the lid on, if you’ve got room — and reheat it over medium heat on the stovetop, stirring often. Add a splash of water or stock or broth as needed to loosen it up as you reheat. It’s also a delicious freezer meal! Freeze it in airtight bags or containers, thaw it in the fridge, and heat it on the stovetop over medium heat, adding liquid as needed.

Gluten-free: Do not — I repeat, DO NOT! — try making a one-pot pasta dish using a gluten-free, chickpea, black bean, or other noodle substitute (especially not chickpea!). It’ll be gross. Here’s what you’ll do instead: Cook the pasta by itself according to package instructions, reserving 1/2 cup of pasta water before draining. Cook the meat and veggies as written. Once the meat is cooked through and veggies are soft, add the ketchup (not the milk or stock!) to the pot and stir well. Add the cooked pasta, 1/4 cup reserved cooking water, and 1/4 cup of milk to the pot and stir. Add the cheese and stir some more. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Add some more cooking water or some splashes of milk if it’s too thick.

Dairy-free: Swap the Cheddar with your favorite df shredded cheese OR dairy-free cream cheese or ricotta (see Cheddar subs below for more info if going the soft “cheese” route). And use almond or soy milk instead of cow’s milk!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 yellow onion, diced (buy it pre-diced and this will be a no-chop meal!)
ingredients.name: yellow onion, diced (buy it pre-diced and this will be a no-chop meal!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound pasta (a short pasta like rigatoni, shells, orzo, or bow ties will be best)
ingredients.name: pasta (a short pasta like rigatoni, shells, orzo, or bow ties will be best)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups any kind of milk (or 1 cup heavy cream plus 3 1/2 cups broth, or 1 1/2 cups half-and-half plus 2 3/4 cups broth)
ingredients.name: any kind of milk (or 1 cup heavy cream plus 3 1/2 cups broth, or 1 1/2 cups half-and-half plus 2 3/4 cups broth)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces (2 cups) shredded sharp Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded sharp Cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large wide pot or braiser. Add 1 diced yellow onion, 1 pound ground meat, 1 1/2 cups cauliflower rice, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes if you like a bit of heat. Use a spatula to chop the meat into tiny crumbles as it cooks.
When the meat is cooked through and the vegetables are soft, 7 to 8 minutes, stir in 1 pound pasta.
Stir 2 1/4 cups stock, 2 cups milk, and 2 tablespoons ketchup into the pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce to a simmer and cook (uncovered) until the pasta is tender, 12 to 15 minutes.
Remove the pot from heat and let it cool down for 2 minutes. Stir in 8 ounces shredded sharp Cheddar cheese.
Taste and season with additional ketchup, salt, pepper, etc. until it’s perfect.

name: cheesy chicken and veggie enchilada skillet
note:
I’m feeding kids: If your kids reject all things green, use a yellow onion instead of green onions and peel the zucchini before dicing it!

Add some greens: If you’re not feeding green-averse eaters and want to up the nutrients of your meal, throw in 2 cups of chopped spinach toward the end of cooking — just before you add the tortilla strips. Stir it around until it’s wilted and incorporated.

Vegetarian: Simply omit the chicken. To add protein, you can add in an extra can of drained and rinsed black or pinto beans. To add more veggies, I’d add 2 diced zucchini, but you can use another bell pepper or pretty much anything! Just sauté them along with the red bell pepper and green onions.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use your favorite df cheese, or simply omit the cheese and bake for only 10 minutes since there’s no cheese to melt. It’s gluten-free as is!

Make ahead + love your leftovers: This is an excellent make-ahead meal. Go ahead and cook the mixture earlier in the day (or even the day before) — just don’t add the cheese yet. Store it covered in the fridge. About 25 minutes out from dinnertime, uncover it, top it with the shredded cheese, and throw it in the oven! Like most What To Cook meals, these leftovers make a superb lunch. You can also freeze individual portions in freezer-safe bags to enjoy for lunches/dinners weeks from now.

Can I use almond/cashew/alternative grain tortillas? You sure can. They get a little smooshier/softer, but I still dig it.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground chicken or turkey (or any ground meat, for that matter, or 4 cups shredded rotisserie chicken)
ingredients.name: ground chicken or turkey (or any ground meat, for that matter, or 4 cups shredded rotisserie chicken)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon taco seasoning (or 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon ground chili, 1/2 teaspoon ground oregano, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning (or 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon ground chili, 1/2 teaspoon ground oregano, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 (6-inch) corn tortillas, cut into 1-inch thick strips
ingredients.name: corn tortillas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded Mexican, cheddar, pepper jack, or whatever cheese you want
ingredients.name: shredded Mexican, cheddar, pepper jack, or whatever cheese you want

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional garnishes: sour cream, avocado slices, hot sauce, cilantro, radishes,pickled red onions, thinly sliced romaine lettuce
ingredients.name: Optional garnishes: sour cream, avocado slices, hot sauce, cilantro, radishes,pickled red onions, thinly sliced romaine lettuce

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

In a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, warm 2 tablespoons olive oil. Add 1 diced red bell pepper, 1 diced zucchini, and 1 thinly sliced bunch of green onions to the skillet and cook until the pepper and zucchini have softened slightly, about 4 minutes.

Scooch the vegetables over to one half of the skillet. Add a smidge of oil to the empty half of the skillet, then add 1 pound ground chicken and season it with 1 tablespoon taco seasoning. Use your spatula to break the chicken apart into tiny crumbles (no big clumps!) and cook until no longer raw. While you’re cooking the chicken, stir the veggies around a bit to make sure the bottom layer doesn’t burn.

Stir in 1 (28-ounce) can enchilada sauce, 1 (4-ounce) can diced green chilis, 2 cups frozen corn, 1 can black beans (drained), and 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes over medium-high heat, until thickened slightly. (Cooking something liquid-y over high heat while stirring frequently helps it “reduce,” AKA thicken up!) Taste. Add more salt if needed.
Add 12 sliced corn tortillas to the skillet and, using your spatula, incorporate them throughout the mixture so that they’re all separated and covered in sauce.
Sprinkle 2 cups of shredded cheese over top and place the skillet in the oven. If your skillet is really full, place it on top of a baking sheet in case it bubbles over.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the cheese is melted.
Let it rest for a few minutes, then garnish it up with your desired toppings and dig in!

name: the perfect tuna melt
note:
I’m feeding kids: This tuna salad is the BEST baby food. Calum and Mattis were raised on it! Calum (age 1 1/2) still loves it. Mattis (age 3 1/2) will eat it 1 out of every 5 times I serve it. Toddlers, man.

I don’t like tuna sandwiches: First of all, are you SURE? If you eat fish/tuna but have felt eh toward canned tuna sandwiches all your life, give this recipe a try!!! The pickle brine, garlic powder, and Dijon mustard combo give it a really fantastic flavor. Not fishy at all! And you simply can’t compare sad tuna salad on toasted bread to this tuna melt situation. That said: If you know you don’t like tuna or are a vegetarian, keep reading, I’ve got subs!

Vegetarian: Swap the tuna for 1 1/2 cans garbanzo beans, smashed (but not so much that it turns completely into a paste). I also like smashing in an entire avocado!

Which canned tuna should I buy? I slightly prefer tuna stored in oil over tuna stored in water, but either works. I usually buy Safe Catch Elite Pure Wild Tuna.

Make it a salad: Tuna melt, hold the bread! A salad of chopped romaine tossed in olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper with a scoop of tuna salad on top, lots of cubed cheddar cheese, cherry tomatoes, maybe some pickled red onions, and toasted pepitas or chopped almonds. SO GOOD.

Gimme some greens: See the note right above this one! That salad — minus the tuna and cheese — would make for a delish and easy side to plate your tuna melt with. (Or, ya know, you can go with a side of potato chips because #summer.)

Dairy-free/gluten-free: To eliminate dairy, use your favorite df cheese slices. For this meal to be gluten-free, go the Tuna Melt Hold the Bread route or use gf bread!

Prep ahead + leftovers are a great thing: The longer this tuna salad chills in the fridge, the more its flavors will meld together and the better it’ll taste! Tuna salad stays good for 3-5 days in the fridge (stored in an airtight container), so enjoy leftovers for snacks on crackers, on a salad for lunch, etc. You could also of course just use 1 or 2 cans of tuna fish and cut back on the other ingredients, as needed, if you don’t want leftovers!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 (5-ounce) cans tuna, preferably packed in olive oil, drained
ingredients.name: tuna, preferably packed in olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup bread and butter pickles, minced (or whatever pickles you like, or relish, or 3 tablespoons minced capers)
ingredients.name: bread and butter pickles, minced (or whatever pickles you like, or relish, or 3 tablespoons minced capers)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, plus more for your bread
ingredients.name: mayonnaise, plus more for your bread

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 slices sourdough (or whatever bread you love)
ingredients.name: sourdough (or whatever bread you love)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 slices sharp cheddar cheese (I like to buy the thin slices from the deli section, but you can also buy a block and slice it yourself of course!)
ingredients.name: sharp cheddar cheese (I like to buy the thin slices from the deli section, but you can also buy a block and slice it yourself of course!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: thinly sliced red onion, thinly sliced ripe tomatoes, lettuce
ingredients.name: Optional: thinly sliced red onion, thinly sliced ripe tomatoes, lettuce

preparationSteps: Place 2 large eggs in a small pot and cover with water by 1 inch. (FYI, I always boil more eggs than I need for a recipe to have on hand for easy snacks or to add to salads!) Bring to a boil over high heat, then immediately turn the water off and cover the pot for 10 minutes. Pour the water out, then add cold water and ice to the pot. This last step is actually pretty crucial for not having the eggshells stick to the eggs.
Peel the eggshells off of the eggs. On the largest hole of a box grater, grate the eggs into a large bowl. (Or: just chop them up really finely). Scooch them to one side of the bowl.

Add 3 drained cans of tuna to the other side of the bowl and use a fork to smash the tuna until no large chunks remain and the tuna looks totally shredded. This is the key to delicious, moist (yeah, I said moist, you’ll live) tuna salad!

Add 1/2 cup minced bread and butter pickles, 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard, 3/4 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon lemon pepper, and 1 tablespoon of pickle brine (AKA liquid from the pickle jar).

Stir to combine. Add more mayo if you like a “wetter” tuna salad. If you have time, let this hang out in the fridge for at least an hour before eating. That’ll let the dry tuna soak up all of the mayo-pickle goodness and become really delicious.
Now, there are many ways to enjoy tuna salad, and you can check out alternates in the notes section below, but a tuna melt is by far the greatest way, so that’s what we’re here to do today.
Lay 4 slices of bread out on your countertop and lay a slice of cheddar on each. Spread your desired amount of tuna salad over each slice, then top with another slice of cheddar.
Warm your largest nonstick skillet (or griddle if you have one!) over medium heat.

Top sandwiches with the remaining 4 slices of bread. Spread mayo over the top of the sandwiches, then add the sandwiches mayo-side-down into the skillet. (If you can’t fit them all in at once, work in batches!) Spread mayo over the slices of bread that are now on top.
After 3 minutes, check your sandwiches. You are looking for the bottom slice of bread to be toasty brown and for the bottom layer of cheese to melt. It might take up to 5 minutes!
Flip the sandwiches.
Check on your sandwiches after another 3 minutes. The skillet will be hotter now, so the second side will likely brown faster.

If your cheese hasn’t melted to your liking, try this burger joint trick: Add a splash of water to the skillet (away from the bread so it doesn’t get it wet!) and cover the skillet (you can use a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid) for 30 seconds to 1 minute. The steam will help the cheese melt!
Transfer the sandwiches to a cutting board and let them chill for a second. You don’t want to cut right in or everything will just ooze out. Slice in half and ENJOY!

name: nutty caramel cinnamon rolls
note:
To bake the next day, just cover tightly with plastic wrap and bake as directed. The sugar will look crystallized and weird - don’t worry - that’s normal, it’ll melt back into a caramel!

I am 99.99% sure you could use heavy cream instead of water to make the caramel, but I didn’t test it!

Try this trick to chop your nuts without having them fly all over the place: measure a heaping the 1/2 cup of nuts and place them directly in the skillet. Take the bottom of a glass or bowl and smash the nuts by applying firm pressure down on them (not whacking them - then they’ll fly!).

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup chopped nuts (any kind! mix and match! pistachios! pecans! i used hazelnuts bc they’ve been in my pantry for like 4 years and i want them gone!)
ingredients.name: chopped nuts (any kind! mix and match! pistachios! pecans! i used hazelnuts bc they’ve been in my pantry for like 4 years and i want them gone!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 stick (8 tablespoons) unsalted butter, room temp, divided
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temp

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12 ounce)this is preferred if you can findor 2 (8-ounce) cans crescent rolls
ingredients.name: crescent rolls
ingredients.quantity: 1 (12 ounce)this is preferred if you can findor 2 (8-ounce) cans

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

If your nuts aren’t toasted, toast 1/2 cup nuts in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Toast for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until browned. Add 4 tablespoons butter, 3/4 cup brown sugar, and 3 tablespoons water. Stir to combine and cook until bubbling and thickened, about 5 minutes. It won’t get completely caramel-thick, but will be about the consistency of maple syrup. Remove skillet from heat.

Meanwhile, bust open the can or cans of crescent rolls (does this scare anyone else?), and carefully roll them out, leaving them attached, onto a lightly floured surface. Use your fingers to smoosh the perforated lines together to create two big rectangles. Now sprinkle a bit of flour over top and use a rolling pin or, if you’re like me, a bourbon or wine bottle, to roll the dough out into a slightly larger rectangle(s) You might have to smoosh the triangles back together.
Stir together the remaining 1/4 cup brown sugar, 4 tablespoons butter, and 2 teaspoons cinnamon.

Spread the butter mixture over the dough, leaving about 1/4-inch of space on all sides. Roll up the dough from the long side, like a jelly roll. It’s ok if the triangles keep trying to break apart, just smoosh them back together as you go. If you used a 12-ounce can of rolls, cut it into 16 1-inch wide slices. If you used 2 8-ounce cans of rolls, cut 32 rolls total.
Place the rolls in the skillet, cut-side down, with just a tiny bit of space between them. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until puffed up and golden brown.

name: honey-roasted chicken, carrots, and brussels sprouts with tahini yogurt
note:
Make ahead: This is a GREAT weeknight meal because you can totally prep ahead. You can make the tahini yogurt sauce days in advance, if you’d like, just store it in an air-tight container in the fridge. If you do make it ahead, you may need to add a little hot water while you’re re-mixing to thin it out. Just add a teaspoon at a time until it’s creamy and drizzly. You can also cut up the veggies and make the marinade up to a day in advance as well, just re-mix the marinade before using so the honey and oil are well combined.

Leftovers are a good thing: If you’re making this for one or two people, count on using the extra for lunches this week! These leftovers are delicious.

Vegetarian: Instead of chicken, use chickpeas or tofu! See sub note below for cooking instructions.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: To eliminate dairy, use a plain-flavored dairy-free yogurt, a vegan sour cream, or mayo in place of the yogurt. It’s gluten-free as is!

Neutral cooking oil: Let’s revisit this. Since we’re cooking at 450°F, we’re looking for a neutral-flavored cooking oil with a very high smoke point. Try avocado, safflower, grapeseed, or olive oil.

Gimme more sheet-pan ideas: Love this recipe and the ease of sheet-pan cooking? Me too. Here’s a sausage, sweet potato, and apple combo that’s early fall on a plate. One of my most popular recipes yet is this salmon + cauliflower rice meal. And this balsamic glazed pork with fennel and potatoes is a decadent but entirely doable weeknight dish.

Any other questions? Leave them in the comments below and I’ll get back ASAP!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound carrots, cut into 2-inch pieces on the bias
ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch pieces on the bias

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup finely minced cilantro or parsley
ingredients.name: finely minced cilantro or parsley

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 garlic clove, minced (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder if you’re feeling lazy)
ingredients.name: garlic clove, minced (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder if you’re feeling lazy)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup honey, 1/4 cup cooking oil, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper, 4 minced garlic cloves, and 2 teaspoons kosher salt.

Place 1 1/2 to 2 pounds of chicken thighs, 1 pound of sliced carrots, and 1 pound of halved Brussels sprouts into the center of the baking sheet in a big pile. Pour the marinade over top and toss to evenly coat everything. Spread the chicken and veggies out so that nothing is overlapping. The chicken should be skin-side up, and the Brussels should be cut-side down (to ensure crispiness all around).

Roast on the center rack in the oven for 40 minutes. You can stir the veggies halfway through to make sure they brown evenly, but honestly, you don’t need to. If the chicken skin starts to burn, simply cover the baking sheet loosely with aluminum foil.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl whisk together 1/4 cup tahini and the juice of 1 lemon. Get all of the lumps out of the tahini. If you need to add a tiny splash of hot water to get it smooth, do it. Then stir in 1 cup greek yogurt, 1 minced garlic clove, and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed. Sometimes I like to use even more lemon juice for a really zingy sauce.
Stir 1/3 cup minced cilantro or parsley into the chicken and veggies. Serve with tahini yogurt.

name: curry roasted chicken and cauliflower salad
note:
Make it a good-all-week salad: Use a 10-ounce bag of shredded kale instead of arugula! Massage the kale with a big pinch of salt before adding the other ingredients. It will be delish stored in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 5 days! Just leave the pistachios off and add them before serving each portion for optimum crunch. The apples might brown a little in the fridge but that’s fine!

Prep ahead: You can roast the chicken and veggies up to 4 days ahead of time and store them in an airtight container in the fridge until you’re ready to make your salad. Same with the dressing — it’ll stay good in the fridge for up to 5 days. Another prep-ahead option: in the morning, prep your sheet pan with veggies, chicken, oil, and spices, wrap it tightly with plastic wrap, and pop the whole baking sheet in the fridge until you’re ready to bake it for dinner (remember to remove the plastic wrap before you bake it). That’s a good option if you need to cook dinner in a hurry/with no fuss immediately after work/school/sports.

Vegetarian: Swap the chicken for extra veggies! Any veg listed in the cauliflower subs section below would be great added to this recipe. Or you could roast a can of chickpeas or another white bean along with your vegetables. If using, rinse and drain your beans and pat them dry with a clean dish cloth/paper towel before putting them on the sheet pan. You may need to add another tablespoon of oil to ensure all the veggies are lightly coated. If needed, separate them onto two sheet pans to ensure they’re not bunched (that would cause them to steam instead of roast).

I want a really cozy dinner: Swap the arugula out for any cooked grain (farro, brown rice, quinoa) and use the dressing as more of a drizzley sauce over top. Or do half greens, half grains!

Gluten-free: Already is.

Dairy-free: Use a DF plain yogurt for the dressing and skip the Parm (or use a dairy-free Parm). Alternatively, you could skip the yogurt and soak 1/2 cup of cashews in hot water in your blender for at least 20 minutes. Drain the water out then add the rest of the dressing ingredients and blend until smooth! You could also swap the Greek yogurt out for half a ripe avocado — use the blender in that case, too.

Feeding kids: If your kids aren’t into salad, serve this meal deconstructed! Chicken in one pile (with ketchup or whatever dipping sauce they’re into), roasted veggies in another, apple in another, nuts in another, cheese in another, etc.

Save time: This homemade dressing is so easy and delicious but, if needed, use a store-bought favorite! I think a balsamic vinaigrette would be great here.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head cauliflower, cut into flat florets
ingredients.name: cauliflower

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small honeycrisp apple, cut into batons
ingredients.name: small honeycrisp apple

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 dates, pits removed, diced, or 1/3 cup dried cranberries or yellow raisins
ingredients.name: dates, pits removed, diced, or 1/3 cup dried cranberries or yellow raisins

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces Parmesan, shaved with a vegetable peeler
ingredients.name: Parmesan, shaved with a vegetable peeler

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup roasted, salted pistachios, sunflower seeds, pepitas, almonds…
ingredients.name: roasted, salted pistachios, sunflower seeds, pepitas, almonds…

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Trim the leaves off of 1 head of cauliflower, cut it into 1/2 inch-thick planks, then cut into 1-inch pieces. Thinly slice 1 small red onion. Toss the cauliflower, onion, and 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs on a large rimmed baking sheet with 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon curry powder, 1 teaspoon ground coriander, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder. Toss until evenly coated.

Roast for 30 minutes, until the chicken registers 165°F internally on a meat thermometer and the cauliflower is tender and golden brown. If the chicken is cooked through but the cauliflower has no color on it, remove the chicken, then broil the cauliflower on high for a few minutes (watch it the entire time with the oven light on! broilers are tricky business — don’t burn the cauliflower!!).While it’s roasting, make the dressing. Add 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup Greek yogurt, the juice of 2 limes, 2 tablespoons water, 1 tablespoon honey, 1 teaspoon curry powder, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper to a jar and shake it all together until well combined. (No jar? Just stir it in a bowl!) Taste and adjust seasoning if needed until it tastes perfect for you.

Cut 1 honeycrisp apple into batons (see cooking school tip here for a how-to). Remove the pits and chop 5 dates. (Yes, the date pieces will clump together, just do your best to separate them as you add them to the salad.)Place 1 (5-ounce) container arugula in a large shallow serving bowl and season with a big pinch of kosher salt. Chop the chicken and place it on top along with the roasted cauliflower and onions, 4 ounces of shaved Parmesan (I use a vegetable peeler to shave it), chopped dates, and 1/4 cup roasted, salted pistachios. Toss with your desired amount of dressing (I always start with half and add more a little bit at a time until it’s perfect!). Dig in!

name: pork & cabbage noodle stir-fry

ingredients.rawIngredient: Half a head of green cabbage, core removed, thinly sliced (or 10-ounce bag shredded cabbage)
ingredients.name: Half a head of green cabbage, core removed, thinly sliced (or 10-ounce bag shredded cabbage)

ingredients.name: fresh ginger, grated (or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger)

ingredients.name: fresh chives, thinly sliced (about ¼ cup)
