ingredients.name: toasted sesame oil, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: hot sauce/chili paste, such as sriracha, gochujang, red pepper flakes, sambal oelek…
ingredients.name: Optional: hot sauce/chili paste, such as sriracha, gochujang, red pepper flakes, sambal oelek…

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook 1 pound spaghetti per package instructions. Reserve 1 cup of the cooking water (!!!!!! don’t forget!!!!!), then drain in a colander and shake dry.

Meanwhile, just a smidge of chopping while the spaghetti cooks: Remove the core from half a head of green cabbage, then slice it as thinly as you possibly can! Use a microplane to grate a 2-inch piece of ginger (no need to peel it) and 2 garlic cloves. No microplane? Finely mince it. Thinly slice enough chives to get 1/4 cup (probably about 8 stalks). There, you’re done! Put the knife away!

Meanwhile, in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, smush 1 pound ground pork into a thin layer to fill the skillet. Leave undisturbed until browned underneath, 5 to 7 minutes. Break up the pork into tiny crumbles, and once it’s almost cooked through, add the cabbage, ginger, garlic, and a little pinch of salt. Cook until the cabbage is wilted, 2 to 4 more minutes. Remove from heat until the noodles are ready.

Add the cooked spaghetti, 1/2 cup pasta water, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, and 1 tablespoon sesame oil. Throw some sriracha or gochujang or red pepper flakes in there too, if you like things spicy. Set over medium heat and toss until the pasta is coated in sauce, 1 to 2 minutes. Add more pasta water as needed until the noodles are glossy and saucy. Remove from heat and stir in the chives and 3 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds.
Serve with another sprinkle of sesame seeds and drizzle of sesame oil as desired.

name: lemony chicken & orzo soup
note:
I like this soup very lemony: I always use at least 1/3 cup lemon juice — sometimes more. But if you or your fam aren’t super into lemon, start with 1/4 cup lemon juice. Taste and add more, as desired!

Make ahead / love your leftovers: ‘Tis the season for cooking ahead of time, and this soup can be made up to 48 hours in advance of serving. Store it covered in the fridge (or transfer to Tupperware, if your pot won’t fit). Reheat over medium heat — don’t let it boil. The soup will thicken up in the fridge, so when you’re reheating, add a little extra stock (or water) until it returns to the consistency that you want. Same goes for when you’re reheating leftovers for lunches this week!

Prep ahead: If you want to get a head start to simplify the cooking process, dice your onion and carrot; wash, de-rib, and chop your kale; and grate your Parm up to a day ahead. Store them in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

Freeze it: This is a freezable soup! Let any leftovers come to room temp then pour into a freezer-safe bag (or bags). Freeze it in portion sizes that you’ll serve when you reheat, whether that’s a gallon-size bag if you’re feeding a family or a sandwich bag if you’ll want it for yourself for a single meal. Once filled, lay the bag flat out on a baking sheet and pop it in the freezer. When it’s frozen, remove it from the sheet pan and you’ll have a thin, easy-to-store sheet of soup ready to reheat and eat later this winter! Let the soup thaw in the fridge then heat it on the stove following the instructions in the note above.

Vegetarian: Add a cup or two of extra diced veggies to the mix — bell peppers, sweet potato, butternut squash, parsnips, and/or celery would all be delicious — as well as another can of white beans. You just might want to add a bit more broth to thin it out a bit.

Dairy-free: Omit the Parm or use a df alternative.

Gluten-free: You can use a gluten-free orzo (I like Banza and RightRice) or use rice! There are instructions for using brown rice in the subs section below.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 quarts (8 cups) low-sodium chicken broth or stock
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth or stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup orzo or 3/4 cup white rice
ingredients.name: orzo or 3/4 cup white rice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5 ounce) can cannellini beans, drained but not rinsed
ingredients.name: cannellini beans, drained but not rinsed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and pepper (white pepper, if you have it)
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and pepper (white pepper, if you have it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup grated Parmesan, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch (4 cups chopped) kale, Swiss chard, escarole, or spinach (you can buy the kale pre-chopped, just pick the stems out before adding it to the soup)
ingredients.name: kale, Swiss chard, escarole, or spinach (you can buy the kale pre-chopped, just pick the stems out before adding it to the soup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup chopped soft green herbs (if you can find dill, use dill, it’s wonderful here — but anything works!)
ingredients.name: chopped soft green herbs (if you can find dill, use dill, it’s wonderful here — but anything works!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: a loaf of fresh crusty bread, more lemon wedges for squeezing over top of your soup
ingredients.name: Optional: a loaf of fresh crusty bread, more lemon wedges for squeezing over top of your soup

preparationSteps: Dice 1 medium yellow onion and 3 large carrots (click the link for demos on how to dice them).
Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the minced onion and carrot and cook for 4 minutes, stirring often.
Meanwhile, mince 4 garlic cloves. Add the minced garlic to the pot and stir for 30 seconds.

Stir in 2 quarts (8 cups) low-sodium chicken broth, 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1 cup orzo, 1 can drained (but not rinsed) cannellini beans, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Bring the soup to a boil then reduce to a simmer and cook (with the lid off) for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk together 4 large eggs, 1/3 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan, and the zest of 1 lemon. Whisk REALLY WELL. Like, really, really well! If there are any streaks of white, they’ll cook into little scrambled egg-like pieces instead of incorporating into the soup. Make sure everything is totally combined. Set aside.
Also, de-rib and chop 1 bunch kale. Set aside.

After the soup has cooked for 20 minutes, transfer the chicken from the pot to a cutting board. Turn off the stove and move the pot to a different burner to let it cool for 5 minutes. While the soup is cooling, use two forks to shred the chicken all apart, then use a knife to roughly chop it into smaller pieces. Leave it on the cutting board for now.

Ladle 1/2 cup of the soup broth (it’s OK if some carrots or orzo come along too) into the egg mixture, whisking as you pour to combine. Ladle 1 more cup of liquid into the egg mixture and whisk to combine.
Stir the tempered egg mixture into the soup. Add the 4 cups chopped kale and the chopped chicken.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, until the soup has thickened and the kale is tender. If you see a few whisps of white egg, no worries, it happens and it’ll still be delicious!
Taste. Add more salt, pepper, and lemon juice as needed until it is perfectly seasoned to your tastebuds!
Serve garnished with 1 cup chopped soft green herbs divided between the 6 bowls, extra grated Parm, and lemon slices (optional). Don’t forget the fresh crusty bread — then dig in!
As the soup sits, it’ll continue to thicken up. Just stir in a bit of broth or water until it’s the thickness you like!

name: one-pot cheesy cajun chicken and rice
note:
Don’t own a wide pot with a lid? Use a 12-inch skillet and throw a baking sheet over top of it as a cover!

Most grocery stores now sell cauliflower rice, but this recipe will only require about half of it. You can freeze the other half, and cook it straight from frozen at a later time! You can also omit it with no issues.

As with most of my one-pot meals - I recommend stirring a few cups of spinach (tear it up with your hands as you add it) to the pot when you add the cheese if you want some greens in your meal!

Pepper Jack, mozzarella, or Monterey Jack would all be good in place of the Cheddar! If you have Parmesan, add 1/2 cup of that for a little extra flavor and cheesiness!

Use chicken thighs instead by cooking them over top of the rice mixture the entire time (as opposed to adding them once the rice has cooked for 7 minutes on its own).

I don’t recommend skin-on chicken here as the skin will get soggy and limp since it will steam with the lid on.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 tablespoons neutral cooking oil (such as olive, grapeseed, avocado)
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil (such as olive, grapeseed, avocado)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 bell peppers (I used orange and red), diced
ingredients.name: bell peppers (I used orange and red)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup white rice (basmati or jasmine are my go-tos)
ingredients.name: white rice (basmati or jasmine are my go-tos)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces (2 cups) grated sharp cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: grated sharp cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup finely chopped parsley, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: finely chopped parsley, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Pat 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts dry with paper towels and season with 1/2 teaspoon cajun seasoning per chicken breast - but do your thing! Cajun seasoning has some heat to it, so really lay it on thick for the spice lovers, and season it very lightly for anyone who doesn’t love heat. You can make everyone’s differently, just remember which chicken breast belongs to whom! Read the label of your cajun seasoning - if it doesn’t have any salt in it, also season the chicken breasts with salt.
Let the chicken marinate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes.

Warm 2 tablespoons cooking oil in a wide (12 inch preferably) pot, saucepan, or Dutch oven over medium-high heat for several minutes, until beginning to smoke. Add the chicken breasts, rough-side down, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden-brown. Flip and cook for an additional 1 to 2 minutes, until golden-brown all oven.
Transfer chicken breasts to a holding plate.

If the pan has no oil left in it, add 1 tablespoon oil. Add 1 diced yellow onion, 2 diced bell peppers,1 to 3 teaspoons of cajun seasoning (depending on how spicy you can handle it!), and 1 teaspoon garlic powder to the pot and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly softened.

Stir in 2 cups low-sodium chicken stock, 2 cups cauliflower rice, and 1 cup white rice and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to the lowest heat possible, cover, and cook for 7 minutes. This timing is important so that the rice and chicken both cook perfectly, so set timers!
After those 7 minutes, uncover the pot, place the seared chicken breasts on top without overlapping them, and re-cover the pot. Cook for an additional 9 minutes.

After those 9 minutes, start checking the chicken for doneness every 1 minute. DON’T YOU DARE OVERCOOK YOUR CHICKEN! When it reaches 160°F internally, remove the chicken from the pot and place it on a cutting board to rest. It will continue cooking to reach 165°F.

Once the chicken is cooked through, taste the rice. When it’s tender, remove the pot from heat and stir in 2 cups grated sharp cheddar cheese and the juice of 1 lemon. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed - the amount needed will depend on the sodium level of your chicken stock. If the rice mixture is too thick, add another splash of stock! If it’s too liquid-y, keep stirring and cooking!
Stir in 1 cup finely chopped parsley.
Slice the chicken breasts into 1/2-inch thick pieces on the bias. Serve immediately, garnished with additional parsley and pepper.

name: a perfect breakfast casserole

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground pork sausage (preferably Jimmy Dean sage)
ingredients.name: ground pork sausage (preferably Jimmy Dean sage)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup roasted red peppers, chopped (from a jar — you don’t need to measure perfectly!) or 1/2 cup sundried tomatoes, chopped
ingredients.name: roasted red peppers, chopped (from a jar — you don’t need to measure perfectly!) or 1/2 cup sundried tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) block medium sharp cheddar cheese (or one 8-ounce bag shredded cheddar)
ingredients.name: medium sharp cheddar cheese (or one 8-ounce bag shredded cheddar)

preparationSteps: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound ground sausage and break it up into tiny crumbles with a spatula until almost cooked through. Add 5 ounces spinach, ripping it up into small pieces as you add it, along with a big pinch of kosher salt. Once the sausage is cooked through and the spinach has wilted, turn off the heat. Stir in 1 cup chopped roasted red peppers.
Drain off any excess grease. This is kind of tricky so I like to use a paper towel to soak it up. Set the sausage mixture aside to cool slightly.
Lightly spray a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

Cut 8 slices white bread into 1/2-inch cubes (I like to cut the crusts off, but you don’t have to). Place them in the baking dish in an even layer. Using a box grater, grate 8 ounces cheddar cheese and sprinkle it over the bread. Add the sausage and spinach mixture to the baking dish. Use your hands to lightly toss the bread, cheese, and sausage together.
In a large bowl, whisk together 8 large eggs, 1 pint heavy cream, 1 cup whole milk, 1 teaspoon salt, and several grinds of black pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over top of the casserole filling. Give the dish a jiggle to spread things out evenly.
Cover the baking dish with foil and let it rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or in the refrigerator for up to 48 hours.
When you’re ready to bake it, preheat oven to 350°F. If the casserole is in the fridge, take it out and let it sit at room temp while the oven heats.

Bake the casserole covered with foil for 45 minutes, then uncover it and cook for an additional 10 to 15 minutes to brown the top a bit. But we don’t want it overly brown and crispy, it should still be quite tender on top!
The top might look greasy from the cheese and sausage — just use a paper towel to dab off any grease.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then slice and serve!

name: skillet zucchini lasagna
note:
I want a lasagna with real noodles!: Grab a 9-ounce box of “no boil” lasagna noodles. I like the flat kind versus the kind with ruffly edges, if you have a choice. Use these noodles (breaking them as needed to fit into the skillet) in place of zucchini noodles! There’s ONE caveat — you need more liquid to cook the noodles, so cook the sauce for a bit less time, so that it still has a thin watery layer on top when you begin to layer the lasagna. You also need to make sure that the TOP layer of noodles is completely covered with sauce, so be sure to reserve some sauce so that you can make that happen! Also, TENT the skillet with foil (AKA make sure it’s not touching the cheese!) while baking, then remove the foil at the very end to broil. Can’t find no-boil? Just use regular lasagna noodles and cook them before you assemble your lasagna (if they’ll be sitting for a bit, toss the cooked noodles in olive oil to keep them from sticking together). You don’t have to worry about having extra liquid in your sauce if you go that route!

I want to make this as healthy as possible: use ground chicken or turkey, cottage cheese (drain off any excess liquid) instead of ricotta, and halve the mozzarella and Parm. It will be absolutely delicious.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Instead of the zucchini strips, use 8 to 10 ounces of zucchini noodles (AKA zoodles). Simply stir them into the sauce, top the skillet with the cheese, bake it for 25 minutes, and call it a “spaghetti pie” instead of a lasagna. You can also use 36 ounces of your favorite pasta sauce instead of making your own with the onion, garlic, canned tomatoes, and dried oregano. Just pour the pasta sauce into the cooked meat and continue cooking.

Vegetarian: Stir 2 cups cooked lentils in with the canned tomatoes and use a spatula to lightly smash them. Or, mince 1 pound mushrooms and cook those just as you’d cook the meat. Once all moisture has evaporated, add the canned tomatoes. Or, use 1 pound ground meatless meat like Impossible Meat.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: This is gluten-free as written! If you’re avoiding dairy, opt for plant-based versions of each of the cheeses. VioLife is a favorite DF cheese brand of readers.

Leftovers are a good thing: This skillet lasagna’s a hefty meal! My fam doesn’t typically finish the skillet in one sitting and we save our leftovers for lunches throughout the week. If you’re not team leftovers-for-lunch, freeze any extra! Freeze leftover portions of cooked lasagna in airtight Ziploc bags and enjoy them for dinner weeks or months in the future.

Make ahead: Make it as far as 2 days in advance, cover, and keep in the refrigerator until ready to bake. You could also make this ahead of time to freeze — just get a tin disposable 10x10” baking dish, and build the lasagna in that instead. Cover well and freeze. To bake, preheat oven to 350°F and bake from frozen for 45 minutes to 1 hour. Then remove foil and bake for another 5-10 minutes or until sauce is bubbly and hot.

name: chipotle cheddar chimichanga tacos
note:
Make ahead: Fully assemble the tacos on the baking sheet and wrap tightly with plastic wrap up to 12 hours before baking. Any longer than that and they might get soggy. If you want to make this a few days in advance, make the meat and store it separately, then assemble just before baking.

Freezer-friendly: After assembling the chimichangas, individually wrap them tightly in a square of tinfoil and freeze! To cook in the oven, place the entire foil-wrapped chimichanga on a baking sheet in a 375°F oven for 20 minutes or until warmed through. To microwave, remove the foil and place on a microwave-safe plate. Microwave for 2 minutes, flip over, and microwave for an additional 1 minute.

Make it uber healthy: use either 2 cans of black beans or ground chicken as your protein, bibb lettuce instead of tortillas, and just a smidge of cheese. Ok fine, you can leave off the cheese.

Riffs: there are so many ways to riff on this recipe. Use the meat to make plain ole tacos, but don’t forget the shredded iceberg. Use the meat for taco salads, or quesadillas, or nachos, or roll the tortillas up tightly instead of folding them to make flautas. Try chimichanga-ing your favorite sandwich: ham, cheese and honey mustard on a crispy flour tortilla? YUM.

Coleslaw sub: bagged coleslaw is always on my grocery list - I love throwing it into tacos and stir fries. If you want to slice it yourself, get a very small head of green cabbage and thinly slice half of it.

Flour tortilla sub: you can use corn tortillas (wrap them in a damp paper towel and microwave for 30 seconds before trying to bend them), whole wheat tortillas, hard tortilla shells (you’ll still bake them, but only for 5 to 7 minutes) or grain-free tortillas (I love Siete brand), but nothing will give you the crispy crunchy chimichanga vibe like a good ole flour tortilla will.

Meat subs: you can use ANY ground meat, or you can even use shredded chicken or leftover carnitas (you don’t need to cook it, so just simmer it with the salsa right from the beginning).

Chipotle en adobo sub: first of all, a can of chipotle en adobo looks like this. You can find it in the international aisle of most major grocers. Secondly, to be clear: you are using two of the peppers from a can of chipotle peppers. Not two cans of peppers. My friend Ashley made this mistake once and really botched a batch of chili. Thirdly, if you can’t find them, you can just sub in 1 tablespoon of chili powder!

Cheese subs: I like cheddar here not just for the alliteration, but also because it has the most flavor of any melty cheese. “Mexican cheese” is a blend of different melty cheeses including Monterey Jack which, frankly, doesn’t taste like much, so I tend to avoid it. If you’re a Trader Joe’s person: I recommend using Unexpected Cheddar!

Vegetarian: use 2 drained cans of black beans! Or a mix of black and pinto or kidney beans! Simmer until tender, then smash about half of them with a fork or spatula.

Cilantro subs: hi again, cilantro haters. Just leave it out. No parsley in your tacos.

Make it a corn side: instead of making a slaw-y salad, saute the frozen corn in a little butter, add the same seasonings (but no yogurt) and stir in the cilantro and 1/2 cup feta.

Dairy-free: use your favorite melty DF cheese, then use a DF coconut or almond milk yogurt for the pink sauce and corn salad.

Gluten-free: GF or corn tortilla lovers - use corn taco tortillas! You’ll need to warm them up before attempting to bend them in half by wrapping them in damp paper towels and microwaving for 30 seconds. Otherwise they’ll just snap in half.

Double it: to double the recipe, try using a can of black or kidney beans instead of a second pound of meat for some delicious plant protein! It’s a great idea to double the meat, and keep half in the fridge for quick tacos, taco salads, or quesadillas later in the week!

The corn salad gets watery as the cabbage absorbs salt and breaks down. All good, just pour off any excess liquid.

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F.

Slice 1 bunch green onions as thinly as you possible can, into thin little rings. Throw the white and light green parts into your largest nonstick skillet along with 1 pound ground beef. Place the dark green parts of the green onions into a large bowl for your corn salad.

Add 1 or 2 chipotles en adobo (depending on your spice preference) plus 1 tablespoon of the sauce from the can into the skillet and use your spatula to smash the peppers up into small pieces. Add 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano. Cook over medium-high heat, jabbing at the beef with your spatula frequently to break it up into the tiniest crumbles possible, for 5 to 7 minutes, or until the beef is no longer pink. Add 3/4 cup red salsa, reduce the heat to medium, and continue cooking until the meat mixture has thickened and looks like sloppy Joe meat, about 10 minutes. If it gets too thick, just add a splash of water. Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in 1/4 cup chopped cilantro.

Meanwhile, line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Place as many soft taco tortillas on the baking sheet as you can fit in a single layer, and sprinkle about 2 tablespoons shredded Cheddar cheese onto half of each tortilla. Spread a heaping 1/4 cup of the meat mixture over the cheese, then sprinkle with another 2 tablespoons of cheese. Close the tortilla to make a “taco”. Add more tortillas to the baking sheet now that you have more room, and repeat until you’re out of taco meat.
Spray with cooking spray and bake on the center rack of the oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown and crisp all over.

Meanwhile, line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Place as many soft taco tortillas on the baking sheet as will fit, and sprinkle about 2 tablespoons shredded Cheddar cheese onto half of each tortilla. Spread a heaping 1/4 cup of the meat mixture over the cheese, then sprinkle with another 2 tablespoons of cheese.
Close the tortillas to make a “taco”. Add more tortillas to the baking sheet and repeat until you’re out of meat.
Spray all over with cooking spray or rub with oil and bake on the center rack of the oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until light golden brown and crisp all over.
While the tacos are cooking, wipe out the skillet, add 1 (16 ounce) bag of frozen corn and cook over high heat, stirring frequently, until defrosted and all water has evaporated, 3 to 5 minutes.

Add to the bowl of green onions: 3/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, the juice of 2 limes, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper and stir until combined. Add 1 (14 ounce) bag of coleslaw, the defrosted corn (it’s ok if the corn is still warm, but if it has any excess liquid be sure to ditch that), 1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro, and 1 cup crumbled feta cheese. Taste and adjust seasonings as preferred (I always need more salt).
Make the pink sauce by stirring together 1/2 cup yogurt, 1/4 cup red salsa, and a tiny pinch of salt. Set aside.
Make the avocado crema by mashing together 1 large avocado, the juice of 1/2 lime, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Add any remaining red salsa to another small bowl.
Serve the chimichanga tacos fresh out of the oven, with all of the dips and the corn salad. Slice into smaller triangles if you like.

name: sunshine pasta
note:
Break down my preparation options one more time, plz! IF YOU HAVE ACCESS TO THE SUN AND WARMTH + 1 TO 2 HOURS OF TIME TO MARINATE: You can either marinate your tomato mixture outside then add it to the cooked noodles, etc., and serve it as a fresh tomato sauce. OR marinate your tomato mixture outside then cook it down on the stovetop so that it’s a more luscious cooked tomato sauce. IF YOU DON’T HAVE ACCESS TO THE SUNLIGHT/HEAT: You can skip the “sun” part and just marinate your tomato mixture inside at room temp for a few hours or in the fridge for up to 24 hours. From there, you can either serve your pasta sauce fresh or cooked. IF YOU DON’T HAVE 1-2 HOURS TO MARINATE TOMATOES: You can throw the sauce ingredients straight into a pan and cook a classic tomato sauce (just follow the instructions in that portion of the recipe).

IF YOU HAVE ACCESS TO THE SUN AND WARMTH + 1 TO 2 HOURS OF TIME TO MARINATE: You can either marinate your tomato mixture outside then add it to the cooked noodles, etc., and serve it as a fresh tomato sauce. OR marinate your tomato mixture outside then cook it down on the stovetop so that it’s a more luscious cooked tomato sauce.

IF YOU DON’T HAVE ACCESS TO THE SUNLIGHT/HEAT: You can skip the “sun” part and just marinate your tomato mixture inside at room temp for a few hours or in the fridge for up to 24 hours. From there, you can either serve your pasta sauce fresh or cooked.

IF YOU DON’T HAVE 1-2 HOURS TO MARINATE TOMATOES: You can throw the sauce ingredients straight into a pan and cook a classic tomato sauce (just follow the instructions in that portion of the recipe).

Make this easier: Use 2 (28 ounce) cans of diced tomatoes instead of the chopped tomatoes. Drain off all of the liquid before adding them to the bowl.

Need meat: Basil balsamic grilled chicken would be a wonderful accompaniment, or some shrimp cooked simply in olive oil with salt and pepper.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: To eliminate dairy, use a plant-based Parmesan alternative, or just skip the cheese! To avoid gluten, use any gf noodle you love!

Prep ahead: You can make the tomato mixture up to a day ahead of time. If you  do so, you can either let it marinate for hours in the fridge and skip the sunbathing part, OR pull it out and into the sun for 1 to 2 hours after it’s hung out in the fridge.

Vegetarian: Already is!

Leftovers are a great thing: You can easily halve this whole recipe. But also, is there anything better than leftover pasta?! Reheat leftovers in a skillet over medium heat and stir in a splash of water at a time as needed until it’s saucy again. Taste and re-season with salt and pepper if needed. OR: If you’re cooking for one or two and know you don’t want lots of leftover cooked pasta chilling in your fridge, you could make the full amount of marinated tomatoes and half of the pasta, reserving half of the tomato mixture to be enjoyed another way. Like on toasted bread or crackers like bruschetta. Or on a sandwich as a sun-marinated tomato spread. Or even pizza style on a flatbread with fresh mozzarella.

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, combine 3 pounds chopped tomatoes, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 minced shallot, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1/4 cup minced fresh basil, 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 2 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Stir to combine, then cover with plastic wrap (or any kind of lid) and set it out in the sunshine for 2 hours. (Doesn’t matter how hot it is!)
If the 2 hours is up and it’s not dinnertime, just throw the bowl of tomatoes in the fridge until you’re ready to eat.
When you’re about 20 minutes from being ready to eat, bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add 1 tablespoon kosher salt to the water.
FROM HERE, THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT OPTIONS:
IF YOU’RE TAKING THE FRESH SAUCE ROUTE:

Cook 1 pound of pasta until tender. Drain it and return it to the cooking pot. Drain all but about 1/4 cup of the excess liquid from the marinated tomatoes, then toss them into the pasta along with 1/2 cup Parmesan. If your tomatoes were in the fridge, you might want to stir everything together over medium-low heat to get it nice and warm.
Serve, garnished with extra Parm and basil.
IF YOU’RE TAKING THE COOKED SAUCE ROUTE:
After your tomatoes have marinated, pour the contents of the bowl (including all collected juices!) into your largest skillet or saucepan. It will need to be large enough to fit the sauce and pasta.

Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat and cook, stirring often, until the sauce only has about 1/3 cup of liquid left and all of the tomatoes have cooked down. This should take about 20 minutes. But! You might have super juicy tomatoes and it could take longer! Just keep it over high heat, stir frequently, and it will reduce down soon.

Cook your 1 pound pasta for 3 minutes less than the package indicates. Drain it (but don’t shake it totally dry — we want a bit of pasta water to still be on the noodles) or use tongs to drag the noodles directly into the skillet of sauce.
With the heat still over high, toss the pasta and sauce together until the pasta is tender and the sauce is clinging to the noodles. Turn off the heat, then stir in 1/2 cup grated parmesan cheese.
Serve, garnished with extra basil and Parm.

name: one-skillet chicken & gingery rice with spicy (or not!!) peanut curry sauce
note:
Love your leftovers: Leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze portions for up to three months to have easy meals within reach!

Add veg: I love the idea of sauteeing some mushrooms in the skillet before adding the rice and ginger, or a bag of shredded cabbage, or a couple big handfuls of shredded carrots! Several big handfuls of chopped spinach or kale could also be added in with the rice! Oh, or throw a bunch of broccoli florets right on top of the chicken for the last 15 minutes of cook time!

Prep ahead: You can make the curry sauce a few days ahead of time and refrigerate it. Warm it on the stovetop or in the microwave while the chicken and rice cooks. The sauce can also be frozen for up to three months.

I am afraid of fish sauce: I know it sounds a little scary because, well, it’s a sauce made from fermented fish, but if you like Pad Thai, or a Thai curry, then you like fish sauce because it’s full of it! It has an unbeatable salty, savory flavor, it does not taste fishy in a bad way, and it is crucial for creating Southeast Asian flavor. Pick up a bottle and trust me. Plus, with it in your pantry you can make coconut curry lentil veggie stew, and beef basil bowls with coconut-ginger rice.

Spice averse: Leave out the sriracha in the peanut sauce! Reduce the amount of curry paste!

Vegetarian: Try crispy tofu cubes or planks  Find a how-to for baking crispy tofu here in the product spotlight section. You could also pan-fry thin strips of extra-firm tofu in the skillet, using a few tablespoons of sesame oil. Or swap in a couple of cans chickpeas (drain and rinse them, first).

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It already is!

Nut-free: To avoid nuts, use a seed butter like sunflower butter or tahini instead of peanut butter.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1 to 2-inch) piece fresh ginger(if feeding spice averse people, ginger can be “spicy” to some, mostly kids, so use less or no ginger!)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger(if feeding spice averse people, ginger can be “spicy” to some, mostly kids, so use less or no ginger!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, white fat trimmed off
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, white fat trimmed off
For the spicy peanut curry sauce:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons red curry paste(if feeding spice averse people, start with just 1 tablespoon, or even less)
ingredients.name: red curry paste(if feeding spice averse people, start with just 1 tablespoon, or even less)

preparationSteps: Make the chicken and rice: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add 1 1/2 cups rinsed long-grain white rice and grate in 1 ( 1 to 2-inch) piece fresh ginger (no need to peel it, use less if spice averse). Cook, stirring, until very fragrant, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 2 1/2 cups water and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low.

Season 2 pounds trimmed boneless, skinless chicken thighs with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt. Lay them over the rice, overlapping slightly if needed to fit. Cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the chicken registers 165°F. If the rice isn’t tender after 25 minutes, just keep cooking it, don’t worry about overcooking the chicken, thighs are resilient!
Remove the skillet from the heat and let sit, covered, for 10 minutes to allow the rice to steam.

While the chicken and rice are cooking, make the peanut curry sauce: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a small pot over medium heat. When it shimmers, add 1 to 2 tablespoons red curry paste and cook, stirring, until very fragrant and sticking to the bottom of the pot, about 1 minute. Stir in 1 (13.5-ounce) can full-fat coconut milk, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 1 tablespoons peanut butter, 1 tablespoon sriracha (if using), and 2 teaspoons honey. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring often, until very thick, like heavy cream or a thin yogurt, 10 to 15 minutes. Don’t let it boil over — reduce the heat to medium-low if needed. Remove the pot from the heat and let cool a bit.

Chop 10 cilantro sprigs and scatter around the chicken and rice. Drizzle the sauce all over the top and serve family-style with extra sauce on the side. I also had some peanuts and threw those on there!

preparationSteps: Wash and scrub 3 large carrots and 1 fennel bulb to clean them, then trim off the ends and roughly chop them into a few big pieces. Throw them, along with 1 large yellow onion (that’s been peeled, trimmed, and quartered) and 4 garlic cloves into a food processor. Pulse until very, very finely chopped.

Heat a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat, then add 1 pound ground sausage (casing removed, if you could only find links). Cook, using a wooden spoon to break it up into 1/2-inch pieces, until it’s golden-brown all over, about 5 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked sausage to a holding plate. Leave any leftover grease and sausage bits in the pot.

Add 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil (I know it seems like a lot, just go with it) to the pot, then stir in the finely chopped vegetables. Season with a huge pinch of salt and pepper (about 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon pepper). Cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes, then partially cover (AKA leave the lid ajar so there's about a 1-inch gap to let some, but not all, of the steam escape) and reduce the heat to medium-low heat for an additional 15 minutes or so, stirring occasionally. The vegetables shouldn’t brown (and definitely shouldn’t blacken!), so turn down the heat if needed.
While you’re waiting, wash and roughly chop the collards and set aside. You do not need to remove the ribs.

Stir in 1 to 2 tablespoons harissa sauce, 2 tablespoons tomato paste, 3/4 teaspoon ground cumin, and the zest of 1 lemon and continue cooking until the paste goes from bright red to kind of a burnt red color, 1 to 2 minutes.

Stir in 12 cups of water, 3 tablespoons Better Than Bouillon, 1 cup French green lentils, 1 cup barley, and 1 chopped bunch of collards. Cut the rind off of 1 block of Parmigiano-Reggiano and throw it in there (the rind is always thrown away, but it has so much flavor!), 2 bay leaves, and 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low. Cover (completely!) and cook for 45 minutes.

While the soup is cooking, make the garlicky olive oil-fried croutons. Warm a huge glug of extra-virgin olive oil (we are not measuring! Just generously coat the bottom of the skillet!) in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 4 cups cubed bread and stir to coat in oil. Add more oil if needed to get a nice olive oil-y coating.

Spread the bread into as even of a layer as possible. Sprinkle generously with kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder. Don't stir them, just let them toast until golden-brown on the first side, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir and toast on the second side. Continue cooking and stirring until golden-brown all over. Turn off the heat and let them cool right there in the skillet.
Stir the cooked sausage and the juice from the lemon you zested earlier into the soup, cooking until the sausage is warmed through, about 3 minutes. Fish out the Parm rind and bay leaves and discard.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Top with garlicky croutons and so much Parmigiano-Regianno that it looks like it snowed on your bowl. Seriously, that last part is very important. Enjoy!

name: 30-minute al pastor enchiladas
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: Yep, you can freeze these after they’ve been baked. Put any leftover enchiladas (or the whole batch if you’re food prepping!) in a gallon-sized Ziploc, taking care to squeeze all of the air out as you do. Next, wrap the bag tightly in foil. Freeze for up to three months. To reheat, either let them thaw then bake in a oven-safe dish (like your cast-iron skillet or a casserole dish) for 20-25ish minutes, or until warm, in a 375°F oven. Or you can bake from frozen — again in an oven-safe dish, for closer to 45 minutes, or until warm.

Special ingredient: You'll have some leftover crushed pineapple. Make a quick pineapple salsa with it by adding some smashed or diced avocado and lots of chopped fresh cilantro. OR freeze the rest of it for next time you make this! Or just add some more on top when you add the salsa verde (they will turn out on the sweeter side) or as garnish.

Make ahead: You can cook and assemble the enchiladas up to 24 hours in advance, but don’t soak them in the salsa verde yet (unless you like your enchiladas really soggy). Store them in the skillet or casserole dish wrapped tightly with plastic wrap or foil, or in an air-tight container. Before cooking, pour the salsa verde into the skillet, place the enchiladas back in, and top with remaining salsa and cheese.

Vegetarian: Use an alternative ground meat product like Impossible Foods meat or tempeh.

Dairy-free: Use vegan sour cream and your favorite df shredded cheese. If you don’t like vegan cheese just omit. If you are going cheese-less you can try this: Use flour tortillas and try to assemble your enchiladas a few hours ahead of time, letting them sit in the salsa verde. The moisture will make the flour tortillas very soft and gooey on the bottom — it’ll feel very cheese-like.

Gluten-free: Use Siete Foods grain-free tortillas or corn tortillas. BUT FIRST, read the preparation note in the “flour tortillas”  sub below.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup crushed pineapple (from a can of crushed pineapple — see notes for ways to use the rest)
ingredients.name: crushed pineapple (from a can of crushed pineapple — see notes for ways to use the rest)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 to 6 (10-inch) flour tortillas (see sub note for alternatives!)
ingredients.name: flour tortillas (see sub note for alternatives!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded cheddar, Mexican, or pepper jack cheese
ingredients.name: shredded cheddar, Mexican, or pepper jack cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings:pickled red onions, thinly sliced red onion, avocado slices, cilantro, hot sauce, etc.
ingredients.name: Optional toppings:pickled red onions, thinly sliced red onion, avocado slices, cilantro, hot sauce, etc.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Warm 1 tablespoon neutral cooking oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the sliced scallions and 4 minced garlic cloves until softened, for 2 to 3 minutes. Add 1 pound ground pork, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon cumin, and 1 teaspoon salt and turn the heat up to high. Break the pork into tiny crumbles with a spatula, stirring frequently until cooked through and all excess moisture has evaporated.
Stir in 1/2 cup crushed pineapple and 1/4 cup salsa verde. Stir until the meat has absorbed the liquid. Stir in 8 ounces spinach until totally wilted.
Turn off the heat and stir in 1/4 cup sour cream.

Roll the enchiladas up by spooning 1/4 to 1/3 cup (depending on how large your tortilla is) of the pork mixture down the center of each tortilla. Top with several tablespoons of shredded cheese. Roll tightly and line the tortillas up, seam-side down, on a cutting board.

Once all of the meat has been rolled into tortillas, pour in enough salsa verde to coat the bottom of the skillet. Add the enchiladas into the skillet, again seam-side down. I can usually fit 5 across, then wedge 1 more in along the top.
Cover the enchiladas with the remaining salsa verde followed by the remaining shredded cheese (about 1 cup).
Bake for 15 minutes, or until the cheese is totally melted.
Garnish with pickled red onions, avocado, cilantro, scallions, more sour cream, etc., as desired. Dig in!

name: roasted BBQ ribs and herby crunch potatoes
note:
Vegetarian: Make the potato salad and serve it with crispy BBQ tofu nuggets. Cut a block of extra-firm tofu into nugget-sized strips. Press them hard between paper towels (put a cast iron on top!) for at least 30 minutes first to drain excess moisture out. Next, toss them with a tablespoon or two of oil and a teaspoon of cornstarch or arrowroot powder (that helps the oil adhere). Spread the nuggets out on a baking sheet and bake at 425°F for 20 to 30 minutes, until crisp. Once crisp, mix it with the barbecue sauce!

Prep ahead: You can cook your ribs for the first 2 hours up to a day in advance. Keep them wrapped tightly in aluminum foil and pop them in the fridge until you’re a little more than an hour out from mealtime. Resume cooking from there!

Love your leftovers: The ribs and potato salad will both stay good in the fridge for 3-4 days. You can also freeze cooked ribs in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Once totally cooled, wrap them in a few layers of foil or in an airtight zip-top bag before freezing.

I need greens: Add a bag of my newest obsession, Taylor Farms’ dill pickle salad kit, to your dinner plan. It’s so damn good. If you can't find that, grab a Caesar kit.

DF/GF: This meal’s already dairy free if you skip the cheese. Be sure your barbecue sauce is gluten free, if needed!

Feeding kids: My kids absolutely inhaled the ribs, but wouldn’t touch the potato dish. They love roasted potatoes though — so I suggest pulling out a portion for the kids and serving them with ketchup.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 2 celery stalks, sliced as thinly as possible (use stalks from the center of the head of celery — the outer stalks can be bitter and fibrous)
ingredients.name: Optional: 2 celery stalks, sliced as thinly as possible (use stalks from the center of the head of celery — the outer stalks can be bitter and fibrous)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons Dijon or whole grain mustard
ingredients.name: Dijon or whole grain mustard

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 1/2 cup crumbled feta or parmesan ribbons
ingredients.name: Optional: 1/2 cup crumbled feta or parmesan ribbons

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 275°F.

Line one large baking sheet with aluminum foil. Line another large baking sheet with parchment paper — or nothing (I find that potatoes really stick to aluminum foil and cause a bigger headache than a dirty pan).
Place 1 rack of ribs on the aluminum foil-lined baking sheet. Pat them completely dry with paper towels. Season all over with 1 tablespoon kosher salt and 1 teaspoon black pepper.
Cover tightly with aluminum foil and place in the oven. Set a timer for TWO HOURS. At that time, you'll add the potatoes to the oven.
On the parchment-lined baking sheet, toss 1 1/2 pounds quartered yellow Dutch potatoes, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper.

In a medium bowl, combine 2 thinly sliced celery stalks, the juice of 1 small lemon, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1/3 cup chopped basil, 2 tablespoons chopped dill, and a big pinch of salt. Throw in the fridge until your potatoes finish cooking.
When the ribs have been cooking for 2 hours, add the potatoes on the rack below the ribs. Set a timer for 45 MINUTES.
When 45 minutes is up, remove the ribs from the oven and uncover them. (Leave the potatoes in there!) Raise the oven temperature to 450°F.
Brush the ribs with a generous coating of barbecue sauce (start with 1/2 cup; add more if needed). Return the ribs to the oven when it reaches 450°F. Cook for 15 additional minutes.

Remove the potatoes and ribs. Set the ribs aside to rest. Test the potatoes to make sure they're creamy on the inside, and a bit crunchy on the outside. If not, you can cook them for a few more minutes.
Toss the potatoes into the bowl of celery and herbs and add 1/2 cup crumbled feta or Parmesan ribbons. Sprinkle with lots of flaky salt. Potatoes like lots of salt!
Cut the rack of ribs into individual ribs. Serve with extra barbecue sauce for dipping and a side of potato salad. Enjoy!

name: sheet-pan sesame soy steak and veggies
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy an Asian-marinated flank steak from Whole Foods or another specialty grocer, or buy a bottle of teriyaki marinade (Veri Veri Teriyaki is so good) and use that instead of mine!

I don’t eat red meat: Use boneless skinless chicken thighs instead, but cook for 5 minutes per side and only add the vegetables after you flip the chicken. Or salmon for the same amount of time — 3 minutes per side, ending with the skin side up.

Vegetarian: Press the liquid out of a firm block of tofu. Cut into 1-inch cubes and marinate it in the marinade. Broil the exact same way as the steak.

I want to grill it: It felt aggressive for me to start busting out the grilling recipes in April, but you should go for it! The grilling times should be very similar to the broiling times. Grill over medium-high (450°F) heat.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds skirt or flank steak
ingredients.name: skirt or flank steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt (or sour cream or mayonnaise)
ingredients.name: plain Greek yogurt (or sour cream or mayonnaise)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 teaspoons sambal oelek or sriracha
ingredients.name: sambal oelek or sriracha

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon neutral cooking oil, such as grapeseed, avocado, or vegetable
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil, such as grapeseed, avocado, or vegetable

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: sesame seeds, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: cilantro for garnish; cooked plain white rice, coconut rice, quinoa, or soba noodles to serve alongside meal
ingredients.name: Optional: cilantro for garnish; cooked plain white rice, coconut rice, quinoa, or soba noodles to serve alongside meal

preparationSteps: In a large bowl or gallon ziplock, combine 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon sambal oelek, 1 tablespoon honey, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, the juice of 1 lime, and 5 smashed garlic cloves.
Place 1 1/2 to 2 pounds skirt steak in the marinade and marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes, or in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours.

While it’s marinating, make the Creamy Sambal Sauce by stirring 1/2 cup yogurt, 1 to 2 teaspoons sambal oelek, the juice of 1 lime, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce together in a bowl. Taste and add more sambal or soy sauce as needed.
Place an oven rack on the top rung. Preheat your oven’s broiler to high heat and line your largest rimmed sheet pan with aluminum foil.

Cut 1 1/2 inches off the bottom of 1 pound asparagus. Thinly slice 2 bell peppers. Throw them on the foil-lined sheet pan and toss with 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 tablespoon neutral cooking oil, 2 teaspoons sesame seeds, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt until evenly coated.

Scooch the veggies over to make room for the steak. Shake all excess marinade off the steak, then place it on the sheet pan. Arrange the vegetables around it so that they are overlapping as little as possible.

Place the sheet pan on the top rung of the oven and broil for 3 minutes for skirt steak, 4 minutes for flank steak. Take it out, flip the steak over, and stir the vegetables. Return the pan to the oven to broil for another 3 minutes for skirt, 4 for flank. Check the internal temperature; it should be between 125 and 130°F. This will give you medium-rare steak.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board to rest for at least 5 minutes.

Cut the steak into thin slices by tilting your knife so that it’s almost parallel to the steak, then shaving the steak very thinly. Serve the steak alongside the cooked veggies, then drizzle with the Creamy Sambal Sauce and top with cilantro, if desired.

name: rainbow chicken chop
note:
Cook your own chicken: Use chicken breasts or thighs. Use the same honey-ginger glaze that Jillian did for the salmon (find that recipe above the main recipe!), then roast for 12 to 17 minutes or until 160°F internally for boneless skinless chicken breasts (let them sit for a few minutes after baking before you chop them — the internal temp will keep climbing), or for about 25 minutes for boneless skinless thighs, until 165°F internally.

Feeding kids: See my recs for this above the recipe!

Vegetarian: Crispy tofu cubes coated in Jillian’s honey-ginger glaze would be so so good. Grab a block of extra-firm (or firm) tofu and gently press the excess moisture out. Slice the block into even bite-sized cubes then set the cubes between dry paper towels or clean dishcloths for about 10 minutes (add a cast-iron skillet on top!) to drain more moisture out. Once you’ve pressed them, add them to a bowl along with oil (sesame oil or a neutral oil), a drizzle of soy sauce, and a teaspoon of cornstarch or arrowroot powder (that will help the flavors adhere to the tofu). Spread the cubes out on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake at 425°F for 30-ish minutes, or until crisp. Once they’re crispy, toss them in the glaze. Yum! A can of drained and rinsed chickpeas, or 1 to 2 cups of cooked shelled edamame would be other good plant-based protein options.

Prep ahead/make ahead/love your leftovers: Prep the dressing and store it in the jar in the fridge. Chop all the ingredients earlier in the day and store them in the serving bowl covered with foil or plastic wrap. When it’s time for dinner, dress the salad, add the crunchy ingredients, and serve! Because we’re using cabbage and other hearty vegetables here, you can store leftovers of the dressed salad in the fridge for up to 4 days. The vegetables will soften a little they sit but I don’t mind it at all!! If it bugs you, only dress the portion you’re about to eat. Also, if you plan to have leftovers, add the crunchy ingredients right before you plan to eat each serving.

I prepped my dressing ahead of time, stored it in the fridge, and now it’s weird and chunky: All you need to do is let it warm to room temp then shake it again to re-emulsify (aka combine) everything! If you want to speed up the process you could microwave it for a few seconds, run it under hot water, stick it in the waistband of your pants (a la how we soften butter!) or add a few splashes of warm water. The oil in chili crisp may solidify when stored in the fridge too!

Save time: See the “make it easier” note above the recipe for tips.

What’s a “four-finger pinch” of salt? This means you’re picking up salt using your thumb and all four fingers. So a real big pinch!

Salad bowl rec? I love the XL serving bowl from Quince. The splatterware-style bowl in the video and pics was a gift, here’s a similar one!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: It’s already df and leave out the ramen to make it gf!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small head of green cabbage, finely chopped
ingredients.name: of green cabbage

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 bell peppers (ideally 1 orange and 1 red), finely chopped
ingredients.name: bell peppers (ideally 1 orange and 1 red)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cooked chicken breasts (from a store-bought rotisserie chicken, or see notes for how to cook at home), finely chopped
ingredients.name: cooked chicken breasts (from a store-bought rotisserie chicken, or see notes for how to cook at home)

ingredients.name: small crown of broccoli, finely chopped (optional — I know many don’t love raw broccoli)

ingredients.name: shredded carrots (buy a bag of shredded carrots or use a box grater to grate 1 large carrot)

ingredients.name: cashews (buy Thai- or Asian-spiced cashews, if you can find them! or just regular roasted cashews), crunched up before adding

ingredients.name: ramen noodles, crunched up before adding (and seasoning packet discarded)
For the Ginger Chili Crisp Dressing:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup sesame oil (ideally regular, but toasted also works — it will just have a  stronger sesame flavor)
ingredients.name: sesame oil (ideally regular, but toasted also works — it will just have a  stronger sesame flavor)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 heaping tablespoon chili crisp (if you already have it!! if not, just add a big pinch/few grinds of black pepper)
ingredients.name: heaping tablespoon chili crisp (if you already have it!! if not, just add a big pinch/few grinds of black pepper)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2-inch piece fresh ginger, grated or minced
ingredients.name: fresh ginger, grated or minced

preparationSteps: Finely chop 1 small head green cabbage, 2 bell peppers, 2 cooked chicken breasts, 1 small crown of broccoli, 1 English cucumber, 1 cup of fresh cilantro, and 1 cup of fresh mint. If you didn’t buy shredded carrots, grate or finely chop 1 carrot.

Add everything to your largest mixing/serving bowl (if you bought pre-shredded carrots, add 1 cup shredded carrots to the bowl now too). Add a huge (!!) four-finger pinch of kosher salt, and toss to season all of the ingredients.

Add all dressing ingredients (1/2 cup sesame oil, 1/2 cup rice wine vinegar, 1/4 cup honey, 1 heaping tablespoon chili crisp OR a big pinch/few grinds of black pepper, a minced/grated 2-inch piece of fresh ginger, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 2 teaspoons kosher salt) to a jar, seal it tightly, and shake until well combined — so 30 seconds or so of hardcore shaking! If you don’t have a large jar, add the ingredients to a mixing bowl and whisk together. If you like red onion, mince 1 red onion and add it to the jar (it’s not necessary for the dressing, this is just a great way to quick-pickle onion and take that harsh bite out!).

Pour 3/4ths of the dressing over the salad and toss to coat. Add additional dressing as needed (I use it all!). Taste and season with additional kosher salt as needed (there are a LOT of raw vegetables in there — I needed to add several big pinches of salt to bring out all of their best flavors! Keep tasting between additional pinches until it’s perfect!)
Right before serving, crunch up 1 cup of cashews and 1 package of ramen noodles (discard the ramen seasoning packet or save it for another use). Add them to the salad and dig in!
*If you plan to have leftovers and eat this salad throughout the week, add the crunched up ramen and cashews to a storage container and sprinkle them on your bowl before serving each time.*
