name: one-skillet broccoli cheddar chicken pot pie
note:
vegetarian: use 1 can of rinsed cannellini beans (or any other white bean such as garbanzo or navy - but cannellini are the most creamy) in place of the chicken, and use vegetable stock. stir in the beans just before adding the cheddar.

gluten-free: years ago i saw this pot pie recipe that uses sliced bread instead of pie crust, and have always wanted to try it! try it with your fave gluten-free sliced bread. of course, you could also make your own gluten-free pie crust.

dairy-free: use df butter (everyone’s fave seems to be mykonos brand!) and instead of using chicken stock and heavy cream, just use 2 cups of almond milk for your liquid. keep cooking until it thickens up, it might take a little bit longer. use your favorite dairy-free melty cheese in place of the cheddar, and VioLife parmesan instead of parm.

freezer-friendly: the chicken and veggie filling freezes perfectly! thaw it, reheat it in your oven-safe skillet, and pick up the recipe from there.

don’t own an ovenproof skillet? first of all, are you sure? many nonsticks are ovenproof - google your brand! stainless steel pans are also ovenproof. you can make this in a dutch oven, your crust just won’t be on the top, it’ll be down in the pot - but that’s fine! it’ll taste the same! if you really don’t own a pan/pot that you can cook with on the stovetop and then put into the oven, after you’ve made the filling, transfer it to a pie dish or pyrex, then put the pie crust over top. if your pyrex is rectangular, you’ll have to cut your round pie crust and re-smoosh it into a rectangular shape. it’ll be very frankenstein-y, but who cares!

make broccoli cheddar chicken soup by stirring in 3 cups of broth and 3/4 cup heavy cream. adjust the other seasonings as needed. yum!

no, you don’t need to buy canned chicken broth! use homemade or the boxed kind if ya want, but i loathe when the second half of a box of broth goes bad because i forget to use it. this solves that problem since we need to use the entire can!

i love the frozen pie crusts from TJ’s, and from Immaculate (Whole Foods carries them).

your sauce will be smoother and more delicious if you grate the cheese yourself. bagged shredded cheese has an anti-caking agent on it to keep it from sticking together - it can make sauces a bit gritty, but it won’t be the worst thing in the world if you’re strapped for time.

want to make a more traditional pot pie? omit the broccoli and cheddar. peel and dice one medium yukon gold potato and sauté it along with the onion. stir in 2 cups of frozen peas with the parmesan. i also like 1 cup of frozen corn in my pot pie!

fun crust alternative: buy one of those cans of biscuits that you whack against the counter to open, place them over top the pot pie filling, and bake according to the biscuit package instructions. broccoli cheddar chicken and biscuits!

instead of purchasing and dicing your own onion, celery, and carrots - look for the pre-cut “mirepoix” that most grocers sell in the produce refrigerator aisle! if they don’t sell that, they might at least sell diced onion, which is another time saving hack that i will fully allow.

if you want to make this today and don’t have time to thaw the pie crust in the fridge overnight, check the refrigerator aisle and see if your store sells any pie crusts that aren’t frozen. if they don’t, just let it sit out, near the warm stove, until it’s time to cook.

if your pie crust starts cracking when you unroll it - it’s too cold! let it come up to room temperature for a few more minutes and try again. if it still cracks, just smoosh it back together and carry on.

what ever will you do with all that leftover heavy cream?! white russians, cream scones, creamy sausage and sundried tomato pasta.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons neutral cooking oil (avocado, grapeseed, olive)
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil (avocado, grapeseed, olive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 pounds), cut into 2-inch cubes
ingredients.name: large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 pounds)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small yellow onion, diced (about 1 1/2 cups onion)
ingredients.name: small yellow onion, diced (about 1 1/2 cups onion)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 medium orange carrots, cleaned and diced
ingredients.name: medium orange carrots, cleaned and diced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 heaping cups (a little over 1/2 pound) broccoli florets
ingredients.name: heaping cups (a little over 1/2 pound) broccoli florets

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5 ounce) can (or 1 3/4 cups) low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 frozen pie crust, thawed overnight in the refrigerator
ingredients.name: frozen pie crust, thawed overnight in the refrigerator

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 10 or 12 inch ovenproof skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 pounds of cubed chicken in an even layer and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook until the chicken releases from the skillet with little or no resistance, 2 to 3 minutes, then stir to turn the chicken.

Cook until no longer pink in the center, about 6 minutes total, then keep stirring until all liquid (which has cooked out of the chicken) evaporates from the skillet. Transfer the chicken to a large bowl and use two forks to shred it into irregular pieces.

While the chicken is cooking, finely dice a small yellow onion, 2 celery stalks, 3 medium carrots and mince 2 garlic cloves. Or, if you bought a precut mirepoix like a smarty timesaver, you just need to mince the garlic! If the chicken finishes cooking before you finish chopping - no worries! Just turn off the skillet and start it back up once you finish chopping.

Warm the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat and add 1/2 pound broccoli florets, the minced onion, celery, and carrots, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Stir everything to coat it in oil, add a big pinch of kosher salt, then add 2 tablespoons water to the skillet and cover it with a lid (or a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid!) for 5 to 7 minutes, until the broccoli is fork tender, and easily falls apart.
Stir 3 tablespoons unsalted butter into the skillet until it has melted and coated all of the vegetables.
Take the pie crust out of the fridge at this point so that it’s not super cold when you try to unroll it!

Now stir 1/4 cup (4 tablespoons) all-purpose flour right into the vegetables. This is going to make everything look weird and pasty - you’re on the right track! Keep cooking for 1 to 2 minutes until the paste starts to stick to the bottom of the skillet. At this point, the broccoli will be breaking up into tons of little bits and looking rather smooshy - don’t worry, you’re doing great!

Stir one 14.5 ounce can of low-sodium chicken broth (1 3/4 cups broth), 1/2 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder into the pasty veggies, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-high and cook until it thickens into a very creamy sauce, 3 to 5 minutes. Keep cooking until this has become a very thick gravy and looks like a nice thick pot pie filling - it won’t thicken up much more in the oven. Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in 1 1/2 cups cheddar cheese and 1/4 cup parmesan cheese until it has completely melted into the sauce.
Stir in the shredded chicken, taking care not to add any liquid has accumulated in the bottom of the bowl to the skillet.

Unroll the pie crust and drape it over the veggie-chicken mixture. This is kinda hard and awkward, just be confident and flip it on there quickly! If you’re using a 10-inch skillet, you’ll be able to crimp the edges of the pie crust to create a pretty little border. If you’re using as 12-inch skillet, the crust should perfectly drape over the filling. If the crust doesn’t go all the way to the edges of the skillet, some of the pot pie filling will bubble over onto your crust, this is no big deal! It’s all going to the same place!
Cut 4 little slits in the pie crust to allow steam to escape.
Brush the top of the pie crust with 1 to 2 tablespoons of heavy cream. Don’t own a pastry brush? Drizzle the cream over top, then use a paper towel to gently spread the cream all over the pie crust.

Place the skillet on a rimmed baking sheet just in case the filling bubbles over, then bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until light golden. You do not want the pie crust to get dark brown, just a nice light color on it.
Allow the pot pie to cool for 5 minutes before serving so that the filling can thicken up.
Now get in there!

name: chopped turkey taco salad
note:
Make it vegetarian: You could use diced mushrooms, squash, or zucchini, or crumbled cauliflower, tofu, or tempeh — or a combination of a few of them! — instead of turkey. Or you could use 2 cans of drained and rinsed beans like black beans and/or pinto for the taco “meat.” If you go the bean route, skip adding more to the salad.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: For df, use a vegan sour cream or a non-sweet df yogurt, and omit the shredded cheese or use a df alternative. For gf, use gluten-free tortilla chips like Siete Foods.

Whole30 it: Omit the black beans and cheese. Use a dairy-free sour cream and grain-free tortilla chips.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. Instead of the crema, just use your favorite creamy Mexican-style dressing. You could even mix ranch with some salsa verde or hot sauce if you’re in a pinch.

Turn them into tacos: You can easily turn this salad into taco night (or taco lunch the next day). Use the same ingredients, just chop the lettuce up and use it as a topping alongside the other salad ingredients and taco meat. Drizzle tacos with the crema. Instead of tortilla chips, use hard and/or soft taco shells. You could also turn the meat filling into cheesy quesadillas served alongside chopped greens, avo, and the crema!

Increase odds of toddler approval: If you’re feeding kids, use mild salsa for the taco meat and omit the hot sauce from the crema (you can always throw some on top of your salad). If your kid’s not into salad, serve the meal deconstructed on a plate with the taco meat, black beans, avocado, and some shredded cheese.

Eat even more greens: Add some spinach to the taco meat alongside the corn and other ingredients, then top the salad with some fresh cilantro.

Make ahead: Fix the taco meat and crema up to a few days in advance. Reheat the meat before you assemble your salad, and check the consistency of the crema — you may need to add more water at this point as it tends to thicken in the fridge.

Leftovers are a good thing: If you’re cooking for one or two, I hiiighly recommend fixing the full recipe of taco meat. Have salads and tacos for lunch all week long! Or freeze the extra meat and use it in a few weeks/months! It also doubles beautifully, if you’re feeding a full table but want to meal prep too.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch green onions, roots discarded, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: green onions, roots discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels (from 4 ears of corn)
ingredients.name: fresh or frozen corn kernels (from 4 ears of corn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup salsa verde (the thin, not chunky, salsa from a jar)
ingredients.name: salsa verde (the thin, not chunky, salsa from a jar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons neutral oil (like avocado or grapeseed)
ingredients.name: neutral oil (like avocado or grapeseed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Water as needed to dilute to dressing consistency
ingredients.name: Water as needed to dilute to dressing consistency

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 cups chopped romaine, mixed greens, or baby kale
ingredients.name: chopped romaine, mixed greens, or baby kale

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup fresh pico de gallo, drained
ingredients.name: fresh pico de gallo

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans

preparationSteps: To make the turkey taco meat: Warm 1 tablespoon cooking oil in your largest nonstick skillet over high heat. Swirl to coat the pan, then add the thinly sliced green onions and 1 pound ground turkey. Chop the turkey quickly with a spatula to break it into tiny crumbles. Cook until the meat is cooked through and no liquid remains in the skillet, then turn the heat down to low and add the remaining ingredients (2 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels, 1 cup salsa verde, the juice of 1 lime, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt). Allow the meat to absorb all of these seasonings for several minutes, then taste and add more salt if needed.
To make the dressing: Stir together all the dressing ingredients. Dilute with water as needed until the dressing is the consistency of heavy cream.

To assemble the salad: In a large bowl, toss 6 cups of chopped greens, a big pinch of salt, 1 cup shredded white cheddar cheese, 1 cup of drained pico de gallo, 1 can of  black beans (drained), and 1 avocado (just scoop it straight into the bowl, no need to chop). Use a fork and chef’s knife to chop the salad over and over until it’s chopped into tiny pieces. Add the turkey taco meat and desired amount of dressing, mixing until it’s all well combined.
Divide the salad between 4 bowls and top with crushed tortilla chips.
DIG IN!

name: (almost) one-pan garlic butter roasted chicken and crispy potatoes with romesco, feta, and lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds of baby potatoes, cut in half
ingredients.name: of baby potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12 ounce) jar of roasted red peppers, drained
ingredients.name: of roasted red peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup blanched almonds, skin off(if you can’t find these, no worries, just use ANY almonds — raw, toasted, slivered, whatever)
ingredients.name: blanched almonds, skin off(if you can’t find these, no worries, just use ANY almonds — raw, toasted, slivered, whatever)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup (plus more for garnish) finely chopped soft green herbs, such as parsley, dill, basil, chives…
ingredients.name: (plus more for garnish) finely chopped soft green herbs, such as parsley, dill, basil, chives…

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon, cut into wedges or slices
ingredients.name: lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: Pita or a good loaf of bread (optional)
ingredients.name: Pita or a good loaf of bread (optional)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Cut 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes in half and place them and 8 chicken thighs on your largest rimmed sheet pan, all in a heap in the center. Add 1/2 cup olive oil, the zest (use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to zest it) and juice of 1 lemon, 4 crushed garlic cloves (just smash them with the side of your knife blade), 1 teaspoon paprika, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper on top and get in there with your hands to distribute and coat everything evenly.

Space everything out on the sheet pan with the chicken skin-side up. If your pan is too crowded, put half of the chicken and potatoes on another pan. Bake in the oven uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes until the potatoes are tender when poked with a fork, the chicken is cooked through (to 165°F), and the skin is crispy. If you’re using two pans, put one on the middle rack and one on the bottom rack, and switch them 30 minutes in.While the chicken is cooking, make the romesco and garlic butter. To make the romesco: in a blender or food processor, combine everything but the olive oil (1 jar of roasted red peppers, drained; 1/2 cup almonds; 1/4 cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained; 1 peeled garlic clove; 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar; and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt). Once mostly blended, drizzle in 1/2 cup olive oil while the motor is running. Keep going for several minutes — you want it to be gorgeously creamy and smooth. Taste and add more salt if it needs it.

If you don’t have a blender or food processor, you can make a coarse romesco sauce by simply hand chopping everything as finely as possible, then stirring it in a bowl with 1/4 cup olive oil (less than the normal recipe since it won’t emulsify into a smooth sauce). For the garlic butter, simply melt 2 tablespoons butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat, add 1 crushed garlic clove (smash it with the side of your knife), and bubble gently for a minute. Remove from the heat and stir in 1/4 cup chopped parsley (or another soft green herb). Remove the chicken and potatoes from the oven and drizzle the warm garlic butter over top. Spoon on some of the romesco sauce, add lemon slices, and crumble 1/4 cup feta over top. Add some fresh herbs for garnish and bring the whole pan to the table to serve family style alongside some good bread or pita, if you’ve got it. Enjoy!

name: grilled gochujang beef and mushroom bowls
note:
Feeding kids/spice averse people: My recipe testers, photographer, and I all loved 1/3 cup gochujang in our marinade and sauce, but if you or someone in your family are sensitive to spice, cut back to 1/4 cup. If you’re super sensitive to it, start with 3 tablespoons. Taste and add more a little at a time until it’s perfect!

I don’t own a grill: Use a grill pan if you have one. If not, use a cast-iron skillet! Heat it over high heat for 4-5 minutes so that it’s super hot (a drop of water should sizzle and evaporate instantly). Lower the heat to medium-high. Add the steak and cook undisturbed for 4-5 minutes. Flip it (if it doesn’t release easily, let it cook for another minute or so until it does) and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until it reaches the desired internal temp. Once you remove the steak, add the mushrooms to the skillet and cook for 6 minutes, flip, and cook for another 4 (or until tender). You can also broil the steak and mushrooms on the same sheet-pan for about 6 minutes per side.

Vegetarian: Add planks of zucchini, squash, and/or eggplant to the portobello mushrooms for a grilled veggie feast. Or, you could add some cooked shelled edamame or drained and rinsed chickpeas to your bowls for extra protein. See fish sauce subs below if needed. And also check your kimchi — some are made with fish sauce or shrimp paste.

Cooking for 1 or 2/love your leftovers: Halve this recipe! Or go ahead and cook it all and save the leftovers for lunches this week — they will stay good in the fridge stored in airtight containers for 3 to 4 days. If you don’t want a repeat of this meal, you could make tacos with the leftover steak and mushroom, a steak sandwich, and/or fried rice with your leftover cooked rice. If you have leftover goshujang sauce, stir in a spoonful of peanut or any nut/seed butter to give it a different vibe. You could use that sauce for peanut veggie noods, as a dipping sauce for potstickers, or to drizzle over any other “bowl.” You can also freeze leftover sauce.

Prep ahead: You can marinate your steak for up to 48 hours. You could also cook your rice way ahead of time — store it in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Add a splash of water as you reheat it on the stovetop or in the microwave.

Gluten-free: Use coconut aminos or tamari in place of soy sauce. Check labels for your gochujang, fish sauce, and kimchi — some are gluten-free but not all are!

Dairy-free: Use plant-based butter for your rice or just omit it.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1/3 cup gochujang (1/3 cup if you like spice and want it to have a kick; 1/4 cup if you don’t want it to be spicy!)
ingredients.name: gochujang (1/3 cup if you like spice and want it to have a kick; 1/4 cup if you don’t want it to be spicy!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup neutral cooking oil, plus more for grilling
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil, plus more for grilling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (2-inch) piece fresh ginger (you can peel it if you want, but you don’t have to!)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger (you can peel it if you want, but you don’t have to!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: One (1 1/2- to 2-pound) flat-iron, skirt, or flank steak
ingredients.name: One flat-iron, skirt, or flank steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons butter (unsalted or salted, whichever you have)
ingredients.name: butter (unsalted or salted, whichever you have)

preparationSteps: In a blender, combine 1/4 cup gochujang, 1/3 cup neutral cooking oil, 4 cloves of peeled garlic, a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger, 3 tablespoons light brown sugar, 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 1 cup of fresh cilantro stems and leaves, and 3 tablespoons water. Blend on high speed until smooth. Taste. Want it spicier? Add another tablespoon of gochujang!

Reserve 1/3 cup (80 ml) of the marinade to use as your sauce later, and pour the remaining marinade into a large resealable plastic bag. Add one (1 1/2- to 2-pound) flat-iron, skirt, or flank steak, seal the bag, and lay it flat in your refrigerator for at least 2 hours, but preferably 12 to 24 hours.
Thirty minutes before you’re ready to cook, remove the bag of steak from the refrigerator and add 1 pound of portobello mushrooms. Let it sit at room temperature until you’re ready to grill.

Meanwhile, cook 1 cup sushi rice per package instructions. Add 2 tablespoons of butter and 1 tablespoon soy sauce, then keep the rice covered until serving. Use a fork to fluff the rice just before serving.

Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high heat. If needed, when the grill is hot, brush the grill grates until they’re totally clean. Cleaning a cold grill doesn’t work! Heat it will burn all of the leftover oil and food bits, then use the brush to easily scrape them away.
Scrape the marinade off of the steak and mushrooms and rub them with neutral cooking oil. You want them to be lightly coated with oil, but not dripping! Oil drips can lead to flare ups.

Cook the steak and mushrooms for 6 minutes on the first side, flip, and cook for 4 minutes more. Your steak will be medium-rare at this point. You can pull it off the grill or let it keep cooking until it reaches your desired doneness (130°F for medium-rare, 140°F for medium, 150°F for medium-well, 160°F or above for well done).
Once you pull the steak and mushrooms off the grill, let them rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Thinly slice the steak against the grain. Look for the lines that run through the steak. Cut across them — perpendicular to them (see photo below!). Cutting against the grain makes each bite of steak more tender, because you’re cutting through tough tendons that would be difficult to chew, rather than leaving them whole.
Slice the mushrooms into 1/4-inch slices.
Serve with rice, 1 cup kimchi split between your bowls, and the reserved 1/3 cup marinade as a sauce on the side. Garnish your bowls with cilantro. Dig in!
*Note: You could cut the steak and mushrooms into bite-sized pieces to make this more of a handheld bowl that doesn’t require a knife!

name: mango peanut chicken salad
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Grab 2 bags of pre-shredded coleslaw mix (the bagged cabbage and carrots) instead of cutting cabbage and shredding carrots. Buy pre-chopped mango and just chop it up a bit smaller. Use a store-bought Asian-inspired dressing like a miso or peanut dressing.

But I have kids and they won’t eat salad: I got you. Save some chicken on the side for each kid. Buy an extra mango and chop that up for them. Add a handful of peanuts to their plate and call it a night.

Special ingredient: If you made the Sheet-pan Sesame Soy Steak and Veggies, you already own sesame oil! You can use toasted or plain (toasted has a lot more flavor). If you haven’t made that recipe yet… add it to your plan for this week! It was a major hit.

Vegetarian: Serve crispy tofu on top! Or just throw a lot of edamame in there for protein.

DF / GF: This meal is already gluten and dairy free… go me.

Make ahead: Make the whole damn thing ahead of time! It only gets better as the dressing absorbs into the cabbage and chicken! This is a wonderful meal prep recipe — delicious salad for days!

Whole30 it: Use almonds instead of peanuts. Coconut aminos instead of soy sauce. Sesame oil instead of peanut butter. Make sure your rotisserie chicken is compliant.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves and stems
ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves and stems

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup finely chopped fresh mint leaves
ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh mint leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup neutral oil such as grapeseed, avocado, or canola
ingredients.name: neutral oil such as grapeseed, avocado, or canola

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon creamy peanut butter OR sesame oil
ingredients.name: creamy peanut butter OR sesame oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated OR 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.note: peeled and grated OR 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger

preparationSteps: Thinly slice 1 head green cabbage following the how-to I share in this video. Throw it in a large bowl. Season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and use your hands to massage the salt into the cabbage by squeezing it together between your fists about 10 times, or until it starts to feel wet.
Add 2 grated carrots, 1 thinly sliced bell pepper, 1 thinly sliced mango, 1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro, 1/4 cup finely chopped mint leaves, and 2 thinly sliced green onions to the bowl of cabbage.
Remove the skin from the rotisserie chicken. Pull all of the meat off the bones and shred it finely. Add it to the bowl.

Make the salad dressing by adding 1/3 cup oil, 1/4 cup rice vinegar, 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon peanut butter OR sesame oil, and 1 inch of ginger, peeled and grated, to a jar. Close it up and shake the hell out of it. Taste and season with more salt if needed. Like things spicy? Add 1 tablespoon sriracha and shake again.

Pour half of the dressing onto the salad and toss. Taste and, if needed, add a little more. Continue tasting and adding more until it’s perfectly dressed. (I like a very dressing-y salad, so I use the entire jar.)
Garnish with an extra sprinkle of fresh herbs, peanuts, and sesame seeds if they’re floating around the pantry.

name: creamy butternut squash farro-tto
note:
Let’s talk pots: Like I said, if you have it in your cabinet, use a cast iron Dutch oven, or a braiser. But did you know that stainless steel is ovenproof too?! Yep. Another option if you have none of the above is a 12-inch cast iron skillet, and you’ll just throw a rimmed baking sheet on top to serve as the lid. When in doubt: Flip your pot over to find the brand name and specs. Google “is XYZ ovenproof?” Finally, if you don’t own an ovenproof pot, you can make this in a Pyrex by sautéing the onion, garlic, and oregano then scraping it into a Pyrex, adding the farro, and pouring boiling vegetable broth over top. Cover tightly with a baking sheet or some foil and proceed as written.

Make ahead: Yes, definitely! You can either prep ahead by chopping the veggies so they’re ready to go when you are, or you can actually cook the whole thing up to several days in advance. Let it come to room temperature in the pot you cooked it in then just throw the lid on and pop it in the fridge until you’re ready to eat. Re-warm it on the stovetop over medium heat, stirring in a splash of water at a time until it gets back to a nice risotto-y consistency.

Make it in a slow cooker: I really recommend sautéing the aromatics first if you can! So follow the first paragraph then transfer the onion and farro mixture to your slow cooker along with the broth, squash, cauliflower, salt, and garlic powder and cook on low for 3 to 4 hours, or on high for 1.5 to 2 hours. Once the farro and squash are both tender (cook it for longer if needed! add more broth if needed!), add the rest of the ingredients, stir, and cook over “keep warm” for another 15 minutes or so until everything is melted and well combined.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: As mentioned in the forward, there are a few chop-saving hacks here: You can buy pre-chopped onion, frozen cubes of crushed garlic (TJs has them!), and pre-chopped butternut squash (or sweet potato, if that’s what your store has). You could also go for pre-shredded cheese, though I much prefer freshly grated. All that will make it as dump and go as it gets!

Leftovers are a good thing: You could halve this recipe if you’re cooking for one or two… or make it all and stockpile your freezer with a cozy home-cooked meal! Freeze leftover portions in quart-sized Ziplocs and enjoy for lunch or dinner any day you please. Once your leftovers are thawed, you can reheat them on the stovetop or in the microwave. You may need to add a few splashes of stock, broth, or water to add some creaminess back as it reheats!

Must have meat: Seriously, this is very filling as is and makes a fantastic meatless meal! BUT you could add in some shredded rotisserie chicken when you add the spinach, peas, etc. Or you could add some pancetta you’ve sautéed until crispy to the mix.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: For dairy-free, use 1 1/2 cups of dairy-free Parm (my favorite is Violife!). For gluten-free, use risotto or short-grain brown rice instead of farro and make sure your broth is gf.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups farro (literally any kind will work, doesn’t matter how long it says it takes to cook)
ingredients.name: farro (literally any kind will work, doesn’t matter how long it says it takes to cook)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups (~20 ounces) chopped butternut squash (or 1 small butternut squash, peeled and chopped)
ingredients.name: (~20 ounces) chopped butternut squash (or 1 small butternut squash

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup cauliflower rice(you can omit if you’re not a cauli person)
ingredients.name: cauliflower rice(you can omit if you’re not a cauli person)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups spinach, chopped(I actually just tear it with my hands as I’m adding it to the pot)
ingredients.name: spinach, chopped(I actually just tear it with my hands as I’m adding it to the pot)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in an ovenproof pot (preferably a cast iron Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Add 1 large diced yellow onion and cook, stirring frequently, until soft, 3 to 4 minutes. Add 1 1/2 cups farro, 4 minced garlic cloves, and 1 1/2 teaspoons dried oregano and cook for an additional minute.
Stir in 4 cups low-sodium vegetable broth, 3 cups butternut squash, 1 cup cauliflower rice, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder and bring the mixture to a boil. Turn off the heat.

Cover the pot and transfer to the oven. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the farro is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed. Smash the butternut squash a bit with the back of your spoon. Stir in 4 cups chopped spinach, the juice of 1 lemon, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/2 cup shredded Gruyère cheese, 1 cup frozen peas, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly grated black pepper until the spinach is wilted and the farro-tto is creamy.
Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed. Serve with extra Parm on top, if desired. Dig in!

name: sheet-pan chicken tagine
note:
Make ahead: This is an amazing weeknight meal because it comes together with minimal effort. If you’re like me, you like to prep ahead as much as possible though. So: You can make the couscous well ahead of time — just store it in the fridge and reheat right before dinner. And you can go ahead and half/pit your olives and slice your onions earlier in the day or the night before, also keeping in the fridge until you’re ready to cook. Then it’s just dump, mix, and go!

Kid food: My one-year-old devoured this entire meal. For my three-year-old, I mixed together the couscous, chopped up apricots, and chopped up chicken with a little plain yogurt so that it was easier for him to scoop up. He devoured it!

Leftovers are a great thing: Like I said in the intro, you can easily halve the chicken if you’re cooking for one or two and don’t want a ton of leftovers. That said… these leftovers make *amazing* lunches. Just reheat then garnish with fresh cilantro! Or, repurpose into a salad by cutting the chicken off the bone and throwing it and everything else over spinach with feta, almonds, a little EVOO and lemon juice. We ate that salad several times last week — so good.

Vegetarian: Make a big Moroccan vegetable feast! Instead of the chicken, use 1 can drained, rinsed, and dried chickpeas, and a pound of sweet potatoes, butternut squash, and/or carrots cubed. Cauliflower would also be delish here! Cook them the same way as the recipe’s written.

GF/DF: For gluten-free, swap the couscous for quinoa or rice. For dairy-free, use df butter.

Whole30: Make sure your olives have no added sulfates and that your chicken stock is compliant. Swap couscous for cauliflower rice and don’t use butter when cooking it.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (you can use 2 pounds if only feeding 2 people, but I recommend making 4 as the leftovers are wonderful!)
ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (you can use 2 pounds if only feeding 2 people, but I recommend making 4 as the leftovers are wonderful!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) jar Castelvetrano olives, pitted (if needed) and halved (tear them in half with your hands, don't use a knife, it looks cooler!)
ingredients.name: and halved (tear them in half with your hands, don't use a knife, it looks cooler!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon, zest of whole and juice of half(If you can find preserved lemons, chop one up and use that instead the zest! But you’ll still need lemon juice for the couscous.)
ingredients.name: lemon, zest of whole and juice of half(If you can find preserved lemons, chop one up and use that instead the zest! But you’ll still need lemon juice for the couscous.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup couscous (NOT *Israeli* couscous, which is actually a type of pasta!)
ingredients.name: couscous (NOT *Israeli* couscous, which is actually a type of pasta!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro (or parsley), plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: chopped fresh cilantro (or parsley), plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

On your largest rimmed sheet pan, toss 2 to 4 pounds chicken thighs, 2 medium thinly sliced yellow onions, 8 ounces halved olives, 16 ounces dried apricots, 3 tablespoons olive oil, 6 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and the zest of 1 lemon. Really get in there with your hands to make sure the spices are evenly distributed.
Spread the ingredients out into as even of a layer as possible, with the chicken skin facing up. Pour 1 cup chicken stock onto the baking sheet.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F internally.

Meanwhile, cook the couscous by bringing 1 cup chicken stock, 2 tablespoons butter, and the juice of 1/2 lemon to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat. Remove the pot from the heat, stir in 1 cup of couscous, cover, and leave it to sit until you’re ready to serve dinner. Stir in 1/4 cup cilantro just before serving.
Serve the chicken over a scoop of couscous, garnish with cilantro, and dig in!

ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
