preparationSteps: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup red wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon pepperoncini brine, 1 tablespoon mayonnaise (optional), 1 tablespoon dried oregano, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Use a microplane to grate in 2 garlic cloves (or mince them if you don’t have a microplane).
Whisk until smooth, then taste and adjust seasoning if needed as desired. Transfer 1/4 cup of the dressing to a small container and set aside for later use.

Drain and rinse 1 can chickpeas and add them to the bowl. Thinly slice 1 small red onion and add it to the bowl. Finely chop 1/2 cup pepperoncini peppers and 1/2 cup pitted olives, halve 1 cup cherry tomatoes, and add all to the bowl. Toss together with the dressing to let these ingredients start marinating.
Continue the chopping!

Thinly slice 4 ounces of sliced salami into ribbons. Grate 4 ounces of cheese using a box grater or microplane. De-rib and finely chop 1 bunch kale and finely chop 2 small hearts of romaine. If you’re wondering, see notes below for how and when I wash my greens.
Add everything to the bowl, but don’t toss until you’re ready to eat! You can add it all to the bowl, with the lettuce on top, up to 12 hours before serving.
When you’re ready to eat, season the greens with salt and pepper, then toss everything together and top with 1 cup salt and vinegar or plain kettle chips. Add more of the reserved dressing if needed.
ENJOY!

name: chicken flautas & roasted corn salad
note:
My favorite salsa verdes: The Hatch Valley Salsa Verde from TJ’s — but it’s spicy, so don’t do this one if you’re feeding spice wimps. I also love TJ’s plain Salsa Verde. My fave grocery store brand is La Victoria.

Vegetarian: Use 1 1/2 cups drained and rinsed black (or pinto!) beans in place of the chicken. Smash them up a bit so that they really absorb the salsa verde. You might also end up wanting to add a bit more salsa verde for more flavor. Alternatively, click here for a vegetarian flautas recipe I wrote last year.

Make ahead: Assemble the flautas and make the crema ahead of time, then bake them right before dinner. You’ll want to wait to make the salad just before you eat so that your avocado doesn’t turn brown, but you can shuck the corn ahead of time too.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the salad, and just serve roasted corn with butter, lime juice, and salt. Or if you want to make the salad, you can skip roasted fresh corn and just warm up a bag of frozen corn and use that — no shucking necessary! Another small hack: Buy pre-minced cilantro. If you do that and use frozen corn, it’ll be a no-chop situation.

Leftovers are a great thing: I just had leftover corn salad with leftover rotisserie chicken and goat cheese on top, with a drizzle of balsamic glaze, and goodness gracious it was heavenly. Flautas are also a perfect freezer meal, so just store those leftovers in a Ziploc after they’ve cooled. Reheat on a baking sheet in a 400°F oven for 10 to 15 minutes. If you have leftover flautas in the fridge, reheat them in the oven at 400°F for 5 to 10 minutes, they’ll crisp right back up!

Dairy-free: Use df sour cream in lieu of the regular sour cream. Either use your favorite non-dairy cheese OR omit the cheese and add a cup of refried beans to the chicken mixture for some creaminess and flavor.

Gluten-free: Corn tortillas work, but they’re more likely to break in the oven. To help prevent that, wrap them in a damp paper towel and microwave for 45 seconds, or until very pliable. Roll and proceed, but know that a couple might crack! No biggie — still delicious.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup sour cream (or cream cheese or plain yogurt)
ingredients.name: sour cream (or cream cheese or plain yogurt)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, finely chopped, divided (you’ll use half for the flautas, half for the salad)
ingredients.name: fresh cilantro, finely chopped, divided (you’ll use half for the flautas, half for the salad)

preparationSteps: Alright team, if we work efficiently, we’re going to have a weeknight fiesta on the table in less than 30 minutes! Let’s do this.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, combine 1 1/2 cups shredded rotisserie chicken, 1/2 cup shredded Mexican cheese, 1/4 sour cream, 3 tablespoons salsa verde, 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, and 1/4 teaspoon chili powder. We’re not adding salt yet because different rotisserie chickens and salsa brands have such different sodium levels.

Mix it all together and take a little nibble. Is it delicious? If so, proceed. Does it need a little more oomph? Stir in some salt and maybe some more chili powder, if you’re into that! Keep seasoning until it’s delicious.

Spread 2 to 3 tablespoons of the chicken mixture down the center of a tortilla, then roll it tightly and place it seam-side down onto the baking sheet. Repeat until all of the chicken filling is gone. Place 4 ears of corn on the baking sheet as well, then spray everything with cooking spray.

Bake for 10 minutes, then flip the flautas and corn and cook for an additional 3 to 6 minutes, until the flautas are golden and crispy all over and the corn is crisp-tender. Honestly, I skip this flipping step a lot of the time. They’re not crispy on the bottom, but no one ever seems to mind.

Meanwhile, let’s made the salad. In a pretty serving bowl, combine 1 1/2 cups of halved cherry tomatoes, 1 large cubed avocado, the juice of 1 large lime, the remaining 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, and 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil. Set it aside.

Now let’s make the crema verde dipping sauce. In a small bowl, stir together 1/3 cup sour cream, 2 tablespoons salsa verde, and a big pinch of salt. This should be very simple and delicious. If it’s not, add more salsa verde and perhaps a splash of lime juice or vinegar.

When the flautas and corn finish cooking, cut the corn off the cob (as soon as it’s cool enough to handle) and stir the kernels into the bowl of tomatoes and avocado. Add a big pinch of salt and stir gently to combine. Taste. Want it tangier? Add more lime juice or a splash of vinegar. Want it a bit creamier? Add more oil. And, of course, salt and pepper always do the trick!
Enjoy your flautas and roasted corn salad!

name: green chicken tortilla soup
note:
Make it soup-ier: Like I said, this is a very thick soup full of goodies. You may find that you want to add more broth — just add more of the chicken stock from the second quart.

Make ahead: This soup will be even better after 24 hours of sitting in the refrigerator! The flavors continue to develop and get even more delicious. Make it as many as 4 days in advance!

Make it in a slow cooker: Add all the ingredients except for the kale, cilantro, and frozen corn to a slow cooker. Start with 4 cups of liquid instead of 6 — if the chicken isn’t totally submerged, add more just until it is. Cook covered on low for 6 hours, then shred the chicken and return it to the slow cooker along with the kale, cilantro, and frozen corn. Let it cook for another 30 minutes with the lid off for the corn to warm and kale and cilantro to wilt!

Short on time: This is pretty much a dump and go recipe — almost no chopping thanks to our salsa verde. The most intensive step is shredding the chicken. If you can find pre-cooked, pre-shredded rotisserie chicken — some Targets, Walmarts, etc. sell them — you could throw that in during the last 10 minutes of cooking to remove that step.

How should I freeze this? Let any leftovers come to room temp then pour into a freezer-safe bag (or bags). Freeze it in portion sizes that you’ll serve when you reheat, whether that’s a gallon-size bag if you’re feeding a family or a sandwich bag if you’ll want it for yourself for a single meal. Once filled, lay the bag flat out on a baking sheet and pop it in the freezer. When it’s frozen, remove it from the sheet-pan and you’ll have a thin, easy-to-store sheet of soup ready to reheat and eat later this fall or winter!

Vegetarian: Double the zucchini. There’s plenty of protein from the beans already!

Vegan/gluten-free: Done and done, just use vegan sour cream and df cheese on top (or omit).

More salsa verde ideas. Okay, okay, I just remembered two more WTC recipes you could cook if you bought an extra jar: my 30-minute al pastor enchiladas and/or the dankest taco salad.

ingredients.name: Tortilla strips (honestly tortilla chips are just as good, but I’m providing this recipe for anyone who wants torture themselves by making things harder than they need to be!):

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 corn tortillas, cut into 1/4-inch thick slices
ingredients.name: corn tortillas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 48 ounces (6 cups) low-sodium chicken stock (aka 1 1/2 32-ounce boxes)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (aka 1 1/2 32-ounce boxes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16- or 24-ounce) jar salsa verde or tomatillo salsa
ingredients.name: salsa verde or tomatillo salsa

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (15-ounce) cans white beans, drained but not rinsed (cannellini, navy, great Northern, or even chickpeas or kidney beans)
ingredients.name: white beans, drained but not rinsed (cannellini, navy, great Northern, or even chickpeas or kidney beans)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen white corn (or 2 cans drained)
ingredients.name: frozen white corn (or 2 cans drained)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups chopped kale (if you buy the bagged, pre-chopped kale, pick out the tough stems)
ingredients.name: chopped kale (if you buy the bagged, pre-chopped kale, pick out the tough stems)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup cilantro (leaves and stems), finely chopped
ingredients.name: cilantro (leaves and stems)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings: tortilla strips or chips, chopped avocado, sour cream or Greek yogurt, shredded cheddar or pepper jack cheese
ingredients.name: Toppings: tortilla strips or chips, chopped avocado, sour cream or Greek yogurt, shredded cheddar or pepper jack cheese

preparationSteps: To make the tortilla strips: Toss the tortilla slices, 2 tablespoons oil, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 3/4 teaspoon chili powder, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder on a rimmed baking sheet until the tortilla strips are evenly coated. Bake at 375°F for 15 to 20 minutes, until crispy and browned.

To make the soup: dump 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock, 1 jar of salsa verde, 1 can green chiles (not drained), 2 cans drained (not rinsed) white beans, 2 pounds chicken thighs, 1 diced zucchini, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1 teaspoon chili powder, and 1 teaspoon smoked paprika into a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 30 minutes.

Pull the chicken out and shred it by using two forks to pull it apart. Stir it back into the pot along with 1 bag of frozen white corn, 3 cups chopped kale, and 1 cup chopped cilantro. When the kale is wilted, taste the soup. Depending on how salty your stock and beans were, you may or may not need to add more salt.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve topped with tortilla strips (or chips), sour cream, avocado, more cilantro, and/or lots of cheese.

name: chicken caesar schnitzel
note:
Save time: Swap in store-bought Caesar dressing!

Vegetarian: Add some roasted cauliflower and chickpeas to your Caesar salad instead. You can swap out the anchovies for capers but you may need to add extra mayo to thicken things up.

Leftover makeover: If you have leftover schnitzel, make chicken Parm the next day! Place the schnitzel on a baking sheet, smother it with marinara and mozzarella, and bake at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes.

Gluten-free: Use GF panko and 1:1 gluten-free baking flour or almond flour.

Dairy-free: Omit the Parm.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 chicken breasts, sliced carefully in half horizontally
ingredients.name: chicken breasts, sliced carefully in half horizontally

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup avocado or vegetable oil (or cooking spray, if baking)
ingredients.name: avocado or vegetable oil (or cooking spray, if baking)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large heads of romaine lettuce, thinly sliced and washed
ingredients.name: of romaine lettuce, thinly sliced and washed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium honey crisp apple (cold from the fridge, ideally!)
ingredients.name: medium honey crisp apple (cold from the fridge, ideally!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons of anchovy paste (depending on how anchovy-y ya like it!)
ingredients.name: of anchovy paste (depending on how anchovy-y ya like it!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon, zested and juiced (buy an extra lemon just in case you want to add more! I always do)
ingredients.name: lemon, zested and juiced (buy an extra lemon just in case you want to add more! I always do)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of kosher salt and several grinds of pepper
ingredients.name: Big pinch of kosher salt and several grinds of pepper

preparationSteps: Cut 2 chicken breasts in half as slowly and carefully as you need to to try to get two perfectly even halves. Place each half between two pieces of parchment paper and use a rolling pin or heavy bottle to flatten each to about 1/4 inch. Don’t pound too hard and break them!
Set out 3 shallow bowls.

In the first bowl, make the Caesar dressing! Combine a heaping 1/2 cup mayo, 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 to 2 tablespoons of anchovy paste (depending on how anchovy-y ya like it!), 1 grated garlic clove, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, a big pinch of kosher salt, and several grinds of pepper. Taste. I like to add a lot more lemon juice, personally, but I know many like a richer Caesar dressing, so do your thing! Add additional salt, lemon, anchovy paste, etc. until it’s your perfect Caesar dressing.
Transfer half of the dressing to a large mixing bowl to use later (we’ll use what’s left in that shallow bowl as a dredge for the chicken!).

Now back to the chicken. Place 1/2 cup all-purpose flour in the second shallow bowl, and place 1 1/2 cups panko and 1/4 cup grated Parm in the third bowl. Season both with kosher salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Dredge each piece of chicken through the flour until fully coated, then through the Caesar dressing that’s still in the shallow bowl until fully coated (it will want to REALLY stick on there — we only need a light coating so use your hands to wipe off any excess), and finally through the panko mixture. If you run out of panko or Caesar dressing while breading the chicken, just add more to the bowl.

To fry it: Heat 1/2 cup avocado oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. When you add a piece of panko and it sizzles, you’re ready to cook. Cook one piece of chicken at a time for 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until golden brown. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with salt. Don’t skip the paper towel step!

To bake it: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Place the chicken on a foil-lined baking sheet in an even layer and spray with cooking spray on both sides. Bake for 6 minutes, then flip and cook for an additional 6 minutes. Check that the chicken is 165°F internally.
Thinly slice 2 large heads of romaine and cut 1 medium honey crisp apple (cold from the fridge, ideally!) into matchsticks. Toss with the reserved dressing in the mixing bowl.

Place one schnitzel on a plate and cover with salad. Use a microplane or box grater to grate fresh Parm all over the top. Add a few grinds of pepper. Repeat with remaining plates. Done! ENJOY IMMEDIATELY!

name: roasted harissa chicken and sweet potato bowls
note:
What else can I do with harissa? These meatballs look delicious, the Ottolenghi shakshuka linked above is a must, but the way I use it most often is just to stir a bit of harissa into yogurt, labne, or sour cream along with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon juice to make a sauce! I use it as kind of a dipping sauce with roasted meat and veggies.

Make ahead: Like I said in the directions, this is a GREAT meal to prep ahead. You can prep the whole thing, wrap the sheet pan up with some plastic wrap, and let it hang in the fridge for up to 24 hours until you’re ready to cook.

Leftovers are a good thing: This is a simple recipe to halve, if needed. But the leftovers make for delish lunches.

Vegetarian: Make a harissa roasted veggie bowl! I’d use a head of cauliflower cut into florets and some halved Brussels sprouts in addition to the sweet potatoes. Carrots would be good here too. You’ll mix them with the oil, harissa, etc., as written. You could also throw a can of chickpeas into the mix. Rinse and drain your chickpeas, drying them with a clean dish cloth/paper towel, before putting them on the sheet pan. You may need to add another tablespoon of oil to ensure all the veggies are lightly coated. If needed, separate them onto two sheet pans to ensure they’re not bunched.

Dairy free/gluten free: To eliminate dairy, use a DF sour cream OR use hummus for your “swoop” instead! For gluten free, check the label of your harissa. It should be gf but you’ll want to double check.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon maple syrup, honey, or brown sugar
ingredients.name: maple syrup, honey, or brown sugar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and 1-inch cubed
ingredients.name: large sweet potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup or so of labne, sour cream, or Greek yogurt
ingredients.name: or so of labne, sour cream, or Greek yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped toasted nuts (pistachios or almonds are my fave here, but use what you have)
ingredients.name: chopped toasted nuts (pistachios or almonds are my fave here, but use what you have)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup golden raisins (or normal raisins, or dried cranberries, or diced dates…)
ingredients.name: golden raisins (or normal raisins, or dried cranberries, or diced dates…)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line your largest baking sheet with parchment paper.

If you’re feeding people who don’t like a bit of kick (harissa won’t kick your ass, but it definitely has a kick), set aside a portion of sweet potatoes and chicken for them, and season it with just olive oil, salt, and a bit of garlic powder and smoked paprika. You can then roast it on the same sheet pan with the harissa chicken and potatoes.
In a large bowl, stir together 3 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons harissa, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, and 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt.
Add 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts and 2 cubed sweet potatoes to the bowl and use your hands to really get in there and toss everything together until it’s all evenly coated.
Leave the chicken breasts in the bowl (because they don’t need to cook as long as the sweet potatoes) but transfer the sweet potatoes to the baking sheet.

Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes. Give them a stir, and scooch things around so that you can place the 4 chicken breasts on the baking sheet. Return the baking sheet to the oven for an additional 15 minutes, until the chicken breasts are 160°F internally (they’ll continue cooking once out of the oven to reach 165°F).
Set the baking sheet aside to let things cool down for a few minutes, then thinly slice the chicken breasts against the grain.
Now I’m going to provide some very specific plating instructions (check out the video above) to make your bowl look like it cost $20 from a bougie restaurant in the West Village:

Grab four plates or low coupe bowls and spoon about 1/4 cup labne or sour cream or Greek yogurt onto the bottom of each bowl. Use the back of the spoon to “swoop” it across about half of the bowl. Pile a handful of arugula over top, then plate the thinly sliced chicken breast and roasted sweet potatoes partly over the arugula and labne, partly over the empty plate. Sprinkle about a tablespoon of chopped nuts and a tablespoon of raisins over top and add a lemon quarter to each plate. Season the arugula with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Dig in!

name: tropical shrimp bowls with coconut rice and pineapple- avocado salsa
note:
How do I rinse rice? Two options: 1) Put it in a fine-mesh strainer and run it under cold water, moving the rice around with your fingers, until the water runs clear, or 2) put it in your pot, add some water, and swirl it around in the water. Drain the water and repeat until the water runs clear.

OK but what should I make for brunch? If your significant other wants brunch, make this Starbucks copycat frittata the night before and bake it in the morning while you let her sleep in. You can skip the sweet potato hash if it sounds hard. Maybe buy frozen hash browns and just crisp that up. Make a nice, simple salad to go with it by adding arugula, lots of shaved Parm, toasted pine nuts, lemon juice, extra-virgin olive oil, a big pinch of salt, and a little pepper to a serving bowl and tossing. Taste it. Is it delicious? If not, it probably needs more salt. Cut up some strawberries to add to your plates. Dig in.

Prep ahead: The rice can be made up to 5 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, adding a splash of water to help loosen it. You can make the sauce up to 3 days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. If it thickens up in the fridge, add some more oil, or even a little water, to loosen it up. But again, DON’T marinate the shrimp for more than 30 minutes! It’ll start to “cook” like ceviche.The slaw can be made up to 3 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge.You want to make the pineapple-avocado salsa right before serving if possible, but if you need to make it ahead, wait to add the avocado until the last minute and press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning.If your shrimp are finished cooking but you’re still working on other components of the meal, tent the plate they’re on with foil!

The rice can be made up to 5 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, adding a splash of water to help loosen it.

You can make the sauce up to 3 days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. If it thickens up in the fridge, add some more oil, or even a little water, to loosen it up. But again, DON’T marinate the shrimp for more than 30 minutes! It’ll start to “cook” like ceviche.

The slaw can be made up to 3 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge.

You want to make the pineapple-avocado salsa right before serving if possible, but if you need to make it ahead, wait to add the avocado until the last minute and press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning.

If your shrimp are finished cooking but you’re still working on other components of the meal, tent the plate they’re on with foil!

Love your leftovers: If you have leftovers, store each component separately. The shrimp will keep for 3 days, rice for 5 days (or freeze it!), but the salsa is best eaten within 24 hours before the avocado starts to brown. The sauce will keep for about 5 days and is excellent drizzled over eggs, roasted vegetables, or grilled chicken.

Got any shortcuts? Yes! Go read the “take shortcuts where you need them” note above the recipe.

I’m feeding spice wimps: Omit the jalapeño!

I don’t like shrimp: This marinade (and whole recipe) would be delicious with any protein you love. Here’s how to swap in chicken, steak, or salmon: For chicken breasts or thighs: Marinate them in the green sauce for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours in the fridge. Grill over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes per side (or until 165°F internally). If cooking in a skillet, I’d cut the chicken into cubes before marinating, then sear them in olive oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until cooked through. For steak (skirt, flank, or sirloin would all be great here): Marinate them for up to 4 hours in the fridge. Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side or until desired internal temp (125-130°F for medium-rare; 135-140°F for medium; or above for well done). For salmon: Marinate the fish for up to 30 minutes. To grill it, oil the grates and grill skin-side down over medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes for the first side, then 2 to 4 minutes on the second side, or until it reaches 120 to 130°F internally and flakes easily with a fork. Or you could bake it at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Or cook it in oil in a skillet over medium-high until cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway through. Or…

For chicken breasts or thighs: Marinate them in the green sauce for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours in the fridge. Grill over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes per side (or until 165°F internally). If cooking in a skillet, I’d cut the chicken into cubes before marinating, then sear them in olive oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

For steak (skirt, flank, or sirloin would all be great here): Marinate them for up to 4 hours in the fridge. Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side or until desired internal temp (125-130°F for medium-rare; 135-140°F for medium; or above for well done).

For salmon: Marinate the fish for up to 30 minutes. To grill it, oil the grates and grill skin-side down over medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes for the first side, then 2 to 4 minutes on the second side, or until it reaches 120 to 130°F internally and flakes easily with a fork. Or you could bake it at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Or cook it in oil in a skillet over medium-high until cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway through.

Or…

Vegetarian: Tofu would be so good with this meal. Press a block of extra firm tofu to remove excess water. You can either slice it lengthwise into big flat planks (best for grilling) or cube it. Marinate it for 30 minutes, then either grill it, pan sear it (AKA, cook it in a skillet until golden), or bake it at 400°F for 20 minutes, or until it starts to crisp up (flipping once halfway through).

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It’s already gluten-free. To avoid dairy, use a plant-based butter or extra olive oil if cooking the shrimp in a skillet.

ingredients.name: For the citrus-cilantro green sauce/marinade and shrimp:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup fresh cilantro (you can use both the leaves and stems)
ingredients.name: fresh cilantro (you can use both the leaves and stems)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 scallion (AKA green onion), roots trimmed off and discarded
ingredients.name: scallion (AKA green onion), roots trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 jalapeño (optional — spice-averse people, skip it!), seeded (AKA seeds removed)
ingredients.name: jalapeño (optional — spice-averse people, skip it!), seeded (AKA seeds removed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds large shrimp (16-20 count), peeled and deveined
ingredients.name: large shrimp (16-20 count)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter (only if you’re cooking the shrimp in a skillet)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter (only if you’re cooking the shrimp in a skillet)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups short-grain white rice, rinsed (see notes section for how to rinse it)
ingredients.name: short-grain white rice, rinsed (see notes section for how to rinse it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small fresh pineapple (or 2 cups pre-cut pineapple), chopped 1/4 inch
ingredients.name: small fresh pineapple (or 2 cups pre-cut pineapple), chopped 1/4 inch

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red bell pepper (optional — the salsa is great without it), chopped 1/4 inch
ingredients.name: red bell pepper (optional — the salsa is great without it), chopped 1/4 inch

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 scallions (AKA green onions), roots trimmed off and discarded, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions (AKA green onions), roots trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag shredded cabbage (purple or green cabbage or “coleslaw mix” all work)
ingredients.name: shredded cabbage (purple or green cabbage or “coleslaw mix” all work)

preparationSteps: First things first, let's make the citrus-cilantro green sauce that will pull this whole dish together. FYI, you’re going to use this sauce 4 different ways: 1) Half of it will be your shrimp marinade. 2) You’ll use a few spoonfuls to flavor the salsa. 3) It is the dressing for your slaw. 4) Any leftover sauce gets drizzled on top of the bowls as a sauce!

In your blender or food processor, combine the juice of 2 large limes, the juice from 1 orange, 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 cup cilantro leaves and stems, 1 scallion (roots trimmed off and discarded first), 2 small peeled garlic cloves, 1 halved and seeded jalapeño (to do this: cut off the stem, then cut it in half lengthwise, then scoop out and discard all of the seeds), 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Blend until smooth and vibrant green. This sauce should be loose enough to pour but thick enough to cling to the back of a spoon. If it's too thick, add another tablespoon of olive oil and blend again.

Pour half of this green sauce into a serving bowl and set it aside for later. Pour the other half into a shallow dish (or Ziploc) along with 1 1/2 pounds large peeled and deveined shrimp. Toss to coat every shrimp thoroughly, then refrigerate for up to 30 minutes. Don't marinate longer than this — the citrus will start "cooking" the shrimp like ceviche!
While the shrimp is marinating, make the rice, salsa, and slaw.
If you’re grilling, now is a good time to preheat your grill! We’re going to be cooking over medium-high heat.

For the rice: Combine 1 1/2 cups rinsed short-grain white rice, 1 can coconut milk, 1 1/4 cups water, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in a small pot and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to the lowest heat possible, COVER, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until all liquid is absorbed. Turn off the heat, keep the lid on, and let it steam for at least another 5 minutes. Just before serving, fluff it with a fork (AKA gently scrape the rice with a fork to un-clump it).

Next up, let’s make the salsa: Chop 2 cups fresh pineapple into small (about 1/4 inch, so about the size of your pinky finger’s nail) pieces and add them to a medium-sized bowl. If you're using a whole pineapple, here’s what to do: cut off the top and bottom, stand it upright, slice off the skin in strips, then quarter it lengthwise, remove the core, and dice. Here’s a visual. Or just buy it pre-cut, and dice up the big chunks! Chop 1 ripe avocado and 1 red bell pepper into roughly 1/4-inch pieces. Remove and discard the root ends of 2 scallions then thinly slice them (the whole scallion, both white and green parts!). Add all the chopped vegetables to the bowl along with 2 tablespoons of the green sauce you set aside and a big pinch of kosher salt. Stir gently — we want the avocado to hold its shape, not turn into guacamole. Taste. If it’s not absolutely delicious, add more sauce and a tiny bit more kosher salt.

Finally, make the slaw! Simply dump the bag of shredded cabbage into a cute bowl, add a pinch of kosher salt, and squeeze the cabbage 5 times with your hands. Pour in 2 to 3 tablespoons of the green sauce and toss to coat. Taste. Add more kosher salt and/or green sauce until it’s delicious.
Time to cook the shrimp!

If you’re grilling: Thread the marinated shrimp onto skewers — don't pack them too tightly; they need a little breathing room. Heat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the skewers for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and have some nice grill marks.

If you’re cooking in a skillet: Warm your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and heat until shimmering. Tilt the pan around to coat it in oil. Shake off as much marinade from the shrimp as possible, then add them to the skillet in an even layer. Cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until golden-brown all over. Add 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and toss to coat the shrimp in melted butter. Transfer shrimp to a serving platter.

Serve! This is a great meal to serve family style — just set the shrimp, rice, salsa, and slaw out and let everyone build their own bowls. Or, make everyone’s bowls for them by dividing the coconut rice among bowls, topping with shrimp (you can leave them on the skewers for presentation or slide them off — your call), and adding a generous scoop of both pineapple-avocado salsa and slaw. Drizzle everything with the reserved green sauce. Garnish with extra cilantro and lime wedges if you're feeling fancy. Dig in!

name: rotisserie-ish chicken with schmaltzy frizzled cabbage

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (2ish pound) head green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced — or 4 (10-ounce) bags shredded cabbage but dang that’s gonna cost a lot more
ingredients.name: shredded cabbage but dang that’s gonna cost a lot more
ingredients.quantity: 1 (2ish pound) head green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced — or 4 (10-ounce) bags

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar (really, any vinegar) or lemon juice
ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar (really, any vinegar) or lemon juice

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Rinse and dry 1 head green cabbage and peel away any leaves on the outside that look dirty/dingy. Cut the head in half, then in half again, through the stem. Cut the tough core out by making a triangular cut through the base of each quarter.
Slice the cabbage into 1/4 inch-thick pieces and throw it onto your biggest rimmed sheet pan. Toss it with 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil and 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt until coated.
In a small bowl, stir together 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon chili powder, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.

Pat the whole chicken totally dry with paper towels or a clean kitchen towel. Place the chicken breast-side up (the legs will be sticking up in the air) and use your hands to coat it all over with the spice-oil paste. Some of the paste will obviously spill onto the cabbage — that’s ok. Tuck the wings under the chicken (if they’re sticking up they’ll burn!) and tie the legs together, one crossing over the other, with kitchen twine.

Wash and dry 4 sweet potatoes and prick them all over with a fork. Rub with a light coat of extra-virgin olive oil, then place them over the cabbage wherever you can. If it freaks you out to put the potatoes right on the cabbage, you can put them on a separate sheet pan and roast them above the chicken.

Transfer the sheet pan to the center rack of the oven and roast for 45 to 60 minutes* (stirring and covering with foil** along the way — see below), until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the leg reads 160°F. Stir the cabbage a few times along the way (every 20 minutes or so).

Once it hits the proper temp, take the sheet pan out of the oven. Pick the chicken up with tongs by grabbing it through the cavity under the legs, and tilting it to let all the juices run from the inside of the chicken out onto the cabbage. Stir the juices into the cabbage. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board to rest.

Return the cabbage and sweet potatoes to the oven for 10 minutes, or until the edges of the cabbage start to brown and frizzle. You can broil the cabbage for a minute if it’s not looking frizzled (crispy on top), but don’t walk away from the oven! It’ll burn if you leave it for too long.
Stir in 1 tablespoon vinegar and more salt as desired. Cut the cooked sweet potatoes in half and mash 1 tablespoon butter and a big pinch of salt and pepper into each potato.
Carve the chicken (click here for a great tutorial) and serve with cabbage and a sweet potato.

name: roasted asparagus farro-tto
note:
WTF do I cook this in? If you own a Dutch oven or a braiser — bingo, one of those. If you own ANY stainless steel pot, you can use that! Stainless steel is ovenproof! A 12-inch cast iron skillet is perfect too, just throw a rimmed baking sheet on top to serve as the lid and to cook the asparagus on. When in doubt: Flip your pot over to find the brand name and specs. Google “is XYZ ovenproof?” Finally, if you truly do not own an ovenproof pan, you can make this in a Pyrex by sautéing the onion and garlic, then scraping it into a Pyrex, adding the farro, and pouring boiling chicken stock over top. Cover tightly with a baking sheet or some foil.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Put the rice and the stock in the pot. Bake it. Stir in some parmesan, white wine, and water at the end. Done. Simple, perfect risotto.

Where’s the meat?: C’mon, you can go meatless ONE night this week! No? Grill some chicken and throw it on top. Or add some shrimp in with the asparagus to roast them.

I’m only feeding two people/freezer-friendly: You can halve the recipe, but I highly recommend cooking the whole thing and freezing leftover portions in quart ziplocks for a quick lunch or dinner later on! Once it’s thawed you can reheat it on the stovetop or in the oven. You may need to add splashes of stock (or water) to loosen it a bit while reheating!

Make ahead: Go for it! Make the whole thing ahead of time (stir in all of the asparagus), then just let it cool down right in the skillet and throw it in the fridge. Re-warm it over medium heat, stirring in a splash of water at a time until it gets back to a nice risotto-y consistency.

I can’t find farro: Arborio rice is the most classic rice for making risotto and you can swap it in here with no issues. Sushi rice is another good option. A short-grained brown rice will also work, but cook it for 35 minutes before adding the asparagus and cooking for another 10.

Dairy-free: Use your fave non-dairy butter and a great melty non-dairy cheese!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups farro (pearled or semi-pearled, if you can find it, but any kind works)
ingredients.name: farro (pearled or semi-pearled, if you can find it, but any kind works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound medium-width asparagus (AKA not the really skinny kind, not the really fat kind — about the width of your pinky finger)
ingredients.name: medium-width asparagus (AKA not the really skinny kind, not the really fat kind — about the width of your pinky finger)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup basil leaves, finely chopped, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: basil leaves, finely chopped, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup dry white wine (or the juice of 1 small lemon - see notes)
ingredients.name: dry white wine (or the juice of 1 small lemon - see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (4 ounces) shredded white cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded white cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

In a heavy-bottomed ovenproof pot (see notes — you definitely own something that will work!), warm 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium-high heat. Cook 1 finely diced yellow onion for 4 minutes, then stir in 1 1/2 cups farro and 4 minced garlic cloves and cook for an additional minute, stirring frequently. Pour in 1 quart (4 cups) low-sodium chicken stock, stir, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, turn off the stove, cover the pot, and place it on the center rack of the oven (or on the bottom rack, if your pot is too tall). Bake for 30 minutes.

While it’s baking, trim 1 1/2 inches off the bottom of 1 pound asparagus to get rid of the hard, fibrous ends. Discard those ends. Cut the trimmed asparagus into bite-sized pieces, 1 1/2 to 2 inches long.

Remove the pot from the oven and carefully turn the lid upside down, so that the handle is pointing down into the pot. It’s OK if it touches the farro! It’s even OK if it touches the bottom of the pot. Add the cut asparagus to the top of the lid along with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper. Carefully toss to coat.
Return pot to the oven for an additional 10 minutes.

Remove the pot from the oven and carefully remove the lid. Place the pot over medium heat on the stovetop and stir in half of the roasted asparagus, 1 cup frozen peas, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup finely chopped basil leaves, 1/3 cup dry white wine, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 cup shredded white cheddar cheese, and 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until everything is saucy and combined and the farro is a risotto-like consistency, 3 to 5 minutes. If it gets too thick, add another splash of water. If it’s still thin, crank up the heat and just keep stirring!

We haven’t seasoned the farro at ALL yet because every brand of stock, cheddar, and Parmesan have different salt levels. So now, it’s time to taste and adjust the seasoning accordingly. I needed to add about 1/2 teaspoon of salt and several grinds of fresh black pepper. Keep tasting and seasoning until it’s perfect.
Throw the remaining asparagus on top, along with a big sprinkle of Parmesan, basil, and freshly ground black pepper. Make it pretty! Then devour it!

name: weeknight lowcountry boil
note:
This will be my first shrimp boil: FUN! So this is a peel-and-eat situation. You will peel the cooked shrimp right there at the table (just throw your shells and spent corn cobs in the empty bowl), then dunk your shrimp in the lemon butter and/or cocktail sauce. I love to dip in both! Some people just dip in cocktail sauce; others, just butter. Like I said in the intro, we always just dig in with our hands, but obviously you can use plates, forks, and knives if that’s more your style!

Leftovers are a good thing: store all components separately so everything doesn’t taste fishy. Go ahead and peel all of the shrimp, it’ll be much easier tonight with many hands than tomorrow when they’re cold and the shells are stuck. Make a shrimp and corn salad with mixed greens, peaches, goat cheese, almonds, red onion, avocado, and a simple vinaigrette. Potato salad. And just throw the extra kielbasa on a cheeseboard with a bowl of mustard for dunking.

Make ahead: Make your cocktail sauce days in advance in you want to! Store it in the fridge. You can also cut up your potatoes, shuck and cut your corn, and slice your sausages up to a day in advance if you’re looking to cut down on your prep time before dinner. To keep your potatoes from browning, store them in an airtight storage container that’s filled with water.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use store-bought cocktail sauce! The lemon butter takes almost no time to whip up but you could also just melt plain butter for dipping.

Cooking shrimp from frozen: Defrost them first if you have the time. If defrosted, you’ll throw them in the pot the same time you would fresh shrimp. If you forgot to defrost them, that’s OK! They’ll just take a couple minutes longer to cook. Totally still works.

What else can I add?? Green beans and broccoli are also great in a Lowcountry boil! Not at all traditional, but who cares! Add them 3 minutes after you add the corn.

Vegetarian: If you don’t eat meat or seafood, you could do a big veggie boil! Add the green beans and broccoli to the mix (see note just above for timing). You could also use plant-based sausage in lieu of the pork sausage.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use plant-based butter to make this meal dairy free. It’s already gluten free (but check your ketchup just to be sure!).

Need carbs: Make these cheddar Old Bay biscuits. For Calum’s birthday party I did a lobster boil and decided to make these biscuits at the last minute and they were the hugest hit!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of garlic, cut in half through the cloves
ingredients.name: of garlic
ingredients.note: cut in half through the cloves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds small potatoes (baby Dutch yellow or red potatoes are best — fingerlings can be a bit dry), halved
ingredients.name: small potatoes (baby Dutch yellow or red potatoes are best — fingerlings can be a bit dry)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound smoked pork sausage, such as kielbasa or andouille, cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: smoked pork sausage, such as kielbasa or andouille

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ears of corn, shucked, cut in half
ingredients.name: of corn, shucked

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds shrimp (preferably fresh, under 25 count and unpeeled, but peeled totally works and makes things easier for eaters — frozen also work if you don’t have access to fresh shrimp!)
ingredients.name: shrimp (preferably fresh, under 25 count and unpeeled, but peeled totally works and makes things easier for eaters — frozen also work if you don’t have access to fresh shrimp!)
Cocktail Sauce (or skip this recipe and just buy cocktail sauce from the store)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 tablespoons horseradish (depending how hot you like it!)
ingredients.name: horseradish (depending how hot you like it!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Dash of hot sauce (Tabasco is the go-to here but anything works)
ingredients.name: of hot sauce (Tabasco is the go-to here but anything works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: a few grinds of black pepper
ingredients.name: a few grinds of black pepper

preparationSteps: Grab your biggest pot (a stockpot, or the one you would use to cook pasta) and add about 4 quarts (16 cups) of water. While it’s coming to a boil over high heat, add 1/3 cup Old Bay seasoning, 1 quartered lemon, 1 halved garlic head (it’s totally fine if the skins are loose and peeling off!), and 3 tablespoons salt.

Place a colander in the sink. If you feel like being festive, line a large rimmed baking sheet (or just the center of your table!) with several layers of newspaper. Or just pull out a baking sheet and set aside.
Make your dipping sauces (AKA the cocktail sauce and lemon butter) while the water comes to a boil.

To make the cocktail sauce, stir together all ingredients (2/3 cup ketchup, 2 to 3 tablespoons horseradish, 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce, zest of 1/4 lemon, juice of 1/2 lemon, and a dash of hot sauce) in a small bowl. Refrigerate until you’re ready to eat.

To make the lemon butter, stir together all ingredients (melted 1/2 stick of unsalted butter, juice of 1/2 lemon, 1/8 teaspoon garlic powder, a few grinds of black pepper, and pinch of salt) in a small bowl. Leave at room temperature until you’re ready to eat. Just give it a stir at go-time.
Once the pot of water has come to a rolling boil, add 1 1/2 pounds halved potatoes, return to a boil, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add 1 pound cut up sausage and 4 halved ears of corn, return to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes.

Add 2 pounds shrimp and cook, stirring gently to ensure they all evenly touch the hot water, until they all turn pink, 1 to 3 minutes depending on their size. (If most shrimp look cooked through but a few still have grey areas, go ahead and drain them — those shrimp will finish cooking in the residual heat.)
Drain in the colander in the sink. Transfer to the rimmed baking sheet (or directly onto the newspaper-lined table!).

Place the baking sheet, dipping sauces (cocktail sauce and lemon butter), and a large empty bowl (for the shrimp shells) in the center of the table. Sprinkle everything with salt, rub a little butter onto those ears of corn (either some of your lemon butter or just some plain unsalted butter!), grab some napkins, and dig in*!!!
*If you’re new to Lowcountry boils, keep reading for more specifics!

name: one-pot cheesy rice and beans
note:
Must have meat: This dish is so filling and has plenty of protein for a meatless meal, but if you must have meat, throw 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts right on top. They’ll cook perfectly along with the rice. Then shred them up and stir them into the rice, or slice and serve over top. Or: Serve the beans and rice alongside any grilled meat (like I said — see last week’s email for the perfect grilled chicken recipe!), or as a side dish on taco night. Or, cook 1 pound of ground sausage or beef in the skillet first, then stir in the other ingredients and continue the recipe.

Gimme greens! Throw in a few handfuls of spinach, torn up a bit, when you stir in the cheese. (Have you noticed that that trick works for just about all of these one-pot meals?!)

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It’s gf as written! For dairy-free, swap your favorite melty vegan cheese in for the grated Mexican.

Leftovers are a good thing: This would be an easy dish to halve, but I highly recommend cooking as written and eating the rest for lunches, or freezing in quart-size Ziplocs.

Special ingredient: Have some leftover chipotle peppers en adobo from making flautas? Chop one up and stir it in. Remove seeds if you want to limit the heat but keep the smoky flavor. Leave them in for spice!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 cups low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: thinly sliced avocado, pickled red onions, chopped cilantro, sour cream, etc…
ingredients.name: Optional: thinly sliced avocado, pickled red onions, chopped cilantro, sour cream, etc…

preparationSteps: To a large heavy-bottomed pot or skillet, add everything but the cheese.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then stir it all together and reduce to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Uncover, turn off the heat, and give it a big stir. It’s OK if a little stuck to the bottom! Taste. Add salt if needed (this will depend on how salty your salsa and stock were).
Sprinkle 1 1/2 cups grated Mexican cheese over top. Cover the pot. Again, the pot is OFF the heat. Keep it covered for 10 minutes to allow the rice to steam and fluff up and the cheese to melt.
Dumpster dive for any yummy toppings (thinly sliced avocado, pickled red onions, chopped cilantro, and/or sour cream) and serve right away!

name: sausage stuffed zucchini
note:
Make ahead: You can make the sausage filling up to a day ahead, just rewarm it in a saucepan before you bake it in the zucchini.

Leftovers are a good thing: Don’t freeze the assembled zucchini “boats” — the zucchini will get mushy. But the filling would do great frozen! Just bag up however much you want to save in a Ziploc, store it in the freezer, and recreate this glorious meal sometime within the next four months. To do so, thaw the mixture in the fridge 24 hours before cook time, and assemble!

Vegetarian/vegan: Look for a vegetarian/vegan “sausage” or chorizo. If vegan, top the assembled zucchinis with your favorite dairy-free cheese (or just omit).

Gluten-free: Swap the couscous for cooked quinoa.

Yum, sausage. May I remind you of my Cheesy Shells alla Sausage Vodka from the WTC archives? Or my very summery One-Pot Sausage and Corn Pasta? This recipe only uses a half pound of sausage, so plan to make a half batch of one of these recipes to use the leftover sausage.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 pound ground sausage (links cut open, or bulk sausage)
ingredients.name: ground sausage (links cut open, or bulk sausage)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes (depending on how much spice you like)
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes (depending on how much spice you like)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cupcouscous(should NOT say “Israeli” couscous, which is a totally different round pasta product)
ingredients.name: cupcouscous(should NOT say “Israeli” couscous, which is a totally different round pasta product)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Warm a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook a 1/2 pound ground sausage, using a wooden spoon to break it up into tiny crumbles. When the sausage is almost cooked through, add 1 large minced shallot and 2 minced garlic cloves to the skillet and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.

Cut the heat down to medium-low and carefully (so that it doesn’t splatter you), stir in 1 can tomato sauce, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Simmer for 5 minutes. Taste. Add seasonings as needed based on taste. We preferred this spicy, so added a full teaspoon of red pepper flakes — but you do you!
Turn off the heat once the sauce is very thick and stir in in 1/4 cup couscous and 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese.
Use a spoon to scoop the guts out of the zucchini so that only about a 1/4 inch-thick shell remains.
Stuff the zucchini halves so that they are each heaping full of the sausage mixture. You should not have leftover filling. Seriously — shove it in there, overflowing on top if needed.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese. Bake for 30 minutes.
Chow down!
servings: Serves 2 to 4 (2 if this is the entire meal, 4 with a salad or other side dish)

name: jammy tomato feta rice with herby pork tenderloin
note:
Explain how we’re using the foil or baking sheet again? We’re covering the 9x12-inch baking dish with foil so that the rice can steam! And then we’re roasting the pork tenderloins on top of that foil to save you from having to use and wash an extra sheet pan. If you don’t have foil, you can use a rimmed sheet pan to cover your baking dish with instead and cook the pork on top of that sheet pan! Or, if you’ve already covered your baking dish with foil but then realize your foil’s too thin to hold the pork, keep that baking dish topped with foil (no need to waste it!) and just whip out a sheet pan to roast the pork on beside your foil-covered baking dish. You’ll have one extra pan to wash but no biggie. Bottom line: your baking dish needs to be covered with foil or a sheet pan or lid once you add the rice so that it can steam, and the pork tenderloins need to cook on something (whether that’s foil or a sheet pan on top of the baking dish, or a separate sheet pan).

Prep ahead: You can marinate the pork tenderloin up to a day ahead of time, stored covered in the fridge. You can also pre-slice and chop the vegetables and store them in the fridge in an airtight container.

A note on shallots: When I say “2 shallots” I mean 2 shallots that you’d pluck out of the bin at the store. One might have more than 1 bulb inside once you peel the skin off, but that still counts as “1 shallot.”

Halve it: If you’re cooking for one or two people and don’t want a ton of leftovers, you can easily halve this recipe. Pork tenderloins typically come packaged in a set of two — freeze the second one to use within 3 to 6 months! Or, use it to cook sheet-pan balsamic glazed pork with fennel and potatoes or one of the pork tenderloin recipes in the “loved this? try that!” section above the recipe sometime in the next few days.

Love your leftovers: This recipe makes a lot of pork. If you have leftovers, make pork tenderloin sandwiches! You can wing it and use whatever sandwich toppings you have on hand, or here’s an idea: fill a potato roll or ciabatta bread with sliced pork tenderloin, arugula or mixed greens, and caramelized onion and/or bell pepper. Melt some mozzarella on the top bun and add a slather of Dijon — or, if you used one, the sauce that you used for dinner. Or! Cube and make quesadillas with your leftover pork plus any veggies hanging out in your fridge. Or add it to a good bagged salad for lunch.

Vegetarian: Add a can of drained white beans (navy, Great Northern, chickpeas, cannellini) to the baking dish when you add the rice.

Gimme some greens: Stir some chopped spinach into the rice once it has steamed or add some fresh arugula drizzled with olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice to your plate.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Omit the feta or use vegan feta if avoiding dairy. It’s already gluten-free!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 fennel bulb, long stalks and root end trimmed off, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: fennel bulb, long stalks and root end trimmed off

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (1-pound each) pork tenderloins (NOT pork loin — that’s a different cut of meat!)
ingredients.name: pork tenderloins (NOT pork loin — that’s a different cut of meat!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons any combination of dried green herbs (such as oregano, dill, basil, parsley, herbs de Provence, etc.)
ingredients.name: any combination of dried green herbs (such as oregano, dill, basil, parsley, herbs de Provence, etc.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: chopped soft green herbs such as basil, dill, or parsley, or a store-bought sauce like pesto, if you're a sauce lover
ingredients.name: Optional: chopped soft green herbs such as basil, dill, or parsley, or a store-bought sauce like pesto, if you're a sauce lover

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Trim the tall stalks and root end off of 1 fennel bulb. Cut it in half through the root, then slice it thinly. Chop 2 shallots and smash 4 garlic cloves. Add it all, along with 2 pints cherry tomatoes, 1 (8-ounce) block of feta, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper to a 9x12-inch baking dish and toss to coat everything.
Roast for 45 to 55 minutes, until the tomatoes are collapsing and the fennel and shallots are tender and starting to brown.

As soon as you get the veggies in the oven, start marinating the pork. Toss 2 pork tenderloins in a large bowl with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 teaspoons dried green herbs, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper. Stir to combine then set aside to marinate at room temperature.
Remove the vegetables from the oven, then increase the oven heat to 425°F. While the oven temperature is rising, bring 2 1/2 cups water to a boil in a small pot.
Sprinkle 1 1/2 cups basmati rice over the veggies, then pour the boiling water over top. Cover the baking dish tightly with aluminum foil (or a baking sheet!).

Remove the pork tenderloins from the bowl of marinade and place them on top of the aluminum foil about an inch apart. If you’re using very thin foil and you're worried that it will rip under the weight of the pork, you can either double up the foil or just place the pork tenderloins on a separate baking sheet (putting them on top of the foil is just a fun little hack to save you from having to wash another dish! See notes if you’re confused).

The rice needs to roast for 25 minutes, but the pork will cook faster than that. Using a meat thermometer, start checking the pork’s internal temperature after 15 minutes — when it reaches 140°F internally, transfer it to a cutting board and cover it with aluminum foil while it rests and reaches 145°F (the safe temp to eat pork).
Remove the rice from the oven after 25 minutes but do not remove the foil for another 10 minutes (the rice will continue steaming and get fluffy and perfect as it sits under the foil).

After those 10 minutes, remove the foil and stir the rice to break up the tomatoes and feta and mix everything together. Taste. What's yours need? Everyone's will be different based on how acidic your tomatoes were, how salty your feta is, etc.! I needed to add more salt and a little pepper. You might need a splash of lemon juice or vinegar if your tomatoes were sweet versus acidic!

Slice the pork tenderloin and serve it over the rice. The middle pieces will be nice and pink internally and the end pieces will be more well done. Drizzle one of the sauces listed above over top, or simply garnish with fresh herbs.

name: lemony brown butter shrimp rolls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons finely minced fresh chives, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: finely minced fresh chives, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds uncooked peeled, deveined, tail-off shrimp (the bigger the better but anything works — see notes below if you’re working with frozen shrimp)
ingredients.name: uncooked peeled, deveined, tail-off shrimp (the bigger the better but anything works — see notes below if you’re working with frozen shrimp)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 big bag of salt and vinegar chips
ingredients.name: big bag of salt and vinegar chips

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 300°F.

Melt 8 tablespoons unsalted butter in your widest skillet (ideally a light-colored skillet such as stainless steel) over medium heat. Once it’s melted, use a pastry brush to brush 4 brioche hot dog buns inside and out with butter. Place them on a baking sheet and throw ‘em in the oven while the shrimp cooks. Set a timer to make sure you don’t leave them in there longer than 8 minutes.

To brown the butter, let it melt completely, then give it a nice vigorous stir every 30 seconds or so for 6 to 8 minutes. The butter will get foamy on top, and then once the foam subsides, that’s when the magic happens. The milk solids in the butter are going to sink to the bottom of the skillet and brown, giving the butter a nutty, almost caramel-y taste.
Once you start to see dark brown bits on the bottom of the skillet, you’re ready to continue.

While the butter is browning, we’ll do a bit of chopping. Mince enough chives to get a little over 3 tablespoons (a nice hefty little pile — no need to actually measure this!) and enough fresh dill to get 1 tablespoon. Keep the herbs separate from the shrimp you’re about to chop.

Roughly chop 1 1/2 pounds uncooked peeled and deveined shrimp. Just throw the shrimp in a pile on your cutting board and use a chef’s knife to chop it over and over again into small bits. You want to kind of rough the shrimp up to make them the texture of lobster meat — so you don’t always have to cut all the way through, just use the knife to scuff them up a bit to mimic the flaky texture of lobster claw meat.
Use a paper towel to pat the shrimp totally dry.

Zest 1 large lemon and 1 garlic clove directly into the skillet and continue cooking for 30 seconds. Add the chopped shrimp and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until the shrimp is opaque.

Turn off the heat and stir in the chives (leave a small amount for garnish) and dill. Use tongs to transfer the buttery shrimp to the toasted rolls. There will be a lot of butter left in the skillet — you can spoon a bit of this over your roll just before serving. Garnish each roll with a sprinkle of chives.
Serve IMMEDIATELY with salt and vinegar chips!
servings: Serves 4 (or 2, if you both want 2 rolls!)

name: greek turkey meatballs with couscous and dill yogurt sauce
note:
What’s couscous? Couscous is somewhere between a pasta and rice — it’s made from the grains of durum wheat. I absolutely love it as a quick and easy weeknight side. But be sure to get plain ole couscous — it’ll look like this — not Israeli couscous, which is a pasta and will not cook the same.

Make ahead: Do everything except the couscous ahead of time. Add the couscous, water, butter, etc., and bake to rewarm the meatballs and cook the couscous when you’re ready to eat.

Leftovers are a good thing: I highly recommend doubling the meatballs. My toddler, and many other toddlers, are obsessed with them. Freeze them, then reheat for 1 minute in the microwave when you need a quick protein. Toss leftover couscous with thinly sliced romaine, chopped up meatballs, lots of crunchy vegetables like cucumbers and bell peppers, and a red wine vinaigrette.

What to do when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy any frozen meatballs instead - beef meatballs work because they’ve already been cooked so they won’t be greasy. Follow the instructions the exact same, but skip the broiling step. Instead of making the dill sauce, buy tzatziki.

Vegetarian: Use a ground meat alternative.

Gluten-free: Omit the couscous and cook rice in a separate pot instead. You’ll need to bake your meatballs for 3 minutes longer since they won’t be baking  with the couscous. Use rice breadcrumbs or 1/3 cup almond meal instead of panko.

Dairy-free: Omit the feta. Use a coconut or almond milk yogurt for the sauce. Use dairy-free Parmesan such as VioLife. Use a plant-based butter.

Whole30: Double the zucchini, or add a red bell pepper into the mix as well. Omit the breadcrumbs. Use a dairy-free Parmesan. Use a coconut or almond yogurt for the sauce. Omit the couscous and serve over cauliflower rice or mashed cauliflower instead.

Neutral oils: As a reminder, grapeseed, avocado, and sunflower oils are my faves.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F. Place one oven rack on the center rung (for baking and roasting), and one on the top rung (for broiling).

In a 9x13-inch baking dish or a 12-inch ovenproof skillet (such as a cast iron), toss the 2 chopped zucchinis with 1 tablespoon neutral oil, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground pepper until evenly coated.
Roast zucchini for 7 minutes on the middle oven rack.
While it roasts, make the meatballs.

Crack 1 egg into a large bowl and whisk. Stir in 1 pound ground turkey (or chicken), 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 finely minced shallot, 2 grated garlic cloves, the zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), 3 tablespoons chopped fresh dill, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Stir it all to mix well, then use your hands to form 8 to 10 meatballs. No need to dirty up another plate here — just shove the meat to one half of the bowl and start forming and piling the meatballs on the other side.
Remove the zucchini from the oven and raise the oven temperature to broil (on high).

Stir the zucchini. (It will not be finished cooking yet and might be watery looking, etc. Don’t worry! It’ll get there). Place the meatballs on top. Drizzle some neutral oil over the meatballs, or spray them with cooking spray.
Slide the dish onto the top oven rack and broil the meatballs for 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly golden-brown on top. Reduce heat to 425°F and continue cooking for an additional 8 minutes.

Reduce heat to 375°F. Remove meatballs from the oven. Carefully pour 1 cup couscous between the meatballs, so that it’s all over the baking dish but not on top of the meatballs. Carefully pour 1 cup hot water (as hot as the sink will go) and the juice of 1 lemon over the couscous. Place 2 tablespoons of butter, cubed up, all over the top of the couscous. Season the couscous with 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Cover the pan tightly with a lid, baking sheet, or aluminum foil.
Bake for 5 minutes. Remove lid and fluff the couscous. Is it fluffy and tender and delicious? Good, you’re finished. Is it still a bit hard? Re-cover and keep cooking for a few more minutes.

Meanwhile, make the dill yogurt sauce. Combine 1 cup plain Greek yogurt, the juice of 1 lemon, 1 garlic clove (grated or minced), 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt in a small bowl. Stir and adjust seasoning to taste.
Use a fork to fluff and combine the couscous and melted butter and zucchini together all around and under the meatballs. Taste and add salt and pepper as needed.

Scatter 1/2 cup feta, a couple tablespoons of nuts, a few cranks of freshly ground black pepper, and a big handful of arugula over top.  Serve meatballs over top of the couscous with lots of dill yogurt sauce and toppings.

name: turkey cheddar meatloaf
note:
A Mediterranean meatloaf riff! Use feta instead of cheddar, chopped olives instead of onion, and throw in some minced sun-dried tomatoes. Try this if you’ve got these ingredients on hand instead or want to mix up the vibe of your meatloaf.

Make it into meatballs: Or cook the mixture in muffin tins!

Short on time: You can skip the step where you cook the onion and garlic IF you make sure to mince the onion very finely AND only use about 1/4 cup of uncooked onion and 2 minced garlic cloves (uncooked allium is much more pungent than cooked). Another time-saving option: You can use pre-grated/shredded cheese — although for the record I much prefer the cubes.

Vegetarian: Swap the turkey for ground Impossible meat.

Make ahead: You can prep ahead up to the step where you put the meat in the loaf pan, just store it tightly covered in the fridge for up to 24 hours in advance of cook time. If you don’t have a loaf pan, just store the prepped meat in a covered bowl and shape the meat into a loaf right before baking. You can also freeze meatloaf either before baking it or after it’s been cooked. Either way, you want to wrap it up super tightly in plastic wrap to prevent freezer burn. If you’re freezing before you cook it, you can actually line the loaf tin with plastic wrap before adding the meat. Pop it in the freezer for a bit to firm it up then pull it out, wrap it up real good, and freeze for up to three months. Either thaw in the fridge before cooking (bake at 375°F for 20 to 30 mins) or bake from frozen (although it can take up to twice as long — like up to 2 hours).

Leftovers are a good thing. Meatloaf sandwiches!!!!!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use your favorite df cheddar cheese and df butter. For gluten sensitivity, use gf breadcrumbs, rice breadcrumbs, or chopped stale gluten-free bread.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup breadcrumbs (you can use Panko or Italian breadcrumbs or just chop up old bread)
ingredients.name: breadcrumbs (you can use Panko or Italian breadcrumbs or just chop up old bread)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons milk (whatever you have — whole, almond, skim, anything)
ingredients.name: milk (whatever you have — whole, almond, skim, anything)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces sharp cheddar cheese, cut into cubes
ingredients.name: sharp cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons ketchup, divided (try to use a sugar-free brand like Sir Kensington’s or True Made)
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons ketchup, divided (try to use a sugar-free brand like Sir Kensington’s or True Made)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 to 6 small sweet potatoes, cut in half lengthwise
ingredients.name: small sweet potatoes

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 1/2 cup breadcrumbs and 2 tablespoons milk in a large bowl and squish the breadcrumbs into the milk so that they soak it all up for several minutes. Once they’ve absorbed all of the milk, use your fingers to mash the bread up.
Meanwhile, warm 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Cook 1 minced yellow onion and 4 minced garlic cloves for 4 to 5 minutes, until tender.

Add the cooked onion and garlic, 1 pound ground turkey, 1 large egg, 4 ounces cubed cheddar cheese, 1/3 cup ketchup, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon paprika, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder to the bowl and use your hands to get everything completely combined. If you used cubed bread, use your fingers to break the cubes apart so that it all evenly combines with the turkey meat.

Transfer the meat mixture to either a loaf pan OR directly onto the lined baking sheet and form the meat into a roughly 8x4-inch loaf shape. If using a loaf pan, place the pan on one side of the lined baking sheet. Spread the remaining 2 tablespoons ketchup over the meatloaf.
Place the halved sweet potatoes cut-side-down on the other side of the baking sheet. Poke the sweet potatoes all over with a fork. Rub the skin with oil.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a thermometer inserted into the center of the meatloaf reads 165°F.
When the meatloaf is ready, there will be a lot of liquid in the loaf pan or on the baking sheet. This is normal! Just drain it off and carry on.

Let the meatloaf rest while you make the mashed sweet potatoes. When the potatoes are cool enough to handle, peel the skins off and discard them. Add the potatoes to a large bowl along with 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper. Mash until smooth.
Cut a slice of meatloaf and serve it with mashed sweet potatoes. Garnish with chopped soft green herbs if you have them.

name: jerk chicken with coconut rice and strawberry salsa

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast tenders
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast tenders

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 tablespoons jerk, Cajun, Cavender’s Greek, blackening, or taco seasoning
ingredients.name: jerk, Cajun, Cavender’s Greek, blackening, or taco seasoning

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups short-grain white rice (such as sushi or arborio)
ingredients.name: short-grain white rice (such as sushi or arborio)

preparationSteps: Marinate the chicken: Toss 1 1/2 to 2 pounds chicken breast tenders in a bowl with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 1/2 tablespoons jerk seasoning, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt (but first, check your jerk seasoning — if it has salt in it, only use 3/4 teaspoon salt), and the juice of 1 lime. If you have time to marinate these ahead of time, throw them in the fridge for a few hours. If not, just set them aside at room temperature until you’re ready to grill.

Cook the coconut rice: Add 1 1/2 cups short-grain white rice, 1 can of coconut milk, 1 cup of water, 1 tablespoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt to a pot, stir, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low, cover, and simmer for 15 to 17 minutes, or until the rice is tender. Stir several times while cooking to make sure the coconut milk doesn’t scorch. Remove from the heat and let it sit, covered, until you’re ready to eat, at least 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork right before you serve.
Grill: Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400°F to 450°F). Non-grilling instructions are in the notes section below.

Peel 1 small red onion, then cut it into thick circular slices (try to keep them in whole slices as best you can — don’t intentionally separate them into individual rings). Add the slices and 1 jalapeño to a bowl and gently toss with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and a big pinch of salt.

Now that your grill is piping hot, use your grill brush to clean the grates, and use tongs to lightly oil them with a wadded up ball of paper towels that you’ve lightly coated with oil (I go into more detail on that process here if needed!).

Place the chicken, red onion slices, and jalapeño on the grill (and close it — always close it!). Note: Don’t wash the bowl that the onion and jalapeño were in! You’re going to make your salsa in there and any leftover oil is fine.

Now you’ve gotta pay close attention! Everything should cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, but we gotta keep an eye on things. Grill the salsa ingredients (AKA the red onion and jalapeño) until grill-marks appear, then flip and cook on the second side until gently charred. It doesn’t matter if the red onion falls apart, just do your best to not let too much fall through the grates. Use a meat thermometer to check your chicken’s internal temp — pull it off as soon as it hits 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a plate, and the onion and jalapeño back to the bowl.

While the chicken rests, make the salsa: Finely chop the grilled red onion and jalapeño (remove the jalapeño seeds if you don’t like things spicy!) and return them to the bowl you already used. Chop 8 ounces of strawberries (nothing needs to look perfect here — you can remove the stems from all of them, place them on the cutting board, and then just roughly chop through all of them at the same time!). Cut 1 avocado into small pieces, and roughly chop 10 sprigs fresh cilantro. Add it all to the bowl along with the juice of 1 lime, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, and a big pinch of salt. Toss to combine. Taste and season with more salt if desired. If your strawberries tasted bad, stir in a little honey or sugar!
Build a bowl (or plate!) with coconut rice, chicken (you might like chopping it first to make this really easy for people to eat without a knife!) and strawberry salsa.

name: happy bowls
note:
How many people does this serve? The veggies and sauce by itself could feed 4 people. If you add grains, greens, and extra toppings, you can stretch this meal to feed 6.

Meal prep/cooking for 1 or 2: I wouldn’t halve the veggies or sauce if you’re cooking for 1 or 2 people — it’s such a great meal prep recipe for the week! Make salads, serve it with meat, make more grain bowls, etc.

Love your leftovers: I eat leftovers of this meal for up to 5 days. It’s the perfect meal prep. The cashew sauce will stay good even longer, up to a full week. You can also freeze extra cashew sauce or cooked grains to use in future grain bowls. my meal-prepped veggies for the (half) week!

Prep ahead: Chop your vegetables up to a day ahead of time and store them raw in airtight containers in the fridge. Or, as I’ve said, prep the whole thing ahead of time!

Feeding kids: I like to serve this one family style Put all of the grains, veggies, sauces, and toppings on the table (even if that’s just putting the sheet-pans and cutting boards on the table!!) and let your kids serve themselves! They might only eat rice and avocado. But they might feel empowered to try new things since you’re giving them choices. It works really well in my house.

Vegetarian/dairy-free/gluten-free: This meal is already vegetarian and dairy-free. If you want it to be gluten free, opt for rice or another GF grain.

Must have meat: See the “add more protein” note above the recipe for ideas.

A note about oven temps: Remember that oven temperatures can sometimes vary a little — or a lot! If you smell any veggies crisping too much in the oven, lower the heat to closer to 400°F, or pull them out early. If you ever suspect that your oven’s temp might be off — maybe you’re consistently needing to cook meat longer than a recipe says to, or your roasted veggies are always getting charred — you can buy an in-oven thermometer to check, then adjust your cooking temp accordingly.

⚠️: If you’re new to beets, your poop may be red after eating them. You’re fine :)
