preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Add 2 cups of roasted cashews to a blender and cover with hot water (as hot as your sink will go). Set aside, so the cashews can soak and soften while we prep the veggies.

Scrub 1 extra large sweet potato and 1 large beet under running water until clean. Peel them if you aren’t into skins (I keep them on!), then chop into 1-inch cubes. Place on separate halves of one baking sheet.

Wash and dry 1 head of cauliflower. Slice it into thin florets like so: Cut off the leaves and the very bottom of the cauliflower stem. Now slice the head of cauliflower in half, through the stem. Place the two halves cut-side down, then slice them into 1/2-inch thick planks. Cut apart the individual florets. There will be little bits of cauliflower everywhere, that’s fine! Add them to the sheet pan too, they crisp up wonderfully.
Place the cauliflower on one side of the second baking sheet. Thinly slice 1 small red onion and add it to the other side of the baking sheet.

Drizzle all of the veggies with enough extra-virgin olive oil to lightly coat them. Sprinkle each sheet pan of veg with a big pinch of kosher salt, a smaller pinch of black pepper, and a couple shakes of garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika. Use your hands to toss and evenly coat the veg, keeping each in its separate section on the sheet pan.
Roast everything for 30 to 40 minutes, until golden-brown and fork-tender. The beets will be on the firmer side and the sweet potatoes will be more tender, that’s good! We want a variety of textures!
Meanwhile, cook your grains, wash and chop your greens if necessary, and make the cashew sauce.

To make the cashew sauce: Drain the water out of the blender. Add all of the other cashew sauce ingredients (1 cup of soft green herbs, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1/2 cup hot water, 1 small garlic clove, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt). Blend until completely smooth. If needed, add 1 tablespoon more warm water at a time until you achieve a thick, drizzle-able sauce. Taste and add more salt if desired.
Scoop some grains and greens into the bottom of your bowl. Add the roasted veggies. Drizzle a big scoop of sauce over top and add any other toppings you’re into. Dig in!!!!
servings: Serves 4-6 (see note below recipe for more info on this)

name: pasta e ceci aka “my cec”
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: In general, stews containing cooked pasta don’t retain their consistency very well when you freeze and thaw them, so you may want to plan on eating any leftovers for lunches or another dinner this week — or take your leftovers to a neighbor or friend! That said, you could definitely freeze in an airtight container (Ziploc or a plastic soup container) and reheat later, if a slightly mushy pasta consistency won’t bother you. It definitely doesn't bother me. The taste will hold!

Prep ahead: This one-pot meal comes together really quickly, but you could pre-cook the pancetta and/or pre-chop all your vegetables if you’re trying to cut the cook time down even more! Store them covered in the fridge. Or pre-cook the whole thing, store it in the fridge, and warm it up on the stove just before dinner.

Vegetarian: Simply skip the pancetta!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Skip the pecorino cheese to make it dairy-free. You can swap in a gluten-free pasta alternative like Banza (bonus: extra chickpea protein!) for the wheat noodles. The smaller the noodle the better, so opt for a shape like macaroni.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more (optional) for drizzling
ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more (optional) for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 can (15 ounces/430 g) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: chickpeas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 cups (210 g) roughly chopped escarole, dandelion greens, kale, spinach, or something else green and wiltable
ingredients.name: roughly chopped escarole, dandelion greens, kale, spinach, or something else green and wiltable

ingredients.rawIngredient: Freshly grated pecorino cheese, for serving

preparationSteps: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large stockpot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add 4 ounces of finely diced pancetta and cook until crispy and golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside on a paper towel–lined plate. Add 1 finely chopped medium yellow onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened but not taking on any color, 4 to 5 minutes. Add 3 finely chopped garlic cloves, 2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute more. Season well with salt and pepper.

Add 1 can diced tomatoes (juices drained) and 1 can chickpeas (drained and rinsed) and stir to combine. With a spatula or the back of a spoon, crush about 1/2 cup (90 g) of the chickpeas so they release some of their creamy texture into the sauce.

Pour in 3 cups of chicken stock and turn the heat to medium-high; when it comes to a boil, add 1 cup of ditalini noodles. Cook, stirring frequently to make sure the pasta is not sticking to the bottom of the pan, until the pasta is just short of al dente, about 8 minutes. Turn down the heat to medium.

Add 5 cups roughly chopped greens and the reserved pancetta to the pot and cook until the greens are wilted, 1 to 2 minutes more. The pasta will absorb most of the stock, so feel free to add in 1/2 to 1 cup (60 to 120 ml) of the remaining chicken stock if you prefer a brothier stew — it’s up to you. Ladle into bowls and top with freshly grated pecorino cheese and a drizzle of olive oil if you please.

name: cheesy polenta bowls with kielbasa and peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pork or beef kielbasa, cut into 1/2-inch thick slices on a diagonal
ingredients.name: pork or beef kielbasa
ingredients.note: cut into 1/2-inch thick slices on a diagonal

ingredients.name: A handful of fresh soft green herbs (such as basil, parsley, or dill)

preparationSteps: Place an oven rack on the second-to-top rung. Preheat your oven’s broiler to high.

Thinly slice 3 bell peppers and 1 red onion and toss onto your largest rimmed sheet pan. Cut 1 kielbasa into 1/2-inch thick slices on the diagonal, and add them to the sheet pan along with 1 pint of cherry tomatoes (leave them whole), 3 tablespoons oil, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1 1/2 teaspoons Greek seasoning.

Place under the broiler for 12 to 15 minutes, checking on things every couple of minutes to make sure nothing’s burning (this is very important! all broilers are different!). We are going for charred, not burnt. If things are starting to burn, move the sheet pan down a rung or two to get it away from the flame.

Meanwhile, cook your polenta! Bring 3 cups of water and 1 teaspoon salt to a boil in a medium-sized pot over high heat. Whisk in 1 cup polenta and reduce the heat to low. Cook, whisking occasionally, for 5 minutes (or per package instructions), until thickened. Stir in 4 ounces shredded Cheddar, 1 ounce grated Parm, and 1 tablespoon butter. If the polenta gets too thick, just stir in a splash of water or milk. I like my polenta quite thick — like loose mashed potatoes, not like soup — but do your thing.
Spoon the polenta into several bowls, add kielbasa, tomatoes, and peppers on top, and garnish with a handful of chopped soft green herbs and Parm! Enjoy!

name: one-skillet roasted chicken and peaches with pesto rice
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: This recipe makes a lot of rice, because you should ALWAYS have leftover rice! Especially leftover pesto rice! If you have no need for it in the next 3 days, freeze it for a quick side dish down the road.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Just cook the pesto rice on the stove (or stir pesto into that frozen rice that “cooks” in the microwave) and serve it alongside fresh peach slices, rotisserie chicken, fresh basil, and feta crumbles!

Prep ahead: Cook it earlier in the day, up until the point where you add the rice, chicken stock, etc. to the skillet. Refrigerate the skillet (covered) until you’re ready to cook, then proceed with the recipe.

Vegetarian: Crispy chickpeas instead of chicken! Or roasted portobello mushroom! You could cook the mushrooms right on top of the rice like the chicken.  Crispy tofu (cooked separately) would also be delightful as a protein.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Skip the cheese or use dairy-free feta crumbles to cut dairy. Double check that your stock doesn’t have gluten, if avoiding it!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds bone-in skin-on chicken thighs (be sure to get at least 1 thigh per person, 2 for eaters with bigger appetites!)
ingredients.name: bone-in skin-on chicken thighs (be sure to get at least 1 thigh per person, 2 for eaters with bigger appetites!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup crumbled feta or goat cheese
ingredients.name: crumbled feta or goat cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Warm an ovenproof skillet (or saucepan or even a pot!) over medium heat. I used a 12-inch cast iron skillet.
Season 2 pounds bone-in skin-on chicken thighs with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.

Place the chicken thighs skin-side down in the skillet. After 3 or 4 minutes, when chicken grease starts to pool up in the skillet, add 2 thinly sliced shallots and 4 thinly sliced garlic cloves around the chicken. Season with a pinch of salt. Use tongs to scooch them around to start sautéing them while the chicken cooks.
When the chicken skin is golden, flip it over and scooch it all to the outside rim of the skillet. If your skillet is totally full of chicken, remove one or two to make room to pour the rice in.

To the empty part of the skillet, pour in 1 1/2 cups white rice, 2 1/4 cups low-sodium chicken stock, 1/4 cup pesto, and the juice of 1 lemon. Use your tongs to evenly distribute the rice and liquid around the chicken. If you removed a chicken thigh, add it back to the skillet, smooshing it down into the rice and liquid.

Raise the stove heat to high to bring the stock to a boil, then turn off the heat. Place the peach slices over the rice, trying not to put them on top of the chicken so that the chicken skin can get nice and crispy.

Place the skillet on the center rack of the oven and roast for 25 to 30 minutes. Check your chicken and rice at the 25 minute mark. The chicken should be at least 160°F internally, and the rice should be tender (it might look hard on the surface where it was exposed to direct heat, so dig your spoon down in there to check!).
Garnish with 1/3 cup thinly sliced basil and 1/3 cup feta, and dig in!! Serve your chicken over pesto rice with lots of peaches, basil, and feta on top.

name: apple butter bourbon smash
preparationSteps: To make lemon sugar, zest 1 lemon into a small bowl. Add 1/2 cup sugar and, using your fingers, pinch the zest into the sugar until evenly mixed. Set aside.

In a large pitcher, combine the juice of 2 lemons, 3 cups apple cider, 1 1/2 cups bourbon, 1/3 cup orange liqueur, and 1/4 cup apple butter. Stir until the apple butter dissolves. Taste. Do you want it more tart? Use that third lemon to add more lemon juice!
Rim your glasses with the lemon sugar by running a cut lemon along the rim of the glass to wet it, then dipping it in the lemon sugar.
Fill the glasses with ice, then fill with bourbon smashes! If you have cinnamon sticks, stick one in each glass.

name: pear and blue cheese salad

ingredients.name: red pear (you can use 2 of either color pear if needed — apple or fuyu persimmon would also be great)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese (or feta or goat cheese!)
ingredients.name: crumbled blue cheese (or feta or goat cheese!)

preparationSteps: To make the dressing: Add 3/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of black pepper to a large jar and shake vigorously until thick and emulsified (AKA until the oil’s incorporated and everything’s well mixed). Taste and adjust as desired — too sweet? Add more oil. Not tart enough? More vinegar. Keep adjusting to make it your own.

To make the salad: Toss 5 ounces mixed greens in a large bowl. Thinly slice 1 green pear and 1 red pear, and chop 1 avocado and 1 cup candied nuts. Add the pears, nuts, avocado, and 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese (or more! do your thing!) to the bowl. Just before serving, season with kosher salt and black pepper and drizzle about 1/4 cup of the dressing over top. Toss to combine, and add more dressing as desired. With family-style salads like this, I like to dress them very lightly, then place the salad dressing with a spoon beside the bowl so that the dressing-heavy people (me) can add more.

name: perfect asparagus
preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Cut 1 1/2 inches off the bottom of the asparagus.

Toss the trimmed asparagus on a parchment-lined baking sheet with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder to evenly coat. Spread in a single layer and roast for 12 minutes.

Take a bite. If they’re almost perfectly crisp-tender, sprinkle 1/2 cup Parmesan over top and roast for another 3 minutes or until the cheese has melted. If they’re still tough, roast for another 3 minutes without the Parm, then proceed with the Parm step.
Serve immediately (but don’t worry if you can’t — it’s great at room temperature too!).

name: roasted boursin mashed potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks (peeled or unpeeled! I keep the peels on!)
ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.note: cut into 1-inch chunks (peeled or unpeeled! I keep the peels on!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5.2-ounce) container Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs
ingredients.name: Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 325°F.

Cut 4 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes into 1-inch chunks. Add them along with 3 cups whole milk, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper to a wide pot (like a braiser) or a baking dish (like a large Pyrex) — a pot is ideal though so that you can keep it warm on the stovetop later. The milk should mostly cover the potatoes — if it doesn't, add a little more.
Cover the pot/baking dish with a lid (if it doesn’t have a lid, you could use aluminum foil or a sheet pan as a lid instead).
Bake for 1 hour. Remove the cover, stir the potatoes, and add 1 container Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs right on top. Return to the oven to bake for 45 more minutes UNCOVERED.

Remove from the oven and mash!!! Ideally using a potato masher, but, if you’re like me and don’t own one, a wooden spoon will (slowly but surely) do the trick. Season to taste with more salt and pepper (you will probably want a lot more salt!). Sometimes I add a little (like 1/2 teaspoon) garlic powder, too! Sometimes I add some Parmesan! Get wild!
NOTE: If you’re avoiding dairy, Boursin makes a dairy-free version! And for a milk swap, I’d suggest extra-creamy unsweetened oat milk (unsweetened almond would be my second pick).

name: cider-braised roast

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 medium or 2 large yellow onions, sliced
ingredients.name: medium or 2 large yellow onions

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 325°F.

Place 1 boneless beef chuck roast in a baking dish (like a large Pyrex) or Dutch oven. Season generously with kosher salt and pepper (1 teaspoon salt per pound, 1/4 teaspoon pepper per pound. Thinly slice 2 large (or 3 medium) onions and place the onions all around the beef. Pour 1 cup apple cider around the beef.
Cover (with a lid or foil), and bake for 1 hour per pound of meat, rounding up to the nearest half hour. So, 4 hours for a 4-pound roast.
Let the meat rest with the lid off for 10 minutes.

Using two forks, shred the meat into large chunks — I like to serve people large chunks so that they can experience the tender shreddable moment themselves, versus a pile of fully shredded meat. If the roast isn’t shredding easily, cover it and put it back in the oven for 30 minutes. (Yes, cook it for longer if it’s not tender and shreddable yet!)
Serve the beef and onions over the mashed potatoes with asparagus on the side. Sprinkle the beef and potatoes with finely chopped parsley to give it some color and freshness.

name: peppermint chocolate pots de creme
note:
I’m just here for a weeknight meal: Skip the cocktail, apps, and dessert! Choose either the salad or asparagus to go with your meat-and-potatoes dinner. Halve the recipes if needed.

Asparagus shopping tip: Asparagus aren’t in season (but they’re a good hothouse veg so it’s fine — tomatoes are an example of a not-so-good hothouse veg), so you probably won’t have a ton of options, but we want to find asparagus that are about the width of a standard Sharpie. If you get the really skinny kind, only roast them for 5 minutes before adding the Parm. If you get the super fat guys, they’ll need closer to 20 minutes before adding the Parm.

My roast is less/more than 4 pounds, what do I do?! Use the “hour per pound” method and round up to the nearest half hour. AKA a 5.25-pound roast would cook for 5 and a half hours.

Make the roast in a slow cooker: Pat the meat dry and season as written. Add the thinly sliced onions to the bottom of the slow cooker’s pot, then set the roast on top. Pour the apple cider around the meat, cover, and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or on high for 5 to 6 hours, until it shreds very easily with a fork! If you take it out and it’s not shredding easily, cook it for another 30 minutes to an hour and check again!

Beef chuck roast shopping tip: Look for a nice fatty roast with lots of marbling (AKA white streaks running through it). A roast that is too lean (AKA all red meat, with not a lot of white streaks) will not break down and be delicious! Note: I am not a huge fan of grass-fed beef ever because I find it to be too lean, but especially here, I do not suggest grass fed!

Blue cheese shopping tip: If we were just making a salad as the meal, I’d make you buy a nice piece of blue cheese and cut it up yourself. Pre-crumbled is simply not as good. But we are doing A LOT with this menu, so pre-crumbled is gonna do the trick.

Love your leftovers:Mashed potatoes: OK, my new obsession after making 45 pounds of mashed potatoes while testing this recipe is turning mashed potatoes into potato soup!!!! Blend a big ole scoop of leftover mashed potatoes with just enough hot chicken stock to get a nice thick soup consistency. Taste and add salt, pepper, maybe some cheese, and blend again. Top with sour cream, bacon, cheddar, chives, etc., etc.Roast: With the leftover roast, we made tacos, quesadillas, but best of all, I made beef ragu by shredding about 3 cups of leftover beef really finely, and simmering it covered over low heat with two jars of Rao’s marinara, plus a little leftover heavy cream from Thanksgiving. Stir often so the bottom doesn’t burn. INSANELY GOOD. I served this to friends and they were absolutely obsessed. Toss with hot pasta (I tried it with orecchiette and spaghetti and we preferred the spaghetti!) and top with tons of Parm!!

Mashed potatoes: OK, my new obsession after making 45 pounds of mashed potatoes while testing this recipe is turning mashed potatoes into potato soup!!!! Blend a big ole scoop of leftover mashed potatoes with just enough hot chicken stock to get a nice thick soup consistency. Taste and add salt, pepper, maybe some cheese, and blend again. Top with sour cream, bacon, cheddar, chives, etc., etc.

Roast: With the leftover roast, we made tacos, quesadillas, but best of all, I made beef ragu by shredding about 3 cups of leftover beef really finely, and simmering it covered over low heat with two jars of Rao’s marinara, plus a little leftover heavy cream from Thanksgiving. Stir often so the bottom doesn’t burn. INSANELY GOOD. I served this to friends and they were absolutely obsessed. Toss with hot pasta (I tried it with orecchiette and spaghetti and we preferred the spaghetti!) and top with tons of Parm!!

Vegetarian: Swap the roast out for a delicious soft, slouchy mushroom main to serve atop the mashed potatoes. You could make my butter balsamic mushrooms (double it). Or, if you’re up for more of a project, Deb Perelman’s mushroom bourguignon would be fab. One other idea would be to move tortellini into the main meal. Cook two packs of it, toss with store-bought pesto (skip making the aioli), and serve with the rest of the meal.

Where are all of the substitutions?! We don’t do our extensive list of subs for these menus, instead we provide a full shopping list to help you avoid needing a last-minute sub! But see the individual recipes for some main-ingredient subs (and ways to cut dairy and gluten), and leave a comment if you have another specific substitution question!Leave a comment

preparationSteps: Blend 8 ounces (about 1 1/2 cups) semisweet or dark chocolate chips, 4 large room-temp eggs, 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract, 1/2 teaspoon mint extract, and a pinch of kosher salt until coarsely combined.
With the motor running on low speed, slowly pour in 2/3 cup very hot coffee. Blend until smooth.

preparationSteps: Start by getting your rice or grain cooking if you’re going to serve some with this meal. I personally would opt for white jasmine rice with some butter stirred in at the end. Cook the rice using the pasta-cooking method that we used here.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed half sheet pan with parchment paper.

Cut 1 pound cherry tomatoes in half. Add them to the baking sheet and toss with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Spread them out so that they’re not touching.
Roast for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim the woody ends off of 1 pound of asparagus (that means cutting usually an inch or two off the bottom) and get started on making the chimichurri.

To make the chimichurri, finely chop 1 cup parsley leaves and tender stems, thinly slice 1 serrano chili pepper (like paper-thin slices! If you can’t get them really, really thin, mince it instead), grate or mince 2 garlic cloves (I like to use my microplane to get them really fine), and zest and juice 1 lemon, adding all to a medium bowl. Stir in 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Taste. I like my chimichurri pretty acidic, so I typically add another splash of vinegar.

After they’ve cooked for 12 minutes, scooch the cherry tomatoes over to one side of the sheet pan (they can be piled on top of each other at this point) and add the trimmed asparagus to the other side. Toss to coat the asparagus with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and season with a big pinch of both salt and pepper.
Scooch things around to make room for 1 1/2 pounds skinless, boneless white fish filets. Season fish with a big pinch of salt, then drizzle a spoonful of chimichurri over each filet.

Roast for 12-ish minutes, until the fish flakes easily when poked at with a fork and the asparagus is crisp tender (go on — take a bite of one!). There will be a lot of liquid on the sheet-pan — don’t worry, that’s normal!
Scoop a bit of cooked rice onto each plate and top with fish. Spoon lots of tomatoes and their juices over the fish. Serve asparagus off to the side. Drizzle chimichurri over everything. Dig in!

preparationSteps: Cut 2 zucchini in half vertically, then into thin half-circle slices.

Warm 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil over medium-high heat in your largest skillet, then add the zucchini in as even a layer as possible. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden-brown, then stir. Do your best to flip them all over, but don’t stress over it! Spread them into an even layer again and cook until the second side is golden-brown, another 3 to 4 minutes. When they are browned all over, season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt.
While the zucchini is cooking, slice 2 chicken sausages into 1/4-inch thick rounds and halve 1 cup cherry tomatoes.
Scooch the cooked zucchini over to one side of the skillet, then reposition your skillet so that the zucchini is off the flame and the now-empty part of the skillet is centered.

name: slow-roasted pork butt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (6 to 8-pound) bone-in pork butt (AKA pork shoulder)
ingredients.name: bone-in pork butt (AKA pork shoulder)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 275°F.

Grab a rimmed baking sheet and cover it with aluminum foil. Place the pork butt on the baking sheet and pat it dry with a paper towel. Rub 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, and 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper all over it.

Place in the center of the oven and roast uncovered until the internal temperature reaches 195°F. If you don’t own a thermometer, stick a fork into the side of the pork and twist. It will meet very little resistance and easily shred the meat when ready. This will take anywhere from 4 to 8 hours depending on the size of your butt and the size of your oven. Once you hit 4 hours, check the internal temp every 30 minutes to avoid overcooking (but also don’t stress — it’s hard to F this one up).
Remove the pork and allow it to rest for 15 to 20 minutes, until it’s cool enough to handle.
Use two forks to shred the meat, mixing the crispy outside layer in with the inner juicy bits. Discard the bone and any big hunks of fat.
Enjoy immediately, and/or use the pork in one (or all!) of the three ideas below.

name: chop sandwiches (or chop plates!) //
note:
Make it in a slow cooker: You’ll prep the meat and coat it in the rub the same way as it’s written. Put the meat in your crockpot fat side up, cover, and cook it on low for 8 to 10 hours (preferred!) or on high for 5-6 hours. Check the temp on the low side of those ranges — you want it to heat to at least 195°F for pulled pork. Let it rest for 15 to 20 minutes (that will help lock in the juices and make it cool enough to handle) then shred it!

Vegetarian: Obviously the pork butt is the star of the show this week. BUT there are some delicious plant-based swaps you can make within each of these sub recipes! For the noodle bowls, I’d opt for crispy tofu. Click here for a how-to. For the carnitas tacos: shredded chanterelles, porcini, or shiitake mushrooms would be delicious and similar to pork carnitas texture-wise. For the BBQ sandwiches, try thinly sliced pan-fried seitan!

Leftovers are a great thing: Freeze any meat that you don’t plan to eat within three to four days. Store it in airtight Ziploc bags — whatever serving size works best for you and your fam. My favorite way to freeze food? Put the meat in the bag and lay it flat on a small sheet pan (one that will fit in your freezer). Pop it in the freezer until frozen, then store the bag flat or up and down.

How to reheat your pork! Whether you’re re-heating it from the fridge or the freezer, the best way to do so is in the oven. The goal is to NOT dry out your meat after you put all that time into cooking it low and slow the first go round! So put the pork in an oven-save dish and add a bit of water (or broth or even apple juice) to add back some of the moisture it will have lost. Cover the dish with foil and bake it at 300°F for about 20-30 minutes, or until the meat reaches 165°F. You could also use the same approach on the stovetop, heating it over low or medium-low.

DF/GF: To omit dairy, leave the cheese off your tacos or swap it for a plant-based alternative. To avoid gluten: Use corn tortillas for the tacos and gluten-free buns for the sandwiches (or opt for the chop plate).

There are so many other ways to serve this pork butt!!!! Ideas include: Cubano sandwiches, pork buns, pork chili verde, cheesy pork sliders, bo ssam lettuce wraps, breakfast sandos, pork and beans, pork and pineapple fried rice, burritos, pork n grits, pork buns… what’d I miss!?

To make the coleslaw: In a separate large bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 2 teaspoons hot sauce, and a big pinch of salt. name: 30-minute pork lettuce wraps with coconut rice and sauces
note:
Vegetarian: you’re gonna make scrambled tofu using all of these ingredients! Skip the marinating step, but add the salt and sugar in while scrambling. Use a firm block of tofu and do it over high heat just like the pork!

Gluten-free: be sure to use a gluten-free soy sauce as tamari or coconut aminos.

Dairy-free: omit the butter, or use a DF one.

What to do when you really don’t feel like cooking: buy a pre-marinated teriyaki or otherwise Asian-flavored pork tenderloin or chicken thighs, have the butcher cube it up, and just saute it in oil and add the butter at the end. Buy premade sriracha mayo. Throw the full scallions and ginger slices in the blender and pulse until still chunky but chopped up. Buy frozen cooked rice.

Double it: to double the meat — use two skillets so that you don’t overcrowd it and make it steamy instead of browned. To double the rice — 3 cups rice, 2 cans coconut milk, but only 1 cup water.

Whole30: ditch the rice completely. If you want to make coconut cauliflower rice, do it. Omit the butter.

Make ahead: marinate the meat and make your serving board with the sauces and toppings and lettuce leaves entirely ahead of time. Just throw that whole board right in the fridge. Cook the rice ahead of time too, refrigerate it right in the pot, add a splash of water and reheat by steaming it over low heat. Cook the pork right when it’s go time.

Leftovers are a good thing: saute several cups of vegetables such as mushrooms and bell peppers in a bit of oil over high heat until tender. Stir in the rice, leftover pork, and ginger-scallion sauce. Drizzle sriracha-mayo over top.

Feeding kids: wraps and taco-y things don’t quite work out for my two-year-old, so to feed this meal to him I made “rice pancakes” by combining about 1 cup of rice with 1 large egg and a couple tablespoons of flour to bind it all together into a pancake-y consistency. Cook like pancakes! He loved the pork, rice pancakes, and sriracha mayo.

preparationSteps: Cut 1 pound pork tenderloin up into 1/2-inch cubes. That’s about the size of your thumbnail. To do this: cut the tenderloin in half lengthwise, then cut each of those halves in half. So at this point, you have four long strips of tenderloin. Now cut each of those strips into 1/2-inch cubes. Right on the cutting board, season the pork with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and 1 tablespoon brown sugar. Toss to coat, then set aside at room temperature while you work on the rice and sauces.

To make the rice: combine 1 1/2 cups white rice (no, you don’t need to rinse it), 1 can coconut milk, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to the lowest heat possible on your stovetop and cover for 15 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and leave covered to allow the rice to steam until you’re ready to eat (at least 5 minutes but up to 1 hour).

To make the ginger scallion sauce: thinly slice the white and light green part of 4 scallions. Like, as thin as possible. Paper thin! Now slice the dark green part of the scallions on the bias (check out the photo), also super thin. Add the light green and white parts to a bowl. The dark green parts are for garnish — set them on the platter. Dice 1/4 cup pickled ginger. Add it to the bowl. Stir in 2 tablespoons neutral oil, 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce until well combined, then set the bowl on the platter. Place a little handful of pickled ginger on the platter before you put it away too.
Now’s a good time to start heating up your skillet. By the time you finish making the sriracha mayo, it’ll be hot enough to cook on. It needs to preheat for at least 4 minutes!

To make the sriracha mayo: stir together 1/3 cup mayo, the juice of 1/2 a lime, 1 tablespoon sriracha, and 1/2 teaspoon soy sauce. Taste. Can you go spicier? Do it! Too spicy? Add more mayo! Set the sriracha mayo and the sriracha bottle on the platter.

Pull the lettuce leaves apart carefully to create your lettuce cups. I like to trim the root off, pull the leaves off, trim more root off, pull the leaves off, and so on. Place on the platter. Place the platter and the rice on the dinner table — it’s almost show time!
Now your skillet should be nice and hot. Are you seeing little wisps of smoke come off the sides? Good, we’re ready to cook! Pat the pork completely dry using a paper towel.

Add 2 tablespoons of neutral oil to the skillet (which, yes, is still on HIGH heat!) and swirl to coat the pan. Add the pork in an even layer and allow it to brown completely through, until only the very top of each piece of pork is still pink, 4 to 6 minutes.

name: eastern north carolina style glazed ribs
note:
How do I test ribs for doneness: The meat should pull back from the bone ends by about 1/4 inch, a toothpick (or fork) should slide into the meat between the bones easily, and the internal temperature of the meat should reach between 195 and 203°F.

I wanna grill! If you’d rather finish your ribs on the grill, you can do that instead of the 450°F oven! Throw them meat-side down on the grill over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, until caramelized. But if you’re cooking the smashed potatoes, you may as well use the oven so you can roast them at the same time.

Prep ahead: Find tips for this in the “prep-ahead game plan” section above the recipe.

Love your leftovers: Leftover ribs will be great for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. For best reheating results, let them come to room temp, brush them with any leftover sauce, wrap them in foil, and bake at 250°F for about 10 to 15 minutes or just until warmed through.

Feeding kids: Omit the cayenne and halve the red pepper flakes if your kids are spice averse kids! My kids love these!

Vegetarian: Make tofu “ribs.” Freeze 2 blocks of extra firm tofu (I know that sounds random bit it helps with texture). Press the block(s) to remove any excess moisture then slice them into rectangular “ribs” 3/4- to 1-inch thick. Coat them in dry rub and let them sit in the fridge for up to 8 hours. Brush them with the sauce then bake at 275°F for 45 minutes. Raise the temp, brush again, and bake for 10 minutes or so, until a golden crust forms.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: The ribs are dairy-free as is. For gluten-free, double check that the ketchup you buy is GF.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (3- to 4-pound) racks baby back ribs or spare ribs
ingredients.name: racks baby back ribs or spare ribs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes (halve this if spice-averse)
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes (halve this if spice-averse)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper (omit this if spice-averse)
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper (omit this if spice-averse)

preparationSteps: Place 2 (3- to 4-pound) racks of baby back ribs on a foil-lined baking sheet (it’s OK if they overlap a little bit) and remove the membrane from the ribs. The membrane is the thin, silvery-white layer on the bone side. Use a knife to loosen one corner, then grab it with a paper towel or clean dish towel (this is important for keeping your grip!) and pull it off completely. It will probably come off in multiple pieces rather than one big piece (like mine did in this video). That’s normal, keep going!

Make the dry rub: Mix all rub ingredients (1/4 cup light brown sugar, 1 heaping tablespoon kosher salt, 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons garlic powder, and 2 teaspoons onion powder) together in a bowl. I honestly just eyeball all of these measurements and dump them straight onto the ribs — you really can’t mess it up.

Pat the ribs dry and coat in dry rub, massaging it in. Place them meat-side up and let them sit at room temperature for 30 minutes, or overnight in the refrigerator, uncovered, if you’ve got the time.

Make the vinegar sauce: Stir all the ingredients (1 cup apple cider vinegar, 2 tablespoons ketchup, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper) together in a small pot. Bring it to a boil, then reduce to a simmer over medium-low heat and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until thickened. Remove from heat and set aside.
Preheat oven to 275°F.

Remove the ribs from the refrigerator (if they were in there). Wrap each rack of ribs tightly with foil, set them on the baking sheet, and place the baking sheet in the oven. Bake spare ribs for 3 hours and baby back ribs for 2 hours.

Remove the ribs from the oven and carefully open the foil (watch out for hot steam!). A paring knife should slide in and out of the meat between the bones easily — if it doesn’t, re-wrap them and cook for 30 more minutes, or until it does.

Increase the oven temperature to 450°F. Remove the top layer of foil and brush the ribs generously with vinegar sauce. If there’s a lot of liquid on your pan, pour it off, then use a clean dish towel or paper towel to dry it off (if you don’t, the foil will burn). Return to the oven, UNCOVERED, for 10 to 15 minutes, until edges are caramelized and slightly charred. Remove from oven and brush with more sauce. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Cut between bones and serve immediately with extra vinegar sauce on the side (and the potatoes and tangy slaw, if making).

name: ranch butter smashed potatoes
note:
I’m cooking these with the ribs: Add the smashed ranch butter potatoes to the oven when you raise the temp to 450°F and return the ribs for their final sear. The ribs will finish first — keep the potatoes in for another 5 or 10 minutes until they are golden brown and crispy.

Don't skip the boiling step: This ensures that the potatoes are creamy inside before getting crispy outside. I tried to slow-roast them in the oven with the ribs and it simply wasn’t as delicious.

More smashing = more crispy: Really press them down for maximum surface area and crispy edges!

Gluten-free: Most ranch seasoning packets are GF but double check! If needed, make your own (recipe in the subs section).

Dairy-free: These are delicious DF! Use plant-based butter or olive oil instead of regular butter. Use DF Parm or nutritional yeast instead of regular Parm. And use the DIY ranch seasoning blend below.

Prep ahead/love your leftovers: Keep leftovers stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. They reheat beautifully in a 450°F oven, they get crispy all over again!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds small Yukon Gold or baby potatoes
ingredients.name: small Yukon Gold or baby potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (to add to the boiling water)
ingredients.name: kosher salt (to add to the boiling water)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup grated (ideally freshly grated) Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: grated (ideally freshly grated) Parmesan cheese

preparationSteps: Place 2 pounds small Yukon Gold or baby potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water. Add 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Bring to a boil and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until fork-tender (AKA, until a fork easily slips in and out). Drain and let cool for 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450°F (same temperature as the final rib sear, if you’re making the recipe above!).

Place the potatoes on a large baking sheet. Place another baking sheet on top and smash down until the potatoes are about 1/2 inch thick. Don't worry if they break apart — those tiny bits are a part of the magic. If you don’t have another baking sheet, you can use a potato masher or large fork to do this instead.

Melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter in the microwave (in a microwave-safe bowl) in 20-second increments, stirring in between. Once melted, stir in 1 packet (1 ounce) ranch dressing mix. Drizzle the ranch butter over the smashed potatoes, making sure to get it into all those crispy edges.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until edges are golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven and immediately sprinkle with 1/4 cup chopped fresh chives, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and a big pinch of flaky sea salt. Serve immediately.

name: tangy slaw
note:
Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good for up to 4 days stored in the fridge in an airtight container.

Save time: Skip this recipe and buy store-bought slaw. Or skip the slaw entirely!

Dairy-free/gluten-free/vegetarian: Already is. If you want to make it vegan, use vegan mayo.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons vinegar sauce (reserved from the ribs recipe above)
ingredients.name: vinegar sauce (reserved from the ribs recipe above)

preparationSteps: Add 14 ounces coleslaw and a pinch of kosher salt to a large bowl and massage to soften the cabbage slightly. Stir in 2 tablespoons mayonnaise and 2 tablespoons vinegar sauce. Adjust seasoning to taste. Want it tangier? Add a splash of apple cider vinegar!
Cover and refrigerate until you’re ready to eat.

name: cookout chicken
preparationSteps: To marinate the chicken: In a large bowl or Ziploc, combine 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/3 cup orange juice, 1/4 cup olive oil, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon chili powder. Add 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs and 1 1/2 pounds drumsticks to the marinade and toss to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator (covered) for at least 4 hours or ideally overnight.

To bake the chicken: Shake off the marinade (BUT KEEP IT!) and place the pieces of chicken on a foil- or parchment-lined baking sheet. Roast in a 400°F oven for 30 to 40 minutes, until the chicken is 160°F internally. If you’re also making the corn, add it to the oven for the final 20 minutes of baking time.

To grill the chicken: Prepare a grill for medium heat (about 350°F). Shake off as much marinade as possible (BUT KEEP IT!) and place the pieces of chicken on the grill. There might be some flare-ups (flames caused by the marinade dripping down), but it’s no big deal! If there’s a flare-up that won’t go out, just move the chicken away from it so that it doesn’t burn. The flare-up will burn out soon. Close the lid and cook for 7 minutes, then flip, close the lid, and cook for another 7 minutes. Using a meat thermometer, make sure the internal temperature has reached 160°F (mine had after those 14 minutes, but all grills are a little different!). Depending on your grill, you might also want to crank the heat up to medium-high at this point to get the outside nice and crispy (I did not need to do this on my grill — it was already crispy!). If so, cook it for 2 minutes per side with the lid closed. If you are also making the corn, add it to the grill when you add the chicken, and roll it around every few minutes to cook all sides.

To make a sauce: This is extra credit! You do not have to do this, the chicken is so good without this step, but it makes it extra saucy! While the chicken is baking or grilling, pour the marinade into a small pot and boil over high heat for 5 to 8 minutes, until it is thick, reduced by half, and looks like maple syrup. Let it cool for a few minutes, then pour it all over the chicken.

name: mexican corn

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup crumbled cotija, feta, or Parm
ingredients.name: crumbled cotija, feta, or Parm

preparationSteps: To bake the corn: Place the corn on a baking sheet, rub all over with olive oil or cooking spray, and roast in a 400°F oven for 20 minutes.
To grill the corn: Rub the shucked corn all over with olive oil or cooking spray. Grill the corn over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until charred all over.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl (ideally what you’ll be serving this dish in), stir together 1/4 cup mayonnaise, the juice of 1 1/2 limes (about 3 tablespoons), 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 3/4 cup crumbled cotija, and 1/4 to 1/2 cup (depending on how much you love cilantro!) finely chopped cilantro.

When the corn is cool enough to handle, cut it off the cob (see notes for a tip on this) and toss it into the bowl of dressing. Sprinkle the corn with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and toss to combine. Taste. You might need more salt depending on how salty your mayo and cheese were (I needed another very big pinch). Garnish with any leftover cotija, cilantro, and a sprinkle of smoked paprika.

name: grilled turkey and zucchini burgers with miso mayo
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. Buy pre-made burger patties and spice them up with the miso mayo sauce. And/or skip the salad and just serve your burgers alongside some good old fashion cubed watermelon.

I don’t have a grill. You can cook your burgers on a grill pan or skillet, or in the oven. If using a skillet: Preheat it for 2 minutes, add some neutral cooking oil, swirl it, then cook your patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until they reach an internal temp of 165°F. To bake them, preheat the oven to 450°F and bake for roughly 10 minutes, or as long as needed until they reach that safe internal temp. Quickly cook your muffin buns by spraying the cut sides with cooking spray and placing them cut-side up on a baking sheet. Broil them for 1 to 2 minutes, watching to ensure they don’t burn.

Special ingredients: First, let’s talk miso. If you haven’t cooked with it yet, you’re in for a TREAT. Miso is a fermented Japanese seasoning that’s salty, sweet, and savory all at once — just a tablespoon of it packs a TON of flavor. Once you buy it (it’s typically in the refrigerated produce section), you can cook my sheet-pan miso-ginger salmon (one of my most popular WTC recipes yet — it’s converted tons of salmon skeptics!) and my miso-coconut chicken with crispy shallots and ginger rice. Now that you love miso, let’s discuss balsamic. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: There’s just not another vinegar out there like balsamic. It’s sweet and tangy and thick — perfect for marinades and dressings. If you made my sheet-pan balsamic glazed pork with fennel and potatoes last month, it’s in your pantry! If not… add it to the menu for the week.

Make ahead: Form the patties and refrigerate them, covered, on the baking sheet for up to 48 hours. Same for the salad. Miso mayo can be made up to a week in advance.

Vegetarian/vegan: Use 1 pound of Impossible Burger or another plant-based meat. For vegan, also use vegan mayo in lieu of regular, swap the egg yolk for a flex egg (see subs below), and skip the feta.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Df — skip the feta. Gf — buy gluten-free bread crumbs and use lettuce leaves (or gf bread) instead of the English muffin.

Leftovers are a good thing: Oh ya, you can freeze these! They’ll be good in the freezer for up to 3 months. Go ahead and cook them, then, once cool, freeze them wrapped in plastic wrap and/or in airtight bags. Thaw in the fridge just a few hours before cooking, or grill them from frozen. You could also reheat them once thawed on the stovetop, in the oven, or in the microwave until warmed through.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Lettuce greens, tomato, onion — whatever burger toppings you have on hand and are into
ingredients.name: Lettuce greens, tomato, onion — whatever burger toppings you have on hand and are into

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon vinegar (preferably balsamic) or lemon/lime juice
ingredients.name: vinegar (preferably balsamic) or lemon/lime juice

preparationSteps: Lay a clean thin dish towel (or two paper towels) down on a cutting board. Place a cheese grater over top and grate 2 cups of zucchini onto the towel. Over a sink, squeeze out as much moisture as possible. Add the grated zucchini to a large bowl.
Slice any remaining zucchini into planks, toss with a bit of oil and salt and throw it on your grill alongside the burgers!

To the bowl, add 1 pound ground turkey, the zest of 1 large lemon, 1/3 cup breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup chopped basil or mint, 1 large egg yolk, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Use your hands to combine the meat mixture together, then divide it into 4 equal pieces and create 4 patties that are slightly larger than an English muffin.

Place the patties on a parchment-lined baking sheet (or plate) and freeze for 20 minutes or refrigerate for up to 48 hours. This is crucial if you’re grilling them. If you want to cook them in a skillet, you can cook them immediately.

Make the miso mayo up to one week in advance by stirring together 1/2 cup mayo, 1 tablespoon miso, and about 1 tablespoon lemon juice. The miso might clump up — just smash it against the sides of the bowl until it combines.

Just before grilling, toss together 3 cups cubed watermelon, 1/2 cup crumbled feta, 1/4 cup chopped basil or mint (mint is the more commonly used herb here but both are delish!), and 1 tablespoon of vinegar or lemon juice.
When it’s 20 minutes from dinner time, preheat an outdoor grill to 500°F.

SPRAY THE PATTIES ALL OVER WITH COOKING SPRAY! This is crucial to the success of these burgers. Grill for 4 minutes per side (or until they reach an internal temperature of 165°F). After you flip them, spray the insides of the English muffins with cooking spray and add them, cut-side down, and grill until toasted, about 1 minute.
Slather the English muffins with mayo, throw the burgers on top, and top them with whatever burger toppings you’re into! I just like greens on mine, but my mom loved hers with a fresh summer tomato!

name: honey soy glazed cod
note:
Prep ahead: This meal comes together very quickly and, as you’ll notice, is a no-chop situation. If you’re looking to simplify the cooking process even more, you could cook the rice earlier in the day (or even the day before) and reheat it just before dinnertime. You could also sort through your bagged kale to pull out the hard stalks, which can sometimes be a bit tedious.

We’re not a fish fam: Are you SURE?? If so — cool, see the subs section for alternatives.

Love your leftovers: Cooking for 1 or 2? Halve it! Fish leftovers are a no-go for me, so I wouldn’t recommend intentionally cooking more than you think you’ll eat. That said, cooked fish is safe to store in the fridge for up to 3 days. If you like leftover fish (to each their own!!), here’s how to reheat it: Wrap the leftover filet — along with a few spoonfuls of the sauce — in foil and bake it at 275°F for about 15 minutes. If you have leftover rice, you could use it for another meal this week (like sriracha shrimp sushi bowls or bacon kimchi fried rice), or an empty-the-fridge lunch bowl (any leftover kale and/or sauce would be delish on that too!). Rice stays good in the fridge for up to 4 days. You can also freeze it in Ziplocs.

Vegetarian: Swap the fish out for tofu! You can cook the tofu just like we do the fish. Buy a cube of extra firm tofu, drain it, and slice it into large rectangles. Add it to the sauce and let it cook for 10-15 minutes, or until totally heated through.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use df butter. To make it gluten-free, use tamari or coconut aminos in lieu of soy sauce.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 garlic clove, peeled (we’ll grate it right into the saucepan!)
ingredients.name: garlic clove, peeled (we’ll grate it right into the saucepan!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups sushi rice, rinsed (you can use any white rice here — and yes, brown also works, see the notes below the recipe)
ingredients.name: sushi rice, rinsed (you can use any white rice here — and yes, brown also works, see the notes below the recipe)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 (6ish-ounce) cod filets (or 2 larger filets — you can cut them in half!), ideally skin off but skin on is totally fine too
ingredients.name: cod filets (or 2 larger filets — you can cut them in half!), ideally skin off but skin on is totally fine too

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10- to 12-ounce) bag chopped kale (discard the big tough stems!)
ingredients.name: chopped kale (discard the big tough stems!)

preparationSteps: Melt 1 tablespoon unsalted butter in a small saucepan or rice pot over medium heat. Using a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater, grate 1 peeled garlic clove into the butter and sauté for a few minutes, until fragrant. Stir in 1 1/2 cups rinsed sushi rice, 1 3/4 cups water, and 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer and cover. Cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat but leave the pot covered for at least an additional 10 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, cook the fish!

Pour 1 tablespoon oil into your largest skillet (keep the heat off). Using a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater, grate 4 peeled garlic cloves into the skillet. Cut a 2-inch piece of ginger off of the ginger root then use a spoon to scrape off the skin. Grate the ginger into the skillet. Note: Ginger can be very tough and fibrous on the inside. If yours is, just grate as much as possible, then throw away the stringy bits! Don’t wash your microplane/grater yet — you will need it once more.
Turn the heat on to medium and sauté the garlic and ginger, stirring often, for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.

Stir in 1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 3 tablespoons honey, 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, the zest of 1/2 of the lime (using the microplane), and the juice of 1/2 of the lime. Cut the second 1/2 of the lime into 4 wedges and set aside for serving.

Bring the sauce to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the bubbles start to get bigger and slower, and the sauce starts to look a bit like caramel.
While the sauce is simmering, season 4 fish filets lightly with salt and pepper.
Once the sauce has thickened, add the filets to the skillet. Cook over medium-low for 5 minutes, then carefully flip and cook for another 4 minutes.
Spoon your desired amount of rice into each bowl/plate. (A 1/3-cup scoop is perfect in my opinion, hence the tip above!)
Top with the cooked fish.
Add the entire bag of chopped kale to the skillet and crank the heat up to medium-high. Sauté until very tender, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the kale to your bowls/plates, spoon some extra sauce over the fish, garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds, add a lime wedge to each bowl for spritzing, and dig in immediately!

name: sheet-pan poblano steak fajitas
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use a taco seasoning packet instead of all of those spices. And/or if you’re one of my TJ’s shoppers, you can use their carne asada for the steak. It’s great here — use it the exact same way, it’ll just be even more flavorful. To save time you could also skip the avocado smash and just slice up an avocado and squeeze some lime juice on top of your fajitas.

Leftovers are a good thing. See the section in my intro!

Make ahead: You can definitely let the steak and vegetables marinate in the fridge up to a day ahead of time. Slice the veggies then mix them and the steak up with the oil and spices. Transfer all into a gallon Ziploc (or two if needed), remove the air from inside and seal, then stick in the fridge.

Vegetarian: Use portobello mushrooms! Slice the caps so they’re the same thickness as the peppers, cooking for the full time. Alternatively, you can throw a can or two of rinsed and drained black or pinto beans onto the sheet-pan once the veggies are finished roasting. The seasonings will spread over the beans, and the cooked veggies will warm them. If they’re not warm enough after sitting with the veggies for a bit, pop the sheet-pans back into the oven until the beans are warmed through.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: For dairy intolerance, just skip sour cream as a topping (or use a df version); otherwise, you’re all set. Gluten-free, opt for flour tortillas.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds skirt or flank steak (keep it whole)
ingredients.name: skirt or flank steak (keep it whole)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced (to be about the width of a pencil)
ingredients.name: red bell pepper, thinly sliced (to be about the width of a pencil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon cayenne (omit if very spice averse)
ingredients.name: cayenne (omit if very spice averse)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large avocado (or 2 if your fam will eat a lot)
ingredients.name: large avocado (or 2 if your fam will eat a lot)

ingredients.rawIngredient: For serving: flour and/or corn tortillas, sour cream, hot sauce, salsa
ingredients.name: For serving: flour and/or corn tortillas, sour cream, hot sauce, salsa

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line one full rimmed sheet-pan or two half rimmed sheet-pans with aluminum foil (if desired — you can also just cook straight on the pan).

Toss 1 1/2 pounds skirt steak, the thinly sliced red, orange, and poblano peppers, a thinly sliced onion, 3 tablespoons cooking oil, 2 teaspoons chili powder, 2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon cayenne on ONE of the baking sheets until everything is evenly coated in oil and spices. Add another tablespoon of oil if needed to nicely coat everything. Toss with your hands so that you don’t accidentally rip the foil, if using.
Spread the steak and vegetables into an even layer. Divide the veggies between the two sheet-pans, if using two.

Place the sheet-pan(s) in the center rack of the oven and roast for 10 minutes. Check the internal temperature of the steak — when it reaches 135°F, remove just the steak from the oven, and transfer it to a cutting board to rest. Tent the steak loosely with foil.

Continue cooking the vegetables for another 8 to 15 minutes (AKA — first check them after 8 minutes) until they’re golden brown all over (so they’ll have cooked for 20 to 25 minutes total). Wrap your desired amount of tortillas in aluminum foil and place them in the oven on the bottom rung (furthest from the heat) for these final 10 to 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, place the avocado in a bowl along with the juice of 1 lime, a big pinch of salt, and 2 tablespoons chopped cilantro. Smash until completely smooth.
When the peppers and onions are ready, remove them from the oven. Slice the steak as thinly as you possibly can, on the bias (see below).
Add the sliced steak and any juices that collect on the cutting board back to the sheet-pan along with the juice of 1 lime and the remaining chopped cilantro (a scant 1/4 cup). Stir to combine.
Serve immediately by loading your tortillas with the fajita mixture, mashed avocado, and whatever else your little heart desires. (Mine desires lots of sour cream.)
Note: I love charring my tortillas by placing them atop my gas burner, but it’s a bit more time consuming than the method in the recipe.

name: pork chops with brown butter creamed corn and kale
note:
Whole30 it: Swap in mashed cauliflower for the creamed corn.

Make ahead: Make the creamed corn as far as 48 hours in advance. Just stir in a splash of water and rewarm over medium heat.

Vegetarian: Cube up a sweet potato, toss with oil, salt, and pepper and roast at 425°F for 20 minutes. Toss in the kale, and roast for 5 to 10 more minutes, until tender but also crispy around the edges. Throw that on top of the creamed corn. Yum!

I’m re-making this during corn season: Well hello from three months ago, how’s summer time?! Are we still wearing masks?? Anyway, use the largest holes on a box grater to grate 3 ears of corn into a bowl. Cut the kernels off of 3 more ears. Use that instead of the frozen stuff — no blender needed.

I forgot to defrost my corn: No big deal. Just proceed with frozen corn. You might have to add a bit more water to get it to blend — that’s fine, it will cook off.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 (1- to 1 1/2-inch thick) boneless pork chops — you want one pork chop per person(see notes for how to cook thinner or bone-in pork chops)
ingredients.name: boneless pork chops — you want one pork chop per person(see notes for how to cook thinner or bone-in pork chops)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen corn (preferably sweet white corn), defrosted
ingredients.name: frozen corn (preferably sweet white corn), defrosted

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup of water plus 1/3 cup water, divided
ingredients.name: of water plus 1/3 cup water

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, plus several sprigs
ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves, plus several sprigs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch kale, de-ribbed and thinly sliced (or just buy a 10-ounce bag of pre-chopped kale and pick out any big stems you see)
ingredients.name: kale, de-ribbed and thinly sliced (or just buy a 10-ounce bag of pre-chopped kale and pick out any big stems you see)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon vinegar (any kind other than plain white vinegar works! I like apple cider or red wine or white balsamic best)
ingredients.name: vinegar (any kind other than plain white vinegar works! I like apple cider or red wine or white balsamic best)

preparationSteps: Season each pork chop with 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds of pepper. Set aside.
Place 1 (16-ounce) bag of defrosted frozen corn in a blender with 1/2 cup water and blend until chunky-smooth, for just a few seconds. Set aside.

name: crispy white bean & cauliflower tahini bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5 ounce) can white beans, such as cannellini, butter, chickpeas, navy, or great northern, drained, rinsed, and patted dry
ingredients.name: white beans, such as cannellini, butter, chickpeas, navy, or great northern, drained, rinsed, and patted dry

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups of whatever grain you love (use up something you already have in the cabinet — farro, barley, quinoa, brown rice, white rice…)
ingredients.name: of whatever grain you love (use up something you already have in the cabinet — farro, barley, quinoa, brown rice, white rice…)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 sprigs fresh parsley, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: fresh parsley, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toasted sesame seeds (or any chopped toasted nut), for garnish
ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds (or any chopped toasted nut), for garnish

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F.

I have a very specific way that I like to cut cauliflower to ensure it gets nicely caramelized and sweet and perfect so pay attention here. Place it on your largest rimmed baking sheet — we’re going to cut it straight on there. Just be careful and don’t slide your knife blade along the pan and your knives will be fine.

First, trim off the leaves and the very bottom of the cauliflower stem. Now slice it in half, through the stem. Place the two halves cut-side down, then slice it into 1/2-inch thick planks. Cut apart the individual florets. There will be little bits of cauliflower everywhere, that’s fine! They crisp up wonderfully and are a part of the magic of this recipe.
Add 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper and toss to evenly coat.
Roast for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, dump 1 can white beans into a colander, rinse, and use paper towels to get them completely dry. Cook 1 1/2 cups of your favorite grain per package instructions. When your grain is finished cooked, use kitchen shears to finely snip 5 parsley sprigs straight into the pot (both leaves and stems). You can chop the parsley if you want, but using kitchen shears here allows us to avoid dirtying a cutting board. Stir it in along with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar, and 3/4 teaspoon salt, cover and remove from heat until you’re ready to serve.

Pull the baking sheet out and flip the cauliflower, then scooch it over to make room for the beans. Pour the beans onto the baking sheet and drizzle them with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and a little pinch of pepper. Spread the beans and cauliflower out so that they are touching as little as possible.

Roast for an additional 20 minutes, or until the cauliflower is browned all over and the beans are crispy. If you need things to get crispier (all ovens are different!), turn the broiler on high and place the baking sheet on the bottom rack of the oven for several more minutes. Keep a close eye on it!

While it’s roasting, make the tahini sauce in a large bowl (large enough to fit the cauliflower and beans) by whisking together 1/3 cup tahini, 2 tablespoons warm water, 1 tablespoon harissa (or 2 if you want more heat), 1 tablespoon honey, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. We are looking for a consistency a tiny bit thinner than heavy cream. Keep adding more splashes of warm water until you achieve that. We want the sauce to lightly coat the vegetables, not be thick and gloopy.
Pour half of the tahini sauce into a container for dinner another night this week.
Add the cauliflower and beans to the bowl and toss to coat. If you need more sauce, steal it from the container.

Add a scoop of grains and a handful of arugula to the bottom of a shallow bowl. Top with cauliflower and crispy beans. Garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and finely chopped parsley. Enjoy immediately.

name: salty minty dogs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large mint sprigs, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: large mint sprigs, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Pour 1/2 cup sea salt onto a small plate and grate the zest of 1 lemon right on top. Use your fingers to pinch the zest into the salt.
Combine 2 cups grapefruit juice, 1 cup gin, and 1/2 cup club soda in a pitcher. Slap 2 large mint sprigs between your hands, then add them to the pitcher.
Cut the lemon in half and use it to wet the rims of your glasses. Dip the rim in the lemon salt. Fill the glasses with ice, then pour in the drink!
*If you want to make these ahead of time, that’s a great plan, but don’t add the club soda until the last minute.
servings: Makes 4 cocktails (AKA you should double this, if you’ll need more than 4 drinks!)

name: rosemary pecans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon finely minced fresh rosemary or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary, crushed
ingredients.name: finely minced fresh rosemary or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 250°F.

Place 4 cups pecan halves on a large rimmed baking sheet. Melt 4 tablespoons butter and pour it over top along with 1 tablespoon minced fresh rosemary, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Use your hands to toss everything around and get the nuts evenly coated.
Spread the nuts into an even layer, then bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until deeply toasted. Give them a stir every 10 minutes or so.
Allow to cool completely, then transfer to an airtight container and store at room temperature for up to 10 days.

name: gruyere + black pepper biscuits with hot honey butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 ounces grated Gruyère cheese (a little less than 1 cup)
ingredients.name: grated Gruyère cheese (a little less than 1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (ground on the largest setting — we want big flecks of pepper)
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper (ground on the largest setting — we want big flecks of pepper)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups heavy cream, plus more for brushing the biscuits
ingredients.name: heavy cream, plus more for brushing the biscuits

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon hot honey (I loveRed Clay(and code CARO15 or CARO20 should work!), or just use regular honey and a dash of hot sauce)
ingredients.name: hot honey (I loveRed Clay(and code CARO15 or CARO20 should work!), or just use regular honey and a dash of hot sauce)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 475°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Add 2 cups self-rising flour, 3 ounces grated gruyère, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper to a large bowl and use a fork to stir to combine. Stir in 1 1/2 cups heavy cream as much as possible with the fork, then use your hands to combine everything. You’ll think that there’s too much flour but there’s not! Use your hands to work it into the dough.

Transfer the dough to the baking sheet and flatten it into about the size of a piece of computer paper, then fold it in half and repeat that process twice more (the process = flatten it out as much as possible, then fold it). It’ll get harder to flatten it with each fold — that’s normal! We’re creating those flaky biscuit layers here!
Pat the thrice-folded dough into a 1 inch-thick rectangle, then cut it into 8 biscuits. Or 16 biscuits, if you want to make little appetizer biscuits!

Separate the biscuits and brush them with a bit of extra heavy cream. If you don’t own a pastry brush, just use your finger to coat the tops and sides of the biscuits. This will help them brown nicely.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden brown and puffy and gorgeous!

While they’re baking, add 4 tablespoons room-temperature unsalted butter, 1 tablespoon hot honey, and a pinch of kosher salt to a small bowl and smash to combine. It takes a sec — just be patient (maybe give this job to a kid!) and keep smashing. After a couple minutes it’ll come together.

name: lamb + potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons Greek seasoning, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 teaspoons Greek seasoning

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon plus 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided
ingredients.name: plus 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 teaspoons freshly ground black pepper, divided
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

preparationSteps: Place 1 boneless leg of lamb on a plastic cutting board and if it came in netting, remove the netting. Open up the lamb, dry with a clean kitchen towel, then use a sharp knife to remove any excess fat from the center (non-smooth side) of the leg. Flip it over and trim off all but a very thin layer of fat (we want to remove the hard, thick white fat, but a thin layer is a good thing).

Season it all over with 3 tablespoons Greek seasoning, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, and 2 teaspoons freshly ground black pepper. Roll the lamb up as tightly as you can into a coil, then use kitchen twine to truss it, AKA cut 3 or 4 long pieces of twine and tie the leg together. Put the lamb in a small roasting dish (a Dutch oven or cast iron skillet works!) fat side UP and place in the refrigerator, uncovered, for at least 4, but ideally 24 hours.
When you’re ready to cook, preheat your oven to 300°F and remove the lamb from the refrigerator. Pour 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken stock around the lamb.

Cut 2 pounds Yukon gold potatoes into 1-inch wedges, and halve and peel 3 shallots and place them in a roasting dish with high sides (I used a 9x13” cake pan!). Drizzle with 1/4 cup oil, 2 teaspoons tablespoon Greek seasoning, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, the juice of 2 large lemons, and 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken stock and toss to coat.
Roast the lamb and potatoes for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring the potatoes every 30 minutes, until an internal thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the lamb registers 130°F.
Remove the potatoes and lamb from the oven and crank the oven up to 500°F. Once it reaches 500°F, return the lamb to the oven for 7 to 10 minutes to crisp up the fatty top.

Transfer the lamb to a clean cutting board to rest for at least 15 minutes. Cut off the twine, then thinly slice and arrange with lots of fresh herbs. Transfer the potatoes to a serving dish (or serve them straight from the roasting pan). Sprinkle flaky sea salt over the potatoes and lamb before serving.

name: springy salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5-ounce container of washed mixed greens or arugula
ingredients.name: of washed mixed greens or arugula

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup Rosemary Pecans (recipe above, or purchase store-bought candied pecans), finely chopped
ingredients.name: Rosemary Pecans (recipe above, or purchase store-bought candied pecans)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces Parmesan cheese (no need to actually measure this, just grab a wedge of Parm and use a vegetable peeler to peel as many pieces as you want onto your salad!)
ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese (no need to actually measure this, just grab a wedge of Parm and use a vegetable peeler to peel as many pieces as you want onto your salad!)

preparationSteps: To make the pickled red onions, slice 1 red onion as thinly as you can and stuff the slices into a jar or glass container. Fill the container 3/4 of the way up with champagne vinegar, then fill it the rest of the way with hot tap water. Add 1 tablespoon sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt and shake to combine. Leave at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or ideally refrigerate for at least 24 hours before using.

To make the champagne vinaigrette, add all the ingredients (1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup champagne vinegar, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt) to a jar and shake to combine. Taste and adjust to your liking (some like it sweeter, some like it tangier!).

Add 5 ounces mixed greens, a handful of pickled red onions (you can also chop these up so that you get just a small bit of onion in each bite), 1/2 cup finely chopped Rosemary Pecans, and a bunch of shaved Parm to a large salad bowl. Toss with your desired amount of champagne vinaigrette, season with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, and serve immediately.
*The pickled red onions are good for up to 10 days in the fridge.

name: balsamic butter asparagus
note:
I prefer shreddable lamb over sliceable lamb: You do you, baby! To get shreddable lamb, cover with foil and cook on 275°F for 4 1/2 hours, basting (aka scooping up the juices in the bottom of the pan and pouring them over the lamb) every hour. Remove the foil, turn the heat up to 375°F, and continue cooking for 20 to 30 more minutes or until browned on top. Remove the twine and use two forks to shred. Cook the potatoes alongside the lamb for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.

Lamb swap:Bone-in lamb: If you can only find bone-in leg of lamb, that works too! Prepare it the same way, but you’ll need to cook it longer to reach 135°F internally. Pork shoulder: This would be a fab sub. Cook it for 50 minutes per pound. See this post for a more specific breakdown of cook time based on the weight of your pork.  Steaks: Grill some steaks using the brine as your rub! See last week’s post for how long and at what temp to grill steaks. Honey baked ham: Outsource the meat altogether and buy a honey-baked ham. Ignore the instructions that come with it. Pour the glaze on top and bake it for just 10 minutes on 450°F. It’s already cooked, so it just needs to heat through.

Bone-in lamb: If you can only find bone-in leg of lamb, that works too! Prepare it the same way, but you’ll need to cook it longer to reach 135°F internally.

Pork shoulder: This would be a fab sub. Cook it for 50 minutes per pound. See this post for a more specific breakdown of cook time based on the weight of your pork.

Steaks: Grill some steaks using the brine as your rub! See last week’s post for how long and at what temp to grill steaks.

Honey baked ham: Outsource the meat altogether and buy a honey-baked ham. Ignore the instructions that come with it. Pour the glaze on top and bake it for just 10 minutes on 450°F. It’s already cooked, so it just needs to heat through.

Mint sub: Mint is the classic accompaniment for lamb and is so springy. But if you aren’t into it, you can swap it out for another leafy green herb you love like basil, parsley, or cilantro.

Gruyère sub: Feel free to use Parm in the biscuits since you’ll already be buying it for the salad! Or Cheddar! Or really any shreddy melty cheese!

Asparagus sub: Green beans, broccoli, or broccolini would all be delicious and cooked the same way. If you love carrots, you can go with the honey-roasted carrots and burrata from the holiday menu instead. Or If you’re wanting to ditch a side dish to simplify things, you could double the springy salad and skip this one… but it’s so good!

Self-rising flour sub: You can use all-purpose flour if you can’t find self-rising flour — you’ll just need to add baking powder and salt too. For every 1 cup of all-purpose flour, add 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/4 teaspoon fine salt.

Pecan sub: Walnut halves or almond slices would be delicious. If you can’t do nuts, make rosemary sunflower seeds!

Trimming fat off meat is my ick: Ask the butcher to do it!

Vegetarian: Make a springy risotto as the main course. This no-stir mushroom risotto, this asparagus and pea iteration, or the boursin risotto from our holiday menu would all be fab. If you’re going the asparagus risotto route, you can swap the asparagus in the side dish out for green beans. One other option, if your group eats seafood: one-pot lemony garlic butter shrimp orzo would make a great main course for a spring feast.

Dairy-free: Swap the butter for a plant-based stick butter and the Greek yogurt for a Greek-style dairy-free yogurt. I haven’t tested the biscuits with a DF milk, but I’d swap the heavy cream out for almond milk! Omit the Gruyère and Parm throughout the recipes. If you want to make things super easy, use a good loaf of bread in place of the biscuits.

Gluten-free: Use a gluten-free Cup4Cup flour substitute for the biscuits. For every 1 cup of GF flour, add 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/4 teaspoon fine salt. I will warn you that I’ve not tried this, but I am 92% positive it will work!

Prep/make ahead: See the “plan of attack” section for all of these tips!

Love your leftovers: There are lots of things you can do with leftover lamb! Chop it up for lamb pitas and use your minty yogurt as the sauce. Add it to a curry. Top a salad with it. It’ll stay good in the fridge stored in an airtight container for 3 to 4 days; you could also freeze it for up to 3 months!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound asparagus (ideally medium sized, about the width of a pencil), woody stems removed (AKA, trim about 2 inches off the bottom and discard them because they are tough and fibrous!)
ingredients.name: asparagus (ideally medium sized, about the width of a pencil), woody stems removed (AKA, trim about 2 inches off the bottom and discard them because they are tough and fibrous!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped roasted salted almonds (or any nut works)
ingredients.name: chopped roasted salted almonds (or any nut works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of red pepper flakes
