ingredients.name: Big pinch of red pepper flakes

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound trimmed asparagus and a big pinch of salt and get the asparagus into as even a layer as possible so that they’re touching the skillet as much as possible. Cover (use a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid that fits) and let them sit for 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, smash 6 garlic cloves as flat as possible using the side of a chef’s knife. Place the flat edge of the knife on top of a garlic clove on a cutting board, then use your fist to bang down on the blade as hard as you can to smash the garlic!
Uncover the skillet, add the smashed garlic, shake the skillet to move the asparagus around, then cover for another 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop 1/4 cup roasted salted almonds and set aside.
Stir a big pinch of red pepper flakes, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, and 1 tablespoon unsalted butter into the asparagus and toss to coat.
Transfer asparagus to a serving platter and scatter the chopped almonds and a pinch of flaky salt over top. I grated a bit of lemon zest on top too!

name: boursin summer squash galette

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds (about 4 smallish) zucchini and/or yellow squash
ingredients.name: (about 4 smallish) zucchini and/or yellow squash

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 refrigerated pie crust (the kind that rolls up —like this, for example)
ingredients.name: refrigerated pie crust (the kind that rolls up —like this, for example)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of soft green herbs (leaves and tender stems)
ingredients.name: Handful of soft green herbs (leaves and tender stems)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Trim off the bottom of 2 pounds of zucchini and/or squash, then, holding it by the stalk end, grate each squash on the largest hole of your box grater, directly onto a clean kitchen towel. You can make quick work of this by using the grater blade on your food processor, if you have one!
Sprinkle the squash with 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and let it hang out on the towel while you go work on the rest of the galette.

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Unroll 1 refrigerated pie crust onto the parchment paper. If it cracks along the way, no worries! Just use your fingers to smoosh the cracks together. Plop the entire package of Boursin right onto the crust, then use your hands to spread it all over the crust, leaving a 1-inch border.

Back to the squash. Over the sink, use the kitchen towel to wring as much moisture out of the squash as possible. Then I like to do an extra squeeze by grabbing handfuls of the squash and squeezing them over the sink, repeating until all has been squeezed. I usually get a lot of extra moisture out when I do this, so don’t skip it!

Plop the squash onto the pie crust and spread it out into an even layer, again leaving that 1-inch border. Fold the dough over the squash to form a crimped crust. Look at the pictures for a visual — it does not have to be perfect!
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of panko breadcrumbs over the squash. Spray the entire galette with a light spritz of cooking spray. Bake until the crust is golden, 20 to 25 minutes.
Let the galette rest for at least 5 minutes. While it’s resting, chop up (or thinly slice, if using basil) a handful of soft green herbs. Sprinkle them over top.
Slice and serve!

name: grilled sesame-ginger steak with a creamy crunchy cucumber and pepper salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 garlic cloves, peeled (or 3 frozen garlic cubes)
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, peeled (or 3 frozen garlic cubes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2-inch piece of fresh ginger, peeled (or 5 frozen ginger cubeslikethese)
ingredients.name: of fresh ginger, peeled (or 5 frozen ginger cubeslikethese)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 flank steak (1 to 2 pounds, depending on how much you want/need! Makes great leftovers!)
ingredients.name: flank steak (1 to 2 pounds, depending on how much you want/need! Makes great leftovers!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 red, orange, or yellow bell peppers (red are the most nutrient dense!)
ingredients.name: red, orange, or yellow bell peppers (red are the most nutrient dense!)

preparationSteps: Add 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup of any neutral-tasting oil, 1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1/3 cup rice vinegar, 3 tablespoons honey, 2 tablespoons tahini, 3 peeled garlic cloves, a peeled 2-inch piece of fresh ginger, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a blender. Blend until smooth.

Place a 1- to 2-pound flank steak in a Ziploc or sealable container. Add just enough of the ginger marinade to cover it. Refrigerate for up to 48 hours, or leave at room temperature for at least 30 minutes (but no more than 2 hours).

Meanwhile (up to 24 hours in advance), make the salad. Cut 2 bell peppers into bite-sized pieces and toss into a bowl. Peel 1 English cucumber like a zebra (make it have stripes), cut in half vertically, then slice into 1/4 inch-thick half circles. Throw them into the bowl with the pepper. Sprinkle with a really big pinch of kosher salt. Let the veggies sit for 10 minutes to draw some of their moisture out, then use a paper towel to dry out the bottom of the bowl and pat the vegetables dry.
Pour in about 1/4 cup of the ginger dressing, 1 tablespoon everything bagel seasoning, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Toss to coat.

Preheat grill to 450°F. Half of the grill should have direct heat, and half should have indirect heat. If you have a gas grill, turn half of the burners on high and leave the other burners off. My grill has 2 burners, so I turn 1 on full blast, and leave 1 off. If you use charcoal, prepare the charcoal, then scooch it over to the side to leave one side with no direct heat source underneath the grates.
When the grill is hot, brush the grill grates until they’re totally clean. We do not need to oil the grates since the steak is already coated in an oily marinade.

Shake off any excess marinade, sprinkle the steak all over with about 1 teaspoon kosher salt (this will help it form a nice crust), then grill the steak for 3 minutes per side over DIRECT heat, until the steak has a really nice sear and releases easily from the grate when you try to flip it.

Transfer the steak to INDIRECT heat, then cook for anywhere from 4 to 10 more minutes, depending on the thickness of your steak, until it reaches 135°F internally for medium-rare, or 145°F for medium. Transfer to a plate and cover loosely with foil for at least 10 minutes.

While the steak rests, cut the avocado into 1/2-inch pieces and gently toss it into the salad. Taste. Add some sriracha or chili crisp if you like a little heat. I add a lot more salt at this point. Continue seasoning until it’s perfect!

Thinly slice the steak against the grain. Look for the lines that run through the steak. Cut across them — perpendicular to them. Cutting against the grain makes each bite of steak more tender, because you’re cutting through tough tendons that would be difficult to chew, rather than leaving them whole. Sprinkle the cut steak with a nice pinch of flaky sea salt so that the inside of the steak is nicely seasoned.
Serve the steak with salad!

name: lemon basil spaghetti!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound dried spaghetti, or any long noodle
ingredients.name: dried spaghetti, or any long noodle

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (it must be freshly grated!)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (it must be freshly grated!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), preferably organic, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), preferably organic, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (no need to measure — about 2 grinds)
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper (no need to measure — about 2 grinds)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 large basil leaves or 6 parsley sprigs, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: large basil leaves or 6 parsley sprigs

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but encouraged: lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below!)
ingredients.name: Optional but encouraged: lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below!)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

Cook 1 pound dried pasta noodles until al dente (almost totally tender, but still with a slight hardness), per package instructions (as in, read the package and cook it for however long it says it will take to reach al dente!).

Meanwhile, in a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 large egg, 1 cup of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, the zest of 1 lemon, 1/3 cup lemon juice, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon (2 grinds) of black pepper.
Thinly slice 12 large basil leaves.

Immediately after draining, add the hot noodles to the sauce you made in the serving bowl, along with 1/2 cup of the hot, reserved pasta cooking water and most of the basil (but leave a little basil out for garnish). Use tongs to toss and toss and toss until the sauce is glossy and coating the noodles. It might look too soupy at first — keep tossing! The cheese, oil, and egg just need time and heat to meld together and work their magic. Add more pasta water as needed if the sauce stiffens up too much.
Serve immediately, garnished with more Parm, lemon zest, basil, and (if making) lots of lemon-parm crunchies.

name: lemon-parm crunchies
note:
Love your leftovers: The pasta will be delicious for up to 4 days stored in the fridge. Add a splash of water when you’re reheating to loosen the sauce up. The lemon-parm crunchies will stay good sealed in an airtight container for up to a week!

Feeding picky eaters: You can leave the basil out if green flecks ick them out — just garnish any basil eaters’ bowls with it instead. Also, FWIW, my boys branded these “Spongebob noodles.” Whatever works!

I *do* feel like cooking/I’m cooking this for guests: You’ve gotta make the crunchies! Also, scroll up to the “bulk it up” section above the recipe for ideas for a meat and/or side salad to stretch this meal further.

Must have meat: I love shrimp and chicken with this one! See the “bulk it up” section above the recipe for how-tos.

Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free Parm alternative. If you don’t like DF cheese, you can use 1/2 cup of an unsweetened dairy-free milk/cream substitute.

Gluten-free: Use any gluten-free pasta alternative you love — but taste the pasta cooking water before you add it, it can be pretty salty so you may want to cut back on salt elsewhere. You could also use zucchini noodles. I prefer to sauté my zoodles in oil to keep them crisp (rather than boiling them). To make up for the lack of starchy pasta water, you can make a slurry: mix 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of cornstarch with 1 cup of water. Bring it to a simmer then use it in the recipe as written. If you’re making the crunchies, use GF breadcrumbs.
preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup breadcrumbs, a big pinch of kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and the zest of 1 lemon and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden brown. Stir in 1/3 cup grated Parm and stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the cheese is crispy and coating the breadcrumbs. Pour into a small bowl to cool and place the bowl directly on the dinner table for people to serve themselves!

name: 3-ingredient chorizo street tacos
note:
But where’s the side dish? I don’t believe in side dishes on taco night. Just eat another damn taco. But we’re all entitled to our own beliefs, and if you think tacos need rice and beans, might I suggest this recipe?

Gimme some greens: Chop up some spinach and throw it in the mixture at the end, stirring until wilted.

Vegetarian: Use a vegan ground meat, or an extra can of your favorite beans — I like black or pinto beans for this!

Gluten-free/dairy-free: To avoid gluten, be sure to use corn tortillas and look carefully at the chorizo you buy; most is gluten-free but not all. For dairy-free, use vegan sour cream for the crema and skip adding cheese (or use a df alternative).

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Like I said above, skip the crema and just use sour cream or Greek yogurt with a squirt of lime juice on top.

Leftovers are a good thing: Cooked chorizo freezes well! Just be sure it cools completely before freezing it in a tightly sealed bag (with no air). This chorizo filling would also be delicious on nachos, in a quesadilla, burrito bowl, etc.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 9-ounce tube of ground Mexican chorizo(Not Spanish chorizo, which is hard like salami. Grocery stores keep chorizo in weird places sometimes — ask where it is!)
ingredients.name: of ground Mexican chorizo(Not Spanish chorizo, which is hard like salami. Grocery stores keep chorizo in weird places sometimes — ask where it is!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained but not rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans, drained but not rinsed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons of sauce from a can of chipotles en adobo
ingredients.name: of sauce from a can of chipotles en adobo

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup sour cream, Greek yogurt, or plain yogurt
ingredients.name: sour cream, Greek yogurt, or plain yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 corn tortillas (try to find “street tacos” — they’re smaller than a normal taco tortilla)
ingredients.name: corn tortillas (try to find “street tacos” — they’re smaller than a normal taco tortilla)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings: cilantro,pickled red onions, cotija cheese (or really, any kind of cheese), sliced radishes, avocado
ingredients.name: Optional toppings: cilantro,pickled red onions, cotija cheese (or really, any kind of cheese), sliced radishes, avocado

preparationSteps: Warm a skillet over medium-high heat. Add 9 ounces of chorizo, break it up using a spatula, and cook it for 5 minutes. (FYI: It will get really loose — almost like chili — once it gets hot.) Stir in 1 can of black beans and 2 teaspoons of the sauce from a can of chipotle peppers and turn the heat down to low. Squeeze in the juice of 1/2 a lime and cook over low heat for 5 more minutes. Taste. I never need to add salt or more chipotle pepper sauce, but you might!
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, stir together 1/3 cup sour cream, the juice of 1/2 a lime, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt.
Warm your tortillas. My favorite way to do so: Char them over the direct flame of a gas stovetop. Turn it on medium-low heat, and cook them on each side until lightly charred.
Spoon the chorizo and black bean filling into the tortillas and top them with lime crema and whatever toppings your heart desires!

name: tandoori chicken bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 garlic cloves, minced or grated using a microplane (or 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder)
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, minced or grated using a microplane (or 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds of boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut lengthwise into 3 pieces per breast
ingredients.name: of boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut lengthwise into 3 pieces per breast
Yellow rice(please, please feel free to skip this recipe and simply buyyellow riceto make life easier, if you’d like):

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup white rice (such as Jasmine or basmati)
ingredients.name: white rice (such as Jasmine or basmati)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups chicken broth (I use 1 1/2 cups water + a spoonful of chicken Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: chicken broth (I use 1 1/2 cups water + a spoonful of chicken Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Chopped lettuce, chopped tomato, avocado slices, thinly sliced red onion, chopped cucumber, feta, and/or chopped soft green herbs (basil, dill, parsley, or cilantro)
ingredients.name: Chopped lettuce, chopped tomato, avocado slices, thinly sliced red onion, chopped cucumber, feta, and/or chopped soft green herbs (basil, dill, parsley, or cilantro)

preparationSteps: First, make the yogurt sauce: In a large bowl, combine 1 cup yogurt, 1/2 cup mayo, the juice of 1 lemon, 3 minced garlic cloves, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Taste and adjust seasonings as desired. Transfer half of this mixture to a small serving bowl — this is your garlicky white sauce! Reserve it in the small bowl for meal time.

To the large bowl of the yogurt mixture, add another 1 teaspoon salt plus 2 tablespoons honey, 2 teaspoons garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon ground turmeric, 1 teaspoon ground ginger, and several grinds of black pepper. Stir to combine. This is your chicken marinade!

Cut 1 1/2 pounds chicken breasts lengthwise (AKA long-ways!) into 3 pieces per breast. Add chicken to the marinade and toss to combine. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 24. (After 24 hours, the yogurt will start to make the chicken texture weird, but, yes, if something comes up, you can grill it after 48 hours and it will not be the end of the world.)
Thirty minutes before you want to eat, preheat your grill to medium-high heat (450°F). See notes for indoor cooking instructions.

While it’s heating, start the rice! Combine 1 cup white rice, 1 1/2 cups chicken broth, 2 tablespoons butter, 1 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a small pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to very low heat and cover the pan with a lid for 15 minutes. Shut the flame off after 15 minutes, but do not take the lid off for at least another 5 minutes. Use a fork to fluff the rice.

While the rice is cooking, grill the chicken! If you haven’t already, use a grill brush to scrape the grates clean. Use tongs to grab the chicken out of the bowl of marinade, and scrape as much excess yogurt marinade as you can off the chicken before adding it to the grill. Grill for 5 minutes per side, or until an internal thermometer inserted into the chicken reads 165°F.
While the chicken rests for 5 minutes, slice/chop your desired toppings up, and throw them on a pretty board or plate.

We’re serving this one family style, because it will make your kids/everyone eat more! Place your rice, chicken, yogurt sauce, and optional toppings onto the table and let everyone dig in, creating their own bowls. It’s a good idea to slice the chicken before serving if you are feeding small people.

name: hella green pasta

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) block of Parmigiano Reggiano (Parmesan) — try your hardest to find “Parmigiano Reggiano” instead of “Parmesan,” it’s the legit good stuff,it will make a difference!
ingredients.name: try your hardest to find “Parmigiano Reggiano” instead of “Parmesan,” it’s the legit good stuff,it will make a difference!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 20 garlic cloves (yes, 20 — buy pre-peeled garlic!), peeled and roughly chopped
ingredients.name: garlic cloves (yes, 20 — buy pre-peeled garlic!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup high-quality extra-virgin olive oil (I useKosterina!)
ingredients.name: high-quality extra-virgin olive oil (I useKosterina!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch lacinato kale (roughly 1 pound), ends trimmed if they look yucky
ingredients.name: lacinato kale (roughly 1 pound), ends trimmed if they look yucky

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch spinach (roughly 12 ounces), ends trimmed if they look yucky, or 2 5-oz bags of baby spinach
ingredients.name: spinach (roughly 12 ounces), ends trimmed if they look yucky, or 2 5-oz bags of baby spinach

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound pasta (absolutely any kind but I actually prefer a thick long noodle here like bucatini)
ingredients.name: pasta (absolutely any kind but I actually prefer a thick long noodle here like bucatini)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup reserved pasta cooking water (I’m listing this as an ingredient to help you not forget!)
ingredients.name: reserved pasta cooking water (I’m listing this as an ingredient to help you not forget!)

preparationSteps: Cut the rind off of an 8-ounce block of Parmesan (save it and throw it in the pot next time you make lemony chicken orzo soup to add tons of flavor), cut the cheese into a few chunks, and throw it in the blender. Blend until it becomes grated, then just leave it in the blender for when we make the sauce in just a bit. If your blender doesn’t do a good job at this, just take the remaining chunks out and grate by hand.

Add 20 peeled and roughly chopped garlic cloves to a small pot and cover with 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil. Cook over low heat until the garlic cloves are light golden-brown and softened, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool.

Meanwhile, bring a big pot of heavily salted water (we’re talking 2 tablespoons of kosher salt!) to a boil. Add 1 bunch kale to the boiling water and cook for 2 minutes. Add 1 bunch spinach and continue cooking for 2 to 3 more minutes, until the spinach and kale are both wilted. Remove the pot from heat.

Use tongs to transfer all of the greens from the pot to the blender. Squeeze or shake the excess water out from the greens as you transfer them — but it’s OK if a bit of water comes over too. DON’T DRAIN THE POT OF WATER! Put the pot back on the stove over high heat and bring the water back to a boil.
Once the water has reached a rolling boil, cook 1 pound pasta per package instructions. Scoop out 1 cup of cooking water, then drain the pasta in a colander. Return the pasta to the cooking pot.

Now, make the sauce: Add the cooled cooked garlic and all of the oil to the blender along with the zest and juice of 1 lemon and 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt. Blend on high until smooth. Add a bit of the reserved pasta cooking water if needed to get a saucy consistency. The amount of water you add will depend on how much water clung to the greens when you dragged them over to the blender — I added 1/2 cup.
The sauce should be the consistency of a marinara — thick, but still very drizzle-able.

Taste. If it isn’t ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS to you, it needs more salt and possibly more lemon juice. I always add more lemon juice, but people are sensitive to acid, so I only included the juice of 1 lemon in the recipe. If you think it needs a bit of brightness, blend in more lemon juice!

Pour 1 cup of the green sauce into the pasta to start. Toss to coat. Add more as desired until the pasta is as saucy as ya like it. I use about 1 1/2 cups of sauce per 1 pound of pasta. It should be glossy and saucy, not thick and chunky. Stir in more pasta cooking water if needed to thin the sauce out a bit to help it coat all of the noodles smoothly.
Divide the pasta between 4 to 6 bowls and garnish with more Parm and red pepper flakes.
servings: Serves 4 to 6 (with lots of extra sauce)

name: blackened fish taco bowls
note:
Whole30 it: Omit the rice and cook cauliflower rice instead. You know how I like to cook it: heat a little bit of oil or ghee in a large nonstick skillet over high heat. Saute until tender, about 4 minutes. Season with salt at the very end so that it doesn’t release liquid (which happens when you salt things) and make it soggy. Omit the sugar from the fish rub.

I forgot to buy foil: Just cook it straight on the sheet pan, but be sure to oil the pan well!

My family hates fish: Totally. It was worth a shot though, right? You can use chicken! See the note below for how to cook it.

But this makes an insane amount of fish and I’m eating alone: Only buy as much fish as you’re going to eat that night. Leftover fish sucks. Everything else is great as leftovers, see the leftovers note below…

Leftovers are a good thing: Fish leftovers are not for me. But the rice, slaw, and salsa? SO GOOD the next day! Grab a rotisserie chicken and repurpose those leftovers into chicken taco bowls!

Make ahead: Absolutely everything can be done up to 24 hours in advance, except the fish. The fish should only be marinated the morning of or later, and should be cooked right before eating. You can go ahead and put it on the foil-lined baking sheet so that all you have to do is pop it under the broiler at dinner time!

What to do when you really don’t feel like cooking: Grab pre-cooked frozen rice and some slaw from the deli section of your grocery store, chop up some pre-sliced mango or pineapple for your fruity topping (or buy pico de gallo or a fruity salsa), and maybe just forget the fish and grab a rotisserie chicken instead.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag shredded purple or green cabbage (about 2 packed cups)
ingredients.name: shredded purple or green cabbage (about 2 packed cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1 small orange or 1/2 large orange (about 3 tablespoons)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1 small orange or 1/2 large orange (about 3 tablespoons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 tablespoons cajun, jerk, or blackening seasoning, OR:2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne (omit if you can’t handle the heat!)
ingredients.name: cajun, jerk, or blackening seasoning, OR:2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne (omit if you can’t handle the heat!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne (omit if you can’t handle the heat!)
ingredients.name: smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne (omit if you can’t handle the heat!)

preparationSteps: First, we’re going to cook our rice just like we’d cook pasta. No perfect water:rice ratios needed with this method!

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Season the water with 1 tablespoon kosher salt and stir in 1 1/2 cups rice. Cook white rice for 15 minutes, or until tender. Cook brown rice for 25 minutes, or until tender. Drain in a colander. Return rice to the pot, add 2 tablespoons unsalted butter and the juice of 1 lime and cover for 10 minutes to allow the rice to steam and the butter to melt.
Meanwhile, make the rest of dinner!
Finely chop 1 cup of cilantro leaves and stems. We’ll use half in the slaw and half in the salsa. After chopping it, you should have about 1/2 cup chopped cilantro.

To make the Cilantro Slaw: Add 1 (10-ounce) bag shredded cabbage to a large bowl. Add a pinch of salt and massage it into the cabbage by squeezing the cabbage with your hands over and over until it starts to feel tender. Stir in 2 tablespoons oil, the juice of 1 small orange, the juice of 1 lime, and half of the finely chopped cilantro. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.

To make the Citrus Salsa: peel and chop 1 grapefruit and 1 orange. Add them to a large bowl along with the juice of 1 lime, 2 tablespoons oil, the second half of the finely chopped cilantro, and a big pinch of salt. Cut the stem off of 1 serrano pepper, cut it in half lengthwise and remove the seeds if you don’t like a lot of heat. Finely mince the pepper and add it to the salsa. Stir the salsa to combine and adjust seasoning as needed.

To make the Blackened Cod: preheat oven to broil on high. Add 2 tablespoons oil, 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun/jerk/blackening seasoning (or all of the spices listed), 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1 teaspoon brown sugar to a large bowl. Stir to combine. Add the cod filets to the bowl one at a time, carefully feeling each filet for bones before you add it. Toss to coat them completely.

Prepare a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil. Coat the foil with oil. Add cod filets in a single layer. Broil on high for 5 to 6 minutes, until the fish flakes easily. (If your filets are thick, you may need to cook them longer — see note below.)
Transfer fish to the cutting board (the filets might fall apart — that’s OK!) and use a fork to break the fish into big flakes.

Build the bowls with rice on the bottom, then pile on the cilantro slaw, fish, and citrus salsa. Be sure to get lots of the citrus salsa juice on there too, not just the fruit. Slice the avocado at the last minute and place on the bowl. Squeeze lime wedges over the fish. DIG IN!!!!

name: thai-ish steak and noodle salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup fresh lime juice (from 5 to 6 limes)
ingredients.name: fresh lime juice (from 5 to 6 limes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 heaping cup roasted, salted cashews, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: heaping cup roasted, salted cashews, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2-inch piece ginger, washed (no need to peel)
ingredients.name: ginger, washed (no need to peel)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound any kind of steaks, 1-inch thick (I used chuck steaks, NY strip would also be great)
ingredients.name: any kind of steaks, 1-inch thick (I used chuck steaks, NY strip would also be great)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 ounces spaghetti (a little less than half of a 1-pound box)
ingredients.name: spaghetti (a little less than half of a 1-pound box)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups thinly sliced Napa or savoy cabbage (this was 1/2 a head of Napa cabbage for me)
ingredients.name: thinly sliced Napa or savoy cabbage (this was 1/2 a head of Napa cabbage for me)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 serrano pepper, thinly sliced, or 1/4 cup pickled jalapeño slices (optional — omit if you don’t like or want any heat)
ingredients.name: serrano pepper, thinly sliced, or 1/4 cup pickled jalapeño slices (optional — omit if you don’t like or want any heat)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 scallions, roots trimmed off, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions, roots trimmed off

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 medium carrots, finely shredded on a mandoline or a box grater (or 1 cup of store-bought shredded carrots)
ingredients.name: medium carrots, finely shredded on a mandoline or a box grater (or 1 cup of store-bought shredded carrots)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large mango, peeled, cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: large mango, peeled

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup roughly chopped cilantro, leaves and soft stems
ingredients.name: roughly chopped cilantro, leaves and soft stems

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup crumbled toasted unsweetened coconut flakes (optional)
ingredients.name: crumbled toasted unsweetened coconut flakes (optional)

preparationSteps: Add 1/2 cup fresh lime juice, 1/2 cup sesame oil, 1/4 heaping cup cashews, 1/4 packed cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup fish sauce, a 2-inch piece of ginger, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and 2 scallions (roots trimmed off) to a blender and blend on high speed until totally smooth, 30 to 45 seconds. If you don’t have a high-powered blender, soak the cashews in warm water for 15 minutes before blending (discard the water they soaked in) to help them blend more easily.

Add 1 pound of steaks to a small resealable plastic bag and add just enough of the dressing to coat them — 1/4 to 1/3 cup max. Close the bag, pressing out all of the air, and squish the steaks and marinade until the steaks are coated. Marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, but ideally in the refrigerator for 6 to 24 hours.

While the steaks are marinating, cook 6 ounces spaghetti in a pot of boiling salted water until al dente (read the box for al dente cook time). Drain and rinse under cold water until the noodles are cold. Dry them off using a clean kitchen towel or paper towels.

Also while the steak is marinating, prepare your veggies, adding them to a large bowl. For that, thinly slice 4 cups cabbage (this was 1/2 a head of Napa cabbage for me) removing and discarding the core, 1/2 a serrano pepper, and 2 scallions (roots trimmed off and discarded). Using a mandoline or box grater, finely shred 2 medium carrots. Cut 1 large peeled mango into 1-inch pieces and 1 avocado into 1/2-inch pieces. Roughly chop cilantro leaves and soft stems (1 cup), basil leaves (1 cup), and mint leaves (1/2 cup), adding them to the bowl as well.

Make sure the noodles are totally dry, then add them to the bowl of veggies. Add your desired amount of dressing (I use it all!) and toss to coat. Taste and add more salt and pepper to your liking (I needed a big pinch of salt, because I love salt!!).

Prepare a grill for medium-high heat. (Or heat a grill pan or cast iron skillet over medium-high.) Remove steaks from marinade and scrape off as much marinade as possible using the bag. Season very lightly with salt. Grill (or cook in the skillet), turning every 2 minutes, until lightly charred all over and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of each steak registers 120° for medium-rare, 8–10 minutes total. Transfer to a cutting board and let rest at least 10 minutes before cutting into 1/2-inch cubes.
Toss the steak and 1/4 cup crumbled toasted unsweetened coconut flakes (if using) into the salad.

Divide salad among plates, piling as high as possible to make it look *fancy.* Top with a nice dusting of finely chopped cashews and serve with lime wedges, if you have a lime leftover, for squeezing over top.

name: one-pot thai-style rice with pork & green beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 Thai chili (AKA bird’s eye chili), thinly sliced, OR 1 teaspoon chili-garlic sauce
ingredients.name: Thai chili (AKA bird’s eye chili), thinly sliced, OR 1 teaspoon chili-garlic sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup basil leaves (holy basil if you can find it)
ingredients.name: basil leaves (holy basil if you can find it)

preparationSteps: In a large Dutch oven over medium-high, smush 1 pound ground pork into a thin layer to fill the skillet. Leave undisturbed until browned underneath, 5 to 7 minutes.

Meanwhile, peel and finely chop 4 garlic cloves and 2 shallots. Thinly slice 1 Thai chili (set the chili aside for later). Once the bottom of the pork has browned, add the garlic and shallots to the pot and break the pork up into little pieces. Cook until the shallots are softened, 1 to 2 minutes.

Add 2 1/2 cups water, 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, and the thinly sliced chili (either with or without its seeds, based on your heat preference). Bring to a boil. Stir in 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook under the rice is tender, about 20 to 22 minutes.

While the rice is cooking, slice 1/2 pound green beans crosswise into 1-inch thick pieces. Line up a handful and slice a bunch at once! (If you’re wondering whether or not to trim the ends off them, the choice is yours. You definitely don’t have to, but if the ends of your green beans are particular long/stringy, you may want to!)

Turn off the heat, add the green beans on top of the rice, then cover and let the rice rest and the green beans steam for 10 minutes. Add 1 cup basil leaves and fluff the rice to stir the basil and green beans into the rice. No, you don’t have to slice your basil! If some of the leaves are huge, you can tear them in half/quarters.

If making the fried eggs, in a large cast-iron or nonstick skillet, heat 1/4 cup neutral oil over medium-high until it ripples like the ocean. Crack 4 large eggs into the pan (keeping them separate from one another). Cover the skillet and cook for 1 minute, until the white is opaque but the yolk is still runny.
Divide the rice between 4 bowls. Top each with a fried egg. Dig in!

name: cajun honey butter shrimp and fresh corn grits
note:
Make it ahead: The corn grits will stay good in the fridge for days, just warm them up in a skillet before it’s time to eat, adding a splash of milk or water to loosen them up.

Make it sweet(er): Stir in 1 tablespoons of sugar for a traditional Southern creamed corn vibe!

Make it savory: Fresh thyme would be great in here for more savory grits. I also always love adding garlic powder to corn grits (I’d use about 1/4 teaspoon)!

Where’s the cheese? I get it! Add some shredded or freshly grated cheddar for super cheesy corn grits, or Parmesan for subtly cheesy grits. Cheese will also make it more savory.

Add some herbs: If you’ve got them, fresh parsley and/or basil would be good!

No box grater (or time): Maybe you’re in a beach rental and it’s the one tool not there. OR maybe grating 8 ears of corn isn’t your jam today. In either case, you can make the corn grits using a food processor or high-powered blender. Cut the kernels off the cobs and place them in a the food processor/blender with 1 tablespoon water. Pulse 5 to 10 times until well ground. Transfer to a large skillet or saucepan and continue cooking as written. You can also use frozen corn to cut down on time! Grab 2 16-ounce bags of frozen white corn. Thaw at room temperature or overnight in the fridge. Throw in a blender and blend until still slightly chunky, but very, very, very well chopped. Pour into the skillet and proceed with the recipe as if you had grated it.

Make it dairy free: Use vegan butter!

Gluten-free: It is as written!

Special ingredient: If you made my one-pot cajun chicken and rice recipe from back in December, you’ve got Cajun seasoning in your pantry! If you haven’t yet, add it to your line up for this week or next. It’s delish.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound (21 to 25 count) peeled, deveined shrimp OR 1 pound large scallops (not bay scallops)
ingredients.name: peeled, deveined shrimp OR 1 pound large scallops (not bay scallops)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 9 ears corn on the cob, husks removed
ingredients.name: corn on the cob, husks removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large red bell pepper, sliced ⅛-inch thick
ingredients.name: large red bell pepper, sliced ⅛-inch thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 scallions, thinly sliced (cut off the root then slice as thinly as you can into rounds — the entire scallion is good!)
ingredients.name: scallions, thinly sliced (cut off the root then slice as thinly as you can into rounds — the entire scallion is good!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon honey (optional — if you don’t use butter only use 1 teaspoon honey)
ingredients.name: honey (optional — if you don’t use butter only use 1 teaspoon honey)

preparationSteps: Toss 1 pound shrimp with 1 tablespoon Cajun seasoning and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Set aside to marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes, or refrigerate covered for up to 24 hours.
Grate 8 ears of corn (i.e. all but one) using the largest hole on a box grater, directly into a large skillet or saucepan. Cut the kernels off the 9th ear of corn and set aside.

Place the skillet full of grated corn over low heat and stir in 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until very thick. Season to taste with additional salt and pepper. (At this point we have not added a lot of salt and pepper, so your corn will still be very sweet! If you want it to be more savory, add more salt!)
While the corn “grits” are cooking, start making the shrimp mixture.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 thinly sliced bell pepper and cook for several minutes, until it’s getting soft. Add the cut corn kernels and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes, until all is softened. Stir in 4 thinly sliced green onions (reserving a tablespoon for garnish), then scoot everything to one side of the skillet.
Position skillet so that the empty side of the skillet is over the highest heat, and the part with the peppers is as far off the heat as possible.
Warm the remaining 1 tablespoon oil on the empty side of the skillet.
Dry off your shrimp REALLY WELL with a clean paper towel, then add them in a single layer (as much as possible) and cook for about a minute per side, until pink.

Stir in 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 tablespoon honey, the zest and juice from 1/2 of a lemon, and 3 minced or grated garlic cloves, cooking for about 1 minute — until everything is combined and saucy!
Serve the shrimp mixture over the corn grits.

name: herby shrimp couscous bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 packed cups baby arugula OR leafy green herbs (I love using cilantro and basil for this!), divided
ingredients.name: packed cups baby arugula OR leafy green herbs (I love using cilantro and basil for this!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds large peeled and deveined shrimp
ingredients.name: large peeled and deveined shrimp

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 mini seedless cucumbers (or 1 English cucumber), cut into 1/2-inch pieces
ingredients.name: mini seedless cucumbers (or 1 English cucumber)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 peaches, sliced 1/2-inch thick (try to find some that are ripe but firm!)
ingredients.name: peaches, sliced 1/2-inch thick (try to find some that are ripe but firm!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces feta cheese, thinly sliced or crumbled
ingredients.name: feta cheese, thinly sliced or crumbled

preparationSteps: We’re going to start by making our herby marinade and sauce! Peel and thinly slice 1 shallot (crosswise — so into rounds). Reserve half of the slices for later, and add the other half to a blender along with 1 teaspoon cumin, a pinch of kosher salt, a few grinds of black pepper, and 2 packed cups of arugula or leafy green herbs.
Use a microplane or box grater to zest 1 lemon and set the zest aside for later.

Add the juice from half that lemon to the blender then press pulse a few times until everything is coarsely chopped (AKA chopped but still chunky). Now you’re going to turn the blender on low speed and, through the pour spout, slowly pour in 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil. Once all of the oil is added and it’s well combined, turn the blender off and taste it. Does it taste dull? If so, add another big pinch of kosher salt and pepper and blend again for a few seconds. Repeat until it tastes punchy and delicious!

Add 1/4 cup of the herb sauce (just eyeball it!) to a medium bowl along with 1 1/2 pounds large peeled and deveined shrimp and stir to combine. Set the shrimp aside to marinate at room temp while you make the salad and couscous.

Time for some chopping/slicing. Cut 2 mini seedless cucumbers (or 1 English cucumber) in half lengthwise, then cut each half in half again, so you end up with 4 long quarters. Line them up side by side and slice them into 1/2-inch pieces. Add the chopped cucumber to a medium bowl. Cut 2 peaches into 1/2-inch slices, halve 1/2 pint of cherry tomatoes, and add them to the bowl along with the reserved shallot slices. Add the juice from the other half of the lemon, 4 ounces of sliced feta, and 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil and stir to combine. Season to taste with salt and pepper and set aside.

In a medium saucepan, bring 1 1/2 cups water, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt to a boil over high heat. As soon as the water is boiling (it won’t take long!), remove the pot from heat, stir in 1 1/2 cups couscous (one 10-ounce box), cover the pot (use a sheet pan if you don’t have a lid), and set it aside to steam while you cook the shrimp.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side or until pink, opaque, and curled into a U-shape, not a C-shape. Taste one. Do they need more salt? Salt ‘em, if so!
Fluff the couscous with a fork and toss with the reserved lemon zest and remaining 1 cup of arugula (or herbs). Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve the couscous topped with salad and shrimp. Drizzle it all with herb sauce and dig in!!

name: chicken, mushroom, and farro soup
note:
Make it in your slow cooker: Add the chopped veggies (not the greens yet) then the farro then the chicken, herbs, and spices on top. Cover with stock. Start with 6 cups liquid — add more if needed to ensure the chicken's totally submerged. Cook on low for 6 hours then remove chicken to shred. Add the shredded chicken back in with the chopped greens, 1/2 lemon juice, and creamy ingredient (if using). Stir and cook for another 30 minutes, then taste and adust seasonings as needed.

Vegetarian: Instead of chicken, add 2 cans of drained white beans — cannellini, navy, or chickpeas would all be great. You could also swap the chicken out for lentils, either 2 cans cooked lentils or 1 cup dried. If using dried, add 2 more cups of stock because they’ll absorb a lot of the liquid. Swap chicken stock for veggie stock too.

Love your leftovers/stock the freezer: This makes a huge pot of soup! Leftovers will be good in the fridge for up to 4 days. It will thicken as it sits — add more stock or water to loosen it up if it gets too thick. You can also stock the freezer with your leftovers. Freeze the soup in quart-sized Ziploc bags. Fill then lay the bags on a sheet pan and stick the pan in the freezer. Once they’re frozen, take them off — they’ll be nice, flat, and easy to store.

Double it: It’s an easy recipe to double, but you’ll need an extra large pot!

Feeding picky eaters/I don’t want the greens: If you’re feeding kids (or adults) who won’t touch anything green, you can omit the kale. I always add greens because I love how they soak up the sauce, get tender and delicious, and add a bunch of extra nutrients. It’s like eating a soup and salad! But the greens are not necessary so feel free to leave it out. If you’re kids won’t touch soup (like my big boys), when you pull out the chicken to shred it, cut up a few pieces for their plate, and serve them chicken + whatever veggie they will eat, while you get to enjoy your soup. My two-year-old LOVES this soup, I just served it to him with less broth!

Gluten-free: Swap the farro out for wild or brown rice. You’ll need to simmer the soup for about 20 extra minutes as they take longer to cook.

Dairy-free: Simply leave out the creamy elements, or use a DF plain yogurt.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large leek, halved vertically and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: large leek, halved vertically and thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 sprigs fresh rosemary or 6 sprigs fresh thyme
ingredients.name: fresh rosemary or 6 sprigs fresh thyme

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 quarts (8 cups) low-sodium chicken stock (or 8 cups water + 3 tablespoons low-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or 8 cups water + 3 tablespoons low-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional to make it creamy: 1/3 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, 4 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/3 cup half and half, 1/3 cup plain yogurt
ingredients.name: Optional to make it creamy: 1/3 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, 4 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/3 cup half and half, 1/3 cup plain yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional:garlicky croutons, cheesy salty honey toast fromthe cookbook(p. 212), lots of Parm on top, freshly chopped parsley… (I love soup toppings! dumpster dive and find something fun to throw on there! chili crisp!), baguette with salted butter (my personal choice)
ingredients.name: Optional:garlicky croutons, cheesy salty honey toast fromthe cookbook(p. 212), lots of Parm on top, freshly chopped parsley… (I love soup toppings! dumpster dive and find something fun to throw on there! chili crisp!), baguette with salted butter (my personal choice)

preparationSteps: Wash and finely chop 4 carrots, 3 celery stalks, 1 leek, and 12 ounces of mushrooms, and mince 4 garlic cloves. Throw them in a large cold pot (off the heat) as you finish chopping them so they don’t overflow off your cutting board.

Once all your veggies are in the pot, drizzle everything with 2 tablespoons olive oil, add 1 teaspoon salt and several grinds of pepper, stir, and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 7 to 10 minutes, until everything is looking very tender and the liquid has all evaporated off. If your veggies look tender but there’s still a lot of liquid in the pot, crank the heat up to high and stir constantly until it’s evaporated.
Meanwhile, wash and chop 1 bunch of kale.

Trim any white fat off of 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, then add them to the pot along with 1 1/4 cups farro, 2 sprigs fresh rosemary (or 6 sprigs thyme), the chopped kale, and 8 cups chicken stock and bring it to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and place the lid on the pot so that it is just slightly ajar to allow for some evaporation, but not a lot. If you don’t have a lid for your pot, use a sheet pan!
Cook for 20 minutes.

Remove the lid, discard the herb sprigs (the leaves likely all fell off, that’s fine), and transfer the chicken thighs to the cutting board. Use two forks to shred the chicken, then return it to the pot. If the chicken isn’t shredding easily or isn’t fully cooked (it needs to be 165°F), just return it to the pot for a few more minutes of cook time.
Stir in the juice of 1/2 a lemon (to start — I always end up adding the juice of the full lemon because I love lemon flavor!).
Now you have two options: You can either taste your soup, adjust with more lemon, salt, and pepper as desired and be finished…

OR, YOU CAN GO CREAMY: Stir in any of the optional creamy additions listed above! Simmer for a few more minutes to let it incorporate and thicken. It might look curdled at first, but keep stirring! If you went the creamy route, now’s the time to taste and adjust with more seasoning (extra lemon juice, kosher salt, and/or black pepper) until it’s perfect.
Top your bowls with any optional toppings you’ve got and ENJOY!

NOTE: As your soup sits in the pot or in the refrigerator, the farro and chicken will soak up the stock! When you reheat it the next day (or even hours later) stir in more stock to make it brothy again.

ingredients.name: fresh minced oregano leaves or 1 teaspoon dried oregano

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Trim two inches off the bottom of 1 pound asparagus, then cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces. Thinly slice 1 large shallot.

Add the asparagus and shallot to your largest rimmed sheet pan along with 1 pound gnocchi (nope, you don’t have to cook it first!), 4 ounces diced pancetta, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon fresh minced oregano leaves (or 1 teaspoon dried oregano), 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. name: one-skillet steak and crispy smashed potatoes
note:
It’s impossible to get a great sear with a nonstick skillet since, by nature, they are built to NOT let food stick (sear) to them! Use a cast iron or stainless steel pan.

Season your steaks the second you get home from the store, if you can! The longer they’re seasoned, the more delicious they’ll be.

You can use any cut of steak, just use that meat thermometer and pull it off when it’s finished! A New York Strip is a great option, but it will cook faster!

Try using mushrooms instead of potatoes! Same cooking method (including smashed them with the bottom of the bowl!), but they’ll take longer to cook. Don’t add the steak juices to the skillet until the mushrooms have released all of their moisture, and it has evaporated.

Want some greens? After you finish cooking the potatoes, add 4 cups of spinach to the pan and wilt them (aka use tongs to toss them until they’re wilted and the liquid has mostly evaporated) over medium heat with the juice of 1/2 a lemon.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1 to 1/2 pound) 1 1/2 to 2-inch thick boneless ribeye steak
ingredients.name: 1 1/2 to 2-inch thick boneless ribeye steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds baby Dutch yellow potatoes (or other small - golf-ball-ish sized potato)
ingredients.name: baby Dutch yellow potatoes (or other small - golf-ball-ish sized potato)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or other neutral cooking oil such as vegetable or canola), plus 2 teaspoons
ingredients.name: olive oil (or other neutral cooking oil such as vegetable or canola), plus 2 teaspoons

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 fresh rosemary sprigs and/or 4 fresh thyme sprigs
ingredients.name: fresh rosemary sprigs and/or 4 fresh thyme sprigs

preparationSteps: Season 1 large boneless ribeye steak aggressively with salt and pepper and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. What does “aggressive” mean? I like to use 1 teaspoon of salt per 1 pound of meat, and about 1/4 teaspoon black pepper (if I’m using pepper! You don’t ALWAYS have to use pepper!).

Allow the steaks to come to room temperature for at least 10 minutes, but up to 1 hour. Meanwhile, add 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes to a large heatproof bowl and add 2 tablespoons water to the bowl. Cover the bowl with a plate, and microwave for 7 minutes. Poke the potatoes with a fork. They should be very tender! If they’re not, microwave for another minute at a time until totally tender. Let the potatoes cool down completely - throw them in the fridge if you’re tight on time.

Warm a 12-inch skillet (preferably cast iron, and NOT nonstick if you can help it) over medium-high heat for three minutes. Add 1 tablespoon oil and warm until it just begins to smoke. Carefully add the ribeye steak into the skillet, then add 4 smashed garlic cloves and fresh herb sprigs on either side of the steak.

Cook the steak for 3 to 5 minutes, until a nice golden-brown sear forms. Flip it, and add 2 tablespoons butter to the pan. Continue cooking for an additional 3 to 5 minutes, basting it with the melted butter the entire time by tilting the skillet to one side and spooning the butter over top of the steak.

For medium-rare, stop cooking your steak when it reaches 125°F internally. Medium, 135°F. But a good, fatty steak like a ribeye should really be enjoyed medium-rare! A good indicator that your steak is finished cooking is when the juices begin to rise on the surface of the steak. The fat will also puff up a bit. You’ll see what I mean!

Transfer the steak to a plate and pour the butter, garlic, and herbs over top. Don’t you dare slice into that steak until the potatoes are finished cooking! It needs to rest so that the juices can redistribute through the meat.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat and warm 2 teaspoons oil for 30 seconds. Add the potatoes to the skillet in a single layer and use the bottom of the bowl you cooked them in to smash them lightly. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then flip and pour all of the juices that have collected under the steak into the skillet along with the remaining 1 tablespoon butter and cook for an additional 3 minutes, until crispy. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Turn off the heat.

Slice the steak into 1/2-inch thick slices. This is not one to slice super thin - you want nice, thick, juicy slices. Divide the steak and potatoes between two plates, garnish with a hit of finely chopped parsley if you’ve got it (I’m not gonna make you buy parsley just for a little garnish, but if you have it, use it!). ENJOY!

name: show off-y greek salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 2 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts (you’ll probably have leftovers but they’re so good!!!)
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts (you’ll probably have leftovers but they’re so good!!!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces cherry tomatoes or 1 large heirloom tomato
ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes or 1 large heirloom tomato

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 packed cup fresh dill fronds (AKA leaves)
ingredients.name: packed cup fresh dill fronds (AKA leaves)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8 ounce) block of feta in brine (not crumbled feta!!!)
ingredients.name: of feta in brine (not crumbled feta!!!)

preparationSteps: First, let’s marinate the chicken! In a large Tupperware container or ziplock bag, combine 2 to 2 1/2 pounds chicken breasts, 1/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon Greek seasoning, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder. Get in there with your hands and make sure everything is evenly coated. Refrigerate for up to 4 hours, or leave at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Now let’s make the vinaigrette. In a jar with a tight-fitting lid (or a bowl, if you don’t have a jar), combine 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup red wine vinegar, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1 teaspoon honey, 1 teaspoon Greek seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon  salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. (If you have a jar, you can shake it until it’s well combined; if using a bowl, whisk it.) Set aside.

Now we have some chopping to do! Chop 1 cucumber, 1 red bell pepper, 1 orange bell pepper, and 10 ounces cherry or heirloom tomatoes in half or into bite-sized pieces (use a serrated knife for tomatoes!). Thinly slice 1 small red onion. Roughly chop 1/2 cup kalamata olives, 1/3 cup fresh mint leaves, and 1/3 cup fresh dill fronds.

Toss all of the vegetables and most of the herbs (leave a bit of each herb out for garnish) into a large bowl with about half of the dressing to start marinating the vegetables (don’t add salt yet, as it will make the vegetables release a lot of liquid). Throw the bowl in the refrigerator.
Preheat your grill to medium-high heat (400 to 450°F).

Cut 1 block of feta into 8 slices. If you’ve got the time, shingle it on a small plate and zhuzh it up with a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil, a drizzle of honey, a sprinkle of chopped herbs, and a sprinkle of Greek seasoning. This is totally unnecessary — just show off-y.
Use the serrated knife to slice 4 thick slices of sourdough. Throw it on a plate and drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
Now let’s head out to the grill (see the notes section below if you’re using an oven)! Head outside with the chicken, the bread, a pair of tongs, and a spatula.

Cook the chicken breasts for 4 to 5 minutes per side (if using chicken thighs, cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side), or until 160°F internally (breasts have so little fat that they will continue cooking after you pull them off to reach 165°F) internally. Check all of the chicken breasts, not just one! Transfer the chicken to a plate and allow it to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Grill the bread (with the lid open) for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until dark grill marks appear.
Thinly slice the chicken. Garnish with fresh herbs if you’re showing off. Season the salad with 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt. Taste. Add more salt and dressing as desired.
Let everyone build their perfect plate!

name: sheet-pan chicken with cauliflower, butternut squash & brown butter sage vinaigrette

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 ½ pounds cubed butternut squash (Use pre-cubed if you can find it! If not, buy a 1 ½-pound butternut squash, peeled and cubed)
ingredients.name: cubed butternut squash (Use pre-cubed if you can find it! If not, buy a 1 ½-pound butternut squash

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken leg quarters (about 2 1/2 pounds)
ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken leg quarters (about 2 1/2 pounds)

preparationSteps: Heat the oven to 425°F.

Cut 1 small head of cauliflower: Trim the leaves and the very bottom off, then slice it in half through the stem. Place the two halves cut-side-down on a cutting board, then slice them into 1/2 inch-thick pieces. Cut or pull apart the individual florets. If your 1 ½ pounds of cubed butternut squash is pre-cut into big cubes, cut them into smaller, roughly 1/2-inch cubes. (If you have a whole squash, peel it, slice it in half, remove the seeds, and cut it into 1/2-inch cubes.)
Transfer the cauliflower and squash to a sheet pan and toss with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Spread into an even layer.

In a big bowl, stir together the remaining 2 tablespoons oil, 2 teaspoons sweet paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 ½ teaspoons kosher salt, and a few grinds of pepper. Add 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken leg quarters to the bowl and toss to coat. Nestle the seasoned chicken (skin-side-up) in the vegetables. If your sheet pan is way too crowded, transfer half of the ingredients to a second baking sheet.

Roast until the chicken’s cooked through (I think chicken legs are more tender and tasty when they reach between 170 and 175°F internally, but they’re safe as soon as they hit 165°F) and the vegetables are tender, 35 to 40 minutes. If using two pans, place one on the middle rack and one on the rack below it. Switch them after 20 minutes.

While the chicken and veggies are roasting, add 8 tablespoons unsalted butter and 10 sage leaves to a small saucepan. Melt over medium heat, stirring until the butter looks and smells golden and toasty, 3 to 5 minutes. Turn off the heat. Use tongs or a fork to transfer the crispy sage to a paper towel, then carefully stir 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar into the butter. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Leave on your stovetop until ready to serve.
Plate up your chicken and veggies, pour some brown butter vinaigrette over top—like you would gravy!—and garnish with the crispy sage leaves. DIG IN!

name: creamy white turkey chili

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds ground turkey (get the highest fat percentage possible — 85% lean 15% fat is ideal, but 93% lean 7% fat will do!)
ingredients.name: ground turkey (get the highest fat percentage possible — 85% lean 15% fat is ideal, but 93% lean 7% fat will do!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 cups chicken broth (I use water + Better than Bouillon), divided
ingredients.name: chicken broth (I use water + Better than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces cream cheese (optional, the blended beans will already make it creamy if you want to make the chili dairy-free!)
ingredients.name: cream cheese (optional, the blended beans will already make it creamy if you want to make the chili dairy-free!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings: shredded cheese, sour cream, hot sauce, green onions, pickled jalapeños, tortilla chips…
ingredients.name: Optional toppings: shredded cheese, sour cream, hot sauce, green onions, pickled jalapeños, tortilla chips…

preparationSteps: Dice 1 large onion and mince 6 garlic cloves.

Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot, such as a Dutch oven, over medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring frequently, for 5 to 7 minutes, or until light golden brown.
Stir in 2 tablespoons chili powder, 1 tablespoon cumin, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, and 2 teaspoons garlic powder and continue cooking for another minute.
Add 2 pounds ground turkey and cook, breaking the meat into as small of crumbles as possible, until the turkey is cooked through.
Meanwhile, blend 1 can cannellini beans (don't drain it — dump the juices in the blender too) and 1 cup stock (I use Better than Bouillon, so I blend 1 cup water and 1 teaspoon BTB) until smooth.

Stir the blended beans, 1 jar salsa verde, 2 cans cannellini beans (drained), 1 cup chicken stock, and 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt into the pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes.

Remove the lid and stir in 1 1/2 cups frozen white corn, 2 cups chopped kale, and 4 ounces cream cheese. Stir until the cream cheese is combined, the kale is tender, and the chili has thickened to your liking, 4 to 5 additional minutes.
If you want it thicker, crank up the heat and stir until it's thickened to your liking. If it gets too thick, add more stock!

Stir in the juice of 1 lime and taste. Is it flavorful enough? All stock brands have different salt levels so I started small. Add more salt and seasonings (and Better than Bouillon!) until it's your perfect chili.
The chili will thicken as it sits, so if you make it in advance, you may have to stir in more stock to get it back to the right consistency.

name: souvla-inspired chicken salad
note:
Leftovers are a great thing:Chicken — With the leftover rotisserie chicken, make the green chicken tortilla soup I send last month. Just shred the leftovers (it’s easiest to shred while the chicken is still warm), store them in the fridge, then stir them in just before the soup is done! Pickled red onion — Make the chipotle black bean flautas or really any tacos, nachos, quesadillas, etc., and garnish with your leftover pickled red onions.Chives — Did you catch that note above about the chives? Chop ‘em all up and use them to brighten those beige-hued Thanksgiving dishes.This salad — If you have leftover salad, it’ll be delish for lunch or dinner the next day! Again, just add the nuts right before eating so they’re crunchy.

Chicken — With the leftover rotisserie chicken, make the green chicken tortilla soup I send last month. Just shred the leftovers (it’s easiest to shred while the chicken is still warm), store them in the fridge, then stir them in just before the soup is done!

Pickled red onion — Make the chipotle black bean flautas or really any tacos, nachos, quesadillas, etc., and garnish with your leftover pickled red onions.

Chives — Did you catch that note above about the chives? Chop ‘em all up and use them to brighten those beige-hued Thanksgiving dishes.

This salad — If you have leftover salad, it’ll be delish for lunch or dinner the next day! Again, just add the nuts right before eating so they’re crunchy.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium red onion, thinly sliced(here’s the proper way to slice an onion; you could also use a mandoline if you have one)
ingredients.name: medium red onion, thinly sliced(here’s the proper way to slice an onion; you could also use a mandoline if you have one)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons minced chives(Might I suggest going ahead and mincing the whole bunch you buy so that you can easily use them as garnish for beige Thanksgiving food?)
ingredients.name: minced chives(Might I suggest going ahead and mincing the whole bunch you buy so that you can easily use them as garnish for beige Thanksgiving food?)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head lacinato kale, deribbed and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: lacinato kale, deribbed and thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 fuyu persimmon (not hachiya — the tag on it will say), halved then thinly sliced
ingredients.name: fuyu persimmon (not hachiya — the tag on it will say), halved then thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup grated ricotta salata (the hard, not soft kind), cotija, or feta cheese
ingredients.name: grated ricotta salata (the hard, not soft kind), cotija, or feta cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds (or chopped walnuts or almonds)
ingredients.name: toasted pumpkin seeds (or chopped walnuts or almonds)

preparationSteps: Let’s kick things off by pickling our red onions. If you can, do this several hours (or days!) in advance. But even marinating them for 30 minutes will be delicious. Stuff 1 thinly sliced red onion in a jar along with 1/3 cup red wine vinegar, 2 teaspoons white sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt.

Fill the jar the rest of the way up with hot water. Shake the jar to combine everything. Set aside. (If you’ve made them way ahead of time, pop them in the fridge once the mixture has come to room temp.)

Now let’s make the Granch. In a Tupperware container or jar (because you’ll have leftover dressing), combine 3/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 2 lemons, 3 tablespoons minced chives, 1/2 teaspoon dried dill weed, 1 grated garlic clove, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Taste. Add additional salt and lemon juice if your tastebuds want it.

Onto the salad! Add 1 bunch of thinly sliced kale to a large bowl and sprinkle with a big pinch of kosher salt. Massage the kale by scrunching it together with your hands seven times, until softened slightly. Add 1 head thinly sliced romaine lettuce to the bowl and season the greens with salt and pepper.

Add 2 cups shredded chicken, 1 small thinly sliced fennel bulb, 1 chopped orange, 1 thinly sliced persimmon, 1/3 cup pea shoots or sprouts, 1/3 cup grated ricotta salata or crumbled cotija or feta cheese, and 1/3 cup of the pickled red onions.

Add 1/4 cup Granch dressing to the bowl to start, and tossy toss toss until all of the leaves are coated. If you’re like me, you like a very well dressed salad, so just keep adding until it’s the way ya like it. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.

Divide the salad between 4 bowls and top with a big sprinkle of toasted pepitas or really any nut. We’re adding the nuts to our individual bowls so that, if there are leftovers, there won’t be any nuts in there. They get all soggy and weird in the fridge.
DIG IN. Pretty damn delicious salad, amiright?
servings: Serves 4 (the leftovers are great for up to 24 hours)

name: kale caesar with crispy chewy croutons

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 slices of bread, preferably a nice crusty sourdough or something, but anything works, cut into small cubes
ingredients.name: of bread, preferably a nice crusty sourdough or something, but anything works

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounce chunk of Parmesan cheese, divided (this will be enough Parm to use for both the salad and the pasta alla vodka — if you’re just making the salad, you will only need a 4-ounce chunk)
ingredients.name: chunk of Parmesan cheese, divided (this will be enough Parm to use for both the salad and the pasta alla vodka — if you’re just making the salad, you will only need a 4-ounce chunk)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 small garlic cloves, smashed with the side of a knife
ingredients.name: small garlic cloves, smashed with the side of a knife

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 hearts of romaine lettuce, trimmed, washed, dried, and cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: hearts of romaine lettuce, trimmed, washed, dried, and cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: lacinato kale, deribbed and cut into 1-inch pieces

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

On a parchment-lined baking sheet, toss 4 slices of cubed bread, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, a big pinch of salt, and a big pinch of garlic powder. Spread into an even layer and bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until crisp on the edges but still chewy in the center.

Blend the entire 8-ounce block of Parmesan cheese until finely grated. To do so, cut the rind off (save the rind in the freezer for future cooking), cut it into a few chunks, and blend until it’s grated into a powdery consistency. Once grated, transfer all but 1/4 cup of the Parm into a bowl for later use.

To make the dressing, blend everything up except the lettuces (1/4 cup grated Parmesan, 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup mayonnaise, the juice of 2 lemons, 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar, 2 small smashed garlic cloves, 6 anchovy fillets, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper). Use 6 anchovies at first — blend in up to 2 more if you want more anchovy flavor.

Put the chopped greens (2 hearts of romaine lettuce and 1 bunch lacinato kale) and the baked croutons in a large bowl and drizzle nearly all of the dressing over it. Use your hands to mix everything together, making sure each and every piece of lettuce is coated with dressing. After tossing, sprinkle 1/4 cup of grated Parmesan on top.
Enjoy!

name: pasta alla vodka
note:
Make ahead: To make the sauce ahead of time (up to 72 hours), you can go ahead and do everything except for adding the pasta cooking water. When it’s dinner time, reheat the sauce over medium heat, cook your pasta, and stir in the pasta cooking water then the cooked pasta. See more prep-ahead notes in the “main event” section of my NYE menu above!

Stock your freezer: This vodka sauce freezes beautifully. Double the recipe and freeze half for later! Let it cool completely (but don’t leave it out for more than 4 hours, since it’s cream-based), then put it in a Ziploc bag or freezable container and store it in the freezer for 3-6 months. When you’re ready to cook it, you can put the frozen sauce in the fridge to thaw overnight, then stir it in a large pot over medium heat to rewarm. Stir in the pasta and pasta cooking water and enjoy! If you forgot or are pressed for time, you can also just throw the frozen sauce in a large pot with a splash of water, cover, and cook on medium until it’s warm, whisking occasionally. Caesar dressing won’t freeze well, FYI, so plan to use any extra in the coming week. If it thickens too much in the fridge, just stir splashes of warm water in until it’s back to a drizzly consistency.

Cooking for one or two: Make the entire batch of sauce and freeze half! Cook only 8 ounces of pasta, drain, then return it to the pot you cooked it in. Add about half of the sauce to the pot with several tablespoons of pasta cooking water, until it’s clinging to each piece of pasta and is as saucy as you want it. For the salad, simply halve the recipe.

Vegetarian: Use 3 tablespoons of capers instead of anchovies in the Caesar dressing.

Dairy-free: Use your favorite vegan Parm throughout both recipes. For the pasta, opt for plant-based butter. You could also swap in coconut cream, soy milk, or almond milk for the heavy cream.

Gluten-free: Find a gluten-free bread you love for the croutons! And any gluten-free noodle alternative (like Banza chickpea noodles) would be delish with this vodka sauce.

Must have meat: Grilled chicken or shrimp would be excellent mixed into your pasta alla vodka. Or, like we’re doing on NYE, serve the pasta and salad alongside whatever meat entrée you’d like. See the NYE menu section above for ideas!

Don’t want a side salad: If you’re cooking this on a weeknight and want a veggie but not a whole side salad, throw some sautéed asparagus and/or mushrooms into the pasta alla vodka.

ingredients.name: tubular pasta, such as paccheri (my fave), rigatoni giganti (pictured), penne, fusilli, or rigatoni

ingredients.name: tomato paste (or a heaping 1/2 cup)

ingredients.name: crushed red pepper flakes (this does add a bit of heat so omit or lessen for a spice averse crowd)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan, plus more for serving (this will come from the 8-ounce block of Parm you grated for the Caesar salad recipe. If you’re making this pasta recipe and NOT the Caesar, you’ll buy and grate a 4-ounce block of Parmesan.)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan, plus more for serving (this will come from the 8-ounce block of Parm you grated for the Caesar salad recipe. If you’re making this pasta recipe and NOT the Caesar, you’ll buy and grate a 4-ounce block of Parmesan.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Thinly sliced fresh basil, for serving
ingredients.name: Thinly sliced fresh basil, for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water (2 tablespoons of kosher salt in the water is my general rule of thumb!) to a boil and cook 1 pound of tubular pasta until al dente (read the box to find your pasta’s ideal cook time!). **RESERVE 2 CUPS OF THE COOKING LIQUID BEFORE YOU DRAIN THE PASTA!! I’M YELLING AT YOU BECAUSE EVERYONE ALWAYS FORGETS TO DO THIS AND IT’S VERY IMPORTANT!** Once you’ve reserved 2 cups cooking liquid, drain the pasta and set aside (don’t rinse it! It’s fine if it looks like it’s clumping together!).
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt 2 tablespoons unsalted butter. Cook 1 minced shallot, 4 minced garlic cloves and a big pinch of salt until softened, 4 to 5 minutes.

Stir in 6 ounces tomato paste and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes and continue cooking until the paste and shallots have combined into a nice chunky paste, and it is turning a nice deep red color, 3 to 4 minutes.

Stir in 1/4 cup vodka and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently. Stir in 1 1/2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup pasta cooking liquid, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan, and 1 big pinch of salt until smooth. You might need to use a whisk to get any clumps out. Stir in the cooked pasta and a small amount of pasta cooking liquid. Add more cooking liquid a splash at a time as needed for the sauce to be very thick and cling to each noodle perfectly (I usually use between 1/2 cup and 3/4 cup). Taste and season with kosher salt as needed.
Serve and garnish with thinly sliced fresh basil and more grated Parmesan.

name: beef bulgogi bowls
note:
Vegetarian: Press a block of drained tofu between paper towels or dish towels,  cut it into small cubes, marinate it in the same marinade as written, and cook on the skillet over medium-high heat in sesame oil until crispy all over.

Gimme a shortcut: Go with microwaveable steam-in-bag rice! Look for thinly sliced beef at the store, or ask the butcher to do it.

Prep ahead: This is a great make-ahead meal! You can quickly freeze the beef (to harden), slice it, then pop it in a Ziploc bag with the marinade for up to 24 hours (stored in the fridge). The rice can also be made ahead of time, refrigerated, then reheated on the stove or in the microwave right before dinner.

Leftovers are a great thing: Two ideas for your bulgogi leftovers! First, make sandwiches (see the note at the bottom of the recipe for a how-to!). Or, make lettuce wraps, filling leaves of bibb, iceberg, or little gem lettuce with leftover beef, rice, kimchi, and toppings. You could also halve the recipe if you don’t want leftovers.

Df/gf: It’s already dairy free! If you’re avoiding gluten, check your soy sauce. Coconut aminos are a gf sub if it does indeed include gluten (some soy sauces do!). Also, use sriracha in lieu of gochujang, or look for a brand of gochujang that’s gluten free as most contain it.

ingredients.name: sesame oil, plus more for cooking

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons gochujang (Korean chili paste) or sriracha
ingredients.name: gochujang (Korean chili paste) or sriracha

ingredients.name: garlic powder or 2 grated or minced garlic cloves
