ingredients.name: ribeye beef (We are going to slice this really thinly — sometimes stores carry it thinly sliced or the butcher will do it for you. Ask! And don’t forget to check the subs section below for lots of other ideas.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup mayonnaise (whatever kind ya like, there are versions for all dietary restrictions)
ingredients.name: mayonnaise (whatever kind ya like, there are versions for all dietary restrictions)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kimchi (this one is crucial, in my opinion!)
ingredients.name: Kimchi (this one is crucial, in my opinion!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: The sky is the limit!! Let us know what you come up with in the comments :)
ingredients.name: The sky is the limit!! Let us know what you come up with in the comments :)

preparationSteps: First up, let’s throw the beef in the freezer for a few minutes. This will make it easier to slice thinly!

In a large bowl, stir together 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons sesame oil, 2 tablespoons gochujang, 1 tablespoon rice wine vinegar, 2 teaspoons sugar, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder. If you have them, throw a couple teaspoons of sesame seeds in here as well.

Grab your frozen beef out of the freezer and slice it into 1/8-inch thin slices. Toss it into the marinade until coated, then set aside. (If you’re prepping ahead, store it in a Ziploc bag in the fridge for up to 24 hours before you’re ready to cook.)

Start by rinsing and cooking the rice: Add 2 cups dry sushi rice to a large saucepan (or whatever you use to cook rice) and cover with water. Use your hand to slosh the water and rice around then carefully drain off the water. There’s no real technique here — just hold your hand over the pot so that the rice doesn’t fall into the drain along with the water. Repeat this process until the water is no longer murky.

Add 2 1/2 cups water to the saucepan and bring it to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and cover the pot for 15 to 17 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat, leave the lid on, and let the rice continue to steam for 10 minutes. Gently stir in a big pinch of salt and sesame seeds (if you have them) before serving.

Make the spicy mayo by stirring 1/3 cup mayo, 1 tablespoon gochujang or sriracha, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl. Taste and add more gochujang or sriracha if you want more heat!

When you’re about 5 minutes from being ready to eat, cook the beef! Grab your largest skillet (cast iron, nonstick, whatever, just the biggest one), and heat it over high heat. Add 1 tablespoon sesame oil once the skillet is really hot, and swirl to coat the pan. Drain as much of the marinade off of the beef as you can (but don’t stress if the beef is still damp), then add the beef in a single layer to the skillet. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side — until JUST cooked through (a little pink is A-OK!) and transfer to a serving bowl.
Pile the rice, beef, kimchi, and whatever toppings you like into a bowl. Drizzle with spicy mayo and sprinkle sesame seeds over top. Dig in!
Or: Make sandwiches! Spread the mayo on both sides of a baguette and pile the beef, kimchi, and some cilantro inside.

name: crispy bean burritos
note:
Make ahead: Roll the burritos up the 24 hours in advance, then crisp them up when you’re ready to eat! Start warming your oil and skillet 10 to 15 minutes before mealtime.

Stock your freezer: After rolling the burritos, individually roll them tightly in a square of tinfoil and freeze! To cook in the oven, place the entire foil-wrapped burrito on a baking sheet in a 375°F oven for 20 minutes or until warmed through. To microwave, remove the foil and place on a microwave-safe plate. Microwave for 2 minutes, flip over, and microwave for an additional 1 minute.

Send some to a friend for dinner: Roll each burrito tightly in foil, and instruct your friends to reheat in a 400°F oven for 10 minutes. Deliver the burritos with lots of dippy things!

Make burrito bowls: If you don’t want leftover burritos, you could roll up half of the rice and bean mixture into tortillas and keep the other half in the fridge to make burrito bowl lunches throughout the week. Burrito bowls are also a good alternative to burritos if you 1) are avoiding gluten, 2) couldn’t find good, soft tortillas, or 3) want to save time/skip the burrito rolling step. Start with the rice and bean mixture as your base and top with whatever you have on hand and love! Options include: shredded cheese, diced avocado, pico de gallo, pickled onions, shredded lettuce, and/or any of your desired dippy things.

If you have leftover chipotle peppers en adobo in the fridge or freezer from this or that: Chop one up and add it to the pot when you add your rice and stock! Remember to remove the seeds if your family is spice-averse.

Must have meat: Add 1/2 pound of any ground meat to the skillet when cooking the onions. Or, when you add the lime and cilantro at the end, stir in 1 or 2 cups of shredded rotisserie chicken. Or take whatever leftover meat you have in the fridge and add that to your burritos!

Gimme extra greens: Stir a handful of chopped spinach into the rice and bean mixture after it sits covered for 10 minutes. It’ll wilt right in.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: To skip dairy, omit the cheese or sub your favorite plant-based alternative. It’ll be delish! Siete Foods has burrito-sized grain-free tortillas that would be a perfect sub for this if you’re avoiding gluten. You could also go the burrito bowl route. (FYI, corn tortillas don’t have the pliability we need for burritos, so don’t try them!)

ingredients.name: Optional dippy things: sour cream or plain yogurt (I like to stir in some lime juice, hot sauce, and a pinch of salt), salsas, mashed avocado

preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoon olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add 1 diced onion, 1 diced bell pepper, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 2 teaspoons taco seasoning. Sauté until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in 3/4 cup white rice, 1 can drained and rinsed beans, 1 1/3 cups stock, and 1/3 cup salsa (if using), and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 18 minutes. Remove from heat and let it continue to sit, covered, for an additional 10 minutes.

In the meantime, warm up 8 tortillas (or 4) in the microwave for 30 seconds, or until very pliable and easy to bend without tearing. Lay them out, then sprinkle your desired amount of cheese in a line down the center of each tortilla.

Stir 1/4 cup cilantro (if using) and the juice of 1 lime into the rice and beans. Scoop 1/2 heaping cup of rice and beans over top of the cheese on each tortilla if using 8-inch tortillas OR 1 heaping cup of rice and beans if using burrito-size tortillas.
Roll up the burritos. They are ready to eat now, OR you can crisp them up, which I highly recommend if you were not able to find fresh tortillas.
If you’re going to crisp your burritos: warm your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 teaspoon oil and swirl to coat the skillet.
Place 3 to 4 burritos in the skillet, seam-side down, for about 3 minutes, or until golden-brown. Cook on all sides until golden and crispy. Repeat as needed with remaining burritos.
Serve alongside your desired dippy things!
servings: Makes 8 baby burritos or 4 big ole taqueria-style burritos

name: pork marbella with couscous
note:
Feeding toddlers: My cousin Marlea inspired me to develop a WTC version of Marbella. She has three young boys who can be picky and says they all devour Chicken Marbella. She cuts the chicken up into bites and puts them in one pile, a few prunes in one pile, and a couple olives in another pile. She likes to make hers with orzo which would also be easier for toddlers to scoop up than couscous. Best of luck to all of you! P.S. Yes, it’s safe to serve children food cooked in wine! The alcohol will be cooked out of it while it’s in the oven.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the searing step entirely and just put the pork tenderloins and all of the ingredients up until the butter in a baking dish and cook for 25-35 minutes. It’ll be great and a lot simpler.

Prep ahead: This is an excellent meal to prep earlier in the day — or even the day before — so that you can just pop it in the oven before dinner. See the “dinner party king” section in the introduction above for specific notes on timing!

Love your leftovers: I can confirm that pork marbella leftovers make an amazing next-day(s) salad. Throw the pork, olives, prunes, etc. (either warmed or cool) over greens with leftover couscous or whatever grain you have in the house, add some crumbled feta or goat cheese if you have it, some nuts that you love (pistachios would be phenomenal), and a vinaigrette. Delish. You could also chop up any leftover pork and throw it into 15-minute peanut noods tomorrow for lunch! The cooked pork will stay good in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. You can also freeze your leftovers, thaw, and reheat them weeks or months from now. Reheat them in a 325°F oven just until the meat is warmed through (don’t overcook it or the meat will dry out!).

Halve it: This is also an easy recipe to halve, if you’re feeding one or two and don’t want lots of leftovers. Only cook one pork tenderloin — and halve the rest of the ingredients — and freeze the other!

Vegetarian: Sub the pork out for 4 to 6 portabella mushroom caps. Or two cans of drained and rinsed chickpeas! Or a combination of both! Sauté the fennel and garlic as written, then add the mushrooms (and/or chickpeas) to the skillet along with the other ingredients. You won’t have to cook as long — 30 minutes should be plenty.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use plant-based butter if cutting dairy. To make this meal gluten-free, swap the couscous for rice (cook it per package instructions) or another gf grain.

Riff options:Pork and Apples: Omit the capers and olives, use apple cider vinegar, use dates instead of prunes, and add 1 large thinly sliced Honeycrisp apple when you add the fennel. Pork Tagine: Remember our chicken tagine? Let’s recreate those vibes by omitting the prunes and capers, and adding in 1 cup of halved dried apricots and 1 cup of halved dates. Use chicken stock instead of wine, and add in a big pinch of paprika, cumin, and ginger instead of the oregano.

Pork and Apples: Omit the capers and olives, use apple cider vinegar, use dates instead of prunes, and add 1 large thinly sliced Honeycrisp apple when you add the fennel.

Pork Tagine: Remember our chicken tagine? Let’s recreate those vibes by omitting the prunes and capers, and adding in 1 cup of halved dried apricots and 1 cup of halved dates. Use chicken stock instead of wine, and add in a big pinch of paprika, cumin, and ginger instead of the oregano.

ingredients.name: *not pork loin*

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups white wine (it truly does not matter which kind, get something you’ll enjoy drinking the rest of!)
ingredients.name: white wine (it truly does not matter which kind, get something you’ll enjoy drinking the rest of!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup red wine or balsamic vinegar
ingredients.name: red wine or balsamic vinegar

ingredients.name: couscous (NOT *Israeli* couscous, which is actually a type of pasta! If you buy that accidentally just cook it per package instructions, it’ll be great too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley (or cilantro), finely chopped, divided
ingredients.name: chopped fresh parsley (or cilantro), finely chopped

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Pat 2 pork tenderloins dry and season all over with nice big pinches of kosher salt and black pepper.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a 12-inch braiser, skillet, or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the tenderloins on the first side for 3 to 4 minutes, until a nice golden-brown crust forms, then flip. Add 1 thinly sliced fennel bulb and 4 minced garlic cloves to the pan and use your tongs to stir them around while the pork sears on the second side. When the second side has a nice crust (after another 3 to 4 minutes), remove the skillet from heat.
To the skillet, add 1 1/2 cups white wine, 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1 cup halved prunes, 1 cup olives, 1 drained container of capers, and 4 bay leaves.
Place the skillet in the oven (WITHOUT a lid!) and roast for 25 to 35 minutes, until an internal thermometer inserted into the pork registers 140°F.

Transfer the pork to a cutting board (don’t slice it yet — it needs to rest or its juices will all just run out the second you slice it!) and place the skillet on the stove over medium-high. Stir in 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.

While the sauce is reducing, cook the couscous by bringing 1 1/3 cup chicken stock or water and 2 tablespoons butter to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat. Remove the pot from the heat, stir in 1 cup of couscous, 2 tablespoons finely chopped parsley, and a big pinch of salt, cover, and leave it to sit until you’re ready to serve dinner.

Once your sauce and couscous are ready, slice the pork tenderloin into 1/4-inch thick pieces. Arrange the slices on a platter or directly on your family’s plates. Spoon the sauce along with the prunes, olives, etc., over top of the pork. Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of parsley over top.
Serve the pork over couscous.

name: one-pot sausage and corn pasta
note:
Freeze it: Make the entire batch even if you’re only serving two. Freeze individual (or double) portions in quart ziplocks, and have a microwaveable pasta party at your fingertips on a night when you don’t feel like cooking! I always microwave frozen food in 45 second increments until warmed through.

Gimme some greens! Skip the side salad and throw some greens in the pasta. Add 3 cups of chopped kale to the pot along with the corn, tomato paste, tomatoes, etc., OR 4 cups chopped spinach when you add the mascarpone. Boom — extra nutrients made easy.

I’m a vegetarian: You can simply omit the sausage, or use 1 pound of sliced white or baby bella mushrooms in lieu of sausage. Sauté the mushrooms in 2 tablespoons of oil, cooking for roughly 8 minutes over medium-high until they’re browned and tender. Continue cooking recipe as written. Further bulk up the meal by adding kale or spinach (see “gimme some greens” note above for the how to).

Gluten-free: Do not — I repeat DO NOT! — try making a one-pot pasta dish using a gluten-free, chickpea, black bean, or other noodle substitute (especially not chickpea!). It’ll be gross. Here’s what you’ll do instead: Cook the pasta by itself according to package instructions, reserving 1/4 cup of pasta water before draining. Do not add the 4 1/2 cups of water to the sauce pot. Cook the sausage, then add the tomatoes and other ingredients and cook over medium-high until saucy. Stir in the mascarpone and basil, season, then toss in the pasta and 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta cooking water. Adjust seasoning to taste.

More corn pasta, plz: Hooked on summer corn like me? If you’ve got my cookbook, Just Married, and love this recipe, check out my “Creamy Corn Pasta” on page 161 and add it to your list of summer faves.

Leftovers are a good thing: Again, this recipe can be halved easily. But it makes for a DELICIOUS lunch, so don’t shy away from having extra. If you have a lot of leftovers, grease up a baking dish and throw the leftover pasta in there. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese over top and cover with foil. Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for 10 more minutes. Boom, summer baked ziti sich.

Dairy-free: Use dairy-free cream cheese instead of the mascarpone, DF parmesan, and skip the mozzarella.

Make ahead: This dish comes together in no time — it’s the perfect weeknight meal. But make it even quicker by cutting the kernels off your corn, halving the tomatoes and mozzarella balls, and slicing your garlic up to a day in advance. In fact, you can add all of the ingredients to the pot up to 24 hours in advance and keep it in the fridge until go time, but add the water right before cooking.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound dried rigatoni pasta (no you cannot just swap in GF pasta — read the notes)
ingredients.name: dried rigatoni pasta (no you cannot just swap in GF pasta — read the notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kernels from 4 ears of white corn (or 2 cups frozen white corn)
ingredients.name: Kernels from 4 ears of white corn (or 2 cups frozen white corn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces ciliegine mozzarella balls (the little ones)
ingredients.name: ciliegine mozzarella balls (the little ones)

preparationSteps: Heat a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound ground sausage to the pot and break it up into small crumbles with a spatula. Continue cooking until almost cooked through. Turn off the heat.

Add 1 pound dried rigatoni, 1 pound halved cherry tomatoes, 1 (6-ounce) can of tomato paste, the corn kernels cut off of 4 ears of corn, 6 thinly sliced garlic cloves, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes to the pot.

Pour 4 1/2 cups water into the pot and bring it to a boil over high heat. Don’t worry about trying to stir the tomato paste in — once the water is hot it’ll melt down into it easily. Reduce the heat to medium-high and simmer, uncovered, until the pasta has cooked through and the sauce has reduced so that there’s only about 1/2 cup of liquid remaining in the pot. Stir often. This will take roughly 9 to 12 minutes depending on the pasta you use.

Stir in 8 ounces of mascarpone cheese, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese and 2 cups of thinly sliced basil leaves until there’s a nice thick sauce coating the pasta. Taste and stir in more salt as needed. I always need more salt, but I love salt. Stir in 8 ounces halved ciliegine mozzarella balls just before serving. If you don’t plan on eating the entire pot of pasta, don’t add the mozzarella to the pot, just add a handful to each bowl. (They harden up and get yucky if they get hot and then cool down).
Serve it up and devour!
servings: Serves 4 to 6 (but it can be halved perfectly!)

name: 30-minute carnitas tacos
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy guacamole to use instead of the crema and skip the pickled red onions and buy pickled jalapeños instead. Easy!

Vegetarian: Swap the pork for 1 1/2 pound of mushrooms — ideally chanterelle, which will have a similar meaty texture. But chopped baby Bellas or white mushrooms would be great too. You’ll cook them the exact same way as the pork, but add 1/2 teaspoon chili powder and 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano.

Df/gf: For dairy-free, use df sour cream for the crema and of course skip the cheese. And for gluten-free, opt for corn tortillas.

Whole30: Use guacamole instead of the crema and don’t add cheese. For the pickled onions, swap the sugar for 1 to 2 tablespoons of lemon juice. And eat your carnitas in lettuce wraps or atop a bed of fresh greens.

Make ahead: Make the pickled red onions up to two weeks in advance, and the avocado crema up to 24 hours in advance (cover it tightly so it doesn’t brown). Cook the carnitas right at dinner time, but you can cut up the meat, jalapeño, and garlic up to 48 hours in advance.

Leftovers are a great thing: Be sure to read the intro up top for serving ideas for lunches this week! You can also freeze any leftover carnitas meat for future dinners. With the leftover half of a jalapeno, make spicy eggs! Mince the other half of the jalapeño and sauté it plus a bit of chopped onion in oil or butter over medium heat, then stir in 4 whisked eggs. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in some cheese and cilantro at the very end.

Feeding kids: It took a LOT of coaxing to get Mattis past the green flecks of cilantro in the carnitas. If your kids are weirdos too — scoop some meat out for them before adding the cilantro. Tacos are hard for my kids to handle still, so I just served them the meat with a cheese quesadilla and some broccoli.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup sour cream or Greek yogurt
ingredients.name: sour cream or Greek yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon neutral cooking oil (such as vegetable, avocado, or grapeseed)
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil (such as vegetable, avocado, or grapeseed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter (optional, but since pork tenderloin is so lean, it helps keep it moist!)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter (optional, but since pork tenderloin is so lean, it helps keep it moist!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Corn or flour tortillas, minced cilantro, Cotija cheese
ingredients.name: Corn or flour tortillas, minced cilantro, Cotija cheese

preparationSteps: Make the pickled red onions first — the night before ideally, but even 1 hour before dinner will be great. Combine 1 thinly sliced red onion, 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, 1/4 cup hot water, 1 tablespoon sugar, and a big pinch of salt in a jar or any container with a lid. Shake it up well so that the sugar and salt dissolve! Refrigerate for up to 2 months.

Then let’s make the avocado crema. In a bowl, mash 1 large avocado until completely smooth then stir in 1/4 cup sour cream, the juice of 1 lime, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/8 teaspoon garlic powder.
Cut 1 pound pork tenderloin into 1/2-inch pieces (about the size of your thumb nail).

Warm a large skillet over high heat for at least 3 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon oil and warm for an additional 30 seconds. Pat the pork completely dry, then carefully add it to the skillet in an even layer.

Season the pork with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper. Once the pork is browned on the first side, after about 3 minutes, stir in 1/2 jalapeño minced and 3 minced garlic cloves and continue stirring until the pork has browned all over, another 3 to 4 minutes. Using two forks, pull the pork apart as best you can to shred it a bit instead of having chunks.

Stir in the juice of 1 lime and the juice of 1 orange and continue stirring frequently until the juices have reduced and there’s almost no liquid in the skillet. Stir in 2 tablespoons minced fresh cilantro and 1 tablespoon butter (optional) and remove the skillet from the heat. Taste a piece of pork and adjust seasoning as needed.
Warm the tortillas (using one of the methods above) and fill with carnitas, avocado crema, minced cilantro, crumbled Cotija, and pickled red onions. Or just use your favorites of those! DIG IN.

name: lamb pita with dilly minty yogurt sauce
preparationSteps: Finely chop enough dill to get about 1/3 cup. Dice 2 large Roma tomatoes and thinly slice 1/2 head iceberg lettuce and 1 small red onion. Place them on a platter.

In a blender, add 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup dill leaves and tender stems, 1/4 cup mint leaves, the juice of 1/2 lemon, and a big pinch of salt and blend until smooth. If it’s too thick to drizzle, add a splash of water to loosen it up.

Now let’s make fresh pita! In a large bowl, combine 2 cups self-rising flour, 1 1/3 cups Greek yogurt, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Sprinkle a bit more flour over top and use your hands to combine the dough into a nice smooth ball. If it’s too dry, don’t worry! Just add more Greek yogurt a spoonful at a time until it’s moist enough to form into a smooth ball. It’ll get there! Sprinkle a light dusting of flour onto a clean surface, and smoosh it down into a flat circle. Cut it into 6 pieces (see image above for a visual). Roll each piece into a ball, then smoosh it flat and use a rolling pin (or wine bottle!) to roll it into a flat shape, about 8 inches across.

Now you’re gonna multitask a bit by cooking the pita while you cook the lamb. If that sounds scary, you can cook just one thing at a time. But multitasking will get dinner on the table faster. You can do this!

Warm your largest skillet (or griddle, if you have one) over medium heat for several minutes. Cook the pitas (a couple at a time, if you can fit them!) for about 3 minutes per side, until golden-brown all over. Transfer to a plate and keep them warm under foil. Repeat with remaining pitas.

Meanwhile, cook the lamb. Warm 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound ground lamb, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric. Stir, using a spatula to chop the meat up into tiny crumbles, until almost cooked through. Stir in 3 tablespoons of the chopped dill, 1/3 cup of the chopped tomatoes, 1 tablespoon tomato paste, and 3 tablespoons water and continue cooking until the tomatoes begin to collapse a bit and everything is saucy, not watery, 2 to 3 minutes.

There are two ways to eat this: either build a big salad with iceberg, all the veggies, lamb, and feta (if using). Drizzle sauce over everything and eat your pita along with it. OR build an open-face pita sandwich like my photo above. Don’t forget to drizzle it with sauce!
Enjoy!
servings: Serves 4 (as always, I recommend doubling the meat because it makes great leftovers!)

name: winter stew
note:
Prep ahead: This is an amazing meal to make earlier in the day (or even the day before) you plan to eat! Store it in the fridge in the pot you cooked it in with the lid on, then just reheat it on the stovetop and serve. As it sits it’ll continue to thicken, so add more stock (or water and Better than Bouillon) as needed to get it back to the perfect consistency.

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good for up to 4 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Again, you’ll likely need to add more liquid to your leftover soup when you reheat it in the microwave or on the stovetop to get it back to the consistency you love. See the “special ingredient” section above the recipe for what to cook with your leftover harissa paste.If you used a half block of cream cheese, set the other half out as an appetizer this holiday week! Let it come to room temperature then spread it into a thin layer on a small plate. Top with pepper jelly and serve with crisp crackers. ENJOY.

See the “special ingredient” section above the recipe for what to cook with your leftover harissa paste.

If you used a half block of cream cheese, set the other half out as an appetizer this holiday week! Let it come to room temperature then spread it into a thin layer on a small plate. Top with pepper jelly and serve with crisp crackers. ENJOY.

Stock the freezer: Let the soup cool completely before freezing. I love these souper cubes. I freeze it in the cubes, then transfer them to a gallon Ziploc once frozen. You could also store leftover portions in sandwich bag-sized Ziplocs. Fill the bags and lay them flat on a sheet pan. Put the whole sheet pan in the freezer. Once they’re frozen, remove the sheet pan and you’ll have flat bags that are easy to store. Let the soup thaw overnight in the fridge then reheat on the stovetop, adding more stock as needed.

Vegetarian: Double the lentils and add 2 more cups of stock (or water + 2 extra teaspoons of BTB). You could also use a plant-based ground meat alternative instead of turkey or a can of drained and rinsed white beans like navy or cannellini!

I don’t feel like chopping: If you have a food processor, you can peel and quarter the onion and throw it in there along with the carrots (halved). Pulse until coarsely chopped! Or grab a store-bought mirepoix and use that instead of the onion and carrot. It'll have celery in it too and that’s fine!

Gluten-free: See the farro sub below for how to cook this with rice. You could also skip the grain if you’d like but reduce the liquid by 3 cups.

Dairy-free: Skip the Parm rind, grated Parm, and cream cheese (or swap the cheeses for dairy-free versions).

Feeding kids: Pile on the grated Parm and call it SNOW! Also, go easy on the harissa paste if they’re sensitive to spice.

Make it in a crock pot/slow cooker: Cook the carrot, onion, garlic, and turkey in a skillet or pot as written. Once the turkey is cooked through, transfer everything to a slow cooker, add the rest of the ingredients (except for the kale and cream cheese!), and cook on low for 6 hours. Add the final ingredients and cook with the lid off for 30 more minutes. Don’t forget to remove the Parm rind!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 large carrots, washed and chopped into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: large carrots, washed and chopped into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small onion (I use yellow but any color works), minced
ingredients.name: small onion (I use yellow but any color works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced or minced
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, thinly sliced or minced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground turkey (or any ground meat!)
ingredients.name: ground turkey (or any ground meat!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small Yukon gold potato (4-6 ounces), chopped into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: small Yukon gold potato (4-6 ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 cups low-sodium chicken stock (I use 8 cups water + 3 heaping tablespoons low-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon), plus more as needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (I use 8 cups water + 3 heaping tablespoons low-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon), plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup farro (I like 10-minute farro from Trader Joe’s, but any farro that cooks in 10 to 20-ish minutes works — check the label, some farro takes closer to 40 minutes)
ingredients.name: farro (I like 10-minute farro from Trader Joe’s, but any farro that cooks in 10 to 20-ish minutes works — check the label, some farro takes closer to 40 minutes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup green lentils, rinsed (as you’re rinsing, push them around with your fingers so any dirt or debris can wash off — and keep an eye out for tiny pebbles/rocks that need to be removed!)
ingredients.name: green lentils, rinsed (as you’re rinsing, push them around with your fingers so any dirt or debris can wash off — and keep an eye out for tiny pebbles/rocks that need to be removed!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons harissa paste (1 will just flavor it, 2 will give it a kick)
ingredients.name: harissa paste (1 will just flavor it, 2 will give it a kick)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch lacinato kale, roughly chopped (about 4 cups)
ingredients.name: lacinato kale, roughly chopped (about 4 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon, ideally organic (because we’re zesting it)
ingredients.name: lemon, ideally organic (because we’re zesting it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces (half a block) of cream cheese (optional! It’s great without)
ingredients.name: (half a block) of cream cheese (optional! It’s great without)

preparationSteps: Thoroughly wash 3 large carrots (you can peel them if you want to but I don’t!), trim off the ends, and chop them into bite-sized pieces. Peel and mince 1 small onion.

Warm 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and add those chopped veggies along with a big pinch of kosher salt. Stir and cook until slightly softened, about 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, thinly slice (or mince) 4 garlic cloves. Once the onion and carrots are soft, add the garlic to the pot along with 1 pound ground turkey and another big pinch of salt. Cook until the turkey is cooked through, using a wooden spoon to chop it into tiny bits.
While that’s cooking, wash and chop 1 small potato into bite-sized pieces.

Once the turkey is cooked through, add the chopped potato, 8 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or 8 cups water + 3 heaping tablespoons chicken-flavored Better Than Bouillon), 1 cup farro, 1 cup green lentils, 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes, the RIND (AKA the hard part!) of the block of Parm, and 1 to 2 tablespoons harissa paste depending on whether you like things spicy or not. If you’re on the fence, start with 1 — you can always add more later! Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20 minutes, or until the farro is tender.

While it’s cooking, wash and roughly chop 1 bunch of lacinato kale (you don’t have to remove the ribs unless they’re really thick and/or you want to). Zest 1 lemon, halve it, and set both the lemon and zest aside.
Remove and discard the Parm rind.
Stir in the chopped kale, the zest and juice of the lemon, and 4 ounces (half a block) of cream cheese (if using). Stir until the kale is wilted and the cream cheese has melted into the soup.
Want it soupier? Stir in more stock. Want it thicker? Keep cooking, uncovered, until thickened to your liking.
Serve with TONS of freshly grated Parm and dollops of harissa on top. ENJOY!

name: “fish and chips” bowls with sesame green beans and gochujang tartar sauce
note: If you don’t like seafood, you could sub in 1 1/2 pounds of boneless, skinless chicken thighs. They’ll need about 35 minutes of cook time to reach an internal temp of 165°F, so start them first, then add the green beans when you have 20 minutes left. Chicken breasts or tenders would also work (they’ll need to bake for 15 to 20 minutes).

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound green beans, trimmed and snapped in half
ingredients.name: green beans, trimmed and snapped in half

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup bread & butter pickles, finely chopped, plus 2 tablespoons pickle brine (dill pickles would work, but add a punch of sugar)
ingredients.name: bread & butter pickles, finely chopped, plus 2 tablespoons pickle brine (dill pickles would work, but add a punch of sugar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup mayonnaise (or plain yogurt, but mayo is better here)
ingredients.name: mayonnaise (or plain yogurt, but mayo is better here)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 tablespoons gochujang (depending on heat preference, start with 1 if your crew is extra wimpy)
ingredients.name: gochujang (depending on heat preference, start with 1 if your crew is extra wimpy)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 18 ounces rockfish, cut into 4 fillets and patted dry
ingredients.name: rockfish
ingredients.note: cut into 4 fillets and patted dry

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (1-ounce) bags plain potato chips, crushed (about 1 cup crushed)
ingredients.name: plain potato chips, crushed (about 1 cup crushed)

preparationSteps: Heat oven to 425°F.

While the oven’s heating, get started on your rice. In a small saucepan, combine 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice, 2 cups water, and a pinch of kosher salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to the lowest heat possible on your stovetop and cook, covered, for 15 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and leave covered to allow the rice to steam until you’re ready to eat (at least 5 minutes but up to 1 hour).

While your rice is cooking, trim the stem end off of 1 pound of green beans (the skinny tip doesn’t need to be removed, though you can if you prefer it that way!). Snap the green beans in half (or just cut them in half with a knife to save time). Note to parents: This is a great kid task!
On a parchment-lined sheet pan, toss the green beans with 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil and season with 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Roast for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the gochujang tartar sauce. Trim off (and discard) the roots from 4 scallions. Thinly slice the scallions and finely chop 1/3 cup bread & butter pickles. In a medium bowl, combine 1 cup mayonnaise, half of the sliced scallions, all of the chopped pickles, 2 tablespoons pickle brine, and 2 to 3 tablespoons gochujang (start with 2 tablespoons and taste it — if you want more heat, add the third). Season to taste with salt and pepper.

If your fish is in one or two large fillets, cut it so that you have 4 about-equal fillets of fish. Pat them dry with paper towels or a clean dish towel. When the 10 minutes on the green beans are up, scooch the green beans to one side of the sheet pan and add the 4 rockfish fillets to the other side. Season the fish all over with salt and pepper. Spoon about a tablespoon of tartar sauce onto each fillet, spreading it out over the fish. Crush up 2 (1-ounce) bags plain potato chips and spread the crushed chips evenly on top of the tartar sauce (about a 1/4 cup of chips per fish). Cook until fish is just cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, and green beans are tender, about 10 minutes.

Sprinkle the fish and green beans with 2 teaspoons toasted sesame seeds. Fluff the rice with a fork and toss in the remaining scallions. Serve the fish and green beans over rice. Drizzle your bowl with gochujang tartar sauce. DIG IN!

name: chilled tomato soup
note:
Toppings: I love crispy crumbled bacon on top and it goes without saying that croutons are a solid choice, too. Chopped Marcona almonds would make this soup feel very fancy (plus add perfect salty crunch). Or top with chopped hardboiled egg, diced cucumber or avocado, chopped green olives, or just a drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of flaky salt. Sometimes I add a big scoop of Greek yogurt or sour cream on top!

Bulk it up: Serve it with grilled cheese! For each sandwich, spread 1 tablespoon of softened unsalted butter on 2 slices of sandwich bread and place them buttered-side-down. Top one slice with a generous handful of shredded cheese like cheddar or gruyere (bonus points if you use a Spanish cheese like manchego), squish the other bread slice on top buttered-side-up and grilled in a skillet on medium heat, flipping occasionally, until toasted and melty. It’s also currently fig season, which means I am really, really into this ham and fig grilled cheese. Or if you have my cookbook handy, flip to page 212 and make the cheesy salty honey toast that’s paired with my creamy creamless tomato soup — it would be right at home here.

Love your leftovers: Refrigerate leftovers all week long to grab when you need a refreshing lunch or snack.

Prep ahead: This is one of those things that’s even better made ahead of time to allow for all the ingredients to mix and mingle, so feel free to blend it up a few hours or even a day or two ahead of time and refrigerate it until ready to serve. It’s also best after being chilled for a few hours, versus straight out of the blender.

I am allergic to tomatoes: Replace the tomatoes with 3 (12-ounce) jars of roasted red bell peppers. Drain and give them a quick rinse, first!

Vegetarian: It already is!

Gluten-free: Use gluten-free bread.

Dairy-free: Swap in dairy-free plain yogurt. Or soak a 1/4 cup of almonds or cashews and blend those in. Or try replacing the yogurt with almond butter or tahini, chickpeas, any white bean, or even hummus.

Spice it up: Add a big pinch of red pepper flakes or hot smoked paprika, or a shake of your favorite hot sauce.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 pounds ripe tomatoes, stem removed and coarsely chopped
ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes, stem removed and coarsely chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and coarsely chopped (I actually just rip it open with my hands and pull out the seeds!)
ingredients.name: red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and coarsely chopped (I actually just rip it open with my hands and pull out the seeds!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 thick slice of good crusty bread (like a sourdough or a baguette!), chopped (should be about 2 heaping cups of chopped bread)
ingredients.name: thick slice of good crusty bread (like a sourdough or a baguette!), chopped (should be about 2 heaping cups of chopped bread)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon any vinegar (sherry or apple cider preferred)
ingredients.name: any vinegar (sherry or apple cider preferred)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 4 slices of bacon, chopped and cooked until crispy
ingredients.name: Optional: 4 slices of bacon, chopped and cooked until crispy

preparationSteps: Add 2 1/2 pounds cored and coarsely chopped ripe tomatoes, 1 cored, seeded, and coarsely chopped red bell pepper, 1 chopped thick slice of crusty bread, 1/4 of a small white onion, 1 very small garlic clove, 1/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, and 1 teaspoon vinegar (preferably sherry or apple cider) to a blender (NOT a food processor, trust me) and blend on high speed until smooth, it’ll take a minute or so!

Taste. I am starting the recipe with the bare minimum of all seasonings so that you can adjust the flavor based on how flavorful your tomatoes and peppers are. Add more salt, pepper, vinegar, or garlic to pump up the flavor. Too acidic? Add a pinch of sugar or honey. Play around with it! Add something, blend, taste. Add more, blend, taste. Make it your perfect summer soup!
Chill for a few hours if you have the time. Pour into bowls and garnish with crispy bacon and a drizzle of olive oil if you’re into that.
PS slice the leftover bread, drizzle it with olive oil, toast it and serve it alongside the soup for dipping!

name: chicken panzanella
note:
Two knives??? You KNOW I have zero tolerance for dirtying unnecessary dishes. But chef’s knives SUCK at cutting through a tomato. A serrated bread knife on the other hand (which you’ll also use while cubing the bread), cuts through tomato skin like silk. But serrated knives aren’t great at slicing basil or mincing garlic. So it’s worth the little bit of extra scrub work I promise!

Leftovers are a good thing: Assembled, this isn’t going to keep well as the bread will get super soggy. But if you’re cooking for one, you can store half of the ingredients prepped but deconstructed, then assemble them when it’s time to eat. To do that: Cook the chicken and bread as directed. Pull out the portion of each you want to save for another meal and store it as needed (chicken in the fridge, bread in an airtight container in the pantry or on the counter). Likewise, go ahead and cut up the whole tomato and pack some up in the fridge. When you want to cook, reheat the chicken and bread, then proceed with the recipe as written.

Make ahead: This recipe comes together super quickly. But you can always cube your bread and chop your tomato(es) up to a day ahead!

I’m vegetarian: Double the tomatoes and make a big salad OR add a can of drained and rinsed chickpeas/garbanzo beans, roasting them along with the bread in lieu of chicken. Yum!

Gluten-free: Use a gluten-free bread loaf. If you can’t find good gf bread, swap the bread for chickpeas.

Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free alternative for the goat cheese or just omit.

I have peaches that I need to use ASAP: Chop them into bite-sized pieces and add them to the mix!

On a late summer salad kick? ME TOO. Don’t forget about my WTC Mango Chicken Peanut Salad or Dankest Taco Salad. If you have my cookbook, Just Married, turn to page 214 for a Cherry Tomato and Fried Goat Cheese Salad.

Special ingredient: Click here for the other WTC recipes that use balsamic!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 4 thighs)
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 4 thighs)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups cubed crusty bread (so a baguette, French bread, or sourdough loaf chopped into cubes)
ingredients.name: cubed crusty bread (so a baguette, French bread, or sourdough loaf chopped into cubes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: balsamic vinegar, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large heirloom or beefsteak tomato (or 1 pint cherry tomatoes), cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: large heirloom or beefsteak tomato (or 1 pint cherry tomatoes)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Toss 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, 4 cups cubed bread, 3 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper in a large roasting pan (9x13-inch is perfect) until everything is evenly coated. Distribute the bread across the bottom of the pan, with the chicken over top.
Roast for 25 minutes.
While the chicken is roasting, cut 1 large heirloom or beefsteak tomato into bite-sized pieces and thinly slice a big handful of fresh basil leaves (you want about 1/2 a cup).

When the chicken finishes roasting, immediately scatter the tomato and basil over top. Crumble the goat cheese into big chunks with your hands and add it too. Season with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, a bit more pepper, and a drizzle of balsamic.
Let everything sit for 5 minutes so the chicken can rest and the goat cheese can get nice and melty.
Throw a big handful of arugula onto each plate (if you want!), then serve the chicken panzanella over top. YUMMMM!

name: 10-ingredient roasted chicken, cauliflower, and potatoes with a ridiculously tasty green sauce
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: consider doubling the entire meal and doing this with the leftovers:Basil Chicken Salad: shred the extra chicken and toss it with a couple tablespoons of green sauce at a time until it’s perfectly coated in sauce. Consider adding chopped grapes and celery. Roasted Cauliflower Soup: blend 1 cup roasted cauliflower with 1/2 cup chicken broth then season as desired for the tastiest, simplest soup. Garnish with a fancy swirl of green sauce. Bacon & Potato Hash: chop up several slices of bacon and cook over medium heat until almost crispy. Add the potatoes, smashing them to create uneven surfaces that can crisp up, and cook until potatoes are warmed through and bacon is crispy. Stir in some basil and garnish with parmesan. Great as a breakfast hash or dinner side dish.

Basil Chicken Salad: shred the extra chicken and toss it with a couple tablespoons of green sauce at a time until it’s perfectly coated in sauce. Consider adding chopped grapes and celery.

Roasted Cauliflower Soup: blend 1 cup roasted cauliflower with 1/2 cup chicken broth then season as desired for the tastiest, simplest soup. Garnish with a fancy swirl of green sauce.

Bacon & Potato Hash: chop up several slices of bacon and cook over medium heat until almost crispy. Add the potatoes, smashing them to create uneven surfaces that can crisp up, and cook until potatoes are warmed through and bacon is crispy. Stir in some basil and garnish with parmesan. Great as a breakfast hash or dinner side dish.

Don’t own a blender or food processor? Chop the basil as finely as you can, and stir it in a large bowl with the vinegar, lemon juice, parmesan, and garlic powder. Slowly whisk in the oil to emulsify it into a nice thick (but chunky) sauce.

Make ahead: partially roast the cauliflower and potatoes and make the green sauce at any point during the day, or the day before, then throw the entire sheet-pan in the fridge. just place the chicken on top and finish cooking everything when it’s dinner time.

Neutral cooking oil: I will always call for you to use a “neutral cooking oil” when it doesn’t matter what oil you use. Avocado, grapeseed, sunflower, olive (NOT extra-virgin) - anything with a high smoke point (this is easy to google if you aren’t sure). Extra-virgin olive oil is not a neutral cooking oil.

Dairy-Free + Whole30: eliminate the parmesan but add 1/4 cup nuts (almonds, walnuts, cashews, etc) to the sauce. Whole30 people also need to make sure their Dijon mustard is compliant.

Spinach: kale will also work here, just be sure to de-rib it, and stir it in with the cauliflower and a smidge of oil when you add the chicken. It’ll get kinda crispy and be very delicious.

Cauliflower sub: yes, fine, you can buy pre-chopped florets, but you must cut them in half to get that nice even cut side for browning! Swap in carrots, parsnips, beets, or any other tough vegetable here if you please!

Yellow baby dutch potato sub:  you can use any potato, or sweet potato you want. Cut non-baby potatoes into 1 1/2-inch cubes. Leave fingerlings or teeny tiny potatoes whole. Quarter red potatoes.

Vegetarian: ditch the chicken and instead stir in 1 can of drained, rinsed, dried chickpeas at the same time that you would have added the chicken. You’ll need a smidge more oil to coat everything evenly.

Parmesan sub: pecorino romano would also be delicious, or check out the dairy-free sub above.

Basil sub: basil can be tricky to find this time of year. Cilantro, parsley, or a combo of the three all work swimmingly. PS even if your basil leaves are brown, they’re still good to use unless slimy or stinky. They discolor really easily!

Garlic powder sub: 1 small garlic clove, or 2 tablespoons chopped shallot, or 1/4 teaspoon onion powder.

Chicken subs:Bone-in skin-on chicken breasts: roast the veggies for 20 minutes on their own, then add the chicken breasts and roast for an additional 20 to 25 minutes.Bone-in skin-on chicken thighs: roast the entire time. Honestly, this would be my first choice but I gotta give the people what they want with the BS chicken breasts occasionally!Boneless skinless chicken thighs: roast the veggies for 15 minutes on their own, then add the chicken thighs and roast for an additional 30 to 40 minutes.Whole, spatchcocked chicken: place the chicken skin-side-up over top the veg and roast the entire time, 45 to 55 minutes, until an internal thermometer placed in the breast reads 160°F. Peeled deveined shrimp: roast the veggies for 45 minutes on their own, then add the shrimp for the last 3 to 5 minutes, until opaque. Salmon: roast the veggies for 40 minutes on their own, then add the salmon for 10 to 12 minutes until 130°F internally. thank you to Maude Ballinger for the fabulous photos.

Bone-in skin-on chicken breasts: roast the veggies for 20 minutes on their own, then add the chicken breasts and roast for an additional 20 to 25 minutes.

Bone-in skin-on chicken thighs: roast the entire time. Honestly, this would be my first choice but I gotta give the people what they want with the BS chicken breasts occasionally!

Boneless skinless chicken thighs: roast the veggies for 15 minutes on their own, then add the chicken thighs and roast for an additional 30 to 40 minutes.

Whole, spatchcocked chicken: place the chicken skin-side-up over top the veg and roast the entire time, 45 to 55 minutes, until an internal thermometer placed in the breast reads 160°F.

Peeled deveined shrimp: roast the veggies for 45 minutes on their own, then add the shrimp for the last 3 to 5 minutes, until opaque.

Salmon: roast the veggies for 40 minutes on their own, then add the salmon for 10 to 12 minutes until 130°F internally.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 4 tablespoons neutral oil*, divided
ingredients.name: plus 4 tablespoons neutral oil*

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 ounces each)
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 ounces each)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F and line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper.

I have a very specific way that I like to cut cauliflower (NO FLORETS!) so pay attention here. First, trim off the leaves and the very bottom of the cauliflower stem. Now slice it in half, through the stem. Place the two halves cut-side down on a cutting board, then slice it into 1/2-inch thick pieces. Cut or pull apart the individual florets.
Place the cauliflower on half of the sheet pan.

Halve 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes, then place them on the other half of the sheet pan. Drizzle the cauliflower and potatoes with 3 tablespoons neutral cooking oil, then season with 2 teaspoons kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Toss to coat, keeping the cauliflower and potatoes separate. Turn the potatoes to that they are all cut-side-down on the sheet pan, and spread the cauliflower into as even of a layer as possible. If the cauliflower is really piled high, consider adding a second sheet-pan so that it will roast more evenly.

Roast for 35 minutes on the center rack in the oven. The cauliflower and potatoes should be tender, and just beginning to brown around the edges. If they’re not, roast for another 5 to 10 minutes before continuing to the next step.

While the vegetables roast, season 2 to 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts with a thin layer of oil, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and a sprinkle of pepper per breast. Set aside to come to room temperature while the vegetables cook.

Make the green sauce by blending 1 cup fresh basil leaves, 1/2 cup grated parmesan, 1/3 cup oil, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, the juice of 1/2 lemon, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt until smooth. If it’s too thick (it should be drizzle-able) or your blender is having a hard time blending it, blend in 1 tablespoon of water at a time. Taste and adjust seasoning to taste (always adjust seasoning for YOUR tastebuds!). Too tangy? Add another splash of oil. Need more flavor? Another pinch of salt. Love spice? Add some red pepper flakes! Pour the sauce into a bowl.
Roughly chop 4 cups of spinach. Finely chop 1/4 cup basil leaves. Keep them separate for later.

After 35 minutes, add the chicken breasts to the pan, on top of the vegetables is fine if there’s no space. No, you don’t need to stir the cauliflower or potatoes! Roast the chicken for 14 minutes, then check the internal temperature using a meat thermometer. If it’s not finished, continue cooking, checking the temperature frequently, until the chicken reaches 160°F.

Transfer the chicken breasts to a cutting board to rest while we fancy up the veggies. Stir the chopped spinach and the juice of the remaining 1/2 lemon into the cauliflower until the spinach has wilted. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir 1/4 cup finely chopped basil and 2 tablespoons grated parmesan into the potatoes. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt and pepper as needed.

Slice the chicken breasts on the bias (see photo - don’t slice straight up and down, slice at an angle, this will make the chicken more tender). Serve the chicken alongside the potatoes and cauliflower, with LOTSA sauce!

name: crispy sesame-honey goat cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounce log of goat cheese (plain or honey)
ingredients.name: log of goat cheese (plain or honey)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup cooking oil such as canola, avocado, or grapeseed
ingredients.name: cooking oil such as canola, avocado, or grapeseed

preparationSteps: Combine 3 tablespoons panko breadcrumbs, 2 tablespoons sesame seeds, and a pinch of salt in a shallow bowl or plate. Roll the goat cheese log in it. On a separate plate, beat together 1 egg. Dip the coated goat cheese in the egg, then back into the panko mixture.

Warm 1/2 cup cooking oil in a small skillet over medium heat until it looks shimmery. Check if it’s ready by flicking a piece of panko into the oil — when it’s ready, the panko will sizzle immediately. Cook the goat cheese for about 20 seconds per side, until the panko and seeds are golden-brown all over.
Transfer to a serving platter and drizzle with lots of honey. Serve with crostini or crackers!

name: bacon kimchi salmon fried rice
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: If you have leftovers… I’m jealous!! My kids, George, and I always devour the whole thing (yes, this is a good one for babies/kids!). Leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, so enjoy them reheated on the stovetop (OK, or in the microwave) for breakfast, lunch, or dinner in the coming days. Who else is team leftovers-for-breakfast?!

Vegetarian: Crispy tofu cubes or planks would be delicious in this! Find a how-to for baking crispy tofu here in the product spotlight section. You could also pan-fry thin strips of extra-firm tofu in the skillet, using a few tablespoons of sesame oil. Tofu typically gets crispiest in the oven, but it’d still be great pan-fried, if that’s easier. You could also skip the tofu and just bulk up the dish with extra veggies. Options include: an extra cup of cabbage, a thinly sliced red bell pepper, chopped broccoli florets, chopped carrot, chopped asparagus, etc. Add them when you add the cabbage.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Already is!

Got any time saving hacks for me? Duh. May I remind you that grocery stores sell microwaveable rice packs? You’d wanna use two of those, if you go that route. You can also buy pre-shredded cabbage if slicing cabbage is too much work today. It’s often advertised as an “Asian Slaw Kit.” Just ditch or repurpose the dressing that might be included.

Whole30: Use 2 (16-ounce) bags of cauliflower rice instead of rice! Delish! Just cook until tender, about 5 minutes.

I actually *do* hate kimchi: If you’ve tried it in a cooked dish before and know it’s not for you (seriously, it’s a totally different experience eating it cooked vs. raw straight out of the jar!), just cut it from the recipe. You’ll want to add more soy sauce for saltiness as well as some light-colored vinegar in lieu of the kimchi juice for tang. Just add a teaspoon-ish of each at a time until it tastes great. If you have fish sauce, add 1 tablespoon of that as well!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups cooked white or brown rice (from 1 1/2 cups dry rice)
ingredients.name: cooked white or brown rice (from 1 1/2 cups dry rice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 skinless salmon filets (about 6 ounces each), cut into 1/2-inch thick slices
ingredients.name: skinless salmon filets (about 6 ounces each)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions (AKA green onions), thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions (AKA green onions)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated (or look for frozen ginger cubes at your grocery: use 3 here)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.note: peeled and grated (or look for frozen ginger cubes at your grocery: use 3 here)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups thinly sliced green or purple cabbage (from about 1/2 a head) —FYI, purple cabbage will turn the eggs a bit purple, don’t be alarmed!
ingredients.name: thinly sliced green or purple cabbage (from about 1/2 a head) —FYI, purple cabbage will turn the eggs a bit purple, don’t be alarmed!

preparationSteps: If you aren’t using leftover rice and need to cook it — do that now! Cook 1 1/2 cups white or brown rice per package instructions.

Warm your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 4 bacon slices that you’ve thinly sliced and cook, stirring often, until crispy, 4 to 5 minutes. Transfer the bacon to a plate but leave all of the grease behind.

Pat the 1/2-inch slices from 2 salmon filets completely dry with a clean dishtowel. Place them in the skillet, not touching, and season with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until lightly golden-brown. It’s OK (and a good thing!) if you still see a bit of pink in the middle. Transfer the salmon to the same plate as the bacon.

Add 1 thinly sliced bunch of scallions to the skillet and sauté until tender, about 3 minutes. Stir in 4 grated garlic cloves and 1 inch of fresh ginger, peeled and grated, for 1 minute (or less, if the garlic starts to get brown).
Stir in 4 cups thinly sliced cabbage. Cook, stirring often, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the cabbage is wilted. Season with a big pinch of salt.

Stir in 4 cups cooked rice, 1 cup chopped kimchi, 2 tablespoons kimchi juice, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 2 tablespoons sesame oil until completely combined. Smooth the rice into a flat layer in the skillet and allow it to cook, undisturbed, for 3 minutes. This will crisp it up!

Scooch the rice over to leave about 1/4 of the skillet empty. Add a smidge of sesame oil to coat the empty part of the skillet and crack 2 eggs in. Scramble them quickly. Once cooked, stir them into the rice.
Taste. What does it need more of? More tang? Stir in some more kimchi or a splash of any clear vinegar! More salt? Add more soy sauce! Want heat? Add some sriracha or red pepper flakes!
Gently stir the cooked bacon and salmon into the rice. Garnish with 1/4 cup chopped cilantro and 2 teaspoons sesame seeds. Dig in!

name: grilled steak caprese (steak only)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Note: Have a favorite steak rub? Skip the rub below and just coat your steaks in that instead!
ingredients.name: Note: Have a favorite steak rub? Skip the rub below and just coat your steaks in that instead!

ingredients.rawIngredient: Olive oil or other neutral oil with a high smoke point
ingredients.name: Olive oil or other neutral oil with a high smoke point

preparationSteps: On a large plate, combine 4 teaspoons kosher salt, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons garlic powder, 2 teaspoons onion powder, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Stir until well combined. Pat your steaks dry with a clean towel, then drag them through the rub and use your hands to really rub it in evenly. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes. If you have time, let it sit uncovered in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Leaving them uncovered will allow the steak to dry out (in a good way), which will help you achieve those great grill marks!
Preheat grill to medium on one burner and medium-high on the others.
Coat the 4 flat iron steaks with a light coating of oil.

Grill the steaks over the medium-high burner, flipping after 5 minutes and cooking on the second side for another 4 to 5 minutes, until 130°F internally for medium-rare, 140°F for medium, or 150°F for medium-well.
Thinly slice the steaks and fan them out on a serving platter.

name: grilled steak caprese
note:
Remember to clean your grill and fill the propane tank!!! If this will be the first time you’ve grilled in a while, click here and read the intro. Note that you DON’T need to oil your grill grates since we’re coating the steaks and corn with a very light layer of oil.

Once it’s clean… Work some other grilled WTC meals into your meal plan for the coming weeks! Like… The Most Perfect Grilled Chicken, Marinated Grilled Veggies with Burrata, and Grilled Pickle-Brined Sandwiches.

I don’t have a grill: If you have a grill pan, that’d be my plan B. If not, use a cast iron skillet! In either case, cook the corn first over medium heat (make sure the skillet or pan is piping hot first!), then move onto the steak after you’ve cranked the heat up to medium-high. Finish with the bread. Cook times will be the same as the grill! Keep that meat thermometer nearby as you’re cooking and pull the steaks when they reach your desired doneness.

Vegetarian: Cauliflower steaks! Or portobello mushroom caps! Or ditch the “steak” theme altogether and add a can of drained and rinsed chickpeas to your caprese salad. Delish!

DF/GF: If you’re cutting dairy, try slices of firm tofu. It offers nearly the same consistency as mozzarella. Or, of course, you could just omit the cheese. To avoid gluten, swap sourdough out for your favorite gf bread.

Feeding kids: My kids get really frazzled when I try to feed them salad-y things where there are many ingredients all mixed together. So for this meal I serve them steak (cut into small bites), corn on the cob with butter, and mozzarella balls — all separate. I try to sneak some tomatoes onto their plates too but… what’s the point.

Leftovers are a great thing: This whole meal will keep well for a few days covered in the fridge! Like I said above, store the salad and steak separately. If you didn’t go the steak bite sandwich route the first go round (or even if you did!), it would make a truly delectable lunch.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound tomatoes (cherry tomatoes are best right now; heirloom or beefsteak or early girls will be better later in the summer), halved (if using cherry) or sliced (if using a larger tomato)
ingredients.name: tomatoes (cherry tomatoes are best right now; heirloom or beefsteak or early girls will be better later in the summer), halved (if using cherry) or sliced (if using a larger tomato)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces mozzarella (you can either cube up a ball of fresh mozzarella or get a container of ciliegine — the little balls — and cut them in half)
ingredients.name: mozzarella (you can either cube up a ball of fresh mozzarella or get a container of ciliegine — the little balls — and cut them in half)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup thinly sliced fresh basil, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: thinly sliced fresh basil, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ears of corn (preferably white), husks removed
ingredients.name: of corn (preferably white), husks removed

preparationSteps: On a large plate, combine 4 teaspoons kosher salt, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons garlic powder, 2 teaspoons onion powder, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Stir until well combined. Pat your steaks dry with a clean towel, then drag them through the rub and use your hands to really rub it in evenly. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes. If you have time, let it sit uncovered in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Leaving them uncovered will allow the steak to dry out (in a good way), which will help you achieve those great grill marks!
Preheat grill to medium on one burner and medium-high on the others.
While the grill is preheating, start making the caprese.

In a large bowl, toss together 1 pound tomatoes (halved/sliced), 1/4 of a medium red onion thinly sliced, 8 ounces mozzarella (cubed or halved), 1/2 cup thinly sliced basil, 1 grated garlic clove, 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar, 1 teaspoon honey, 3/4 teaspoon salt, and a few grinds of black pepper. Set aside while you grill.
Coat the 4 flat iron steaks and 4 ears of corn with a light coating of oil.
Grill the corn over the medium burner, rotating it every few minutes as it browns. It should take 6 to 8 minutes total.

At the same time, grill the steaks over the medium-high burner, flipping after 5 minutes and cooking on the second side for another 4 to 5 minutes, until 130°F internally for medium-rare, 140°F for medium, or 150°F for medium-well.

Drizzle the sliced sourdough bread with oil. Grill over the medium burner until golden-brown grill marks appear. Just a couple minutes! Watch them closely — bread loves catching on fire when left unattended!

When the corn is cool enough to handle, cut the kernels off the cob (lay the corn down on the cutting board to do so without the kernels flying away!) and add them to the caprese bowl. Toss to combine, then taste and adjust salt, oil, and vinegar to taste.

Thinly slice the steaks and fan them out on a serving platter. Spoon the caprese over top. (Or keep them separate if you don’t plan on eating everything tonight — the leftovers will keep better separate.) Garnish with more thinly sliced basil. Plate the grilled sourdough alongside the steak caprese.
Enjoy! Best served with slices of watermelon or ice cream sandwiches for dessert.

name: cheesy chipotle shrimp tacos

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound (20-30 count) peeled and deveined shrimp, thawed if using frozen (I usually buy mine frozen, they often have tails that I have to remove)
ingredients.name: peeled and deveined shrimp, thawed if using frozen (I usually buy mine frozen, they often have tails that I have to remove)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoonschipotle hot sauceor the liquid from a can of chipotles en adobo
ingredients.name: tablespoonschipotle hot sauceor the liquid from a can of chipotles en adobo

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bag of the smallest flour tortillas you can find (I lovethese)
ingredients.name: of the smallest flour tortillas you can find (I lovethese)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded sharp white (or yellow) Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded sharp white (or yellow) Cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Marinate the shrimp: In a large bowl or Ziploc, combine 1 pound shrimp, 2 tablespoons chipotle hot sauce, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon honey, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Use a microplane to grate the zest from 1 lime into the bowl/bag. Mix and set aside to marinate at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Place one oven rack in the middle of the oven, and one right above the middle.

Make the pico de gallo: Dice 1 pound tomatoes and 1 small white onion. Cut the stem off of 1 jalapeño, cut it in half, and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds (and discard them) then mince. Finely chop enough cilantro to get 1/4 cup. Throw all of that in a bowl and stir in the juice of 1/2 lime (the one you zested earlier) and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Taste and if it isn’t delicious, add more salt. Tomatoes love salt.

Bake the shrimp and cheesy tortillas: Now grab two rimmed sheet pans! Line one with foil. Place the shrimp in an even layer on the foil-lined sheet pan, and place as many tortillas as you need on the naked sheet pan, overlapping them slightly if needed. Sprinkle about 3 tablespoons of Cheddar cheese (but you absolutely do not need to measure) onto each tortilla.
Place the tortillas on the middle rack in the oven, and the shrimp on the rack right above it. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the shrimp are firm and the cheese is melty.

Make the chipotle crema: I know, another step! Trust me, it’s worth it. In a small tupperware container or jar (because you’ll have leftovers and I’m saving you a dirty dish!), combine 1/2 cup mayo, 1 tablespoon chipotle hot sauce, the juice from the remaining 1/2 lime, and a pinch of salt. Taste and adjust seasonings as you like.
Assemble: Pile 3 to 4 shrimp onto each tortilla and top with tons of pico de gallo and chipotle crema. Sprinkle any remaining cilantro on top.
Pretend you're poolside and enjoy :)

name: turkey meatballs with corn butter rice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup brown or white rice (or really, whatever grain you want to use)
ingredients.name: brown or white rice (or really, whatever grain you want to use)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch soft green herbs (any mixture of basil, parsley, dill, and/or cilantro)
ingredients.name: soft green herbs (any mixture of basil, parsley, dill, and/or cilantro)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional extras: greens such as arugula or spring mix, thinly sliced cucumbers, thinly sliced radishes, green onions, more fresh herbs, toasted nuts, chopped tomatoes, the sky’s the limit!
ingredients.name: Optional extras: greens such as arugula or spring mix, thinly sliced cucumbers, thinly sliced radishes, green onions, more fresh herbs, toasted nuts, chopped tomatoes, the sky’s the limit!

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper (seriously, do this now — your hands are gonna be dirty when you need it later).
Cut the corn kernels off of 4 ears of corn. Set the kernels aside and don't throw the cobs out!

Cook 1 cup dried rice according to package instructions, but add an extra 1/4 cup of water and throw the 4 spent corn cobs into the pot too. For the last 5 minutes of cooking, use tongs to remove the cobs, discard them, and stir in the corn kernels.
When the rice is cooked, stir in the zest and juice of 1 lemon and 2 tablespoons unsalted butter. Taste and add kosher salt as needed. Leave the rice covered, off the heat.
While the rice is cooking, make the sauce and meatballs.
To make the sauce, in a medium bowl, combine 3/4 cup sour cream, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Set aside.
Finely chop enough soft green herbs (leaves and tender stems) to get 1/2 cup.

In a large bowl, lightly whisk 1 egg. Add 2 tablespoons of the lemony sour cream sauce, 1 pound ground turkey, 1/3 cup breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup finely chopped soft green herbs, 1 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric, and 1/2 teaspoon cumin. Use your hands to combine everything.
Form 12 to 15 meatballs — they should be 1 1/2-ish inches in diameter each (a little bigger than a ping pong ball) — and place them on the parchment-lined baking sheet, at least 1 inch apart.
Bake for 10 minutes. You can cut a meatball in half to make sure they’re cooked through, or use a meat thermometer to make sure they’re at least 165°F internally.
Scoop your desired amount of rice into a bowl, top with a few meatballs, a big drizzle of lemony sour cream, and any desired extras (including the leftover chopped herbs you’ll have). Dig in!

name: yogurt-marinated grilled chicken with rice pilaf
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Grab some microwaveable jasmine rice, microwave it for 90 seconds, then, while it’s still steaming hot, zhoosh it up in a bowl with the other rice ingredients. Or just microwave some long-grain wild rice and call it a day. For the chicken, grab a yogurt or buttermilk-based dressing from the store and use that as a marinade. See below if you’re not in the mood to grill.

Make ahead: Make the marinade a full day ahead, then add the chicken up to 6 hours before grill time. You can cook the rice pilaf up to a day ahead of time, but don’t add the nuts yet. Store the rice in its pot, covered, in the refrigerator. About 20 minutes before dinnertime, cover it with foil and throw it in the oven at 350°F. Add the nuts, stir, then dig in!

Gluten-free/dairy-free: Ta-da — it’s already gf! If you’re lactose intolerant, try to find a plain lactose-free yogurt (like one that’s still made from cow’s milk but is lactose free). If you can’t find one, or if you can’t eat any dairy, use a plain almond or coconut yogurt instead. If you go that route, double the amount of lemon juice in the marinade — it will help tenderize the chicken since you don’t have the dairy’s calcium and lactic acid doing so. Use a vegan butter for the rice.

I don’t have a grill: Check Craigslist! JK — kinda. Here’s what you’ll do: Cook the rice on the stove by bringing it to a boil over high heat, then reducing to low and covering for 15 minutes. Cook the chicken on the stovetop following this method. Alternatively, you could roast it in the oven at 450°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through.

Vegetarian: Serve the zucchini and squash from two weeks ago alongside the rice. And/or grill some portobello mushroom caps! OR go the kebab route, using bell peppers, onions, button mushrooms, squash, and zucchini. That’ll be delicious with a side of rice pilaf. Skip the yogurt marinade, simply rub them with a very light coating of oil, and season with salt and pepper.

Kebab it: Make kebabs by cubing up the chicken, then threading it onto skewers (if wooden, soak them in cold water for at least 30 minutes before threading so they don’t catch on fire). Grill kebabs for 3 to 4 minutes per side, flipping once. You can add onion slices, summer squash, bell pepper, and/or any other vegetable that also cooks quickly.

I want more veggies: Also grill the squash and zucchini side from two weeks ago! It would go perfectly here.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons neutral cooking oil (grapeseed, avocado, canola, or vegetable)
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil (grapeseed, avocado, canola, or vegetable)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 cups fresh spinach, torn (I don’t recommend frozen here)
ingredients.name: fresh spinach, torn (I don’t recommend frozen here)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup raisins (or ANY dried fruit, chopped finely)
ingredients.name: raisins (or ANY dried fruit, chopped finely)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup chopped toasted almonds (or ANY toasted nut)
ingredients.name: chopped toasted almonds (or ANY toasted nut)

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, stir to combine 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt, the juice of 1 lemon, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Transfer half of the yogurt to a serving bowl and refrigerate it — this is your sauce.
If your chicken breasts seem very thick, cut them in half lengthwise, into two thinner planks.
Add 1 1/2 to 2 pounds chicken breasts or thighs to what’s left in the bowl of yogurt and toss to coat.
Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature or for up to 6 hours in the refrigerator.
When you’re ready to grill:
Preheat your grill to 450°F with all burners on.

While the grill is heating up, prepare the rice. Add 1 cup of white rice (no — you don’t need to rinse it), 1 1/2 cups water, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, the juice of 1 lemon, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt to a cast iron skillet, Dutch oven, or stainless steel pot. Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil.
Place the rice skillet onto the grill — on the burner on the far right side — and turn that burner to low heat.

Set a timer for 15 minutes — that’s when we’ll check on the rice. Keep an eye on the grill — you want the temperature to stay around 450°F so you might need to play around with the knobs to keep it there.

Meanwhile, soak a wadded-up paper towel in 2 tablespoons cooking oil. When the rice has been cooking for 10 minutes, grab the oily wad with tongs, and rub it on the grill grates. THIS IS A VERY IMPORTANT STEP — DO NOT SKIP IT!

When the 15-minute timer goes off, carefully peel the rice’s foil back (there will be steam!!) and check rice for doneness. Cover and keep cooking (if needed) until the rice is plump, then remove the skillet from the grill.

Stir 2 to 3 cups torn spinach and 1/2 cup raisins (or other dried fruit) into the rice, then re-cover with the foil until dinnertime. Just before serving, sprinkle 1/2 cup chopped toasted almonds (or other chopped toasted nut) over top.
Now it’s time to cook the chicken on those grates you oiled. Cook the chicken breasts for about 4 minutes per side (if using chicken thighs, cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side).
When flipping, use a spatula — not tongs. The yogurt marinade can stick to the grill a bit, so you need to really scrape under there to release the chicken from the grill.

About 2 minutes into cooking the second side of the chicken, start checking the internal temperature. We want chicken breasts to reach 160°F (they have so little fat that they will continue cooking after you pull them off to reach 165°F) and thighs to be at 165°F. Remove the chicken from the grill when it’s cooked through.
Slice the chicken and serve it over rice with a big ole dollop of the yogurt sauce.

name: grilled chicken and vegetables with burrata and green sauce
note:
I don’t feel like cooking this much: Here’s a marinade/sauce shortcut: Grab a container of store-bought pesto. Add it to a large bowl. Stir in 1/4 cup of any clear vinegar. Reserve a little bowl full for serving. Add your veggies and chicken.

I don’t have a grill: Throw the chicken and vegetables on two sheet pans and roast them at 425°F for 20 to 25 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F internally.

Other protein: Not feeling chicken? Swap it for the same amount steak — flank or skirt steak cut into large pieces works especially well with the herby marinade. Or try shrimp or pork! I love the idea of pork tenderloin or chops here.

Other veggies: There is no end to what veggies you can use. Eggplant, green beans, asparagus, corn, and red onion are just a few favorites.
