Gimme a grain: This meal is filling as written but if you're trying to stretch it to feed more people or if your family is super hungry, it goes great served alongside a grain like couscous, farro, or quinoa. This coconut rice would also be a major win. Oh, or for a real summer feast make it with the corn butter rice from last summer.

Freezer friendly: The chicken can be frozen before cooking directly in the marinade! Just toss the Ziploc bag in the freezer (making sure to squeeze any air out) and freeze for up to 2 months. All that’s left to do is defrost the bag in the refrigerator overnight before grilling. Slice up some veggies and toss them into the bag to get coated in sauce before grilling — we don’t want to freeze them, they get weird when defrosted.

Make ahead: This recipe is primed to be prepped ahead. Make the green sauce and marinate the chicken and vegetables the day before.

Love your leftovers: If we have any leftovers, George likes to throw his over rice or couscous, whereas I like to make a big chopped salad by tossing the grilled chicken and veggies, romaine lettuce, some feta cheese, and some almonds into a big bowl and hacking away at it all with a chef’s knife until everything is cut into very small pieces. For both of our leftover creations, a generous dousing of green sauce adds the finishing touch.

Vegetarian: Swap the chicken for slabs of extra-firm tofu or skip the grill and drain a couple of cans of chickpeas or white beans to roast and serve alongside the veggies. Tofu is REALLY good here! I love grilling it — just be sure to oil your grill grates before grilling so it doesn’t stick.

Dairy-free: Leave off the burrata and dollop the platter with plain, non-dairy yogurt. Or crumble vegan feta over everything — it won’t lend creaminess to the situation but you can’t argue with a salty pop!

Gluten-free: Skip the grilled bread and serve it over a grain like quinoa or rice. Or grab your favorite gf bread, of course!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup packed cilantro leaves and stems
ingredients.name: packed cilantro leaves and stems

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large zucchini, sliced lengthwise into 1/4-inch thick planks
ingredients.name: large zucchini, sliced lengthwise into 1/4-inch thick planks

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large yellow squash, sliced lengthwise into 1/4-inch thick planks
ingredients.name: large yellow squash, sliced lengthwise into 1/4-inch thick planks

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large red bell pepper, cut lengthwise into quarters
ingredients.name: large red bell pepper, cut lengthwise into quarters

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 of a loaf of country or Italian bread, sliced
ingredients.name: of a loaf of country or Italian bread

preparationSteps: First, make the green marinade/sauce: Add 1 cup cilantro, 1 cup parsley, 4 scallions, 2 garlic cloves, 1/3 cup olive oil, juice of 1 lime, juice of 1 lemon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt to a blender and blend until smooth.

Place 1 pound chicken breasts, 1 pound chicken thighs, 1 zucchini sliced lengthwise into thin planks, 1 yellow squash sliced lengthwise into thin planks, and 1 quartered red bell pepper into a large bowl or gallon Ziploc bag and cover with half of the green sauce. Add 1 teaspoon salt. Reserve the second half of the sauce for serving. (Yes – the vegetables and chicken can touch even though the chicken is raw! We are cooking them! It’s all good!)

Toss the chicken and vegetables to coat them in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours (flip the bag occasionally), or marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes, flipping once, if you happen to think of it. (After 24 hours the citrus juice in the marinade starts to mess with the chicken’s texture, but if you really need to — because, life — you can let it go for up to 48 hours.)
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat (450°F). See notes for indoor cooking instructions.

If you haven’t already, use a grill brush to scrape the grates clean. Use tongs to lift the chicken and vegetables out of the marinade and shake off as much of the marinade as possible as you add them to the grill, to prevent flare-ups (aka the flames shooting up when oil drops down into the grill). Grill the chicken thighs and peppers for 5 minutes per side, breasts for 4 minutes per side, and squash and zucchini for 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until charred and tender. Check the internal temperature of the chicken, it’s finished when 160°F internally (it will continue cooking once off the grill to reach 165°F). Transfer everything to a large platter as it finishes.
Brush the bread slices with olive oil and grill until toasty and charred in spots, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Transfer to the platter as they finish.

Garnish the chicken and vegetable platter with 4 ounces burrata, torn into 2 or 3 pieces and 2 cups arugula, tucked under and around the chicken and veggies, and drizzle it all with the reserved green sauce. Sprinkle salt and pepper over everything. Serve the remaining green sauce in a bowl on the side, along with the grilled bread. Enjoy hot or at room temperature.

name: cheesy chicken + kimchi rice
note:
Can I use the red chili flakes/crushed red pepper I already own instead of Korean red pepper flakes? Yes, BUT: Korean red pepper flakes are way more mild than the red pepper flakes you probably have sitting in your pantry. Use 1/4 teaspoon of those red pepper flakes and add more spice at the end, if you want.

Feeding kids: In case you skimmed over the “special ingredient” note above the recipe, use mild (instead of spicy) kimchi, especially if you’re feeding kids or people wary of spice. It’s easy to add extra heat to individual bowls after the fact with gochujang, sriracha, or chili crisp.

Riff: Follow this same formula to make a Mexican rice by adding a 16-ounce jar of salsa instead of the kimchi. Add a can of drained black or pinto beans along with the rice for extra protein and fiber. Chorizo would be delicious with that combo! And see the chart in the intro for more one-pot rice bowl riff ideas from Julia.

More veggies, please: This meal packs a ton of veg thanks to the cabbage kimchi, but there’s always room for more! Add a diced onion and/or a bell pepper or sliced mushrooms — sauté them in the oil for a few minutes before you add the chicken (and add more oil if needed when you add the chicken). You could also add 2 cups of riced cauliflower to the pot along with the rice. Frozen corn or shredded or grated carrots would also be great — stir them in along with the cheese.

Add some toppings: Now’s a good time to dumpster dive! Go through your fridge/pantry for any of the following: thinly sliced scallions, chopped cilantro, chopped avocado, pickled onion or jalapeño, shredded carrot, chopped cashews or peanuts, more kimchi...

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will keep for up to three days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Eat them for breakfast or lunch the next day with a fried egg on top!

Vegetarian: So many options! Swap the chopped chicken out for crumbled tempeh or a vegan ground “meat.” Or add 2 cups of shelled edamame to the pot along with the rice. Or top your bowls with fried eggs. Or add all of the extra veggie options mentioned above for a cheesy veggie kimchi rice.

Dairy-free: The cheese is totally optional.

Gluten-free: Some brands of kimchi have gluten, others don’t. Read ingredient labels and choose one accordingly!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup neutral oil (such as vegetable, grapeseed, or canola)
ingredients.name: neutral oil (such as vegetable, grapeseed, or canola)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoonsKorean red pepper flakes, plus more for serving (see notes for more on this ingredient!)
ingredients.name: teaspoonsKorean red pepper flakes, plus more for serving (see notes for more on this ingredient!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: One 16-ounce jar cabbage kimchi, with its juice
ingredients.name: One 16-ounce jar cabbage kimchi, with its juice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups chicken or vegetable broth (or 2 cups water + 2 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable broth (or 2 cups water + 2 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon)

preparationSteps: Place 1/4 cup neutral oil in a large heavy pot (such as a Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces, and season with a large pinch of kosher salt and 2 teaspoons Korean red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring, until the chicken is firm and browned in spots, about 8 minutes.

Add the jar of kimchi to the pot, juice and all, along with 1 cup short-grain white rice and 2 cups broth. Turn the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, then immediately lower the heat so that the mixture simmers. Season the cooking liquid to taste with salt (the exact amount will depend on how salty your broth is), cover the pot, and cook until the rice is tender, 25 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and let the rice sit, covered, for 10 minutes.

Uncover the pot and stir in 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese. Keep stirring until the cheese is melted and well incorporated then season to taste one final time with salt, if more is needed. Serve immediately, with pepper flakes alongside for sprinkling on top.

name: sausage and pepper patty melts
note:
Riff: Not in the mood for a sandwich? Make sausage and pepper pasta instead! Cook the ground Italian sausage in a nonstick skillet until brown and cooked through, using a spatula to break it into crumbles as it cooks. Stir in a cup of thinly sliced roasted red peppers. Meanwhile, boil a pound of noodles. When they’re ready, drain them and add the noodles to the skillet and stir to combine. Top your bowls with grated Parm and red pepper flakes.

Do you own two cast-iron skillets? If so, use them both so you don’t have to work in batches!!

Prep ahead: Form your patties up to a day ahead of time and store them in an airtight container in the fridge. You could even pre-cook the patties and store them in the fridge then pick back up later with assembling and grilling the sandwiches.

Love your leftovers: Store any leftover sammies in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in an air fryer or the oven at 350°F until warmed through.

I’m feeling extra. Thinly slice and caramelize a yellow or white onion and add it to the mix. Here’s a good way to caramelize it as quickly as possible!

Vegetarian: Buy vegan sausage links, roasted red peppers, hot dog or hoagie  buns, and shredded cheese (mozzarella, provolone, or havarti would be good — you can buy pre-shredded or shred it yourself!). Warm the sausages per package directions (they’ll be pre cooked) then put them in the buns and top with peppers and shredded cheese. Bake or toast them until the cheese is melty and delicious. YUM!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use DF cheeses or omit the cheese, and use DF butter. Use gluten-free bread if avoiding gluten.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup thinly sliced roasted red peppers (from a jar that’s at least 8 ounces)
ingredients.name: thinly sliced roasted red peppers (from a jar that’s at least 8 ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning (or 1/4 teaspoon each dried thyme, dried oregano, and dried parsley)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning (or 1/4 teaspoon each dried thyme, dried oregano, and dried parsley)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound bulk Italian sausage  (I used mild, but you could use sweet or spicy)
ingredients.name: bulk Italian sausage  (I used mild, but you could use sweet or spicy)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more if needed, divided
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, plus more if needed

preparationSteps: On a sheet pan or clean countertop, place 4 slices of provolone on 4 slices of bread. Sprinkle evenly with 1 cup roasted red peppers, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan, and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning.

Lay a large piece of parchment paper on a cutting board or on the counter. Divide 1 pound Italian sausage into 4 even-sized balls, and place them on the parchment. Take another piece of parchment paper and, one at a time, cover the balls with the parchment and use your hand to smush them into flat, thin patties.

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tablespoon butter to the skillet and swirl until melted. Rip off another small piece of parchment. Add 2 of the patties to the skillet. Cover 1 patty with the parchment and smush it one more time using a spatula until the patty is very thin and about the size of your bread slices.

Season the patties with a pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper. Cook until browned and cooked through, 1 to 3 minutes per side. If the butter starts burning, just reduce the heat! Transfer the patties to 2 of the cheese-topped slices of bread, then repeat with the remaining patties and another tablespoon of butter.
Top the patties with the remaining 4 slices of cheese and bread.

Wipe out the skillet with paper towels or a clean dish cloth then, over medium-low heat, melt another tablespoon of unsalted butter, swirling it around the pan. Add 2 sandwiches and cook, flipping and moving the sandwiches around, until golden brown on both sides and the cheese has melted, 3 to 5 minutes. Transfer to plates. Repeat with the remaining sandwiches, adding more butter if the skillet is dry. Cut in half and serve!

name: one-pot chicken tikka masala stew
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: And you will have a LOT of them! Freeze 2-cup portions in quart Ziplocs for a quick lunch when you need it in a few weeks or months.

Vegetarian: Omit the chicken, add 1 pound diced Yukon gold potatoes or another can of chickpeas. Use vegetable stock.

Make ahead: This is a GREAT make ahead meal. If it thickens up too much, just stir in liquid until it’s a nice stew-y consistency that you like.

Can I use brown rice: Yes, but it won’t break down as much and in my opinion won’t be as tasty.

Special ingredient: Use the leftover curry paste to make my chicken and rice with coconut curry sauce next. Want another stew? Try my Red Curry Chickpea Stew.

Feeding kids: Mattis (age 2) is comically bad at using spoons, so to feed this to him, I fished out big chunks of chicken, chickpeas and cauliflower and fed it to him with a fork! Calum (5 months) is going to start eating soon, and to feed this to him I will just cut up the chicken into tiny pieces, lightly mash the chickpeas and cauliflower, and let him go at it!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons cooking oil, preferably coconut oil
ingredients.name: cooking oil, preferably coconut oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2/3 cup white rice (such as long grain or jasmine)
ingredients.name: white rice (such as long grain or jasmine)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch kale (preferably lacinato/dinosaur kale but curly works)
ingredients.name: kale (preferably lacinato/dinosaur kale but curly works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: yogurt or sour cream for dolloping on top, bread or naan for dunking
ingredients.name: Optional: yogurt or sour cream for dolloping on top, bread or naan for dunking

preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoons oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Stir in 1 medium diced yellow onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring often. Add 4 minced garlic cloves and cook for an additional 2 minutes.

When the onion and garlic are tender and translucent, stir in 3 tablespoons red curry paste, 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon garam masala, and 3/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Stir until spices are fragrant, about 1 minute.

Stir in 3 cups chicken stock, 1 (28-ounce) can tomato purée, and 1 (14-ounce) can coconut milk and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low heat and stir in 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, 1 (10- to 16- ounce) bag cauliflower florets — break up any large florets before you throw them in, you want each piece to be easy to eat with a spoon! — 1 (14-ounce) can drained chickpeas, 2/3 cup white rice, 1 tablespoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, until the chicken easily shreds when pulled apart with two forks.
Meanwhile, pull the stems out of 1 bunch of kale and roughly chop it. Finely chop 1/2 cup cilantro leaves and stems.
Transfer the chicken thighs to the cutting board and use two forks to shred apart. Return chicken to the pot along with the chopped kale and cilantro. Stir until the kale is tender, 2 to 3 minutes.

Stir in the juice of 1 lemon, and adjust salt and pepper seasoning to taste. I always need more salt! You might want your stew to be more liquidy — if so, stir in more chicken broth. If you love spicy food, stir in some cayenne!
Serve stew with a dollop of yogurt and a sprinkle of cilantro on top and a piece of bread for dunking.

If you serve the soup later, the rice will continue to soak up the liquid, so it will continue to thicken. Heat it back up over medium heat and stir in chicken broth or water a little bit at a time until it reaches the soup-y consistency you like.

name: crispy artichoke and chicken salad
note:
Leftovers are a great thing: Kale is a very hearty green (even when dressed!), so you can store your leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days! Like I said, just don’t add your croutons or nuts until you’re ready to eat or they’ll get soggy. Store the croutons at room temp in an airtight container.

Prep ahead: You can pre-make the dressing days in advance, stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Feel free to marinate the chicken up to 24 hours (also covered in the fridge), but don’t go any longer than that or it’ll get rubbery.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Choose from any or all of these shortcuts: Go the pre-chopped kale route. Use a rotisserie chicken in lieu of baking chicken breasts. Buy some pre-made croutons. Use your favorite salad dressing instead of making this one from scratch (but DO come back to this dressing when you’ve got a little more time bc it’s so so good).

Air fry the artichokes: I don’t love air fryers because the basket is tiny and you have to cook in batches and I ain’t got time for that. But if you love it — air fry them at 425°F for 12 to 15 minutes. FYI, crispy artichokes also make a great snack/appetizer — serve them with the dilly sauce from the salmon for dipping!

What to do with your leftover half bunch of parsley: Put it on EVERYTHING! Leave no recipe ungarnished! Mince it all up and keep it in a tupperware in the fridge. Throw it in tuna salad! Over grilled veggies! etc. Parsley is a diuretic and can assist in the body’s natural detoxification process. I LOVE the stuff and always have it around.

Vegetarian: Throw in a second can of white beans. Aim to get two varieties  (like Great Northern + navy or cannellini + Great Northern) for extra biodiversity/nutrients. Another option would be to swap the chicken for sliced or whole bella mushrooms (you can marinate them in the artichoke brine and all!).

Df/gf: Use your favorite dairy-free Parmesan or just omit it from the dressing. For gf: Make your croutons from gluten-free bread (or buy gluten-free croutons).

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (14- to 16-ounce) cans or jars ofmarinatedartichokes or 1 Costco-sized jar (Read the instructions below before you even think about draining those artichokes! And see the “subs” section if you can’t find marinated artichokes.)
ingredients.name: or jars ofmarinatedartichokes or 1 Costco-sized jar (Read the instructions below before you even think about draining those artichokes! And see the “subs” section if you can’t find marinated artichokes.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14-ounce) can white beans such as cannellini, navy, or Great Northern, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: white beans such as cannellini, navy, or Great Northern

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch lacinato (flat leaf) kale, ribs removed and thinly sliced (or, 4 to 5 packed cups of pre-chopped kale!)
ingredients.name: lacinato (flat leaf) kale, ribs removed and thinly sliced (or, 4 to 5 packed cups of pre-chopped kale!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 bunch flat leaf parsley, finely chopped
ingredients.name: flat leaf parsley

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup chopped roasted almonds (or really any nut!)
ingredients.name: chopped roasted almonds (or really any nut!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Worcestershire or 1 anchovy filet, mashed to a paste
ingredients.name: Worcestershire or 1 anchovy filet, mashed to a paste

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Place 2 chicken breasts in a shallow bowl. Drain the juice from 2 jars/cans of marinated artichokes right over top of the chicken — this is going to marinate the chicken! Add a big pinch of salt and pepper to the bowl and toss to coat.

Place a kitchen towel over your largest rimmed baking sheet, then pour the drained artichokes over top. Pull off any tough leaves you see. Squeeze them to get off any excess moisture, then remove the towel so that the artichokes are directly on the baking sheet. Spread them out so they’re not touching, then roast for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, pat the chicken breasts dry, then scooch the artichokes over and add the chicken to the baking sheet.
On a separate rimmed baking sheet, toss together 2 cups cubed sourdough bread, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1 grated garlic clove.

Place both baking sheets in the oven for 15 minutes (chicken and artichokes on the bottom rack, bread on the middle rack), or until the chicken breasts register an internal temperature of 160°F. Transfer the chicken breasts to a cutting board so that they don’t continue cooking on the hot baking sheet. I like my croutons crisp on the outside but soft on the inside, so 15 minutes is perfect for me. But if you like yours super crunchy, you might need to keep cooking them!

Meanwhile, while everything’s in the oven, make the dressing! In a large salad bowl (we’re going to make the dressing right in the bowl where we toss the salad), whisk together all of the ingredients (3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, the zest of 1 lemon, the juice of 2 lemons, 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon worcestershire, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, 1 grated  garlic clove, a pinch of red pepper flakes, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt). Taste and season with more salt or vinegar if you want it saltier or tangier!

Drain 1 can white beans and add them to the bowl of dressing. I like to lightly mash them with a fork to help them absorb the dressing, but that’s optional. Add 1 bunch kale, thinly sliced (or 5 cups chopped kale), right on top, and sprinkle with a big pinch of salt. Use your hands to massage the kale, AKA squeeze it together in your fists, 8 to 12 times, until it starts to feel soft. Cut the cooked chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces and throw them in the bowl along with 1/2 bunch of chopped parsley and the crispy artichokes.

If you plan to eat the entire salad right now: Toss 1/3 cup chopped almonds and the croutons into the salad. But if you’re planning to have leftovers, keep those on the side and add to each salad individually!
Toss everything together. Taste. You might need to add salt and pepper to make it all come together — this is a lot of ingredients! Add salt ‘til it tastes good, that’s my motto.
Garnish with more Parm because why the heck not and DIG IN!

name: sheet-pan roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and 1-inch cubed
ingredients.name: large sweet potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (15 ounce) cans chickpeas, drained but not rinsed (try to find the canned chickpeas that are salted — they’re much more flavorful)
ingredients.name: chickpeas, drained but not rinsed (try to find the canned chickpeas that are salted — they’re much more flavorful)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped soft green herbs such as cilantro, dill, parsley, mint, and/or basil (I used dill and parsley)
ingredients.name: chopped soft green herbs such as cilantro, dill, parsley, mint, and/or basil (I used dill and parsley)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Peel and cut 2 sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes. Dump 2 cans of chickpeas into a colander. Shake them so that all of the liquid drains out, but do not rinse them.

Put a couple paper towels down on your largest rimmed baking sheet, then pour the drained chickpeas over top. Use another paper towel to blot them to remove all of the liquid. Discard the paper towels. There will be some chickpea skins on the baking sheet now — no need to pick them out. They’ll roast up into crispy little bits and be delicious!

Add the cubed sweet potatoes, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon ground coriander, 3/4 teaspoon ground turmeric, and a pinch of cayenne pepper to the baking sheet and use your hands to toss everything together to evenly coat all the veggies.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are golden on the outside but fork tender on the inside.
While that’s in the oven, pickle the onions and make the whipped feta.

To pickle the onions, slice 1 red onion as thinly as you can. Place the slices in a jar or sealable container, then squeeze the juice of 4 limes in, plus 2 teaspoons sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Put the lid on and shake to combine! The longer these sit, the better (and prettier — they’ll turn bright pink after a few hours!) they’ll be, but 30 minutes is plenty of time to be very tasty. They stay good for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

To make the whipped feta, add 1 8-ounce block feta, 1/2 cup Greek yogurt, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, and a pinch of salt to a blender and blend until smooth, scraping down the sides several times if needed. If it’s too thick and your blender is having a hard time blending, just add a tiny bit of water at a time until it’s able to blend more smoothly.
Once roasted, taste a chickpea and a sweet potato to make sure they have enough salt. If not, sprinkle salt over them a pinch at a time until they’re salted to your taste.
Spread a nice big spoonful of whipped feta over the bottom of your bowl or plate and top it with a pile of roasted veggies. Add some chopped green herbs and pickled onions. Dig in!
servings: Serves 4 (could feed 6 if you add a grain)

name: peanut vegetable curry
note:
So how much curry paste do I use? This will depend on how spicy the brand you have is — they vary a lot. Thai Kitchen red curry paste is really weak, so use 4 to 5 tablespoons of it. Mae Ploy, Mekhala, and Maesri on the other hand are REALLY spicy, so start with 2 tablespoons. Blue Elephant brand has medium spice, so start with 2 tablespoons, and add more if desired. If you have a brand of red curry paste not mentioned here, taste it before you add any. Is it super spicy? Use the scant tablespoon starting point. Is it totally mild? Go the 2 to 3 tablespoon route. Remember, it’s easier to add more spice than it is to dial it back!!

Cook it in a slow cooker: Sauté the onion and aromatics in a skillet as written. Add them to your slow cooker along with the other veggies, all the liquid ingredients, and peanut butter. Stir to combine, cover, and cook on low for 5 to 6 hours or high for 3 to 4 hours. Add cilantro at the end and serve over rice you’ve prepped separately!

Leftovers are a good thing: This curry freezes wonderfully. If you are cooking for one or two, go ahead and fix it all and freeze the rest in a freezer-safe Ziploc. You could even double the recipe if you want a yummy freezer meal ready to go in the coming weeks/months.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Save time by buying pre-chopped vegetables. Look for pre-chopped fresh onions or frozen onions. And you can always find pre-chopped butternut squash this time of year. Add a pound of pre-sliced mushrooms and you’ve got yourself a delicious curry!

Gimme greens: Chopped spinach, kale, or chard would be delicious in this. Just add it at the end, stirring until it wilts.

Must have meat: Add cubed chicken breast or thighs (I prefer thighs here!) at the same time as the liquids. Or you could add cubed tofu, also at the same time as the liquids. First press the tofu between two paper towels and under a heavy book for 20 minutes.

Dairy-free/gluten-free/vegetarian: It’s already dairy free. Use tamari or coconut aminos instead of soy sauce to avoid gluten. Use a vegan fish sauce or soy sauce if you need to eliminate the fish sauce.

Now I’m on a Thai kick: I know: Thai flavors are addicting. Try my Thai Turkey Curry Meatballs or One-Pan Coconut Curry Chicken with Roasted Vegetables and Lime next! They’re fan faves.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons cooking oil (I like using coconut oil for curries)
ingredients.name: cooking oil (I like using coconut oil for curries)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 5 tablespoons red curry paste (see notes)
ingredients.name: red curry paste (see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12- to 16-ounce) bag cauliflower florets, cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: cauliflower florets

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 ½ cups sweet potatoes, cut into bite-size pieces (peeling is optional — I just wash them well)
ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: cut into bite-size pieces (peeling is optional — I just wash them well)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large carrots, peeled and cut ¼ inch thick
ingredients.name: large carrots
ingredients.note: peeled and cut ¼ inch thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon maple syrup (or coconut sugar or brown sugar or omit)
ingredients.name: maple syrup (or coconut sugar or brown sugar or omit)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup chopped cilantro (use the leaves AND stems!)
ingredients.name: chopped cilantro (use the leaves AND stems!)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil (as if you’re cooking pasta). Add 1 1/2 cups rice and cook until tender, about 17 minutes for white rice or 30 minutes for brown rice. Drain the rice, then return it to the pot and cover it until you’re ready to eat.
While the rice is cooking, heat a large pot or dutch oven over medium-high heat. Warm 2 tablespoons oil then add 1 diced yellow onion. Sauté for 3 minutes, stirring frequently.

Once the onion is soft, stir in 5 tablespoons red curry paste, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute. It’ll be clumping around the onion and starting to stick to the pot — you’re right on track!
Stir the cauliflower, sweet potatoes, and carrots into the pot until they are coated in the curry mixture.
Stir in 1 can of coconut milk, 1 cup stock, 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tablespoons peanut butter, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, and 1 tablespoon maple syrup.

If all of your vegetables are not covered with liquid, add more stock until they are. Crank the heat up to high, and once you reach a low boil, reduce the heat to medium-low so that it’s just barely simmering (small little bubbles). Cook for 15 minutes uncovered, until all vegetables are tender and the curry broth has thickened.

Turn off the heat and stir in the juice of 1 lime and 1/2 cup chopped cilantro. Taste. Add more soy sauce if it needs more salt, more lime juice if it needs more tang, more peanut butter if it needs more… peanut flavor.
Serve the curry over rice.

name: one-skillet crispy chicken burrito bowls
note:
You can use bone-in skin-on chicken breasts, but add them to the top of the rice after it’s been cooking in the oven for 10 minutes.

You can use boneless skinless chicken thighs, but skip the searing step completely and add them to the top of the rice at the same time as the directions above.

Nope: you can’t use brown rice, but you can use any white rice.

Try sauteeing an onion and a bell pepper in the chicken fat for 4 minutes before adding the rice for adding veggies. Or, try stirring in 1 cup of cauliflower rice along with the salsa!

Or, try stirring in 1 cup of cauliflower rice along with the salsa!

You can use any salsa you like! I also tested this recipe using La Victoria’s salsa verde. I use mild when I’m feeding kids, medium when feeding adults-only.

Kidney beans or pinto beans would be great in place of the black beans. Really, any canned (or simply pre-cooked) bean works!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2  1/4 cups water or low-sodium chicken stock
ingredients.name: water or low-sodium chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5 ounce) can black or kidney beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black or kidney beans

ingredients.name: shredded Cheddar cheese (depending on how cheesy ya like it!)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Place one oven rack in the center and one on the top rung.

Season 4 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs with about 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt per thigh. Warm a 12-inch skillet, Dutch oven, or other ovenproof skillet/pot over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs, skin-side down. Nope, you don’t need any oil - you’ll see how much grease those thighs are about to put off!

Cook thighs, skin-side down, for 4 to 6 minutes, until crispy and golden-brown. Transfer to a holding plate. Stir 1 1/2 cups white rice into the chicken fat until it is coated and toast the grains for about 3 minute, or until they’re actually browning a bit. Stir in 1 jar La Victoria Suprema Salsa, 2 1/4 cups water or chicken stock, and 1 can black beans. If you use water, also stir in 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low and cover for 7 minutes.

Uncover, stir, then place the chicken thighs over the rice, skin-side up, so that the skin is above the liquid. If the rice is stuck to the bottom of the skillet when you stir in, add another little splash of water to the skillet to make it easy to scrape up. Bake on the center rack in the oven, uncovered, for 30 to 35 minutes, until the rice is tender. The rice on top might look crunchy from the heat, so be sure to actually stick a fork in there and check the rice underneath the top layer.
Raise the oven heat to broil.

Use a fork to fluff the rice all around and under chicken. Scatter 1 to 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese all over the top of the rice and chicken. Broil for 2 to 3 minutes, until cheese is melted - keeping an eye on it with the oven light on the entire time to make sure the chicken skin doesn’t burn.
Top with your desired burrito bowl toppings!

name: crispy butternut squash salad with aged gouda and pecans
note: Make it a meal: To keep it vegetarian, I’d roast some chickpeas along with the butternut squash. For my meat lovers, serve this salad alongside any meat. To keep things simple, buy a rotisserie chicken and call it a night.

ingredients.name: olive oil (for coating squash slices)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces aged gouda, shaved with a vegetable peeler (or shaved then crumbled), a bit over a half a cup
ingredients.name: aged gouda, shaved with a vegetable peeler (or shaved then crumbled), a bit over a half a cup

ingredients.name: cuppecan halves, lightly toastedthen broken using your actual hands

ingredients.name: salt and pepper to taste (start with a good pinch of salt)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F (218°C)
Place the sliced squash in a big bowl and toss with enough olive oil (about 2 tablespoons) to coat evenly. Season with a good pinch of salt and pepper and toss again.

Spread the slices on a parchment-lined baking sheet in a single layer (use two baking sheets if you’re making a ton of chips, they should not overlap because they’ll steam instead of getting crisp). Sprinkle the squash lightly on one side with smoked paprika.

Roast until the squash slices begin to turn dark brown or black at the edges, about 30 minutes, checking occasionally and turning them over halfway through. You may need to remove some of the smaller ones earlier because they’ll brown faster. Again: this sounds like a drag. It’s worth it.

While the squash is roasting, make the dressing. Combine all of the ingredients (6 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, 1 teaspoon maple syrup, a big pinch of salt, and a few grinds of pepper) in a jar with a tight-fitting lid and shake until emulsified and creamy. Taste and add more salt and pepper as needed.

When the squash has cooled, arrange 5 big handfuls of mixed greens on a large platter. Top with 4 ounces shaved gouda, 1/2 cup toasted pecans, and the cooled butternut squash chips. Drizzle with desired amount of the dressing (not all of it! start with about 1/3, then add more as desired).
Show off your gorgeous salad at the table. Toss, taste for dressing, add more if desired, and serve. Serve any remaining dressing on the side.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Thinly slice 2 heads of romaine and set aside in a large bowl.

In a food processor, place 4 small torn-up slices of sourdough bread and pulse until the texture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add 1/2 cup pepitas. Pulse until roughly chopped. Place crumble on one half of the prepared sheet pan. Drizzle with 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and a few grinds of pepper, and toss to coat. Don’t place in the oven yet!

Wipe out the food processor (it doesn’t need to be perfect) and add 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 6 anchovies, 2 garlic cloves, the zest (use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to grate it right into the food processor) and juice of 1 lemon, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Process until smooth. Taste and add more lemon juice or salt as desired. Set aside.
Place 4 salmon filets on the other half of your sheet pan. Smear the filets with just enough Caesar dressing to coat them lightly. Spread the filets at least 1 inch apart.

Roast for 12 to 15 minutes or until the salmon reaches 125°F internally for medium (my preferred!) or 145°F or more well done salmon (if you have really thick filets, they may need to cook a few extra minutes). If your crumble is getting really brown but your salmon isn’t done yet, cover the crumble with foil (or remove it from the sheet pan) to prevent it from burning.
Toss the romaine with your preferred amount of dressing and half of the crumble then add the remaining crumble and salmon on top. Top with more Parm and dig in!

name: seared tuna with sesame noodles
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the noodle sauce recipe above and buy a pre-made peanut noodle sauce from the store and toss that with the cooked noodles. Or you could go for the super quick tuna and wilted spinach combo I mentioned above in the foreword.

Meal prep: You can go ahead and prep the tuna with the marinade and everything bagel seasoning, wrap it tightly, and keep in the fridge until it’s time to cook and eat. Pat it dry again before searing in case any condensation got on it. You could also go ahead and cook the noodles and/or the noodle sauce and reheat just before it’s time to eat.

Leftovers are a good thing: If you’re cooking for one or two, you can easily halve this recipe. Or cook it all and enjoy for lunches over the next two days!

Vegetarian: Sesame-crusted tofu would be delish! Press a block of extra-firm tofu between two paper towels or dish towels for at least 10 minutes to drain out excess water. Cut it into 1/2-inch think planks, and marinate them in the soy sauce and sesame oil while you prepare the noodles and sauce. Before cooking, dip the tofu planks in a whisked egg wash then press them into the everything bagel seasoning. If vegan, you can omit the egg, but the seasonings won’t stay on quite as well. Pan fry the sesame planks in the cooking oil for about 3 to 4 minutes per side.

Dairy-free, gluten-free: It’s both! (Just be sure whichever noodles you use are free of gluten.)

I’m new here — what’s the other WTC tahini recipe? Sheet-Pan Honey-Roasted Chicken, Carrots, and Brussels Sprouts with Tahini Yogurt! And here are two more from my blog archives: Roasted Veggie Grain Bowls with Lemon-Tahini Sauce and Salmon & Cauliflower Rice Bowls with Tahini Green Goddess Sauce.

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Do NOT add salt to the water. Cook the noodles per package instructions adding 6 ounces of snow or snap peas to the water for the last 1 minute. Drain, rinse well, and set aside.
Meanwhile, rub 4 tuna steaks with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. Let them sit out at room temperature marinating while you get the noodle sauce going.

In a large saucepan or skillet, warm 1 tablespoon sesame oil over medium-high heat. Cook 1 thinly sliced red bell pepper, 1 bunch of thinly sliced green onions, 4 minced garlic cloves, and 1 inch of fresh ginger that you’ve grated or minced for 3 to 4 minutes, until the bell pepper is tender. Stir in 1 to 3 teaspoons of red chili flakes, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon for 30 seconds to toast the spices. Turn the heat down to medium and stir in 1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tablespoons tahini, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1 tablespoon lime juice or vinegar. Stir until the tahini has dissolved into the sauce. It will look kinda chunky and weird — don’t fret. Turn the heat to low.
Now let’s cook the tuna! Warm a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. We want it really perfectly hot, so we are going to go ahead and start preheating the pan while we prep the tuna.

Pat the tuna steaks dry with a paper towel or clean dish towel. Rub them with 1 tablespoon sesame oil (total). Pour 3 tablespoons everything bagel seasoning onto a plate in an even layer, then press the tuna steaks into it until completely coated. You might need to add more seasoning to the plate as you go.

Add 1 tablespoon cooking oil to the skillet, which should now be piping hot. Swirl to coat the skillet, then add the tuna steaks to the skillet. Cook for 30 to 45 seconds, until the seeds on the first side are lightly golden. Use tongs to flip it and cook the second side for 30 to 45 seconds. Then, using the tongs, sear the smaller two sides for about 20 seconds each. Transfer the tuna to a cutting board.
Toss the cooked noodles and snow peas in the prepared noodle sauce until well coated. You might need to add a splash of water to make things more saucy.
Slice the tuna and serve with the noodles!

name: cheesy one-pan baked meatballs
note:
Make ahead: Prep these meatballs up to two days ahead of time and keep them in the fridge until you’re ready to bake ‘em for dinner.

Freezer meal: Meatballs are the ultimate stock-the-freezer meal. If you’re planning to save some of your batch, I’d recommend freezing them after their first bake. So once you pour the fat off, pull out however many you want to freeze and let those cool completely. (Continue cooking the rest as written, and just reduce the marinara as needed based on how many you pulled out!) Once the leftover meatballs are cool, throw them in a Ziploc bag and freeze. To cook, let them thaw in the fridge then pick the recipe where you left off! You can also freeze fully cooked meatballs + the sauce — just reheat together in a pot on the stove.

Riffs:Meatball subs: Cook the meatballs up until the cheese step. Scoop 3 meatballs and plenty of sauce into toasted sandwich rolls. Sprinkle lots of mozzarella in there. Broil until the cheese is melty. Meatball sliders: Grab a 12 pack of King’s Hawaiian rolls and cut the entire flat of rolls in half horizontally to create a top and a bottom. Spread marinara over the bottom and place one meatball on each bun. Sprinkle with lots of cheese. Put the top on. Brush the tops with butter and sprinkle with salt. Bake for 15 minutes on 375°F until melty and delicious. Creamy pesto meatballs: Bake the raw meatballs for 35 minutes at 375°F. Meanwhile, your largest skillet or saucepan, whisk 2 cups of pesto together with 1/2 cup heavy cream over medium heat until Warm. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed. Stir the cooked meatballs into the creamy pesto sauce and cook, lid on, over medium-low for an additional 10 minutes.

Meatball subs: Cook the meatballs up until the cheese step. Scoop 3 meatballs and plenty of sauce into toasted sandwich rolls. Sprinkle lots of mozzarella in there. Broil until the cheese is melty.

Meatball sliders: Grab a 12 pack of King’s Hawaiian rolls and cut the entire flat of rolls in half horizontally to create a top and a bottom. Spread marinara over the bottom and place one meatball on each bun. Sprinkle with lots of cheese. Put the top on. Brush the tops with butter and sprinkle with salt. Bake for 15 minutes on 375°F until melty and delicious.

Creamy pesto meatballs: Bake the raw meatballs for 35 minutes at 375°F. Meanwhile, your largest skillet or saucepan, whisk 2 cups of pesto together with 1/2 cup heavy cream over medium heat until Warm. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed. Stir the cooked meatballs into the creamy pesto sauce and cook, lid on, over medium-low for an additional 10 minutes.

Feeding kids: My toddlers (and many others!!) LOVE meatballs. If they’re sensitive to spice, you can cut back on the red pepper flakes, but this amount really doesn’t make them spicy. If they hate marinara, just pull a couple out and bake separately without sauce.

Gimme some greens: These would be delicious served alongside my Simple Green Salad with Apple Cider Vinaigrette. Or, make this sautéed kale (cook it in 1 tablespoon oil instead of the pork fat).

Vegetarian: Use a ground meat alternative like Beyond Beef.

Dairy-free: Omit the Parmesan or use a dairy-free sub, such as VioLife. Same with the mozzarella — omit or use a plant-based alternative.

Gluten-free: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs like this or almond meal, and gf bread. Instead of bread, you could also serve the meatballs over gluten-free noodles like Banza.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds ground beef (or 2 pounds of truly any combination of ground meat)
ingredients.name: ground beef (or 2 pounds of truly any combination of ground meat)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh parsley or basil, finely chopped, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: fresh parsley or basil, finely chopped, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 loaf of good crusty bread, like a sourdough
ingredients.name: of good crusty bread, like a sourdough

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (25 ounce) jar of your favorite pasta sauce (mine is Rao’s brand marinara)
ingredients.name: of your favorite pasta sauce (mine is Rao’s brand marinara)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil.

In a large bowl, use your hands to combine 2 pounds ground beef, 2 large eggs, 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.
Form 25 to 30 meatballs (they should be a little bigger than golf balls) and place them in the baking pan. You’ll have to really cram them in there!
Bake the meatballs for 20 minutes. Slice the loaf of bread into big thick slices, place them on a baking sheet and set aside for later.

After 20 minutes, remove the meatballs from the oven and carefully pour off the fat (pour it into an old jar or a bowl lined with aluminum foil. Once it cools you can just crumple it up and throw it away).
Pour 1 (25 ounce) jar of tomato sauce over top and stir gently (so that you don’t break the meatballs apart) to combine everything together.

Lower the oven temperature to 325°F and return the meatballs to the oven for 30 minutes. The sauce might look a little watery after this, just stir everything together gently until it looks delicious.

Turn the broiler to high. Sprinkle 1 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese all over the top of the meatballs. Place the meatballs on the top rack of the oven and the bread on the rack beneath them and broil for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese is melted and lightly golden brown and the bread is warm. Watch them closely while broiling — all broilers are different and I don’t want you to burn the cheese!
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley (and more red pepper flakes if you like) and dig in :)

name: sheet-pan chicken with artichokes and potatoes
note:
Make ahead: The most time-consuming / hands-on part of this recipe is halving the baby potatoes and chopping the herbs. You can do that up to a day in advance, storing them in the fridge. You can marinate the chicken ahead of time too, but again, don’t marinate it for more than 24 hours — the acidity in the brine will make it rubbery!

How many artichoke hearts? It doesn’t really matter what size your jar of artichoke hearts is. Anything between 10 and 30 is great! See marinated artichoke sub below if you can’t find them.

Dairy-free + Whole30: Omit the butter (or, for df, use plant-based butter) and cheese!

Gluten-free: Already is!

Add more veg: You can throw a few handfuls of cruciferous veggies like broccoli or cauliflower florets into the mix! Or carrots or beets! But don’t overcrowd the pan. If needed, use a second sheet-pan.

Refresher on cooking oils: I rarely recommend cooking with extra-virgin olive oil. It has a smoke point of under 400°F and we are cooking at 450°F here, so your oven could get smoky and your food could burn… not what you want! Olive oil, avocado oil, or grapeseed oil are all neutral-tasting cooking oils with high smoke points that would be great for this.

Leftovers are a good thing: Whip out another sheet-pan and double this baby to reheat for lunches! That’s what I did. Mattis devoured the potatoes and chicken, but avoided the artichokes, for what it’s worth. Wait until you reheat to garnish with the Parm and herbs.

Vegetarian: Sub the chicken for a can of chickpeas.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, toss 1 1/2 to 2 pounds chicken thighs with 1 jar marinated artichoke hearts, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Dump the entire jar in — artichoke hearts, juices, everything. Cover and marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes or in the refrigerator for up to 12 hours. Don’t exceed 24 hours: The chicken will get rubbery from being in an acidic marinade for too long.
Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment paper.

Add 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes, 1 tablespoon cooking oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper to the baking sheet and toss to coat. Move the chicken and artichokes from the bowl of marinade to the sheet-pan, creating as even a layer as possible. DON’T just dump them onto the sheet-pan with the marinade — we don’t want all of that liquid on the baking sheet! So use some tongs or your hands to transfer them from bowl to pan.
Roast for 30 minutes.

Stir in 2 tablespoons butter, mixing the ingredients around on the sheet-pan to lightly coat them all. Taste a potato and season with more salt if needed. Garnish with 1/4 cup Parmesan and 2 tablespoons chopped soft herbs then dig in.

name: sheet-pan balsamic pork tenderloin with fennel and potatoes
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: You can skip marinating the pork and making the glaze (but what a waste of balsamic!) and simply roast everything per my timing instructions and serve with pesto!

Make ahead: Marinate the pork and chop the veggies as far as 24 hours in advance. Throw it in the oven and off you go!

But I’m obsessed with your green sauce and need to eat it: Skip the balsamic marinade, roast the pork totally plain, and serve this meal with green sauce!

I’m a vegetarian: Make the glaze (just don’t marinate pork with it!) and add chickpeas in with the potatoes and fennel for protein! Drizzle the vegetables with glaze.

Dairy-free: Omit the cheese or use your fave crumbly dairy-free cheese!

Leftovers are a good thing: Chop up any leftover pork and throw it into 15-minute peanut noods tomorrow for lunch!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds baby Dutch potatoes, halved
ingredients.name: baby Dutch potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup thinly sliced basil, dill, or parsley
ingredients.name: thinly sliced basil, dill, or parsley

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup crumbled ricotta salata, feta, goat cheese, or shaved Parmesan
ingredients.name: crumbled ricotta salata, feta, goat cheese, or shaved Parmesan

preparationSteps: Arrange oven grates so that they’re in the middle and bottom third of the oven. Preheat oven to 450°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Combine 1/2 cup balsamic vinegar, the juice of 1 orange, 1 tablespoon honey, 1 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes in a small pot or skillet. Place 1 1/2 to 2 pounds pork tenderloin in there too, curling it up so that it fits and is as submerged as possible. This will look kind of weird and gross — stay strong. Marinate the pork at room temperature while you prep and roast the veggies, OR marinate it for up to 24 hours in the refrigerator, if you’ve got time.

Trim the tall stems and root end off of the fennel. Cut it in half through the root, then cut it into 1/4-inch thick slices. Throw the slices on the sheet pan. Add 1 1/2 to 2 pounds halved baby Dutch potatoes to the pan. Drizzle veggies with 2 tablespoons neutral cooking oil and season generously with kosher salt and black pepper. Spread the vegetables out into an even layer.

Roast the vegetables for 25 minutes on the bottom rack of the oven. Stir, then make room for the pork tenderloin and add it to the pan, shaking off as much marinade as possible into the pot first. Don’t discard the marinade!

Return the sheet pan to the center rack of the oven and roast for 12 to 16 minutes, until the pork registers at least 140°F internally, but not over 145°F. Start checking it at the 12-minute mark, then stay very close by so that you can keep checking every minute or two after that!
While the pork roasts, bring the pot of marinade to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium until the sauce has reduced by half and thickened slightly. (It will continue thickening as it cools.)
Transfer the pork to a cutting board and let it rest for at least 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve the pork and vegetables garnished with basil, cheese, and the balsamic glaze.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Cut 1 head cabbage into four quarters by cutting it in half through the stem end, then in half again. Place on a large baking sheet. Add 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs to the same baking sheet. Drizzle all with a light coating of extra-virgin olive oil, sprinkle with 2 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper, and use your hands to evenly distribute the oil and spices.
Set aside (at room temperature) while you prep the rest of the salad.

Make the dressing by adding 1/3 cup creamy peanut butter, 1/3 cup toasted sesame oil, 3 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1 heaping tablespoon honey, 1 heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard, a big pinch of kosher salt, and several grinds of pepper to a large jar and shaking to combine. (If you don’t have a jar, just whisk the ingredients together in a bowl.) It’s going to be thick! Now, add water a tiny splash at a time then shake, and repeat until you get a nice thick-but-drizzleable consistency — like a Caesar dressing. Taste and keep as is or adjust as desired — you can add more salt, more vinegar, whatever sounds/tastes good to you!
Now’s a good time to preheat the grill to 450°F.

Remove the ribs from 1 bunch of kale then chop the leaves into small pieces. Finely chop 1 cup cilantro leaves and stems and 1/2 cup mint leaves, and thinly slice 4 scallions. Add to a large serving bowl. Sprinkle with a big pinch of salt and massage the greens by squeezing them in your palms 7 to 10 times, until the kale feels a bit more tender.

Add 1 cup grated Parmesan or cheddar and 1/2 cup chopped peanuts to the bowl. (Caveat: If you plan to have leftovers, don’t add the peanuts to the big bowl — add them to each individual bowl instead as they’d get soft and mushy in the fridge.)
Now your grill should be nice and hot, so head outside to grill the cabbage and chicken.
If you haven’t already, clean the grates before grilling. Grill the chicken thighs for 6 to 7 minutes per side, and the cabbage for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until lightly charred all over.
Let them cool slightly, then chop the chicken and cabbage into small pieces and add to the bowl.
Toss with your desired amount of dressing (start with half of it and, if needed, add more a little at a time until it’s dressed to your liking!).
Divide the salad into bowls and serve with a lime wedge for squeezing over top just before digging in! (This is important!)

name: sheet-pan harvest bowl with cranberry vinaigrette

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (6- to 8-inch) pocket pita, spit into two layers
ingredients.name: pocket pita, spit into two layers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup roasted pepitas or chopped roasted pistachios
ingredients.name: roasted pepitas or chopped roasted pistachios

preparationSteps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Prep 2 sweet potatoes: Trim and peel the sweet potatoes. Slice in half crosswise, then in half lengthwise. Slice into 1/2-inch thick wedges. Transfer to a large bowl.
Chop fresh thyme leaves until you have 1 tablespoon, then add to the bowl. Add 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper and toss to coat.
Spread the sweet potatoes into an even layer on a baking sheet. Roast until golden brown underneath, 15 to 20 minutes.

While the sweet potatoes are roasting, split 1 pocket pita into two layers and tear into bite-size pieces. Add to the now-empty bowl with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil. Toss to coat. Cut 1 (8-ounce) block feta into 1/2-inch-thick slabs.

In a separate small bowl, whisk 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, the remaining 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, and a pinch each of salt and pepper until combined. Add 1/4 cup dried cranberries and toss to coat.

Flip the sweet potatoes, then scatter the pita over top. Break the feta into large pieces and add to the baking sheet. Return to the oven and roast until the pita is crisp and the feta is soft, 7 to 9 minutes.

Meanwhile, halve, core, and thinly slice 1 small Honeycrisp apple. Chop pistachios until you have 1/4 cup (if using; no need to chop if you’re using pepitas). Remove the pan from the oven, add 4 packed cups baby arugula, the apple, pepitas or pistachios, and the vinaigrette, and toss to combine. Serve warm.

name: grilled chicken and pita chop
note:
Feta brine = marinade: If you have time to marinate your chicken overnight (I wanted this recipe to be a quickie, which is why this isn’t written into the recipe!), add the chicken, all of the brine (liquid) from the feta, the Greek seasoning, and 2 tablespoons olive oil to a large bowl or ziploc. Refrigerate for up to 24 hours (but not much longer as it’ll start to make the chicken mushy). Shake it off and grill as written. DELISH!

Make it a pita sandwich: Instead of grilling your pita until crispy, simply grill it to warm it, then stuff it with the salad instead of cutting it into strips! Pita pockets!

Meal prep it: Make the entire salad minus tossing the pita strips into the salad. Divide the salad into 4 to 5 containers, store the grilled pita in an airtight container at room temperature, then toss in the pita and dressing before eating.

Tomato allergy: Add 3 thinly sliced and chopped radishes, 1 red bell pepper, and 1 green bell pepper in place of the tomatoes.

Love your leftovers: If you think you’ll have leftovers, sprinkle the grilled pita onto individual servings rather than tossing it all in, otherwise it will get soft and soggy. Store the salad sans pita in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days and store the pita in an airtight container at room temperature. You’ll have tossed that extra dressing in the fridge, too, so just freshen up leftover salad with a drizzle or two and top it with some crispy pita.

Vegetarian: Skip the chicken and this salad is still stellar but you can also sprinkle some crispy chickpeas in instead for added protein. Chickpeas or any white bean straight from the jar would also be great here — if you have time, let them marinate in the dressing for 30 minutes before adding everything else.

Gluten-free: Use gluten-free pita or cut corners and just grab a bag of gluten-free pita chips.

Dairy-free: Swap in dairy-free feta or a big handful of pitted Kalamata olives that you’ve roughly chopped to lend a similar salty, briny punch.

I don’t have a grill: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Place the pita on one rimmed baking sheet, and the chicken on another. Cook the pita for 7 to 10 minutes, until golden-brown and crisp. Cook the chicken for 20 to 25 minutes, until 165°F internally.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pita (or 2 slices of any good fresh bread, like a sourdough)
ingredients.name: pita (or 2 slices of any good fresh bread, like a sourdough)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon Greek or Italian seasoning (or za’atar!)
ingredients.name: Greek or Italian seasoning (or za’atar!)

preparationSteps: Preheat the grill (or oven!) to 450°F.

Place 1 1/2 pounds chicken on a plate and toss until evenly coated with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 teaspoons Greek seasoning, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Set aside at room temperature while you start chopping.

Use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to zest 1 lemon into a large serving bowl. Then add the juice from the zested lemon and the other lemon. Cut the third lemon into 4 wedges and set aside in a small bowl for serving later. Stir in 1 teaspoon Greek seasoning*, 2 teaspoons mustard, 1 teaspoon honey, and 1 teaspoon salt. Then, whisking as you stir, slowly pour in 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil. Taste and adjust as desired. Pour half of this dressing into a small jar or container for another time or to add more later based on how dressed you like your salads!!

Peel 1 English cucumbers like a zebra — meaning, peel every other strip so that the cucumber has stripes. Dice the cucumber and add it to the bowl. Dice 1 pound tomatoes, 1 red onion, 1 avocado, and finely chop 1/2 cup mint and add it all to the bowl. Toss to coat everything evenly. Taste and add more salt until delicious (I needed several big pinches!).
Coat 2 pita lightly all over in extra-virgin olive oil (and sprinkle with a little Greek seasoning and salt for bonus points).
TO USE THE GRILL TO COOK THE CHICKEN AND PITA:
Once the grill is preheated, cook the chicken for about 7 minutes per side (with the lid closed), or until 165°F internally. Transfer to a cutting board to cool.

Now turn one of the burners to medium-low, or if using charcoal, toast the pita over indirect heat, until crisp and golden-brown all over. Don’t close the lid, stand there and watch it closely! Bread loves to light on fire, especially when covered in oil, so don’t let that happen! Transfer the pita to the same cutting board as the chicken.
TO USE THE OVEN THE CHICKEN AND PITA:

Once the oven is preheated to 450°F, place the pita on one rimmed baking sheet, and the chicken on another (if using thighs, make sure they’re totally spread out). Cook the pita for 7 to 10 minutes, until golden-brown and crisp. Cook the chicken for 20 to 25 minutes, until 165°F internally.
FINISH THE SALAD:

Chop the chicken into pieces the same size as your veggies.add to the bowl. Crumble or chop the pita into small pieces right into the bowl (only if you think you'll eat the entire salad — otherwise add it straight to each individual portion). Remove 4 ounces feta from its brine and crumble it into the salad bowl.
Serve with a lemon wedge, and don’t forget to squeeze it over your salad just before eating! Trust me, it really brightens it up in a special way!

* Let the record state that I listed this ingredient out of order so that your teaspoon measuring spoon would be clean to measure the Greek seasoning instead of covered in honey and mustard. Out of order ingredients are my biggest pet peeve, but your cooking ease is my priority. Here to serve!!
servings: Serves: 4 (double or 1.5x the veggies if people are really hungry!

name: unstuffed tomatoes
note:
One less ingredient: If you want to avoid buying basil/parsley and having to chop it, you can just stir 2 tablespoons of pesto into the rice! But I do prefer it with chopped parsley.

Feeding picky eaters: My big boys (5 and 4) wouldn’t touch this, the baby (almost 2) ate enough for three grown men. To feed this meal work for my entire family, I would cook the turkey, then remove enough to make turkey quesadillas for the kids (just tortillas + cheese + turkey), then continue cooking the recipe as written for the adults. It’s fine that it’s missing some turkey — the recipe will still work. Actually, many containers of ground turkey come in 1.5 pound increments — get one of those and use 1/2 pound for the kids’ dinner!

I want cheesy rice: Amen! Stir in 1 cup of any cheese (feta, shredded cheddar, provolone, havarti, pepperjack, Parm!!!) after the rice bakes for 30 minutes, before adding the breadcrumbs on top. Delish!! Only reason I didn’t add cheese was to stay true to the classic stuffed tomato!

Serve it with chili crisp mayo: We had chili crisp mayo from last week in the fridge and dangggg it’s good served right on top of a big bowl of unstuffed tomatoes :).

Love your leftovers: If you’re anything like my house, there won’t be, but leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 4 days!

Prep ahead: Chop the onion and mince the garlic and refrigerate them together in an airtight container up to a day ahead. You can do the same with the chopped tomatoes, just refrigerate them in a separate container. The parsley can also be chopped and refrigerated up to a day ahead but if you’re using basil, wait to chop it because otherwise it will brown.

Vegetarian: Replace the ground turkey for 1 pound of ground plant-based sausage. Or swap in chopped mushrooms or a couple of cans of drained and rinsed chickpeas or white beans. And instead of chicken stock, use low-sodium vegetable stock.

Dairy-free: Use vegan pesto.

Gluten-free: Swap in gluten-free breadcrumbs.

Nut-free: Most jarred pestos contain pine nuts and some contain cashews or walnuts, so check the label if you or those your feeding have an allergy. Classico is one common brand that’s totally nut-free.
