ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons pesto (any kind! I love the one from Costco!)
ingredients.name: pesto (any kind! I love the one from Costco!)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Cook 1 finely chopped onion and 3 minced garlic cloves for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion has softened. Add 1 pound ground turkey, 1 teaspoon salt, and several grinds of pepper (about 1/4 teaspoon) and crank the heat up to medium-high. Cook, using a spatula to break the meat up into tiny crumbles, until no longer pink.

Stir in 1 cup short-grain white rice rice, 1 1/2 pounds diced tomatoes, 1/4 cup finely chopped basil or parsley, and a big pinch of salt (about 1/4 teaspoon) until combined. Stir in 1 1/2 cups chicken stock, bring it to a simmer over high heat, then turn off the heat. Squish everything down so that all of the rice is submerged in liquid. If needed, you can add another splash of liquid.
Cover the skillet (you can use any mismatched pot lid, or a baking sheet, or aluminum foil!) and bake for 30 minutes.
While the rice is baking, in a small bowl stir together 1 cup panko breadcrumbs and 2 tablespoons pesto to coat the breadcrumbs.
Remove the lid and test the rice. Is it tender? Proceed with the recipe! Is it still crunchy? Cover and cook for another 5 to 10, until tender.
Remove the lid and spread the pesto breadcrumbs over the rice. Return to the oven (uncovered!) for 10 minutes, or until golden-brown.
Let it cool down for 5 minutes, then serve!

name: seared steak with herby zhug-marinated tomatoes
note:
Feeding kids: Zhug is spicy! If you’re feeding littles or people sensitive to spice, you can discard the jalapeño seeds and/or one — or both! — jalapeños.

Prep ahead/love your leftovers: Leftover zhug will stay good for up to a week stored in an airtight container in the fridge. The oil will separate in the fridge; to reincorporate it, let it warm up on the counter, or you can microwave it for just a few seconds, then stir to combine. If you have leftover zhug, it’s delicious on pita, falafel, eggs, and roasted vegetables. You can swirl it into hummus for a snack or use it in place of hot sauce in pretty much any recipe. From Carolina: I often find myself making a triple batch at the beginning of the week and using it on my dinners, salads, and everything in between. Here are a few WTC meals that a drizzle of zhug would be an amazing addition to: sheet-pan chicken with artichokes and potatoessweet and spicy grilled chicken and onionsturkey zucchini burgersgreen chicken tortilla soupbacon kimchi fried ricecoconut curry lentil veggie stew

sheet-pan chicken with artichokes and potatoes

sweet and spicy grilled chicken and onions

turkey zucchini burgers

green chicken tortilla soup

bacon kimchi fried rice

coconut curry lentil veggie stew

Save time: From Carolina: Do you just want to put dinner on the table without chilling the steak ahead? Do it, I won’t tell anyone. I can’t tell you how many times I cooked a steak straight from the fridge and it still turned out great. Also, if you skipped the intro of this email, go back up and read the “gimme a shortcut” section under the Q&A for more time-saving tips!

I don’t have a food processor: You can use a blender. Add a small splash of water or extra EVOO if needed to get it going.

Vegetarian: Zhug — and a side of zhug-marinated tomatoes — would be great with falafel, crispy tofu, a frittata, or any other vegetarian main or side. I absolutely love it with roasted vegetables.

GF/DF: The recipe is both!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds bone-in rib eye (1 large or 2 small steaks), about 1 inch thick
ingredients.name: bone-in rib eye (1 large or 2 small steaks), about 1 inch thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: fresh lemon juice, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds beefsteak or heirloom tomatoes, sliced about 1/2 inch thick
ingredients.name: beefsteak or heirloom tomatoes, sliced about 1/2 inch thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: Neutral oil, such as sunflower or grapeseed
ingredients.name: Neutral oil, such as sunflower or grapeseed

preparationSteps: Prepare the steak: Place 1 1/2 pounds bone-in rib eye on a piece of parchment paper and season generously on all sides with kosher salt. Set aside at room temperature for at least 30 minutes; up to 1 hour.

Make the zhug-marinated tomatoes: In a mortar and pestle, combine the seeds of 4 green cardamom pods, 1 teaspoon coriander seeds, and 1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds. Crush them roughly, but no need to make a powder. (You can also do this by putting the spices between layers of paper towel and going over them a few times with a rolling pin.)
Transfer the crushed spices to a small dry skillet over medium heat and toast, shaking the pan occasionally, until slightly smoky and fragrant, about 2 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat.

Transfer the toasted spices to a food processor and add 1 cup roughly chopped fresh cilantro, 1/2 cup roughly chopped fresh parsley, 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 2 small roughly chopped jalapeños, 3 peeled garlic cloves, 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice, and a pinch of kosher salt. Pulse until the zhug reaches a chunky, loose consistency. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding more salt, lemon juice, or oil as needed.
In a medium bowl, add 1 1/2 pounds sliced tomatoes and about 1/3 cup of the zhug and gently toss to coat. Set aside to marinate while you cook the steak. Reserve the rest of the zhug for serving.
Pat the steak dry with paper towels. Season on all sides with kosher salt (not as much as you used the first time, just a regular pinch).

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat until it starts smoking, about 5 minutes. Add about 1 tablespoon of neutral oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Carefully lay the steak in the pan, laying it down away from you to keep the oil from splashing in your direction. If you have a grill press or a smaller skillet, set it on the steak to weight it down and increase contact with the hot surface. Cook, undisturbed, until the underside takes on a beautifully caramelized crust, 5 to 6 minutes.

Use tongs to carefully flip the steak and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes. The perfect medium-rare steak will measure 120°F at its thickest point; cook the steak to your desired temperature. Transfer the steak to a plate, and let it rest for 8 to 10 minutes.
Slice the steak against the grain. Top with flaky salt and dollops of zhug, and serve with the tomato salad.

name: sheet-pan spring salmon
note:
Leftovers are a great thing: If you have leftover salmon, make salmon salad! Throw the filets into a bowl. Stir in a small amount of dilly sauce at a time, mixing it with and shredding the salmon with your fork, until it holds together like tuna salad. You can add thinly sliced celery, but it’s delicious without! Thanks to my friend Bob for this leftovers tip!

Make it a niçoise: by adding soft-boiled eggs, olives, and some mixed greens to the platter.

Make ahead: Like I said, this is a great make-ahead situation. You can make the whole meal earlier in the day then pull it out for 30 minutes before mealtime to bring it to room temp! You could also of course prep your veggies and make the sauce a day (or even two days!) ahead of when you plan to cook.

If you’re feeding kids: I find that serving meals like this on a platter helps to give them “authority” over the situation. I let them “choose” their vegetable (potatoes and/or asparagus), then “choose” whether they want a whole or half piece of salmon. I serve it with the dilly sauce and ketchup. To be transparent: Calum (19 months) devoured this meal. Mattis (3) only ate the potatoes. Toddlers 

Vegetarian: I love the idea of a vegetarian niçoise salad. Cook the potatoes, asparagus, and dilly sauce as written, and serve them on a bed of greens (arugula, spinach, mixed greens, whatever!) with some hard- or soft-boiled eggs, olives, and any other veggie you’ve got (cucumber, tomatoes, etc.). You could add some cooked peas — or maybe some drained, rinsed, and roasted chickpeas — for added protein. Yum!

What’s with the organic lemon? Anytime I’m zesting lemons (or any citrus for that matter) I try to buy organic. Organic lemons are also typically larger than conventional, so you’ll get more zest and more juice. Obviously non-organic is a fine swap for this recipe if needed!

Gf/df: This meal is both gluten and dairy free as written!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes (fingerling or any little potato), halved lengthwise
ingredients.name: baby potatoes (fingerling or any little potato), halved lengthwise

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large organic lemon (Meyer lemon, if you can find them)
ingredients.name: large organic lemon (Meyer lemon, if you can find them)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons finely chopped dill (but go ahead and chop up 5 tablespoons — you will need 2 more for the sauce)
ingredients.name: finely chopped dill (but go ahead and chop up 5 tablespoons — you will need 2 more for the sauce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch asparagus (see paragraph above for a size explanation!)
ingredients.name: asparagus (see paragraph above for a size explanation!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 (6-ounce) salmon filets (skin on or off — doesn’t matter; buy the biggest, thickest filets and make sure they’re all about the same size)
ingredients.name: salmon filets (skin on or off — doesn’t matter; buy the biggest, thickest filets and make sure they’re all about the same size)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons finely minced chives (but go ahead and chop up 3 tablespoons — you need 1 more for the sauce!)
ingredients.name: finely minced chives (but go ahead and chop up 3 tablespoons — you need 1 more for the sauce!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 large organic lemon
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 large organic lemon

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper (or foil; I just prefer parchment).

Place 1 1/2 pounds of halved baby potatoes on the baking sheet and drizzle with 1 1/2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Spread them out so that they are not touching.
Place in the oven and roast for 20 minutes.
While the potatoes are roasting, prep 1 bunch asparagus by chopping 1 1/2 inches off of the bottom.

Now make the dilly sauce: Combine all ingredients (1 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard, the zest and juice of 1 large organic lemon, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/8 teaspoon black pepper, 2 tablespoons finely chopped dill, 1 tablespoon finely minced chives) in a pretty serving bowl.
After the potatoes have cooked for 20 minutes, remove the baking sheet from oven.

Scooch the potatoes all to one side — it’s OK if they’re touching now. In the middle of the sheet pan, add the salmon filets and drizzle them with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, a big pinch of salt and pepper, the zest of half a lemon, the juice of half a lemon, and 1 tablespoon dill (depending on how much dill ya like you can add more here if you want!). Use your hands to rub it in all over the salmon. The salmon filets can be touching — this will actually help them cook evenly!

Add the trimmed asparagus to the remaining empty spot on the baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper, and toss to coat.

Return the baking sheet to the oven to roast for 12 to 15 minutes. At the 12-minute mark, you’re going to peek inside. If the salmon is leaking white stuff, it’s finished! But it’s also a good idea to use a meat thermometer here. I like my salmon medium-rare (125°F) but you might like yours medium (135°) to medium-well (140°F). Do not surpass 140°! This is where salmon gets dry and chalky.

Toss the remaining 2 tablespoons chopped dill, 1 tablespoon minced chives, and juice of 1/2 lemon into the potatoes. Taste and add salt and pepper as needed. Sprinkle the rest of the chives over the asparagus and salmon.
If you’re eating immediately: Divide the salmon and vegetables between four plates, drizzle with the sauce (or serve it on the side — it’s good on everything), and dig in!
If you’re eating later: Throw everything on a pretty platter and refrigerate until meal time. Pull it out of the fridge 30 minutes before eating so that it comes to room temperature.
servings: Serves 4 (but can be adjusted to feed as many as you want!)

name: chicken meatballs with meyer lemon orzotto

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil (or any cooking oil)
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil (or any cooking oil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup of any breadcrumbs or almond flour (I used almond flour and they were so tender and perfect)
ingredients.name: of any breadcrumbs or almond flour (I used almond flour and they were so tender and perfect)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 organic lemon (preferably Meyer), divided
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 organic lemon (preferably Meyer)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Grease up a 12-inch oven-proof skillet with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil.

Crack 1 large egg into a bowl and whisk it. Add 1 pound ground chicken, 1/2 cup grated Parm, 1 tablespoon minced rosemary (mince the HECK out of it! Keep chopping until the pieces are teeny tiny! I hate getting a pokey piece of rosemary in my bite!), 1/3 cup breadcrumbs or almond flour, the zest of 1 lemon, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (omit if feeding spice wimps) to a large bowl and use a fork or your hands to stir until just combined.

Grease a tablespoon-sized measuring spoon with a bit of oil so that the chicken mixture doesn’t stick, then use it to scoop heaping (like majorly overflowing — each meatball should be about 2 tablespoons) spoonfuls of the chicken mixture into the skillet (don’t roll them until the end). You should wind up with anywhere from 14 to 18 meatballs. Grease up your hands (to prevent the meat mixture from sticking to your skin!) and roll the meat into meatballs.
Bake for 18 minutes.
Meanwhile, mince 1 shallot and 2 garlic cloves (but keep them separated on your cutting board — we’re going to add them at different times). Cut the zested lemon in half.
Transfer the cooked meatballs to a plate or bowl.

Place the skillet over medium heat (no need to wipe it out) and melt 3 tablespoons butter. Place the lemon cut-side down over on one side of the skillet to char it up (this will deepen the lemony flavor!).

Add the minced shallot and a pinch of salt to the other side of the skillet and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until tender. Stir in the minced garlic, 1 cup orzo, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes and continue cooking for 1 minute. Transfer the lemon to the cutting board. Stir in 2 cups chicken stock and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and cook, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the orzo is al dente.
Stir in more stock as needed until it’s loose and saucy, along with 1 cup frozen peas, the remaining 1/2 cup Parm, and the juice from the charred lemon.
Turn off the heat. Add the meatballs on top of the orzo and cover for several minutes to heat them through. Garnish with parm and red pepper flakes and some chopped parsley if you’ve got it. Dig in!

preparationSteps: Place 1/2 cup roasted salted cashews into a blender and cover with warm water. Set aside to soak while you start cooking the chicken.

Warm 1 tablespoon sesame oil in a 12-inch (preferably nonstick) skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 diced shallot and cook, stirring often, until tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 1 to 2 tablespoons red curry paste (2 will be a bit spicy), smashing it against the skillet to allow it to toast a bit. Stir in 2 pounds ground chicken and use your spatula to chop the chicken into tiny crumbles as it cooks. Once it is nearly cooked through and most of the moisture from the meat has evaporated, stir in 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, the juice of 1 lime, and 1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro until the excess liquid has all been absorbed. Set the meat aside.

Now let’s finish making the dressing. Drain the liquid out of the blender and add the remaining dressing ingredients (1/2 cup cilantro leaves and stems, juice of 1 lime, 1 tablespoon red curry paste, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon maple syrup or honey, pinch of salt, and water — start with 1/3 cup). Blend on high speed until smooth. If it’s too thick, blend in 1 tablespoon of water at a time until you get the right consistency. Set aside.

Now let’s put it all together! Grab a really large serving bowl. Chop 2 large romaine hearts into 1/2-inch pieces and throw them in the bowl. If there’s any leftover cilantro, chop it up and throw it in there. Season the greens with a big pinch of salt and pepper and toss to coast.
Add 1 diced avocado, 2 cups edamame, 1 1/2 cups shredded carrots, 1 cup chopped cashews, 1 cup wonton strips, and half of the cooked chicken. Pour 1/2 cup dressing over top and toss to coat.
I like to take a chef’s knife and fork and chop the salad into tiny bits at this point! It seriously makes it taste better, you must try it!
Toss in more dressing until it’s dressed to your liking.
Divide between 4 bowls and chow down! Might I recommend eating this salad with a soup spoon?

**Once cool, add the remaining cooked chicken to a gallon-sized ziplock. Lay it flat on a baking sheet and freeze. Once frozen, you can remove the baking sheet and store the ziplock wherever in the freezer. Doing this will ensure the meat doesn’t all freeze into one big clump, which will allow you to defrost just a bit at a time for individual salads or whatever!**

name: 20-minute kale, chicken, apple, and cheddar salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and finely ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and finely ground black pepper

ingredients.name: curly or flat leaf (lacinato) kale, tough stems removed, finely chopped (4 heaping cups — feel free to buy store-bought chopped kale, just pick through it to remove any tough stems)

ingredients.name: large cooked chicken breast (from a rotisserie chicken, or see recipe below for how to cook it at home), finely chopped (about 1 1/2 cups chopped chicken)

ingredients.name: salted, roasted almonds

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces white cheddar cheese, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: dates, pits removed and finely chopped (or 1/4 cup yellow raisins, dried cranberries, or dried cherries)

preparationSteps: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder (or one grated garlic clove). Taste and add 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup if your dressing is too tangy (the balsamic I use is sweet enough that I don’t need any).

Add 1 bunch finely chopped kale to the bowl of dressing, sprinkle with a big pinch of kosher salt, and use clean hands to massage the salt and dressing into the kale until it feels soft — about 7 squeezes between your palms. If it feels too heavily dressed, don’t worry, the chicken is going to soak up the dressing.
Add 1 1/2 cups chopped chicken, 1 apple cut into thin batons, 1/3 cup roughly chopped almonds, 4 ounces roughly chopped cheddar cheese, and 3 chopped dates. Toss to coat. DIG IN!

name: harissa bolognese spaghetti squash bake

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons high-quality extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: high-quality extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Cut 1 small spaghetti squash in half (here’s a demo!), use a spoon to scrape out the seeds, then rub each inside with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil. Place it cut-side down on a baking sheet and roast for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, we’ll make the sauce. Dice 1 small yellow onion and mince 4 garlic cloves.

Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large oven-proof skillet (I used my cast iron) or another wide, ovenproof cooking pan (a Dutch oven works!) over medium-high heat. Add the onion, garlic, 1 pound ground beef, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, 1 tablespoon cumin, and 3 tablespoons harissa paste. (Harissa is typically not very spicy, but start with 2 if you’re nervous or are feeding people who are sensitive to heat.)

Cook, breaking the meat into tiny crumbles, until the beef is cooked through and all excess liquid has evaporated. Stir in a 28-ounce can of diced tomatoes and 1/2 cup heavy cream and bring to a simmer over medium-low (ish) heat. We want it to be bubbling, but not so much that red sauce is popping all over you and your kitchen. So bubbling, not spluttering. Adjust your heat accordingly! Cover the pan with a lid if needed to protect yourself/your kitchen while you get the temperature just right.
Cook, stirring often, for about 10 minutes, or until the sauce is THICK! Like, no runny liquid on top. Turn off the heat.

Use a fork to scrape the strands out of the spaghetti squash and stir the squash into the sauce. I had about 1/2 cup of spaghetti squash left over that I didn’t stir in, because it was too much, and I like a high sauce ratio.
Stir in 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese and 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella.
Smooth the top out, then sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup Parmesan and 1 cup mozzarella over top.
Bake (at 400°F still) for 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and lightly golden brown. Sprinkle with more Parm, and chopped parsley or basil if you've got it.

name: one-pot mushroom orzo kinda-carbonara
note:
Make ahead: Make the entire thing in advance and refrigerate it right in the pot. To warm it up, just add a splash of water and heat over low heat until warm. You might need to add a lot of splashes of water to get it back to a nice saucy consistency!

Leftovers are a great thing: If you’re going to eat your leftovers in the coming few days, see the “make ahead” note just above. You can just store them in the pot so that you don’t have to dirty Tupperware! You can also freeze individual portions in freezer-safe bags (wait until it’s totally cooled before bagging). Add splashes of water or broth or stock while you’re reheating to make it creamy again. This recipe can also be halved if you don’t want leftovers and are cooking for 1 or 2.

Must have meat: See the “mushroom” sub below for how to cook this with bacon! You could also top it with some cooked chicken, if you happen to have some in the fridge (or want to grab a rotisserie chicken while you’re shopping), or some sautéed or roasted shrimp.

Df/gf: For dairy-free, use vegan Parm instead of regular. For gluten-free, use arborio rice instead of orzo pasta.

Add greens! Stir in 3 cups of torn spinach when you add the egg-Parm mixture. You could also add 1 to 2 cups of frozen peas! I loves peas in carbonara.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound (16 ounces) sliced baby bella or button mushrooms
ingredients.name: sliced baby bella or button mushrooms

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup parsley leaves and tender stems
ingredients.name: parsley leaves and tender stems

preparationSteps: Warm your largest skillet or saucepan over medium-high heat for at least 3 minutes. Add 3 tablespoons olive oil and warm for an additional 30 seconds. Add 1 pound sliced mushrooms to the skillet and toss to coat in oil. Spread them into an even layer, then let them sit for 4 minutes. Stir, then let them sit for another 4 minutes. Continue repeating this process (one or two more times should do it) until the mushrooms are golden-brown. It’ll take about 15 minutes total!

While the mushrooms are cooking, let’s do some prep work: Mince 1 large shallot and 4 garlic cloves and scooch them aside. In a medium bowl, whisk together 4 egg yolks, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, the juice of 1 lemon, and 1/2 teaspoon ground pepper. Set aside for later. If you have time, go ahead and finely chop 1 cup parsley leaves and tender stems as well (we’ll use this at the very end).

When the mushrooms are golden-brown, add the minced shallot and garlic and 1 tablespoon soy sauce to the pan. (If your skillet is dry, drizzle some more olive oil into the pan before adding the shallot and garlic.) Sauté for 1 minute just to soften them slightly, then stir in 16 ounces orzo pasta, 1 quart (4 cups) low-sodium chicken stock, and 1 cup water.

Bring to a boil over high heat then reduce to a simmer (this will probably be medium heat — you just want a low, steady bubbling) and cook for 10 to 13 minutes, until the orzo is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed but the dish is still runny. If you cook it for too long and all of the liquid absorbs — no worries! Just stir in another 1/4 cup water or so until you have a loose consistency.
Remove the pan from heat for at least 2 minutes. Seriously, set a timer. Stir it a lot too, to help the heat escape. We need it to cool down so it doesn’t scramble the eggs we’re about to stir in!

Stir in egg-Parm-lemon mixture and chopped parsley until everything melds together into a creamy, luxurious sauce — when it’s ready, you won’t see any white Parmesan specs. If it seems too thick, just stir in a splash of water!
Taste. We haven’t added ANY salt yet because the soy sauce and Parm are salty! But if you’re like me, you’ll want even more salt, so go for it! I probably wound up adding 1/2 teaspoon or so.
Serve. Top with more Parm and pepper. DIG IN!

name: chopped italian goddess
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: The beauty of the platter approach is that no leftovers get soggy and nothing goes to waste. I put the cheese and salami into one container and took it as a snack for the boys, and threw all of the other leftovers into a salad the next day with some leftover chicken!

I’m only cooking for 1 or 2 people: Skip the radicchio and frisée. Go with chopped romaine or baby romaine. Simply halve the rest of the ingredients! Or, go ahead and prep the salad as written, store the chopped bits that you aren’t using in separate containers and assemble salads all week long.

Feeding kids: Consider adding one or two things your kids love to the platter so that they see something they’re comfortable with when they sit down. Let them build their own dinner plates with whatever they want! Cheese and salami? Sure. Olives and tomatoes? Why not. No bad ingredients here — any combination is a win! BTW, my kids found the Manchego too strong. Consider going with feta or white cheddar if you also have tiny food critics in your home.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use store-bought green goddess dressing for this to save time. I really like Gotham Greens and Primal Kitchen brand dressings, if you can find ‘em.

Vegetarian: Crispy chickpeas would be my go-to here. I love the snack kind you can find at the store. Chickpeas straight from the can would be great too though if they’re what you’ve got and you don’t have time to bake them.

DF: For dairy-free, skip the cheese or swap in your favorite plant-based alternative. Also, go with mayo in the dressing.

ingredients.name: Other things that would be fun to add or swap in for any of the ingredients that your family doesn’t like: charred corn, roasted red peppers, pickled red onions, raw red onion, crispy chickpeas (buy the healthy snack kind, they’re so much better than homemade)

preparationSteps: To make the dressing: Add all ingredients (1 cup mayo, 1 cup basil leaves, 1/2 cup parsley leaves, 1 garlic clove, 1 anchovy filet, juice of 2 lemons, zest of 1 lemon, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, and 3/4 teaspoon salt) to a blender and blend until smooth. Taste. Adjust seasoning as desired. For example: I like a tangier dressing so I always add a bit of vinegar. Want it saltier? Add another anchovy. More garlicky? Blend in another garlic clove! Do your thing to make this dressing perfect for your tastebuds.

For the salad: Combine 3 ounces baby romaine, 1 chopped head of radicchio, and 1 chopped head of frisée in a large bowl. (Or just use 5 ounces of baby romaine to make life easier.) Season with a big pinch of kosher salt and pepper.

Now, you have two options for how to proceed: Either just add everything to the bowl and toss it together, or serve this salad “platter style” so that all of your eaters can choose their own adventure.
FOR SALAD STYLE:

Add 1 cup halved cherry tomatoes, 2 thinly sliced Persian cucumbers, 6 ounces thinly sliced salami, 6 ounces cubed Manchego cheese, 1/3 cup sliced pepperoncini peppers, 1/3 cup halved Castelvetrano olives, 1 thinly sliced avocado, and 1/3 cup chopped almonds to the bowl of lettuces. Season with a big pinch of salt and toss with your desired amount of green goddess dressing. DO NOT DUMP ALL OF THE DRESSING IN THERE TO START! You’ll likely have leftover dressing! Once tossed, taste. If it needs more dressing, drizzle a little more in, toss, and taste again. Repeat as needed until it’s perfectly dressed.
I like to chop my salads up like the salad restaurants do — check out the end of the video to see how!
Divide between 4 bowls or plates and dig in!
FOR PLATTER STYLE:

Arrange 1 cup halved cherry tomatoes, 2 thinly sliced Persian cucumbers, 6 ounces thinly sliced salami, 6 ounces cubed Manchego cheese, 1/3 cup sliced pepperoncini peppers, 1/3 cup halved Castelvetrano olives, 1 thinly sliced avocado, 1/3 cup chopped almonds, and a bowl of the green goddess dressing on a large serving platter. Season the tomatoes, cucumbers, and avocado with salt and pepper.

Let your eaters serve themselves however they choose! Add a spoon to the dressing bowl so people can dress their own! Give them a fork and steak knife so that they can chop up their salads like the salad restaurants do!
servings: Serves 4 to 6 (if cooking for less than 4 people, see notes section)

name: tiny tomato pasta

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds (32 ounces) cherry, sun gold, or grape tomatoes
ingredients.name: cherry, sun gold, or grape tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup fresh basil leaves, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces Parmesan cheese (1 cup grated), divided
ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese (1 cup grated)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook 1 pound angel hair pasta until al dente, 6 to 8 minutes. Reserve 1 1/2 cups pasta water then drain pasta in a colander. (Leave it in the colander, do not rinse it or toss olive oil into it!)

Meanwhile, in your largest skillet, melt 6 tablespoons unsalted butter over medium heat. While it’s melting, thinly slice 6 garlic cloves. Add the garlic, 2 pounds cherry tomatoes, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes to the skillet and turn the heat up to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have started to burst and form a pan sauce, about 8 minutes. If you have a potato smasher, I like to carefully (because they’ll explode hot liquid on you!) smash the tomatoes. If you don’t, you can use a spatula to smash them. Turn off the heat.
Meanwhile, thinly slice 1 cup basil leaves and grate 4 ounces of Parmesan (you want 1 cup grated).

Toss the cooked pasta, 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta cooking water, the basil, and 1/2 cup of the grated Parm into the sauce until all of the cheese has melted into a smooth sauce. Stir in the remaining 1/2 cup grated Parm until smooth. (Stirring in half of the cheese at a time helps it melt more evenly without clumping.)
Stir in more of the pasta cooking water until things are looking saucy and delicious. Taste and add more salt as needed.
Serve, garnished with some extra fresh basil and Parm.

name: summer steak tostadas
note:
What to do with leftover tostadas: Next time you have leftover meat in the fridge, make it a tostada night! Such a great way to repurpose leftovers in a way that no one will know they’re eating leftovers. Grab a can of refried beans or storebought guac, chop up the leftover meat, and top them with storebought salsa and cheese. Done! Easiest meal of all time.

Make ahead: All of the sauces can be made up to 24 hours ahead, just cover the mashed avocado tightly (the plastic wrap should be touching the avocado). Seasoning the steak 24 hours in advance is also a great idea!

Vegetarian: Black or pinto beans would be a delicious sub for the steak! If you have time and want to add some flavor to your beans, chop up half an onion and mince 3 garlic cloves and sauté them in oil in a pot over medium heat. Once your onion is soft, add a can of black or pinto beans WITH the liquid and stir. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring every now and then, until the liquid has reduced and thickened. If you like heat, you can add a teaspoon or more of hot sauce when you pour in the beans. Another option in case you don’t want beans: the grilled squash and zucchini make an EXCELLENT tostada topping! Just chop those up and throw them on top!

DIY tostadas: This is a big extra step, but if you have corn tortillas and want to use them up, you can make your own tostadas! Two options for doing so: You can fry them in a good frying oil (like avocado, safflower, canola, or peanut oil) for about 4 minutes per side, finishing them off with some flaky salt. Or you can bake them. To do so, coat a baking sheet (or two, if you have them!) with cooking spray. Spray your corn tortillas with cooking spray too, then spread them out in a single layer on your baking sheet(s) and sprinkle with salt. Bake at 400°F for 5 minutes, flip them over, and bake for another 5 to 10 minutes, or until they’re crispy.

DF/GF: Omit the cheese and proceed as written to make it dairy free! The charred scallion salsa will just be more of a vinaigrette than chunky salsa without it. This recipe’s already gluten free.

Leftovers are a great thing: Make a big salad with your leftovers! Put the various ingredients on a big bed of your favorite greens (thinly sliced Romaine would be delicious) and enjoy. I’d top mine with crushed tostadas for some crunch.

Grilled Summer Squash and Zucchini with Charred Scallion and Cotija Salsa

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons cooking oil (such as avocado, grapeseed, or vegetable)
ingredients.name: cooking oil (such as avocado, grapeseed, or vegetable)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces (about 1/3 cup) crumbled cotija or feta cheese
ingredients.name: (about 1/3 cup) crumbled cotija or feta cheese

preparationSteps: Prepare the steaks for grilling by patting 2 ribeye steaks dry, then rubbing all over with about 1 teaspoon garlic powder (no need to actually measure, just coat them nicely) and salt (same).

Prepare 2 summer squash and 2 zucchini for grilling by cutting off the stem and root ends, then cutting them into 4 to 5 long skinny planks. Place on a serving plate (the one you’ll actually serve dinner from) along with 6 scallions, and toss all with 2 tablespoons cooking oil, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano.
Set the squash, scallions, and steak aside at room temperature while we prep everything else.

To make the mashed avocado: Scoop the insides of 2 large avocados out into a small bowl and mash with the juice of 1 lime, 1 tablespoon minced cilantro (but go ahead and chop the entire bunch — you will need more later), and a big pinch of salt. Set aside.
To make the peach salsa: In a medium bowl, combine 1/4 cup pickled jalapeños, 2 large diced peaches, the juice of 1 lime, 2 tablespoons cilantro, and a big pinch of salt. Set aside.

To make the charred scallion and cotija salsa: In a medium bowl, combine 1/3 cup crumbled cotija or feta cheese, 3 tablespoons minced cilantro, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, and the juice of 1 lime. Set aside — you’ll add the charred scallions to this bowl in a bit.
When you’re ready to eat in about 20 minutes, preheat an outdoor grill to 450°F, or an indoor grill pan or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.

Rub the seasoned steak with a light layer of cooking oil. Add the steak, squash, zucchini, and scallions to the grill. Cook the steak for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the steaks reach 135°F internally for medium-rare (or 145°F for medium). Cook the squash and zucchini for about 4 minutes per side as well, or until nice grill marks appear. Meanwhile, turn the scallions often, for just a couple minutes, as the tips will char easily. Remove scallions when they’re a bit charred.
Transfer the squash, zucchini, and scallions back to their serving plate. Transfer the steak to a cutting board to rest.

Finely chop the charred scallions (discard the rooty ends) and stir them into the bowl with the cotija and cilantro. Scatter the charred scallion and cotija salsa over top the grilled zucchini and squash.

Once the steak has rested for 5 minutes, slice as thinly as you can against the grain, then chop into small pieces. (Chopping the meat will make these easier to eat — otherwise, the long strips will slide right off the tostada when you try to take a bite!)
Spread a layer of mashed avocado onto 8 to 10 tostadas. Pile on the chopped steak. Top it off with peach-jalapeño salsa and a nice sprinkle of cotija.
Enjoy your tostadas with a side of grilled zucchini and squash!
And because someone on Instagram last night asked me how to eat a tostada… pick it up and bite it! No forks/knives here!

name: lemon-parm chicken, quinoa, and kale salad
note:
My salad got soft in the fridge: This salad does get softer as the days go on, but in a tasty way — like I actually prefer it on day two or three. That said, if you like really bouncy, full kale, then you should dress it individually each day versus all at once on the first day!

Double the quinoa: One of my healthy eating hacks is cooking once, but eating twice. AKA if I am going to the effort of making a salad dressing or cooking quinoa or a grain from scratch, I’m going to double it to set future-me up for success. You’ll already have a little extra quinoa, but if you double it, you’ll have enough to freeze in 2- or 3-cup increments for a later night when you can make fried rice (using quinoa instead of rice) or serve it under roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, or basically swap it in anywhere a recipe uses rice (except for one-pot rice dishes as the cook time is a little different!).

Bulk it up: The quinoa, chicken, and nuts make it really filling, but if you want to bulk it up further, cube and roast a sweet potato or some cauliflower and throw that in there too!

Do I eat this warm or cold? It’s great either way! If I’m cooking it for dinner, I’ll add warm quinoa to the bowl and am typically working with a warm rotisserie chicken. If I’m eating it for lunches, I’ll eat it cold straight out of the fridge!

Love your leftovers: This prepped salad lasts in the fridge in an airtight container for 4 days! Here are ideas for how to use the extra quinoa and chicken you’ll have leftover: Quinoa: Store leftover quinoa in an airtight container with a damp paper towel over it to keep it moist! In addition to the ideas above (under “double the quinoa”), you can throw leftover quinoa into any soup or stew, make burrito bowls with it, serve it with sheet-pan orange teriyaki steak and broccoli, etc. Chicken: You can add shredded or chopped leftover rotisserie chicken to a soup or stew or use it to make quesadillas, chicken salad, a chicken pot pie, or another salad. Use them together! Make a quinoa and chicken grain bowl! Add your quinoa and chicken to a bowl and microwave to reheat. Add a dollop of pesto, some greens, olives, hummus, roasted bell peppers, etc., to make a nice little grain bowl!

Quinoa: Store leftover quinoa in an airtight container with a damp paper towel over it to keep it moist! In addition to the ideas above (under “double the quinoa”), you can throw leftover quinoa into any soup or stew, make burrito bowls with it, serve it with sheet-pan orange teriyaki steak and broccoli, etc.

Chicken: You can add shredded or chopped leftover rotisserie chicken to a soup or stew or use it to make quesadillas, chicken salad, a chicken pot pie, or another salad.

Use them together! Make a quinoa and chicken grain bowl! Add your quinoa and chicken to a bowl and microwave to reheat. Add a dollop of pesto, some greens, olives, hummus, roasted bell peppers, etc., to make a nice little grain bowl!

I hate quinoa and don’t want a grain: Just omit the quinoa and double the nuts/pepitas.

Feeding kids: For picky eaters, I serve this salad deconstructed with the chicken in a pile, undressed kale in another, nuts in another, quinoa in another, raisins in another, etc. Also fyi, quinoa is a great food for babies and toddlers! You can mix it with some hummus or yogurt to make it easier for them to spoon and eat.

Vegetarian: Swap the chicken for a can of drained white beans (garbanzo, navy, Great Northern, cannellini). Add the beans and dressing to the salad bowl first for about 10 minutes to marinate them. Or just omit the chicken — quinoa is a complete protein and a staple of many vegetarians’ diets!

Dairy-free: Use a DF Parm or omit it. Nutritional yeast would also be nice here but I’d use a quarter to half the amount. Start with 1/4 cup and add more to taste.

Gluten-free: Already is thanks to the quinoa!

Nut-free: Opt for a seed like pepitas instead of almonds or omit.

preparationSteps: To make the lemon vinaigrette, add all ingredients (1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 cup lemon juice, 1 heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme or oregano, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of black pepper) to a large jar and shake vigorously until combined. Adjust seasoning to taste. (As always, that is the most important part of making a dressing — my perfect dressing is not the same as yours! Add more vinegar to make it more acidic, more honey to make it sweeter, more oil to make it thicker and less acidic, more salt to make the flavors pop, etc.) Dressing will keep in the fridge for up to 10 days.

To make the quinoa, add 1 cup uncooked quinoa and 1 1/2 cups water (or any kind of stock) to a small pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 13 to 15 minutes, until all of the liquid has been absorbed. Remove from heat but keep the lid on for an additional 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. You’ll use 2 cups of COOKED quinoa in this recipe and have about a cup left over. Let the leftovers cool completely then store them in an airtight container in the fridge for later use this week (see notes for ideas).

Add 16 ounces chopped kale to a large bowl and season with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Use your hands to massage the kale until it JUST starts to feel damp — so squeeze it between your fists about 10 times. If you come across any pieces of thick stem while you’re massaging, discard them.

Now let’s tackle that rotisserie chicken. Pull the thighs/legs and wings off, store them in the refrigerator in an airtight container, and use them for another meal within 4 days. Pull the breast meat off (I discard the skin but you can shred it in with the meat if you’d like!), shred it finely, and add the meat right on top of the kale. Add 2 cups cooked quinoa, 1 bag shredded carrots, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 cup golden raisins, and your desired amount of dressing. (If I’m cooking this salad for dinner/to serve immediately, I use almost all of the dressing, about 1/3 cup! If I’m meal prepping it for lunches, I go lighter with the dressing initially then add a little more to each serving when I’m ready to eat it.)

Toss to combine. Add more dressing as needed until your greens are coated to your liking. Divide the salad between four to six bowls, and garnish with more Parm and a sprinkle of chopped nuts. I love lemon so much that I serve each serving of salad with a lemon wedge for squeezing over top!
(PS, I add the nuts at the end so that they don’t go into the big salad and get soggy in the fridge, but this is personal preference!)

name: sheet-pan roasted chicken with bourbon and citrus
note:
i rarely recommend cooking with extra-virgin olive oil. first of all, it’s expensive, and it simply isn’t necessary to use an expensive oil for cooking. secondly, it has a low smoke point of under 400°F! we are cooking the chicken at 475°F, so your oven will be a smoky mess, your chicken will burn, no bueno.

whenever i call for olive oil, you can also use avocado or grapeseed oil. those are all neutral cooking oils with high smoke points. when i call for extra-virgin olive oil, it’s because i really want that olive-y, grassy flavor.

all of your chicken swap questions answered here. first of all - PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE try bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs! they are incredibly flavorful and they never overcook and they’re just the best. but if you must use chicken breasts, at least make them bone-in chicken breasts, ok? cook the fennel etc for 15 minutes, then add the chicken breasts and cook for an additional 20 to 25 minutes, or until the chicken is 165 internally. boneless chicken breasts - same, then add the chicken breasts and cook for 10 to 15 more minutes. boneless chicken thighs - same, then roast the chicken thighs for 15 to 20 minutes.

yes, you can use dijon instead of whole grain mustard, but only use 1 tablespoon.

i used cara cara and navel oranges here. you can use grapefruits, blood oranges, clementines, mandarins, etc! do yo thang.

feel free to swap in any grain that you have floating around your pantry. quinoa, rice, barley, etc can all be cooked using the boiling method that i used for the farro here!

dairy-free: omit the butter!

gluten-free: cook brown rice, or any other grain that works for you, in the same manner as the farro.

non-alcoholic: just omit the bourbon, you don’t need to sub anything in!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar (or other light colored vinegar
ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar (or other light colored vinegar

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups farro (or ANY grain of your choosing, see notes below)
ingredients.name: farro (or ANY grain of your choosing, see notes below)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped parsley, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: chopped parsley, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: In a really large bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons of olive oil, 3 tablespoons bourbon, 3 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 tablespoons whole grain mustard, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 2 teaspoons salt, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
Squeeze in the juice of ONE of the oranges.
That was easy right? Ok, now we’ve got a little chopping to do.
First, you’re gonna peel the remaining two oranges (using the technique you learned in the video I linked above!), then slice them into 1/4-inch thick rounds. Throw those in the bowl of marinade.
Add the 2 pounds of bone-in chicken thighs to the bowl.

Now we’re gonna tackle that fennel. Trim the stalks off of 2 fennel bulbs, then trim the bottom off if it looks dirty/knobbly. You’ll be left with just the fennel bulb. If the first layer looks tough or brown, remove it. Cut the fennel bulb in half lengthwise, aka through the root end, to create two halves. Now cut each of those halves into 5 or 6 big wedges, each about 1/2-inch thick.
Toss the fennel wedges in the bowl of marinade! Now add 6 thyme sprigs, and toss everything together to evenly coat it.
When you’re ready, preheat the oven to 475°F and place one oven rack in the center and one on the top rung.

Dump the entire bowl - chicken, fennel, marinade and all onto a rimmed baking sheet. First get the chicken thighs flipped over skin side UP, then arrange the fennel and oranges into as even of a layer as you can around them.
Make sure that nothing is touching the chicken skin, though, since we want crispy chicken skin!
Roast for 35 to 45 minutes on the center rack of the oven. When the chicken has reached an internal temperature of 165°F, remove it from the oven and transfer it to a holding plate.

Spread the fennel and oranges out into an even layer, and raise the oven temperature to a broil. Return the sheet-pan to the TOP rung of the oven and broil for 4 to 7 minutes, until the fennel and orange have crisped up, and the sauce is bubbling and thickened. I highly recommend sitting on your butt in front of the oven, with the oven light on, and watching it intently while the broiler is on. Things can burn QUICKLY!

While the chicken is cooking, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Boil 1 1/2 cups farro until tender, which will take anywhere from 10 to 30 minutes, depending on the type of farro you bought. When the farro is tender but slightly chewy, drain it, shaking all of the water off, then return to the pot and stir in 1/4 cup chopped parsley, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
When the vegetables are nicely crisped up, remove the sheet-pan from the oven, and stir 1 tablespoon butter into the pan juices, tossing the vegetables into the pan juices to coat them.
Plate your desired amount of farro (I like about 1/2 cup) with chicken and vegetables over top. Drizzle the pan sauce over everything. Garnish with parsley. ENJOY!!!!!

name: sesame chicken schnitzel
note:
What To Cook When You *Really* Don’t Feel Like Cooking: Buy frozen chicken tenders, heat ‘em up, and throw them on top of this salad!

Feeding kids + make it easier: Buy raw chicken tenders instead of pounding your own chicken breasts. Serve them with ketchup and call it chicken finger night instead! Alternate time-saving option: If you have a friendly butcher, ask them to pre-pound your chicken breasts to be 1/8-inch thick. Most will be happy to oblige.

Leftover makeover: if you have a leftover schnitzel, make chicken parm the next day! Place the schnitzel on a baking sheet, smother it with marinara and mozzarella, and bake at 400F for 12 to 15 minutes.

Prep ahead + leftovers: You can pound your chicken cutlets and bread them up to a day ahead of when you’re ready to cook. Just store them covered in the fridge and pull them out about 15 minutes before you’re ready to cook so they’ll come to room temp. If you’re cooking for one or two, you can easily halve the recipe. (Half of 1/3 cup flours = 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons, if you’re wondering!) You can also freeze leftover chicken schnitzel if you don’t want leftovers in the fridge or are looking to stock your freezer. You have two options: To freeze them breaded but not cooked, or to freeze them after they’ve been cooked and cool down. In both cases, wrap each cutlet individually in an airtight container.

My fam needs another side: Serve the schnitzel with these cauliflower mashed potatoes! They’re very quick and easy. Another option? Store-bought mashed potatoes.

Vegetarian: I’m very intrigued by this vegan schnitzel recipe! Or, buy some vegetarian nuggets and serve them with the salad for a really quick and easy meal.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use your fave vegan Parm or just omit it from the salad! If you’re omitting, throw some sunflower seeds or pepitas in if you have them — they’ll add some nice saltiness to the mix. For gf, be sure to buy gluten-free panko and use almond flour in lieu of all-purpose flour.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup sesame seeds (or any finely chopped nuts)
ingredients.name: sesame seeds (or any finely chopped nuts)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup avocado, vegetable, or canola oil
ingredients.name: avocado, vegetable, or canola oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: Block of Parmesan cheese (you’ll only need 1/4 cup of shavings)
ingredients.name: of Parmesan cheese (you’ll only need 1/4 cup of shavings)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional additions: halved cherry tomatoes, shaved raw carrots, thinly sliced celery or fennel, nuts or seeds, etc.!
ingredients.name: Optional additions: halved cherry tomatoes, shaved raw carrots, thinly sliced celery or fennel, nuts or seeds, etc.!

preparationSteps: Place 4 (4-ounce) chicken breasts one at a time in a large gallon-sized Ziploc or between two pieces of plastic wrap. Use a rolling pin or a wine bottle to pound the chicken breasts until they’re 1/8-inch thick.
Set out 3 shallow bowls.

Place 1/3 cup flour in the first bowl and stir in 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Crack 2 large eggs in the second shallow bowl and whisk until combined. Place 1 1/2 cups panko, 1/4 cup sesame seeds, and a big pinch of salt in the third bowl and stir until combined.

Dredge the chicken through the flour until fully coated, then through the egg until fully coated, and finally through the panko mixture. If you run out of panko while breading the chicken, just add more.
Now there are two options for how to cook your schnitzel! You can bake it (healthier + easier) or you can fry it (less healthy + harder + more delicious).

To bake it: Preheat your oven to 425°F. Place the chicken on a foil-lined baking sheet in an even layer and spray with cooking spray on both sides. Bake for 6 minutes, then flip and cook for an additional 6 minutes. Check that the chicken is 165°F internally.

To fry it: Heat 1/4 cup oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. When you add a piece of panko and it sizzles, you’re ready to cook. Cook one piece of chicken at a time for 5 minutes per side, or until golden brown. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with salt. Don’t skip the paper towel step!

To make the arugula salad: Place 4 cups arugula into a large bowl and drizzle in 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1 large lemon, and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Grab a block of Parmesan cheese and use a vegetable peeler to peel in about 1/4 cup. Toss to coat. Taste and add more salt and pepper as needed.
Serve the chicken with the arugula salad and a schmear of mustard if you’re into that. Enjoy immediately!

ingredients.name: veggie stock (or 4 cups water plus 1 heaping tablespoon veggie or chicken Better Than Bouillon)

preparationSteps: We’ve got some chopping to do! You are free to do it in the food processor (chop each veggie into 4 big pieces, then pulse) or use a knife and get to it!

If using a knife: Mince 1 medium onion and 2 celery stalks. Thinly slice 3 carrots into round pieces. If the carrot is so thick that the piece would be too big to eat, cut the carrot in half vertically first.

Warm 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped veggies and a big pinch of salt and pepper and stir until tender, 4 to 5 minutes. Turn up the heat if needed, but don’t let them brown too much. Meanwhile, mince or grate a 2-inch piece of ginger (no need to peel it) and 4 garlic cloves.
Stir in the the red curry paste (read notes below to determine how much you should add). Add the minced garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add 16 ounces red lentils, 1 quart (4 cups) veggie stock, 2 cans coconut milk, and 1 can crushed tomatoes.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low to simmer for 20 to 25 minutes. The lentils should be tender, but not totally mushy.

While the lentils are cooking, finely chop 1 small bunch fresh cilantro (both leaves and stems). We are looking for 1/3 to 1/2 cup of chopped cilantro. Set some aside for garnish, and add the rest to the pot.

Stir in 1 tablespoon fish sauce and 1 tablespoon lime juice. Taste. If it’s not delicious, it probably needs more salt. Mine needed about 1/2 teaspoon salt, but this will depend entirely on how salty your stock and fish sauce are. Stir in a little pinch of salt at a time and keep tasting and adding until it’s perfect.
Serve with cilantro on top.

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 450°F.

To start, let’s wash the 2 medium leeks. Washing leeks is annoying, but they’re worth it, promise! Chop off and discard the tough dark green parts and the roots, then slice the light green parts into thin rings. Place them in a colander set within a large bowl and fill it with water. Use your hands to submerge and wash the dirt off the leeks. Don't forget to look inside the layers! That's where the dirt hides. Once clean, lift the colander out of the bowl and rinse thoroughly. Dry them off with a clean dish towel.
Set a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Once warm, add 3 tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil.

While your oil is warming, cut 12 ounces of andouille or chorizo sausage into 1/4- to 1/2-inch thick slices. Add the washed leeks and sliced sausage to the pan, sautéing them for 5 minutes, until the leeks are softened and the sausage is beginning to brown. Add 3 minced garlic cloves and 1 1⁄2 teaspoons of smoked paprika and continue cooking until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add 2 cups of short-grain white rice, tossing to coat the rice in the oil and other cooked ingredients. Add 4 cups of chicken or vegetable stock and a generous pinch of both salt and pepper, and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, carefully add the pan to the oven, UNCOVERED!!, and bake for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make your lemon aioli. In a small bowl, mix 1/2 cup mayonnaise, the zest and juice of half of your lemon, a handful of chopped basil, and a pinch of salt. Set aside. Slice up the other half of the lemon to use later as garnish.
Cut the woody stems off of 1 bunch of asparagus and discard them, then slice the stalks into 1-inch pieces.

Once your skillet has been in the oven for 15 minutes, remove it and carefully add the chopped asparagus and 1 cup of frozen peas, stirring them into the rice. Place 1 pound of peeled and deveined shrimp on top. Return the skillet to the oven and cook (still uncovered!) for an additional 10 minutes, until the veggies are vibrant and cooked and your shrimp is pink, opaque, and curled like a C.
Serve garnished with a generous dollop or drizzle of your aioli, a lemon slice, and a few whole basil leaves. Enjoy!

name: fries

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 pounds Yukon or Dutch Gold potatoes (1 pound for 2 people, 2 pounds for 4 people)
ingredients.name: Yukon or Dutch Gold potatoes (1 pound for 2 people, 2 pounds for 4 people)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt (or good, flaky sea salt such as Maldon, if you have it!)
ingredients.name: Kosher salt (or good, flaky sea salt such as Maldon, if you have it!)

preparationSteps: Cut the short ends off 2 pounds of potatoes (but don’t peel them) so that they can sit up vertically, and then slice into ½ inch-thick fries. Place fries on a clean dish towel, dry them off, then place them in a wide, heavy-bottomed pot. Pour vegetable oil over top, you’ll use roughly 1 quart oil but the most important thing is that it should cover the potatoes by 1 inch.
Put the pan over high heat and bring to a boil. It’ll take about 5 to 8 minutes. Don’t throw away the oil bottle — we’ll need it later for cleanup!

Once the oil starts to boil, cook the fries — without stirring them! — for another 15 minutes (set a timer!). The oil will be bubbling vigorously. If the oil starts to bubble aggressively (like splashing over the sides of the pan), reduce the heat a little. Always keep a close eye on it.

If you have an oil thermometer, use it! Once the oil temperature reaches 325°F, turn down the heat slightly and keep the fries cooking between 300-325°F. If you don’t have one — which is likely most of you — just keep the oil at a vigorous bubble. If the bubbles get SCARY BIG, turn it down!
Once your 15-minute timer goes off, stir the fries using a slotted spoon or spider (put on an oven mitt to prevent oil burns!), moving any that have stuck to the bottom or sides of the pan.

Test a fry — you’re aiming for crispness on the outside and tenderness on the inside. They might need another 5 minutes or so more, but stand by your pan: fries can burn QUICKLY at this phase! Once done, scoop the fries out with a spider or slotted spoon and transfer to a plate lined with a paper towels. Season with tons of kosher salt. Enjoy IMMEDIATELY! Or, if you need to, keep them warm on a baking sheet in a 250°F oven until you’re ready to eat!

name: smash burgers with special sauce
note:
Make ahead: You can make the special sauce, slice your potatoes, and even mix + partition your burger meat hours ahead of time, storing all in the fridge until it’s go time. Wrap the potatoes tightly in a towel and they won’t brown much (a little browning doesn’t matter).

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Smash burgers come together and cook really quickly, so they’re actually perfect for a busy night. If homemade fries aren’t in the cards for your night, you can either: 1. Chop the potatoes into cubes and roast them. To do so, dice the potatoes, mix them with a tablespoon or two of a neutral cooking oil (like grapeseed or avocado), season with salt and pepper, and roast them at 425°F for 25 minutes or until they’re crispy. OR… 2. Bake up some store-bought fries. These are a personal fave!

Vegetarian: Make a plant-based smash burger! Grab your favorite vegetarian ground “meat” — like Impossible Burger — and proceed as the recipe’s written.

Dairy-free: Mayo is dairy-free, so the only change would be the cheese, subbing in your favorite dairy-free alternative or leaving it off.

Gluten-free + Whole30: Three options. 1. Use a gf bun that you like. If you can’t find one that’s tasty… 2) Cook the smash burger patties and use them in my  Whole30-compliant burger salad. 3) Make a lettuce bun by cutting two “cheeks” off of a head of iceberg lettuce, and using those cheeks as your bun.

Leftovers are a great thing: Reheat your patties tomorrow and have burgers for lunch! Or again, use the patties to make this bomb burger salad.
