ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 hamburger buns (the thinner the better — this is not the place for a big thick bun. I like potato or brioche buns but good ole Ball Park buns will do the trick!)
ingredients.name: hamburger buns (the thinner the better — this is not the place for a big thick bun. I like potato or brioche buns but good ole Ball Park buns will do the trick!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, plus more for the buns
ingredients.name: mayonnaise, plus more for the buns

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup finely chopped bread and butter pickles (or just use relish, or yes — dill work)
ingredients.name: finely chopped bread and butter pickles (or just use relish, or yes — dill work)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds ground beef (80/20 — this fat percentage is really important!)
ingredients.name: ground beef (80/20 — this fat percentage is really important!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but encouraged for serving: thinly sliced iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato, dill pickle slices
ingredients.name: Optional but encouraged for serving: thinly sliced iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato, dill pickle slices

preparationSteps: Warm your largest skillet (or griddle, if you have one) over medium-high heat. Spread mayo over the the insides of your buns. Set them aside. Keep the skillet over heat.

Make the special sauce by stirring together 1/3 cup mayo, 1/4 cup finely chopped bread and butter pickles (or relish), 2 tablespoons ketchup, and 1 tablespoon yellow mustard in a small- to medium-sized bowl. Set aside.

In a large bowl, use your hands to combine 1 1/2 pounds ground beef, 1 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt, 3/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Divide the ground beef into 8 portions and squeeze into rough balls.

Crank the skillet up to high heat. Add 2 to 3 balls of meat to the skillet and use your largest spatula to smash the beef into a flat patty. If your spatula has holes in it, cover the meat ball with a small square of parchment paper then smash. That’ll make it a lot easier!

Cook the patties for 2 minutes, then flip, add a slice of cheese, and cook for 1 additional minute. If your cheese isn’t melting, cover the skillet for 30 seconds (use a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid large enough).
Place a handful of shredded iceberg lettuce on the bottom bun, then layer on two patties and top it off with tomato, onion, and pickles. Dig in IMMEDIATELY!
servings: Makes 4 double burgers (or 8 single burgers but… you want a double burger)

name: sheet-pan miso-ginger salmon with cauliflower rice and charred snap peas
note:
First up, yes, you can sub a different fish for salmon, but I beg of you, even if you “hate salmon” give this a shot?! It is a completely different way of cooking salmon. I used to hate it too, now I love it!

Use as many salmon filets as you have people to serve. Or throw on an extra - I typically don’t recommend purposefully having fish leftovers, but because of the slow-roast here, this salmon actually reheats beautifully in the microwave.

Salmon fish sub: halibut, bass, arctic char, grouper.

Or use chicken instead: use boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs and marinate the same way, but roast at 425°F for about 20 minutes, or until 160°F internally (the temp will continue to rise to get to 165°F). When it comes time to add the snap peas, don’t remove the chicken, broil it as well. Keep an eye on it as miso can burn quickly!

Vegetarian: slice 1 block of firm tofu into 1/2-inch thick slices. Cook the exact same way. When it comes time to add the snap peas, don’t remove the tofu, broil it as well. Keep an eye on it as miso can burn quickly!

Gluten-free / Dairy-free: check me out! This recipe is already GF and DF! Just make sure you use a GF soy sauce.

Miso sub: can’t find miso, or have a soy aversion? Use dijon or wholegrain mustard instead! You’ll end up with a maple mustard salmon sich and it will be fab.

Maple syrup sub: it’s expensive. If you don’t already own it, and don’t imagine yourself using it in the future, you can use brown sugar or honey! I love using maple syrup as a refined sugar substitute, and will undoubtedly be using it in more WTC recipes, if that helps justify the grocery expense.

Lime juice sub: rice wine vinegar is best, but ANY clear vinegar works.

Soy sauce sub: if you have a soy aversion, use coconut aminos. If you just don’t have it in your pantry and don’t want to go to the store, use 1 teaspoon kosher salt instead.

Cauliflower rice sub: there isn’t really another great veggie that you can slow roast alongside the salmon. But, you can make a pot of normal rice while the salmon roasts, and serve the salmon and snap peas over rice.

Want to make your own cauliflower rice? Ok, show off! Throw half a head of chopped up head of cauliflower into the food processor at a time, and pulse until it’s the size of rice grains. No food processor: grate the head of cauliflower on a box grater.

Speaking of cauliflower rice, after roasting, try blending it up with 1/4 cup heavy cream to make an unbelievable cauliflower puree instead of cauliflower rice.

Snap pea sub: green beans, asparagus (cut into 2-inch pieces), snow peas, frozen edamame. Watch closely while broiling so that you don’t overcook. Green beans will need more time, edamame will need less.

The sesame seeds are pretty much for looks only, but if you don’t own any, I do love garnishing Asian (and other!) dishes with them.

To make this a complete “dump” recipe, aka no chopping/grating of any kind, use 1/2 teaspoon ginger powder instead of fresh ginger. Or, omit the ginger altogether.

Any other questions? Leave ‘em in the comments below and I’ll get back to you in a jif.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger root, peeled and grated
ingredients.name: fresh ginger root

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 (6 to 8 ounce) salmon filets, preferably skin-on (see notes)
ingredients.name: salmon filets, preferably skin-on (see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 16 ounce bag of cauliflower rice (preferably fresh, frozen OK. can’t find either? see notes)
ingredients.name: of cauliflower rice (preferably fresh, frozen OK. can’t find either? see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 16 ounces snap peas (or whatever size your bag is)
ingredients.name: snap peas (or whatever size your bag is)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of finely chopped soft green herbs such as cilantro, mint, basil, scallions, or chives
ingredients.name: Handful of finely chopped soft green herbs such as cilantro, mint, basil, scallions, or chives

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, stir together 2 tablespoons miso, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 tablespoons olive oil, the juice of half of a lime, and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.

Now, it’s ginger time. I promise it’s not as scary as it looks. Grab a hold of it, and use a small spoon to scrape the skin off of about 1 inch of ginger. Use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to grate the peeled ginger into the marinade. No grater? Just mince it as finely as you possibly can.
Run your fingers along the flesh of the salmon to feel for any tiny bones that the fishmonger (yep, that’s the word for a fish butcher) may have accidentally left behind. Pull those suckers out!
Add 2 to 4 (6 to 8 ounce) salmon filets and turn to coat it. Allow the salmon to marinate for at least 15 minutes at room temperature or up to 24 hours covered in the refrigerator.
When you’re about 1 hour from when you want to eat, place one oven rack in the center of the oven, and one on the top rung. Preheat oven to 275°F.

Place the salmon fillets skin-side down, tightly together — touching, so that it looks like one big piece of salmon — in the corner of a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet. Spread a thin layer of the miso-maple marinade over top.
Stir 16 ounces cauliflower rice and a big pinch of kosher salt into the bowl of remaining marinade until evenly coated.
Transfer the cauliflower rice to the baking sheet and spread it into as even a layer as possible around the salmon. Don’t wash the bowl yet, you’re going to use it again!
Cook for 20 to 30 minutes, or until an internal thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the salmon registers 125°F for medium-rare, 135°F for medium, or 145°F for well done.
Meanwhile, toss 16 ounces of snap peas in the marinade bowl with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper until coated.
Transfer the salmon to serving plates.
Turn the oven to broil on high.

Stir the cauliflower rice and spread it out across the entire baking sheet, taking up the empty space left by the salmon. Scatter the snap peas over the cauliflower rice in an even layer and return the baking sheet to the top rung of the oven.

Now it’s time to turn on the oven light, sit on your butt in front of the oven, and WATCH! Depending on how hot your broiler runs, it’s going to take between 3 and 5 minutes to lightly char those snap peas. It’s important that you watch closely so that 1) you don’t overcook the snap peas (we just want a bit of color on them!) and 2) the parchment paper doesn’t burn!
Divide the cauliflower rice and snap peas between the plates. Garnish with soft green herbs and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: chipotle black bean flautas
note:
Whole30 it: Ditch the cheese and make black bean lettuce wraps by wrapping the black bean filling, mango, and pickled red onion (minus the sugar) in iceberg lettuce leaves.

Make ahead/freezer-friendly: Assemble the flautas and make the crema and pickled red onions ahead of time, then bake them right before dinner! They also freeze really well — bake or fry them, allow them to cool, then freeze. Reheat on a baking sheet in a 400°F oven for 5 to 10 minutes.

Must have meat: Swap in 2 cups of shredded chicken plus 2 tablespoons sour cream for the black beans. So good. Honestly I had such a hard time deciding which direction to choose!

Gluten-free: Use corn or another alt-flour tortilla! But you’ll likely need to warm the tortillas before rolling so that they don’t just crack on you. To do that, wrap ‘em in damp paper towels and microwave for 45 seconds. Take one out and make sure it’s very pliable. If not, keep microwaving until they’re ready.

Dairy-free: Just omit the cheese and use a non-dairy yogurt or vegan sour cream in place of the sour cream.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 chipotle peppers en adobo sauce (from a can of chipotles en adobo), minced
ingredients.name: chipotle peppers en adobo sauce (from a can of chipotles en adobo)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups shredded Mexican, cheddar, or pepper jack cheese
ingredients.name: shredded Mexican, cheddar, or pepper jack cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Cooking spray or neutral cooking oil
ingredients.name: Cooking spray or neutral cooking oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons adobo sauce (from the same can of chipotles en adobo)
ingredients.name: adobo sauce (from the same can of chipotles en adobo)

preparationSteps: Make the pickled red onions first — the night before ideally, but even 1 hour before dinner will be great. Combine 1 thinly sliced red onion, 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, 1/4 cup hot water, 1 tablespoon sugar, and a big pinch of salt in a jar or any container with a lid. Refrigerate for up to 2 months. Preheat oven to 400°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

To make the flautas, combine 1 can drained black beans and 1 can refried beans in a large bowl. Depending on how much heat you like, mince 1 or 2 chipotle peppers. You can also remove the seeds to make it less spicy — I like the seeds in. Stir the minced chipotle pepper into the beans, then taste and season as needed with kosher salt. Stir 1 1/2 cups shredded cheese into the bean mixture. Taste and adjust seasoning again if needed. (Some refried beans are super flavorful as is; others might need more salt and/or cumin, chili powder, cayenne, etc. to suit your taste.)

Spread 3 tablespoons of the bean and cheese mixture down the center of a tortilla, then roll it up tightly. Repeat process with remaining tortillas. Place the assembled flautas seam-side down on a baking sheet, at least 1 inch apart. Spray with cooking spray (or drizzle some oil on top and rub it in with your fingers) and bake for 10 minutes, then flip and cook for another 10 minutes, until golden-brown all over.

While they’re cooking, make the chipotle crema by stirring together 1/2 cup sour cream, 2 teaspoons adobo sauce (from the can of chipotles), the juice of 1 lime, and a pinch of kosher salt. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Top the flautas with thinly sliced iceberg lettuce, 1 chopped mango, avocado slices, 1/4 cup cilantro, and 3 tablespoons pickled red onions, and serve with lots of chipotle crema.

name: thai tofu curry noodle soup
note:
I want meat! To add meat, I recommend using ground chicken or pork. Simply cook it, crumbling it into tiny bits, while you cook the onions and peppers. Or, stir in 2 cups of shredded rotisserie chicken right at the end. OR, stir in shrimp for the final 3 minutes of the noodles cooking.

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It’s already df! Rice noodles are almost always gf, but check the label and make sure they don’t have an added glutenous ingredient!

Leftovers are a good thing: I speak from experience when I say these leftovers are delicious for up to 1 week!

Prep ahead: Go ahead and dice your veggies up to a day ahead. Otherwise it comes together super quick!

More Thai recipes, plz: Thai Turkey Curry Meatballs or One-Pan Coconut Curry Chicken with Roasted Vegetables and Lime are some fan faves.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 quart (4 cups) vegetable or chicken stock
ingredients.name: vegetable or chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces (AKA half a box) rice noodles (sometimes called pad Thai or stir-fry noodles)
ingredients.name: (AKA half a box) rice noodles (sometimes called pad Thai or stir-fry noodles)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14- to 16-ounce) block of firm tofu, cut into 1/2 inch cubes
ingredients.name: of firm tofu

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1 lime (or 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar or any clear vinegar)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1 lime (or 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar or any clear vinegar)

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add 1 diced yellow onion and 2 diced red bell peppers to the pot and stir to coat in oil.

While the onion and peppers are starting to cook, let’s chop up 2 baby bok choy. Cut each head of box choy in half, separating the tough white stems from the leafy green tops. Cut the root end off of the bok choy so that the stems come apart, then rinse the bok choy off really well (they can be very dirty).
Dice up the white bok choy stems and add them to the pot. Thinly slice the bok choy greens and set them aside.

When the onions, peppers, and bok choy stems have softened a bit, stir in 3 tablespoons red curry paste until it’s coating the vegetables, about 2 minutes. Stir in 1 quart (4 cups) chicken stock, 1 can coconut milk, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, and 1 tablespoon brown sugar and bring to a boil over high heat.
Stir in 4 ounces of noodles, 1 cubed block of tofu, and the bok choy greens.

Reduce the heat to medium-high and stir frequently until the noodles are tender, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in the juice of 1 lime. Serve by using tongs for the noodles, and a ladle for the broth and veggies/tofu.
DIG IN!

name: tandoori-spiced chicken and potatoes with peanut chutney & crispy kale

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 serrano or jalapeño peppers, coarsely chopped (if you don’t want heat, use one pepper or remove the seeds!)
ingredients.name: serrano or jalapeño peppers, coarsely chopped (if you don’t want heat, use one pepper or remove the seeds!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch curly kale, stems removed and leaves torn
ingredients.name: curly kale, stems removed and leaves torn

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Smash and peel 2 garlic cloves and coarsely chop 3 inches of fresh ginger (no need to peel it, but you can if you want) and 2 serrano or jalapeño peppers (if you don’t want heat, use one pepper or remove and discard the seeds). Add the garlic, ginger, and peppers to a blender along with 1 cup yogurt and blend until smooth. Transfer half to a large bowl.

To the yogurt mixture in the large bowl, stir in 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon ground turmeric, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, and a few grinds of pepper. Pat dry your 3 1/2 to 4 pound chicken using paper towels. Add the chicken to the large bowl and use yours hands to coat every nook and cranny with the yogurt. Let it sit at room temperature while you prep the sauce and potatoes. If you have time, you can let the chicken marinate for up to 24 hours covered in the fridge. The longer it marinates, the juicier it’ll be — but it’ll still be delicious even after a quick marinade!

Transfer the yogurt mixture from the blender to a medium bowl. Add 1/2 cup chunky peanut butter and 1 tablespoon lemon juice (hold onto the squeezed lemon, we’re not done with it yet!), and season to taste with kosher salt and pepper. Stir to combine, then thin with water as needed/desired, adding a teaspoon at a time until it reaches a drizzly consistency. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

On a parchment-lined sheet pan, toss together 2 pounds small Yukon gold potatoes and 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Scooch the potatoes to make space in the center of the sheet pan for the chicken. Lift the chicken from the yogurt, letting any excess yogurt drip back into the bowl, and add it to the sheet pan. Stick the lemon halves in the chicken cavity. Tie the legs together using kitchen twine, or if you don’t have kitchen twine, grab a 2 inch-thick strip of aluminum foil, scrunch/roll it up to create a little coil. Use this to fasten the legs together. Easy peasy.
Roast for 45 to 50 minutes, until the thickest part of the thigh registers 165°F.
While the chicken is roasting, wash and de-stem 1 bunch curly kale, then tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces (or roughly chop them if that feels easier).

Transfer the cooked chicken to a cutting board to rest for 15 minutes. Keep the potatoes on the sheet pan and add the kale. Stir to coat in the drippings. Roast until the kale is wilted and crisp in spots, 7 to 10 minutes.
Discard the lemons, carve the chicken (click here for a great tutorial!), and serve with the crispy kale, potatoes, and peanut chutney.

name: creamy cream-less tomato soup
note:
Leftovers are a great thing: You can enjoy leftovers for lunches this week! Reheat the soup on your stovetop (or microwave it), and reheat your biscuit leftovers in the oven (not microwave!) for 5 minutes at 400°F.  These babies also freeze like a charm — both the soup and the biscuits. For the biscuits: I throw them in a gallon Ziploc once cool, get all the air out, and freeze for months. When it’s time to reheat, I throw them on a baking sheet and bake at 400°F for 7 to 10 minutes. Delish! For the soup: Let it cool completely then freeze in either Tupperware or a Ziploc bag with excess air removed for up to 6 months.

Babies love this meal! If you’re feeding a babe, keep their portion (or the whole thing, if it’s easier/you’re OK with the texture) a little thick/chucky — you know… like baby food. If your baby is younger than 1 year, omit the honey. I’ve been feeding this to Calum all week and they’ve been loving it.

But I need a grilled cheese with my tomato soup: I feel you — go for it. Have you ever made grilled cheese croutons? Just make a simple grilled cheese, then cut it up into tiny squares and sprinkle them on top. *chef’s kiss*

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. Make the soup. It’s easy, promise! If a grilled cheese or these biscuits feels like too much for tonight… just toast some yummy cheese on bread and dip it while you eat.

Whole30: You can Whole30-fy the soup! Use ghee instead of butter, and omit the honey. For a bit of texture, toast some pepitas or any nut and sprinkle over top.

Dairy-free: Olive oil instead of butter in the soup. DF butter instead of butter in the biscuits. DF cheese in the biscuits or just eliminate it — they’ll still be delish without.

Gluten-free: Use Bob’s Red Mill gluten-free flour in your biscuits.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/8 teaspoon lemon pepper or freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: lemon pepper or freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons cold butter, diced or grated on the largest hole of a box grater
ingredients.name: cold butter, diced or grated on the largest hole of a box grater

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces (1/2 cup) grated sharp cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: grated sharp cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, stir together 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/8 teaspoon lemon pepper (or regular pepper).

Dice up or grate 4 tablespoons of cold butter, toss it into the flour, then use your fingers to pinch it into the flour until everything’s crumbly and combined. Big butter clumps are A-OK, that’s how we get flaky biscuits!
Toss in 2 ounces (1/2 cup) grated cheddar cheese (or whatever!) and 2 tablespoons minced chives (or 1 tablespoon fresh thyme, or 1 teaspoon of a dried herb you like).
Stir in 1/2 cup whole milk until just combined. Don’t over-stir! The dough will be wet and sticky.
Drop the batter by big spoonfuls (I use an ice cream scoop and made 7 biscuits) onto the lined baking sheet, 1 inch apart. Spray the tops with cooking spray.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the tops are golden-brown and crispy.
Serve alongside your soup and DIG IN!

name: one-pan creamy boursin pasta with shrimp
note:
But I don’t eat carbs: omit the spaghetti and bake everything else UNCOVERED for just 30 minutes. Toss in 4 spiralized zucchini once it’s finished cooking, they’ll cook in the residual heat.

Gluten-free: cook your favorite gluten-free pasta in a separate pot, but bake everything else the exact same minus the pasta and the water. Toss the cooked pasta into the tomato baking dish with a big splash of pasta cooking water and toss until evenly coated.

But this makes an insane amount of pasta and I’m eating alone: halve the recipe, but find a smaller pan so that the spaghetti is still covered in water.

How does this work? the heat of the oven heats up the water, which allows it to be absorbed by the spaghetti. It does not absorb all of the water, and what’s left gets really starchy and helps create a creamy sauce when stirred together with the Boursin and Parmesan.

Make ahead: cook until the step where you add the shrimp. When you’re ready to eat, add the shrimp on top and finish that final 10 minutes of cooking.

Leftovers are a good thing: but if you don’t think you’ll be able to eat a pound of shrimp, only use half a pound! Leftover shrimp aren’t the best, but leftover pasta might actually be *the* best. Reheat leftovers in a skillet over medium heat and stir in a splash of water at a time until it’s really saucy and creamy. You might end up adding a lot of water to get it nice and creamy, that’s normal, just re-season with salt and pepper as needed!

What to do when you really don’t feel like cooking: ditch the red bell pepper and use garlic powder. Then you don’t have to chop a single thing!

Dairy-free: use dairy-free cream cheese! 5 to 8 ounces is great.

I need a salad: to make your life easy, skip serving a side salad, and instead toss in 4 cups of spinach when you add the parmesan and basil at the very end. Just toss until wilted!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 20 to 24 ounces cherry tomatoes (depending on your package size)
ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes (depending on your package size)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 thinly sliced garlic cloves or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder (depending on how much or how little effort you feel like putting forth)
ingredients.name: thinly sliced garlic cloves or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder (depending on how much or how little effort you feel like putting forth)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5.2-ounce) package Boursin Garlic & Herbs(or any flavor Boursin!)see notes for other cheese options
ingredients.name: see notes for other cheese options
ingredients.quantity: 1 (5.2-ounce) package Boursin Garlic & Herbs(or any flavor Boursin!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup thinly sliced basil or finely chopped parsley
ingredients.name: thinly sliced basil or finely chopped parsley

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

In a 9x13-inch baking dish, layer in 1 pound of spaghetti, 20 to 24 ounces cherry tomatoes, 2 thinly sliced red bell peppers, and 6 thinly sliced garlic cloves (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder). Drizzle 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil over top and season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper.

name: white bean chicken chili

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 diced bell pepper (any color) OR 1 can (about 4.5 ounces) chopped green chiles, undrained
ingredients.name: diced bell pepper (any color) OR 1 can (about 4.5 ounces) chopped green chiles, undrained

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon, or more to taste, cayenne pepper
ingredients.name: or more to taste, cayenne pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 rotisserie chicken, skin removed, meat pulled off the bone and shredded, bones discarded
ingredients.name: rotisserie chicken, skin removed, meat pulled off the bone and shredded, bones discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cans (15 ounces each) great northern or navy beans, drained (not rinsed)
ingredients.name: great northern or navy beans, drained (not rinsed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.name: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: Shredded cheese, such as Cheddar, Pepper Jack or a crumbled queso fresco
ingredients.name: Shredded cheese, such as Cheddar, Pepper Jack or a crumbled queso fresco

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon olive or avocado oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add 1 diced yellow onion, 6 minced garlic cloves, 1 diced bell pepper (or 1 can chopped green chiles), 2 teaspoons cumin, 2 teaspoons oregano, and 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (or more to taste). Cook, stirring, until the veggies soften, 3 to 5 minutes. If the spices start to stick to the bottom of the pot, just add a splash of water.

Pour in 1 quart low-sodium chicken broth, 3 cans drained (but not rinsed) great northern or navy beans, 1 shredded rotisserie chicken, and enough water to fill one empty can of beans. Increase the heat to medium-high and stir until the mixture comes to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and let the chili simmer UNCOVERED until it thickens, 35 to 40 minutes. Once your soup has thickened to your liking, cover it and keep it warm over low heat throughout dinner time. Note: You can make this chili as far as 3 days in advance!
Taste the chili for seasoning, adding salt, pepper, and/or more cumin if needed. Ladle into bowls and serve with desired toppings.

name: mini cheesy corn muffins
note:
Prep ahead: You can pre-shred your rotisserie chicken up to a day ahead of time  and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. In fact, I’d recommend doing this if you’re not going to cook the soup right after grocery shopping. Rotisserie chicken is much easier to shred when it’s warm and fresh than it is after it’s been refrigerated. You could also pre-chop your onion and pepper.

Make ahead: Make this soup up to 3 days ahead of time, let it totally cool down, then refrigerate it right in the pot (with the lid on). Or transfer it to another airtight container, if the pot won’t fit in the fridge. To reheat, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low heat and cover during dinnertime.

Make it in your slow cooker: You can sauté the veggies first, or just dump all the ingredients in the slow cooker and cook it on low for 4-6 hours.

Love your leftovers: This is a perfect stock-your-freezer meal. Think ahead and double the recipe, then freeze half for the winter months!

I’m serving kids: Buy the Scoops tortilla chips and let them dip them into the chili. Arrange the toppings in little bowls like ice cream toppings to the side. Autonomy really encourages my kids to eat!

Vegetarian: Omit the chicken, add an extra can of beans, and use vegetable broth.

Dairy-free: This chili is dairy free, just omit the sour cream and cheese as toppings, or swap them with plant-based versions.

Gluten-free: This chili is also gluten-free, but make sure the tortillas chips are labeled gluten-free, if serving alongside your chili.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 package (8.5 ounces) Jiffy Corn Muffin Mix (vegetarian)
ingredients.name: Jiffy Corn Muffin Mix (vegetarian)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack or sharp Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded Pepper Jack or sharp Cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Vegetable oil spray (or any cooking spray), for misting the pan
ingredients.name: Vegetable oil spray (or any cooking spray), for misting the pan

preparationSteps: Place a rack in the center of the oven, and preheat the oven to 425°F. Place 1 package Jiffy Corn Muffin mix, 1/2 cup buttermilk, 1 large egg, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, and 1 cup shredded cheese in a medium bowl. Stir until just combined. The batter will be thick.

Coat a mini muffin pan (or pans) with cooking spray, then scoop the batter to fill each cup two-thirds of the way full. Place in the oven and bake until golden, about 10 to 15 minutes for mini muffins (or 15 to 20 minutes for standard size). Remove and serve warm, or let cool, wrap in foil, and freeze.
servings: Makes 18 mini muffins or 12 standard muffins

name: creamy chicken, leek, and sun-dried tomato orzotto
note:
Prep ahead: To make this meal come together even faster, you could pre-cube your chicken, pre-slice and wash your leeks, and pre-mince your garlic up to a day ahead of cook time — store them in separate airtight containers (meat in one, veggies in another) in the fridge until it’s time to cook.

Save time: Swap the leek for pre-chopped onion and use frozen crushed garlic cubes instead of mincing your own.

Vegetarian: To make it vegetarian, leave out the chicken, but stir all of those seasonings into the pot when you add the orzo. If you wanted, you could add a pound of chopped or sliced mushrooms. Cook them in the skillet until they have released and absorbed their liquid and are nice and tender before you add the leek and garlic and continue with the recipe.

Dairy-free: Use a DF heavy whipping cream or a container of vegan Boursin in place of the cream (but if you are using the Boursin, add more stock in place of the cream and mix the “cheese” in after the orzo is cooked!). Use dairy-free Parm like VioLife or add a couple tablespoons of nutritional yeast in place of the Parm or just omit it. And use DF butter or oil for the butter.

Gluten-free: Swap the orzo out for arborio or white rice (cooked the same way) or a gluten-free noodle alternative! If you’re using a GF pasta like Banza, I would cook the noodles separately in stock or water. While the noodles are cooking in a separate pot, keep cooking the chicken, leeks, and garlic in the skillet until the chicken is cooked through (about 8 minutes, or until it’s 165°F internally) — lower the heat as needed so the garlic doesn’t burn. Reserve 1/4 cup of the pasta water before you drain it then add the drained noodles along with the cream, pasta water, and sun-dried tomatoes to the skillet. Once they’re warm, proceed with the recipe as written.

Using oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes? Reserve the oil and make a salad dressing with it later this week! Measure the oil, then whisk in 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt and pepper, and half as much lemon juice as you have oil. Delish.

A reminder about Parm: When I say Parmesan, I really want you to buy Parmigiano Reggiano (it’s tastier!). And when we’re using grated Parm in a recipe where we want it to get melty — like this one — we want to grate it by hand or in your blender rather than use pre-grated, which contains preservatives that don’t allow it to melt as well.

Feeding kids: In case you glazed over this in the intro, if your children are averse to anything green, I recommend pulling their servings out before you add the spinach!

Riffs + love your leftovers + freezer friendly: See above the recipe for these notes.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional if you like heat: 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: Optional if you like heat: 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups julienned (AKA, thinly sliced) sun-dried tomatoes (this will be about a full 8-ounce jar of oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, or a full 3-ounce bag of dry-packed sun-dried tomatoes)
ingredients.name: julienned (AKA, thinly sliced) sun-dried tomatoes (this will be about a full 8-ounce jar of oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, or a full 3-ounce bag of dry-packed sun-dried tomatoes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese (roughly 2 ounces), plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese (roughly 2 ounces), plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Trim off and discard all of the fat (AKA the white stuff!) from 1 1/2 pounds chicken breasts, then cut the breasts into 1-inch cubes (the top joint of your thumb is about 1 inch for reference — you don’t have to be precise about this, just eyeball it and err on the smaller side so they are nice and bite-sized). Sprinkle the cubed chicken with 1 1/2 teaspoons dried oregano, 1 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, and 3/4 teaspoon garlic powder and toss to coat (right there on the cutting board — no need to dirty a bowl). If you like a bit of heat, I also recommend seasoning your chicken with 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.
Thinly slice and wash 1 large leek (here’s a demo) and mince 6 garlic cloves. It’s OK if they touch the raw chicken.

Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a wide skillet or heavy-bottomed pot or braiser over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in an even layer and cook until browned on one side, 2 to 3 minutes. Add 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, the sliced leek, and the minced garlic and stir to cook for 2 minutes, or until the leek is tender. If the garlic starts to turn dark brown before 2 minutes has passed, go ahead and move on to the next step.

Stir in 3 cups low-sodium chicken stock, 16 ounces (2 1/2 cups) uncooked orzo pasta, and 1 1/2 cups thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes (if you’re using oil-packed tomatoes, don’t add the oil!). Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer over medium-low heat. Stir in 1 pint (2 cups) heavy cream and simmer until the orzo is cooked and the sauce has thickened, 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every minute or so.

Turn off the heat then stir in 2 huge handfuls fresh spinach, tearing it with your hands as you add it. Using a microplane or grater, grate the zest of 1 lemon directly into the skillet. Grate 1/2 cup Parm and add it too.
Stir until the spinach has wilted, 1 to 2 minutes. If your pasta has thickened up and is no longer saucy and loose like a risotto, add more stock (or water!) to loosen it up.

Taste. What does it need? More kosher salt? A pinch of red pepper flakes to heat things up? Maybe some lemon juice if you’re liking that lemony flavor and want even more. Remember that everyone’s taste buds are different and that the last step of every recipe is to taste and adjust until it’s perfect for you.
Serve in bowls, garnished with more Parm and freshly grated black pepper.

name: 30-minute pork lettuce wraps with coconut rice and sauces
note:
Vegetarian: You’re gonna make scrambled tofu using all of these ingredients! Skip the marinating step, but add the salt and sugar in while scrambling. Use a firm block of tofu and do it over high heat just like the pork!

Gluten-free: Be sure to use a gluten-free soy sauce as tamari or coconut aminos.

Dairy-free: Omit the butter, or use a DF one.

What to do when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy a pre-marinated teriyaki or otherwise Asian-flavored pork tenderloin or chicken thighs, have the butcher cube it up, and just saute it in oil and add the butter at the end. Buy premade sriracha mayo. Throw the full scallions and ginger slices in the blender and pulse until still chunky but chopped up. Buy frozen cooked rice.

Double it: To double the meat — use two skillets so that you don’t overcrowd it and make it steamy instead of browned. To double the rice — 3 cups rice, 2 cans coconut milk, but only 1 cup water.

Whole30: Ditch the rice completely. If you want to make coconut cauliflower rice, do it. Omit the butter.

Make ahead: Marinate the meat and make your serving board with the sauces and toppings and lettuce leaves entirely ahead of time. Just throw that whole board right in the fridge. Cook the rice ahead of time too, refrigerate it right in the pot, add a splash of water and reheat by steaming it over low heat. Cook the pork right when it’s go time.

Leftovers are a good thing: Saute several cups of vegetables such as mushrooms and bell peppers in a bit of oil over high heat until tender. Stir in the rice, leftover pork, and ginger-scallion sauce. Drizzle sriracha-mayo over top.

Feeding kids: Wraps and taco-y things don’t quite work out for my two-year-old, so to feed this meal to him I made “rice pancakes” by combining about 1 cup of rice with 1 large egg and a couple tablespoons of flour to bind it all together into a pancake-y consistency. Cook like pancakes! He loved the pork, rice pancakes, and sriracha mayo.

You don’t need to buy them, but if you have them, use them!): chopped peanuts, toasted sesame seeds, chopped cilantro, mint, or basil, pickled red onions, diced cucumber, diced bell pepper, thinly sliced jalapeño, pickled jalapeño….
ingredients.name: Dumpster dive (Go hunt through your fridge and pantry and find things like this! You don’t need to buy them, but if you have them, use them!): chopped peanuts, toasted sesame seeds, chopped cilantro, mint, or basil, pickled red onions, diced cucumber, diced bell pepper, thinly sliced jalapeño, pickled jalapeño….

preparationSteps: Cut 1 pound pork tenderloin up into 1/2-inch cubes. That’s about the size of your thumbnail. To do this: cut the tenderloin in half lengthwise, then cut each of those halves in half. So at this point, you have four long strips of tenderloin. Now cut each of those strips into 1/2-inch cubes. Right on the cutting board, season the pork with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and 1 tablespoon brown sugar. Toss to coat, then set aside at room temperature while you work on the rice and sauces.

To make the rice: combine 1 1/2 cups white rice (no, you don’t need to rinse it), 1 can coconut milk, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to the lowest heat possible on your stovetop and cover for 15 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and leave covered to allow the rice to steam until you’re ready to eat (at least 5 minutes but up to 1 hour).

To make the ginger scallion sauce: thinly slice the white and light green part of 4 scallions. Like, as thin as possible. Paper thin! Now slice the dark green part of the scallions on the bias (check out the photo), also super thin. Add the light green and white parts to a bowl. The dark green parts are for garnish — set them on the platter. Dice 1/4 cup pickled ginger. Add it to the bowl. Stir in 2 tablespoons neutral oil, 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce until well combined, then set the bowl on the platter. Place a little handful of pickled ginger on the platter before you put it away too.
Now’s a good time to start heating up your skillet. By the time you finish making the sriracha mayo, it’ll be hot enough to cook on. It needs to preheat for at least 4 minutes!

To make the sriracha mayo: stir together 1/3 cup mayo, the juice of 1/2 a lime, 1 tablespoon sriracha, and 1/2 teaspoon soy sauce. Taste. Can you go spicier? Do it! Too spicy? Add more mayo! Set the sriracha mayo and the sriracha bottle on the platter.

Pull the lettuce leaves apart carefully to create your lettuce cups. I like to trim the root off, pull the leaves off, trim more root off, pull the leaves off, and so on. Place on the platter. Place the platter and the rice on the dinner table — it’s almost show time!
Now your skillet should be nice and hot. Are you seeing little wisps of smoke come off the sides? Good, we’re ready to cook! Pat the pork completely dry using a paper towel.

Add 2 tablespoons of neutral oil to the skillet (which, yes, is still on HIGH heat!) and swirl to coat the pan. Add the pork in an even layer and allow it to brown completely through, until only the very top of each piece of pork is still pink, 4 to 6 minutes.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound large shell pasta (but any short noodle works)
ingredients.name: large shell pasta (but any short noodle works)

ingredients.name: OPTIONAL: pesto, buffalo sauce, crab meat, sun-dried tomatoes, lobster meat, you get the drill!

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add a HUGE pinch of kosher salt. Cook 1 pound short pasta noodles al dente per package instructions. That means that when you test a piece, it should still taste a little bit hard. Why? Because we’re actually going to bake the mac and cheese, so the pasta is going to keep cooking and we don’t want it to get too soft!
Meanwhile, grate 12 ounces cheddar cheese and 1 cup of Parmesan cheese.

After draining the pasta, return it to the pot along with 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta cooking water, 8 ounces shredded cheddar cheese (AKA A LITTLE MORE THAN HALF BUT NOT ALL OF IT!), 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 4 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup whole milk, 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt.

Continue stirring until everything is totally melted and smooth. If the sauce is too thick, stir in more pasta cooking water. Everything should melt nicely off the heat, but, if needed, you can turn the burner back onto very low heat to help the cheeses melt.

Taste and season! You can add salt, pepper, nutmeg, a little ground mustard. Maybe you’re in the mood for something a little different — try adding a swirl of pesto, a handful of sun-dried tomatoes, or buffalo sauce. Or make it fancy with some crab or lobster meat! Or add a green like steamed chopped broccoli! Do your thing!

Transfer the mac and cheese to a greased 9x13-inch baking dish or 12-inch cast iron skillet. IF COOKING IMMEDIATELY, sprinkle with the remaining 4 ounces shredded cheddar cheese. If not cooking immediately, let it cool down. Once cool, top with the remaining cheese and cover and refrigerate for up to 72 hours.
When you want to eat in about 45 minutes, preheat oven to 375°F.
Bake uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Let the mac and cheese rest for at least 5 minutes before beginning to serve it. Enjoy!

name: healthy sloppy joes
note:
Pinched for time: Buy store-bought diced onion (and green pepper, if available) and pre-minced garlic.

Vegetarian: Swap the ground meat for dried green lentils. To cook, rinse 1 cup green lentils (be sure to sift through them for little rocks while you’re rinsing — it can happen!). Add them to a medium or large pot with 2 cups of liquid (either low-sodium broth or water — or half broth and half water). Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered until tender (about 20 minutes, but it’ll vary on the age and type of your lentils), stirring occasionally. Don’t drain any excess water from the pot. Continue with the recipe. You may not need to add all 3 tablespoons of water, depending on how much is left in your pot from cooking the lentils.

Whole30: Check your tomato paste to be sure there are no added sugars, omit the honey/sugar throughout the recipe, and opt for the roasted potato or cauli rice serving options!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: No dairy already! But check the ingredient label for your buns — some have dairy, some don’t. Gf: Serve it on a baked potato or cauli rice.

Leftovers are a good thing: If you’ve got extra, freeze it in either individual portions or in a family-sized portions, depending on who you’ll be cooking for. This is a great dish to double if you’re looking to meal prep (like if you’re pregnant right now — double this recipe and freeze half!). Thaw the sloppy Joe meat in the fridge up to a day before you plan to make the meal, or just plop the frozen block in a skillet, breaking it up with your spatula as it warms. Add water one tablespoon at a time as needed. If you’re looking for some delish lunches, just keep the leftovers in the fridge, and mix up how your serve them throughout the week (like on a potato then bun then rice). The salad dressing will stay good in a a refrigerated jar for up to 2 weeks.

Add some plant protein: Seeds and nuts are packed with healthy fats, so I try to add them to my salads whenever I’ve got them in the pantry. Some pistachios, pepitas, or sunflower seeds would be delicious on this simple salad!

Simple Green Salad with Apple Cider Vinaigrette:

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook 1 small diced yellow onion and 1 small diced green bell pepper for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft. Add 4 minced garlic cloves and cook for an additional minute, stirring frequently so that the garlic doesn’t burn.

Add 1 pound ground turkey and use a spatula to break the turkey up into teeny tiny crumbles — no big clumps! Once the turkey is cooked and only about 1 tablespoon of liquid remains in the skillet, stir in 3 tablespoons tomato paste, 3 tablespoons water, 1 tablespoon honey, 2 teaspoons apple cider vinegar, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 3/4 teaspoon chili powder, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.
Turn the heat down to medium-low and continue cooking, stirring often, for about 3 to 4 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened around the turkey.
Serve on a bun or over a roasted potato or rice!

If making the salad, simply add all of the dressing ingredients to a large jar and shake until combined. Add 4 cups mixed greens to a large bowl, season with a pinch of salt, then toss with 1 tablespoon of dressing at a time until the greens are dressed to your liking. The dressing will be good in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 red bell peppers, very thinly sliced
ingredients.name: red bell peppers, very thinly sliced

ingredients.name: of lacinato (flat leaf) kale, ribs removed and discarded, leaves thinly sliced

preparationSteps: In a gallon-size resealable bag or bowl, combine ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar, and 1 tablespoon sesame oil. Grate in a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger and 1 peeled garlic clove. Add 4 halibut filets and do your best to cover them in marinade. Refrigerate for up to 24 hours or marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 400°F.

Slice 2 red bell peppers as thinly as possible. Like, really, really thinly! Pull the stems/ribs out of 1 large bunch of kale (and discard), then thinly slice the leaves too. Throw the peppers and kale on your largest rimmed baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tablespoon sesame oil and season with a big pinch of salt. Stir (or use your hands) to evenly coat all the veggies with oil.
Bake for 6 minutes.

Remove baking sheet from the oven, then scooch things around to make room for the 4 halibut filets. Drizzle the marinade (yes, it was touching the fish, but yes, this is totally food safe since we are about to cook it at a high temperature) all over the kale and peppers. Sprinkle 1/3 cup finely chopped macadamia nuts and 1/3 cup panko on top of the fish. Add a pat (about ½ tablespoon) of butter on top of each filet.
Bake for an additional 6 to 10 minutes, checking at the 6-minute mark for the first time. When the fish reaches 130°F internally or flakes easily when you insert a fork and twist, it’s done.
Serve the fish, kale, and peppers over rice or on their own.

name: fried egg pasta with garlicky crunchies
note:
I got some egg shell in the pan: Use half of an empty egg shell to fish it out — egg shell attracts egg shell!

Cracking eggs “quickly” stresses me out: First of all, it doesn’t have to be SUPER quick. Just crack one egg after the other as swiftly as you can. But if the thought of this stresses you out, instead of cracking them right into the pan,  crack the eggs into a big bowl then gently pour the batch of cracked eggs into the skillet.

Feeding picky eaters: My big kids don’t do eggs (I know, it’s a real bummer), so I just pulled out some pasta before tossing it in with the eggs. They got pasta with butter and Parm, we got fried egg pasta, everyone was very happy!

Must have meat: Eggs provide *plenty* of protein, but if you’re a must-have-meat household, you could cook some chopped bacon or diced pancetta in another skillet over medium heat while your sauce is coming together. Add the crispy bacon/pancetta to the pan when you stir in the cooked pasta. Or, serve the pasta with some grilled chicken or shrimp on top, or some shredded store-bought rotisserie chicken.

Gimme some more greens: You could add some chopped spinach to the mix when you stir in the noodles. Or if you want to keep the pasta recipe as is (like if you’re a parent and know better than to add something GREEN to a beautifully beige meal), the simple arugula salad recipe included in this post would be a fab addition to dinner.

I don’t/can’t eat eggs: Make a simple and delicious aglio e olio (garlic and oil) pasta instead. For that: After you’ve made your garlicky crunchies and wiped the skillet clean, add 1/2 cup of your very best EVOO to the skillet over medium-low heat. Once the oil is warm, add your sliced garlic cloves (and a couple shakes of red pepper flakes or some chili crisp if you want some heat!). Stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until your garlic is lightly golden and smells delicious, making sure that it doesn’t burn. Reserve a cup of pasta water before you drain your noodles. Add the cooked noodles to the oil and toss. If they look too dry, add a splash of the reserved pasta water. Repeat until they’re all coated in oil, then season to taste with salt and pepper.

Save time: You could skip the garlicky crunchies… but dang they’re delicious.

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good for up to 3 days stored in the fridge in an airtight container. Reheat them in the microwave or on the stovetop. If you want to mix up the flavors a bit, warm your leftovers in a skillet with a splash of soy sauce and a scoop of chili crisp.

Dairy-free: Use plant-based butter and DF Parm (or just skip the cheese).

Gluten-free: Use GF spaghetti and gluten-free panko! My cousin Marlea swears that GF panko stays crunchy longer than the regular kind!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound angel hair (or spaghetti or bucatini) pasta
ingredients.name: angel hair (or spaghetti or bucatini) pasta

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 garlic cloves, peeled and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: garlic cloves

ingredients.rawIngredient: Lots of freshly grated Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: Lots of freshly grated Parmesan cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: finely chopped parsley (I really like it here)
ingredients.name: Optional: finely chopped parsley (I really like it here)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. While you’re waiting, start cooking the breadcrumb crunchies (the next step below). When the water reaches a boil, add 1 pound pasta and cook until al dente (cook times vary — follow the instructions on your box of pasta).

To make your garlicky crunchies: In a very large skillet (if you don’t have one, use a large pot, such as a Dutch oven), melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat then add 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Stir often until golden-brown, 4 to 5 minutes. Turn off the heat, transfer the breadcrumbs to a small bowl to cool, and wipe out the skillet.
Thinly slice 8 peeled garlic cloves.

Return the wiped-out skillet to the stovetop over medium-low heat. Warm 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil and 4 tablespoons unsalted butter. Add the garlic and let it cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until it’s just starting to turn golden.

Quickly crack 8 large eggs straight into the skillet. We’re moving quickly here because we want them to all cook for roughly the same amount of time. If cracking eggs stresses you out — or if you get a bit of shell in the pan — see the notes section for tips! The eggs should not sizzle or pop when you add them to the oil; if they do, turn the heat down!

Season the eggs generously with a big pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper and cover the skillet with a lid or anything that’ll cover it (baking sheet, mismatched lid, whatever). Cook the eggs for 2 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny. WATCH THEM CLOSELY — DO NOT OVERCOOK YOUR EGGS, K!? Even if you don’t love a runny fried egg, trust me here, you want these yolks to be runny — they’ll keep cooking when you toss the eggs into the pasta and make a delightful sauce.

Drain the pasta (but again, scoop out some of the pasta water with a mug before you do!!) and toss the noodles straight into the skillet full of fried eggs along with a big splash (about 3 tablespoons) of reserved pasta water. If your pasta turned into one giant clump, don’t worry, it’ll de-clump when you start tossing it into the sauce/eggs! Use tongs to toss everything together, breaking the eggs up as you toss!

Take a big bite and then season with however much salt and pepper you need (for me it was about 1/2 teaspoon salt and five grinds of pepper). Want it to be saucier? Add more pasta water and toss toss toss.

Serve, ideally in low bowls. Top with garlicky crunchies and grate so much Parmesan cheese on top that it looks like it snowed on your bowl! Add some really finely chopped parsley, if you’ve got it, and dig in!

name: marinated grilled veggies with burrata
note:
Add some meat! Cook chicken breasts if you want additional protein. Make them the exact same way — grilled for about 4 minutes per side until 160°F internally (they’ll continue to cook once pulled off to reach 165°F). Slice them up then soak them in the marinade along with the veggies.

I don’t have a grill: To roast, you’ll need several rimmed baking sheets. Preheat your oven to 425°F and roast thicker vegetables like fennel and onion and broccoli rabe for 30 to 40 minutes, and more water-filled or smaller vegetables like zucchini or green beans for 20 to 30.

Meal prep: While you’re cooking the vegetables, go ahead and grill a pound or two of chicken thighs or breasts for the week (or for dinner tonight)!

Make ahead: This is a great recipe for entertaining. You can prep your veggies days in advance, keeping them in the fridge until it’s time to grill. Make the dressing up to 24 hours in advance, also stored in the fridge. Don’t forget to pull the burrata out before you light the grill so it has a chance to come to room temp!

Special ingredient: Burrata, baby! If you’ve never had it before, get ready. It’s rich, creamy, and has the most delicious flavor. Like I said in the intro, it’s a super fresh mozzarella that’s absolutely delectable. You may have had it at a restaurant before — thankfully in recent years it’s become more widely available at Whole Foods, TJ’s, and even some local grocers. Once you’ve made this meal and burrata’s part of your repertoire, try the Burrata with Garlic Confit app in my cookbook, Just Married. Or click here for some extra burrata recipes from my blog. OR just serve some fresh burrata with a sliced juicy tomato and/or peach and call it a lunch.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 pounds grilling vegetables (such as bell or mini or shishito peppers, asparagus, zucchini, yellow squash, broccoli rabe, portobello mushrooms, fennel, corn, onions, green beans)
ingredients.name: grilling vegetables (such as bell or mini or shishito peppers, asparagus, zucchini, yellow squash, broccoli rabe, portobello mushrooms, fennel, corn, onions, green beans)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh basil, or other soft herbs, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: fresh basil, or other soft herbs

preparationSteps: Leave any small vegetables like asparagus or green beans whole (except for trimming off the woody asparagus ends — still do that!). Cut the other vegetables into long, skinny planks (like the width of two quarters stacked on top of each other) so that they won’t fall through the grill grates.
Place all your vegetables on a rimmed baking sheet and toss with just enough cooking oil to VERY lightly coat them (only about 2 tablespoons max). Season with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.
Preheat outdoor grill to 450°F. Take the burrata out of the refrigerator and set it on the counter to come to room temperature.

While the grill is heating up, make the marinade. In a jar or bowl, combine 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup champagne vinegar, 1 finely minced shallot, 1 tablespoon whole-grain mustard, 2 teaspoons maple syrup, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.
Soak a wadded-up paper towel in 2 tablespoons of cooking oil. Grab the oily wad with tongs and rub it on the grill grates. THIS IS A VERY IMPORTANT STEP — DO NOT SKIP IT!
Grill baby, grill!

As the vegetables finish cooking, return them to the baking sheet and pour some of the marinade over top. Continue grilling in batches until all vegetables are cooked, adding more marinade if you think it needs it. Let the vegetables marinate for at least 10 minutes or up to 1 hour at room temperature before serving.
Season with a little more salt and pepper (to taste), tear the burrata up and place it over top with the thinly sliced fresh basil.
DIG IN!
servings: Serves 4 to 6 (THIS IS GREAT FOR MEAL PREP!)

name: starbucks egg bite copycat frittata with sweet potato hash
note:
WTC when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy frozen sweet potato fries and serve those alongside your frittata. Or simply serve it with an olive oil and lemon juice dressed salad.

*Aesthetic*: Annoyingly, the bacon all falls to the bottom of the frittata since it’s heavier than the eggs. If you want your frittata to look like the real egg bites — where the bacon is on top — remove the bacon from the skillet before pouring the egg mixture in. Bake the frittata for 25 minutes, then gently sprinkle the bacon over top and continue cooking. The eggs will be solidified enough at this point that most of the bacon should remain on top. Or actually… just flip your slice of frittata upside down. Duh.

Vegetarian: Swap in 1 cup of chopped roasted red bell peppers for the bacon. Just stir them into the egg mixture after pouring it into the skillet. Another veggie option would be 1 cup of chopped and cooked mushrooms and kale. If using veggies, cook the sweet potatoes with olive oil in lieu of the bacon grease. Also be sure to grease your frittata skillet really well if you’re not using non-stick. Bacon fat *does* add a lot of flavor to the hash, so I’d also add a pinch of chili powder, celery salt, and cumin.

Leftovers are a good thing: Enjoy your B4D leftovers for breakfast all week long! Let the frittata cool completely before storing it in the fridge covered. You can eat it cool, at room temp, or lightly reheated (just don’t overheat it as the eggs will get rubbery).

Dairy-free/gluten-free: For df: You can use a df cheese that you love, like shredded plant-based mozzarella or cheddar. Instead of cottage cheese, use cashew yogurt ideally, or almond yogurt, or 1/3 cup almond milk. It’s already gluten-free!

Gimme some greens: Wilt a big handful of chopped spinach or kale in the skillet with the bacon before you add the egg mixture. Or, like I noted above, just serve a side salad with the meal!

Make ahead: You can prep the frittata earlier in the day or even the day before. Follow the directions until it’s ready to bake, and just store it covered in the fridge. Hold off on making the hash! If you’re going the make-ahead route, pour the bacon grease into a jar or glass container rather than onto the sheet pan. Once it’s cool, cover it and store it in the fridge. When you’re ready to cook the hash, reheat 3 tablespoons of bacon grease (either on the stove or covered and in short increments in the microwave) and proceed as written.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5-ounce block of Gruyère (most Gruyère comes in 5-ounce increments; if yours does not, just use 5 ounces of it!)
ingredients.name: of Gruyère (most Gruyère comes in 5-ounce increments; if yours does not, just use 5 ounces of it!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large sweet potato (about 1 pound, but it doesn’t need to be perfect), washed and dried, but not peeled unless you want to!
ingredients.name: large sweet potato (about 1 pound, but it doesn’t need to be perfect), washed and dried, but not peeled unless you want to!

ingredients.rawIngredient: Note: I also love serving a simple green salad with this meal. Mixed greens or arugula with salt, lemon juice, and good extra-virgin olive oil.
ingredients.name: Note: I also love serving a simple green salad with this meal. Mixed greens or arugula with salt, lemon juice, and good extra-virgin olive oil.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 275°F.

Cook 8 to 10 slices of chopped-up bacon in a 10-inch skillet, preferably non-stick but cast iron works too, over medium-high heat. (A 12-inch skillet would also work but your frittata will be skinnier and cook faster!) As the skillet collects grease, pour it off onto a large rimmed baking sheet to help the bacon cook up really nice and crispy.
While the bacon cooks, let’s make the custardy egg mixture!
Cut a 5-ounce block of Gruyère into a few pieces and toss it in a blender. Pulse until grated. Remove 1/3 cup of grated Gruyère from the blender and save for another use.

Add 10 large eggs, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and a couple shakes of hot sauce to the blender. Blend until smooth, 10 to 20 seconds. The less you blend, the better — stop blending as soon as it looks smooth! My Vitamix only takes about 8 seconds.
When the bacon is crispy, pour any remaining grease onto the sheet pan.
Turn off the skillet’s heat and let it cool down for a while, then pour the egg mixture into the skillet. Give it a stir.
Now let’s turn our attention to the sweet potato hash.
First, pour all but 3 tablespoons bacon grease from the sheet pan into a jar (if you want to save it for later cooking) or into the trash (but wait until it has cooled down some before doing so).

Use the largest hole of a box grater to grate 1 large sweet potato directly onto the sheet pan. Stir in 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and a few grinds (or 1/4 teaspoon) of black pepper. Spread into an even layer.
Place the frittata in the center of the oven and the sweet potato on the rung below it.

Cook for 30 to 40 minutes, until the frittata no longer jiggles when you shake the handle of the skillet. Note: it took most testers the full 40 minutes, but ovens often run hot, so start checking at 30 minutes.

Remove the frittata from the oven and allow it to rest. Turn your broiler on high. Transfer the sweet potatoes to the top rung of your oven and broil them for a few minutes. BE VERY CAREFUL THAT YOU DON’T BURN THEM! I highly recommend sitting on your tush in front of the oven with the oven light on to watch them until they brown. Remove them from the oven once they’ve started to brown.

Sprinkle 1/4 cup chopped parsley over everything to combat the beige-ness of this meal, then CAREFULLY slice the frittata with a BUTTER KNIFE (not a sharp knife or you’ll ruin your skillet’s non-stick coating!). Serve!

name: chicken and rice soup

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (2-inch) pieces of ginger, peeled and sliced
ingredients.name: of ginger

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 lemongrass stalks, cut into 3 pieces (some stores sell lemongrass paste in a tube — use 1 tablespoon if that’s all you can find)
ingredients.name: lemongrass stalks
ingredients.note: cut into 3 pieces (some stores sell lemongrass paste in a tube — use 1 tablespoon if that’s all you can find)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1 lime, plus wedges for serving
ingredients.name: Juice of 1 lime, plus wedges for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon coconut oil¼ cup chopped peanuts¼ cup shaved coconutPinch of kosher salt
ingredients.name: coconut oil¼ cup chopped peanuts¼ cup shaved coconutPinch of kosher salt

preparationSteps: Place chicken, ginger, garlic, lemongrass and salt in a large pot. Cover with chicken stock.
Bring pot to a boil over high heat. Cover and reduce to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes.

Remove the chicken to a holding plate. Stir rice, soy sauce and brown sugar into the pot. Cook at a simmer until rice is tender, about 20 additional minutes. While the rice is cooking, use two forks to shred the chicken.

Also while the rice is cooking, make the coconut-peanut topping. In a small skillet, warm the coconut oil over medium- high heat. Add the peanuts and stir until lightly browned. Add the coconut and a pinch of salt and continue stirring until golden-brown. Set aside to cool.

When the rice is tender, use a slotted spoon to fish out the ginger, garlic and lemongrass. Use the side of a chef’s knife to smash the garlic into a paste, and return it to the pot. Discard the ginger and lemongrass.

Stir the shredded chicken and lime juice into the soup. You can enjoy it immediately, or if you have time, cover the soup and refrigerate, and the rice will continue to absorb the liquid and the soup will thicken.
Enjoy the soup with a sprinkle of the coconut-peanut topping, scallions and a lime wedge.
NOTES:

name: rosemary garlic pork shoulder with sweet potato purée

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4- to 6-pound) bone-in pork shoulder blade roast(see notes if you can’t find this cut or if your pork is larger than 6 pounds)
ingredients.name: bone-in pork shoulder blade roast(see notes if you can’t find this cut or if your pork is larger than 6 pounds)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons minced fresh rosemary (from 1 large sprig)
ingredients.name: minced fresh rosemary (from 1 large sprig)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 very large sweet potato (or 2 small — you want about 2 pounds), peeled
ingredients.name: very large sweet potato (or 2 small — you want about 2 pounds)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley (curly or flat leaf)
ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh parsley (curly or flat leaf)

ingredients.name: of any vinegar other than balsamic

preparationSteps: Ideally you’ll rub the pork with the rosemary mixture up to 48 hours in advance, but absolutely no worries if you don’t have time. I didn’t and it’s still fab.
Preheat oven to 300°F.

Place the pork shoulder in a roasting pan or Dutch oven. If your pork butt has a really thick layer of fat, trim about half of it off — but not all of it! (If you trimmed off some fat, see notes for a way you can use it.)

Mince 6 garlic cloves and 2 tablespoons of rosemary and stir together in a bowl with 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, and 1 teaspoon black pepper. Rub this all over the pork. Pour 1 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken stock around the pork.
Peel 2 pounds sweet potatoes and slice into 1/2 inch-thick rounds (or cube them, whatever’s easier for you). Pile the sweet potatoes around the pork.

name: sriracha shrimp sushi bowls
note:
Make it ahead/leftovers are a great thing: Prepare and marinate the shrimp and cucumbers up to 24 hours in advance. Ideally, you’ll cook the rice and shrimp at go-time, but both will reheat well if you need to just knock all of the cooking out earlier in the day, or if end up with leftovers! To reheat the rice, place it in a bowl and stick an ice cube in the center of it. Cover the bowl loosely with parchment paper and reheat in the microwave in 45-second intervals until warmed through. Reheat the shrimp in the microwave in 10-second intervals until heated through.

Vegetarian: Just nix the shrimp and make it a cucumber avocado bowl night! Or add some edamame! Or tofu!

Save time: Cook the sushi rice as directed, if possible — it’s seriously so good. But you could also grab some microwavable rice if you’re tight on time.

Df/gf: Opt for oil over butter for df. Use coconut aminos instead of soy sauce for gf.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons sriracha (1 tablespoon if feeding spice-averse people)
ingredients.name: sriracha (1 tablespoon if feeding spice-averse people)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds peeled and deveined shrimp (preferably 21-25 per pound)
ingredients.name: peeled and deveined shrimp (preferably 21-25 per pound)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon olive oil or unsalted butter
ingredients.name: olive oil or unsalted butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 cups water (plus more for pre-rinsing the rice)
ingredients.name: water (plus more for pre-rinsing the rice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Sesame seeds (I used black and white but honestly, they don’t add a ton of flavor, they’re just to make things look bougie, so you can def skip this)
ingredients.name: Sesame seeds (I used black and white but honestly, they don’t add a ton of flavor, they’re just to make things look bougie, so you can def skip this)

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, combine 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1/4 cup honey, 3 tablespoons sriracha (less if feeding spice-averse people), and 3 tablespoons rice vinegar. Whisk until smooth.

Place 2 pounds peeled and deveined shrimp in a separate large bowl or ziploc. Cover with about 1/4 cup of the marinade and toss to coat. Marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. (FYI, save the rest of that marinade — you’ll use it as the sauce when compiling your bowls!)
When you’re 30 minutes out from dinnertime:

Start by rinsing and cooking the rice: Add 2 cups dry sushi rice to a large saucepan (or whatever you use to cook rice) and cover with water. Use your hand to slosh the water and rice around then carefully drain off the water. There’s no real technique here — just hold your hand over the pot so that the rice doesn’t fall into the drain along with the water. Repeat this process until the water is no longer murky.

Add 2 1/2 cups water to the saucepan and bring it to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and cover the pot for 15 to 17 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat, leave the lid on, and let the rice continue to steam for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, gently stir 3 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt into the rice.

Meanwhile, make the marinated cucumbers: Peel 1 English cucumber like a zebra (AKA make it look striped), cut it in half vertically and scoop out/discard the guts. Thinly slice and place in a Tupperware container (let’s make it easy for if you have leftovers!). Stir in 3 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Marinate at room temperature if eating right away, or marinate in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours.

Finally, let’s cook the shrimp! Warm a large skillet over medium-high heat for several minutes. Melt 1 tablespoon butter or oil. Pour off (and discard) as much of the marinade as possible, then add the shrimp to the skillet in an even layer. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until opaque all over. Serve immediately so they don’t overcook!

To build your bowls: Start with a layer of sushi rice then throw on piles of the shrimp, marinated cucumbers, diced avocado, and pickled ginger. If you’ve got ‘em, sprinkle sesame seeds over top. Pour your desired amount of sauce over top and GET IN THERE.

name: 10-Minute Pot de Creme

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces (1 1/2 cups) semisweet or dark chocolate chips
ingredients.name: semisweet or dark chocolate chips

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2/3 cup strong, VERY hot coffee (decaf is fine!) (You can also use coconut milk, milk, oat milk, almond milk etc - the consistency will be softer but still delicious!)
ingredients.name: strong, VERY hot coffee (decaf is fine!) (You can also use coconut milk, milk, oat milk, almond milk etc - the consistency will be softer but still delicious!)

preparationSteps: Blend 8 ounces (about 1 ¼ cups) chocolate, 4 large eggs, 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, and a pinch of kosher salt until coarsely combined.
With the motor on low speed, slowly pour in 2/3 cup very hot coffee. Blend until smooth.
Taste. Do you want it to be sweeter? If so, blend in 1 or 2 tablespoons sugar.
Pour into 4 to 6 small bowls/ramekins and refrigerate to set for at least 1 hour.
Serve with a dollop of creme fraîche or whipped cream and chocolate shavings or chopped chocolate.

name: beef enchilada bake

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large red bell pepper, finely chopped
ingredients.name: large red bell pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 big handfuls of spinach or kale
ingredients.name: big handfuls of spinach or kale

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 corn tortillas (ideally 6- to 8-inch — but any diameter size works. I actually used Siete brand almond tortillas!)
ingredients.name: corn tortillas (ideally 6- to 8-inch — but any diameter size works. I actually used Siete brand almond tortillas!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packed cup grated/shredded Cheddar or Mexican cheese
ingredients.name: packed cup grated/shredded Cheddar or Mexican cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings: sour cream (or Greek yogurt for more superfood goodness!), avocado slices (another superfood!),pickled red onions,salsa, hot sauce, lime wedges, cilantro, etc.!
ingredients.name: Optional toppings: sour cream (or Greek yogurt for more superfood goodness!), avocado slices (another superfood!),pickled red onions,salsa, hot sauce, lime wedges, cilantro, etc.!

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Finely chop 1 medium yellow onion and 1 red bell pepper. Mince 4 garlic cloves.

Warm a 12-inch ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, all of the chopped veggies and garlic, 1 pound ground beef, 1 pound cauliflower rice, 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons taco seasoning, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt to the skillet and cook, breaking the beef into tiny crumbles, until the beef is cooked through and the veggies are tender, 5 to 6 minutes.

Meanwhile, chop 2 big handfuls of spinach and kale. If you have kids and are trying to hide the greens from them, chop them VERY, VERY FINELY and all of the spices and tomatoes and beef *should* be hide the green!

Taste the cooked beef mixture and add more seasoning as needed until it’s absolutely delicious. Stir in 1 tablespoon flour, then, once it’s totally absorbed, stir in a 28-ounce can of diced tomatoes and the chopped greens until the greens wilt and the mixture thickens and is no longer liquidy. You shouldn’t need to drain any fat/liquid, just crank up the heat if there’s a lot in there and keep stirring until it’s gone. Turn off the heat.

Char 6 corn tortillas one by one by placing them right on top of the gas flame of your stove. If you don’t have a gas burner, you can skip this step or toast them up in a dry skillet over medium-high heat.

Smoosh the tortillas into the meat and veggies. There’s no grace to this, just move the mixture around so that you can imperfectly layer the tortillas in there, making sure there’s a bit of the mixture between each tortilla. Top with 1 cup grated cheese.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese is browned and the mixture is bubbling.
Let it cool, then scoop it onto plates and serve with desired toppings!

name: summery pork and peach bowls
note:
Why don’t I need to rinse my rice? When you’re cooking a rice dish where you want every single grain to be separate and not stick together, like a rice pilaf, you want to rinse your rice until it runs clear. You’re rinsing off all of the starch that will make it sticky. But here, we are going for a sticky, starchy vibe. That’s what makes it so delicious. So keep the starch!

Leftovers are a good thing: Double the coconut rice and use the leftover rice and cucumbers to easily make sriracha shrimp sushi bowls in a couple nights!

I could use a drink: Use the leftover pineapple orange juice for margaritas! Specifically: Juice of 2 limes, 2 tablespoons pineapple OJ, 1/4 cup tequila. And if you have leftovers of any meal component, check the links above for the original recipe I wrote it for and add that to your meal plan for the coming days.

I’m feeding toddlers: Serve this meal all in separate piles — chopped up pork (I have to call it chicken to get Mattis to eat it…), coconut rice, peaches, cucumbers (mine don’t like them pickled so I save some plain for them), peanut sauce for dipping. This is actually one of my 3 year old’s most reliable meals. My kids LOVE coconut rice.

Vegetarian: Options! You can swap the pork tenderloin out for grilled veggies. Chop some summery vegetables (mushrooms, zucchini, squash, bell peppers, red onion, etc.) into 1-inch pieces, marinate them (for as long as you want), then cook them kebab-style on the grill. If you don’t have a grill, you can broil them on the top rack on high to achieve a similar effect. You could also grill (or pan fry) extra-firm tofu! Just be sure to press it between clean towels to remove excess moisture before you mix it with the marinade. Tofu sticks to the grill easily, so, after you shake off the marinade, coat it with a light layer of oil.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: It’s already df! For gf, swap the soy sauce for coconut aminos.

Prep ahead: Part of what makes this such a perfect meal for company is that its various elements are so very prep ahead-able. You can make the pickled cucumbers and peanut sauce days ahead if ya want and store them in the fridge. I highly encourage marinating the meat for up to 24 hours, and even the coconut rice can be made ahead of time and reheated on the stove (though you can easily cook that while the grill is preheating and the pork is cooking!). Aside from grilling, all you have left to do is to chop the herbs, slice the peaches, and serve!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 or 2 pork tenderloins (not loins! totally different cut of meat!)
ingredients.name: pork tenderloins (not loins! totally different cut of meat!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup pineapple-orange juice (plain OJ works too, but pineapple actually does tenderize the meat!)
