ingredients.name: pineapple-orange juice (plain OJ works too, but pineapple actually does tenderize the meat!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 grated garlic cloves or 1 teaspoon garlic powder
ingredients.name: grated garlic cloves or 1 teaspoon garlic powder

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon lemon pepper (or 1/2 teaspoon regular pepper plus the zest of one lemon)
ingredients.name: lemon pepper (or 1/2 teaspoon regular pepper plus the zest of one lemon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 1 tablespoon fresh grated ginger or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
ingredients.name: Optional: 1 tablespoon fresh grated ginger or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups sticky/sushi rice (or any white rice)
ingredients.name: sticky/sushi rice (or any white rice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha or sambal oelek
ingredients.name: sriracha or sambal oelek

ingredients.rawIngredient: Chopped fresh green herbs, such as basil or cilantro
ingredients.name: Chopped fresh green herbs, such as basil or cilantro

preparationSteps: Marinate the pork for at least 30 minutes at room temperature or up to 24 hours in the refrigerator. Place the pork tenderloin(s), 1 cup pineapple OJ, 1/3 cup soy sauce, 3 grated garlic cloves (or 1 teaspoon garlic powder), and 1/2 teaspoon lemon pepper in a bowl. If you have some ginger, add 1 tablespoon fresh grated ginger or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger.

Do a really quick pickle on those cucumbers by peeling 1 English cucumber like a zebra (aka peeling off half the skin, in stripes), then cutting it into batons. Throw everything in a storage container (because you’ll probably have leftovers), then add 1/3 cup rice vinegar and 1 tablespoon white sugar. Cover the rest of the way with water. Stir to coat.

Now let’s get the coconut rice going. Combine 1 1/2 cups white rice (no, you don’t need to rinse it), 1 (14-ounce) can coconut milk, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon white sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to the lowest heat possible on your stovetop, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and leave covered to allow the rice to steam until you’re ready to eat (at least 5 minutes).

Peanut sauce time! In a jar (or you can stir in a bowl), shake together 1/3 cup smooth peanut butter, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha or sambal oelek (my kids can handle 1 tablespoon), and 2 tablespoons warm water until smooth. Add more water as needed until you achieve a nice drizzle-able consistency.
Final step — cook the pork tenderloin!
To grill it: Preheat the grill to medium-high (450°F).

Shake off the marinade and add the tenderloin to the grill. Cook, rotating it every 3 minutes, until it reaches 140°F internally, 12 to 15 minutes total. Let it rest for 10 minutes before thinly slicing. If you are not going to let it rest for a full 10 minutes, cook the meat until it reaches 145°F.
To roast it in the oven: Preheat your oven to 425°F.

Shake off the marinade, pat it completely dry, and place it on a roasting pan. Rub a light coat of oil (any kind) all over the pork. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until it reaches 140°F internally. Let it rest for 10 minutes before thinly slicing. If you are not going to let it rest for a full 10 minutes, cook the meat until it reaches 145°F.

If you haven’t already, slice 2 large peaches, chop a lot of fresh herbs (I love cilantro and/or basil for this), and grab a big handful of roasted, salted peanuts for garnish. I like to set everything out on the table, family style, and let everyone build their own bowls!

name: roasted red pepper and butternut squash soup

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of garlic, kept whole with top cut off
ingredients.name: of garlic, kept whole with top cut off

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 red bell peppers, deseeded and chopped into large pieces
ingredients.name: red bell peppers, deseeded and chopped into large pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large yellow onion, peeled and chopped into large pieces
ingredients.name: large yellow onion
ingredients.note: peeled and chopped into large pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (8 ounces) butternut squash cubes(Try to find pre-cut to make it easy! If you can’t find pre-cut, buy 1 small butternut squash and see recipe for how to cube. Frozen cubes are perfect here!)
ingredients.name: butternut squash cubes(Try to find pre-cut to make it easy! If you can’t find pre-cut, buy 1 small butternut squash and see recipe for how to cube. Frozen cubes are perfect here!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 to 5 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, depending on spice preference (if you don’t want the soup to be spicy at all, omit this altogether!)
ingredients.name: crushed red pepper flakes, depending on spice preference (if you don’t want the soup to be spicy at all, omit this altogether!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 slices of a good loaf of bread (any type — country levain, sourdough, ciabatta, etc.)
ingredients.name: of a good loaf of bread (any type — country levain, sourdough, ciabatta, etc.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves, plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Line a sheet pan with parchment paper. Cut the top off of 1 head of garlic, keeping the skin on and the bulb intact. Place the garlic bulb cut-side down on the sheet pan.

Deseed and chop 2 red bell peppers (click here for a demo, if needed!) and peel and chop 1 yellow onion into large pieces. Add them to the sheet pan, along with 1 cup butternut squash cubes. If you couldn’t find pre-cubed butternut squash, cut a butternut squash in half, deseed it, peel it (or just cut off the skin) and cube enough to fill a cup.

To the sheet pan, add 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes (1/4 teaspoon will add some mild heat to the soup; 1/2 teaspoon will make it spicy; omit it if you’re feeding people averse to any spice!), 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon thyme leaves, and salt and pepper to taste. Use your hands to coat all the veggies and the garlic bulb thoroughly with the EVOO and spices.
Roast for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, cube 4 slices of bread. After the veggies have roasted for 20 minutes, take the sheet pan out of the oven, scooch the veggies over a little, and add the cubed bread to one side of the sheet pan. Toss the bread with 1 to 2 tablespoons EVOO. Return the baking sheet to the oven and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until the veggies are soft and starting to caramelize and the croutons are toasty.
Remove the sheet pan from the oven and let the veggies cool slightly, until the garlic bulb is cool enough to handle. Remove the croutons, setting them aside until you serve the soup.

Squeeze half of the roasted garlic into a blender (you’ll literally just squeeze the bulb and the roasted garlic will slide right out! Use your fingers to keep little pieces of the  garlic skin from going with it). Reserve the other half of the roasted garlic for another use.
Add the other veggies to the blender along with 1 cup of vegetable broth. Blend until smooth.

Place the blended soup in a saucepan over medium heat. Thin it out with up to 1 cup of broth, using however much broth it takes for the soup to reach a consistency that you love. Once the soup is heated through, remove the saucepan from heat and stir in 1/4 cup sour cream. Taste! If it’s not absolutely delicious, add more salt a 1/4 teaspoon at a time until it is.
Serve topped with crispy croutons, crumbled feta, a drizzle of EVOO, and a few thyme leaves. DIG IN!
servings: Serves 2-4 (more detail on this in the notes section below the recipe!)

name: skillet cheddar turkey burgers
note:
Make meatballs instead: Form the turkey mixture into 12 to 15 meatballs — they should be about 1 1/2 inches in diameter each (a little bigger than a ping pong ball) — and place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet, at least 1 inch apart. Bake for 10 minutes, until cooked through and a meat thermometer inserted into the center of the meatballs reads 165°F. Serve them alongside the iceberg salad and burger sauce for dipping!

Make sliders instead: Form the turkey mixture into 12 slider-sized patties, about 1/2 inch thick, and cook them as directed in a nonstick skillet, just 2 to 3 minutes per side, since they’re smaller and will cook faster. Divide them among slider buns with all the fixings!

Love your leftovers: Crumble leftover cooked patties into salads or tuck them  (and the fixings) inside split pita bread spread with burger sauce for lunch. Any leftover sauce can be used as a dressing for just about any green salad as well as pasta or potato salad, as a dipping sauce for veggies and fries, or as a sandwich spread.

I need a side other than chips: Ok, ok. Try one of these: Antipasto Pasta Salad, Sesame-Scallion Slaw, Marinated Vegetables with Burrata, Grilled Summer Squash and Zucchini with Charred Scallion and Cotija Salsa.

Prep ahead: The burger sauce can be made up to a week in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator. The burger patties can be shaped and frozen on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Once frozen solid, transfer to a zip-top freezer bag or airtight container and freeze for up to a couple of months. Let them thaw in the refrigerator overnight before cooking.

Spice averse: Leave out the hot sauce in the burger sauce and use a mild chili powder. Or swap the chili powder out with a combination of equal parts sweet paprika and ground cumin.

Vegetarian: Swap the turkey burger patties out for your favorite veggie burger patties, roasted or grilled portobello mushrooms caps, or thick rounds of roasted or grilled eggplant.

Gluten-free: Use gluten-free burger buns.

Dairy-free: Reach for vegan shredded cheddar or Colby cheese.

Toppings: Not feeling sliced tomato and red onion? Try smashed avocado (or guacamole!), sliced roasted red peppers, pickle chips, or if you’re craving even more heat, pickled jalapeños. Really, just about any favorite burger topping works here.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): thinly sliced tomato, thinly sliced red onion
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): thinly sliced tomato, thinly sliced red onion

preparationSteps: Prep the burgers: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl, combine 1 pound ground turkey, 1/2 cup shredded white cheddar cheese, 1/4 cup mayonnaise, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon chili powder, and 3/4 teaspoon salt.
Thinly slice 4 scallions and add them to the turkey mixture. Use your hands to mix well, then divide the meat into four thin patties, about 1/2 inch thick.

Make the burger sauce/salad dressing: In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons hot sauce, and a pinch of salt. Cut 1 lime in half and squeeze in the juice; stir to combine. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Thinly slice 1 head iceberg lettuce and place it in a large serving bowl.

Cook the burgers: Warm your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. When you flick a drop of water into it and it dances around the pan, it’s hot enough. Add 1 tablespoon neutral oil to the pan and swirl to coat the pan evenly. Cook as many patties at a time as you can without having them touch, for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden brown all over.
When you flip the burgers, throw the 4 burger buns on a baking sheet and place them in the oven to warm them up for the final 4 to 5 minutes.

Spread the burger sauce on both sides of the bun, then add a patty to each, along with your desired toppings, including chips, if you’re into that. Throw 1/4 cup of the burger sauce and a big pinch of salt into the iceberg and toss to dress it. Serve the burgers with the iceberg (and more chips, if you like) alongside.
(You can grill your burgers if you prefer. Cook them on medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side. Throw some veggies on there while you’re at it!)

name: cheesy cranberry turkey melt sliders
note:
I have everything but Hawaiian rolls: If you have leftover Parker House rolls, those would be great here in place of the King’s Hawaiian rolls! Any roll works, really, but the sheet-like aspect of King’s Hawaiian makes assembly a breeze. You could also make sandwiches! Just skip the honey butter, and instead smear butter on the outsides of the bread and toast in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.

Prep ahead: Shred the turkey ahead of time — it’s actually easiest to shred while it’s still warm/room temp. You could go ahead and make the cranberry mayo the night before too. Don’t assemble the sandwiches ahead of time though because the bread would get soggy.

It’s not the holiday season: If you’re making these sometime in the future when you don’t have an abundance of Thanksgiving leftovers in your fridge, you can swap raspberry jam in for the cranberry sauce, and use sliced deli turkey or ham (about 12 thick slices) or shredded chicken instead of shredded turkey. If you’re using sliced deli meat instead of shredded turkey or chicken, skip the step when you mix the meat in with the cranberry mayo. Instead, just spread the bottom layer of rolls with 1/3 cup mayonnaise followed by 3 tablespoons cranberry sauce or jam.

Can I put other leftovers on these sliders? Sure! They’re perfect as is but if you want to experiment, I think a thin layer of mashed potatoes or stuffing spread on top of the turkey layer would be fab.

Vegetarian: You could apply this slider method to any Thanksgiving leftovers. Roasted veggies or stuffing spread out onto Kings Hawaiian rolls with the cranberry mayo, mustard, cheese, and honey butter would be delicious, I’m sure!

Dairy-free: Use DF cheese (or omit it) and plant-based butter

Gluten-free: Use any gluten-free sandwich bread or slider buns or rolls you can find. See the “I have everything but the Hawaiian rolls” note above for how to make these using sandwich bread instead of rolls.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 package (12-count) King’s Hawaiian Original Hawaiian Sweet Dinner Rolls
ingredients.name: King’s Hawaiian Original Hawaiian Sweet Dinner Rolls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded roasted turkey meat (or 12 thick slices of deli turkey)
ingredients.name: shredded roasted turkey meat (or 12 thick slices of deli turkey)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon whole grain mustard, divided (or 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon Dijon)
ingredients.name: plus 1 teaspoon whole grain mustard, divided (or 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon Dijon)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, stir 1/2 cup mayonnaise and 1/4 cup cranberry sauce together.

Keeping the buns attached to one another, use a long serrated knife to slice a pack of 12 Hawaiian rolls in half horizontally (so you’ll end up with one large bottom half and one large top half). Place the bottom half of the buns on the baking sheet. Spread a nice layer of cranberry mayonnaise on the cut side of the bottom layer of the buns.
Add 2 cups shredded turkey meat to the remaining cranberry mayonnaise and stir to combine. If it’s too mayo-y for you, add more turkey, this will really depend on how dry your turkey is.

Now start layering the sliders! On top of the mayo layer, add a layer of Havarti cheese, then all of the turkey, then a layer of Provolone. Spread the cut side of the top buns with 2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard and place the top bun on top.
Melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter in a small bowl in the microwave. Stir in 2 teaspoons honey and 1 teaspoon whole-grain mustard.

Pour the honey butter over the tops and sides of the buns until they’re all coated. If you have a pastry brush, use it to make sure the butter spreads evenly. If you don’t have a pastry brush, use your fingers! Sprinkle 1 tablespoon Everything Bagel seasoning evenly across the tops of the buns.

Place the sheet pan in the oven and bake until the buns are golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Set a timer and don’t overcook them! It’s very sad when the buns get too hard! Slice into individual sliders and serve.

name: roasted butternut squash soup

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 heads of garlic (AKA 2 whole bulbs of it — not 2 individual cloves)
ingredients.name: of garlic (AKA 2 whole bulbs of it — not 2 individual cloves)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 quart (AKA 4 cups) of chicken bone broth, divided
ingredients.name: (AKA 4 cups) of chicken bone broth

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup cottage cheese (any kind, but I likedouble cream Good Culturebest)
ingredients.name: cottage cheese (any kind, but I likedouble cream Good Culturebest)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon any vinegar (I like balsamic or apple cider)
ingredients.name: any vinegar (I like balsamic or apple cider)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Completely optional: sexy garnishes like a swirl of chili oil, chili crisp, pepitas…
ingredients.name: Completely optional: sexy garnishes like a swirl of chili oil, chili crisp, pepitas…

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Cut the stem end off of the top of 1 butternut squash, then stand it up on its root end to more easily cut it in half vertically. Use a spoon to scoop the seeds out. Cut the tippy top end off of 2 heads of garlic to expose the tops of the cloves and place them on a large square of foil.

Place the squash on a baking sheet and drizzle/rub all over with extra-virgin olive oil (no need to measure here — just use enough to coat it well!). Place it cut-side down on the baking sheet (so you should only be able to see the skin!). Drizzle and rub the  garlic heads all over with EVOO too, place them cut-side down, then close the tin foil, making a pouch for the garlic. Add the foil pouch to the sheet pan.

Roast for 45 minutes. Using tongs, transfer the garlic to a small plate. Carefully open the pouch and see if the garlic is nice and squishy. If it is, it’s ready! Just keep it on the plate to cool. If it’s not, close the pouch and add it back to the baking sheet.
Continue roasting the squash (and potentially the garlic) for another 30 minutes or until very, very squishy when you poke the skin.
Flip the squash over and let it cool for 20 minutes.

If you own an immersion blender, scrape the squash flesh out of the skins and into a large pot, and squeeze the squishy cloves of 1 whole roasted garlic head in. Add 3 cups of bone broth, 1 cup cottage cheese, 1 teaspoon of any vinegar, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and several cranks of freshly ground black pepper. Blend until smooth!

If you are using a standard blender, blend the soup in batches as it’ll be too much to fit at once. It doesn’t matter what ingredients get blended with what as long as it’s all smooth. As they’re ready, transfer the blended batches to a large pot then stir well to combine.

Now, you’re going to taste and adjust to make it perfect for you! You can blend in as much of the second head of roasted garlic as you like! I added the whole thing, but some people prefer less, so taste and add it a clove or two at a time until it’s perfect. You can also add up to 1 more cup of bone broth (and if you need even more: Better Than Bouillon + water!) as needed until you reach your desired consistency. Some people like it really thick, others like it more thin like a broth, do your thing! Taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Keep the soup warm over low heat and enjoy with your biscuits! Top your bowls with a sprinkle of pepitas and chili crisp and/or a swirl of chili oil, if using.

name: ham and cheese biscuits
note:
Jazz up your soup: (from the start, or jazz up the leftovers by adding a smaller amount of these ingredients)Curried Butternut Squash Soup: Blend in 1 can coconut milk, 2 tablespoons red curry paste (to start since spice levels vary), 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, and the juice of 1 lime. Miso-Ginger Butternut Squash Soup: Blend in a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger (no need to peel) and 2 tablespoons miso (I like white miso). What else? Leave your ideas!Leave a comment

Curried Butternut Squash Soup: Blend in 1 can coconut milk, 2 tablespoons red curry paste (to start since spice levels vary), 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, and the juice of 1 lime.

Miso-Ginger Butternut Squash Soup: Blend in a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger (no need to peel) and 2 tablespoons miso (I like white miso).

What else? Leave your ideas!Leave a comment

I have leftover roasted garlic: If you didn’t add the whole second head of garlic, spread your leftovers onto bread and make it into a grilled cheese! Or add it to a homemade salad dressing. Or eat it plain to boost your immune system.

I wish it were sweeter: This is sweet enough for my taste but feel free to blend in a teaspoon or two (or more to taste!) of honey or maple syrup if you’d like!

Make ahead: Like I said in the headnote, this is a great meal to make days before you plan to eat it! You can store the soup in the fridge in the pot you blended it in with the lid on for up to 2 days — or up to 4 days in an airtight container. Store the biscuits for up to 2 days in the fridge in an airtight container. Reheat the soup over low on the stovetop (add a splash more broth or stock if it’s thicker than you want after sitting in the fridge!), and heat the biscuits in a 400°F oven for 5 minutes.

Double it/freezer-friendly: Double this whole meal and freeze half of it!! It doubles perfectly. Once it has fully cooled, pour leftover soup into Ziploc bags, lay them flat on a baking sheet, and put the baking sheet in the freezer. Once they’re frozen, you’ll have flat bags of soup easy to store in the freezer for a day up to 3 months from now.. Thaw in the fridge overnight then reheat, following the instructions above in the “make ahead” note.

No, I so sorry, you cannot prep the biscuit dough the night before: The baking powder will deactivate and they’ll be flat. You could make it up until the step when you stir in the milk though!

If you think of it… pop your butter in the freezer for a few minutes before you grate it. But that’s not necessary — using it fresh out of the fridge will be fine.

If you have… carrots, a bell pepper, or some celery in the crisper that need to be used, throw them on the baking sheet and roast them up with the squash and garlic. Blend them right in!

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. Make the soup. It’s easy, promise! If making biscuits feels like too much for tonight… just toast a slice of yummy cheese on bread and dip it while you eat! Or throw some croutons in the bowl!

Vegetarian: Use veggie stock instead of bone broth and omit the ham from the biscuits.

Dairy free: Good Culture makes a lactose-free cottage cheese, if that’d help. Or to omit it from the soup altogether: soak 1/2 cup cashews (any kind) in the stock while the squash roasts then blend them in with the soup for that creaminess and extra protein. You may need to use a high-powered standing blender in lieu of the immersion blender if you’re blending nuts. One other option: blend in a can of drained, rinsed white beans (like cannellini or navy) instead of the cottage cheese. For the biscuits, use a DF stick of butter and a plant-based milk alternative like unsweetened almond or soy milk.

Gluten-free: Use a gluten-free 1 to 1 baking flour.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons very cold butter (so straight from the fridge)
ingredients.name: very cold butter (so straight from the fridge)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces Gruyère (or white cheddar or literally any hard cheese)
ingredients.name: Gruyère (or white cheddar or literally any hard cheese)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup finely chopped ham (any kind! country, deli, honey-baked!)
ingredients.name: finely chopped ham (any kind! country, deli, honey-baked!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup milk plus more for brushing the biscuits
ingredients.name: milk plus more for brushing the biscuits

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together 1 cup flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper. Grate 4 tablespoons cold butter and 4 ounces Gruyère on the largest hole of a box grater and toss to combine with the flour. Use your fingers to pinch the butter and cheese into the flour a bit (spend about 15 seconds pinching)
Stir in 1 cup finely chopped ham. Then stir in 1/2 cup milk until you have a rough, shaggy looking dough.
You can either simply scoop the dough in heaping spoonfuls onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, or you can laminate the dough, which is a fancy word for how to make flaky, layered biscuits.

To do so: Plop all of the dough down onto the parchment-lined baking sheet. Sprinkle with flour. Use your hands to smoosh the dough down into a rough rectangle. Fold it over itself to make a square. Repeat this process 3 times, ending by smooshing the dough into a 1-inch tall square or rectangle (watch the video I shared above the recipes for a visual of this!).

Cut the dough into 8 square biscuits. Separate and spread them out on the baking sheet. Brush the tops with milk (if you don’t have a pastry brush, just dab a paper towel into milk and pat it on top). Optional but delicious: Grind a little more pepper on top of your biscuits. Maybe sprinkle some freshly grated Parm or a little leftover grated Gruyère on top too if you want to go for it?!

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden brown and puffed up. Enjoy immediately! (Or, if you’re baking these ahead of time, only bake them for 12 minutes, then store in the fridge and reheat in a 400°F oven for 5 minutes when you’re ready to eat!)

name: honey chipotle salmon tacos
note:
Supermarket shortcuts: Simply marinate the salmon in some good hot sauce and honey. Buy a store-bought pico de gallo and add in chopped mango. Buy store-bought guac to use as a topping. One extra time-saving idea: Skip charring your tortillas and microwave them instead. Wrap the entire stack of tortillas in dampened paper towels and microwave for 45 seconds.

Prep ahead: If you’re looking to prep ahead, you can prepare the marinade in a jar up to 3 days in advance and store it in the fridge. Whenever you’re ready to make this recipe, cube the salmon, coat it in the marinade (be sure to give the jar a shake first to reincorporate the oil), and roast right away — no need to marinate the salmon ahead of time. To prep the pico de gallo in advance: chop the mango, shallot, and jalapeño up to 2 days ahead of time and store them in an airtight container in the fridge. Whenever you’re ready to cook, add them to the mixing bowl along with the other ingredients.

Leftovers are a good thing: Transfer your leftover chipotle peppers en adobo to a small airtight container — they will be good in the fridge for months! You can use them for these chipotle black bean flautas or these 3-ingredient chorizo street tacos. If you have leftover salmon or mango pico de gallo, both will keep in the fridge for days stored in separate airtight containers. Throw them over cooked rice for a super quick and delicious burrito bowl lunch this week!

Vegetarian/vegan: Try cubed firm tofu or chickpeas instead of salmon. For tofu: press the cubed tofu between dry paper towels or dish cloths and under a heavy weight for a few minutes before you mix it with the marinade (this helps take some of the liquid out). You can either skewer and roast the tofu like the salmon or roast it straight on a sheet pan. For chickpeas: drain and rinse a can of them and pat them dry. Coat the chickpeas in the marinade then spread them out in a single layer on a parchment-lined sheet pan. Both chickpeas and tofu should bake for 20-30 minutes at 400°F, or until crispy.

Skewers: You can use metal or bamboo skewers for this. If you have time, soak your bamboo skewers for 30 minutes before you thread the salmon onto them to help keep them from charring (but no worries if you don’t). If you don’t have skewers, just roast the salmon cubes on a parchment-lined sheet pan, flipping once halfway through cooking.

Gluten-free/dairy-free: Use corn tortillas or another gluten-free alternative if avoiding gluten. Avoid topping your tacos with cheese if you’re dairy-free.

Gimme a side: If you want a side dish with your tacos, try this one-pot cheesy rice and bean situation!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 thick salmon fillets, skin removed, cut into 1-inch (2.5-cm) cubes
ingredients.name: thick salmon fillets, skin removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons any vinegar, or lemon or lime juice
ingredients.name: any vinegar, or lemon or lime juice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 to 5 canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce (seeds removed if you are spice averse)
ingredients.name: canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce (seeds removed if you are spice averse)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 jalapeños, finely chopped (remove the seeds if you don’t like things spicy!)
ingredients.name: jalapeños, finely chopped (remove the seeds if you don’t like things spicy!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: The juice and zest of 1 lime, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: The juice and zest of 1 lime, plus more to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 tortillas, for serving (either corn or flour, whichever type and size you like best)
ingredients.name: tortillas, for serving (either corn or flour, whichever type and size you like best)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: Guacamole, sour cream, feta, etc.
ingredients.name: Optional: Guacamole, sour cream, feta, etc.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Any other toppings of choice, but keep it simple!
ingredients.name: Any other toppings of choice, but keep it simple!

preparationSteps: Heat the oven to 400°F (205°C).

If you haven’t already, remove the skin from 3 thick salmon fillets and cut them into 1-inch cubes. Combine all marinade ingredients (1/2 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon cayenne, 2 teaspoons roughly crushed whole coriander, 3 minced garlic cloves, 2 teaspoons any vinegar, 2 tablespoons honey, 3 to 5 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce — seeds removed if you are spice averse — a big pinch of salt, and 3 to 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil) in a blender, food processor, or mortar and pestle. Crush or pulse until smooth. Coat the salmon in marinade. Thread the salmon cubes onto skewers.

Line a deep baking dish (such as an 8x8-inch) with parchment paper. Rest the ends of the skewers on the rim of the baking dish, so the salmon remains suspended. Roast for 12 to 13 minutes. After that, broil on high for 1 to 2 minutes, until the salmon is slightly charred. (If you’re using a sheet pan: roast the skewers for 6 minutes, flip your skewers and roast for another 6 or 7 minutes before broiling.)
servings: Serves 2 to 3 on its own, or 4 with a side dish

name: 5-ingredient eggplant parm
note:
But I thought you taught us not to use EVOO above 375°F? Yes — but the eggplant totally absorbs it, as opposed to the oil sitting on the outside of the vegetables, so it works here!

Make ahead: You can go ahead and assemble the eggplant Parm in advance. To do so, prep the eggplant then roast it for 20 minutes. Top it with marinara and cheese then refrigerate it until you’re ready to eat. Bake it for 15 minutes, garnish with the crushed crisps and herbs (if using), and dig in.

I hate eggplant: Are you sure you hate eggplant?! If you’re just skeptical, give it a try. It’s truly delicious. If you do indeed know you hate eggplant, try it with portobello mushrooms caps instead.

Must have meat: Make a super-simple chicken Parm, again sans the breadcrumbs and frying steps, using chicken breasts. Cook for 10 minutes, then add the sauce and cheese and keep cooking until the internal temp hits 165°F.

Leftovers are a good thing: These aren’t going to freeze well, so enjoy them for lunches over the next few days. You can totally use the microwave to reheat.

Gluten-free: Opt for the Parm crisps over croutons as they’re gluten-free.

Dairy-free: Use your favorite melty vegan cheese and skip the Parm. My friend made this with the vegan gouda from Whole Foods and loved it.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup jarred marinara sauce (absolutely any tomato sauce works — a vodka sauce would be damn good; Rao’s is my favorite brand)
ingredients.name: jarred marinara sauce (absolutely any tomato sauce works — a vodka sauce would be damn good; Rao’s is my favorite brand)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: Cheese crisps such asWhispsor Trader Joe’s “Oven Baked Cheese Bites” (AKA crackers made from 100% Parmesan cheese) OR your favorite croutons
ingredients.name: Optional: Cheese crisps such asWhispsor Trader Joe’s “Oven Baked Cheese Bites” (AKA crackers made from 100% Parmesan cheese) OR your favorite croutons

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley or basil
ingredients.name: Optional: 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley or basil

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Cut the top off of the eggplant. Place eggplant on the cutting board so that the flat, cut side is down. Cut eggplant into 1/2-inch thick planks (it should make 5 to 7 ovals). Lay the planks on a dish towel and coat both sides with salt. Let the eggplant hang out there for 15 to 20 minutes (or longer if need be; were drawing the moisture out). It might turn a bit brown but it doesn’t matter — you’re about to smother it in cheese.

Use another towel to wipe away all excess moisture and salt. Transfer the eggplant to the parchment-lined baking sheet and coat all sides with a thin layer of extra-virgin olive oil (2 to 3 tablespoons worth). Lay the eggplant planks flat, so that they’re not overlapping.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Spoon jarred marinara sauce over each eggplant slice. Cover with however much Havarti and Parmesan you damn well please.
Roast for 10 more minutes, or until the cheese is totally melted.

Garnish with crushed up cheese crackers or croutons and finely chopped parsley or basil. Serve immediately over a bed of baby arugula or spinach, and/or alongside cooked noodles tossed in leftover marinara.

name: cheesy shells alla sausage vodka
note:
Need some greens? Kale is the answer. Strip the ribs out of two bunches of kale, chop it up finely, and wash it. Add it to the pot two minutes after you add the sausage.

Dairy-free? Use (canned) coconut milk instead. Use VioLife or another Parmesan alternative, and your favorite melty dairy-free cheese on top in place of the mozzarella.

Gluten-free? I developed a zoodles alla vodka recipe for Mealthy when I worked there, and it was DELISH.

Booze a problem? Skip the vodka. Totally fine to just omit it.

Don’t want to make a massive pasta dish? Just toss as much pasta as you want with as much sausage ragu as you want. Dig in.

Freeze leftover ragu by allowing it to cool completely, then freezing in quart ziplocs.

You can assemble this dish entirely ahead of time, then bake it up to three days later. After you sprinkle the mozzarella on top, let the dish cool completely, then refrigerate. When you’re ready to eat, bake at 350°F for 30 minutes covered, then 5 minutes uncovered.

Vegetarian? Omit the sausage! Will be totally fine without it.

Chicken sausage (the raw kind in a tube, not the pre-cooked links) is a great sub for the pork sausage.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, minced (or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary)
ingredients.name: fresh rosemary, minced (or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary)

preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large ovenproof heavy bottomed pan or pot (such as a Dutch oven, braiser, or any stainless steel pot) over medium-high heat. Sauté 1 large, finely diced onion until translucent, then add in 6 minced garlic cloves, the zest of 1 lemon, 1 tablespoon minced rosemary, and 2 teaspoons dried oregano and cook for 1 more minute.
Add 1 pound of Italian sausage meat and cook until no longer pink, breaking it up with a spoon into tiny crumbles - we don’t want any big chunks!

Deglaze the pan with 1/2 cup vodka (yes - vodka! don’t worry, your pasta isn’t going to taste like vodka!) for about 1 minute. What the hell does deglaze mean? Basically, just pour in the vodka and use that liquid to scrape the bottom of the pot and get any bits that are stuck to the pan unstuck - aka, “deglazed”. It’ll sizzle and a lot of the vodka will “burn off” aka evaporate. The booziness evaporates quickly (alcohol evaporates faster than water!), so yes, you can serve this to your kids.

Stir in one 28-ounce can of whole peeled tomatoes and one 14-ounce can tomato sauce, crushing each tomato with your hands before you add it to the pot. Add 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1 tablespoon sugar and simmer the sauce over medium heat until thickened and no longer watery, about 30 minutes.

Season to taste with salt and red pepper flakes (if desired). I can’t tell ya exactly how much salt to use because that’ll depend on what sausage and tomatoes you use! But I bet it’ll be about 1 teaspoon. Keep tasting and seasoning until it’s perfect.
Remove sauce from heat.

Meanwhile, cook 12 ounces of jumbo shells until al dente. Quickly drain in a colander, but throw it into the pasta sauce before all of the pasta water drains off of it. Never, ever, ever rinse this (or any!) pasta. The starch on the noodles helps thicken the sauce and make it silky, and helps the sauce stick to the noodles!

Stir the shells and 1/2 cup grated Parmesan into the sauce, taking care to peel apart any shells that have gotten stuck together, and to fill each shell with sauce. Smooth the pasta into an even layer, then sprinkle 1 1/2 cups mozzarella cheese over top.
Now we need to melt that cheese, so cover the pot with a lid, and place the pot over medium-low heat. Cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted.
Serve with more Parm and fresh basil.

name: sticky honey-ginger salmon and snap peas
note:
Prep ahead: You can cut your snap peas and salmon into 1-inch pieces up to a day ahead of time. Store them in separate airtight containers in the fridge. You can also make the brown butter scallion rice up to 3 days ahead of time! Let it cool completely then store it in an airtight container in the fridge. When you reheat the rice (either in a pot on the stovetop or in the microwave) add a tablespoon or 2 of water to prevent it from drying out.

Can I use microwavable frozen rice? Always! If you have time, brown the butter and cook the scallions and garlic in the pot, then add the microwaved rice. Or just serve the saucy sticky salmon and snap peas over plain microwaved rice, it’ll still be delicious.

Love your leftovers/cooking for 1 or 2: I can say from firsthand experience that leftovers of this meal are delicious. They’ll keep for 2-3 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. That said, when I’m cooking fish, I typically only buy as much as I’m planning to serve (rather than intentionally cooking more than I need to stock up on leftovers), and you can easily halve this recipe.

If you happen to have cilantro in the fridge: Garnish your bowls with it!

Vegetarian: I’d cook tofu cubes. Use firm or extra firm tofu, drain and press the block between your hands to remove the excess liquid, and cube it. Cook it the same way as the salmon.

DF/GF: Use plant-based butter to omit the dairy. To omit gluten, swap the soy sauce with coconut aminos or tamari, and use gluten-free 1:1 baking flour (or 1 tablespoon of cornstarch or arrowroot powder) instead of the all-purpose flour.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound skinless salmon filets, cut into 1-inch cubes
ingredients.name: skinless salmon filets

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons all-purpose flour, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 teaspoons all-purpose flour

ingredients.rawIngredient: Neutral oil such as avocado or vegetable
ingredients.name: Neutral oil such as avocado or vegetable

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, minced or grated
ingredients.name: fresh ginger, minced or grated

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 to 16 ounces snap peas (however big the bag is at your store), cut into 1-inch pieces if you want, or left whole
ingredients.name: snap peas (however big the bag is at your store)
ingredients.note: cut into 1-inch pieces if you want, or left whole

ingredients.rawIngredient: To garnish: sesame seeds (toastedif you have them!), sriracha
ingredients.name: To garnish: sesame seeds (toastedif you have them!), sriracha

preparationSteps: Use whatever cutting board you use to cut raw meat on to cut everything else too so that you only dirty one board. If you’re going to cut your snap peas into 1-inch pieces, go ahead and do that now and set them to the side. It’s nice for the snap peas to be a uniform size as the salmon, but it’s completely optional — don’t bother with it if you’re in a hurry!
Melt 3 tablespoons unsalted butter in a small pot over medium-low heat. Let it melt and begin to brown while you thinly slice 1 bunch scallions and mince 6 garlic cloves.

Turn the heat up to medium-high and add the sliced scallions and HALF of the minced garlic. Stir for 30 seconds. Add 1 1/2 cups white rice and stir to coat in brown butter and toast the rice for 1 minute. Stir in 2 1/2 cups water and 3/4 teaspoon salt and raise the heat to high to bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, turn the heat off but leave the rice covered until ready to eat.

Meanwhile, make the salmon. Cut 1 pound skinless salmon filets into 1-inch cubes (1 inch is about the size of your top thumb joint) and season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds black pepper. Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour and toss it around to coat it (yes, right there on the cutting board!). It’s fine if it doesn’t all stick, but you want each piece to be covered in flour.

In your largest skillet (preferably nonstick, especially if you aren’t comfortable with cooking fish), warm enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet (it was about 2 tablespoons for my 12-inch skillet) over medium-high heat.

While it’s heating, make the sauce: in a small bowl stir together 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1/4 cup honey, 1/4 cup water, the remaining minced garlic, a 1-inch piece of grated or minced fresh ginger, and 2 teaspoons flour. Set aside.

Add the salmon cubes to the skillet in an even layer and cook until browned, 3 to 4 minutes. Use a thin spatula to get underneath the fish without tearing it. Flip the salmon and add 10 ounces (or however many ounces your bag contains) snap peas to the skillet and cook for another 2 minutes, then add the sauce to the skillet and cook for an additional 1 to 3 minutes, until the sauce thickens and coats the salmon. Gently flip the salmon over a few times to coat it. Keep a close eye on things — we want the sauce to thicken to a nice saucy consistency, not evaporate to the point of burning.
Use a fork to gently fluff the rice (aka use the fork to kind of rake it until the rice separates).
Make bowls with rice, salmon, snap peas, and plenty of sauce. Garnish with sesame seeds and sriracha if you’d like. ENJOY!

name: weeknight vongole

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound spaghetti or bucatini (or any pasta noodle)
ingredients.name: spaghetti or bucatini (or any pasta noodle)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 ounce (1/4 cup) grated Pecorino cheese, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: grated Pecorino cheese, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 large lemon
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 large lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon butter, cut into small cubes
ingredients.name: butter

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add 1 pound spaghetti (or bucatini) and cook until tender, according to package directions.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl (go ahead and use a pretty serving bowl, if you’ll be serving the pasta family-style), add 1 (10-ounce) can whole clams (including the juices), 1/4 cup grated Pecorino cheese, 2 tablespoons high-quality extra-virgin olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 large lemon, 1 grated garlic clove, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Stir until well mixed.
When the noodles are ready, drain them in a colander but DON‘T shake the excess water off — we want just a bit of pasta water there to help it get saucy!

Immediately return the noodles to the bowl of clam sauce along with 1 tablespoon butter, cut into small cubes. Toss vigorously until the noodles are well coated in the lemon-clam mixture and the butter is melted. Add 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley and toss again to combine.
This pasta is good right when you make it but even better a few minutes after, once the noodles have had a chance to soak up some of the sauce.
Serve, garnishing with as much extra grated Pecorino and red pepper flakes as you’d like!

name: beef and three bean chili
note:
Make it Texas chili: Texans don’t like beans in their chili. I love Texans, but I will never understand this. If you’re a Texan, omit the beans and use 5 pounds of beef!

Vegetarian: Since you’ll be omitting the beef, let’s bulk it up with extra veggies. I’d do an extra bell pepper, 2 carrots and 2 stalks of celery. Mince them the same way you’re doing the bell pepper and onion! You’ll sauté all the vegetables together then proceed with the recipe. Three cans of beans should be plenty, but feel free to add another if you think it needs it! Alternatively, if you like Impossible ground meat or another plant-based “meat” option, that’d make for a good swap too.

Serve this with these: Don’t forget about the mini cornbread muffins Anne Byrn shared with us in last week’s white chicken chili post! They’d make a fab accompaniment to this chili as well.

Prep ahead: Just like last week’s chili, you can cook this whole thing up to 4 days ahead of time and store it in the fridge, covered, in the pot you cooked it in. Reheat on the stovetop before dinner, and keep it warm over low heat throughout mealtime.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: This recipe is already both as written! Just be sure to use df cheese and sour cream, if needed, for your toppings.

Feeding kids: Do your kids abhor spice as much as mine? You can swap the jalapeños out for another bell pepper (or just omit) and add hot sauce(s) to your serving spread for the adults to enjoy.

Freeze it! Chili freezes so perfectly. I love souper cubes. I freeze it in the cubes, then transfer them to a gallon Ziploc once frozen.

Use your slow cooker: Brown your meat like the recipe’s written. You can also sauté your veggies in the pot, if you have time, or you can just let them cook in the slow cooker (sautéing them will bring out a little more flavor; skipping that will save you time). Add the pre-cooked beef, veggies, and all other ingredients to the slow cooker and cook on low for 6 hours, or until the meat is perfectly tender.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 pounds boneless chuck beef, fat trimmed and 1-inch cubed
ingredients.name: boneless chuck beef, fat trimmed and 1-inch cubed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 jalapeños (leave them out if your eaters are super wimpy about spice, but I promise this chili is not overly spicy!)
ingredients.name: jalapeños (leave them out if your eaters are super wimpy about spice, but I promise this chili is not overly spicy!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5-ounce) can tomato sauce (sometimes called puréed tomato)
ingredients.name: tomato sauce (sometimes called puréed tomato)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon brown sugar (white also works, or omit if avoiding extra sugar on the sugariest day of the year)
ingredients.name: brown sugar (white also works, or omit if avoiding extra sugar on the sugariest day of the year)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional (but not really optional) toppings: Fritos scoops or tortilla chips, sour cream, shredded sharp Cheddar cheese, chopped cilantro, pickled jalapeños…
ingredients.name: Optional (but not really optional) toppings: Fritos scoops or tortilla chips, sour cream, shredded sharp Cheddar cheese, chopped cilantro, pickled jalapeños…

preparationSteps: Season 3 pounds boneless chuck beef with a heavy sprinkle of salt and pepper. No need to measure here, just make sure all sides are seasoned nicely.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat. Add all of the beef to the pot and spread it out as evenly as possible. Your pot is going to be way overcrowded, and thus you will not be able to get a perfect sear here. The beef will also release a lot of liquid and it won’t be able to evaporate off quickly because your pot is so full. But ya know what? This is a chili. Easy over perfect.
Let the beef cook for 4 minutes on the first side, then give it a big stir and let it cook for 4 minutes on the next side.
While the beef is cooking, prep your veggies. We’re gonna do it all in the food processor or blender.

De-stem and de-seed the red bell pepper and jalapeños. Did you know most the the spiciness of jalapeños is in the seeds? Ditching the seeds will give us the flavor without the heat. Also, wash your hands really well after cutting the jalapeños! Throw the peppers in the food processor or blender.

Cut the tops and bottoms off of the yellow onion, cut it into quarters, and remove the skin (and discard). Throw the quartered onion in the food processor or blender along with 6 peeled garlic cloves.

If using a food processor, pulse several times until minced. If using a blender, pulse a couple times then pick the blender carafe up and shake it (so that the vegetables all get exposed to the blades) and continue pulsing and shaking until everything is minced.

Once the meat is brown (actually it’ll be kinda grey since we aren't searing it “properly”) all over, add the minced onion and pepper mixture, 1 tablespoon chili powder, 1 tablespoon cumin, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, and 1 teaspoon smoked paprika to the pot and stir often for an additional 4 minutes.

Stir in 1 can fire roasted tomatoes, 1 can tomato sauce, and 1 tablespoon brown sugar. Fill one of the empty cans up with water and dump that in there too. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer (probably your lowest heat, we only want to see the occasional small bubble) and cook for 1 1/2 hours uncovered. Stir every 20 minutes or so or it’ll stick to the bottom (here’s how to reduce sticking and over-bubbling).
After 1 1/2 hours, stir in 1 can red kidney beans, 1 can pinto beans, and 1 can black beans (all drained but not rinsed). If at any point your chili seems too thick, just stir in some water!
Cook for an additional 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until the beef is perfectly tender, like the best beef stew you’ve ever had.
Stir in the juice of 1 lime before serving.

Now that your chili is the perfect consistency, keep the lid ON in between serving it so that it doesn’t continue reducing! We just keep it on the stovetop over the lowest heat possible all night long on Halloween night!
Garnish your bowl with your favorite chili toppings and ENJOY!

name: kale salad with fancy chicken fingers
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Make the kale salad as written, but grab a rotisserie chicken and some store-bought croutons. Shred 1 1/2 cups of chicken and toss that in with 1/2 cup croutons.

I don’t wanna chop kale: I feel you, but FYI, the only bagged kale that I have ever liked is the organic shredded kale from Trader Joe’s. Every other kind has tons of thick stems in it and is chopped way too large. If you have a suggestion to the contrary, please let us know in the notes!

Leftovers are a good thing: Kale is hearty, so this salad is fantastic the next day. Reheat the chicken fingers by baking them on a baking sheet in a 400°F oven for 5 to 7 minutes or until they’re crispy again. You can also freeze any leftover chicken fingers in an air-tight Ziploc! Bake them from frozen at 400°F for about 20 minutes, or until heated through (flipping once halfway through).

Make ahead: Follow the directions just above to reheat the chicken fingers. The salad will keep in the fridge for up to a day. Hold off on adding the nectarines until you’re serving.

I’m feeding a toddler: Better safe than sorry — leave the everything bagel off of a few chicken fingers if you’re feeding opinionated kiddos. You can coat a few tenders in the Panko mixture before adding the seasoning, then add 2 tablespoons of it for the rest of them.

Can I use my air fryer? YEP. Preheat it to 400°F (200°C). Spray the Panko-coated chicken all over with cooking spray. Place chicken in air fryer basket in a single layer. Cook for 7 minutes. Flip and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes or until crispy all over and 165°F internally.

Vegetarian: Roast some chickpeas and sweet potato cubes instead of the chicken fingers! It’ll be delish!

Gluten-free: Use almond flour in lieu of Panko.

Dairy-free: Use dairy-free Parmesan cheese.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 bunches lacinato kale (AKA the flat, not curly kind), or 2 10-ounce bags of shredded kale
ingredients.name: lacinato kale (AKA the flat, not curly kind), or 2 10-ounce bags of shredded kale

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 large lemon
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 large lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup cooking oil such as canola, vegetable, grapeseed, or avocado
ingredients.name: cooking oil such as canola, vegetable, grapeseed, or avocado

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 1 1/2 pounds chicken tenders (or 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, sliced lengthwise into 1/2-inch thick strips)
ingredients.name: chicken tenders (or 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, sliced lengthwise into 1/2-inch thick strips)

preparationSteps: To make the salad: Pull or cut the tough ribs out of 2 large bunches of kale, then stack all of the leaves together, facing the same direction and slice the kale as thinly as you can. Use a salad spinner to soak the kale, then spin it until it’s completely dry.
In a large bowl, combine 1/2 cup grated Parmesan, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 grated garlic clove, and a pinch of red pepper flakes.

To zest the lemon and grate the garlic clove, you can either use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater. If you have neither, omit the lemon zest and just mince the garlic. Whisk together to combine. This will not look like your average salad dressing. It’ll be really thick and chunky. That’s normal!

Add the thinly sliced kale to the bowl and sprinkle a bit of salt over top. Using both hands, massage the kale, tossing it with the salad dressing, until it’s tender. You want the kale to be tender, but not totally limp, so only massage (AKA squeeze it between your fist) about 10 times. Taste and add more salt if needed. Place your salad in the refrigerator until the chicken is ready. (We didn’t forget the nectarines — they’re coming later!)
To make the chicken: Combine 1 cup Panko breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan, and 3 tablespoons everything bagel seasoning to a large bowl.

Now go ahead and start warming 1/3 cup cooking oil in your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. When you add a piece of Panko to the skillet and it sizzles immediately, it’s hot enough to cook in.
Add 1 1/2 pounds of chicken tenders, 1 large egg, and 1 teaspoon salt to a bowl and use your hands to combine and coat the chicken in egg wash.

Transfer one chicken tender at a time into the Panko mixture, coat it completely, then transfer it to the skillet. Keep going until the skillet is full, leaving about 1 inch of space between each piece of chicken. You’ll probably need to fry them in two batches.

Cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden-brown all over. You can use an internal meat thermometer to check and make sure the chicken is 165°F internally. Transfer the chicken to a wire rack if you have one (it prevents the crispy coating from  getting soggy), or to a plate if you don’t. Continue until all of the chicken is cooked.
Divide the kale salad between 2 to 4 plates, and place nectarine slices and the crispy chicken on top. DIG IN!

name: balsamic basil grilled chicken (sandwich and/or salad!)
note:
I don’t have a grill: No prob! Preheat the broiler to high. Throw the chicken on a large foil-lined baking sheet and broil on the top rack for 6 to 7 minutes (or until the chicken has reached at least 165°F internally). Take the chicken out, then broil the buns for 30 seconds to 1 minute but SIT ON YOUR BUTT AND WATCH! Buns burn quickly.

Vegetarian: Throw a bowl of edamame on the table for a vegetarian protein option for the salad! It’s so delicious with these ingredients. Crispy chickpeas (just buy them in the bag, already crispy!) are also a great option. If you want a vegetarian sandwich, cut seitan into strips, marinate it in the balsamic marinade, then grill it for a couple minutes per side!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: To cut dairy, don’t add cheese to the sandwiches and use df cheese on your salad or just omit. And to avoid gluten, make sure your Dijon mustard is gluten free (most but not all brands are!), and either use gf buns or go the salad route!

Make ahead: Marinate the chicken and make the mayo up to 24 hours in advance. Make the salad up to 12 hours in advance, just don’t add the nuts until you’re ready to eat.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Grab a rotisserie chicken. Slice it up. Throw it on a potato bun, top it with your favorite chicken sandwich toppings and serve it alongside this salad. OR just make the salad and throw the sliced rotisserie chicken on top.

Kebab it: Make kebabs by cubing up the chicken and letting it marinate. Thread it onto skewers (if wooden, soak them in cold water for at least 30 minutes before threading so they don’t catch on fire) and grill the kebabs for 3 to 4 minutes per side, flipping once. You could also add onion slices, summer squash, bell pepper, and/or any other vegetable that also cooks quickly to your kebabs!

I need even more veggies, please. My picky chicky sandos recipe has a side of grilled zucchini and/or squash that is an amazing and easy add on to any grilled meal. Click here for the recipe!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard (OK to skip if you don’t have)
ingredients.name: Dijon mustard (OK to skip if you don’t have)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs (4 to 5 thighs)
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs (4 to 5 thighs)

ingredients.rawIngredient: As many buns as you want (I like potato buns)
ingredients.name: As many buns as you want (I like potato buns)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 ounces mixed greens or arugula (if everyone wants a lot of salad, you should double all salad ingredients!)
ingredients.name: mixed greens or arugula (if everyone wants a lot of salad, you should double all salad ingredients!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 medium red onion, thinly sliced (no thick rings! slice as thinly as you can!), divided
ingredients.name: medium red onion, thinly sliced (no thick rings! slice as thinly as you can!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but encouraged for sandwiches: slices of havarti or white cheddar, thinly sliced tomato, and thinly sliced avocado
ingredients.name: Optional but encouraged for sandwiches: slices of havarti or white cheddar, thinly sliced tomato, and thinly sliced avocado
Sun-Dried Tomato & Basil Mayo (makes a little under 1 cup):

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of salt and pepper
ingredients.name: Big pinch of salt and pepper

preparationSteps: Add 1/4 cup minced fresh basil, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to a large bowl and stir to combine. Pull out 3 tablespoons of marinade and add it to a small jar or lidded container. Set aside. Add  2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs to the bowl of marinade and allow chicken to marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or in the refrigerator (covered) for up to 24 hours.

To the small jar of dressing, add a splash (about 1 tablespoon) of water and shake to emulsify. Taste. Want it tangier? Add more balsamic, or some fresh lemon juice if you have it. Want it less tangy? Add a smidge more oil.

While the chicken is marinating, make the sun-dried tomato & basil mayo: Add all ingredients (3/4 cup mayonnaise, 1/4 cup sun-dried tomatoes, 6 large fresh basil leaves, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, and a big pinch of salt and pepper) to a food processor or blender and blend until smooth.

You can also go ahead and assemble the salad up to 12 hours in advance, but add the nuts at the last minute. Throw 5 ounces mixed greens into a serving bowl, but reserve a handful for garnishing chicken sandwiches. Top with 1 1/2 cups thinly sliced strawberries, about 1/4 cup of thinly sliced red onion (you’ll top your burgers with the remaining slices!), 4 ounces crumbled goat cheese, and 1/4 cup chopped roasted almonds. Set aside until dinner time.
When you’re ready to eat in about 30 minutes, start preheating the grill to 450°F.

While it’s preheating, open the buns, slather them with sun-dried tomato & basil mayo, and grill them cut-side down with the lid open until they’re lightly toasted. Don’t take your eyes off of them! They burn quickly. Once toasted, place the buns on a platter.
When the grill is hot, clean it with your grill brush.

Wad up a paper towel and soak it in a neutral cooking oil. It should be saturated but not dripping (so wring it out if you have to). Grab the (saturated-but-not-dripping!) paper towel with tongs and rub it all over the grill grates.

Remove the chicken thighs from the brine, shaking them as dry as you can. Add the chicken to the grill and cook for 5 minutes per side, or until at least 165°F internally. If you’re adding cheese, add a slice for the last 30 seconds of grilling. Fold the slice of cheese in half if needed to make it fit on the thigh better!)

Take the chicken off the grill and allow it to rest and cool down for a few minutes while you assemble your final sandwich toppings and throw them on a platter. (Thinly slice the tomatoes and avocado! Throw that reserved handful of greens, leftover red onion, and bowl of mayo on there!)
Build your sandwiches however you like ‘em! I like this sandwich all the way: greens on the bottom, topped with a cheesy chicken thigh, topped with tomato, avocado, and onion slices.
Or, make a salad by simply filling your plate with salad and throwing a slice of grilled chicken on top! I like to steal some avocado and add that to mine too.
Dig in!

name: pan-fried dover sole + corn risotto

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 cups chicken or vegetable stock, divided
ingredients.name: chicken or vegetable stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup packed basil leaves, plus the stems
ingredients.name: packed basil leaves, plus the stems

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen corn, unthawed (AKA still frozen)
ingredients.name: frozen corn, unthawed (AKA still frozen)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 18 ounces Dover sole, cut into 4 fillets (if not already separated) and patted dry
ingredients.name: Dover sole
ingredients.note: cut into 4 fillets (if not already separated) and patted dry

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Position an oven rack in the middle of your oven.

Add 5 cups stock to a large oven-proof heavy pot or Dutch oven and bring to a boil over high heat. While it’s coming to a boil, thinly slice 2 shallots and measure out 1/2 cup packed basil leaves, reserving the basil stems.

Once the stock is boiling, stir in 2 cups arborio rice, 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen corn, the basil stems, and half of the sliced shallots. Cover the pot (you can use a baking sheet if your pot doesn’t have a lid) and transfer it to the oven. Bake for 40 minutes.

When the risotto is halfway done cooking (so, after 20 minutes of baking), place 1/2 cup all-purpose flour in a shallow dish. Pat 18 ounces Dover sole fillets dry with paper towels or a clean dish towel and season the fish on both sides with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Dip each fillet in the flour — lightly coat it on both sides and shake off any excess flour.

Heat 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high. It’ll hiss and pop a bit as the butter melts — that’s OK! Cook the fillets, working in batches if needed, until they’re golden brown on the outside and cooked through on the inside. This won’t take long! 1 to 2 minutes per side. You’ll know a fillet is ready to flip when it releases easily from the pan. Transfer the cooked fish to a platter and tent the platter with foil. To tent it, just loosely cover the platter with foil, keeping some space between the fish and the foil. This will keep the fillets from getting cold while we finish up the rest of the meal!

Wipe out the skillet (it doesn’t have be perfectly clean and you definitely don’t need to wash it — we’re about to use it again). Return the skillet to the stovetop over medium heat. Add remaining 4 tablespoons butter and cook until it turns golden and starts to smell nutty, 1 to 2 minutes. Add 2 pints cherry tomatoes and the rest of the sliced shallots and cook, stirring, until the tomatoes start to burst, 2 to 4 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon white wine vinegar and 3/4 cup water, bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, and cook until the sauce has thickened slightly, 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from heat, stir in half of the basil leaves, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

By now your risotto should be done! Take it out of the oven and remove and discard the basil stems. Stir in the remaining 1 cup stock, 1/2 cup heavy cream, and 1 cup grated Parmesan. Season it with a pinch of salt and pepper then taste it. If needed, add more salt and pepper a little pinch at a time until it’s perfectly seasoned. If it’s too thick, just add more stock or water to loosen it up. If it’s too thin, just turn the stove on medium heat and stir until thickened to your liking.
Serve your pan-seared fish over corn risotto and topped with burst cherry tomato sauce. Garnish with the remaining basil. DIG IN!

name: esquites chicken salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 lime, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 lime, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 heads romaine or 4 heads little gem lettuce, large leaves torn
ingredients.name: romaine or 4 heads little gem lettuce, large leaves torn

ingredients.rawIngredient: Dash of cayenne, smoked paprika, or another ground chile, for sprinkling (optional)
ingredients.name: of cayenne, smoked paprika, or another ground chile, for sprinkling (optional)

preparationSteps: Place 1/2 cup mayonnaise in a medium bowl, then use a microplane to grate in the zest of 1 lime (don’t add the lime juice — we’ll use that later!) and 2 garlic cloves. Finely chop 1 bunch cilantro, and stir 1/4 cup of it into the mayo mixture.

Transfer half of the mayo mixture to a large serving bowl (one that you’d serve salad from). Pat 1 1/2 to 2 pounds chicken thighs dry and season all over with 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Add chicken to the medium bowl and stir to coat in the mayo mixture. (The chicken can sit in the marinade for up to 24 hours in the fridge, but it’s OK if it doesn’t.)
Heat the grill to medium-high (400°F to 450°F) heat. While the grill is heating, shuck 2 ears of corn.
Now that your grill is piping hot, use your grill brush to clean the grates, and use tongs to lightly oil them with a wadded up ball of paper towels that you’ve soaked in oil.

Grill the corn and chicken for about 5 minutes per side, until the chicken is cooked through (to an internal temperature of 165°F) and the corn is golden. (Remember: You want the chicken to release easily from the grill! If it doesn’t, it’s not ready to flip.) Transfer to a plate to rest. When the corn and chicken are cool enough to handle, cut the kernels off the cob and slice the chicken.

To the reserved mayo mixture in the large bowl, add the juice from the zested lime and stir to combine. Use your hands to tear the leaves of 2 heads of romaine into big pieces, and add them to the bowl along with 4 ounces crumbled Cotija, 1/4 cup toasted pepitas, the remaining cilantro, the grilled corn kernels, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. (When you’re trying to show off, it’s always a good idea to hang on to a bit of every ingredient for garnishing at the end!)

Toss to combine, then season to taste with extra salt and lime juice as needed. Serve the salad topped with the sliced chicken and a dash of cayenne pepper if you want some heat. Sprinkle with any garnish ingredients you hung on to. DIG IN!

name: stuffed prosciutto pesto chicken with cauliflower mashed potatoes
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the cheese stuffing step. Use store-bought pesto. Just roast the chicken for 12 to 15 minutes — skip the searing step. Grab a bag of cauliflower florets and chop them in half instead of breaking down a full head.

Make it healthier: Skip stuffing the chicken with cheese, and omit the cheese from the cauliflower mashed potatoes. You might need to add a bit of water or chicken broth so that they aren’t quite so thick.

I don’t eat pork: Omit the prosciutto and warm some oil in your skillet before adding the pesto-covered chicken.

Make it ahead: Get the chicken totally ready to rock as far as 2 days in advance — I like to add the prosciutto just before cooking though. The cauliflower mashed potatoes can be made as far as 3 days in advance! Cover tightly and rewarm with a splash of water in the microwave or in a pot on the stove.

Dairy-free: Skip stuffing the chicken with cheese, rub the chicken with minced herbs and oil instead of pesto, and use dairy-free butter in the mashed cauliflower.

Vegetarian: Roast some vegetables (carrots, fennel, mushrooms) in oil, salt, and pepper in a 425°F oven until tender. Throw those over the cauliflower mashed potatoes and drizzle pesto over everything!

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 ounces semi-hard cheese (such as Cheddar, Gouda, Asiago, Monterey Jack, Mozzarella, Colby…)
ingredients.name: semi-hard cheese (such as Cheddar, Gouda, Asiago, Monterey Jack, Mozzarella, Colby…)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 to 6 tablespoons pesto (store-bought or see recipe below)
ingredients.name: pesto (store-bought or see recipe below)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups greens (such as basil, dill, parsley, cilantro, kale, arugula, spinach)
ingredients.name: greens (such as basil, dill, parsley, cilantro, kale, arugula, spinach)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup toasted nuts (such as pine nuts, walnuts, almonds, cashews, Brazil nuts)
ingredients.name: toasted nuts (such as pine nuts, walnuts, almonds, cashews, Brazil nuts)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup hard grated cheese (such as Parmesan, Grana Padano, asiago, manchego)
ingredients.name: hard grated cheese (such as Parmesan, Grana Padano, asiago, manchego)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup oil (extra-virgin is preferred, but anything goes)
ingredients.name: oil (extra-virgin is preferred, but anything goes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons of anything acidic (lemon or lime juice or vinegar)
ingredients.name: of anything acidic (lemon or lime juice or vinegar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup shredded semi-hard cheese (use the same cheese you stuffed in the chicken, or a different one!)
ingredients.name: shredded semi-hard cheese (use the same cheese you stuffed in the chicken, or a different one!)

preparationSteps: Insert a paring knife into the side of the fat end of the chicken breasts and carefully carve out a pocket, as deep as you can jab your paring knife (this is hard to explain, so I made a video — see below!). Season each chicken breast with about 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and a big pinch of black pepper. Stuff as much cheese into the cavity of the chicken breasts as you can — I usually just cut one big slice as wide as the opening and cram that in there.

To make the pesto, combine ingredients (the greens, nuts, cheese, oil, and acid of your choice) in a food processor or blender and blend until only slightly chunky. Taste and add more salt or acid until perfect. Rub pesto all over the chicken breasts and let it marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 400°F.

Warm a large ovenproof skillet (preferably nonstick or cast iron) over medium-high heat for 4 minutes. Just before cooking, place 1 piece of prosciutto on top of each chicken breast, smoothing it down so that it sticks to the pesto.

Place the chicken breasts into the skillet, prosciutto-side down (no oil needed in the skillet). Cook for 3 to 4 minutes without touching so that the prosciutto sears and gets really crispy. Using tongs, carefully flip the chicken over. If it doesn’t release easily, give it another 30 seconds. Once the prosciutto is crisp, it will release easily from the pan.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and cook for 10 minutes. Check the internal temperature, and continue cooking until the chicken is 165°F.

While the chicken is cooking, place 1 chopped head of cauliflower and 2 chopped Yukon gold potatoes into a large bowl with 3 tablespoons water. Cover with a plate and microwave on high for 13 minutes. Carefully remove the plate (it’s gonna be HOT!) and poke the cauliflower and potatoes with a fork. They should be extremely tender and easy to mash. Keep cooking until they are.
Drain out all but 1 tablespoon of the liquid from the bowl.

Mash (or puree in a food processor) with 2 tablespoons butter and season with 3/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Stir in 1/2 cup of whatever cheese ya want. If they’re too thick, stir in 1 tablespoon water or milk until they’ve reached the consistency you like.
Serve the chicken over the mashed cauliflower, with extra pesto on the side!

name: cheesy chicken baked spaghetti squash
note:
Love your leftovers: This is a great make-it-once, eat-it-four-times meal for a singleton! You could also freeze single-size portions of leftovers in Ziploc bags to enjoy for lunch weeks or months from now.

Prep ahead: You can assemble this whole skillet up to a day in advance — just keep it covered with foil in the fridge — and pop it into the oven uncovered before dinner.

Cook this recipe faster: Use 2 cups of shredded store-bought rotisserie chicken (or leftover turkey) instead of cooking your own. Microwave the halved spaghetti squash instead of roasting it. Place the two halves in a large bowl, add 2 tablespoons water, cover with a plate, and microwave for 12 minutes or until tender enough to easily scrape the strands out.

Vegetarian: Sauté 1 pound of sliced mushrooms in the skillet and mix everything else together in a large bowl. Stir the cheese mixture and squash strands straight into the mushrooms in the skillet!

Gimme some greens: Chop up a few handfuls of spinach and stir them into the skillet along with the squash, chicken, and cheese mixture. They’ll wilt right in. Or serve this alongside a simple salad of arugula topped with your favorite nuts and drizzled with EVOO and lemon juice.

Gluten-free/dairy-free: This meal is already gluten-free. You could use dairy-free versions of the cheese and sour cream elements of the cheese mixture to avoid dairy. Or, if you don’t love those, you could find a creamy plant-based “cheese” sauce (like this vegan alfredo) and use that instead.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 small (4 to 6 ounce) boneless skinless chicken breasts (or 2 cups shredded chicken or turkey or pork for that matter!)
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts (or 2 cups shredded chicken or turkey or pork for that matter!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (about 2 cups), divided
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (about 2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup sour cream, ricotta, Greek yogurt, or cottage cheese (I used ricotta. These flavors will all be very different, but delicious, and I want you to use what you have!)
ingredients.name: sour cream, ricotta, Greek yogurt, or cottage cheese (I used ricotta. These flavors will all be very different, but delicious, and I want you to use what you have!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for sprinkling on top
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for sprinkling on top

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon dried oregano(consider skipping it if your children get freaked out by green specks like mine do?)
ingredients.name: dried oregano(consider skipping it if your children get freaked out by green specks like mine do?)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut the spaghetti squash in half with a large chef’s knife using the bite and slam method. Scrape out the seeds and guts and discard. Place on the baking sheet.

Place 2 small chicken breasts on the lined baking sheet. Drizzle the inside of the squash and the chicken with a light amount of olive oil. What does that mean? It means that you absolutely do not need to measure this perfectly, we just want a nice light coating over both the squash and the chicken. Season the chicken and squash with a big pinch of salt and a few cranks of pepper.
Adjust the squash so that it’s cut side down, and the chicken so that it’s smooth side up.
Roast for 20 minutes, then remove the chicken, placing it on a cutting board. Continue roasting the squash for another 20 minutes.
While the squash is cooking, shred the chicken and make the cheese mixture.

When the chicken is cool enough to handle, chop it up into a few big pieces, put those pieces in a large bowl, then use two forks to shred it. Set the bowl aside and move onto making the cheese mixture.

We’re going to make the cheese mixture (which will melt into a delicious sauce) right in whatever you’re going to bake this in. I used a 10-inch cast iron skillet, but absolutely any oven-proof dish with an 8- to 10-inch diameter will do the trick.

Add 1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese, 1 cup ricotta (or another creamy white thing from the list above), 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 2 large eggs, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground pepper to your baking dish and stir to combine.
