Once the squash is done cooking and cool enough to handle, use a fork to scrape the strands out.

Add the squash and chicken into the skillet and combine it well with the cheese mixture. Sometimes I like to use my hands to make sure everything is getting really nicely incorporated into the strands. Smooth the top and sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 cup shredded cheddar and a few tablespoons of grated Parmesan.
Bake for 40 minutes. Let cool for 5 minutes, then DIG IN!

name: one-skillet sausage and mushroom cassoulet
note:
I don’t do tomatoes: Drain an 16-ounce can of roasted red peppers. Blend them with 2 cups of water and use in place of the canned tomatoes.

Prep ahead: If you’re like me and work from home and like to take advantage of 10-minute spurts of alone time throughout the day… this is a good one for you! Go ahead and cook the sausage and shallot (you can do that up to a day in advance and store it in the fridge). Wash and chop up those mushrooms and parsley and grate the cheese (store all in the fridge until it’s time to cook). With all that prepped, it’ll come together super quickly. Re-warm the sausage mixture in the pan, add your mushrooms, and you’re off! OR you can go ahead and compile the cassoulet in the skillet up to the step where you add use a spatula to smooth the top. Cover the skillet with foil and pop it into the fridge until you’re about 30 minutes from dinner time. Uncover it, add the Panko and Parmesan, and pop it in the oven!

Leftovers are a good thing: Can confirm that leftover cassoulet makes a DELISH breakfast, lunch, and/or dinner. Just cover the skillet in foil and enjoy over the next day or two.

Vegetarian: Two options: Either use a vegetarian sausage alternative OR use 2 pounds of mushrooms and 2 cans of beans. If you go the latter route, cook the shallot on its own in 2 tablespoons of oil, then add the mushrooms and continue cooking as the recipe is written. If you have some carrots and celery rolling around in your produce drawer, dice up one of each and add them to the pan with the onion. (You could also do that if you’re using sausage but want to add more veggies. Add them when you add the shallot to the skillet.)

Gluten-free/dairy-free: Use gf Panko-style breadcrumbs (you should have no problem finding them at the grocery store) if eliminating gluten. For df, use Mykonos or VioLife dairy-free Parm — or omit it completely.

Can I use dried beans? Absolutely!!! If you cook with beans a lot, using dried beans will save money. But it’ll add some time and legwork to the recipe as you’ll need to pre-cook them, so if you’re going for ease, definitely opt for canned. Here’s a straightforward tutorial on how to pre-cook dried beans.

I just ran out of cooking spray. Proceed with this recipe. It’s not essential.

OK, I’m sold on the power of beans. Good! They’re so healthy for the digestive system and easy to cook with! Check the vegetarian notes for all WTC recipes — beans are usually in there. And also let me remind you of my… One-Pot Cheesy Rice & BeansChipotle Black Bean Flautas

One-Pot Cheesy Rice & Beans

Chipotle Black Bean Flautas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground mild or spicy Italian sausage (up to your spice preference!)
ingredients.name: ground mild or spicy Italian sausage (up to your spice preference!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound any kind of mushrooms, roughly chopped
ingredients.name: any kind of mushrooms

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can Great Northern Beans, drained and rinsed (or any white beans such as navy or cannellini)
ingredients.name: Great Northern Beans
ingredients.note: drained and rinsed (or any white beans such as navy or cannellini)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon sherry or red wine vinegar
ingredients.name: sherry or red wine vinegar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup finely chopped parsley leaves, divided
ingredients.name: finely chopped parsley leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Warm a 12-inch skillet (preferably cast iron) or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound ground Italian sausage and 1 diced shallot to the pan and cook until the sausage has browned. Use a spatula to crumble it into tiny pieces.

Add 1 pound of chopped mushrooms and cook, stirring every few minutes, until all liquid has evaporated from the mushrooms, 6 to 7 minutes. Add 4 minced garlic cloves and cook, stirring constantly, for another 30 seconds.

Reduce the heat to a simmer (medium or medium-low on most stoves) and stir 1 (28-ounce) can diced tomatoes, 1 can of beans (drained and rinsed), 1 tablespoon vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring often, for 10 minutes, or until thickened. Stir in most of the 1/3 cup finely chopped parsley (but leave a few tablespoons for garnish), then remove the skillet from heat. Taste and add more salt if needed. (Some sausage brands have a ton of salt, so we’ve only added a small amount so far. You might find that you need to add up to 1 teaspoon before it tastes delicious!) Use a spatula to smooth the top.
Sprinkle 3/4 cup Panko breadcrumbs and 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese over top. Spray the top with cooking spray (this will help the Panko brown nicely!).
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the breadcrumbs are golden-brown. If they start to burn, just cover the skillet with foil and keep baking for at least 20 minutes!
Allow to cool for several minutes before serving. Garnish with leftover chopped parsley and dig in!

name: wontons and veggies in curry broth
note:
Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good for up to 4 days in the fridge. The wontons will absorb the broth as they sit, so add a splash more broth as needed to get it saucy again. This recipe’s easy to double if you want to meal prep for the week or are cooking for a larger group.

What to do with your leftover curry paste: Make one (or a few) of these recipes! Thai chicken chop, peanut vegetable curry, coconut curry lentil veggie stew, one-skillet chicken & gingery rice, thai tofu curry noodle soup

Make it a soup: This isn’t a soup, it’s wontons in a thick curry broth. If you want more or a brothy, liquidy soup, double the amount of vegetables, add another teaspoon of curry paste, and add 2 cups more stock plus another splash of lime juice, soy sauce, and fish sauce.

Add more veggies: I intentionally kept the ingredient list super short, but the more veggies the merrier. Add some sliced red bell pepper or shredded carrots if you have them. You could also add extra greens like sliced kale, bok choy, baby bok choy, or cabbage. Sliced green onions and cilantro would be great. See the “use what you’ve got” note above the recipe for even more ideas.

Feeding kids: My big kids don’t do curry, but they do love potstickers. See the “do kids eat this?” note above the recipe for how I fix this dinner for them instead.

Give it a protein boost: Use bone broth instead of chicken or veggie broth.

Vegetarian:: Use veggie potstickers and vegetable stock and see sub options for the fish sauce. Red curry paste can sometimes contain shrimp paste and/or fish sauce, so check the label! Thai Kitchen I know is vegan.

Gluten-free: Wontons/dumplings typically contain gluten, but there are some great GF options on the market like Feel Good Foods. Also use coconut aminos, liquid aminos, or tamari instead of soy sauce. Curry paste is typically gluten free, but double check your brand to be sure!

Dairy-free: Check the ingredient labels of wontons/dumplings as some contain dairy and others don’t. Otherwise, this meal’s dairy free.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon any neutral oil (avocado, coconut, olive)
ingredients.name: any neutral oil (avocado, coconut, olive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon red curry paste (more if you like it spicy)
ingredients.name: red curry paste (more if you like it spicy)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth (I use 2 cups water + 2 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth (I use 2 cups water + 2 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fish sauce (or another 2 teaspoons soy sauce)
ingredients.name: fish sauce (or another 2 teaspoons soy sauce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (24-ounce) bag frozen mini wontons/potstickers/dumplings, any flavor you like – chicken, pork, or veggie (so, about 60 mini potstickers, or you can use a 24-ounce bag of about 20 normal-sized potstickers)
ingredients.name: frozen mini wontons/potstickers/dumplings, any flavor you like – chicken, pork, or veggie (so, about 60 mini potstickers, or you can use a 24-ounce bag of about 20 normal-sized potstickers)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1/2 lime or 1 tablespoon rice wine vinegar or any clear vinegar
ingredients.name: Juice of 1/2 lime or 1 tablespoon rice wine vinegar or any clear vinegar

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large saucepan or pot over medium-high heat. Add 8 ounces sliced mushrooms and sauté until golden and tender and all liquid has evaporated, 4 to 5 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon red curry paste (or more if you like things spicy) and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells amazing and is starting to stick to the bottom of the pan.
Stir in 1 can coconut milk, 2 cups broth, 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon fish sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Gently drop in the frozen wontons and simmer for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, finely chop 2 big handfuls of spinach. Or skip the chopping, if you want to make it a totally no-chop meal!

Stir in the spinach (if you didn’t chop it, you can tear it apart as you add it, or just throw the leaves in whole!) and the juice of 1/2 lime. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed — more soy sauce for saltiness or fish sauce for umami or lime juice for brightness. Ladle into bowls and, if desired, top with chili crisp for a little extra kick.

name: crispy fish and lemon butter spring veg
note:
I have fresh veg! If you want to use fresh English peas or snap peas, do it! If using English peas, add them to the skillet first, after cooking the scallion and garlic, along with a splash of water, and cover to steam them for 3 to 4 minutes. Then continue with the recipe as written. But honestly, I really, really like and often prefer frozen peas!

Riff: Give the vegetables succotash vibes by adding lima beans and/or cherry tomatoes.

Prep ahead: Prep all your vegetables up to a day in advance! Your hot honey sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead of time.

Chop less: Omit the asparagus and use full bags of peas and corn instead.

Feeding 1 or 2: This recipe’s easy to halve if you don’t want leftovers!

Love your leftovers: If you do have leftovers, they’ll be good for 3 days stored in the fridge in airtight containers. Here are some ideas for what to do with them: Fish tacos: Warm corn tortillas and fill them with warmed flaky fish, the lemony veggies, crumbled feta or cotija, avocado, and hot honey sauce. Fried rice: Sauté your leftover veggies with 2 cups of cooked white rice. Add garlic, ginger, and a splash of soy sauce, then stir in leftover fish until warm. Drizzle with hot honey sauce. A great salad: Toss some mixed greens or chopped romaine with the leftover veggies and top with the warmed flaked fish. Make a dressing using your leftover hot honey sauce by adding 1 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice and a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar. If needed, stir in more oil until it’s the consistency of a vinaigrette.

Fish tacos: Warm corn tortillas and fill them with warmed flaky fish, the lemony veggies, crumbled feta or cotija, avocado, and hot honey sauce.

Fried rice: Sauté your leftover veggies with 2 cups of cooked white rice. Add garlic, ginger, and a splash of soy sauce, then stir in leftover fish until warm. Drizzle with hot honey sauce.

A great salad: Toss some mixed greens or chopped romaine with the leftover veggies and top with the warmed flaked fish. Make a dressing using your leftover hot honey sauce by adding 1 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice and a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar. If needed, stir in more oil until it’s the consistency of a vinaigrette.

Vegetarian: Use 4 large king oyster mushrooms, halved lengthwise, or a block of firm or extra-firm tofu. If using tofu, press the block between clean dish cloths for 15 to 30 minutes to remove excess moisture. Slice it into 4 “filets” and pat dry. Season with salt and pepper like you would the fish and, if you have some, lightly dust the filets with cornstarch or arrowroot powder (this will help them crisp up). Whether you’re cooking tofu or mushrooms, sear them for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crispy and golden.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use a plant-based butter to make it DF. Check that your mustard and hot sauce are gluten free (most are, but it’s always good to check) — otherwise, it’s already GF.

ingredients.name: Crispy fish and lemon butter vegetables:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions (aka spring onions!), thinly sliced (roots discarded)
ingredients.name: scallions (aka spring onions!), thinly sliced (roots discarded)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch asparagus (~1 pound), bottom 1 1/2 inches trimmed and discarded
ingredients.name: asparagus (~1 pound), bottom 1 1/2 inches trimmed and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 handful fresh basil leaves, finely chopped
ingredients.name: handful fresh basil leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided, more if needed
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, divided, more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups frozen English peas (or 1 pound snap peas, cut into thirds)
ingredients.name: frozen English peas (or 1 pound snap peas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups frozen corn (ideally sweet white corn)
ingredients.name: frozen corn (ideally sweet white corn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 lemons, 1 cut in half, 1 cut into wedges for serving
ingredients.name: lemons, 1 cut in half, 1 cut into wedges for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon of your favorite hot sauce or 1/8 teaspoon red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: of your favorite hot sauce or 1/8 teaspoon red pepper flakes

preparationSteps: Place 4 (6-ounce) halibut filets on a clean paper towel or dish towel and pat dry. Season with about 1/8 teaspoon kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper per filet, and set aside at room temperature.

Make your hot honey sauce: In a medium bowl, stir together 1/4 cup Dijon mustard, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 tablespoon of your favorite hot sauce (or 1/8 teaspoon red pepper flakes), and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Stirring continuously, pour in 1/4 cup olive oil until smooth. Taste and adjust for seasoning. Do you want it spicier? Sweeter? Saltier? Do your thing here.

Prep all your vegetables now, because things will move quickly once we start cooking. Thinly slice 1 bunch scallions, using every part but discarding the roots, and 4 garlic cloves. Cut off (and discard) the bottom 1 1/2 inches of 1 bunch asparagus, then slice the stalks into 1/4-inch pieces on a diagonal. Finely chop 1 handful fresh basil leaves.

Warm a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil, swirl to coat the pan, and warm for 30 seconds. This step is VERY important, your skillet needs to be properly preheated!

Add the filets to the skillet skin-side UP (if they have skin) and press down firmly with a spatula to ensure the edges don’t curl up. Cook for 3 minutes, until they are crispy and golden and release easily from the skillet (if they aren’t ready yet, cook them for 30 more seconds and try again. Repeat as needed). Turn heat down to medium and flip the fish. Add 2 tablespoons butter to the skillet, tilt the skillet to the side, and use a spoon to baste the fish with the melted butter almost continuously for the next 3 minutes, until an internal thermometer reads between 125°F (medium-rare — ideal for salmon and tuna in my opinion!) and 140°F (well-done — ideal for halibut and other white fish). Fish cooking time can vary a bit based on how thick your filets are, so use your meat thermometer! If you don’t have one, you are looking for the fish to turn opaque and flake easily with a fork.
Transfer fish to a holding plate, skin-side up.

Do not wipe out the skillet! Add 2 more tablespoons butter to the skillet along with the thinly sliced scallions (reserving a couple tablespoons of raw scallions for garnish!) and the thinly sliced garlic and cook for 2 minutes, until becoming tender.

Add the sliced asparagus and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until almost crisp-tender (AKA, until it has softened some but still has a crunch) — take a bite to see! Add 2 cups frozen English peas and 1 1/2 cups frozen corn and cook until asparagus is bright green and the frozen veg have warmed through, about 2 minutes.

Stir in the chopped basil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Taste for seasoning and add more butter, salt, lemon juice, or pepper as desired. If the flavor isn’t totally popping, it likely needs more lemon juice and kosher salt.

Nestle the filets into the vegetables (skin-side up, if they have skin, to keep it crispy), for a few minutes to re-warm. Garnish with extra basil and the reserved scallions, serve with lemon wedges, and finish with a drizzle of hot honey sauce. DIG IN!

name: roasted pork tenderloin with couscous, pears, and shallots
note:
I’m cooking for a crowd: My sister Annie cooked this recipe for 6 people last week and simply cooked another pork tenderloin in the same skillet at the same time. It was plenty of couscous for 6 people.

Leftovers are a good thing: The cooked recipe doesn’t freeze well, so plan on enjoying leftovers for lunches this week! You could put some of the pork tenderloin slices, pears, and dates on a potato roll for an amazing sandwich, or add some more arugula to a bowl and top it with the leftovers for a salad. Uncooked pork tenderloin does freeze very well, so you could also halve the recipe and freeze the second half of the pork.

Prep it: You can work on chopping ahead of time: Cut the shallots into wedges, halve and pit the dates, cube the feta. Just don’t slice the pears ahead of time or they’ll brown. This meal comes together really quickly!

Vegetarian: Roast a can of rinsed, drained, and dried chickpeas instead. To dry them, just wipe them down with a dish towel or paper towel. You’ll want to cover them in roughly 2 tablespoons of a cooking oil with a high smoke point before seasoning with salt and pepper. They’ll need about 20 minutes to cook.

Gluten-free/dairy-free: For gf, leave out the couscous and chicken stock. You can either serve it just over arugula, or cook your favorite grain to serve on the side. For dairy-free, use df butter and omit the feta (or use a vegan substitute).

Cooking oils: As a reminder, grapeseed, avocado, and sunflower oils are my favorite neutral cooking oils that can withstand a high heat (like we use here).

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1- to 2-pound) pork tenderloin (Notporkloin. There’s a big difference!)
ingredients.name: pork tenderloin (Notporkloin. There’s a big difference!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 shallots, cut into wedges (cut each bulb into 2 or 3 pieces)
ingredients.name: shallots
ingredients.note: cut into wedges (cut each bulb into 2 or 3 pieces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 Boscpears, cut into 6 pieces each (Bosc are the brown ones with rough skin — they are best for roasting. other types of pears will get too squishy)
ingredients.name: Boscpears
ingredients.note: cut into 6 pieces each (Bosc are the brown ones with rough skin — they are best for roasting. other types of pears will get too squishy)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons low-sodium chicken stock
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons low-sodium chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup whole wheat couscous (NOT Israeli couscous, which is actually a round pasta)
ingredients.name: whole wheat couscous (NOT Israeli couscous, which is actually a round pasta)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8-ounce block of feta, cut into 1-inch cubes (try to avoid using pre-crumbled)
ingredients.name: of feta
ingredients.note: cut into 1-inch cubes (try to avoid using pre-crumbled)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Season a 1- to 2-pound pork tenderloin with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Warm 1 tablespoon of oil in a 12-inch ovenproof skillet, preferably a cast iron, over medium-high heat. Pat the pork tenderloin dry, then place it in the middle of the skillet.

Cook the pork until golden-brown on the first side, 3 to 4 minutes. When it’s ready to flip, it will release easily from the skillet. Cook the pork for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, until golden-brown on the second side. Scooch the pork over to one side of the skillet.

To the other side of the skillet, add 3 sliced shallots, 3 sliced pears, 4 smashed garlic cloves (bash them with the flat side of your knife until they’re flat), 2 tablespoons of butter, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom, and 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger to the skillet and stir until the butter melts and everything is evenly coated in butter and spices.

Place the skillet in the oven, uncovered, and roast until the internal temperature of the pork tenderloin is 145°F. This will take between 15 and 20 minutes. Transfer the pork to your cutting board, and loosely tent with aluminum foil.

Into the skillet, stir 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons chicken stock, 1 cup couscous (again — make sure you are using WHOLE WHEAT couscous, NOT Israeli couscous), 6 halved and pitted dates, and 8 ounces of cubed feta. The couscous will immediately absorb most or all of the liquid — that’s normal!
Cover the skillet and return it to the oven for 12 minutes. (If you don’t have a lid for your skillet, just cover it tightly with foil.)

Pull it out of the oven and use a fork to fluff the couscous. Taste it; it should be tender. If it’s still hard, cover the skillet for 5 more minutes (don’t return it to the oven — just cover it). Once tender, stir in 2 cups baby arugula and the juice of half a lemon. Taste the couscous pilaf and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper, and maybe a bit more lemon juice.
Slice the pork tenderloin into 1/4-inch thick rounds.
Serve the pork over the couscous.

name: pimento cheese blt
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use your favorite store-bought pimento cheese if you don’t feel up to making your own. And pick up a fully cooked bacon at the grocery store, either in a package or from the hot food bar.

Other ways to make pimento cheese: Add fresh diced jalapeño, or diced pickled jalapeño, or my mother-in-law even adds chopped green olives!

Prep ahead: The bacon can be cooked up to 4 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. Reheat it in the microwave for 20 to 30 seconds before assembling your sandwiches. The pimento cheese can be made up to a 5 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. Let it sit out on the counter to loosen up a bit before serving.

Love your leftovers: These sandwiches are best enjoyed soon after assembling them, so if you don’t think you’ll eat all of them, just toast as many slices of bread as you need for the number of sandwiches you want to make. Store the pimento cheese in an airtight container in the fridge. The tomatoes and lettuce will also store well for up to 24 hours. Bacon gets soft in the fridge, so just throw it in a 400°F oven for a few minutes to bring it back to life. Serve the leftover pimento cheese with crackers, or put it on a burger, or make good ole pimento cheese sandwiches with white bread and pimento cheese. Yum.

Vegetarian: Replace the bacon with plant-based bacon strips! Crispy tempeh (cut into big strips instead of cubes) could also be great here. Or just make sandwiches with pimento cheese, tomato, and lettuce. Delish!

Dairy-free: Swap the cheddar and pepper jack for shredded vegan cheese, either all cheddar or a combination of cheddar and pepper jack, Colby, or Monterey Jack.

Gluten-free: Go ahead and use gluten-free sandwich bread.

Cooking for a crowd: This recipe is easy to double or triple if you’re serving all of your family and friends. Or on the opposite end of the spectrum, it’s just as easy to cut in half if you only want to make one or two sandwiches.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 large, ripe tomatoes (beef steak, early girls, heirloom, anything goes!)
ingredients.name: large ripe tomatoes (beef steak, early girls, heirloom, anything goes!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 24 leaves crisp green leaf lettuce such as butter or iceberg
ingredients.name: crisp green leaf lettuce such as butter or iceberg

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups (8 ounces) shredded, sharp yellow cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded, sharp yellow cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (4 ounces) shredded pepper jack cheese
ingredients.name: shredded pepper jack cheese

preparationSteps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil, including up the sides. Arrange 2 pounds thick-cut bacon on one or two sheet-pans, overlapping slightly as needed to fit. Rub with 1/2 cup light brown sugar, if desired, and sprinkle generously with black pepper. Roast until golden brown and curling in spots, 20 to 30 minutes. If it is not getting crispy by 30 minutes, pour off the grease and return it to the oven. You can crank the oven up to 400°F, but you must sit on your butt in front of the oven, with the light on, and watch it closely! At this point if will go from “not quite ready” to “burnt and smoking the whole house up” very quickly. Use tongs to transfer the bacon to a plate, letting any excess grease drip off before adding it to the plate. Do not put it on a paper towel — it’ll stick.
While the bacon’s cooking, add 8 slices sourdough bread directly to the open rack and toast, 5 to 7 minutes. We want it very light golden-brown, not crunchy! Just toasted a smidge.

Meanwhile, make the pimento cheese by stirring together the 2 cups shredded, sharp yellow cheddar cheese, 1 cup shredded pepper jack cheese, 2/3 cup mayonnaise, 1 (4-ounce) drained jar chopped pimentos, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a medium mixing bowl. Adjust to taste with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until it’s time to eat.
Thinly slice 3 large tomatoes and season with a pinch of salt.
I like to set everything out and let everyone build their own perfect sandwich, but below are instructions for how to build 4 gigantic (as pictured) BLTs).

Top half the slices of bread with pimento cheese (about 1/3 cup per slice). Now layer with bacon, tomato, and 2 pieces of lettuce—three times! (Or one or two times if you don’t want such a big stack.) Top with the remaining slices of bread and press down. A couple toothpicks will help keep the sandwich intact, or wrap it in paper to take it to go. Enjoy the best bite of summer!

name: 20-minute fish tacos

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless firm white fish filets (like cod, mahi mahi, flounder…), cut into 4 filets, if not already done so
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless firm white fish filets (like cod, mahi mahi, flounder…)
ingredients.note: cut into 4 filets, if not already done so

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 tortillas (flour, corn, whatever kind you like!)
ingredients.name: tortillas (flour, corn, whatever kind you like!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8- to 10-ounce) bag shredded cabbage or coleslaw
ingredients.name: shredded cabbage or coleslaw

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro leaves and stems
ingredients.name: finely chopped cilantro leaves and stems

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Cook the fish: Line a baking sheet with foil. Add 4 fish filets to the center of the baking sheet and drizzle with 2 tablespoons neutral oil, the juice of 1/2 a lime, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Toss to coat everything evenly. Spread the filets out so no fish is overlapping. Wrap a stack of 12 tortillas in foil and throw the tortillas (you can just place the foil right on the oven grate) and fish in the oven. Bake for 8 to 12 minutes. You’ll know the fish is done when you poke it with a fork and it flakes easily — the thinner your fish, the faster it’ll cook!

Make the slaw: To a large bowl, add 1 bag shredded cabbage/slaw and a pinch of kosher salt. Use your hands to massage the cabbage 7 times by scrunching it between your fists. This will soften it and allow it to absorb the flavors quickly. Add 2 thinly sliced peaches, 1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro, 2 tablespoons neutral oil, the juice of 1 lime, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Stir to combine, taste and adjust seasonings as needed, and set aside.

Make the chili lime sauce: In a small bowl, combine 1/2 cup mayo, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, a big pinch of kosher salt, and the juice of 1/2 lime. Taste and adjust seasoning as desired!
Flake your fish filets right on the baking sheet. Pile your warm tortillas with fish, slaw, and sauce!

name: one-pot pasta alla norma

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
ingredients.name: plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups pearl couscous or orzo pasta
ingredients.name: pearl couscous or orzo pasta

preparationSteps: Peel 1 eggplant like a zebra then cut it into 1/2-inch cubes. Warm 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil in a wide skillet or saucepan over medium-high heat, then add the eggplant and 1 teaspoon kosher salt and toss to coat. Cook, stirring every minute or so, until very tender and browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer the eggplant to a bowl.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat and warm 1 tablespoon oil. Add 1 pound mild Italian sausage and cook, using a wooden spoon to break it into small crumbles, until almost cooked through. Meanwhile, mince 4 garlic cloves. Add the garlic to the sausage, then continue cooking until the sausage is cooked through.

Add the cooked eggplant and 2 cups pearl couscous and stir for several minutes to toast the couscous a bit. Stir in 1 (28 ounce) jar marinara sauce, 2 1/2 cups water, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Continue cooking over medium-high for several minutes, until the liquid reaches a boil-like consistency, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until the pasta is tender.
Meanwhile, grate your Parmesan if needed (break it into chunks and throw it in the blender!) and thinly slice 1 packed cup fresh basil leaves.
Stir in 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese and most of the basil (leave some out for garnish).
Serve the pasta with a sprinkle of Parm, basil, and red pepper flakes if you’re into those.

name: jalapeño pork chops

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons honey, divided, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: honey, divided, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 bone-in pork chops about 1/2- to 3/4-inch thick
ingredients.name: bone-in pork chops about 1/2- to 3/4-inch thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds watermelon, cut into bite-size pieces and chilled (pre-cut, or one 3- to 4-pound mini seedless watermelon)If you bought a whole melon, store it in the fridge so that it’s chilled before you cut it!
ingredients.name: watermelon
ingredients.note: cut into bite-size pieces and chilled (pre-cut, or one 3- to 4-pound mini seedless watermelon)If you bought a whole melon, store it in the fridge so that it’s chilled before you cut it!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 English cucumber, zebra-striped and cut into bite-size pieces
ingredients.name: English cucumber, zebra-striped and cut into bite-size pieces

preparationSteps: Start by making the marinade: In a food processor, add 1 1/2 cups basil, 1/4 cup olive oil, 4 peeled garlic cloves, 2 jalapeños (stems and seeds removed and discarded first!), 1 teaspoon honey, the zest and juice of half a lemon, and 2 teaspoons salt. Buzz until well combined.

Transfer the marinade to a large bowl or resealable container (like a gallon-sized Ziploc). Add 4 bone-in pork chops and turn them over to coat. Marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes while you heat the grill, or in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours.
Heat your grill to high heat (450°F to 500°F).

While it’s heating, chop your produce. If you’re working with a 3- to 4-pound mini seedless watermelon, cut the whole thing into bite-sized pieces using this method. If you have pre-sliced watermelon, you may still need to chop it a bit to make bite-sized pieces. Peel 1 English cucumber like a zebra (AKA make it look striped) and cut it into bite-sized pieces. If your produce isn’t already chilled, transfer the chopped pieces to a bowl and pop it in the fridge while you grill.

Back to the grill: Grab a couple paper towels and wad them up into a ball. Soak the paper towels with several tablespoons of oil — any kind, you can use the cheapest oil you have. Now that the grill is piping hot, use your grill brush to get those grates completely clean. Preheating it for so long allowed all the crap that was stuck on there from last time you grilled to turn to ash and be easily scraped away. Now, grab the ball of oily paper towels with a long pair of tongs and use it to grease the grates.

Grill the pork chops with the marinade on them over direct heat, covered, for 3 to 5 minutes, until they lift easily off the grill grate and are browned on the bottom. Flip and cook for another 3 to 5 minutes, again until they lift easily, are browned on the bottom, and reach 145°F internally. Transfer the pork chops to a cutting board to rest for at least 5 minutes.

While the pork chops rest, let’s make the salad. In a big bowl, stir together the zest and juice of 1 lemon, the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, the remaining 1 teaspoon honey, and 1 teaspoon salt. Add the chopped watermelon and cucumber and stir gently to combine. The flavor will depend on the ripeness of your watermelon, so taste the salad and add more honey, salt, and lemon if needed until it’s delicious. Top with 4 ounces crumbled feta and the remaining 1/4 cup basil leaves.
Serve the salad alongside the pork chops. Dig in!!

name: chicken parm burgers with baked sweet potato fries
note:
Make ahead: Form the patties and refrigerate them, covered, on the baking sheet for up to 48 hours. Same goes for the fries.

Freezer friendly: Burgers are a great stock-the-freezer meal! Go ahead and cook the extra patties to make reheating easier. Once cool, wrap them individually in plastic wrap or tin foil and store in an airtight container (or you can pop them individually in sandwich-bag size Ziplocs). Thaw them in the fridge for a few hours before mealtime, then cook them as directed above.

Special ingredient: Yep, sun-dried tomatoes 2 weeks in a row! If you missed it, we also used them in last week’s one-skillet chicken and orzo.

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy a bag of frozen sweet potato fries. Skip the tomato mayo and go for straight up mayo and ketchup instead.

Make it into meatballs: Make 8 to 10 meatballs with the same mixture. Bake at 425°F for 10 to 15 minutes or until 165°F internally.

Vegetarian: Use 1 pound of Impossible Burger or other plant-based meat!

Dairy-free: Use Mykonos dairy-free Parmesan. It’s great!

Gluten-free: Make a lettuce bun by chopping the sides off of a head of iceberg lettuce and using that as the bun!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes (dry or oil-packed — just squeeze out the oil if using oil packed kind)
ingredients.name: finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes (dry or oil-packed — just squeeze out the oil if using oil packed kind)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup finely chopped fresh basil (or 2 teaspoons dried basil)
ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh basil (or 2 teaspoons dried basil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: mozzarella (melt on top if you want more cheese!), thinly sliced red onion, romaine leaves with the tough rib stripped out, etc.
ingredients.name: Optional: mozzarella (melt on top if you want more cheese!), thinly sliced red onion, romaine leaves with the tough rib stripped out, etc.

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F and place your largest rimmed baking sheet in the oven.

Cut 2 large sweet potatoes into long 1/2 inch-thick rectangles (fry shape!). Toss the cut potatoes, 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika in a large bowl. That’s right — no salt yet! Salt draws out moisture and we don’t want that! Set aside for now.

In another large bowl, combine 1 pound ground chicken or turkey, 1 large egg, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/4 cup finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes, 1/4 cup finely chopped fresh basil, 1 tablespoon tomato paste, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/8 teaspoon black pepper, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Divide the meat into 4 equal patties that are slightly wider than your burger buns (that way when they shrink while cooking they’ll become the perfect size!).
Bake the sweet potato fries on the lowest oven rack for 15 minutes, then flip the fries (yep — this is a pain, but worth it) and bake for an additional 10 minutes. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt.

To grill burgers: Refrigerate the patties for at least 10 minutes before grilling. Preheat the grill to 400°F. Clean the grill grates very well. Spray the tops of the burgers with cooking spray and place them on the grill, sprayed-side-down. Close the lid and cook for 4 minutes. Spray the tops of the burgers carefully (don’t spray the flames with oil — bad plan!) and flip them over. Cover and cook for an additional 4 minutes. Smear a light layer of mayo on the cut sides of the burger buns. Remove the burgers and quickly toast your burger buns on the grate for about 1 minute with the grill lid open. Watch them CLOSELY! Buns like to burn.

To bake: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Place the patties on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until cooked through. They will look FUNKY — lots of liquid will ooze out. Don’t worry, that’s normal! Once your fries are finished baking, quickly broil your burger buns by spreading a thin layer of mayo on the cut sides, placing them cut-side up on a baking sheet, and broiling for 1 to 2 minutes. Sit on your butt and watch them closely — again, buns BURN QUICKLY!

To pan-fry: Heat your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for several minutes. Add 1 tablespoon cooking oil and swirl to coat the pan. Cook the burgers for 2 to 3 minutes per side (you can probably only cook 1 or 2 at a time… hence why baking is an easier option).

Meanwhile, make the tomato mayo by stirring together 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes, 2 tablespoons tomato paste, and the juice of 1/2 lemon (about 1 tablespoon). Season with salt to taste.

Smear the mayo on both sides of the toasted bun. Throw a burger patty (or two!) on there. Sprinkle with a bit of Parm and top with whatever toppings you’re feeling. I like mine with just tomato mayo. Devour.
servings: Serves 2 to 4(Sometimes I eat two burger patties, sometimes I eat one. Each burger is about 3 ounces of cooked meat.)

name: scallops with succotash
note:
What’s a neutral cooking oil again??? Avocado, grapeseed, sunflower, olive oil — these all have high smoke points and can be used interchangeably based on what’s in your pantry. Important to note: Extra-virgin olive oil is not on that list because it’s not a neutral cooking oil.

Watch that clock! I’ve written my cook times carefully. Scallops cook quickly and become chewy when overcooked. Get your spatula and spoon ready ahead of time and be ready to flip!

Prep your scallops: Most scallops come ready to eat, but you may notice that your scallops have a tough little flap on the side. That’s a muscle, and you can easily remove it by gently pulling it.

Vegetarian: This succotash recipe is packed with protein as written — enjoy it as a main course! It’d also be great alongside veggie burgers, or with some feta or goat cheese sprinkled over top.

Gluten-free/dairy-free: Already gluten free. For dairy free, use df butter in lieu of regular.

Make ahead: You can make the succotash entirely ahead of time! Go ahead and knock that out, then just gently reheat it in a skillet when you’re ready for dinner. Cook the scallops just before eating — they only take a couple minutes!

Leftovers are a good thing: If you’re cooking for 1 or 2 and don’t want leftovers, you could easily halve this recipe. But you could also go ahead and cook as written and enjoy leftovers for lunches! Store leftover succotash and scallops separately in airtight containers for up to two days. Skip the microwave; the best way to reheat scallops is in the oven or on the stovetop.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small white or yellow onion, diced
ingredients.name: small white or yellow onion

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 large ears of white corn, kernels removed (or 1 pound of frozen white corn)
ingredients.name: of white corn, kernels removed (or 1 pound of frozen white corn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-oz.) can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: cannellini beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound fresh jumbo scallops (10 to 20 scallops per pound) —NOT bay scallops which are small and rubbery and yucky IMO
ingredients.name: fresh jumbo scallops —NOT bay scallops which are small and rubbery and yucky IMO

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Place 1 pound scallops on a paper towel, cover with another paper towel, and press gently to remove all moisture.

Warm 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot or saucepan or skillet (reserve your best nonstick skillet for cooking the scallops later) over medium heat. Cook 1 diced yellow onion, 1 diced red bell pepper, and 2 minced garlic cloves for about 5 minutes, until tender. Add the kernels from 4 ears of corn and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Stir in 1 drained and rinsed can of cannellini beans, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper and continue stirring until the corn is crisp-tender, an additional 4 to 5 minutes. Remove the skillet from heat.
Stir in 1/4 cup thinly sliced basil leaves and the juice of 1/2 lemon. Taste. Season with more salt and pepper if needed!
MEANWHILE, while the corn is cooking…
Season the scallops with a big pinch of salt and pepper. The exact amount is not important here, just lightly coat each scallop on both sides.
Warm your largest nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for at least 3 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon cooking oil and swirl to coat the pan. Let the oil heat up for at least 30 seconds.

Place the scallops in the skillet at least 1 inch apart. You might have to cook two batches. Use a spatula to press them firmly down into the skillet to ensure a nice sear. Cook until golden-brown, for 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook on the second side for 1 minute, then add 2 tablespoons butter to the pan. Tilt the skillet to the side and use a large spoon to spoon the melted butter all over the scallops. Cook for 2 additional minutes once you’ve added the butter. Remove the skillet from the heat.

Divide the succotash between 4 plates. Top with seared scallops. Drizzle any melted butter remaining in the skillet over top. Garnish with a bit of thinly sliced basil and freshly ground black pepper.
Freak out — you just made restaurant-worthy scallops at HOME!

name: boudreaux gumbo
note:
Do your thing: If you read the headnote, you know that there is not one right way to make gumbo. If you hate okra, skip it. If you’re not into or can’t eat tomatoes, leave the tomato sauce out. You can choose whichever protein — or which combination of proteins — you want to use: chicken, sausage, and/or shrimp (or others like shredded turkey or crab meat!). It’ll be great any way you cook it!

Vegetarian: Thinly sliced vegan sausage. Mushrooms would also be great. King oyster mushrooms can be shredded (Google how to do this, it’s so cool and looks just like shredded chicken) and incorporated. Or just use chopped or thinly sliced baby Bella or white mushrooms. I would sauté mushrooms in oil in a skillet to let them release and absorb their liquid and cook down first, then add them to the pot for the last 10 minutes or so of cooking. Or you could just incorporate more vegetables, adding cauliflower florets to the mix (sauté them along with the “Holy Trinity”), and maybe some chopped kale or collard greens (add them for the last 10 minutes of cooking).

Make your own Cajun seasoning: First of all, you could swap Cajun seasoning with Creole seasoning. These spice blends have a lot of overlap in spices, though Cajun has a little more of a kick. You could also make your own Cajun seasoning using spices you probably already have in your spice cabinet. Make 1 tablespoon of Cajun seasoning by mixing 1 teaspoon paprika, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt.

Prep ahead: You can pre-chop your “holy trinity” veggies and okra and store them in airtight containers in the fridge for up to a day ahead of time. Or, go ahead and cook the whole thing the day before and store it in the fridge, covered, in the pot you cooked it in.

Feeding kids: This gumbo isn’t spicy spicy, but there’s a bit of a kick from the Cajun seasoning and Andouille sausage. If you’re trying to feed this to kids, you could use kielbasa sausage, which is mild, and cut back a bit on the Cajun seasoning. If it’s still “too spicy!!” stir some sour cream or Greek yogurt or POTATO SALAD! into their bowls to negate it.

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. Reheat on the stove over medium heat (or in the microwave), adding more broth, stock, or water if needed for it to return to your favorite consistency. Leftover gumbo could also be frozen in Souper cubes or quart-sized Ziploc bags for future meals! Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use a plant-based butter or oil for your roux instead of butter. Vegetable oil, peanut oil, avocado oil, olive oil — these or any neutral cooking oil would work. To make your gumbo gluten-free, use a gluten-free 1:1 all-purpose flour or fine sweet sorghum flour instead of regular all-purpose flour.

What do I serve this with? I always go with cooked white or brown rice. I highly recommend stirring a pat or two (so like a tablespoon) of butter into your cooked rice to make it extra delicious. You can also eat gumbo by itself, or with bread or a side of cornbread, or, apparently, potato salad!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs (raw), white skin trimmed off and each thigh cut in half
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs (raw), white skin trimmed off and each thigh cut in half

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Cajun seasoning (see notes if you can’t find/don’t want to buy any)
ingredients.name: Cajun seasoning (see notes if you can’t find/don’t want to buy any)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 quarts (8 cups) low-sodium chicken stock (or 8 cups water + 3 tablespoons low-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or 8 cups water + 3 tablespoons low-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound fresh okra, sliced 1/4-inch thick on the diagonal (or a bag of pre-sliced frozen okra)
ingredients.name: fresh okra, sliced 1/4-inch thick on the diagonal (or a bag of pre-sliced frozen okra)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound andouille sausage links, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: andouille sausage links

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional, for serving: Cooked white rice, thinly sliced scallions, hot sauce (ideallyCrystal)
ingredients.name: Optional, for serving: Cooked white rice, thinly sliced scallions, hot sauce (ideallyCrystal)

preparationSteps: Melt 1 stick unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in 3/4 cup all-purpose flour and turn the heat down to medium-low. You're going to cook this roux (butter plus flour mixture), stirring often, for about 30 minutes, until it deepens to a rich brown color (set a timer for 30 minutes so you don’t forget!).

While your roux is browning, dice 1 large yellow onion, 3 celery ribs, and 1 red bell pepper. Mince 4 garlic cloves. Trim the fat off of 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs and cut each thigh in half. When the roux is a dark brown color, stir in the onion, celery, bell pepper, and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Stir in 1 tablespoon Cajun seasoning, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1 tablespoon tomato paste and cook, stirring, for an additional 1 minute.Stir in 8 cups low-sodium chicken stock and 1 (14-ounce) can of tomato sauce and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to medium and add the prepped chicken thighs and 2 bay leaves. Cook, uncovered, for 15 minutes.
While that’s cooking, slice 1 pound fresh okra into 1/4 inch-thick slices on the diagonal, and thinly slice 1 pound of andouille sausage.
Add the sliced okra and sausage and cook for an additional 15 minutes, or until the okra is tender.
With the gumbo still over medium heat, remove the chicken thighs and use two forks to shred them (or just use a knife to chop them up, if this feels tedious to you!).
Stir the chicken back in. Fish out the 2 bay leaves and discard them.

Now taste and season! You might need a lot of kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, you might need only a little — this will depend on your stock and how much salt is in your Cajun seasoning. The trick is to season a tiny bit at a time until things are really delicious! Serve over white rice — or just in a bowl by itself — with hot sauce on the side, preferably Crystal. Garnish with thinly sliced scallions if you feel like it. Dig in!!

name: black pepper pork chops with ramen noodle veggie salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh lime juice plus 2 teaspoons lime zest (from 2 limes)
ingredients.name: fresh lime juice plus 2 teaspoons lime zest (from 2 limes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 (3-ounce) packages instant ramen noodles, seasoning packets removed
ingredients.name: instant ramen noodles, seasoning packets removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small red onion, halved and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: small red onion

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup packed mint, cilantro, and/or basil leaves
ingredients.name: packed mint, cilantro, and/or basil leaves

preparationSteps: Heat your grill to medium-high. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Meanwhile, zest 2 limes and set the zest aside for later (it’s easier to zest them now vs. after they’ve been juiced!).

In a large bowl, whisk together the juice from those 2 limes, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup neutral oil, 1/3 cup packed brown sugar, and 2 finely grated garlic cloves (you can use your microplane to grate them straight into the bowl!). Keep whisking until the sugar is totally dissolved.

Transfer 1/2 cup of the dressing to a shallow dish and stir in 1 tablespoon black pepper. Using a fork, pierce 2 (12-ounce) bone-in pork chops all over on both sides, then place them in the shallow dish. Let the pork chops marinate at room temperature, turning occasionally, while you make the noodle salad.

Remove (and discard) the seasoning packet from 3 (3-ounce) packages instant ramen noodles. Add the noodles to the boiling water and cook, stirring occasionally, until just tender, about 3 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water, then drain again. Keep the pot out! We’re going to use it again later to make a glaze.

Add the cooked noodles to the large bowl with the dressing along with the reserved lime zest. Halve and thinly slice 1 small red onion, and thinly slice 4 radishes. Add them to the bowl along with 1 (10- to 12-ounce) bag slaw blend. Toss well to coat everything in the dressing.
OK, it’s time to head to the grill!
Now that they’re hot, clean the grill grates with your grill brush.

Shake off as much of the marinade as possible (but DON’T throw the marinade away!!), add the pork chops to the grill, and close the lid. Flip them occasionally, keeping the lid closed between flips, and cook until they are browned, release easily from the grill grate, and are 145°F internally — this will take about 10 to 12 minutes of total grilling time.
Transfer the pork chops to a cutting board to rest for at least 5 minutes.
While they rest, transfer the pork marinade to the large pot and bring it to a simmer over medium-high heat. Keep cooking, whisking occasionally, until it has reduced by half, 2 to 3 minutes.

Toss 1 cup packed mint, cilantro, and/or basil leaves into the noodle salad and season to taste with salt and pepper. Slice up the pork chops and brush with the glaze. Serve with the noodle salad. DIG IN!

name: sweet and spicy grilled chicken and onions (and grilled apricots with halloumi and basil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large onion (I used white, but anything works), sliced into 1/2 inch-thick rounds
ingredients.name: large onion (I used white, but anything works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 sprigs of fresh basil, leaves plucked off and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: of fresh basil, leaves plucked off and thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 8 thighs)
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 8 thighs)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) package halloumi (sometimes called grilling cheese), sliced into 8 pieces*lots of subs below — if you can’t find it, don’t stress!
ingredients.name: halloumi (sometimes called grilling cheese)
ingredients.note: sliced into 8 pieces*lots of subs below — if you can’t find it, don’t stress!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound apricots (or any stone fruit!), halved and pitted
ingredients.name: apricots (or any stone fruit!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup red pepper jelly*lots of subs below — if you can’t find it, don’t stress!
ingredients.name: red pepper jelly*lots of subs below — if you can’t find it, don’t stress!

preparationSteps: Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high heat (400°F to 450°F).
Prep the ingredients:

Cut the ends off of 1 large onion, then thinly slice through the papery skin to help you peel it off. Slice into 1/2 inch-thick rounds. Place in a large bowl. Pull the leaves from 2 sprigs fresh basil and thinly slice. Set aside.

Add 2 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs to the bowl and toss with 1 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil. Really get in there with your hands to get the oil and seasonings evenly dispersed. Let rest at room temperature while we prep the other ingredients (or throw it in the fridge, covered, for up to 72 hours).

Cut 2 lemons in half. Slice 1 (8-ounce) block of halloumi into 8 pieces. Halve 1 pound of apricots and discard the stones. Place the lemons, halloumi, and apricots on a large, pretty platter and drizzle with a light coating of extra-virgin olive oil, then sprinkle a touch of kosher salt onto the apricots.
Prep the grill:

Grab a couple paper towels and wad them up into a ball. Soak the paper towels with several tablespoons of oil — any kind, you can use the cheapest oil you have. Grab the ball with a long pair of tongs.

Now that the grill is piping hot, use your grill brush to get those grates completely clean. Preheating it for so long allowed all the crap that was stuck on there from last time you grilled to turn to ash and be easily scraped away. Now use your oily paper towels to grease every single grill grate until glistening.
Close the grill and let it heat back up.
Grill:

If you have a grill large enough to cook everything at one time, hooray for you! Throw it all on there and time it appropriately. But I’m assuming most of us have 2- to 3-burner grills, so I’ve written the grilling in phases.

To the grill, add the halved lemons cut-side down, onion slices, and chicken smooth-side down (one side will be smooth, one side will be a bit mangled from where they cut out the bone). Cook for 5 minutes, then flip the chicken and cook for an additional 4. Check on the lemons, pull them off when they’ve got nice grill marks. Brush a generous amount of red pepper jelly over the smooth side of each piece of chicken. Note: this is not a perfect process. Some might slide off, just do your best! If you don’t have a brush, use a spoon to spoon it and smear it. Close the lid and let cook for an additional 1 minute.

Use your meat thermometer to check that the chicken has reached 165°F. Once it has, transfer the chicken, and onions if they feel really nice and tender, to a serving platter and cover with foil (or any lid / plate). If the onions aren’t nice and tender yet, continue cooking them for 1 to 2 more minutes until they are, then transfer them to the platter too.
Close the grill lid and let it get really hot again, then use your grill brush to get the grates totally clean.

Now let’s tackle the apricots and halloumi! Grill both the apricots and halloumi for 2 to 4 minutes per side, until there are nice grill marks on both sides and the apricots get nice and jammy. Transfer to the serving platter you brought them out on.

Squeeze 1 grilled lemon half and sprinkle the sliced basil over the apricots and halloumi. Squeeze 1 grilled lemon half over the chicken and onions, then serve together IMMEDIATELY. Seriously, grilled halloumi is delicious for about 15 minutes, and then it gets hard and weird and rubbery. Enjoy it right away!

name: one-pot crispy chicken and orzo

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons fresh oregano leaves (or 1 1/2 teaspoons dried)
ingredients.name: fresh oregano leaves (or 1 1/2 teaspoons dried)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Season 4 to 6 chicken thighs with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon ground pepper per thigh.

Place chicken thighs skin-side down in a room temperature 12-inch ovenproof skillet or Dutch oven. Place the skillet over medium heat and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the skin is crispy and golden-brown. You might have to cook the chicken in two batches — you don’t want the thighs to touch as you’re cooking them. Transfer chicken to a holding plate.
Stir in 1 diced yellow onion and cook over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until tender. Stir in 1 cup orzo and 4 minced garlic cloves and cook for an additional minute.

Stir in 1/2 cup white wine and scrape the bottom of the pan to get up any stuck bits. When it is completely absorbed, stir in 2 1/2 cups chicken stock, 1/2 cup chopped sun-dried tomatoes, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 2 tablespoons fresh oregano leaves, and 1/2 cup halved olives.
Place the chicken on top of the orzo and roast, uncovered, for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken has reached 165°F internally and the orzo is tender and has absorbed all of the liquid.
Allow everything to rest for 5 minutes. Stir more salt and pepper into the orzo if needed.
Scatter the 1/2 cup crumbled feta and 1/2 cup thinly sliced basil over top and dig in.

name: salmon tempura crunch bowls
note:
Make ahead: This is a great meal to prep little by little as you’re able. You can do pretty much everything except dress the greens and cook the salmon up to a day ahead of time! Store all the different elements (sriracha mayo, greens and things, rice, sesame butter panko) in separate airtight containers in the fridge. Just don’t spread the panko mixture on the salmon until you’re ready to bake it. And wait until you’re ready to serve the greens to dress them so they don’t get soggy.

Love your leftovers: Store your leftovers in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 4 days. (The sriracha mayo will be good for weeks!) Reheat the salmon in the oven so it gets nice and crispy again — 400F for 5 minutes should be perfect. You could also freeze the cooked salmon and any leftover rice.

Cooking for 1 or 2? Halve it! If you’re cooking for 1, you’ll have delicious leftovers for lunch tomorrow (and maybe the next day too!).

Feeding kids: If they’re sensitive to spice, omit the sriracha from the recipe and just top your bowl with it.

Vegetarian: Make tempura tofu! Place a cube of extra-firm tofu between two clean towels and put something heavy on top (like a cast-iron skillet) for 15 minutes to drain excess water. Slice the block into 1/2 inch-thick planks. Season and marinate them just like the salmon, add the tempura topping, and bake until the tofu and panko breading are firm and crispy, roughly 20-25 minutes.

Dairy-free: Use dairy-free butter throughout the recipe.

Gluten-free: Use tamari or coconut aminos instead of soy sauce and gluten-free breadcrumbs.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups brown rice (or just buy frozen rice — I’m really into ease right now!)
ingredients.name: brown rice (or just buy frozen rice — I’m really into ease right now!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds salmon, skin on or off (I like farmed Atlantic, even though I know it’s not as nutritious or as good for the environment — sorry! It tastes better!)
ingredients.name: salmon, skin on or off (I like farmed Atlantic, even though I know it’s not as nutritious or as good for the environment — sorry! It tastes better!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon maple syrup or brown sugar
ingredients.name: maple syrup or brown sugar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 ounces mixed greens (that’s the size of standard box of greens!)
ingredients.name: mixed greens (that’s the size of standard box of greens!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 English cucumber, cut in half then thinly sliced into half moons
ingredients.name: English cucumber
ingredients.note: cut in half then thinly sliced into half moons

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional additions: thinly sliced apple or persimmon, thinly sliced fennel or red onion, thinly sliced scallions, peanuts
ingredients.name: Optional additions: thinly sliced apple or persimmon, thinly sliced fennel or red onion, thinly sliced scallions, peanuts

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add 1 1/2 cups brown rice and boil it just like pasta until tender, about 40 minutes. Drain, then return the rice to the pot and stir in 2 tablespoons butter and a big pinch of salt. Cover until dinnertime.
While the rice is cooking, work on everything else!
Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Sprinkle 1 1/2 pounds salmon with 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon ginger powder, then rub with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha (1 will not make it spicy, it’ll just flavor it, add another for heat!), 1 tablespoon sesame oil, and 1 tablespoon maple syrup. If your salmon has skin, place it skin-side down on the parchment-lined baking sheet.

In a medium bowl, melt 2 tablespoons butter in the microwave. Add 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1/4 cup panko breadcrumbs, 3 tablespoons sesame seeds, and a big pinch of salt. Roughly chop up 1 bunch of cilantro (the entire thing — leaves and stems!). Separate 1/3 cup of the chopped cilantro, finely dice it, and add it to the panko. Set the rest of the chopped cilantro aside for the salad. Stir the breadcrumb mixture until all is well combined and the panko is coated in butter and oil.
Spread the breadcrumbs over the top of the salmon. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the salmon easily flakes when you prod at it with a fork.
While the salmon is cooking, make the greens and sriracha mayo.

Throw 5 ounces mixed greens into a large bowl along with the rest of the chopped cilantro, then slice up 1/2 a halved English cucumber really thinly (you’re aiming for half moon shapes) and throw it in there too. Add the juice of 1 large lime, 2 tablespoons sesame oil, and a big pinch of salt. Toss to coat the greens. Taste. Want it zingier? More lime juice or any vinegar! I usually add several more pinches of salt when I do simple dressings like this. Maybe some pepper too if you’re feeling wild.
Now make the sriracha mayo by stirring together 1/2 cup mayo, 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha, the juice of 1/2 lime, and a small pinch of salt. Taste and add more sriracha if you want it spicier.

Now set everything out (the buttery brown rice, salmon, bowl of dressed greens, sriracha mayo, and any or all optional additions) and let your eaters build their own bowls! If hosting a lunch or dinner, I like to make an example bowl so that your guests understand what to do. I like for the base of my bowl to be rice on one side, greens on the other side, with the salmon on top drizzled with sriracha mayo.
Yum. Enjoy!

name: healthy-ish turkey bolognese
note:
I’m feeling healthy, not healthy-ish: Omit the Parmesan; use whole milk instead of half and half or omit it completely; use brown rice pasta, hearts of palm noodles, or zoodles in lieu of traditional pasta. If you’re opting for zoodles or hearts of palm noodles, cook them directly in the sauce, exactly as this recipe is written for tossing the cooked pasta with the sauce, pasta water, and cheese.

I want a more traditional bolognese: Instead of the 2 pounds of ground turkey, use 1 pound ground pork and 1 pound ground beef. Omit the cauliflower rice. Use heavy cream instead of half and half. There we go, now your nonna is proud!

I don’t want this much food. If you’re not into stocking your freezer for some reason, just halve the recipe! Use 1 (14-ounce) can diced tomatoes and 1 (14-ounce) can tomato sauce. The rest is easy to halve. You’ll still have enough bolognese for 1 pound of pasta.

GF: Any GF pasta is great here!

DF: Use 3/4 cup almond milk or cashew milk. Also, use dairy-free Parmesan or just omit it completely.

Whole30: Use zoodles, another spiralized veggie, or hearts of palm noodles. Follow the “feeling healthy” note above, but cut the dairy completely, swapping it for 1 cup of broth or stock (or some water if you have neither).

I need a salad to pull me out of my January blues: Check my Mango Peanut Chicken Salad. This one is so flavorful, crisp, crunchy, healthy, and delightful! You could serve it alongside this sans the chicken… or just eat it for dinner tonight (it’s a quick one!) and save the bolognese for later this week. Another fine option: The Greatest Kale Salad (without chicken, if you’re serving as a side).

How to store your leftovers: You can either use Tupperware — a size in which you don’t have excess space/air left — or a gallon-sized Ziploc! If you’re feeding 1 or 2 people instead of 4, store it in smaller bags for multiple days worth of freezer meals!

I forgot to reserve the pasta water: Can’t say I’ve never done it! If you’re short on time, just use hot tap water. If you have the time, mix 1/4 teaspoon each of cornstarch and kosher salt into one cup of water and bring it to a boil. Cut the heat and it’s ready to use.

Vegetarian: You’ve got options!You can make a lentil bolognese by adding 4 cups of red lentils at the same time as the canned tomatoes, then simmering until thickened, 30 to 45 minutes. You could also swap the meat for diced mushrooms. If you’re cooking the whole recipe, use 2 (16-ounce) containers of white or baby bellas finely diced. Cook them with the celery, carrots, etc. until all the moisture has been released and evaporated before adding the tomato ingredients. Last option: Use a plant-based ground beef substitute like Beyond Beef or Impossible brands. Cook it like you would the meat.

You can make a lentil bolognese by adding 4 cups of red lentils at the same time as the canned tomatoes, then simmering until thickened, 30 to 45 minutes.

You could also swap the meat for diced mushrooms. If you’re cooking the whole recipe, use 2 (16-ounce) containers of white or baby bellas finely diced. Cook them with the celery, carrots, etc. until all the moisture has been released and evaporated before adding the tomato ingredients.
