ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 medium carrots, washed (no need to peel) and trimmed
ingredients.name: medium carrots, washed (no need to peel) and trimmed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg (you can omit this if you don’t already own it)
ingredients.name: ground nutmeg (you can omit this if you don’t already own it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup half and half (or 1 1/2 cups whole milk, or 1 cup heavy cream)
ingredients.name: half and half (or 1 1/2 cups whole milk, or 1 cup heavy cream)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1 lemon (you can omit this if zesting a lemon sounds annoying to you right now, but it adds a nice freshness!)
ingredients.name: Zest of 1 lemon (you can omit this if zesting a lemon sounds annoying to you right now, but it adds a nice freshness!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound pasta (I like a tubular pasta like rigatoni, penne, or radiatori for bolognese, but spaghetti or fettuccine are traditional!)
ingredients.name: pasta (I like a tubular pasta like rigatoni, penne, or radiatori for bolognese, but spaghetti or fettuccine are traditional!)

preparationSteps: Cut 2 medium carrots, 3 celery stalks, and 1 medium yellow onion into 3 or 4 pieces each and throw them in a food processor or blender along with 4 garlic cloves. Pulse until very finely diced. (If you have neither a food processor nor a blender, you can finely dice them all by hand.)

Melt 2 tablespoons butter (or oil) in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. I actually used my 14-inch skillet — the more surface area, the better! Add the diced vegetables and 1 tablespoon dried oregano, 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes, and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg and cook, stirring often, for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 2 pounds ground turkey and cook, chopping into tiny crumbles, until cooked through and all moisture has evaporated, 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir in 28 ounces tomato puree, 28 ounces diced tomatoes, 16 ounces cauliflower rice, 4 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 cup half and half, and the zest of 1 lemon until combined.

Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 30 minutes to 3 hours. It will be best after 3 hours (the meat will become super tender!), but it will still be absolutely delicious if you only have 30 minutes.

20 minutes before you’re ready to eat, boil 1 pound of rigatoni in heavily salted water. Cook until al dente. Seriously, the pasta should still have a “bite” to it — aka feel uncooked in the center. We’re going to keep cooking it!

Scoop 1 cup of pasta cooking water out of the pot and reserve it. Drain the pasta in a colander and return it to the empty pot. Stir 4 cups of the bolognese, 1/2 cup pasta cooking water, and 1/2 cup grated Parmesan into the pasta over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until the pasta is cooked to your liking and the sauce has thickened and is sticking to the pasta. You might need to add another splash of pasta cooking water to get the perfect consistency. Taste before serving — you might want to add more cheese, more salt, more pepper! Do your thing! Make it your own!
Divide the pasta between 4 to 6 bowls and top with more grated Parmesan.
Buon appetito!

name: sheet-pan chicken and squash
note:
Prep ahead: Slice and chop all your fruits and veggies up to a day in advance, storing them in the fridge (covered). Apples do best sliced right before cooking, but it’s not a big deal if they brown a bit before you roast them. You could also pre-mix your marinade and store it covered in the bowl that you’ll add the squash and onions to when you’re ready to cook!

Make it a side dish: This is honestly a stunning Thanksgiving or anytime side dish. Just omit the chicken!

Make it a salad: Serve it over a big bed of arugula tossed with EVOO and lemon juice or my apple cider vinaigrette. Done! Salad! So good!

Love your leftovers: See the salad note above! Or skip the salad idea and just reheat the meal (in the microwave or oven) and eat it like you did the first go-round. If you plan to have leftovers, just add the parsley and pomegranate seeds to the portion you’re going to eat tonight, then add them just before eating your leftovers, after you’ve warmed them. If you don’t want leftovers and are cooking for one or two, you can easily halve this recipe.

Have less clean up: If you want to avoid having to wash your sheet pan(s), you can line them with parchment paper before adding the ingredients. Your food won’t brown as well as without parchment, but it will still be delish.

Vegetarian: Instead of chicken, use a can of rinsed and dried chickpeas, roasted the entire time with the squash.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use a favorite soft and melty dairy-free cheese alternative or just omit for df! And this is a gluten-free meal as written.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves or 1 teaspoon dried thyme leaves
ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves or 1 teaspoon dried thyme leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs (look inside the package — you want at least 1 1/2 thighs per person, so you might need more than 2 pounds!)
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs (look inside the package — you want at least 1 1/2 thighs per person, so you might need more than 2 pounds!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large Honeycrisp apple, chopped into 1/2 inch pieces
ingredients.name: large Honeycrisp apple

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup halved and pitted dates (preferably Medjools but any kind works)
ingredients.name: halved and pitted dates (preferably Medjools but any kind works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley (or any soft green herb, or arugula)
ingredients.name: chopped fresh parsley (or any soft green herb, or arugula)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds, AKA arils (optional — if you can’t find pomegranate seeds at your store, don’t worry about buying one and taking the seeds out, that’s too much work for a sheet-pan meal!)
ingredients.name: pomegranate seeds, AKA arils (optional — if you can’t find pomegranate seeds at your store, don’t worry about buying one and taking the seeds out, that’s too much work for a sheet-pan meal!)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Trim the ends off of 2 small delicata squash and cut them in half vertically (AKA cut them from end to end). Use a large spoon to scrape the seeds out and discard them. Cut the squash into 1/2 inch-thick half moons.

Trim the ends off 1 large yellow onion and cut it in half, end to end. Peel the skins off, then cut the onion into 1 inch-thick wedges. The layers will fall apart — that’s OK, but, where possible, keep them together.
Go ahead and grab your 1 full or 2 half sheet pans, placing them on the counter beside a large bowl so that you don’t have to wash your hands between steps to go hunting for them in a second…

In a large bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 3 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 1/4 teaspoons garam masala, and 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger. Add the cut squash and onions and use clean hands to toss to combine.

Use your hands (don’t dump the bowl) to transfer the squash and onions to a full sheet pan (or 2 half sheet pans). Spread it out into an even layer so nothing is overlapping (do your best — a bit of overlapping won’t kill anyone). Don’t wash the bowl yet!
Place the sheet pan(s) on the center rung of your oven. Roast for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, add 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs and 1 sliced Honeycrisp apple to the bowl and toss to coat all in the marinade that’s left at the bottom of the bowl. If not much is left, drizzle a bit of oil, maple syrup, garam masala, and salt in there. Exact measurements are not even remotely important here — just a nice light coating.

After the squash and onions have roasted for 15 minutes, pull the sheet-pan out and dump the chicken and apples, 1/2 cup halved and pitted dates, and 1/2 cup walnut or pecan halves right on top. Use tongs to toss everything around with the squash, and then spread it back out into an even layer.
Roast for an additional 20 minutes.

Scatter your desired amount of goat cheese (I say go for the full 8 ounces, but you do you!) over top and return the sheet pan to the oven for an additional 1 to 2 minutes, until the goat cheese gets very soft and warm, but not totally melted.
Scatter 1/4 cup chopped parsley and 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds over top and serve immediately, straight off the sheet pan!

name: 30-minute chicken parm meatballs
note:
Save time: Skip the step where you roll the meatballs in panko. Doing that gives them the crispy “chicken parm” vibe that their name implies, but it’s totally optional and they’d be delish without it.

Gimme some greens: Here’s a simple side salad I make all the time: In a serving bowl, whisk together 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, the juice of 1 lemon, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Add 4 cups mixed greens or arugula and toss to combine. Throw in some nuts or seeds if you’ve got them (pepitas, sunflower seeds, or pistachios, etc.) for crunch and extra nutrients. I also typically add freshly grated Parm.

I/my kids hate marinara: Bake these meatballs without the sauce and use them as a protein in a salad or grain bowl instead. Or add them to a bowl of pesto noodles.

Make ahead: Form the meatballs up to a day ahead of time and store them in the fridge in an airtight container. Bake them when you’re getting ready to eat!

Freezer-friendly: You can freeze meatballs either raw or pre-cooked for up to 3 months. If you’re freezing them raw, lay the formed meatballs on a sheet pan lined with parchment paper or foil with an inch or so between each meatball. Pop the whole sheet pan in the freezer. Once they’re frozen, transfer them to an airtight container like a Ziploc bag. If you’re freezing cooked meatballs: bake them the full time but without the sauce. Let them cool completely them freeze them in an airtight container. Let them thaw in the fridge overnight then bake them with the sauce until cooked or warmed through.

Meatballs rock: Meatballs are one of the most reliably eaten proteins in my house. If you also love meatballs, here are some others to make next! Messy meatball sliders, chicken meatballs with lemon orzo, one-pot cheesy baked meatballs, and greek turkey meatballs with couscous and dill yogurt sauce. If you have What to Cook the book, you can also cook coconut curry chicken meatballs (p. 147) and pesto meatballs with tomato salad (p. 122).

Vegetarian: Use a plant-based ground meat alternative.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Omit the Parm or use a dairy-free sub, such as VioLife. Same with the mozzarella — omit or use a plant-based alternative. For gluten-free, use GF breadcrumbs!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs, plus more for rolling the meatballs
ingredients.name: panko breadcrumbs, plus more for rolling the meatballs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning (or 1 teaspoon each dried thyme, dried oregano, and dried parsley)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning (or 1 teaspoon each dried thyme, dried oregano, and dried parsley)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, finely chopped, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves, finely chopped, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 garlic cloves, grated, or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, grated, or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (24-ounce) jar marinara sauce (I love Rao’s Roasted Garlic Sauce)
ingredients.name: marinara sauce (I love Rao’s Roasted Garlic Sauce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces any mozzarella (ciliegine, shredded, burrata — you pick!)
ingredients.name: any mozzarella (ciliegine, shredded, burrata — you pick!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Something carby for serving — either a good loaf of French bread or sourdough, 1 pound of cooked noodles (any type or shape!), or cooked cauliflower rice
ingredients.name: Something carby for serving — either a good loaf of French bread or sourdough, 1 pound of cooked noodles (any type or shape!), or cooked cauliflower rice

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Place 1 pound ground chicken, 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan, 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 cup finely chopped basil, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 1 egg in a large bowl. Beat the egg with a fork, then use your hands to combine all of the ingredients.
Spray the inside of a 10-inch oven-proof skillet all over with cooking spray and set aside.

Pour about 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs into a shallow bowl or plate. Form 10 meatballs out of the chicken mixture, roll each one through the panko to coat them in breadcrumbs (add more breadcrumbs to the plate if needed to coat them all!), and place them in the oiled skillet. Spray with cooking spray, or drizzle with oil.

Bake the meatballs for 15 minutes. Remove the skillet from the oven and pour 1 (24-ounce) jar marinara sauce into the skillet around the meatballs so they’re nestled in the sauce. Be careful as you pour! The sauce could splatter a bit since the skillet will be hot.
Scatter 4 ounces of mozzarella over top of it all then return the skillet to the oven for another 10 minutes, until the cheese is melty.
Scatter more fresh basil and Parmesan over top and serve immediately, straight out of the skillet!

name: a pitcher of strawberry j argaritas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups lime juice (you’ll need to juice about 16 limes for this!)
ingredients.name: lime juice (you’ll need to juice about 16 limes for this!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1/2 cup strawberry jam (or any flavor jam)
ingredients.name: strawberry jam (or any flavor jam)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup cold water (I know it feels weird to add water but just trust)
ingredients.name: cold water (I know it feels weird to add water but just trust)

preparationSteps: Combine all ingredients (2 cups blanco tequila, 2 cups lime juice, 1 1/2 cups Cointreau, 1/4 to 1/2 cup strawberry jam, and 1/2 cup cold water) in a jar (or pitcher), shake (or stir), and refrigerate until party time, up to 24 hours in advance.
Serve in glasses with salted rims that are filled to the brim with ice.

*If you’re new to margaritas: Use a lime wedge to wet the rim of your glass (so buy 3-4 extra limes when you’re shopping, then cut them into wedges before the party). Pour salt (kosher salt, never table salt — you want a coarse grain!) onto a plate, then shove the rim of the glass into the salt until it’s coated. Fill all the way to the brim with ice and pour in your cocktail!
**I like to keep bottles of Topo Chico (or any club soda) by the drink station so that people can cut their margarita, if they so choose!

name: beef basil bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece ginger, washed and grated (no need to peel), or 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
ingredients.name: ginger, washed and grated (no need to peel), or 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1 lime (or 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1 lime (or 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha or sambal oelek or really any spicy chili paste
ingredients.name: sriracha or sambal oelek or really any spicy chili paste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground beef (ideally 90% lean/10% fat, but anything works)
ingredients.name: ground beef (ideally 90% lean/10% fat, but anything works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2-inch piece fresh ginger, washed and grated (no need to peel), or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
ingredients.name: fresh ginger, washed and grated (no need to peel), or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 garlic cloves, grated (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, grated (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup finely chopped basil leaves (or cilantro)
ingredients.name: finely chopped basil leaves (or cilantro)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings (you need at least 2!): chopped mango (or nectarines like I used), diced cucumber, shredded carrot, thinly sliced avocado, thinly sliced bell pepper, fresh cilantro, fresh mint leaves, roasted peanuts or cashews, toasted coconut, toasted sesame seeds, lime wedges
ingredients.name: Optional toppings (you need at least 2!): chopped mango (or nectarines like I used), diced cucumber, shredded carrot, thinly sliced avocado, thinly sliced bell pepper, fresh cilantro, fresh mint leaves, roasted peanuts or cashews, toasted coconut, toasted sesame seeds, lime wedges

preparationSteps: Start with the coconut rice! Add 1 1/2 cups white rice, 1 can coconut milk, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon honey, a grated 1-inch piece of ginger, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a pot, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 14 to 16 minutes, until rice is tender (give it a taste to check!). Remove from heat and let sit covered until you’re ready to eat, at least 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork before serving.
While the rice is cooking, make the peanut sauce and cook the basil beef.

For the sauce: Stir 1/3 cup smooth peanut butter, 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce, the juice of 1 lime, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha (1 will give it some heat, 2 will be spicy!) in a large bowl until smooth. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons (or more, if needed) of warm water to make it drizzle-able. Set aside.

To cook the basil beef: Warm 1 tablespoon sesame oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 diced medium yellow onion and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until softened. Add 1 pound ground beef. Use a microplane to grate 2-inches of fresh ginger (no need to peel it) and 3 peeled garlic cloves directly into the skillet.

Add 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, using a spatula to incorporate the seasonings and crumble the beef. Liquid will accumulate in the skillet from the beef — that’s normal. Continue cooking, stirring constantly, until all the liquid has evaporated. Resist the urge to pour off the fat (unless you used 80/20%, in which case you can pour off half of the fat) — this is flavor!

Stir in 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 3 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, 1 tablespoon sriracha, and 1 tablespoon fish sauce until almost fully absorbed, about 1 minute. There should still be some sauce in the bottom of the skillet — that’s a good thing! We like it saucy.
Turn off the heat and stir in 1/2 cup finely chopped basil leaves.
Build your bowl with coconut-ginger rice, basil beef, peanut sauce, and lots of toppings!

name: 30-minute cheesy broccoli pesto pasta with lemon pepper chicken

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound of pasta of your choice (I chose Cavatappi but truly anything works here)
ingredients.name: of pasta of your choice (I chose Cavatappi but truly anything works here)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups of broccoli florets (or one 10-ounce bag steam-in-bag broccoli — see the “quick note” section above the recipe for more on this)
ingredients.name: of broccoli florets (or one 10-ounce bag steam-in-bag broccoli — see the “quick note” section above the recipe for more on this)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound of boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.name: of boneless skinless chicken thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 lemons (ideally organic since we’re zesting them)
ingredients.name: lemons (ideally organic since we’re zesting them)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup of full-fat cottage cheese (ideally Good Culture brand, it is truly superior)
ingredients.name: of full-fat cottage cheese (ideally Good Culture brand, it is truly superior)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup of grated Parm (Parmigiano Reggiano if you can find it)
ingredients.name: of grated Parm (Parmigiano Reggiano if you can find it)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook 1 pound of pasta of your choice about 1 minute less than package instructions (we will cook the pasta more in the sauce). Before you drain the pasta, RESERVE ABOUT 1 CUP OF PASTA COOKING WATER (bolding this so you don’t forget!!!). Drain the noodles, return the cooked pasta to the pot, and set aside.
Meanwhile, steam 2 cups of broccoli florets (see the entire notes section about this above!) until bright green and crisp tender, 5 to 8 minutes.

While the noodles boil and the broccoli steams, pat 1 pound of boneless skinless chicken thighs dry, drizzle them generously all over with EVOO and season both sides with a big pinch of salt and lots of pepper. No need to measure the pepper, just sprinkle/grind it on liberally. Use a microplane to grate the zest of 1 lemon evenly over the chicken thighs.

Heat a large cast-iron (or non-stick) skillet over medium-high heat (no, you don’t need to add oil to the pan, unless you’re using a carbon or stainless steel pan!), and when almost smoking, add your seasoned chicken thighs and cook for 4 minutes. Peek at the bottom of the chicken — if it’s golden brown, flip it using tongs or a spatula. If not, let it cook for 1 more minute then flip it. Cook for another 4 or 5 minutes, until the other side is also golden brown and the chicken is cooked through (use a meat thermometer to double check temperature, if you have one — it’s done at 165°F). Set the cooked chicken aside. Using the lemon you zested, squeeze some lemon juice over the chicken then let it rest while you prepare the pasta sauce.

To a blender, add the steamed broccoli, 1 cup of full-fat cottage cheese, 1/2 cup of grated Parm, 2 peeled garlic cloves, 1 cup packed basil leaves, 1 cup packed spinach leaves, 1/2 cup milk of choice, a large pinch of salt, and the zest and juice of the second lemon. Blend until smooth. I like a smooth alfredo-y consistency for this sauce! If it’s too thick, add more milk until it’s a nice creamy, saucy, consistency.

Returning back to your pasta pot, turn the heat on to medium. Add your broccoli pesto to the pasta, along with 1/4 cup of pasta water. Stir and toss to coat your pasta in the sauce, until saucy and glossy, about 2 minutes. Add more pasta water if you feel like the sauce needs to loosen up a bit (aka looks too thick / chunky). Taste it! Does it need more salt, pepper, or lemon juice? Add it until it’s perfectly seasoned.

Serve your pasta with sliced pieces of chicken on top, freshly grated Parm, and a few basil leaves. For extra deliciousness, also garnish with a drizzle of EVOO, a squeeze of lemon, red pepper flakes, and some flaky salt. ENJOY!

name: sheet-pan crispy pork chops with fennel and peaches
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use precooked chicken sausages instead of pork chops. No need to use mustard and breadcrumbs with these, they’re already packed with flavor! See substitution note below for cook time.

What to cook when you’re starving: Serve this with a side of cooked polenta or grits! I almost made this the real recipe, but I decided it wasn’t necessary. But if you’re starving, maybe it is!

I’m a vegetarian: Use a plant-based sausage in lieu of the chop. Or, drain, rinse, and dry a can of chickpeas. Mix them with 1 to 2 tablespoons of cooking oil and season them with salt and pepper. Add them to the sheet-pan along with the fennel and onions. Crispy chickpeas are delish!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Check your breadcrumbs to be sure they’re dairy-free. To avoid gluten, opt for rice crumbs (TJ’s has them!) instead of breadcrumbs. Or, skip the crispy part all together!

Make ahead: Chop your veggies and cut your peaches up to 24 hours in advance and store ‘em in the fridge.

Leftovers are a good thing. If you’re cooking for 1 or 2, don’t hesitate making extra to have on hand for lunches. Or double it if you’re cooking for 4 and want leftovers! You’ll just need to use another half sheet-pan. You could also cut up leftover pork chop (scrape any breadcrumbs off as they’ll get soggy) and add it to my 15-minute noods. Or, add the chopped pork to TJ’s veggie fried rice for a SUPER easy and delicious weeknight dinner.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 bone-in pork chops (3/4- to 1-inch thick)
ingredients.name: bone-in pork chops (3/4- to 1-inch thick)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons whole-grain or Dijon mustard
ingredients.name: whole-grain or Dijon mustard

ingredients.rawIngredient: Breadcrumbs (Panko, Italian, or rice crumbs all work, or see substitution note for how to make your own using stale bread)
ingredients.name: Breadcrumbs (Panko, Italian, or rice crumbs all work, or see substitution note for how to make your own using stale bread)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 large peaches, each cut into 6 wedges
ingredients.name: large peaches, each cut into 6 wedges

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft green herbs, such as basil, parsley, oregano, or chives, chopped
ingredients.name: Soft green herbs, such as basil, parsley, oregano, or chives

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a rimmed half baking sheet with parchment paper or foil (or nothing if you don’t mind the cleanup).

Toss 2 thinly sliced fennel bulbs and 1 thinly sliced red onion with 1 tablespoon cooking oil, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Spread out into an even layer and roast on the BOTTOM OF THE OVEN for 15 to 20 minutes, until very tender and starting to turn golden brown. Yes, the very bottom — like the floor of the oven! If you have exposed coils on the bottom, place your baking sheet on the bottom rack.

While that’s roasting, pat 2 to 4 bone-in pork chops dry using a paper or reusable dish towel, then season generously with salt and pepper all over. Smear a very light layer of mustard on top of each pork chop, then press roughly 1 tablespoon of breadcrumbs into the mustard — or just enough to completely cover it with a thin layer of crumbs. Season each chop with a tiny bit of salt and pepper, then spray them all over with cooking oil spray so that they’ll brown nicely.

After the fennel and onions have roasted for 15 minutes, give them a stir then make space for the pork chops. Add the pork chops to the empty space, then scatter the peaches wherever — on top of the fennel and onions is fine.
Return the baking sheet to the oven for 12 to 15 more minutes, or until the pork chops reach about 142°F internally (they’ll keep cooking to reach 145°F).
Plate it up, sprinkle chopped fresh soft herbs on top, and ENJOY! I like to cut the peaches into small pieces and eat one piece of peach with each bite of pork. Yummm!

name: one-pot lemony garlic butter shrimp orzo

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (omit or reduce if you’re feeding people who are spice averse)
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes (omit or reduce if you’re feeding people who are spice averse)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups fresh or frozen English peas (no need to thaw if frozen)
ingredients.name: fresh or frozen English peas (no need to thaw if frozen)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces (1/2 cup) grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup finely chopped basil leaves, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: finely chopped basil leaves, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Using a microplane, grate 4 garlic cloves and zest 1 lemon.

Combine 1 pound peeled and deveined shrimp, half of the grated garlic, all of the lemon zest, 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt in a bowl and set aside at room temperature to marinate.

In a 12-inch skillet or braiser, melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat. Cook 1 large minced shallot, the remaining grated garlic, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes until softened, about 4 minutes. Stir in 3 cups chicken stock and 1 1/2 cups orzo and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, reduce to low heat, and cook for 8 minutes.

Remove the lid and place the marinated shrimp over top in an even layer, so they’re all spread out. If using fresh peas, add them in an even layer on top of the shrimp now. Cover again and cook for 5 minutes, until most of the shrimp look cooked through (some might still be a bit translucent looking and that’s OK! They’re going to keep cooking!).

Stir in 1 1/2 cups frozen peas (if you didn’t use fresh), 1/2 cup grated Parmesan, the juice of the lemon, 1/2 cup finely chopped basil leaves, plus more stock if the skillet is starting to look dry. Keep stirring until all of your shrimp are opaque pink and curled into a “C” shape. The orzo should be a nice risotto-y consistency, not too thick. If it is too thick, add more stock as needed (a splash at a time) to loosen.
Garnish with extra fresh basil, red pepper flakes, and grated Parm just before serving!

name: adobo pork & roasted cauliflower rice bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (1 to 1 1/2 pound) pork tenderloins (TENDERLOINS,notpork loins!),silver skin removed
ingredients.name: pork tenderloins (TENDERLOINS,notpork loins!),silver skin removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups frozen corn or 1 can drained and rinsed corn
ingredients.name: frozen corn or 1 can drained and rinsed corn

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup crumbled cotija or feta cheese (or shredded Mexican cheese or Cheddar)
ingredients.name: crumbled cotija or feta cheese (or shredded Mexican cheese or Cheddar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings: tortilla chips, pico de gallo, salsa, sour cream, shredded lettuce
ingredients.name: Optional toppings: tortilla chips, pico de gallo, salsa, sour cream, shredded lettuce

preparationSteps: Add 2 pork tenderloins to a large bowl or Ziploc along with 3 tablespoons oil, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 2 teaspoons chili powder, 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon cayenne. Marinate for at least 15 minutes at room temperature, or, if you have the time, up to 48 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 425°F.

Grab your largest rimmed baking sheet. Add the pork tenderloins to one side, 1 inch apart. Add 1 pound cauliflower rice to the other side and toss with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder until evenly coated. Spread into an even layer, right up to where the pork is.
Roast for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pork reaches 145°F internally. Transfer the pork to a cutting board.

Stir 1 can drained and rinsed black beans, 2 cups frozen corn, and another tiny sprinkle of salt into the cauliflower rice and spread into an even layer, stirring any juices from the pork tenderloin into the cauliflower rice.
Return to the oven to roast for an additional 5 to 7 minutes, until the corn is crisp-tender.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, smash 1 avocado with the juice of 1/2 lime and a pinch of salt. Sprinkle 1/4 cup chopped cilantro and 1/4 cup crumbled cotija over top.

Slice the pork tenderloin into 1/2-inch thick slices or into cubes for more of a burrito bowl-style meal. Squeeze the remaining 1/2 lime over the cauliflower rice. Serve the pork over the cauliflower rice. Top with the smashed avocado and any other toppings you want (crumbled tortilla chips, salsa, sour cream, etc.)

PS: I broiled the top of my pork tenderloin because it looks a bit, um, phallic, when it’s just roasted but not seared. But this does not affect the taste, and once you slice it, it looks the same either way! In sum: Broil it if you want, but you don’t need to. If you do broil it, keep an eye on it the whole time to make sure your cauliflower rice doesn’t burn!

name: 30-minute shawarma lettuce wraps
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Make the beef, buy hummus or the “herbed tahini sauce” from Trader Joe’s instead of making the tahini sauce, and skip the salad — a simple, delicious meal. It’s also worth noting that McCormick (and other brands) do sell a shawarma seasoning blend. Use 1 tablespoon of a store-bought shawarma seasoning for the ground beef mixture and call it a day.

Potential add-ons to the salad: Try adding chopped hearts of palm (from the can) and/or diced jalapeño to the salad! Jana, an IG follower, recommended this and it sounds so good.

I don’t have a vegetable peeler. If for some reason your kitchen doesn’t have one at the moment, you can totally just cut a series of strips of cucumber skin off lengthwise using your knife.

Vegetarian: Lots of options here! Basically you’re going to use shawarma spices on whatever legume and/or vegetable combination you love. You could dice up a pound of mushrooms in lieu of the beef, and add the cauliflower rice. Prepare that combo just like the recipe’s written, cooking the mixture until the moisture from the mushrooms has evaporated and all are tender. You could also dice up vegetables like onion, squash, zucchini, and broccoli, and sauté them with the spices, and/or sauté a package of firm tofu or tempeh along with the vegetables. Another option is to roast vegetables in the shawarma spices. A good combo for this would be a can of rinsed and drained chickpeas, one or two diced sweet potatoes, and a head of cauliflower diced. To do this, preheat your oven to 425°F, mix the veggies on a baking sheet (or two if needed to spread everything out flat) with three tablespoons neutral cooking oil and the shawarma spices, and bake them until roasted, about 20-25 minutes.

You could dice up a pound of mushrooms in lieu of the beef, and add the cauliflower rice. Prepare that combo just like the recipe’s written, cooking the mixture until the moisture from the mushrooms has evaporated and all are tender. You could also dice up vegetables like onion, squash, zucchini, and broccoli, and sauté them with the spices, and/or sauté a package of firm tofu or tempeh along with the vegetables.

Another option is to roast vegetables in the shawarma spices. A good combo for this would be a can of rinsed and drained chickpeas, one or two diced sweet potatoes, and a head of cauliflower diced. To do this, preheat your oven to 425°F, mix the veggies on a baking sheet (or two if needed to spread everything out flat) with three tablespoons neutral cooking oil and the shawarma spices, and bake them until roasted, about 20-25 minutes.

Gluten free/dairy free: It’s already dairy free! If avoiding gluten, be sure your tahini has none added (most brands are gf but some contain thickening agents with gluten).

Make ahead: Make the tahini sauce as far ahead as you’d like! It will stay good in the fridge for weeks. You can also pre-cook the meat and just reheat it on the stovetop before mealtime. The salad’s best to fix right before you eat because... avocados.

Love your leftovers: Did you skip my intro copy?! If so, scroll up to “other ways to enjoy this recipe” and get ideas for this week’s lunches! You can easily double the recipe for the shawarma meat to have ample leftovers for lunches. You could also freeze your leftovers for an easy dinner in the coming weeks. Just let the meat cool and freeze it in a freezer-safe bag with any air squeezed out.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of butter lettuce, leaves separated
ingredients.name: of butter lettuce, leaves separated

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup finely chopped flat-leaf parsley, divided between the three sub-recipes
ingredients.name: finely chopped flat-leaf parsley, divided between the three sub-recipes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound cucumbers (I prefer using about 6 small Persian cucumbers here, but 1 English cucumber will work as well!)
ingredients.name: cucumbers (I prefer using about 6 small Persian cucumbers here, but 1 English cucumber will work as well!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: optional: a couple shakes of hot sauce (Whatever you like! Sriracha is great here)
ingredients.name: optional: a couple shakes of hot sauce (Whatever you like! Sriracha is great here)

preparationSteps: Warm a large skillet over high heat. Break 1 pound ground beef into small pieces as you add it to the skillet. Add 1 1/2 cups cauliflower rice, 4 thinly sliced scallions (but go ahead and slice 6 — you need 2 for the salad), 1 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric, 1/8 teaspoon ground cloves, 1/8 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Cook, breaking the meat up into tiny crumbles with a spatula, until the meat is cooked through and most of the fat has either evaporated or been absorbed (do not pour it off), 7 to 10 minutes. Don’t let the meat dry out! Cut off the heat as soon as there’s not a layer of fat at the bottom of the skillet. Stir in 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley.
Meanwhile, make the tahini sauce and cucumber avocado salad…

To make the tahini sauce, whisk all ingredients (1/3 cup tahini, the juice of 1 large lemon, 2 teaspoons honey, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, a big pinch of salt, and 3 tablespoons warm water) together in a large bowl. This is an ANNOYING process. It’s hard to get the water to combine, but stick with it! Use a fork to smash the tahini and help it absorb the liquid. Add more water as needed (you might need no more, you might need a lot more, depending on the consistency of your tahini) until you get a drizzle-able consistency, like a thick vinaigrette. Stir in 2 tablespoons finely chopped parsley. Taste and adjust salt, honey, and lemon until you love it!

Now let’s make the cucumber avocado salad. Use a vegetable peeler to peel 1 pound of cucumbers in alternating strips like a zebra. This will make them more enjoyable to chew, while leaving enough skin to hold their shape. Chop the peeled cucumbers into quarters or halves, depending on how big your cucumber(s) are, and toss them in a large bowl. Now grab 2 avocados, cut them in half, then remove the pit. Use a large spoon to scoop the flesh out of the skin, then chop the avocado flesh into 1/2-inch pieces. Add the chopped avocado to the bowl with the cucumbers and stir in the 2 thinly sliced scallions, the juice of 1 large lemon, 2 tablespoons finely chopped parsley (this should be about what’s left at this point — just use everything left on the cutting board), 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and a couple shakes of hot sauce (if desired — it’s great without it, if you’re spice-averse).

Stack two butter lettuce leaves on top of each other and fill with several tablespoons of beef shawarma meat. You can add the cucumber avocado salad to the wrap, or serve it on the side. Drizzle the wraps with tahini sauce. ENJOY!

name: shortcut shakshuka with feta
note:
Make ahead: Make the peppers, onion, and sauce mixture entirely ahead (up to 48 hours) and store it right in the skillet, covered. When you’re ready to eat, just reheat the sauce over medium heat and when it’s hot, crack in the eggs.

Leftovers are a good thing: If you have leftover sauce, save it! Reheat it in a smaller skillet and poach another egg in it for breakfast tomorrow.

What to do when you really don’t feel like cooking: Just warm up the tomato sauce and poach the eggs into that. No onions, no peppers, no spices. It’s delightful.

Must have meat: Cook 1/2 pound ground sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it into small crumbles. Then start cooking the peppers and onions and proceed with the recipe.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons neutral cooking oil (such as avocado or grapeseed)
ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil (such as avocado or grapeseed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) jar (or 2 cups) of a garlicky tomato sauce (I usedRao’sbut any brand works!)
ingredients.name: of a garlicky tomato sauce (I usedRao’sbut any brand works!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon of any vinegar you have (red wine! balsamic! whatev!)
ingredients.name: of any vinegar you have (red wine! balsamic! whatev!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
