ingredients.name: crumbled feta cheese (try to buy feta that is packed in the brine, it’s infinitely tastier)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: chopped basil, cilantro, or chives
ingredients.name: Optional: chopped basil, cilantro, or chives

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 really good loaf of bread — baguette, sourdough, whatever
ingredients.name: really good loaf of bread — baguette, sourdough, whatever

preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook 2 large bell peppers and 1 diced onion, stirring frequently, for 4 to 5 minutes, until very tender. Stir in 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1 teaspoon paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes and continue cooking for 30 seconds.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups spinach or chopped kale until wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 1 (16-ounce) jar tomato sauce, 1 teaspoon vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Reduce heat to medium and allow the tomato sauce to simmer and warm up for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed.

Use the back of a wooden spoon or spatula to create 4 to 6 divots in the sauce. Crack an egg into each divot. It’s OK if the whites run a bit and don’t stay perfectly in the divot — no biggie! Season the eggs with salt and pepper.

Cover the skillet and cook over medium-low heat for 7 to 10 minutes, checking beginning at the 7-minute mark. When the whites are almost cooked through, add 1/2 cup crumbled feta over top and cover the pan again until the eggs are cooked to your liking. The yolks are best runny, in my opinion!

If you have some soft green herbs like basil, cilantro, or chives hanging out in the fridge, scatter those over top. Add a big crank of black pepper. Throw that skillet in the center of the table and DIG IN!
Serve with bread for DIPPIN’!

name: sheet-pan greek chicken and potatoes
note:
How to cut fennel: If you’ve missed all 500 times I’ve demoed how to cut fennel on my Instagram stories, let’s talk it out. First, you’re going to lob off those big tall stalks so that all that’s left is the bulb itself. You can throw away the stalks or save them to make stock. Now chop off the knobbly root end. Cut the fennel in half, from root end to stalk end. Place the cut sides down on the cutting board. Thinly slice (1/4-inch thick) the fennel, from root end to stalk end.

Gimme a grain: Cooked brown rice, quinoa, or farro would be an excellent addition to this meal.

Prep ahead: Do all your veggie cutting up to a day in advance and store them in air-tight containers in the fridge. You can even cook this whole recipe earlier in the day, cover the sheet pan with foil, and pop it in the fridge. To reheat: Keep the foil on and bake it in a 300°F oven for 10-15 minutes.

Leftovers are a great thing: Whip out another sheet pan and double this baby to reheat for lunches! (Or just make the full recipe if you’re cooking for one or two). See just above for the best way to reheat it.

Vegetarian: In lieu of chicken, use a block of cubed tofu (press it under something heavy between towels for a few minutes before cubing it!) or a can of drained and rinsed chickpeas.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: Use a plant-based feta for df. The VioLife brand feta is actually really delicious. This recipe is already gf.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 1 lemon, divided
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 1 lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon dried oregano (or 2 teaspoons fresh oregano)
ingredients.name: dried oregano (or 2 teaspoons fresh oregano)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds fingerling potatoes, halved (or quartered, if very large)
ingredients.name: fingerling potatoes, halved (or quartered, if very large)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of fennel, thinly sliced (see notes)
ingredients.name: of fennel, thinly sliced (see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 ounces feta cheese, crumbled (depending on how much you love cheese!)
ingredients.name: feta cheese, crumbled (depending on how much you love cheese!)

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons olive oil, the zest and juice of 1/2 lemon, 2 grated garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano. Add 2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate for up to 12 hours if possible. If you don’t have time to marinate, just continue on with the recipe. It’ll still be delicious!
Preheat oven to 425°F.

Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Place 1 1/2 pounds halved fingerling potatoes and 1 thinly sliced head of fennel on the baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil and sprinkle with 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Toss to coat and spread into an even layer on the baking sheet.
Roast the potatoes and fennel for 15 minutes then give everything a stir.

Shake any excess marinade off of the chicken thighs, then nestle them down onto the baking sheet between the potatoes and fennel, skin side up. Pat the skin dry with a paper towel or clean dish towel to ensure the skin gets nice and crispy.
Roast for an additional 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken registers 165°F internally and the potatoes and fennel are browned and tender.

Sprinkle everything with the juice from the remaining 1/2 lemon, 2 to 4 ounces crumbled feta, and 3 tablespoons fresh chopped dill. Sprinkle more salt and pepper over everything and serve immediately!

name: crispy farro with sausage and asparagus

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups uncooked pearled farro (or 3 cups pre-cooked farro)
ingredients.name: uncooked pearled farro (or 3 cups pre-cooked farro)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mild or hot Italian sausage, casings removed
ingredients.name: mild or hot Italian sausage, casings removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced on a diagonal, dark green parts separated
ingredients.name: scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced on a diagonal, dark green parts separated

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed and thinly sliced on a diagonal
ingredients.name: asparagus, trimmed and thinly sliced on a diagonal

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: red wine vinegar, plus more as needed

preparationSteps: First, let’s get your farro cooking. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add 1 1/2 cups pearled farro and simmer until al dente, between 15 and 20 minutes. Note: If you can’t find pearled farro at the store, your farro will need to cook for longer. See the notes section below for more info if this applies to you!

While the farro is cooking, prep the other ingredients. Remove the casings from 1 pound mild or hot Italian sausage. Trim the roots off of 1 bunch scallions. Thinly slice the scallions on a diagonal, keeping the dark green parts separate from the white and light green parts. Trim the woody ends off of 1 bunch of asparagus, then thinly slice them on a diagonal into 1/2 inch (ish)-long pieces.

Taste the farro after 15 minutes of cooking. You’re looking for it to be tender but still slightly chewy. If it’s too firm, keep cooking until you reach al dente. Once al dente, drain, rinse the farro under cold water, and shake it super dry.
Wipe down the pot you cooked the farro in. (Alternatively, you could use a large nonstick or cast iron skillet from here.) Heat 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil over medium-high heat.

Add the sausage and cook, stirring occasionally and breaking it up into small pieces, for 8 to 10 minutes, until it’s crispy. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the sausage to a plate, keeping the fat in the pot.

Stir the cooked farro and scallion whites into the sausage fat. Spread them out flat along the bottom and cook undisturbed until golden underneath, 3 to 5 minutes. Listen for the sizzle to turn to a crackle-pop. If you see or smell burning, add some EVOO to the pot!
Add the asparagus, season with a big pinch of kosher salt, and stir. Spread the farro out flat again, and cook until the bottom is golden once more, 3 to 5 minutes.

Add back the sausage and any juices that may have collected on the plate and stir until the asparagus is crisp-tender, 1 to 2 minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in the scallion greens and 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar.
Season to taste with kosher salt and more vinegar (adding a small splash at a time) until it’s punchy and delicious. Dig in!

name: my mom’s egg salad
note:
How to hard boil eggs: My favorite method is to place all of the eggs in a wide, empty pot. Cover with 2 inches of water. Bring to a rolling boil. Turn off the heat. Cover the pot for 12 minutes. Drain and peel! If you have a hard time peeling the first one, give the eggs an ice bath for a few minutes… that can help make it easier.

How to hard boil eggs with an InstantPot: One of my all-time fave uses of my InstantPot is hard boiling eggs! The peels truly slip right off using this method. Place 1 cup water in the base of the InstantPot. Place your trivet over top (if you don’t have one, you can place the eggs straight in the water, but they’re more likely to crack). Cook on high pressure for 5 minutes. Allow the pressure to naturally release for 5 minutes before manually releasing the rest. Place into an ice bath (a bowl full of water and ice) to cool them quickly, then peel!

If you have leftover sauce from last week’s sheet-pan spring salmon: Grate 8 eggs and stir 1/4 cup of the dilly sauce into them. Add 3 tablespoons minced chives and you're done! Might need to add a bit more salt.

I’m not into eggs: I get it. The majority of my IG voters chose egg salad for this week’s recipe so here we are! BUT if you’re an egg hater, use this same approach to dinnertime with chicken salad (here’s my very delicious and easy curry chicken salad) or tuna salad (here’s my Mediterranean tuna salad)! Plate whichever salad you dig most with some crackers, on a sandwich, or on a simple salad — et voila.

Must have meat: Add a can of drained canned tuna fish for an egg-y tuna salad! Mix in extra teaspoons of the condiments as needed to get everything well coated.

I don’t have a box grater: You could use a mandoline to finely slice the eggs, then cut them into shreds. Or, obviously, you can just use a knife. Or you can buy a box grater just for this recipe because you’ll use it all the time once you have one!

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy pre-cooked hard-boiled eggs from the grocery and pre-minced herbs. Dinner could literally not get any easier.

Leftovers are a good thing: This egg salad stores for up to 4 days in an airtight container in the fridge!

Prep ahead: Pre-cook your hard-boiled eggs. If you keep them in their shell, hard-boiled eggs can hang in the fridge in an airtight container for up to a week. Though you want the eggs to be consumed within that week, so keep that timeframe in mind if you plan to have leftover egg salad.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons whole grain (or absolutely any) mustard
ingredients.name: whole grain (or absolutely any) mustard

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 hard-boiled eggs, grated on the largest hole of a box grater (instructions below for how to hard boil eggs)
ingredients.name: hard-boiled eggs, grated on the largest hole of a box grater (instructions below for how to hard boil eggs)

ingredients.rawIngredient: For serving: soft bread, butter lettuce leaves, Ritz crackers, or your preferred egg salad vessel!
ingredients.name: For serving: soft bread, butter lettuce leaves, Ritz crackers, or your preferred egg salad vessel!

preparationSteps: Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Add more salt and pepper to taste. THAT’S IT!! Serve it as a sandwich, alongside crackers, in lettuce cups, or however you’d like. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
servings: Serves 2 to 4 (double it if feeding 4 really hungry people)

name: Chocolate Sprinkle Sugar Cookies
note: Chocolate Sprinkle Sugar Cookies. These chocolate sugar cookies are thin and chewy, and rolled in sprinkles instead of the traditional sugar, which gives them a perfect crunch and super cute rainbow sprinkle finish. These are similar to crinkle cookies, but the sprinkle coating makes them extra cute, and they are so easy to make!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tsp vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
ingredients.name: vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°f / 180°c. Line three baking trays with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, sift together the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside.

In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, 3-4 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla, and beat until combined. Add the flour and cocoa mixture, and beat on low until just incorporated.

Using a cookie scoop, scoop 2 tbsp worth of mixture at a time. Roll into a ball using your hands, then roll generously in sprinkles. Place on the baking tray, leaving plenty of room to spread (I had 6 cookies per baking tray).

Bake one tray at a time for 11-12 minutes, until the cookies have puffed up and are beginning to crack on the tops, and the edges are set. Remove from the oven and allow to cool on the baking tray for 15 minutes then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: moroccan pork tenderloin and carrots with whipped pistachio feta and pita fries
note:
Leftovers are a good thing: Dip: Your whipped pistachio feta will last in the fridge for 5 or so days (eat it with veggies, crackers, as a spread on a sandwich, with grilled chicken the next night, whatever!!!). Pork: Thinly slice leftovers and use for sandwiches! Or finely chop, reheat in a hot skillet with a little oil, and make tacos with the leftover dip, chili crisp, and some pickled red onions. Pita fries: Snack on them!! Toast them up in the oven if they get stale.

Dip: Your whipped pistachio feta will last in the fridge for 5 or so days (eat it with veggies, crackers, as a spread on a sandwich, with grilled chicken the next night, whatever!!!).

Pork: Thinly slice leftovers and use for sandwiches! Or finely chop, reheat in a hot skillet with a little oil, and make tacos with the leftover dip, chili crisp, and some pickled red onions.

Pita fries: Snack on them!! Toast them up in the oven if they get stale.

I can only find a 5/6/7 ounce block of feta! That’s fine, carry on with the recipe as written. Will still be delish. Add more salt if needed since you’re missing a little salty feta.

I don’t own a food processor and my blender isn’t very good: If you’re worried your blender can’t handle pistachios, soak them for an hour before you blend them with the other ingredients.

Prep ahead: You can make the whipped feta days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. You can also prep the pork and carrots on the sheet pan in the morning, wrap the sheet pan tightly with plastic, and keep it in the fridge until it’s time to cook dinner! The pita fries can also be cooked days ahead of time — let them cool completely then store at room temp in an airtight bag.

Vegetarian: Roast 2 cans of chickpeas (or any white bean) along with your carrots. Drain, rinse, and pat them dry then mix them on the sheet pan with the carrots, oil, and seasonings as written. They’ll be delish!

Halve it: The pork and carrots and the pita fries are both easy to halve if you are cooking for 1 or 2 and don’t want leftovers. I’d go ahead and make the whole batch of whipped feta though so you aren’t left with half a block of cheese — it’d also be harder for your blender/food processor to mix. See the “leftovers are a good thing” note for what to do with your extra dip.

Gimme some greens: You’ll find instructions for a simple arugula salad in the recipe! I just want to note that if you love lemon and are also making the salad, pick up a second lemon at the store — you might want to add more juice to the whipped feta and/or the arugula salad and I don’t want you to run out!

I don’t wanna measure all those spices: You could buy Ras El Hanout, a Moroccan spice blend that contains these spices and others! Or skip the Moroccan vibes and use a great everyday spice blend that you love. You’d use a heaping tablespoon of it for your pork and carrots. Or, just do like I do when I’m not developing a recipe, and don’t measure anything — eyeball it!

Feeding kids: My kids loved the dip and pita chips (I called it green hummus). My pickiest eaters didn’t go for the meat and carrots — my least picky did! You could keep the spices off of one of the tenderloins and just season it with salt and pepper if you’re worried about the spices throwing your kids off!

Dairy-free: VioLife DF feta is SO GOOD if you can find it. Use that and a DF plain yogurt to make something very similar to the original sauce. Another option would be to trade the pistachio feta for a dairy-free tzatziki or a store-bought hummus like Little Sesame or Ithaca. Any of these will add a delicious saucy element!

Nut/seed-free: Omit the pistachios — the whipped feta will still be delicious without it. Or, use pepitas or sunflower seeds instead. I like the idea of pepitas here.

Gluten-free: Buy gluten-free pita.

ingredients.name: Sheet-pan Moroccan pork tenderloin and carrots:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 bunches (1 1/2-ish pounds) small carrots, greens removed, halved lengthwise
ingredients.name: small carrots, greens removed, halved lengthwise

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional if you want some greens: 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper
ingredients.name: Optional if you want some greens: 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 to 4 pita, cut into 1/2-inch thick strips
ingredients.name: pita

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, throw some of that in there too)
ingredients.name: packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, throw some of that in there too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup toasted pistachios (shelled — AKA, without the shells)
ingredients.name: toasted pistachios (shelled — AKA, without the shells)

preparationSteps: Position one oven rack in the center of the oven and one above it. Preheat oven to 400°F.

Remove the stems from 2 bunches of small carrots then cut them in half lengthwise. If you’re using big standard grocery store carrots, you’ll need to cut them in half (or into quarters if they’re really fat!) lengthwise and in half widthwise. Your goal is for them all to be about even size. Place the carrots on your largest rimmed sheet pan. Add 2 pork tenderloins, 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric, 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Use your hands to toss to coat everything evenly in oil and spices.
Roast on the center rack for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pork tenderloin reaches an internal temperature of 130°F.

Right after you put the pork and carrots in the oven, prep your pita fries: Cut 3 or 4 pita in half, then into 1/2-inch thick strips. Toss on a second sheet pan with 3 or 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon dried dill, 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and the zest of 1/2 lemon. Add the sheet pan to the oven so the pita fries can bake with the pork and carrots for 10 to 15 minutes, until golden brown and toasted on the outside, but still chewy and soft on the inside. Ideally you’ll position the sheet pans side by side on the center rack. If they can’t fit, put the pita on the rack above the pork and carrots.

Once the pork has reached 130°F (and you’ve removed the pita fries from the oven), switch the oven to Broil on High and broil the pork and carrots (still on the center rack) for 3 to 5 minutes, until everything gets nice and browned and the pork reaches 140°F.

Transfer the pork to a cutting board to rest (the internal temp will continue rising to 145°F as it sits). If your carrots are not fork tender at this point (fork tender means you can easily cut through them with a fork), continue broiling them on the center rack of the oven for a few more minutes (this ensures that they’re not too close to the heat — we want them to brown but not burn). Keep a close eye on them — they can go from being nicely browned to burnt quickly!
While the pork and pita are roasting…

Make the whipped pistachio feta: In a food processor (ideal) or a blender, blend 1 block of feta cheese (I cut it into quarters before I add it), 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (and a little dill, mint, or basil if you have it), 3/4 cup toasted pistachios, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup plain yogurt, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and the juice of 1/2 lemon together until chunky smooth. If you’re using a blender, you can use the tamp (if yours has one!) or a spoon to push and scrape the feta down as needed. Taste. I needed to add about 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt at this point, but this will totally depend on how salty your feta and pistachios are. I love lemon flavor, so I also wound up adding the juice from the other half of the lemon.

If you want some greens (I did, and it was excellent): Toss 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper in a serving bowl. Thinly sliced radishes, apple, or snap peas would also be excellent here if you have some!
Slice your pork 1/4-inch thick and serve it with lots of whipped pistachio feta, carrots, salad (if you made one), and pita fries!!

name: sheet-pan orange teriyaki steak and broccoli
note:
How to slice skirt steak:

I like my steak well done: Pop it back in the broiler until it’s as cooked as you like for it to be! BUT keep in mind that the internal temp rises about 5°F while the steak rests before you cut into it. Here’s a great article about steak doneness, with temps and visuals.

I don’t have a broiler: Can you grill this time of year? If so, grill on high for 3-4 mins per side, then roast the broccoli on 500 for 8-10 mins. If not: if you want the nice crust on your steak, cook it in a cast-iron skillet or grill pan over medium high for 4 mins per side. Roast the broccoli on 500 for 8-10 mins. If you don't care about the crust, roast it on the highest heat your oven will go for 7 minutes, then check the steak temp and keep cooking if it's not 135°F yet.

Double it + freezer friendly: See the “do your thing” and “prep ahead” notes above the recipe!

Love your leftovers: I can tell you from firsthand experience that leftovers of this meal are phenomenal. Just reheat them in the microwave and you’re good to go. Keep them stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Also, the recipe purposefully makes tons of teriyaki sauce because you guys ALWAYS want things saucier. Freeze leftover sauce and use it in a few months, or store it in the fridge and use it within 1 week.

How I serve this to my kids: I love a “bowl” dinner because it’s beyond easy to plate for my kids. I just put some steak in one pile, rice in another, broccoli in another, and, if I’ve got some, fruit in another.  My kids absolutely devoured the steak. No sesame seeds for them, and they don’t like extra sauce on top!

Vegetarian: Make a veggie teriyaki bowl! Mushrooms, broccoli, asparagus, carrots cut into rounds, thinly sliced bell peppers… any or all would be great. Broil the veggies for 3 minutes, stir, then broil for another 3. Then douse them in teriyaki sauce. Serve over rice, or quinoa for extra protein. Even though it isn’t touching meat, follow the recipe to turn the marinade into a sauce (it’ll cook down/glaze up).

Dairy-free/gluten-free: It’s already dairy-free. Use coconut aminos or tamari in place of soy sauce to avoid gluten.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup orange juice (orange-pineapple is also great here, or use the juice of 1 large orange)
ingredients.name: orange juice (orange-pineapple is also great here, or use the juice of 1 large orange)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup maple syrup (or 1/3 cup honey or 1/4 cup brown sugar)
ingredients.name: maple syrup (or 1/3 cup honey or 1/4 cup brown sugar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2-inch piece fresh ginger, grated or minced (no need to peel)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger, grated or minced (no need to peel)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds skirt steak (I used two 1-pound skirt steaks)
ingredients.name: skirt steak (I used two 1-pound skirt steaks)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 or 2 (depending on how much broccoli your fam will eat) (12- to 14-ounce) bags broccoli florets
ingredients.name: (depending on how much broccoli your fam will eat) bags broccoli florets

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons sesame oil (or any plain oil)
ingredients.name: sesame oil (or any plain oil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: cooked rice, quinoa, cauliflower rice, frozen vegetable fried rice (I used Trader Joe’s fried rice in these photos), etc. to make it a rice bowl
ingredients.name: Optional: cooked rice, quinoa, cauliflower rice, frozen vegetable fried rice (I used Trader Joe’s fried rice in these photos), etc. to make it a rice bowl

preparationSteps: In a medium pot or saucepan, combine 1 cup reduced-sodium soy sauce, 1/2 cup orange juice, 1/2 cup water, 1/3 cup maple syrup, and 2 tablespoons rice vinegar. Grate in (using a microplane or the smallest hole of a box grater) a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger and 8 garlic cloves.
Trim any large, hard chunks of white fat off of 1 1/2 to 2 pounds skirt steak, then add it to the pot. I know, this seems weird. But just go with it, OK!? I’m saving you a dirty dish.
Cover (with a lid or foil or anything) and refrigerate for at least 4 but up to 36 hours, or let it sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
When you’re ready to cook dinner, situate an oven rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat your oven’s broiler to high.

Add 14 to 24 ounces broccoli florets to your largest rimmed sheet pan. Toss with 2 tablespoons sesame oil and a big pinch of salt. Scooch the broccoli to one side. Shake the marinade off of the steak and place it on the other half of the sheet pan.
Now we’re gonna multitask cooking the steak and broccoli and boiling your marinade into a sauce, OK?! You got this!

Place the pot of marinade on the stovetop and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil for at least 5 minutes (to kill off those raw steak germs — yes, this is safe and fully food safety approved). In a small bowl, stir together 2 tablespoons cornstarch and 2 tablespoons water (this is called a “slurry” and it’s to ensure your cornstarch doesn’t just clump up when you stir it in). Mix the slurry into the teriyaki sauce, reduce the heat to medium-low, and keep cooking it, stirring every so often, until thickened, 5 to 7 minutes.
Meanwhile, place the sheet pan with steak and broccoli on the middle rack in the oven and broil for 4 minutes.

Pour any juices that accumulated into the boiling pot of teriyaki sauce, flip the steak, and stir the broccoli around a bit. Return the sheet pan to the oven and broil for an additional 4 minutes. There should be some nice charring around the edges after the first 4 minutes of cooking — if there isn’t, move the oven rack to the top rung for the second side to get it closer to the broiler.
Let the steak rest for 5 minutes. Cut the skirt steak into 3 big pieces, then rotate it and cut it into thin slices on an angle. (See video below for a demo.)
Stir sesame seeds into your sauce, and shake ‘em all over everything!
Serve the steak and broccoli on its own with lots of sauce, or over rice!

name: lemon basil spaghetti

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound dried spaghetti, or any long noodle
ingredients.name: dried spaghetti, or any long noodle

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (it must be freshly grated!)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (it must be freshly grated!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), preferably organic, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), preferably organic, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (no need to measure — about 2 grinds)
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper (no need to measure — about 2 grinds)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 large basil leaves or 6 parsley sprigs, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: large basil leaves or 6 parsley sprigs

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but encouraged: lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below!)
ingredients.name: Optional but encouraged: lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below!)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

Cook 1 pound dried pasta noodles until al dente (almost totally tender, but still with a slight hardness), per package instructions (as in, read the package and cook it for however long it says it will take to reach al dente!).

Meanwhile, in a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 large egg, 1 cup of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, the zest of 1 lemon, 1/3 cup lemon juice, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon (2 grinds) of black pepper.
Thinly slice 12 large basil leaves.

Immediately after draining, add the hot noodles to the sauce you made in the serving bowl, along with 1/2 cup of the hot, reserved pasta cooking water and most of the basil (but leave a little basil out for garnish). Use tongs to toss and toss and toss until the sauce is glossy and coating the noodles. It might look too soupy at first — keep tossing! The cheese, oil, and egg just need time and heat to meld together and work their magic. Add more pasta water as needed if the sauce stiffens up too much.
Serve immediately, garnished with more Parm, lemon zest, basil, and (if making) lots of lemon-parm crunchies.

name: tropical shrimp bowls with coconut rice and pineapple-avocado salsa
note:
How do I rinse rice? Two options: 1) Put it in a fine-mesh strainer and run it under cold water, moving the rice around with your fingers, until the water runs clear, or 2) put it in your pot, add some water, and swirl it around in the water. Drain the water and repeat until the water runs clear.

OK but what should I make for brunch? If your significant other wants brunch, make this Starbucks copycat frittata the night before and bake it in the morning while you let her sleep in. You can skip the sweet potato hash if it sounds hard. Maybe buy frozen hash browns and just crisp that up. Make a nice, simple salad to go with it by adding arugula, lots of shaved Parm, toasted pine nuts, lemon juice, extra-virgin olive oil, a big pinch of salt, and a little pepper to a serving bowl and tossing. Taste it. Is it delicious? If not, it probably needs more salt. Cut up some strawberries to add to your plates. Dig in.

Prep ahead: The rice can be made up to 5 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, adding a splash of water to help loosen it. You can make the sauce up to 3 days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. If it thickens up in the fridge, add some more oil, or even a little water, to loosen it up. But again, DON’T marinate the shrimp for more than 30 minutes! It’ll start to “cook” like ceviche.The slaw can be made up to 3 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge.You want to make the pineapple-avocado salsa right before serving if possible, but if you need to make it ahead, wait to add the avocado until the last minute and press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning.If your shrimp are finished cooking but you’re still working on other components of the meal, tent the plate they’re on with foil!

The rice can be made up to 5 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, adding a splash of water to help loosen it.

You can make the sauce up to 3 days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. If it thickens up in the fridge, add some more oil, or even a little water, to loosen it up. But again, DON’T marinate the shrimp for more than 30 minutes! It’ll start to “cook” like ceviche.

The slaw can be made up to 3 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge.

You want to make the pineapple-avocado salsa right before serving if possible, but if you need to make it ahead, wait to add the avocado until the last minute and press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning.

If your shrimp are finished cooking but you’re still working on other components of the meal, tent the plate they’re on with foil!

Love your leftovers: If you have leftovers, store each component separately. The shrimp will keep for 3 days, rice for 5 days (or freeze it!), but the salsa is best eaten within 24 hours before the avocado starts to brown. The sauce will keep for about 5 days and is excellent drizzled over eggs, roasted vegetables, or grilled chicken.

Got any shortcuts? Yes! Go read the “take shortcuts where you need them” note above the recipe.

I’m feeding spice wimps: Omit the jalapeño!

I don’t like shrimp: This marinade (and whole recipe) would be delicious with any protein you love. Here’s how to swap in chicken, steak, or salmon: For chicken breasts or thighs: Marinate them in the green sauce for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours in the fridge. Grill over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes per side (or until 165°F internally). If cooking in a skillet, I’d cut the chicken into cubes before marinating, then sear them in olive oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until cooked through. For steak (skirt, flank, or sirloin would all be great here): Marinate them for up to 4 hours in the fridge. Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side or until desired internal temp (125-130°F for medium-rare; 135-140°F for medium; or above for well done). For salmon: Marinate the fish for up to 30 minutes. To grill it, oil the grates and grill skin-side down over medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes for the first side, then 2 to 4 minutes on the second side, or until it reaches 120 to 130°F internally and flakes easily with a fork. Or you could bake it at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Or cook it in oil in a skillet over medium-high until cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway through. Or…

For chicken breasts or thighs: Marinate them in the green sauce for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours in the fridge. Grill over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes per side (or until 165°F internally). If cooking in a skillet, I’d cut the chicken into cubes before marinating, then sear them in olive oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

For steak (skirt, flank, or sirloin would all be great here): Marinate them for up to 4 hours in the fridge. Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side or until desired internal temp (125-130°F for medium-rare; 135-140°F for medium; or above for well done).

For salmon: Marinate the fish for up to 30 minutes. To grill it, oil the grates and grill skin-side down over medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes for the first side, then 2 to 4 minutes on the second side, or until it reaches 120 to 130°F internally and flakes easily with a fork. Or you could bake it at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Or cook it in oil in a skillet over medium-high until cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway through.

Or…

Vegetarian: Tofu would be so good with this meal. Press a block of extra firm tofu to remove excess water. You can either slice it lengthwise into big flat planks (best for grilling) or cube it. Marinate it for 30 minutes, then either grill it, pan sear it (AKA, cook it in a skillet until golden), or bake it at 400°F for 20 minutes, or until it starts to crisp up (flipping once halfway through).

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It’s already gluten-free. To avoid dairy, use a plant-based butter or extra olive oil if cooking the shrimp in a skillet.

ingredients.name: For the citrus-cilantro green sauce/marinade and shrimp:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup fresh cilantro (you can use both the leaves and stems)
ingredients.name: fresh cilantro (you can use both the leaves and stems)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 scallion (AKA green onion), roots trimmed off and discarded
ingredients.name: scallion (AKA green onion), roots trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 jalapeño (optional — spice-averse people, skip it!), seeded (AKA seeds removed)
ingredients.name: jalapeño (optional — spice-averse people, skip it!), seeded (AKA seeds removed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds large shrimp (16-20 count), peeled and deveined
ingredients.name: large shrimp (16-20 count)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter (only if you’re cooking the shrimp in a skillet)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter (only if you’re cooking the shrimp in a skillet)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups short-grain white rice, rinsed (see notes section for how to rinse it)
ingredients.name: short-grain white rice, rinsed (see notes section for how to rinse it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small fresh pineapple (or 2 cups pre-cut pineapple), chopped 1/4 inch
ingredients.name: small fresh pineapple (or 2 cups pre-cut pineapple), chopped 1/4 inch

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red bell pepper (optional — the salsa is great without it), chopped 1/4 inch
ingredients.name: red bell pepper (optional — the salsa is great without it), chopped 1/4 inch

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 scallions (AKA green onions), roots trimmed off and discarded, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions (AKA green onions), roots trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag shredded cabbage (purple or green cabbage or “coleslaw mix” all work)
ingredients.name: shredded cabbage (purple or green cabbage or “coleslaw mix” all work)

preparationSteps: First things first, let's make the citrus-cilantro green sauce that will pull this whole dish together. FYI, you’re going to use this sauce 4 different ways: 1) Half of it will be your shrimp marinade. 2) You’ll use a few spoonfuls to flavor the salsa. 3) It is the dressing for your slaw. 4) Any leftover sauce gets drizzled on top of the bowls as a sauce!

In your blender or food processor, combine the juice of 2 large limes, the juice from 1 orange, 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 cup cilantro leaves and stems, 1 scallion (roots trimmed off and discarded first), 2 small peeled garlic cloves, 1 halved and seeded jalapeño (to do this: cut off the stem, then cut it in half lengthwise, then scoop out and discard all of the seeds), 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Blend until smooth and vibrant green. This sauce should be loose enough to pour but thick enough to cling to the back of a spoon. If it's too thick, add another tablespoon of olive oil and blend again.

Pour half of this green sauce into a serving bowl and set it aside for later. Pour the other half into a shallow dish (or Ziploc) along with 1 1/2 pounds large peeled and deveined shrimp. Toss to coat every shrimp thoroughly, then refrigerate for up to 30 minutes. Don't marinate longer than this — the citrus will start "cooking" the shrimp like ceviche!
While the shrimp is marinating, make the rice, salsa, and slaw.
If you’re grilling, now is a good time to preheat your grill! We’re going to be cooking over medium-high heat.

For the rice: Combine 1 1/2 cups rinsed short-grain white rice, 1 can coconut milk, 1 1/4 cups water, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in a small pot and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to the lowest heat possible, COVER, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until all liquid is absorbed. Turn off the heat, keep the lid on, and let it steam for at least another 5 minutes. Just before serving, fluff it with a fork (AKA gently scrape the rice with a fork to un-clump it).

Next up, let’s make the salsa: Chop 2 cups fresh pineapple into small (about 1/4 inch, so about the size of your pinky finger’s nail) pieces and add them to a medium-sized bowl. If you're using a whole pineapple, here’s what to do: cut off the top and bottom, stand it upright, slice off the skin in strips, then quarter it lengthwise, remove the core, and dice. Here’s a visual. Or just buy it pre-cut, and dice up the big chunks! Chop 1 ripe avocado and 1 red bell pepper into roughly 1/4-inch pieces. Remove and discard the root ends of 2 scallions then thinly slice them (the whole scallion, both white and green parts!). Add all the chopped vegetables to the bowl along with 2 tablespoons of the green sauce you set aside and a big pinch of kosher salt. Stir gently — we want the avocado to hold its shape, not turn into guacamole. Taste. If it’s not absolutely delicious, add more sauce and a tiny bit more kosher salt.

Finally, make the slaw! Simply dump the bag of shredded cabbage into a cute bowl, add a pinch of kosher salt, and squeeze the cabbage 5 times with your hands. Pour in 2 to 3 tablespoons of the green sauce and toss to coat. Taste. Add more kosher salt and/or green sauce until it’s delicious.
Time to cook the shrimp!

If you’re grilling: Thread the marinated shrimp onto skewers — don't pack them too tightly; they need a little breathing room. Heat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the skewers for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and have some nice grill marks.

If you’re cooking in a skillet: Warm your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and heat until shimmering. Tilt the pan around to coat it in oil. Shake off as much marinade from the shrimp as possible, then add them to the skillet in an even layer. Cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until golden-brown all over. Add 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and toss to coat the shrimp in melted butter. Transfer shrimp to a serving platter.

Serve! This is a great meal to serve family style — just set the shrimp, rice, salsa, and slaw out and let everyone build their own bowls. Or, make everyone’s bowls for them by dividing the coconut rice among bowls, topping with shrimp (you can leave them on the skewers for presentation or slide them off — your call), and adding a generous scoop of both pineapple-avocado salsa and slaw. Drizzle everything with the reserved green sauce. Garnish with extra cilantro and lime wedges if you're feeling fancy. Dig in!

preparationSteps: Add 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup mayo, 1 1/2 packed cups mint leaves, 1 peeled garlic clove, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a food processor or blender and blend until smooth. Transfer to a serving bowl.

name: honey roasted carrots with burrata and pistachios

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pound carrots, cleaned and sliced in half vertically
ingredients.name: carrots, cleaned and sliced in half vertically

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup roasted, salted pistachios, finely chopped
ingredients.name: roasted, salted pistachios

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Wash and slice 2 pounds carrots in half vertically. You don’t need to peel them, but you can if you want to. Drizzle with 3 tablespoons oil, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, and use your hands to really get in there and toss everything together to evenly distribute the ingredients.
Spread the carrots into an even layer and roast for 40 minutes. Meanwhile, take the burrata out of the fridge to let it come to room temperature, and finely chop 1/4 cup pistachios.

Transfer the roasted carrots to a platter. Tear the burrata ball into several pieces and place them on top. Scatter the chopped pistachios over top. Finish with a drizzle of honey and extra-virgin olive oil.

name: crispy chicken chili verde street corn tacos
note:
Grocery shopping/ingredient notes: Ground chicken: First of all, ground turkey is a great swap! In either case, check the packaging and if possible, buy your ground meat with no added water or fillers. If your store doesn’t sell any without it, you could ask the butcher to grind some fresh. If they can’t, add a tablespoon of panko to the meat mixture to offset that extra moisture.Taco seasoning: Look at the ingredient list of your taco seasoning. If salt is listed, reduce the amount of salt you add to 1/2 teaspoon.“Street taco” tortillas: If you can’t find small “street taco” tortillas, go with 12 (6-inch) tortillas (any kind) and use a heaping 1/3 cup of the meat mixture filling for each taco. When making these, I used half flour (specifically, Mission “street taco” tortillas) and half corn (Mi Rancho’s “slider” tortillas).

Ground chicken: First of all, ground turkey is a great swap! In either case, check the packaging and if possible, buy your ground meat with no added water or fillers. If your store doesn’t sell any without it, you could ask the butcher to grind some fresh. If they can’t, add a tablespoon of panko to the meat mixture to offset that extra moisture.

Taco seasoning: Look at the ingredient list of your taco seasoning. If salt is listed, reduce the amount of salt you add to 1/2 teaspoon.

“Street taco” tortillas: If you can’t find small “street taco” tortillas, go with 12 (6-inch) tortillas (any kind) and use a heaping 1/3 cup of the meat mixture filling for each taco. When making these, I used half flour (specifically, Mission “street taco” tortillas) and half corn (Mi Rancho’s “slider” tortillas).

I want to make these really healthy: Use whatever tortillas work best with your health preferences, but when I’m eating really clean, I love using Siete almond or cashew tortillas. For the sauce, use greek yogurt. You can omit the cheese, but add 1 egg and 1/3 cup breadcrumbs or almond flour to keep the meat moist.

Prep ahead: Assemble your tacos up to a day ahead of time, wrap the sheet pans tightly with plastic wrap, and store them in the fridge until you’re ready to bake.

Riff: Make these into meatballs! Add 1 egg and 1/3 cup breadcrumbs (or almond flour). Roll into golf ball-sized meatballs. Bake for 18-20 minutes. You could throw some broccoli on the sheet pan to roast too!

Freezer friendly/love your leftovers: Leftovers will be great stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to four days. These freeze beautifully, too — once cool, store them in a Ziploc or whatever container you use for freezing. Reheat from frozen in a 425°F oven for 10 to 15 mins. If reheating from the fridge, reheat in a 425°F oven for 7 to 10 minutes, or throw ’em in the air fryer at 450 for like… 4 minutes??

Gimme some greens: I kept mine greens free to both simplify things and increase the odds of child approval (which worked!), but you could finely chop a handful or two of spinach and add it to the meat mixture. Or, add some minced cilantro to your crema and/or the meat mixture.

I’m cooking this for Cinco de Mayo/I want to bulk the meal up: I didn’t even realize until after I’d written the recipe that Monday is Cinco de Mayo! We all know by now that it’s more of an American construct than a holiday celebrated throughout Mexico, but I’ll take any opportunity to celebrate the country of Mexico and its incredible cuisine. If you are hosting this weekend (or just want to add a side to this meal), here are a few ideas:One-pot cheesy rice and beansMexican street corn saladEsquites salad (without the chicken)The dankest taco salad (without the turkey) Grilled summer squash and zucchini with charred scallion and cotija salsa

One-pot cheesy rice and beans

Mexican street corn salad

Esquites salad (without the chicken)

The dankest taco salad (without the turkey)

Grilled summer squash and zucchini with charred scallion and cotija salsa

Vegetarian: Swap the chicken out for 2 drained cans of black or pinto beans! Or use vegan ground “meat.”

Dairy-free: DF shredded “cheese,” or see the “I want to make these really healthy” note above for what to do if you’re omitting the cheese. Use a DF creamy thing, like mayo or a dairy-free sour cream or plain yogurt.

Gluten-free: Use corn, almond flour, or another non-flour tortilla.

I have half a lime now… Quarter it and squeeze it into your water glasses!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground chicken (see shopping note in the notes section below)
ingredients.name: ground chicken (see shopping note in the notes section below)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4-ounce can) diced green chiles, drained if watery, but mine weren’t
ingredients.name: diced green chiles, drained if watery, but mine weren’t

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 teaspoons taco seasoning (ideally sodium-free, see notes), divided
ingredients.name: taco seasoning (ideally sodium-free, see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces (1 cup) shredded cheddar, pepper jack, or Monterey Jack cheese
ingredients.name: shredded cheddar, pepper jack, or Monterey Jack cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 20 “street taco” tortillas (either flour or corn — flour are easier to work with)
ingredients.name: “street taco” tortillas (either flour or corn — flour are easier to work with)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup creamy white thing (mayo, sour cream, Greek yogurt — I like using 1/4 cup mayo and 1/4 cup sour cream!)
ingredients.name: creamy white thing (mayo, sour cream, Greek yogurt — I like using 1/4 cup mayo and 1/4 cup sour cream!)

preparationSteps: Position an oven rack in the top 1/3 of your oven, then preheat the oven to 425°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.

In a large mixing bowl, combine 1 pound ground chicken, 1 can drained white corn, 1 can diced green chiles (drain them if they seem watery, but if there is just a small amount of thick liquid that’s fine to keep), 2 teaspoons taco seasoning, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1 cup of shredded cheese.

If using corn tortillas, wrap the stack in damp paper towels (or a damp dish towel) and microwave for 30 seconds, or until pliable (aka you can bend them in half and they won’t break!). If using flour tortillas, you can skip this step.

Scoop a big spoonful of the meat mixture (yes, the raw meat mixture, trust the process, it’ll cook!) onto half of a tortilla. Fold the other half of the tortilla over top and press it closed. To make cheesier tacos, you can sprinkle a little extra shredded cheese over the ground meat before you press the tortilla closed. Also, if you are using corn tortillas and they still break in half when you fold them over, don’t sweat it — you’ll get the same outcome!

As you assemble your tacos, add them to the parchment-lined sheet pans, at least 1 inch from each other. Repeat until you’ve used all of the meat. Spray the tacos all over with cooking spray, flip them, and spray the second side.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until golden-brown and crispy.
Meanwhile, make the sauce: In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup of a creamy white thing, 1 teaspoon taco seasoning, the juice of 1/2 lime, and 1/8 teaspoon kosher salt.
Let the tacos cool for a few minutes, then dig in.
servings: Makes about 20 tiny tacos, or 12 (6-inch) tacos

name: one-skillet chicken & gingery rice with spicy (or not!) peanut curry sauce
note:
Love your leftovers: Leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze portions for up to three months to have easy meals within reach!

Add veg: I love the idea of sauteeing some mushrooms in the skillet before adding the rice and ginger, or a bag of shredded cabbage, or a couple big handfuls of shredded carrots! Several big handfuls of chopped spinach or kale could also be added in with the rice! Oh, or throw a bunch of broccoli florets right on top of the chicken for the last 15 minutes of cook time!

Prep ahead: You can make the curry sauce a few days ahead of time and refrigerate it. Warm it on the stovetop or in the microwave while the chicken and rice cooks. The sauce can also be frozen for up to three months.

I am afraid of fish sauce: I know it sounds a little scary because, well, it’s a sauce made from fermented fish, but if you like Pad Thai, or a Thai curry, then you like fish sauce because it’s full of it! It has an unbeatable salty, savory flavor, it does not taste fishy in a bad way, and it is crucial for creating Southeast Asian flavor. Pick up a bottle and trust me. Plus, with it in your pantry you can make coconut curry lentil veggie stew, and beef basil bowls with coconut-ginger rice.

Spice averse: Leave out the sriracha in the peanut sauce! Reduce the amount of curry paste!

Vegetarian: Try crispy tofu cubes or planks  Find a how-to for baking crispy tofu here in the product spotlight section. You could also pan-fry thin strips of extra-firm tofu in the skillet, using a few tablespoons of sesame oil. Or swap in a couple of cans chickpeas (drain and rinse them, first).

Gluten-free/dairy-free: It already is!

Nut-free: To avoid nuts, use a seed butter like sunflower butter or tahini instead of peanut butter.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1 to 2-inch) piece fresh ginger (if feeding spice averse people, ginger can be “spicy” to some, mostly kids, so use less or no ginger!)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger (if feeding spice averse people, ginger can be “spicy” to some, mostly kids, so use less or no ginger!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, white fat trimmed off
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, white fat trimmed off
For the spicy peanut curry sauce:

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons red curry paste (if feeding spice averse people, start with just 1 tablespoon, or even less)
ingredients.name: red curry paste (if feeding spice averse people, start with just 1 tablespoon, or even less)

preparationSteps:
cilantro sprigs, for serving

Make the chicken and rice: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add 1 1/2 cups rinsed long-grain white rice and grate in 1 ( 1 to 2-inch) piece fresh ginger (no need to peel it, use less if spice averse). Cook, stirring, until very fragrant, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 2 1/2 cups water and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low.

Season 2 pounds trimmed boneless, skinless chicken thighs with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt. Lay them over the rice, overlapping slightly if needed to fit. Cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the chicken registers 165°F. If the rice isn’t tender after 25 minutes, just keep cooking it, don’t worry about overcooking the chicken, thighs are resilient!

Remove the skillet from the heat and let sit, covered, for 10 minutes to allow the rice to steam.

While the chicken and rice are cooking, make the peanut curry sauce: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a small pot over medium heat. When it shimmers, add 1 to 2 tablespoons red curry paste and cook, stirring, until very fragrant and sticking to the bottom of the pot, about 1 minute. Stir in 1 (13.5-ounce) can full-fat coconut milk, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 1 tablespoons peanut butter, 1 tablespoon sriracha (if using), and 2 teaspoons honey. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring often, until very thick, like heavy cream or a thin yogurt, 10 to 15 minutes. Don’t let it boil over — reduce the heat to medium-low if needed. Remove the pot from the heat and let cool a bit.

Chop 10 cilantro sprigs and scatter around the chicken and rice. Drizzle the sauce all over the top and serve family-style with extra sauce on the side. I also had some peanuts and threw those on there!

name: a pitcher of strawberry jargaritas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups lime juice (you’ll need to juice about 16 limes for this!)
ingredients.name: lime juice (you’ll need to juice about 16 limes for this!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1/2 cup strawberry jam (or any flavor jam)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup cold water (I know it feels weird to add water but just trust)
ingredients.name: cold water (I know it feels weird to add water but just trust)

preparationSteps: Combine all ingredients (2 cups blanco tequila, 2 cups lime juice, 1 1/2 cups Cointreau, 1/4 to 1/2 cup strawberry jam, and 1/2 cup cold water) in a jar (or pitcher), shake (or stir), and refrigerate until party time, up to 24 hours in advance.
Serve in glasses with salted rims that are filled to the brim with ice.

*If you’re new to margaritas: Use a lime wedge to wet the rim of your glass (so buy 3-4 extra limes when you’re shopping, then cut them into wedges before the party). Pour salt (kosher salt, never table salt — you want a coarse grain!) onto a plate, then shove the rim of the glass into the salt until it’s coated. Fill all the way to the brim with ice and pour in your cocktail!
**I like to keep bottles of Topo Chico (or any club soda) by the drink station so that people can cut their margarita, if they so choose!

name: grilled brie and grapes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 tablespoons olive oil, divided, plus more to oil the Brie
ingredients.name: olive oil, divided, plus more to oil the Brie

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 clusters seedless red or green grapes
ingredients.name: clusters seedless red or green grapes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12- to 14-ounce/340 to 397 g) wheel Brie cheese
ingredients.name: wheel Brie cheese

preparationSteps: Whisk together 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar, 3 tablespoons olive oil, 1 minced garlic clove, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 teaspoon crushed fennel seeds, and a pinch of red pepper flakes in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, gently toss 2 to 3 clusters seedless grapes in the vinaigrette, and let sit for 30 minutes, tossing the grapes occasionally.
Preheat a gas or charcoal grill to medium-high heat (400ºF to 450ºF) and lightly oil the grates.

Place the sliced baguette in a large bowl, drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, and toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper. Drizzle 1 wheel of Brie cheese with olive oil and rub it around to coat. Remove the grapes and RESERVE THE LEFTOVER VINAIGRETTE!

Place the crostini, grapes, and cheese on the grill. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning occasionally, until the crostini are toasty and charred. Remove the crostini from the grill to a platter and rub a clove of garlic on the toasted bread for extra flavor. Continue to cook the grapes for 3 to 5 minutes, until they are lightly charred. Remove grapes to the platter with the toasted bread. Continue to grill the cheese, turning as needed, until there are grill marks and the cheese is soft but not falling apart, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Add to the platter.
When ready to serve, drizzle the grapes and cheese with the reserved vinaigrette and serve with the crostini.
*Save time: Instead of individually making and grilling crostini, you can just grill the entire baguette then thinly slice it!

ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper (optional)

preparationSteps: Preheat your grill to medium heat (350ºF to 400°F) and lightly oil the grates.

TO MAKE THE DRESSING: Put all the ingredients (1/4 cup mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons anchovy paste, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 2 cloves garlic, smashed, 1/2 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese, kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste) in a wide-mouth jar and blend with an immersion blender until evenly combined and smooth. If you don’t have an immersion blender, use a regular blender instead! Taste and season with more salt and pepper as needed. Set aside until ready to serve (refrigerate if making in advance).

TO MAKE THE CROUTONS: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a medium nonstick skillet. Add 2 slices French bread torn into small pieces and cook, stirring often, until light golden brown. Add the 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and 2 minced garlic cloves and stir continuously for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until the garlic is fragrant and golden. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer the croutons to a plate to cool.

TO GRILL THE ROMAINE HEARTS: Trim the roots off of 4 romaine hearts then cut the hearts in half. Use a pastry brush to lightly brush the cut sides of the romaine hearts with olive oil. Transfer to the grill, cut-side down. Grill for 3 to 5 minutes, until char marks form.
Transfer the lettuce to a serving platter, cut-side up. Drizzle with the dressing and top with the croutons and 1/2 cup shaved Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper, if desired.

*As a side, this salad will feed 6-8 people. But we are going to top our Chicken Caesar Sliders with 2 cups worth of it, so if you’re feeding that many people (as opposed to 2-4) add an extra head of romaine to the mix to chop up for your sliders! You can grill it if you want, or skip that step and just chop it up and add some Parm, dressing, and croutons.
**If you want your Chicken Caesar Sliders to be extra saucy, double the Caesar dressing so you can smear some on the slider buns.

name: juicy lucys (aka cheese-stuffed burgers!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings: Shredded iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato, sliced dill pickles
ingredients.name: Toppings: Shredded iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato, sliced dill pickles

preparationSteps: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat (400ºF to 450ºF) and lightly oil the grates.

Put 1 ½ pounds ground beef, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 heaping teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper in a large bowl. Use clean hands to mix the meat mixture until evenly combined. Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions, then divide each portion in half, leaving you with 8 equal portions.

To form a burger, take one portion of beef and smash it into a round patty, slightly bigger than the bun. Take 1 slice of cheese and tear it into quarters. Shingle the cheese on the patty, leaving a 1/2-inch border. Take another portion of beef and flatten it to the same size as the first patty. Place it on top and gently crimp the patties together. Set the finished patty aside on a plate and continue the process with the remaining meat and cheese to make 4 patties total.

Put the burger patties on the grill and cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the cheese is melted and gooey and the burger is cooked through. Remove the burger patties from the grill and let rest for 5 minutes.

While the burgers are resting, put 4 open potato buns on the grill, cut-side down, and grill for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly toasted. To assemble the burgers, put a spoonful of Special Sauce and a patty on each bottom bun. Top with your desired toppings and the top bun. Serve immediately.

*1 1/2 pounds of beef can be hard to buy for. Feel free to buy 2 pounds instead to make 6 patties instead of 4! Just add a little extra of each of the spices to the meat mixture, and make sure you have 2 extra cheese slices and buns.

name: chicken caesar sliders

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1/2 lemon (save that half-zested lemon for your crisp recipe!)
ingredients.name: Zest of 1/2 lemon (save that half-zested lemon for your crisp recipe!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 garlic clove, grated (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Caesar dressing (if you like things extra saucy!)
ingredients.name: Caesar dressing (if you like things extra saucy!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups Grilled Caesar Salad, finely chopped
ingredients.name: Grilled Caesar Salad

preparationSteps: Add 1 pound ground chicken, zest of 1/2 lemon, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 large egg, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 heaping teaspoon anchovy paste, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper to a large bowl. Use clean hands to mix the meat mixture until evenly combined.

To form the sliders, spray a baking sheet with cooking spray, then scoop out golf ball- sized portions of meat and place them on the baking sheet. Roll the meat around to grease it up all over, then use your fingers to smoosh the meat down into the baking sheet to create the slider patties.
Wrap with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, but up to 72 hours. (Or throw them in the freezer for at least 20 minutes.)

Preheat your grill to 400ºF. Use your grill brush to clean your grates really well — do not skip this, it will help prevent them from sticking! Lightly oil the grill grates after they’ve been scraped.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip the patties and grill for another 3 to 4 minutes, or until they’ve reached an internal temp of 165°F.

Towards the end of cooking the sliders, throw the entire pack of slider buns onto the grill — attached, if using King’s Hawaiian. Grill on each side for 30 to 45 seconds, until just lightly toasted but nice and warm.

Pull the slider buns apart and cut in half to open them. If you like things extra saucy, spread Caesar dressing onto each side of the bun, add a patty, then top with some chopped Grilled Caesar Salad. Close the bun.
*Not making the grilled Caesar from this menu? Just toss 2 cups chopped romaine with a pinch of salt, enough Caesar dressing to coat it, and some crushed up croutons (the crunch is essential!).

**If you want these to be extra saucy, be sure to double the Caesar dressing when you’re prepping your salad! Or just buy a jar of pre-made Caesar dressing from the store and use that on the buns instead.

name: grilled pb + j crisp with vanilla ice cream
note:
I don’t have a grill: On a parchment-lined sheet pan, bake the Brie and marinated grapes at 400°F for about 15 minutes. Broil your romaine lettuce heart halves for 4 minutes. Cook your burgers and slider patties on the stove in a pre-heated cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Add enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet before adding the patties. Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes per side, or until done. Bake your crisp at 375°F for 30-40 minutes, until the top is golden and the blueberries are bubbling.

On a parchment-lined sheet pan, bake the Brie and marinated grapes at 400°F for about 15 minutes.

Broil your romaine lettuce heart halves for 4 minutes.

Cook your burgers and slider patties on the stove in a pre-heated cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Add enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet before adding the patties. Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes per side, or until done.

Bake your crisp at 375°F for 30-40 minutes, until the top is golden and the blueberries are bubbling.

Make it even easier!!! As with all WTC meal plans, adjust this menu as needed! If making two types of burgers/sliders stresses you out, just stick with one and double it. If making a grilled Caesar salad feels like too much for you, buy a bagged Caesar salad kit, or buy a storebought Caesar dressing (I swear Ken’s Steakhouse is the best). You can even find “special sauce” at a lot of stores — a mayo, ketchup, relish sauce like Gaby’s. If you don’t feel like cooking dessert, just serve vanilla ice cream with sprinkles and other toppings or ask a guest to bring something sweet.

Vegetarian: Use a plant-based ground meat (like Beyond) for the Juicy Lucys and/or Chicken Caesar Sliders. For a vegetarian sub for anchovy paste, try capers or miso. Look for a Worcestershire sauce that’s labeled “vegetarian” or “vegan” as it contains anchovy too!

Dairy-free: Use dairy-free Parm, plant-based butter, DF sliced cheese (or omit the cheese for the burgers; in that case, you can just make regular burger patties for the Juicy Lucys), and dairy-free ice cream. Swap the grilled Brie out for hummus with lots of pita chips and veggies.

Gluten-free: Ingredients you’ll need to use GF versions of include the breads and buns, the breadcrumbs, the all-purpose flour, and potentially the Worcestershire sauce (read the label!).

Nut-free: Swap the peanut butter out for a seed butter like Sunbutter.

Note on beef: 80% fat/20% lean is our rec for moist and delicious Juicy Lucys. But you can use another fat combo if you can’t find 80/20!

Feeding kids: If you don’t think the bambinos in the group will eat a burger or slider (or you want to save those for the adults), add some hot dogs to the lineup and serve them with chips. A fruit salad, watermelon slices, and/or corn on the cob are always a hit for the kids table too!

Ground chicken sub: You can use ground turkey or plant-based “meat” instead of the ground chicken.

Mayo sub: Plain yogurt or Greek yogurt

Blueberry sub: Sliced strawberries, raspberries, pitted cherries, or a berry mix would all be delicious here. Either fresh or frozen work.
preparationSteps: Preheat grill (or oven) to 375°F and prepare for indirect heat (this means you will NOT be cooking the crisp over an open flame, so keep the flame under half but not all of the grill grates, and place the skillet on the section without the flame.)

In a 10-inch oven-proof skillet, toss all of the fruit filling ingredients (3 pounds blueberries, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 tablespoon vanilla extract, 1/3 cup packed brown sugar, 2 tablespoons cornstarch).

In a large bowl, stir together 1/2 cup very soft unsalted butter, 1/3 cup creamy peanut butter, 1 cup old-fashioned oats, 1 cup dark brown sugar, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Sprinkle the dough over the blueberries — don’t worry if not totally covering them, it will spread out as it cooks.
Grill for 20 to 25 minutes over indirect heat, until lightly golden on top and still very gooey.
Let the crisp rest for at least 5 minutes. Serve with vanilla ice cream!
servings: Serves 8 to 10 people (the leftovers are so good with yogurt for breakfast)

name: roasted chicken delicata squash kale apple and cheddar salad
note:
Riffs, feeding kids, what to do with your leftover rotisserie chicken, and what balsamic do I buy? If you skipped over the intro, go back up and read it! We go over all these things there!

Double the dressing: When I have delicious homemade dressing in the fridge, I’m far more likely to make salads throughout my week. You can easily double this dressing — if you’re doing so, make it in a jar or glass storage container (rather than in the serving bowl) and pour half of it into the bowl for this meal. Store the leftover dressing in that tightly sealed container in the fridge for up to a week. It’ll separate while it sits. Let it warm up slightly and shake or stir to recombine it.

Skip the dressing: Yes, you can use a store-bought balsamic vinaigrette… but it really is so easy and delicious to DIY it!

Prep ahead: The chicken and squash will stay good in the fridge for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container, so feel free to prep those ahead of time as much as you’d like!

Love your leftovers: Since kale’s a hearty green, this salad will actually hold up pretty well in the fridge if you have leftovers.

Vegetarian: Roast a can of drained and dried chickpeas. You may as well add the squash to the mix since you’ll be turning the oven on, so follow the second version of this recipe’s instructions, just using chickpeas instead of chicken. You can also add raw chickpeas, but definitely let them marinate in the dressing for at least 15 minutes.

Dairy-free/gluten-free/nut-free: Omit the cheese or use your fave DF option. It’s already gluten free! And instead of almonds, you can use seeds (roasted, salted pepitas or sunflower seeds). If you can’t eat seeds either, croutons or garlicky crunchies would be a great crunchy element!
