preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

Toss 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts and 1 sliced delicata squash with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, 2 teaspoons honey, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon of dried oregano or Italian seasoning, and several grinds pepper. Cook for 15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through (to 165°F internally), then transfer the chicken to a cutting board to rest.

Return the squash to the oven to cook for another 10 to 15 minutes, or until very tender and browned. After letting the chicken rest for 5 minutes, chop one chicken breast up. Save 1 chicken breast for later.

While the chicken and squash are cooking: In large serving bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder (or one grated clove). Taste and add 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup if your dressing is too tangy (the balsamic I use is sweet enough that I don’t need any).

Add 1 bunch finely chopped kale to the bowl of dressing, sprinkle with a big pinch of kosher salt, and use clean hands to massage the salt and dressing into the kale until it feels soft — about 7 squeezes between your palms.
Add the finely chopped chicken, roasted squash, 1 apple cut into thin batons, 1/3 cup roughly chopped almonds, 4 ounces roughly chopped cheddar cheese, and 3 chopped dates. Toss to coat. DIG IN!

name: fried chicken sandos

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 hamburger buns (ideally potato rolls or a nice brioche bun but anything works!)
ingredients.name: hamburger buns (ideally potato rolls or a nice brioche bun but anything works!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons finely minced parsley (or chives or dill or basil!)
ingredients.name: finely minced parsley (or chives or dill or basil!)

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, whisk together 2 cups buttermilk, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1 teaspoon black pepper.

Working one at a time, place a chicken breast on a cutting board and firmly press your hand over top. Use a very sharp knife to cut it into two skinny halves. Cut all of the chicken in half, adding it to the marinade as you go.
Marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour, but up to 12 hours. Don’t go much beyond 12 hours, or the chicken will start to get mushy.

While the chicken is marinating, whisk together 3 ½ cups flour, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, 4 teaspoons baking powder, 2 ½ teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon celery salt in a separate large bowl or a 9x13 baking dish is actually nice.
Preheat the oven to 250°F and place a rimmed baking sheet inside.
I like to warm my buns by just throwing them in the 250°F oven while the chicken cooks.

Pour canola oil into a wide heavy-bottomed pot such as a Dutch oven until it’s at least 3 inches deep. Heat the oil over high heat until it reaches 350F. If you don’t have an oil thermometer, the oil will look very shimmery when it’s ready.

Grab each piece of chicken out of the marinade, dredge it through the flour mixture, back into the marinade, then back into the flour mixture. Place all of the breaded chicken onto a rimmed baking sheet until ready to fry.

When the oil reaches 350°F, lower several pieces of chicken into it and cook for 5 minutes, turning several times to ensure its golden-brown all over. Transfer the chicken to the sheet pan in the oven, sprinkle with salt, and continue cooking until all chicken is cooked.

While the chicken is frying, make the herby buttermilk mayo: combine 1/2 cup mayo + 1 tablespoon buttermilk + 2 tbsp minced parsley + pinch of salt + pinch of pepper in a small bowl. Sometimes I add a shake of hot sauce in there too.
Build your sandwiches. Spread herb buttermilk mayo on both sides of the bun. Throw the chicken on there, some shredded iceberg, and lots of bread and butter pickles. Dig in!
servings: Makes 8 sandwiches (halve it all if you just want to make 4!)

name: mango pie by khushbu shah

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups finely ground graham cracker crumbs (about 24 sheets)
ingredients.name: finely ground graham cracker crumbs (about 24 sheets)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) block full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
ingredients.name: full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

To make the crust, combine 3 cups finely ground graham cracker crumbs, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 teaspoon ground black cardamom, and a pinch of salt in a medium bowl and stir to evenly combine. Pour in 1 1/2 sticks (12 tablespoons) melted butter and mix again so that the butter is evenly distributed and the mixture starts to clump together. If you’re making 2 pies, divide the mixture between 2 (9-inch) pie pans and use your fingers to press down on the mixture to create an even and compact crust that runs up the sides of the pans. If you’re making 1 large pie, line a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with parchment paper so that it overhangs the sides of the pan (this will make it easier to serve), then press the crumbs into an even layer across the bottom of the pan.

Bake for 10 to 12 minutes (you might need a few more minutes if using the 9 x 13 pan). The crust should be golden brown but not too dark—like it spent time in the sun but wore lots of sunscreen. Let cool completely.

To make the filling, pour 1/2 cup cold water into a saucepan and sprinkle 2 (3/4-ounce) envelopes unflavored gelatin over the water. Let it sit for 5 minutes, then place the saucepan over medium heat and stir until the gelatin is fully dissolved. Let the mixture cool. Transfer the gelatin mixture to a blender, along with 1 (30-ounce) can mango pulp, 1 (8-ounce) block full-fat cream cheese, and 1/2 cup condensed milk. Blitz until well combined and there are no cream cheese chunks.

Divide the mango mixture between the pie crusts or pour into the 9 x 13 pan and use a silicone spatula to make sure the filling is even and smooth. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until firm. (I prefer to refrigerate it overnight.) Serve chilled, garnished with whipped cream, if you so desire.

name: grilled chili lime chicken fajita bowls
note:
I want a sheet-pan meal/I don’t own a grill: Make it sheet-pan fajita night! Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line one full rimmed sheet pan or two half rimmed sheet pans with aluminum foil (if you want — you can also just cook straight on the pan). Spread the marinated chicken and veggies out so they are in one layer on the sheet pan(s) and bake for 30 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F internally.

Feeding kids: If your kiddos are sensitive to spice, you can cut the taco seasoning by half. You can add a couple shakes of cumin and garlic and/or onion powder for some extra non-spicy flavor. If they hate anything green, leave the cilantro out of the rice. And if they’re more likely to eat the chicken and veggies in a taco or cheesy quesadilla (like my kids), consider doing that!

Prep ahead: Get the chicken and veggies in the marinade up to a day ahead of time. You can make the slaw minus the avocado crema up to 3 days in advance — same with the rice, just store them in airtight containers in the fridge. Make the crema (and stir it into the slaw) right before you eat so the avocado doesn’t turn brown.

Love your leftovers. Leftovers will stay good in the fridge in airtight containers for up to 3 days. See delicious ways to repurpose leftovers in the “do your thing” note above the recipe!

Vegetarian: Swap the chicken for 2 packs of big portobello mushrooms caps (4 to 6 of them). You can also add drained and rinsed black or pinto beans to your bowls for extra protein.

Dairy-free/gluten-free/nut-free: Use a DF sour cream or plain yogurt for the crema, DF butter (or skip it) in the rice, and skip any cheese toppings. It’s gluten and nut free as is!

What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the slaw and rice and just serve the chicken and veggies on warmed tortillas!

ingredients.name: Crumbled cotija or shredded Mexican or Cheddar cheese, hot sauce, store-bought pico de gallo, chopped mango or pineapple, pepitas

preparationSteps: We’re going to start by marinating the chicken and veggies! In a large bowl, mix together 1/4 cup olive oil, the juice of 1 lime, 2 tablespoons taco seasoning, and 1 to 2 teaspoons kosher salt (if your taco seasoning includes salt, use 1 teaspoon). Cut 2 red bell peppers into 3 big pieces each, discarding the core. Slice 1 red onion into 1/2 inch-thick rounds. Trim any white fat off of 2 pounds (6 to 8 pieces) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, then toss the chicken and veggies in the bowl, using your hands to evenly coat everything in marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 24 hours (the longer the better!).

Make the Cilantro Avocado Crema: Go ahead and chop the entire bunch of cilantro — you’ll use some here, some in other places. Combine all ingredients (1 large ripe avocado, 3/4 cup sour cream or Greek yogurt, 1 cup chopped cilantro leaves and stems, 1 peeled garlic clove, the juice of 1 lime, 1 teaspoon honey, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt) in a food processor or blender and blend until smooth. Taste and add salt or more lime juice as desired.

Make the slaw: Add 1/2 head thinly sliced green cabbage and a big pinch of kosher salt to a large bowl and use your hands to massage the salt into the cabbage until it softens slightly. Add the remaining ingredients (1/2 cup chopped cilantro, 2 tablespoons of the Cilantro Avocado Crema, and the juice of 1 lime) and toss to coat. Add more Cilantro Avocado Crema as desired. Taste and add more kosher salt, if needed.
When you want to eat in 30 minutes, preheat your grill to medium-high heat (about 400°F).

Cook the Cilantro Lime Rice: Add 1 1/2 cups short-grain white rice, 2 1/2 cups water, 2 tablespoons butter, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a pot, stir, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low, cover, and simmer for 15 to 17 minutes, or until the rice is tender. Remove from the heat and let it sit, covered, until you’re ready to eat, at least 10 minutes. Add 1/2 cup chopped cilantro and the juice of 1/2 lime, and fluff with a fork right before you serve.

Once the grill is hot, use a grill brush to clean it well. Grab a couple paper towels (or a rag) and wad them up into a ball. Soak them with several tablespoons of oil — any kind, you can use the cheapest oil you have. You want it to be soaked but not dripping. Now, grab the ball of oily paper towels with a long pair of tongs and use it to grease the grates. This helps prevent sticking!
Place the chicken thighs, peppers, and onions on the grill and grill them for about 6 to 7 minutes per side, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 165°F and has nice grill marks.
Let the chicken rest for at least 5 minutes before chopping it into bite-sized pieces. Thinly slice the red bell peppers.
Make bowls with rice, slaw, chicken, veggies, crema, plus any desired optional toppings, such as shredded cheese, pico de gallo, hot sauce, chopped mango, pepitas, and/or more cilantro.

preparationSteps: Combine 1 1/2 cups rinsed white rice (see notes for how to rinse it), 1 can coconut milk, 1 1/4 cups water, 2 tablespoons honey, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in a wide saucepan/pot. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to the lowest heat possible and COVER for 10 minutes.

Take a big piece of parchment paper and poke holes all over it. After the rice has cooked for 10 minutes, give the rice a stir, place the parchment paper on top of the rice, and add 1 pound broccoli florets to the parchment paper. COVER and cook on low for 10 more minutes, or until the broccoli is tender to your liking (some like it super soft, some like it with a bite — do your thing!) and the rice is cooked through. Turn off the heat. Keep it covered until it’s time to serve.

While the rice is cooking, get cranking on the salmon! In a bowl, combine 1/4 cup soy sauce, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 1 tablespoon gochujang, 1 tablespoon water, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Whisk or stir until well combined.
Cut 4 salmon filets into 1-inch cubes (fyi, your top thumb joint is about 1 inch!). Season with a tiny pinch of salt.

In your largest skillet (preferably non-stick if you aren’t comfortable with cooking fish), warm enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet (it was about 2 tablespoons for my 12-inch skillet) over medium-high heat.

Add the salmon cubes in an even layer and cook until crisp, 3 to 4 minutes. Use a thin spatula to get underneath the fish without tearing it. Flip and cook for another 3 minutes, or until the salmon easily releases from the skillet. Add the bowl full of sauce plus 2 tablespoons butter to the skillet, crank the heat up to high, cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the salmon. Gently flip the salmon over a few times to coat it. Keep a close eye on things after you turn the heat up to high — we want the sauce to thicken to a nice saucy consistency, not evaporate to the point of burning. The salmon will turn a nice golden brown on the edges when it’s ready.
Make bowls with coconut rice, salmon, and broccoli. Drizzle the sauce over everything. YUMMMM!

name: parmesan pot pie

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) bag mixed frozen veggies (the kind with green beans, corn, carrots, and peas)
ingredients.name: mixed frozen veggies (the kind with green beans, corn, carrots, and peas)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups turkey or chicken stock (I use water + Better Than Bouillon!)
ingredients.name: turkey or chicken stock (I use water + Better Than Bouillon!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 2 tablespoons hot sauce (something like Frank’s, Cholula, or Red Clay Original)
ingredients.name: Optional: 2 tablespoons hot sauce (something like Frank’s, Cholula, or Red Clay Original)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups shredded cooked turkey or chicken
ingredients.name: shredded cooked turkey or chicken

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 frozen pie crust, thawed (make sure you get the rolled-up kind, not the kind pre-frozen into a pie tin!)or 1 (12-ounce) sheet frozen puff pastry, thawed
ingredients.name: frozen pie crust, thawed (make sure you get the rolled-up kind, not the kind pre-frozen into a pie tin!)or 1 sheet frozen puff pastry

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Dice 1 small yellow onion and mince 3 garlic cloves. That’s it! That’s all the chopping you have to do! Phew.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion, garlic, 1 tablespoon thyme leaves, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.

Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is tender and translucent, 5 to 6 minutes. Add 16 ounces frozen mixed vegetables and cook until they’re thaw and any excess water has evaporated from the skillet. Stir in 1/3 cup all-purpose flour until no white flecks are visible and the flour has toasted a bit, turning slightly golden brown.

Slowly stir in 2 cups chicken stock, scraping up any bits that are stuck to the skillet. Turn the heat up to medium-high to simmer the filling and thicken it to the consistency of a thick pot pie (no runny pot pies allowed). Taste and adjust for seasoning. Turn off the heat.
Stir in 3 cups shredded turkey or chicken and 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese. If you have some leftover parsley in the fridge, mince 1/4 cup and stir it in too.

Unroll 1 pie crust and place it over top of the skillet. Sometimes pie crusts can be really, really annoying to unroll. Don’t worry! It’s ok if it tears and looks ugly, just smoosh it back together! It can just hang over the sides, or you can crimp it if you’re feeling fancy. Whisk 1 egg in a small bowl with a tiny splash of water, brush it over the top of the pie crust, then, if you’re into it, sprinkle 2 teaspoons everything bagel seasoning over top. If you know your oven runs hot from the top, add the everything bagel seasoning for only the final 10 minutes of baking so it doesn’t burn.
Cut three 3-inch slits in the pie — about an inch apart from each other.
Place the skillet on a baking sheet, then bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until the pie crust is light golden-brown.
If using puff pastry, bake at 425°F for 20 minutes, then reduce to 375°F and continue cooking for 15 to 20 additional minutes, until the puff pastry is puffed up and golden.
Let it cool for 5 minutes before serving.

name: mushroom-leek galette
note:
I want a side: The simple green salad with apple cider vinaigrette from the healthy sloppy joes would be absolutely perfect to serve alongside this galette.

Must have meat: This meal is rich and filling without the addition of animal protein, but you could add some cooked ground sausage or sliced prosciutto to the mix if you’d like.

Make it cheesy: If you want a cheesier galette, similar to the tomato galette, sprinkle up to 1/2 cup of cheese on the pie dough before adding the filling. Any cheese you have will work, but 2 ounces of goat cheese or blue cheese would be wonderful, or up to 1/2 cup of shredded cheddar, havarti, gouda, or some other melty cheese.

I’ve got time to make my own dough: Use this one from the tomato galette recipe!

Prep ahead: This is a perfect make-ahead meal. You can cook the mushroom-leek filling and store it in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. If you have room in your fridge, you could also prep the whole galette, cover the sheet pan tightly with foil or plastic wrap, and pop it into the fridge up to a day ahead of time (just don’t brush the dough with the egg wash until it’s ready to bake). You could also cook the whole thing up to a day in advance, store it covered in the fridge, and reheat it just before dinner.

Love your leftovers: Leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. This is also a freezer-friendly meal, whether you want to save your leftovers in individual portions (freeze them in Ziplocs, if so!) or prep the whole thing ahead of time to enjoy weeks or months down the road. It’s fine to freeze this galette (for up to 3 months) either after it’s been cooked or before you bake it. If you do the latter, leave off the egg wash until it’s time to bake and add about 15-20 minutes to the cook time since you’re cooking it from frozen. To freeze an unbaked galette: pop it in the freezer on the baking sheet for about an hour to let it harden, then wrap it tightly in foil and plastic wrap.

Dairy-free/gluten-free: This galette’s already dairy-free if you go the nutritional yeast route. For gluten-free, make your own crust and use a gf alternative to flour (click here for both the recipe and a gf rec).

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large or 2 medium leeks, white parts only, finely chopped (about 3 cups) (how to cut and clean leeks)
ingredients.name: large or 2 medium leeks, white parts only, finely chopped (about 3 cups) (how to cut and clean leeks)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mushrooms (any kind: cremini, white, shiitake, etc.), stemmed, cleaned, and roughly chopped (about 7 cups)
ingredients.name: mushrooms (any kind: cremini, white, shiitake, etc.), stemmed, cleaned, and roughly chopped (about 7 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (9-inch) round of pie dough (store-bought is fine!)
ingredients.name: round of pie dough (store-bought is fine!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast or 2 tablespoons of any cheese
ingredients.name: nutritional yeast or 2 tablespoons of any cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Flaky sea salt, for sprinkling, preferably Maldon
ingredients.name: Flaky sea salt, for sprinkling, preferably Maldon

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

In a large skillet set over medium heat, combine 3 tablespoons of the extra-virgin olive oil, 1 large (or 2 medium) thinly sliced leeks (white parts only), a big pinch of kosher salt and black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the leeks are soft, about 4 minutes. Push the leeks to the perimeter of the pan, then add the remaining 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and 1 pound roughly chopped mushrooms. Cook until the mushrooms have given off their juices and then shriveled, about 10 minutes, leaving the leeks on the perimeter, stirring them occasionally to prevent them from burning. Stir in the leaves from 3 sprigs of fresh thyme and 1/3 cup frozen peas and cook another minute, stirring in the leeks.

Place 1 (9-inch) round of pie dough on the prepared sheet pan and sprinkle 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast (or 2 tablespoons of cheese) all over it, pressing the flakes into the dough with your fingers or a rolling pin. Spoon the mushroom-leek filling into the center, spreading it in an even layer and leaving a 1-inch border, then fold the edges in over the filling, overlapping as you work your way around the perimeter. Brush the crust with the whisked egg (or just spray with cooking spray) and sprinkle with the flaky sea salt. Bake until the crust is golden, 20 to 25 minutes.
Slice and enjoy!

name: crunchy refried bean tacos
note: I

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup plain Greek yogurt or sour cream
ingredients.name: plain Greek yogurt or sour cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 to 12 hard corn taco shells (10/10 recommend Old El Paso “Stand ‘n Stuff”)
ingredients.name: hard corn taco shells (10/10 recommend Old El Paso “Stand ‘n Stuff”)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup shredded cheese (cheddar, pepper jack, or Mexican are all great)
ingredients.name: shredded cheese (cheddar, pepper jack, or Mexican are all great)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: store-bought pico de gallo or other favorite salsa
ingredients.name: Optional: store-bought pico de gallo or other favorite salsa

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.

Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan or skillet over medium heat. Add 1 finely chopped onion (like, as small as you can possibly chop it!), 3 minced garlic cloves, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt and cook, stirring often, until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the spices (1/2 teaspoon chili powder and 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin) and cook for an additional 1 minute.

Drain 1 can pinto beans (only 1!), but don’t rinse. Add the drained beans to the skillet/saucepan. Dump the second can of pinto beans (including the liquid) into the pot along with 4 cilantro stems and 2 tablespoons water.

Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and cook for about 10 minutes, or until there’s no longer any liquid. Remove from heat. Remove the cilantro stems and use a fork or potato masher to smash the beans. They don’t need to be totally smooth, but every bean should be smashed at least a little bit. Taste and add more salt as needed.

While the beans are cooking, make the magic green sauce. Add 1 cup plain Greek yogurt or sour cream, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 lime, 1 cup cilantro leaves and stems, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of garlic powder to a blender. Blend until smooth. If needed, add some water to the blender a teaspoon at a time until the sauce reaches a smooth consistency. Sometimes using and cleaning a blender feels like a pain in the butt: if you’re in that state of mind, just chop the cilantro as finely as you can and stir everything together!

Place 8 to 12 (depending on how hungry everyone is) taco shells on a baking sheet and bake for 5 minutes just prior to eating. Do not skip this step — the shells need to be heated before eating to be crispy and delicious!
Load the tacos with refried beans, shredded iceberg lettuce, shredded cheese, store-bought salsa or pico de gallo (if using), and magic green sauce.

name: one-pot cheesy sausage & squash orzotto
note:
Sausage: if you can’t find the kind in a tube, buy links and cut them out of their casings!

Orzo: can’t find it? Use arborio or any kind of white rice instead. I am not sure how a pasta noodle would swap in!

You can use ANY ground meat, just double the salt, garlic powder, and lemon juice.

Butternut squash: buy the smallest one you can, and use the whole thing. Exact amount is not important here. Or, buy the pre-cut kind, but you need to cut it smaller than it comes! Cut each piece in half or quarters.

Gouda would also be delish! Monterey Jack or mozzarella are less flavorful, but more ooey gooey! I seriously considered goat cheese for the lead role - I encourage you to do it!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound butternut squash, peeled and chopped into 1/4-inch cubes (2 to 3 cups)
ingredients.name: butternut squash
ingredients.note: peeled and chopped into 1/4-inch cubes (2 to 3 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups ( 6 ounces) grated aged Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: ( 6 ounces) grated aged Cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Add1 pound ground sausageto a large skillet over medium heat. Cook, breaking it up with a spatula, until it starts to let off a bit of grease, 2 to 3 minutes. Add1 pound of cubed butternut squashand anda large splash of waterand continue cooking for 4 to 5 minutes until the squash is beginning to feel tender and the sausage is cooked through. If the skillet gets dry at any point, add another little splash of water.

Add1 large, minced shallotand6 minced garlic clovesand continue cooking until they’re soft, about 1 minute. Stir in2 cups orzo, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakesand toast for about 30 additional seconds.
Stir in4 cups chicken stock and 1 cup whole milkand bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low, cover, and cook for 13 to 16 minutes, or until orzo and squash are tender.
Remove skillet from heat.
Stir in1 1/2 cups Cheddar cheese, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/2 cup finely chopped Parsley, and 2 tablespoons unsalted butter.As you stir, smash the squash to combine it into the orzo.
If at any point the orzo seems too thick, and loses it’s “risotto-like” consistency, stir in a splash of water.
Stir inthe juice of 1 lemonand taste. Season with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve with lots of fresh Parm and parsley on top.

name: sesame soy tuna poke bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound fresh ahi tuna fillet, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
ingredients.name: fresh ahi tuna fillet

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 scallions, white and green parts, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions, white and green parts

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, whisk 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, 2 teaspoons sriracha, 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds, a 1-inch piece of fresh ginger (peeled and grated), and 1 grated garlic clove. Toss in 1 pound cubed fresh ahi tuna, cover, and refrigerate to marinate.

Meanwhile, cook your rice (you’ll want 1 to 2 cups of cooked rice) and prepare the toppings of your choice (1 cup shredded napa cabbage, 1 thinly sliced avocado, 1/2 cup cooked and shelled edamame, 1/4 cup shredded carrot, 1/4 cup cubed cucumber, 3 tablespoons store-bought pickled ginger).
To prepare the bowls, divide the rice, tuna, and desired toppings between two bowls. Enjoy immediately!

name: cheesy pumpkin pasta

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 cups whole milk (or any milk, but whole will work best)
ingredients.name: whole milk (or any milk, but whole will work best)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup canned pumpkin or butternut squash purée
ingredients.name: canned pumpkin or butternut squash purée

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces grated sharp Cheddar (about 2 cups grated)
ingredients.name: grated sharp Cheddar (about 2 cups grated)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces grated smoked Gouda (about 1 cup grated)
ingredients.name: grated smoked Gouda (about 1 cup grated)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to broil on high.

In a large ovenproof pot such as a Dutch oven, combine 1 pound of medium shells pasta, 2 1/2 cups milk, 3 cups water, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper.

Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the pasta is cooked. Stir often so that the milk doesn’t scorch and the pasta doesn’t stick to the pot.
We’re gonna do a little multitasking here: Grate 8 ounces of Cheddar and 4 ounces of Gouda cheese in between stirring the pasta.

When the pasta is tender and the milk has reduced to the consistency of cream, turn off the heat and let it sit for a couple minutes to cool a bit. Stir in 1 cup canned pumpkin or butternut squash purée. One handful of cheese at a time, stir in all of the Gouda and all but 2 ounces (about 1/2 cup) of the Cheddar.
Taste and add more seasonings as desired. You can eat it right now, and this is how my kids prefer it. But I love a baked mac and cheese so I….
Sprinkle 3/4 cup breadcrumbs and 2 ounces grated Cheddar over top.
Broil for 2 to 5 minutes, until golden brown and the cheese has melted.
DIG IN!

name: beach sandwiches

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can any white bean, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: any white bean

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 big ciabatta or focaccia loaf, halved through the middle
ingredients.name: big ciabatta or focaccia loaf, halved through the middle

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups crisp lettuce leaves, such as Little Gem, Romaine, butter
ingredients.name: crisp lettuce leaves, such as Little Gem, Romaine, butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 English cucumber, zebra-peeled and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: English cucumber, zebra-peeled and thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded carrots (buy a 10-ounce bag of shredded carrots)
ingredients.name: shredded carrots (buy a 10-ounce bag of shredded carrots)

preparationSteps: First, make the lemon-pickled red onions. Thinly slice 1 medium red onion and place the slices in a jar or Tupperware container. Add the juice of 2 lemons, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Get your sink water as hot as it will go, then fill the rest of the jar (to cover the onions) with hot water. Shake to combine and set aside.

Now make the avocado-bean spread: In a food processor or blender, combine the 2 pitted avocados, 1 drained and rinsed can of white beans, thejuice from 1 lemon, 1 garlic clove, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper. Blend until smooth.
Slice 1 big ciabatta or focaccia loaf in half through the middle (so that there’s a big top half and big bottom half) using a serrated knife. Spread the cut sides with the avocado-bean mixture.

Now we’re going to layer on the veggies. If you will be eating right away, as you add each layer, sprinkle a tiny bit of kosher salt onto each veggie layer. Properly seasoning each vegetable will make it an even more delicious sandwich. HOWEVER, if you’re not eating the sandwich within 30 minutes, skip this step so that the vegetables don’t sweat and make the sandwich soggy.

On the bottom half of the ciabatta, add a layer of lettuce leaves, 1 thinly sliced cucumber, 3 cups sprouts, 2 cups shredded carrots, and the lemon-pickled red onion.Drizzle lightly with extra-virgin olive oil.
Top with the top half of the loaf and cut into 4 or 6 sandwiches. Enjoy!

name: messy meatball sliders

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground beef (preferably 85/15, meaning 85% lean, 15% fat)
ingredients.name: ground beef (preferably 85/15, meaning 85% lean, 15% fat)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 ish cup store-bought pesto (or leftover hella green sauce), divided
ingredients.name: store-bought pesto (or leftover hella green sauce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4- to 6-ounce) ball fresh mozzarella (or an 8-ounce bag of shredded mozzarella if that feels easier)
ingredients.name: ball fresh mozzarella (or an 8-ounce bag of shredded mozzarella if that feels easier)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup or so marinara sauce, divided
ingredients.name: marinara sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: Everything bagel seasoning or sesame seeds
ingredients.name: Everything bagel seasoning or sesame seeds

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: Whatever greens and veggies you have in the fridge, some good olive oil, and some lemon juice or fancy vinegar (to make a simple salad)
ingredients.name: Optional: Whatever greens and veggies you have in the fridge, some good olive oil, and some lemon juice or fancy vinegar (to make a simple salad)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Line a rimmed half sheet pan with parchment paper. Add 1 pound ground beef to the center of it and add 2 tablespoons pesto, 3/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Use your hands to combine everything together, then smush it into a rectangle slightly larger than the 12-pack of slider buns (I hold the buns over top to compare).

Use a long serrated knife to cut the whole 12-pack of sweet rolls in half to make a giant top bun and a giant bottom bun. Go really slowly while you do this to try to make the top and bottom as even as possible. If you totally whiff and end up with lopsided buns, who cares. Place both the top and bottom buns cut-side up on a separate baking sheet. Spread a nice thin layer of pesto over both cut sides.
Bake the beef patty (on the oven’s lower rack) for 10 minutes. After the beef has cooked for 5 minutes, add the sheet pan with the buns to the upper rack, letting them cook for the second 5 minutes.
While the patty and buns are cooking, slice the mozzarella ball into very thin slices. Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a bowl in the microwave or in a small skillet.

Now’s also the time to throw together a simple salad if you want to, using whatever the hell you have in the fridge. Dress it by tossing it with a big pinch of salt, really good olive oil, and either lemon juice or the fanciest vinegar in the pantry.
Pour the excess grease off of the beef patty and blot it dry with paper towels.

Use a spatula and your hands to lift the giant beef patty onto the giant bottom bun. Spoon a nice messy layer of marinara sauce (about 1/3 cup or so) over top. Note: Only put marinara on as many sliders as you think your family will eat right away. The marinara will make them soggy after a while so it’s best to eat these immediately!

Layer the mozzarella slices over top of the marinara. Flip the top bun on top. Brush the top bun all over with the melted butter then sprinkle it with everything bagel seasoning. Cover the entire sheet pan with foil.

Bake for another 10 minutes, until the cheese is melty. Then take the foil off for ONE MINUTE! JUST ONE MINUTE OR THEY’LL BURN! SKIP THIS STEP IF YOU DON’T HAVE TIME TO SIT BESIDE THE OVEN AND WAIT FOR ONE MINUTE. Sorry for yelling at you but when one of you inevitably lets your tops burn, well, I tried!
While they’re in the oven, pour some marinara into a few bowls and microwave them in 20-second spurts until warm.

Let the giant slider cool for several minutes before you cut into it, or the cheese will just slide all over the place. Slice into 12 sliders. Serve with the warm bowls of marinara for dunking and the salad, if you made one.

name: sheet-pan gnocchi with sausage, brussels, mushrooms, and burrata

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound gnocchi (this is pasta, found in the pasta aisle!)
ingredients.name: gnocchi (this is pasta, found in the pasta aisle!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 to 4 ounces mushrooms (any kind — I used brown enoki)
ingredients.name: mushrooms (any kind — I used brown enoki)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mild or spicy Italian sausage links
ingredients.name: mild or spicy Italian sausage links

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: pinch of red pepper flakes, store-bought pesto if you like things extra saucy
ingredients.name: Optional: pinch of red pepper flakes, store-bought pesto if you like things extra saucy

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Trim 1 pound Brussels sprouts if they have brown roots; otherwise, you don't need to trim them. Cut them into skinny planks through the root end — as skinny as you can, 5 or 6 planks per sprout. If it gets too difficult to hold, just place it on its flat side on the cutting board and slice into skinny pieces. This is mildly tedious but it'll only take you about 5 minutes so throw on a podcast and get 'er done.
Cut 4 ounces mushrooms into 1/4-inch thick slices.

Place the veggies on your largest rimmed baking sheet along with 1 pound gnocchi. I know some of you are going to wonder if you should have pre-cooked (or thawed) your gnocchi, and nope! This is uncooked gnocchi, straight from the package. Use a microplane to grate 2 garlic cloves and the zest of 1 lemon right on top. Add ¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, 1 ½ teaspoons kosher salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper and toss to coat. Spread into an even layer.

Grab 1 pound sausage links. Squeeze the sausage out of the end of the link in ½ inch or so increments to create about 5 little meatballs per link. Plop them onto the baking sheet, on top of the gnocchi and vegetables if needed. They don’t have to be perfectly round! Just plop them down. Spread everything out as much as possible.
Take 8 ounces of burrata out of the fridge to let it come to room temperature.

Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until everything is a bit crispy on the outside, but tender on the inside. At the end, you may want to turn the broiler on (SIT ON YOUR BUTT IN FRONT OF THE OVEN AND WATCH CLOSELY SO YOU DON’T BURN DINNER!) if things aren’t looking crispy on top.

Divide between four bowls and top with burrata (the container usually comes with two balls, so I just rip them in half and plop a half onto each bowl), red pepper flakes (if you like a little heat), a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil, and/or some pesto (if you like things extra saucy).

name: crispy bbq chicken tacos

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded white (or yellow) sharp Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded white (or yellow) sharp Cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook 1 minced red onion, stirring often, until soft, 4 to 5 minutes.

Add 1 pound ground chicken, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 3/4 teaspoon garlic powder and cook, using a wooden spoon to break the chicken up into tiny crumbles, until the chicken is cooked through and all of the liquid has evaporated, 5 to 7 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop 1/2 bunch cilantro leaves and tender stems to get about 1/4 cup chopped cilantro (you can use any leftover for garnish).
Stir in 1/4 cup BBQ sauce and the chopped cilantro until incorporated. Turn off the heat and taste the BBQ chicken. Does it need more salt? More cilantro? A little pepper? Do your thing.

Place the tortillas on a large baking sheet and add 1/2 cup of the BBQ chicken to one side of each tortilla. Sprinkle a nice layer of shredded Cheddar over top, then fold it in half. Repeat until you’ve used all of the BBQ chicken.
Spray the tops of the tortillas with cooking spray (or drizzle with a bit of oil and rub it all over). Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden-brown and crispy.

Meanwhile, make some mashed avocado for dipping. Scoop 1 avocado into a bowl along with the juice of 1/2 lime, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder. Mash, mash, mash! Taste and add more lime juice if desired.
Serve the crispy tacos with mashed avocado and more BBQ sauce for dipping!

name: steak, salad & garlic fries

ingredients.rawIngredient: About 1 pound frozen French fries (McCain or Grown in Idaho are my fave brands)
ingredients.name: About 1 pound frozen French fries (McCain or Grown in Idaho are my fave brands)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 boneless ribeye, sirloin, or New York strip steaks, 1 to 1 ½ inches thick
ingredients.name: boneless ribeye, sirloin, or New York strip steaks, 1 to 1 ½ inches thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil (aka 4 tablespoons), divided
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil (aka 4 tablespoons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup parsley leaves, finely chopped
ingredients.name: parsley leaves

preparationSteps: Start by roasting about 1 pound frozen French fries in the oven according to package directions. Make sure they cook until they’re crispy though — it will probably take a little more time than what the package says.
While the fries are cooking, season 2 steaks generously with salt and pepper. A good rule of thumb is to use roughly 1 teaspoon of salt per pound of meat. Rub all over with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until just smoking. Add the steaks and cook, flipping every minute, until the steak reaches an internal temperature of 120°F for medium-rare or 130°F for medium, 8 to 10 minutes. If the steak has a thick fat cap, sear until browned. Turn off the heat, transfer steaks to a cutting board to rest, wipe out the skillet, and let it cool for a second.

To the skillet, add the remaining 3 tablespoons oil, 4 finely chopped garlic cloves, and a pinch of salt. Set over medium-low heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until the garlic is translucent but not browned, 2 to 4 minutes. Turn off the heat until the fries are ready.

When the fries are hot and ready, tilt the skillet and use a spoon to fish out the garlic, leaving as much oil in the skillet as you can. Add the garlic and ¼ cup parsley leaves (finely chopped) to the fries, season with salt and pepper, and toss to combine.

Slice the steaks against the grain. Look for the lines that run through the steak. Cut across them — perpendicular to them. Cutting against the grain makes each bite of steak more tender, because you’re cutting through tough tendons that would be difficult to chew, rather than leaving them whole.

Slice 1 lemon into quarters. Spread 1 (5-ounce) box worth of baby arugula onto a big platter (or on individual dinner plates) and drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the garlicky oil (from the skillet), a squeeze of 1 lemon wedge, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Top arugula with the steak and any resting juices. Use a vegetable peeler to shave 1 ounce Parmesan on top. Serve with the crispy garlic fries and remaining lemon wedges alongside. DIG IN!

name: 30-minute pork and kimchi CYOA bowls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups brown or white rice (or 1 or 2 bags of frozen rice)
ingredients.name: brown or white rice (or 1 or 2 bags of frozen rice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds ground pork (preferably 80% lean, 20% fat) FYI, I tried it with 95% lean pork and it’s not nearly as good (duh?) — if you ARE using a leaner meat, you’ll want to add 1 tablespoon cooking oil to the skillet before adding your meat
ingredients.name: ground pork (preferably 80% lean, 20% fat) FYI, I tried it with 95% lean pork and it’s not nearly as good (duh?) — if you ARE using a leaner meat, you’ll want to add 1 tablespoon cooking oil to the skillet before adding your meat

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup kimchi, finely chopped (mild or spicy, whatever you like!)
ingredients.name: kimchi, finely chopped (mild or spicy, whatever you like!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon gochujang (skip it if you’re feeding spice wimps)
ingredients.name: gochujang (skip it if you’re feeding spice wimps)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head romaine or butter lettuce, leaves pulled apart and washed
ingredients.name: romaine or butter lettuce, leaves pulled apart and washed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Dumpster dive for toppings like shredded carrots, thinly sliced onion, pickled jalapeños, more cilantro, diced avocado, edamame, more kimchi, chopped peanuts, etc.
ingredients.name: Dumpster dive for toppings like shredded carrots, thinly sliced onion, pickled jalapeños, more cilantro, diced avocado, edamame, more kimchi, chopped peanuts, etc.
Tahini-jang sauce (if you are sauce lovers, double this! Also, this is a great thing to make ahead of time to make dinnertime easier!):

preparationSteps: If you didn’t buy frozen rice (you really should if you’ve never tried it — it makes dinnertime that much easier), we’re gonna start out by cooking the rice, because we ALWAYS start recipes that involve rice by cooking the rice so that we don’t wind up waiting on the rice to finish cooking before we can eat dinner. We’re going to use the pasta method to cook our rice this week.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add 1 1/2 cups brown or white rice (no, you don’t need to rinse it) and reduce the heat to medium. Cook uncovered for anywhere from 7 to 8 minutes for white rice, or 25 to 30 minutes for brown rice. Taste! When it’s tender, it’s ready. Drain it in a colander, then return it to the pot along with a big pinch of salt. You can also add a little butter if you’re in the mood! Cover the pot and let it rest until dinner’s ready.

Meanwhile, cook the pork! Warm your largest skillet over high heat. Add 2 pounds of 80% lean, 20% fat ground pork and a small pinch of salt to the skillet, spread it into an even layer and let it sit for 4 minutes. Important note! If you are using a leaner cut of pork (like 95% lean) or ground chicken or turkey, you should warm 1 tablespoon cooking oil in the skillet BEFORE you add the meat.

After letting it sit for 4 minutes, use a wooden spoon or spatula to break the meat into very small crumbles and continue cooking until the pork is crisp. A lot of liquid and grease will pool in the skillet as the meat cooks, that’s normal! Keep cooking until the watery liquid has evaporated (there will probably still be a lot of grease, don’t drain it off!).
Meanwhile, chop 1 cup of kimchi into really tiny pieces.

Stir in the chopped kimchi (and any juices that accumulated on the cutting board!), a splash of kimchi brine (aka liquid), 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon gochujang (if you/your family can handle the heat!).
Continue cooking over high heat, stirring frequently, until all of the liquid has absorbed into the meat, 4 to 5 minutes.
While it’s cooking, finely chop 1/4 cup cilantro leaves and stems. When the meat looks and tastes delicious, turn off the heat and stir in the cilantro.

Also while the meat is cooking, pull apart and wash the leaves from 1 head romaine or butter lettuce. Next, it’s time to DUMPSTER DIVE! It’s been a while since we’ve done a good dumpster dive, so let me reintroduce the concept: This is when, rather than instructing you to purchase a bunch of toppings, I actually want you to use up the random bits and bobs threatening to go bad in your fridge. Grab a sad carrot and grate it up, thinly slice some celery, grab that half an onion in the back of the crisper drawer and thinly slice it. Chop up some cashews or peanuts! Check all the jars in the fridge — got any pickled jalapeños? Those will be great on here. Or, skip the dive and just serve the meat, rice, and lettuce. Delicious!

To make the gochujang sauce: Add 2 tablespoons gochujang, the juice of 1/2 a lime, 1 tablespoon tahini, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon honey to a jar and shake until combined. You might have to use a spoon to smoosh the tahini to help it incorporate. Add a tiny splash of water if needed to make it nice and drizzle-able. Taste. Too spicy? Add a little soy sauce and honey. Not thick enough? More tahini.
Lay out all your components (cooked meat, rice, lettuce, dumpster dive finds, and sauce), and let everyone choose their own adventure! There are so many ways to eat this — ideas below!
servings: Serves 4 to 6 (I find that 1 pound of ground meat cooks down so much that just 2 people can typically finish it, so we are using 2 pounds! Makes great leftovers!)

name: no-stir mushroom risotto with walnut chili crunch

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mushrooms (any kind!), washed, trimmed, and sliced (or buy them pre-sliced)
ingredients.name: mushrooms (any kind!), washed, trimmed, and sliced (or buy them pre-sliced)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 1/2 to 7 cups beef stock, divided (I use low-sodium beef-flavored Better Than Bouillon, duh!)
ingredients.name: beef stock, divided (I use low-sodium beef-flavored Better Than Bouillon, duh!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup white wine (whatever kind you like as long as it’s not super sweet … and if you don’t like white, you can use 1/4 cup red)
ingredients.name: white wine (whatever kind you like as long as it’s not super sweet … and if you don’t like white, you can use 1/4 cup red)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces (1/4 cup) grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese (aka good Parmesan), plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese (aka good Parmesan), plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup raw walnuts (or pecans, or hazelnuts, or basically any nut)
ingredients.name: raw walnuts (or pecans, or hazelnuts, or basically any nut)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Position an oven rack in the middle of your oven.
Slice 1 medium yellow onion as thinly as you can. Thinly slice 1 pound mushrooms.

Warm 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil in a large ovenproof pot over high heat. Add the sliced onions and mushrooms and stir to coat in oil. Let them sit for 3 minutes, stir, then let them sit for another 3 minutes. If the mushrooms or onions are burning, turn down the heat, but cooking them over high heat will help their moisture evaporate and let them brown quickly! Add 1 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper and continue stirring until the mushrooms and onions are very tender and browned.

Stir in 1 1/2 cups brown rice and continue stirring for 1 minute to toast the grains a bit (this adds flavor and helps the rice grains stay evenly cooked). Pour in 6 cups beef stock (or 6 cups water and 2 tablespoons beef-flavored Better Than Bouillon) and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cover the pot (use a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid!) and transfer the pot to the center rack of the oven. Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until all of the liquid is absorbed.

While the risotto is in the oven, make the Walnut Chili Crunch. Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a medium skillet (10 inches or so) over medium heat, then add 1 cup walnuts (crunch them in your fist to break them into small bits as you add them to the skillet) and a big pinch of salt and toast, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden-brown. Add the zest of 1 lemon (set the zested lemon aside — we’ll use it in a bit) and 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (depending on how much heat you like), and keep stirring for 30 more seconds (no longer — the zest and pepper flakes will burn!). Turn off the heat and stir in 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley. Leave the crunch in the skillet to cool. Taste and add more salt and red pepper flakes as needed.
After 50 to 60 minutes of baking, take the pot out of the oven.

Place the pot over low heat on the stove. Stir in 1/2 cup white wine, 1/4 cup stock, the juice of 1/2 lemon (use the one you zested for the crunch!), 1 1/2 cups grated Gruyère, and 1/4 cup grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir until the cheese is melted and the the rice has come together into a risotto consistency.
You might want to add more stock depending on how your rice is absorbing the liquid. The risotto should be saucy and loose, not thick and gloopy.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Divide the risotto between 4 to 6 bowls and add a nice sprinkle of Parm and Walnut Chili Crunch. Enjoy!

name: sheet-pan spiced chicken

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 small leeks (or 1 large red onion), trimmed and 1/4-inch sliced
ingredients.name: small leeks (or 1 large red onion), trimmed and 1/4-inch sliced

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Quarter 1 pound of baby potatoes. Trim, thinly slice, and wash 2 leeks (here’s a video to help — I like to slice them, then wash them in a salad spinner).

Add the potatoes and leeks to your largest rimmed sheet pan, along with 2 pounds chicken thighs, 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1 tablespoon cumin, 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon cayenne, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon. Use a microplane to grate 4 garlic cloves onto the sheet pan and 1 garlic clove into a small bowl.

Toss all of the ingredients on the sheet pan together, using your hands to really get in there and distribute the spices evenly. Your sheet pan will be really crowded, but I’m not mad about it — the tops of the veggies are going to crisp up, while the bottom half will be tender and jammy.

Place on the center rack of the oven and cook for 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (to an internal temp of 165°F), the leeks are frizzled on top but jammy on the bottom, and the potatoes are crispy on the outside and tender inside. If at the 30-minute mark things aren’t looking crispy, you can place the sheet pan on the top rack and broil for a couple minutes (WATCH THE ENTIRE TIME SO YOU DON’T BURN DINNER DURING THE FINAL LAP!).
While it’s cooking, make the garlic aioli by stirring 1/2 cup plain yogurt and a two-finger pinch of salt into the bowl with the grated garlic.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and thinly slice it. Toss the potatoes and leeks in the juices on the baking sheet. Serve it all with garlicky aioli!

name: beef & broccoli (and lots of other veggies)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups uncooked white or brown rice (but seriously, try to find frozen rice)
ingredients.name: uncooked white or brown rice (but seriously, try to find frozen rice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup hot water (hottest your sink will go)
ingredients.name: hot water (hottest your sink will go)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large carrots, washed well and thinly sliced (no need to peel)
ingredients.name: large carrots, washed well and thinly sliced (no need to peel)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound broccoli florets, cut into 2-inch pieces
ingredients.name: broccoli florets

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional for garnish: toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.name: Optional for garnish: toasted sesame seeds

preparationSteps: To cook the rice, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add 1 1/2 cups uncooked white or brown rice and cook for 12 to 15 minutes for white rice and 25 to 30 minutes for brown rice. Test a grain of rice starting at the lower minute mark, when it’s tender with a slight chew, it’s ready (it will continue cooking while it steams). Drain, then return rice to the pot and cover for at least 10 minutes, or until dinner time.
Thinly slice 1 pound beef sirloin. It’s a lot easier to slice if you freeze it for 30 minutes first, but I rarely have the patience to do this. Season the slices generously with salt and pepper.

In a large bowl, whisk together 1/3 cup hot water (just as hot as your sink will go), 6 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons sesame oil, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 tablespoons corn starch, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Set aside.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in your largest skillet over medium-high heat for several minutes. Add 1 thinly sliced bell pepper, 2 thinly sliced carrots, 1 pound of broccoli florets, 4 grated garlic cloves, and a grated 1-inch piece of ginger.

To grate the garlic and ginger, use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater. You do not even need to peel the ginger, just wash it. But if you prefer to peel the skin off, use a spoon to scrape the thin skin away.
Stir the vegetables for 4 to 5 minutes, until crisp-tender. Transfer them to a large bowl.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil. Pat the steak slices dry with a paper towel, then add them to the skillet in a single layer. Cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the sauce and cooked vegetables.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Serve over rice, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds.
servings: Serves 4 to 6 (bulk up your rice portion to stretch it further, or serve without rice to serve less)

name: 5-ingredient berry cobbler
preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Stir 2 pounds of berries (if you’re using strawberries, roughly chop them; otherwise, no need to prep), 3 tablespoons sugar, and 3 tablespoons cornstarch together in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet or 9x13-inch baking dish (or anything ovenproof with similar dimensions).
Pour 1 (16- to 18-ounce) box of vanilla cake mix evenly over top. Scatter 12 tablespoons of cold butter, cut into cubes, over the top.
DO NOT MIX!
Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour, until the cake turns light brown, but is still very soft looking. No worries if there are a few dry spots, they’ll dissolve right in when you scoop it out.
Serve with vanilla ice cream and/or whipped cream!

name: creamy corn pasta
note:
If your Parm isn’t pre-grated: Grate it in the blender before adding the corn! Cut off the rind and break the block of Parm into pieces. Blend until finely grated. Transfer all but 2/3 cup of the Parm to a container and refrigerate for later use.

Remind me how to mince garlic?  Use the side of your knife blade to smash the cloves as flat as possible by placing the flat part of the blade over the clove, then your fist to smash it down into the clove, then use the blade to mince, AKA very finely chop, them up.

Why do I have to use a small noodle? I only have spaghetti! Spaghetti will be great, I just really like this pasta with a small noodle shape!

Cooking school: When you thinly slice basil, it’s called a chiffonade. To do so easily, stack the leaves together, roll the stack up tightly, then cut into very thin slices.

I forgot to save the pasta water womp womp: Mix 1/2 teaspoon of cornstarch with 1 cup of water. Use this as your pasta water.

Riff: Smoky corn pasta! Char the corn on the grill (or over the open flame of a gas stovetop) before removing the kernels to add a smoky depth to the pasta. You could also add a little smoked paprika in with the corn while blending (do this is you’re using frozen corn!). If you go the charred corn route, adjust your cook time accordingly — the corn won’t need as much time on the stove, since it’ll already be cooked.

Feeding kids: My kids LOVE this pasta. I call it “sugar pasta” because the corn makes it delectably sweet lol. If your kids hate all things green, just top your individual serving bowls with the basil rather than stirring it in! You can also omit the red pepper flakes if they’re super sensitive to spice. If you’re worried your kids might not love it, reserve some pasta on the side that isn’t tossed in the sauce and add whatever sauce they like to it. Grab an extra ear of corn and serve them pasta and corn separately instead of together!

Prep ahead/love your leftovers: This pasta is delish stored in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 4 days. When you reheat, add splashes of water to loosen things up.

Gluten-free: Swap in your favorite gluten-free pasta.

Dairy-free: Just use DF butter and omit the Parm — it’s still absolutely delicious without it. Seriously: bookmark this one if you ever need to cook for someone who’s dairy-free!

Must have meat: Grilled chicken, shrimp, pork tenderloin, or salmon would be lovely with this pasta! See the “summer feast loading” note above the recipe for a specific idea.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound farfalle, orecchiette, rigatoni gigante, cheese tortellini (!!) or another small-ish noodle
ingredients.name: farfalle, orecchiette, rigatoni gigante, cheese tortellini (!!) or another small-ish noodle

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 large ears corn, husked, kernels removed (about 2 3/4 cups [315 g] kernels) OR 2 (16 ounce) bags frozen corn (ideally white corn)
ingredients.name: corn, husked, kernels removed (about 2 3/4 cups [315 g] kernels) OR 2 bags frozen corn (ideally white corn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/8 teaspoon red pepper flakes, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup water (not the reserved pasta water)
ingredients.name: water (not the reserved pasta water)

preparationSteps: In a large pot, bring salted water to a boil and cook 1 pound farfalle until al dente per package instructions. Use a coffee mug or glass measuring cup to scoop up and reserve 1 cup of the pasta cooking water (!!! I’m bolding this so you don’t forget it!!! When you forget it anyway, see the notes section below!) and drain the pasta.

Meanwhile, make the corn pasta sauce! Dice 1 large shallot and mince 2 garlic cloves. Cut the kernels off of 6 ears of corn. To do this without kernels flying everywhere, lay your corn flat horizontally on the cutting board rather than putting a skinny tip on the cutting board!

In a large sauté pan or skillet over medium heat, melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter. Add the shallot, garlic, and 1/8 teaspoon red pepper flakes and cook, stirring frequently, for 3 to 5 minutes, until the shallot is translucent. Add the corn kernels and 1/2 cup water (just tap water! not the pasta cooking water) and cook over medium-high for 4 to 5 minutes, until tender.

Transfer the corn mixture to a blender and add 2/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese, the juice of 1 lemon, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Blend on high speed until smooth. Add a little of the reserved pasta water, as needed, to make it pourable and smooth. Taste. This sauce should be absolutely delicious. If it is a little flat, it needs lemon juice and/or salt. If it is a little bland, your corn might not have been perfectly sweet and delicious. Add a tiny bit of sugar to bring it to life.
Pull the leaves off of 1/2 bunch fresh basil and thinly slice them (see notes for a tip!).

Add the cooked pasta back to the pot you cooked it in, then pour in the corn sauce and a big handful of sliced basil. Toss to combine, adding additional splashes of the reserved pasta water if the sauce seems too thick. Add additional lemon juice, kosher salt, or red pepper flakes if needed until it tastes delicious.
Transfer the pasta to bowls. Garnish with more basil, Parm, and red pepper flakes.

name: summer chop with (or without) perfect-every-time pan-seared chicken breasts
note:
Cook once, eat twice: I highly recommend doubling this dressing! Store half of it in the fridge to enjoy with another salad later this week. If it separates, just let it warm up a little and whisk it again to re-emulsify it.

I want to grill! Grill the corn and chicken at the same time! Corn grilling instructions are above. Grill the chicken over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until 165°F internally.

Prep ahead: The vinaigrette can be made up to 4 days ahead and stored in the refrigerator. You can cook your corn up to 3 days in advance, too — either store it on the cob or off in an airtight container in the fridge.

Love your leftovers: Leftover chicken will keep for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container. Make tacos or quesadillas with it. Add it to a pasta dish. Turn it into chicken salad. So many options! Leftover salad might get a little soggy (it’s best within 2 hours of making it), but I’d still eat it within 2 days! Leave the avocado out if you don’t anticipate eating the whole thing — it’d turn brown.

Vegetarian: Serve your summer chop with pan-fried tofu or portobello mushrooms, or add some crispy chickpeas to the salad.

Bulk it up: Add any grain to your plate. Couscous would be great! To cook: In a medium saucepan, bring 1 1/2 cups water, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt to a boil over high heat. As soon as the water is boiling (it won’t take long!), remove the pot from heat, stir in 1 1/2 cups couscous (one 10-ounce box), cover the pot (use a sheet pan if you don’t have a lid), and set it aside to steam while you cook the rest of this meal.

Dairy-free: Omit the feta.

Gluten-free/nut-free: Already is!

Feeding picky eaters: Scroll up to the intro and read about how I deconstruct this meal for my kids.

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: Any other seasonings you have and love like Lemon Pepper or Italian, to taste
ingredients.name: Optional: Any other seasonings you have and love like Lemon Pepper or Italian

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or avocado oil, or whatever neutral oil you have)
ingredients.name: olive oil (or avocado oil, or whatever neutral oil you have)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (from about 2 lemons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tiny garlic clove, grated (omit if you are a person who finds raw garlic spicy/offensive in any way!)
ingredients.name: tiny garlic clove, grated (omit if you are a person who finds raw garlic spicy/offensive in any way!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil (or olive oil, avocado oil, or whatever neutral oil you have)
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil (or olive oil, avocado oil, or whatever neutral oil you have)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ears of corn (I like white corn), shucked
ingredients.name: of corn (I like white corn), shucked

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 of a small red onion, diced (about 1/3 cup)
ingredients.name: of a small red onion, diced (about 1/3 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces snap peas or snow peas (about 2 cups), very thinly sliced
ingredients.name: snap peas or snow peas (about 2 cups), very thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and black pepper

preparationSteps: We’re going to start by cooking the corn for the salad. You can either cook your corn on the stovetop or on the grill — your choice!

To cook the corn on the stovetop: Cut the kernels off of 4 ears of corn with a chef’s knife (lay the corn flat on your cutting board to do this). Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet or saucepan that has a lid over medium-high heat, and sauté the corn for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly charred. Transfer the corn to a bowl or plate to cool. To grill the corn: Shuck the corn, brush the cobs with oil (just as much as it takes for them to be lightly coated), and grill on high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side (for a total of 8 to 10 minutes). Let cool, then slice the kernels off the cob.
Let the corn cool while you cook the chicken.
Season 4 (6-ounce) chicken breasts to taste with kosher salt, black pepper, and optionally, any other seasonings you’re feelin’! I typically season with salt and lemon pepper.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet or saucepan that has a lid (the same one you just cooked the corn in, if you cooked it inside) over medium-high heat. Add the chicken to the skillet and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown. Flip and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is also golden brown.

After the chicken is seared all over, reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes (set a timer!). Take the lid off and use a meat thermometer to ensure your chicken has reached an internal temp of 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and allow it to rest for 5 minutes.
While the chicken is cooking and resting, we’re going to make the salad.

Make the Lemon Vinaigrette: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 teaspoon honey, a big pinch of kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper. While whisking continuously, slowly drizzle in 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil until emulsified (AKA, all combined and thickened). Taste and add more kosher salt and/or pepper, if needed, until it tastes perfect.

Dice 1/2 a small red onion and add it to the dressing — letting it sit in the dressing will mellow out its sharp bite. Dice 2 English cucumbers, halve 1 pint cherry tomatoes, and very thinly slice 10 ounces snap peas. Finely chop 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, and 2 tablespoons fresh dill. Add it all to the bowl of dressing along with the cooled corn kernels and 8 ounces crumbled feta cheese (this is a solid amount of cheese — start smaller if you wish!).
Toss gently to combine. Let the salad sit for at least 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

Just before serving, dice 1 large avocado, and gently toss it in along with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper. Adding the salt at the last minute is important so that the salad doesn't release too much liquid. Taste. If needed, add more salt and pepper until delicious.
I like to serve this meal two ways (as shown in the pictures above):
Choose your adventure and dig in!

name: Cream Cheese Macaron Filling
note: This small batch recipe makes the perfect cream cheese macaron filling! It's tangy, sweet, and makes just the right amount to fill a batch of macarons.

ingredients.name: cream cheese, room temperature (1/4 cup)

ingredients.name: salted butter, room temperature (2 Tbsp)

preparationSteps: Beat 56g room-temperature cream cheese and 28g room-temperature butter on a medium-high speed for 2 minute with a hand mixer until combined and fluffy.
Mix in 4g vanilla extract on a low speed.
Slowly add in 125g of powdered sugar. Halfway through add 10g of heavy cream or milk to make the filling easier to mix.
If the frosting is too thick, add in additional heavy cream or milk (1 tsp at a time). If the frosting is too thin, add in more powdered sugar (1 Tbsp at a time).
Once the frosting is the right consistency, place in a piping bag with a round tip.
After pairing up your macaron shells, pipe a dollop of cream cheese buttercream on one macaron shell. Gently press a second shell on top of the frosting to create a sandwich.
Place the finished macarons in an airtight container and chill in the fridge overnight, then enjoy! Store any leftover macarons and/or filling in the fridge.

ingredients.name: superfine almond flour - blanched (1 1/2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ml vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (1 tsp)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (1 tsp)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ml heavy whipping cream, room temperature (2 tsp)
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream, room temperature (2 tsp)

preparationSteps: Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper or Silpat mats. Set aside.

Pour 110g of aged egg whites into the bowl of a stand mixer with a whisk and mix on a medium speed until the surface of the egg whites is covered in small bubbles. Add 1/4 tsp cream of tartar and continue to mix until it reaches the soft peak stage and leaves visible tracks.

Gradually mix 110g of granulated sugar into the egg whites over a few minutes while mixing on a medium-low speed. Increase the mixing speed to a medium-high speed (6 on a KitchenAid). Keep mixing until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Sift 140g of superfine almond flour and 125g of powdered sugar into the meringue. Use a rubber spatula to break up any big clumps and press them through the sieve.

Add in a squirt of gel food coloring if desired. Then fold the ingredients together with a rubber spatula. Use a circular motion that sweeps around the edge of the bowl and then pulls through the bottom of the bowl to make sure everything is getting mixed together. Don't forget to scrape off the inside of the spatula intermittently. Sometimes meringue can get stuck there and not get mixed in properly.

Fold the batter until a thick ribbon of batter runs off the spatula when it's lifted. You should be able to draw a couple of figure 8s with the batter running off your spatula in a continuous stream when it's the right consistency. If the stream of batter breaks before you're able to do this, you may need to stir it a bit more.
Pour the batter into a large piping bag fit with a medium-sized round piping tip and pipe 1 1/2-inch rounds on the prepared baking sheets. Space them about 1 inch apart.
Bang the pans firmly on the counter a few times to release air bubbles, then pop any remaining air bubbles that come to the surface with a toothpick.
Let the macarons rest for 30 minutes, or until they develop a skin. The macarons should look matte once the skin has formed. While the macarons rest, preheat the oven to 320 F/160°C.

Bake one tray of macarons at a time on the middle rack of your oven for 18-21 minutes and rotate the pan halfway through to help the macarons bake evenly. Bake time can vary based on the size of your shells, so if you pipe them smaller than 1 1/2 inches, they may be done a few minutes earlier.

Remove the macaron shells from the oven and let them cool fully on the pan (about 30 minutes), then gently peel them off the Silpat mat. If they're properly baked, they should peel off the mat cleanly and have a shiny bottom.
While the macaron shells bake and cool, make the filling for the macarons.
Beat 56g of room-temperature butter on a medium speed for a minute with a whisk attachment until it becomes lighter in color and smooth.
Mix in 4ml vanilla extract and 1g salt on a low speed. Slowly mix 125g of powdered sugar and 10g of heavy cream on a low speed.

Continue to mix on low for a couple of minutes until the ingredients are fully incorporated and the desired consistency is reached. If the frosting is too thick, add in additional heavy cream or milk (1 tsp at a time). If the frosting is too thin, add more powdered sugar (1 Tbsp at a time).
Place in a piping bag with a small round tip, and set aside.
Pipe a small dollop of frosting or filling of your choice on the center of one macaron shell and top with a second shell to create a sandwich.
Place the finished macarons in an airtight container and chill in the fridge overnight, then enjoy!
