name: Mini Key Lime Pies
note: What's better than key lime pie? Little mini key lime pies!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 and 1/2 cups (180g) graham cracker crumbs (about 12 full sheet graham crackers)
ingredients.name: and 1/2 cups (180g) graham cracker crumbs (about 12 full sheet graham crackers)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces (113g) full-fat brick cream cheese, softened to room temperature
ingredients.name: full-fat brick cream cheese, softened to room temperature

ingredients.rawIngredient: one 14-ounce can (396g) full-fat sweetened condensed milk
ingredients.name: one 14-ounce can (396g) full-fat sweetened condensed milk

ingredients.rawIngredient: optional: lime slices and whipped cream for garnish
ingredients.name: optional: lime slices and whipped cream for garnish

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (177°C). Line a 12-count muffin pan with liners and a second 12-count muffin pan with only 4 (since this recipe makes only around 16). Set pans aside.

Before you begin, here are all of my tips for a perfect graham cracker crust. If you’re starting out with full-sheet graham crackers, you can use a food processor or blender to grind them up. Or crush them in a zipped top bag with a rolling pin. Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and granulated sugar together with a silicone spatula in a medium bowl until combined. The mixture will be thick, coarse, and sandy. Press a heaping Tablespoon of mixture down into each liner, making sure the crust is tight and compact. You might have a little crust leftover. If so, press a little more into each liner—if desired! Pre-bake the crusts for 5 minutes. Remove from the oven.

In a large bowl using a handheld or stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, beat the cream cheese on high speed until smooth, about 1 minute. On medium-high speed, beat in the egg yolks, scraping down the sides as needed. On high speed, beat in the sweetened condensed milk and lime juice until combined.

Pour the filling evenly into each crust. Bake for 15–16 minutes or until the centers of the pies only slightly jiggle (I check this by wiggling the muffin pan—with an oven mitt on!—while it’s still in the oven). Allow the pies to cool at room temperature in the pan set on a wire rack. Once completely cool, place the pan in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours and up to 1 day.
Once chilled, serve the key lime pies cold with whipped cream and a lime slice if desired. Store leftover pies in the refrigerator (covered) for up to 1 week. If they last that long!

name: Santa Maria Style Tri-Tip
note: Tri-tip beef roast, from the bottom sirloin, is one of the best steak cuts for grilling. Rub it up with seasonings and then grill with wood chips for a unique and simply unbeatable smoky flavor.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tri-tip roast (also known as triangle steak, a bottom sirloin cut), anywhere from 2 1/2 pounds to 4 pounds, look for one well-marbled with fat
ingredients.name: tri-tip roast (also known as triangle steak, a bottom sirloin cut), anywhere from 2 1/2 pounds to 4 pounds, look for one well-marbled with fat

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon coarse or chunky kosher salt
ingredients.name: coarse or chunky kosher salt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon dried rosemary (or fresh, finely minced)
ingredients.name: dried rosemary (or fresh, finely minced)

preparationSteps: Mix the rub and massage into roast: Mix the rub ingredients together in a bowl. Place the roast in a roasting pan or a baking pan with edges (this will help keep the rub from getting all over the floor). Sprinkle the rub on the meat on all sides, and massage the rub into the meat.

Cover the steak and let sit at room temp for an hour: Cover the roast with foil or plastic wrap and let it sit at room temp for an hour to take the chill off and allow the rub to work its magic on the roast.

Prepare the grill: Prepare your grill for hot direct heat on one side, and indirect heat on the other. (By the way, if you are working with a wood-fired grill, Santa Maria BBQ traditionally uses red oak wood.)

Sear the roast: Sear the roast for 3 to 4 minutes per side. Carefully watch the roast during this process as one side of the roast is typically quite fatty and as the fat heats up it can drip down and cause flare-ups. Keep moving the tri-tip away from the flame if flare-ups occur.

Move the roast to cool side of grill, fat side up: Once the tri-tip is seared on all sides, move it away from direct heat and place it fat-side up on the grill rack. If you are using a gas grill with a top rack, I recommend placing the roast on that rack, with an aluminum tray on the bottom rack underneath to catch the fat drippings. If you are grilling on charcoal or wood, you may want to turn the roast over every few minutes, for more even cooking. Try to maintain a grill temperature of 250°F to 300°F.

Cover the grill, finish cooking: Cover the grill and cook until the temperature of the interior of the tri-tip reaches 120°F for a rare roast, 130°F for medium-rare and 140°F for medium. At this point the meat will take anywhere from 20 to 40 minutes to cook, depending on how hot your grill is, how well done you want it, and the size of the cut. Note that the interior temperature will continue to rise at least 5°F after you take the roast off the heat.

Tent the roast with foil to let it rest: Once the roast reaches temperature, remove it from the grill and let it rest, loosely tented with foil, for 10 to 15 minutes. Slice across the grain to serve. Did you enjoy this recipe? Let us know with a rating and review!

name: spicy cherry tomato and garlic pasta
note:
I don’t want it to be spicy: 2 teaspoons of chilli/red pepper flakes will have a good bit of heat. If you’re feeding kids or people who don’t love spice, reduce it!If you want mild heat, use 1/4 teaspoon or less for the whole recipe.If you want gentle warmth, use 1/2 to 1 teaspoon. If you want noticeable spice, use 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons.

If you want mild heat, use 1/4 teaspoon or less for the whole recipe.

If you want gentle warmth, use 1/2 to 1 teaspoon.

If you want noticeable spice, use 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons.

I can’t eat tomatoes: See the “on the flip side…” note above the recipe for what to cook tonight instead.

Prep ahead: Pre-chop/mince your garlic and onion up to 2 days ahead of time and store them in the fridge in an airtight container. You can also pre-slice your cherry tomatoes and store them in the fridge.

Love your leftovers/feeding 1 or 2: Reheat leftovers in a skillet over medium heat and stir in a splash of water at a time as needed until it’s saucy again. Taste and re-season with salt and pepper if needed. You could also easily halve this recipe!

Freezer-friendly: This sauce freezes well for up to 6 months. Just whip it out any time you’re craving a really delicious pasta — it’s a game changer on a rushed night.

Must have meat: If you want to cook some meat to accompany your pasta, here are some great options: basil balsamic grilled chicken, the most perfect grilled chicken, shrimp cooked on the stovetop in olive oil with salt and pepper, grilled shrimp, Crash’s pork tenderloin, or meatballs

Gimme some greens: Make a simple side salad!

Dairy-free/gluten-free: To eliminate dairy, use a plant-based Parm for the garnish or just omit it. And to avoid gluten, use any GF noodle you love! Cook it just as you would the spaghetti.

Whoops, I know you told me not to, but I accidentally drained all the pasta water: It happens! Starchy pasta water serves as a thickening agent to make our sauce creamy. To replace it, make a slurry: Mix 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch or flour with 2 cups of water and microwave the mixture for 1 to 2 minutes until hot.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons chilli flakes/red pepper flakes or a minced red Fresno chile (reduce this if you don’t want your sauce to be spicy! see the notes section below recipe for more)
ingredients.name: chilli flakes/red pepper flakes or a minced red Fresno chile (reduce this if you don’t want your sauce to be spicy! see the notes section below recipe for more)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 bunches of fresh basil, leaves and stems separated
ingredients.name: of fresh basil, leaves and stems separated

ingredients.rawIngredient: Pasta water, reserved from the cooking pot
ingredients.name: Pasta water, reserved from the cooking pot

ingredients.rawIngredient: Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano, finely grated, for garnish
ingredients.name: Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano, finely grated, for garnish

preparationSteps: Thinly slice 3 cloves of garlic (if you love garlic, you can add an extra clove or 2) and finely mince 1 shallot. You want the shallot really finely minced – no large pieces of onion, just keep running that knife through until it looks like it’s been grated through a microplane.

Add 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil to a large skillet off heat. Add the prepped garlic and shallot along with 2 teaspoons of chilli flakes/red pepper flakes (or less if you don’t want that much spice — see notes below recipe for more) and 2 bunches of basil stems (6-12 stems). These contain heaps of flavor, which will infuse nicely. Save the basil leaves for later.

Turn the heat under the pan on to medium-high and allow everything to sizzle and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes until it’s all nice and fragrant. You aren’t looking for any color or browning on the onion or garlic, so keep an eye on it and reduce heat if needed. Remove and discard the basil stems.

Add in 2 heaping tablespoons of tomato paste and stir to combine. Continue to sauté everything for another 1 to 2 minutes. The tomato paste will start to darken and stick to the bottom of the pan – that’s exactly what you’re after. This is extra flavor that will seep into the sauce during the next few steps.

Halve 2 pints of cherry tomatoes. Add the cherry tomatoes to the skillet and season with some sea salt and black pepper, to taste. Stir everything together for a minute so that it’s all coated in the tomato paste and the ingredients are evenly dispersed.
Pour in 1/2 cup (150 ml) white wine (or water). Stir to combine and allow it to simmer away and reduce for around 2 minutes.
Cover the skillet with a lid and reduce the heat down to medium. This will create a nice steamy environment for the tomatoes to soften and break down, and prevent any unwanted splattering!

Let simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, then remove the lid and take a peek. The tomatoes should have broken down nicely and released lots of their juices. Use a spatula or potato masher to mash the tomatoes down gently to extract all their additional flavor (it will only take a few presses). The tomato skins will have loosened and should be scattered throughout the sauce. Optionally, you can fish the tomato skins out using tongs (I do this because I find the result worth it, but it’s tedious, and the sauce is delicious either way).

Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Add more sea salt if the flavors are dull, or more red pepper flakes if you want additional spice. Let things gently bubble away on medium-low, uncovered, as you move on to the next step.

Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil over high heat. I advise using about half the amount of water as the box of noodles tells you to — this will give your pasta water a higher concentration of starch, which will help your tomato sauce become more cohesive later. Once boiling, add 1 pound of spaghetti and cook for 7 minutes, or until very al dente — 2 minutes less than the lower end of your package instructions.

Once al dente, use tongs to transfer the pasta directly to the tomato sauce — no need to drain it, the starchy pasta water is welcome here. Add in an additional ladle of your pasta water and allow the pasta to finish cooking in the tomato sauce. You want it to be bubbling away nicely and for the pasta to absorb all of that goodness.
After 3 to 4 minutes, the sauce should have thickened slightly, and the pasta should be cooked but still nice and al dente. Use the pasta water to adjust consistency if you want it slightly looser.
Turn off the heat, then add in some torn basil leaves and give everything a good stir. Adding the fresh basil at this stage will impart a really delicate herbal note.

Use your tongs to grab a hefty amount of the pasta and place the tip of the tongs into the middle of a large ladle — begin twirling and continue to twirl until you have a nice, neat serving, then add to a plate. Alternatively, carefully pour out all the spaghetti onto one large serving bowl and serve family-style.
Top with any remaining tomato sauce and garnish with some extra-virgin olive oil, finely grated pecorino Romano (or Parmigiano Reggiano), and a few fresh leaves of basil.

name: greek-style sheet-pan gnocchi with lemon dill yogurt sauce
note:
My gnocchi package isn’t 12 ounces: Gnocchi packages vary, typically ranging from 9 to 12 ounces depending on the brand. Anywhere in that range is great, or, if you are buying a 9 ounce package, you’re welcome to grab 2 and double the gnocchi! See the “bulk it up” note for more on this.

Bulk it up: If you know you have extra-hungry family members or you want to have leftovers for tomorrow’s lunch, you can double the amount of gnocchi for a heartier meal. If you do this, you may want to assemble across 2 sheet pans so everything still gets crispy (or just use one reallyyyy large sheet pan) and add a little extra oil.

Can I use parchment paper to make clean up easy? I try to avoid using parchment for sheet-pan gnocchi because it gets less crispy and delish IMO, but for easy clean up, that would be OK!

Clean out the fridge: Let this recipe use up any veggies hanging out in your fridge! Just make sure you don’t over-crowd your sheet pan by doing so. Try to swap and sub in even cup amounts to the recipe as written for best results.

Gimme a short cut: Use pre-chopped veg! There isn’t a ton of chopping required here, but for the places it is needed, go for pre-chopped/sliced, if you can find it at the store.

Feeding kids: Add the dill to individual bowls instead of the whole sheet pan if the green would scare them off.

Prep ahead: Add all of the prepped sheet pan components, aside from the oil, spices, and lemon halves, to a large mixing bowl. Cover and leave it in the fridge for up to a day, until you’re ready to transfer to the sheet pan and get cooking. You can even measure out your spices in a pinch bowl ahead of time and set aside. The yogurt sauce (sans roasted lemon) can be prepped ahead and stored in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 7 days.

Love your leftovers: Store the sheet pan components and yogurt sauce separately in sealed containers in the refrigerator for up to 4 and 7 days, respectively. Add the roasted veggies to a scramble in the morning, mix them into a grain bowl or another pasta dish, or even use them as pizza toppings. Leftover chicken sausage and feta can also be added to a variety dishes, including eggs/omelettes. The yogurt sauce has endless uses—on a sandwich, grain bowl, in a wrap, or as a dip for veggies/chips.

How should I reheat this? For best results, return the sheet pan components to a sheet pan and roast at 425°F for 6 to 10 minutes, until warmed and re-crisped. Plate with the yogurt sauce and serve. Alternatively, microwave the sheet pan components until warmed, about 2 minutes, and plate with the yogurt sauce.

Vegetarian: Use plant-based sausages or a can of drained, rinsed, and dried chickpeas.

Gluten-free: It already is if you use the gnocchi Jenn recommends in the recipe!

Dairy-free: Use a DF feta (or omit it and add some extra olives for their saltiness) and dairy-free plain yogurt for the sauce.

What to do with your leftover red onion: Make pickled red onions! Here’s a recipe.

ingredients.name: pre-cooked chicken sausage
ingredients.note: cut into 1/4-inch slices (I recommend spinach and feta chicken sausage)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8-ounce block feta cheese, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
ingredients.name: feta cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 (ish) ounces potato gnocchi (shelf stable or frozen both work! I used shelf stable gluten-free gnocchi)
ingredients.name: (ish) ounces potato gnocchi (shelf stable or frozen both work! I used shelf stable gluten-free gnocchi)
For the lemon dill yogurt sauce:

ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh dill, additional for topping

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup whole-milk or low-fat Greek yogurt (or non-dairy yogurt of choice)
ingredients.name: whole-milk or low-fat Greek yogurt (or non-dairy yogurt of choice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more to taste

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F and grab the largest sheet pan you own. If you’re using a non-stick sheet pan, you don’t have to prep it in any way. If yours is aluminum rather than non-stick, spray it with cooking spray.

Cut 12 ounces of pre-cooked chicken sausages into 1/4-inch slices and add them to the sheet pan. Thinly slice 1/2 a red onion (reserve the other half for another use), dice 1 small zucchini, and cut an 8-ounce block feta cheese into 1/2-inch cubes. Add it all to the sheet pan along with 12 ounces potato gnocchi, 1 cup of cherry tomatoes, and 1/3 cup pitted kalamata olives.

Pour 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper on top and use clean hands to toss and coat everything in the oil and spices. Arrange all of the components in a single layer on the sheet pan so nothing overlaps. Place 1 halved lemon, face down, on each end of the sheet pan in a cleared space.
Bake until the vegetables and gnocchi are lightly crisped and the feta is soft, 20 to 24 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the yogurt sauce. Finely chop 2 tablespoons of fresh dill and add it to a small bowl along with 1 cup yogurt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and whisk to combine. Set aside.

Remove the roasted lemon halves from the sheet pan and squeeze them directly into the yogurt sauce (if you don’t love a strong lemon taste, start with one half and taste before adding the second half). Stir again to combine and season with additional kosher salt, if needed, to taste.
Sprinkle the sheet pan with additional chopped dill. Add about 1/4 cup of the yogurt sauce onto four plates and spread it out, then evenly divide the sheet pan components on top of the sauce. Dig in!

name: chicken sausage, spinach, and white cheddar egg bake

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 ounces chicken sausages, sliced into rounds
ingredients.name: chicken sausages

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 ounces fresh baby spinach (or 10 ounces frozen spinach, thawed and drained)
ingredients.name: fresh baby spinach (or 10 ounces frozen spinach

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces cream cheese, cut into tiny pieces
ingredients.name: cream cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces white Cheddar cheese, shredded (about 2 cups), divided
ingredients.name: white Cheddar cheese, shredded (about 2 cups)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 275°F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Heat 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully add 12 ounces sliced chicken sausage and 1 diced red bell pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sausage is browned on both sides and pepper is softened, about 6 to 7 minutes. Add the baby spinach and cook until wilted (if using fresh) or heated through (if using frozen). Season to taste with kosher salt and black pepper.

In a large bowl, whisk together 12 large eggs, 1/2 cup whole milk, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes until well combined.

Spread the sausage and vegetable mixture evenly in the prepared baking dish. Scatter 4 ounces of cream cheese cut into tiny pieces and sprinkle 1 1/2 cups shredded white Cheddar cheese over top. Pour the egg mixture over everything. Top with remaining 1/2 cup shredded white Cheddar cheese.
Bake for 1 hour, or until the center is set and the top is golden brown. A knife inserted in the center should come out clean.
Let cool for 5 minutes before slicing and serve warm.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound skinless salmon filets, cut into 1-inch cubes
ingredients.name: skinless salmon filets

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons all-purpose flour, divided
ingredients.name: all-purpose flour

ingredients.rawIngredient: Neutral oil, such as avocado or vegetable
ingredients.name: Neutral oil, such as avocado or vegetable

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, minced or grated
ingredients.name: fresh ginger

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup shelled edamame (frozen is fine, but ensure you thaw it for this recipe)
ingredients.name: shelled edamame (frozen is fine, but ensure you thaw it for this recipe)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional garnish: sesame seeds (toasted if you have them!), sriracha
ingredients.name: Optional garnish: sesame seeds (toasted if you have them!), sriracha

preparationSteps: Melt 3 tablespoons unsalted butter in a small pot over medium-low heat. Add 1 1/2 cups rinsed white rice, stir to coat it in butter, and toast the rice for 1 minute. Stir in 2 1/2 cups water, 2 tablespoons sesame oil, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt and raise the heat to high to bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, turn the heat off but leave the rice covered until ready to eat.

Meanwhile, make the salmon. Cut 1 pound skinless salmon filets into 1-inch cubes (1 inch is about the size of your top thumb joint) and season it with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds black pepper. Sprinkle salmon with 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour and toss it around to coat it (yes, right there on the cutting board!). It's fine if it doesn't all stick, but you want each piece of salmon to be covered in flour.

In your largest skillet (preferably nonstick, especially if you aren't super comfortable with cooking fish), warm enough neutral oil to coat the bottom of the skillet (it was about 2 tablespoons for my 12-inch skillet) over medium-high heat.

While it's heating, make the sauce: In a small bowl, stir together 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1/4 cup brown sugar or honey, 1/4 cup water, 3 minced garlic cloves, a 1-inch piece of grated/minced fresh ginger, and 2 teaspoons all-purpose flour. Set aside.

Carefully add the salmon cubes to the skillet in an even layer and cook until browned on the bottom, 3 to 4 minutes. Use a thin spatula to get underneath the fish without tearing it. Flip the salmon and cook for another 2 minutes, then add the sauce to the skillet and cook for an additional 1 to 3 minutes, until the sauce thickens and coats the salmon. Gently flip the salmon over a few times to coat it. Keep a close eye on things — we want the sauce to thicken to a nice saucy consistency, not evaporate to the point of burning.
Use a fork to gently fluff the rice.
Make bowls with rice, salmon, and plenty of sauce. Top with diced cucumber and thawed edamame. Garnish with sesame seeds and sriracha if you'd like. ENJOY!

name: ricotta custard pancakes
note:
Love your leftovers: Store any leftover pancakes in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat them in the oven (at 350°F for 5 to 10 minutes, covered with foil), on the stove top over medium heat until warmed through, or in the microwave. If microwaving, wrap them in a damp paper towel and heat them in 20-second bursts until warmed through.

Freezer-friendly: You can also freeze any leftover pancakes! Let them cool completely then transfer them to a zip-top airtight bag, placing a small sheet of parchment between each pancake so they don’t stick together. Reheat them from frozen (no need to thaw!) in the oven or toaster oven.

Vegetarian: Already is, unless you don’t eat eggs. In that case…

Egg-free: This won’t yield the exact same pancakes of course, but here’s a good workaround if you can’t eat eggs! For the egg whites, use 3 tablespoons aquafaba (the liquid from a can of chickpeas). Whip them like you would the egg whites. For the yolks, use flax “eggs” — mix 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed + 5 tablespoons warm water (let it sit 5 minutes to gel).

For the egg whites, use 3 tablespoons aquafaba (the liquid from a can of chickpeas). Whip them like you would the egg whites.

For the yolks, use flax “eggs” — mix 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed + 5 tablespoons warm water (let it sit 5 minutes to gel).

Dairy-free: Use dairy-free ricotta, a non-flavored plant-based milk like unsweetened oat or almond milk, and a plant-based butter or oil for greasing your skillet.

Gluten-free: Use a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour instead of all-purpose flour.

Must have meat/gimme a side: Read the “make it a meal” section above the recipes for easy meat ideas and/or a vegetarian side!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large eggs, yolks and egg whites separated
ingredients.name: large eggs, yolks and egg whites separated

ingredients.rawIngredient: Unsalted butter, for cooking and serving
ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, for cooking and serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Maple syrup, powdered sugar, and/or fresh fruit, for serving
ingredients.name: Maple syrup, powdered sugar, and/or fresh fruit, for serving

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, whisk together 1 scant cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon sugar, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder. Set this bowl aside. FYI, a “scant” cup means just short of a full cup — AKA, do not pack the flour in there to be even across the top of the measuring cup! It should hit right beneath the line.

OK, now we’re going to separate our 2 eggs. To do this, set your small and your medium bowls out on the counter side by side. Crack an egg and, working over the small bowl, gently pass the yolk back and forth between the two halves of the broken egg shell, letting the egg white drip down into the small bowl. Once the egg whites have oozed out, drop the yolk into the medium bowl. Repeat with the second egg.
To the medium bowl with the egg yolks, add 1 cup whole milk ricotta and 3/4 cup whole milk and whisk together until well combined and very smooth. Set this bowl aside.
Preheat a 10-inch or larger cast-iron skillet (or griddle) over medium-low heat while you whip the egg whites (which is our next step!).

In the small bowl, use a whisk (or handheld electric mixer on medium speed) to whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, about 3 minutes. Yes, your hand will get tired, but keep whipping — your pancakes will be SO light and fluffy. Set this bowl aside.

Add the ricotta mixture to the bowl with the dry ingredients and whisk gently until just barely combined. Then use a silicone spatula to stir in a small amount of the egg whites to lighten the batter. Finally, fold in the rest of the egg whites with a light touch.
Melt just enough unsalted butter in the skillet to coat the surface and increase the heat to medium.

Measure a scant 1/4 cup of the batter into the pan. If it doesn’t immediately begin to sizzle, wait until it does before pouring out more pancakes. Cook the pancakes on the first side until the bottoms are golden brown and bubbles appear around the edges, 2 to 3 minutes. Use a thin flexible metal spatula to flip — this is when they will thrillingly begin to defy gravity — and cook until golden brown on the second side, another 1 to 2 minutes.
Sometimes I like to flip a second time to make sure the pancakes get completely cooked through, but the only way to be sure that they are cooked is to tear one open and check.

Transfer the pancakes to individual plates or a warmed serving platter, wipe out the pan, and repeat with remaining batter. Serve immediately, with butter or ghee; syrup, jam, or powdered sugar; fresh fruit; or any other desired garnishes.

name: 30-minute crunchy-cheesy bean bake
note:
Can I use fresh tomatoes instead? Yes! If your garden is still producing, you can swap the can of diced tomatoes for 2 cups of chopped tomatoes (any kind!).

What to serve with this: You don’t have to put anything else on your plate — you’ve already got beans and cheese for protein, tomato and onion for veg, and breadcrumbs for a grain. But if you’re wanting to round out the meal, Jenny recommends a VERY simple green salad — something like arugula + salt + pepper + lemon juice + EVOO (or a bagged salad kit!) — and/or a loaf of crusty bread for dipping.

Must have meat: With fiber- and protein-packed legumes (the beans!), this meal is satiating and satisfying all on its own. That said, if you want to stretch the meal further, it goes beautifully with any meat. Here are a few ideas: Perfect Pan-Seared Chicken Breasts: Season 4 (6 ounce) chicken breasts to taste with kosher salt, black pepper, and optionally, any other seasonings you’re feelin’! Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet or saucepan that has a lid over medium-high heat. Add the chicken to the skillet and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown. Flip and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is also golden brown. After the chicken is seared all over, reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes (set a timer!). Take the lid off and use a meat thermometer to ensure your chicken has reached an internal temp of 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and allow it to rest for 5 minutes.Pesto Shrimp: Toss 1 pound of peeled, deveined shrimp in pesto (store-bought or homemade) and let them marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes. Grill the shrimp on skewers, or cook them for about 4 minutes in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally.Crash’s Pork Tenderloin: Recipe hereChicken Parmesan Meatballs: Recipe here

Perfect Pan-Seared Chicken Breasts: Season 4 (6 ounce) chicken breasts to taste with kosher salt, black pepper, and optionally, any other seasonings you’re feelin’! Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet or saucepan that has a lid over medium-high heat. Add the chicken to the skillet and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown. Flip and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is also golden brown. After the chicken is seared all over, reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes (set a timer!). Take the lid off and use a meat thermometer to ensure your chicken has reached an internal temp of 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and allow it to rest for 5 minutes.

Pesto Shrimp: Toss 1 pound of peeled, deveined shrimp in pesto (store-bought or homemade) and let them marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes. Grill the shrimp on skewers, or cook them for about 4 minutes in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally.

Crash’s Pork Tenderloin: Recipe here

Chicken Parmesan Meatballs: Recipe here

Prep ahead: You can prep your bean bake until just before the step when you add the mozzarella and panko topping up to a day ahead of time. Let the skillet cool completely then either cover it with its lid, or wrap it tightly with plastic wrap/foil and store it in the fridge. That way all you have to do is top it with the mozzarella slices and the panko mixture and bake right before dinner! Add a few extra minutes to the cook time since it’ll be cold coming out of the fridge.

Save time: Buy pre-diced onion from the store.

Love your leftovers/freezer-friendly: Leftovers will be delicious for up to 4 days stored in the fridge in an airtight container. You could also freeze any leftovers to enjoy for dinner weeks from now. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge, then cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 20ish minutes, until heated through. Take the foil off for the last few minutes to let the panko topping crisp up again. If you want, you could freshen things up with a new batch of the panko mixture. If you’re baking from frozen, it’ll take closer to an hour to warm through.

Feeding kids: Like Jenny said in the intro, this is a very kid-friendly recipe! If they are wary of anything green, skip the thyme or just mince the leaves up very finely. The oregano should blend in.

Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free Parm like VioLife and a dairy-free mozzarella like Miyoko’s. Alternatively, if you don’t like plant-based cheese, you could add 2 tablespoons of nutritional yeast to your panko breadcrumbs mixture for vegan cheesy flavor.

Gluten-free: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs.

Bean-free: If you can’t do beans, swap them out for a pound of cooked ziti noodles (or any noodle! Banza would be good for the added protein) for a baked ziti situation.

ingredients.name: of dried red pepper flakes

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups cooked white beans, such as gigantes or cannellini, or 2 (15-ounce) cans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: cooked white beans, such as gigantes or cannellini, or 2 cans

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but delicious: a simple green salad (or even a bagged salad kit!) and/or a crusty loaf of bread, for serving
ingredients.name: Optional but delicious: a simple green salad (or even a bagged salad kit!) and/or a crusty loaf of bread, for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Finely chop 1/2 a medium yellow onion and mince 2 garlic cloves.

Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a deep, large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet along with a pinch of red pepper flakes, a large four-finger pinch of kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper and cook until the onion is soft, about 3 minutes.

Add 1 heaping tablespoon of tomato paste and smush it in with a wooden spoon until the onion becomes pink and the paste gets toasty and deepens in color a bit. Stir in 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, 1 tablespoon dried oregano, and 1/4 cup water, increase the heat to medium-high, and cook until warmed through, about another 5 minutes. Add the beans (3 cups cooked white beans or two 15-ounce cans of rinsed and drained white beans) and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are warmed through, another 4 to 5 minutes.

While the beans warm, prepare your panko topping. In a small bowl, use a fork to mix together 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, the leaves from 3 fresh thyme sprigs, and the remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil until every crumb is glistening with oil.

Arrange 5 thin slices of mozzarella over the warm beans, then, using your hands, evenly sprinkle the panko mixture around the slices, covering as much of the beans as possible. Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 15 minutes, until bubbly and golden. Sometimes I broil this at the very end to help along the browning.
Serve with a simple green salad and/or crusty bread, if desired.

name: Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Cookies
note: These soft and chewy apple cinnamon oatmeal cookies are exploding with sweet apple flavor. Filled with cinnamon and apple spices, loaded with applesauce and apple chunks, and topped with a creamy maple icing, they’re absolutely perfect for the fall season. Do not skip reducing the applesauce on the stove (step 1); it is key to the texture and flavor.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, softened to room temperature

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup (100g) light or dark brown sugar (I use dark)
ingredients.name: light or dark brown sugar (I use dark)

preparationSteps: Place the applesauce in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a low boil and then simmer, stirring occasionally, until the amount is reduced by half (to 1/3 cup/80g). On my stove, this takes about 10 minutes. Transfer the applesauce to a heat-proof bowl and set aside to cool to room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (177°C). Line large baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone baking mats.
Whisk the oats, flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, allspice, and nutmeg together in a large bowl. Set aside.

Using a handheld or stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, beat the butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar on medium speed until creamed together, about 5 minutes. (Here’s a helpful tutorial if you need guidance on how to cream butter and sugar.) Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl with a silicone spatula as needed. Add the reduced applesauce, egg yolk, and vanilla, and beat on medium-high speed until combined. Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl as needed.
Add in the dry ingredients and beat on low speed until combined. Finally, beat in the chopped apples and walnuts (if using). The cookie dough will be thick and sticky.
Using a medium cookie scoop, scoop mounds of cookie dough (about 1.5 Tbsp/35g of dough each) and arrange 3 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets.

Bake for 14–16 minutes or until lightly browned and set around the edges. The cookies will look very soft in the middle but will continue to set as they cool. Remove the cookies from the oven and allow to cool for 10 minutes on the baking sheet, then transfer to a cooling rack.

In a small saucepan over low heat, melt the butter and maple syrup together, whisking occasionally. Once the butter has melted, remove from heat and whisk in the sifted confectioners’ sugar. Taste. Add a pinch of salt, if desired. Drizzle over cookies. Icing will set after about 1 hour.
Store cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

name: German Chocolate Cupcake Recipe
note: This german chocolate cupcake recipe is made with moist chocolate cupcakes, decadent chocolate frosting and that classic coconut pecan topping we know and love.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup milk or dark chocolate chips (60g)
ingredients.name: milk or dark chocolate chips (60g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (4g)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (4g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2/3 cup packed dark or light brown sugar (133g)
ingredients.name: packed dark or light brown sugar (133g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (4g)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (4g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup (1/2 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature (56 grams)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature (56 grams)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 tsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (2g)
ingredients.name: vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste (2g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup dark or Dutch-processed cocoa powder (22g)
ingredients.name: dark or Dutch-processed cocoa powder (22g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 Tbsp heavy whipping cream, room temperature (45g)
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream, room temperature (45g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup dark chocolate, melted and cooled (45g)
ingredients.name: dark chocolate

preparationSteps: Begin by preheating oven to 350°F / 175°C. Place 12 cupcake liners in cupcake pan.

Add 3/4 cup buttermilk, 1/3 cup chocolate chips, and 1 tsp instant espresso powder into a heat proof bowl. Heat in the microwave at power level 8 for 1 minute or over a double boiler until the chocolate has melted. Don't worry if the buttermilk separates a little after it's heated!
Whisk together until the ingredients are combined and all the chocolate is melted. The mixture might look a little separated, but it will come together once you add in the dry ingredients.

Sift 3/4 cup all purpose flour, 3/4 cup granulated sugar,  1/3 cup cocoa powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt into chocolate espresso mixture and stir until combined. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl as needed with a spatula.
Add 2 large eggs, 1/3 cup vegetable oil, 1 tsp vinegar, and 1 tsp vanilla. Mix until the batter is smooth.
Fill the cupcake liners 2/3 full and bake for about 18-20 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Let the cupcakes cool for 5 minutes in the pan before moving them to a cooling rack to finish cooling.
While the cupcakes bake and cool, make the German chocolate cake (or in this case cupcake) filling.
In a medium saucepan combine 1/2 cup evaporated milk, 2 egg yolks, 2/3 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup butter and 1/2 tsp salt.

Cook the mixture over a medium heat. Stir constantly until the mixture thickens (you don't want to the egg yolks to scramble!). This usually takes me 7-10 minutes. Test the mixture by dragging a rubber spatula through the center of the pan. If it's ready, you should be able to see the bottom of the pan for a few seconds before the filling covers it.
Remove the filling from heat and pour into a large bowl.

Fold in 1 cup of shredded coconut, 1 cup chopped pecans, and 1 tsp vanilla extract with a rubber spatula. Mix until the coconut and pecans are fully coated in the mixture. Set aside to let the filling cool to room temperature.
While the cupcakes cool, make the chocolate buttercream. Beat 1/4 cup of unsalted butter on a medium speed for 30 seconds with a hand mixer until smooth.
Mix in 1/2 tsp vanilla extract and 1/4 tsp salt on a low speed.
Slowly mix in 1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1/4 cup dark cocoa powder, and 3 Tbsp heavy cream on a low speed. Scrape the side and bottom of the bowl as need with a rubber spatula.
Mix in 1/4 cup of cooled, melted dark chocolate.
Beat on low until the ingredients are fully incorporated and the desired consistency is reached.
If the frosting seems too thick, add an extra Tbsp of heavy cream. If it's too thin, add in another 1/4 cup of powdered sugar.
Stir by hand with a rubber spatula to get the frosting SUPER smooth. Place into a large piping bag fit with a Wilton 1M frosting tip.

To decorate these German chocolate cupcakes, use a cookie scoop to add a generous dollop of cooled coconut pecan filling on top of each cupcake. If you don't have a cookie scoop, use a large spoon to add about 1 Tbsp of filling on top of each cupcake.
Smooth out the coconut mixture with an offset spatula to create a flat, even layer.
Pipe a rosette on top with the chocolate buttercream using a Wilton 1M piping tip, then enjoy!

name: maple-roasted butternut squash and chicken salad
note:
I need an onion slicing tutorial: You got it! Click here and scroll down to the “thinly sliced onion” section.

I need a butternut squash cutting tutorial: I filmed a tutorial for you almost exactly 5 years ago (while wearing baby Calum!).

Prep ahead/cook ahead/love your leftovers: This is a great meal to chip away at to make your before-dinner cook time as short as possible. This salad dressing will keep for up to 2 weeks stored in an airtight container in the fridge, so make it as far ahead of time as you’d like. The roasted veggies and chicken can be cooked up to 3 days ahead of time and stored in the fridge in airtight containers. And the kale can also be chopped, washed, and dried up to 3 days ahead of time. If you are planning to meal prep this salad (it’s a good-all-week salad!), you can hold the nuts and apple, adding them to individual servings to keep them fresh. If you have leftovers with those mixed in, they’ll still be great! Store it in an airtight container, and enjoy it over the next 3 to 4 days.

What do I serve this in? Find all of our favorite salad serving bowls and coupe bowls, which are ideal for dinner salads, here.

Bulk it up/feed more people/feed less people: Add a cooked grain like farro, quinoa, or brown rice to bulk it up. You could easily double this salad if feeding a crowd — you’ll just need to use more sheet pans. Alternatively, you could halve it if you are feeding 1 or 2 and don’t want leftovers.

Feeding kids: Serve the salad deconstructed if your kids prefer meals that way — mine certainly do. My guys had chicken, candied nuts, feta, apple, and a few pieces of squash (that they hated if I’m being honest) all in separate piles. They actually loved this meal (minus the squash!). You may also want to try the hot meal riff — see the “I’m not in the mood for a salad” note above the recipe. You can call the crispy kale “green chips.”

Make it a side: Simply cut the chicken to make it a side salad. It’d be amazing on a Thanksgiving table.

Vegetarian: Swap the chicken for a can of chickpeas that you’ve drained, rinsed, and patted dry. Keep the chickpeas on the baking sheet with the squash and onion for the full 30 minutes of cook time. I also like the idea of adding the chickpeas even if you are also using chicken!

Dairy-free: Omit the cheese or use a dairy-free sub you love (like DF Parm or feta or a sprinkle of nutritional yeast).

Gluten-free: All the ingredients in this recipe are inherently gluten free, but you should double check the ingredient labels for the Dijon mustard, candied nuts, and dried fruit to be sure there aren’t any additives that contain gluten.

Nut-free: Roasted pepitas or sunflower seeds, or just omit. If you are omitting but want some crunch, you could add croutons or smashed pita chips instead.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons lemon juice (from typically 1/2 of a large lemon)
ingredients.name: lemon juice (from typically 1/2 of a large lemon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: A few grinds of black pepper
ingredients.name: A few grinds of black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound cubed butternut squash (1-inch cubes, if you’re cutting it yourself) (preferably fresh but frozen works — cook straight from frozen, if using)
ingredients.name: cubed butternut squash (preferably fresh but frozen works — cook straight from frozen, if using)
ingredients.quantity: 1 pound (1-inch cubes, if you’re cutting it yourself)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 fresh thyme sprigs or 3 fresh rosemary sprigs
ingredients.name: fresh thyme sprigs or 3 fresh rosemary sprigs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch curly kale, de-ribbed and chopped (or a 10- to 12-ounce bag of pre-chopped kale, tough stems picked out)
ingredients.name: curly kale, de-ribbed and chopped (or a 10- to 12-ounce bag of pre-chopped kale, tough stems picked out)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 dates, chopped, or 1/4 cup dried cranberries or golden raisins
ingredients.name: dates, chopped, or 1/4 cup dried cranberries or golden raisins

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup candied pecans or roasted pecans or pistachios
ingredients.name: candied pecans or roasted pecans or pistachios

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces goat cheese or feta, crumbled
ingredients.name: goat cheese or feta, crumbled

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Make the dressing: Add 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, 1 heaping teaspoon Dijon mustard, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and a few grinds of black pepper to a jar, seal it with the lid, and shake until well combined. If you don’t have a jar, you can whisk the dressing ingredients together in a bowl. Set aside.

Slice 1 red onion 1/4-inch thick. Add it to a rimmed sheet pan along with 1 pound cubed butternut squash and 6 fresh thyme sprigs (or 3 fresh rosemary sprigs). Add 2 tablespoons of the maple-balsamic dressing and 1 teaspoon kosher salt to the sheet pan and use your hands to toss until the veggies are all lightly coated. Spread the vegetables out evenly and roast for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, de-rib and chop 1 bunch of curly kale. Wash and spin it dry. Place it in a large serving bowl. If you’re using pre-chopped bagged kale, pull out any big pieces of stem you see as you add it to the serving bowl.

After the vegetables have roasted for 20 minutes, stir them, then add 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts to the baking sheet. Drizzle the chicken with a little bit of the maple-balsamic dressing and season generously with kosher salt and black pepper. Roast everything for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken registers an internal temperature of 160°F (while the chicken cools, the temperature will continue to rise to reach 165°F) and the squash is super tender. Set aside to cool down. If the chicken reaches 160°F before the squash becomes super tender (you should be able to easily squish a piece of squash with a fork), continue cooking the squash and onions until it is while the chicken cools.

While the chicken and squash are cooking, let’s “massage” our kale. Add 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to the kale and squeeze it in your hands 5 to 10 times until it feels softened, but not wet. Thinly slice 1 large apple and chop 5 dates and add them to the bowl along with 1/2 cup candied nuts and 8 ounces of crumbled goat or feta cheese.

When the chicken has cooled enough to handle it, chop into bite-sized pieces and add it to the salad along with the roasted squash and onions. You can discard the herb sprigs — they will have imparted their flavor on everything.

Add desired amount of dressing and toss to combine. Remember that you can always add more dressing but you can’t take it off, so add it a little at a time until it’s dressed to your liking. For what it’s worth, I use the entire amount! Season to taste with kosher salt and black pepper. Serve the salad in bowls and enjoy!

name: spicy (or not) pork, eggplant, and basil
note:
What kind of ground pork? Try to get a fattier one, like 80% lean/20% fat. If you can only find 93% lean, you will need to add extra oil to the skillet with your veggies because you won’t have any grease from the pork. I’d use a neutral oil like avocado or light olive oil rather than additional sesame oil.

What kind of eggplant? I really love Chinese eggplants, which are long and skinny with thin skin. If you can find them, a pound of those would be my pick! Otherwise, globe eggplant(s) work.

What are scallions? They’re the same thing as green onions! You are going to use both the white and green parts — you only need to trim off the roots.

Prep ahead: If you’d like to chip away at the prep work to make cooking this meal more passive, you can pre-mix the sauce up to 2 days in advance and store it in an airtight container in the fridge, and chop and slice your veg up to a day ahead (again, store them in an airtight container in the fridge).

Love your leftovers: These leftovers are SO GOOD. They will keep for up to 3 or 4 days in the fridge — reheat them on the stove or in the microwave, adding a splash of water to loosen up the sauce.

Freezer-friendly: This is a great stock-the-freezer meal! Let the finished dish cool then add it to a zip-top bag or airtight freezer-friendly container, and freeze for up to 4 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge then reheat on the stove, adding a little water to loosen up the sauce.

Double/halve it: You can double or halve this recipe, if needed. If your skillet isn’t big enough to hold the doubled ingredients (mine isn’t), you could use a big pot like a Dutch oven or a huge wok instead — just increase cook time as needed to reach the visual cues for doneness.

Feeding picky eaters: Go easy on the chili crisp/spicy element! Remember that you can always add more to individual servings at the end. If your kids don’t like saucy dishes, you can pull out some cooked pork, eggplant, and bell pepper for them before you add the sauce. When I was feeding my boys, I plated those with rice and fruit.

Vegetarian: Get 2 blocks of extra-firm tofu. Squeeze as much moisture out as possible over the sink, then crumble the tofu directly into the hot sesame oil. Use your spatula to break it apart, we’re going for ground meat vibes.

Dairy-free: Already is!

Gluten-free: Use coconut aminos or tamari in place of the soy sauce. Make sure you are using a GF chicken stock (most are!) and spicy ingredient (some chili crisps contain gluten).

Nut/seed-free: Don’t add the nut garnish. Swap the sesame oil for a neutral one like canola or avocado oil.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground pork (see notes for pork buying tip)
ingredients.name: ground pork (see notes for pork buying tip)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound eggplant (typically equal to 1 large or 2 small eggplants), cut into 1/2-inch cubes
ingredients.name: eggplant (typically equal to 1 large or 2 small eggplants)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions, roots trimmed off and discarded, sliced about 1-inch thick diagonally
ingredients.name: scallions, roots trimmed off and discarded, sliced about 1-inch thick diagonally

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup fresh basil leaves, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons rice vinegar (either seasoned or unseasoned will work)
ingredients.name: rice vinegar (either seasoned or unseasoned will work)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons chili crisp, sriracha, or sambal oelek
ingredients.name: chili crisp, sriracha, or sambal oelek

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 big handfuls of spinach, torn (or roughly chopped)
ingredients.name: big handfuls of spinach, torn (or roughly chopped)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: chopped roasted cashews or peanuts
ingredients.name: Optional: chopped roasted cashews or peanuts

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon sesame oil in your largest skillet over high heat. Add 1 pound ground pork and a sprinkle of kosher salt and break up into 1/2-inch-ish pieces (some will be much smaller, that’s OK). Cook, stirring every few minutes, until the pork is golden-brown and crispy all over, about 8 minutes total. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked pork to a bowl, leaving all of the pork grease in the skillet.

While your pork is cooking, cut 1 large or 2 small eggplants into 1/2-inch cubes, slice 1 large red bell pepper, and slice an entire bunch of scallions about 1-inch thick diagonally. Thinly slice about 1 cup of fresh basil leaves. Keep the scallions and basil separate from the eggplant and bell pepper — they will be added at different times.

Once you have removed the cooked pork from the skillet, add the remaining 3 tablespoons sesame oil to the pan, then add the chopped eggplant, sliced bell pepper, and a pinch of kosher salt. Cook, stirring every 3 minutes or so, until the eggplant is golden-brown and very tender, about 10 minutes total.

While the veggies are cooking, make the sauce. In a medium bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken stock, 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 to 2 tablespoons chili crisp (depending on your spice preference!), and 2 teaspoons brown sugar or honey.

Once the eggplant is golden-brown and tender, add the sliced scallions, 2 big handfuls of spinach (tear it into bite sized pieces as you add it), most of the sliced basil (reserve some for garnish), the cooked pork, and the sauce to the skillet. Stir until the sauce has thickened and everything is well coated.
Serve in bowls, garnished with basil, more chili crisp, and chopped cashews or peanuts, if you’ve got them.

name: Cinnamon Maple Rice Krispie Treats
note: Brown butter, maple syrup, and cinnamon create a fall flavored treat that is easy to make!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 oz cinnamon sweet bits (plus more for topping)
ingredients.name: cinnamon sweet bits (plus more for topping)

preparationSteps: Prepare a 9x13 dish by spraying with oil, then line it with parchment paper. Spray the paper lightly and set the pan aside for later.
Place the butter in a large pot and melt over a medium- low heat. Once melted, bump the heat up to medium and cook, stirring regularly, until the butter begins to turn a light amber.

Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the marshmallows. Once the marshmallows are starting to melt and incorporate into the butter, place the pot back on a low heat. Stir until the mixture is completely melted and combined.

Remove from the heat and stir in the maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt. Once well combined, scrape any excess mixture off of the spatula and spray the spatula with oil. Fold in the puffed rice cereal and cinnamon sweet bits until completely combined.

Dump the mixture into the prepared pan and press gently into an even layer. Sprinkle with a few more cinnamon sweet bits and use a greased spatula to gently, but firmly, press it into the pan. I like to finish it off by greasing the bottom of a glass and gently pressing the surface to ensure it is well packed and even.
Let the rice krispie treats cool and set up for at least 30 minutes, or overnight. Once firm, slice into squares.
To store: layer the squares between parchment paper in an airtight container. Keep on the counter for up to a week.

name: citrusy carnitas
note:
Save time: I said it a few times above, but I’ll say it again: When you’re grocery shopping, ask the butcher if he or she would be so kind as to cube your pork butt/shoulder for you. If they aren’t busy, they more than likely will! That is the most time-consuming part of this process.

I’m feeling extra: You are welcome to add more spices to your pork, like chili powder, smoked paprika, taco seasoning, or chipotle peppers. But why mess with perfection?

Use your slow cooker: This is a great slow-cooker meal. Add the ingredients to your slow cooker and cook on low for 5 to 6 hours or high for 3 to 4 hours, or until the meat shreds easily with a fork. To crisp it up at the end, transfer the pork and juices to a skillet or Dutch oven and cook it as written, stirring until the liquid evaporates and the meat crisps up. Or just skip the crisping step, it’ll still taste great.

There are many more ways to enjoy carnitas! I gave you a few ideas in the headnotes, but here are some more: Cubano sandwiches, quesadillas, pork buns, pork chili verde, cheesy pork sliders, bo ssam lettuce wraps, breakfast sandwiches, pork and beans, pork and pineapple fried rice, burritos, chop sandwiches… anything else!?

Feeding kids: These carnitas aren’t spicy, so just serve them however your kids are most likely to eat them! Quesadillas? Nachos? By themselves with rice and corn on the side?

Prep ahead/love your leftovers: You can store your carnitas in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. The best way to reheat them is in the oven. The goal is to NOT dry out your meat after you put all that time into cooking it low and slow the first go round! So put the pork in an oven-save dish and add a bit of water (or broth or even orange juice) to add back some of the moisture it will have lost. Cover the dish with foil and bake it at 300°F for about 20-30 minutes, or until the meat reaches 165°F. You could also use the same approach on the stovetop, heating it over low or medium-low with a little added liquid. Or just use the microwave in 20-second bursts so you don’t overdo it. See the “make it a meal” section above the recipe and the note just above and choose a new way to serve them for lunches!

Freezer-friendly: Carnitas are perfect to stock your freezer with, too. Once they have cooled completely, transfer them to an airtight freezer-safe zip-top bag or container and freeze for up to 3 months (or however long you feel comfortable with, I am personally very generous with my freezer foods’ lifespan!). Thaw overnight in the fridge and follow the reheating instructions just above.

I don’t have enough time to cook this, but now I want carnitas: Cook this recipe instead! Or use boneless,skinless chicken thighs and only cook them for an hour!

Vegetarian: No way to avoid meat here. Instead, have a taco night with crunchy refried bean tacos instead! Or make some chipotle black bean flautas, or cheesy rice and beans.

Dairy-free/gluten-free/nut-free: These carnitas are inherently dairy, gluten, and nut free, just choose your serving style and accoutrements accordingly.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 pounds boneless pork shoulder or butt, cut into 2-inch pieces (you can ask your butcher to do this for you!)
ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder or butt
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch pieces (you can ask your butcher to do this for you!)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Cut 4 pounds boneless pork shoulder or butt into 2-inch pieces, discarding any large hunks of fat. Add pork to a large Dutch oven or 12-inch cast-iron skillet and season with 1 tablespoon kosher salt. Add 1/2 cup orange juice, the juice of 3 limes, and 2 bay leaves. Using the side of your knife, smash 8 garlic cloves. Peel away and discard the skins and add the smashed cloves to the pot/skillet.

Cover the pot or skillet with its lid (if you don’t have a tightly fitting lid, you can cover it tightly with foil instead), and roast for 2 hours, or until the meat easily shreds when prodded with a fork. I know it seems counter-intuitive, but if your meat cannot easily shred and seems tough, KEEP COOKING IT! Also, you don’t actually have to shred it all right now, it’ll break apart on its own when we stir later.
Remove the lid from the Dutch oven/skillet and cook uncovered for 30 additional minutes, until most of the liquid has evaporated. Remove and discard the bay leaves.
Transfer the skillet to the stovetop, turn the heat to medium-high, and cook, stirring every few minutes, until all liquid evaporates and the meat breaks up into pieces and crisps up.
Serve as desired — find lots of ideas (including the burrito bowls pictured above) in the headnotes!

name: good mood chicken and bean soup
note:
Don’t even dirty a knife! Use pre-chopped kale — tearing any big pieces and removing thick stems as you add it to the pot — and 6 cubes of frozen crushed garlic to make this recipe chop free.

Extra extra: On the other hand, if you have a little extra time and energy, dice a medium yellow onion and add it to the pot along with the beans and other ingredients. If you want to really amp things up, you could sauté the onion first (plus any other extra veg you want like diced zucchini and/or red bell pepper) in 2 tablespoons of sun-dried tomato oil (or olive oil) until soft and translucent. Do that before you add the beans, chicken, etc.

I want some bread: Buy a nice crusty loaf to serve with your soup, or make some homemade croutons like we did here.

Use your slow cooker: This is an excellent slow cooker recipe. Add all the ingredients except for kale, cream, and Parm. Cook covered on low for 6 hours, then shred the chicken and return it to the slow cooker along with the remaining ingredients. Let it cook for another 30 minutes with the lid off for the kale to wilt and flavors to meld.

Use your pressure cooker: Cook this soup (all the ingredients except for the cream and Parm) for 15 minutes on high pressure with a natural release. Stir in the dairy elements at the end along with your shredded chicken.

Feeding kids: You can leave the red pepper flakes out or reduce them for anyone who’s sensitive to spice. Cashy and Molly’s son Cole both inhaled this soup! For pickier eaters/soup haters, you could deconstruct it by serving shredded chicken alongside cooked kale and beans, plating them with cubes of Parm.

Love your leftovers/freezer-friendly: Leftovers will last for up to 4 days in the fridge. It reheats beautifully in the microwave or on the stovetop. You can also freeze it! I like to freeze my soups in quart-size zip-top bags. Fill the bags and let them freeze flat on a sheet pan. Once frozen, remove them from the sheet pan and your flat bags will store easily. Thaw frozen soup in the fridge overnight, then reheat on the stovetop or in the microwave. If needed, add a splash of broth or water to loosen things up.

Double it: Use your hugest pot and double this recipe to freeze half for later! See freezer note above for tips.

I can’t do beans: Beans are a big part of the equation here. Browse our soup index for a delicious bean-free option!

Vegetarian: See the “make it vegetarian” note above the recipe.

Gluten-free/dairy-free: This soup is already gluten free (just double check that your chicken broth doesn’t contain any gluten). And see the “make it vegan” note above the recipe for how to easily cut dairy. Here’s one more idea to cut dairy…

Make it creamy but creamless: Add an extra can of cannellini beans. After the soup has simmered for 20 minutes, scoop 2 ladles full of beans and broth into a blender and blend until smooth. Add the blended mixture back to the pot for extra creaminess.

preparationSteps: In a large colander, drain and rinse 1 can chickpeas, 1 can cannellini beans, and 1 can kidney beans. Add the beans to a large, heavy-bottomed pot.

Finely chop 4 cups of kale (remove and discard the kale’s thick stems/ribs before you chop it — or, if you’re using pre-chopped bagged kale, sort through it to pluck out any thick stems you see), and peel and mince 6 garlic cloves. Add them to the pot along with 1 1/2 pounds of boneless, skinless chicken, 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, 1 drained jar of oil-packed julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes, 6 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1 teaspoon dried Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. If all of your ingredients aren’t covered by the broth at this point, that’s OK — the kale will wilt quickly! If the kale has wilted and your chicken and beans are still not submerged, you can add more broth, as needed.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low and cook, uncovered, for 20 minutes.

Shred the chicken by using two forks to pull it apart. I actually do this right in the soup pot, but you can transfer the chicken to a cutting board or mixing bowl and shred it there if you’d prefer. Stir in 1 cup heavy cream and 1/2 cup grated Parmesan until well combined. Taste and, if needed, add more kosher salt, a pinch at a time until it’s absolutely delicious.

name: saucy pork and sweet potato bowls
note:
I don’t like sweet potatoes: No prob, swap them for a grain. Brown rice, coconut rice, farro, quinoa — whatever floats your boat!

I need to feed more people: You could double this recipe, and/or add a grain to your bowls to stretch it. Another option is to top the bowls with a fried egg!

Prep ahead/meal prep/love your leftovers: Like we said above, leftovers of this meal will stay good for up to 3 days stored in separate airtight containers in the fridge, making it a perfect meal to prep over the weekend to have ready for a night when you only have 10 minutes to get dinner on the table. Reheat the meat and potatoes in the microwave (for 1 minute, then in 20-second increments until totally warmed through) or, if you have a little more time, in a skillet and oven (see “meal prep it” note before the recipe for reheating instructions).

Cooking for 1 or 2/freezer-friendly: If you’re cooking for 1 or 2 people and don’t want leftovers for lunches, go ahead and still cook all the meat since it’ll be sold in a 1-pound package, and freeze half for a future dinner. Wait until the cooked pork has cooled completely then freeze it in a zip-top bag.

Feeding kids: Bowl dinners are great for kids because they can choose their own adventure! Serve it family style and let them pick whatever they want. You can add plain rice to the spread if that’s a food they love. You could also set out non-pickled cucumber slices and carrots with ranch, if they’re more likely to go for that. Go easy on the sriracha — or just omit it — throughout the recipe if your kids are sensitive to spice. You can always drizzle your bowl with it!

Gimme some greens: I love plating this with peppery arugula. You could also add thinly sliced kale (squeezed in your hands a few times first, to soften it) or mixed greens as the optional greens. Alternatively, you could add chopped spinach to your ground pork. Add it along with the sauce ingredients so it can wilt during the final few minutes of cooking.

Store-bought swaps: Does your store sell pre-cubed sweet potatoes? If so, grab those. You can also use store-bought sriracha mayo.

Vegetarian: Tofu would be so delicious here. Squeeze a block of extra-firm tofu to remove excess moisture. Over the sink, use your hands to crumble it, squeezing out even more moisture as you do so, and add the crumbled tofu to the warmed skillet with sesame oil (use 2 tablespoons of oil instead of 1). Cook undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden on the bottom, then flip it and repeat. Use your spatula to break it into crumbles then add the sauce ingredients, cooking until absorbed.

Dairy-free: Already is, if you use mayo instead of yogurt!

Gluten-free: Use coconut aminos or tamari instead of soy sauce.

Nut-free: Use pepitas, sesame seeds, or omit the nut topping altogether

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Peel and cut 2 large or 3 medium sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes and add them to a sheet pan. Toss the cubed sweet potatoes with 2 tablespoons olive oil, a big pinch of kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper and spread into a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until tender on the inside and crispy at the edges.

While the sweet potatoes roast, mix 1 cup pre-shredded carrots, 2 thinly sliced Persian cucumbers (or 1/2 a thinly sliced English cucumber), 1/2 cup rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, and a pinch of kosher salt in a bowl. Set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon sesame oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound ground pork and half of the thinly sliced scallions and cook, breaking the pork up with a wooden spoon, until browned and cooked through, 6 to 8 minutes. FYI, unless you’re using a leaner meat, a good bit of fat will release from the pork as it cooks — continue cooking and stirring until all of the excess liquid evaporates and the pork starts to crisp up.

Add 1 teaspoon garlic powder (or 4 grated/minced cloves of garlic) and 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger (or a grated/minced 1-inch piece of fresh ginger) to the pork and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon honey (or brown sugar), 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, and 1 to 3 teaspoons sriracha (how much you use will depend on how spicy you want it to be!). Stir and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the pork. Remove from heat.
To make the sriracha mayo, mix 1/3 cup mayo (or plain yogurt) with 1 to 3 teaspoons sriracha (start with 1 and keep adding more until it is the ideal spice level for you).

Divide roasted sweet potatoes among 4 bowls. If using, add a handful of arugula (or another green) to each bowl. Top with ground pork, the quick-pickled carrots and cucumbers, extra sliced green onion, a sprinkle of crushed peanuts, and a dollop of sriracha mayo. Dig in!
