name: one-pot pumpkin curry
note:
How much curry paste should I use? This will depend on how spicy the brand you have is — they vary a lot. Thai Kitchen red curry paste is really mild, so use closer to 3 tablespoons (maybe even more if you love spice!). Mae Ploy, Mekhala, and Maesri, on the other hand, are REALLY spicy, so start with 1 tablespoon. Blue Elephant brand has medium spice, so I would start with 1 1/2 to 2 tablespoons. If you have a brand of red curry paste not mentioned here, taste it before you add any to the pot. Is it super spicy? Use the 1 tablespoon starting point. Is it totally mild? Go the 2 to 3 tablespoons route. Taste and add more, if desired.

I don’t like/can’t eat pumpkin: A few options: You could use a can of puréed butternut squash instead. You could just omit it (if you do, you won’t need to sauté the curry paste as long, just for 2 minutes or until fragrant). If you are cutting the pumpkin and want to replace those nutrients and flavor with something similar, you could add a pound of cubed butternut squash or sweet potatoes to the pot. You could also do that in addition to using the pumpkin purée to bulk it up even more.

Feeding kids: If you’re feeding kids (or adults) who hate spice, start with the minimum amount of red curry paste. If you’re working with a really spicy brand, you can even start with 1/2 tablespoon. Otherwise, this is a really kid-friendly meal! If they’re not into stewy things or curry flavor, you can fish the chickpeas and veg out at the end of cooking, give them a rinse, and plate ‘em.

Love your leftovers/make-ahead: This is one of those dishes that just gets better the next day and the next! Leftovers will be good for up to 4 days, so enjoy them for lunches, or make the whole meal well ahead of time, store it in an airtight container, and reheat it right before dinner. Reheat it on the stovetop over medium heat (or in the microwave!), adding a splash more stock, coconut milk, or water, if needed, to loosen things up.

Freezer-friendly: This is an excellent stock-your-freezer meal. Cook the curry as written, let it cool, then freeze it in a zip-top bag or freezer-friendly container. I like to freeze my meals in quart-sized bags — that way I can thaw just one if it’s for just myself or for me and George, or I can thaw multiple bags if I am feeding the whole family. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat as directed above. You can also freeze rice, FYI!

Cook it in a slow cooker: I would sauté the onion, red bell pepper, pumpkin purée, and curry paste as written, then transfer them over to the slow cooker and add the liquid ingredients and chickpeas. Some slow cookers have a sauté setting to let you do all that in the same pot! Cook on low for 5 to 6 hours or on high for 3 to 4, then add the remaining ingredients (spinach, soy sauce, etc.) and cook for another 30 minutes or so to let the flavors meld and spinach wilt.

Cook it in a pressure cooker: Sauté the onion, red bell pepper, pumpkin purée, and curry paste as written. Add all the other ingredients and cook on high pressure for 5 minutes. Let pressure naturally release for 5 minutes, then quick release the rest.

Must have meat/extra protein: Add cubed chicken breast or thighs (I prefer thighs here!) for the last 15 minutes of the curry’s cook time, making sure it cooks through (to 165°F). You could also add cubed tofu at the same time as the liquids. First press the tofu between two paper towels and under a heavy book for 20 minutes.

What to do with your leftover red curry paste: Make the thai chicken chop or coconut curry lentil stew!

How do I cook rice? First of all, might I suggest microwaveable frozen rice to save you some time and effort? But here’s a quick and easy way, should you want to DIY! Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil (as if you’re cooking pasta). Add 1 1/2 cups rice and cook until tender, about 17 minutes for white rice or 30 minutes for brown rice. Drain the rice, then return it to the pot, and cover it until you’re ready to eat.

Extra extra: If you’re feeling fancy, you can make cilantro-lime rice. Follow the directions right above. Once your rice is ready, use a microplane to scrape the zest of 1 lime straight into the pot, then add the juice of that lime, 1 tablespoon butter, a 3-finger pinch of salt, and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro. Another fancy rice option that would be delicious here is coconut rice!

Cook once, eat twice: If you’re cooking rice for this meal, double it so that tomorrow you can make bacon kimchi fried rice.

Vegetarian: Swap the fish sauce for extra soy sauce

Dairy-free/gluten-free: It’s already DF. Swap the soy sauce for coconut aminos or tamari, and make sure your stock is GF.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can pumpkin purée (NOT pumpkin pie filling)
ingredients.name: pumpkin purée (NOT pumpkin pie filling)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 3 tablespoons red curry paste (see note below recipe for how much to use)
ingredients.name: red curry paste (see note below recipe for how much to use)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: To serve: Cooked rice or naan or even really good sourdough, cilantro, more lime wedges
ingredients.name: To serve: Cooked rice or naan or even really good sourdough, cilantro, more lime wedges

preparationSteps: Heat 2 tablespoons neutral oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 diced yellow onion and 2 thinly sliced red bell peppers and cook until they are soft and starting to brown, 5 to 6 minutes.

Add 1 (15-ounce) can pumpkin purée and 1 to 3 tablespoons red curry paste (see note below recipe for how much to use) and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 to 7 minutes. You’ll see the pumpkin start to darken, and the moisture will cook off — it’ll turn almost paste-like. This is what you want! You’re concentrating all that pumpkin-curry flavor. If it’s popping at/splattering you, turn the heat down slightly.

Pour in 2 (drained and rinsed) cans of chickpeas, 1 can full-fat coconut milk, and 2 cups of low-sodium stock. Stir everything together, scraping up any stuck bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a slow simmer (there should only be an occasional small bubble) over medium-low and cook UNCOVERED for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the curry thickens. Stir it occasionally, and really scrape the bottom of the pot when you do to make sure it doesn’t burn. If your curry is getting too thick, just add a little more stock or coconut milk.

Stir in 3 cups chopped spinach, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, and the juice from 1/2 lime. Cook until the spinach wilts, 2 to 3 minutes. Keep tasting and adding more soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice, and/or curry paste, as desired, until it tastes perfect. I add a lot more soy sauce because I like things salty!
Serve over cooked rice (or with naan or sourdough) and topped with lots of cilantro and extra lime wedges.

name: thanksgiving turkey meatballs with roasted delicata squash & shallots
note:
I’m not ready for Thanksgiving vibes: If you want to dial back the Thanksgiving flavors, skip the dried rosemary. You could also swap the cranberry sauce for lingonberry jam/spread, or change the sauce up altogether. Crème fraîche plus a tablespoon of Dijon mustard, a teaspoon or 2 of maple syrup, kosher salt, and a squirt of lemon juice would be great. Or you could make the tahini lemon sauce or the cashew sauce from the sauce guide.

I want more Thanksgiving turkey meatballs! My friend Gaby Dalkin has a version with gravy!

What kind of cranberry sauce? Like I said in the recipe, you’ll ideally use whole berry cranberry sauce. If you can’t find any, the jellied kind is fine. I tested with both — if you’re using the jelly, you just gotta smoosh it. It’ll blend!

I’m feeding more than 4 people: Double the whole thing! Cook all the meatballs on one sheet pan, and all the vegetables on another.

What’s the ideal Cheddar here? A block of Unexpected Cheddar from Trader Joe’s, or any aged white Cheddar! But any Cheddar or Parm will do. Or Gouda! Or more swaps below.

Freezer-friendly: I highly recommend freezing any extra meatballs — or doubling the meatballs and freezing half of them. They’re a perfect protein to stock your freezer with. Reheat them from frozen for about 2 minutes in the microwave.

Cook once, eat twice thrice / love your leftovers: You could also double both the veg and meatballs to prep ahead on multiple meals: Serve the extra meatballs with store-bought marinara (I love Rao’s) and spaghetti.Make the autumn chop with the extra squash and shallot and a store-bought rotisserie chicken.

Serve the extra meatballs with store-bought marinara (I love Rao’s) and spaghetti.

Make the autumn chop with the extra squash and shallot and a store-bought rotisserie chicken.

Feeding picky eaters: Even my picky-eating kids loved these meatballs. Some of the boys even ate the squash!

Prep ahead: Pre-slice your veggies and form your meatballs up to a day ahead of time. Store them in the fridge in airtight containers.

Vegetarian: Use a ground meat alternative.

Gluten-free / dairy-free: Use rice breadcrumbs or 1/4 cup almond meal if avoiding gluten. To make the meal dairy-free, swap the crème fraîche for a dairy-free yogurt or sour cream or coconut cream, and use a DF Cheddar “cheese.” If you’d rather skip the cheese, add a tablespoon of olive oil (to keep the mixture moist) and a tablespoon of nutritional yeast (for umami).

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.

Slice 1 delicata squash in half lengthwise and discard the seeds. Cut each half into 1/2-inch half-moons (they will look like Cs!). Cut 3 shallots into quarters and discard the skins. Toss the vegetables on the baking sheet with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, a big pinch of kosher salt, and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper, making sure all the vegetables are lightly coated. Spread them out in a single layer on the sheet pan and roast for 10 minutes.

While the vegetables roast, in a large bowl, mix 1 pound ground turkey, 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 2 teaspoons maple syrup, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/4 teaspoon dried rosemary, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper until just combined. Roll into 15 meatballs — about 2 tablespoons of meat each.

Remove the sheet pan from the oven and scooch the squash and shallots over to one side to make room for the meatballs. Add the meatballs to the sheet pan alongside the vegetables. Return to the oven and roast for another 15 minutes, until the meatballs reach an internal temperature of 165°F. If the vegetables and meatballs aren’t browned to your liking at that point, turn on the broiler and broil them for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden and caramelized. Turn the oven light on and watch the whole time. Don’t let ‘em burn!

While everything roasts, make the sauce by stirring together 1/2 cup crème fraîche and 1/4 cup cranberry sauce in a small bowl. Taste. Depending on how sweet your cranberry sauce is, you might want to add a tiny bit of lemon juice or vinegar to cut through the richness and sweetness. Or if you want it sweeter, add a teeny bit of honey or maple syrup.

Serve the meatballs, roasted delicata squash, and shallots with the creamy cranberry sauce drizzled over top or swooped onto the plate. Sprinkle each plate with chopped parsley or arugula, a little shredded Cheddar, and chopped pecans.

name: choose-your-adventure beef ragu
note:
Use your slow cooker to make the ragù: Throw all the ragù ingredients in a slow cooker and cook on low for 6 hours. Remove the beef and shred it — while it’s out of the pot, blend the sauce using an immersion blender. Return the shredded beef and stir to combine.

Use your Instant Pot: Put all the ragù ingredients in the pressure cooker and cook on high pressure for 60 minutes (if your beef cubes are larger than 2 to 3 inches, go up to 75 minutes!). Let it natural release for 20 minutes, then quick-release the rest. Remove the beef and shred it — while it’s out of the pot, blend the sauce using an immersion blender. Return the shredded beef and stir to combine.

While you’re shopping: Feel free to kindly ask the butcher to cut your beef chuck into 4 pieces to save yourself a step! They’re usually happy to oblige, if they’re not too busy.

Can I use my regular blender? If it doesn’t bug you to dirty another kitchen tool, you can of course use that instead of the immersion blender to blend the tomato sauce, it’ll just be a little annoying. Alternatively, like I wrote in the recipe, you can just discard the onion and fennel — they’ll have imparted their flavor while cooking.

I don’t own a Dutch oven: You can make the ragù in a 9x12-inch baking dish rather than a Dutch oven, but transfer the sauce to a pot to blend so that you don’t get splattered!

Freezer-friendly/feeding 1 or 2: This ragù is very freezable! You can eat half now (the polenta and pasta serving options are both easy to halve), then freeze the rest for later. Once cooled, freeze it in an airtight zip-top bag or container. Thaw it overnight in the fridge, and reheat on the stovetop, adding splashes of liquid (pasta cooking water, regular water, broth, or tomato sauce) as needed to get it saucy again. You could also freeze the assembled lasagna if you’d like. You can freeze it either before or after you bake it, wrapped tightly with both foil and plastic wrap (if you cook it first let it cool completely before wrapping it). Thaw in the fridge, then bake as directed. Or bake from frozen but add extra cook time (20ish minutes, or until warmed through).

Love your leftovers/prep ahead: Leftover ragù will be great stored in the fridge in an airtight container for 3 to 4 days. If making lasagna, you can prep the whole thing up to a day in advance and store it in the fridge covered with foil or plastic wrap. Pop it in the oven covered with foil when you’re ready to cook dinner! It may take 10 or so minutes extra to warm through since it will have been chilled.

Vegetarian: Just cook Marcella’s legendary sauce!!! If you want to add protein, use Banza noodles. You could also sauté a pound of chopped mushrooms in olive oil and stir those into the sauce.

Dairy-free: The ragù already is! Swap in dairy-free ricotta, DF Parm, DF mozzarella, DF Cheddar, and/or DF butter as needed.

Gluten-free: Polenta is naturally gluten free. Swap in GF noodles or GF oven-ready lasagna noodles (yes, those are a thing!) if needed.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cut 2 pounds boneless beef chuck into 4 pieces. Cut 1 yellow onion in half and discard the peel. Trim the root end and branchy arms off of 1 fennel bulb and discard. Cut the fennel bulb in half.

Add 1 (28-ounce) can of whole or diced tomatoes, 1 (14-ounce) can of tomato sauce, and 1 teaspoon red wine vinegar to a large Dutch oven. Nestle the beef, onion, and fennel into the pot. Sprinkle 2 teaspoons kosher salt and 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper over everything. Cover with a lid (or aluminum foil if you have no lid).
Transfer to the oven and cook for 2 hours.
Pull at the beef with a fork — if it shreds easily, it’s ready. If it doesn’t, cook for another 30 minutes or until it’s fall-apart tender.

Transfer the beef to a plate or bowl (I use the inside of the lid of my Dutch oven!). Use an immersion blender to blend the sauce (WITH NO BEEF IN IT!) until smooth. Tilt the pot if needed to ensure that the blades are submerged in liquid at all times, or else you’ll fling hot sauce all over yourself/your kitchen. If you don’t own an immersion blender, just discard the onion and fennel and give the tomato sauce a whisk.

Shred the beef, return it to the pot, and stir to combine. Discard any yucky fat you come across while you’re shredding. If it shreds easily, leave it. But if it’s the hard kind that you can’t shred, discard it.
Now your ragù is ready, and you get to decide what to do with it!
To serve it with pasta:

During the last 30 minutes of the beef’s cook time, bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. Cook 1 pound of pasta until al dente (follow the cook time instructions on the box). RESERVE 1/2 CUP OF PASTA COOKING WATER BEFORE DRAINING THE NOODLES (shouting this so you don’t forget!).

Stir the cooked pasta and 1/4 cup pasta water into the pot of ragù. Add more pasta water as needed, until the noodles are saucy and coated. Serve in shallow bowls with lots of freshly grated Parm and chopped basil and/or parsley on top.
To serve it over polenta:

During the last 30 minutes of the beef’s cook time, make the polenta. Bring 6 cups of water and 2 teaspoons kosher salt to a boil in a large pot over high heat. Whisk in 2 cups quick-cooking polenta or grits and reduce the heat to low. Cook, whisking occasionally, for 6 minutes (or per package instructions), until thickened. Stir in 2 cups shredded Cheddar, 1/2 cup grated Parm, and 2 tablespoons unsalted butter. If the polenta gets too thick, just stir in a splash of water or milk. I like my polenta quite thick — like loose mashed potatoes, not like soup — but do your thing.
Spoon the polenta into shallow bowls and top with ragù, lots of freshly grated Parm, and lots of freshly chopped parsley and/or basil.
To make lasagna:
Increase oven temperature to 375°F.

Grease a 9x12-inch baking dish (if you don’t own one, they sell this size as disposable tins at most grocery stores!) with cooking spray, oil, or butter. Use a small amount of beef ragù to coat the bottom of the pan, then layer your ingredients in this order:
servings: Serves 6 to 10 (depending how you serve it)

name: The Best Classic Apple Pie
note: There is nothing better than a slice of buttery, warm apple pie à la mode. Made with a flaky, homemade pie crust and a perfectly spiced brown sugar apple filling, this classic apple pie recipe will become a staple recipe you come back to again and again.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup unsalted butter, cold and cut into cubes
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, cold and cut into cubes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 to 4 tablespoons ice water (or chilled vodka)
ingredients.name: ice water (or chilled vodka)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds apples (6 to 7 apples. I like to use a mix of Granny Smith and a sweeter, but still crisp apple like Pink Lady, Envy, or Cosmic )
ingredients.name: apples (6 to 7 apples. I like to use a mix of Granny Smith and a sweeter, but still crisp apple like Pink Lady, Envy, or Cosmic )

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup packed light brown sugar
ingredients.name: packed light brown sugar

preparationSteps: First, make the pie dough. Add the flour, granulated sugar, and salt to a food processor and pulse to combine. Add the butter cubes and pulse until the mixture resembles wet sand and starts to clump together, about 20 seconds.

Add 3 tablespoons of the ice water (or vodka), then pulse until a dough begins to form a ball around the blade, about 20 seconds. If your dough doesn’t come together, add another tablespoon of liquid and pulse again.

Turn the dough out onto a clean work surface and divide it into two equal pieces. Flatten each piece into a 1-inch-thick oval disc, then wrap in plastic wrap. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (and up to 3 days).

Next, make the apple filling. Peel and core the apples, then slice them into thin slices about ¼-inch thick. For a truly packed-in apple filling, cut the slices in half—this will help you be able to pack in more apples into your pie.
Add the apples into a large mixing bowl along with the brown sugar, flour, lemon juice, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt. Toss to combine and set aside

Remove both pie discs from the fridge and set on the counter to soften for 5 minutes. Lightly dust a clean work surface with flour, unwrap one dough disc, and place it onto the surface. Dust with more flour and use a rolling pin to roll out the dough into a roughly 12-inch circle, dusting the top and underside with more flour as needed. Carefully roll up the dough around your rolling pin like a scroll, then drape it into a 9-inch pie pan. Press the dough into the bottom and sides of the pie dish, then use scissors to trim around the edges of the pie crust, leaving a ½ inch overhang.

Pour the apple filling into the pie pan, then set aside while you roll out your second dough disc. Dust your work surface with more flour and use a rolling pin to roll out the second dough disc into a roughly 12-inch circle, dusting the top and underside with more flour as needed. Carefully transfer the top pie crust over the apples and trim the excess crust to match the bottom pie crust. Use your fingers to smoosh the two crusts together, rolling them in and underneath like a scroll to form a thick edge around the rim of your pie dish. Use your index finger on one hand and your peace fingers on the other hand to create a crimp around the edge of the pie. Use a sharp knife to cut 5 vents into the top of the pie.

In a small bowl, whisk the egg with 2 tablespoons of water. Use a pastry brush to brush the top of the pie with the egg wash. If desired, sprinkle all over with coarse sugar. Place the pie into the freezer to chill while your oven preheats (this will keep the pie dough from becoming too soft at room temperature).

Preheat the oven to 375°F. Once heated, remove the pie from the fridge and bake until the crust is golden brown and the apples are bubbling, about 1 hour. Remove the pie from the oven and allow it to cool on a cooling rack for at least 1 hour, then serve!

name: chicken paillard with a pear & manchego salad
note:
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy candied nuts at the store. Use a store-bought French vinaigrette for your dressing. Buy pre-washed mixed greens or butter lettuce so you don’t have to wash any lettuce. All you’ll have to do is assemble your salad and cook the chicken!

Prep ahead: This meal is best served right away, but there are elements of it that you can definitely prep ahead of time. You can make the candied nuts up to 3 weeks in advance — store them in an airtight container at room temp or in the fridge. You can make the dressing up to 10 days in advance — again, store it in an airtight container in the fridge. Give the dressing a good shake or whisk to emulsify everything again before using. If the oil has separated and hardened in the fridge, just let it sit on the counter for a few minutes (or microwave it in a microwave-safe container for just a few seconds) to warm it up first.

Love your leftovers: Since we’re using delicate greens here, leftover salad won’t keep well in the fridge. You could swap in kale though, if you wanted it to! If you have leftover chicken, you can add it to any salad, chop it up and use it for chicken quesadillas, or throw it in a soup!

Double it: This complete meal serves 2 adults as an entrée, while the salad by itself would serve 4 to 6 as a side. You can double or triple the chicken recipe (or halve it) as needed to feed your crew.

Feeding kids: Chicken paillard is a very kid-friendly protein. Feel free to go light or skip the lemon juice on their serving, if that’d deter them. When I served this dinner to my family, I gave the boys chicken, sliced pear, cubed cheese, and candied nuts. They loved it!

Vegetarian: Pan-fry thin tofu cutlets to mimic chicken paillard and serve it with this salad! Use a block of extra-firm tofu and press it between clean kitchen towels under something heavy (like some cookbooks or a skillet) for 10 to 20 minutes before you slice it into 1/2-inch thick slabs. Pan-fry them as I instruct for the chicken — they’ll need 4 to 6 minutes on each side to turn golden brown.

Dairy-free: Use a DF butter and skip the cheese (or use a plant-based cheese alternative)

Gluten-free: Already is.

Nut-free: Candied pepitas would be great here!

ingredients.name: A big glug of olive oil

preparationSteps: Our order of operations for cooking this meal will be: 1) Make the candied nuts. 2) Make the dressing. 3) Prep the salad. 4) Cook the chicken paillard. 5) Toss the salad with dressing and serve it alongside the chicken. It’s a hands-on, active process, but nothing is hard, and an absolutely delightful dinner will be on the table in less than 40 minutes!

TO MAKE THE CANDIED NUTS: Add all the candied nut ingredients (2 cups nuts or seeds, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1/3 cup white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, a big pinch of flaky sea salt, and a tiny pinch/shake of cayenne) to a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Use a spatula to break the cold butter up into little pieces right in the pain (this will help it melt quickly). Cook, stirring often, until the sugar also melts (aka turns into a glossy liquid), 6 to 10 minutes. Some of the sugar will clump to the nuts as it warms — that’s OK! Just keep stirring, it’ll melt. Once the sugar has turned glossy, stir to coat the nuts then pour them onto a piece of parchment paper and spread flat. Set aside to harden and cool.

TO MAKE THE DRESSING: Add all the dressing ingredients except for the EVOO to a jar — so 1 heaping tablespoon of minced shallot, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, 1 tablespoon tahini, 1 tablespoon honey, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, a pinch of kosher salt, and a pinch or few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper. Close the lid and shake vigorously to combine.

Add 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil and shake again — for longer than you’d think! — to get it to emulsify (aka combine into a creamy smooth dressing). Taste and, if needed, adjust seasonings until it’s perfect (you may want to add more kosher salt, pepper, honey, etc., depending on your taste).

TO PREP THE SALAD: Cut out the core of 1 head of red leaf or butter lettuce, then separate the leaves and wash and dry them. Place the washed leaves in a large, low bowl. Season with a pinch of kosher salt and a pinch/few grinds of black pepper.

Thinly slice 2 pears and add on top. Use a vegetable peeler to peel big pieces of manchego onto the salad. No need to measure, just add as much as you’d like! Sprinkle 4 chopped dates on top. Use a cup or your hands to break the candied nuts apart and add them to the salad.

When you’re ready to eat (so after you’ve cooked your chicken), toss the salad with your desired amount of dressing. You will not need to use all of the dressing, and whatever’s left will stay good in the fridge for 10 days.

TO MAKE THE CHICKEN PAILLARD: Place 2 (4- to 6-ounce) chicken breasts onto a cutting board. Place a large piece of plastic wrap over top. Use a meat mallet or rolling pin or olive oil/wine bottle to pound the chicken breasts to about 1/2-inch thickness. You want to push down and out as you pound vs. bash directly down — see the video below for a visual! Season generously with kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, then use a microplane to zest the lemon directly onto both sides of the chicken breasts.

Heat your largest skillet (preferably NOT non-stick) over medium-high heat. Add a generous glug of olive oil — just enough to nicely coat the skillet. Carefully add the flattened chicken breasts to the pan taking care that the oil doesn’t splatter on you. Cook for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until golden-brown on the bottom. Flip and cook for another 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until that bottom side is golden brown, too, and the chicken has reached 165°F internally.
Transfer to a plate and squeeze juice from the lemon over top (however much you want based on how much you like lemon flavor!).

TO PLATE YOUR CHICKEN AND SALAD: Serving salad over top of chicken paillard is extremely chic and French. So if you want to feel fancy, place the chicken on a plate, then pile some of the salad over top (like in the opening pic)! If you want it to be a bit more practical, chop or slice the chicken up and toss it into the salad. Do your thing!
servings: Serves: As an entrée salad with chicken, this meal serves dinner for 2; as a side salad by itself, it serves 4 to 6

name: Pie Crust
note: This best and easiest Pie Crust recipe made with only 4 pantry ingredients and it can even be made ahead of time and frozen. You'll never buy store-bought pie crust again!
preparationSteps: Mix flour and salt in a large mixing bowl. Add ice cubes to a measuring cup and fill with 1/2 cup cold water. Set aside.

Add fats: Grate frozen butter into the bowl, or cut it into very small pieces. Add chilled shortening and use a pastry blender or fork to cut the fats into the flour until well combined and resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water a spoonful at a time, mixing until the dough begins to come together into a ball. Be careful not to over mix, and you may not need all of the water. Gently mold the dough into a ball.
Divide dough into 2 pieces and press each to flatten into a disk.

Refrigerate: Cover dough discs with plastic wrap and refrigerate the dough for 2 hours (or freeze for 30 minutes). Refrigeration is mandatory as you need the fats in the pie dough to be cold when it's rolled out and placed in oven).

Roll out dough on a floured countertop. If you're new to pie making, it may be helpful to use this method: dampen a large cloth and lay it flat on your countertop, with a large piece of parchment paper over it (the damp towel will keep the parchment from moving). Lightly flour the parchment and dough and roll the dough into a large circle, about 1-inch larger then the diameter of your pie dish. Always start at the center of the crust, and roll outwards.
Place in pie pan: Gently turn the dough into your pie dish and remove the parchment paper. Settle it smoothly into the bottom and sides of the pan. Trim and crimp the edges of the crust.
For Pies requiring an unbaked pie crust (like pumpkin, apple, or even chicken pot pie): Fill the unbaked crust with pie filling and bake according to pie recipe instructions.

For a blind Baked Pie Crust (pre-baked crust) you need pie weights, dry beans or dry rice. (Without pie weights the crust will shrink into the pan as it bakes). Place a large piece of parchment paper over the unbaked crust and add pie weights, (or 1-2 cups dry beans, or dry rice) on top. Bake at 375° F for 15-20 minutes. Remove pie weights by carefully lifting up on parchment paper. Prick the bottom of the pie crust with a fork, then return to oven for 10-15 minutes, until lightly golden. Allow crust to cool before adding filling.

name: Pecan Pie
note: Not only is this Pecan Pie recipe one of the easiest pies to make, it's absolutely fantastic with its rich caramel pecan filling paired with a flakey, buttery crust.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 Homemade pie crust (, unbaked (my recipe makes 2 crusts, so you can freeze the other crust))
ingredients.name: Homemade pie crust (, unbaked (my recipe makes 2 crusts, so you can freeze the other crust))

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup salted butter (, softened or melted (75 g))
ingredients.name: salted butter (, softened or melted (75 g))

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups pecan halves ((can chop the pecans or leave whole) (150 g))
ingredients.name: pecan halves ((can chop the pecans or leave whole) (150 g))

preparationSteps: Prepare my perfect pie crust recipe and place pie dough in a deep dish pie plate. Refrigerate while you prepare the pecan pie filling.
In a large bowl cream together sugar, brown sugar, salt, corn syrup, and softened (or melted) butter. Mix in the eggs and vanilla.

Reserve a few pecans and stir the rest into the batter. Pour into unbaked pie shell. Add a few of the reserved pecans on top of the pie in any empty spots, to make it look pretty. Use a small spoon to cover them with batter.

Bake at 425 degrees for 10 minutes, then lower the oven temp to 350 degrees F and continue baking for about 50 minutes. Check the pie half way through cooking and tent a large piece of greased aluminum foil over the top of the pie. (I tent it high so it doesn't touch the pie filling).  You will know your pecan pie is done when you can shake it gently and it is not overly jiggly.  If it jiggles a lot when shaking, continue cooking until the center is more set, 5-10 more minutes, or longer if needed. Err on the side of cooking it longer rather than shorter to ensure that the middle has set.
Allow pie to cool completely for several hours before cutting and serving. Or refrigerate for 1-3 days, until ready to serve.

name: Toffee Recipe
note: A great classic Toffee Recipe! Be sure to check out the recipe VIDEO at the bottom of the post!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (2 sticks ) unsalted butter (cut into pieces)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter (cut into pieces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-2 Tablespoons finely chopped almonds (for topping, optional)
ingredients.name: finely chopped almonds (for topping, optional)

preparationSteps: Line a 9x9 pan with parchment paper and scatter coarsely chopped almonds evenly over the bottom. Set aside.
Combine butter, sugar, water, and salt in a medium-sized pot over low heat. Meanwhile measure out your vanilla extract and have it ready nearby.

Stir ingredients frequently over medium heat. During this time (only before boiling), use a wet pastry brush to brush down the sides where any sugar may settle on the side of the pot to prevent sugar crystals.

Once butter is melted, increase heat to medium and continue to stir frequently until mixture comes to a boil (this may take a while, have patience and do not turn up the heat or you will ruin your toffee).
Once the mixture comes to a boil, attach your candy thermometer. Make sure that the point of the candy thermometer is not touching the bottom of your pan.
Continue to stir occasionally, the mixture will slowly thicken and will turn a more yellow hue as it cooks, and cook to hard crack (305°F/151°C).
Once toffee reaches 305°F/151°C, immediately remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract (careful, it bubbles and steams a bit).

Pour mixture evenly into your prepared pan over the almonds. Allow to sit for 5 minutes and then sprinkle chocolate chips evenly overtop the mixture. Cover with foil and allow to sit another 5 minutes, then remove the foil and use a spatula to gently spread chocolate chips evenly over your toffee.
Immediately sprinkle with additional finely chopped almonds and flaky sea salt, if desired. Allow to cool completely at room temperature before breaking and serving.

name: Pistachio-Orange Biscotti
note: You can enhance these long-keeping cookies with either a chocolate coating or a caramel glaze.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 Tbs. (1 stick) unsalted butter, at room temperature
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, at room temperature

preparationSteps: Sift together the flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt into a bowl; set aside.

In a large bowl Combine the butter, sugar, orange zest and vanilla. Using an electric mixer set on high speed, beat until light and fluffy. Mix in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Reduce the speed to low, add the pistachios and mix in. Add the flour mixture and mix just until incorporated. Cover and refrigerate until well chilled, about 1 hour.
Preheat an oven to 350ºF. Butter and flour a large baking sheet.

Divide the dough in half. On a lightly floured surface, using lightly floured hands, roll each half into a log 1 1/2 inches in diameter. Arrange the logs on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 5 inches apart.
Bake until light brown and firm to the touch, about 30 minutes (the logs will spread during baking). Remove from the oven and let cool slightly on the baking sheet. Leave the oven set at 350ºF.

Using a spatula, carefully transfer the logs to a work surface. Using a serrated knife, cut on the diagonal into slices 3/4 inch thick. Arrange the slices, cut side down, on the baking sheet and bake until golden brown, about 15 minutes. Transfer the cookies to wire racks to cool. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

preparationSteps: In a large bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer, beat 1 cup butter and 2/3 cup granulated sugar on a medium-high speed for a couple of minutes, until the mixture becomes lighter in color.
Add in 1 egg yolk and 1 tsp vanilla extract. Mix on a medium speed until combined.
Whisk together 1 1/2 cups flour, 2/3 cup almond flour, 1/3 cup dark or Dutch-processed cocoa powder, 1 Tbsp cornstarch, and 1/4 tsp salt in a separate bowl.
Mix the flour mixture into the butter mixture on a low speed until it is JUST incorporated. Scrape the sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula between additions.

At this point, the dough should be quite thick. Divide the dough in half and wrap each portion of dough in a piece of plastic wrap. I like to flatten the dough out into a rectangle that's about 1/3 inch tall to make it easier to roll out once it's chilled.

Chill the dough in the fridge for about 45 minutes. If you need to chill the dough longer than that or overnight, let it sit out at room temperature for about 5 minutes before trying to roll it out. This will make it easier to roll out.
Turn on the oven to 350 F / 175 C about 30 minutes before you plan to roll out the dough, and line two large baking sheets with silicone baking mats or parchment paper. Set aside.

Take one piece of dough out of the fridge, leaving the other in there to continue to chill. Unwrap the cookie dough and lay the plastic wrap out flat on your counter. We will be rolling out the cookie dough on the plastic wrap to make cleanup a breeze and to make it easier to pick up the cut out cookies. Dust the top of the cookie dough and your rolling pin with flour.

Roll the chilled dough to be 1/4 inch thick (I use these bands on my rolling pin to make sure I get the thickness just right). If the dough cracks/splits a bit as you roll it out, don't worry! It will come back together as you roll it out and you can cut the cookies out around any big splits. If the dough is too soft to pick up the cut-out cookies, lift the entire sheet of cookie dough with the plastic wrap and place it in the fridge for 5-10 minutes to let it firm up.

Then cut out 1 1/2-inch scalloped circles. If you don't have a cutter that size, use a round glass that's similar in size.  Use a 3/4-inch heart or circle cutter to remove the centers from half the cookies. Feel free to get creative with the cookie cutters you use! Save the dough from the centers to be rolled out with the next piece of dough.

The cookies don't spread much as they bake, so place them about 1 inch apart on the prepared baking sheets. Bake one sheet of cookies at a time. Bake for 9-10 minutes on the middle rack of your oven (bake time will vary based on the size of the cookies and the thickness of the dough). Let the baked cookies cool on the pan for about 15 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to finish cooling.
While the first batch bakes and cools, knead together the cookie dough scraps and rewrap them in plastic wrap. Pop them back in the fridge to chill.
Pull out the 2nd chilled portion of dough and repeat steps 8-12. Then repeat with the chilled dough scraps.

Once the cookies have fully cooled, use powdered sugar or cocoa powder (or both) to generously dust the tops of the cookies with the center cut-outs. I used a small piece of parchment paper to dust half of each cookie with cocoa powder and the other half with powdered sugar. I like to use this little little duster, but you can also use a small sifter.

Then spread or pipe 2 tsp of Nutella on the center of each uncut cookie. Top with a cut-out cookie, squeezing a little to spread out the Nutella and push it up into the cutout section. Repeat with the remaining cookies, then enjoy! These can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days.

preparationSteps: Snip off the hard stems of the figs with scissors or a small knife and coarsely chop the figs. In a medium bowl, combine the figs, raisins, cherries, apricots, honey, sherry, lemon juice, pecans, and a pinch of salt. Cover with plastic wrap and allow to sit overnight at room temperature.

In the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, cream the butter, cloves, superfine sugar, and brown sugar on medium speed until smooth, about 3 minutes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
With a small, sharp knife, cut the logs into 1/2-inch-thick slices. Place the slices 1/2-inch apart on ungreased sheet pans and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until lightly golden.

name: Soft Gingerbread Cookies
note: Say goodbye to dry, flavorless gingerbread men. These cut-out soft gingerbread cookies are tender, chewy, packed full of spiced flavor and perfect for celebrating the holidays.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup shortening (you can also use butter, but they tend to spread more!)

preparationSteps: Place the shortening, granulated sugar, and molasses in a medium saucepan and set over medium low heat. Cook, occasionally stirring with a whisk, until the crisco has melted completely. Remove from heat and pour the mixture into a large bowl. Set aside to cool slightly (the shortening should still be liquid just not hot!).
Once the mixture has cooled slightly add the egg and vanilla extract to the bowl, whisking until smooth and glossy.

Add the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon and salt to the mixture and use a rubber spatula to fold together until combined and no streaks of flour remain. The dough will be soft and a little sticky—don’t worry it will firm up in the fridge! Transfer the dough to a sheet of plastic wrap or tin foil, shaping into a disc, seal and chill for at least 2 hours but up to 2 days!
When you’re ready to roll out the cookies preheat the oven to 350°F and line a cookie sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.

Lightly flour a clean work surface. Roll the dough out to about 1/4 inch thickness. Use cookie cutters (we used a 3-inch gingerbread man!) and cut out cookies. Place the cookies 2 inches apart on the prepared pan and bake for 8 to 9 minutes for full size cookies (if you do smaller cookies you’ll want to bake them for less time!) The edges should be lightly brown but still slightly underbaked in the middle—this will keep them super soft and moist! Do not overbake unless you like crisp, harder cookies! Place the cookies on a cooling rack to cool completely.

Once the cookies are completely cool, make the royal icing. Combine the egg white, powdered sugar, vanilla, and salt in a medium bowl and whisk to combine. If the frosting feels too thick add 1/4 teaspoon of water at a time. If the frosting feels too thin, add a little more powdered sugar. Whisk until smooth. Transfer to a piping bag fitted with a small round tip and decorate the cooled cookies! Enjoy!

name: Bacon Balsamic Brussels

Chop 8 slices of bacon. Cook the bacon over medium-high heat in your largest skillet, stirring often. When crispy, use a slotted spoon to transfer the bacon to a plate, leaving the bacon grease in the skillet.

Crank the heat up to high and add the shredded Brussels sprouts. Stir to coat in bacon grease, then spread them out into an even layer and let them brown up for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes, until very tender and browned. Stir in 1 teaspoon kosher salt, a pinch of red pepper flakes, 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, and 1 tablespoon honey or hot honey. Cook for an additional minute or 2, until the balsamic is all absorbed. Stir in the cooked bacon. Taste and add more salt if needed.

ingredients.name: oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes

Add sun-dried tomatoes and garlic and continue cooking for 2 minutes.

name: Thin and Crispy Chocolate Chip Cookies
note: Thin and crispy chocolate chip cookies bake up super crisp with a rich, buttery toffee flavor ~ they're even better than Tate's!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup unsalted butter at room temperature
ingredients.name: unsalted butter at room temperature

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup light brown sugar, lightly packed.
ingredients.name: light brown sugar, lightly packed.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Note: the parchment paper is important for preventing sticking, and getting the right texture in these cookies. Don't substitute silicone mats.
In the bowl of a stand mixer or with electric beaters, cream together the butter and sugars until well combined. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as necessary.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, baking soda, and cinnamon.
Add the egg and vanilla to the butter mixture, and mix until well combined.
Add the flour to the bowl in two batches, mixing after each addition just until everything is combined. Add the chocolate chips, and mix briefly once more to incorporate them evenly.

Scoop the cookie dough into balls a little more than 1 tablespoon, and roll them into a ball. Space them evenly on your cookie sheet, leaving about 2-3 inches between each cookie to allow for spreading in the oven.
Bake for about 14-15 minutes until the cookies are a rich golden brown.
Allow to partially cool on the baking sheet, they will be very soft when they come out of the oven but will crisp up as they cool. Then transfer to a baking rack to completely cool.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 325°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a standmixer fit with the whisk attachment, beat the room temperature butter and the vegetable oil together until homogenous, about 2 minutes.

Continue beating the butter as you stream in the granulated sugar. Next, add the powdered sugar and mix until combined. Scrape down the bowl and add the egg, milk, vanilla extract and almond extract and beat until combined..
Scrape down the bowl and add the cake flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Beat until no streaks or clumps of flour remain, but do not over mix.

name: everyone-loves-this-salmon (and brocolli)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon grainy Dijon mustard (or whatever mustard you have)
ingredients.name: grainy Dijon mustard (or whatever mustard you have)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-pound bag broccoli florets (or 1 bunch broccolini, tough stem ends trimmed and discarded)
ingredients.name: broccoli florets (or 1 bunch broccolini, tough stem ends trimmed and discarded)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 4 (6-ounce) salmon filets skin-side down and grouped together like one big piece of salmon in one corner of the baking sheet. Pat the salmon dry with a paper towel or clean dish towel then plop 1 tablespoon grainy mustard, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon paprika right there on top of the salmon and rub everything all over with your hands.

Melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter in a small bowl in the microwave, then stir in 1/2 cup panko, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon dried Italian seasoning. Press the mixture evenly on top of the salmon. Keep the filets grouped together (this will help them cook evenly).

Place 1 pound broccoli florets on the other half of the baking sheet. If your bagged broccoli florets are huge, use your hands to break them into smaller pieces. If you are using broccolini, trim and discard the rough bottoms off of the stems first. Toss the broccoli with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder then spread the florets out in a single layer.

Roast for 13 to 16 minutes, until the salmon is firm but flakes easily when prodded with a fork, and the broccoli is crisp at the edges. For perfect doneness, use an instant-read thermometer on the salmon: 125-130°F for medium-rare, 135-140°F for medium (my fave), or 145°F for well done.
If your broccoli isn’t as crisp as you like it yet, transfer the salmon to plates and return the broccoli to the oven for another few minutes, making sure not to let it burn.
Serve the salmon with broccoli.

name: sheet-pan hot honey chicken sausage & veggies
note:
I NEED SAUCE!! If you are a sauce house, stir a little sriracha into a big scoop of mayo or plain yogurt and add just a tiny bit of lime juice and a pinch of salt. Drizzle all over your bowl.

What kind of chicken sausage? You’re shopping for pre-cooked Italian chicken sausage. I’d do mild since we’re bringing in heat via the sauce. Italian-flavored turkey or pork or plant-based sausages work, too! See the substitutions below for more swap ideas.

I accidentally bought raw chicken sausage instead of pre-cooked: No prob! Squeeze the meat out of the casings a little at a time and roll it into “meatballs” about an inch in diameter. They will cook in the same amount of time as the veg! Safe internal temp for chicken is 165°F, if you’re using raw chicken sausage and you want to double check.

What kind of grain? A grain for serving is completely optional — I typically eat it without — but if your fam is really hungry it does help stretch the meal. Microwaveable brown rice is an excellent option (stir a little butter and soy sauce into it once heated!), but any cooked grain would be great, like white rice, quinoa, farro, etc.

How do I thinly slice an onion? Watch a demo here.

Love your leftovers/meal prep: This is an excellent meal prep recipe! Leftovers reheat beautifully in the microwave — just don’t add the feta and fresh herbs to your bowl until after you’ve reheated the meat and veggies. Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Option to toss your leftovers with chopped romaine or mixed greens and this dressing for an A+ salad. Or eat them with rice or another grain, wrapped up like a taco, or just like you ate them for dinner.

Prep ahead: You can prep the whole sheet pan of meat and veggies up to a day in advance. Cover the sheet pan tightly and put it in the fridge. When you’re ready to cook dinner, take it out of the fridge, uncover it, add your oil and sauces and seasonings, mix it well, and roast. This is a great option if you get home from work and need dinner on the table in 30 minutes!

Feeding kids: See the “I don’t do spicy” section above the recipe. To sum it up: omit the “hot” ingredient (sriracha/gochujang) if your kids don’t do spicy things. Also, keep the vegetables separate on the sheet pan. Chickpeas in one area, then chicken sausage, onion, carrots. Maybe add one of their safe vegetables like broccoli or sweet potato, if you have it. When you toss on the oil and seasonings, keep everything separate so that you can serve the different components to your kids in separate piles versus all jumbled together.

Vegetarian: Either omit the chicken sausage and double the chickpeas, or swap the chicken sausage out for a plant-based sausage.

Dairy-free: You could skip the feta, but I recommend using a dairy-free feta if you can find one — the cool, creamy texture really is so good here!

Gluten-free: Use coconut aminos or tamari instead of soy sauce. You’ll also need to read ingredient labels for the chicken sausage and gochujang to be sure you buy a certified gluten-free version (or stick with sriracha which is GF).

ingredients.name: pre-cooked Italian chicken sausage, cut on the bias into 1/4-inch thick ovals

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha or gochujang (amount depending on spice preference)
ingredients.name: sriracha or gochujang (amount depending on spice preference)

ingredients.rawIngredient: A little bit of soy sauce (about 1 teaspoon)
ingredients.name: A little bit of soy sauce (about 1 teaspoon)

ingredients.name: Optional for serving: any cooked grain and/or greens

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Clean (but I do not peel) and slice 2 pounds carrots, cutting on the bias (aka at a slight angle), into 1/4-inch thick ovals. Thinly slice 1 red onion. Drain, rinse, and pat dry 1 can chickpeas. Slice 12 ounces pre-cooked chicken sausages into 1/4-inch thick ovals.

Place everything on your largest rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle 3 tablespoons olive oil, 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha/gochujang, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin over everything, then use your hands to really get in there and make sure the honey and sriracha are evenly coating everything.

If things are really crowded (like if everything is touching and overlapping), pull out another rimmed baking sheet and divide the ingredients between the two. Roast for 25 minutes, stirring halfway through if you feel like it. You’re finished cooking when everything is a nice golden-brown.
Stir in the juice of 1/2 a lime and a tiny splash of soy sauce (like 1 teaspoon, if you want to measure).

Scoop into bowls and top with lots of feta and fresh herbs. Option to serve over some greens or a cooked grain (I highly recommend adding butter and a tiny bit of soy sauce to your cooked grain, if using!).

name: winter sunshine soup

ingredients.name: whole peeled tomatoes (do not drain)

ingredients.name: large carrots

ingredients.name: low-sodium white beans, such as butter, cannellini, or navy beans (do not drain)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon red curry paste, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: red curry paste, plus more to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups of 1/2-inch cubed bread (I love sourdough here but any kind of bread works)
ingredients.name: of 1/2-inch cubed bread (I love sourdough here but any kind of bread works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Splash of low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
ingredients.name: Splash of low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional, but be sure to have some on hand if you know you like your puréed soups on the thinner side: Broth, stock, bone broth (any kind works, but use a vegetable broth/stock if you want to keep it vegetarian)
ingredients.name: Optional, but be sure to have some on hand if you know you like your puréed soups on the thinner side: Broth, stock, bone broth (any kind works, but use a vegetable broth/stock if you want to keep it vegetarian)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.

To a large ovenproof pot, ideally a Dutch oven, add 2 (28-ounce) cans whole peeled tomatoes (with their juices), 1 halved medium yellow onion, 1 red bell pepper cut into 3 or 4 pieces, 2 large carrots cut into 3 or 4 pieces each, 6 peeled garlic cloves, 1 can low-sodium white beans (with the liquid), 1/2 stick butter, 1 tablespoon red curry paste, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt.
Cover and bake for 3 hours, until the vegetables are all totally collapsing and squishy.

While the pot is in the oven, make garlicky olive oil-fried croutons. Warm a huge glug of extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat (we are not measuring! Just generously coat the bottom of the skillet!). Add 4 cups of 1/2-inch cubed bread and stir to coat in oil. Add more oil if needed to get a nice olive oil-y coating on all the cubes.

Spread the bread into as even of a layer as possible. Sprinkle generously with kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder. Don’t stir them, just let them toast until golden-brown on the first side, 3 to 5 minutes. Keep an eye on them — if they are burning, just turn the heat down and carry on. Stir and toast on the second side. Continue cooking and stirring until golden-brown all over. Turn off the heat and let them cool right there in the skillet.

Blend the soup until totally smooth using an immersion blender or by using a ladle to scoop the ingredients into your regular stand blender, then pouring the blended soup back into the pot. If you’re using a regular blender, see notes below for more info.
Once blended, stir in HALF a (14-ounce) can of coconut milk and a tiny splash (like 1 teaspoon) of low-sodium soy sauce.

Technically this is the end of the recipe, but now is when you really need to put on your chef’s hat. If the soup is thicker than you’d like, add more coconut milk and/or some broth or stock (about a 1/4 cup at a time) until it’s your desired consistency. All of our soups will taste a little different — my carrots might be more flavorful than yours, your tomatoes might be more acidic than mine, our canned ingredients will vary a little by brand — so taste and adjust seasonings as needed. You can add up to 1 more tablespoon of red curry paste (or a scoop of Better Than Bouillon, if you happen to have some!) if you need more overall flavor. Or add another splash of soy sauce or pinch of kosher salt if it needs more saltiness. Keep going until it is absolutely perfect for your taste buds.
Serve in bowls garnished with garlicky olive oil-fried croutons.

name: sheet-pan salt and vinegar chicken and potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large fennel bulb, trimmed and 1/4-inch sliced (see notes for a detailed how-to)
ingredients.name: large fennel bulb, trimmed and 1/4-inch sliced (see notes for a detailed how-to)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small red onion, very thinly sliced
ingredients.name: small red onion, very thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup fresh dill, finely chopped (a 1/2 ounce container is perfect)
ingredients.name: fresh dill, finely chopped (a 1/2 ounce container is perfect)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper, if you’d like. Lining the pan with parchment is optional! It makes clean up easier, but, if you don’t mind scrubbing the pan, you can skip it. Also, if you have a very big rimmed sheet pan, you can use one pan. If the ingredients aren’t all fitting in a single layer, use two smaller sheet pans instead, and distribute the ingredients evenly between them.

Quarter 1 1/2 pounds small red-skinned potatoes and add them to the sheet pan. Trim and discard the tall stems and root end off of 1 large fennel bulb. Cut the bulb in half then slice it lengthwise into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Add the sliced fennel to the sheet pan along with 2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 3/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Toss everything until the chicken and vegetables are evenly coated in oil and seasonings. Arrange the chicken thighs skin-side up and spread the vegetables out so that they’re not overlapping.
Place the sheet pan in the oven and cook for 50 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F internally, stirring the vegetables halfway through (keep the chicken as is with the skin side up!).

While the chicken and vegetables roast, make the quick pickled onions: In a small pot, combine 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, 1/2 cup water, 1 tablespoon sugar, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar and salt dissolve. While the liquid is coming to a boil, VERY thinly slice 1 small red onion (you could carefully use a mandoline for this, if you have one). Once the liquid is boiling and the salt and sugar have dissolved, add the sliced onion to the pot, remove the pot from heat, and let it sit while everything finishes cooking. If your onion was on the larger side and all the slices aren’t covered by liquid at first, just occasionally stir it — the onion will soften, allowing all to be submerged.
Meanwhile, mince 2 garlic cloves and finely chop 1/2 cup fresh dill.

Remove the sheet pan from the oven and scatter the minced garlic, chopped dill, and 1 tablespoon of red wine vinegar over top. Use a spatula or tongs to toss everything together right there on the sheet pan, being sure that you scoop up all of the chicken drippings/fat on the pan and mix it in, too. Keep stirring until everything is well coated.
Divide the chicken, potatoes, and fennel between plates. Allow everyone to garnish their own plate with their desired amounts of olives, feta, and pickled red onions.

ingredients.name: large yellow onion

preparationSteps: Heat 2 tablespoons of the avocado oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Add 1 large yellow onion thinly sliced into half-moons and 2 thinly sliced green bell peppers and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is caramelized and the peppers are soft, 25 to 30 minutes, taking care not to burn them (reduce the heat to medium-low if needed). FYI, caramelized onions look soft, jammy, and deep golden brown. Add a splash of water if the onion and peppers brown too quickly.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add 10 ounces thinly sliced white mushrooms and 4 minced garlic cloves and cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are softened, about 5 to 7 more minutes.

Create a well in the center of pan and add the remaining 1 tablespoon avocado oil. Carefully add 14 ounces shaved Angus steak and cook, stirring frequently, until it is cooked through and browned, about 2 minutes.

Add 2 teaspoons tapioca flour or arrowroot starch, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and mix until well combined. Stir in 1/4 cup coconut aminos and reduce the heat to low. Sprinkle 1 cup shredded mozzarella over the top, cover, and cook until the sauce is thickened and the cheese is melted, about 5 minutes. If your skillet doesn’t have a lid, you can use a sheet pan as your lid instead!
Divide the steak and vegetables among four plates and serve.

name: Buckeye Cake
note: This buckeye cake recipe is packed with peanut butter and chocolate! It's made with moist chocolate cake layers and the best peanut butter frosting.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature (226 grams)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature (226 grams)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup full-fat sour cream, room temperature (255 grams)
ingredients.name: full-fat sour cream, room temperature (255 grams)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, sifted (100 grams)
ingredients.name: unsweetened cocoa powder, sifted (100 grams)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups (3 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature (339 grams)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature (339 grams)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup heavy whipping cream, room temperature (115 grams)
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream, room temperature (115 grams)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup heavy whipping cream, room temperature (77 grams)
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream, room temperature (77 grams)

preparationSteps: Begin by preheating the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Line four 7-inch or three 8-inch pans with parchment rounds and spray with non-stick baking spray.
Add 2 1/2 cups sugar and 1 cup butter into the bowl of a stand mixer. Cream together on a high speed for 1-2 minutes with a whisk attachment or hand mixer. The mixture should become light in color.
Mix in 4 large eggs on a medium speed, two at a time.
Add 1 tsp baking soda, 1 1/2 baking powder, and 1 tsp salt. Mix on high for another minute.
In a separate bowl whisk together 1 cup of hot water,  1 cup of sour cream and 1 cup of cocoa powder until no clumps remain.
Next, add 1 cup of flour into the butter/egg mixture. Scrape the sides of the bowl with a spatula, to ensure the flour is fully incorporated.
Pour in half of the sour cream/cocoa mixture and gently pulse the mixture to incorporate the liquid (if you don't, you'll end up splattering the cocoa mixture all over you kitchen!)
Mix in the 2nd cup of flour, at a low speed. Pour in the remaining sour cream/cocoa mixture, and again gently pulse, then mix on low until fully combined.
Add in the last cup of flour, and mix on low until the flour is incorporated.
Evenly divide between the prepared pans. I like to use a kitchen scale to ensure each pan has exactly the same amount of batter.
Bake for 32-35 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Allow layers to cool in the pans for about 10 minutes, then run an offset spatula around the edge of the pans to help separate the layers from the pans.
Place the pans in the freezer for about 45 minutes, to accelerate the cooling process. Once the layers are fully cooled, carefully flip the pans and remove the layers from the pans.
Use a serrated knife to level the tops of the layers, then set aside. If you make the cake layers in advance, you can wrap and freeze them for up to 3 weeks.
While the cake layers bake and cool, make the peanut butter buttercream frosting.
Beat 1 1/2 cups of butter and 1/2 cup peanut butter on a medium speed for 30 seconds with a paddle attachment or hand mixer until smooth.
Mix in 1/2 tsp of salt.
Slowly add in 7 cups of powdered sugar, 1 cup at a time. Half way through adding the powdered sugar, pour in 1/2 cup of heavy cream or milk to make it easier to mix the frosting.
Beat on low until the ingredients are fully incorporated, and the desired consistency is reached.
If the frosting is too thick, add an extra Tbsp of heavy cream. If it's too thin, add in another 1/2 cup of powdered sugar.
Stir by hand with a rubber spatula for a couple minutes to get the frosting SUPER smooth.
Cover with plastic wrap and set aside.
Place 1/2 cup milk chocolate chips in a heatproof bowl and set aside.
Heat 1/3 cup of heavy cream in a heatproof bowl in the microwave for 45 seconds to 1 minute, until gently bubbling.
If you don’t have a microwave or prefer to use the stove top, you can heat the cream over a medium heat in a pan until it begins to simmer. Remove from heat.
Gently pour the heavy cream over the chocolate chips, making sure they are covered with cream. Allow mixture to sit for 1-2 minutes.

Stir slowly until the cream and chocolate are fully combined, and ganache is silky smooth. Pour into a plastic squirt bottle to easily add drips to a cake. If you don’t have any plastic bottles on hand, you can also use a spoon to drizzle it over cakes.
Set aside to cool for about 20 minutes (or place in fridge for about 10 minutes), until the mixture is just slightly warm to the touch.
Stack and frost cake layers on a greaseproof cake board, using a dab of frosting to help stick the first cake layer to the board.
Spread an even layer of peanut butter buttercream between each cake layer with a large offset spatula. Top with chopped up bits of buckeye and a drizzle of chocolate ganache.
Repeat with remaining cake layers.
Once the cake layers are stacked, spread a thin coat of frosting around the the cake, to fully cover the cake layers.
Smooth using a bench scraper, then chill the cake in the fridge (20 minutes) or freezer (10 minutes) until the frosting is firm to the touch.
Add a second, thicker layer of frosting to the cake. Smooth using either a bench scraper or a frosting comb.
Chill the cake in the fridge (20 minutes) or freezer (10 minutes) until the frosting is firm to the touch again before adding the chocolate drip.

Once the cake is chilled, complete a test drip to check the consistency of you ganache. If the test drip seems too thick, try heating up the ganache for 5-10 additional seconds in the microwave. If the mixture seems too thin, allow it cool a bit longer, then try another test drip.
Top the cake with a ring of buckeyes and enjoy!

ingredients.name: chipotle peppers from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce (start with 2 and taste before adding more)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons roasted sesame seeds (or 1 tablespoon tahini)
ingredients.name: roasted sesame seeds (or 1 tablespoon tahini)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bell pepper (red, yellow, or orange), thinly sliced
ingredients.name: bell pepper (red, yellow, or orange)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, thinly sliced into bite-sized (1/2-inch thick) strips
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 to 10 large (roughly 10-inch) tortillas (I like flour because they’re easier to roll, but corn works, too)
ingredients.name: large (roughly 10-inch) tortillas (I like flour because they’re easier to roll, but corn works, too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded Monterey Jack or Mexican blend cheese (one 8-ounce bag)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Water, as needed to reach drizzling consistency

preparationSteps: In a blender, add 3 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 2 chipotle peppers from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce, a heaping 1/3 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, a heaping 1/3 cup tomato paste, 3 tablespoons roasted sesame seeds, 3 tablespoons creamy peanut butter, 1 tablespoon chili powder, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon cumin. Blend on high until totally smooth, about 30 seconds. Taste and add 1 to 2 more chipotle peppers if you want more heat. Set aside.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet (like cast-iron) over medium-high heat. Add 1/2 a thinly sliced white onion and 1 thinly sliced bell pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden, about 5 minutes.

Add 1 1/2 pounds thinly sliced chicken breasts to the pan with the veggies. Season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add 1 cup of the mole sauce and stir so the chicken and vegetables are nicely coated.

Turn the stove off, leaving the chicken mixture in the skillet. Put a plate on the counter beside the stove, and the bag of shredded cheese beside the plate. Hold a tortilla in your hand, and use a spoon to scoop in about 1/2 cup of the enchilada filling. Sprinkle a little shredded cheese on top, roll it up, and place it seam-side down on the plate. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, placing them seam-side down on the plate and stacking them on top of each other as needed until all the filling is used. If your tortillas aren’t super fresh and are cracking (or if you are using corn tortillas), microwave them in a damp paper towel for 10-second increments to make them more pliable.

Spread about 1/2 cup mole sauce across the bottom of the now-empty skillet (no need to wipe it out — it’s OK if there are some chicken/veggie bits in there), then transfer the enchiladas to the skillet, snuggling them in tightly, seam-side down.

Pour the remaining mole sauce down the center of the enchiladas and around the edges of the skillet. Sprinkle the remaining cheese over top. Bake until the cheese is melted and golden and the sauce is bubbling, 15 to 20 minutes.

While the enchiladas bake, make the lime crema: In a small bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup sour cream, the zest and juice of 1 lime, and enough water to thin it to a drizzleable consistency (start with 1 teaspoon and add more a little at a time until it’s perfect).
Let the enchiladas cool for a few minutes. Use a spatula to gently cut around and lift each enchilada onto plates, then drizzle with lime crema, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve.

: Add everything to the Instant Pot. If it’s thawed, cook for 12 minutes manual high pressure + 10 minutes for natural release. If it’s frozen, cook for 16 minutes manual high pressure + 10 minutes natural release. Shred and serve over rice!

Add in the chicken thighs. Season the chicken with the spice mixture. Cook for a minute or two on each side. Add in the honey and coconut milk. Cover the skillet and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the chicken is fork tender and can be easily shredded.

name: honey harissa chicken
preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.

Toss 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons harissa, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika together on the prepared sheet pan and spread into a single layer so that the chicken thighs are not touching each other.
Roast for 30 minutes. Check to make sure they have reached 165°F internally (they should have!), remove from oven, and let rest for 5 minutes.
Slice or chop, then serve in bowls on top of Fancy Rice and garnished with Lemon Honey Pickled Red Onions, Harissa Labneh, and any other optional extras you want (recipes below).

name: fancy rice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/8 teaspoon ground cinnamon (or throw in a cinnamon stick)
ingredients.name: ground cinnamon (or throw in a cinnamon stick)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or 3 cups water + 3 teaspoons reduced-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or 3 cups water + 3 teaspoons reduced-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.name: dried currants (or chopped dried raisins, cranberries, dates, apricots, or a mixture)

Add 2 cups white rice and stir until coated, about 1 minute. Stir in 3 cups low-sodium chicken stock, the juice of 1/2 lemon, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/2 cup dried currants. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Keep the lid ON and let the rice sit covered for 10 more minutes (this will allow it to steam).
Meanwhile, thinly slice 3 scallions (both white and green parts — only discard the root tip) and finely chop 1/2 cup green olives and 1/2 cup soft green herbs.

After the rice has steamed for 10 minutes, stir in the prepped scallions, green olives, and soft green herbs (if you used a cinnamon stick, fish out and discard it now). Crumble 4 ounces feta into the pot and stir again. Taste and add more kosher salt or lemon juice as desired! I added another big pinch of salt because my stock was very low sodium. And I always like things very lemony, so I added more lemon juice, too!

name: Lemon Honey Pickled Red Onions
preparationSteps: Thinly slice 1 small red onion. Add the sliced onion, the juice of 2 large lemons, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt to a jar. Fill it the rest of the way with the hottest water possible from your tap. Cover tightly and shake to combine. Let the jar sit on the counter until dinnertime, or in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

name: Harissa Labneh

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 teaspoons harissa (amount depending on spice preference)
ingredients.name: harissa (amount depending on spice preference)

preparationSteps: Combine 1 cup labneh, 2 to 3 teaspoons harissa (if you want it mild, add 2 — if you want it spicier, add 3), the juice of 1/2 lemon, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Taste. Add more labneh if it tastes too spicy, more harissa if it’s not spicy enough, more lemon juice if it tastes too flat, and/or more kosher salt if it’s not flavorful enough. Make it your own!

name: Instant Pot Chicken Tagine
note: An intoxicating blend of spicy, sweet and savory ingredients make this Instant Pot chicken tagine a memorable meal that’s ready fast.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup thinly sliced red onion, optional

preparationSteps: Pat the chicken dry. Season all over with the salt.

Add the olive oil to the Instant Pot, hit Sauté, and Adjust to select the More or High setting. After 3 minutes of the oil heating, working in batches as needed, add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Flip the chicken and repeat on the other side. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Add the shallots, garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon and stir to combine; cook until fragrant, 1-2 minutes. Use a little chicken stock to deglaze if necessary.
Stir in the chicken stock, tomato paste, apricots, ⅓ cup of pistachios, brown sugar, and tomatoes until combined.

Return the chicken to the pot and turn to coat. Secure the lid, moving the valve so it is in the sealed position. Hit Cancel and then hit Manual or Pressure Cook. Pressure cook for 8 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then manually vent to release the remaining pressure.

name: 30-minute pork and asparagus bowls
note:
Tell me more about what I’m doing with the chili crisp: We are aiming to use mostly just the crunchy bits in the jar rather than the oil, which holds a ton of heat. When you scoop it out, angle your teaspoon to the side so that the oil can drip off. You don’t have to stress about this — there will be some oil clinging to the crunchy bits and that is fine! — I just don’t want you to use a teaspoon of straight up chili crisp oil.

Fave brands: No need to run out and buy a new jar, but next time you run out of tahini, for what it’s worth, I love Soom and the Whole Foods 365 brands best. For chili crisp, I love Red Clay and Fly by Jing.

Extra extra: Make coconut-ginger rice! And/or grab 1 large head green leaf or bibb/butter/Boston lettuce, separate and wash the leaves, and serve them with dinner so people have the option to make lettuce wraps.

Gimme more veg: Lots of ideas for this! A crunchy vegetable like shredded carrots or diced red bell pepper would be great as a topping for your bowls, if you have some in the fridge. You could also add chopped romaine to your bowls or make lettuce wraps with green leaf lettuce. Or stir some chopped spinach or cilantro into your pork mixture at the very end. Or swap the rice out for roasted sweet potatoes like we did in saucy pork and sweet potato bowls!
What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use microwaveable frozen rice and the powder subs (or pre-minced frozen cubes!) for the ginger and garlic.

Make ahead/love your leftovers/double it: This whole meal can be cooked ahead of time and reheated at mealtime. If you want to cook dinner and prep lunches for the week at the same time, double the pork mixture! Leftovers will stay good stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to four days. Reheat in the microwave for an easy and delicious meal. You could serve it with leftover rice, stuff the filling into lettuce wraps, or wrap the pork, asparagus, and rice up in a tortilla for a fresh spin on things. Leftover rice and/or pork and asparagus can also be frozen in airtight zip-top bags. Thaw in the fridge overnight then reheat on the stove or in the microwave. Store your tahini sauce in an airtight container in the fridge to up to a week. If it’s too thick, stir in a splash of really warm water to loosen it up.

Feeding kids: Scroll back up to the “why I love bowl dinners” section above the recipe! I talk kid stuff there. Also, if you kids are very sensitive to spice, you can omit chili crisp from the recipe and add a little on top of adult bowls only.

Vegetarian: Use a plant-based ground meat substitute, a pound of chopped mushrooms, and/or crumbled tofu. For the latter, squeeze a block of extra-firm tofu over the sink to remove any excess moisture. Also over the sink, use your hands to crumble it, squeezing out even more moisture as you do so, and add the crumbled tofu to the warmed skillet with oil (use 2 tablespoons of oil instead of 1). Cook undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden on the bottom, then flip it and repeat. Use your spatula to break it into crumbles then add the asparagus followed by the other ingredients, cooking until mostly absorbed.

Dairy-free: Already is!

Gluten-free: Swap the soy sauce for coconut aminos and double check that your chili crisp is gluten-free (the brands I recommend above both are!).
Seed/sesame-free: Use peanut butter, a nut butter, or plain or Greek yogurt as a sub for tahini. Omit the sesame seed garnish. And double check that your chili crisp is seed-free (most are!).
