preparationSteps: First, start cooking 1 1/2 cups dry white or brown rice so that it’s ready when your pork is ready! We will all be using different kinds of rice, so follow the cooking instructions on the package you have. Once it’s ready, keep it covered to stay warm.

Once your rice is underway, make the Creamy Chili Crisp Tahini Sauce by combining 1/4 cup tahini, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1 teaspoon chili crisp (just the crisp part, not the oil!) in a medium bowl. Add a splash of hot water, if needed, to achieve a drizzle-able consistency. Add more chili crisp, if desired, for more heat and flavor! Don’t put any of these ingredients away (except for the tahini, you can put that away!) — you’ll need them again soon.

Next, cook the Pork and Asparagus. Thinly slice 1 bunch scallions (we’re using both the white and green parts — only trim off and discard the dangly roots at the very bottom). Warm 1 tablespoon neutral oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add all but a small pile (for garnish) of the sliced scallions and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until softened. Use a microplane or box grater to grate a peeled 2-inch piece fresh ginger and 3 peeled garlic cloves right into the skillet. Cook, stirring, for another 30 to 45 seconds.

Add 1 pound ground pork to the skillet and turn the heat up to medium-high. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, using a wooden spoon to break the pork apart into as small of pieces as possible. The pork will release liquid as it cooks — keep cooking and stirring until almost all of the liquid in the pan evaporates and the pork is almost entirely cooked through, with just a bit of pink remaining.

Trim 1 1/2 inches off the bottom of 1 bunch asparagus to get rid of the hard, fibrous ends. Discard those ends. Chop the trimmed asparagus into 1/4-inch pieces cut on the diagonal. Add the asparagus to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute, then stir in 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 3 tablespoons rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1 teaspoon chili crisp (just the crisp part, not the oil!). Continue stirring until much of it has been absorbed, about 1 minute. Taste and adjust as needed to suit your taste buds! You can add more low-sodium soy sauce for salt, vinegar for tang, and/or chili crisp for heat!

Divide the rice and pork mixture between 4 bowls, or serve family style. Garnish bowls with the reserved sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Drizzle the Creamy Chili Crisp Tahini Sauce over top.

ingredients.name: freshly grated sharp cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper (seriously, do this now before your hands get dirty!).
Use a box grater to grate 2 cups of sharp cheddar cheese and set it aside.

In a large bowl, combine 1 pound ground chicken or turkey, 1 large egg, 1 cup of the grated sharp cheddar, 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup BBQ sauce, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Use your hands to mix everything together, then form 12 golf ball-sized meatballs and place them on one of the prepared baking sheets as close together as possible without touching. Drizzle the tops of the meatballs with extra-virgin olive oil.

Add 1 pound broccoli florets and 1 pint whole cherry tomatoes to the second baking sheet. Drizzle with 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil and season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Toss to coat, then spread the vegetables into an even layer.
Roast both sheet pans on the center rack for 17 to 20 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through (they should reach an internal temp of 165°F) and the broccoli is crispy around the edges.

While the meatballs and vegetables roast, finely chop 2 cups baby spinach and add the spinach to the bottom of a large microwave-safe bowl. Add 2 tablespoons unsalted butter on top of the spinach. Cut open 2 (10-ounce) bags frozen white rice and pour the frozen rice over the spinach and butter.

Cover the bowl tightly with a large plate and microwave according to the package instructions, increasing the cook time by 50%, until the rice is piping hot and the spinach has wilted. For example, if your package directs you to microwave the rice for 3 minutes, you will microwave it for 4 1/2 minutes!

While the rice is still piping hot, add the remaining 1 cup of grated cheddar, 1/4 cup whole milk, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and a few cracks of black pepper. Stir vigorously until creamy, melty, and fully combined. If needed, microwave in 30-second increments, stirring between each, until the cheese is fully melted.
Build bowls with the cheesy spinach rice, meatballs, broccoli, and tomatoes. Finish with a drizzle of BBQ sauce and serve.

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Make the dressing: Add 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, 1 heaping teaspoon Dijon mustard, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and a few grinds of black pepper to a jar, seal it with the lid, and shake until well combined. If you don’t have a jar, you can whisk the dressing ingredients together in a bowl. Set aside.

Slice 1 red onion 1/4-inch thick. Add it to a rimmed sheet pan along with 1 pound cubed butternut squash and 6 fresh thyme sprigs (or 3 fresh rosemary sprigs). Add 2 tablespoons of the maple-balsamic dressing and 1 teaspoon kosher salt to the sheet pan and use your hands to toss until the veggies are all lightly coated. Spread the vegetables out evenly and roast for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, de-rib and chop 1 bunch of curly kale. Wash and spin it dry. Place it in a large serving bowl. If you’re using pre-chopped bagged kale, pull out any big pieces of stem you see as you add it to the serving bowl.

After the vegetables have roasted for 20 minutes, stir them, then add 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts to the baking sheet. Drizzle the chicken with a little bit of the maple-balsamic dressing and season generously with kosher salt and black pepper. Roast everything for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken registers an internal temperature of 160°F (while the chicken cools, the temperature will continue to rise to reach 165°F) and the squash is super tender. Set aside to cool down. If the chicken reaches 160°F before the squash becomes super tender (you should be able to easily squish a piece of squash with a fork), continue cooking the squash and onions until it is while the chicken cools.

While the chicken and squash are cooking, let’s “massage” our kale. Add 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to the kale and squeeze it in your hands 5 to 10 times until it feels softened, but not wet. Thinly slice 1 large apple and chop 5 dates and add them to the bowl along with 1/2 cup candied nuts and 8 ounces of crumbled goat or feta cheese .

When the chicken has cooled enough to handle it, chop into bite-sized pieces and add it to the salad along with the roasted squash and onions. You can discard the herb sprigs — they will have imparted their flavor on everything.

Add desired amount of dressing and toss to combine. Remember that you can always add more dressing but you can’t take it off, so add it a little at a time until it’s dressed to your liking. For what it’s worth, I use the entire amount! Season to taste with kosher salt and black pepper. Serve the salad in bowls and enjoy!

preparationSteps: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat (450°F).

Keep cooking as needed until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (cook time will vary based on how thick your chicken is). Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest while you make the salad.

Make the honey-soy vinaigrette: To a large jar, add 1 1/4 cups avocado oil, 1/2 cup rice vinegar, 1/3 cup honey, 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce , and 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil . Use a microplane or grater to grate in a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger and 1 garlic clove. Close the lid tightly and shake well to combine. Set the dressing aside.

Cut 1 small red cabbage in half and save one half for another use. Cut the remaining half in half and remove (and discard) the core then thinly slice the cabbage (you want about 3 cups). Add to the biggest serving bowl you have.

Repeat that process with the iceberg: Cut 1 head of iceberg lettuce in half and save one half for another use. Cut the other half in half, remove (and discard) the core, then thinly slice the lettuce (about 3 cups) and add it to the bowl.

Wash and dry 1 large head romaine , thinly slice it (about 5 cups), and add to the bowl. Thinly slice 10 ounces of sugar snap peas on the diagonal (I only trim off the tips if they’re really thick and fibrous otherwise, I leave them!) and 5 scallions (use both the white and green parts — only discard the root tip ends). Add these along with 1 1/2 cups toasted sliced almonds to the bowl. Peel 5 mandarins , separate the segments, and, you guessed it, add them to the bowl. If you’re using 2 large oranges, you can peel, then thinly slice them into bite-sized pieces instead.
Thinly slice the chicken breasts against the grain, then cut the thin slices into thirds to get bite-sized pieces, and add to the bowl. Cube 2 avocados and add 1 of the cubed avocados to the bowl.
Pour half the dressing on the salad and, using serving utensils or your clean hands, gently toss everything together. Taste and add more dressing depending on how well dressed you like your salad.
Garnish with the remaining avocado cubes and a handful of the wonton crisps . Serve the remaining wonton crisps at the table for guests to add so they don’t get soggy.

name: one-skillet steak and crispy smashed potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1 to 1/2 pound) 1 1/2 to 2-inch thick boneless ribeye steak
ingredients.name: 1 1/2 to 2-inch thick boneless ribeye steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds baby Dutch yellow potatoes (or other small - golf-ball-ish sized potato)
ingredients.name: baby Dutch yellow potatoes (or other small - golf-ball-ish sized potato)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or other neutral cooking oil such as vegetable or canola), plus 2 teaspoons
ingredients.name: olive oil (or other neutral cooking oil such as vegetable or canola), plus 2 teaspoons

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 fresh rosemary sprigs and/or 4 fresh thyme sprigs
ingredients.name: fresh rosemary sprigs and/or 4 fresh thyme sprigs

preparationSteps: Season 1 large boneless ribeye steak aggressively with salt and pepper and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. What does “aggressive” mean? I like to use 1 teaspoon of salt per 1 pound of meat, and about 1/4 teaspoon black pepper ( if I’m using pepper! You don’t ALWAYS have to use pepper!).

Allow the steaks to come to room temperature for at least 10 minutes, but up to 1 hour. Meanwhile, add 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes to a large heatproof bowl and add 2 tablespoons water to the bowl. Cover the bowl with a plate, and microwave for 7 minutes. Poke the potatoes with a fork. They should be very tender! If they’re not, microwave for another minute at a time until totally tender. Let the potatoes cool down completely - throw them in the fridge if you’re tight on time.

Warm a 12-inch skillet (preferably cast iron, and NOT nonstick if you can help it) over medium-high heat for three minutes. Add 1 tablespoon oil and warm until it just begins to smoke. Carefully add the ribeye steak into the skillet, then add 4 smashed garlic cloves and fresh herb sprigs on either side of the steak.

Cook the steak for 3 to 5 minutes, until a nice golden-brown sear forms. Flip it, and add 2 tablespoons butter to the pan. Continue cooking for an additional 3 to 5 minutes, basting it with the melted butter the entire time by tilting the skillet to one side and spooning the butter over top of the steak.

For medium-rare, stop cooking your steak when it reaches 125°F internally. Medium, 135°F. But a good, fatty steak like a ribeye should really be enjoyed medium-rare! A good indicator that your steak is finished cooking is when the juices begin to rise on the surface of the steak. The fat will also puff up a bit. You’ll see what I mean!

Transfer the steak to a plate and pour the butter, garlic, and herbs over top. Don’t you dare slice into that steak until the potatoes are finished cooking! It needs to rest so that the juices can redistribute through the meat.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat and warm 2 teaspoons oil for 30 seconds. Add the potatoes to the skillet in a single layer and use the bottom of the bowl you cooked them in to smash them lightly. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then flip and pour all of the juices that have collected under the steak into the skillet along with the remaining 1 tablespoon butter and cook for an additional 3 minutes, until crispy. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Turn off the heat.

Slice the steak into 1/2-inch thick slices. This is not one to slice super thin - you want nice, thick, juicy slices. Divide the steak and potatoes between two plates, garnish with a hit of finely chopped parsley if you’ve got it (I’m not gonna make you buy parsley just for a little garnish, but if you have it, use it!). ENJOY!

name: one-pan roasted chicken, cauliflower, and potatoes with a ridiculously tasty green sauce
note: Time: 25 minutes active, 1 hour total

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 or 2 rimmed half sheet pans (depending on how large your head of cauliflower is)
ingredients.name: rimmed half sheet pans (depending on how large your head of cauliflower is)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Blender or Food Processor (see the notes below the recipe if you have neither)
ingredients.name: Blender or Food Processor (see the notes below the recipe if you have neither)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 4 tablespoons neutral oil*, divided
ingredients.name: plus 4 tablespoons neutral oil*

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 ounces each)
ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 ounces each)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F and line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper.

I have a very specific way that I like to cut cauliflower (NO FLORETS!) so pay attention here. First, trim off the leaves and the very bottom of the cauliflower stem. Now slice it in half, through the stem. Place the two halves cut-side down on a cutting board, then slice it into 1/2-inch thick pieces. Cut or pull apart the individual florets.
Lots of little cauliflower bits crumbles will fall off - that’s OK! Add them to the sheet-pan, too. They’ll crisp up like little croutons and add lots of texture to our dish.
Place the cauliflower on half of the sheet pan.

Halve 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes , then place them on the other half of the sheet pan. Drizzle the cauliflower and potatoes with 3 tablespoons neutral cooking oil , then season with 2 teaspoons kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Toss to coat, keeping the cauliflower and potatoes separate. Turn the potatoes to that they are all cut-side-down on the sheet pan, and spread the cauliflower into as even of a layer as possible. If the cauliflower is really piled high, consider adding a second sheet-pan so that it will roast more evenly.

Roast for 35 minutes on the center rack in the oven. The cauliflower and potatoes should be tender, and just beginning to brown around the edges. If they’re not, roast for another 5 to 10 minutes before continuing to the next step.

While the vegetables roast, season 2 to 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts with a thin layer of oil, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and a sprinkle of pepper per breast. Set aside to come to room temperature while the vegetables cook.

Make the green sauce by blending 1 cup fresh basil leaves, 1/2 cup grated parmesan, 1/4 cup oil, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, the juice of 1/2 lemon, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt until smooth. If it’s too thick (it should be drizzle-able) or your blender is having a hard time blending it, blend in 1 tablespoon of water at a time. Taste and adjust seasoning to taste (always adjust seasoning for YOUR tastebuds!). Too tangy? Add another splash of oil. Need more flavor? Another pinch of salt. Love spice? Add some red pepper flakes! Pour the sauce into a bowl.
Roughly chop 4 cups of spinach. Finely chop 1/4 cup basil leaves. Keep them separate for later.

After 35 minutes, add the chicken breasts to the pan, on top of the vegetables is fine if there’s no space. No, you don’t need to stir the cauliflower or potatoes! Roast the chicken for 14 minutes, then check the internal temperature using a meat thermometer. If it’s not finished, continue cooking, checking the temperature frequently, until the chicken reaches 160°F.

Chicken must be 165°F to be safely served, but I like to pull chicken breasts out at 160°F as they will continue cooking even once removed from the oven, and have so little fat that we don’t want to risk overcooking them.

Transfer the chicken breasts to a cutting board to rest while we fancy up the veggies. Stir the chopped spinach and the juice of the remaining 1/2 lemon into the cauliflower until the spinach has wilted. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir 1/4 cup finely chopped basil and 2 tablespoons grated parmesan into the potatoes. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt and pepper as needed.

Slice the chicken breasts on the bias (see photo - don’t slice straight up and down, slice at an angle, this will make the chicken more tender). Serve the chicken alongside the potatoes and cauliflower, with LOTSA sauce!

name: cheddar drop biscuits

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/8 teaspoon lemon pepper or freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: lemon pepper or freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons cold butter, diced or grated on the largest hole of a box grater
ingredients.name: cold butter, diced or grated on the largest hole of a box grater

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces (1/2 cup) grated sharp cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: grated sharp cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, stir together 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/8 teaspoon lemon pepper (or regular pepper).

Dice up or grate 4 tablespoons of cold butter , toss it into the flour, then use your fingers to pinch it into the flour until everything’s crumbly and combined. Big butter clumps are A-OK, that’s how we get flaky biscuits!
Toss in 2 ounces (1/2 cup) grated cheddar cheese (or whatever!) and 2 tablespoons minced chives (or 1 tablespoon fresh thyme, or 1 teaspoon of a dried herb you like).
Stir in 1/2 cup whole milk until just combined. Don’t over-stir! The dough will be wet and sticky.
Drop the batter by big spoonfuls (I use an ice cream scoop and made 7 biscuits) onto the lined baking sheet, 1 inch apart. Spray the tops with cooking spray.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the tops are golden-brown and crispy.
Serve alongside your soup and DIG IN!

name: one-pot cheesy baked meatballs
note: Cook time: ~1 hour (15 minutes active, 45 minutes inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds ground beef (or 2 pounds of truly any combination of ground meat)
ingredients.name: ground beef (or 2 pounds of truly any combination of ground meat)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh parsley or basil, finely chopped, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: fresh parsley or basil, finely chopped, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 loaf of good crusty bread, like a sourdough
ingredients.name: of good crusty bread, like a sourdough

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (25 ounce) jar of your favorite pasta sauce (mine is Rao’s brand marinara)
ingredients.name: of your favorite pasta sauce (mine is Rao’s brand marinara)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil.

In a large bowl, use your hands to combine 2 pounds ground beef, 2 large eggs, 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.
Form 25 to 30 meatballs (they should be a little bigger than golf balls) and place them in the baking pan. You’ll have to really cram them in there!
Bake the meatballs for 20 minutes. Slice the loaf of bread into big thick slices, place them on a baking sheet and set aside for later.

After 20 minutes, remove the meatballs from the oven and carefully pour off the fat (pour it into an old jar or a bowl lined with aluminum foil. Once it cools you can just crumple it up and throw it away).
Pour 1 (25 ounce) jar of tomato sauce over top and stir gently (so that you don’t break the meatballs apart) to combine everything together.

Lower the oven temperature to 325°F and return the meatballs to the oven for 30 minutes. The sauce might look a little watery after this, just stir everything together gently until it looks delicious.

Turn the broiler to high. Sprinkle 1 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese all over the top of the meatballs. Place the meatballs on the top rack of the oven and the bread on the rack beneath them and broil for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese is melted and lightly golden brown and the bread is warm. Watch them closely while broiling — all broilers are different and I don’t want you to burn the cheese!
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley (and more red pepper flakes if you like) and dig in :)

name: Chicken Soup with Masa Dumplings
note: cook time: active ~15 minutes, total ~50 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 12 ounces/350 grams total), cut into 1⁄2- to 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 12 ounces/350 grams total)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium jalapeño, finely chopped (seeds removed if you want)
ingredients.name: medium jalapeño, finely chopped (seeds removed if you want)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium yellow or white onion, finely chopped
ingredients.name: medium yellow or white onion

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium bunch kale, stemmed and roughly chopped
ingredients.name: kale, stemmed and roughly chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 quarts high-quality chicken bone broth, store-bought or homemade
ingredients.name: high-quality chicken bone broth, store-bought or homemade

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1⁄2 cups cooked black beans, home-cooked or from one 15-ounce can
ingredients.name: cooked black beans, home-cooked or from one 15-ounce can

preparationSteps: Season the chicken: In a medium bowl, toss the chicken breasts with the salt and sugar and let sit in the fridge.

Make the soup: Heat a large Dutch oven or large pot over medium heat. Add the butter, jalapeño, onion, garlic, and a big pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and translucent, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the kale and cook, stirring occasionally, until wilted and darkened, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the bone broth, beans, bay leaves, oregano, and kosher salt and bring to a simmer over high heat. Cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and cook until the kale is silky and tender, about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the masa dumplings: In a medium bowl, combine masa harina, boiling water, melted butter, and salt and mix well with a rubber spatula. Once everything is evenly combined, knead with your hands until the mixture comes together into a smooth ball.

With a #60 scoop (or two spoons), scoop the dumpling dough into generous 1-tablespoon portions onto a sheet pan or large plate. With wet hands, roll each dumpling into a smooth ball. Use a chopstick to press a divot into each dumpling (this helps them cook evenly).
Taste the soup and add more salt if needed. Gently add all the dumplings to the simmering soup. Cover, adjust the heat to maintain a gentle simmer, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer, stirring gently to distribute the heat, until cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve with cilantro, white onion, sour cream, avocado, and lime wedges.

name: (almost) one-pan garlic butter roasted chicken and crispy potatoes
note: Cook time: ~1 hour, 10 minutes (30 minutes active; 40 minutes inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds of baby potatoes, cut in half
ingredients.name: of baby potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12 ounce) jar of roasted red peppers, drained
ingredients.name: of roasted red peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup blanched almonds, skin off (if you can’t find these, no worries, just use ANY almonds — raw, toasted, slivered, whatever)
ingredients.name: blanched almonds, skin off (if you can’t find these, no worries, just use ANY almonds — raw, toasted, slivered, whatever)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup (plus more for garnish) finely chopped soft green herbs, such as parsley, dill, basil, chives…
ingredients.name: (plus more for garnish) finely chopped soft green herbs, such as parsley, dill, basil, chives…

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon, cut into wedges or slices
ingredients.name: lemon

ingredients.rawIngredient: Pita or a good loaf of bread (optional)
ingredients.name: Pita or a good loaf of bread (optional)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Cut 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes in half and place them and 8 chicken thighs on your largest rimmed sheet pan, all in a heap in the center. Add 1/2 cup olive oil, the zest (use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to zest it) and juice of 1 lemon, 4 crushed garlic cloves (just smash them with the side of your knife blade) , 1 teaspoon paprika, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper on top and get in there with your hands to distribute and coat everything evenly.

Space everything out on the sheet pan with the chicken skin-side up. If your pan is too crowded, put half of the chicken and potatoes on another pan. Bake in the oven uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes until the potatoes are tender when poked with a fork, the chicken is cooked through (to 165°F), and the skin is crispy . If you’re using two pans, put one on the middle rack and one on the bottom rack, and switch them 30 minutes in. While the chicken is cooking, make the romesco and garlic butter. To make the romesco: in a blender or food processor, combine everything but the olive oil (1 jar of roasted red peppers, drained; 1/2 cup almonds; 1/4 cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained; 1 peeled garlic clove; 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar; and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt) . Once mostly blended, drizzle in 1/2 cup olive oil while the motor is running. Keep going for several minutes — you want it to be gorgeously creamy and smooth. Taste and add more salt if it needs it.

If you don’t have a blender or food processor, you can make a coarse romesco sauce by simply hand chopping everything as finely as possible, then stirring it in a bowl with 1/4 cup olive oil (less than the normal recipe since it won’t emulsify into a smooth sauce). For the garlic butter, simply melt 2 tablespoons butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat, add 1 crushed garlic clove (smash it with the side of your knife), and bubble gently for a minute. Remove from the heat and stir in 1/4 cup chopped parsley (or another soft green herb). Remove the chicken and potatoes from the oven and drizzle the warm garlic butter over top. Spoon on some of the romesco sauce, add lemon slices, and crumble 1/4 cup feta over top. Add some fresh herbs for garnish and bring the whole pan to the table to serve family style alongside some good bread or pita, if you’ve got it. Enjoy!

name: one-skillet chicken & gingery rice
note: Cook time: 40 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1 to 2-inch) piece fresh ginger (if feeding spice averse people, ginger can be “spicy” to some, mostly kids, so use less or no ginger!)
ingredients.name: fresh ginger (if feeding spice averse people, ginger can be “spicy” to some, mostly kids, so use less or no ginger!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, white fat trimmed off
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, white fat trimmed off
For the spicy peanut curry sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons red curry paste (if feeding spice averse people, start with just 1 tablespoon, or even less)
ingredients.name: red curry paste (if feeding spice averse people, start with just 1 tablespoon, or even less)

preparationSteps:
cilantro sprigs, for serving

Make the chicken and rice: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add 1 1/2 cups rinsed long-grain white rice and grate in 1 ( 1 to 2-inch) piece fresh ginger (no need to peel it, use less if spice averse). Cook, stirring, until very fragrant, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 2 1/2 cups water and 3/4 teaspoon salt . Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low.

Season 2 pounds trimmed boneless, skinless chicken thighs with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt . Lay them over the rice, overlapping slightly if needed to fit. Cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the chicken registers 165°F. If the rice isn’t tender after 25 minutes, just keep cooking it, don’t worry about overcooking the chicken, thighs are resilient!

Remove the skillet from the heat and let sit, covered, for 10 minutes to allow the rice to steam.

While the chicken and rice are cooking, make the peanut curry sauce: Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a small pot over medium heat. When it shimmers, add 1 to 2 tablespoons red curry paste and cook, stirring, until very fragrant and sticking to the bottom of the pot, about 1 minute. Stir in 1 (13.5-ounce) can full-fat coconut milk , 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce , 1 tablespoon fish sauce , 1 tablespoons peanut butter , 1 tablespoon sriracha (if using), and 2 teaspoons honey . Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring often, until very thick, like heavy cream or a thin yogurt, 10 to 15 minutes. Don’t let it boil over — reduce the heat to medium-low if needed. Remove the pot from the heat and let cool a bit.

Chop 10 cilantro sprigs and scatter around the chicken and rice. Drizzle the sauce all over the top and serve family-style with extra sauce on the side. I also had some peanuts and threw those on there!

name: sheet-pan miso maple mustard chicken, sweet potato, and brussels
note:
Cook time: 1 hour (20 minutes active, 40 minutes inactive)

• Save time : If your store sells it, buy pre-cubed sweet potato or butternut squash.

• Feeding kids: Add a different sauce to their plate if it’ll get them to eat the chicken. Ketchup, BBQ, ranch… whatever it takes! If they love fries, you could swap the sweet potato cubes out for TJ’s butternut zig zags.

• Love your leftovers/meal prep: These leftovers make a 10/10 lunch. Store them in an airtight container in the fridge. See the “bowl” section in the “do your thing” note in the intro.

• Prep ahead: Pre chop/cube your veggies earlier in the day or even the day before and store them in the fridge in an airtight container. If it’ll fit in your fridge, you can even prep the whole sheet pan ahead of time, wrap it tightly with plastic wrap, then just throw it in the oven when you’re ready to cook! You might have to go the two half sheet pan route for that though unless you have a really big fridge.

• Vegetarian: Chickpeas!! Drain, rinse, and dry 1 or 2 cans of chickpeas and use those in place of the chicken. Since you’re not getting fat from the chicken, add another tablespoon of oil to the sheet pan.

• Gimme some cheese: Goat cheese, crumbled feta, shredded white cheddar, grated Parm — any would be a delicious addition to this.

• Gimme some greens: Add a handful of mixed greens, arugula, or some lacinato kale (that you’ve sprinkled with salt and massaged/squeezed a few times to soften) to your bowls.

• Gimme a grain: Add cooked farro, brown rice, or quinoa!

• DF/GF : For DF, swap the yogurt for a plain DF yogurt or mayo. If you need to avoid gluten, check your miso paste to make sure there are no added grains. The brand Miso Master is gluten-free!

• Chicken: I love bone-in, skin-on chicken (thighs, leg quarters, drumsticks, breasts, whatever!) best for this meal. The skin gets perfectly crispy and is full of flavor while keeping the meat incredibly moist. That said, any cuts of chicken — even boneless, skinless options — as well as pork tenderloin would all be really good here! If using boneless, you won’t need 2 to 3 pounds of it… more like 1.5 pounds. In general, boneless cuts of chicken cook faster than bone-in, but they’re also less forgiving if you overcook them. Best advice? Google the recommended cook time for the cut of meat you have in front of you (at 425°F) and adjust when you pull it off your sheet pan accordingly. Keep your meat thermometer handy and pull the chicken when it hits 165°F — or 145°F for pork tenderloin. Chickpeas are another good protein option for this meal (see vegetarian note above). If your veggies aren’t very tender by the time your protein is fully cooked, keep them in the oven until they are, checking every few minutes.

• Sweet potato: Butternut squash, delicata squash (y’all’s fave!!), any other type of winter squash you love, Yukon gold potatoes, parsnips, carrots, cauliflower… all would be good! Just make sure that you cube/cut them into pieces roughly the same size as your Brussels so they’ll cook uniformly.

• Brussels sprouts: Cauliflower, broccoli, or any of the veggies listed just above!

• EVOO : Olive oil or a neutral cooking oil like canola, grapeseed, safflower, etc.

• Miso (for the chicken + veggies): The miso adds delicious umami to this meal, but if you don’t have any you can omit it and still have a lovely maple-mustard situation. I’d add an extra 1/2 teaspoon of salt to make up for the saltiness you’ll be missing from the miso.

• Maple syrup : Honey or brown sugar

• Dijon mustard: Grainy or yellow mustard. Omit if you hate mustard!

• Lemon zest : Omit

• Lemon juice: A light-colored vinegar like white wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar

• Plain yogurt: Plain Greek yogurt, sour cream, mayo

• Miso (for the yogurt sauce) : Juice from the other half of that lemon and extra salt!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 pounds bone-in skin-on chicken (use whatever cut of chicken your fam likes, I used 4 leg quarters!)
ingredients.name: bone-in skin-on chicken (use whatever cut of chicken your fam likes, I used 4 leg quarters!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large (3/4-pound to 1-pound) sweet potato, peeled (or not! but I like to peel mine) and 1 1/2-inch cubed
ingredients.name: and 1 1/2-inch cubed
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (3/4-pound to 1-pound) sweet potato, peeled (or not! but I like to peel mine)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound Brussels sprouts, ends trimmed (only if they look grubby! no need to if not), and halved
ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts, ends trimmed (only if they look grubby! no need to if not), and halved

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1/2 lemon, plus more to taste (use the lemon you zested for the chicken + veggies!)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1/2 lemon, plus more to taste (use the lemon you zested for the chicken + veggies!)

preparationSteps: Position an oven rack in the center of the oven. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 2 to 3 pounds of bone-in skin-on chicken on the baking sheet. Peel (or don’t, but I do!) and cut 1 large sweet potato into 1 1/2-inch cubes and add it to the baking sheet. Trim (only if the root ends look grubby — if they don’t, you don’t have to worry about it) and halve 1 pound Brussels sprouts and add them to the baking sheet.

Right on top of everything, add 3 tablespoons EVOO, 3 tablespoons miso paste, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, the zest from 1 lemon (use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to zest it), 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper.
Now GET IN THERE with your hands and smoosh and toss until all the chicken and veggies are evenly coated with all the ingredients!!!

Spread everything out into an even layer — it’s OK if everything is smooshed tightly, but it shouldn’t be overlapping. If it is, grab another baking sheet, line it with parchment paper, and transfer half of the chicken and veggies over there. The chicken should be skin-side up, and the Brussels should be cut-side down (to ensure crispiness all around).

Roast on the center rack in the oven for 35 to 40 minutes, draining off the accumulated liquid from the sheet pan at the halfway mark (just bring the pan to the sink and tilt it to drain off excess liquid), until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are very tender. If the chicken skin starts to burn (start peeking at it at the 30 minute mark), simply cover the baking sheet loosely with aluminum foil and keep roasting. I didn't need to do this but all ovens are different!

While the sheet pan is in the oven, make your miso yogurt: In a medium bowl, stir together all the ingredients ( 1/3 cup plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons miso paste, the juice of half the zested lemon, 2 teaspoons maple syrup, and a pinch of salt ). Taste and adjust seasonings if needed until it’s perfect. If it’s too sweet, add a bit more lemon juice. If it’s too tart, add more syrup. If it’s dull tasting, add a little more miso or salt.
Serve the chicken and veggies drizzled with miso yogurt. DIG IN!

name: LESSON #2: Roasted garlic is your new best friend.
note:
Cook time: 1 hour

• I don’t like squash skin. Delicata squash skins are entirely edible, but if you’re not into it, you can actually just discard the skins, leave the filling in the skillet, smooth it out, sprinkle it with cheese, and bake it right in the skillet. Scoop it out and serve it like a casserole — plop it in a bowl and enjoy!

• Feeding kids: Remember team, branding is everything! Perhaps your kids will go for “sausage boats?” If they’re casserole lovers, see the “I don’t like squash skin” note above.

• Bulk up the salad: Add candied nuts or any roasted nut, apple (I know there’s already apple in the squash but it would be great raw and crisp in the salad), pomegranate seeds, and/or more shredded white Cheddar cuz why not?

• Bump up the protein: Add a can of rinsed and dried cannellini beans to the sheet pan along with the kale. Yum.

• OK but what if I want to make this a side dish? This would be a delightful holiday side. I would make it this exact same way, but cut the squash halves in half after they’ve finished twice-baking so they’re more “side” portions.

• Add something sweet: Raisins, dates, or another dried fruit would give the filling a nice pop of sweetness, if you have them and and would be into that!

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be great for up to 3 days. I wouldn’t freeze the assembled stuffed squash as the squash would get mushy. But the filling would freeze so well! The warmed kale salad is best right of the oven, so only cook as much as you plan to eat for this meal.

• Prep ahead: You can prep the whole recipe through the step when you assemble the stuffed squash up to a day ahead. Store the stuffed squash covered in the fridge until you’re ready to bake. Bake them for 20 minutes instead of 10 so they’re warmed all the way through. If the cheese is scorching on top with the added bake time. Cover them all with foil while they finish cooking.

• Vegetarian : Grate 8 ounces of tempeh on the largest hole of a box grater. Cook it in a skillet in a little oil and all of the same seasonings I mention in the “you can make lean ground meat taste like sausage” section above the recipe. Or, use a vegan ground “sausage.”

• Dairy-free: Use a DF cheese if you’re into it, or just skip the cheese! It’d be delicious without it.

• Gluten-free: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs like these or cooked rice.

• Delicata squash : Any winter squash will work, I just love that delicata are so perfectly portioned. If you’re using acorn or butternut squash, buy smaller ones — they'll still be great individual portions. And yes, OK, you could also use sweet or russet potatoes!

• Garlic : You could skip roasting the garlic if you need to, but man is it tasty. If you need to skip it, mince 4 garlic cloves (or use 4 frozen cubes of minced garlic) and cook them with the sausage instead, or add 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder to the sausage while it browns.

• EVOO : Olive oil, any other cooking oil you have

• Jimmy Dean sage sausage: Any ground sausage, or any plain ground meat (other than beef) doctored up how I explain it in the “cooking school” section above the recipe. Or see the vegetarian ideas in the “notes” section.

• Panko breadcrumbs : Any breadcrumbs you’ve got, or throw any bread you have (the staler the better!) in the blender, pulse until it’s small crumbles, and use that. You could also swap breadcrumbs out for a COOKED grain like rice, quinoa, or farro.

• Honey crisp apple : Any apple, an unripe pear (it will need to be hard in order to grate it!), raisins, chopped dates, or pomegranate seeds

• Cheddar : Sharp Cheddar’s my favorite for this. Pre-shredded is fine! If needed, you can swap in something like Gruyere, manchego, goat cheese, pepper Jack, Monterey Jack, havarti… whatever you have in the fridge! Or you could skip it.

• Bagged kale: A large head of kale, de-ribbed and chopped, or another dark leafy green like collard greens or Swiss chard

• Balsamic vinegar: White wine vinegar, apple cider vinegar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 delicata squash, halved (try to buy squash that are as uniform in size as possible)
ingredients.name: delicata squash, halved (try to buy squash that are as uniform in size as possible)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of garlic (AKA the entire bulb!)
ingredients.name: of garlic (AKA the entire bulb!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound Jimmy Dean sage sausage (or any ground sausage, but if you have the choice, that’s the one)
ingredients.name: Jimmy Dean sage sausage (or any ground sausage, but if you have the choice, that’s the one)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces chopped, washed kale (store-bought in a bag)
ingredients.name: chopped, washed kale (store-bought in a bag)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Trim the tiniest bit off of both ends of 4 delicata squash to remove the root end and the stem. Trim the top off of 1 head of garlic (see minute 6:55 of the video above for a demo!) so that the tops of all of the cloves are exposed.

Cut the squash in half vertically, then use a spoon to scoop out (and discard) the seeds. Place the squash halves on the sheet pan skin-side down, along with the head of garlic. Drizzle the insides of the squash and the exposed garlic cloves with extra-virgin olive oil . Season everything with kosher salt (about a teaspoon total between all 8 squash halves plus another pinch for the garlic) and freshly cracked black pepper.
Flip the squash cut-side down on the baking sheet. Wrap the garlic head in aluminum foil — just tightly smoosh some foil around it.
Roast for 30 to 40 minutes, until the squash and garlic are very tender. Check at the 30 minute mark — if the squash is still hard, keep roasting! You want it to be squishy when you push down on it.

Meanwhile, prepare the filling. Add 1 pound ground sausage to a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, using a spatula to break the sausage up into tiny crumbles, until it’s brown all over, 6 to 8 minutes. While it’s cooking, grate 1 apple using the largest hole of a box grater, and add it into the skillet along with 1/2 cup panko. Stir to combine everything and continue crumbling the meat. Once the sausage is cooked through, remove the skillet from heat.
Grate 8 ounces of white cheddar cheese on the largest hole of the box grater (it’s OK if it’s covered in apple guts, no need to wash it) and set it aside.

Once the squash and garlic are out of the oven and cool enough to handle, squeeze the roasted garlic directly into the sausage mixture. Use a spoon to carefully scrape as much of the squash flesh out as possible without ripping the skins. You don’t need to get all of the squash out! The skins are thin and will rip easily if you try to scrape them down completely. Even if the skins rip, don’t stress — when the filling is in there you can squeeze everything back together. Add the scooped-out flesh and half of the shredded cheese to the skillet and stir to combine. Use your spatula to break up large chunks of garlic and squash so it’s all well incorporated. Taste and add more salt and/or pepper if needed. I add about 1/2 teaspoon of salt here!
Scoop the filling back into the now-empty squash skins. Add the remaining cheese on top. Bake for 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melty.

Right after you put the stuffed squash in the oven, line a second baking sheet with parchment paper. Dump 10 ounces of chopped kale (or however much you want to eat for this meal) onto the baking sheet. Drizzle the kale with 2 tablespoons EVOO, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, and a big pinch of salt (about 1/2 teaspoon) . Use your hands to lightly massage the kale to make sure it’s evenly coated. Add the baking sheet to the oven with the squash and let it cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until crispy on the edges but still tender on the bottom.
Remove both pans from the oven and plate a stuffed squash (or 2 if you’re really hungry!) with a side of warmed kale salad. ENJOY!

name: recs from my girlfriends + a delicious mango pie
note:
By Khushbu Shah, edited to suit WTC style

• NOTE: You can freeze leftover pie in an airtight container for up to a month.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups finely ground graham cracker crumbs (about 24 sheets)
ingredients.name: finely ground graham cracker crumbs (about 24 sheets)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) block full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
ingredients.name: full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

To make the crust, combine 3 cups finely ground graham cracker crumbs, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 teaspoon ground black cardamom, and a pinch of salt in a medium bowl and stir to evenly combine. Pour in 1 1/2 sticks (12 tablespoons) melted butter and mix again so that the butter is evenly distributed and the mixture starts to clump together. If you’re making 2 pies, divide the mixture between 2 (9-inch) pie pans and use your fingers to press down on the mixture to create an even and compact crust that runs up the sides of the pans. If you’re making 1 large pie, line a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with parchment paper so that it overhangs the sides of the pan (this will make it easier to serve), then press the crumbs into an even layer across the bottom of the pan.

Bake for 10 to 12 minutes (you might need a few more minutes if using the 9 x 13 pan). The crust should be golden brown but not too dark—like it spent time in the sun but wore lots of sunscreen. Let cool completely.

To make the filling, pour 1/2 cup cold water into a saucepan and sprinkle 2 (3/4-ounce) envelopes unflavored gelatin over the water. Let it sit for 5 minutes, then place the saucepan over medium heat and stir until the gelatin is fully dissolved. Let the mixture cool. Transfer the gelatin mixture to a blender, along with 1 (30-ounce) can mango pulp , 1 (8-ounce) block full-fat cream cheese , and 1/2 cup condensed milk . Blitz until well combined and there are no cream cheese chunks.

Divide the mango mixture between the pie crusts or pour into the 9 x 13 pan and use a silicone spatula to make sure the filling is even and smooth. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until firm. (I prefer to refrigerate it overnight.) Serve chilled, garnished with whipped cream , if you so desire.

name: How to make flaky biscuits!
note: Cook time: 2 hours (most of this is hands off time while the veggies roast and cool!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 heads of garlic (AKA 2 whole bulbs of it — not 2 individual cloves)
ingredients.name: of garlic (AKA 2 whole bulbs of it — not 2 individual cloves)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 quart (AKA 4 cups) of chicken bone broth, divided
ingredients.name: (AKA 4 cups) of chicken bone broth

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup cottage cheese (any kind, but I like double cream Good Culture best)
ingredients.name: cottage cheese (any kind, but I like double cream Good Culture best)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon any vinegar (I like balsamic or apple cider)
ingredients.name: any vinegar (I like balsamic or apple cider)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Completely optional: sexy garnishes like a swirl of chili oil, chili crisp, pepitas…
ingredients.name: Completely optional: sexy garnishes like a swirl of chili oil, chili crisp, pepitas…

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Cut the stem end off of the top of 1 butternut squash , then stand it up on its root end to more easily cut it in half vertically. Use a spoon to scoop the seeds out. Cut the tippy top end off of 2 heads of garlic to expose the tops of the cloves and place them on a large square of foil.

Place the squash on a baking sheet and drizzle/rub all over with extra-virgin olive oil (no need to measure here — just use enough to coat it well!). Place it cut-side down on the baking sheet (so you should only be able to see the skin!). Drizzle and rub the garlic heads all over with EVOO too, place them cut-side down, then close the tin foil, making a pouch for the garlic. Add the foil pouch to the sheet pan.

Roast for 45 minutes. Using tongs, transfer the garlic to a small plate. Carefully open the pouch and see if the garlic is nice and squishy. If it is, it’s ready! Just keep it on the plate to cool. If it’s not, close the pouch and add it back to the baking sheet.
Continue roasting the squash (and potentially the garlic) for another 30 minutes or until very, very squishy when you poke the skin.
While it’s roasting, make your biscuits! See recipe below.
Flip the squash over and let it cool for 20 minutes.
While it’s cooling, bake your biscuits! Turn the oven up to 425°F and bake those puppies.

If you own an immersion blender, scrape the squash flesh out of the skins and into a large pot, and squeeze the squishy cloves of 1 whole roasted garlic head in. Add 3 cups of bone broth, 1 cup cottage cheese, 1 teaspoon of any vinegar, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and several cranks of freshly ground black pepper. Blend until smooth!

If you are using a standard blender, blend the soup in batches as it’ll be too much to fit at once. It doesn’t matter what ingredients get blended with what as long as it’s all smooth. As they’re ready, transfer the blended batches to a large pot then stir well to combine.

Now, you’re going to taste and adjust to make it perfect for you! You can blend in as much of the second head of roasted garlic as you like! I added the whole thing, but some people prefer less, so taste and add it a clove or two at a time until it’s perfect. You can also add up to 1 more cup of bone broth (and if you need even more: Better Than Bouillon + water!) as needed until you reach your desired consistency. Some people like it really thick, others like it more thin like a broth, do your thing! Taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Keep the soup warm over low heat and enjoy with your biscuits! Top your bowls with a sprinkle of pepitas and chili crisp and/or a swirl of chili oil, if using.

name: thanksgiving leftover sliders
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes

• I have everything but Hawaiian rolls: If you have leftover Parker House rolls, those would be great here in place of the King’s Hawaiian rolls! Any roll works, really, but the sheet-like aspect of King’s Hawaiian makes assembly a breeze. You could also make sandwiches! Just skip the honey butter, and instead smear butter on the outsides of the bread and toast in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.

• Prep ahead: Shred the turkey ahead of time — it’s actually easiest to shred while it’s still warm/room temp. You could go ahead and make the cranberry mayo the night before too. Don’t assemble the sandwiches ahead of time though because the bread would get soggy.

• It’s not the holiday season: If you’re making these sometime in the future when you don’t have an abundance of Thanksgiving leftovers in your fridge, you can swap raspberry jam in for the cranberry sauce, and use sliced deli turkey or ham (about 12 thick slices) or shredded chicken instead of shredded turkey. If you’re using sliced deli meat instead of shredded turkey or chicken, skip the step when you mix the meat in with the cranberry mayo. Instead, just spread the bottom layer of rolls with 1/3 cup mayonnaise followed by 3 tablespoons cranberry sauce or jam.

• Can I put other leftovers on these sliders? Sure! They’re perfect as is but if you want to experiment, I think a thin layer of mashed potatoes or stuffing spread on top of the turkey layer would be fab.

• Vegetarian: You could apply this slider method to any Thanksgiving leftovers. Roasted veggies or stuffing spread out onto Kings Hawaiian rolls with the cranberry mayo, mustard, cheese, and honey butter would be delicious, I’m sure!

• Dairy-free : Use DF cheese (or omit it) and plant-based butter

• Gluten-free: Use any gluten-free sandwich bread or slider buns or rolls you can find. See the “I have everything but the Hawaiian rolls” note above for how to make these using sandwich bread instead of rolls.

• Mayonnaise : Vegan mayo if you’re trying to avoid eggs. You could also omit and just use cranberry sauce as the bottom layer condiment if you hate mayo.

• Leftover cranberry sauce: Raspberry jam (or any jam)

• King’s Hawaiian Original Hawaiian Sweet Dinner Rolls : See the “I have everything but the Hawaiian rolls” note above.

• Turkey : 2 cups of leftover shredded chicken would work perfectly, or 12-ish thick slices of deli ham or turkey. See the “it’s not the holiday season” note above for more info if using sliced deli meat.

• Havarti + Provolone: You could use all of one kind of cheese if you can’t find both. Sliced Swiss, mozzarella, or Muenster would also be great! Omit or use DF sliced cheese if you can’t do dairy.

• Whole-grain mustard: Dijon, but reduce the amount to 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon, divided, as it’s more pungent than whole grain. Yes, you could use yellow mustard if it’s all you have (same measurements as whole grain). Or, if you don’t like mustard, omit it and use more of the cranberry mayo on the top layer of buns.

• Unsalted butter : A plant-based unsalted butter — or salted butter if it’s all you have. If you have no butter, spray the tops and sides with cooking spray then sprinkle with the Everything Bagel seasoning (ditch the honey and mustard for the buns).

• Honey : Maple syrup. Or brown sugar, but you’d need to stir hard to help it dissolve into the melted butter! You could also omit — the cranberry sauce and Hawaiian buns would lend enough sweetness.

• Everything Bagel seasoning : Everything Bagel seasoning is essentially a mix of toasted sesame seeds, poppy seeds, garlic, onion, and salt — the perfect salty, savory complement to the sweetness of the cranberry sauce, honey butter, and rolls. You can find it at most grocery stores — I always buy it at Trader Joe’s. If you can’t find it, poppy seeds would be a great sub. Or you can just omit!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 package (12-count) King’s Hawaiian Original Hawaiian Sweet Dinner Rolls
ingredients.name: King’s Hawaiian Original Hawaiian Sweet Dinner Rolls

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded roasted turkey meat (or 12 thick slices of deli turkey)
ingredients.name: shredded roasted turkey meat (or 12 thick slices of deli turkey)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon whole grain mustard, divided (or 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon Dijon)
ingredients.name: plus 1 teaspoon whole grain mustard, divided (or 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon Dijon)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, stir 1/2 cup mayonnaise and 1/4 cup cranberry sauce together.

Keeping the buns attached to one another, use a long serrated knife to slice a pack of 12 Hawaiian rolls in half horizontally (so you’ll end up with one large bottom half and one large top half). Place the bottom half of the buns on the baking sheet. Spread a nice layer of cranberry mayonnaise on the cut side of the bottom layer of the buns.
Add 2 cups shredded turkey meat to the remaining cranberry mayonnaise and stir to combine. If it’s too mayo-y for you, add more turkey, this will really depend on how dry your turkey is.

Now start layering the sliders! On top of the mayo layer, add a layer of Havarti cheese, then all of the turkey, then a layer of Provolone. Spread the cut side of the top buns with 2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard and place the top bun on top.
Melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter in a small bowl in the microwave. Stir in 2 teaspoons honey and 1 teaspoon whole-grain mustard.

Pour the honey butter over the tops and sides of the buns until they’re all coated. If you have a pastry brush, use it to make sure the butter spreads evenly. If you don’t have a pastry brush, use your fingers! Sprinkle 1 tablespoon Everything Bagel seasoning evenly across the tops of the buns.

Place the sheet pan in the oven and bake until the buns are golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Set a timer and don’t overcook them! It’s very sad when the buns get too hard! Slice into individual sliders and serve.

name: cheesy shells alla sausage vodka, 2020

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (1 stick), room temperature and cut into small chunks
ingredients.name: unsalted butter (1 stick), room temperature and cut into small chunks

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup smooth peanut butter (or any other nut/seed butter)
ingredients.name: smooth peanut butter (or any other nut/seed butter)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup firmly packed light brown sugar
ingredients.name: firmly packed light brown sugar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup mini M&Ms (try to find Christmas colors!)
ingredients.name: mini M&Ms (try to find Christmas colors!)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

Add 1/2 cup room-temperature unsalted butter (that you’ve cut into small chunks), 1/2 cup smooth peanut butter, 1/2 cut white granulated sugar, and 1/2 cup firmly packed brown sugar to the bowl of a stand mixer fixed with the paddle attachment. Beat on high until creamed (it will be fluffy and smooth), about 4 to 6 minutes. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed.
Add 1 large egg and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and continue beating until smooth.

Reduce mixer speed to low and gradually incorporate 1 cup all-purpose flour , 1/2 teaspoon baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Once fully incorporated, mix in 1/2 cup semisweet chocolate baking chunks, 1/2 cup mini M&Ms, 1 cup Rice Krispies Cereal, 1/2 cup old-fashioned rolled oats, and 1/2 cup raisins (if using) .

Turn the mixer off immediately once all ingredients are mixed in (over mixing your dough will make the cookies tough!). Use a 1 tablespoon scoop to drop the dough 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets. Leaving space between the cookies is important, they will spread as they bake! Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, or until the edges have lightly browned but the tops are still very blonde. (This is very important!! The tops should look like they aren’t quite cooked yet! They’ll firm up as they cool, I promise!)
BANG the sheet pan firmly on the countertop 5 times to flatten the cookies out a bit. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking sheet.

name: lemon-parm chicken, quinoa, & kale salad
note: Cook time: ~25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup lemon juice (roughly the juice of 2 small lemons)
ingredients.name: lemon juice (roughly the juice of 2 small lemons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard (omit if you hate mustard)
ingredients.name: heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard (omit if you hate mustard)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup uncooked quinoa (but I suggest doubling it and freezing a ziplock bag full for your future self — see notes)
ingredients.name: uncooked quinoa (but I suggest doubling it and freezing a ziplock bag full for your future self — see notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups water (I also add a heaping teaspoon of any flavor of Better Than Bouillon but that’s optional — also, if you double the quinoa, you’ll need to double this too!)
ingredients.name: water (I also add a heaping teaspoon of any flavor of Better Than Bouillon but that’s optional — also, if you double the quinoa, you’ll need to double this too!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup golden raisins or dried cranberries
ingredients.name: golden raisins or dried cranberries

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup roasted and salted almonds, pepitas, or pistachios, chopped
ingredients.name: roasted and salted almonds, pepitas, or pistachios

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 1 cup of any fresh chopped soft green herbs you might have available (such as basil, parsley, or cilantro — I love parsley here and it has wonderful anti-inflammatory properties); additional lemon for cutting into wedges for serving
ingredients.name: Optional: 1 cup of any fresh chopped soft green herbs you might have available (such as basil, parsley, or cilantro — I love parsley here and it has wonderful anti-inflammatory properties); additional lemon for cutting into wedges for serving

preparationSteps: To make the lemon vinaigrette, add all ingredients ( 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 cup lemon juice, 1 heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme or oregano, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of black pepper ) to a large jar and shake vigorously until combined. Adjust seasoning to taste. (As always, that is the most important part of making a dressing — my perfect dressing is not the same as yours! Add more vinegar to make it more acidic, more honey to make it sweeter, more oil to make it thicker and less acidic, more salt to make the flavors pop, etc.) Dressing will keep in the fridge for up to 10 days.

To make the quinoa, add 1 cup uncooked quinoa and 1 1/2 cups water (or any kind of stock) to a small pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 13 to 15 minutes, until all of the liquid has been absorbed. Remove from heat but keep the lid on for an additional 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. You’ll use 2 cups of COOKED quinoa in this recipe and have about a cup left over. Let the leftovers cool completely then store them in an airtight container in the fridge for later use this week (see notes for ideas).

Add 16 ounces chopped kale to a large bowl and season with a big pinch of salt and pepper . Use your hands to massage the kale until it JUST starts to feel damp — so squeeze it between your fists about 10 times. If you come across any pieces of thick stem while you’re massaging, discard them.

Now let’s tackle that rotisserie chicken. Pull the thighs/legs and wings off, store them in the refrigerator in an airtight container, and use them for another meal within 4 days. Pull the breast meat off (I discard the skin but you can shred it in with the meat if you’d like!), shred it finely, and add the meat right on top of the kale. Add 2 cups cooked quinoa, 1 bag shredded carrots, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 cup golden raisins, and your desired amount of dressing. (If I’m cooking this salad for dinner/to serve immediately, I use almost all of the dressing, about 1/3 cup! If I’m meal prepping it for lunches, I go lighter with the dressing initially then add a little more to each serving when I’m ready to eat it.)

Toss to combine. Add more dressing as needed until your greens are coated to your liking. Divide the salad between four to six bowls, and garnish with more Parm and a sprinkle of chopped nuts. I love lemon so much that I serve each serving of salad with a lemon wedge for squeezing over top!
(PS, I add the nuts at the end so that they don’t go into the big salad and get soggy in the fridge, but this is personal preference!)

name: market plate
note: Cook time: 1 hour

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large lemon, preferably organic, zested then halved
ingredients.name: large lemon, preferably organic, zested then halved

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

On top of the parchment paper, put down a double layer of paper towels or (what I use) a clean thick dish cloth. Drain and rinse 1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas and put the chickpeas on the cloth. Use another cloth to pat the chickpeas dry them remove the cloths, shaking the dried chickpeas onto the dry parchment paper. Many chickpea skins will fall off — that’s fine, leave them on the parchment!

I have a very specific way that I like to cut cauliflower . First, trim off the leaves and the very bottom of the cauliflower stem. Now slice it in half, through the stem. Place the two halves cut-side down on a cutting board, then slice them into 1/2-inch thick pieces. Cut or pull apart the individual florets.

Add the cauliflower florets to the sheet pan along with 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, several grinds of pepper, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, the zest of 1 lemon, and the juice of 1/2 that lemon. Get in there with your hands to make sure that everything — the Dijon, especially! — gets evenly distributed.

Roast for 30 minutes. Stir. Roast for 15 to 25 more minutes, until really, really golden and tender. The chickpeas should be very crunchy, and no hard cauliflower here! We want the cauliflower almost squishy — it should taste sweet and caramelized and like the best thing you’ve ever eaten, none of that sulfuric raw cauliflower taste.
While the veggies are roasting, finely chop 0.5 ounce of dill.
Squeeze the juice from the remaining 1/2 lemon over top, add the dill, give it all a stir, and enjoy!

name: chipotle cheddar chimichanga tacos, 2021
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes (or 30 minutes, if you use store-bought Caesar dressing instead!)

• Save time: Swap in store-bought Caesar dressing!

• Vegetarian: Add some roasted cauliflower and chickpeas to your Caesar salad instead. You can swap out the anchovies for capers but you may need to add extra mayo to thicken things up.

• Leftover makeover: If you have leftover schnitzel, make chicken Parm the next day! Place the schnitzel on a baking sheet, smother it with marinara and mozzarella, and bake at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes.

• Gluten-free: Use GF panko and 1:1 gluten-free baking flour or almond flour.

• Dairy-free: Omit the Parm.

• Chicken breasts: You could use chicken tenders instead — no need to slice them in half.

• All-purpose flour: Almond flour, 1:1 baking flour, whole-wheat flour…

• Panko bread crumbs: Panko will yield the crispiest chicken but any breadcrumbs will do!

• Parmesan cheese : Pecorino romano, vegan Parm, or a sprinkle of nutritional yeast

• Avocado oil: Vegetable oil, canola oil, or another neutral cooking oil

• Romaine : I love a kale Caesar! Or use another crunchy lettuce like green leaf.

• Honey crisp apple: Another type of apple, pear, fuyu persimmon

• Mayo : Greek yogurt, plain yogurt, vegan mayo

• Anchovy paste: 3-6 anchovies, 1-2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, or 1-2 tablespoons capers (you may need to add extra mayo to thicken things up if using capers)

• Garlic clove : 1/8 teaspoon garlic powder or a thawed cube of crushed garlic

• Lemon : No sub for zest, but you could use 2 tablespoons of a light-colored vinegar in place of the juice.

• Dijon : Whole-grain mustard or omit

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 chicken breasts, sliced carefully in half horizontally

preparationSteps: Cut 2 chicken breasts in half as slowly and carefully as you need to to try to get two perfectly even halves. Place each half between two pieces of parchment paper and use a rolling pin or heavy bottle to flatten each to about 1/4 inch. Don’t pound too hard and break them!
Set out 3 shallow bowls.

In the first bowl, make the Caesar dressing! Combine a heaping 1/2 cup mayo, 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 to 2 tablespoons of anchovy paste (depending on how anchovy-y ya like it!), 1 grated garlic clove, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, a big pinch of kosher salt, and several grinds of pepper . Taste. I like to add a lot more lemon juice, personally, but I know many like a richer Caesar dressing, so do your thing! Add additional salt, lemon, anchovy paste, etc. until it’s your perfect Caesar dressing.
Transfer half of the dressing to a large mixing bowl to use later (we’ll use what’s left in that shallow bowl as a dredge for the chicken!).

Now back to the chicken. Place 1/2 cup all-purpose flour in the second shallow bowl, and place 1 1/2 cups panko and 1/4 cup grated Parm in the third bowl. Season both with kosher salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Dredge each piece of chicken through the flour until fully coated, then through the Caesar dressing that’s still in the shallow bowl until fully coated (it will want to REALLY stick on there — we only need a light coating so use your hands to wipe off any excess), and finally through the panko mixture. If you run out of panko or Caesar dressing while breading the chicken, just add more to the bowl.

To fry it: Heat 1/2 cup avocado oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. When you add a piece of panko and it sizzles, you’re ready to cook. Cook one piece of chicken at a time for 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until golden brown. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with salt. Don’t skip the paper towel step!

To bake it : Preheat the oven to 425°F. Place the chicken on a foil-lined baking sheet in an even layer and spray with cooking spray on both sides. Bake for 6 minutes, then flip and cook for an additional 6 minutes. Check that the chicken is 165°F internally.
Thinly slice 2 large heads of romaine and cut 1 medium honey crisp apple (cold from the fridge, ideally!) into matchsticks. Toss with the reserved dressing in the mixing bowl.

Place one schnitzel on a plate and cover with salad. Use a microplane or box grater to grate fresh Parm all over the top. Add a few grinds of pepper. Repeat with remaining plates. Done! ENJOY IMMEDIATELY!

name: 30-minute broccoli shrimp alfredo-ish
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes total, 10 minutes active

• Do I use one or two Boursin?! I cant decide! It’s so good both ways. I had my testers try it first with one, and then with two, and we simply couldn’t pick which one was better which is why we are giving you the option. Using one package gives you a light sauce, two gives you a more rich sauce. Both are delightful. I recommend buying 2 packages and starting with one, seeing if you like it as is, but if you want a creamier sauce, add the second.

• Woops, I know you told me not to, but I accidentally drained all the pasta water: It happens! Starchy pasta water serves as a thickening agent to make our sauce creamy. To replace it, make a slurry: Mix 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch or flour with 2 cups of water and microwave the mixture for 1 to 2 minutes until hot.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be good in the fridge for up to 4 days. Add water (it’s OK if it’s not pasta cooking water) or some broth or stock to loosen things back up when you’re reheating.

• Vegetarian: See the "mushroom Alfredo” riff above the recipe.

• Dairy-free/gluten-free: Boursin makes a dairy-free version! So use that and a plant-based butter. You can use any gluten-free noodle sub here.

• Can I use fresh noodles for this? YES! If you have fresh noodles, yum, go for it. Since they’ll only need a few minutes of cook time, you’ll likely add the broccoli first, then the noodles, then the shrimp.

• I’m feeling extra: Make the garlicky crunchies from this recipe to go on top. 10/10 recommend this to level this pasta up.

• What’s a “four-finger pinch?” Read the note all about it here .

• Shrimp : Chicken or mushroom Alfredo would be excellent. See the “riffs” section above the recipe for how-tos. If you have a pork tenderloin needing to be cooked, you could cube that and follow the instructions for the chicken Alfredo.

• Pasta : Any pasta or pasta alternative (gluten-free noodles, black bean noodles, etc.) works.

• Broccoli : Yes, you can use frozen broccoli, but ideally you’d thaw it first so it doesn’t bring down the boiling temp of the water and mess up our timing. Frozen green peas would be delish and cooked the same way/for the same amount of time as the shrimp. There are many other veggie sub options! Chopped asparagus, sliced mushrooms, half-mooned zucchini or squash, halved cherry tomatoes… For those, follow the cooking instructions for the asparagus in the “creamy sausage and asparagus pasta” riff above the recipe. You just need to sauté the veg in butter for a few minutes until softened after you’ve drained the noodles! You could also stir in chopped or torn-apart spinach leaves when you’re adding the Boursin, etc. to the pot.

• Boursin (any kind, but I like Herbs and Garlic): 5 to 10 ounces of any other creamy cheese you like. Feta, goat cheese, even cream cheese will do the trick. But if you don’t use the garlic and herbs cheese, you’ll need to add a teaspoon of oregano or dried thyme or Italian seasoning.

• Unsalted butter: Any butter alternative or ghee

• Lemon juice: If you’re in a pinch, you could swap the lemon juice for a light-colored vinegar like champagne vinegar.
