ingredients.name: Optional garnish: red pepper flakes, grated Parm, finely chopped basil or parsley

preparationSteps: This recipe is absurdly easy, the most important thing is timing. So grab your iPhone or whatever you use to set timers in the kitchen (I probably say “Alexa: set a timer for X minutes” 20 times a day) and get ready to drop things into boiling water when your timers go off.
Bring a large pot of heavily salted (two big four-finger pinches!) water to a boil over high heat.
While the water is coming to a boil, season 1 pound peeled and deveined shrimp with a big pinch of kosher salt and several grinds of pepper. If you’re feeling lazy, you can skip this step.
Drop 1 pound pasta in the boiling water and set three timers:
for the amount of cook time it says on the package of noodles
for the amount of cook time that it says on the package minus 4 minutes (this is when you’ll add the broccoli)
for the amount of cook time that it says on the package minus 1 minute (this is when you’ll add the shrimp)
I cooked spaghetti, which takes 11 minutes to cook, so I set a timer for 11 minutes, 7 minutes, and 10 minutes.
Stir the noodles occasionally to keep them from clumping.
When the first timer goes off (aka there are 4 minutes left of cook time for the noodles), add the broccoli florets and stir (with tongs, because you’ll need tongs soon) so they all submerge.

When the second timer goes off (aka there is 1 minute left of cook time), SCOOP TWO CUPS OF PASTA COOKING WATER OUT OF THE POT (!!! this is important!), then add the shrimp. Stir gently to separate and submerge the shrimp.

When the third and final timer goes off, drain the pasta, shrimp, and broccoli in a colander and return the pot to the stove, off heat. To the pot, add 3/4 cup reserved pasta cooking water and the drained noodles, shrimp, and broccoli. It’s OK if the shrimp doesn’t look totally cooked through yet, it’ll continue cooking!

To the pot add 1 package (or 2!) of Boursin (use your hands to crumble it into smaller pieces as you add it to the pot), 4 tablespoons unsalted butter (before you add it, cut it into 4 pieces), 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, and 2 tablespoons lemon juice. (If you’re using 2 packs of Boursin, add another 1/4 to 1/2 cup pasta cooking water).
Using tongs, toss, toss, toss until everything has melted together into a creamy sauce. The broccoli will break apart — that’s a good thing, those little broccoli bits are forming the sauce, too!

Too thick? Add more pasta water — that’s why we scooped 2 cups! Too watery at the bottom of the pot? Keep tossing. If your cheese isn’t melting easily or you want to warm everything up more, turn the heat on to low as you stir.

Taste. Add more kosher salt, lemon juice, and black pepper a little at a time until it's absolutely delicious. If you have them, garnish with finely chopped fresh herbs, red pepper flakes, and/or Parm.

Note: As the pasta sits, the sauce will continue to thicken. So when you go back for seconds, if it’s too thick/stiff, toss in a bit more of that pasta water! That’s what it’s there for! I used all 2 cups.

name: moroccan-spiced pork tenderloin and carrots
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes

• Leftovers are a good thing: Dip: Your whipped pistachio feta will last in the fridge for 5 or so days (eat it with veggies, crackers, as a spread on a sandwich, with grilled chicken the next night, whatever!!!). Pork: Thinly slice leftovers and use for sandwiches! Or finely chop, reheat in a hot skillet with a little oil, and make tacos with the leftover dip, chili crisp, and some pickled red onions. Pita fries: Snack on them!! Toast them up in the oven if they get stale.

• I can only find a 5/6/7 ounce block of feta! That’s fine, carry on with the recipe as written. Will still be delish. Add more salt if needed since you’re missing a little salty feta.

• I don’t own a food processor and my blender isn’t very good: If you’re worried your blender can’t handle pistachios, soak them for an hour before you blend them with the other ingredients.

• Prep ahead: You can make the whipped feta days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. You can also prep the pork and carrots on the sheet pan in the morning, wrap the sheet pan tightly with plastic, and keep it in the fridge until it’s time to cook dinner! The pita fries can also be cooked days ahead of time — let them cool completely then store at room temp in an airtight bag.

• Vegetarian : Roast 2 cans of chickpeas (or any white bean) along with your carrots. Drain, rinse, and pat them dry then mix them on the sheet pan with the carrots, oil, and seasonings as written. They’ll be delish!

• Halve it: The pork and carrots and the pita fries are both easy to halve if you are cooking for 1 or 2 and don’t want leftovers. I’d go ahead and make the whole batch of whipped feta though so you aren’t left with half a block of cheese — it’d also be harder for your blender/food processor to mix. See the “leftovers are a good thing” note for what to do with your extra dip.

• Gimme some greens: You’ll find instructions for a simple arugula salad in the recipe! I just want to note that if you love lemon and are also making the salad, pick up a second lemon at the store — you might want to add more juice to the whipped feta and/or the arugula salad and I don’t want you to run out!

• I don’t wanna measure all those spices: You could buy Ras El Hanout , a Moroccan spice blend that contains these spices and others! Or skip the Moroccan vibes and use a great everyday spice blend that you love. You’d use a heaping tablespoon of it for your pork and carrots. Or, just do like I do when I’m not developing a recipe, and don’t measure anything — eyeball it!

• Feeding kids: My kids loved the dip and pita chips (I called it green hummus). My pickiest eaters didn’t go for the meat and carrots — my least picky did! You could keep the spices off of one of the tenderloins and just season it with salt and pepper if you’re worried about the spices throwing your kids off!

• Dairy-free: VioLife DF feta is SO GOOD if you can find it. Use that and a DF plain yogurt to make something very similar to the original sauce. Another option would be to trade the pistachio feta for a dairy-free tzatziki or a store-bought hummus like Little Sesame or Ithaca. Any of these will add a delicious saucy element!

• Nut/seed-free : Omit the pistachios — the whipped feta will still be delicious without it. Or, use pepitas or sunflower seeds instead. I like the idea of pepitas here.

• Gluten-free : Buy gluten-free pita.

• Carrots : 2 medium onions (sliced 1/4-inch thick), cubed sweet potato, cauliflower florets (sliced 1/4-inch thick), zucchini cut into quarters lengthwise and half widthwise

• Pork tenderloins: Chicken! Use your meat thermometer — chicken is ready when it’s 165°F internally. Here are different cuts you could use: 4 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, but you’ll need to roast them for 30 to 35 minutes (you can skip the broiling step) 2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, but cook it for 25 minutes 2 pounds bone-in chicken breasts, cooked for 25 to 30 minutes 2 pounds boneless chicken breasts, cooked for 15 to 20 minutes You could also sub the pork for a rack of lamb. For lamb: Cook for 15 minutes on one side, flip and cook for 10 more minutes, until 145°F internally.

• EVOO : Olive oil or another neutral tasting oil

• Honey : Maple syrup or brown sugar

• Smoked paprika: Try to find smoked paprika if possible! It has a smoky flavor profile — that isn’t spicy — and is delicious and hard to replicate. BUT you can definitely swap it for sweet paprika, if it’s all you have. You could also sub in chipotle powder if you like heat… but I’d suggest only using 1/2 teaspoon unless you like it super spicy.

• Cumin : Garam masala, ground coriander, curry powder, or chili powder

• Turmeric : Extra ginger, curry powder, or omit

• Ground ginger : If you have some fresh ginger lingering in your fridge, you could grate 1/2 tablespoon of it onto the sheet pan along with the other ingredients. Or sub it with 1/4 teaspoon of garam masala, turmeric, or saffron. Or omit!

• Ground cinnamon: Nutmeg, garam masala, all spice, or omit

• Arugula: Again, this is optional! But if you want a green that isn’t arugula, I’d use spinach or lacinato kale (that you’ve sliced thin and massaged/squeezed in your hands a few times).

• Pita : Naan bread. You could also skip the pita fries and buy some pita chips and crunch them up over your plates instead, or just toast a some big slices of pita or naan to scoop your whipped feta up with.

• Dried dill: Dried basil, dried tarragon, dried parsley, dried oregano

• Flaky sea salt: Kosher salt is fine if it’s all you have! Or any coarse or flaky finishing salt

• Garlic powder: Onion powder or 2 minced garlic cloves, but it won’t spread quite so evenly across the sliced pita.

• Lemon zest : Omit if needed

• Feta : VioLife has a great DF feta if you’re dairy-free. You could do a log of goat cheese instead if you love it. Or swap the whipped feta for a great hummus or tzatziki sauce instead!

• Toasted pistachios : I think cashews would be great instead. Or pepitas. Or just skip it and do whipped feta.

• Cilantro : Dill, mint, and/or basil

• Yogurt : Absolutely any plain yogurt (Greek, regular, any fat content, a DF version), sour cream, or labneh

• 2 garlic cloves: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder

• Lemon zest and juice: Swap it for lime zest and juice. Or omit the zest and use 2 tablespoons of a light-colored vinegar like apple cider or white wine vinegar in place of the juice.

ingredients.name: packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, throw some of that in there too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup toasted pistachios (shelled — AKA, without the shells)
ingredients.name: toasted pistachios (shelled — AKA, without the shells)

preparationSteps: Position one oven rack in the center of the oven and one above it. Preheat oven to 400°F.

Remove the stems from 2 bunches of small carrots then cut them in half lengthwise. If you’re using big standard grocery store carrots, you’ll need to cut them in half (or into quarters if they’re really fat!) lengthwise and in half widthwise. Your goal is for them all to be about even size. Place the carrots on your largest rimmed sheet pan. Add 2 pork tenderloins, 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric, 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Use your hands to toss to coat everything evenly in oil and spices.
Roast on the center rack for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pork tenderloin reaches an internal temperature of 130°F.

Right after you put the pork and carrots in the oven, prep your pita fries: Cut 3 or 4 pita in half, then into 1/2-inch thick strips. Toss on a second sheet pan with 3 or 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon dried dill, 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and the zest of 1/2 lemon. Add the sheet pan to the oven so the pita fries can bake with the pork and carrots for 10 to 15 minutes, until golden brown and toasted on the outside, but still chewy and soft on the inside. Ideally you’ll position the sheet pans side by side on the center rack. If they can’t fit, put the pita on the rack above the pork and carrots.

Once the pork has reached 130°F (and you’ve removed the pita fries from the oven), switch the oven to Broil on High and broil the pork and carrots (still on the center rack) for 3 to 5 minutes, until everything gets nice and browned and the pork reaches 140°F.

Transfer the pork to a cutting board to rest (the internal temp will continue rising to 145°F as it sits). If your carrots are not fork tender at this point (fork tender means you can easily cut through them with a fork), continue broiling them on the center rack of the oven for a few more minutes (this ensures that they’re not too close to the heat — we want them to brown but not burn). Keep a close eye on them — they can go from being nicely browned to burnt quickly!
While the pork and pita are roasting…

Make the whipped pistachio feta: In a food processor (ideal) or a blender, blend 1 block of feta cheese (I cut it into quarters before I add it), 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (and a little dill, mint, or basil if you have it) , 3/4 cup toasted pistachios, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup plain yogurt, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and the juice of 1/2 lemon together until chunky smooth. If you’re using a blender, you can use the tamp (if yours has one!) or a spoon to push and scrape the feta down as needed. Taste. I needed to add about 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt at this point, but this will totally depend on how salty your feta and pistachios are. I love lemon flavor, so I also wound up adding the juice from the other half of the lemon.

If you want some greens (I did, and it was excellent): Toss 5 ounces baby arugula, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1/2 lemon, lots of shaved Parm, chopped pistachios, and a big pinch of salt and pepper in a serving bowl. Thinly sliced radishes, apple, or snap peas would also be excellent here if you have some!
Slice your pork 1/4-inch thick and serve it with lots of whipped pistachio feta, carrots, salad (if you made one), and pita fries!!

preparationSteps: Position the top oven rack about 6 inches under the broiler. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

In a small baking dish, combine 1/2 cup pitted or whole Castelvetrano olives, 1/2 cup pitted or whole Kalamata olives, 5 fresh oregano sprigs , 1 1/2 tablespoons fennel seeds, the zest of 1/2 orange, and 1 sliced fresh cayenne chili. Nestle 1 pound Greek feta (that you have first drained and patted dry with a paper towel) in the middle and drizzle everything with 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil .
Bake until the feta and olives have softened, about 20 minutes. Set the oven to broil and broil for 3 to 5 minutes, until golden on top.
Drizzle with 2 tablespoons honey and sprinkle with flaky sea salt . Serve with good crusty bread.

name: tropical shrimp (or chicken, salmon, or steak!!) bowls
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes

• How do I rinse rice? Two options: 1) Put it in a fine-mesh strainer and run it under cold water, moving the rice around with your fingers, until the water runs clear, or 2) put it in your pot, add some water, and swirl it around in the water. Drain the water and repeat until the water runs clear.

• OK but what should I make for brunch? If your significant other wants brunch, make this Starbucks copycat frittata the night before and bake it in the morning while you let her sleep in. You can skip the sweet potato hash if it sounds hard. Maybe buy frozen hash browns and just crisp that up. Make a nice, simple salad to go with it by adding arugula, lots of shaved Parm, toasted pine nuts, lemon juice, extra-virgin olive oil, a big pinch of salt, and a little pepper to a serving bowl and tossing. Taste it. Is it delicious? If not, it probably needs more salt. Cut up some strawberries to add to your plates. Dig in.

• Prep ahead: The rice can be made up to 5 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, adding a splash of water to help loosen it. You can make the sauce up to 3 days ahead of time and store it in an airtight container in the fridge. If it thickens up in the fridge, add some more oil, or even a little water, to loosen it up. But again, DON’T marinate the shrimp for more than 30 minutes! It’ll start to “cook” like ceviche. The slaw can be made up to 3 days ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge. You want to make the pineapple-avocado salsa right before serving if possible, but if you need to make it ahead, wait to add the avocado until the last minute and press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning. If your shrimp are finished cooking but you’re still working on other components of the meal, tent the plate they’re on with foil!

• Love your leftovers: If you have leftovers, store each component separately. The shrimp will keep for 3 days, rice for 5 days (or freeze it!), but the salsa is best eaten within 24 hours before the avocado starts to brown. The sauce will keep for about 5 days and is excellent drizzled over eggs, roasted vegetables, or grilled chicken.

• Got any shortcuts? Yes! Go read the “take shortcuts where you need them” note above the recipe.

• I’m feeding spice wimps: Omit the jalapeño!

• I don’t like shrimp: This marinade (and whole recipe) would be delicious with any protein you love. Here’s how to swap in chicken, steak, or salmon: For chicken breasts or thighs: Marinate them in the green sauce for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours in the fridge. Grill over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes per side (or until 165°F internally). If cooking in a skillet, I’d cut the chicken into cubes before marinating, then sear them in olive oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until cooked through. For steak (skirt, flank, or sirloin would all be great here): Marinate them for up to 4 hours in the fridge. Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side or until desired internal temp (125-130°F for medium-rare; 135-140°F for medium; or above for well done). For salmon: Marinate the fish for up to 30 minutes. To grill it, oil the grates and grill skin-side down over medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes for the first side, then 2 to 4 minutes on the second side, or until it reaches 120 to 130°F internally and flakes easily with a fork. Or you could bake it at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Or cook it in oil in a skillet over medium-high until cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway through. Or…

• Vegetarian : Tofu would be so good with this meal. Press a block of extra firm tofu to remove excess water. You can either slice it lengthwise into big flat planks (best for grilling) or cube it. Marinate it for 30 minutes, then either grill it, pan sear it (AKA, cook it in a skillet until golden), or bake it at 400°F for 20 minutes, or until it starts to crisp up (flipping once halfway through).

• Gluten-free/dairy-free: It’s already gluten-free. To avoid dairy, use a plant-based butter or extra olive oil if cooking the shrimp in a skillet.

• Limes : Lemons! Or swap the lime juice out for a clear vinegar like rice or white wine vinegar.

• Freshly squeezed orange juice : You could use 1/4 cup store-bought OJ, pineapple juice, or mango juice.

• Olive oil: EVOO, avocado oil, or any other neutral oil (grapeseed, canola oil, etc.)

• Honey : Maple syrup or agave nectar

• Cilantro : Basil

• Scallions : Chives, shallot

• Garlic cloves: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder or 2 thawed cubes of crushed garlic

• Jalapeño : Fresno chili (equal spice level) or serrano pepper (this would be spicier! maybe use half), or just omit

• Cumin : Ground coriander or smoked paprika — paprika would give it a different but delish flavor

• Kosher salt: You can use sea salt, but use less of it throughout the recipe because it tastes saltier!

• Black pepper : White pepper or omit if needed

• Shrimp : You can use frozen peeled and deveined shrimp. Thaw it before you add it to the marinade! See the “I don’t like shrimp” note above for other subs.

• Unsalted butter: Salted butter, if it’s what you have, coconut oil, ghee, or an extra tablespoon of olive oil

• Short-grain white rice: Any white rice — jasmine, basmati, sushi — will do! You can use brown rice if you’d rather, but you’ll need to increase the water and cook time (see package instructions for details).

• Coconut milk: Coconut cream will also work, or omit and cook 1 1/2 cups of rice with 2 cups of water, if you aren’t into coconut.

• Pineapple : Mango or strawberry

• Avocado : Store-bought guacamole, diced cucumber, or omit

• Red bell pepper: A yellow or orange bell pepper or omit — it’s optional

• Bag of shredded cabbage: You could thinly slice your own head of cabbage — you’ll only need half a head for this. Or sub it for thinly sliced Brussels sprouts (Trader Joe’s sells ‘em), shredded kale, or a cucumber cut into batons. You could also omit the slaw element completely.

ingredients.name: shredded cabbage (purple or green cabbage or “coleslaw mix” all work)

preparationSteps: You can either grill your shrimp or cook it indoors in a skillet! If you plan to grill, be sure to buy wooden skewers (if you don’t own metal ones). Start soaking them in water right away when you begin cooking! Place them on a baking sheet or in any shallow baking pan that’ll fit them when laying flat, and cover with water. This will keep them from catching on fire :)

First things first, let's make the citrus-cilantro green sauce that will pull this whole dish together. FYI, you’re going to use this sauce 4 different ways: 1) Half of it will be your shrimp marinade. 2) You’ll use a few spoonfuls to flavor the salsa. 3) It is the dressing for your slaw. 4) Any leftover sauce gets drizzled on top of the bowls as a sauce!

In your blender or food processor, combine the juice of 2 large limes , the juice from 1 orange , 1/4 cup olive oil , 3 tablespoons honey , 1 cup cilantro leaves and stems, 1 scallion (roots trimmed off and discarded first), 2 small peeled garlic cloves, 1 halved and seeded jalapeño (to do this: cut off the stem, then cut it in half lengthwise, then scoop out and discard all of the seeds), 1 teaspoon ground cumin , 1 teaspoon kosher salt , and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper . Blend until smooth and vibrant green. This sauce should be loose enough to pour but thick enough to cling to the back of a spoon. If it's too thick, add another tablespoon of olive oil and blend again.

Pour half of this green sauce into a serving bowl and set it aside for later. Pour the other half into a shallow dish (or Ziploc) along with 1 1/2 pounds large peeled and deveined shrimp . Toss to coat every shrimp thoroughly, then refrigerate for up to 30 minutes. Don't marinate longer than this — the citrus will start "cooking" the shrimp like ceviche!
While the shrimp is marinating, make the rice, salsa, and slaw.
If you’re grilling, now is a good time to preheat your grill! We’re going to be cooking over medium-high heat.

For the rice: Combine 1 1/2 cups rinsed short-grain white rice, 1 can coconut milk, 1 1/4 cups water, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in a small pot and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to the lowest heat possible, COVER, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until all liquid is absorbed. Turn off the heat, keep the lid on, and let it steam for at least another 5 minutes. Just before serving, fluff it with a fork (AKA gently scrape the rice with a fork to un-clump it).

Next up, let’s make the salsa: Chop 2 cups fresh pineapple into small (about 1/4 inch, so about the size of your pinky finger’s nail) pieces and add them to a medium-sized bowl. If you're using a whole pineapple, here’s what to do: cut off the top and bottom, stand it upright, slice off the skin in strips, then quarter it lengthwise, remove the core, and dice. Here’s a visual. Or just buy it pre-cut, and dice up the big chunks! Chop 1 ripe avocado and 1 red bell pepper into roughly 1/4-inch pieces. Remove and discard the root ends of 2 scallions then thinly slice them (the whole scallion, both white and green parts!). Add all the chopped vegetables to the bowl along with 2 tablespoons of the green sauce you set aside and a big pinch of kosher salt . Stir gently — we want the avocado to hold its shape, not turn into guacamole. Taste. If it’s not absolutely delicious, add more sauce and a tiny bit more kosher salt.

Finally, make the slaw! Simply dump the bag of shredded cabbage into a cute bowl, add a pinch of kosher salt , and squeeze the cabbage 5 times with your hands. Pour in 2 to 3 tablespoons of the green sauce and toss to coat. Taste. Add more kosher salt and/or green sauce until it’s delicious.
Time to cook the shrimp!

If you’re grilling: Thread the marinated shrimp onto skewers — don't pack them too tightly; they need a little breathing room. Heat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the skewers for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and have some nice grill marks.

If you’re cooking in a skillet: Warm your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and heat until shimmering. Tilt the pan around to coat it in oil. Shake off as much marinade from the shrimp as possible, then add them to the skillet in an even layer. Cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side , until golden-brown all over. Add 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and toss to coat the shrimp in melted butter. Transfer shrimp to a serving platter.

Serve! This is a great meal to serve family style — just set the shrimp, rice, salsa, and slaw out and let everyone build their own bowls. Or, make everyone’s bowls for them by dividing the coconut rice among bowls, topping with shrimp (you can leave them on the skewers for presentation or slide them off — your call), and adding a generous scoop of both pineapple-avocado salsa and slaw. Drizzle everything with the reserved green sauce. Garnish with extra cilantro and lime wedges if you're feeling fancy. Dig in!

name: the ultimate potluck guide

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) block cream cheese, at room temperature
ingredients.name: cream cheese, at room temperature

preparationSteps: Two hours before you start, pull 1 (8-ounce) block cream cheese out of the fridge to soften.

Make the cake: Preheat the oven to 350°F and set a rack in the center. Lay a large piece of parchment over the base of a 9-inch (or 8-inch) springform pan, then set the springform ring on the base and snap it into place. I like the rustic look of the flowing parchment in the final presentation, but you can trim it to the edge of the pan if you want. Coat the pan and parchment with nonstick spray. (If you're using a pie plate, coat the plate with spray and skip the parchment.)

In a large bowl, whisk 1/2 cup (1 stick) melted unsalted butter and 1 cup (200 grams) sugar until it pulls together. Zest 1 large lemon directly into the bowl, add 1 large egg , and whisk again. One more whisk for the 2 teaspoons cream of tartar , 1 teaspoon baking powder , and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt , then switch to a rubber spatula and fold in 1 1⁄4 cups (175 grams) all-purpose flour . Scrape the dough into the prepared cake pan and press into an even layer.

Make the filling: In the same bowl, zest 1 large lemon . Add 1 teaspoon kosher salt and use your fingers to pinch and rub until the mixture is super fragrant. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze the juice right in. Whisk in 1 large egg, 2 teaspoons cream of tartar , and the softened cream cheese until completely smooth. Scoop out 3 tablespoons of the powdered sugar into a small bowl and set it aside for dusting the cake. Pour the rest of the powdered sugar into the filling bowl and whisk to combine.

Scrape the filling into the center of the cake pan. Wiggle the pan once or twice to help it spread toward the edges. Slide the cake into the oven and set a timer for 40 minutes. (If you’re using an 8-inch pan, set the timer for 45 minutes.) The edge of the cake will be nicely golden brown and the center will be bubbly and lightly browned all over. Add 5 more minutes to the timer if it needs it. Cool for 15 minutes, then run a butter knife around the perimeter of the pan to make sure the edges don’t stick. Keep cooling the cake in the pan for another 45 minutes, then cover the top of the pan with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight. Let the cake sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour before serving.

To serve, unlatch and remove the spring from. I like to serve the cake right on the base with a skirt of parchment, but you can run an offset spatula under the cake to release and transfer to a platter. (Or slice and serve directly from the pie plate.) Either way, dust the cake with the reserved powdered sugar before serving.

preparationSteps: We’re going to make the sauce (which will double as our marinade) first: To a large bowl, add 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup fish sauce, 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce, 1/4 cup chopped mint, 3 tablespoons neutral oil, 2 tablespoons sesame oil, 2 tablespoons lime juice or rice vinegar, and 2 teaspoons sambal oelek . Use a microplane or the smallest hole of a box grater to grate in 3 garlic cloves (or mince them), then whisk it all together until the sugar completely dissolves.
PAY ATTENTION! Take 1/2 cup of this marinade and put it in a small tupperware container or jar. Cover and stick it in the fridge — this is the sauce for your bowls!

If you only have 30 minutes to marinate your meat, poke it all over with a fork right now! If you have more time to marinate, you can skip this step. Add 2 pork tenderloins or 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts to the remaining marinade in the big bowl. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate it for at least 30 minutes, or up to 12 hours.

I definitely don’t want you to marinate it for longer than 12 hours! Life happens and plans change though, so, if yours do, simply pour off the marinade, keep the meat covered in the fridge, and grill it tomorrow or the next day.

Up to 1 hour before eating, make the cucumber-avocado-ginger salad: Slice 1 English cucumber as thinly as possible. Dice 1 large ripe avocado. Chop 1/3 cup sushi ginger . Add everything to a bowl and toss with 2 tablespoons of the reserved sauce . Refrigerate until ready to eat.
Preheat your grill to medium-high.
Start cooking 1 1/2 cups rice or quinoa per package directions (or microwave it, if you’re using frozen microwaveable rice).

Time to grill! Now that your grill is hot, use a grill brush to scrape the grates clean. Grab a couple paper towels (or a rag) and wad them up into a ball. Soak them with several tablespoons of oil — any kind, you can use the cheapest oil you have. You want it to be soaked but not dripping. Now, grab the ball of oily paper towels with a long pair of tongs and use it to grease the grates. This helps prevent sticking!

Pull the meat out of the marinade and discard the used marinade. Grill the pork tenderloin for 6 to 8 minutes per side, acting like there are 3 sides of a tenderloin. You’re looking for an internal temp of 145°F. Grill the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes per side if using thighs, or 5 to 7 minutes per side for breasts. You're looking for an internal temp of 165°F. Let the meat rest for 5 minutes, then chop it into bite-sized pieces.

Scoop your cooked rice into bowls and top with chopped meat, cucumber salad, and any optional toppings you’d like. Drizzle generously with the reserved sauce. Garnish with fresh mint leaves and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

preparationSteps: We’re going to start by cooking the corn for the salad. You can either cook your corn on the stovetop or on the grill — your choice!

To cook the corn on the stovetop: Cut the kernels off of 4 ears of corn with a chef’s knife (lay the corn flat on your cutting board to do this). Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet or saucepan that has a lid over medium-high heat, and sauté the corn for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly charred. Transfer the corn to a bowl or plate to cool. To grill the corn: Shuck the corn, brush the cobs with oil (just as much as it takes for them to be lightly coated), and grill on high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side (for a total of 8 to 10 minutes). Let cool, then slice the kernels off the cob.
Let the corn cool while you cook the chicken.
Season 4 (6-ounce) chicken breasts to taste with kosher salt, black pepper , and optionally, any other seasonings you’re feelin’ ! I typically season with salt and lemon pepper.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet or saucepan that has a lid (the same one you just cooked the corn in, if you cooked it inside) over medium-high heat. Add the chicken to the skillet and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown. Flip and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is also golden brown.

After the chicken is seared all over, reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes (set a timer!). Take the lid off and use a meat thermometer to ensure your chicken has reached an internal temp of 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and allow it to rest for 5 minutes.
While the chicken is cooking and resting, we’re going to make the salad.

Make the Lemon Vinaigrette: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 teaspoon honey, a big pinch of kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper. While whisking continuously, slowly drizzle in 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil until emulsified (AKA, all combined and thickened). Taste and add more kosher salt and/or pepper, if needed, until it tastes perfect.

Dice 1/2 a small red onion and add it to the dressing — letting it sit in the dressing will mellow out its sharp bite. Dice 2 English cucumbers, halve 1 pint cherry tomatoes , and very thinly slice 10 ounces snap peas. Finely chop 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, and 2 tablespoons fresh dill . Add it all to the bowl of dressing along with the cooled corn kernels and 8 ounces crumbled feta cheese (this is a solid amount of cheese — start smaller if you wish!).
Toss gently to combine. Let the salad sit for at least 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

Just before serving, dice 1 large avocado , and gently toss it in along with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper . Adding the salt at the last minute is important so that the salad doesn't release too much liquid. Taste. If needed, add more salt and pepper until delicious.
I like to serve this meal two ways (as shown in the pictures above):
On a platter: Slice the chicken on the bias, fan it out, and place it on a platter. Spoon the salad over top, almost like a relish.
As a Summer Chicken Chop : Chop up the chicken and mix it in with the salad.
Choose your adventure and dig in!

Add 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock to a large oven-proof heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven and bring to a boil over high heat. While it's coming to a boil, mince 2 shallots and 4 garlic cloves , and grate 3 medium zucchini .

ingredients.name: finely grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 to 4 thin slices prosciutto (about 2 ounces), torn into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: thin slices prosciutto (about 2 ounces), torn into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts (see notes section if you can only find raw pine nuts)
ingredients.name: toasted pine nuts (see notes section if you can only find raw pine nuts)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Place a 10x12-inch piece of parchment paper on the counter and sprinkle it with all-purpose flour . Unfold 1 thawed puff pastry onto the parchment. Sometimes puff pastry comes in 4 pieces — if yours did, just smoosh the 4 pieces together. Sprinkle the dough with a dusting of flour. Use a rolling pin (or wine bottle!) to roll out the puff pastry to fill the parchment — you should only need to roll a few times, we’re not trying to make it much bigger. Transfer the parchment paper with the dough on top to a baking sheet.

Score (AKA lightly drag a knife over, but don’t cut all the way through) a 1-inch border around the edges of the pastry. This creates a raised edge when baked. You can also score a little design into the border if you’re feeling wild!

Whisk 1 egg in a small bowl and brush over the border for a golden finish (this is called an egg wash). You can skip this if you’re in a hurry, but it will be prettier with the egg wash. If you don’t have a pastry brush, you can use a (very clean) paint brush, a paper towel, or your fingers to do this.

We are going to par-bake the puff pastry (AKA, bake it about halfway through before adding ingredients on top), and while we’re doing that we’ll prep the tart ingredients. Prick the pastry all over with a fork (avoiding the border), then bake for 10 minutes or until just starting to puff but not brown.

While it’s in the oven, in a medium bowl, whisk together 1 cup ricotta, 1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan, 1 egg, 1 tablespoon honey, 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt until combined. Set aside.
Slice 3 to 4 peaches very thinly — about the width of a quarter.

After 10 minutes, remove the puff pastry from the oven. Spread the ricotta mixture evenly within the scored border, leaving the edges clean (it’s fine if the edges aren’t perfect). Arrange the peach slices in slightly overlapping rows over the ricotta base. Drizzle peaches with 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon honey.
Bake for 15 to 20 more minutes until the pastry is golden brown and puffed up around the edges and the peaches are tender.
Remove from oven. Right away, tear 3 to 4 thin prosciutto slices into bite-sized pieces and arrange over the warm tart (the heat will warm and soften the prosciutto).

Let it cool for at least 5 minutes, then scatter a handful of baby arugula, 2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts, and a pinch of flaky sea salt over top. Grate a nice dusting of Parm on there too. Slice and serve!
servings: Serves 6 to 8 as an appetizer, or 4 as a light meal

name: one-pan orecchiette puttanesca
note:
Cook time: 40 minutes

• A note about olives: Yotam’s recipe initially called for 125g of Nocellara olives, pits included. If you buy pre-pitted (it will save you time and effort!) the measurement will be 80g, or 1/2 cup pitted olives. If you are using olives with pits, you’ll still use 1/2 cup — you can remove the pits efficiently by smashing the olives with the side of your knife and then just plucking out the pits.

• I’m making this during winter: Amazing — it’s a perfect cozy winter dish. If you can’t find tasty fresh cherry tomatoes at the store, use a 14.5 ounce can of diced, crushed, chopped, whole plum, or whole cherry tomatoes instead. If using whole plum tomatoes, break them apart using your spatula while cooking. Alternatively, just grab those less-than-ideal cherry tomatoes from the store and add an extra pinch of sugar to sweeten things up.

• Feeding picky eaters: If they are sensitive to spice, you can use smoked paprika instead of “hot” smoked paprika. You could also halve the paprika or omit it entirely if you want to play it safe. If your kids aren’t into olives and capers, you can fish out some of the cooked noodles and plate those alone with some crispy chickpeas and whatever fruit they love.

• Feeding a crowd : Use a large Dutch oven or pot and double it! Increase the cook time of both the chickpeas and pasta by a few minutes.

• Must have meat and greens : This pasta is very filling as is, but if you want extra protein (or if you want to stretch the meal to feed more people — this will nearly double its yield), here’s an idea: In a separate skillet over medium-high heat, brown 1/2 pound ground Italian sausage. Once it has browned, stir in 3 cups finely chopped kale or spinach and continue cooking until wilted, 3 to 5 minutes, adding splashes of stock or water as needed to help wilt the kale. Stir this mixture into the pasta before serving.

• Gimme some greens: If you just want some extra greens, stir a handful or 2 of torn spinach in at the end of cooking your pasta — it will wilt right in.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will keep for up to 4 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat, adding more stock or water as needed to loosen things up.

• Cook this soon: Use up the second half of that orecchiette by making spring pea pasta .

• Vegetarian/dairy-free : Already is!

• Gluten-free: As is typically the case with one-pot pasta recipes, we don’t recommend swapping in GF pasta as written. If you’re using gluten-free pasta, boil it separately per package directions, until al dente. Make the sauce as written, but only add half the amount of stock. Check on it as it simmers — if the sauce needs more liquid, add more stock. If it’s too liquidy at the end of cooking, take the lid off, crank the heat up, and cook stirring constantly until it has absorbed into the sauce. Once the sauce and pasta are both cooked, pour the noodles into the sauce, stir, and dig in! While you’re shopping, also check labels for your capers, olives, and stock as some brands may use a brine or additives that contain gluten.

• Olive oil: Avocado oil, grapeseed oil, sunflower oil, EVOO, or another oil you have. Use the tastiest oil you’ve got — like a nice EVOO — for the garnish.

• Garlic: 6 cubes of frozen crushed garlic or 1 1/2 teaspoons of garlic powder… but fresh is going to taste best in this case.

• Chickpeas : A can of any other white bean like cannellini or navy. Omit if you hate/can’t do beans!

• Hot smoked paprika : Regular smoked paprika, chili powder, or sweet paprika (but if you want some heat, add a shake of cayenne or red pepper flakes with it). If you don’t have any paprika, you could add a teaspoon of garam masala for some extra flavor complexity, or just omit.

• Ground cumin: Ground coriander or garam masala

• Tomato paste: Tomato sauce but double it, or omit

• Parsley : FYI, we recommend Italian/flat-leaf parsley over curly parsley. If you have no parsley, you could use basil or cilantro, or omit the herb.

• Lemon zest: There’s no sub — omit if you need to.

• Capers: Extra olives, or minced cornichons

• Olives : Double the capers

• Cherry tomatoes: A 14.5 ounce can of diced, crushed, chopped, or whole cherry (ideal!) tomatoes. If you can’t do tomatoes, you can leave them out for a totally different yet still tasty pasta.

• Caster sugar : Granulated or brown sugar

• Caraway seeds: Fennel seeds, whole cumin seeds, or coriander seeds (all of these should be toasted — do that yourself while cooking, or buy them toasted from the store). If you really don’t feel like cooking, you can omit the ground seed — though like Ottolenghi said in the intro, it is a lovely touch!

• Orecchiette : Another small-shaped pasta like penne, farfalle, fusilli, or rigatoni. See notes for a GF swap.

• Vegetable or chicken stock: 2 teaspoons vegetable- or chicken-flavored Better Than Bouillon plus 2 cups of water, or chicken or veggie broth

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces (250g) dried orecchiette (AKA, half a bag)
ingredients.name: dried orecchiette (AKA, half a bag)

preparationSteps: Add the first 6 ingredients ( 1/4 cup olive oil, 6 crushed garlic cloves, 1 can of drained and patted-dried chickpeas , 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons ground cumin, and 3/4 tablespoon tomato paste ) along with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a large sauté pan and place over medium-high heat.

Cook for 12 minutes, stirring every now and then, until the chickpeas are slightly crisp — you may need to turn down the heat a little if they start to colour too much. Remove 1/3 of the chickpeas and set aside to use as a garnish.
While your chickpeas are cooking, in a small bowl, combine 2/3 cup roughly chopped fresh parsley, 2 teaspoons lemon zest, 3 tablespoons baby capers, and 1/2 cup roughly chopped pitted green olives .

Also while your chickpeas are frying: If your caraway seeds aren’t already toasted, add 1/2 tablespoon caraway seeds to a small skillet over medium heat and toast for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they turn fragrant and a slightly darker shade. Once toasted, transfer them to a cutting board and use a rolling pin or wine bottle to crush them. (You could also crush them using a mortar and pestle, or in a bowl with the back of a cooking spoon.)

When your chickpeas are done cooking (and you’ve removed some for garnish), add 2/3 of the parsley mixture to the sauté pan along with 1 1/2 cups cherry tomatoes , 2 teaspoons sugar , and the toasted, crushed caraway seeds. Cook for 2 minutes over medium-high heat, stirring often.

Add 8 ounces (half a bag of) orecchiette, 2 cups of stock, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 3/4 cup (200ml) of water to the pan and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium, cover with the lid, and cook for 12 to 14 minutes, or until the pasta is al dente.

If you open the lid at the end of that cook time and there’s no liquid left but your pasta isn’t al dente yet, add a little bit more water, close the lid, and cook for another minute or 2 and check again. Conversely, if you open the lid and you still have liquid left but your pasta is ready, keep the lid off, crank the heat up to high, and stir constantly to quickly cook that liquid off without overcooking the noodles.
Stir in the remaining parsley mixture, drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil , and garnish with the crispy chickpeas and a good grind of black pepper .

name: chopped italian deli wraps
note:
Prep time: 15-20 minutes

• Prep ahead: You can prep the dressing up to 4 days ahead of time. Store it in a jar or airtight container in the fridge. Give it a good shake to recombine it all before you use it. If it solidifies while it’s in the fridge (this is normal! oil will do this if it’s cold enough), just let it come to room temp or, if you’re in a hurry, pop it in the microwave for 5 to 10 seconds, then stir/shake to combine. Don’t prep your wrap filling ahead of time — it would get soggy in the fridge.

• Feeding kids: Skip the pepperoncini, chili flakes, and red onion if you’ve got sensitive palates at the table. If you don’t think your kid will go for a wrap, serve it deconstructed, snack plate style.

• Make it a salad: Simply skip the wrapping step!

• What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip the homemade dressing and use a store-bought Italian dressing you love.

• Love your leftovers: Leftover wraps will stay good in the fridge for up to a day.

• Feeding 1 or 2/feeding a crowd: This recipe can easily be halved or doubled to feed more or less than 4 people. If you’re doubling it, work in batches so your cutting board doesn’t overflow.

• Vegetarian: Omit the meats and add a can or 2 of drained and rinsed chickpeas (or another white bean), chopped artichoke hearts, and/or marinated tofu.

• Dairy-free: Use dairy-free mozzarella or leave the cheese out entirely, it’s still delicious.

• Gluten-free: Use gluten-free tortillas or serve as a chopped salad.

• Nut-free: This is naturally nut-free — no swaps needed.

• Use what’s in your pantry: If you’re low on fresh produce, pull in more jarred ingredients like roasted red peppers, olives, pickled onions, sun-dried tomatoes, etc., instead!

• Iceberg lettuce: Romaine, green leaf, or any crisp lettuce. You could also use shredded kale, but give it a massage (AKA, squeeze it in your fists with a pinch of salt about 7 to 10 times) first to make it less bitter and easier to chew.

• Salami : Pepperoni or soppressata (see “vegetarian” note for more)

• Turkey : Grilled chicken, sliced deli ham, or omit for vegetarian

• Prosciutto : Extra turkey, sliced deli ham, bacon, or skip it

• Mozzarella : Provolone, Cheddar, dairy-free cheese, or omit

• Pepperoncini : Chopped pickles, pickled banana peppers, or pickled red onion

• Cherry tomatoes : Sun-dried tomatoes or omit

• Red onion: Green onion, pickled red onion, or shallot

• Roasted red peppers: Fresh bell pepper, sun-dried tomatoes, or omit

• Fresh parsley or basil: Omit it needed — it’s optional, but it adds freshness.

• Flour tortillas: Any large burrito-size/wrap-size tortilla works — sun-dried tomato, spinach, plain, gluten-free, etc. Or skip it and eat your filling as an Italian chop salad instead.

• Red wine vinegar: Another light-colored vinegar like white wine, apple cider, or champagne vinegar. You could also swap the vinegar out for 2 tablespoons lemon juice plus 1 tablespoon water.

• Dijon mustard : Yellow mustard, whole-grain mustard, 1/2 teaspoon ground mustard

• Dried oregano: Dried Italian seasoning, basil, or thyme. You could also use fresh oregano, but double the amount and finely mince it before adding.

• Garlic powder: Onion powder, or swap it for 1 minced garlic clove

• Chili flakes: Roasted red pepper flakes, 1/8 teaspoon cayenne powder, a dash of hot sauce, or omit

• EVOO : Olive oil, avocado oil, or another oil you love the taste of

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons fresh parsley or basil, chopped
ingredients.name: fresh parsley or basil

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 large burrito-size flour tortillas or wraps
ingredients.name: large burrito-size flour tortillas or wraps

preparationSteps: Make the dressing: In a small bowl (or a jar with a lid), whisk (or shake) together 3 tablespoons red wine vinegar , 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon chili flakes . Slowly whisk in 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil until emulsified (AKA, until the oil and vinegar are well combined). Set aside.

Cut a head of iceberg lettuce in half and save half for later. On the biggest cutting board you own, roughly chop the lettuce you’re using. On top of the roughly chopped lettuce, pile on all of the meats, cheeses, and veggies ( 6 slices salami, 4 slices deli turkey, 3 slices prosciutto, 4 ounces mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup sliced pepperoncini, 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, 1/4 cup red onion, 1/4 cup roasted red peppers, and 2 tablespoons fresh parsley or basil ). Using the largest, sharpest knife you have, roughly chop everything on your cutting board into small, bite-sized pieces. Just keep chopping until everything is small and evenly mixed!

Transfer the chopped mixture to a large bowl, pour in the dressing, and toss to coat. Stir in a big pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper . Taste and add more salt and pepper as needed until it tastes perfect.

Warm 4 large burrito-size flour tortillas or wraps in the microwave or in a dry pan to make them more pliable. Divide the chopped filling between each wrap. Roll them up like burritos, slice in half, and serve.

name: salmorejo
note:
Prep time: 30 minutes, plus 2 to 3 hours for letting the soup chill

• Love your leftovers/prep ahead: Store leftovers in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. If the soup separates while it sits, just whisk it together again before eating.

• What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Buy pre-prepped hard-boiled eggs from the store to avoid having to boil water and peel shells.

• Vegetarian : Skip the jamón serrano. Double the eggs if you want to make up for that protein.

• Dairy-free/nut-free: Already is!

• Gluten-free: Use gluten-free bread and crackers.

• I’m allergic to tomatoes: Replace the tomatoes with 3 (12 ounce) jars of roasted red bell peppers. Drain and give them a quick rinse first!

• I’m feeling fancy : Add some chopped olives and/or Marcona almonds to your bowls, too.

• Bulk it up: Serve this soup with grilled cheese! For each sandwich, spread 1 tablespoon of softened unsalted butter on 2 slices of sandwich bread (or you could use slices from your rustic loaf) and place them buttered-side-down. Top one slice with a generous handful of shredded cheese like Cheddar or Gruyère (bonus points if you use a Spanish cheese like manchego), squish the other bread slice on top buttered-side-up and grill in a skillet over medium heat, flipping occasionally, until toasted and melty. It’s also currently fig season, which means a ham and fig grilled cheese would be an excellent choice.

• Spice it up: If you love spice, add a big pinch of red pepper flakes or hot smoked paprika (that would likely be José’s choice !), or a shake of your favorite hot sauce.

• Plum tomatoes: If you can’t find plum tomatoes, swap with 2 pounds of any ripe summer tomatoes (heirloom, cherry, Sungold, etc.). See the tomato allergy note above for another idea.

• Bread : You’re looking for a fresh baked loaf of white bread from the bakery section of your store (or a bakery!). It’ll be round with a crusty exterior and may be called “rustic loaf,” “country bread,” “artisanal loaf” — even fresh sourdough would do. If you’re in a bind, you can use white sandwich bread!

• Garlic clove: Swap in a big pinch of garlic powder if you don’t have fresh.

• Sherry vinegar: Sherry vinegar and apple cider vinegar are our top picks, but any other vinegar like red wine, white wine, or even balsamic will do the trick. Or use 1 teaspoon of lemon juice.

• Fine sea salt: You can swap for kosher salt, but you might want to increase the amount a little — fine sea salt tends to taste “saltier” than kosher. Start with an even swap and add more a little at a time, as needed, until the flavors pop!

• EVOO : Use the best-quality EVOO you have for this recipe. EVOO is definitely ideal, but if you have none, you can use olive oil or avocado oil.

• Eggs : Omit if you hate/can’t eat/don’t have eggs. Add more jamón for added protein, if you want!

• Jamón serrano: Cooked bacon crumbles or pancetta, diced prosciutto or country ham, or omit

• Crackers : Croutons or omit

ingredients.name: very ripe plum tomatoes

ingredients.name: rustic bread or other dense white country bread, crusts removed (and discarded/repurposed) and cubed (about 2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling, divided
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 pound jamón serrano, cut into 1/4-inch dice (can substitute another cured ham)
ingredients.name: jamón serrano
ingredients.note: cut into 1/4-inch dice (can substitute another cured ham)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup small bread sticks or crackers, such as picos
ingredients.name: small bread sticks or crackers, such as picos

preparationSteps: Quarter 2 pounds of very ripe plum tomatoes and add them to a blender. Remove and discard (or repurpose) the crusts from 2 to 3 slices of rustic bread . Cube the bread and add it to the blender along with 1 peeled garlic clove, 1 teaspoon sherry vinegar, 1/2 tablespoon fine sea salt, and 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil. Purée until smooth.
Continue to purée the soup while you slowly drizzle in the remaining 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil and continue blending until the soup is creamy and emulsified; this will take about 8 minutes.

Place a large pot or bowl beneath a fine mesh strainer and pour the blended soup through the strainer. Discard the chunky bits caught by the strainer. If you don’t have a fine mesh strainer, no problem — skip this step, your soup will still taste delicious!
Refrigerate the soup for 2 to 3 hours until it’s very cold.
Meanwhile, bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add 3 large eggs (shells still on!), reduce the heat slightly, and cook at a simmer (meaning slow, gentle bubbles) for 9 minutes.
Transfer the cooked eggs to an ice bath (AKA, put the eggs in a bowl of ice water). Once cool enough to handle, peel the shells off and rinse the eggs.
Meanwhile, chop 1/4 pound jamón serrano into a 1/4-inch dice (for reference, 1/4 inch is a little longer than your pinky finger’s fingernail).

To serve, divide the cold soup among 4 to 6 bowls. Slice the hard-boiled eggs in half and place a half into each bowl. Garnish each bowl with a spoonful of diced jamón and a few crackers . Sprinkle flaky sea salt over the eggs and drizzle each bowl with extra-virgin olive oil .

name: greek-style sheet-pan gnocchi
note:
• My gnocchi package isn’t 12 ounces: Gnocchi packages vary, typically ranging from 9 to 12 ounces depending on the brand. Anywhere in that range is great, or, if you are buying a 9 ounce package, you’re welcome to grab 2 and double the gnocchi! See the “bulk it up” note for more on this.

• Bulk it up: If you know you have extra-hungry family members or you want to have leftovers for tomorrow’s lunch, you can double the amount of gnocchi for a heartier meal. If you do this, you may want to assemble across 2 sheet pans so everything still gets crispy (or just use one reallyyyy large sheet pan) and add a little extra oil.

• Can I use parchment paper to make clean up easy? I try to avoid using parchment for sheet-pan gnocchi because it gets less crispy and delish IMO, but for easy clean up, that would be OK!

• Clean out the fridge: Let this recipe use up any veggies hanging out in your fridge! Just make sure you don’t over-crowd your sheet pan by doing so. Try to swap and sub in even cup amounts to the recipe as written for best results.

• Gimme a short cut: Use pre-chopped veg! There isn’t a ton of chopping required here, but for the places it is needed, go for pre-chopped/sliced, if you can find it at the store.

• Feeding kids: Add the dill to individual bowls instead of the whole sheet pan if the green would scare them off.

• Prep ahead : Add all of the prepped sheet pan components, aside from the oil, spices, and lemon halves, to a large mixing bowl. Cover and leave it in the fridge for up to a day, until you’re ready to transfer to the sheet pan and get cooking. You can even measure out your spices in a pinch bowl ahead of time and set aside. The yogurt sauce (sans roasted lemon) can be prepped ahead and stored in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 7 days.

• Love your leftovers: Store the sheet pan components and yogurt sauce separately in sealed containers in the refrigerator for up to 4 and 7 days, respectively. Add the roasted veggies to a scramble in the morning, mix them into a grain bowl or another pasta dish, or even use them as pizza toppings. Leftover chicken sausage and feta can also be added to a variety dishes, including eggs/omelettes. The yogurt sauce has endless uses—on a sandwich, grain bowl, in a wrap, or as a dip for veggies/chips.

• How should I reheat this? For best results, return the sheet pan components to a sheet pan and roast at 425°F for 6 to 10 minutes, until warmed and re-crisped. Plate with the yogurt sauce and serve. Alternatively, microwave the sheet pan components until warmed, about 2 minutes, and plate with the yogurt sauce.

• Vegetarian : Use plant-based sausages or a can of drained, rinsed, and dried chickpeas.

• Gluten-free: It already is if you use the gnocchi Jenn recommends in the recipe!

• Dairy-free: Use a DF feta (or omit it and add some extra olives for their saltiness) and dairy-free plain yogurt for the sauce.

• What to do with your leftover red onion : Make pickled red onions! Here’s a recipe.

• Gnocchi : Here are a few options: If you have a Trader Joe’s near you, I’m a big fan of their frozen cauliflower gnocchi (which is also gluten-free). You can cook it the same way as written. There are a variety of shelf-stable and frozen gnocchi options at different grocery stores — I’ve tried both versions and either will work. Skip the gnocchi, prepare 8 to 12 ounces of any pasta separately according to package instructions, and mix in the sheet pan components like a pasta salad instead. Although if you’re just hesitant to roast gnocchi, I highly recommend giving it a try! Swap the gnocchi for 2 medium russet or Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and diced into 1/2-inch cubes. The cook time should be about the same — keep an eye on it and cook until fork tender and crisp.

• Chicken sausage: I highly recommend a spinach and feta chicken sausage for this recipe to lean into the Greek vibes, but if you can’t find that, other pre-cooked chicken sausages will work. A second best would be a garlic-flavored chicken sausage. Two more options: You can also get plant-based “sausages” or even plant-based “meatballs.” Alternatively, use a 15-ounce can of chickpeas, drained and rinsed, to make it easy (the Greek vibe is so delicious with the chickpeas!). If you’d prefer to use ground meat instead of pre-cooked, you can make mini meatballs with a pound of ground chicken (about 16-20 total) and place them on the sheet pan to bake while the veggies roast. I recommend seasoning the ground chicken with the same spices that are on the sheet pan (I would halve all of the spices and add them in, in addition). I do something similar here .

• Feta : The saltiness and creaminess of the feta really brings this dish up to a 10/10, but I know not everyone loves it. You can opt for crumbled goat cheese instead — add it on top right after the sheet pan comes out of the oven. For dairy-free, there are great vegan feta options out there you can try, or leave it out completely if you have to (if omitting, I’d add some extra olives for flavor!).

• Cherry tomatoes: Oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, diced roma tomato, or omit if needed

• Red onion : Yellow onion, shallot, leeks

• Zucchini : Summer squash, eggplant, mushrooms

• Kalamata olives : Black olives, marinated artichokes, capers

• Olive oil : EVOO, avocado oil, another neutral cooking oil

• Dried oregano: Dried dill or dried parsley

• Garlic powder: Onion powder, or fresh minced garlic or thawed cubes of frozen crushed garlic (4 cloves for the sheet pan components, 2 for the sauce)

• Smoked paprika : Regular paprika, chili powder

• Lemon : Plain lemon juice or 2 tablespoons of a light-colored vinegar like apple cider or white wine vinegar

• Greek yogurt: Any plain yogurt, including dairy-free yogurt, will work for this. You can even swap it out for blended cottage cheese for even more protein! Or sour cream.

• Dill : Fresh parsley, or dried dill or parsley

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F and grab the largest sheet pan you own. If you’re using a non-stick sheet pan, you don’t have to prep it in any way. If yours is aluminum rather than non-stick, spray it with cooking spray.

Cut 12 ounces of pre-cooked chicken sausages into 1/4-inch slices and add them to the sheet pan. Thinly slice 1/2 a red onion (reserve the other half for another use), dice 1 small zucchini , and cut an 8-ounce block feta cheese into 1/2-inch cubes . Add it all to the sheet pan along with 12 ounces potato gnocchi, 1 cup of cherry tomatoes , and 1/3 cup pitted kalamata olives.

Pour 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper on top and use clean hands to toss and coat everything in the oil and spices. Arrange all of the components in a single layer on the sheet pan so nothing overlaps. Place 1 halved lemon , face down, on each end of the sheet pan in a cleared space.
Bake until the vegetables and gnocchi are lightly crisped and the feta is soft, 20 to 24 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the yogurt sauce. Finely chop 2 tablespoons of fresh dill and add it to a small bowl along with 1 cup yogurt , 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and whisk to combine. Set aside.

Remove the roasted lemon halves from the sheet pan and squeeze them directly into the yogurt sauce (if you don’t love a strong lemon taste, start with one half and taste before adding the second half). Stir again to combine and season with additional kosher salt, if needed, to taste.

Sprinkle the sheet pan with additional chopped dill . Add about 1/4 cup of the yogurt sauce onto four plates and spread it out, then evenly divide the sheet pan components on top of the sauce. Dig in!

name: saucy ground beef teriyaki bowls
note:
Cook time: 25 minutes

• Get creative with your veggies: Add or swap in snap peas, water chestnuts, chopped spinach, shaved Brussels sprouts, shredded cabbage, diced zucchini or squash — or really anything you want/need to use up!

• What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Skip cooking the rice and use microwaveable frozen rice instead. Boom, done, one less thing to do. You could also buy a bottle of pre-made teriyaki sauce from the store … but this DIY version is SO easy and will be much more delicious!

• I want fancy rice : Make coconut rice , cilantro-lime rice , or kimchi rice !

• Love your leftovers/prep ahead: You can cook this whole thing ahead of time if you want — leftovers heat up beautifully either on the stovetop or in the microwave. When reheating, add splashes of water as needed to loosen up the sauce and the rice. If you just want to get a head start on cooking, chop the vegetables up to a day ahead of time and store them in airtight containers in the fridge.

• I’m feeding a crowd/cooking for 1: Like Nicole said in the headnote, this recipe is easy to double if you’re cooking for a crowd. You could also halve it if you’re cooking for 1 or 2 — though the leftovers are SO GOOD, so we highly suggest you make the whole thing and eat the leftovers for lunches (or freeze them for a future dinner!).

• Freezer-friendly: This recipe is a great stock-the-freezer meal — just store the rice and beef/veggie mixture in separate Ziploc bags or airtight containers.

• Vegetarian : Use plant-based ground “meat” or make it a veggie stir fry! You could swap the beef with chopped mushrooms — add those when you would add the beef and wait until they’ve released then absorbed their liquid before you add the other vegetables to the pan. Shelled edamame — added with the other veg — would be another great option for extra protein. Cubes or crumbled tofu would also be great here!

• Gluten-free/dairy-free: Use coconut aminos or tamari instead of the soy sauce to avoid gluten. It’s already dairy-free!

• Low-sodium soy sauce: If you’re using regular soy sauce, use 1/4 cup soy plus 1/4 cup water so it’s not too salty. You can always add more soy or kosher salt if needed at the end! Other good swaps would be coconut aminos or tamari.

• Cornstarch : Arrowroot or tapioca powder

• Sesame oil: Any sesame oil will do! Or swap for a neutral cooking oil like avocado oil, olive oil, or canola oil.

• Coconut sugar: Brown sugar, honey, or maple syrup (you may way to add a little extra honey or maple syrup if using — taste and adjust until it’s sweet enough for your liking)

• Garlic powder: 2 cloves of fresh garlic grated, or onion powder

• Ground ginger: 1 inch of fresh ginger grated, 1 tablespoon ginger paste, or omit

• Small onion : Any color onion works! If you only have a huge onion, you can use half and save the other half for later (maybe for pickled onions ?), or you can just double the amount.

• Garlic cloves: 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder or 3 cubes of frozen crushed garlic

• Avocado oil : Olive oil or another neutral cooking oil

• Ground beef: 90% lean, 10% fat is the ratio Nicole recommends. If you get home from the store and see that your beef is higher in fat, you can drain off the excess grease once your meat has browned. If you don’t like beef — ground chicken, turkey, or pork would be great instead and cooked the same way. You could also sub in cubed chicken breast or cubed salmon (follow the cooking instructions here if using salmon!). See “vegetarian” note above for more ideas.

• Shredded carrots : Shredded cabbage, shredded Brussels sprouts, another diced bell pepper (maybe a yellow or orange one for variety), snap peas

• Red bell pepper: Another color of bell pepper, extra broccoli or carrots, diced zucchini or squash, water chestnuts

• Broccoli : Diced cauliflower, shredded cabbage, snap peas, shredded Brussels sprouts, or another veggie you have and love!

• Jasmine rice: Swap with any rice or grain you love (quinoa! farro! couscous!) prepared according to package instructions. Or use cauliflower rice as the base of your bowls. For a delicious way to cook cauliflower rice, use this recipe as your guide. Mix it with a teaspoon or 2 of the teriyaki sauce in in lieu of the miso marinade before you roast it.

• Green onions: Fresh herbs like cilantro or basil, or omit

• Sesame seeds : Everything but the bagel seasoning or omit

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon cornstarch or arrowroot or tapioca powder
ingredients.name: cornstarch or arrowroot or tapioca powder

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup shredded carrots (from 1 large or 2 medium-sized carrots — or just buy your carrots pre-shredded!)
ingredients.name: shredded carrots (from 1 large or 2 medium-sized carrots — or just buy your carrots pre-shredded!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup jasmine rice, cooked per package instructions
ingredients.name: jasmine rice, cooked per package instructions

ingredients.rawIngredient: Garnishes: sliced green onions, sesame seeds
ingredients.name: Garnishes: sliced green onions, sesame seeds

preparationSteps: As always, we’re going to start by getting our rice going so that it can cook while we fix the rest of dinner. Cook 1 cup of jasmine rice according to package instructions. When it’s done, take the pot off heat and set it aside, keeping it covered.

While your rice cooks, let’s make the magic teriyaki sauce. In a small bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce and 1 tablespoon cornstarch until the cornstarch is fully dissolved. Add the rest of the ingredients — 1/2 cup water , 2 tablespoons sesame oil, 1/4 cup coconut sugar, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon ground ginger — and whisk again until dissolved, then set aside.
Now let’s prep all of our veggies so they’re ready to go when we need them. Keep them separated as you chop because we are going to add them to the pan at different times.

Finely dice 1 small onion . Mash 3 cloves of garlic using the side of your knife and the knife blade (you could also grate the garlic using a microplane if that feels easier!). Dice 1 red bell pepper , finely dice 1 1/2 cups of broccoli florets , and (unless you bought pre-shredded carrots), grate 1 large or 2 medium carrots to get 3/4 cup shredded carrots .

Add 2 tablespoons avocado oil to a large pan/skillet over medium heat. Once the pan is hot, add the onion and sauté for about 4 minutes, until it becomes soft. Add the mashed garlic and cook for 1 more minute. Next, add 1 pound 90/10 ground beef and cook for about 4 minutes, breaking it up into as tiny of pieces as you can.
Add the diced bell pepper, broccoli, and shredded carrots and continue cooking until the beef is cooked through and the veggies have softened.
Pour the teriyaki sauce on top and stir for a few minutes until thickened.

Remove from the heat. Fluff your cooked rice with a fork then assemble your bowls. Be sure to spoon some of the teriyaki sauce over top! Garnish your bowls with sliced green onions and sesame seeds . Enjoy!

name: mustard-roasted fish with haricots verts
note:
Cook time: 20 minutes

• This makes me want to host a dinner party: Us too. You can double this recipe if feeding a crowd. Ina’s Tomato Crostini with Whipped Feta would be a lovely app to serve. Or, if you’re ready for fall flavors, go with Butternut Squash & Ricotta Bruschetta !

• What kind of fish works here? Any firm, thick white fish like halibut, cod, and snapper. Ina uses snapper, but you can use whatever looks really good at the fish store.

• I don’t eat fish: Swap it for boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs but roast at 400°F for about 20 minutes, or until 160°F internally (the temp will continue to rise and get to 165°F once you pull the chicken out of the oven). See “vegetarian” note below for more ideas.

• Can I cook the fish and haricots verts on one sheet pan rather than dirtying two? If you have a big enough sheet pan and want to dirty one less dish, you could cook the fish on one half and the green beans on the other. BUT! The sauce from the fish will seep over to the beans, and that plus roasting on parchment instead of on a bare sheet pan will prevent the beans from getting as browned on the bottom as they would roasting on their own pan. Everything will be fully cooked and tasty! There will just be a different texture/finish on the haricots verts.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers of this meal will be delicious stored in an airtight container for up to 3 days. If you’re not a leftover-fish lover, you can easily halve the recipe if you’re feeding 1 or 2 people.

• Prep ahead: You can make the crème fraîche mixture up to a day ahead of time and store it in the fridge in an airtight container. You could also wash and trim your haricots verts to make cooking dinner even more of a breeze.

• Feeding kids: Your kids really might go for this beautiful meal!!! You can pick the capers off their serving of fish if that would improve their odds of eating it.

• Vegetarian : This sauce would be delicious over cauliflower steaks, tofu planks, or portobello mushroom caps. Roast the plant-based protein until golden first — that will take about 20 to 25 minutes, flipping halfway through, for tofu planks and cauliflower, and roughly 15 to 20 minutes for portobello mushroom caps. Once they’re golden, cover with the sauce and cook for another 10 minutes.

• Dairy-free: Swap the crème fraîche with store-bought dairy-free sour cream, unsweetened coconut yogurt, or a homemade cashew cream .

• Gluten-free: Read the labels of the mustards you buy to ensure they’re gluten free!

• Red snapper: Read the notes above for Ina’s fish sub recommendations, as well as for non-fish ideas.

• Shallot : You need 2 tablespoons of minced shallot, which equals about 1 medium shallot, 2 small shallots, or 1/2 a very large shallot. You could swap the shallot with 2 tablespoons of minced white, yellow, or red onion, chives, or thinly sliced scallions (white parts only).

• Crème fraîche : Mascarpone, cream cheese, sour cream, or Greek yogurt (see “dairy-free” note for more)

• Dijon mustard: Yellow mustard, honey mustard (it’d add sweetness to the sauce, which would be different but tasty), or use all grainy mustard

• Whole-grain mustard: Stone ground mustard, or use extra Dijon

• Capers : Chopped green olives, cornichons, or pickles. Alternatively, you can add a squirt of lemon juice and a little extra kosher salt for an extra dimension of flavor.

• French string beans (haricots verts) : Snap peas (same cook time), regular green beans or trimmed asparagus (may need to roast 2 to 3 more minutes), or any other vegetable you love to roast (for example, broccoli florets or broccolini would be excellent!).

• Olive oil: EVOO or another neutral cooking oil like avocado

• Garlic cloves: 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder or onion powder. Or, if you have any leftover minced shallot, you could use that.

• Lemon zest: Orange zest would be good. Or you could add a small splash of vinegar at the end of cooking like champagne, white wine, or apple cider vinegar. Or just omit.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 (8 ounce) fish fillets, snapper, halibut, or cod
ingredients.name: fish fillets

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound French string beans (haricots verts), stem ends removed
ingredients.name: French string beans (haricots verts), stem ends removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 garlic cloves, grated on a microplane
ingredients.name: garlic cloves, grated on a microplane

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Freshly grated lemon zest, to taste (from 1 lemon)
ingredients.name: Freshly grated lemon zest, to taste (from 1 lemon)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Line a sheet pan with parchment paper. (You could also use an ovenproof baking dish.) Place 4 (8 ounce) fish fillets such as red snapper skin side down on the sheet pan. Sprinkle generously with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper .

Combine 2 tablespoons of minced shallot , 8 ounces crème fraîche, 3 tablespoons Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon whole-grain mustard, 2 teaspoons drained capers, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper in a small bowl. Spoon the sauce evenly over the fish fillets, making sure the fish is completely covered.
Roast for 5 minutes.

While the fish is roasting, trim the stem ends off 1 pound haricots verts (AKA French string beans) and add them to a second sheet pan (don’t add parchment to this pan). Toss with 3 tablespoons good olive oil, 3 garlic cloves grated with a microplane directly onto the sheet pan , 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt , and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper . Spread the string beans out evenly on the pan.

After the fish has cooked for 5 minutes, add the haricots verts to the oven and cook both for 5 to 10 minutes. The cook time for the fish will depend on the thickness of the fillets; cook it until the fish is just barely done (it will flake easily at the thickest part when it’s ready — be sure not to overcook it!). The haricots verts are ready when they are crisp-tender and starting to brown on the bottom. The fish and haricots verts might finish right at the same time, or you may need to leave one or the other in the oven for a few extra minutes.

Zest 1 lemon , to taste, directly onto the warm haricots verts and toss with a spatula. Sprinkle them with kosher salt and serve hot or warm alongside your fish. Serve the fish hot or at room temperature with the sauce from the pan spooned over the top.

name: one-pot pumpkin chickpea curry
note:
Cook time: 10 minutes active, 50 minutes inactive

• How much curry paste should I use? This will depend on how spicy the brand you have is — they vary a lot. Thai Kitchen red curry paste is really mild, so use closer to 3 tablespoons (maybe even more if you love spice!). Mae Ploy, Mekhala, and Maesri, on the other hand, are REALLY spicy, so start with 1 tablespoon. Blue Elephant brand has medium spice, so I would start with 1 1/2 to 2 tablespoons. If you have a brand of red curry paste not mentioned here, taste it before you add any to the pot. Is it super spicy? Use the 1 tablespoon starting point. Is it totally mild? Go the 2 to 3 tablespoons route. Taste and add more, if desired.

• I don’t like/can’t eat pumpkin: A few options: You could use a can of puréed butternut squash instead. You could just omit it (if you do, you won’t need to sauté the curry paste as long, just for 2 minutes or until fragrant). If you are cutting the pumpkin and want to replace those nutrients and flavor with something similar, you could add a pound of cubed butternut squash or sweet potatoes to the pot. You could also do that in addition to using the pumpkin purée to bulk it up even more.

• Feeding kids: If you’re feeding kids (or adults) who hate spice, start with the minimum amount of red curry paste. If you’re working with a really spicy brand, you can even start with 1/2 tablespoon. Otherwise, this is a really kid-friendly meal! If they’re not into stewy things or curry flavor, you can fish the chickpeas and veg out at the end of cooking, give them a rinse, and plate ‘em.

• Love your leftovers/make-ahead: This is one of those dishes that just gets better the next day and the next! Leftovers will be good for up to 4 days, so enjoy them for lunches, or make the whole meal well ahead of time, store it in an airtight container, and reheat it right before dinner. Reheat it on the stovetop over medium heat (or in the microwave!), adding a splash more stock, coconut milk, or water, if needed, to loosen things up.
