• Freezer-friendly: This is an excellent stock-your-freezer meal. Cook the curry as written, let it cool, then freeze it in a zip-top bag or freezer-friendly container. I like to freeze my meals in quart-sized bags — that way I can thaw just one if it’s for just myself or for me and George, or I can thaw multiple bags if I am feeding the whole family. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat as directed above. You can also freeze rice, FYI!

• Cook it in a slow cooker: I would sauté the onion, red bell pepper, pumpkin purée, and curry paste as written, then transfer them over to the slow cooker and add the liquid ingredients and chickpeas. Some slow cookers have a sauté setting to let you do all that in the same pot! Cook on low for 5 to 6 hours or on high for 3 to 4, then add the remaining ingredients (spinach, soy sauce, etc.) and cook for another 30 minutes or so to let the flavors meld and spinach wilt.

• Cook it in a pressure cooker: Sauté the onion, red bell pepper, pumpkin purée, and curry paste as written. Add all the other ingredients and cook on high pressure for 5 minutes. Let pressure naturally release for 5 minutes, then quick release the rest.

• Must have meat/extra protein: Add cubed chicken breast or thighs (I prefer thighs here!) for the last 15 minutes of the curry’s cook time, making sure it cooks through (to 165°F). You could also add cubed tofu at the same time as the liquids. First press the tofu between two paper towels and under a heavy book for 20 minutes.

• What to do with your leftover red curry paste: Make the thai chicken chop or coconut curry lentil stew !

• How do I cook rice? First of all, might I suggest microwaveable frozen rice to save you some time and effort? But here’s a quick and easy way, should you want to DIY! Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil (as if you’re cooking pasta). Add 1 1/2 cups rice and cook until tender, about 17 minutes for white rice or 30 minutes for brown rice. Drain the rice, then return it to the pot, and cover it until you’re ready to eat.

• Extra extra: If you’re feeling fancy, you can make cilantro-lime rice. Follow the directions right above. Once your rice is ready, use a microplane to scrape the zest of 1 lime straight into the pot, then add the juice of that lime, 1 tablespoon butter, a 3-finger pinch of salt, and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro. Another fancy rice option that would be delicious here is coconut rice !

• Cook once, eat twice: If you’re cooking rice for this meal, double it so that tomorrow you can make bacon kimchi fried rice .

• Vegetarian: Swap the fish sauce for extra soy sauce

• Dairy-free/gluten-free: It’s already DF. Swap the soy sauce for coconut aminos or tamari, and make sure your stock is GF.

• Neutral oil: You can use pretty much any oil here — avocado, olive, canola, coconut, grapeseed…

• Yellow onion: Red or white onion, thinly sliced leeks, 2 shallots

• Red bell peppers : Yellow or orange bell peppers. Or another veg you love like bite-sized cauliflower or broccoli florets; 1/2-inch cubed sweet potatoes, carrots, or butternut squash; or yellow squash or zucchini sliced into half circles.

• Pumpkin purée: See the “I don’t like pumpkin” note above for sub ideas.

• Red curry paste : Yellow curry paste, or you can use curry powder — 1 teaspoon to replace each tablespoon of paste.

• Chickpeas : Chickpeas are definitely my favorite for this, but another white bean like navy or cannellini would be good. See the “must have meat” note above for additional protein options. You could also bulk it up with extra veg (see the red bell peppers sub ideas).

• Full-fat coconut milk: A can of coconut cream would work! Lite coconut milk isn’t going to thicken the curry up quite as much, but it’s fine if that’s what you have. If you can’t do coconut or are out of coconut milk, you could use Greek yogurt, heavy cream, or even sour cream to thicken it. Start with a 1/4 cup and add more as needed, tasting as you go — you don’t want the dairy to overpower the curry!

• Vegetable or chicken stock: Low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, 2 cups water + 2 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon, or bone broth

• Spinach : Kale, collard greens, mustard greens

• Low-sodium soy sauce : Coconut aminos or tamari

• Fish sauce: Oyster sauce, tamari, or extra soy sauce

• Lime juice : 1 tablespoon of a light-colored vinegar like white wine or rice vinegar

• Cilantro : Fresh basil, thinly sliced green onion, or omit

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can pumpkin purée (NOT pumpkin pie filling)
ingredients.name: pumpkin purée (NOT pumpkin pie filling)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 3 tablespoons red curry paste (see note below recipe for how much to use)
ingredients.name: red curry paste (see note below recipe for how much to use)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock

ingredients.rawIngredient: To serve: Cooked rice or naan or even really good sourdough, cilantro, more lime wedges
ingredients.name: To serve: Cooked rice or naan or even really good sourdough, cilantro, more lime wedges

preparationSteps: Heat 2 tablespoons neutral oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 diced yellow onion and 2 thinly sliced red bell peppers and cook until they are soft and starting to brown, 5 to 6 minutes.

Add 1 (15-ounce) can pumpkin purée and 1 to 3 tablespoons red curry paste (see note below recipe for how much to use) and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 to 7 minutes. You’ll see the pumpkin start to darken, and the moisture will cook off — it’ll turn almost paste-like. This is what you want! You’re concentrating all that pumpkin-curry flavor. If it’s popping at/splattering you, turn the heat down slightly.

Pour in 2 (drained and rinsed) cans of chickpeas, 1 can full-fat coconut milk, and 2 cups of low-sodium stock. Stir everything together, scraping up any stuck bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a slow simmer (there should only be an occasional small bubble) over medium-low and cook UNCOVERED for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the curry thickens. Stir it occasionally, and really scrape the bottom of the pot when you do to make sure it doesn’t burn. If your curry is getting too thick, just add a little more stock or coconut milk.

Stir in 3 cups chopped spinach, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, and the juice from 1/2 lime. Cook until the spinach wilts, 2 to 3 minutes . Keep tasting and adding more soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice, and/or curry paste, as desired, until it tastes perfect. I add a lot more soy sauce because I like things salty!
Serve over cooked rice (or with naan or sourdough) and topped with lots of cilantro and extra lime wedges .

name: sheet-pan thanksgiving turkey meatballs
note:
Cook time: 35 minutes

• I’m not ready for Thanksgiving vibes: If you want to dial back the Thanksgiving flavors, skip the dried rosemary. You could also swap the cranberry sauce for lingonberry jam/spread, or change the sauce up altogether. Crème fraîche plus a tablespoon of Dijon mustard, a teaspoon or 2 of maple syrup, kosher salt, and a squirt of lemon juice would be great. Or you could make the tahini lemon sauce or the cashew sauce from the sauce guide.

• I want more Thanksgiving turkey meatballs! My friend Gaby Dalkin has a version with gravy!

• What kind of cranberry sauce? Like I said in the recipe, you’ll ideally use whole berry cranberry sauce. If you can’t find any, the jellied kind is fine. I tested with both — if you’re using the jelly, you just gotta smoosh it. It’ll blend!

• I’m feeding more than 4 people: Double the whole thing! Cook all the meatballs on one sheet pan, and all the vegetables on another.

• What’s the ideal Cheddar here? A block of Unexpected Cheddar from Trader Joe’s, or any aged white Cheddar! But any Cheddar or Parm will do. Or Gouda! Or more swaps below.

• Freezer-friendly : I highly recommend freezing any extra meatballs — or doubling the meatballs and freezing half of them. They’re a perfect protein to stock your freezer with. Reheat them from frozen for about 2 minutes in the microwave.

• Cook once, eat twice thrice / love your leftovers: You could also double both the veg and meatballs to prep ahead on multiple meals: Serve the extra meatballs with store-bought marinara (I love Rao’s) and spaghetti. Make the autumn chop with the extra squash and shallot and a store-bought rotisserie chicken.

• Feeding picky eaters: Even my picky-eating kids loved these meatballs. Some of the boys even ate the squash!

• Prep ahead: Pre-slice your veggies and form your meatballs up to a day ahead of time. Store them in the fridge in airtight containers.

• Vegetarian: Use a ground meat alternative.

• Gluten-free / dairy-free: Use rice breadcrumbs or 1/4 cup almond meal if avoiding gluten. To make the meal dairy-free, swap the crème fraîche for a dairy-free yogurt or sour cream or coconut cream, and use a DF Cheddar “cheese.” If you’d rather skip the cheese, add a tablespoon of olive oil (to keep the mixture moist) and a tablespoon of nutritional yeast (for umami).

• Delicata squash : Butternut, kabocha, or acorn squash, sweet potatoes, or carrots. The key here is to slice your squash or veg uniformly so that it will roast evenly.

• Shallots : Red onion or yellow onion sliced into 1/2-inch thick pieces, or thinly sliced leeks.

• Olive oil: Any neutral oil (avocado, grapeseed, canola, etc.)

• Maple syrup: Honey (ideal sub!), agave nectar, or brown sugar

• Ground turkey: Ground chicken or a plant-based ground meat. Ground beef or pork would get too greasy here.

• Panko breadcrumbs: Rice breadcrumbs, almond meal, Italian breadcrumbs, or even crushed up Rice Krispies

• Egg: Make a flax egg. Mix 1 tablespoon ground flax with 3 tablespoons water, stirring until well combined. Let it sit for about 5 minutes before mixing with the other ingredients.

• Cheddar cheese: Any hard melting cheese like Monterey Jack, Gruyère, or Fontina, Gouda, Parm, or a DF cheese.

• Onion powder and garlic powder : Double up on the other one if you only have one. You could also swap them for fresh — you would use 1 finely minced shallot in place of the onion powder, and 2 finely minced garlic cloves in lieu of garlic powder.

• Dried oregano: Dried thyme or Italian seasoning. Or use 1 teaspoon minced fresh oregano.

• Smoked paprika: Just skip it if you have none.

• Dried rosemary: This gives a really nice Thanksgiving-y touch, but I loved the meatballs without it, too. You could use dried sage instead, if you have it. Or swap it for 1/2 teaspoon minced fresh rosemary.

• Crème fraîche : Sour cream, Greek yogurt, mascarpone, coconut cream (see dairy-free note above for DF swaps)

• Cranberry sauce: Lingonberry jam, raspberry jam, fresh cranberries cooked down in sugar, or see the “it’s not Thanksgiving” note above for more ideas.

• Arugula/parsley: Skip if needed, but I love the pop of green!

• Pecans : Cashews, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, or omit

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 delicata squash, halved lengthwise, seeded, and sliced into 1/2-inch half-moons
ingredients.name: delicata squash, halved lengthwise, seeded, and sliced into 1/2-inch half-moons

ingredients.rawIngredient: A big pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper
ingredients.name: A big pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese (see Notes for what kind)
ingredients.name: shredded Cheddar cheese (see Notes for what kind)

ingredients.rawIngredient: A few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper
ingredients.name: A few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup crème fraîche (this is half of a standard 8-ounce container) or sour cream
ingredients.name: crème fraîche (this is half of a standard 8-ounce container) or sour cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup cranberry sauce (ideally whole berry — see Notes beneath recipe)
ingredients.name: cranberry sauce (ideally whole berry — see Notes beneath recipe)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped, or a handful of arugula
ingredients.name: fresh parsley, chopped, or a handful of arugula

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.

Slice 1 delicata squash in half lengthwise and discard the seeds. Cut each half into 1/2-inch half-moons (they will look like Cs!). Cut 3 shallots into quarters and discard the skins. Toss the vegetables on the baking sheet with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, a big pinch of kosher salt, and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper , making sure all the vegetables are lightly coated. Spread them out in a single layer on the sheet pan and roast for 10 minutes.

While the vegetables roast, in a large bowl, mix 1 pound ground turkey, 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 2 teaspoons maple syrup, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/4 teaspoon dried rosemary , 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper until just combined. Roll into 15 meatballs — about 2 tablespoons of meat each.

Remove the sheet pan from the oven and scooch the squash and shallots over to one side to make room for the meatballs. Add the meatballs to the sheet pan alongside the vegetables. Return to the oven and roast for another 15 minutes, until the meatballs reach an internal temperature of 165°F. If the vegetables and meatballs aren’t browned to your liking at that point, turn on the broiler and broil them for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden and caramelized. Turn the oven light on and watch the whole time. Don’t let ‘em burn!

While everything roasts, make the sauce by stirring together 1/2 cup crème fraîche and 1/4 cup cranberry sauce in a small bowl. Taste. Depending on how sweet your cranberry sauce is, you might want to add a tiny bit of lemon juice or vinegar to cut through the richness and sweetness. Or if you want it sweeter, add a teeny bit of honey or maple syrup.

Serve the meatballs, roasted delicata squash, and shallots with the creamy cranberry sauce drizzled over top or swooped onto the plate. Sprinkle each plate with chopped parsley or arugula, a little shredded Cheddar, and chopped pecans .

name: creamy cajun turkey, sausage, and wild rice soup
note:
Cook time: 1 hour 10 minutes

• I don’t have any leftover turkey! You can shred a rotisserie chicken and use that instead. Or you can cook raw boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts right in the soup! Add them when you add the rice and stock, then once cooked transfer them to the bowl with the cooked sausage, use two forks to shred the chicken, then stir them both back in. See the “what to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking” note above the recipe for more ideas.

• I don’t want a grain in my soup : OK! Omit the rice and double the veggies and turkey/chicken.

• I have more leftovers to use up : You can swap in pretty much any veggie you have leftover from Thanksgiving for the celery, carrots, onion, and mushrooms here. Sweet potatoes! Potatoes! Parsnips! It would all be great.

• Should I put a Parm rind in the pot? This is a GREAT time to cut the rind off of your block of GOOD PARM (only if it says Parmigiano Reggiano) and simmer it in the soup. Discard it (it’ll be very soft and falling apart) when you discard the bay leaves.

• Make/prep ahead and love your leftovers : Leftovers of this soup will be good for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. If you plan to serve it within 24 hours, just keep it in the pot you cooked it in and stick the whole thing with its lid on in your fridge! Reheat your soup on the stove, adding more stock as needed to get it to your desired consistency. If you’re just wanting to knock out some prep work ahead of time, you can finely chop all your veggies days ahead of time and store them in an airtight container! You could pre-cook your sausage, too, but add a tablespoon or 2 of oil to the pot with the butter to make up for the sausage grease. This soup is also very freezable! Let it cool completely then freeze in a zip-top bag.

• Slow cooker : I haven’t cooked it in a slow cooker but it can definitely be done! Cook the sausage in a pan first and reserve it, then sauté the mirepoix (aka carrots, celery, and onion) and mushrooms in the pan before you add it to your slow cooker. If you want to skip that, follow the instructions I gave up top in the “what to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking” section — dump everything but pre-cooked meat, dairy, and lemon juice in. Cook on low for 5 to 7 hours or on high for 3 to 5 hours, until the rice is cooked through. Add the pre-cooked meat, dairy, and lemon juice in for the last hour. Remember to discard the bay leaves!

• Pressure cooker : We haven’t tested it in an Instant Pot but this is what I would do: Sauté the sausage (and reserve it) plus the celery, onion, carrots, and mushrooms using the sauté setting. Once the moisture has cooked off, add the other ingredients except for the cooked meat, dairy, and lemon. Cook for 15 minutes on high pressure. Natural release. Remove the bay leaves and stir in the cooked meat, dairy, and lemon, cooking over sauté mode until they’re melted and incorporated.

• Feeding kids : If you’re feeding kids/people sensitive to spice, go for mild Italian sausage instead of spicy/hot. The Cajun spice doesn’t really add heat but you can swap it for garlic powder if you’re nervous it’ll deter your kids.

• Vegetarian : Double the vegetables!

• Dairy-free/gluten-free : For dairy free, use DF butter (or swap in oil). Also leave out the creamy element (it’s delicious without it!!!) or use a DF sub like plant-based cream cheese. If you have to avoid gluten, use arrowroot powder or cornstarch instead of all-purpose flour (see the subs below for more details). Check your Italian sausage’s ingredients list (some contain gluten fillers) and omit if needed. Ditto for the stock. Wild rice is gluten-free! Serve with a GF bread.

• Sausage : Either sausage links in casings or bulk sausage work for this, just make sure they’re uncooked. You could use chicken sausages instead of pork. Kielbasa or andouille sausage also work — just slice them and brown them in a little oil before you add them to the soup. You could also just leave the sausage out entirely! It’s so good without, adding it is just a little special and different than a classic turkey rice soup.

• Celery and onion : Fennel would be delicious in addition to or in place of either of these. You could also use a red or white onion, 2 shallots, or thinly sliced leek or green onions in place of the yellow onion.

• Carrots : Diced parsnips, sweet potato, or potato, or double up on the celery!

• Unsalted butter : Dairy-free butter, olive oil, another neutral oil, or ghee

• Sliced mushrooms : Pre-sliced is great here — I like the thickness of them. If you can’t find them pre-sliced, slice your own! Omit if you hate mushrooms.

• All-purpose flour : Adding the flour makes a quick little roux to thicken the soup. If you’re out of it or can’t eat it, you could sub 1 tablespoon of arrowroot powder or cornstarch stirred together with 1 tablespoon of water. Almond or coconut flour wouldn’t work the same way… if needed, you can omit the flour, it’d still taste great.

• Dried rosemary or Italian seasoning : Dried thyme or oregano (or 1/4 teaspoon of each), or 1 teaspoon of fresh rosemary, thyme, or oregano leaves (minced)

• Smoked paprika : Regular paprika or chili powder

• Cajun seasoning : I also tested and loved the soup with garlic powder here instead of Cajun. Use 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Or you could add 4 minced cloves of fresh garlic (or 4 cubes of crushed frozen garlic) when you add the mirepoix.

• Low-sodium chicken stock : 6 cups water + 2 tablespoons Better Than Bouillon (either chicken or veggie flavor), veggie stock, chicken or veggie broth, or bone broth. If you can’t find stock that’s low-sodium, just cut back on the amount of kosher salt you add and add more to taste at the end if needed.

• Kale : Swiss chard, collards, or cabbage would be great here! Spinach works, too, but don’t stir it in until the very end with the turkey, cooked sausage, etc.

• Wild rice : Brown rice, barley, or farro are the best substitutions here. A wild rice blend also works!

• Bay leaves : Omit if you have none.

• Cooked turkey or chicken: See the “I don’t have any leftover turkey” note above for how to use raw chicken for this recipe, and the “vegetarian” note for that sub idea.

• Lemon juice : A light-colored vinegar like apple cider, white wine, or red wine vinegar.

• Creamy ingredient : There are so many other things that would work — cream cheese and Parm are just my favorites flavor-wise. You could stir in 1/3 to 1/2 cup heavy cream at the end. Or shredded white or yellow Cheddar.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mild or spicy ground Italian sausage (either links or bulk)
ingredients.name: mild or spicy ground Italian sausage (either links or bulk)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 carrots, finely chopped (I don’t peel them, I just scrub them clean)
ingredients.name: carrots, finely chopped (I don’t peel them, I just scrub them clean)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces sliced mushrooms (buy them pre-sliced if possible!)
ingredients.name: sliced mushrooms (buy them pre-sliced if possible!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon dried rosemary or Italian seasoning
ingredients.name: dried rosemary or Italian seasoning

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or 6 cups water + 2 tablespoons Better Than Bouillon), plus up to 2 more cups if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or 6 cups water + 2 tablespoons Better Than Bouillon), plus up to 2 more cups if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 cups cooked turkey or chicken, shredded or chopped
ingredients.name: cooked turkey or chicken, shredded or chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 block (4 ounces) cream cheese, cut into small pieces, or 1/3 cup grated Parm (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano) — skip this if you’d rather have a brothy soup than a creamy soup!
ingredients.name: skip this if you’d rather have a brothy soup than a creamy soup!
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 block (4 ounces) cream cheese, cut into small pieces, or 1/3 cup grated Parm (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but not really: really delicious toasted sourdough bread with good butter and flaky sea salt!!
ingredients.name: Optional but not really: really delicious toasted sourdough bread with good butter and flaky sea salt!!

preparationSteps: Squeeze 1 pound ground Italian sausage out of the casings and into a large pot over medium-high heat. Discard the casings. If you bought bulk Italian sausage instead of links, just plop the ground sausage in the pot! Cook, stirring often, breaking it up into little pieces as you cook it. Once crispy and browned, use a slotted spoon to transfer the sausage to a bowl but do not wipe the grease out of the pot.
While your sausage is cooking, finely chop 3 celery stalks, 3 carrots, and 1 large yellow onion.

Once the cooked sausage has been removed, add 4 tablespoons unsalted butter to the pot. Once melted, add the chopped celery, carrots, onion, and 8 ounces sliced mushrooms and cook, stirring every minute or so, until all of the excess moisture evaporates. This could take 10 to 15 minutes!

Once all moisture has evaporated, stir in 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon dried rosemary or Italian seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon Cajun seasoning and stir for another minute.

Add 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock, 2 big handfuls of chopped kale, 1 cup wild rice, and 2 bay leaves to the pot and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a simmer over medium-low heat, cover, and cook for 30 to 40 minutes, or until your rice is tender.
While the soup is cooking, shred or chop 2 to 3 cups of cooked turkey or chicken and cut 1/2 a block of cream cheese (so 4 ounces) into small pieces (or grate 1/3 cup of Parm).

Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the shredded turkey or chicken, the cooked sausage, the cream cheese or Parm, and the juice of 1/2 a lemon (about 2 tablespoons of juice) and simmer for a couple more minutes uncovered. Taste and season until perfect! The salt level in particular will really vary depending on how salty your turkey was! I like a THICK soup, but if you prefer things a little more brothy (or your rice soaks up all the stock) add up to 2 more cups of stock! If you love lemony flavor, add in some extra juice from the other half of that lemon.
Serve with a big hunk of sourdough smeared with good butter and sprinkled with flaky sea salt!

name: one-pan caramelized onion pasta
note: Cook time: ~1 hour, 20 minutes (~20 minutes active, 1 hour inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound yellow onion, very thinly sliced (this will be 1 large or 2 small onions, but weigh them to be sure — the amount is important! See notes for a slicing demo)
ingredients.name: yellow onion, very thinly sliced (this will be 1 large or 2 small onions, but weigh them to be sure — the amount is important! See notes for a slicing demo)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons reduced-sodium Vegetable Better Than Bouillon (see notes if you can’t find it)
ingredients.name: reduced-sodium Vegetable Better Than Bouillon (see notes if you can’t find it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 1/4 cups hot water (as hot as your sink will go)
ingredients.name: hot water (as hot as your sink will go)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon any clear vinegar or lemon juice (I used champagne vinegar)
ingredients.name: any clear vinegar or lemon juice (I used champagne vinegar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional, for serving: more grated Parm and red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: Optional, for serving: more grated Parm and red pepper flakes

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

In a 9x13-inch baking dish, layer (in this exact order!!!) 1 pound of spaghetti , 1 large or 2 small very thinly sliced (take your time and slice as thinly as you can!) yellow onions, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup tomato paste, 2 tablespoons reduced-sodium Vegetable Better Than Bouillon, 1 tablespoon anchovy paste, 2 teaspoons dried Italian seasoning, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.
Get in there with your hands and toss the onions with all of the pastes and oil and seasonings but DON’T toss the spaghetti — leave it on the bottom!

Pour in 4 1/4 cups of hot water (as hot as your sink will go!) down one corner of the dish so that it doesn’t wash everything off of the onions (don’t stress if it does a bit — it’ll be fine). Place 1 block of Boursin Garlic and Herbs over top. Cover the baking dish tightly with foil or simply place a baking sheet over top of the baking dish.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Carefully uncover the baking dish (but DO NOT stir or touch a thing!!!) and bake uncovered for an additional 10 to 15 minutes, checking at the 10-minute mark, until the onions are browned and soft.

Add 1 tablespoon vinegar or lemon juice and 1/2 cup freshly grated Parm and use tongs to toss everything together until combined and saucy. If a couple noodles are hard, no worries, it happens, just discard them. Taste. Need more salt? Add a pinch at a time until it’s perfect. Need more heat? Add some more red pepper flakes. Want more tang? Add more vinegar. Want it to be saucier? Toss in a little extra hot water. Keep tasting and seasoning until it’s delicious!
Serve and, optionally, garnish with grated Parm and/or red pepper flakes.
As it sits, the pasta will soak up the sauce. If you want to make it saucy again, add a splash of hot water and toss.

name: christmas strata

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound ground pork sausage (such as Jimmy Dean, I like the sage kind)
ingredients.name: ground pork sausage (such as Jimmy Dean, I like the sage kind)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 slices sourdough bread, 1-inch cubed (we are looking for about 4 cups)
ingredients.name: sourdough bread, 1-inch cubed (we are looking for about 4 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14-ounce) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
ingredients.name: artichoke hearts

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of thinly sliced chives (to get about 1/4 cup sliced), chopped
ingredients.name: Handful of thinly sliced chives (to get about 1/4 cup sliced)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (4-ounce) jars diced pimientos, drained (or 8 ounces of roasted red bell peppers, drained and chopped)
ingredients.name: diced pimientos, drained (or 8 ounces of roasted red bell peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces (2 cups) shredded sharp Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded sharp Cheddar cheese

preparationSteps: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook 1 pound ground pork sausage , breaking it into small crumbles as it cooks, for 8 to 10 minutes, until cooked through and browned all over.

While it’s cooking, cut 6 slices sourdough bread (or enough to get about 4 cups) into 1-inch cubes. Once the sausage is cooked through, stir the bread into the skillet to soak up any grease and toast for a minute. Turn off the heat and set aside to cool.

While it’s cooling, in a large bowl, whisk together 12 large eggs, 1 pint heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon onion powder.
Chop 1 can drained artichokes (discard any hard leaves you come across) and a handful of chives .
Into the bowl with the egg mixture, stir in the sausage and bread, the chopped artichoke hearts and chives, 2 DRAINED jars diced pimientos, and 2 cups shredded Cheddar .
Lightly spray a 9×13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Pour in the egg mixture and smooth the top. Cover with foil and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 3 days .
When ready to bake, remove from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature while the oven preheats.
Preheat oven to 325°F. Bake for 40 minutes covered with foil, then remove the foil and bake uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, or until firm on top.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then slice and serve. Option to garnish with extra chopped fresh chives, if you’d like!

name: julie's fudge pie with peppermint ice cream
note: Cook time: 1 hour, plus at least 2 1/2 hours to cool and refrigerate

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup (35g) all-purpose flour (plus another 1 tablespoon for the pie dish)
ingredients.name: all-purpose flour (plus another 1 tablespoon for the pie dish)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon peppermint extract, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: peppermint extract, plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup (about 5 ounces) crushed peppermint candies, preferably pink and white ones, or candy canes
ingredients.name: (about 5 ounces) crushed peppermint candies, preferably pink and white ones, or candy canes

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.

Melt 4 ounces bittersweet chocolate and 8 tablespoons (1 stick) unsalted butter together in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Don’t throw away the butter wrapper! Set the melted chocolate aside to cool.

Using the buttery wrapper, coat the entire inside of a 9-inch pie dish. Be very thorough and if you run out of butter from the wrapper, grab more or rub some oil on there. Add 1 tablespoon of all-purpose flour and tilt and tap the dish until the entire inside of the dish is coated. Tap out any extra flour.

In a large bowl, whisk 3 large eggs and 1 cup (200g) granulated sugar together until bubbles form and the color lightens, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in the cooled chocolate mixture and 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract . Use a sieve or flour sifter to sift 1/4 cup (35g) all-purpose flour into the mixture and gently mix it into the batter. Stop mixing as soon as no flour flecks are visible.
Pour the mixture into the pie dish and bake for 15 minutes.

Turn off the heat and let the pie sit in the oven (with the oven door closed) until it sets, another 15 minutes or so. The pie may come out of the oven puffed up, then it will settle and sink in the center, which is normal!
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. This step is essential to achieve the fudgy-ness.

While the pie is in the oven, make the peppermint ice cream: Let 1 1/2 quarts (about 6 cups) vanilla ice cream sit at room temperature for 5 to 10 minutes, until it’s soft and stirrable, but not melted.
Scoop the ice cream into a large bowl. Add 1/2 teaspoon peppermint extract and mix well. Taste. Add a little more extract if you want the peppermint flavor to be stronger.
Mix in 3/4 cup (about 5 ounces) crushed peppermint candies . If you want that classic pink peppermint look (you do!), stir in a couple drops of red food coloring , too.
Transfer the ice cream back into its container or another freezer-safe container. Freeze for at least 2 hours to firm it back up.

Pull the pie out of the fridge 1 hour before you plan to serve it so it can come to room temperature. It’s also good straight out of the fridge for a firmer fudgy bite! Serve with a scoop of peppermint ice cream beside or on top of each slice.

name: GOOD-ALL-WEEK BREAKFAST: High-protein cheesy pork, pepper, and onion breakfast biscuits
note: Cook time: 50 minutes (20 minutes active, 30 minutes inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or you can use avocado oil since you’re using it for other recipes this week)
ingredients.name: olive oil (or you can use avocado oil since you’re using it for other recipes this week)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and small-diced (about 1 cup)
ingredients.name: red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and small-diced (about 1 cup)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper and set aside.

In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add 1 large yellow onion (small diced) and 1 red bell pepper (cored, seeded, and small-diced) and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes.

Push the onion and pepper to the sides of the skillet to make a hole in the center. Add 1 pound 90% lean ground pork in the center and cook, breaking up any large chunks with a wooden spoon, until the pork is browned and the onion is translucent, about 8 minutes.

Remove from the heat, season with 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon ground black pepper, and 1 teaspoon ground sage and mix well. Carefully pour off any excess oil and set the mixture aside to cool in the pan for 10 minutes.

In a large bowl, whisk 6 large eggs until no streaks remain. Add the pork mixture and 1 cup of shredded Cheddar and mix well. Add 1 1/2 cups blanched almond flour, 1/3 cup coconut flour, and 2 teaspoons baking powder and mix until just combined. Do not overmix.

Using a lightly oiled large cookie scoop, a spoon, or your clean hands, scoop about 12 balls of dough onto the sheet pan, spacing them 1 to 2 inches apart. Press down gently on the top of each ball to form a biscuit. Evenly sprinkle the top of the biscuits with the remaining 1/2 cup Cheddar .
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the biscuits are baked through and lightly browned all over.

name: sheet-pan miso-ginger salmon
note: Cook time: 1 hour (20 minutes active, 40 minutes inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-inch piece fresh ginger root, skin removed (optional) and grated
ingredients.name: fresh ginger root, skin removed (optional) and grated

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 (6- to 8-ounce) salmon filets, preferably skin-on (see the notes section for how much to buy)
ingredients.name: salmon filets, preferably skin-on (see the notes section for how much to buy)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 16-ounce bag of cauliflower rice (preferably fresh, but frozen is OK — can’t find either? See notes)
ingredients.name: of cauliflower rice (preferably fresh, but frozen is OK — can’t find either? See notes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 16 ounces snap peas (or whatever size your bag is)
ingredients.name: snap peas (or whatever size your bag is)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of finely chopped soft green herbs such as cilantro, mint, basil, scallions, or chives, for garnish
ingredients.name: Handful of finely chopped soft green herbs such as cilantro, mint, basil, scallions, or chives, for garnish

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, stir together 2 tablespoons miso, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 tablespoons olive oil, the juice of 1/2 a lime, and 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce.

Now, it’s ginger time. Grab a hold of it and use a small spoon to scrape the skin off of about 1 inch of ginger . Use a microplane or the smallest hole on a box grater to grate the peeled ginger straight into the bowl with the marinade. No grater? Just mince it as finely as you can with a chef’s knife. If your ginger is really fresh and has thin skin, you can skip scraping the skin off!

Run your fingers along the flesh of 2 to 4 (6- to 8-ounce) salmon filets to feel for any tiny bones that the fishmonger (yep, that’s the word for a fish butcher) may have accidentally left behind. Pull those suckers out, if you find some!
Add the salmon filets to the bowl and turn to coat them in marinade. Allow the salmon to marinate for at least 15 minutes at room temperature or up to 24 hours covered in the refrigerator.
When you’re about 1 hour from when you want to eat, place one oven rack in the center of the oven, and one on the top rung.
Preheat oven to 275°F .

Transfer the salmon filets from the marinade bowl to a rimmed sheet pan. Place them skin-side down and grouped tightly together — touching, so that it looks like one big piece of salmon — in one corner. Spread a thin layer of the miso-maple marinade over top of the salmon.
Keep the remaining marinade in the bowl and add to it 16 ounces of cauliflower rice and a big pinch of kosher salt . Stir until the cauliflower rice is evenly coated.
Yes, this is completely food safe, and no, it will not make the cauliflower rice taste fishy. Trust!
Transfer the cauliflower rice to the baking sheet and spread it into as even a layer as possible around the salmon. Don’t wash the bowl yet, you’re going to use it again!
Cook for 20 to 30 minutes, or until an internal thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the salmon registers 125°F for medium-rare, 135°F for medium, or 145°F for well done.
If you love sashimi, go for 125°F! If raw fish freaks you out, go for 145°F.

Meanwhile, toss 16 ounces of snap peas in the marinade bowl with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper until coated.
Transfer the salmon to serving plates.
Turn the oven to broil on high.

Stir the cauliflower rice and spread it out across the entire baking sheet, taking up the empty space left by the salmon. Scatter the snap peas over the cauliflower rice in an even layer and return the baking sheet to the TOP rung of the oven.

Now it’s time to turn on the oven light, sit on your butt in front of the oven, and WATCH! Depending on how hot your broiler runs, it’s going to take between 3 and 5 minutes to quickly char those snap peas. When the snap peas are a bright, vibrant green and are just starting to char/blister in small spots, they’re ready. It’s OK if yours have more char (aka black spots) on them than the pic — just don’t let them burn to a crisp!
Divide the cauliflower rice and snap peas between the plates. Garnish with soft green herbs and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Cut the remaining lime half into wedges and use those for a garnish, too!

name: creamy tuscan turkey spaghetti squash
note: Cook time: 20 minutes active, 1 hour total

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces sliced mushrooms (buy them pre-sliced so that you don’t have to dirty a cutting board!)
ingredients.name: sliced mushrooms (buy them pre-sliced so that you don’t have to dirty a cutting board!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 block cream cheese (or 1/2 cup grated Parm or ricotta)
ingredients.name: cream cheese (or 1/2 cup grated Parm or ricotta)

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 375°F.

Cut 1 spaghetti squash in half crosswise through the center (aka NOT lengthwise through the stem) and scoop out the seeds by firmly scraping with a large spoon. Drizzle the cut sides with extra-virgin olive oil and season with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper . Place cut-side down on a baking sheet and roast for 45 minutes, or until the strands of “spaghetti” easily pull apart when you pull at it with a fork. Set aside until cool enough to handle.

While the squash is roasting, make the sauce. Warm 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat . Add 1 pound ground turkey and 8 ounces sliced mushrooms to the skillet . Using a spatula, chop the meat into tiny crumbles as it cooks, stirring often until all of the liquid in the pan has evaporated and the meat is cooked through, 5 to 7 minutes. Add 2 huge handfuls of spinach and cook, stirring often, until wilted. Stir in 1 teaspoon kosher salt , 1 teaspoon oregano , 1 teaspoon garlic powder , 1 teaspoon onion powder, and a pinch of red pepper flakes .
Add 1 (24-ounce) jar marinara sauce and 1/2 block cream cheese (or 1/2 cup Parm or ricotta) and stir until the cream cheese has melted and the sauce is warm.

Once the squash is cool enough to handle, use a fork to scrape the insides into shreds, adding them right into the skillet, in a pile on top of the sauce. Discard or repurpose the empty squash skins — see notes below for ideas. Season the pile of squash with a big pinch of kosher salt , then stir the squash into the skillet until well combined with the sauce.

Turn the heat down to medium-low . Smooth the top of the meat and squash mixture out and sprinkle 2 cups shredded mozzarella over top. Cover the skillet with a lid (or a baking sheet or foil) and let cook until the cheese has melted, about 5 minutes. Scoop into bowls and serve!

name: vietnamese chicken noodle chop
note: Cook time: 40 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons kosher salt and several grinds of fresh black pepper, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: kosher salt and several grinds of fresh black pepper, plus more to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 of a 6.75-ounce package of rice vermicelli noodles (also called rice sticks)
ingredients.name: of a 6.75-ounce package of rice vermicelli noodles (also called rice sticks)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small (2- to 3-pound) head of Napa or savoy cabbage, thinly sliced (about 8 cups)
ingredients.name: head of Napa or savoy cabbage, thinly sliced (about 8 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch fresh cilantro leaves and stems, chopped (1 to 2 cups)
ingredients.name: fresh cilantro leaves and stems, chopped (1 to 2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch fresh mint leaves, chopped (1/2 to 1 cup)
ingredients.name: fresh mint leaves, chopped (1/2 to 1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup lime juice (from 3 to 4 limes), plus 1 more lime
ingredients.name: lime juice (from 3 to 4 limes), plus 1 more lime

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup creamy peanut butter (read notes beneath the recipe for more on this)
ingredients.name: creamy peanut butter (read notes beneath the recipe for more on this)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons chili garlic paste or sambal oelek
ingredients.name: chili garlic paste or sambal oelek

preparationSteps: In a medium saucepan, arrange 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts in a single layer. Sprinkle with 2 teaspoons kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper and cover with 1 inch of water. Bring the water to a boil over high heat. Once it starts to boil, cover the pot and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 11 to 14 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (75°C) internally using an instant-read thermometer. Use tongs to take the cooked chicken out and place it on a cutting board. Use a spoon to skim off any weird foamy chicken bits from the surface of the water. Add 1/2 of a 6.75-ounce package of rice vermicelli noodles , cover the pot, and let the noodles sit in the hot water (off the heat) for 5 minutes, or until you taste one and it’s tender. Drain the noodles in a colander and leave them in the colander to dry.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. In a very large (HUGE) serving bowl, whisk together 1/3 cup lime juice (from 3 to 4 limes), 1/4 cup fish sauce, 1/4 cup creamy peanut butter, 1/4 cup neutral oil, 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, and 2 tablespoons chili garlic paste or sambal oelek until combined. (Heads up that whisking the peanut butter in takes a sec. Be patient and keep pushing past the “curdled looking” phase into the "creamy and combined” phase. It only takes a few minutes! Alternatively, if washing your blender afterward wouldn’t annoy you, blend the ingredients to save yourself the elbow grease!) Now put away all of these ingredients before moving on so that your kitchen feels less chaotic.

Thinly slice 1 small head of Napa cabbage , cutting around and discarding the tough core. Add 6 cups of it to the serving bowl on top of the dressing and season the cabbage with a big pinch of kosher salt . Chop the cooked chicken, 1 bunch fresh cilantro leaves and stems, and 1 bunch fresh mint leaves , and thinly slice the 6 scallions , using the whole scallion and discarding only the root end. Add all of that along with the cooked noodles, 1/2 cup peanuts, and 2 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds to the bowl. It will be easiest if you use your (clean!) hands to toss everything together, but if that freaks you out, use tongs. If it is too heavily dressed for your liking, toss in some of the remaining cabbage until it’s perfect.
Let sit for several minutes to marinate before serving. Taste and season with more kosher salt and pepper as needed.

Serve in bowls, topped with more peanuts and sesame seeds, if you’d like. Cut 1 lime into 4 wedges and add a wedge to each bowl for garnish. I love the acidity that another big squirt of lime juice gives, but some people prefer it without, so I let everyone do their own thing!

name: one-pot spaghetti al limone
note: Cook time: 20 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 lemons, preferably organic, zested and juiced
ingredients.name: lemons, preferably organic, zested and juiced

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 ounces (2 to 3 cups) finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese
ingredients.name: finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese

preparationSteps: Put 1 pound dry spaghetti in a large saucepan or pot that is wide enough that it can fit across the bottom. If you don’t have a pot wide enough, just choose your widest and smoosh the spaghetti down into the water as soon as it becomes soft enough to do so (that will make sense in a second). Use a microplane or grater to grate in the zest of 2 lemons and 2 peeled garlic cloves. Cut 6 tablespoons of unsalted butter into several pieces and add them to the pot. Add 1 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper.

Add 4 1/2 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-high and use tongs to turn the pasta every 30 seconds or so until the pasta is al dente (that means until it’s tender but still has a slightly firm, chewy bite to it) and most (but not all — there should be a thin layer of liquid on the bottom of the pot) of the water has evaporated, 7 to 9 minutes. If the water evaporates before the pasta is al dente, add another splash and keep cooking.
Stir in 1/4 cup lemon juice from the 2 zested lemons. Remove from heat, and let the pasta cool for 3 minutes. This is important! Let it cool! Otherwise the cheese will clump up and harden!

While the noodles are cooling, use a microplane (or the smallest hole of a box grater) to finely grate 3 ounces (2 to 3 cups) of Pecorino Romano cheese . A little bit at a time, add the grated cheese, using tongs to vigorously mix it into the pasta. Add the next tiny bit only once the first bit is incorporated. Stir VERY vigorously with your tongs as you work.

Keep stirring vigorously and adding more cheese until everything is saucy and combined. Want it creamier? Add more butter, or another splash of water! Taste and keep adding more lemon juice (I like more!) or cheese until it’s as lemony and salty as you like it.
Plop onto 4 to 6 plates and garnish with more grated cheese and pepper.

name: lunch break: chocolate covered strawberries!
note: Cook time: 30 minutes, plus 30 minutes or more for the chocolate to set in the refrigerator

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings: toffee, nuts, sprinkles, etc.
ingredients.name: Optional toppings: toffee, nuts, sprinkles, etc.

preparationSteps: Wash and dry 1 pound of strawberries . Make sure they are VERY dry. Not a drop of water on them! It’ll mess up the chocolate. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Finely chop a 6-ounce bar of semisweet chocolate and place ALL BUT A SMALL HANDFUL OF IT (maybe 2 tablespoons) in a large heatproof bowl that you have wiped out to be sure that there’s NO WATER in there!

Fill a medium saucepan with a couple inches of water and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low so the water maintains a light simmer. Set the bowl of chocolate over the saucepan (without letting it touch the water) and stir until the chocolate is completely melted. Check the temperature with a meat or candy thermometer and pull it off when it reaches 122-133°F.
Off the heat, add in your reserved handful of chocolate. Stir to melt it, being sure to scrape down the sides. Keep stirring until the heat of your chocolate reduces to 81-83°F.
Place the bowl back over the heat VERY BRIEFLY, and stir until the chocolate reaches 88-90°F.
Remove from the heat. If the heat went past 88-90°F, stir until it cools back down to that range.

Holding the strawberry by the stem, dip the fruit into the chocolate, lift and twist slightly, letting any excess chocolate fall back into the bowl. If you’re using an optional topping (sprinkles, nuts, etc.), sprinkle it on now.
Set the dipped strawberry on the parchment paper. Repeat with the rest of the strawberries.
Refrigerate until the chocolate sets, about 30 minutes, or until you’re ready to eat.

name: everyone-loves-this-salmon
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes

• Prep ahead: If you plan to walk in the door from work and cook dinner immediately, you can take out all the pantry ingredients and put them on the counter and prep your largest sheet pan with parchment paper ahead of time. That way you can immediately get to work while the oven preheats, and put the ingredients away while the food roasts. You’ll only have a bowl to wash and piece of parchment to throw away after you eat! Or, even better, go ahead and prep the entire sheet pan and wrap it tightly with plastic wrap or foil. Just come home, unwrap it, and pop it in the oven!

• I’m a sauce lover: I am, too, and love this meal as is. But if you really want one, I get it! Hot honey or dill sauce would be fab.

• Extra extra: If you’re cooking this for guests and want the salmon to look prettier — or if you happen to have some fresh parsley you need to use up — swap the Italian seasoning for 1/4 cup of chopped fresh parsley.

• My bag of broccoli isn’t 1 pound : No prob if yours is a little over or under a pound (aka 16 ounces). If you’re feeding four people and you can only find a 10-ounce bag, I’d buy two of them.

• Inspiration for this meal: There’s a Food Network recipe called “the best baked salmon” and it is absolutely wonderful — this recipe is very inspired by that recipe, turned into a sheet-pan dinner.

• Gimme a grain: See the “bulk it up” section above the recipe.

• Love your leftovers/halve it: Leftovers will stay good for up to three days stored in the fridge in an airtight container. You could roughly shred leftover salmon and use it in place of crab to make salmon cakes ! Or swap it for the tuna here . If you don’t want leftovers, you can easily halve or quarter this entire recipe.

• Feeding kids: Call the salmon “pink chicken?” Serve it with ketchup or ranch?! Salmon is hit or miss with my kids but I don’t let it stop me from cooking it regularly for me and George — I don’t mind throwing a hotdog or nuggets on their plate during phases when they’re out on fish. They all love “crispy,” aka roasted, broccoli though.

• Vegetarian: This topping would be delicious on cauliflower “steaks.” Wash and dry two heads of cauliflower and remove the leaves around the core, keeping the core intact. Cut them through the stem/core into 3/4-inch planks — you should get at least two good “steaks” per head (but definitely roast up all the broken bits, too! Just add them to the sheet pan tossed with EVOO and salt and pepper). Coat the steaks with oil and season them with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes. Flip the steaks then add the toppings as directed in the recipe and cook again for another 15 minutes. If the broccoli finishes before you’re done cooking the cauliflower, take it off the sheet pan so it doesn’t burn. Maybe add some quinoa or brown rice to your plate for extra protein, too! If you have pesto or a good vinaigrette in the fridge, you could drizzle some on the rice for extra flavor.

• Dairy-free: Use plant-based butter.

• Gluten-free: Use gluten-free panko and double check that your mustard is certified gluten-free.

• Salmon : Halibut, trout, Arctic char, cod, mahi mahi, or any other white fish you love. If you have very thin fish filets, cook for less time. Boneless, skinless chicken breasts would be great with this topping, too. They need 15 to 25 minutes of cook time depending on their thickness — use your meat thermometer and pull them right at 165°F. If needed, remove the broccoli from the sheet pan before the chicken is done — don’t let it burn!

• Grainy Dijon mustard: Smooth Dijon mustard or regular mustard. If you have honey mustard, you can use that and cut back a bit on the brown sugar. Or miso!

• Brown sugar: Either light or dark brown sugar work here. You could also swap with coconut sugar, honey, or maple syrup.

• Garlic powder: Onion powder, or fresh minced garlic (use 1 clove per 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)

• Paprika: Smoked or sweet paprika, chili powder, or 1/8 teaspoon cayenne powder

• Butter: Ghee or olive oil or another neutral oil

• Panko breadcrumbs: Regular breadcrumbs, GF panko, homemade breadcrumbs using stale bread, crushed-up Rice Krispies or Ritz crackers

• Dried Italian seasoning: Dried parsley, oregano, and/or basil. Or 1/4 cup fresh chopped parsley.

• Broccoli florets: Broccolini, just trim the rough bottoms off of the stems first, if needed. Or you could roast thinly sliced cauliflower florets, asparagus, snap peas, or any other vegetable you love!

• EVOO: Olive oil, avocado oil, or another neutral cooking oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon grainy Dijon mustard (or whatever mustard you have)
ingredients.name: grainy Dijon mustard (or whatever mustard you have)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1-pound bag broccoli florets (or 1 bunch broccolini, tough stem ends trimmed and discarded)
ingredients.name: broccoli florets (or 1 bunch broccolini, tough stem ends trimmed and discarded)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 4 (6-ounce) salmon filets skin-side down and grouped together like one big piece of salmon in one corner of the baking sheet. Pat the salmon dry with a paper towel or clean dish towel then plop 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 tablespoon grainy mustard , 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon paprika right there on top of the salmon and rub everything all over with your hands.

Melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter in a small bowl in the microwave, then stir in 1/2 cup panko, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon dried Italian seasoning. Press the mixture evenly on top of the salmon. Keep the filets grouped together (this will help them cook evenly).

Place 1 pound broccoli florets on the other half of the baking sheet. If your bagged broccoli florets are huge, use your hands to break them into smaller pieces. If you are using broccolini, trim and discard the rough bottoms off of the stems first. Toss the broccoli with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder then spread the florets out in a single layer.

Roast for 13 to 16 minutes, until the salmon is firm but flakes easily when prodded with a fork, and the broccoli is crisp at the edges. For perfect doneness, use an instant-read thermometer on the salmon: 125-130°F for medium-rare, 135-140°F for medium (my fave), or 145°F for well done.
If your broccoli isn’t as crisp as you like it yet, transfer the salmon to plates and return the broccoli to the oven for another few minutes, making sure not to let it burn.
Serve the salmon with broccoli.

name: one-skillet pizza chicken
note: Cook time: 45 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts (4 breasts)
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts (4 breasts)

ingredients.rawIngredient: For garnish: fresh basil leaves, freshly grated Parmesan, and/or red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: For garnish: fresh basil leaves, freshly grated Parmesan, and/or red pepper flakes

ingredients.rawIngredient: For serving (choose one): a loaf of the most delicious bread you can find (this is my preference!), cooked rice, roasted potatoes, cooked spaghetti (or any noodle), a bed of spinach
ingredients.name: For serving (choose one): a loaf of the most delicious bread you can find (this is my preference!), cooked rice, roasted potatoes, cooked spaghetti (or any noodle), a bed of spinach

preparationSteps: Season 2 pounds of boneless, skinless chicken breasts with 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning.

Preheat a 12-inch ovenproof (preferably cast iron) skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, then warm 1 tablespoon olive oil for 30 seconds. Add the chicken breasts to the skillet and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden brown. Transfer to a plate. The chicken won’t be cooked through yet, that’s OK.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Carefully pour 24 ounces of marinara sauce into the skillet (it may splatter, beware!). Stir in half of the halved cherry tomatoes.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
While the oven is preheating, cook the sauce, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened and the tomatoes have softened.

Nestle the chicken breasts down into the tomato sauce and transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes. Use a meat thermometer to check the chicken temperature at the 15-minute mark. Pull the skillet out when the chicken reaches 160°F (it will go back in the oven and finish cooking soon).
Bump the oven temperature up to 450°F.

Evenly distribute 20 pepperoni slices over the chicken and sauce. Tear apart 6 ounces fresh mozzarella and distribute it over top, too. Return the skillet to the oven for 2 to 3 minutes, until the pepperonis are lightly crispy and the cheese is melted, but not too brown.

Remove the skillet from the oven and scatter the remaining halved cherry tomatoes over top, along with fresh basil leaves (thinly slice them if the leaves are big), freshly grated Parmesan , and red pepper flakes. Serve with your desired side — see options in the ingredients list.

name: roast chicken with onion gravy and sweet potatoes
note: Cook time: 1 hour 45 minutes (plus 24 to 48 hours for dry-brining)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to lightly coat your potatoes
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to lightly coat your potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 medium-sized sweet potatoes, washed and pricked all over with a fork
ingredients.name: medium-sized sweet potatoes, washed and pricked all over with a fork

preparationSteps: A day or two before cooking, place a whole 5-pound chicken in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet or Dutch oven. Pat it dry with paper towels or a clean dish towel. Season it generously all over with kosher salt (about 1 tablespoon) and freshly ground black pepper (about 1/2 teaspoon) , including inside the cavity. Refrigerate uncovered for 24 to 48 hours.
When you’re ready to cook, preheat the oven to 425°F .

Remove the chicken from the fridge. If your skillet has liquid in it from the dry-brining process, discard it. Pat the chicken dry again then rub it all over with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil and 2 tablespoons melted unsalted butter (I melt it in the microwave) . The butter will harden up as it hits the cold chicken — this is normal, just keep rubbing! Season it again, lightly, with a pinch of kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Place the chicken breast-side up in the skillet (see the notes section for a visual of this if you’re unsure) . Tuck the wings underneath the chicken and tie the legs together, one crossing over the other, with kitchen twine. If you don’t have twine, you could use a “rope” made of rolled-up aluminum foil, or just skip it.
Thinly slice 1 large yellow onion and scatter it around the chicken.

Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 1 ½ hours, or until fully cooked — the chicken should reach 165°F internally both in the leg and breast when poked with a meat thermometer. After the skillet has been in there for about 30 minutes, give the onions a little stir to mix them with the schmaltz.

Right when you put the chicken in the oven, line a sheet pan with parchment paper. Wash and dry 4 medium-sized sweet potatoes and place them on the sheet pan . Prick them all over with a fork and rub with a light coating of extra-virgin olive oil and a big pinch of kosher salt. Throw ‘em in the oven to cook along with the chicken.
If at any point the chicken skin or the onions start to get too dark (this will totally depend on your oven!), cover the skillet loosely with foil (like a blanket, not like a helmet).

Once the chicken is ready, remove the skillet and sheet pan from the oven. Transfer the cooked chicken to a cutting board and tent it loosely with aluminum foil while you make the gravy. Don’t skip this — letting it rest for 10 minutes will help lock in the juices!

To make the gravy, place the skillet full of cooked onions on the stove over medium-high heat. Sprinkle 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour over top and stir until the onions are pasty. Stir in 1/4 cup white wine until evaporated, then stir in 1 cup low-sodium chicken stock . Keep cooking, stirring occasionally, until thickened to your liking. Add more stock if it gets too thick (sometimes I end up using up to another 1 cup of stock). Season to taste with kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper. By that I mean stir in a pinch of salt and a little pepper and taste — repeat as needed, a little at a time, until the flavors pop and taste perfect to you! Sometimes I like to add some lemon juice here, too, to make it brighter!
Carve and plate the chicken . Cut the sweet potatoes in half and use a fork to fluff the insides, then season them with kosher salt and black pepper.
Place chicken and a sweet potato onto a plate and smother with onion gravy. Garnish everything with lots of chopped fresh parsley to cut through the beige.

name: sticky orange chicky and brussels
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes

• Learn : The only semi-difficult part of this entire recipe is trimming the fat off of the chicken. I like to use kitchen shears to do this really quickly and easily. It isn’t 100 percent mandatory, but it will save you from any weird bites of chicken.

• Shortcut : You don’t need to trim Brussels sprouts! Only trim them if they’re looking super brown. It’ll save you a lot of time to skip this step! Once roasted, the ends will get nice and soft and tender. This applies to all recipes.

• Swap : In place of or in addition to the Brussels, try zucchini, yellow squash, green beans, broccoli, or cauliflower. (You can omit the chicken and double the veg for an excellent veggie dish!). Sriracha or gochujang are great swaps for sambal oelek, and red pepper flakes will also work — use 1/2 teaspoon to start. Or omit the hot sauce completely for a more traditional sweet orange chicken vibe!

• Riff : Go Italian-ish instead by tossing the chicken and Brussels with a full 1 ½ teaspoons salt, a few shakes each of garlic powder and Italian seasoning, 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, and 1 teaspoon honey. Roast the same way, then grate fresh Parm over the top

• Bulk it up : Serve it over white rice, brown rice, or quinoa!

• How do I know if my chicken is cooked through? Whip out that meat thermometer ! It needs to reach an internal temp of 165°F.

• I added too much sambal oelek and now the sauce is too spicy: Do what Amanda did and add some honey to counter that heat.

• OJ shopping note: You can squeeze your own orange juice from 3 large or 4 medium navel oranges, or buy a good bottled OJ (Uncle Matt’s is excellent).

• One more shortcut: While you’re grocery shopping, you could very politely ask the butcher if they’re available to trim the fat off of and pre-cube the chicken. I’ve found that butchers are usually happy to, if they aren’t too busy! That would save you about 5 minutes of prep work.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat them in the microwave until warm, or, to get them crispy again, bake or air-fry them at 400°F for 5 to 7 minutes, just until warmed through.

• Feeding kids : My kids and I do not find the sauce to be spicy using 1 tablespoon of sambal oelek (or gochujang, etc.). I wouldn’t add any more than that if you’re feeding spice-averse eaters!

• Extra extra: Like in the “bulk it up” note above, rice or quinoa are a great addition to this meal. If you want to take it up another notch, you could make brown butter scallion rice or coconut rice .

• Feeding 1 or 2: I suggest halving the chicken — so use 1 pound instead of 2 — but otherwise keeping the recipe as is. You will have 1 or 2 servings leftover for lunch the next day!

• Prep ahead: If you want to do your prep work earlier in the day so that it’s ready to go when you get home from work/carpool, cube the chicken and halve/quarter the Brussels sprouts. Add them to the sheet pan, wrap it tightly with plastic wrap, and stick it in the fridge until you’re ready to make dinner. When the oven’s preheated, unwrap the sheet pan, add the oil, cornstarch, and salt, and throw it in the oven. Make the sauce while the meat and veg cook.

• Vegetarian: See the “swap” note above for extra vegetables you can add in place of the chicken. Option to plate it with quinoa for extra protein. If you want to omit the fish sauce, add an extra splash of soy sauce plus a squeeze of lime juice.

• Dairy-free: Already is!

• Gluten-free: Swap the soy sauce for coconut aminos or tamari. Also check the label for fish sauce — some brands are gluten-free certified but not all are.

• Neutral oil: Neutral oils include avocado oil, vegetable oil, canola oil, and light olive oil. Or use regular olive oil.

• Boneless, skinless chicken thighs: Chicken breasts work! They cook much faster than thighs do though and dry out more easily, so pull the chicken off right when it hits 165°F. Start checking after 10 minutes of cooking. The chicken may not get golden and crispy since it’s not cooking for very long, but it’ll still taste delicious covered in the sauce. Return the Brussels sprouts to the oven to finish cooking. Pork tenderloin cut into cubes would also be excellent. Cook it for 10 to 14 minutes, until 145°F internally. Use tofu (pressed and cubed) or cauliflower florets for a vegetarian version, or see more veg options in the “swap” note above.

• Brussels sprouts: See the “swap” note above.

• Cornstarch: Arrowroot powder works 1:1. If you have neither, just omit it! It will be less “sticky,” but you’ll still have a very tasty dinner.

• Fresh orange juice: See the OJ shopping note above. As a sub, you could use pineapple juice or pineapple-orange juice. I also think that fresh lime juice plus a tablespoon of honey would be good!

• Sambal oelek: See the “swap” note above.

• Low-sodium soy sauce: Regular soy sauce diluted with some water, tamari, coconut aminos, or shoyu

• Rice vinegar: Another light-colored vinegar (like apple cider or white wine vinegar) or lime juice

• Fish sauce: Worcestershire sauce, or add extra soy sauce plus a squirt of lime juice

• Scallions: Chopped fresh cilantro would be great! Or just omit the green garnish.

• Toasted sesame seeds: Skip them if needed!
preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Drizzle a little bit of neutral oil on a baking sheet. Trim any white fat off 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs and cut them into 1-inch cubes.

Cut 1 pound Brussels sprouts in half, or in quarters if they’re large. Combine the chicken and Brussels sprouts on the baking sheet and toss with 2 tablespoons of neutral oil, 3 tablespoons cornstarch, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to coat. Spread the chicken and Brussels out into an even layer and roast for about 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sprouts are dark brown and crispy, opening the oven to carefully stir once or twice.

Meanwhile, in a small skillet, combine 3/4 cup fresh orange juice , 1 tablespoon of the sambal oelek , 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce , 2 tablespoons rice vinegar , and 1 tablespoon fish sauce . Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to medium and cook until the sauce is thickened and reduced to about 1/3 cup, 10 to 15 minutes. Keep a close eye on it — if you reduce it too far, it will burn! Taste and add the remaining tablespoon of sambal if you want it spicier.
Meanwhile, thinly slice 2 scallions .
Drizzle the sauce all over the roasted chicken and Brussels and toss to coat. Divide among plates and top with the scallions and some toasted sesame seeds before serving.

name: springy green goddess shrimp + orzo chop
note:
Cook time: 30

• I don’t like shrimp: This recipe would be delicious with pretty much any protein. For chicken: See the “use chicken instead” note above the recipe. For steak (skirt, flank, or sirloin would all be great here): Marinate them for up to 4 hours in the fridge with a few spoonfuls of green goddess dressing. Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side or until desired internal temp (125-130°F for medium-rare; 135-140°F for medium; or above for well done). For salmon: Marinate the fish in a few spoonfuls of green goddess dressing for up to 30 minutes. To grill it, oil the grates and grill skin-side down over medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes for the first side, then 2 to 4 minutes on the second side, or until it reaches 120 to 130°F internally and flakes easily with a fork. Or you could bake it at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Or cook it in oil in a skillet over medium-high until cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway through. Or…

• Vegetarian : Tofu would be so good with this meal. Press a block of extra-firm tofu to remove excess water. You can either slice it lengthwise into big flat planks (best for grilling) or cube it. Marinate it for 30 minutes in a few spoonfuls of green goddess dressing, then either grill it, pan sear it (aka, cook it in a skillet until golden), or bake it at 400°F for 20 minutes, or until it starts to crisp up (flipping once halfway through). Crispy baked chickpeas or cannellini beans would also be delicious here. You can use a vegan Worcestershire sauce (regular Worcestershire contains anchovy) or swap it out for soy sauce or tamari.

• I’d rather cook the shrimp a different way: Boiling them is easy and straightforward, but not the most exciting method. I will say, the dressing adds enough flavor that it really is not a problem to cook them more simply. They still end up super flavorful! But if you want to cook them another way (or just read about some great ways to cook shrimp!) here ya go. Start all of these methods by marinating your shrimp in a few spoonfuls of green goddess dressing for between 30 minutes and 4 hours — no longer than that or the texture will get weird. To cook shrimp on the grill: Thread the marinated shrimp onto skewers — don’t pack them too tightly, they need a little breathing room. Heat your grill or grill pan to high heat. Once hot, cook the skewers for about 1 minute per side, until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and have some nice grill marks. To cook them in a skillet: Warm your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and heat until shimmering. Tilt the pan around to coat it in oil. Shake off as much marinade from the shrimp as possible, then add them to the skillet in an even layer. Cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until golden-brown all over. Add 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and toss to coat the shrimp in melted butter. To broil them: Position your oven rack about 6 inches from the broiler element and preheat on high for at least 5 minutes. Shake as much marinade as you can off the shrimp as you add them in a single layer on a sheet pan. Don't crowd them. Broil for 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium shrimp, 3 to 4 for large/jumbo. They're done when pink, opaque, and just starting to curl. Pull them the second they look done — shrimp go from perfect to rubbery very fast under a broiler!

• Feeding kids: Serve the salad deconstructed. Shrimp in a pile, orzo in a pile (pull the orzo and shrimp out for them before you add them to the salad), and any veggies they’d eat in piles. If needed, add some marinara or Parmesan or whatever they like to the orzo!

• What do you mean “leaves/fronds and tender stems?” By this I mean you don’t have to pluck the leaves off like you would for herbs such as rosemary, where the stem is super thick. You can include those thin, tender stems that the leaves are attached to in the dressing.

• Prep ahead: You can make the green goddess dressing up to 3 days ahead of time. You could also prep the orzo and shrimp mixture up to a day in advance if you wanted to. Let it cool completely, cover it, and store in the fridge. Reheat until just warm in a pot on the stove, adding splashes of water to separate everything as it warms. You could also pre-chop your veg! Alternatively, you could just go ahead and….

• Love your leftovers/make this a good-all-week salad: Romaine doesn’t hold up well once dressed. If you aren’t planning to eat the whole salad at one meal, you can swap the romaine out for kale. If swapping: after adding the kale and cabbage to the bowl, add a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of kosher salt, then use your hands to massage the kale for 30 to 60 seconds, until slightly softened and darker in color. This will let the salad hold up great in the fridge for up to 4 days! One caveat is that avocado will brown, so don’t add that if you’re prepping the salad ahead of time. Just top individual servings with it.

• Feeding 1 or 2: You could halve the whole recipe. Or, read the tip above to turn it into a good-all-week salad that will hold up dressed in the fridge so that you have lunch leftovers for days.

• Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free plain yogurt. Use DF feta or omit it. If you want briny flavor in place of it, you could add some chopped castelvetrano olives.

• Gluten-free: Use gluten-free orzo or see below for more sub ideas. Check that your Worcestershire is GF (not all are).

• Orzo: Israeli couscous or another tiny pasta like ditalini, small shells, or acini de pepe. For gluten-free, use a GF orzo, quinoa, or brown rice. Farro or couscous would also work well. If you’re swapping in a grain that isn’t cooked in a big pot of boiling water (for example, quinoa), see the “I’d rather cook the shrimp a different way” note above for alternative ways to cook the shrimp. You could also skip the grain altogether.

• Extra-virgin olive oil: Olive oil or a neutral cooking oil like avocado, grapeseed, or canola

• Lemon juice: Light-colored vinegar like white wine, apple cider, or rice vinegar

• Parsley: Basil or cilantro or a mix of both. I prefer parsley for this but either sub would work!

• Dill: Basil, cilantro, more parsley, tarragon

• Chives: More dill or scallions

• Garlic: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder or a thawed frozen cube of crushed garlic

• Dijon: Any smooth mustard. Or mayo.

• Worcestershire sauce: Vegan Worcestershire, an anchovy filet (or anchovy paste), soy sauce, or tamari

• Honey: Maple syrup or agave

• Greek yogurt: Plain yogurt, sour cream, labneh, or a dairy-free yogurt. Mayo would work but would make it richer.

• Shrimp: See the notes section above for lots of shrimp subs!

• Romaine: Any leafy green lettuce, kale (see the “make it a good-all-week salad” note above), or double the cabbage.

• Pre-shredded cabbage or slaw mix: 1/2 a head of any green cabbage thinly sliced, thinly sliced kale, or double the romaine

• Snap peas: Blanched or steamed peas or green beans, or chopped bell pepper for crunch

• Cucumber: Thinly sliced celery, chopped bell pepper, or omit

• Scallions: Chopped chives, pickled red onions, or omit

• Avocado: Omit if needed. For some alternative healthy fats, you could garnish your salad with a nut like toasted, salted pistachios or almonds.

• Feta: Cotija, goat cheese, grated Parm, or skip it

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds U-20 raw shrimp, peeled and deveined (thawed and patted dry if using frozen)
ingredients.name: U-20 raw shrimp
ingredients.note: peeled and deveined (thawed and patted dry if using frozen)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packed cup fresh parsley (leaves and tender stems) (about 1 1/2 to 2 ounces)
ingredients.name: packed cup fresh parsley (leaves and tender stems) (about 1 1/2 to 2 ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 packed cup fresh dill (fronds and tender stems) (about 1 ounce)
ingredients.name: packed cup fresh dill (fronds and tender stems) (about 1 ounce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice of 1 medium lemon (2 to 3 tablespoons)
ingredients.name: Juice of 1 medium lemon (2 to 3 tablespoons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 romaine hearts, chopped into small bite-sized (1/2-inch) pieces
ingredients.name: romaine hearts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10- to 12-ounce) bag pre-shredded cabbage or slaw mix (I love angel hair coleslaw here)
ingredients.name: pre-shredded cabbage or slaw mix (I love angel hair coleslaw here)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup snap peas, thinly sliced on a slight diagonal into thin strips
ingredients.name: snap peas, thinly sliced on a slight diagonal into thin strips

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 to 6 ounces feta, crumbled (about 1 to 1 1/2 cups)
