ingredients.name: feta, crumbled (about 1 to 1 1/2 cups)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water (use 2 big four-finger pinches of kosher salt ) to a boil over high heat.

While the water is coming to a boil, season 1 1/2 pounds peeled and deveined shrimp with a big pinch of kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper . If you’re feeling lazy, you can skip this step.
Drop 1 cup dry orzo in the boiling water and immediately set two timers:
Set one timer for the amount of cook time it says on your package of orzo (mine said 10 minutes).
Set a second timer for the amount of cook time that it says on your package of orzo MINUS 1 minute — this is when you’ll add the shrimp. (So I set it for 9 minutes.)

While the orzo cooks, stir it occasionally to prevent it from clumping together. When your shorter timer goes off, add the shrimp to the pot and stir gently to separate and submerge the shrimp. When the longer timer goes off and the shrimp have just turned opaque, drain the orzo and shrimp in a colander. If the shrimp still look translucent when your timer goes off, cook for another 10 to 20 seconds. Right when they turn opaque, drain — they’ll continue cooking from the residual heat. Shrimp cook very quickly and can turn rubbery if overcooked, so keep a close eye on them!

With the orzo and shrimp still in the colander, add a big drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, and a big pinch of kosher salt. Toss gently right away, then let cool for a few minutes. Give the orzo and shrimp a stir once or twice as it cools to release some steam and prevent clumping. Some of the orzo, lemon juice, and EVOO may slip through the holes in the colander — that’s OK!

While the orzo is cooking, start on your green goddess dressing. Add 1 packed cup parsley leaves and tender stems , 1/2 packed cup fresh dill fronds and tender stems , 1/4 cup roughly chopped chives , 1/2 cup Greek yogurt, 1 small peeled garlic clove , the juice of 1 medium lemon (2 to 3 tablespoons) , 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil , 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard , 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce , 1 teaspoon honey , and 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt to a blender. Blend until smooth and creamy but still flecked with herbs — you want to see little green bits throughout. Add a splash of water, if needed, to get it to a drizzle-able consistency. Taste and adjust if needed, blending in more kosher salt, lemon juice, and/or another small clove of garlic (if you’re a garlic-lover, you may want more garlicky flavor!) until it tastes bright and balanced.

Chop 2 romaine hearts into small, bite-sized pieces (about a 1/2-inch chop — the smaller the better since this is a chopped salad!) and add to a large serving bowl along with 1 (10- to 12-ounce) bag shredded cabbage .

Thinly slice 1 cup snap peas , cutting on a slight diagonal into thin strips. Chop 1/2 an English cucumber into small pieces (I quartered the cucumber lengthwise, then chopped into 1/3-inch pieces) and thinly slice 3 scallions (use both the green and white parts, only discarding the roots at the bottom). Add everything to the serving bowl, season with a big pinch of kosher salt , and toss to combine.

Add the cooled orzo and shrimp to the bowl, along with 1 diced avocado and 4 to 6 ounces of crumbled feta . Pour as much green goddess dressing as you’d like over top and toss to coat. I typically use all of it, but we all have different preferences here, so s tart with half and add more a little at a time until it’s perfectly dressed for your liking (you can always add more, but you can’t take it off once it’s on there !).
Serve immediately.

name: bourbon spritz
note: Prep time: 25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 English cucumber, sliced in half vertically, seeds scooped out and discarded
ingredients.name: English cucumber, sliced in half vertically, seeds scooped out and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons whipped cream cheese
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons whipped cream cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 32 slices very soft white sandwich bread (about 1 1/2 loaves depending on brand)
ingredients.name: very soft white sandwich bread (about 1 1/2 loaves depending on brand)

preparationSteps: Place 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts in a saucepan or skillet and cover with an inch of water. Season generously with kosher salt and pepper . Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer over low heat. Cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken registers at 165°F internally using a meat thermometer.
Slice 1/2 an English cucumber in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds (you can discard them). Using the largest hole of a box grater, grate the cucumber along with 1/4 of a sweet onion .
Let the chicken cool slightly, then finely chop it — it should resemble grains of rice in size.

In a large bowl, combine the chicken with the grated cucumber and onion. Add 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons whipped cream cheese, 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon mango chutney (if using), 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon dried dill weed, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of freshly cracked black pepper .
Taste and add more kosher salt or lemon juice if needed. The mixture should feel light and very spreadable.
Lay out the 32 slices of soft white sandwich bread and spread the chicken salad evenly over 16 of them. Top with the remaining bread slices.
Trim the crusts off the sandwiches, cut each sandwich into triangles (either 2 or 4 per sandwich), stack them high on a cake stand or platter to create a sandwich tower, and serve.

name: smoky mole chicken enchiladas with lime crema
note: Cook time: 45 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 4 chipotle peppers from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce (start with 2 and taste before adding more)
ingredients.name: chipotle peppers from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce (start with 2 and taste before adding more)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons roasted sesame seeds (or 1 tablespoon tahini)
ingredients.name: roasted sesame seeds (or 1 tablespoon tahini)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bell pepper (red, yellow, or orange), thinly sliced
ingredients.name: bell pepper (red, yellow, or orange)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, thinly sliced into bite-sized (1/2-inch thick) strips
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 to 10 large (roughly 10-inch) tortillas (I like flour because they’re easier to roll, but corn works, too)
ingredients.name: large (roughly 10-inch) tortillas (I like flour because they’re easier to roll, but corn works, too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded Monterey Jack or Mexican blend cheese (one 8-ounce bag)
ingredients.name: shredded Monterey Jack or Mexican blend cheese (one 8-ounce bag)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Water, as needed to reach drizzling consistency
ingredients.name: Water, as needed to reach drizzling consistency

preparationSteps: In a blender, add 3 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 2 chipotle peppers from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce, a heaping 1/3 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, a heaping 1/3 cup tomato paste, 3 tablespoons roasted sesame seeds, 3 tablespoons creamy peanut butter, 1 tablespoon chili powder, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon cumin . Blend on high until totally smooth, 30 seconds to 1 minute (or until all the chocolate chips are blended). Taste and add 1 to 2 more chipotle peppers if you want more heat. Set aside.
Preheat the oven to 375°F .

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet (like cast-iron) over medium-high heat. Add 1/2 a thinly sliced white onion and 1 thinly sliced bell pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden, about 5 minutes.

Add 1 1/2 pounds thinly sliced chicken breasts to the pan with the veggies. Season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add 1 cup of the mole sauce and stir so the chicken and vegetables are nicely coated.

Turn the stove off, leaving the chicken mixture in the skillet. Put a plate on the counter beside the stove, and the bag of shredded cheese beside the plate. Hold a tortilla in your hand, and use a spoon to scoop in about 1/2 cup of the enchilada filling . Sprinkle a little shredded cheese on top, roll it up, and place it seam-side down on the plate. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, placing them seam-side down on the plate and stacking them on top of each other as needed until all the filling is used. If your tortillas aren’t super fresh and are cracking (or if you are using corn tortillas), microwave them in a damp paper towel for 10-second increments to make them more pliable.

Spread about 1/2 cup mole sauce across the bottom of the now-empty skillet (no need to wipe it out — it’s OK if there are some chicken/veggie bits in there), then transfer the enchiladas to the skillet, snuggling them in tightly, seam-side down.

Pour the remaining mole sauce down the center of the enchiladas and around the edges of the skillet. Sprinkle the remaining cheese over top. Bake until the cheese is melted and golden and the sauce is bubbling, 15 to 20 minutes.

While the enchiladas bake, make the lime crema: In a small bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup sour cream, the zest and juice of 1 lime, and enough water to thin it to a drizzleable consistency (start with 1 teaspoon and add more a little at a time until it’s perfect).
Let the enchiladas cool for a few minutes. Use a spatula to gently cut around and lift each enchilada onto plates, then drizzle with lime crema, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve.

name: herby grilled steak with greek feta bruschetta
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes + 30 minutes to 2 hours for marinating the steak

• I don’t have a grill: Cook the steak (and bread) in a cast-iron skillet or grill pan over high heat, or broil on high for 4 minutes or so per side (less time needed for the bread!).

• What does “slicing against the grain” mean? You will see lines running through your steak — you do not want to cut with those lines, you want to cut perpendicular to them. Here’s a visual. If you’re using hanger steak, you’ll want to cut it into 3 shorter pieces lengthwise, then cut each smaller piece sideways against the grain.

• What to do with your leftover 3/4 onion: I know it’s annoying to only use 1/4 of an onion, but I don’t want it to overpower the bruschetta! I highly recommend going ahead and slicing the rest of the onion while you’re at it and pickling it — I love pickled onion on salads, nachos, quesadillas, grain bowls. Follow this how to ! Or, you could swap the onion for a shallot instead.

• Save time: You can skip marinating the steak in the dressing and instead just season it with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper. Rub it with a little olive oil, then grill as directed. Be generous with the dressing at the end!

• Gimme a grain/bulk it up: Any grain would be good on this plate — quinoa, any brown or white rice, farro, etc., but I think that cooked couscous mixed with a little lemon juice/zest, garlic powder, and olive oil would be A+. More ideas: cook the rice pilaf from this recipe (you’ll cook it on the grill!) or serve it with roasted baby potatoes. Or mix the bruschetta with some cooked orzo for a pasta salad base for your steak! I really love this idea, someone please do it and send me a pic. Another way to bulk the meal up would be to add an avocado to your bruschetta.

• Gimme more greens: Add a bed of arugula drizzled with olive oil and lemon juice to your plate. Or serve it all atop chopped romaine.

• Prep ahead: The dressing (with the onions added) can be made up to 3 days in advance. The steak can marinate for up to 2 hours. You can chop the vegetables for the bruschetta a few hours ahead of dinner, but wait to add the feta and dressing until closer to serving.

• Love your leftovers: Store the steak and bruschetta separately in airtight containers in the fridge. The steak is great cold or gently reheated (it keeps for up to 3 days), and the Greek bruschetta makes an excellent topping for toast, eggs, or grain bowls the next day.

• Make it an app: Top a bite-sized piece of grilled bread with a little Greek bruschetta and a steak bite on top. Or skip the steak and just make bruschetta to serve with store-bought crostini.

• Feeding kids: My kids LOVE this steak. And they’ve eaten some of the bruschetta, too! Add some fruit or a grain you know they love to their plates if you don’t think they’ll get their fill on the steak and veg.

• Vegetarian: Pan-fried marinated tofu would be amazing with the bruschetta. For that, press a cube of firm or extra-firm tofu to remove excess water. Cut it into cubes, add them to a Ziploc or wide bowl, and add the marinade portion of the dressing. Seal the bag or cover the bowl and let it marinate for 30 minutes (or up to a day), stirring every now and then so all the tofu gets marinated. When you’re ready to eat, heat a tablespoon or 2 of neutral oil over medium heat in a nonstick skillet and add the tofu. Let it sit for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden brown, then flip and repeat. Keep stirring until it’s all crispy and golden on the outside. Or you could grill tofu “steaks” of extra-firm tofu marinated in the dressing.

• Dairy-free: Use dairy-free feta or an avocado instead!

• Gluten-free: Use a gluten-free loaf of bread, or serve the steak and bruschetta over rice or another GF grain like quinoa, or with roasted potatoes.

• EVOO: Olive oil or a neutral oil like avocado or grapeseed

• Red wine vinegar: Another light-colored vinegar like white wine, sherry, or apple cider vinegar, or extra lemon juice.

• Lemon: There’s no sub for lemon zest, but you can add a little more vinegar — ideally white wine vinegar to add a little variety in flavor — in place of the juice.

• Dijon mustard: Any smooth mustard, or you could use a spoonful of mayo with a splash of Worcestershire.

• Garlic clove: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder per clove

• Parsley: Fresh basil, cilantro, chives

• Fresh dill: Fresh tarragon, mint, or extra parsley

• Skirt/flank/hanger steak : Any of these three are interchangeable with each other. Beyond that, flat iron steak is an excellent sub. Ribeye or NY strip work too but are pricier (you could def skip marinating those if you want!). Or sub in chicken (thighs or breasts), portobello mushroom, or tofu “steaks.” This bruschetta is also amazing with grilled or pan-fried salmon! See the grilling guide for cook times for many other types of meat.

• Dried oregano: Dried parsley, Italian herbs, Greek seasoning, marjoram, or 1 tablespoon minced fresh oregano

• 1/4 small red onion: 1 golf ball-sized shallot, or you could use 4 sliced scallions, or a handful of minced chives

• Cherry tomatoes: You can use larger tomatoes instead of cherry tomatoes, but scoop out and discard the insides so that your bruschetta isn’t too watery. If you can’t do tomatoes, you could use another fresh bell pepper or chopped roasted red pepper.

• Cucumber : Another bell pepper

• Red bell pepper: Yellow or orange bell pepper, or extra tomatoes and cucumber

• Castelvetrano olives: Any olives! Pepperoncini would also be nice.

• Feta: A block of feta is going to be creamier and more delicious than pre-crumbled feta, but you can definitely use pre-crumbled if it’s what you have in the fridge. Goat cheese, ricotta salata, shaved Parm, and vegan feta would all be good, too! Or skip the cheese.

• Loaf of bread: Store-bought crostini, pita bread, naan, crackers, or swap the bread out for a grain like couscous or rice.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 very small (or 1/2 large) garlic clove, finely grated
ingredients.name: very small (or 1/2 large) garlic clove

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small lemon, zested and juiced (2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice)
ingredients.name: small lemon, zested and juiced (2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley leaves and tender stems, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh parsley leaves and tender stems, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh dill fronds and tender stems, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh dill fronds and tender stems, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds skirt (or flank or hanger) steak
ingredients.name: skirt (or flank or hanger) steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 small red onion, finely chopped (about 1/4 cup)
ingredients.name: small red onion, finely chopped (about 1/4 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup cherry tomatoes, cut into eighths
ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 English cucumber, or 4 Persian cucumbers, finely chopped
ingredients.name: English cucumber, or 4 Persian cucumbers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces feta (from a block), crumbled into small pieces
ingredients.name: feta (from a block), crumbled into small pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 loaf good bread (sourdough or similar), cut into thick slices
ingredients.name: good bread (sourdough or similar)

preparationSteps: At least 30 minutes but up to 2 hours before cooking the steak, make the marinade/dressing: Using a microplane, grate 1 very small garlic clove (or half a large one) into a large jar. Zest and juice 1 small lemon (you want 2 tablespoons of lemon juice), adding both to the jar. Finely chop 1/4 cup parsley leaves and tender stems and 2 tablespoons of dill fronds and tender stems and add them to the jar along with 3/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil , 3 tablespoons red wine vinegar , 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard , and 1 teaspoon dried oregano . Season with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and several grinds of black pepper . Shake until well combined.

Place 2 pounds steak in a mixing bowl and season all over with 1 teaspoon kosher salt . Spoon roughly half of the dressing over the steak, turning the steak to coat it. Cover and let marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes or in the fridge for up to 2 hours. Don’t exceed a two-hour marinade — the texture of the steak gets weird. If your plans change, simply wipe the marinade off of the steak and cook it within 48 hours.

Finely chop 1/4 small red onion , add it to the jar with the remaining dressing, and leave the dressing on the counter. This step is worth doing in advance! It helps the onion soften, mellow, and soak up all that herby, lemony flavor. If you are prepping this more than two hours ahead, store it in the fridge.
When you’re ready to cook, preheat your grill to high heat for 10 to 15 minutes.

While the grill heats, make the bruschetta. Cut 1 cup cherry tomatoes into eighths. Finely chop 1/2 English cucumber , 1 red bell pepper , and 1 cup Castelvetrano olives and add to a serving bowl. Toss with a small pinch of kosher salt.

Cut 1 loaf bread into thick slices and generously drizzle both sides of each slice with extra-virgin olive oil . Place the bread directly onto your serving platter (this is the same plate you’ll use to serve — I don’t want you dirtying an extra dish!) . Bring the platter, along with the steak in its marinade, out to the grill.
Scrape your grill grates clean.

Remove the steak from the marinade, wiping as much off as possible, and place on the grill (discard this used marinade) . Close the lid and cook over direct heat for 3 to 5 minutes per side, flipping once halfway through. Peek underneath the steak to see if nice grill marks have formed. If so, it’s ready to flip. Keep the lid closed as much as possible.
Cook until the steak is nicely browned with grill marks and reaches your desired doneness (130°F for medium-rare, 140°F for medium, 150°F for medium-well).

At the same time, grill the bread slices over medium heat (just lower one of the grill’s burners to medium and cook it over that flame) , flipping once or twice, until golden with crisp edges and grill marks (remove them when they reach that visual — don’t let them burn!).
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let rest for 5 to 10 minutes. Cut the bread into smaller pieces, if desired.

While the steak rests, crumble 4 ounces feta on top of the chopped vegetables and add half of the remaining dressing (the dressing with onion that has been sitting on the counter) and toss. Taste and adjust, adding more dressing, kosher salt, and/or lemon juice until it tastes perfect. I used most of the dressing and added a nice big pinch of kosher salt.

Slice the steak thinly against the grain (see notes for a visual) and arrange on the serving platter. Spoon bruschetta over top and garnish with some chopped parsley and dill — I like tons of dill on here.
Serve immediately with the grilled bread.

name: honey harissa chicken bowls
note: Cook time: 45 minutes
preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.

Toss 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons harissa, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika together on the prepared sheet pan and spread into a single layer so that the chicken thighs are not touching each other.
Roast for 30 minutes. Check to make sure they have reached 165°F internally (they should have!), remove from oven, and let rest for 5 minutes.
Slice or chop, then serve in bowls on top of Fancy Rice and garnished with Lemon Honey Pickled Red Onions , Harissa Labneh , and any other optional extras you want (recipes below).

name: buttery balsamic pork chops and asparagus with crispy rosemary parmesan potatoes
note: Cook time: 45 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: A block of Parmesan cheese (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano), for grating
ingredients.name: A block of Parmesan cheese (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano), for grating

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch asparagus (medium-width if you have options), cut into 1-inch pieces on the bias (AKA on a diagonal), woody ends discarded
ingredients.name: asparagus (medium-width if you have options)
ingredients.note: cut into 1-inch pieces on the bias (AKA on a diagonal), woody ends discarded

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Dice 2 pounds of Yukon Gold potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes (this is small! Roughly half the length of the top joint of your thumb) and place them on a large rimmed sheet pan.

Mince 2 sprigs of rosemary . To do that, strip the leaves off of the woody stem, discard the stem, and mince the leaves. Add the rosemary to the sheet pan along with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder . Toss until the potatoes are evenly coated then spread them out into a single layer — they need a little breathing room or else they’ll steam. If your sheet pan isn’t big enough for the potatoes to not be touching, divide them between two sheet pans.

Roast for 15 to 20 minutes, until they start to turn golden. Take the potatoes out of the oven and use a metal spatula to scrape them off the bottom of the pan and give them a quick stir. Use a microplane or grater to grate a generous amount of Parmesan all over until all the potatoes are lightly covered. Don’t worry if some of the Parm falls between the potatoes onto the pan — those bits will melt and turn into extra crispy, golden pieces. Return the potatoes to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes, until the Parm melts and starts to get golden and crispy.
While the potatoes roast, cook the pork chops and asparagus: Season 2 bone-in pork chops all over with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper . Rub with 1 tablespoon olive oil .
Heat a 10- to 12-inch skillet (preferably cast iron, *not* a nonstick) over medium-high heat for several minutes, until a drop of water sizzles when it hits the pan.

While the cast-iron skillet is heating, prep your asparagus. Trim off and discard the bottom 1 1/2 inches of 1 bunch of asparagus to get rid of the woody stems. Line the trimmed asparagus up and cut them into 1-inch pieces, cutting on a bias (AKA on a diagonal).

Once the skillet is hot, add the pork chops and use a pair of tongs to press down firmly all over (you want the whole surface of the meat to make contact with the skillet). Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until that side is golden brown, then flip and use tongs to again press down all over. Add 2 tablespoons unsalted butter and 1 whole rosemary sprig to the skillet and (wearing your oven mitt!), use the handle to tilt the skillet to the side so that the melted butter collects. Use a spoon to scoop it up and pour it over the pork chops. Cook on the second side for another 4 to 5 minutes.

Use a meat thermometer to check the internal temperature of the pork. If the pork has reached 145°F (if you have a thin cut, it might already be there!), transfer it to a cutting board and cover loosely with foil or an inverted plate. If not, continue with the pork in the skillet.

Remove the rosemary sprig from the skillet and discard. Add the chopped asparagus all around the pork chops and season with a big pinch of kosher salt . Cover your skillet (you can use a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid big enough) and let it steam for 1 minute, until the asparagus is bright green and just starting to become tender.
Uncover the skillet and, again, check the pork’s internal temperature — remove it if it has reached 145°F. If not, it can stay in the skillet.

Use tongs to toss the asparagus and move the pork chops around, letting any liquid the asparagus may have released cook off until the pan goes from wet and steamy to mostly dry and sizzling again, about 2 minutes. If the pan still looks watery, increase the heat to high to help it cook off faster — once it does, return the heat to medium-high.

Add 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar , 3 teaspoons honey , and a few grinds of black pepper and cook, tossing the asparagus and flipping the pork chops, until the mixture bubbles rapidly and reduces into a glossy, lightly thickened glaze that coats the meat and vegetables, about 1 minute. Reduce the heat to low and add 1 tablespoon unsalted butter , swirling until it has melted and emulsified into the glaze.

Check your pork’s temperature again — if it’s at 145°F transfer the pork chops to a cutting board and let rest for 5 minutes. If you pulled your pork chops earlier and they’ve already rested, you can add them to the pan briefly to coat all over in the glaze.
Slice the meat off the bone, then cut into 1/2-inch slices against the grain.

While the pork rests, make the lemon garlic aioli. In a small bowl, mix together 1/2 cup mayonnaise, the zest and juice of 1 lemon , 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan. Taste! If it’s too lemony for you, add some more mayo. If it needs more salt, add another little pinch.

Serve the sliced pork with asparagus and crispy rosemary Parmesan potatoes. If you have some, sprinkle a pinch of flaky sea salt and a grind of black pepper over the meat and asparagus, then spoon some of the balsamic butter glaze over top so it seeps into the meat. Dip your potatoes into lemon aioli as you eat, or dollop the sauce over top of them.

name: gringa cochinita
note: Cook time: 4 hours (30 minutes active + up to 3.5 hours of inactive cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 pounds boneless pork butt, cut into 6 chunks
ingredients.name: boneless pork butt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons taco seasoning (or 2 tablespoons achiote paste, if you can find it!)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning (or 2 tablespoons achiote paste, if you can find it!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ripe tomatoes (such as Roma but anything works), roughly chopped
ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes (such as Roma but anything works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 habanero pepper, cut into 4 pieces (optional, but traditional — use gloves when handling!)
ingredients.name: habanero pepper
ingredients.note: cut into 4 pieces (optional, but traditional — use gloves when handling!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: A package of your favorite tortillas — I love the street taco size that many brands sell
ingredients.name: A package of your favorite tortillas — I love the street taco size that many brands sell

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: other taco toppings like avocado, cilantro, sour cream, cheese
ingredients.name: Optional: other taco toppings like avocado, cilantro, sour cream, cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 300°F.

Cut 3 pounds boneless pork butt into 6 big chunks. Do not trim off the fat. Place the pork in a Dutch oven. Rub all over with 2 tablespoons taco seasoning, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/8 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/8 teaspoon allspice, and 1/8 teaspoon ground cloves.
Roughly chop 1 white onion and 2 tomatoes and place them around/on top of the pork.

Squeeze the juice of 1 grapefruit, 2 oranges, and 2 limes over the pork. Cover tightly with a piece of parchment paper (tuck it tightly on top of the food), then cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and put in the oven. Cook for 3 hours, until the pork pulls apart easily. (Alternatively, cook on the lowest stovetop simmer for 3 hours — don’t lift the lid!)

Now make your pickled onions! Dice 1 large red onion . If using, cut 1 habanero into 4 pieces (be sure to wear gloves when handling — the capsaicin on the seeds and pith can burn your skin). Place them in a glass storage container and add the juice of 5 limes , 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon sugar. Cover the container, shake well, and set aside. They’ll be perfectly quick-pickled by the time the pork is done.

Remove the pork from the oven. Pick out any large white fatty pieces you see and discard them. Shred the pork using two forks right in the pot so it soaks up all of that braising liquid. If it is not easily pulling apart, re-cover it and place it back in the oven for another 30 minutes, or until it shreds very easily.
Taste and add more kosher salt if needed. Taco seasonings vary by brand, so everyone’s salt levels will be different. If needed, stir in kosher salt a small pinch at a time until it tastes delicious.
Serve in warm tortillas topped with the pickled red onions (and any other toppings you may want).
Enjoy immediately! These are juicy, drippy tacos — best to only make two at a time and keep going back for more.

name: indian-spiced chicken, mango crunch salad & coconut rice bowls
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes to 1 hour (depending on how efficiently you multitask!)

• Prep ahead: Good news as we get closer to the beautiful chaos that is summer: this recipe is great for prepping ahead! The dressing/marinade can be made days in advance and stored covered in the fridge — just give it a nice shake/whisk to reincorporate everything before using. You can marinate the chicken up to 6 hours in advance (or even overnight if that works better for you) in an airtight bag or container in the fridge. Make the coconut rice up to a day in advance and just reheat on the stove, adding splashes of water to loosen it up while it warms. You can pre-chop your cucumber days in advance, but wait to assemble the salad right before dinner so everything stays fresh.

• Love your leftovers: Leftover chicken and rice will stay good for up to 4 days stored in airtight containers in the fridge. If you don’t want to eat the same meal again, you could serve your leftover rice with sriracha sushi shrimp ! And the chicken would be good on top of any bagged or homemade salad for an easy lunch. If you have leftover mango salad, the cilantro will get a little soggy and the avocado will brown, but I’d definitely eat it the next day if it was still in my fridge!

• OK so, I didn’t wash my hands after I cut the jalapeño and I touched my eyes / another sensitive area and now they’re burning what do I do: Soak a clean rag with some milk. Put it over your eye and gently open to let a little milk seep in. Gross, I know! But it’ll help. I told you to wash your hands!! If you want to avoid this, you could also wear gloves while prepping the jalapeño.

• Feeding 1 or 2/freezer-friendly: You could halve everything… or you can cook the whole thing and freeze components for future you. You can freeze extra chicken breast fillets right in the marinade (thaw them overnight in the fridge). Cooked coconut rice freezes beautifully, too.

• I’m a spice lover: I really love the look and feel of slicing a jalapeño into rounds rather than removing the seeds and slicing it into batons like the recipe is written, BUT it is very spicy this way. If you know you like the heat of jalapeño seeds, cut it into rounds!

• I’m a grilling newbie : If this is the first time you’ll be grilling, watch and read my grill guide for tons of tips. If TLDR: Once your grill is piping hot, scrape it clean, and lightly oil the grates when you’re cooking a lean meat like chicken. Always grill with the lid closed (unless a recipe tells you not to).

• I don’t have a grill: Cook the chicken over medium-high heat in a cast-iron skillet or grill pan. Times will be about the same! Use your meat thermometer.

• Feeding kids: My kids love this coconut rice and grilled chicken. I reserved some plain cucumber slices and mango chunks for their plates!

• Vegetarian: Tofu would be so good here. If using, lightly squeeze a block of extra-firm tofu over the sink to remove excess liquid, then cut it into 5 long planks and add them to the marinade. Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and coat it lightly with avocado oil. Add the planks and cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden.

• Dairy-free & gluten-free: Already is!

• Frozen mango: You are, of course, welcome to use fresh mango if you’d rather. Grab 2 ripe mangos and cube them. If you can’t find mango, you could swap it for cubed pineapple, papaya, peaches, or strawberries.

• Red onion: Pickled onions (no need to soak them in water) or 3-ish thinly sliced green onions (AKA scallions — no need to soak them).

• Chicken breasts: Ideally you’re looking for “chicken breast fillets,” which are thin cuts of chicken breast as opposed to huge fat chicken breasts, which take much longer to cook. (If you have hawk eyes, you may notice in the video above that I used the big fat chicken breasts for that test — I like the fillets better!) If you can’t find fillets, you can cut thick chicken breasts in half through the center to form 2 thinner fillets, or use a meat mallet to pound them into even thickness, or just cook them as is and add more time. Chicken tenderloins would also work (cook them for 3 to 4 minutes per side) as would boneless, skinless chicken thighs (cook for 7 to 10 minutes per side). If you’re not in the mood for chicken, swap in 1 or 2 pork tenderloins (depending how much meat you want!) and grill for 8 to 12 minutes total, flipping every few minutes, until 145°F internally; shrimp — thread them onto skewers or use a grill basket and grill for 2 to 3 minutes per side; any steak (see the grill guide for cook time depending on the cut of steak you have); or tofu (see “vegetarian” note above).

• Lime: Lime juice is ideal here! If you have a citrus allergy, you can swap in a light-colored vinegar like white wine or red wine vinegar. There’s no good sub for the zest.

• Avocado oil: Olive oil or a neutral oil like grapeseed or canola. If all you have is EVOO, you can definitely use it, I just prefer a more neutral tasting oil for this so the spices don’t get buried.

• Garam masala: Curry powder, ras el hanout, or a DIY mix of cumin + coriander + cinnamon + cardamom

• Maple syrup: Honey, agave

• White rice: A long-grain white rice would work, just check the bag and adjust cook time as needed based on what you’re working with. Brown rice would do, but it’ll take more water and time (again, use the package as your guide for liquid ratio and cook time). You could ditch the idea of coconut rice and cook microwaveable frozen rice or any other grain like quinoa or farro. Or skip the grain and add shredded cabbage or arugula to the mango salad.

• Coconut milk: Light coconut milk may not be quite as tasty, but it will work. Or skip the coconut milk and cook the rice with only water (follow the package directions as to how much), stirring in lime zest at the end.

• Cucumber : Chopped bell pepper would give the salad some nice crunch in place of the cucumber. Chopped tomatoes would also be good. Or just skip it!

• Avocado : Omit if needed/desired

• Jalapeño : Serrano pepper, chili crisp, red pepper flakes, or omit

• Cilantro: If you’re a cilantro hater, you can sub it for another leafy green herb you love like parsley, mint, or basil. Arugula would also be great!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (from about 3 limes), plus zest from 1 lime
ingredients.name: fresh lime juice (from about 3 limes), plus zest from 1 lime

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast fillets (if you can’t find “fillets,” buy regular breasts and if they’re very thick, cut them in half through the center to make 2 thinner fillets)
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast fillets (if you can’t find “fillets,” buy regular breasts and if they’re very thick, cut them in half through the center to make 2 thinner fillets)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 jalapeño, halved lengthwise, seeded, and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: jalapeño, halved lengthwise, seeded, and thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: For serving: 1 more lime, cut into wedges
ingredients.name: For serving: 1 more lime

preparationSteps: If possible, the night before you plan to cook this dinner, transfer the 10-ounce bag of frozen mango chunks to the fridge so they can thaw. Alternatively, about 1 hour before cooking, leave the bag out on the counter. If you can’t/forgot to do either, put the mango chunks in a colander and run them under water until they thaw.

Thinly slice 1/2 red onion and add it to a serving bowl. Cover with a thin layer of water (just enough to cover the slices) and let it hang out while you prepare everything else — this will tone down the intensity of the onion’s bite.
Use a microplane to zest 1 lime and set the zest aside for later.

Make your dressing: In a jar (or small bowl), shake (or whisk) together 1/4 cup lime juice , 1/4 cup avocado (or any neutral-flavored) oil , 1 tablespoon maple syrup, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt , 1 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper .

Add 2 pounds of chicken breast fillets to a resealable bag or bowl along with 1/4 cup of the dressing. (I repeat: Only 1/4 cup of it! Set the rest of the dressing aside — you will use it later as a dressing for the salad!) Mix so that all the chicken is coated. Let it sit for 15 to 30 minutes at room temperature while you preheat the grill and make the rice.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat (400°F to 450°F).

Make the coconut lime rice: Add 1 1/2 cups short-grain white rice , 1 can full-fat coconut milk , 1 cup water , 1 tablespoon maple syrup , and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a medium pot. Stir to combine, then bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to the lowest heat possible on your stovetop, COVER, and cook for 15 to 17 minutes, until the rice is tender and all the liquid has been absorbed. Remove from heat and let the rice sit, covered, for at least 10 minutes. Right before serving, add the reserved lime zest and fluff the rice with a fork.

Now that your grill is heated: Scrape the grill grates clean, lightly oil them, and grill the chicken (with the lid closed!) for 5 to 7 minutes per side, until it’s nicely charred on the outside and reaches 165°F on the inside when measured with a meat thermometer. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then slice.

While the chicken is resting, drain the water from the onions. Thinly slice 4 Persian cucumbers , dice 1 large avocado , and roughly chop 1 bunch of cilantro (use both the leaves and tender stems, keeping the pieces big like lettuce leaves), adding all the veg to the bowl with the onion. Slice 1 jalapeño in half lengthwise, scoop out and discard the seeds and ribs using a spoon, then thinly slice. WASH YOUR HANDS so you don’t accidentally touch your eyeballs three hours from now and injure yourself.

To the bowl, add half or all the sliced jalapeño (depending on your spice preference), the thawed mango, and the remaining dressing and toss gently to combine. Taste! Add more kosher salt and pepper as needed.
Spoon the coconut lime rice into bowls and top with sliced chicken and heaps of mango salad. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing over the top.

name: charred corn & green onion miso pasta salad
note:
Cook time: 25 minutes

• My dressing is lumpy: Some miso pastes are thicker than others, but you want to make sure your miso is fully mixed into the dressing. It may take some muscle to get it nice and smooth! Just keep stirring.

• French fried onions? Oh yes. These are a totally optional, totally delightful garnish. I love the crunch they bring!

• Must have meat: Scroll back up and read the “wait, is this a full meal?” section above the recipe! Lots of ideas there.

• Prep ahead/take it to go/love your leftovers/meal prep it: You can make this pasta salad up to 3 days ahead of time and store it in the fridge in an airtight container. Like any good pasta salad, it’s delicious either cold right out of the fridge or at room temp. Given that, it’s great for lunches, picnics, dinners on the go, or cookouts!

• Feeding kids: If your kids are on high alert for spice, you can omit the hot honey and just drizzle it over adult servings. If they won’t touch pasta mixed with things, grab a handful or two of the plain cooked noodles for their plates.

• Vegetarian: Already is!

• Dairy-free: Use a DF sour cream or swap it for mayo.

• Gluten-free: Check the labels of white miso paste while you’re shopping to see if it has gluten. Miso master , a brand many grocers carry, is GF. Use a gluten-free noodle alternative, and skip the French fried onions.

• Soy-free: Soy is a common ingredient in miso paste, but here’s a soy-free sub!

• Sesame-free: Swap the sesame oil out for another like avocado or olive oil, and omit the seeds.

• Short noodles: Any short noodles work, such as farfalle (bow tie), fusilli, penne, gemelli, or cavatappi. I definitely prefer short noodles in my pasta salad but if you’re trying to cook your way through your pantry and only have long noodles, it’ll taste the same! It just won’t be as easy to eat. Sub in any type of noodle you need to if you can’t do gluten — just boil them per package directions.

• Fresh corn: If you’re sticking with corn, you can use 4 1/2 cups of canned (and drained), or thawed frozen corn. If you can’t do corn, you could swap in 2 to 3 cups of halved cherry tomatoes or grilled and chopped zucchini, squash, or red bell pepper.

• Scallions: Chives prepped the same way. Grilled or roasted red onion would also be great!

• Sesame oil: See the “sesame-free” note.

• Sour cream: Mayo is great!

• Miso paste: There’s not a good sub — we’re using a lot of miso! It’s available in the international aisle or refrigerated section of most grocery stores, we’ve also linked some you could buy online in the “ingredient spotlight” section, and see notes above for allergen info.

• Rice vinegar: Use all lime juice or apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. FYI that unless I’ve called for “seasoned“ rice vinegar, I always use regular/unseasoned.

• Lime : Just use more rice vinegar in place of the juice (there’s no sub for the zest so just omit it!).

• Hot honey : 1 tablespoon honey plus 1 1/2 teaspoons sriracha or gochujang. Or omit if you need to!

• Cilantro: Basil would be my top sub. Flat-leaf parsley would also be great.

• Toasted sesame seeds : Omit if needed.

• Flaky salt: Omit if needed.

• Bacon: See the “wait, is this a full meal?” section above the recipe for other suggestions, or keep it vegetarian!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 16 ounces short pasta (farfalle, fusilli, gemelli, or cavatappi)
ingredients.name: short pasta (farfalle, fusilli, gemelli, or cavatappi)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 ears of fresh corn (or 4 1/2 cups of canned or thawed frozen corn)
ingredients.name: of fresh corn (or 4 1/2 cups of canned or thawed frozen corn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 scallions (AKA green onions), thinly sliced, root ends discarded
ingredients.name: scallions (AKA green onions), thinly sliced, root ends discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest and juice of 2 medium limes (about 3 tablespoons fresh lime juice)
ingredients.name: Zest and juice of 2 medium limes (about 3 tablespoons fresh lime juice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon hot honey (or 1 tablespoon honey plus 1 1/2 teaspoons sriracha or gochujang)
ingredients.name: hot honey (or 1 tablespoon honey plus 1 1/2 teaspoons sriracha or gochujang)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch cilantro, leaves and tender stems finely chopped (about 1 cup chopped)
ingredients.name: cilantro, leaves and tender stems finely chopped (about 1 cup chopped)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 1 pound crispy cooked bacon, chopped
ingredients.name: Optional: 1 pound crispy cooked bacon

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional for garnish: French fried onions
ingredients.name: Optional for garnish: French fried onions

preparationSteps: Cook 16 ounces short pasta in heavily salted water until tender. Drain, and leave the pasta in the colander.

Meanwhile, char the corn and scallions: Cut the kernels off of 6 ears of fresh corn . Thinly slice 6 scallions. Heat a dry cast-iron skillet over high heat and add the corn kernels along with the white and light green parts of the scallions (reserve the dark green parts for later) and a really big pinch of kosher salt . We are aiming to char everything, so stir only every 2 to 3 minutes, until deeply golden in spots, 8 to 9 minutes total. The corn will pop and hiss — don’t be scared, you’re doing great!

Meanwhile, make the creamy miso dressing in a large serving bowl (large enough to hold the entire pasta salad): Whisk together 1/3 cup sesame oil, 1/3 cup sour cream, 1/3 cup white miso paste, 1/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, the zest and juice of 2 limes (about 3 tablespoons of lime juice), and 1 tablespoon hot honey until completely smooth.
Finely chop 1 bunch of cilantro (both the leaves and tender stems — you want about 1 cup) .

Add the charred corn and scallions, the reserved dark green parts of the scallions, the cooked pasta, chopped cilantro, and 2 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds to the bowl of dressing and toss to coat. (If you’re adding cooked crumbled bacon or another protein, stir it in now, too.)

Serve immediately at room temperature, or refrigerate and serve either chilled or at room temp within 3 days. When you’re ready to serve, sprinkle 1 teaspoon flaky salt over top. Option to add French fried onions as a garnish, too!

name: sheet-pan salmon with jammy tomatoes and peppers and polenta
note:
Cook time: 40 minutes

• I hate salmon: I know there are many of you out there! You can absolutely sub it for a white fish like halibut (or cod, tilapia, mahi mahi, swordfish, flounder, etc.). Bake those for 6 to 15 minutes (cook time varies widely based on thickness!), checking at the 6-minute mark for the first time. Or sub in peeled and deveined shrimp — they need about 6 to 9 minutes to roast at 400°F (they’re ready when they are opaque, pink, and curled into a “C”). You could also swap in chicken tenders or breasts — cook them for 15 to 20 minutes or 20 to 25 minutes, respectively, until they’ve reached an internal temp of 165°F. Or make it vegetarian — add a can or two of chickpeas that you’ve drained, rinsed, and patted dry to the sheet pan with the veggies. Add another tablespoon of olive oil as well as a little extra of each spice to make sure all the chickpeas are coated.

• Prep ahead: You can prep the vegetables and place them on the sheet pan up to a day ahead of time. Cover the pan and stick it in the fridge. When you’re ready to cook dinner, uncover the pan, add the seasonings, and stick it in the oven. The polenta can also be cooked a day in advance and stored covered in the fridge. Reheat it over medium heat, stirring and adding splashes of stock to loosen it back up as needed.

• Feeding kids: There’s nothing spicy about this meal, so no need to adjust for spice-averse eaters. My older boys aren’t into salmon, but Tav is!

• Gimme some greens: You could skip the polenta and serve the roasted fish and vegetables with some mixed greens or arugula dressed in olive oil, a little of the roasted lemon juice, and a sprinkle of flaky sea salt (or some Italian dressing!).

• Cooking for two : You can easily halve the fish and the polenta. You could also halve the veg, but I recommend cooking all of it! See the next note for ways to repurpose the leftovers.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be good stored in the fridge in airtight containers for up to 3 days. The peperonata-style vegetables are SO GOOD with just about anything. Serve them with rotisserie chicken and rice for an easy meal. Toss them with warm noodles. Pile them on top of a piece of crusty bread with some balsamic glaze. Delish! Leftover polenta can be used as a grain with any protein. And leftover salmon can be shredded and used in place of tuna in tuna salad , or served whole on top of a bagged salad for an easy lunch.

• Vegetarian/budget-friendly: Use chickpeas in place of salmon! See the “I hate salmon” note above for more info.

• Dairy-free: Use a DF Cheddar and plant-based butter. Or skip the cheese in the polenta, it’ll still be creamy. Or skip the polenta altogether and keep it fish + veg (option to add an extra bell pepper, more tomatoes, and/or sliced zucchini to bulk it up further). Or plate it with microwaveable frozen rice for a grain.

• Gluten-free: Make sure your stock doesn’t contain gluten (Better Than Bouillon is not certified gluten-free!). Otherwise, it’s naturally GF!

• Bell peppers: Any combo of red, orange, or yellow bell peppers would be good here. Or sub in a bag of sliced baby bell peppers. If you can’t do bell pepper, swap it for zucchini or summer squash sliced into half moons, or thickly sliced fennel or red onion.

• Garlic cloves: Use 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder (or onion powder) instead, or add 2 frozen cubes of pre-crushed garlic to the pan, no need to thaw.

• Lemon : The roasted lemon juice is sooo good here, but you could swap it with plain lemon juice or 2 tablespoons of a light-colored vinegar like apple cider or white wine vinegar.

• Cherry tomatoes: Chunks of ripe heirloom or roma tomato. If you can’t eat tomatoes, try one of the “loved this? cook that!” recipes listed above. I don’t trust subbing something else in for tomatoes here!

• Olive oil: EVOO, avocado oil, or a neutral oil like grapeseed or canola

• Smoked paprika: Regular paprika, chipotle powder, za’atar, or aleppo pepper though the latter will add some spice. Or just omit! You already get lots of great flavor from the roasted vegetables.

• Salmon: See the “I hate salmon” note above.

• Unsalted butter: Regular butter, crème fraîche, mascarpone, labneh, vegan butter

• Basil: Dill, chives, Italian parsley, or thinly sliced arugula (but I really love basil here!)

• Chicken broth: Veggie broth or water

• Polenta: Quick-cooking grits. If you came home with a tube of cooked polenta, scroll up to the “shopping note” section above the recipe for how to cook it. You could also skip the polenta or serve the fish and veg with rice instead or by themselves.

• Cheddar: Parmesan, Gruyère, fontina, goat cheese, DF Cheddar, or omit

ingredients.name: For the sheet-pan salmon, tomatoes, and peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small bunch fresh basil leaves, sliced into thin ribbons
ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth (or 4 cups water + 1 heaping tablespoon Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth (or 4 cups water + 1 heaping tablespoon Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup sharp white Cheddar cheese, grated
ingredients.name: sharp white Cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more to taste

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Thinly slice 1 orange bell pepper and 1 red bell pepper , smash 2 garlic cloves (and discard their peels), and slice 1 lemon in half. Add them all to your largest rimmed baking sheet along with 1 pound whole cherry tomatoes . Drizzle with 3 tablespoons olive oil and season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt , 3 to 5 cracks of black pepper (roughly 1/8 teaspoon but no need to measure!), and 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika . Toss everything together and spread into an even layer.
Roast for 15 minutes, until the tomatoes start to burst and the peppers begin to soften and get color around the edges.

While those are roasting, use a paper towel or clean dish towel to pat 4 salmon fillets dry. Season all over with a big pinch of kosher salt, a few cracks of black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil .

When the timer goes off, remove the sheet pan from the oven and scooch all of the vegetables to one side of the pan. Place the seasoned salmon fillets on the empty side (skin-side down, if yours have skin). Return to the oven and roast for 10 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork. For perfect doneness, use an instant-read thermometer on the salmon: 125-130°F for medium-rare, 135-140°F for medium (my fave), or 145°F for well done.

While the salmon cooks, make the polenta: Bring 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth (or 4 cups water + 1 heaping tablespoon Better Than Bouillon) to a boil in a medium pot. Once boiling, slowly whisk in 1 cup quick-cooking polenta . Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, for 5 to 7 minutes, until thickened and creamy.
Meanwhile, use the smallest holes on a box grater to grate 1 cup of sharp white Cheddar cheese.

When the polenta is creamy, stir in 3 tablespoons unsalted butter , the grated Cheddar cheese, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt . Taste. Does it need more salt? If so, add another pinch, stir, and taste again — repeat as needed until it’s absolutely delicious. Keep on the lowest heat and stir occasionally until ready to serve, adding a splash of broth to loosen, if needed.
Slice 1 bunch of basil leaves into very thin ribbons (this is called a chiffonade).

When the salmon comes out of the oven, smash the tomatoes and garlic to release their juices. Squeeze 1 of the roasted lemon halves over the salmon and the second half over the tomatoes and peppers, then discard them (try to catch the seeds as you squeeze, or pick them out if they fall!). Add 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter and half of the sliced basil, then stir everything together until a saucy, glossy mixture forms.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the salmon and roasted vegetables. Garnish with the remaining fresh basil.

name: sheet-pan bbq chicken meatballs, broccoli, and blistered tomatoes
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes

• Love your leftovers/freezer-friendly/double it: Leftovers will be good for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge, and they make great lunches. Reheat in the microwave. You could also freeze any leftover meatballs! Maybe even double the meatball portion so you can stock your freezer with them? If you’re freezing cooked meatballs, let them cool completely before transferring to a freezer-safe bag and store in the freezer for up to 3 months. I microwave frozen meatballs in a microwave-safe bowl covered with a damp paper towel/dish towel for 2 minutes, or until warmed through. You could also freeze them uncooked if you’d prefer. Thaw them in the fridge then cook as directed in the recipe.

• Make it an app/riffs: Read these tips right above the recipe!

• I don’t want to dirty my knife: Just tear the spinach into little pieces instead.

• Can I use regular rice? Of course! If you can’t/don’t want to cook frozen rice in the microwave, cook 1.5 cups dried rice (any kind!) per package directions. Once it’s ready, add the chopped spinach and butter, stirring until wilted and melted, then add the cheese, milk, etc., stirring until melted and well combined.

• I’m out of parchment paper: No prob, just grease the pans with oil.

• Prep ahead: You can go ahead and form the meatballs and prep the vegetables, putting them on the sheet pans. Cover the sheet pans tightly with plastic wrap and store them in the fridge. When you’re ready to cook, uncover and throw them in the oven.

• My sheet pans won’t fit side-by-side in the oven: Put both oven racks as close to the center of the oven as they’ll go. Put one sheet pan on the top rack toward the left, and the other on the bottom rack toward the right. The goal is to avoid stacking them right on top of each other.

• Feeding kids: My kids love these meatballs and the roasted broccoli! You can skip the spinach in the rice if they wouldn’t eat it because of the green bits.

• Vegetarian : Use a plant-based ground meat alternative.

• Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free shredded cheddar in the meatballs and rice. If you hate DF cheeses, here’s what I’d do for the meatballs (though I have not tested it this way!): omit the cheese, add 2 extra tablespoons panko, and 1 tablespoon mayo. That should keep their bulk without drying out. For the rice, use a thick DF milk like unflavored oat and DF cheese and butter. Or just keep the rice simple with wilted spinach and DF butter.

• Gluten-free: Use GF breadcrumbs and make sure the barbecue sauce you buy is certified gluten-free (many are, but not all! Stubb’s is!).

• Ground chicken or turkey: Any ground meat (turkey, chicken, beef, pork, venison) or vegetarian ground meat. If you’re using meat high in fat like pork, sausage, or 80% lean/20% fat beef, you can skip the EVOO drizzle on top of the meatballs since they’re fattier than the lean meat the recipe’s written with.

• Egg: Make a flax egg: Mix 1 tablespoon ground flax plus 3 tablespoons water. Stir together and let it sit for 5 minutes before using. Or you could use 2 tablespoons of mayo.

• Sharp cheddar: A smoky cheddar would be excellent here. Other cheeses that’d work are Pepper Jack, Monterey Jack, Gouda, or even Parm.

• Panko: GF panko, rice breadcrumbs, Italian breadcrumbs, or almond flour/meal will all work. You could even blend up a slice of bread (the staler it is, the better) and use that instead. Or crushed up Ritz crackers!

• Barbecue sauce: See the riffs section above the recipe for ideas.

• Garlic powder: 3 cloves of fresh minced garlic

• EVOO: Olive oil or a neutral oil like avocado or grapeseed oil

• Broccoli: Zucchini chunks, green beans, broccolini, or cauliflower florets

• Cherry tomatoes: Grape tomatoes, diced roma tomatoes, roasted red peppers from a jar, or just omit the tomatoes if you can’t eat them.

• Baby spinach: Regular spinach, finely chopped kale, arugula (though it’ll add some peppery flavor so maybe don’t use this if you’re feeding kids), or just skip the greens!

• Unsalted butter: Salted butter or a DF butter sub. Skip it if you have no butter.

• Whole milk: 2% milk, cream (but cut it by half), an unsweetened, unflavored DF milk, or omit

• Frozen white rice: Frozen brown rice, frozen rice blend, frozen quinoa, frozen cauliflower rice, or see the “can I use regular rice instead?” note above if you don’t want to use frozen.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups freshly grated sharp cheddar cheese, divided
ingredients.name: freshly grated sharp cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup BBQ sauce (I love Stubb’s), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: BBQ sauce (I love Stubb’s), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound broccoli florets (you can buy a bag of florets or cut a head of broccoli into florets, whichever works!)
ingredients.name: broccoli florets (you can buy a bag of florets or cut a head of broccoli into florets, whichever works!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (10-ounce) bags frozen white rice (see notes if you only have dry rice)
ingredients.name: frozen white rice (see notes if you only have dry rice)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper (seriously, do this now before your hands get dirty!) .
Use a box grater to grate 2 cups of sharp cheddar cheese and set it aside.

In a large bowl, combine 1 pound ground chicken or turkey , 1 large egg , 1 cup of the grated sharp cheddar , 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs , 1/4 cup BBQ sauce , 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder , and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt . Use your hands to mix everything together, then form 12 golf ball-sized meatballs and place them on one of the prepared baking sheets as close together as possible without touching. Drizzle the tops of the meatballs with extra-virgin olive oil.

Add 1 pound broccoli florets and 1 pint whole cherry tomatoes to the second baking sheet. Drizzle with 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil and season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder . Toss to coat, then spread the vegetables into an even layer.

Roast both sheet pans on the center rack for 17 to 20 minutes , until the meatballs are cooked through (they should reach an internal temperature of 165°F) and the broccoli is crispy around the edges.

While the meatballs and vegetables roast, finely chop 2 cups baby spinach and add the spinach to the bottom of a large microwave-safe bowl. Add 2 tablespoons unsalted butter on top of the spinach. Cut open 2 (10-ounce) bags frozen white rice and pour the frozen rice over the spinach and butter.

Cover the bowl tightly with a large plate and microwave according to the package instructions, increasing the cook time by 50%, until the rice is piping hot and the spinach has wilted. For example, if your package directs you to microwave the rice for 3 minutes, you will microwave it for 4 1/2 minutes!

While the rice is still piping hot, add the remaining 1 cup of grated cheddar, 1/4 cup whole milk , 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt , 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder , and a few cracks of black pepper . Stir vigorously until creamy, melty, and fully combined. If needed, microwave in 30-second increments, stirring between each, until the cheese is fully melted.
Build bowls with the cheesy spinach rice, meatballs, broccoli, and tomatoes. Finish with a drizzle of BBQ sauce and serve.

name: george's perfect steak caesar sandwich
note: Cook time: 35 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 anchovy fillets packed in oil, finely chopped
ingredients.name: anchovy fillets packed in oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds New York strip steak (2 to 3 one-inch-thick steaks)
ingredients.name: New York strip steak (2 to 3 one-inch-thick steaks)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large focaccia loaf, cut into 4 even pieces
ingredients.name: large focaccia loaf

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large romaine hearts, thinly sliced (about 4 cups)
ingredients.name: large romaine hearts, thinly sliced (about 4 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 head of radicchio (you will only use half of it), cored and thinly sliced (about 2 cups)
ingredients.name: of radicchio (you will only use half of it)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup pre-sliced pepperoncini, drained (if you can only find whole pepperoncini, that’s OK!)
ingredients.name: pre-sliced pepperoncini, drained (if you can only find whole pepperoncini, that’s OK!)

preparationSteps: Remove 2 pounds New York strip steak from the fridge. Pat both sides dry with paper towels, and season all over with kosher salt and black pepper. Let it rest at room temperature for 20 minutes. We’re going to multitask and start making the rest of the recipe during this time!

Meanwhile, make the Caesar aioli. Add 1 1/4 cups mayonnaise to a large bowl. Use a microplane or the smallest holes on a box grater to grate 2 small garlic cloves and the zest of 1 lemon into the bowl. Add 1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan , 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper . Finely chop 3 anchovy fillets and add them to the bowl. Mix well and set aside for now.
Cut 1 large focaccia loaf into 4 equal pieces (roughly 5-by-6 inches each). Cut each piece in half horizontally to make 8 slices. Place them cut-side up on a large sheet pan.

Thinly slice 2 large romaine hearts (you want about 4 cups of lettuce). Cut 1 head of radicchio in half, then remove the core from and thinly slice one half of it (you want about 2 cups). Save the other half of the radicchio for another use. If you have whole pepperoncinis instead of pre-sliced, slice them now, too. Leave everything on the cutting board for now.

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat until slightly smoking. Rub 2 tablespoons of avocado oil all over the steaks, then add the steaks to the skillet. Cook over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until a golden-brown crust forms. If you try to flip the steak and it’s stuck to the skillet, that means it hasn’t formed a sear (crust) yet. Give it another 30 seconds and try again!

Meanwhile, smash 3 garlic cloves and remove their skins. Flip the steaks over, lower the heat to medium, then add 3 tablespoons butter and the smashed garlic cloves to the skillet. Using an oven mitt to protect your hand, tilt the pan and use a spoon to scoop up and pour the garlicky butter over the steaks for another 2 to 3 minutes. When the steaks reach your desired doneness, transfer them to a cutting board to rest. To check for doneness, use a meat thermometer to check the internal temperature: For medium-rare, cook until 125°F (if you like it on the rarer side) or 130°F (if you like it a little less red). For medium, cook it between 135°F and 140°F.
While the steaks rest, turn the broiler on high.
Spread half of the Caesar aioli evenly across the cut side of the focaccia slices then sprinkle 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan onto each slice.

Add the sheet pan to the oven and broil for 1 to 2 minutes, until the Parm is golden crispy, then promptly remove. DO NOT WALK AWAY FROM THE OVEN! Turn the light on, sit in front of it, and watch for the cheese to turn golden and crispy — do not let your bread burn!

Stir 2 tablespoons of lemon juice (from the lemon you zested earlier) into the aioli (this turns the Caesar aioli into a Caesar dressing!). Add the sliced romaine, radicchio, and 1/2 cup sliced (and drained) pepperoncini to the bowl with the dressing, and toss to coat.

Cut the steak into thin slices against the grain (aka perpendicular to the direction of the lines you can see on the steak). Evenly divide the steak slices over each bottom piece of focaccia. Top each with French fried onions , pepperoncini Caesar salad, and the top piece of focaccia. Serve whole or sliced in half!

ingredients.name: large handful pickled carrots (drain them first!)

preparationSteps: First, make the pickled carrots: Place 1 cup (240 mL) boiling water, 1/2 cup (120 mL) rice wine vinegar, 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, and 1 tablespoon kosher salt in a large bowl and whisk well to dissolve the sugar and salt. Add 2 large carrots , peeled and cut into matchsticks, and let them sit at room temperature for 2 hours. Leftovers can be stored in the brine in a jar in your refrigerator for up to a month.

Then make your sandwich: Place 3 tablespoons mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons chili garlic sauce, and 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice in a small bowl and season generously with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Stir the mixture together and then divide it between the two sides of 1 halved ciabatta roll , spreading it out so it completely covers the bread. Layer a few very thin slices of your favorite ham , 1 large handful fresh cilantro sprigs, and 1 large handful pickled carrots (drain them first!) on one half of the roll. name: good-all-week minty dilly kale lentil feta salad
note: Prep time: 30 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large bunch lacinato (aka Tuscan/dino) kale (about 10 ounces), thinly sliced
ingredients.name: lacinato (aka Tuscan/dino) kale (about 10 ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5-ounce jar pitted Castelvetrano olives, drained and chopped
ingredients.name: pitted Castelvetrano olives

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup dill fronds and tender stems, thinly sliced, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: dill fronds and tender stems, thinly sliced, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, thinly sliced, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: fresh mint leaves, thinly sliced, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions (aka green onions), thinly sliced
ingredients.name: scallions (aka green onions)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional if you love sweet and savory salads (I do!): 4 dates, chopped, and 1 apple, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: Optional if you love sweet and savory salads (I do!): 4 dates, chopped, and 1 apple

ingredients.rawIngredient: 16 ounces pre-cooked lentils, often found in the refrigerated aisle (or 1 cup dry black or green lentils, cooked — see notes section for how to cook them, if using)
ingredients.name: pre-cooked lentils, often found in the refrigerated aisle (or 1 cup dry black or green lentils, cooked — see notes section for how to cook them, if using)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup roasted pistachios, chopped, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: roasted pistachios, chopped, plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Wash, de-rib, and thinly slice 1 large bunch of lacinato kale . Put the kale in a large serving bowl and add a big pinch of kosher salt . Massage the kale (aka squeeze it with both hands) 5 to 10 times, until slightly softened.

Prep the following vegetables, adding them to the bowl while you work. Thinly slice 3 celery stalks . Drain then chop a 5-ounce jar pitted Castelvetrano olives . Thinly slice 1/2 cup dill fronds and tender stems , 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves , and 1 bunch of scallions (use both the white and green parts of the scallions — only trim off and discard the root tip ends). If using, chop 4 dates and thinly slice 1 apple (reminder that this is optional!).

Add 16 ounces cooked lentils , 8 ounces crumbled feta, and 1/2 cup chopped pistachios to the bowl, then squeeze the juice of 1 lemon over everything (catching the lemon seeds as you go, if you’re not using a lemon press).

Make the dressing: To a large jar, add all the ingredients ( 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt ), then cover tightly and shake to emulsify. Taste and add a little more of any ingredient the dressing needs to taste perfect to you ! (Does it need more tang? Add a little lemon juice or vinegar. More flavor? Add kosher salt. More sweetness? Add honey.)

Add your desired amount of dressing and toss everything until well combined and coated with dressing. Take another bite after it’s all melded for a few minutes. Does it need more salt? A splash of vinegar? Don’t stop seasoning until it’s delicious. Serve with some more chopped fresh herbs and pistachios on top.

name: butternut squash soup + ham and cheese biscuits: ham and cheese biscuits
note:
Cook time: 20-30 minutes

• Jazz up your soup: (from the start, or jazz up the leftovers by adding a smaller amount of these ingredients) Curried Butternut Squash Soup: Blend in 1 can coconut milk, 2 tablespoons red curry paste (to start since spice levels vary), 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, and the juice of 1 lime. Miso-Ginger Butternut Squash Soup: Blend in a 2-inch piece of fresh ginger (no need to peel) and 2 tablespoons miso (I like white miso). What else? Leave your ideas! Leave a comment

• I have leftover roasted garlic: If you didn’t add the whole second head of garlic, spread your leftovers onto bread and make it into a grilled cheese! Or add it to a homemade salad dressing. Or eat it plain to boost your immune system.

• I wish it were sweeter: This is sweet enough for my taste but feel free to blend in a teaspoon or two (or more to taste!) of honey or maple syrup if you’d like!

• Make ahead: Like I said in the headnote, this is a great meal to make days before you plan to eat it! You can store the soup in the fridge in the pot you blended it in with the lid on for up to 2 days — or up to 4 days in an airtight container. Store the biscuits for up to 2 days in the fridge in an airtight container. Reheat the soup over low on the stovetop (add a splash more broth or stock if it’s thicker than you want after sitting in the fridge!), and heat the biscuits in a 400°F oven for 5 minutes.

• Double it/freezer-friendly: Double this whole meal and freeze half of it!! It doubles perfectly. Once it has fully cooled, pour leftover soup into Ziploc bags, lay them flat on a baking sheet, and put the baking sheet in the freezer. Once they’re frozen, you’ll have flat bags of soup easy to store in the freezer for a day up to 3 months from now.. Thaw in the fridge overnight then reheat, following the instructions above in the “make ahead” note.

• No, I so sorry, you cannot prep the biscuit dough the night before: The baking powder will deactivate and they’ll be flat. You could make it up until the step when you stir in the milk though!

• If you think of it… pop your butter in the freezer for a few minutes before you grate it. But that’s not necessary — using it fresh out of the fridge will be fine.

• If you have… carrots, a bell pepper, or some celery in the crisper that need to be used, throw them on the baking sheet and roast them up with the squash and garlic. Blend them right in!

• What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking. Make the soup. It’s easy, promise! If making biscuits feels like too much for tonight… just toast a slice of yummy cheese on bread and dip it while you eat! Or throw some croutons in the bowl!

• Vegetarian : Use veggie stock instead of bone broth and omit the ham from the biscuits.

• Dairy free: Good Culture makes a lactose-free cottage cheese, if that’d help. Or to omit it from the soup altogether: soak 1/2 cup cashews (any kind) in the stock while the squash roasts then blend them in with the soup for that creaminess and extra protein. You may need to use a high-powered standing blender in lieu of the immersion blender if you’re blending nuts. One other option: blend in a can of drained, rinsed white beans (like cannellini or navy) instead of the cottage cheese. For the biscuits, use a DF stick of butter and a plant-based milk alternative like unsweetened almond or soy milk.

• Gluten-free : Use a gluten-free 1 to 1 baking flour .

• Butternut squash: A pureed carrot, cauliflower, or sweet potato soup would be great! Or you can use a mix of veggies (see the “if you have…” note above for more ideas). You want about 2 1/2 pounds of veg total.

• Garlic : I love the depth of flavor roasted garlic gives this soup! But you could also roast a red or yellow onion cut into wedges.

• EVOO : Olive oil or a neutral cooking oil

• Chicken bone broth: Turkey bone broth would be my second choice after chicken. You could try beef bone broth, but I’d probably opt for veggie or chicken stock first. A regular broth would also work, or water + Better than Bouillon (1 teaspoon per 1 cup of water).

• Cottage cheese: 1/2 cup Greek or plain yogurt, 1/3 cup sour cream or crème fraîche, or see the dairy-free note above for a DF options.

• Vinegar : Again, I like balsamic or apple cider best but anything will do! Or lemon juice.

• All purpose flour: Whole wheat flour, white wheat flour, pastry flour, or bread flour but you might need a tiny bit more milk.

• Baking powder: A very rare occurrence here but there’s really no sub! Gotta have it. You can technically combine cream of tartar and baking soda but do you have cream of tartar laying around?! If so: combine ¼ teaspoon of baking soda with ½ teaspoon of cream of tartar to replace one teaspoon of baking powder.

• Black pepper : Lemon powder or a few shakes of red pepper flakes would be great (unless you’re cooking for spice wimps). Or omit.

• Butter : You can use a dairy-free butter stick, but we need some butter!

• Gruyère : White cheddar or literally any hard cheese or DF cheese or omit

• Chopped ham: Chopped turkey or prosciutto or cooked bacon or pancetta would be good. Or omit for cheese biscuits!

• Milk : I used whole milk but any milk or cream will do the trick! If you use cream you’ll likely need a smidge more than 1/2 cup to hydrate the flour. You could also use a plant-based milk alternative like unsweetened almond or soy.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons very cold butter (so straight from the fridge)
ingredients.name: very cold butter (so straight from the fridge)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces Gruyère (or white cheddar or literally any hard cheese)
ingredients.name: Gruyère (or white cheddar or literally any hard cheese)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup finely chopped ham (any kind! country, deli, honey-baked!)
ingredients.name: finely chopped ham (any kind! country, deli, honey-baked!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup milk plus more for brushing the biscuits
ingredients.name: milk plus more for brushing the biscuits

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together 1 cup flour , 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper . Grate 4 tablespoons cold butter and 4 ounces Gruyère on the largest hole of a box grater and toss to combine with the flour. Use your fingers to pinch the butter and cheese into the flour a bit (spend about 15 seconds pinching)
Stir in 1 cup finely chopped ham . Then stir in 1/2 cup milk until you have a rough, shaggy looking dough.
You can either simply scoop the dough in heaping spoonfuls onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, or you can laminate the dough, which is a fancy word for how to make flaky, layered biscuits.

To do so: Plop all of the dough down onto the parchment-lined baking sheet. Sprinkle with flour. Use your hands to smoosh the dough down into a rough rectangle. Fold it over itself to make a square. Repeat this process 3 times, ending by smooshing the dough into a 1-inch tall square or rectangle (watch the video I shared above the recipes for a visual of this!).

Cut the dough into 8 square biscuits. Separate and spread them out on the baking sheet. Brush the tops with milk (if you don’t have a pastry brush, just dab a paper towel into milk and pat it on top). Optional but delicious: Grind a little more pepper on top of your biscuits. Maybe sprinkle some freshly grated Parm or a little leftover grated Gruyère on top too if you want to go for it?!

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden brown and puffed up. Enjoy immediately! (Or, if you’re baking these ahead of time, only bake them for 12 minutes, then store in the fridge and reheat in a 400°F oven for 5 minutes when you’re ready to eat!)
