note: Cook time: 50 minutes (10 minutes active, 40 minutes inactive)

ingredients.name: reduced-sodium chicken stock (I use water + Better Than Bouillon!), plus more as needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) jar julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil, drained
ingredients.name: julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 minced garlic cloves (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
ingredients.name: minced garlic cloves (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Add 5 cups reduced-sodium chicken stock to a Dutch oven (or another oven-safe pot) and bring to a boil over high heat. Stir in 2 cups arborio rice , 1 DRAINED jar of sun-dried tomatoes, 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Cover the pot (you can use a sheet pan if yours doesn’t have a lid) and transfer to the middle rack of the oven. Bake for 40 minutes.

Remove from oven and vigorously stir in 1/2 cup heavy cream and 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (use a microplane or the smallest holes on a box grater to grate it). Add more stock, if needed, to achieve the consistency you like (I usually add 1/2 to 1 cup more stock to get a looser consistency). Season to taste with kosher salt and pepper — you might need a lot more salt depending on the saltiness of your stock and Parm. If you’re drinking a bottle of white wine, stir a splash of that in, too!

name: <3 easy-but-fancy valentine's menu <3: perfect crab cakes
note: Cook time: 50 minutes (15 minutes to prep, at least 30 minutes to refrigerate, and 5 to 7 minutes to cook)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 lemons, 1 zested and juiced, 1 cut into wedges
ingredients.name: lemons, 1 zested and juiced, 1 cut into wedges

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces crab meat (ideally lump crab meat but anything refrigerated works)
ingredients.name: crab meat (ideally lump crab meat but anything refrigerated works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into 4 thin slices
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

preparationSteps: Prep a large rimmed baking sheet by spraying it with nonstick cooking spray (or rubbing it with butter).

In a large bowl, mix 1 large egg, 2 tablespoons mayonnaise, 1/2 teaspoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon minced chives, the zest of 1 lemon, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Add 8 ounces crab meat , using your fingers to very gently feel for any remaining bits of hard shell as you add it to the bowl (discard any that you find). Try not to break up the chunks of crab as you sift through it!

Gently stir in about half of the 10 crushed-up crackers to start, then keep adding more until the crab cakes hold together just enough to form 4 crab cakes and place them on one side of the greased baking sheet. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 4 hours maximum.
Preheat oven to broil on high.
Uncover the baking sheet and place a very skinny slice of butter on top of each crab cake.
If you are also cooking crispy garlicky broccolini (recipe below), you will add it to the empty half of the sheet pan now.

Broil on the top rack for 5 to 7 minutes, until the crab cakes are golden-brown all over. The crab is already cooked through so no need to worry about that — as long as they’re crispy on the outside and warm throughout, they’re ready.
Serve crab cakes over risotto with broccolini on the side. Add a lemon wedge to each plate for squeezing over top.

name: <3 easy-but-fancy valentine's menu <3: crispy garlicky broccolini
note: Cook time: 10 to 12 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch broccolini, tough bottoms trimmed and discarded
ingredients.name: broccolini, tough bottoms trimmed and discarded

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to broil on high.
Cut the tough bottoms off of 1 bunch broccolini (not the whole stem — just the very bottom tough part). If there are any fat stalks, cut them in half lengthwise through the stalk.

Add the prepped broccolini to a greased rimmed baking sheet (if you’re making the crab cakes, too, add the broccolini to the empty side of the sheet pan) along with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 grated garlic cove, the zest of 1 lemon, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt . Toss, using your hands to really get the broccolini evenly coated in oil, garlic, zest, and salt. Lay the broccolini out flat.
Broil on the top rack for 5 to 7 minutes.
If the crab cakes are golden-brown but the broccolini needs more time, transfer the crab cakes to a plate and keep cooking the broccolini until it’s ready.
The broccolini should be crispy on the outside and tender inside.

name: a back-to-school meal plan (with 5 new recipes!): chicken sausage, spinach, and white cheddar egg bake

ingredients.name: fresh baby spinach (or 10 ounces frozen spinach

ingredients.name: white Cheddar cheese, shredded (about 2 cups)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 275°F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Heat 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully add 12 ounces sliced chicken sausage and 1 diced red bell pepper . Cook, stirring occasionally, until sausage is browned on both sides and pepper is softened, about 6 to 7 minutes. Add the baby spinach and cook until wilted (if using fresh) or heated through (if using frozen). Season to taste with kosher salt and black pepper.

In a large bowl, whisk together 12 large eggs , 1/2 cup whole milk, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes until well combined.

Spread the sausage and vegetable mixture evenly in the prepared baking dish. Scatter 4 ounces of cream cheese cut into tiny pieces and sprinkle 1 1/2 cups shredded white Cheddar cheese over top. Pour the egg mixture over everything. Top with remaining 1/2 cup shredded white Cheddar cheese .
Bake for 1 hour, or until the center is set and the top is golden brown. A knife inserted in the center should come out clean.
Let cool for 5 minutes before slicing and serve warm.

name: a back-to-school meal plan (with 5 new recipes!): good-all-week chop salad
note:
Prep time: 30 minutes
Cook time: 0 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano or Italian herbs
ingredients.name: dried oregano or Italian herbs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15 ounce) can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: cannellini beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large bunch kale, ribs removed and leaves chopped
ingredients.name: kale, ribs removed and leaves chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 rotisserie chicken, skin removed and meat shredded
ingredients.name: rotisserie chicken, skin removed and meat shredded

preparationSteps: Make the marinated beans by whisking together 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil , 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar , 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano or Italian herbs, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt , and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large bowl. Add 1 can of drained cannellini beans and toss to coat. Let marinate for at least 30 minutes or overnight in the refrigerator.

Prepare the thousand island dressing by stirring together 1/2 cup mayonnaise , 2 tablespoons ketchup , 2 tablespoons sweet pickle relish , 1 tablespoon white wine vinegar , 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder , and 1/4 teaspoon onion powder in a small bowl or jar. Season with kosher salt and black pepper to taste . Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.

For the salad, chop 1 large bunch of kale leaves and add the chopped kale to a large salad bowl along with a pinch of salt . Using your (clean!) hands, massage (AKA squeeze) the kale 10 times, or until the leaves become slightly wet feeling and darker in color.

Shred the meat from 1 rotisserie chicken , dice 1 English cucumber , and chop 6 ounces of Gruyère cheese , and add them all to the bowl of massaged kale. Add the marinated beans and toss everything together.
When ready to eat, portion out the desired amount and dress with the thousand island just before serving.

name: a back-to-school meal plan (with 5 new recipes!): creamy chicken enchilada stew
note:
Prep time: 10 minutes
Cook time: 40 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12 to 16 ounce) jar green enchilada sauce (or salsa verde)
ingredients.name: green enchilada sauce (or salsa verde)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (15 ounce) cans cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: cannellini beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16 ounce) bag frozen corn, preferably white corn
ingredients.name: frozen corn, preferably white corn

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups kale, ribs removed and finely chopped
ingredients.name: kale, ribs removed and finely chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces cream cheese, room temp, cubed
ingredients.name: cream cheese, room temp

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional garnish: diced avocado , chopped fresh cilantro , sour cream , extra shredded cheese, crushed tortilla chips , lime wedges
ingredients.name: Optional garnish: diced avocado , chopped fresh cilantro , sour cream , extra shredded cheese, crushed tortilla chips , lime wedges

preparationSteps: Take your cream cheese out of the fridge so it can come to room temp!

Add 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth , 1 jar green enchilada sauce (or salsa verde), 1 1/2 to 2 pounds chicken thighs, 2 drained and rinsed cans of cannellini beans , 1 can diced green chiles (no need to drain), 1 bag frozen corn, 2 cups of finely chopped kale, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano to a large pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 30 minutes.

After 30 minutes, reduce heat to low and transfer the chicken to the cutting board. Use two forks to shred the chicken (or chop it if that feels easier), then return it to the pot along with 4 ounces of cubed room temperature cream cheese and 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese , stirring until the cheese is melted and the soup is creamy.
Remove from heat and stir in 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice . Taste and season as needed with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper .
Serve hot in bowls. Garnish with diced avocado , chopped cilantro , sour cream , extra cheese , crushed tortilla chips , and lime wedges , if desired.

name: a back-to-school meal plan (with 5 new recipes!): sheet-pan gnocchi with sausage meatballs and toasted shallot and tomato butter sauce
note:
Prep time: 10 minutes
Cook time: 30 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh minced oregano leaves or 1 teaspoon dried oregano
ingredients.name: fresh minced oregano leaves or 1 teaspoon dried oregano

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano, divided
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (ideally Parmigiano Reggiano

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: Just like with any sheet-pan gnocchi, if you want this to be saucy , add a big dollop of store-bought pesto on top. Burrata would also be delicious here!
ingredients.name: Optional: Just like with any sheet-pan gnocchi, if you want this to be saucy , add a big dollop of store-bought pesto on top. Burrata would also be delicious here!

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set your largest sheet pan out on the counter.

Squeeze the meat out of the casings of 1 pound Italian sausage a little at a time right into your hand and roll into rough meatballs, about 1 inch in diameter (1 inch is about the size of your top thumb joint). As you make the meatballs, add them to your sheet pan.

Thinly slice 1 large shallot and add it to the sheet pan too, along with 2 pints cherry tomatoes , 1 pound potato gnocchi (nope, you don't have to cook it first!), 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil , 1 tablespoon fresh minced oregano leaves (or 1 teaspoon dried oregano), 1 teaspoon kosher salt , 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper , and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder .
Use your hands to get in there and toss to evenly coat everything. If any of the gnocchi feels dry, add a little more EVOO and mix some more.
Place on the center rack of the oven and roast for 25 to 30 minutes.
Taste, and add more salt as needed. Different sausages can be more or less salty, so we only added a base amount to start.

Add 3 tablespoons unsalted butter and 1/4 cup grated Parmesan to the sheet pan and stir until incorporated. Serve with the rest of the Parm sprinkled on top. If desired, add a dollop of something creamy like pesto or burrata to each serving.

name: a remixed easy-but-fancy spring menu: whipped pistachio feta dip
note: Prep time: 10 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, you can throw some of that in there, too)
ingredients.name: packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (if you have dill, mint, or basil, you can throw some of that in there, too)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup toasted pistachios (buy them shelled — aka, without their shells)
ingredients.name: toasted pistachios (buy them shelled — aka, without their shells)

preparationSteps: In a food processor (ideal) or a blender, blend 1 block of feta cheese (I cut it into quarters before I add it), 1 packed cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems (and a little dill, mint, or basil if you have it) , 3/4 cup toasted pistachios, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup plain yogurt, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and the juice of 1/2 lemon together until chunky smooth. If you’re using a blender, you can use the tamp (if yours has one!) or a spoon to push and scrape the feta down as needed.

Taste. I needed to add about 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt at this point, but this will totally depend on how salty your feta and pistachios are. I love lemon flavor, so I also wound up adding the juice from the other half of the lemon.
Serve along with crudités (raw bite-sized veggies like carrot sticks, cucumbers, and cauliflower florets) and/or store-bought pita chips .

name: a remixed easy-but-fancy spring menu: maple dijon baked ham
note: Cook time: 30 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons whole grain mustard or 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard (I love Maille brand)
ingredients.name: whole grain mustard or 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard (I love Maille brand)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Place 1 cooked 6- to 8-pound, spiral-sliced, bone-in ham in a baking dish with high sides.

Meanwhile, whisk all glaze ingredients — 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup maple syrup, 3 tablespoons whole grain mustard (or 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard), and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon — together in a small pot. Bring glaze to a boil over medium-high then reduce to medium-low and simmer, stirring frequently, for 3 minutes.
Brush half of the glaze all over the ham and down into the slices. Bake for 10 minutes.
Remove the ham from the oven and paint with the second half of the glaze. Bake for 10 more minutes. Tent with foil until serving to keep it warm.

name: a remixed easy-but-fancy spring menu: poppy seed rolls
note: Cook time: 15 to 20 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of flaky sea salt
ingredients.name: Big pinch of flaky sea salt

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a small baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, stir together 4 tablespoons melted unsalted butter, 1 teaspoon poppy seeds, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard .
Brush the butter mixture over the tops of a 12-pack of King’s Hawaiian rolls (keep them all together). Sprinkle with a big pinch of flaky sea salt .

Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, until golden brown. Keep a close eye on them, they’ll go from golden-brown to burnt quickly! Once cool enough to handle, separate the rolls and arrange them on a serving plate. Serve along with whole grain and/or Dijon mustard to make little ham sandwiches.

name: a remixed easy-but-fancy spring menu: lemon-parm quinoa lite kale salad
note: Cook time: ~25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup lemon juice (roughly the juice of 2 small lemons)
ingredients.name: lemon juice (roughly the juice of 2 small lemons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup uncooked quinoa (option to omit the quinoa since we’re serving farro with this spring menu, too, but the quinoa is so good! If you’re omitting it, use less dressing)
ingredients.name: uncooked quinoa (option to omit the quinoa since we’re serving farro with this spring menu, too, but the quinoa is so good! If you’re omitting it, use less dressing)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups water (plus 1 heaping teaspoon of any flavor of Better Than Bouillon, if you have some)
ingredients.name: water (plus 1 heaping teaspoon of any flavor of Better Than Bouillon, if you have some)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup golden raisins or dried cranberries
ingredients.name: golden raisins or dried cranberries

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup roasted and salted shelled pistachios (or almonds or pepitas), chopped
ingredients.name: roasted and salted shelled pistachios (or almonds or pepitas)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional: 1 cup of any fresh chopped soft green herbs you might have available (such as basil, parsley, or cilantro)
ingredients.name: Optional: 1 cup of any fresh chopped soft green herbs you might have available (such as basil, parsley, or cilantro)

preparationSteps: Make the lemon vinaigrette: Add all ingredients ( 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 cup lemon juice, 1 heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme or oregano, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of black pepper ) to a large jar and shake vigorously until combined. Adjust seasoning to taste. As always, that is the most important part of making a dressing — my perfect dressing is not the same as yours! Add more vinegar to make it more acidic, more honey to make it sweeter, more oil to make it thicker and less acidic, more salt to make the flavors pop, etc.

Make the quinoa: Add 1 cup uncooked quinoa and 1 1/2 cups water (option to add 1 heaping teaspoon of Better than Bouillon OR to sub the water out for any kind of stock) to a small pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 13 to 15 minutes, until all of the liquid has been absorbed. Remove from heat but keep the lid on for an additional 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. You’ll use 2 cups of COOKED quinoa in this recipe and have about a cup left over. Let the leftovers cool completely then store them in an airtight container in the fridge for later use this week.

Add 16 ounces chopped kale to a large serving bowl and season with a big pinch of kosher salt and pepper . Use your hands to massage the kale until it JUST starts to feel damp — so squeeze it between your fists about 10 times. If you come across any pieces of thick stem while you’re massaging, discard them. Add 2 cups cooked quinoa, 1 bag shredded carrots, 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese, 1 cup golden raisins, and your desired amount of dressing.
Toss to combine. Add more dressing as needed until your greens are coated to your liking. Garnish with more Parm, a sprinkle of chopped nuts, and fresh herbs, if you have some.

name: a remixed easy-but-fancy spring menu: roasted asparagus farrotto
note: Cook time: 15 minutes active, 50 minutes total

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups farro (pearled or semi-pearled, if you can find it, but any kind works)
ingredients.name: farro (pearled or semi-pearled, if you can find it, but any kind works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound medium-width asparagus (aka not the really skinny kind, not the really fat kind — about the width of your pinky finger)
ingredients.name: medium-width asparagus (aka not the really skinny kind, not the really fat kind — about the width of your pinky finger)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup basil leaves, finely chopped, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: basil leaves, finely chopped, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup dry white wine (or the juice of 1 small lemon)
ingredients.name: dry white wine (or the juice of 1 small lemon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (4 ounces) shredded white Cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded white Cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.

In a heavy-bottomed OVENPROOF pot, warm 1 tablespoon EVOO over medium-high heat. Cook 1 finely diced yellow onion for 4 minutes, then stir in 1 1/2 cups farro and 4 minced garlic cloves and cook for an additional minute, stirring frequently. Pour in 1 quart (4 cups) low-sodium chicken stock , stir, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, turn off the stove, cover the pot, and place it on the center rack of the oven (or on the bottom rack, if your pot is too tall). Bake for 30 minutes.

While it’s baking, trim 1 1/2 inches off the bottom of 1 pound asparagus to get rid of the hard, fibrous ends. Discard those ends. Cut the trimmed asparagus into bite-sized pieces, 1 1/2 to 2 inches long.

Remove the pot from the oven and carefully turn the lid upside down, so that the handle is pointing down into the pot. It’s OK if it touches the farro! It’s even OK if it touches the bottom of the pot. Add the cut asparagus to the top of the lid along with 1 tablespoon EVOO, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper. Carefully toss to coat.
Return the pot to the oven for an additional 10 minutes.

Remove the pot from the oven and carefully remove the lid. Place the pot over medium heat on the stovetop and stir in half of the roasted asparagus, 1 cup frozen peas, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup finely chopped basil leaves, 1/3 cup dry white wine, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 cup shredded white cheddar cheese, and 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until everything is saucy and combined and the farro is a risotto-like consistency, 3 to 5 minutes. If it gets too thick, add another splash of water. If it’s still thin, crank up the heat and just keep stirring!

We haven’t seasoned the farro at ALL yet because every brand of stock, Cheddar, and Parmesan have different salt levels. So now, it’s time to taste and adjust the seasoning accordingly. I needed to add about 1/2 teaspoon of salt and several grinds of fresh black pepper. Keep tasting and seasoning until it’s perfect.
Throw the remaining asparagus on top , along with a big sprinkle of Parmesan, basil, and freshly ground black pepper.

name: a remixed easy-but-fancy spring menu: honey roasted carrots with burrata
note:
Cook time: 50 minutes (10 minutes active, 40 minutes inactive)

• How do I time this if I’m making it for a post-church Easter meal? This is a perfect menu to make since it’s so prep ahead-able, and the ham just needs to be warmed (it is pre-cooked!). Let the carrots come to room temperature while you are at church. Before church, make the ham glaze and unwrap the ham and put it in the baking dish. You can pour half the glaze on now or wait until right before it goes into the oven after church. Cover the ham and pop it in the fridge. Right when you walk in the door, uncover the ham and stick it in the oven (once heated). Enlist someone to help you in the kitchen and let the others snack on the feta dip (maybe stock up on some other apps, too, if you’re worried people are going to be really hungry) and have a cocktail while you bake the ham and rolls, rewarm the farrotto, dress the salad, and finish off the carrots.

• What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking: Use a store-bought Bitchin’ sauce or hummus instead of making your own whipped feta, and omit the quinoa from the salad. If you’re omitting the quinoa, use a little less dressing.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will be good for 3 to 4 days stored in airtight containers in the fridge. Here are delicious ways to use them up: Dice up ham and add it to the farrotto. Add sliced ham to poppy seed rolls. Toss any leftover roasted carrots and/or diced ham into the quinoa and kale salad. If you have a ton of leftover ham, you can freeze it! Wrap the sliced ham in plastic wrap, then place it in a freezer-safe bag or container and use, ideally, within one to two months. Leftover salad will stay good dressed in the fridge for up to four days stored in an airtight container. It’s a good-all-week salad!

• Vegetarian: Read the ham swaps section above the recipe.

• I’m cooking for Passover: Omit the rolls, farrotto, and pita chips (you could swap the pita for matzo crackers). If you want the menu to work for a traditional Passover seder, swap the ham for lamb or a whole chicken. Additional swaps may be needed based on your family's level of observance and traditions. For example, some families avoid legumes and seeds. And if you're keeping kosher, avoid serving dairy and meat at the same meal.

• Dairy-free: You can sub the whipped feta out for a DF version like Violife OR you can serve an app that’s inherently dairy-free instead like hummus or guacamole. Use sticks of plant-based butter instead of regular throughout. Violife’s DF feta would be great crumbled over the carrots as a DF sub for the burrata! Or just omit it from a portion of the carrots, for those who can’t eat dairy. For the farrotto, swap the Cheddar and Parm out for dairy-free versions, or cut the cheese and sprinkle in some nutritional yeast for some umami instead. You may want to add splashes of a dairy-free heavy cream for added creaminess, too. The salad would still be great without the Parm (or you could use a DF Parm).

• Gluten-free: Serve GF crackers and/or crudités with the whipped feta. Double check that your mustard doesn’t have gluten (most don’t!). Use a gluten-free roll sub because King’s Hawaiian do indeed have gluten (or the people who have to avoid gluten can just skip a roll). Swap the farro for arborio rice or short-grain brown rice to make that dish gluten-free. Start checking around the 25-minute mark in case your swapped grain is cooking faster. TLDR: Use a gluten-free roll (or the gluten-sensitive diners can skip them!) and swap the farro out for rice. Also check your stock to make sure it’s GF certified.

• Nut-free: Either omit the pistachios or, if seeds are OK, swap them with pepitas throughout.

• Seed-free: If seeds are an issue, omit the poppy seeds from the rolls. Ask if quinoa is doable (it is technically a seed). If quinoa is a no go, omit it and use less dressing.

• whipped pistachio feta dip

• maple dijon spiral ham

• poppy seed rolls

• lemon-Parm quinoa and kale salad (we’re omitting the chicken for this menu)

• roasted asparagus farrotto

• roasted carrots with burrata and pistachios

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds carrots, cleaned and sliced in half vertically
ingredients.name: carrots, cleaned and sliced in half vertically

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup roasted, salted pistachios, finely chopped
ingredients.name: roasted, salted pistachios

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Wash and slice 2 pounds carrots in half vertically. You don’t need to peel them, but you can if you want to. Drizzle with 3 tablespoons oil, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin , and use your hands to really get in there and toss everything together to evenly distribute the ingredients.
Spread the carrots into an even layer and roast for 40 minutes. Meanwhile, take the burrata out of the fridge to let it come to room temperature, and finely chop 1/4 cup pistachios.

Transfer the roasted carrots to a platter. Tear the burrata ball into several pieces and place them on top. Scatter the chopped pistachios over top. Finish with a drizzle of honey and extra-virgin olive oil.

name: eastern nc ribs with ranch butter smashed potatoes: eastern north carolina style glazed ribs
note:
• How do I test ribs for doneness: The meat should pull back from the bone ends by about 1/4 inch, a toothpick (or fork) should slide into the meat between the bones easily, and the internal temperature of the meat should reach between 195 and 203°F.

• I wanna grill! If you’d rather finish your ribs on the grill, you can do that instead of the 450°F oven! Throw them meat-side down on the grill over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, until caramelized. But if you’re cooking the smashed potatoes, you may as well use the oven so you can roast them at the same time.

• Prep ahead: Find tips for this in the “prep-ahead game plan” section above the recipe.

• Love your leftovers: Leftover ribs will be great for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container in the fridge. For best reheating results, let them come to room temp, brush them with any leftover sauce, wrap them in foil, and bake at 250°F for about 10 to 15 minutes or just until warmed through.

• Feeding kids : Omit the cayenne and halve the red pepper flakes if your kids are spice averse kids! My kids love these!

• Vegetarian : Make tofu “ribs.” Freeze 2 blocks of extra firm tofu (I know that sounds random bit it helps with texture). Press the block(s) to remove any excess moisture then slice them into rectangular “ribs” 3/4- to 1-inch thick. Coat them in dry rub and let them sit in the fridge for up to 8 hours. Brush them with the sauce then bake at 275°F for 45 minutes. Raise the temp, brush again, and bake for 10 minutes or so, until a golden crust forms.

• Dairy-free/gluten-free : The ribs are dairy-free as is. For gluten-free, double check that the ketchup you buy is GF.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (3- to 4-pound) racks baby back ribs or spare ribs
ingredients.name: racks baby back ribs or spare ribs

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes (halve this if spice-averse)
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes (halve this if spice-averse)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper (omit this if spice-averse)
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper (omit this if spice-averse)

preparationSteps: Place 2 (3- to 4-pound) racks of baby back ribs on a foil-lined baking sheet (it’s OK if they overlap a little bit) and remove the membrane from the ribs. The membrane is the thin, silvery-white layer on the bone side. Use a knife to loosen one corner, then grab it with a paper towel or clean dish towel (this is important for keeping your grip!) and pull it off completely. It will probably come off in multiple pieces rather than one big piece (like mine did in this video). That’s normal, keep going!

Make the dry rub: Mix all rub ingredients ( 1/4 cup light brown sugar, 1 heaping tablespoon kosher salt, 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons garlic powder, and 2 teaspoons onion powder ) together in a bowl. I honestly just eyeball all of these measurements and dump them straight onto the ribs — you really can’t mess it up.

Pat the ribs dry and coat in dry rub, massaging it in. Place them meat-side up and let them sit at room temperature for 30 minutes, or overnight in the refrigerator, uncovered, if you’ve got the time.

Make the vinegar sauce: Stir all the ingredients ( 1 cup apple cider vinegar, 2 tablespoons ketchup, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper ) together in a small pot. Bring it to a boil, then reduce to a simmer over medium-low heat and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until thickened. Remove from heat and set aside.
Preheat oven to 275°F.

Remove the ribs from the refrigerator (if they were in there). Wrap each rack of ribs tightly with foil, set them on the baking sheet, and place the baking sheet in the oven. Bake spare ribs for 3 hours and baby back ribs for 2 hours.

If you are serving your ribs with ranch butter smashed potatoes (recipe below), boil, cool, and smash the potatoes while the ribs are slow cooking in the oven. You can also make the tangy slaw (recipe below) now and refrigerate it until dinner time.

Remove the ribs from the oven and carefully open the foil (watch out for hot steam!). A paring knife should slide in and out of the meat between the bones easily — if it doesn’t, re-wrap them and cook for 30 more minutes, or until it does.

Increase the oven temperature to 450°F. Remove the top layer of foil and brush the ribs generously with vinegar sauce. If there’s a lot of liquid on your pan, pour it off, then use a clean dish towel or paper towel to dry it off (if you don’t, the foil will burn). Return to the oven, UNCOVERED, for 10 to 15 minutes, until edges are caramelized and slightly charred. Remove from oven and brush with more sauce. Let rest for 10 minutes.
If you’re making the potatoes, they’ll cook in the 450°F oven at the same time as the ribs! Keep cooking them while the ribs are resting, for 20 to 25 minutes total, or until crispy.
Cut between bones and serve immediately with extra vinegar sauce on the side (and the potatoes and tangy slaw, if making).

name: eastern nc ribs with ranch butter smashed potatoes: ranch butter smashed potatoes
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes

• I’m cooking these with the ribs: Add the smashed ranch butter potatoes to the oven when you raise the temp to 450°F and return the ribs for their final sear. The ribs will finish first — keep the potatoes in for another 5 or 10 minutes until they are golden brown and crispy.

• Don't skip the boiling step: This ensures that the potatoes are creamy inside before getting crispy outside. I tried to slow-roast them in the oven with the ribs and it simply wasn’t as delicious.

• More smashing = more crispy: Really press them down for maximum surface area and crispy edges!

• Gluten-free: Most ranch seasoning packets are GF but double check! If needed, make your own (recipe in the subs section).

• Dairy-free: These are delicious DF! Use plant-based butter or olive oil instead of regular butter. Use DF Parm or nutritional yeast instead of regular Parm. And use the DIY ranch seasoning blend below.

• Prep ahead/love your leftovers: Keep leftovers stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. They reheat beautifully in a 450°F oven, they get crispy all over again!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds small Yukon Gold or baby potatoes
ingredients.name: small Yukon Gold or baby potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (to add to the boiling water)
ingredients.name: kosher salt (to add to the boiling water)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup grated (ideally freshly grated) Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: grated (ideally freshly grated) Parmesan cheese

preparationSteps: Place 2 pounds small Yukon Gold or baby potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water. Add 1 teaspoon kosher salt . Bring to a boil and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until fork-tender (AKA, until a fork easily slips in and out). Drain and let cool for 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450°F (same temperature as the final rib sear, if you’re making the recipe above!) .

Place the potatoes on a large baking sheet. Place another baking sheet on top and smash down until the potatoes are about 1/2 inch thick. Don't worry if they break apart — those tiny bits are a part of the magic. If you don’t have another baking sheet, you can use a potato masher or large fork to do this instead.

Melt 4 tablespoons unsalted butter in the microwave (in a microwave-safe bowl) in 20-second increments, stirring in between. Once melted, stir in 1 packet (1 ounce) ranch dressing mix. Drizzle the ranch butter over the smashed potatoes, making sure to get it into all those crispy edges.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until edges are golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven and immediately sprinkle with 1/4 cup chopped fresh chives, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and a big pinch of flaky sea salt. Serve immediately.

name: eastern nc ribs with ranch butter smashed potatoes: tangy slaw
note:
Prep time: 3 minutes

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers will stay good for up to 4 days stored in the fridge in an airtight container.

• Save time: Skip this recipe and buy store-bought slaw. Or skip the slaw entirely!

• Dairy-free/gluten-free/vegetarian : Already is. If you want to make it vegan, use vegan mayo.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons vinegar sauce (reserved from the ribs recipe above)
ingredients.name: vinegar sauce (reserved from the ribs recipe above)

preparationSteps: Add 14 ounces coleslaw and a pinch of kosher salt to a large bowl and massage to soften the cabbage slightly. Stir in 2 tablespoons mayonnaise and 2 tablespoons vinegar sauce. Adjust seasoning to taste. Want it tangier? Add a splash of apple cider vinegar!
Cover and refrigerate until you’re ready to eat.

name: easy-but-fancy summer grilling menu: a pitcher of strawberry margaritas
note: Prep time: 15 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups lime juice (you’ll need to juice about 16 limes for this!)
ingredients.name: lime juice (you’ll need to juice about 16 limes for this!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 to 1/2 cup strawberry jam (or any flavor jam)
ingredients.name: strawberry jam (or any flavor jam)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup cold water (I know it feels weird to add water but just trust)
ingredients.name: cold water (I know it feels weird to add water but just trust)

preparationSteps: Combine all ingredients ( 2 cups blanco tequila, 2 cups lime juice, 1 1/2 cups Cointreau, 1/4 to 1/2 cup strawberry jam, and 1/2 cup cold water ) in a jar (or pitcher), shake (or stir), and refrigerate until party time, up to 24 hours in advance.
Serve in glasses with salted rims that are filled to the brim with ice.

*If you’re new to margaritas: Use a lime wedge to wet the rim of your glass (so buy 3-4 extra limes when you’re shopping, then cut them into wedges before the party). Pour salt (kosher salt, never table salt — you want a coarse grain!) onto a plate, then shove the rim of the glass into the salt until it’s coated. Fill all the way to the brim with ice and pour in your cocktail!
**I like to keep bottles of Topo Chico (or any club soda) by the drink station so that people can cut their margarita, if they so choose!

name: easy-but-fancy summer grilling menu: grilled brie and grapes
note: Cook time: 1 hour total (20 minutes prep time, 30 minutes marinating time, 8 minutes cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 tablespoons olive oil, divided, plus more to oil the Brie
ingredients.name: olive oil, divided, plus more to oil the Brie

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 clusters seedless red or green grapes
ingredients.name: clusters seedless red or green grapes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (12- to 14-ounce/340 to 397 g) wheel Brie cheese
ingredients.name: wheel Brie cheese

preparationSteps: Whisk together 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar , 3 tablespoons olive oil , 1 minced garlic clove , 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 teaspoon crushed fennel seeds, and a pinch of red pepper flakes in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper , gently toss 2 to 3 clusters seedless grapes in the vinaigrette, and let sit for 30 minutes, tossing the grapes occasionally.
Preheat a gas or charcoal grill to medium-high heat (400ºF to 450ºF) and lightly oil the grates.

Place the sliced baguette in a large bowl, drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil , and toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper . Drizzle 1 wheel of Brie cheese with olive oil and rub it around to coat. Remove the grapes and RESERVE THE LEFTOVER VINAIGRETTE!

Place the crostini, grapes, and cheese on the grill. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning occasionally, until the crostini are toasty and charred. Remove the crostini from the grill to a platter and rub a clove of garlic on the toasted bread for extra flavor. Continue to cook the grapes for 3 to 5 minutes, until they are lightly charred. Remove grapes to the platter with the toasted bread. Continue to grill the cheese, turning as needed, until there are grill marks and the cheese is soft but not falling apart, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Add to the platter.
When ready to serve, drizzle the grapes and cheese with the reserved vinaigrette and serve with the crostini.
*Save time: Instead of individually making and grilling crostini, you can just grill the entire baguette then thinly slice it!
We’re including this as its own section so you don’t overlook it. Grab a few options — regular, BBQ, salt and vinegar, Doritos — whatever! They’ll double as both an app and side.

name: easy-but-fancy summer grilling menu: grilled caesar salad with garlic croutons
note: Cook time: 40 minutes (5 minutes prep time, 35 minutes cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh lemon juice (from 2 lemons)
ingredients.name: fresh lemon juice (from 2 lemons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 slices French bread, torn into small pieces (about 1 ½ cups/70 g)
ingredients.name: French bread, torn into small pieces (about 1 ½ cups/70 g)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper (optional)
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper (optional)

preparationSteps: Preheat your grill to medium heat (350ºF to 400°F) and lightly oil the grates.

TO MAKE THE DRESSING: Put all the ingredients ( 1/4 cup mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons anchovy paste, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 2 cloves garlic, smashed, 1/2 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese, kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste ) in a wide-mouth jar and blend with an immersion blender until evenly combined and smooth. If you don’t have an immersion blender, use a regular blender instead! Taste and season with more salt and pepper as needed. Set aside until ready to serve (refrigerate if making in advance).

TO MAKE THE CROUTONS: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a medium nonstick skillet. Add 2 slices French bread torn into small pieces and cook, stirring often, until light golden brown. Add the 1 tablespoon unsalted butter and 2 minced garlic cloves and stir continuously for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until the garlic is fragrant and golden. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer the croutons to a plate to cool.

TO GRILL THE ROMAINE HEARTS: Trim the roots off of 4 romaine hearts then cut the hearts in half. Use a pastry brush to lightly brush the cut sides of the romaine hearts with olive oil . Transfer to the grill, cut-side down. Grill for 3 to 5 minutes, until char marks form.
Transfer the lettuce to a serving platter, cut-side up. Drizzle with the dressing and top with the croutons and 1/2 cup shaved Parmesan cheese . Season with salt and pepper, if desired.

* As a side, this salad will feed 6-8 people. But we are going to top our Chicken Caesar Sliders with 2 cups worth of it, so if you’re feeding that many people (as opposed to 2-4) add an extra head of romaine to the mix to chop up for your sliders! You can grill it if you want, or skip that step and just chop it up and add some Parm, dressing, and croutons.
**If you want your Chicken Caesar Sliders to be extra saucy, double the Caesar dressing so you can smear some on the slider buns.
S erves 4

name: easy-but-fancy summer grilling menu: juicy lucys aka cheese-stuffed burgers
note: Cook time: 40 minutes total (25 minutes prep time, 15 minutes active cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings: Shredded iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato, sliced dill pickles
ingredients.name: Toppings: Shredded iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato, sliced dill pickles

preparationSteps: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat (400ºF to 450ºF) and lightly oil the grates.

Put 1 ½ pounds ground beef, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 heaping teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper in a large bowl. Use clean hands to mix the meat mixture until evenly combined. Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions, then divide each portion in half, leaving you with 8 equal portions.

To form a burger, take one portion of beef and smash it into a round patty, slightly bigger than the bun. Take 1 slice of cheese and tear it into quarters. Shingle the cheese on the patty, leaving a 1/2-inch border. Take another portion of beef and flatten it to the same size as the first patty. Place it on top and gently crimp the patties together. Set the finished patty aside on a plate and continue the process with the remaining meat and cheese to make 4 patties total.

Put the burger patties on the grill and cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the cheese is melted and gooey and the burger is cooked through. Remove the burger patties from the grill and let rest for 5 minutes.

While the burgers are resting, put 4 open potato buns on the grill, cut-side down, and grill for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly toasted. To assemble the burgers, put a spoonful of Special Sauce and a patty on each bottom bun. Top with your desired toppings and the top bun. Serve immediately.

*1 1/2 pounds of beef can be hard to buy for. Feel free to buy 2 pounds instead to make 6 patties instead of 4! Just add a little extra of each of the spices to the meat mixture, and make sure you have 2 extra cheese slices and buns.

name: easy-but-fancy summer grilling menu: special sauce
note: Prep time: 5 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 clove garlic, grated on a microplane
ingredients.name: garlic, grated on a microplane

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Whisk together all the ingredients in a small bowl. Taste and adjust seasonings as desired.
Makes 10 sliders (or 4-6 regular burgers!)

name: easy-but-fancy summer grilling menu: chicken caesar sliders
note: Cook time: 50 minutes total (20 minutes prep time, at least 20 minutes rest time, 8 minutes cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1/2 lemon (save that half-zested lemon for your crisp recipe!)
ingredients.name: Zest of 1/2 lemon (save that half-zested lemon for your crisp recipe!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 garlic clove, grated (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)
ingredients.name: garlic clove, grated (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Caesar dressing (if you like things extra saucy!)
ingredients.name: Caesar dressing (if you like things extra saucy!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups Grilled Caesar Salad, finely chopped
ingredients.name: Grilled Caesar Salad

preparationSteps: Add 1 pound ground chicken, zest of 1/2 lemon, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 large egg, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 heaping teaspoon anchovy paste, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper to a large bowl. Use clean hands to mix the meat mixture until evenly combined.

To form the sliders, spray a baking sheet with cooking spray, then scoop out golf ball- sized portions of meat and place them on the baking sheet. Roll the meat around to grease it up all over, then use your fingers to smoosh the meat down into the baking sheet to create the slider patties.
Wrap with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, but up to 72 hours. (Or throw them in the freezer for at least 20 minutes.)

Preheat your grill to 400ºF. Use your grill brush to clean your grates really well — do not skip this, it will help prevent them from sticking! Lightly oil the grill grates after they’ve been scraped.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip the patties and grill for another 3 to 4 minutes, or until they’ve reached an internal temp of 165°F.

Towards the end of cooking the sliders, throw the entire pack of slider buns onto the grill — attached, if using King’s Hawaiian. Grill on each side for 30 to 45 seconds, until just lightly toasted but nice and warm.

Pull the slider buns apart and cut in half to open them. If you like things extra saucy, spread Caesar dressing onto each side of the bun, add a patty, then top with some chopped Grilled Caesar Salad . Close the bun.
*Not making the grilled Caesar from this menu? Just toss 2 cups chopped romaine with a pinch of salt, enough Caesar dressing to coat it, and some crushed up croutons (the crunch is essential!).

** If you want these to be extra saucy, be sure to double the Caesar dressing when you’re prepping your salad! Or just buy a jar of pre-made Caesar dressing from the store and use that on the buns instead.
Serves 8 to 10 people (the leftovers are so good with yogurt for breakfast)

name: lemon basil pasta: lemon basil spaghetti
note: Cook time: 25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound dried spaghetti, or any long noodle
ingredients.name: dried spaghetti, or any long noodle

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (it must be freshly grated!)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (it must be freshly grated!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), preferably organic, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon), preferably organic, plus more for garnish

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (no need to measure — about 2 grinds)
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper (no need to measure — about 2 grinds)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 large basil leaves or 6 parsley sprigs, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: large basil leaves or 6 parsley sprigs

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional but encouraged: lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below!)
ingredients.name: Optional but encouraged: lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below!)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
If you’re making the lemon-parm crunchies (recipe below), cook them now while your water is coming to a boil!

Cook 1 pound dried pasta noodles until al dente (almost totally tender, but still with a slight hardness), per package instructions (as in, read the package and cook it for however long it says it will take to reach al dente!).
Before draining, use a glass measuring cup or coffee mug to scoop out 1 cup of pasta cooking water! I’m bolding this so you do not forget!

Meanwhile, in a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 large egg, 1 cup of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, the zest of 1 lemon, 1/3 cup lemon juice, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon (2 grinds) of black pepper .
Thinly slice 12 large basil leaves.

Immediately after draining, add the hot noodles to the sauce you made in the serving bowl, along with 1/2 cup of the hot, reserved pasta cooking water and most of the basil (but leave a little basil out for garnish). Use tongs to toss and toss and toss until the sauce is glossy and coating the noodles. It might look too soupy at first — keep tossing! The cheese, oil, and egg just need time and heat to meld together and work their magic. Add more pasta water as needed if the sauce stiffens up too much.
Serve immediately, garnished with more Parm, lemon zest, basil, and (if making) lots of lemon-parm crunchies.

name: lemon basil pasta: lemon-parm crunchies
note:
Cook time: 10 minutes

• Love your leftovers: The pasta will be delicious for up to 4 days stored in the fridge. Add a splash of water when you’re reheating to loosen the sauce up. The lemon-parm crunchies will stay good sealed in an airtight container for up to a week!

• Feeding picky eaters : You can leave the basil out if green flecks ick them out — just garnish any basil eaters’ bowls with it instead. Also, FWIW, my boys branded these “Spongebob noodles.” Whatever works!

• I *do* feel like cooking/I’m cooking this for guests: You’ve gotta make the crunchies! Also, scroll up to the “bulk it up” section above the recipe for ideas for a meat and/or side salad to stretch this meal further.

• Must have meat : I love shrimp and chicken with this one! See the “bulk it up” section above the recipe for how-tos.

• Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free Parm alternative. If you don’t like DF cheese, you can use 1/2 cup of an unsweetened dairy-free milk/cream substitute.

• Gluten-free: Use any gluten-free pasta alternative you love — but taste the pasta cooking water before you add it, it can be pretty salty so you may want to cut back on salt elsewhere. You could also use zucchini noodles. I prefer to sauté my zoodles in oil to keep them crisp (rather than boiling them). To make up for the lack of starchy pasta water, you can make a slurry: mix 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of cornstarch with 1 cup of water. Bring it to a simmer then use it in the recipe as written. If you’re making the crunchies, use GF breadcrumbs.

• Spaghetti : I really love long noodles for this one, so bucatini, linguine, fettuccine, or angel hair pasta. But a short pasta like rigatoni or farfalle would totally work too. See “gluten free” note above for more.

• EVOO : I love the flavor of EVOO here but olive oil or melted butter also work here.

• Egg : Another 2 tablespoons of EVOO.

• Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano : Don’t sub with pre-grated! Unless it’s the good, freshly grated kind from a fancy market or Whole Foods. Otherwise, it’ll have anti-caking agents that will make the sauce clumpy not creamy. You could also grate Grana Padano, Pecorino Romano, or regular Parm. Or see the dairy-free note above for DF options.

• Lemon : I’m gonna say no subs on this one. Vinegar just ain’t it for this recipe. Limes ain’t it either. Go get some lemons.

• Black pepper: White pepper, or a few shakes of red pepper flakes

• Basil : Flat-leaf (AKA Italian) parsley. I also think a LITTLE mint would be delish here.

• Panko : Regular breadcrumbs, homemade breadcrumbs, or crushed cornflakes!

• Garlic powder : 1 minced fresh garlic clove, a thawed cube of frozen crushed garlic, or swap for onion powder
preparationSteps: Warm 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup breadcrumbs , a big pinch of kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder , and the zest of 1 lemon and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden brown. Stir in 1/3 cup grated Parm and stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the cheese is crispy and coating the breadcrumbs. Pour into a small bowl to cool and place the bowl directly on the dinner table for people to serve themselves!

name: marinated steak tips over herby rice: steak tips with herby rice
note: Cook time: 45 minutes active, plus 8 to 48 hours for marinating the steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 pounds steak tips or sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: steak tips or sirloin steak

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce or soy sauce
ingredients.name: Worcestershire sauce or soy sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: Neutral oil, for greasing the grill
ingredients.name: Neutral oil, for greasing the grill

preparationSteps: If you’re making the pickled cucumber salad (recipe below!), do that at least 24 hours before you plan to eat.

MARINATE THE STEAK TIPS : Cut 3 pounds steak tips or sirloin steak into 1-inch cubes and add them to a large zip-top bag or airtight container. Chop 1 large red onion and add it to the bag along with 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon onion powder , and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes . Seal the bag and smoosh everything around until the steak is well coated. Add the herbs ( 10 thyme sprigs, 4 rosemary sprigs , 4 parsley sprigs ) to the bag, seal, and smoosh again. Marinate in the fridge for at least 8 hours or up to 48 hours.

MAKE THE HERBY RICE : Rinse 2 cups long-grain white rice (see notes for a how-to, if needed) and add it to a large saucepan with 3 cups water . Set over high heat to bring to a boil. Stir the rice well, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Simmer until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the rice is cooked through, about 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let rest, still covered, for about 5 minutes. Add 3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and stir until the butter is melted. Add the herbs ( 2 tablespoons fresh thyme leaves, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh rosemary leaves , 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley ) and stir again. Cover to keep warm.
COOK THE STEAK: Prepare the grill for high heat. Once preheated, scrape your grill grates clean and lightly grease the grates with neutral oil.
While your grill heats, remove the steak from the marinade and allow the excess marinade to drip off. Thread the steak and onions onto separate skewers, until mostly full.

Arrange the skewers on the greased grill grates. Close the lid and cook for about 5 minutes, until the bottoms of the skewers are nicely charred. Flip the skewers, cover again, and cook for another 5 minutes, until charred on the other side.
Spread the rice out on a serving platter. Place the grilled skewers on top of the rice and let rest for about 10 minutes, lightly tented with foil to keep warm.

Meanwhile, set the lemon halves , cut side down, on the grill and cook until the bottoms are nicely charred, about 4 minutes, then arrange on the side of the rice. Squeeze the grilled lemon over the skewers and rice just before serving. Serve family style along with your smashed pickled cucumber salad .
By Dan Pelosi (formatting modified for What To Cook)

name: marinated steak tips over herby rice: smashed pickled cucumber salad
note: Prep time: 15 minutes plus at least 24 hours to pickle in the fridge

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds mini cucumbers, smashed and roughly chopped
ingredients.name: mini cucumbers, smashed and roughly chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons coarsely chopped fresh dill, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: coarsely chopped fresh dill, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups distilled white vinegar, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: distilled white vinegar, plus more as needed

preparationSteps: Trim the stems off of 8 radishes , then cut them into quarters. Add them to a clean 2-quart jar or airtight container. Use the flat side of a knife to lightly smash 2 pounds of mini cucumbers , then roughly chop them and add them to the jar. Thinly slice 2 garlic cloves and coarsely chop 2 tablespoons fresh dill and add them to the jar along with 1/4 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon kosher salt , and a pinch of red pepper flakes (if using).

Pour 2 cups distilled white vinegar into the jar. Screw on the lid and shake until the sugar and salt dissolve. Fill the jar to the brim with more vinegar as needed, then tighten the lid and refrigerate for at least 24 hours or up to 1 month.
Drain the brine and arrange the pickled salad in a serving bowl. Finish with a little bit of fresh dill and a few grinds of black pepper before serving.

name: the 2024 ultimate easy-but-fancy holiday menu: apple butter bourbon smash
note:
• Not into alcohol? I love apple cider with a little club soda and a lemon wedge!

• FYI, Southern Living taste-tested store-bought apple ciders and here are the results . (Trader Joe’s “Spiced Cider” won, which is what I use too.)

• Kosher salt

• 9-ounce package of cheese tortellini (or a bigger package for a bigger crowd — I used a “family size” package in the photo above!)

• 1 cup mayonnaise

• 1/2 cup store-bought pesto

• Zest and juice of 1/2 lemon (preferably organic)

• 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan

• Extra-virgin olive oil

• Finely chopped parsley

• Optional: crudités such as celery sticks, carrot sticks, etc.

• If you’re hosting a fancy dinner party, you can make the aioli in a mixing bowl, then transfer it to a nice serving bowl so there are no smudges along the side. If you’re hosting a cozy, more casual meal, just mix it straight in the bowl you’ll put on the platter to skip having to clean another bowl.

• Dairy-free/gluten-free: Shop for vegan or GF tortellini if needed (you can find both on the market). There are also vegan mayos and pestos out there!
preparationSteps: To make lemon sugar, zest 1 lemon into a small bowl. Add 1/2 cup sugar and, using your fingers, pinch the zest into the sugar until evenly mixed. Set aside.

In a large pitcher, combine the juice of 2 lemons, 3 cups apple cider, 1 1/2 cups bourbon, 1/3 cup orange liqueur, and 1/4 cup apple butter. Stir until the apple butter dissolves. Taste. Do you want it more tart? Use that third lemon to add more lemon juice!
Rim your glasses with the lemon sugar by running a cut lemon along the rim of the glass to wet it, then dipping it in the lemon sugar.
Fill the glasses with ice, then fill with bourbon smashes! If you have cinnamon sticks, stick one in each glass.

name: the 2024 ultimate easy-but-fancy holiday menu: pear and blue cheese salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red pear (you can use 2 of either color pear if needed — apple or fuyu persimmon would also be great)
ingredients.name: red pear (you can use 2 of either color pear if needed — apple or fuyu persimmon would also be great)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup candied/honey-roasted pecans, roughly chopped (you can use any nut, although honey-roasted peanuts aren’t really the vibe — the sweet and spicy pecans from Trader Joe’s are my favorite here if you have a TJ’s)
ingredients.name: candied/honey-roasted pecans, roughly chopped (you can use any nut, although honey-roasted peanuts aren’t really the vibe — the sweet and spicy pecans from Trader Joe’s are my favorite here if you have a TJ’s)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese (or feta or goat cheese!)
ingredients.name: crumbled blue cheese (or feta or goat cheese!)

preparationSteps: To make the dressing: Add 3/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of black pepper to a large jar and shake vigorously until thick and emulsified (AKA until the oil’s incorporated and everything’s well mixed). Taste and adjust as desired — too sweet? Add more oil. Not tart enough? More vinegar. Keep adjusting to make it your own.

To make the salad: Toss 5 ounces mixed greens in a large bowl. Thinly slice 1 green pear and 1 red pear, and chop 1 avocado and 1 cup candied nuts. Add the pears, nuts, avocado, and 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese (or more! do your thing!) to the bowl. Just before serving, season with kosher salt and black pepper and drizzle about 1/4 cup of the dressing over top. Toss to combine, and add more dressing as desired. With family-style salads like this, I like to dress them very lightly, then place the salad dressing with a spoon beside the bowl so that the dressing-heavy people (me) can add more.

name: the 2024 ultimate easy-but-fancy holiday menu: perfect asparagus
note:
• Skip the cheese if you’re avoiding dairy or want to simplify a dish! It’s delish without, just more festive with.

• Note that I served this asparagus straight off the sheet pan! Yep! Throw a pretty napkin under there, add some lemon wedges if you’ve got ‘em, and serve it straight off the pan.
preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Cut 1 1/2 inches off the bottom of the asparagus.

Toss the trimmed asparagus on a parchment-lined baking sheet with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder to evenly coat. Spread in a single layer and roast for 12 minutes.

Take a bite. If they’re almost perfectly crisp-tender, sprinkle 1/2 cup Parmesan over top and roast for another 3 minutes or until the cheese has melted. If they’re still tough, roast for another 3 minutes without the Parm, then proceed with the Parm step.
Serve immediately (but don’t worry if you can’t — it’s great at room temperature too!).

name: the 2024 ultimate easy-but-fancy holiday menu: roasted boursin mashed potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks (peeled or unpeeled! I keep the peels on!)
ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.note: cut into 1-inch chunks (peeled or unpeeled! I keep the peels on!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5.2-ounce) container Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs
ingredients.name: Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 325°F.

Cut 4 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes into 1-inch chunks. Add them along with 3 cups whole milk, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper to a wide pot (like a braiser) or a baking dish (like a large Pyrex) — a pot is ideal though so that you can keep it warm on the stovetop later. The milk should mostly cover the potatoes — if it doesn't, add a little more.
Cover the pot/baking dish with a lid (if it doesn’t have a lid, you could use aluminum foil or a sheet pan as a lid instead).
Bake for 1 hour. Remove the cover, stir the potatoes, and add 1 container Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs right on top. Return to the oven to bake for 45 more minutes UNCOVERED.

Remove from the oven and mash!!! Ideally using a potato masher, but, if you’re like me and don’t own one, a wooden spoon will (slowly but surely) do the trick. Season to taste with more salt and pepper (you will probably want a lot more salt!). Sometimes I add a little (like 1/2 teaspoon) garlic powder, too! Sometimes I add some Parmesan! Get wild!
NOTE : If you’re avoiding dairy, Boursin makes a dairy-free version! And for a milk swap, I’d suggest extra-creamy unsweetened oat milk (unsweetened almond would be my second pick).

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: spicy sweet rosemary pecans
note: Cook time: 30 to 40 minutes total (10 minutes prep, 20 to 30 minutes cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt (or an additional 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt)
ingredients.name: flaky sea salt (or an additional 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon dried rosemary or 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely minced
ingredients.name: dried rosemary or 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary

ingredients.rawIngredient: Dash (just a TINY BIT!) of cayenne pepper
ingredients.name: (just a TINY BIT!) of cayenne pepper

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Add all ingredients to the prepared baking sheet — 16 ounces raw pecans, 4 tablespoons melted unsalted butter, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt, 1 teaspoon dried rosemary (or 1 tablespoon finely minced fresh rosemary), 2 tablespoons brown sugar , and a dash (aka just a TINY BIT!) of cayenne pepper — and toss until the pecans are evenly coated.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until the nuts are deep golden-brown. Let cool completely then store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 10 days.

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: whipped ricotta with hot honey and rosemary pecans
note: Prep time: 10 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: A nice big drizzle of honey or hot honey
ingredients.name: A nice big drizzle of honey or hot honey

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons Spicy Sweet Rosemary Pecans, chopped
ingredients.name: Spicy Sweet Rosemary Pecans

preparationSteps: In a food processor, combine 16 ounces ricotta, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, the zest of 1/2 lemon, a tiny bit (like 1 teaspoon) of lemon juice, and the zest of 1/4 orange until creamy and smooth. Transfer to a small serving platter and swoop to make it have pretty peaks and valleys.

Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, your desired amount of honey (I like a nice big drizzle), and 2 tablespoons chopped Spicy Sweet Rosemary Pecans . A little more lemon and orange zest on top for garnish wouldn’t hurt!

Serve with a really good baguette cut into 1/4-inch slices . If it’s a good baguette, you don’t need to toast it! If it’s a kinda crappy grocery store baguette, drizzle with olive oil on a baking sheet and toast on 375°F for 10 to 15 minutes or until golden-brown.

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: merry and bright kale salad
note: Prep time: 20 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (from about 2 large lemons)
ingredients.name: fresh lemon juice (from about 2 large lemons)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small garlic clove, grated or minced
ingredients.name: small garlic clove, grated or minced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons anchovy paste or 2 anchovies, minced then smushed into a paste with the side of your knife
ingredients.name: anchovy paste or 2 anchovies, minced then smushed into a paste with the side of your knife

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch (about 12 ounces) curly or flat leaf kale, stems removed, finely chopped
ingredients.name: (about 12 ounces) curly or flat leaf kale, stems removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 Serrano or jalapeño pepper, thinly sliced (Serrano if your crew likes heat — seriously, they’re spicy; jalapeño if they are more spice-averse; or skip completely)
ingredients.name: Serrano or jalapeño pepper, thinly sliced (Serrano if your crew likes heat — seriously, they’re spicy; jalapeño if they are more spice-averse; or skip completely)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: fresh mint leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup Parmesan (ideally Parmigiano-Reggiano) shavings, shaved using a vegetable peeler
ingredients.name: Parmesan (ideally Parmigiano-Reggiano) shavings, shaved using a vegetable peeler

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup Spicy Sweet Rosemary Pecans, chopped
ingredients.name: Spicy Sweet Rosemary Pecans

preparationSteps: To a jar or bowl, add 1/4 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, the zest of 1 lemon, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice , 1 small minced or grated garlic clove, 2 teaspoons anchovy paste (or 2 anchovies minced then smushed into a paste with the side of your knife), 1/4 cup microplane-grated Parmesan , and a big pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper . Shake or whisk until well combined. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed (you may find that it needs more salt, pepper, lemon zest, lemon juice, anchovy, etc. — everyone’s taste buds and ingredients are a little different!). If you’re making this ahead of time, store covered in the fridge.

De-rib then finely chop 1 bunch of curly or flat leaf kale . Wash and dry the kale in a salad spinner and add it to a serving bowl. Sprinkle with a big pinch of kosher salt , then use your hands to massage it, aka scrunch it together in your fists, 8 to 10 times, until it feels a tiny bit wet in your hands.

Thinly slice 1/2 a Serrano or jalapeño pepper and 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves , and add them to the bowl with 1/2 cup pomegranate seeds and 1/2 cup Parmesan shavings (shaved using a vegetable peeler). When ready to serve, toss with your desired amount of dressing (about half should be good!) and top with 1/2 cup chopped Spicy Sweet Rosemary Pecans.

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: bacon balsamic brussels
note: Cook time: 30 minutes total (10 minutes prep time, 15 to 20 minutes cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds Brussels sprouts (stem ends removed and discarded), shredded in a food processor or thinly sliced
ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts (stem ends removed and discarded), shredded in a food processor or thinly sliced

preparationSteps: Before you start cooking, prep your Brussels sprouts. Trim and discard the stem ends from 2 pounds Brussels sprouts . Shred the sprouts in a food processor equipped with the slicing disc ( like so !), or thinly slice them using a knife.

Chop 8 slices of bacon . Cook the bacon over medium-high heat in your largest skillet, stirring often. When crispy, use a slotted spoon to transfer the bacon to a plate, leaving the bacon grease in the skillet.

Crank the heat up to high and add the shredded Brussels sprouts. Stir to coat in bacon grease, then spread them out into an even layer and let them brown up for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes, until very tender and browned. Stir in 1 teaspoon kosher salt, a pinch of red pepper flakes, 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, and 1 tablespoon honey or hot honey. Cook for an additional minute or 2, until the balsamic is all absorbed. Stir in the cooked bacon. Taste and add more salt if needed.

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: meyer lemon ricotta spoon bread
note: Cook time: 50 minutes to 1 hour total (5 minutes prep time, 45 to 55 minutes cook time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted (plus more butter for greasing the baking dish)
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, melted (plus more butter for greasing the baking dish)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Zest of 1/2 lemon (about 1 teaspoon, ideally from a Meyer lemon)
ingredients.name: Zest of 1/2 lemon (about 1 teaspoon, ideally from a Meyer lemon)

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 350°F and butter an 8x8-inch baking dish (a 10-inch cast-iron skillet will also work).

In a large bowl, stir together 1 can drained corn , 1 can creamed corn , 1 cup ricotta , 1/2 cup melted unsalted butter, and the zest of 1/2 lemon until combined. Add 1 box Jiffy cornbread mix and stir until just incorporated — don’t overmix.

Pour into your prepared pan and bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the top is golden, the sides are slightly browned, and the center is just set (it should still have a slight jiggle). Let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Note: This has a soft, moist consistency like a bread pudding, not firm and dry like cornbread!

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: dilly horseradish sauce
note: Prep time: 10 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 tablespoons prepared horseradish, drained (see notes if you’re confused by this!)
ingredients.name: prepared horseradish, drained (see notes if you’re confused by this!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon salt (ideally a fine sea salt like this one )
ingredients.name: salt (ideally a fine sea salt like this one )

preparationSteps: Mix all the ingredients together in a serving bowl and serve alongside the tenderloin.

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy spring menu: roasted carrots, fennel, and red onion with pistachio
note: Cook time: 45 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch spring carrots, tops trimmed off, scrubbed clean, halved vertically
ingredients.name: spring carrots, tops trimmed off, scrubbed clean, halved vertically

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large head of fennel, green stalks trimmed off and discarded, 1/2-inch sliced
ingredients.name: of fennel, green stalks trimmed off and discarded, 1/2-inch sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of micro greens (or any chopped fresh green herb)
ingredients.name: Handful of micro greens (or any chopped fresh green herb)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of roasted, salted pistachios (or any nut), finely chopped
ingredients.name: Handful of roasted, salted pistachios (or any nut)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

Prep your vegetables, adding them to the sheet pan as you work. Trim the tops off of 1 bunch spring carrots. Scrub them clean and halve them vertically. Trim off (and discard) the green stalks of 1 large head of fennel and cut the bulb into 1/2-inch slices. Cut 1 large red onion into 1/2-inch slices. Add 4 tablespoons honey, 3 tablespoons olive oil, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 3/4 teaspoon ground cumin, 3/4 teaspoon smoked paprika, and the leaves from 6 sprigs of thyme to the sheet pan. Use your hands to toss so everything is combined and well coated.

Roast for 30 minutes, until golden-brown and fork-tender. Transfer to a serving platter. Top with a handful of micro greens , a handful of finely chopped roasted, salted pistachios (or any nut), a pinch of minced chives, and a pinch of flaky sea salt .
If you want to double this salad, combine 1 package spring greens and 1 package baby arugula and double the other ingredients.

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy spring menu: strawberry poppy seed crunch salad
note: Prep time: 15 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces strawberries (half of a standard clamshell container), de-stemmed and quartered, or cut into sixths if large
ingredients.name: strawberries (half of a standard clamshell container), de-stemmed and quartered, or cut into sixths if large

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup plain-ish (like no chocolate or dried fruit) granola
ingredients.name: plain-ish (like no chocolate or dried fruit) granola

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces plain or honey goat cheese, crumbled
ingredients.name: plain or honey goat cheese, crumbled

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped
ingredients.name: Handful of fresh mint leaves

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup champagne vinegar + more to taste
ingredients.name: champagne vinegar + more to taste

preparationSteps: Make the poppy seed dressing: Add all the ingredients ( 2/3 cup avocado oil, 1/3 cup champagne vinegar, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 tablespoon minced chives, 1 teaspoon poppy seeds, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard (preferably Maille), and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt ) to a Mason jar, put the lid on tight, and shake until emulsified. If you don’t have a Mason jar, you can whisk them together in a bowl.
Taste. Want it less sweet/more vinegary? Add another 2 or 3 tablespoons of champagne vinegar.

Assemble the salad in a serving bowl with 1 (5-ounce) package spring greens on bottom and the other ingredients — 8 ounces de-stemmed and quartered strawberries , 1 large cubed avocado, 1/2 cup plain-ish granola, 4 ounces crumbled plain or honey goat cheese, and a handful of roughly chopped fresh mint in piles on top. Toss with desired amount of dressing (not all of it — you’ll likely have leftover!!). If you’re prepping ahead, wait to add the chopped avocado and dressing until you’re ready to serve.
Inspired by the classic Pasta e Piselli (aka pasta and peas). This recipe is easy to double if needed!

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy spring menu: spring pea pasta
note: Cook time: 30 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch asparagus, woody ends trimmed off and discarded, finely chopped
ingredients.name: asparagus, woody ends trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon (preferably organic), zested and juiced (if you love lemony flavor, grab 2!)
ingredients.name: lemon (preferably organic), zested and juiced (if you love lemony flavor, grab 2!)
