ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water (add 2 big 4-finger pinches of kosher salt!) to a boil over high heat.
While the water is coming to a boil, trim off (and discard) the bottom 1 1/2 inches of 1 bunch asparagus , then finely chop the stalks.

Once your water is boiling, drop in 8 ounces of dried Ditalini and set a timer for the amount of time the box of pasta says to cook it until al dente MINUS 1 minute. (For example, my ditalini box said to cook the noodles for 11 minutes to reach al dente, so I set a timer for 10 minutes). When your timer goes off, add the finely chopped asparagus and 1 cup frozen English peas (that’s half the bag of frozen peas, if you don’t want to measure!) to the pot and set a timer for 1 more minute.
SCOOP OUT AND SAVE 2 CUPS OF PASTA COOKING WATER (!!! this is important!) then drain the noodles and vegetables in a colander.

Return them to the pot (off heat) and add 1/3 cup reserved pasta cooking water, 1 (5.2-ounce) package Boursin Herbs & Garlic Cheese, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, and several grinds of black pepper. Stir until everything is creamy and well combined.

Too thick? Add more pasta water — that’s why we scooped out a lot! Too watery at the bottom of the pot? Keep tossing. If your Boursin isn’t melting easily or you want to warm everything up more, turn the heat on to low as you stir.
Taste. If needed, add more kosher salt, lemon juice, and black pepper a little at a time until it's absolutely delicious.
Top with 3 tablespoons minced dill, 2 tablespoons minced chives, more lemon zest (optional) , and grated Parm (however much you want — I added a lot!).

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy spring menu: maple dijon baked ham
note: Cook time: 30 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons whole grain mustard or 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard (preferably Maille)*
ingredients.name: whole grain mustard or 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard (preferably Maille)*

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Place 1 cooked 6- to 8-pound, spiral-sliced, bone-in ham in a baking dish with high sides.

Meanwhile, whisk all glaze ingredients — 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup maple syrup, 3 tablespoons whole grain mustard (or 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard), and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon — together in a small pot. Bring glaze to a boil over medium-high then reduce to medium-low and simmer, stirring frequently, for 3 minutes.
Brush half of the glaze all over the ham and down into the slices. Bake for 10 minutes.
Remove the ham from the oven and paint with the second half of the glaze. Bake for 10 more minutes. Tent with foil until serving to keep it warm.
*As you can see in the photo, using whole grain mustard here provides gorgeous texture (and those little mustard seed pops add so much delicious flavor).

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy spring menu: poppy seed rolls
note: Cook time: 20-25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of flaky sea salt
ingredients.name: Big pinch of flaky sea salt

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a small baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, stir together 4 tablespoons melted unsalted butter, 1 teaspoon poppy seeds, 1 tablespoon honey, and 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard .
Brush the butter mixture over the tops of a 12-pack of King’s Hawaiian rolls (keep them all together). Sprinkle with a big pinch of flaky sea salt .

Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, until golden brown. Keep a close eye on them, they’ll go from golden-brown to burnt quickly! Once cool enough to handle, separate the rolls and arrange them on a serving plate. Serve along with whole grain and/or Dijon mustard to make little ham sandwiches.
Inspired by Marian Burros’s “Original Plum Torte.”
servings: Makes 12 rolls, easily doubled if needed

name: the 2025 easy-but-fancy spring menu: brown butter strawberry skillet torte with sweet cream
note: Cook time: 1 hour 30 minutes total (30 minutes of prep time, ~1 hour of baking time)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons granulated sugar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lemon (ideally an organic Meyer lemon), zested, 1/2 of it juiced
ingredients.name: lemon (ideally an organic Meyer lemon), zested, 1/2 of it juiced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound (aka 16 ounces, aka 1 standard clamshell container) of strawberries, de-stemmed and halved (or quartered if your strawberries are big)
ingredients.name: (aka 16 ounces, aka 1 standard clamshell container) of strawberries, de-stemmed and halved (or quartered if your strawberries are big)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Add 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter to a 10-inch (well seasoned!) cast-iron or nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook until browned, swirling the skillet occasionally. Let cool for 10 minutes (put it in the fridge to expedite).

Stir in 3/4 cup granulated sugar and the zest of 1 lemon for 30 full seconds. Add 2 large eggs (just crack them right into the skillet!). Add 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and a tiny pinch of kosher salt in a pile and use your fingers to mix the dry ingredients together. Now stir to combine them with the rest of the ingredients.

Smooth out the top of the mixture. Wipe/clean off the sides of the skillet (you can use your finger but, I’m just warning you, once you taste this cake batter your life will never be the same). Add 1 pound de-stemmed and halved/quartered strawberries on top with the cut sides facing down (see the pic for a visual). Sprinkle 1 tablespoon granulated sugar and the juice of 1/2 lemon over top.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center of the cake (don’t poke near a strawberry) comes out clean and the top and edges have turned golden.
While it’s baking, make your sweet cream by mixing together 1 cup of sour cream and 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar .
Slice the cake and serve with a big dollop of the sweet cream!

name: the 2026 easy-but-fancy summer menu: honey, goat cheese with strawberries
note: Prep time: 10 minutes (plus 30 to 45 minutes inactive for the goat cheese to reach room temperature)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces goat cheese (brought to room temperature)
ingredients.name: goat cheese (brought to room temperature)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon honey, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: honey, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: Balsamic glaze, for drizzling (optional but encouraged!)
ingredients.name: Balsamic glaze, for drizzling (optional but encouraged!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: A handful of fresh mint leaves, torn or chopped
ingredients.name: A handful of fresh mint leaves, torn or chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: A pinch of flaky sea salt
ingredients.name: A pinch of flaky sea salt

ingredients.rawIngredient: Sturdy crackers, for serving (like Firehook or Rustic Bakery)
ingredients.name: Sturdy crackers, for serving (like Firehook or Rustic Bakery)

preparationSteps: About 30 to 45 minutes before you plan to assemble this appetizer, remove 8 ounces of goat cheese from the fridge and allow it to come to room temperature.

Place the room-temperature goat cheese on an 8- to 10-inch plate or shallow serving platter. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tablespoon honey , then use the back of a spoon to combine the honey and extra-virgin olive oil into the cheese. Spread and swoosh the goat cheese into an even layer.
Hull (aka remove the leaves and stem from) and dice 1/2 pound strawberries , then scatter them evenly over top of the cheese. Drizzle with more honey and balsamic glaze , if using.

Finely chop 1/4 cup roasted pistachios and sprinkle them on top along with a handful of fresh mint leaves (you can either tear the leaves into smaller pieces or chop them), a pinch of flaky sea salt , and several grinds of black pepper .
Serve immediately with sturdy crackers for scooping.

name: the 2026 easy-but-fancy summer menu: sour cream and onion potato salad
note: Cook time: 40 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons kosher salt, plus more for cooking the potatoes
ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more for cooking the potatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 scallions (aka green onions), thinly sliced, divided
ingredients.name: scallions (aka green onions), thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup fresh dill fronds and tender stems (1 ounce), finely chopped, divided
ingredients.name: fresh dill fronds and tender stems (1 ounce), finely chopped

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 cups crushed salt and vinegar potato chips
ingredients.name: crushed salt and vinegar potato chips

preparationSteps: Cut 3 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes into 1-inch chunks and place them in a large pot. Cover the potatoes with a few inches of cold water (as in, there should be a few inches of water on top of the covered potatoes) . Season the water generously with kosher salt and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are very fork-tender, 12 to 15 minutes. Drain the potatoes and shake out any excess moisture.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk together 1 cup sour cream , 1/2 cup mayonnaise , 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar , 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard , 1 teaspoon onion powder , 3/4 teaspoon garlic powder , 2 teaspoons kosher salt , and several grinds of black pepper .

Dice 2 celery stalks . Thinly slice 6 scallions (use both the white and green parts — only trim off and discard the root tip ends). Finely chop 1 bunch fresh chives and 1/2 cup fresh dill fronds and tender stems .

Add the warm potatoes, all of the celery, 3/4 of the sliced scallions, 3/4 of the chopped chives, and 3/4 of the chopped dill to the bowl with the dressing and gently toss until the potatoes are evenly coated. Taste and add more kosher salt and black pepper if needed. I sometimes add a bit more vinegar, too.
Transfer to a serving bowl or platter. Top with the remaining prepped scallions, chives, and dill.
Just before serving, generously sprinkle 2 to 3 cups crushed salt and vinegar potato chips over top.

name: the 2026 easy-but-fancy summer menu: heirloom tomato and watermelon salad with salty feta
note: Prep time: 15 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh oregano, chopped, plus more for serving (do NOT sub in dried oregano here — use fresh dill or basil instead if needed)
ingredients.name: fresh oregano, chopped, plus more for serving (do NOT sub in dried oregano here — use fresh dill or basil instead if needed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds heirloom tomatoes, cut into bite-sized wedges
ingredients.name: heirloom tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups seedless watermelon, cut into bite-sized chunks
ingredients.name: seedless watermelon

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces block feta cheese (preferably the kind packed in brine), crumbled
ingredients.name: feta cheese (preferably the kind packed in brine), crumbled

ingredients.rawIngredient: A sprinkle of flaky sea salt
ingredients.name: A sprinkle of flaky sea salt

preparationSteps: Chop 1 tablespoon of fresh oregano and add it to a large serving platter along with 2 tablespoons champagne vinegar , 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil , 1 teaspoon kosher salt , and several grinds of black pepper . Whisk together until well combined. Taste and add a pinch more kosher salt, if needed.

Cut 2 pounds of heirloom tomatoes into bite-sized wedges and 4 cups seedless watermelon into bite-sized chunks. Add the tomatoes and watermelon to the platter, gently toss to coat them in dressing, then spread them out into an even layer.
Crumble 8 ounces of feta cheese over top.
Garnish with a little more fresh oregano, a few more grinds of black pepper, and a sprinkle of flaky sea salt. Serve immediately.

name: the 2026 easy-but-fancy summer menu: kale salad with creamy lemon dressing and garlicky pistachio crunch
note: Cook time: 30 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: Juice from 1 large lemon (3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice)
ingredients.name: Juice from 1 large lemon (3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 garlic clove, finely grated or minced
ingredients.name: garlic clove, finely grated or minced

ingredients.rawIngredient: A few dashes of hot sauce
ingredients.name: A few dashes of hot sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large bunch kale (about 10 ounces), ribs removed and leaves very, very thinly sliced
ingredients.name: kale (about 10 ounces), ribs removed and leaves very, very thinly sliced

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: finely grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 garlic clove, finely grated or minced
ingredients.name: garlic clove, finely grated or minced

preparationSteps: Make the creamy lemon dressing: In a large bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup mayonnaise , 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (from 1 large lemon), 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil , 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard , 1 finely grated garlic clove (use a microplane or grater to grate it right into the bowl!), a few dashes of hot sauce , 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt , and several grinds of black pepper until smooth.

Make the salad: Remove the stems from 1 large bunch kale (about 10 ounces) and very, very thinly slice the leaves. Leave the kale right on the cutting board, sprinkle with a pinch of kosher salt , and massage it with your hands until it softens and shrinks slightly, for about 1 minute. Transfer the kale to the bowl with the dressing along with 1 cup of finely grated Parmesan cheese. Toss to coat.

Make the garlicky pistachio crunch: Finely chop 1/2 cup roasted pistachios and set aside . Melt 3 tablespoons unsalted butter in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup panko breadcrumbs , the chopped pistachios, 1 finely grated garlic clove (use a microplane or grater to grate it right into the skillet), and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt . Stir and cook until golden-brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool completely. Keep stirring while the skillet is cooling so that it doesn’t burn.

Pile the salad onto a serving platter/serving bowl and generously sprinkle the garlicky pistachio crunch over top. Finish with more freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a few grinds of black pepper before serving.

name: the 2026 easy-but-fancy summer menu: grilled peaches with vanilla ice cream and shortbread crumbles
note: Cook time: 15 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 ripe but firm freestone peaches, halved and pitted (see the shopping tip beneath the recipe!)
ingredients.name: ripe but firm freestone peaches
ingredients.note: halved and pitted (see the shopping tip beneath the recipe!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pint vanilla or pistachio ice cream
ingredients.name: vanilla or pistachio ice cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: Store-bought shortbread or gingersnap cookies (like Walker’s)
ingredients.name: Store-bought shortbread or gingersnap cookies (like Walker’s)

preparationSteps: Heat the grill to medium-high (450°F).
Halve and remove the pits from 6 peaches.
Brush the cut sides of the peaches lightly with neutral oil . Grill cut-side down (with the grill lid closed) until grill marks appear and the peaches soften slightly, 3 to 5 minutes.
Transfer the peaches to a serving platter, cut-side up. Place a scoop of ice cream inside each peach half and sprinkle generously with crumbled shortbread cookies . Serve immediately.

name: the perfect fall chicken and kale salad: 20-minute kale, chicken, apple and cheddar salad

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and finely ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and finely ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder or 1 very small garlic clove, grated with a microplane
ingredients.name: garlic powder or 1 very small garlic clove, grated with a microplane

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch curly or flat leaf (lacinato) kale, tough stems removed, finely chopped (4 heaping cups — feel free to buy store-bought chopped kale, just pick through it to remove any tough stems)
ingredients.name: curly or flat leaf (lacinato) kale, tough stems removed, finely chopped (4 heaping cups — feel free to buy store-bought chopped kale, just pick through it to remove any tough stems)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large cooked chicken breast (from a rotisserie chicken, or see recipe below for how to cook it at home), finely chopped (about 1 1/2 cups chopped chicken)
ingredients.name: large cooked chicken breast (from a rotisserie chicken, or see recipe below for how to cook it at home), finely chopped (about 1 1/2 cups chopped chicken)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium honey crisp apple, cut into thin batons (or chopped if that’s easier)
ingredients.name: medium honey crisp apple
ingredients.note: cut into thin batons (or chopped if that’s easier)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/3 cup salted, roasted almonds, roughly chopped
ingredients.name: salted, roasted almonds

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces white cheddar cheese, roughly chopped
ingredients.name: white cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 dates, pits removed and finely chopped (or 1/4 cup yellow raisins, dried cranberries, or dried cherries)
ingredients.name: dates, pits removed and finely chopped (or 1/4 cup yellow raisins, dried cranberries, or dried cherries)

preparationSteps: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder (or one grated garlic clove). Taste and add 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup if your dressing is too tangy (the balsamic I use is sweet enough that I don’t need any).

Add 1 bunch finely chopped kale to the bowl of dressing, sprinkle with a big pinch of kosher salt , and use clean hands to massage the salt and dressing into the kale until it feels soft — about 7 squeezes between your palms. If it feels too heavily dressed, don’t worry, the chicken is going to soak up the dressing.
Add 1 1/2 cups chopped chicken, 1 apple cut into thin batons, 1/3 cup roughly chopped almonds, 4 ounces roughly chopped cheddar cheese, and 3 chopped dates. Toss to coat. DIG IN!
Note: if you have the time, give the salad 10 minutes to marinate.

name: the perfect fall chicken and kale salad: roasted chicken, delicata squash, kale, apple, and cheddar salad
note:
Cook time: 45 minutes

• Riffs, feeding kids, what to do with your leftover rotisserie chicken, and what balsamic do I buy? If you skipped over the intro, go back up and read it! We go over all these things there!

• Double the dressing : When I have delicious homemade dressing in the fridge, I’m far more likely to make salads throughout my week. You can easily double this dressing — if you’re doing so, make it in a jar or glass storage container (rather than in the serving bowl) and pour half of it into the bowl for this meal. Store the leftover dressing in that tightly sealed container in the fridge for up to a week. It’ll separate while it sits. Let it warm up slightly and shake or stir to recombine it.

• Skip the dressing: Yes, you can use a store-bought balsamic vinaigrette… but it really is so easy and delicious to DIY it!

• Prep ahead : The chicken and squash will stay good in the fridge for up to 3 days stored in an airtight container, so feel free to prep those ahead of time as much as you’d like!

• Love your leftovers: Since kale’s a hearty green, this salad will actually hold up pretty well in the fridge if you have leftovers.

• Vegetarian : Roast a can of drained and dried chickpeas. You may as well add the squash to the mix since you’ll be turning the oven on, so follow the second version of this recipe’s instructions, just using chickpeas instead of chicken. You can also add raw chickpeas, but definitely let them marinate in the dressing for at least 15 minutes.

• Dairy-free/gluten-free/nut-free: Omit the cheese or use your fave DF option. It’s already gluten free! And instead of almonds, you can use seeds (roasted, salted pepitas or sunflower seeds). If you can’t eat seeds either, croutons or garlicky crunchies would be a great crunchy element!

• Chicken breasts: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs. They take longer to reach 165°F than breasts — more like 35 to 40 minutes — so keep them on the sheet pan with the squash (and beyond if needed). Chicken sausage (or turkey) would also be great. Heat it however’s easiest for you (in a skillet, in the oven, in an air fryer, or in the microwave) then slice. Chopped up sliced deli ham or turkey would also be great!

• Delicata squash: Trader Joe’s is selling delicata sliced, FYI! Or use 3 to 4 cups cubed butternut squash (a lot of stores sell it pre-chopped this time of year!) or 1 large, cubed sweet potato.

• Balsamic : Apple cider vinegar (ideal sub!) or any other vinegar. If you’re not using balsamic (which is sweeter than these subs), add about a teaspoon of honey or maple syrup to your dressing. If your balsamic isn’t as sweet as mine , you may need to do that anyways.

• Olive oil/EVOO : It’s really important to use extra-virgin olive oil here! It’s so incredibly good for you! And delicious! But if you need to use something else, plain olive oil or a neutral oil like avocado is it.

• Honey : Maple syrup

• Dried oregano: Italian seasoning, dried basil, dried thyme, fresh oregano (but use a tablespoon of it instead)

• Garlic powder: 1 very small garlic clove grated (I use a microplane for that) or onion powder

• Kale : Mixed greens, mesclun greens, arugula, spinach, or another green leaf lettuce

• Honey crisp apple: Any apple, pear, persimmons

• Almonds : Salted, roasted pistachios, walnuts, pecans, sunflower seeds, pepitas. Omit if you’re allergic to both nuts and seeds! Maybe add croutons instead for crunch!

• White cheddar cheese : Blue cheese, goat cheese, Parm, Gruyère… basically any cheese you love would be good in here.

• Dates : Yellow raisins, dried cranberries, dried cherries, or omit

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 delicata squash, thinly sliced (watch this video for how to slice it!)
ingredients.name: delicata squash, thinly sliced (watch this video for how to slice it!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon dried oregano or Italian seasoning
ingredients.name: dried oregano or Italian seasoning

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and finely ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and finely ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder or 1 very small garlic clove, grated
ingredients.name: garlic powder or 1 very small garlic clove

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch curly or flat leaf kale, tough stems removed, finely chopped (4 heaping cups — feel free to buy store-bought chopped kale, just pick through it to remove any tough stems)
ingredients.name: curly or flat leaf kale, tough stems removed, finely chopped (4 heaping cups — feel free to buy store-bought chopped kale, just pick through it to remove any tough stems)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium honey crisp apple, cut into thin batons (or chopped if that’s easier for you)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 dates, pits removed and finely chopped

preparationSteps: Preheat your oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

Toss 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts and 1 sliced delicata squash with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, 2 teaspoons honey, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon of dried oregano or Italian seasoning, and several grinds pepper. Cook for 15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through (to 165°F internally), then transfer the chicken to a cutting board to rest.

Return the squash to the oven to cook for another 10 to 15 minutes, or until very tender and browned. After letting the chicken rest for 5 minutes, chop one chicken breast up. Save 1 chicken breast for later.

While the chicken and squash are cooking: In large serving bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder (or one grated clove). Taste and add 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup if your dressing is too tangy (the balsamic I use is sweet enough that I don’t need any).

Add 1 bunch finely chopped kale to the bowl of dressing, sprinkle with a big pinch of kosher salt , and use clean hands to massage the salt and dressing into the kale until it feels soft — about 7 squeezes between your palms.
Add the finely chopped chicken, roasted squash, 1 apple cut into thin batons, 1/3 cup roughly chopped almonds, 4 ounces roughly chopped cheddar cheese, and 3 chopped dates. Toss to coat. DIG IN!

name: the perfect kentucky derby party menu: mint julep garden bar
note: Prep time: 20 minutes to make the simple syrups + a few hours to let them cool

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 ripe peach, chopped, or 1 cup frozen peaches
ingredients.name: ripe peach, chopped, or 1 cup frozen peaches

preparationSteps: Make a simple syrup by adding 3 cups sugar and 3 cups water to a small saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat.
Add a large handful of fresh mint leaves to the first bottle. Pour about 1/3 of the warm simple syrup over the mint and let it steep while you prepare the other syrups.
Place 1 cup strawberries, raspberries, or blueberries in a blender with 1/3 of the simple syrup and blend until completely smooth. Transfer to the second bottle.
Rinse the blender, then add 1 chopped peach or 1 cup of frozen peaches with the remaining 1/3 of the simple syrup and blend until fully pureed. Transfer to the third bottle.
Let the syrups cool completely before serving.

To make mint sugar: Combine 1/2 cup sugar, grated zest from 1 lemon, and 4 mint leaves in a shallow bowl. Use your fingers to rub everything together until fragrant, then remove and discard the mint leaves and transfer the mint sugar to a small plate or bowl for rimming glasses.
Cut 2 lemons (including the one you just zested) into wedges and place in a small bowl.

Now the fun part! Set up the mint julep garden bar by placing the mint syrup, berry syrup, peach syrup, bottle of bourbon, club soda, crushed ice, lemon wedges, and the remaining mint sprigs together.
Once everything is set up, guests can build their drinks right at the bar. Here are two easy cocktail ideas using any of the flavored syrups.

name: the perfect kentucky derby party menu: salt vinegar deviled eggs
note: Cook time: ~15 minutes (plus time to hard boil eggs, if needed)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 peeled hard-boiled eggs (if hard-boiling your own, you’ll also need a splash of a light-colored vinegar)
ingredients.name: peeled hard-boiled eggs (if hard-boiling your own, you’ll also need a splash of a light-colored vinegar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Salt & vinegar potato chips, for topping
ingredients.name: Salt & vinegar potato chips, for topping

preparationSteps: Pre-peeled hard-boiled eggs are a great shortcut, but if you’re boiling them yourself, here’s the easy way:

Place 12 eggs in a sauté pan or saucepan that fits them in a single layer. Add enough water to just cover the eggs and a splash of light-colored vinegar (like apple cider, white wine, or red wine vinegar). Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Once the water reaches a boil, turn off the heat, move the pan off the burner, and let the eggs sit in the hot water for 10 minutes.

Drain the hot water from the pot then add cold water with ice. Drain again. Once cool enough to handle, gently roll each egg on the counter to crack the shell all over. Start peeling from the wider end, then slide a spoon under the shell to help lift it off. Rinse away any stray shell pieces and you’re ready to go.
Slice the 12 hard-boiled eggs in half lengthwise and scoop the yolks into a mixing bowl.

Mash the yolks with a fork until smooth, then stir in 1/2 cup crème fraîche, 1/4 cup mayonnaise , 1 tablespoon sweet pickle juice, 1 tablespoon Dijon or yellow mustard, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika, grated zest from 1 lemon, and a few grinds of freshly cracked black pepper. Taste and add more kosher salt if needed. If the mixture looks a little lumpy, you can switch to a whisk to make it extra smooth.
Spoon the filling into a plastic zip-top bag, snip a small corner off the bag, and pipe the filling back into the egg whites. If this feels too fussy, you can just use a spoon.
Just before serving, top each deviled egg with a salt & vinegar chip and garnish with chopped chives . Set the rest of the chips out, too, for extra snacking.

name: the 2023 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: california christmas roast

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups red wine (whatever kind you like to drink)
ingredients.name: red wine (whatever kind you like to drink)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

preparationSteps: Add 2 cups red wine, 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tablespoon garlic powder, 1 tablespoon dried oregano, and 1 tablespoon black pepper to a large ziplock or bowl and stir to combine.

Trim the fat (the hard white stuff) off of 1 tri-tip roast. It doesn’t have to be perfect, but there’s usually a large fatty piece on one side of the roast, and we want to trim as much of that off as possible. (Fat on meat usually = good, but this is too much.) Add the tri-tip to the marinade and marinate for up to 24 hours, but 4 at the bare minimum.

When you’re ready to cook, preheat the oven to 350°F. Bring 4 tablespoons of butter to room temperature. If you follow me on IG you know my tip — stick half a stick of (wrapped) butter in the waistline of your pants to bring it to room temp quickly.
Shake off as much marinade from the tri-tip as possible, then pat it completely dry.

Warm 2 tablespoons oil in your largest oven-proof skillet (such as a cast iron or stainless steel) over medium-high heat. When it starts to smoke, add the tri-tip and cook until a nice golden-brown crust forms, 4 to 6 minutes.
Flip, then smoosh the room-temperature butter onto the top (seared) side of the tri-tip.

Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 11 minutes per pound to cook it to medium (which is better than medium-rare when cooking tri-tip). So, if you purchased a 3 1/2 pound tri-tip and cut off 1/2 pound of fat, 3x11 = 33 minutes of roast time. It should reach between 140 and 145°F internally.
Remove the tri-tip from the oven and let it rest in the skillet. Tilt the skillet to the side and use a large spoon to spoon the pan juices over top of the tri-tip.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then slice against the grain .

name: the 2023 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: honey roasted carrots
note: Cook time: 50 minutes (10 minutes active, 40 minutes inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pound carrots, cleaned and sliced in half vertically
ingredients.name: carrots, cleaned and sliced in half vertically

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup roasted, salted pistachios, finely chopped
ingredients.name: roasted, salted pistachios

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line your largest rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Wash and slice 2 pounds carrots in half vertically. You don’t need to peel them, but you can if you want to. Drizzle with 3 tablespoons oil, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin , and use your hands to really get in there and toss everything together to evenly distribute the ingredients.
Spread the carrots into an even layer and roast for 40 minutes. Meanwhile, take the burrata out of the fridge to let it come to room temperature, and finely chop 1/4 cup pistachios.

Transfer the roasted carrots to a platter. Tear the burrata ball into several pieces and place them on top. Scatter the chopped pistachios over top. Finish with a drizzle of honey and extra-virgin olive oil.

name: the 2023 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: kale salad for all
note: Cook time: 15 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 to 12 ounces shredded kale (yes, I’m telling you to buy it pre-chopped)
ingredients.name: shredded kale (yes, I’m telling you to buy it pre-chopped)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large Honeycrisp apple, sliced into batons
ingredients.name: large Honeycrisp apple

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup roasted, salted almonds, finely chopped
ingredients.name: roasted, salted almonds

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces Parmesan cheese, finely chopped (we want random chunks, not a fine powder)
ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese, finely chopped (we want random chunks, not a fine powder)

preparationSteps: In a jar, combine the juice of 2 lemons, 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tablespoon honey, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Shake to combine. Taste and add more salt, honey, or whatever to your liking. I like a tart dressing, but some people like it sweeter, do your thing!

Add 10 to 12 ounces shredded kale to a large salad bowl. Pick out any big stems and discard. Sprinkle with a big pinch of salt , then use your hands to massage it, AKA scrunch it together in your fists, 8 to 10 times, until it feels a tiny bit wet in your hands.
Thinly slice 1 large Honeycrisp apple into batons, finely chop 1/2 cup roasted, salted almonds , and finely chop 4 ounces of Parmesan cheese . Add them to the bowl along with 1/3 cup yellow raisins .
Just before serving, shake the salad dressing to combine it again, then toss your desired amount into the salad.

name: the 2023 easy-but-fancy holiday menu: roasted mushrooms
note: Cook time: 45 minutes (5 minutes active, 40 minutes inactive)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds of sliced mushrooms (buy them sliced)
ingredients.name: of sliced mushrooms (buy them sliced)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Toss 2 pounds sliced mushrooms, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 1/4 teaspoons garlic powder, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to your largest rimmed baking sheet and toss to evenly coat.
Roast for 40 minutes.
If you are cooking the tri-tip at the same time, stir several spoonfuls of those pan juices into the mushrooms at the end.
Transfer to a platter and sprinkle with a little chopped parsley .

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: salty minty dogs
note: Prep time: 10 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 large mint sprigs, plus more for garnish
ingredients.name: large mint sprigs, plus more for garnish

preparationSteps: Pour 1/2 cup sea salt onto a small plate and grate the zest of 1 lemon right on top. Use your fingers to pinch the zest into the salt.
Combine 2 cups grapefruit juice, 1 cup gin, and 1/2 cup club soda in a pitcher. Slap 2 large mint sprigs between your hands, then add them to the pitcher.
Cut the lemon in half and use it to wet the rims of your glasses. Dip the rim in the lemon salt. Fill the glasses with ice, then pour in the drink!
*If you want to make these ahead of time, that’s a great plan, but don’t add the club soda until the last minute.

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: rosemary pecans
note: Cook time: 35 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon finely minced fresh rosemary or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary, crushed
ingredients.name: finely minced fresh rosemary or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 250°F.

Place 4 cups pecan halves on a large rimmed baking sheet. Melt 4 tablespoons butter and pour it over top along with 1 tablespoon minced fresh rosemary, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Use your hands to toss everything around and get the nuts evenly coated.
Spread the nuts into an even layer, then bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until deeply toasted. Give them a stir every 10 minutes or so.
Allow to cool completely, then transfer to an airtight container and store at room temperature for up to 10 days.

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: biscuits with hot honey butter
note: Cook time: 45 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 ounces grated Gruyère cheese (a little less than 1 cup)
ingredients.name: grated Gruyère cheese (a little less than 1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (ground on the largest setting — we want big flecks of pepper)
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper (ground on the largest setting — we want big flecks of pepper)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 cups heavy cream, plus more for brushing the biscuits
ingredients.name: heavy cream, plus more for brushing the biscuits

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon hot honey (I love Red Clay (and code CARO15 or CARO20 should work!), or just use regular honey and a dash of hot sauce)
ingredients.name: hot honey (I love Red Clay (and code CARO15 or CARO20 should work!), or just use regular honey and a dash of hot sauce)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 475°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Add 2 cups self-rising flour, 3 ounces grated gruyère, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper to a large bowl and use a fork to stir to combine. Stir in 1 1/2 cups heavy cream as much as possible with the fork, then use your hands to combine everything. You’ll think that there’s too much flour but there’s not! Use your hands to work it into the dough.

Transfer the dough to the baking sheet and flatten it into about the size of a piece of computer paper, then fold it in half and repeat that process twice more (the process = flatten it out as much as possible, then fold it). It’ll get harder to flatten it with each fold — that’s normal! We’re creating those flaky biscuit layers here!
Pat the thrice-folded dough into a 1 inch-thick rectangle, then cut it into 8 biscuits . Or 16 biscuits, if you want to make little appetizer biscuits!

Separate the biscuits and brush them with a bit of extra heavy cream. If you don’t own a pastry brush, just use your finger to coat the tops and sides of the biscuits. This will help them brown nicely.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden brown and puffy and gorgeous!

While they’re baking, add 4 tablespoons room-temperature unsalted butter , 1 tablespoon hot honey , and a pinch of kosher salt to a small bowl and smash to combine. It takes a sec — just be patient (maybe give this job to a kid!) and keep smashing. After a couple minutes it’ll come together.

*You can make the biscuits ahead of time all the way until the step of baking them (don’t brush them with heavy cream until they’re about to go into the oven!). Wrap and refrigerate the entire baking sheet with the cut biscuits on it, then bake them while the lamb is resting so that they’re fresh and perfect. Or, bake them the morning of and simply reheat them for a couple minutes in the hot oven while the lamb rests.

**FYI, one of my kids got mad because the biscuits were “spicy.” They aren’t what I’d consider spicy — they just have a little kick from the pepper — but perhaps omit it if you’re feeding a bunch of kids averse to spice.

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: lamb potatoes
note: Cook time: 2 hours + 15 minutes rest time (if possible, brine the lamb for up to 24 hours)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons Greek seasoning, divided
ingredients.name: plus 2 teaspoons Greek seasoning

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon plus 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided
ingredients.name: plus 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 1/2 teaspoons freshly ground black pepper, divided
ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, divided
ingredients.name: plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

preparationSteps: Place 1 boneless leg of lamb on a plastic cutting board and if it came in netting, remove the netting. Open up the lamb, dry with a clean kitchen towel, then use a sharp knife to remove any excess fat from the center (non-smooth side) of the leg. Flip it over and trim off all but a very thin layer of fat (we want to remove the hard, thick white fat, but a thin layer is a good thing).

Season it all over with 3 tablespoons Greek seasoning, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, and 2 teaspoons freshly ground black pepper. Roll the lamb up as tightly as you can into a coil, then use kitchen twine to truss it, AKA cut 3 or 4 long pieces of twine and tie the leg together. Put the lamb in a small roasting dish (a Dutch oven or cast iron skillet works!) fat side UP and place in the refrigerator, uncovered, for at least 4, but ideally 24 hours.
When you’re ready to cook, preheat your oven to 300°F and remove the lamb from the refrigerator. Pour 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken stock around the lamb.

Cut 2 pounds Yukon gold potatoes into 1-inch wedges, and halve and peel 3 shallots and place them in a roasting dish with high sides (I used a 9x13” cake pan!). Drizzle with 1/4 cup oil, 2 teaspoons tablespoon Greek seasoning, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, the juice of 2 large lemons, and 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken stock and toss to coat.
Roast the lamb and potatoes for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring the potatoes every 30 minutes, until an internal thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the lamb registers 130°F.
Remove the potatoes and lamb from the oven and crank the oven up to 500°F. Once it reaches 500°F, return the lamb to the oven for 7 to 10 minutes to crisp up the fatty top.

Transfer the lamb to a clean cutting board to rest for at least 15 minutes. Cut off the twine, then thinly slice and arrange with lots of fresh herbs. Transfer the potatoes to a serving dish (or serve them straight from the roasting pan). Sprinkle flaky sea salt over the potatoes and lamb before serving.

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: minty yogurt sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large lemon, ideally organic because we’re zesting it
ingredients.name: large lemon, ideally organic because we’re zesting it

preparationSteps: Add 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup mayo, 1 1/2 packed cups mint leaves, 1 peeled garlic clove, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a food processor or blender and blend until smooth. Transfer to a serving bowl.

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: springy salad
note: Cook time: 10 minutes (plus 20 minutes or more to let the onions pickle)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5-ounce container of washed mixed greens or arugula
ingredients.name: of washed mixed greens or arugula

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup Rosemary Pecans (recipe above, or purchase store-bought candied pecans), finely chopped
ingredients.name: Rosemary Pecans (recipe above, or purchase store-bought candied pecans)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces Parmesan cheese (no need to actually measure this, just grab a wedge of Parm and use a vegetable peeler to peel as many pieces as you want onto your salad!)
ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese (no need to actually measure this, just grab a wedge of Parm and use a vegetable peeler to peel as many pieces as you want onto your salad!)

preparationSteps: To make the pickled red onions, slice 1 red onion as thinly as you can and stuff the slices into a jar or glass container. Fill the container 3/4 of the way up with champagne vinegar, then fill it the rest of the way with hot tap water. Add 1 tablespoon sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt and shake to combine. Leave at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or ideally refrigerate for at least 24 hours before using.

To make the champagne vinaigrette, add all the ingredients ( 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup champagne vinegar, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 2 teaspoons honey , and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt ) to a jar and shake to combine. Taste and adjust to your liking (some like it sweeter, some like it tangier!).

Add 5 ounces mixed greens, a handful of pickled red onions (you can also chop these up so that you get just a small bit of onion in each bite) , 1/2 cup finely chopped Rosemary Pecans, and a bunch of shaved Parm to a large salad bowl. Toss with your desired amount of champagne vinaigrette, season with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, and serve immediately.
*The pickled red onions are good for up to 10 days in the fridge.

name: the ultimate easy-but-fancy spring menu: balsamic butter asparagus
note: Cook time: 15 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound asparagus (ideally medium sized, about the width of a pencil), woody stems removed (AKA, trim about 2 inches off the bottom and discard them because they are tough and fibrous!)
ingredients.name: asparagus (ideally medium sized, about the width of a pencil), woody stems removed (AKA, trim about 2 inches off the bottom and discard them because they are tough and fibrous!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chopped roasted salted almonds (or any nut works)
ingredients.name: chopped roasted salted almonds (or any nut works)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: Big pinch of red pepper flakes

preparationSteps: Warm 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound trimmed asparagus and a big pinch of salt and get the asparagus into as even a layer as possible so that they’re touching the skillet as much as possible. Cover (use a baking sheet if you don’t have a lid that fits) and let them sit for 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, smash 6 garlic cloves as flat as possible using the side of a chef’s knife. Place the flat edge of the knife on top of a garlic clove on a cutting board, then use your fist to bang down on the blade as hard as you can to smash the garlic!
Uncover the skillet, add the smashed garlic, shake the skillet to move the asparagus around, then cover for another 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop 1/4 cup roasted salted almonds and set aside.
Stir a big pinch of red pepper flakes, 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, and 1 tablespoon unsalted butter into the asparagus and toss to coat.
Transfer asparagus to a serving platter and scatter the chopped almonds and a pinch of flaky salt over top. I grated a bit of lemon zest on top too!

name: lemony protein “alfredo”
note: Cook time: 25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound spaghetti or another long pasta like fettuccini or linguini (or any noodle, but I like long best for this)
ingredients.name: spaghetti or another long pasta like fettuccini or linguini (or any noodle, but I like long best for this)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup grated Parmesan (about 3 1/2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: grated Parmesan (about 3 1/2 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small garlic clove, smashed and peeled
ingredients.name: small garlic clove, smashed and peeled

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into chunks
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add 1 pound pasta to the boiling water and cook according to package instructions for al dente.

While the pasta’s cooking, add the zest and juice of 1 lemon to a blender along with 1 cup whole-milk cottage cheese , 1 cup grated Parmesan, 1 small smashed garlic clove (smash it with the side of your knife then peel off and discard the peel), and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt .
A couple of minutes before the pasta’s ready, use a coffee mug or glass measuring cup to scoop out 1 1/2 cups of the pasta water.

Add 1/2 cup of the pasta water to the blender and blend until smooth (it may take a minute or so!). If it’s not blending well, add another 1/4 cup of pasta water (or however much you need to get it going) and blend again.

Drain the pasta and return it to the pot. Chop 4 tablespoons unsalted butter into small chunks. Off the heat, add the blended cottage cheese mixture and the butter to the noodles. Stir and toss vigorously until the butter is melted and the pasta is coated in sauce, adding more pasta water as needed, about 1/4 cup at a time, until glossy . The sauce may clump at first but keep stirring, tossing, and adding pasta water until it’s smooth! It may take 2 to 3 minutes — just keep going, it’ll get there. (You may not use all the pasta water you reserved — stop when it gets glossy and smooth!)
Season to taste with more kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper until it’s absolutely delicious.
Serve topped with more freshly grated Parmesan and black pepper.

name: sheet-pan crispy polenta, eggplant, tomatoes, sausage, and burrata
note: Cook time: 32 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 globe eggplant, zebra-peeled, sliced into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: globe eggplant, zebra-peeled

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (1-pound) tube precooked polenta, cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: precooked polenta

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons (or up to 1 tablespoon if you want more spice!) Calabrian chili paste, or 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (omit if you don’t want any spice)
ingredients.name: (or up to 1 tablespoon if you want more spice!) Calabrian chili paste, or 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (omit if you don’t want any spice)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mild or spicy Italian sausage (the uncooked links that come in casings)
ingredients.name: mild or spicy Italian sausage (the uncooked links that come in casings)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 container burrata, brought to room temperature
ingredients.name: burrata, brought to room temperature

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Take the burrata container out of the fridge, pour the liquid out, and let it sit on the counter to come to room temperature while you cook the rest of the recipe.

Add everything to your largest rimmed baking sheet as you go: Peel 1 globe eggplant into zebra stripes (AKA don’t peel the whole thing — rather, peel alternating stripes all over) and slice it into 1-inch bite-sized pieces. Cut 1 tube precooked polenta into 1-inch pieces (I quarter it length-wise, then slice into quarters). Thinly slice 4 garlic cloves. Drizzle 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil over everything, then add 1 pint cherry tomatoes, 4 large thyme sprigs, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt , and 2 teaspoons Calabrian chili paste (or up to 1 tablespoon if you like spice!) and use your hands to really get in there and toss until evenly coated .
Squeeze 1 pound Italian sausages out of the casings into small pieces and place them all over the sheet pan. No need to roll into perfect balls — I actually like it better with craggy edges!

Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the eggplant is tender. Take the sheet pan out of the oven and give everything a stir (gently! you don’t want the polenta to fall apart! though it’s OK if it does a little). Fish out and discard the thyme sprigs. Grate about 1/4 cup of Parmesan over everything.
Turn the broiler on high.

Return the sheet pan to the middle rack of the oven and broil for 3 to 5 minutes to crisp everything up a bit, until the polenta gets some nice crispy brown spots. You might need to rotate the baking sheet once to get even browning all over. If you don’t have a broiler, roast at 450°F for 4 to 6 minutes.
As always, I want you to turn the oven light on and sit on the ground right in front of your oven, watching the entire time it broils. DO NOT LET YOUR DINNER BURN!!!
Divide between 4 plates or bowls and tear chunks of burrata over top of each. Dollop more Calabrian chili paste over top if you love heat! Serve immediately.

name: New York Times Chocolate Chip Cookies
note: The New York Times Chocolate Chip Cookie has cracked the code for the perfect recipe for chocolate chip cookies. The results are a chewy cookie with crispy edges and a soft, gooey center.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups minus 2 tablespoons cake flour (8½ ounces)
ingredients.name: minus 2 tablespoons cake flour (8½ ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons granulated sugar (8 ounces)
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons granulated sugar (8 ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/4 pounds bittersweet chocolate, at least 60% cacao
ingredients.name: bittersweet chocolate, at least 60% cacao

preparationSteps: In a medium sized mixing bowl, combine the cake flour, bread flour, baking soda, baking powder, and coarse salt. Stir using a wire whisk until well sifted. Set aside.
In the bowl of a stand mixer, add the softened butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar. Beat using the paddle attachment until well creamed and very light, approximately 5 minutes.
While continuing to mix, add one egg at a time, mixing in between each addition. Then, stir in the vanilla extract.
Decrease the mixer speed to low. Slowly add the flour mixture 1 cup at a time. Scrape down the sides of the mixing bowl using a silicone spatula if needed.
After all of the flour has been added, scrape down the sides again and continue to mix on low speed just until combined, about 10 seconds.
Add the chocolate, stirring slowing so the pieces don't break.
Remove the bowl from the stand mixer and transfer the chocolate chip cookie dough to a container with a lid and refrigerate for 24-36 hours before baking cookies.
Remove the dough from the refrigerator and let sit at room temperature while the oven preheats and you prepare the baking pans.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Scoop cookie dough in 3½-ounce sized balls (approximately golf ball size). Place 6 balls of cookie dough onto each prepared baking sheet, spacing them so they don't stick together while cookie.
Lightly sprinkle the tops of each cookie dough ball with a pinch of sea salt.
Transfer the baking sheet to the preheated oven. Bake cookies at 350 degrees F for 16-20 minutes, or until golden brown but still soft.
After baking, place the cookie sheets on a wire cooling rack and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Then, remove cookies from the baking sheet and place directly on the wire rack to cool for 5 more minutes before serving.
Repeat the process with the remaining cookie dough, transfer leftover cookie dough back to the refrigerator, or freeze cookie dough.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 Bunches Scallions , trimmed to match the length of beans
ingredients.name: Scallions

preparationSteps: Heat oven to 425 F.

To the beans and scallions with a healthy glug of olive oil, half a teaspoon salt, and many twists of black pepper. Spread onto two baking sheets in a single layer, so the ingredients aren’t too crowded. Roast until nicely, softened, and brown – even char, dashing places, 20 to 30 minutes. Parentheses rotate the pants during cooking if you need to so everything cooks evenly.
Pile the beans and scallions into a large bowl and sprinkle with the vinegar. Toss to mix and let rest for about 10 minutes to cool slightly.

Whisk together the pine nut vinaigrette, lemon juice, and chile flakes in a small bowl. Pour over the beans and scallions and toss to coat evenly. Taste the beans and dress with more lemon juice, salt, black pepper, or chile flakes to make the dressing zingy. Add the mint, basil, and pine nuts and toss gently again.

name: Pine Nut Vinaigrette
preparationSteps: Pour the vinegar, fish sauce, and water into a small bowl.

Put the pine nuts, garlic, chile flakes, and about half the vinegar mixture into a food processor and process until you have a slightly smooth puree, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed. With the motor running, drizzle in the olive oil and then the rest of the vinegar mixture. The ingredients should emulsify into a creamy, thick-but-pourable dressing.
Taste and adjust the flavors with more vinegar, fish sauce, or chile flakes. Adjust the consistency with more water if need be.
Store in the fridge for up to one week.

name: Gloriously Huge Chicken Focaccia Sandwich
note: Hooooo baby. Toasted focaccia, pesto mayo, melty cheese, and fresh veggies make this chicken focaccia sandwich an easy, flavor-packed lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: thinly sliced deli chicken (or turkey)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or silicone baking mat.

Lay the focaccia flat on a cutting board and use a serrated knife to make a horizontal cut all the way through, slicing it in half lengthwise. Work slowly and be careful to make the halves as even as possible!

Slice the tomatoes and use a paper towel to pat out a bit of the moisture. Layer them on top of the red onions and season the tomatoes/sandwich with pinches of salt, pepper and all-purpose seasoning. Add a pile of arugula and drizzle with a little olive oil and pinch of salt.
Flip the top piece onto the sandwich. Slice into 6-8 pieces and serve warm! Diviiiiine.

name: melty zucchini pasta with goat cheese and parm
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes (or 34 if you forget to add your noodles right away!)

• Order of operations: If you watched episode two of the What To Cook show, you saw that I actually added the sliced zucchini and onion to the cold skillet as I sliced. You can absolutely do it that way!!! It’s standard to warm the oil in the skillet before adding the vegetables, but when we’re working with so much veg I often add it to the cold pan, then add the oil, then put the skillet over the heat and start cooking. Either way works!

• I don’t have a skillet big enough to fit all this zucchini: A 12-inch skillet will work and a 14-inch skillet is even better. If you don’t have one big enough, you can use a Dutch oven!

• Tip: If/when your zucchini starts releasing a ton of liquid, just keep cooking — it’ll concentrate into a jammy, sweet-savory base that coats the pasta beautifully.

• Bulk it up/extra extra : Toast chopped walnuts in butter and scatter them over the pasta for a really nice crunch.

• Make it an app: Cook the zucchini, onion, and garlic down until totally soft. Add some more olive oil and balsamic and serve it with big hunks of bread! Or, for more of a passed hors d’oeuvre situation, spread goat cheese or Boursin on crostini and top it with the melty zucchini mixture.

• Feeding kids: Omit the red pepper flakes if your kids are sensitive to spice. You can add a little shake to bowls of people who want them instead. Also, if your kids hate anything green, you could peel your zucchini before slicing them and they’ll totally blend in with the noods!

• A Parm grating hack: Pulse it in your food processor or blender until finely grated.

• Prep ahead: You can make this whole meal a day or two ahead of time, let it cool, and store it covered in the fridge. Reheat it on the stove, adding water a splash at a time until it’s loose and creamy again. Or, you can just prep your sliced zucchini and onion a day or two ahead of time and store those in an airtight container in the fridge. That’ll make dinner come together so quickly when you’re ready to cook!

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers are great stored in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

• Must have meat/extra protein: Pretty much any meat would be great on top of or served beside this pasta — chicken, shrimp, steak, pork tenderloin. For extra vegetarian protein, you can add a can of drained and rinsed soft white beans into the mix, like butter beans, cannellini, or navy (I wouldn’t use chickpeas — they’d be too hard!). Stir them into the zucchini mixture before you add the garlic so they can get warm. I’d probably go with chicken or shrimp marinated simply in some olive oil, lemon juice, chopped fresh herbs, salt, and pepper! Here’s cook times for those, if using: For shrimp: Bake at 400°F for 6 to 10 minutes, or until pink and opaque. To grill: Thread the shrimp onto skewers (if you’re using wooden skewers, be sure to soak them in cold water for 20 or so minutes first so they don’t catch on fire!); don’t pack the shrimp too tightly when threading them, they need a little breathing room. Heat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the skewers for 2 to 3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp are pink, opaque, shaped like a “C,” and have some nice grill marks. For chicken thighs : Bake at 425°F for 25 to 30 minutes, or until 165°F internally. Or grill over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes per side, or until cooked through. For chicken breasts : Bake at 425°F for 15 to 20 minutes (could be up to 30 if they’re monster breasts), or until 165°F internally. Or grill over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

• Dairy-free: Use Boursin’s dairy-free Garlic & Fine Herbs (you can use 1, 1 1/2, or 2 blocks of it depending how rich and “cheesy” you want it to be! And just skip the Parm.

• Gluten-free: Use your favorite gluten-free noodles cooked per package directions!

• Long pasta noodles: Short noodles, or any noodle substitute cooked according to package directions

• Zucchini: Yellow squash also works here — or use half squash and half zucchini!

• Red or white onion: 2 shallots, thinly sliced scallions, or chives

• Garlic cloves: 1 teaspoon garlic or onion powder, or cubes of frozen pre-crushed garlic

• Soft green herbs: Any fresh green herb you love! Chives, parsley, basil, etc.

• Extra-virgin olive oil: Olive oil, avocado oil, grapeseed oil, or another neutral oil

• Red pepper flakes: Chili crisp, Calabrian chili paste, or omit

• Balsamic vinegar: The balsamic is a big player flavor-wise, so I really recommend using it if you can! If you’re in a bind, white wine vinegar, red wine vinegar, or sherry vinegar could add that acidity, but I’d probably add a little drizzle of honey or pinch of salt to make up for the sweetness balsamic brings the dish!

• Goat cheese: Fromage blanc, feta, or Boursin! Boursin would be so, so good. A block of Boursin is 5.3 ounces, so you can use 1 1/2 blocks since I call for 8 ounces of goat cheese. Or use 2 whole ones! Or just 1 if you don’t mind it being a little less creamy and cheesy.

• Parmesan: Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (aka fancy Parm) is the best if you can find it. Or use regular Parm, pecorino romano, or Grana Padano. Or skip it and use extra goat cheese.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound long pasta noodles, such as spaghetti, linguine, or bucatini
ingredients.name: long pasta noodles, such as spaghetti, linguine, or bucatini

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 bunch soft green herbs, such as fresh basil, parsley, and/or mint
ingredients.name: soft green herbs, such as fresh basil, parsley, and/or mint

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, plus more to taste
ingredients.name: balsamic vinegar, plus more to taste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2/3 cup freshly grated Parmesan (2 2/3 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan (2 2/3 ounces), plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add 1 pound long pasta noodles and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out about 1 cup of the pasta cooking water (!!! DON’T SKIP THIS!) , then drain the pasta and return it to the hot pot.

Meanwhile, halve 6 zucchini lengthwise, then slice them crosswise into thin half circles. If you own a mandoline, you can use it here to slice your zucchini! Very thinly slice 1 red or white onion and thinly slice 8 garlic cloves . Roughly chop 1/2 bunch soft green herb leaves and tender stems .

Warm 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil in your largest skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the zucchini , onion , 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (if using — omit if you don’t want any spice) , 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt , and a few grinds of black pepper . Cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is softened and has released a lot of liquid, 8 to 10 minutes. Turn the heat up to high and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated, any remaining liquid is slightly thickened, and the zucchini is breaking down, 10 to 12 minutes; turn down the heat if the vegetables are browning too quickly. Stir in the sliced garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar and cook, stirring to coat the zucchini, until well incorporated, about 1 minute. Remove from the heat.

Scrape the zucchini mixture into the pasta in the pot. Crumble in 8 ounces goat cheese , then add 2/3 cup freshly grated Parm and a splash of the reserved pasta cooking water and stir until everything is coated and creamy. Add the Parm a little at a time, stirring until it’s well incorporated before you add a little more! This will help prevent it from clumping . Add more pasta cooking water a splash at a time if you’d like a looser sauce. Stir in most of the chopped herbs , reserving about 1/3 cup for serving. Taste and add more vinegar , kosher salt , and/or pepper if needed.
Use tongs to lift the pasta into shallow bowls, getting plenty of the melty zucchini, too. Top with the reserved chopped herbs and some grated Parm and serve warm.

name: sheet-pan chicken with artichokes and potatoes, 2021

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Toss 1 pound gnocchi, 2 thinly sliced yellow squash, 1 pint cherry tomatoes, 1/4 cup sliced sundried tomatoes and a splash of their oil, the kernels from 2 ears of corn, 1/4 cup finely chopped herbs, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, several grinds of black pepper, and the zest of 1 lemon on a large baking sheet. name: summer shrimp panzanella
note:
Cook time: 32 minutes and 38 seconds

• Prep ahead: The veg and bread can be totally prepped ahead of time. Store the vegetables in the fridge (either covered on the sheet pan or in an airtight container) and store the bread in a zip-top bag at room temp.

• Halve it/love your leftovers/meal prep it : You could very easily halve this recipe if you’re feeding 1 or 2 people. If you have leftovers, store them in the fridge in an airtight container and eat ASAP. Panzanella is best right away when the crispy bread is starting to soften from the dressing but isn’t mushy yet — but I’d definitely eat leftovers of this if I had them in the fridge! If you want to meal prep this recipe, keep all the parts separate (dressing, veg and shrimp, and bread) and compile your serving of panzanella right before you eat.

• Feeding kids: At one point, all of my kids reliably ate shrimp, and it was a glorious time. Frozen shrimp are IMO the easiest protein out there — you can thaw them quickly in a bowl of cold water, then just pat them dry and cook in mere minutes! These days, only my baby will eat them, but that’s OK! George, Tav, and I enjoy this whole meal while the other boys crush the croutons and corn, and I throw a meat stick on their plate for some protein.

• Bring it to a party: Watch this episode of the What To Cook show to see my favorite trick for bringing a delicious salad to a party. Here are the Cliff’s Notes: Make the dressing in the serving bowl and cover it with a big piece of parchment. Let the veggies and shrimp cool to room temperature, then add them on top of the parchment. Top with the bread then the herbs, and wrap the bowl tightly with plastic. Once you’re ready to eat, uncover the bowl, slide the sheet of parchment out, and toss! It’s OK if the dressing separated, it will still taste great.

• Vegetarian: Swap the shrimp for white beans — add a can of rinsed and drained navy, cannellini beans, or chickpeas to the sheet pan with the other veg!

• Dairy-free: Use dairy-free feta, goat cheese if that would work for you, or just skip the cheese altogether. Cubed avocado would be a tasty, creamy, DF alternative.

• Gluten-free: Use a loaf of gluten-free bread. If you can’t find good-quality GF bread, you could swap the bread for roasted chickpeas.

• Zucchini: Squash, eggplant, red onion, or omit

• Corn: You can use 2 to 3 cups frozen corn if it’s what you’ve got (you can add it to the sheet pan frozen). Canned corn (drained) would also work. If you don’t like corn, you can omit it and swap in a red onion cut into wedges, or add another pint of tomatoes.

• Cherry tomatoes: Chopped heirloom tomatoes, but remove some of the seeds so there isn’t too much liquid. If you can’t eat tomatoes, swap them for chopped red bell pepper, a red onion cut into wedges, or extra corn and/or zucchini.

• Extra-virgin olive oil: Olive oil, avocado oil, or another neutral cooking oil

• Garlic powder: Onion powder or 4 minced fresh cloves of garlic (divided)

• Flaky sea salt: Kosher salt

• Sourdough: Ciabatta, country loaf, French bread, Italian bread, baguette, whole-wheat bread, gluten-free artisan bread. Or swap the bread out for crispy chickpeas!

• Lemon juice: A light-colored vinegar like white wine, red wine, or apple cider vinegar

• Whole-grain mustard: Dijon mustard, yellow mustard, or omit

• Honey: Maple syrup, agave, brown sugar

• Basil and parsley : You can just use one rather than both, or you can swap either herb for another soft leafy green herb like cilantro or chives. Arugula would be good here, too!

• Shrimp: Chicken thighs would be great instead of shrimp! Add them to the sheet pan at the same time as your vegetables — add more oil and an extra big pinch of salt and few grinds of pepper to make sure everything is well coated. Cook them for the whole 20 minutes then measure their internal temp. You may need to cook them for about 5 more minutes to hit the safe internal temperature of 165°F. The vegetables can cook that extra time, too. See “vegetarian” note above for another idea.

• Feta: Goat cheese, fromage blanc, ricotta salata, freshly shaved Parmesan or pecorino romano, or just omit the cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 medium zucchini, sliced into 1/4-inch-thick half moons
ingredients.name: medium zucchini

ingredients.name: of corn, shucked, kernels cut off

ingredients.name: into bite-size pieces
ingredients.quantity: 6 cups (12 ounces, about 4 thick slices) really good sourdough bread, cut (or torn)

ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves

ingredients.name: fresh parsley leaves and tender stems

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds U-20 peeled and deveined shrimp
ingredients.name: U-20 peeled and deveined shrimp

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces feta or goat cheese, crumbled
ingredients.name: feta or goat cheese, crumbled

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Cut 1 medium zucchini in half vertically, then into 1/4-inch-thick half moons. Cut the kernels off 4 (shucked) ears of corn . Place the zucchini, corn, and 1 pint of cherry tomatoes on a large rimmed sheet pan. Toss with 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and several grinds of black pepper. Spread into an even layer and roast for 20 minutes (heads up that we’re going to add another sheet pan to the oven about halfway through!).

As soon as the vegetables go in the oven, prep the bread: Tear or cut about 4 thick slices of sourdough bread into 6 cups of bite-size pieces and throw them on a second sheet pan with 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt, several grinds of black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder . Use your hands to combine it all then spread into an even layer. If any of the bread looks dry, add a little more oil! Add to the oven and roast for 10 minutes, or until the bread pieces are golden-brown and crispy on the outside, but still chewy inside.

While everything is roasting: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 2 teaspoons whole-grain mustard, 1/2 teaspoon honey, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil , whisking as you go.
Season 1 1/2 to 2 pounds of U-20 peeled and deveined shrimp with a big pinch of kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper and let it sit out on the counter while everything’s roasting.
Roughly chop 1 cup basil leaves and 1/2 cup parsley leaves.

Remove the bread from the oven and set it aside. Remove the sheet pan with the vegetables, too. Add the seasoned shrimp evenly on top of the vegetables and drizzle the shrimp with some extra-virgin olive oil.
Turn the broiler on high.

Add the sheet pan with the shrimp and vegetables to the oven and broil for 2 to 3 minutes, until the shrimp are cooked through (they will be pink, opaque, and curled into a “C”). If you don’t have a broiler, just roast them at 400°F for 4 to 5 minutes.
Like always, sit in front of the oven and watch your food broil! Do not walk away and get distracted and let your dinner burn!

Just before serving, add the bread, warm veggies, shrimp, any juices that have collected on the pan, the chopped herbs, and 8 ounces crumbled feta to the serving bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Scoop into four bowls, add a little pepper on top, and dig in.

name: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
note: These Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas feature juicy sliced chicken breast, colorful bell peppers, and red onion, tossed in a zesty lime and taco seasoning marinade, then roasted on a single sheet pan for a bold, flavor-packed weeknight dinner in just 35 minutes.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice, (from 1 to 2 limes)
ingredients.name: fresh lime juice, (from 1 to 2 limes)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut against the grain into ½-inch-thick slices
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut against the grain into ½-inch-thick slices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small red onion, halved and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: red onion

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center position.
In a large bowl, stir together the taco seasoning, lime juice, and olive oil. Add the chicken, bell peppers, and onion and toss to coat. Spread the mixture onto a rimmed sheet pan.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through. If desired, turn the oven to broil and cook for 3 more minutes, or until the chicken is lightly charred.
Transfer the chicken and veggies to a serving dish. Serve with warm tortillas, salsa, avocado, sour cream, fresh cilantro, and lime wedges alongside.

name: Baked Tortellini
note: Baked Tortellini has fresh cheese tortellini nestled into a rich, creamy tomato sauce with savory Italian sausage and hearty kale, blanketed in a generous layer of melted mozzarella, and baked until bubbly and golden for the ultimate cozy pasta bake.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch kale, stemmed and roughly chopped (about 4 cups)
ingredients.name: kale, stemmed and roughly chopped (about 4 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Minced flat leaf parsley, for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: Minced flat leaf parsley, for serving (optional)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center position. Lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish.

Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once the oil is glistening, add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and sausage and cook, breaking up the sausage with a wooden spoon, until browned, about 5 minutes more. Drain off any excess fat.
Stir in the tomato paste, bouillon, and kale until the kale is wilted, about 4 minutes. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, heavy cream, and salt.

Add the tortellini to the prepared baking dish and sprinkle with 1½ cups of the mozzarella. Pour the kale and tomato mixture over the tortellini and gently stir to combine. Sprinkle it with the remaining mozzarella.
Cover tightly with foil and bake until bubbling, about 35 minutes. Remove the foil and turn on the broiler. Broil until the cheese is lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Divide between bowls and top with Parmesan, parsley, and red pepper flakes, if using, before serving.

name: Ginger Chicken, Snap Peas, and Bok Choy with Garlicky Brown Butter Rice
note:
Confession: This saucy stir-fry will take you a touch over 15 minutes—but not long enough to kick it out of this chapter. We’re spending that little bit of bonus time browning butter for our rice, but I promise you won’t regret those extra few minutes, which turn a potentially forgettable pot of grains into a fragrant, nutty, toasty treat. It foils the crisp, quick-cooking veg perfectly and soaks up the sauce in the best way possible. But, of course, if you need the store-bought shortcut tonight, I implore you to take it! As delightful as the rice is, you can also skip it entirely and just have a meat and veg stir-fry for dinner!

LEARN
FYI for when you’re shopping: 1 large orange typically yields ¼ cup juice, or you can buy a small individual bottle if your family doesn’t drink OJ regularly.

I never have an actual ruler in the kitchen, so when I say to cut the chicken into “1-inch” pieces, I use the top of my thumb as a guide.

SHORTCUT
If you do need to make the dish even snappier, use store-bought frozen rice; once it’s cooked, simply stir in some butter, garlic powder, and salt to season it.

SWAP
If you can’t find bok choy at the store, simply double the snap peas.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 31

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 to 16 ounces snap peas (however big the bag is at your store)
ingredients.name: snap peas (however big the bag is at your store)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small (not baby) head bok choy (about 1 pound)
ingredients.name: small (not baby) head bok choy (about 1 pound)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup fresh orange juice (see Learn)
ingredients.name: fresh orange juice (see Learn)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons honey or brown sugar (light or dark)
ingredients.name: honey or brown sugar (light or dark)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): sesame seeds (toasted, if you have them!), sriracha
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): sesame seeds (toasted, if you have them!), sriracha

preparationSteps: Melt the butter in a small pot over medium-low heat until it foams, then cook until the milk solids drop to the bottom and turn brown and the butterfat turns golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes total.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic and mince or grate the ginger (no need to peel it). Cut the snap peas into 1-inch pieces, if you want (or leave them whole), and roughly chop the bok choy.

Add the rice and half the garlic to the pot with the brown butter. Stir to coat and cook until toasted, about 1 minute. Stir in 2½ cups water and 2 tablespoons of the soy sauce. Turn up the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, then turn down the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes, or until ready to serve.

Meanwhile, trim any fat off the chicken, then cut the meat into 1-inch cubes (see Learn) and season with ½ teaspoon salt and some pepper. Sprinkle the chicken with 2 tablespoons of the flour and toss to coat. It’s okay if it doesn’t all stick, but you want each piece to be covered with flour.
