Warm enough oil to coat the bottom of your largest skillet (about 2 tablespoons for a 12-inch skillet) over medium-high heat. While it’s heating, in a small bowl, stir together the remaining ¼ cup soy sauce, the orange juice, honey, remaining garlic, the ginger, and the remaining 2 teaspoons flour.

When the oil is shimmering, add the chicken in an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until browned all over, 4 to 6 minutes per side, flipping halfway through. Add the snap peas and bok choy, scattering them around and on top of the chicken, and cook until bright green, another minute. Pour in the sauce and cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens, 1 to 3 minutes. Keep a close eye on things—you want the sauce to get saucy, not reduce to the point of burning.
Uncover the rice and use a fork to gently fluff it. Assemble bowls with rice, chicken and veggies, and plenty of sauce. Finish with sesame seeds and sriracha, if you like. Enjoy!

name: Greek Chop
note:
If you’re a fan of the Turkey Taco Salad from the first What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking, I know you’ll love this Greek-ified version. Did you know that in Greece, they don’t add greens to their Greek “salads”? So here, we’re going Greek, skipping the lettuce altogether, but using a super-flavorful ground-chicken-and-chickpea mixture as a protein-heavy base. I highly recommend doubling the Greek vinaigrette—pour half into a jar, stick it in the fridge, and repeat this dinner next week—and do not even consider skipping the pita chips. Their crunch puts this one over the top!

LEARN
I like using “handful” in recipes because it’s how we cook in real life. It’s quick, it’s flexible, and it encourages you to trust your own judgment. My handful of pita chips or parsley or spinach might be a little more or less than yours, and that’s okay.

RIFF
If you’re an olive lover or have an extra-salty tooth, about ½ cup torn or chopped pitted kalamata olives would be wonderful here, either in place of or in addition to the avocado.

For an even more authentic Greek salad vibe, skip the vinaigrette. Combine everything else in the bowl as directed, then sprinkle with a generous amount of dried oregano, drizzle with olive oil, and add a splash of red wine vinegar.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 32

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons Greek seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Greek seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14-ounce) can chickpeas or other white beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: chickpeas or other white beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon Greek or Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20), or za’atar
ingredients.name: Greek or Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20), or za’atar

preparationSteps: Make the chicken. Warm the olive oil in your largest skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the chicken and cook, breaking it up into small pieces with a wooden spoon, until almost cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the Greek seasoning and stir it into the chicken, then add the chickpeas and use the spoon to lightly smash some of them against the side of the pan. Cook until the chicken is cooked through and the ingredients are well incorporated, 3 minutes more. Halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice, then cook until all the liquid has been absorbed, about 2 minutes more.

Meanwhile, make the vinaigrette. In a large serving bowl, whisk together the vinegar, Greek seasoning, mustard, honey, and ½ teaspoon salt. While whisking vigorously, slowly pour in the olive oil and whisk until emulsified. Taste and adjust the seasoning as desired.

Make the salad. Dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, chop the red onion, and dice the avocado, adding them to the bowl with the vinaigrette as you go. Sprinkle ¼ teaspoon salt over everything and toss to coat in the dressing. Add the chicken and chickpeas and toss again to combine.
Crumble the feta and pita chips into the bowl. Tear the mint leaves and scatter them on top. Toss to coat everything evenly. Taste and add more salt until it’s all delicious. Serve immediately.

name: Open-Faced Cheesy Chutney Chicken Melts with Tomato, Cuke, and Mint Salad
note:
My parents are chutney fiends. If we’re having any kind of grilled meat for dinner, there’s a jar of either my mom’s homemade fig chutney or their beloved store-bought Major Grey’s mango chutney on the table. Chutney also loves sneaking its way into her chicken and tuna salads, of which there is always, always at least one type in the refrigerator. You don’t hear about chicken melts as much as you do tuna melts, but they really deserve more hype. The melty cheese with the sweet mango chutney in the chicken salad is just such a treat.

TIP
The pickled onions can be stored, covered, in the fridge for up to 1 week.

SHORTCUT
Skip the broiling and serve the chicken salad cold on toasted naan with thin slices of cheese layered underneath.

SWAP
Instead of the chutney, drizzle each sandwich with a couple teaspoons of hot honey.

RIFF
Add thinly sliced pears or apples on top of (or instead of) the chutney.

Use fresh basil or cilantro instead of mint.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 33

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups shredded or chopped cooked chicken
ingredients.name: shredded or chopped cooked chicken

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 to 8 ounces shredded sharp white cheddar or fontina cheese (1½ to 2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp white cheddar or fontina cheese (1½ to 2 cups)

preparationSteps: Cut the onion in half. Thinly slice 1 half and place it in a glass measuring cup or small bowl. Halve the lemons and squeeze the juice of 1 half into the cup with the onion. Add the sugar and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine and set aside to let the onions pickle while you continue cooking.

Dice the remaining onion half and place it in a large bowl. Finely chop enough mint leaves to make ¼ cup and add them to the bowl with the chopped onion. Squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon half. Add the chicken, mayonnaise, mustard, ½ teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Stir to combine well. Taste and add more lemon juice and/or salt.

Halve the cucumbers lengthwise, then thinly slice them crosswise into half circles and place in a medium bowl. Halve the tomatoes and add them to the cucumbers. Roughly chop or tear enough mint leaves to make ¼ cup and add them to the bowl. Add the sliced onion and any liquid from the cup to the bowl. Add the olive oil and squeeze in the juice of the remaining lemon half. Add ½ teaspoon salt and some pepper. Toss well, taste, and add more lemon juice, salt, and/or pepper, if needed.
Position a rack about 6 inches from the broiler heat element and turn the broiler to high.

Arrange the naan on a baking sheet. Broil for 1 to 2 minutes, until lightly crisp on top, then carefully flip and broil until lightly crisp on the other side, 1 to 2 minutes more—watch carefully so they don’t burn.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven and spoon the chicken salad over the toasted naan, dividing it evenly. Spread 1 heaping tablespoon chutney on top of each. Top with the cheese, spreading it out to the edges. Return the baking sheet to the oven and broil for 2 to 4 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the edges of the naan are golden. Let cool slightly, then cut into halves or 8 wedges. To serve, divide the melt halves or wedges among individual plates and scoop the tomato-and-cucumber salad alongside.

name: Apple Chicken Caesar Lettuce Wraps
note:
My husband, George, is the president of the Chicken Caesar Salad Fan Club. If he sees one on the menu, he’s ordering it—and he has strong opinions on where to find the best version in every major city. I’m no perfect housewife, but I am very good at one thing, and that’s packing lunch for George to take to work. It’s my love language and satisfies my innate desire to turn leftovers into a second, delicious meal. One night after having grilled chicken Caesar salads for dinner, I made a chicken salad with Caesar dressing by finely chopping the leftover chicken and tossing with the leftover dressing. It was missing a little crunch, so I added apple and, just, whoa—trust me, it works. And if you don’t trust me, trust Caesar King George, who often requests a Caesar for dinner just so I can make this for lunch the next day.

LEARN
Anchovy paste is a shortcut to deep, savory flavor without any fishiness, and it melts right into dressings and sauces without any mess or chopping. Use ½ teaspoon paste to replace 1 anchovy fillet.

To “smash” garlic, lay an unpeeled garlic clove on your work surface and hold a chef’s knife so that the flat side of the blade is resting on top of the garlic. Firmly smack the knife blade with the heel of your other hand to flatten and break up the garlic clove; it’ll burst out of its skin, which can be easily removed and discarded.

SHORTCUT
Use your favorite store-bought dressing! My picks are Ken’s Steakhouse Caesar and SideDish Miso Caesar.

RIFF
Buy mini croissants, cut a slit in them, and stuff this chicken salad inside. It’s a go-to when I’m feeding a crowd.

Or make it a straight-up chicken Caesar salad! Double the dressing, chop a large head of romaine, and toss with 2 cups crushed-up store-bought (or homemade—see page 244) croutons, the chicken, and the apple. Add more Parm on top.

Or or or! Throw that salad into burrito-size tortillas and roll it all up to make a delightful chicken Caesar wrap! Toast the wrap in a skillet over medium heat for optimum enjoyment.

EXTRA EXTRA
Make a nutty Parm crumble: In a medium skillet, stir together 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, ½ cup finely chopped nuts, ½ teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon garlic powder. Toast over medium heat until the panko is golden, then stir in ¼ cup freshly grated Parm (1 ounce). Turn off the heat and keep stirring until the crumbs are coated in Parm. This is a delicious topping for practically any salad or roasted veggies.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 36

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5.3-ounce) container plain full-fat Greek yogurt (about ½ cup)
ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt (about ½ cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon anchovy paste, or 6 anchovy fillets, minced, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: anchovy paste, or 6 anchovy fillets, minced, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Leaves and tender stems of ½ bunch parsley
ingredients.name: and tender stems of ½ bunch parsley

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3½ cups very finely chopped cooked chicken
ingredients.name: very finely chopped cooked chicken

preparationSteps: In a large bowl, combine the yogurt, mayonnaise, Parm, olive oil, anchovy paste, ½ teaspoon salt, and a little bit of pepper. Using a Microplane, grate the garlic and lemon zest directly into the bowl, then halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Stir until smooth. Taste and add more anchovy paste, lemon, and/or salt.

Core and finely chop the apple. Finely chop the parsley. Add the apple, parsley, and chicken to the bowl with the Caesar dressing and stir to coat. Taste and add more salt, pepper, and/or lemon as needed.

Separate the lettuce leaves, then wash and dry them. Scoop the chicken salad into the lettuce leaves. Roughly chop the almonds and sprinkle them over top for crunch. Grind some pepper on top and enjoy!

name: BBQ Chicken and Peach Chop
note:
A few summers ago, our dear friends Gray and Tate invited us to their family’s house on Lake Minnetonka, Minnesota, and, whoa. It was one of those immediately starts browsing Zillow because, wait, should we move here? moments for us. One afternoon we got babysitters and the adults took the boat from the house into the town of Wayzata for lunch at The Grocer’s Table. I still dream about their summer-in-your-mouth BBQ chicken salad with a BBQ vinaigrette—so much so that, years later, it’s still a regular in my summer grill-out rotation. I simplified things to make it a quick, no-cook recipe, but it’s kinda worth going the Extra Extra route if you have more time to grill the chicken, corn, and peaches like I do for special-occasion summer dinners.

SWAP
Thinly sliced romaine, kale, cabbage, or a combo would be great instead of mixed greens.

Use ground turkey or chicken instead of rotisserie: Brown it in a skillet with a little oil and add a big pinch each of salt, garlic powder, chili powder, and smoked paprika and a splash of the BBQ vinaigrette at the very end.

EXTRA EXTRA
If you have a little more time, add the beans to the serving bowl first, along with a big pour of dressing. Lightly smash the beans so they can absorb the dressing a bit while you assemble the rest of the salad.

RIFF
Grill it all! Double the BBQ vinaigrette and marinate a couple of chicken breasts in it for at least 30 minutes (or overnight, if you can). Drizzle 2 ears of corn and 2 sliced peaches with oil. Shake the marinade off the chicken and grill it along with the corn and peaches over medium-high heat until grill marks appear on the corn and peaches and the chicken reaches 165°F internally, about 10 minutes total, flipping everything halfway through.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 39

ingredients.rawIngredient: ⅓ cup barbecue sauce (I like Stubb’s)
ingredients.name: barbecue sauce (I like Stubb’s)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15.25-ounce) can white corn, drained, or 1 (16-ounce) frozen white corn bag thawed
ingredients.name: white corn, drained
ingredients.note: or 1 (16-ounce) frozen white corn bag thawed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded white cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded white cheddar cheese (2 cups)

preparationSteps: Make the vinaigrette. In a large jar or container with a lid, combine the barbecue sauce, neutral oil, vinegar, ½ teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Taste for sweetness and add a little honey or sugar if needed (this will depend on your BBQ sauce).
Make the salad. Place the greens in a large, shallow serving bowl and season with a big pinch each of salt and pepper. Scatter the chicken over the greens.

Cut the peaches and avocado into small cubes and add them to the greens. Thinly slice the scallions and add them to the greens, along with the corn and beans. Sprinkle the cheese and tortilla chips over the top.
Drizzle with your desired amount of vinaigrette and toss to mix and coat the salad well. Enjoy immediately.

name: Southwestern Chicken and Veggie Chowder
note:
My mom is big on chowder. Clam, corn, potato—whatever she’s got, she’s turning it into a chowder. This is one she made for me when I was postpartum with Cashel, and it has since become a family staple. Thanks to the frozen veg, it’s both highly efficient and filled with flavor. Frozen vegetables may get a bad rap (especially among my farmers’-market-loving California friends), but they’re prewashed, prepped, and frozen at peak freshness—and therefore always in season at my house.

TIP
The remaining chipotles and adobo sauce can be frozen for later use in a few different ways: Transfer them to an airtight container or to one or two sandwich-size zip-top bags; lay them flat and freeze for up to 4 months, then break off a pepper or a piece and chop to use. Or blend the rest of the chipotles and adobo in a blender. Use a tablespoon measure to scoop portions of the puree onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Freeze, then transfer the chipotle blobs to a zip-top bag and freeze for up to 6 months. I figure each blob is equivalent to about 1 chipotle pepper plus 1 teaspoon adobo!

SWAP
For a milder version, add a dash of smoked paprika instead of the chipotle and adobo.

SHORTCUT
Use 2 cups diced or shredded rotisserie chicken instead of the chicken breast; stir in when the vegetables are almost cooked through.

RIFF
Skip the chicken entirely and use vegetable stock to make it a vegetarian chowder!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 40

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 tablespoon adobo from the can (optional; see Tip)
ingredients.name: chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 tablespoon adobo from the can (optional; see Tip)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen mixed broccoli, cauliflower, and carrots
ingredients.name: frozen mixed broccoli, cauliflower, and carrots

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15.25-ounce) can white corn, drained, or 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen white corn
ingredients.name: can white corn, drained

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup heavy cream, half-and-half, or whole milk
ingredients.name: heavy cream, half-and-half, or whole milk

preparationSteps: In a large Dutch oven, combine the stock, chipotle and adobo (if using), taco seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon salt. Use a wooden spoon to smash the chipotle against the side of the pan to break it apart. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Stir in the frozen vegetables, corn, and beans, then cover and return to a boil.

Meanwhile, cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Stir the chicken into the pot, partially cover with the lid, and return to a boil. Turn down the heat to medium and simmer until the vegetables and chicken are cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the lime into 8 wedges and finely chop the cilantro.
Stir the cream into the soup and heat just until it’s warmed through, about 1 minute. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Ladle the chowder into bowls and top each serving with a handful of crushed tortilla chips and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Lasagna-Vibes Turkey Zucchini Skillet
note:
For years, one of my go-to dinners in the summer was zucchini lasagna, where zucchini is used in place of noodles. It’s delightful, but it’s also very labor-intensive, requiring you to slice the zucchini into long, thin planks, salt each individual plank, wipe each individual plank, and then layer the zucchini “noodles” with ricotta, sauce, and mozzarella. Now I have far too many children to be salting individual planks of zucchini—so I make this! It’s a dump-and-go skillet meal that has all of those favorite flavors in a way, way quicker and easier format.

SWAP
For a vegetarian lasagna, squeeze the moisture from a block of firm tofu, crumble the tofu into the skillet in place of turkey, and cook the rest of the recipe exactly as written.

• Use ground Italian sausage instead of ground turkey for a richer dish.

• Cottage cheese instead of ricotta will give the dish a more delicate flavor.

RIFF
Make it a chicken Parm lasagna skillet by using ground chicken and adding ¼ cup freshly grated Parm (1 ounce) when you add the mozzarella. Stir in 1½ cups or so of leftover cooked pasta—any kind—to give it baked-pasta vibes.

BULK IT UP
Add a thinly sliced bell pepper or 8 ounces thinly sliced mushrooms when you add the zucchini.

• For some greens, stir in two big handfuls of spinach with the tomato sauce and cook until wilted.

• Serve with garlic bread to stretch this to feed more people!

EXTRA EXTRA
To brown the cheese, throw the skillet under the broiler for a few minutes (watch it the entire time so you don’t burn it!) instead of cooking it, covered, on the stovetop.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 43

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

preparationSteps: Halve the zucchini lengthwise, then thinly slice them crosswise into ⅛-inch-thick half circles. Thinly slice the basil.

Warm the olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the turkey and cook, breaking it up into small crumbles with a wooden spoon. Add the zucchini, 1½ teaspoons salt, and some black pepper. Turn up the heat to high and cook, stirring often, until the meat is totally cooked through (no longer pink) and the zucchini is tender, 6 to 8 minutes.

Turn down the heat to medium and stir in the tomato sauce, half the basil, the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, and another ¼ teaspoon salt. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed—it should be very tasty by this point! Swirl in spoonfuls of the ricotta all over, then sprinkle the mozzarella over the top. Turn down the heat to low, cover, and cook until the mozzarella has melted, 3 to 5 minutes.
Finish with the remaining basil and some red pepper flakes, if you like, before serving straight from the pot.

name: Quickie Burger Sliders
note:
Burger night is always a hit in my house, but the more beasts we’ve added to our family, the less time we have to execute dinner. Even a simple burger night can be too time-consuming some nights! Enter: sliced roast beef. These sliders deliver all the deliciousness of cheeseburgers with none of the patty-making mess. Make them on a whirlwind weeknight, set them out as an app next time you entertain, or bring them to a neighborhood potluck—they’ll get devoured in minutes. PS: I know this sounds like a lot of pickles, but have faith.

TIP
To bring these to a picnic or anywhere on the go, keep the bottom of the rolls on the cardboard that comes in the package while building and slicing your sliders, then simply slide them back into the bag to store and/or transport!

SWAP
Use your favorite burger sauce or other condiment instead of the ketchup/mayo/mustard combo.

• If you only have Dijon mustard, that works here.

EXTRA EXTRA
For a green salad alongside, thinly slice the rest of the head of iceberg and toss it in a big bowl with salt, pepper, and your favorite dressing. A nice ranch sounds pretty perfect here.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 44

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): ¼ head iceberg lettuce, 1 big juicy tomato (any kind!), kosher salt
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): ¼ head iceberg lettuce, 1 big juicy tomato (any kind!), kosher salt

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Using a serrated knife, slice the rolls in half horizontally, leaving them all connected, to make one giant top sheet and one giant bottom sheet. Work slowly to make the top and bottom as even in thickness as possible.

Place the bottom bun sheet cut side up on one side of the prepared baking sheet. Thinly spread the bottom buns with the mayo, ketchup, and mustard. Sprinkle the garlic powder and onion powder over the condiments. Arrange 4 slices of the cheese in an even layer on top, tearing them to fit as needed.

Layer the roast beef over the cheese, individually piling each slice high by folding it over itself several times (don’t just lay it down flat—we need height!). Add the pickles on top of the meat and the remaining 4 slices of cheese on top of the pickles.

Place the top bun sheet cut side down on the baking sheet next to the bottom buns. Spray the top buns with cooking spray and sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is melty.
If you’re in the mood for lettuce and tomato on your sliders, slice the iceberg as thinly as possible. Thinly slice the tomato and sprinkle it with salt.

When the sliders are finished baking, add a layer of tomatoes and iceberg (if using) on top of the cheese. Close the sliders with the top bun sheet. Use the serrated knife to slice into individual sliders and serve.

name: Good-All-Week Sesame Chicken Kale Salad
note:
In my January 4, 2025, newsletter, I rolled out my first official “Good-All-Week Salad”—that is, a meal-prep-able salad that’s as tasty when it’s 4 days old as it is when it’s freshly assembled. It caught on like wildfire, as did the handful of others I rolled out that year and beyond. Prepping a week’s worth of meals in 15 minutes? It’s a no-brainer! In this Good-All-Week salad, we pull in kale for its heartiness and a sweet-and-savory sesame chicken. Cook it once and eat it all week, or devour it all immediately—your call!

TIP
Don’t add any avocado to anything you’re not eating right away! It’ll get brown and slimy.

LEARN
I’m not typically a cucumber seed-scooper, but when I want the salad to last all week, removing the seeds reduces moisture, which can lead to unpleasant sogginess.

SWAP
You can substitute any nut or seed butter for the peanut butter. Sunflower butter makes a great allergy swap for peanut butter.

RIFF
For bigger flavor, try marinating your chicken in a store-bought teriyaki sauce before you cook it. For a more Mediterranean salad, stir together a big scoop of Greek yogurt and some lemon juice, salt, pepper, and Greek seasoning, then use that to marinate the chicken. For a rotisserie-ish taste, use the seasoning blend from the Rotisserie-ish Chicken on page 192.

BULK IT UP
Toss in 1½ cups cooked quinoa or brown rice. It absorbs the dressing and is so delicious.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 47

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup sesame oil (toasted or not)
ingredients.name: sesame oil (toasted or not)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar
ingredients.name: rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar

preparationSteps: In your largest bowl, whisk together the sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, peanut butter, and chili crisp. Remove the tough stems from the kale and add it to the bowl. Use your hands to massage the dressing into the leaves until the kale is softened and no dressing remains at the bottom of the bowl. Add the carrots to the bowl.

Finely chop the chicken and bell peppers and add them to the bowl. Halve the cucumber lengthwise and use a spoon to scoop out and discard the seeds, then cut the halves in half lengthwise again and finely chop. Add the cucumber to the bowl. Toss everything to combine. At this point, you can transfer the salad to an airtight container and store it in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
Just before serving, dice the avocados and add them to the salad.

name: Flank Steak with Elote Salsa
note:
I first tasted authentic elote—grilled corn coated with mayo, Cotija, and tons of chili powder, lime juice, and cilantro—years ago on a street in Sayulita, Mexico, during a stroll from the beach back to our $40/night Airbnb. Street vendors set up full grills to perfectly char the corn to order before slathering it in all the toppings. I can’t even count all the ways I’ve remixed elote since that trip, but this elote salsa served with perfectly grilled flank steak has to be one of my favorites. Grilling, IMO, is the ultimate move on a night when you don’t feel like cooking!

TIP
No grill? Use a cast-iron skillet instead. Cook the corn first over medium heat (make sure the skillet is piping hot first!), then crank the heat up to medium-high and cook the steak.

LEARN
To slice the corn kernels off of the cob, lay the corn on its side—don’t stand it up on its end—and run a sharp knife along the length of the cob. Now those kernels will fall neatly onto your cutting board instead of flying all over the place.

• If you look closely at a steak, you can see the muscle fibers; they’re the lines running through the meat like tiny ropes. When you slice steak “against the grain,” you’re cutting across those fibers, not parallel to them. This makes the steak more tender and much easier to chew.

SHORTCUT
Use a bag of frozen corn instead of grilling and cutting kernels off the cob. Warm a little oil in a skillet over high heat until it shimmers, add the corn, and cook until it’s charred in spots. You can even stir the rest of the elote salsa ingredients straight into the skillet off the heat to save on dishes!

BULK IT UP
If you’re extra hungry, cut some planks of zucchini or yellow squash or another veg that you love, lightly coat with neutral oil, season with salt and pepper, and throw them on the grill, too.

• Add a finely chopped red bell pepper and avocado to the elote salsa mixture for some more veg and more color.

EXTRA EXTRA
For deeper flavor, let the steak and corn marinate in the mayo mixture for a few hours or even overnight (in the fridge if more than an hour-ish!).
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 52

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ bunch cilantro, plus more if needed for serving
ingredients.name: cilantro, plus more if needed for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese
ingredients.name: Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese

preparationSteps: Heat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400° to 450°F).
Place the mayonnaise in a large bowl. Halve the lime and squeeze in the juice. Add the taco seasoning and 1 teaspoon salt and stir to combine. Transfer half this mixture to a medium bowl.
Add the steak and corn to the mayo mixture that’s left in the large bowl—yes, it’s okay for them to touch. Toss to coat well. Sprinkle with a big pinch of salt.

Transfer the steak and the corn to the grill. Grill the steak for 5 minutes, then flip it and grill for about 5 minutes longer, until the meat reaches 130°F internally for medium-rare, 140°F for medium, or 150°F for medium-well. Grill the corn, rotating it as it cooks to grill all sides, for about 9 minutes total.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and the cilantro leaves and tender stems (about 1 cup) and add them to the mayo mixture. Crumble the Cotija into the bowl.

Transfer the corn and steak to a cutting board. Let the steak rest while you slice the corn off the cob (see Learn) and add it to the bowl with the mayo mixture. Toss to combine. Taste and adjust the seasoning (you’ll likely need to add a big pinch of salt!).
Slice the steak against the grain, arrange it on a serving platter, and serve with the elote salsa over top. Finish with more cilantro if you’re feeling fancy.

name: Skillet Un-Stuffed Peppers
note:
Stuffed peppers? A delight. Actually stuffing peppers on a night when you need dinner ready in a hurry? Never gonna happen. This recipe has all the stuffed pepper flavors and textures that you love without the multi-step—and multi-heat-source, ugh!—method of carefully carving the bell peppers, sautéing the filling, stuffing the peppers, then baking them. Instead, you’ll cook it all in one skillet, plop it on the table, and dig in!

LEARN
When I say to use the “leaves and tender stems” of parsley or cilantro, I mean just ditch the fat stems at the bottom, then chop up the rest! The tender stems are just as flavorful as the leaves, if not more.

SHORTCUT
The cook time here is super fast, but the recipe does require some chopping. To make that part faster, cut the seeds and stems out of the peppers, quarter the onion, and throw it all in a food processor, then pulse to chop. After you scrape those out, pulse the parsley leaves and tender stems a few times to chop them, too.

SWAP
If the pepper Jack is a little too spicy, any shredded cheese is great here—cheddar, mozzarella, provolone, whatever.

• To make this gluten-free, replace the couscous with 1½ cups cooked rice or quinoa, or skip the grains entirely and stir in 2 cups cauliflower rice with the peppers and beef.

• To ramp up the flavor, use 1 pound ground Italian sausage instead of ground beef—so good.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 55

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 red, yellow, or orange bell peppers
ingredients.name: red, yellow, or orange bell peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can diced fire-roasted tomatoes, with their juices
ingredients.name: diced fire-roasted tomatoes, with their juices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded pepper Jack cheese, (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded pepper Jack cheese

preparationSteps: Position a rack about 4 inches from the broiler heat element and turn the broiler to high.

Finely chop the bell peppers, onion, and the parsley leaves and tender stems. Warm the olive oil in a deep 12-inch ovenproof skillet or saucepan over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the ground beef, peppers, onion, and salt and cook, breaking up the meat into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until the beef is cooked through and the vegetables have softened, 5 to 6 minutes.

Add the couscous, diced tomatoes with their juices, tomato sauce, oregano, garlic powder, paprika, cumin, and half the chopped parsley. Stir to combine and cook until the tomatoes are simmering, about 1 minute. Stir half the cheese into the mixture. Smooth the surface of the mixture, then sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top and transfer the skillet to the oven. Broil until the cheese is melted and golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes.
Garnish with more parsley, scoop into four bowls, and enjoy immediately!

name: Crispy Lamb Arayes with Harissa Crème Fraîche
note:
Anytime I’m in New York City, lunch at Shuka is at the top of my agenda. I’ve met my high school girlfriends there infinite times over the years—it’s one of those Manhattan gems that, despite being wildly popular, can always seat you. And the menu—it’s perfect. Bright, crisp salads, juicy meat skewers, and the DIPS! So many dips. Last time I had their harissa crème fraîche, I was up literally all night thinking of the possibilities for how I could make and use a version of it. I ultimately landed on having it be the perfect dunking sauce for lamb-stuffed arayes, a wildly delicious Middle Eastern street food. They’re basically crispy, meat-stuffed pita pockets, and they’re a major win if you’re short on time since the meat cooks right in the pita while you crisp everything up to golden perfection in a skillet coated with oil (also called pan-frying).

LEARN
Harissa that’s labeled “mild” can still be seriously spicy hot. The best way to be sure of its heat level is to taste it right out of the jar. If your harissa is more than mildly spicy, use less than I call for here; if you like a lot of spice, add more!

RIFF
Make a spiced lamb bowl instead! Cook the ground meat in a large skillet over medium heat with oil and spices instead, breaking it up with a wooden spoon or spatula. When crumbled and cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes, serve over rice or whatever grain you like, topped with lots of sauce and any/all of the Bulk It Up toppings.

BULK IT UP
Put out bowls of shredded lettuce, chopped tomato, chopped onion, and feta so people can pile their pitas with whatever they’d like.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 56

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 regular pita breads, or 8 mini pitas
ingredients.name: regular pita breads, or 8 mini pitas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds ground lamb, beef (90/10), or pork
ingredients.name: ground lamb, beef (90/10), or pork

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons mild harissa, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: plus 2 teaspoons mild harissa, plus more if needed

preparationSteps: Place your largest skillet over medium-low heat.

Cut the pitas in half to make 8 half circles (if you’re using minis, slit the edge to make a roughly 2-inch opening). Most pitas you’ll find in the grocery store are hollow inside; if yours are not, use a knife to create a pocket (don’t worry if the pita tears a little).

In a large bowl, combine the lamb, cumin, 2 teaspoons salt, 2 teaspoons of the harissa, the paprika, turmeric, garlic powder, onion powder, and cinnamon. Use your hands to mix well. While your hands are still covered in meat, stuff about ½ cup of the mixture into each pita half, dividing it evenly (use about ¼ cup per mini pita). Push on the pita to flatten the meat mixture and make sure it’s smooshed into every corner inside—kind of like you’re putting on a duvet cover.

Turn up the heat under the skillet to medium and add enough olive oil to generously coat the bottom, 2 to 3 tablespoons. Add a few stuffed pita halves to the skillet and cook, pressing down on them with a spatula, until the pita is crispy and golden brown on the outside and the meat is cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Throw the pitas on a platter as they’re cooked and cover with aluminum foil (or another plate) to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining stuffed pitas, adding more oil between batches as needed.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl, stir together the crème fraîche, the remaining 1 tablespoon harissa, and ¼ teaspoon salt. If you want to make the sauce thinner, stir in some water, a tiny bit at a time. Taste and add more harissa and/or salt as desired.
Serve the pitas with the sauce alongside for dipping. These are wonderful just like this, or you can Bulk It Up.

name: Cheddar Chorizo Fideo
note:
Sopa de fideo is a cozy soup made by cooking fideo noodles in a spice- and veg-filled broth. I first tried it at Mi Tierra, an amazing Mexican grocery store in Seaside, California, that has a little taco shop in the back, and I have made endless riffs on it since (I’ve included a few). There’s really no wrong answer, and I encourage you to try them all. This chorizo version is one of my favorites—it takes that simple fideo base (tomato broth + noodles) and makes it a protein- and veggie-loaded soup, perfect for a weeknight meal.

SWAP
Fideo noodles are short (about 1-inch) vermicelli noodles. If you can’t find them in the store, make your own! Snap vermicelli noodles, spaghetti, or angel hair directly into the pot. Doesn’t matter if they’re totally uniform in size, as long as they’re about 1 inch.

• If you can’t find chorizo, you can use any ground meat and season it with 1 teaspoon salt and lots of taco seasoning.

RIFF
Add salsa verde to your broth in place of the tomato sauce, or blend up a jar of salsa in place of the tomato sauce.

• Use macaroni noodles in place of the fideo.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 59

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: pinto beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (7-ounce) bag fideo noodles or spaghetti, broken into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: fideo noodles or spaghetti, broken into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15.25-ounce) can White corn, drained, or 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen white corn
ingredients.name: White corn, drained

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): plain full-fat Greek yogurt or sour cream, diced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): plain full-fat Greek yogurt or sour cream, diced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro

preparationSteps: In a large pot, combine the chorizo, pinto beans, taco seasoning, and 1 teaspoon salt. (This seems like a lot of spices, but it’s to season the entire soup, don’t worry.) Cook over medium-high heat, breaking up the chorizo into small crumbles and lightly mashing the beans with a wooden spoon, until the chorizo is almost cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes. Add the fideo noodles and stir until they are lightly toasted, about 2 minutes.
Add the stock, tomato sauce, and corn. Turn up the heat to high and bring to a boil, then turn it down to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the noodles are tender, 6 to 8 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the lime in half. When the noodles are tender, remove the pot from the heat and squeeze in the juice of 1 lime half. Add almost all the cheese, reserving a handful for sprinkling on each bowl. Taste and add more salt and/or lime juice (I always end up squeezing in the other lime half!). If you prefer a brothier soup, stir in more stock or water.
Ladle the soup into bowls, dividing it evenly. Top with the reserved cheese and any other toppings you like, then enjoy!

name: Crispy Sausage Meatballs and Caramelized Cabbage Pasta with Burrata
note:
Meatballs are reliably enjoyed by every single one of my children, so they’re at the top of the food pyramid in my house. This recipe features my favorite hack for making meatballs without even dirtying a bowl: leaning on the built-in flavor—and round-ish shape—of uncooked sausage wrapped in casings. You can use pork or chicken sausage, mild or spicy. If you want to cook only the quickie meatballs (they’re great for meal prep!), bake them on a baking sheet at 400°F for about 20 minutes, or until 165°F internally. But then come back to this meal for a novel spin on pasta night. Thinly sliced, deliciously caramelized cabbage bulks up our noodles, and burrata makes everything better, this meal included!

TIP
Stick with green cabbage here. Purple cabbage sure is pretty, but it’ll turn your pasta purplish brownish, which is not so pretty!

LEARN
Did you forget to reserve a cup of pasta cooking water even though I used ALL CAPS? Stir together 1 cup water and 1 teaspoon cornstarch or all-purpose flour and use that as your “pasta cooking water”—it’ll work the same way.

SWAP
Napa cabbage, kale, or Swiss chard will work here in place of the cabbage.

BULK IT UP
Thinly slice a red bell pepper or fennel bulb and add it while you’re sautéing the cabbage.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 60

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces small pasta noodles, such as farfalle, rotini, or orecchiette
ingredients.name: small pasta noodles, such as farfalle, rotini, or orecchiette

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound hot or mild Italian sausage links (in their casings)
ingredients.name: hot or mild Italian sausage links (in their casings)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag shredded green cabbage, or 2 cups thinly sliced green cabbage
ingredients.name: shredded green cabbage, or 2 cups thinly sliced green cabbage

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4-ounce) ball burrata cheese, at room temperature
ingredients.name: ball burrata cheese, at room temperature

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until just shy of al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta cooking water (this is VERY IMPORTANT!), then drain the pasta.

Warm the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot (such as a Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, snip the casing on one end of each sausage and use your hands to squeeze the meat out of the casings—almost as if you are piping them—and shaping it into little 1-tablespoon(ish) meatballs before adding it to the pan. They do not need to be perfectly round. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sausage is golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes.

Scooch the meatballs to one side of the pot. If the cleared spot in the pot doesn’t have any grease in it, add a glug of olive oil and let it warm up for 30 seconds before adding the cabbage and a pinch of salt. Turn up the heat to high and cook, stirring the cabbage frequently, until wilted, about 2 minutes. Stir the cabbage into the meatballs and cook until the cabbage cooks down and caramelizes a bit, 1 to 3 minutes more.

Add the cooked pasta, ¼ cup of the reserved pasta cooking water, the garlic powder, onion powder, and ½ teaspoon salt to the sausage and cabbage. Toss well to combine, then turn off the heat. Sprinkle the Parm over the top, a little bit at a time, stirring as you go. Add another splash of the pasta cooking water to make everything saucier, if needed. Taste and add more salt as needed.

Divide the pasta among bowls. Rip the burrata ball into 4 to 6 pieces and add 1 piece to each serving, then drizzle with olive oil. Using a Microplane, grate a touch of lemon zest on top of each bowl. Sprinkle on some red pepper flakes if you want it spicier, and enjoy!

name: Wilted Spinach Salad with Crispy Pancetta and Fried Eggs
note:
This meal feels incredibly fahn-cy except for how little effort it requires. It also hits the spot any time of day—I’ve made it for breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner. If anyone in your family poo-poos salad for dinner, you’ll change their minds with this one. Also fun: You can call it green eggs and ham!

TIP
“Crusty bread” = good, freshly baked bread with a nice thick, crunchy crust, like sourdough or peasant bread.

LEARN
Deglazing—adding liquid to a hot pan to loosen the browned bits stuck to the bottom—lifts all that built-in flavor and turns it into a quick, delicious sauce with no extra effort (and it makes cleaning the skillet easier, too!).

SWAP
Arugula instead of spinach will give you a spicier bite.

• Chopped ham or smoked turkey works in place of the pancetta or bacon. Toss in some toasted nuts or seeds for more crunch and a protein boost.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 63

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar
ingredients.name: red wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ teaspoon dried thyme or oregano
ingredients.name: dried thyme or oregano

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil or unsalted butter
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil or unsalted butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: Large loaf of fresh crusty bread, for serving
ingredients.name: of fresh crusty bread, for serving

preparationSteps: Dice the pancetta (if necessary) and thinly slice the shallot. Place the spinach and carrots in a large bowl.

Place the pancetta in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the pancetta is crisp and the fat has rendered, 5 to 7 minutes. Add the shallot and cook, stirring, until fragrant and softened, about 1 minute.

Pour in the vinegar and stir with a wooden spoon, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in the honey, thyme, a pinch of salt, and some pepper. Simmer for 30 seconds, then immediately pour the warm dressing over the spinach and carrots and toss to coat.

In the same skillet (no need to wipe it out), heat the olive oil over medium heat. When it shimmers, crack in the eggs and cook until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 1 to 3 minutes—since your pan is already hot, the eggs will cook quickly and crisp up around the edges. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide the wilted spinach among individual serving plates and top each portion with 2 fried eggs. Serve immediately, with crusty bread for sopping up the dressing and runny egg yolks.

name: Sheet Pan Kielbasa and Okra with Cheesy Grits
note:
I’ve adopted my cousin Lexie and her Cajun husband Aaron Boudreaux’s gumbo recipe as my own, and I cook it every year around Fat Tuesday (you can find it on What to Cook the newsletter—search for “Boudreaux Gumbo”!). But making the requisite roux? Not in my usual weeknight repertoire. Enter: this deconstructed gumbo-vibed sheet pan dinner. It scratches the itch with about a fifth of the effort.

TIP
Frozen whole okra works great—just make sure it’s fully thawed. To speed that up, put the pods in a colander and run cold water over them, then pat dry. If you want to roast them from frozen, keep the pods spaced out so they brown instead of steam.

SWAP
Use 1 pound peeled and deveined jumbo (16/20) shrimp in place of the kielbasa. The shrimp will only take 4 to 6 minutes, so add them to the baking sheet after the vegetables have been under the broiler for 5 to 10 minutes. Broil the shrimp until pink and opaque throughout, flipping them once about halfway through.

RIFF
Skip the grits and make a quick, creamy comeback sauce to drizzle over everything: In a small bowl, stir together ½ cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons chili sauce, 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion, 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice, and ½ teaspoon garlic powder.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 64

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 red, yellow, or orange bell pepper
ingredients.name: red, yellow, or orange bell pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 ounces fresh or thawed frozen whole okra pods (ideally smaller ones, around 2 inches long; see Tip)
ingredients.name: fresh or thawed frozen whole okra pods (ideally smaller ones, around 2 inches long; see Tip)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (1 cup)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley or basil, for serving
ingredients.name: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley or basil, for serving

preparationSteps: Position a rack about 4 inches from the broiler heat element and turn the broiler to high.

Cut the kielbasa on the diagonal into ½-inch-thick slices and place it on your largest rimmed baking sheet. Thinly slice the bell pepper and onion and add them to the pan with the kielbasa, along with the okra pods and tomatoes. Add the olive oil, 1½ teaspoons salt, the thyme, paprika, and garlic powder and toss to coat evenly.

Broil for 12 to 15 minutes, until the kielbasa and vegetables are roasty and browned in parts. Give things a stir every couple of minutes and check to make sure nothing’s burning (really check—all broilers are different!). If anything starts to burn, move the baking sheet down a rack or two to give it distance from the heat.

Meanwhile, in a large saucepan, combine 3 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Whisk in the grits and turn down the heat to low. Cook, whisking occasionally, until thickened, about 5 minutes (or according to the package directions). Stir in the cheese and butter. If the grits get too thick, stir in another splash of water. I like my grits quite thick—almost like loose mashed potatoes, not like soup—but do your thing.
Divide the grits among shallow bowls, top with the kielbasa and veggies, and garnish with fresh herbs. Enjoy!

name: Ramen Vongole
note:
My best friend Lily lives in New York City, so I spend every work trip to the city squeezing in as much time as possible with her and her babies. On a recent trip, we snagged a last-minute reservation at the infamous Union Square Cafe. I was super pregnant, and she had been running around to her interior design clients’ homes all day and was famished—needless to say, we feasted like kings. One of the dishes we had was the most incredible vongole, and Lily (the worst cook in the entire world, and I say that with love) said, “I feel like you could hack this with instant ramen somehow?” I flew back to California the next day and did exactly that.

SWAP
If you can’t find frozen clams, drain 2 (10-ounce) cans whole baby clams in water and use those—the method works the same. Or swap in fresh clams in their shells. Clean them really well, then add them after stirring in the seasoning packets and let them simmer alone for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the ramen, then cover the pan and cook until the shells open (discard any that don’t). • If you can’t find Maruchan ramen noodles and are using seasoning-packet-less ramen, use 1 teaspoon reduced-sodium Better Than Bouillon or bouillon powder, ½ teaspoon garlic powder, ¼ teaspoon onion powder, ¼ teaspoon sugar, a couple dashes of soy sauce, and some pepper in place of the 2 seasoning packets.

RIFF
For more crunch or color or both, top each serving with chili crisp, chopped roasted cashews, and/or sliced scallions.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 67

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¾ cup dry white wine (I like sauvignon blanc) or bottled clam juice
ingredients.name: dry white wine (I like sauvignon blanc) or bottled clam juice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 (3-ounce) packages Maruchan instant ramen noodles (any flavor)
ingredients.name: Maruchan instant ramen noodles (any flavor)

preparationSteps: Mince the garlic. Roughly chop the parsley leaves and tender stems. Cut the lemon into 6 wedges.

Warm the butter and olive oil together in a wide, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. When the butter is melted, add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook, stirring often, until the garlic is fragrant and just beginning to turn golden, about 2 minutes.

Add the wine and ¾ cup water and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Stir in 2 seasoning packets from the ramen noodles (discard the remaining packet). Nestle the ramen noodles into the liquid, then place the clams on top. Return to a boil, then cover the pan and cook for 3 minutes. Uncover and use tongs to mix up the noodles and clams and cook, uncovered, until the noodles are tender, the clams are heated through, and the sauce has thickened slightly, 1 to 2 minutes more.

Squeeze in the juice from 1 lemon wedge. Taste and squeeze in the juice from 1 more lemon wedge and/or add salt, if needed. Remove the pan from the heat and stir in most of the parsley. Serve in individual bowls, sprinkled with the remaining parsley.

name: Toasty Pistachio Salad with Roasted Salmon
note:
I’ve been pistachio obsessed my entire life. As a kid, I’d pass the time on summer road trips by buying a bag of pistachios at one of the little stands on the country roads we’d take to avoid the beach traffic and cracking them from their shells. My fingertips would be red and salty by the end of our trek from Winston-Salem, North Carolina, to Bald Head, an island off the coast of North Carolina, where my whole extended family has been vacationing since the 1970s. I love to simply add pistachios to my salads, but what happens when they become the star? It doesn’t get any better than this toasty pistachio vinaigrette made by toasting them in olive oil and then stirring together a punchy, crunchy dressing right in the skillet. Toss the vin with arugula, apple, Parm, and top it off with lemon pepper salmon for a truly restaurant-worthy entrée salad.

TIP
Measuring honey is very, very annoying. I’ve provided measurements here in case you need them, but my recommended method is to add just a little, taste, and add more if you want it.

LEARN
I really love slow roasting salmon. If you have a bit more time, try cooking it at 275°F for 20 to 30 minutes for an incredibly tender, sashimi-like texture.

SWAP
In the springtime, swap in thinly sliced radishes and snap peas for the apple. In the winter, swap in thinly sliced oranges. In the summer, strawberries are so, so good here. • Or use a vegetable peeler to shave 2 medium zucchini into thin ribbons, pile them on a serving platter, and spoon the cooled dressing over top with lots of shaved Parm. • The vinaigrette is also so delicious over roasted butternut squash with lots of goat cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

EXTRA EXTRA
If you have the time, chop the pistachios before you brown them for more even pistachio coverage.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 68

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup shelled raw or roasted pistachios
ingredients.name: shelled raw or roasted pistachios

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large crisp apple, such as Pink Lady or Honeycrisp
ingredients.name: large crisp apple, such as Pink Lady or Honeycrisp

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more if needed

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil.

Warm ½ cup olive oil and the pistachios together in a small saucepan or skillet over medium-low heat until the pistachios are deeply, deeply browned. The pistachios will begin to sizzle and fizzle and bubble, and that’s how you’ll know you’re on the right track. This will take as many as 10 minutes if they’re raw, fewer if they’re already roasted, so watch closely—they’ll go from brown to black quickly! Pour the oil and pistachios into a large bowl to cool.

Meanwhile, arrange the salmon fillets on the prepared baking sheet (skin side down, if they have skin). Generously drizzle the tops with olive oil to coat. Using a Microplane, grate the lemon zest on top and then add 2 teaspoons of the honey, 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Use your hands to rub everything in and evenly coat the salmon.

Roast the salmon for 12 minutes, or until the fish reaches 125°F internally for medium-rare (my preferred temp), 135°F for medium, or 140°F for medium-well. (Do not pass 140°F! This is where salmon gets dry and chalky.)

Halve the zested lemon and squeeze the juice into the bowl with the pistachios. Stir in the mustard, the remaining 2 teaspoons honey, and a little pinch each of salt and pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Add the arugula to the bowl with the dressing. Core the apple, slice it into thin batons, and add them on top. Add the Parm and toss to coat well. Taste and adjust the seasonings as needed.
Divide the salad among four bowls and top each with a salmon fillet. Grate more Parm over top if you like and serve.

name: One-Pot Springy Shrimp Primavera Pasta
note:
When the first bunches of locally grown asparagus make their debut at the Sunday farmers’ market in Carmel Valley each year, I grab a bunch and immediately get to cooking this spring thing. Here we’re using my favorite method for one-pot veggie pastas: throwing the veg and shrimp right into the pot of boiling water to cook them with your pasta—no sautéing required, and that means no dirtying another pan. We call upon the Boursin gods (or any other herby cheese spread your favorite store sells!) to bestow tons of richness and flavor with literally no effort on our end.

TIPS
Use 1 block of Boursin for a delicious light sauce or 2 packages for a rich, super-creamy sauce. • Medium-thick asparagus is about the same diameter as your pinkie finger. • As the pasta sits, the sauce will continue to thicken. If it’s too thick/stiff when you go back for seconds, toss in a bit more of that pasta cooking water—that’s what it’s there for! I typically use all 2 cups by the end of dinner.

LEARN
Shrimp sizes are denoted with a number, which represents the number of shrimp that make up a pound. For example, “16/20” translates to 16 to 20 shrimp per pound. The higher the number, the smaller the shrimp, and vice versa. Words like “small,” “medium,” “large,” “extra-large,” “jumbo,” or “colossal” are also used, though these vary widely depending on where you buy them.

SWAP
You can summer-ize this pasta by swapping out the asparagus for yellow squash or zucchini (quartered lengthwise and thinly sliced) and/or halved cherry tomatoes.

RIFF
Give it a chicken Alfredo spin by ditching the shrimp and stirring in 2 cups chopped cooked chicken at the end.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 71

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound small pasta noodles, such as rotini, farfalle, or orecchiette
ingredients.name: small pasta noodles, such as rotini, farfalle, or orecchiette

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound peeled and deveined jumbo (16/20) raw shrimp (tails on or off)
ingredients.name: peeled and deveined jumbo raw shrimp (tails on or off)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 or 2 (5.3-ounce) blocks Boursin cheese (any flavor—I like Garlic and Fine Herbs; see Tip)
ingredients.name: Boursin cheese (any flavor—I like Garlic and Fine Herbs; see Tip)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): finely chopped fresh basil or parsley, red pepper flakes, freshly grated Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): finely chopped fresh basil or parsley, red pepper flakes, freshly grated Parmesan cheese

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until al dente according to the package directions.
Meanwhile, trim the asparagus and cut the stalks into 1-inch pieces. Halve the lemon.

Two minutes before the pasta is finished cooking, add the asparagus to the pot. One minute before the pasta is done, add the shrimp and peas to the pot as well. Stir to make sure everything is submerged.
Scoop out 2 cups of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta, asparagus, shrimp, and peas. (It’s okay if the shrimp don’t look totally cooked yet; they’ll continue cooking in the sauce.)

Place the empty pot over medium heat. Add ¾ cup of the reserved pasta cooking water, the juice of both lemon halves, the Boursin, butter, 2 teaspoons salt, and some black pepper. (If you’re using 2 blocks of Boursin, add another ¼ to ½ cup pasta cooking water.) Stir until a smooth sauce forms, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the pasta, asparagus, shrimp, and peas to the pot of sauce. Use a big spoon to toss to coat everything evenly. If your sauce is too thick, add more pasta cooking water; if it’s too liquidy at the bottom of the pot, keep tossing. Taste and add more salt, black pepper, and/or lemon juice until it’s absolutely delicious. If you like, sprinkle with fresh herbs, red pepper flakes, and/or Parm before serving.

name: Tiny Tomato Pasta (Book)
note:
Starring vine-ripe tiny tomatoes and a handful of fragrant basil—this, my friends, is peak summer cooking. What to Cookers everywhere are addicted to this pasta! It’s best with the freshest summer tomatoes—especially Sungolds—but if you’re craving it midwinter, you can make it with cherry tomatoes and add a pinch of sugar. Use whatever pasta you’ve got, but I’m telling you, angel hair is absolutely elite here.

TIP
If you’re feeding picky/texture-averse eaters, blend the sauce with an immersion blender or transfer it to a standing blender before adding the pasta, basil, and Parm.

LEARN
Stirring in the cheese in two batches helps it melt more evenly without clumping.

SHORTCUT
I will always and forever grate my own Parm in the blender or food processor. Just cut off the rind, cut it into a few hunks, and blend or process until grated!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 78

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 pounds cherry, Sungold, or grape tomatoes
ingredients.name: cherry, Sungold, or grape tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (4 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (4 ounces), plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out 1½ cups of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.

Melt the butter in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Thinly slice the garlic. Add the garlic, tomatoes, 1½ teaspoons salt, and the red pepper flakes to the pot and turn up the heat to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are bursting and forming a sauce with the butter, about 8 minutes. Use a spatula to carefully smash any tomatoes that haven’t burst on their own against the side of the pan. Turn off the heat.
Thinly slice the basil.

To the sauce in the pot, add the cooked pasta, ¼ cup of the reserved pasta cooking water (see Learn, page 60), most of the basil (reserve a little bit for garnish), and ½ cup of the Parm and stir until all the cheese has melted into a smooth sauce. Stir in the remaining ½ cup Parm until smooth. Stir in more of the pasta cooking water until everything looks saucy and delicious. Taste and add more salt as needed.
Scoop into shallow bowls and top each serving with some of the reserved basil and more Parm.

name: Hot Honey Roasted Broccoli and Chickpeas with Couscous
note:
Whenever I return home from any trip, I have one blanket craving: vegetables. I’ll grab whatever veg is on the brink of expiring in my fridge (it’s almost always a bag of broccoli florets) and roast it to crisp perfection along with a can of chickpeas, which my pantry is never without. Add a nice dressing and an easy grain, and this simple, delicious veggie bowl becomes a full welcome-home feast.

TIP
For milder heat, use a drizzle of sriracha or some smoked paprika in the honey instead of red pepper flakes, or just skip the pepper flakes!

SWAP
Swap in fine or quick-cooking bulgur for the couscous (increase the water to 2 cups and let it stand for 10 to 12 minutes). • Use cubed firm or extra-firm tofu or cooked lentils in place of the chickpeas.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 81

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1¼ cups low-sodium vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup roasted salted peanuts, almonds, or cashews
ingredients.name: roasted salted peanuts, almonds, or cashews

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry
ingredients.name: chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup honey, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: honey, plus more if needed

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Warm the stock in a small saucepan over medium heat for a few minutes or in the microwave for a few seconds.

Combine the couscous and ½ teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Pour the warm stock and 1 tablespoon olive oil over the couscous and stir together with the couscous. Cover the bowl with a plate or plastic wrap and let stand for 5 minutes, until the liquid has been completely absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, chop the nuts and the cilantro leaves and tender stems.

Place the broccoli on the prepared baking sheet; use your hands to break any large florets into smaller ones as you do this. Scatter the chickpeas around the broccoli. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil, the paprika (if using), 1 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Toss to coat well and spread out the broccoli and chickpeas in an even layer. Roast for 15 to 20 minutes, until the edges are crisp and golden, shaking the pan halfway through.

Meanwhile, halve the lime and squeeze the juice into a small bowl. Whisk in 1 tablespoon olive oil, the honey, red pepper flakes, ¼ teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Taste and adjust the flavor with more lime juice, honey, and/or salt.

Drizzle the roasted broccoli and chickpeas with half the dressing and toss to coat. Spoon the couscous into shallow bowls and top with the broccoli and chickpeas. Garnish with the chopped nuts and cilantro and pass the remaining dressing at the table.

name: Pantry Soup (Curry Noodle Soup)
note:
When I need comfort food, and fast, I often turn to a pantry soup—that is, a soup that uses whatever the heck I can find in my pantry. One day after surveying my spice drawer and collection of canned goods, I ended up with this iteration, which marries the cozy flavors of curry with the satiating duo of pasta and chickpeas (à la the Italian classic pasta e ceci), and wow, did it hit the spot. This has since become one of my go-to meals when my fridge is bare and my family is starving—or whenever I need a very low-lift food hug.

LEARN
I love using canned coconut cream when I want a really creamy soup or curry, but it can be hard to find! It’s basically coconut milk with a higher fat content (whichever you use, shake the can first to reincorporate the fat and coconut water). Note that I am not talking about cream of coconut (or crema de coco), the sweetened ingredient used in piña coladas!

SWAP
Any white bean works here! Feel free to mix and match your beans: ½ can of chickpeas, ½ can of cannellini, whatever! • If you’re swapping in gluten-free noodles, cook the noodles per the package directions in a separate pot. Drain and add them to the soup pot when you add the coconut milk. • Sub in coconut aminos for the soy sauce.

RIFF
For a thicker, more curry-like dish, add only 1 canful of water.

BULK IT UP
Add a big handful of chopped hearty greens such as spinach, kale, collards, chard, or cabbage when you add the pasta to the pot.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 82

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can any white bean (chickpeas, cannellini, navy, etc.)
ingredients.name: any white bean (chickpeas, cannellini, navy, etc.)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon curry powder, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: plus 1 teaspoon curry powder, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (13.5-ounce) can full-fat coconut milk or coconut cream
ingredients.name: full-fat coconut milk or coconut cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5-ounce) can diced tomatoes, with their juices
ingredients.name: diced tomatoes, with their juices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces small pasta noodles, such as orecchiette, farfalle, or rotini
ingredients.name: small pasta noodles, such as orecchiette, farfalle, or rotini

preparationSteps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the chickpeas and cook, stirring occasionally, until they’re beginning to break apart and turn golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the curry powder, turmeric, and salt and cook, stirring, until fragrant, 30 seconds more.

Pour in the coconut milk, tomatoes with their juices, and soy sauce. Fill up the tomato can with water and add that to the pot, then fill it up again and add that (so, that’s 2 canfuls of water). Turn up the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, then turn it down to medium and drop in the pasta. Cook according to the package directions until al dente, stirring often. Halve the lime and stir in the juice of 1 half. Taste and add more soy sauce, lime juice, and/or curry powder as desired.
Ladle the soup into bowls and enjoy.

name: Spicy Saucy Tofu with Quick Slaw and Sesame Rice
note:
Tofu haters often cite “blandness” as an excuse to steer clear of the plant-based protein. But its blandness is actually its biggest strength! It so wonderfully absorbs whatever sauce you add to it—like this utterly craveable Korean-inspired gochujang sauce. The sauce does the heavy lifting here; all you do is add some prepped vegetables and a grain, and you’ll have a home-run dinner in minutes.

SWAP
Swap out the tofu for ground chicken, turkey, or pork and use your spatula to break the meat into small crumbles as it cooks.

RIFF
I love a lot of slaw with this tofu dish, so I wrote the recipe that way. If you have leftover slaw but no more rice or tofu, toss it into Warm Sesame Noodles (page 89) or Beef Basil Bowls (page 129). Or, throw the slaw into a hot, lightly oiled skillet and warm it through to serve alongside roasted chicken or pork.

BULK IT UP
Add sliced avocado or a fried egg on top of each serving. • Toss some chopped peanuts or cashews into the slaw or the tofu. • Add sliced cucumbers or radishes to the slaw.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 85

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ tablespoons plus ½ cup low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: plus ½ cup low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 teaspoons toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag shredded green cabbage or coleslaw mix
ingredients.name: shredded green cabbage or coleslaw mix

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons plus 2 tablespoons honey, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons honey, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons gochujang, sambal oelek, or sriracha
ingredients.name: gochujang, sambal oelek, or sriracha

preparationSteps: In a medium saucepan, combine the rice, 1¾ cups water, 2 tablespoons neutral oil, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, and ½ teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes or until ready to serve. Uncover and use a fork to fluff the rice, then gently stir in 2 teaspoons of the sesame seeds and 1 teaspoon of the sesame oil.

Meanwhile, combine the cabbage and carrots in a large bowl. Halve 1 lime and squeeze in the juice. Add the remaining 4 teaspoons sesame seeds, 3 teaspoons sesame oil, ½ tablespoon of the soy sauce, and 2 teaspoons of the honey. Toss to coat well. Taste and add more lime juice, soy sauce, or honey.

Warm your largest skillet over medium-high heat until a drop of water flicked into the pan dances on the surface. Meanwhile, drain the tofu, then use your hands to squeeze out as much liquid as you possibly can. It’ll break apart a bit and that’s fine.

Add 2 tablespoons neutral oil to the hot skillet. When it shimmers, break the tofu into bite-size pieces and add them directly to the pan in an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until lightly browned on the bottom, 2 to 3 minutes. Give it a stir, then cook until lightly browned all over, 3 to 5 minutes more. It’s fine if some bits stick to the pan; the sauce will get them. Scooch all the tofu into a pile on one side of the pan.

To the cleared side of the skillet, add 2 tablespoons neutral oil, then use a Microplane to grate the garlic and ginger (no need to peel it) into the oil. Cook, stirring, until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds. Pour in the remaining ½ cup soy sauce, 2 tablespoons honey, and the remaining 2 teaspoons sesame oil, then add ½ cup water, the gochujang, vinegar, and some pepper. Stir with a wooden spoon, scraping up any browned bits from the skillet, and bring the sauce to a simmer.
Push the tofu into the sauce and cook, stirring once or twice, until the tofu has absorbed the flavors and the sauce has thickened, 3 to 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the remaining lime into 8 wedges and slice the scallions.

Divide the rice among bowls. Top with the tofu, spooning extra sauce over the top. Add a generous scoop of the slaw and garnish with the scallions and sesame seeds. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing.

name: The Only Egg Salad You’ll Ever Need
note:
Every Southern baby shower, funeral, and wedding luncheon has tiny crustless white bread sandwiches (also known as tea sandwiches) stuffed with egg salad. They are typically delightfully nostalgic and woefully underseasoned at once. But not my egg salad! My egg salad—inspired by my mom’s, which broke the internet—is bright, zippy, and full of herby lemon flavor. And it tastes even better the next day! Serve it on soft white bread, scoop it up onto Ritz crackers, or toast a really good slice of sourdough bread and make it open-faced. If, like me, you hate peeling hard-boiled eggs but love egg salad, you’re gonna love my trick for cracking and steaming them instead (it’s even easier than my mom’s method!). You’ll never wrestle with eggshells—or eat boring egg salad—again.

TIP
If I’m leaving you with leftover herbs, I’m sorry—but they’re important here! Plan to make Open-Faced Cheesy Chutney Chicken Melts (page 35) and a Dilly Feta Salad (page 146) this week to use up the rest of the chives and dill.

SWAP
If you have cilantro or parsley, you can use those instead of dill and chives for a different herby vibe! • Try Greek yogurt or cottage cheese instead of the mayo for a protein hit.

RIFF
Make a curry egg salad! Omit the dill and mustard, and add 1 teaspoon curry powder, ¼ teaspoon paprika, and 1 small grated carrot.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 86

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon light vinegar, such as apple cider, champagne, or distilled white
ingredients.name: light vinegar, such as apple cider, champagne, or distilled white

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 dill sprigs, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: dill sprigs, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 tablespoons mayonnaise, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: mayonnaise, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: Dijon mustard, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft white bread, toasted sourdough bread, butter lettuce leaves, Ritz crackers, or your preferred egg salad vessel, for serving
ingredients.name: Soft white bread, toasted sourdough bread, butter lettuce leaves, Ritz crackers, or your preferred egg salad vessel, for serving

preparationSteps: Warm 2 inches of water in a 10-inch medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add a big pinch of salt and the vinegar. When small bubbles begin to appear, crack in the eggs and reduce the heat to medium. The water should not be boiling, it should be a nice gentle steam; adjust the heat as needed. Season with a little pinch of salt and some pepper, then cover. Cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are set, 4 to 6 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop the celery, chives, and dill.

Use a slotted spoon to transfer the eggs to a cutting board. Chop them really finely—like when you think you’re done chopping, chop through them one more time. Transfer them to a large bowl. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of the lemon half into the bowl, then squeeze in the juice. Add the celery and herbs, along with the mayonnaise, mustard, ½ teaspoon salt, and a little bit of pepper and mix to combine. Taste and adjust the ingredients as needed—sometimes I like more mayo or mustard or salt! If you have time, cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before eating.
