Scoop the egg salad onto your serving vessel of choice and, if you like, top it with more chives and dill. Or eat it straight with a spoon like I do! Store any leftover egg salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

name: Warm Sesame Noodles with Bok Choy and Bell Peppers
note:
When George and I spent a summer in New York City during his time in business school, we lived in Tribeca, just below Canal Street, the heart of Chinatown. Our favorite thing was to meet up after work and walk east on Canal Street until we found the spicy, slurpy noodles we were craving. Our favorite spot was a place called Noodletown, where we’d happily gobble up ginormous servings of warm sesame noodles while we caught up on the day’s events. Now that we live in the country, we have to fend for ourselves when saucy noodle cravings hit. Warning: When I make these, I have to resist eating half the sesame-tahini sauce with a spoon over the kitchen sink. It’s that good—but it’s always worth waiting for the hot noodles and veg (and leftover chicken, tofu, steak, or pork, if I have some in the fridge!) to join the party.

SHORTCUT
Use frozen precut stir-fry vegetables. Add during the last 2 minutes of cooking.

SWAP
Any long noodle will work here. I like spaghetti, udon, or whatever is in my pantry! • Any nut or seed butter works in place of tahini for a different delicious nutty profile.

BULK IT UP
Add roasted cubed firm or extra-firm tofu or shredded rotisserie chicken. • Or the Spicy Saucy Tofu (page 85) would be great on top of these noodles.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 89

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small (not baby) head bok choy (about 1 pound)
ingredients.name: small (not baby) head bok choy (about 1 pound)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup tahini, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: tahini, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons sesame oil (preferably toasted), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: sesame oil (preferably toasted), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: rice vinegar, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ tablespoons maple syrup or honey, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: maple syrup or honey, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ teaspoon garlic powder, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: garlic powder, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ teaspoon ground ginger, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: ground ginger, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces ramen noodles (flavor packets discarded, if using instant)
ingredients.name: ramen noodles (flavor packets discarded, if using instant)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Chopped roasted salted peanuts, for serving
ingredients.name: Chopped roasted salted peanuts, for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, trim the bok choy and cut the leaves from the stems. Thinly slice the stems and leaves. Slice the bell pepper into thin strips. Thinly slice the scallions.
In a large bowl, whisk together the tahini, sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, maple syrup, garlic powder, ginger, and a pinch of salt. Taste and add more of anything you’d like.

Add the noodles to the boiling water and cook according to the package directions. During the last 3 minutes of cooking, add the bok choy. During the last 1½ minutes of cooking, add the bell pepper. Scoop out ½ cup of the noodle cooking water and drain everything in a colander.
Add the hot noodles and vegetables to the bowl with the sauce. Toss well, adding noodle water one splash at a time, until the sauce is creamy and everything is coated evenly.
Divide among shallow bowls and top each serving with scallions, toasted sesame seeds, and chopped peanuts. Serve warm.

name: Miso Peanut Chicken Bowls with Cilantro Lime Slaw
note:
Before I was What to Cook-ing, I had a host of developer/tester/ghostwriter gigs. One of those was for a book called Eat to Beat Depression and Anxiety by Dr. Drew Ramsey, through which I came to understand that fermented foods like miso (and sauerkraut, kimchi, kefir, and kombucha, among others) are packed with probiotics that benefit our gut health, which, in turn, can boost our mental health. I was already a miso devotee for flavor reasons—it’s such an easy way to add umami to a meal—but after learning about its health benefits, I became even more obsessed with incorporating it anywhere I could.

TIP
Once you’ve made this meal, use your leftover miso to make the miso-creamed spinach and mushrooms on page 126.

SWAP
You can use boneless, skinless chicken thighs instead of breasts: Trim off any white fat, cut into 2-inch pieces, and cook in the sauce until easy to shred, 14 to 16 minutes.

SHORTCUT
Shred the meat from 1 warm rotisserie chicken and toss it with the warmed sauce over medium heat until coated and saucy.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 93

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: rice vinegar, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 2 tablespoons sriracha, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: sriracha, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 or 2 limes (or 4 more tablespoons rice vinegar)
ingredients.name: limes (or 4 more tablespoons rice vinegar)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces shredded green cabbage or coleslaw mix
ingredients.name: shredded green cabbage or coleslaw mix

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toasted sesame seeds or chopped peanuts, for serving
ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds or chopped peanuts, for serving

preparationSteps: In a small pot, combine the rice, 2½ cups of the stock, and the butter. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes, or until you’re ready to serve. Fluff with a fork before serving.

In a large saucepan or wide pot, working off the heat, whisk together the remaining 1½ cups stock, the peanut butter, soy sauce, miso paste, maple syrup, vinegar, sriracha, and garlic powder. You might need to use a fork to smoosh the peanut butter and miso and get them to combine into the liquid. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to medium-low.

Trim any white fat off the chicken breasts, then cut them into 2-inch cubes. Add the chicken to the pan with the sauce in an even layer, cover, and cook for 5 minutes. Flip the chicken pieces, cover, and cook until the chicken is cooked through, 5 to 8 minutes more. You can check by pulling a piece apart with two forks—it should shred easily.

Turn up the heat to medium-high and cook, uncovered, stirring often, until the sauce thickens, 3 to 4 minutes. It’s okay if the chicken shreds apart a bit—in fact, if you have the time, use two forks to shred it a bit for optimum sauce absorption. Taste and add more vinegar for tang, soy sauce for salt, and/or sriracha for heat.

Meanwhile, finely chop the cilantro leaves and tender stems and transfer to a large bowl. Halve 1 lime and squeeze in the juice. Add the cabbage, sesame oil, neutral oil, and a big pinch of salt. Toss to combine. Add the juice from the second lime, if desired (I like it really tangy, so I do!).
Scoop the rice into bowls. Top with the chicken and slaw. Drizzle extra sauce from the chicken over the top. Finish with sriracha and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Sheet Pan Summery Lemon Oregano Chicken and Squash
note:
Sometimes it’s the dead of summer—also known as high grilling season—but you simply do not feel like grilling. There’s a strong dividing line between “hot enough to grill” and “too hot to grill.” When yellow squash and zucchini are abundant but you cannot bear to stand near a flame, this sheet pan chicken dinner is the move. It’s important to note that the bread isn’t an afterthought! Using it to scoop up the softened veg, creamy cheese, and briny olives (and to wipe the plate clean) is arguably the best part.

RIFF
Use dried Italian seasoning in place of Greek seasoning, and serve with pesto!

BULK IT UP
Serve with herby couscous (see Bulk It Up, page 202). Top with hummus and/or tzatziki.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 94

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5- to 6-ounce) jar pitted green olives, such as Castelvetrano, drained (about 1 cup)
ingredients.name: pitted green olives, such as Castelvetrano, drained (about 1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Greek seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Greek seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large loaf focaccia or other chewy bread
ingredients.name: focaccia or other chewy bread

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of flaky sea salt
ingredients.name: Big pinch of flaky sea salt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces goat, brine-packed feta, or ricotta salata cheese
ingredients.name: goat, brine-packed feta, or ricotta salata cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Freshly ground black pepper, for serving
ingredients.name: Freshly ground black pepper, for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Trim off any white fat from the chicken thighs. Slice the zucchini and yellow squash into ¼-inch-thick rounds. Thinly slice the lemon. Tear or slice the olives in half.

Place the chicken, zucchini, squash, lemon slices, and olives on a baking sheet and toss with 3 tablespoons of the olive oil, the Greek seasoning, 1¼ teaspoons kosher salt, and oregano sprigs to coat well. Spread the chicken, zucchini, squash, lemon slices, and olives into an even layer, overlapping them as little as possible.

Roast until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender and lightly browned, about 25 minutes. If they’re lacking color, broil for a few minutes at the very end to brown things up a bit.

Meanwhile, place the focaccia on a separate baking sheet. Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and sprinkle with the flaky salt. During the final 5 minutes of cooking the chicken thighs, place the pan in the oven to warm the focaccia through (but don’t broil it).

Crumble the cheese over the chicken and veggies, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with some pepper. Serve your summer medley straight from the baking sheet, with big hunks of sliced or torn focaccia for sopping up all the juices.

name: Sheet Pan Wintry Butter Roasted Chicken and Delicata Squash
note:
This is my wintry foil to the Sheet Pan Summery Lemon Oregano Chicken and Squash on page 94. We call upon my all-time favorite winter squash—delicata—and pair it with cozy notes like maple syrup, cumin, curry, and thyme. It’s incredibly simple to make, yet comes out of the oven impressive enough to serve for a special occasion. If you find yourself hosting a small crew on a holiday, or if you’re a turkey hater looking for an alternative main for Thanksgiving, this would be an excellent choice. Or just make it on a Monday—it’s that easy! (Full transparency: It’s gonna take you closer to 40 minutes than 30, but it still deserves a spot in this chapter.)

TIP
Containers of pomegranate seeds are available in the produce section of most grocery stores. If you can’t find them, you can grab a pomegranate and remove the seeds yourself (meh) or thinly slice a crisp apple to add a pop of sweetness and crunch here instead (I’d vote for apple).

SWAP
If you prefer boneless, skinless chicken thighs here, roast as directed. It’s very hard to overcook chicken thighs, but if they’re done before the squash, use tongs to transfer them to a platter and cover loosely with aluminum foil while you finish roasting the veggies, then toss it all together on a single baking sheet as directed.

EXTRA EXTRA
The arugula, pom seeds, and goat cheese quite frankly are extra extra. You can omit them to make this a simpler sheet pan meal, but they really bring it all together in a special way—and it’s not like they take any extra prep time (unless you opt to remove the seeds from the pomegranate yourself . . .)!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 97

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup halved pitted dates (preferably Medjool)
ingredients.name: halved pitted dates (preferably Medjool)

preparationSteps: Position racks in the top and bottom thirds of the oven (if your oven is wide enough to fit two baking sheets on one rack, just position a rack in the middle) and preheat to 450°F.

Trim the ends off the delicata squash and halve them lengthwise. Use a large spoon to scrape out and discard the seeds. Cut the squash into ½-inch-thick slices. Cut the onion in half through the root end, then into 1-inch wedges. The layers will fall apart—that’s okay, but keep them together if at all possible.

Pile the chicken, squash, onion, and thyme sprigs onto a baking sheet. Add the melted butter, maple syrup, salt, cumin, curry powder, and ginger and toss to coat well—really get in there! Transfer half the mixture to a separate baking sheet and spread everything on both pans into an even layer.

Roast everything for about 25 minutes, until the thickest part of the chicken reaches 165°F internally, swapping the pans on the top and bottom racks halfway through cooking. Pull the baking sheets out and flip the squash (or don’t, if you’re feeling lazy), then scatter the dates and walnut halves on top and roast for 3 to 4 minutes more, until they’re warm and toasty.
Toss everything together on one of the baking sheets. Scatter the arugula, goat cheese, and pomegranate seeds over the top and drizzle with balsamic. Serve straight from the pan.

name: Chicken Parm Meatballs with Broccoli Butter Noodles
note:
These meatballs are masquerading as chicken Parm, harnessing the taste of the Italian classic (breaded chicken, tangy tomato sauce, a boatload of gooey cheese) while demanding a lot less work (no pounding of chicken cutlets or flour dredging here!). If you’re on the hook for a potluck dish or drop-off meal for a friend, might I recommend these? You can even halve the meatball size so they’re more grazeable (and shave 6 to 8 minutes from their total baking time as a bonus). I really like pairing them with silky buttery broccoli noodles to check off both a grain and a vegetable—the broccoli breaks down into creamy little green specks my kids gobble right up.

RIFF
Make it a meatloaf! See the Riff on page 105.

SWAP
You could ditch the meatballs and serve grilled shrimp or chicken over the noodles instead. • Or keep the meatballs, ditch the noodles, and serve with sourdough bread to sop up the sauce!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 98

ingredients.rawIngredient: ⅔ cup panko breadcrumbs, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: panko breadcrumbs, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (4 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (4 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Coat a 10-inch ovenproof skillet with cooking spray. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Finely chop the basil leaves.

In a large bowl, combine the ground chicken, ⅓ cup of the panko, ½ cup of the Parm, ¼ cup of the chopped basil, the Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon salt, the garlic powder, and the egg. Use your hands to mix well, then scoop out and roll 12 even-size meatballs.

Pour the remaining ⅓ cup panko into a shallow bowl or plate. Roll each meatball through the panko, pressing to adhere (add more breadcrumbs to the bowl if needed to coat them all!), and place them in the prepared skillet. Coat the meatballs with cooking spray.

Bake the meatballs for 12 minutes. Remove the skillet from the oven and pour in the marinara so the meatballs are nestled in the sauce (be careful—the sauce might splatter a bit since the skillet is super-hot). Sprinkle the mozzarella over everything, then return the skillet to the oven and bake for 10 minutes more, until the cheese is melty.

While the meatballs are cooking, add the pasta and broccoli to the boiling water (use your hands to break any large florets into smaller ones as you drop them in) and cook until the pasta is al dente, according to the package directions. Scoop out ½ cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta and broccoli and return them to the empty pot. Add the butter, ¼ cup of the reserved pasta cooking water (see Learn, page 60), remaining ½ cup of the Parm, a nice handful of the chopped basil, and ¾ teaspoon salt. Use tongs to toss until the broccoli breaks down into tiny bits and combines with the pasta and Parm into a silky sauce. Add more pasta water if you want things saucier and a pinch of red pepper flakes if you like.
Scatter more fresh basil and Parm over the meatballs and serve immediately, over or alongside the broccoli noodles.

name: One-Pan Butter Chicken–Inspired Meatballs
note:
Butter chicken—spiced chicken floating in a velvety tomato sauce—is a North Indian comfort food beloved around the world. It’s a dish I crave often and have riffed on countlessly in my kitchen. When I repackaged the flavors of that dish into this meatball meal, I felt like I’d struck weeknight gold. I can double the meatballs and freeze them for future dinners, and I can easily deconstruct the meal for my pickiest children. For them, I serve the meatballs sauceless with a spoonful of beans, raw spinach (can’t tell you why, but they’ll eat it raw and only raw), and naan. For my more adventurous kids, George, and me, I serve them soaked in sauce, with beans and (wilted!) spinach.

SWAP
If you don’t love beans, leave them out, and serve the meatballs and sauce over quinoa or Israeli couscous instead. • Kale, Swiss chard, or escarole are great in place of the spinach, but stir them in right before you add the meatballs to the sauce, as they need a bit longer to cook.

RIFF
You can make pretty much any meatball recipe into a meatloaf instead. Spray a loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray, lightly pack the meat in, and bake at 350°F for 1 hour, or until the internal temperature reaches 160°F for beef and pork or 165°F for turkey and chicken.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 105

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can white beans, such as cannellini or great northern, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: white beans, such as cannellini or great northern

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 big handfuls of fresh baby spinach
ingredients.name: big handfuls of fresh baby spinach

preparationSteps: Make the meatballs. In a large bowl, combine the ground chicken, ricotta, breadcrumbs, garam masala, salt, and garlic powder. Use your hands to mix well, then scoop out and lay them on a sheet of parchment paper. (I don’t even roll them to make sure they’re perfectly round!) You should have about 20 meatballs.

Make the sauce. Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the garam masala, garlic powder, and onion powder and cook, stirring, until very fragrant, about 1 minute. Carefully stir in the tomato sauce (it might splatter when it hits the hot butter), coconut milk, beans, and sugar. Turn up the heat to high to bring to a boil, then reduce to medium-high and stir for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.

Turn down the heat to medium and add the meatballs. Cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice. The sauce should be gently bubbling, but if it starts to bubble too much and splatter, turn down the heat a little more. Uncover to stir in the spinach and flip all the meatballs over in the sauce, then replace the lid and cook until the spinach is wilted and the meatballs are cooked through and reach 165°F internally, 5 to 7 minutes more. Taste the sauce and add salt as needed. If it’s too thick, add a splash of water to thin it to your liking.
Meanwhile, finely chop the cilantro. Cut the lime into 4 wedges. Throw the naan on a baking sheet and slide it under the broiler until it’s warm and golden brown (don’t burn it!).
Spoon the meatballs and sauce into bowls. Sprinkle each with cilantro and serve with a lime wedge for squeezing and naan for scooping.

name: One-Pot Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Orzotto
note:
Think of this meal as a cross between a hearty winter soup (à la mushroom barley or chicken and wild rice) and a decadent risotto. One-pot pastas like this orzotto (aka risotto-style orzo) are one of my go-to meals when hosting a crowd. They couldn’t take less effort and yet never fail to impress—I’d happily pay $20 for a big bowl of this at a restaurant. If I’m feeding picky kids, I’ll hold back the spinach, serve the kids, then stir it in for the adult portions.

SWAP
If you’re in the mood for a lighter meal, you could swap out half or all the cream for extra stock. Or, you could just double the Parm. Or, stir in a block of Boursin instead of heavy cream.

RIFF
Ditch the chicken, double the mushrooms, and use low-sodium vegetable stock to make it vegetarian. Try adding ½ cup chopped sun-dried tomatoes, too.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 106

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ teaspoons Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ to ½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes (optional)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 huge handfuls of fresh baby spinach
ingredients.name: huge handfuls of fresh baby spinach

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Trim off any white fat from the chicken, then cut the breasts into bite-size cubes. Right there on the cutting board, sprinkle the chicken with the Italian seasoning, 1¼ teaspoons salt, some black pepper, the garlic powder, and, if you want a little heat, the red pepper flakes. Toss to coat.

Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet or heavy-bottomed pot or braiser over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the chicken in an even layer and cook until browned on the bottom, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook until browned all over, 2 to 3 minutes more. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the chicken to a plate.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the mushrooms. Mince the shallot and garlic.

In the same skillet (no need to wipe it out), melt the butter over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms, shallot, and garlic. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms release all their liquid and the shallot is tender, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in a big pinch of salt, then return the chicken to the pan along with any juices that collected on the plate and add the stock and orzo. Turn up the heat to high and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon and scraping up any orzo stuck to the bottom of the pan. Stir in the cream and turn down the heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally and adjusting the heat as needed to keep it bubbling gently, until the orzo is cooked and the sauce has thickened, 10 to 12 minutes.

Turn off the heat and stir in the spinach, tearing the leaves with your hands as you add them. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of the lemon directly into the skillet, then cut the lemon in half and squeeze in the juice from half of it. Add the Parm. Cook, stirring, until the spinach has wilted, 1 to 2 minutes. If your pasta has thickened up and is no longer saucy and loose like a risotto, add more water or stock to loosen it. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Spoon the orzotto into bowls and serve topped with more Parm and black pepper. Cut the other lemon half into small wedges for serving.

name: White Cheddar Chili Crisp Flautas with Lime Crema
note:
I have a note on my iPhone titled “Leftover Dinners,” in which I jot down home-run meals I’ve made using odds and ends from my fridge. Flautas are at the top of the list and make an A+ dinner anytime you find your fridge stocked with leftover cooked meat or beans.

SWAP
Corn tortillas are tricky here—they dry out and crack, and it’s just not great. If you need a gluten-free option, I’d rather you used something like a Siete grain-free tortilla.

TIP
For the crema, if you have mayo and something like sour cream or yogurt, use ¼ cup of each. If you have something thicker, like cream cheese or labneh, you can use a tiny bit of water to make it more saucy.

RIFF
These are very riffable—the basic equation is a precooked protein + something creamy + cheese + some sort of flavor. Swap out the chopped chicken for 2 (15-ounce) cans of drained and rinsed black beans or pinto beans, or 1 pound of cooked ground meat. • Swap the white cheddar for shredded Mexican blend or Jack cheese. • Flavor add-ins range from salsa verde, harissa, a can of diced green chiles plus a little taco seasoning (that one will yield a more traditional flauta), or even honey mustard for McDonald’s Snack Wrap vibes (in the best way possible).

BULK IT UP
Roast shucked corn on the baking sheet right alongside the flautas for an easy side. Slather with butter, salt, and lime juice when they come out of the oven.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 109

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded white cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded white cheddar cheese (2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1¼ cups sour cream or plain yogurt
ingredients.name: sour cream or plain yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4-ounce) can diced green chiles, drained if very liquidy
ingredients.name: diced green chiles, drained if very liquidy

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 3 tablespoons chili crisp (crisp only—drain off the oil)
ingredients.name: chili crisp (crisp only—drain off the oil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings: shredded iceberg lettuce (optional), pico de gallo
ingredients.name: Toppings: shredded iceberg lettuce (optional), pico de gallo

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, mix together the chicken, cheese, ¾ cup of the sour cream, the chiles, 1 tablespoon of the chili crisp, and ¼ teaspoon salt. Take a little nibble. Is it delicious? If so, proceed. Does it need a little more oomph? Stir in some more salt and maybe some more chili crisp. Keep seasoning until it’s delicious.
Spread ¼ cup of the chicken mixture down the center of a tortilla, then roll it very tightly, and place it seam side down on the prepared baking sheet. Repeat until all the chicken filling is gone.
Spray the flautas really well with cooking spray. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until golden and crispy all over.

Meanwhile, halve the lime and squeeze the juice of 1 half into a small bowl. Stir it together with the remaining ½ cup sour cream (see Tip) and a little pinch of salt. Taste and add more lime juice or salt as needed.
Let the flautas cool for 5 minutes, then top with shredded iceberg, if you like, and drizzle with the lime crema! Serve with pico de gallo on the side.

name: Lemon-Parm Chicken, Quinoa, and Kale Salad (Book)
note:
I can’t begin to count how many times I’ve made this; it’s a constant in my fridge. When I shared it in the What to Cook newsletter, readers went crazy! And for good reason: The chicken and quinoa are sponges for the lemony vinaigrette, and the dish has loads of tasty add-ins that keep things interesting (almonds! cranberries! shredded carrots!). Heads up that you will need a truly enormous serving bowl to assemble this salad—a standard mixing bowl ain’t gonna cut it. If you don’t have one, whip out your big pasta pot instead. Seriously.

TIP
If I’m making this salad for dinner/to serve immediately, I use almost all the dressing! If I’m meal prepping it (which I pretty much always am), I go lighter with the dressing initially, then add a little more to each serving when I’m ready to eat it because the quinoa absorbs it. Store the salad, extra dressing, almonds, and lemon wedges in separate airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

SHORTCUT
Buy precooked quinoa (it typically comes in a tube in the refrigerated section, near the salad dressings) to make this a 15-minute recipe!

SWAP
For a hearty vegetarian meal, chickpeas or any white bean are wonderful in place of chicken. Just drain and rinse them before adding them to the mix.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 113

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¾ teaspoon reduced-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon (optional)
ingredients.name: reduced-sodium chicken Better Than Bouillon (optional)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ heaping teaspoon dried thyme or oregano
ingredients.name: heaping teaspoon dried thyme or oregano

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (16-ounce) bag chopped kale, tough stems removed
ingredients.name: chopped kale, tough stems removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (4 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (4 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup golden raisins or dried cranberries
ingredients.name: golden raisins or dried cranberries

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ bunch soft green herbs, such as fresh basil, parsley, and/or cilantro, for topping (optional)
ingredients.name: soft green herbs, such as fresh basil, parsley, and/or cilantro, for topping (optional)

preparationSteps: Make the quinoa. In a small pot, combine the quinoa, Better Than Bouillon (if using), and ¾ cup water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to low, cover, and cook until all the liquid has been absorbed, 13 to 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Uncover and fluff with a fork.

Meanwhile, make the lemon vinaigrette. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of 1 lemon into a jar with a lid, then cut all 3 lemons in half and squeeze in the juice. Add the olive oil, mustard, honey, thyme, garlic powder, ¾ teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Close the jar and shake vigorously until combined, about 30 seconds. Taste and adjust any of the flavors as desired.

Make the salad. Place the kale in a gigantic bowl and season with a big pinch each of salt and pepper. Use your hands to massage the kale until it JUST starts to feel damp—squeeze it between your fists about 10 times. If you come across any thick stem pieces, discard them. Add the cooked quinoa, chicken, carrots, Parm, raisins, and about two-thirds of the vinaigrette. Toss to combine. Add more dressing as needed until the greens are coated to your liking.

Chop the almonds and herbs (if using). If you’re using the lemon, cut it into 6 wedges. Place however much salad you like in a shallow bowl and top with the almonds. Garnish with more Parm and the chopped herbs and serve with the lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Southwestern Caesar Chicken Burgers
note:
As a professional recipe developer, my quest is not to fill your fridge with a million random bottles of things that will collect dust (or, worse, mold) over years of neglect. That’s why I’m extra proud of this meal: You’re gonna use a whole 12-ounce bottle of Caesar dressing to make a harmonious burger and side salad. Your leftover chipotle peppers in adobo are perfectly freezable (see Tip, page 40), and there are so many other recipes that use chipotles in this book! But you know you best: If you know in your heart the peppers will never see the light of day again, divert your eyes to the swap below.

TIP
If your chili powder and/or smoked paprika are super spicy (and that’s not what you’re going for), use a little less of one or both.

SWAP
You can use ground turkey instead of ground chicken. • Swap out the chipotles for 1 teaspoon smoked paprika plus ½ teaspoon chili powder.

RIFF
Make sliders instead! Grab a 24-pack of King’s Hawaiian Original rolls. Scoop the meat into heaping ¼-cup balls and flatten them into patties. Bake them for 15 minutes.

EXTRA EXTRA
Make your own Caesar dressing (see page 36). Top the burgers with avocado slices or sliced pepper Jack cheese.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 114

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon (or more to taste) adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon (or more to taste) adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup crushed croutons, store-bought or homemade (see page 244)
ingredients.name: crushed croutons, store-bought or homemade (see page 244)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, combine the ground chicken, chiles, ½ cup of the Caesar dressing, the panko, cumin, paprika, chili powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Use your hands to mix well. Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions and plop them on the prepared baking sheet. Use your hands to form each portion into a patty (try to make them roughly the diameter of your burger buns). If the mixture is very sticky, rub your hands with a little oil. Bake the patties for about 15 minutes, until they reach 165°F internally. (Don’t worry if a bunch of liquid oozes out; that’s normal!)

Meanwhile, cut the lime in half and squeeze the juice from 1 half into a small bowl. Add the remaining 1 cup Caesar dressing, the chipotle, and the adobo. Use a fork to smash the chipotle against the side of the bowl to break it up, then stir to combine. Taste and adjust the flavor with more adobo and/or lime juice as needed.
Chop the romaine and place it in a large bowl. Toss with a couple big pinches of salt, about half the chipotle Caesar dressing, and the crushed croutons.

When the burgers are done, remove them from the oven and turn the broiler to high. Split the buns and place them cut side up on a clean baking sheet. Toast the buns under the broiler for 1 to 2 minutes, just until lightly golden. Turn on the oven light and watch them closely so they don’t burn!
Spread the remaining dressing on both cut sides of each bun. To the bottom halves, add a burger patty and a scoop of the salad, then close the buns and serve.

name: Corn and Basil Pasta Salad with Perfect Baked Chicken
note:
My friends Jenna, Jess, Charlotte, and I have kids the same ages and husbands who love each other as much as we do. We all have too many kids to throw proper dinner parties, so instead we trade off “hosting”—which really just means being the person with the dirtiest house at the end of the night because we all pitch in on the cooking and dig in potluck-style. One summer we got really addicted to corn salads—chipotle corn salad, corn and tomato salad, and others—but when I showed up with this corn and basil pasta salad, I knew I’d hit the jackpot: instant empty bowl.

TIP
This dish is extra delicious when the chicken and the corn are grilled. Throw them on medium-high and grill the chicken for 5 to 7 minutes per side and the corn for about 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred in spots.

SHORTCUT
Skip the ears of corn and just dump a bag of frozen corn into the pasta pot for the last minute of cooking to thaw it.

RIFF
Skip the chicken entirely, serve it on the side, or chop it up and stir it in.

EXTRA EXTRA
If you have some extra time, let the chicken and corn marinate in the sauce for up to 24 hours (stick them in the refrigerator if you’re marinating for longer than 30 minutes) before you bake them.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 117

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound small pasta noodles, such as cavatappi, rotini, or farfalle
ingredients.name: small pasta noodles, such as cavatappi, rotini, or farfalle

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup fresh basil leaves, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt or sour cream
ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt or sour cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 heaping tablespoon taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: heaping tablespoon taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more if needed

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Drain.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the scallions and the basil leaves.

Place the chipotle and adobo in a large bowl and use a fork or spoon to smash the chipotle against the sides of the bowl. Add the mayonnaise, yogurt, 2 tablespoons olive oil, the taco seasoning, and 1½ teaspoons salt and whisk to combine. Cut the limes in half and squeeze in the juice. Stir it all together, smashing up the chipotle even more. Taste and add more lime juice and/or salt if needed.

Place the chicken breasts and corn on the prepared baking sheet. Season the chicken lightly with salt. Brush or rub about one-quarter of the sauce all over the chicken and corn. Arrange them in an even layer on the pan. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F internally and the corn is crisp-tender. Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then thinly slice it crosswise. Cut the corn kernels off the cobs (see Learn, page 52). Thinly slice some more basil leaves for serving.

To the large bowl with the remaining sauce, add the drained pasta, corn, arugula, scallions, basil, and ¼ cup of the Parm. Use tongs or a spoon to toss until everything is combined and well coated. Taste and add more Parm, lime juice, and/or salt as needed.
Arrange the sliced chicken on top of the salad and sprinkle the basil and the remaining ¼ cup Parm over everything. Enjoy!

name: Pork Al Pastor Rice
note:
When I was in my twenties in New York City, I lived in a tiny fifth-floor walk-up in Alphabet City with four other girls. I was spending basically my entire salary on rent, so many of my meals came from a taco stand on the corner of Second Street and Avenue A. That’s where I fell in love with al pastor tacos, and ever since, I’ve been re-creating those flavors on a weeknight timeframe as often as I can. Traditional Mexican tacos al pastor involve spit-roasting pineapple-juice-marinated pork for hours and hours. Here, we’re borrowing those flavors and morphing the tacos into a one-pot meal with ground pork, canned pineapple, and pantry-staple spices to infuse rice with those sweet-and-savory flavors in just half an hour.

SWAP
If you’re cooking for someone who doesn’t eat dairy, just omit the cheddar. Cheese lovers can add it to their individual bowls.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 125

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1¼ cups low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): avocado or guacamole, pickled red onions, sour cream
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): avocado or guacamole, pickled red onions, sour cream

preparationSteps: Warm the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the ground pork, taco seasoning, and 1 teaspoon salt. Cook, breaking up the pork into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until it’s cooked through and no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Turn up the heat to high if it’s taking too long.

Add the pineapple, salsa verde, rice, and stock. Turn up the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, then turn down the heat to medium-low or low to maintain a simmer. Cover and cook until the rice is tender and all the liquid has been absorbed, about 20 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Uncover and stir in the cheese until it has melted, then taste and season with salt, if needed. Serve immediately, with toppings, if you like.

name: Soy Butter Rib Eyes with Miso-Creamed Spinach and Mushrooms
note:
My book editor, Amanda; literary agent, Sarah; and I have made it a tradition that any time we have something to celebrate or discuss when I’m in New York, we meet up at one of the city’s famed steakhouses. We celebrated the pub day for the first What to Cook book at Keens, and it was the most fun, special night. Steak is great, but everyone knows the sides are the best part of that kind of meal. Here I’ve combined two favorites—creamed spinach and sautéed mushrooms—into one dish and given them a savory twist by adding miso. Pour yourself a big fat glass of red wine and make it a 30-minute steakhouse dinner at home.

LEARN
Miso flavor and sodium level vary widely from brand to brand. Start small, taste, and add more if you want a more salty, umami flavor. • If you try to flip the steak and it’s stuck to the skillet, that means it hasn’t formed a sear (crust) yet. Give it 30 seconds more and try again! • For medium-rare, cook until 125°F (if you like it on the rarer side) or 130°F (if you like it a little less red). For medium, cook it between 135° and 140°F.

SWAP
Try cooking pork chops the exact same way, in place of the steak. Cook until 140°F internally and then let them rest until they come up to 145°F. • Use sour cream in place of the crème fraîche.

BULK IT UP
Go even steakhouseier and serve it with roasted baby gold potatoes! Halve 1 pound of potatoes, then toss them on a baking sheet with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and some pepper. Spread ’em out and roast at 425°F for 30 minutes. • Or just cook up some frozen hashbrowns in a skillet until crispy!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 126

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon white or yellow miso paste
ingredients.name: white or yellow miso paste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon low-sodium soy sauce
ingredients.name: plus 1 teaspoon low-sodium soy sauce

preparationSteps: Pat the rib eyes dry with a paper towel or clean kitchen towel, then season them generously with salt and pepper.
Smash and peel 2 of the garlic cloves. Thinly slice the remaining 4 garlic cloves and mince the shallot. Wash and thinly slice the mushrooms.

Place 2 tablespoons of the oil and the sliced mushrooms in a large saucepan. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring every 2 minutes, until the mushrooms are browned, about 6 minutes total. Add 2 tablespoons of the butter, the shallot, and the sliced garlic and cook until the butter has melted, 1 minute more. Add the spinach in batches and cook, stirring, until the leaves have wilted and all the moisture has evaporated, 3 to 5 minutes. (You can crank the heat to high to make this go faster!)

Turn down the heat to medium and stir in the crème fraîche, miso, and 1 teaspoon of the soy sauce. Cook, stirring, until the sauce coats the spinach and mushrooms, 3 to 4 minutes. Cover and turn off the heat.

Meanwhile, warm your largest cast-iron or stainless-steel (not nonstick!) skillet over medium-high heat until a drop of water flicked into the pan dances on the surface. Rub the rib eyes all over with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, then place them in the skillet and press down on them firmly with a spatula. Cook until a golden brown crust forms on the bottoms and the steaks lift easily from the pan, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip the steaks and cook for 1 minute, then add the remaining 2 tablespoons butter, the 2 smashed garlic cloves, and the remaining 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Tilt the skillet and use a spoon to scoop up the melted butter and pour it over the steaks; do this repeatedly for about 10 seconds. Cook until a crust forms on the second side, 2 to 3 minutes, then use tongs to pick up the steaks and hold the fatty sides against the pan to sear, about 30 seconds per side. Continue flipping the steaks every 30 seconds or so until they reach your desired doneness on a meat thermometer (see Learn). Transfer the steaks to a cutting board to rest for 10 minutes.

Divide the creamed mushrooms and spinach among four plates. Cut the steaks against the grain into ¼-inch-thick slices and place them over the mushrooms and spinach. Pour the soy butter and garlic from the pan on top of the steak and serve.

name: Steak and Potato Bites with Chipotle Almond Sauce and Arugula Salad
note:
Once you’re hooked on this chipotle almond sauce, you’ll want to make it again and again to drizzle on grain bowls and roasted veggies and to use as a dipping sauce for quesadillas, french fries, and more. It’s my take on Chipotle Bitchin’ Sauce, a brand that originated at the San Diego farmers’ markets I frequented when I had a catering business down there. They used to lure me (and everyone else!) into their stall by yelling, “COME ON, TRY OUR SAUCE, IT’S BITCHIN’!!!” Irresistible!—especially when served with these easy weeknight steak and potato bites.

TIP
For a less spicy sauce, remove the seeds from the chipotle before adding it to the blender. Those seeds are where the heat lives.

LEARN
The steak will keep cooking out of the oven, so it’s good to pull it while it still looks a little more rare than you like it.

SHORTCUT
To skip the 15-minute soak, use 1 cup almond or cashew butter instead of whole nuts.

SWAP
Any quick-cooking cut of steak will work here, like New York strip, tri-tip, or even boneless lamb leg (which isn’t steak, but is still very good). Or use boneless, skinless chicken thighs, roasted and sliced.

RIFF
For a pourable version of the sauce, blend in up to ¼ cup more hot water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until it reaches a consistency you like.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 130

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup (4 ounces) blanched almonds or roasted unsalted cashews
ingredients.name: blanched almonds or roasted unsalted cashews

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 chipotle peppers (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 2 teaspoons adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle peppers (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 2 teaspoons adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar or rice vinegar
ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar or rice vinegar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 ounces baby potatoes (red, gold, or tricolor)
ingredients.name: baby potatoes (red, gold, or tricolor)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound sirloin or flat iron steak, about 1 inch thick
ingredients.name: sirloin or flat iron steak, about 1 inch thick

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (1 ounce), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (1 ounce), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the almonds in a high-powered blender, cover with very hot tap water, and set aside to soften for 10 to 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the steak and potatoes. Halve the baby potatoes (or quarter them if large) and toss them on the prepared baking sheet with 1 tablespoon olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Arrange them cut side down and roast for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the steak into roughly 1-inch cubes and pat them dry.

After the potatoes have roasted for 20 minutes, push them to one side of the pan and add the steak to the empty space on the baking sheet. Drizzle the steak with 1 tablespoon olive oil, sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper, and grate the zest of the lemon on top (reserve the zested lemon). Carefully toss to coat (the pan is hot!), then arrange the steak in a single layer, spacing apart the pieces. Return the baking sheet to the oven and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with the tip of a sharp knife and the steak is just cooked through and lightly browned.

Make the sauce. Drain the water out of the blender. Halve the lemon and squeeze the juice into the blender. Add the neutral oil, nutritional yeast, chipotles and adobo, soy sauce, vinegar, onion powder, garlic powder, cumin, 1 teaspoon salt, and ½ cup hot tap water. Blend on high speed until smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed, about 1 minute. Taste and add more salt and/or lemon juice if desired. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

Make the salad. Place the arugula in a serving bowl. Cut the reserved zested lemon in half and squeeze in the juice of 1 half. Add the Parm, olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a little bit of pepper. Toss, then taste and add more of whatever you like.
Serve the steak and potato bites with the arugula salad and the chipotle almond sauce alongside for drizzling and dipping.

name: Lamb Chops with Potatoes, Fennel, and Orange-Shallot Vin
note:
In my house growing up, lamb chops were reserved for only the most special occasions (like Easter, when I’d come to the table decked out in a scratchy smocked dress and Mary Janes), and they always, always came with a side of bright green mint jelly. These days, I don’t reserve lamb for holidays—this meal’s as suitable for a Monday after work as it is for Easter supper. And as an adult, I’ve strayed from mint jelly and instead typically serve lamb coated in this sweet orange-shallot vin, which balances out the gaminess of the meat—and dresses up the veg!—beautifully.

SWAP
Try pork tenderloin medallions or boneless, skinless chicken thighs, adjusting the broiling time accordingly: 6 to 8 minutes for 1-inch-thick pork medallions and 12 to 14 minutes for chicken thighs.

RIFF
For extra crunch and protein, add a handful of roasted salted almonds or pistachios just before serving.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 133

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound baby potatoes (red, gold, or tricolor)
ingredients.name: baby potatoes (red, gold, or tricolor)

preparationSteps: Position a rack in the top third of the oven and another in the bottom third and preheat to 450°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the lamb chops in a shallow dish. Season them lightly all over with a few pinches of salt and some pepper.

Halve the potatoes (or quarter them, if large) and place them on the prepared baking sheet. Trim the fennel bulbs (reserve the fronds), slice them through the core into ⅛-inch-thick wedges, and add them to the pan with the potatoes.

Mince the shallot and finely chop the mint leaves and place them in a liquid measuring cup. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of the orange into the measuring cup, then halve the orange and squeeze in the juice. Add the vinegar, honey, mustard, olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Whisk to combine the vinaigrette.

Pour about a third of the vinaigrette over the lamb chops and turn them to coat. Pour about half the remaining vinaigrette over the potatoes and fennel and toss to coat. Reserve the remaining vinaigrette for serving.

Roast the potatoes and fennel in the bottom third of the oven until the potatoes are golden and the fennel is tender with crispy edges, about 20 minutes, flipping once halfway through. Remove the pan from the oven and turn on the broiler. Scooch the potatoes and fennel to the sides of the pan. Remove the lamb chops from the vinaigrette, allowing any excess to drip off, and place them in the empty space on the baking sheet. Broil on the top rack of the oven for 8 to 10 minutes, until the lamb is browned on the outside but still pink in the center and reaches 130°F internally for medium-rare or 140°F for medium, flipping them halfway through. Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes.
Transfer the lamb chops, potatoes, and fennel to a serving platter and drizzle the reserved vinaigrette over everything. Garnish with the reserved fennel fronds and serve warm.

name: Boney’s Coronado Pork Chops
note:
While George was in the SEAL teams, we lived in Coronado, California, in a 400-square-foot guesthouse that didn’t have a full oven—just a stovetop burner and a countertop oven that I could barely shove a full chicken into. We had a postage-stamp-size backyard, but we loved it and spent all our time out there, basking in the 75-degree-and-sunny weather nearly 365 days a year. We cooked almost every single meal on the grill, no exaggeration. One of our favorite quickie dinners was grabbing some marinated black pepper steaks from Boney’s, the local market, and throwing them on the grill with whatever vegetables I had left over from that week’s catering gigs. This is still one of our favorite ways to eat: grilled meat + grilled veg + tons of toppings thrown on the veg to make them feel fancy. This marinade is my version, and I’ve come to love it on big ol’ bone-in pork chops. No matter the protein—try it with chicken, shrimp, mushrooms, or steaks as Boney’s originally intended—it’s completely addictive.

TIP
If grilling isn’t an option, position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and preheat to 425°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Arrange the pork chops on one and the vegetables on the other. Roast the pork on the upper rack for 18 to 22 minutes, flipping halfway through cooking; roast the vegetables on the lower rack for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender and browned. For more color, switch the oven to broil on high for a minute or two at the end.

SHORTCUT
Well, I already did the shortcut for you—we marinate the pork chops in a skillet to save a dirty dish! I know, why aren’t we all doing this more often?

SWAP
Use any vegetables—just grill until they have grill marks and are tender. And use any cheese, nuts, and herbs! I really like goat cheese + roasted salted cashews + mint or crumbled Parm + toasted pine nuts + basil.

BULK IT UP
Serve with herby couscous (see Bulk It Up, page 202), buttery rice, or quinoa. A salad would also be great here.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 135

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup packed light brown sugar
ingredients.name: packed light brown sugar

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound sweet red, orange, and/or yellow mini peppers
ingredients.name: sweet red, orange, and/or yellow mini peppers

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of soft green herbs, such as fresh mint, cilantro, parsley, and/or basil
ingredients.name: Handful of soft green herbs, such as fresh mint, cilantro, parsley, and/or basil

preparationSteps: Heat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400° to 450°F).

In a large skillet or saucepan, stir together the soy sauce, brown sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire, 2 tablespoons of the neutral oil, the garlic powder, and some black pepper. Pierce the pork chops all over with a fork and add them to the skillet. Set aside at room temperature to marinate while you prepare the vegetables, flipping them every few minutes.
Place the mushroom caps and mini bell peppers on a rimmed baking sheet and toss with the remaining 2 tablespoons neutral oil and 1 teaspoon salt.

Remove the pork chops from the marinade, allowing the excess to drip off into the skillet (reserve the marinade). Place the vegetables and pork chops on the grill and close the lid. Cook until the vegetables are charred all over, 4 to 5 minutes per side, and the pork reaches 145°F internally, about 8 minutes per side. Transfer the pork chops and vegetables to the same baking sheet and let the pork chops rest for at least 5 minutes or until ready to serve.
Meanwhile, set the skillet of marinade over high heat and bring to a boil, then turn down the heat to medium and simmer, stirring often, until reduced by half, 4 to 5 minutes.

Chop the herbs and the almonds. Slice the mushroom caps about ¼ inch thick and toss them with the peppers on a serving platter. Brush the reduced marinade over the vegetables and pork chops. Crumble the feta over the vegetables, then sprinkle with the almonds and herbs. Keep the pork chops whole, or slice them if you’re feeding more people than you have chops, and transfer them to a separate platter before serving.

name: Crispy Pork Chili Verde Street Tacos with Dipping Sauces
note:
I love Middle Eastern arayes (see page 56), where spiced raw ground meat is stuffed into pitas, then pan-fried until the pita is crispy and the meat is cooked through. The cooking method kills two birds with one stone (compared to, say, a chicken quesadilla, where you’d typically cook the filling before you stuff and cook the tortilla) and simply tastes amazing. One night when tacos were calling my name, it dawned on me: Why can’t I use that same concept with a tortilla to make crispy little tacos without having to cook the meat first? Turns out, I can. I stuffed the tortillas with one of my go-to taco fillings, green chile pork, cooked it all at once, and bam—my new favorite Taco Tuesday offering was born. Now what else can I apply this method to? (P.S. I’m a firm believer that you can never have too many sauces, which is why I like two here!)

TIP
These smaller tortillas may say “street tacos” on the package.

SWAP
Flour tortillas work best here because they’re soft. If you must use corn tortillas, wrap them in damp paper towels and microwave in 20-second increments until they’re pliable. (Even if they break, they’ll still taste good!) • If you can’t find this small size, use 6-inch ones and make fewer. • Any ground meat will work, but if you’re using beef, the less fatty the better—93/7 is ideal. They’ll still be kinda greasy, but in a good way.

BULK IT UP
I am a big advocate of taco night being all about the tacos. But if you want sides, serve with rice and Smoky Black Beans (page 74). • For the dressing, simply stir some salsa verde into the cream cheese + lime juice sauce here, adding more lime juice if necessary to thin it out.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 136

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: taco seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces shredded cheddar, pepper Jack, or Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup)
ingredients.name: shredded cheddar, pepper Jack, or Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¾ cup cream cheese, mayo, plain yogurt, sour cream, or Mexican crema
ingredients.name: cream cheese, mayo, plain yogurt, sour cream, or Mexican crema

preparationSteps: Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and preheat to 425°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, chiles (drain them if they seem watery, but if there is just a small amount of thick liquid, pour it in), taco seasoning, 1 teaspoon salt, and the shredded cheese. Use your hands to mix well.

Scoop a big spoonful of the meat mixture (yes, the raw meat mixture, trust the process!) onto half of a tortilla. Fold it closed and give it a little press so it stays that way, then place it on the prepared baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining tortillas and meat mixture, dividing it evenly and spacing them apart on the pans. Spritz the assembled tacos with cooking spray.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the tacos are golden brown and crispy on the outside and the meat reaches 160°F internally.

Meanwhile, halve the lime. Place the cream cheese in a small bowl, add a pinch of salt, and squeeze in the juice of 1 lime half. Taste and add more salt and/or lime if needed (it’s probably needed). Halve the avocado and scoop the flesh into a separate small bowl. Mash the avocado until it’s as smooth as possible, then season with a pinch of salt and stir in the salsa verde. Taste and add more salt as needed.
Serve the crispy tacos straight from the baking sheets with the dipping sauces for passing around.

name: Tortellini and Sausage Soup
note:
This soup is the ultimate cozy people-pleaser. Sausage for the meat lovers, a variety of nutrient-rich veg, and tortellini—because who could say no to plump little pasta rings stuffed with cheese?! It has kind of an Italian-wedding-soup vibe, with clear broth, veggies, Italian sausage, and pasta, and is extremely filling and nourishing without feeling too heavy—which we can’t always say about a big bowl of tortellini!

SHORTCUT
You can buy deli containers of Parm rinds in the cheese section of many grocery stores.

RIFF
For a creamy soup, stir in ½ cup heavy cream before serving. • If you’re feeding soup haters (I’m looking at you, my beloved children), simply deconstruct it! Fish out a few tortellini, veggies, and sausage chunks and plate them without the broth.

BULK IT UP
Add a drained (15-ounce) can of white beans or chickpeas and a couple handfuls of spinach or baby kale in the last few minutes of cooking.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 139

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound mild or hot Italian sausage, casings removed
ingredients.name: mild or hot Italian sausage, casings removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8- to 12-ounce) package fresh or frozen cheese tortellini
ingredients.name: fresh or frozen cheese tortellini

ingredients.rawIngredient: Fresh basil or parsley, for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: Fresh basil or parsley, for serving (optional)

preparationSteps: Dice the onion, zucchini, and bell pepper. Mince the garlic. Grate (or grind—see Shortcut, page 78) 2 cups Parm and reserve it and the rind separately.

Warm 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the sausage and cook, breaking it up into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until browned, about 8 minutes.

Add the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil to the pot. Add the onion, garlic, and a pinch of salt and cook until softened, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the zucchini and bell pepper and cook, stirring, until slightly softened, 3 to 5 minutes.

Add the tomato paste and red pepper flakes (if using) and cook, stirring frequently, until the paste darkens in color and begins sticking to the pot, about 1 minute. Add the soy sauce, Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Pour in the stock and drop in the reserved Parm rind. Turn up the heat to high and bring to a boil, then turn down the heat to low and simmer until the vegetables are tender when pierced with the tip of a sharp knife, about 10 minutes.
Turn up the heat to high and add the tortellini and about half the grated Parm to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tortellini is cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the basil, if using.
Use tongs to fish out the Parm rind and discard. Ladle into bowls. Top with the remaining grated Parm and the basil.

name: Warm Farro and Pasta Salad with Andouille, Pickled Peppers, and Feta
note:
I’m addicted to this beautiful mess of a meal. It’s a fun explosion of all kinds of contrasts and textures, and it’s just as delicious warm as it is at room temp as it is cold. There’s a lot going on flavor-wise and texture-wise, too, with both nutty, chewy farro and al dente pasta (and I love when the farro gets stuck in the folds of the cooked pasta!). The feta shape-shifts: When warm, it softens, adding a creamy element to the dish; when cold, it regains its structure and serves as a nice cool counterpoint to the heat of the peppers. Speaking of, you get to pick your pickled pepper path, too. If you use pickled hot peppers (like I do), I’d recommend adding that optional tablespoon of honey to counter their heat. Or you could go with sweet-and-hot pickled peppers (like Peppadews, sweet pickled banana peppers, or “sweet ’n’ hot salad peppers”) and skip the honey—or add a quarter, half, or the whole tablespoon of it if you like things sweet. This is your adventure, not mine!

SWAP
You can use another grain, such as pearled barley, wheat berries, or quinoa, in place of the farro. Simply adjust the overall cooking time to whatever the grain needs and add the pasta during the last 11 to 13 minutes of cooking. • You can also swap in any pasta shape!

BULK IT UP
Toss in a handful of toasted walnuts or sunflower seeds for extra crunch. • Stir in a couple handfuls of arugula or baby kale or spinach when you add the feta and herbs.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 140

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces small pasta noodles, such as orecchiette, farfalle, or rotini
ingredients.name: small pasta noodles, such as orecchiette, farfalle, or rotini

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup drained jarred pickled hot peppers, plus ¼ cup brine (or more to taste) from the jar
ingredients.name: drained jarred pickled hot peppers, plus ¼ cup brine (or more to taste) from the jar

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the farro and cook for 10 minutes. Add the pasta and cook until the farro is tender but still chewy and the pasta is al dente according to the package directions. Drain the farro and pasta and return them to the hot pot. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil and toss to coat to keep everything fluffy and separated.
Meanwhile, halve the andouille lengthwise, then slice it crosswise into ¼-inch-thick half circles. Dice the onion and roughly chop the peppers. Chop the parsley and basil.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the andouille and onion, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the andouille is browned and crisp around the edges, 10 to 12 minutes. Scrape the andouille and onion into the pot with the farro and pasta.

Return the skillet to medium heat. Pour in the pickled pepper brine and use a wooden spoon to scrape up all the stuck-on bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in the honey (if using), mustard, oregano, garlic powder, ½ teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Add the chopped peppers and stir to coat.

Transfer the pepper mixture to the warm farro and pasta. Crumble over the feta and add the parsley and basil. Toss until everything is well coated in everything else. Taste and adjust, adding more oil if the flavor is too sharp or more brine if you like it sharper.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Or cold!

name: Pesto Crunch Baked Salmon with Roasted Sweet Potatoes and Crispy Kale
note:
Store-bought pesto is one of my greatest pantry heroes. In one simple scoop, you’re getting fresh herbs, roasted nuts, garlic, olive oil, salt, and Parm, with absolutely no mincing, chopping, or roasting on your part. And these days, you can easily find delicious vegan, dairy-free, and/or nut-free pesto at the store, meaning everyone can get in on the action. If you have a green thumb and a few extra minutes to use your own herb bounty for a fresh version, be my guest! Either way, you’re about to meet your new favorite sheet pan fish-and-potatoes dinner, in which we combine pesto and panko to make a quickie topping for salmon before it swims through the oven. And let’s not forget your new favorite kale side dish, essentially green chips coated with crisp Parm. Doubly delightful.

TIP
For an even crunchier topping, put the pan under the broiler for 1 to 2 minutes at the end.

SWAP
Crushed crackers or finely chopped nuts (like almonds or pistachios) work beautifully in place of the panko.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 143

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 tablespoons freshly grated Parmesan cheese (1⅓ ounces)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (1⅓ ounces)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Dice the sweet potatoes and place them in a large bowl. Add the paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 tablespoon olive oil. Toss to coat. Spread the potatoes in an even layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, stem the kale leaves and slice them crosswise into thick ribbons. Place them in the same bowl you used for the sweet potato and add 1 tablespoon olive oil, 3 tablespoons of the Parm, and ¼ teaspoon salt. Massage the oil and seasonings into the kale.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven and push the sweet potatoes to one side. Scatter the kale on the other side of the pan and return to the oven for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, stir together the pesto, panko, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and the remaining 2 tablespoons Parm until well combined.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven and push the kale to the side opposite the potatoes. Add the salmon (skin side down, if it has skin) and season it with 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper. Spread the pesto-panko mixture evenly over the salmon, pressing to adhere. Return the baking sheet to the oven and bake for about 15 minutes more, until the sweet potatoes are soft when pierced with the tip of a sharp knife, the kale is crispy, and the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Meanwhile, cut the lemon into 8 wedges.
Divide the kale, sweet potatoes, and salmon among plates. Serve with the lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Twenty-First-Century Tuna Noodle Casserole
note:
Growing up, one of my mom’s (and every other mom’s in the Southeast/maybe everywhere) specialties was tuna noodle casserole. You know: noodles, canned tuna, canned cream of mushroom soup, bagged shredded cheese. It is delicious, and you should absolutely make it—but you’re going to have to google it, because this is not a recipe for that. Here I’ve remixed the classic a bit, bringing brighter flavors and fresher ingredients into the mix—and less processed stuff, too (no offense to cream of mushroom).

TIP
Oil-packed tuna gives the best flavor and texture here—if you’re using water-packed tuna, increase the olive oil to 3 tablespoons.

SHORTCUT
Skip the oven and the panko topping. Cook the pasta until al dente. After adding the tuna, simmer the mixture to meld the flavors, about 2 minutes, then add the noodles, etc., and cook until heated through, 1 to 2 minutes more. Ready to serve!

RIFF
Add capers or chopped artichoke hearts for extra zingy flavor.

SWAP
Any small pasta noodles, such as farfalle, cavatappi, rotini, or orecchiette, will work here.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 144

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup pitted green or Castelvetrano olives
ingredients.name: pitted green or Castelvetrano olives

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley, dill, chives, and/or scallions
ingredients.name: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley, dill, chives, and/or scallions

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for topping
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for topping

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the noodles and cook until just shy of al dente (about 1 minute under) according to the package directions. Scoop out about ½ cup of the noodle cooking water, then drain the noodles.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Dice the roasted pepper. Roughly chop the olives. Chop enough herbs to make ½ cup.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring frequently, until soft and golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Stir in the sour cream, stock, and ½ teaspoon salt. Using a Microplane, grate in the zest from the lemon. Stir in the roasted pepper, olives, and tuna. Turn up the heat to medium-high to bring to a simmer, then turn down the heat to medium-low and let it bubble gently for a minute.

Halve the zested lemon and squeeze in the juice, then stir in the cooked noodles, Parm, herbs, and some black pepper. The mixture should be creamy but not soupy; add a splash of the reserved noodle cooking water if it seems dry.
Top with the panko and a couple spoonfuls of Parm. Spritz the top with cooking spray. Bake for about 15 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Dilly Feta Salad with Feta-Brined Grilled Shrimp
note:
It’s not scientific data, but from what I can tell through Instagram (pics I’m tagged in and DMs people have sent me), the Dilly Chop is one of the most-beloved recipes from the first What to Cook book. It was originally inspired by a salad that I order nonstop from my friends Anthony and Alissa Carnazzo’s utterly charming restaurant, Stationæry, in Carmel-by-the-Sea (it’s the Farmer’s Salad, if you’re local!). This salad evolved over time from the Dilly Chop—you can think of it as its posh cousin who lives in a Grecian villa overlooking the Mediterranean.

TIP
If you can only find those small plastic clamshells of dill, buy THREE! We are looking for a big bushy bunch of dill here. • If you don’t have a grill, spread out the shrimp on a foil-lined baking sheet and broil them in the top third of the oven until they’re just opaque, 2 to 3 minutes per side, flipping them once. Broil the bread on a separate baking sheet for a minute or two per side until golden and crisp.

SWAP
Feta-brined chicken is excellent, too—note that it will need to marinate longer, at least 30 minutes at room temperature or up to 6 hours in the fridge. Grill boneless, skinless breasts for about 4 minutes per side or thighs for about 6 minutes per side. Most important, use a meat thermometer to make sure the chicken has reached 165°F internally. • If you can’t find feta in brine, swap out the brine for ¼ cup water, 2 tablespoons of any light vinegar or lemon juice, and a big pinch of salt. • If you can’t find dill, parsley will be great here! In fact, 2 cups of any mixed soft green herbs (fresh mint, dill, parsley, basil) will be great. Yum.

RIFF
Make it a Dilly Feta Shrimp PASTA Salad! Omit the iceberg and cook 8 ounces of any cute little noodle instead. Add a pint of halved cherry tomatoes, 1 (14-ounce) can of drained and chopped artichoke hearts, and a chopped red bell pepper. Toss everything together and let stand for at least 1 hour or up to 3 hours before serving so the dressing soaks into the noodles.

BULK IT UP
Add a grain! A cup and a half of cooked farro, brown rice, or quinoa would be excellent tossed in here.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 146

ingredients.rawIngredient: Big pinch of red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: Big pinch of red pepper flakes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds peeled and deveined jumbo (16/20) shrimp (tails on or off)
ingredients.name: peeled and deveined jumbo shrimp (tails on or off)

preparationSteps: Heat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400° to 450°F).

Pour the feta brine into a large bowl or zip-top bag. Using a Microplane, grate 4 of the garlic cloves directly into the brine. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil, the oregano, and the red pepper flakes. Mix well, then add the shrimp and turn to coat. Let stand for at least 10 minutes. (You can do this up to 4 hours before cooking—just pop the shrimp in the fridge and wait to heat the grill.)

Using a Microplane, grate the remaining 2 garlic cloves and the zest of the lemon directly into a lidded jar, then halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Add the vinegar, ⅓ cup olive oil, and 1½ teaspoons salt. Close the lid and shake vigorously until combined, about 30 seconds. Taste and adjust the seasoning as desired.

Thinly slice the iceberg and scallions, and finely chop the dill (including the stems, minus the very tough bottom; you should have about 2 cups). Place it all in a large serving bowl. Use your hands to break the feta into both tiny crumbles and several large hunks and scatter them over the top.
Drizzle the sourdough on both sides with olive oil. Drain the shrimp, add a little bit of olive oil to them in the bowl or bag, and toss to coat.

Add the bread and shrimp to the grill and cook (with the lid open, because both cook quickly!), until the shrimp are pink, opaque, firm, and curled into a C shape and dark grill marks appear on the bread, 2 to 3 minutes per side for both. Watch them closely—don’t let the bread catch on fire!
