Chop or tear the grilled bread into very small croutons and add them to the salad. Add half the dressing and toss the salad. Add more dressing as desired (I use all of it!). Taste and add salt and black pepper. Divide among plates and top with the grilled shrimp. Enjoy!

name: Fish and Veggie Curry
note:
One of my favorite things about being a recipe developer is how one dish inspires another, which inspires another, which inspires another. Recipe development is a vibrant exchange of creativity and perspectives. In my previous book, I shared a recipe for braised fish, which was initially inspired by an insanely delicious curried vegetable soup by Yotam Ottolenghi (an Israeli-born British chef and restaurateur whose cookbooks I adore). This meal is a riff on that riff! I switched around the veg, added a grain, changed up the flavor profile, and bam—you have a brand-new, absolutely delightful fish-and-veg dinner.

SWAP
Use halibut or salmon in place of cod. • Shrimp also works beautifully here—just add it in the last 4 to 6 minutes instead of 15.

RIFF
Want to make it vegetarian? Two options: (1) Use tofu instead of fish and vegetable stock instead of chicken stock. (2) Make an egg curry! SO GOOD. Crack eggs into the curry broth, cover, and cook over medium-low heat until the whites are cooked through but the yolks are still runny, 4 to 5 minutes.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 150

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce or fish sauce
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce or fish sauce

preparationSteps: Core the cauliflower and cut it into florets. Thinly slice the carrot. Chop the onion. Stem the kale leaves and thinly slice them lengthwise. Finely chop the cilantro. Cut 1 lime in half and the other into 8 wedges.

Warm the oil in a large Dutch oven or other large pot with a lid over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the cauliflower, carrot, onion, and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are beginning to soften, 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in the rice and curry paste and cook, stirring, until well coated and fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, coconut milk, and soy sauce. Squeeze in the juice of 1 lime half and stir in the sliced kale. Turn up the heat to high and bring to a simmer.

Pat the cod fillets completely dry and season all over with 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper. Arrange the cod in a single layer in the pot, gently nestling the fillets into the veggies and just under the surface of the simmering liquid. Sprinkle half the cilantro on top. Cover the pot and cook until the rice is tender and the cod is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, about 15 minutes.

Before serving, taste and add the juice from the other lime half, if you like (I usually do). Ladle the curried vegetables into shallow bowls, being sure each serving gets lots of broth and a piece of cod. Finish with the remaining cilantro and place 1 or 2 lime wedges on each serving.

name: Lemon-Butter Black Cod with Lemony Couscous and Arugula Salad
note:
This gorgeous fish, grain, and greens dinner is for my fellow lemon lovers—the citrus is the tangy, fresh star of the show. Lemon and fish are friends for a good reason: The acidity in the citrus makes fish taste less fishy! Eat it on a Tuesday night with the latest episodes of Bridgerton, or serve it at a garden luncheon—it’s right at home dressed up or down.

LEARN
Dredging the fish (or any protein) in flour before cooking it creates a delicate crust that helps it soak up the lemony sauce.

SWAP
For a dairy-free version, replace the butter with more olive oil. • Use cod, sole, flounder, or halibut instead of black cod. Salmon also works beautifully here. • Use pearl couscous, quinoa, or farro instead of couscous; note that these require more cooking time, so check the package directions.

RIFF
For a spicy kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes along with the garlic. For some extra brightness in the salad, add diced cucumbers or halved cherry tomatoes, and for creaminess, toss in some crumbled feta.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 152

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1¾ cups low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup drained capers or chopped green olives
ingredients.name: drained capers or chopped green olives

preparationSteps: Warm 1¼ cups of the stock in a small saucepan over medium heat or in the microwave in 30-second intervals until heated.

Slice 1 lemon into thin rounds and another lemon into 8 wedges (don’t worry about the other 2 lemons yet). Chop the garlic. Finely chop the parsley leaves and tender stems and the basil leaves; keep them separate. Chop the almonds.

Combine the couscous and ½ teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Pour over the warm stock and stir to combine. Cover the bowl with a plate or plastic wrap and let stand for 5 minutes, until the liquid has been completely absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.

Meanwhile, grate the zest of 1 of the remaining lemons directly into a lidded jar, then halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Add 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the mustard, ½ teaspoon of the honey, ½ teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Close the jar and shake vigorously until combined, about 30 seconds.
Pour the dressing over the couscous and toss to coat. Stir in the almonds, capers, half the parsley, all the basil, and the arugula. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Pour the flour onto a plate. Pat the black cod fillets completely dry and season all over with 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper. Lightly dredge the fillets in the flour, pressing to adhere and shaking off any excess.

Warm the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the fish and cook until the bottom is golden and the fish is mostly opaque, 4 to 6 minutes. Flip gently and cook on the second side just until the fish flakes easily, 2 to 3 minutes more. Transfer the fish to a plate.

Turn down the heat under the skillet to medium (no need to wipe it out) and add the butter. When the butter has melted, add the garlic and cook just until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Grate the zest of the remaining lemon into the skillet, then halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Add the remaining ½ cup stock and 1 tablespoon honey and stir, scraping the bottom of the pan to loosen any stuck-on bits. Add the lemon slices. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then return the fish to the skillet and spoon the sauce over the fillets. Cook for 1 minute more to warm everything through.

Divide the couscous among shallow bowls. Use a spatula to place a fish fillet on top of each serving and spoon over the sauce, including the lemon slices. Garnish with the remaining parsley and pass the lemon wedges at the table for anyone who likes it very, very lemony.

name: Sheet Pan Halibut with Gremolata, Blistered Grape Tomatoes, and Crispy Fingerling Potatoes
note:
By the time you finish cooking this gorgeous meal, you’ll have just one bowl to wash (and maybe a baking sheet, though the parchment should keep that totally clean!). Minimizing dirty dishes is a founding bylaw of What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking because when a day gets away from me, just the thought of cleaning up a torn-apart kitchen is enough to deter me from cooking a homemade meal (and I bet it is for you, too!). That one bowl will get your potatoes and tomatoes ready for their time in the oven, and make a vibrant herby gremolata, all of which will make this halibut absolutely sing.

SWAP
Instead of the fingerlings, you can use baby Yukon Golds or even sweet potatoes cut into similar-size pieces. • Use black cod, flounder, cod, or salmon in place of the halibut.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 155

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds halibut steaks or fillets (1 to 1½ inches thick)
ingredients.name: halibut steaks or fillets (1 to 1½ inches thick)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Halve the potatoes lengthwise into 1-inch-thick slices. Place them in a large bowl and toss with the garlic powder, onion powder, ½ teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Pour over a glug or two of olive oil and toss to coat again. Spread the potatoes on the prepared baking sheet (don’t wipe out the bowl!) and roast for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley leaves and tender stems so you have about 2 cups and place them in the same bowl. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of 1 lemon directly into the bowl, then halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice of 1 half. Mince the garlic and add it, too, along with ¼ cup olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Stir together to make the gremolata.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven (leave the oven on!). Toss and flip the potatoes and scooch them to one side of the baking sheet. Pat the halibut steaks dry and arrange them in the center of the pan, leaving some space on one side. Spoon the gremolata over the fish, coating the tops evenly.
Add the grape tomatoes to the same bowl and toss to coat them in any remnants of the gremolata. Scatter the tomatoes in the open spot on the baking sheet.

Return the pan to the oven and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the potatoes are golden and crisp, the halibut is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, and the tomatoes are blistered. Squeeze the juice of the remaining lemon half on top of the fish (and use another lemon if you like things extra lemony).
Transfer the halibut, roasted potatoes, and blistered tomatoes to a platter and serve.

name: Grilled Chipotle Shrimp Tacos with Crispy Cheese Tortillas
note:
Some meals you want to totally cook ahead of time, then sit down and eat in peace. Other times, cooking is part of the hang. This recipe is the latter: a kind of stand-up, hang-out, eat-a-few-tacos, make-a-few-more-tortillas, assemble-a-few-more-tacos situation. I love cooking this dinner for a casual night with friends—I’ll set out chips, guac, and salsa, make a big batch of margaritas, and have the shrimp marinated and pico slaw, and chipotle crema made ahead of time. When you’re ready to eat, just grill the shrimp and make the cheesy tortillas to order. If this sounds delicious but isn’t your vibe, see the Shortcut for how to cook all the cheesy tortillas at once in the oven.

TIP
If you don’t have a grill, you can broil the shrimp on a foil-lined baking sheet in the top third of the oven until they’re just opaque, 2 to 3 minutes per side, flipping them once.

SHORTCUT
Grab chipotle mayo or sriracha mayo from the store instead of making the crema. • To speed up the tortilla process, preheat the oven to 400°F, lay the tortillas on a baking sheet, sprinkle with cheese, and bake for about 5 minutes, until the cheese has melted. The cheese doesn’t get crispy this way, but it’s hands-off, fast, and still delish!

EXTRA EXTRA
To make your own pico de gallo, dice 1 pound tomatoes (any kind), 1 small white onion, and 1 seeded jalapeño, then toss them in a bowl with ½ bunch chopped cilantro, the juice of 1 lime half, and salt to taste. This will make about twice what you need for these tacos, and the rest will keep in an airtight container in the fridge for several days so you can put a big spoonful on cottage cheese, eggs, or grilled fish or steak, or just eat it with tortilla chips!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 156

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 chipotle peppers (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus all the adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle peppers (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus all the adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound peeled and deveined extra-large (21/30) shrimp (tails off)
ingredients.name: peeled and deveined extra-large shrimp (tails off)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 ounces shredded green cabbage or coleslaw mix
ingredients.name: shredded green cabbage or coleslaw mix

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded Monterey Jack cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded Monterey Jack cheese (2 cups)

preparationSteps: In a large bowl or zip-top bag, combine 1 chipotle and the adobo, the oil, honey, and ¾ teaspoon salt. Use a Microplane to grate in the zest from 1 lime. Mix, smashing the chipotle against the side of the bowl with the spoon or mashing it with your hands through the outside of the bag to break it up. Add the shrimp and turn to coat, then set aside to marinate at room temperature.
Chop the cilantro leaves and tender stems. Cut the remaining lime into 8 wedges.
Heat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400° to 450°F).

Halve the zested lime and squeeze the juice from 1 half into a medium bowl. Add the mayo, the remaining chipotle, and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine, smashing the chipotle to break it up and incorporate it. Taste and adjust the seasoning as you like. Transfer half the crema to a small serving bowl.
Add the cabbage to the remaining crema in the medium bowl and toss to coat well. Taste and add salt or lime juice as needed.
Place the shrimp on the grill, close the lid, and cook for about 1 minute per side, until nice grill marks appear. Transfer the shrimp to a plate and tent with foil to keep warm.

Warm your largest nonstick skillet over medium heat until a drop of water flicked into the pan dances on the surface, 3 to 4 minutes. Make two circles of cheese about the size of the tortillas on opposite sides of the skillet, using 2 tablespoons for each circle. As soon as the cheese is completely melted and the edges start to get brown, 4 to 5 minutes, place 1 tortilla on top of each cheese circle so the cheese and tortilla stick together. Use a thin spatula to get under the cheese and flip the whole thing over, then warm on the other side of the tortillas for a few seconds. Use the spatula to transfer the tortillas to a plate.
Pile 3 or 4 shrimp onto each tortilla and top with tons of pico de gallo, slaw, and chipotle crema. Sprinkle chopped cilantro on top and squeeze on a little bit of lime juice. Eat and repeat!

name: Secret Ingredient Scallop Scampi
note:
Gochujang in a scallop scampi? Oh yes. Stay with me: Scallops replace shrimp (because who says you can’t scampi a scallop?!), and the Korean chile paste infuses this classic Italian entrée with umami, subtle heat, and a hint of sweetness, while an abundance of lemon keeps the flavor from straying too far. “Guess the secret ingredient” would be a fun game to play at the dinner table, should there be other home cooks or savvy diners enjoying this meal with you!

LEARN
There’s a small rectangular tag of tissue on the side of a scallop. It feels tougher than the rest of the scallop, and its muscle fibers run opposite to the fibers in the scallop itself. To remove it, pinch it between your thumb and pointer finger and tear it away. Not every scallop will have one, so just remove it when it’s obvious. • Cooking the scallops in two batches ensures that you don’t crowd the pan, which would steam them instead of giving them a nice brown crust. This takes more time, but will actually make your scallops better.

SWAP
Use 1½ pounds peeled and deveined jumbo (16/20) raw shrimp (tails on or off) in place of the scallops; cook them just until they’re opaque and curl into a loose C shape, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 159

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound long pasta noodles, such as linguine, spaghetti, or bucatini
ingredients.name: long pasta noodles, such as linguine, spaghetti, or bucatini

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds large fresh sea scallops, tough ligament removed (see Learn)
ingredients.name: large fresh sea scallops, tough ligament removed (see Learn)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out about 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, pat the scallops completely dry. Season all over with 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper.
Cut the lemons in half and thinly slice the garlic. Roughly chop the parsley leaves and tender stems (you should have about ¾ cup).

Warm a 12-inch skillet (preferably stainless steel or cast iron) over medium-high heat until a drop of water flicked into the pan dances on the surface. Place the 4 lemon halves cut side down in the skillet and cook, undisturbed, until charred on the bottom, about 3 minutes. Remove them from the pan.

Pat the scallops dry one more time. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil to the hot pan and swirl the pan to coat. When it shimmers, add half the scallops and cook, undisturbed, until golden brown on the bottom, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip the scallops, add 1 tablespoon of the butter to the pan, and cook, tilting the pan and spooning the butter over the scallops, until the scallops are golden brown on the second side, 1 to 2 minutes more. Transfer the scallops to a plate and pour the butter over them, then cover loosely with aluminum foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining scallops, adding a little more oil to the pan first and another tablespoon of the butter to the pan after flipping them.

Reduce the heat under the empty skillet to medium and add the remaining 4 tablespoons butter and the garlic. Cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in the gochujang. Squeeze in the juice of the charred lemons and stir in the honey. Add about ½ cup of the reserved pasta cooking water (see Learn, page 60), 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper. Cook until the sauce thickens slightly, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the drained pasta and most of the parsley to the pan and use tongs to toss and coat with the sauce. Taste and add some salt or squeeze in some lemon juice, if it needs it.
Serve the pasta topped with the scallops and any liquid collected on the plate and sprinkled with the remaining parsley.

name: Cheesy Polenta with Roasty Balsamic Mushrooms
note:
Polenta is typically made with coarse-ground cornmeal, but I actually prefer using finely ground, as it yields an incredibly silky, creamy texture. Enormous thanks to longtime What to Cooker Sara, who, a few years ago, completely randomly emailed me her method for oven polenta and was like, “I think you’d like this!” You were right, Sara, I do like this! If not for Sara, you’d all be standing over the stovetop whisking like a bunch of chumps! The balsamic-roasted mushrooms bring meaty texture and tangy-sweet depth to the polenta’s creamy canvas.

TIP
Polenta needs a LOT of salt to succeed, in my opinion, but how much salt you add before serving will depend on how salty your cheeses are.

LEARN
You’ll find cornmeal in the flour or grain aisle, or sometimes in the international aisle. Sometimes it’s labeled “polenta,” sometimes it’s labeled “cornmeal.” Fine, medium, or coarse will all work (fine will be the creamiest, coarse will have the most texture)—I never met a polenta I didn’t like!

SHORTCUT
Use a tube of precooked polenta: Open two 16- to 18-ounce tubes and pat the polenta dry, then chop it into small cubes. Place the cubes in a large saucepan along with 4 cups water and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until the polenta is soft, 2 to 3 minutes, then whisk vigorously until smooth. Stir in 1 cup milk and return to a simmer, then stir in the Parm and cheddar and remove from the heat. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

SWAP
Use 1 teaspoon dried thyme in place of the tablespoon (which is 3 teaspoons) fresh thyme. This 1-to-3 ratio is a good one to know; you can generally replace any fresh herb with one-third the amount of dried.

RIFF
Serve the mushrooms over pasta instead of polenta. Toss the pasta with a splash of the pasta cooking water and a 5.3-ounce block of Boursin, then top everything with lots of freshly grated Parm.

BULK IT UP
Add a few handfuls of chopped spinach or kale to the baking sheet of mushrooms for the final 5 minutes of cooking. Add some cherry tomatoes to the baking sheet and roast those with the mushrooms. • Need meat? Slice some Italian sausage links into 4 big pieces each, nestle them down into the mushrooms, and roast together. Or make some meatballs (see page 100) or throw some store-bought frozen meatballs on the baking sheet with the mushrooms for the second half of the mushroom roasting time.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 160

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds fresh mushrooms (any kind, though I don’t love shiitakes here)
ingredients.name: fresh mushrooms (any kind, though I don’t love shiitakes here)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: balsamic vinegar, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces grated sharp cheddar cheese (1 cup)
ingredients.name: grated sharp cheddar cheese (1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Make the polenta. In a large Dutch oven, combine the milk, 1 teaspoon salt, and 4 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn off the heat, then, while whisking continuously, slowly pour in the cornmeal. After it’s all been added, cover the pot and let it stand for a moment while you work on the mushrooms—we want everything to go into the oven at the same time.

Make the mushrooms. On the prepared baking sheet, toss together the mushrooms, olive oil, thyme, vinegar, 1 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. If you’re using large mushrooms, break them as you toss; you want everything in bite-size pieces.

Transfer the polenta and mushrooms to the oven (ideally on the same rack, but mushrooms below polenta if not). Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until the mushrooms are golden brown. Remove the polenta and mushrooms from the oven.

Carefully remove the lid from the pot of polenta (it’s hot!). Stir in the Parm and cheddar. Taste and add more salt and black pepper as needed. Stir in more water if it is too thick; or, if you want it thicker, place the pot on the stovetop and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until it reaches your desired consistency.
Spoon the polenta into shallow bowls and serve with the mushrooms on top, drizzled with more balsamic vinegar and sprinkled with tons of Parm and red pepper flakes.

name: Hella Green Soup with Garlic Toasts
note:
Hella Green Pasta is an iconic recipe from both my newsletter and the first What to Cook book. I’ve probably gotten 1,000 messages at this point that said something along the lines of “This sauce is so good we were eating it like soup!” So . . . I made a hella green soup! Prepare to slurp down an obscene amount of vegetables and to be so, so delighted as you do. Heavy cream brings richness and, well, creaminess to what could otherwise be labeled a blended salad. The crunchy, dunkable garlic toasts are, IMO, a non-skippable part of this equation.

TIP
For the smoothest result here, you really want to use a high-powered blender; a food processor or an immersion blender—as much as I love them both—won’t be up to the task.

LEARN
When blending hot liquid, never fill the blender more than halfway. Before turning the blender on, remove the center cap from the lid and cover the lid with a folded kitchen towel. This lets the steam escape rather than building up pressure that can blow the lid off! • Steaming spinach and kale separately before combining them with the rest of the ingredients locks in that bright green color—otherwise, the color can get really muddy and not so pretty. And adding the fresh herbs at the end keeps their color and flavor bright.

SWAP
For a vegan version, use coconut milk, or add ½ cup raw unsalted cashews when you add the stock to the pot. When you blend the soup, the cashews will add a lovely creaminess. • Replace the garlic toasts with Pancetta Croutons (page 174) or Herby-Garlicky Croutons (page 244)!

BULK IT UP
Stir 1 cup cooked rice or quinoa into the pot just before serving and simmer for a minute to warm it up. • Top each serving with shredded chicken or flaked salmon or cooked shrimp. If you’re going in this direction, it’s nice to use chicken or fish stock in place of vegetable stock if you’ve got it!

EXTRA EXTRA
For perfectly smooth and super-elegant soup, strain it through a fine-mesh strainer, using a wooden spoon to push it through. Garnish the top of the soup with little dots of leftover heavy cream. Fancy!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 163

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small baguette, or ½ loaf crusty bread, sliced into 4 pieces
ingredients.name: small baguette, or ½ loaf crusty bread

preparationSteps: Position a rack in the center of the oven and turn the broiler to high.
Make the soup. Trim the stems of the spinach and kale leaves. Rinse them, leaving some water clinging to the leaves.

Place the spinach and kale in a large pot (if you’re using prewashed spinach, sprinkle in 2 to 3 tablespoons of water). Cover and cook over medium-high heat to steam until all the leaves are wilted and the stems are softening, 3 to 4 minutes. Use tongs to immediately transfer the spinach and kale to a high-powered blender. Repeat with the remaining spinach and kale. Blend on high speed until completely smooth, 3 to 4 minutes (see Tip, page 165). Dump out the liquid from the pot.
Meanwhile, dice the onion, celery, and potatoes. Mince the garlic. Roughly chop the mint leaves (you should have about ½ cup).

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in the same pot over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion, celery, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened but not browned, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in the coriander and cumin and cook until fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds.

Add the potatoes and stock. Turn up the heat to medium-high and bring to a boil, then turn down the heat to medium, partially cover the pot, and simmer until the potatoes are very tender, 15 to 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the toasts. Arrange the sliced bread on a rimmed baking sheet and coat both sides with olive oil. Broil until golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes per side. While the toasts are still warm, peel and halve the garlic cloves and gently rub each piece cut side down over one side of each toast. Sprinkle with flaky salt.

Stir the pureed greens and chopped mint into the soup. Working in batches as needed, blend the soup on medium-high speed until very smooth, about 1 minute (see Learn, page 165). Return the soup to the pot. Stir in ½ cup cream, or more if you like it richer. Taste and add more kosher salt if needed.
Ladle the warm soup into bowls. Serve with the toasts whole, or break them into crouton-size pieces and float them on top.

name: Broccoli, Cheddar, and Bacon Mac and Cheese
note:
My mom used to make broccoli with cheese sauce (as in Velveeta) as our vegetable like . . . every single night of the week. Eating it and loving it is a core childhood memory and, honestly, in retrospect, I’m impressed by the amount of broccoli I ate as a kid. I’ve been chasing that ’90s nostalgia in my own kitchen for years and have finally landed on this loaded, complete-meal mac and cheese that, I’m happy to report, my kids also demolish.

TIP
This recipe makes a great case for using frozen broccoli florets. Just throw them straight into the pot—no need to thaw! They’ll bring down the water temp, so you might need to cook the pasta and broccoli for a few extra minutes.

RIFF
Stir in a pinch of cayenne for some heat. Or use smoked cheddar or Gouda cheese, or add ½ teaspoon smoked paprika for a smoky vibe.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 166

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces small pasta noodles, such as rigatoni, rotini, or orecchiette
ingredients.name: small pasta noodles, such as rigatoni, rotini, or orecchiette

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Break the broccoli florets into 1-inch pieces. Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook until al dente according to the package directions, adding the broccoli to the pot during the last 3 minutes of cooking. Drain.

Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy, about 5 minutes, flipping once or twice during cooking. Break up the bacon into pieces (big or little, up to you) directly in the pan. You should have about 2 tablespoons rendered fat in the pan; if not, add enough butter to make up the difference and let it melt. Add the flour and cook, stirring, until golden, about 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the milk, breaking up any lumps that form. Add the mustard, garlic powder, and ½ teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer and cook until slightly thickened, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat for a few minutes to let it cool down so that when you add the cheese, it doesn’t “break” and get gritty. Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time, until completely melted and smooth, 2 to 3 minutes total.
Add the drained pasta and broccoli to the cheese sauce, stirring to coat evenly. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed. Serve hot!

name: Cherry Tomato, Goat Cheese, and Herb Frittata with Arugula Salad
note:
In my first What to Cook book, I waxed poetic about frittatas—my favorite clean-out-the-fridge dinner, breakfast, or lunch. I even devoted a whole special section to them (“Frittata How You Want-ta” on page 130—honestly such a good sidebar title that I simply had to say it again here). So, duh, it’s frittata time! I stressed about which one to share with you here, ultimately landing on this vegetarian iteration that is effortlessly fancy and that would be as much at home at a chic bridal luncheon as on your breakfast or dinner (yup!) table. I highly recommend prepping this before bedtime the next time you have houseguests. Pop it in the oven to bake first thing in the morning and watch the crowd go wild.

TIP
If you have a little extra time, you can bake this my favorite way, low and slow, which makes the eggs even softer and more tender. Preheat the oven to 250°F and bake for 30 to 40 minutes.

SWAP
Use ricotta or feta instead of goat cheese.

BULK IT UP
Add zucchini ribbons for more veg. • Serve with roasted potatoes or toast.

EXTRA EXTRA
Add ½ to 1 teaspoon honey and ½ to 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard to the salad dressing to round out the flavor and help it cling to the arugula. • Or add a spoonful of pesto for an herby punch.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 169

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley, chives, and/or dill
ingredients.name: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley, chives, and/or dill

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry
ingredients.name: chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 325°F.

Cut the cherry tomatoes in half, thinly slice the onion, and chop enough herbs to make ¼ cup. Place half the sliced onion in a small bowl with the vinegar, sugar, and ½ teaspoon salt. Use a fork to stir and let stand at room temperature for at least 15 minutes or up to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, half-and-half, 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 10-inch nonstick ovenproof skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the remaining onion and cook, stirring until slightly softened, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook until their skins soften slightly, another minute. Pour in the egg mixture. Crumble in the goat cheese and scatter the herbs all over. Cook the frittata on the stovetop until the edges begin to set, about 2 minutes, then transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the eggs are puffed and just set in the center.

Meanwhile, warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the chickpeas and cook, stirring often, until golden and crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Season with a big pinch of salt. Remove from the heat and let stand for 5 minutes.

Place the arugula in a serving bowl. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of the lemon directly into the bowl. Halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice from 1 half. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil and a pinch each of salt and pepper and toss to coat. Add the pickled onions with their liquid. Add the crispy chickpeas and gently toss again to combine. Taste and add more lemon juice and/or salt if needed.

Use a spatula to loosen the frittata from the skillet and slide it onto a cutting board. Slice into 4 triangles and serve warm or at room temperature with a big scoop of the arugula salad on the side.

name: Migas with Enchilada Sauce and Cotija
note:
My grandmother Frances had an identical twin named Anne, and they each had five children, giving me the gift of twelve female cousins (plus a bunch of boy cousins, too!) who are my closest friends in the world. Though we grew up scattered across the Southeast and Texas, our parents made a point to plan regular family gatherings so we could be close, and our generation is continuing that tradition now that we’re the adults. Every year, we meet in a different city for a long weekend together, and 2024’s trip was to Austin, Texas. I went home with a pair of Tecovas on my feet and an obsession with Tex-Mex-style migas in my heart: tortilla chips + scrambled eggs + onions and/or peppers + hot sauce + tons of cheese = my ideal breakfast/brunch/lunch/dinner. Enchilada sauce isn’t a traditional component of migas, but its sauciness puts these over the top for me.

TIP
Fewer tortillas make saucier migas, and more tortillas make them crunchier.

SHORTCUT
You can use a 9-ounce bag of REALLY GOOD tortilla chips (I love Tostitos, but they don’t work here) instead of frying your own, but stir them in right before serving so they don’t get too soggy.

RIFF
Make it a bake! Stir the fried tortilla bits and cooked onion into the beaten eggs along with the milk and enchilada sauce (no need to warm it unless it’s hard to pour). Pour it all into a greased 2-quart baking dish and bake at 375°F for 25 to 30 minutes, until cooked through and puffed on top.

BULK IT UP
Add cooked chorizo or black beans to the eggs.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 170

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup whole or low-fat milk or heavy cream
ingredients.name: whole or low-fat milk or heavy cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 ounces Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese
ingredients.name: Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Hot sauce (I like Cholula), for serving
ingredients.name: Hot sauce (I like Cholula), for serving

preparationSteps: Stack the tortillas and cut them into strips about ¾ inch wide, then cut them the other way into roughly 1½-inch-long pieces. Dice the onion, slice the avocados, chop enough cilantro leaves and tender stems to make ½ cup, and cut the limes into 8 wedges.

Crack the eggs into a large bowl and add the milk, 1 teaspoon salt, and a lot of pepper, and beat well. Warm the enchilada sauce in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, or microwave it in 30-second bursts until just heated through.

Line a tray with paper towels and set it near the stove. Pour enough olive oil into a large skillet to generously coat the bottom (about 2 tablespoons) and warm it over medium heat. When it shimmers, working in batches, scatter in a handful of the tortilla pieces in a single layer and cook until crisp and golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Use a slotted spoon or tongs to transfer them to the prepared tray and immediately sprinkle with salt. Repeat with the remaining tortilla strips, adding more oil to the pan as needed.

Wipe out the skillet and warm 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened and just starting to brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Turn down the heat to medium-low and pour in the egg mixture. Let it sit for a moment, then stir gently and slowly with a spatula until the eggs are mostly cooked but still creamy, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in the warm enchilada sauce, then add the tortilla strips. Mix everything together gently to coat the tortillas and warm them through, 2 to 5 minutes. Turn off the heat.

Scrape the migas into a serving bowl. Crumble over the Cotija, then sprinkle with the avocado and cilantro, and arrange the lime wedges along the edges or place them in a separate small bowl. Pass hot sauce at the table for extra heat.

name: Melty Zucchini Pasta with Goat Cheese and Parm (Book)
note:
If you have a friend, coworker, or neighbor who grows zucchini, you probably know they grow zucchini. This veg is a prolific producer come peak summer, so friendly backyard farmers everywhere start emphatically doling out pounds and pounds of it to avoid waste (or having to cook with it for three months straight—and probably still have enough to share). Next time you find yourself with a zucchini overload, whether it’s been gifted to you or you’ve sought it out, this vegetarian pasta—in which we sauté three whole pounds (!) of the verdant summertime squash—is an easy, elegant way to make good use of it.

TIP
If/when your zucchini starts releasing a ton of liquid, just keep cooking—it’ll concentrate into a jammy, sweet-savory base that coats the pasta beautifully.

SWAP
Feta works in place of the goat cheese, and you can skip the Parm or add more if you want it extra savory. • Yellow squash also works here—or use half squash and half zucchini!

BULK IT UP
Toast chopped walnuts in butter and scatter them over the pasta for a really nice crunch.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 173

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound long pasta noodles, such as spaghetti, linguine, or bucatini
ingredients.name: long pasta noodles, such as spaghetti, linguine, or bucatini

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ bunch soft green herbs, such as fresh basil, parsley, and/or mint
ingredients.name: soft green herbs, such as fresh basil, parsley, and/or mint

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: balsamic vinegar, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ⅔ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2⅔ ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2⅔ ounces), plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out about 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta and return it to the hot pot.
Meanwhile, halve the zucchini lengthwise, then slice it crosswise into thin half circles. Very thinly slice the onion and thinly slice the garlic. Roughly chop the herb leaves and tender stems.

Warm ¼ cup olive oil in your largest skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the zucchini, onion, red pepper flakes (if using), 1½ teaspoons salt, and some black pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is softened and has released a lot of liquid, 8 to 10 minutes. Turn up the heat to high and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated, any remaining liquid is slightly thickened, and the zucchini is breaking down, 10 to 12 minutes; turn down the heat if the vegetables are browning too quickly. Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the vinegar and cook, stirring to coat the zucchini, until well incorporated, about 1 minute. Remove from the heat.

Scrape the zucchini mixture into the pasta in the pot. Crumble in the goat cheese, then add the Parm and a splash of the reserved pasta cooking water and stir until everything is coated and creamy. Add more pasta cooking water a splash at a time if you’d like a looser sauce. Stir in most of the herbs, reserving about ⅓ cup for serving. Taste and add more vinegar, salt, and/or pepper if needed.
Use tongs to lift the spaghetti into shallow bowls, getting plenty of the melty zucchini, too. Top with the reserved chopped herbs and more Parm and serve warm.

name: Good Luck Soup (Book)
note:
When I was growing up in North Carolina, my mom, like many Southerners, would cook up collard greens, black-eyed peas, and ham on New Year’s Day. Collard greens are said to symbolize money; black-eyed peas, luck and abundance; and pork, forward-moving progress (because pigs always “root forward” when they eat, as opposed to chickens and turkeys, who “scratch backward”). Hoppin’ John—a dish rich with heritage that’s woven into the culinary quilt of America, adopted from the enslaved African community, like so many Southern food traditions—is the traditional way to combine these lucky and favorable ingredients on New Year’s Day. While that dish is delicious and important, I also found another way to get those lucky little beans and greens into my belly. The result is this utterly delicious melting pot of a soup, which brings in ingredients from all over the globe (turmeric! yellow curry paste! soy sauce!). Here’s to good luck, progress, prosperity, and a delicious blending of cuisines and cultures!

LEARN
If you don’t have a lid for your pot, you can use a baking sheet!

SWAP
If black-eyed peas aren’t your thing, canned chickpeas or white beans would be great here. • If you can’t find chopped collards, use chopped kale or spinach.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 174

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups low-sodium vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (15-ounce) cans black-eyed peas, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black-eyed peas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 lime, or 1 tablespoon light vinegar, such as red wine, apple cider, or champagne, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: lime, or 1 tablespoon light vinegar, such as red wine, apple cider, or champagne, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons fish sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: fish sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4-ounce) container diced pancetta, or 3 slices bacon, diced
ingredients.name: diced pancetta, or 3 slices bacon

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 to 3 tablespoons unsalted butter or extra-virgin olive oil, if needed
ingredients.name: unsalted butter or extra-virgin olive oil, if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley and/or basil
ingredients.name: Handful of soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley and/or basil

preparationSteps: Make the soup. Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into ½-inch cubes. Warm the oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the sweet potatoes, curry paste, turmeric, onion powder, and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until the paste starts to stick to the bottom of the pot, about 1 minute.

Pour in the stock, coconut milk, and black-eyed peas. Turn up the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, then turn it down to medium and stir with a wooden spoon, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes. Meanwhile, cut the lime in half.

Stir in the collards, soy sauce, fish sauce, and a squirt of sriracha if you like a little heat. Squeeze in the juice from the lime. Cover the pot and cook until the collards wilt, about 4 minutes. Taste and add more salt, soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice, and/or stock as you like.

Meanwhile, make the croutons. Cook the pancetta in a medium skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it’s almost crispy, 4 to 5 minutes. Roughly chop the bread into tiny pieces and add it to the skillet. Stir to coat the bread in the rendered pancetta fat. If the bread still looks dry, add butter as needed. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the bread is looking toasty, 4 or 5 minutes. Chop the herbs and stir them in, along with a few shakes of garlic powder and a pinch of salt. Remove the skillet from the heat.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the pancetta croutons, and get ready to get lucky.

name: Cheater Ratatouille
note:
Traditional/purist ratatouille (including the way Julia Child made the Provençal French vegetable stew famous) is a pretty fussy pursuit when all you want to do is maximize the flavor of each and every vegetable. It often includes steps like peeling and seeding the tomatoes, salting and draining the eggplant (and sometimes the zucchini, too), and cooking the veggies in stages. There is a time and place for this perfected multistep method—and there are other times and places (say, 6 p.m. on a Wednesday, in a house full of hangry people) in which this ratatouille-inspired sheet pan dinner is just the ticket. All ya do is chop up some summer veg, roast ’em into golden, jammy submission, and serve in bowls topped with some decadent toppings. Bon appétit!

LEARN
Switching racks and rotating the baking sheets helps everything cook evenly, especially in ovens that run hotter in the back or on one side. It helps all the vegetables get nice and brown instead of burning or steaming. Spreading out the vegetables on the pans also helps them to brown.

SWAP
Use labneh or whipped goat cheese instead of ricotta for a tangier twist.

RIFF
Spread leftover ratatouille in an appropriately sized baking dish so your leftovers are about 2 inches thick in the pan. If you have any ricotta left, spoon that around the surface of the ratatouille, then stir it in a little. Use a spoon to make four divots in the ratatouille. Crack an egg into each divot and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Bake at 375°F for about 8 minutes, until the yolks are as set as you like them. Serve with couscous or crusty bread.

BULK IT UP
Toss the vegetables with pasta or spoon them over sourdough toast or cheesy polenta (page 160).

EXTRA EXTRA
For another layer of savoriness, when you add the vinegar, add a couple big spoonfuls of grated Parm, too.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 177

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ teaspoons dried oregano or herbes de Provence
ingredients.name: dried oregano or herbes de Provence

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon balsamic or aged sherry vinegar
ingredients.name: balsamic or aged sherry vinegar

ingredients.rawIngredient: Fresh basil and/or parsley, for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: Fresh basil and/or parsley, for serving (optional)

preparationSteps: Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and preheat to 450°F.

Cut the eggplant, zucchini, and squash into 1-inch cubes, and cut the red onion into ¼-inch-thick wedges, placing them all on a baking sheet as you go. Smash the garlic with the side of your knife, and add that to the baking sheet, too. Add the tomatoes, then drizzle everything with about ¼ cup olive oil and sprinkle with the coriander, oregano, 2 teaspoons salt, and some pepper. Toss to coat the vegetables evenly, then transfer half to a second baking sheet. Spread out the vegetables on both baking sheets.

Roast the vegetables until they’re browned, the tomatoes are collapsed, and everything looks soft, jammy, and caramelized, 30 to 40 minutes, stirring once or twice and switching racks and rotating the pans once. As soon as you remove the pans from the oven, combine all the vegetables onto one baking sheet, drizzle on the vinegar, and toss gently.
Meanwhile, chop enough basil leaves (if using) to make ¼ cup.
Scoop the ratatouille into bowls and top each with a big spoonful of ricotta. Drizzle each serving with a little olive oil and sprinkle with the basil.

name: Black Bean Tamale Pie
note:
We live less than half an hour away from Monterey, California, a seaside town my boys love for its beaches and its aquarium. While the Monterey Bay Aquarium truly is incredible, so too is Elroy’s, a little fancy grocer where we grab prepared food anytime we’re in the area. I’ve never had a bad meal at Elroy’s, but one of my all-time favorites has been their tamale pie—basically cornbread baked directly on top of boldly seasoned beef-and-veggie chili. They sell it out of their refrigerated case by the slice, and it reheats like a dream. This version, my perfect vegetarian version, was inspired by that!

SHORTCUT
Instead of making a homemade cornbread topping, you can use any boxed cornbread mix, adding the cheese to it.

SWAP
Use 2 pounds ground turkey, chicken, or beef in place of the beans—or use 1 can of beans and 1 pound of meat. Brown the meat in the skillet (if using beef, drain off the fat before adding the other ingredients!) before getting started with the recipe.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 178

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (28-ounce) can diced tomatoes, with their juices
ingredients.name: diced tomatoes, with their juices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15.25-ounce) can White corn, drained, or 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen white corn
ingredients.name: White corn, drained

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces grated cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup)
ingredients.name: grated cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons (½ stick) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces grated cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup)
ingredients.name: grated cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese (1 cup)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Make the filling. Warm the olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the chipotle and adobo, chili powder, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, cinnamon, 1 teaspoon salt, and some pepper and stir, smashing the chipotle with your spoon to break it up. Stir in the diced tomatoes with their juices, the tomato sauce, beans, and corn. Turn up the heat to medium-high and bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then turn down the heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the filling thickens slightly, 5 to 8 minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in the cheese.

Meanwhile, make the topping. In a large bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. In a separate bowl or large glass measuring cup, whisk together the milk and eggs to combine, then whisk in the melted butter. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just until blended. Gently stir in the cheese.

Spoon the topping batter over the filling and use a spatula to gently spread it to the edges. Bake the tamale pie for 20 to 25 minutes, until the cornbread topping is golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let stand for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, if you’re using them, slice the avocados and cut the limes into 8 wedges each.
Slice the tamale pie into wedges, then scoop the beans and cornbread into shallow bowls. Serve with the avocados, sour cream, and salsa, if you like, with the lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Spanakopita-Style Eggs
note:
My hometown of Winston-Salem, North Carolina, has a large Greek population, and a highlight of school potlucks and holiday parties for me growing up was feasting on homemade spanakopita, a classic Greek dish made with layers of flaky phyllo dough wrapped around a savory blend of spinach and feta. This is basically a skillet full of spanakopita filling, with eggs cracked into it for protein and toasty bread to act as a crunchy, carby spoon for scooping it all up. It’s kind of like shakshuka meets spinach dip meets spanakopita (yep, it tastes as good as it sounds), and it makes an A+ meal any time of day.

TIP
If you prefer firmer egg yolks, keep the lid on for a few more minutes, until the eggs are cooked to your liking.

SWAP
Use 1 pound thawed frozen spinach in place of the fresh. Squeeze out as much moisture as you can before adding it to the skillet. Fresh Swiss chard or kale work in place of the spinach; just note that they take a few extra minutes of cooking to become tender.

RIFF
For more of a shakshuka vibe, omit the dill and stir in 1 teaspoon ground coriander, 1 teaspoon sweet paprika, ½ teaspoon ground cumin, and a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 181
preparationSteps: Position a rack in the center of the oven and turn the broiler to high.
Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the scallions. Roughly chop the parsley leaves and tender stems. Chop the dill (you want about ½ cup), keeping it separate from the parsley.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion and a pinch of kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and starting to brown, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and nutmeg and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Working in batches, add the spinach and cook, stirring, until wilted and all the moisture has evaporated, 3 to 5 minutes. Turn down the heat to medium. Stir in the scallions, most of the parsley (reserve a little bit for serving), and the dill. Season with ½ teaspoon kosher salt and some pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is dark green, soft, and a little glossy, 2 to 3 minutes.

Crumble half the feta into the pan and stir. Use the back of a spoon to create 8 shallow divots in the greens, then crack an egg into each divot and season with a pinch each of kosher salt and pepper. Crumble the remaining feta over the top, avoiding the egg yolks if you can. Cover the skillet and cook until the egg whites are just set and the yolks are still runny, 5 to 7 minutes (see Tip).
Meanwhile, place the sliced bread on a rimmed baking sheet and coat both sides with olive oil. Sprinkle with flaky salt. Broil until golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Sprinkle the reserved parsley over the eggs. Spoon and serve the spanakopita in shallow bowls with the toasted bread for scooping.

name: Kinda Tabbouleh Grain Salad
note:
Classic tabbouleh is a Levantine salad built around finely chopped parsley, mint, tomatoes, and bulgur, dressed simply with lemon and olive oil. My version plays off those flavors while welcoming whatever grain you have in the pantry, and is particularly wonderful with quinoa. Full of herbs and bright flavor, this is a delightful vegetarian dish anytime but especially in the peak of tomato season.

SWAP
No quinoa? Try farro, bulgur, or pearl couscous. • Any fresh herbs are great either in place of or in addition to what’s called for, such as dill, basil, or oregano.

RIFF
Stir in toasted pistachios or pine nuts for crunch.

BULK IT UP
Add 2 cups chopped cooked rotisserie chicken. Or start the quinoa in a large saucepan and toss 1 pound shrimp right on top after the quinoa has been cooking for 10 minutes. Let them finish cooking together, and when you fluff, mix it all up.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 182

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 Persian cucumbers, or ½ English cucumber
ingredients.name: Persian cucumbers, or ½ English cucumber

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (5- to 6-ounce) jar pitted kalamata or Castelvetrano olives, drained (about 1 cup)
ingredients.name: pitted kalamata or Castelvetrano olives, drained (about 1 cup)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Combine the quinoa and 1¾ cups water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Stir, turn down the heat to low, cover, and cook until tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.

Meanwhile, place the chickpeas in a serving bowl. Cut the tomatoes in half and add them to the bowl. Dice the cucumbers, thinly slice the scallions, and chop the olives. Finely chop the mint leaves and the parsley leaves and tender stems (about 3 cups each), and add it all to the bowl along with the red pepper flakes (if using).

In a lidded jar, combine the olive oil, mustard, 1 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Using a Microplane, grate the garlic and the zest of 1 lemon directly into the jar. Halve both lemons and squeeze in their juice. Close the lid and shake vigorously to combine.

Transfer the quinoa to the bowl and crumble in the feta. Add about half the dressing and use a big spoon to toss and coat. Taste and adjust the seasoning and add more dressing as desired. Serve immediately or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

name: Green Curry Wontons
note:
The summer between George’s two years in business school, we lived in Bangkok, Thailand, for a month. Every morning when he went off to work, I went off to eat, scouring the city for the best curries, skewers, noodles, and sticky rice Bangkok had to offer. I took as many Thai cooking classes as possible, but mostly I just watched street vendors cook, ate at hole-in-the-wall establishments recommended by Anthony Bourdain, and asked lots of questions via Google Translate. One of my favorite dishes to order was curry; I’d watch as chefs casually threw together a life-changing paste in a mortar and pestle, pulling from at least fifteen different containers. Luckily for us, a delicious curry is within reach at home—even on a busy weeknight—thanks to the beauty that is jarred curry paste. This is not a dish you’d find in Bangkok, but curry broth, vegetables, and store-bought frozen wontons will quickly become one of your favorite weeknight meals.

TIPS
If you’re near an Asian market, you can buy great canned curry pastes for half the cost of the jarred kind at a typical grocery store. • Extra canned curry paste will keep in the fridge for up to a week. (You can portion it into ice cube trays and freeze it for up to 3 months, too.)

SWAP
Use 2 teaspoons low-sodium soy sauce in place of the fish sauce. • Use 1 tablespoon rice vinegar in place of the lime juice. • Use any color curry paste! Every brand has different heat levels, so best to start with 1 tablespoon and add more at the end if needed. • Use thinly sliced mushrooms, bell peppers, carrots, spinach, or kale in place of the snap peas.

RIFF
Use 1 (14-ounce) block of firm or extra-firm cubed tofu or 1 pound of cubed chicken breast in place of the wontons! The tofu will cook for the same amount of time; the chicken should cook for 5 minutes before you add the snap peas.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 183

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 small (not baby) head bok choy (about 1 pound)
ingredients.name: small (not baby) head bok choy (about 1 pound)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon green curry paste (more if you like it spicy)
ingredients.name: green curry paste (more if you like it spicy)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium soy sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fish sauce, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: fish sauce, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 10 to 16 ounces snap peas (however big the bag is at your store)
ingredients.name: snap peas (however big the bag is at your store)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (24-ounce) bag frozen wontons, potstickers, or dumplings (any kind; about 60 mini or 20 full-size)
ingredients.name: frozen wontons, potstickers, or dumplings (any kind; about 60 mini or 20 full-size)

preparationSteps: Finely chop the broccoli and bok choy (the pieces should be small enough to fit on a spoon).

Warm the oil in a large saucepan or pot over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the broccoli and bok choy and cook until tender, 3 to 4 minutes. Add the curry paste and stir until fragrant and starting to stick to the bottom of the pan, about 30 seconds. Stir in the coconut milk, stock, soy sauce, and fish sauce and bring to a simmer.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the snap peas.

Drop the frozen wontons into the simmering liquid and cook, uncovered, stirring to separate the wontons as needed, for 2 minutes. Add the snap peas and cook until the wontons are tender and the snap peas are bright green, about 3 minutes more. Halve the lime and squeeze in the juice from 1 half. Taste and adjust the seasonings as needed—more soy sauce for saltiness, fish sauce for umami, and/or lime juice for brightness.
Ladle the curry into bowls and, if desired, top with chili crisp for a little extra kick.

name: Bean and Butternut Enchiladas with Creamy Salsa Verde
note:
As if you needed any convincing, this recipe is proof that with a well-stocked pantry, you’ll be able to pull together a delicious dinner anytime. We’re calling on canned beans, canned butternut squash puree, canned chipotles in adobo, jarred salsa verde (aka conveniently pre-prepped tomatillos, green chiles, onions, garlic, cilantro, and lime juice), and flour tortillas to whip up a skillet full of sweet, spicy, savory enchiladas. Is this a meal you could make when you’re out of other options? Yes. Will it taste like a plan B? Absolutely not.

TIP
Canned pumpkin or sweet potato also works great here in place of the squash. Just make sure the can isn’t labeled “pie filling,” which means it’s sweetened and spiced. Not bad, but not the vibe.

SWAP
You can also make this dish with 10 (6-inch) corn tortillas. Wrap them in damp paper towels and microwave for 20 to 40 seconds, until warm and pliable, then use about ¼ cup filling in each. If they break, whatever, you’re about to cover them with sauce and cheese. • In place of the squash, you can use another can of beans; just smash them up until quite smooth!

RIFF
Instead of rolling up enchiladas, make it a crunchwrap casserole situation: In a 3-quart baking dish, layer the sauce, filling, and store-bought tostadas, ending with a layer of sauce. Top with the cheese and bake as directed.

BULK IT UP
Add shredded rotisserie chicken or browned chorizo to the filling. • Top with pepitas for crunch.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 186

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can white beans, such as cannellini or great northern, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: white beans, such as cannellini or great northern

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: pinto beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups (8 ounces) shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 1 teaspoon adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 ounce Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese
ingredients.name: Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a 12-inch ovenproof skillet, whisk together the salsa verde, sour cream, and ½ teaspoon of the cumin.

In a large bowl, combine the white beans, pinto beans, butternut squash, 1 cup of the shredded cheese, the chipotle and adobo, the remaining 1 teaspoon cumin, the garlic powder, paprika, and salt. Stir to combine, smashing the chipotle to break it up.

Lay 1 tortilla on a clean surface. Spoon a heaping ½ cup of the bean filling on the bottom third of the tortilla, closest to you. Roll it up tightly away from you and place it in the skillet, rotating it to really coat it in the sauce and leaving it seam side down. Repeat with the remaining tortillas and filling, adding them to the skillet and rolling them to coat as you go. Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup shredded cheese over the top.
Bake the enchiladas for 20 to 25 minutes, until the filling is heated through and the cheese is melted and lightly browned.
Meanwhile, chop the cilantro and slice the lime into 8 wedges.
Crumble the Cotija over the baked enchiladas, sprinkle with the cilantro, and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Yogurt-Marinated Grilled Chicken with Yellow Rice
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 4 hours

Turmeric—a kinda-sweet, kinda-earthy-tasting spice that’s packed with health benefits—is a leading character in tonight’s dinner. It’s the yellow in our yellow rice, and it plays nicely with the Mediterranean flavors in your new-favorite golden grilled chicken. Marinating chicken in yogurt locks in its moisture, ensuring that it’ll be amazingly juicy and delicious after cooking. I like to serve this family-style with chicken, rice, and a table full of toppings, and let everyone build their perfect plate.

TIP
Keep the whole party inside and roast the chicken on a parchment-lined baking sheet at 425°F for 14 to 18 minutes.

SHORTCUT
Cutting the chicken into long strips lets the yogurt marinade touch more surface area and gives you meltingly tender chicken. But if you’re in a rush, keep the breasts whole (it’ll still be delicious!) and cook for 5 to 10 minutes longer. • Or you can use packaged, already sliced chicken tenders.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 191

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Greek seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Greek seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Chopped lettuce, chopped tomato, avocado slices, thinly sliced red onion, chopped cucumber, feta, chopped soft green herbs (such as fresh basil, dill, parsley, and/or cilantro)
ingredients.name: Chopped lettuce, chopped tomato, avocado slices, thinly sliced red onion, chopped cucumber, feta, chopped soft green herbs (such as fresh basil, dill, parsley, and/or cilantro)

preparationSteps: Make the chicken. In a large bowl, stir together the yogurt, mayo, and garlic powder. Halve the lemon, squeeze in the juice, and stir to blend well. Transfer half of this mixture to a small serving bowl, stir in ¼ teaspoon salt, and reserve for serving.
To the remaining yogurt mixture in the large bowl, add the honey, Greek seasoning, turmeric, and some pepper. If your Greek seasoning doesn’t include salt, add ¼ teaspoon salt. Stir to combine.

Cut each chicken breast lengthwise into 3 or 4 strips. Add the chicken to the marinade and toss to coat well. Cover with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or up to overnight.
Thirty minutes before you want to eat, heat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400° to 450°F).

Meanwhile, make the rice. In a small pot, combine the rice, stock, butter, turmeric, garlic powder, and salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Use a fork to fluff the rice.

Grill the chicken. Use tongs to remove the chicken from the marinade, scraping off as much excess as possible, and place the chicken strips on the grill. Grill until the meat reaches 165°F internally, about 5 minutes per side. Transfer the chicken to a serving platter and let rest for at least 10 minutes or until ready to serve.
Slice/chop up your desired toppings and place them on a platter. Transfer the rice to a serving bowl.
Place your rice, chicken, yogurt sauce, and optional toppings on the table and let everyone dig in, creating their own bowls.

name: Rotisserie-ish Chicken with Schmaltzy Lemon Dressing
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2½ hours

I don’t think I’m allowed to pick favorites, but this is one of my favorite recipes in the entire book. I love rotisserie chicken so very much, and here we’ve captured the smoky sweet flavors and the slow-roasty texture of a rotisserie chicken, while also making two side dishes on the same pan. I am absolutely addicted to this kale and roasted carrot salad, where we use the chicken schmaltz (drippings) in place of olive oil to make a salad dressing. Add some roasted potatoes and we’ve got a really beautiful meal, all cooked on one pan.

TIP
You should get 3 to 4 tablespoons of lemon juice from your lemon; if you had a skimpy lemon, add a splash of any vinegar you like to make up for it.

SHORTCUT
Use 3 to 4 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs in place of the whole chicken. Roast as directed. This way you can skip the carving!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 192–193

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds baby potatoes (red, gold, or tricolor)
ingredients.name: baby potatoes (red, gold, or tricolor)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag chopped kale, tough stems removed
ingredients.name: chopped kale, tough stems removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup golden raisins or chopped dates
ingredients.name: golden raisins or chopped dates

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Quarter 1 lemon and cut the garlic head in half crosswise.

Place the chicken on the prepared baking sheet. If needed, remove and discard the giblets (also known as the guts) from the cavity of the chicken (some chickens have them, some don’t—they’ll be in a little bag; you can’t miss them!). Pat the chicken dry. In a small bowl, stir together ¼ cup olive oil, the paprika, brown sugar, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 teaspoon of the garlic powder, the chili powder, and the thyme. Rub the paste all over the inside and outside of the chicken, using your fingers to pry the skin from the chicken and rubbing the paste between the skin and the meat as much as possible. Stuff the lemon quarters and halved garlic head inside the cavity of the chicken.
Roast the chicken for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, wash the carrots (no need to peel unless the skins look unappealing—sometimes they’re quite furry), trim off the tops, and cut on a diagonal into 1-inch-thick slices. Halve the potatoes.

Remove the chicken from the oven. Pile the carrots on one side of the bird and the potatoes on the other side. To the carrots, add 2 tablespoons olive oil and ½ teaspoon salt and toss to coat. Spread them into as even a layer as possible (it’s okay if they’re quite crowded). To the potatoes add 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, and the remaining ½ teaspoon garlic powder and toss to coat. Spread them into as even a layer as possible, too.
Return the baking sheet to the oven and roast for 1½ hours more, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 165°F in multiple places (breast, thigh, etc.).
While everything roasts, grate the zest of the remaining lemon into a large serving bowl, then halve it and squeeze in the juice. Add the mustard to the bowl.
Chop the almonds.

Scoop up 3 tablespoons of the chicken drippings from the pan and add them to the bowl. Whisk to combine. Add the kale and a pinch of salt and use your hands to massage the dressing into the kale until it just starts to soften, about 10 scrunches, discarding any big tough stems if you find them. Crumble over the feta, then add the roasted carrots, almonds, and raisins. Toss to coat well.
Carve the chicken and serve with the potatoes and the kale salad. Pour the remaining pan juices over the chicken before serving.

name: Creamy Turkey Chili
note:
Hands on for: 20 minutes
Walk away for: 2 hours

When we lived in Coronado, California, while George was in the navy, we were lucky to meet the Hartigans—the nicest family on the entire island—who have become our dear friends. They welcomed me with open arms into their weekly Friday Night Pizza Night (FNPN) among many other hangouts while George was deployed. But I knew I’d really found my people when they invited me over on Halloween and put out two huge pots of chili—one white chili and the other a tomato-based beef chili. My mom does the exact same thing when she hosts chili nights, setting out her mismatched collection of mugs for people to fill up and top as they like. Chili—and in recent years, this exact chili!—on Halloween has been a tradition in my house ever since that night at the Hartigans’ house. Make a pot (on October 31 or absolutely any other day of the year), leave it simmering on the stove over low heat, and invite everyone to make a bowl (or mug) whenever they please.

TIPS
The blended beans make this a creamy chili even without the cream cheese, so leave it out if you prefer dairy-free chili! • The chili will thicken as it sits, so if you make it in advance, you may have to stir in more stock to get it back to the right consistency.

SHORTCUT
If you’re in a hurry, you can simmer the chili for as little as 20 minutes instead of 2 hours, but the beans and turkey get wonderfully tender if you can wait.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 195

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15.25-ounce) can White corn, drained, or 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen white corn
ingredients.name: White corn, drained

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups chopped kale, tough stems removed
ingredients.name: chopped kale, tough stems removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Shredded cheese, sour cream, hot sauce, green onions, pickled jalapeños, tortilla chips or Fritos, diced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro or parsley
ingredients.name: Shredded cheese, sour cream, hot sauce, green onions, pickled jalapeños, tortilla chips or Fritos, diced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro or parsley

preparationSteps: Dice the onion and mince the garlic.

Warm the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring frequently, until light golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano, and garlic powder and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the ground turkey, turn up the heat to high, and cook, breaking the meat into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until the turkey is cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a blender, combine 1 can of the cannellini beans and its liquid and 1 cup stock. Blend on high speed until smooth, about 1 minute. Stir the blended beans into the pot.

Drain and rinse the remaining 2 cans of cannellini beans and stir them into the pot along with the salsa verde, 1 cup of the stock, and 1½ teaspoons salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to low, cover, and simmer very gently for 2 hours.

Uncover and stir in the corn, kale, and cream cheese (if using). Cook, stirring occasionally, until the cream cheese is completely melted, the kale is tender, and the chili has thickened to your liking, 4 to 5 minutes more. If you want it even thicker, turn up the heat, stir, and keep going! If it gets too thick, add more stock.
Halve the lime and squeeze in the juice. Stir, then taste and adjust the seasonings. Spoon the chili into whatever’s handy and serve with whatever toppings you like.

name: Beach-Day BBQ-Spiced Chicken Thighs with Peach and Tomato Caprese
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2½ to 3 hours

One summer during college, I nannied for a family in Holden Beach, North Carolina, and they introduced me to beach-day chicken: a tender, succulent, slow-roasted chicken recipe that was practically impossible to mess up. It uses chicken thighs (which are much more forgiving than breasts) and is cooked at such a low temp that if the kids wanted to stay on the beach for an extra hour, it was no biggie for the chicken to stay in the oven an extra hour, too. A peach caprese screams “summer” and will only take you 10 minutes to slice up and throw together while everyone rinses off the sand.

LEARN
The low oven temp slowly concentrates the sugars and spices, forming a sticky glaze without burning—perfect for boneless thighs.

SWAP
Instead of burrata or mozz, use ricotta salata for a salty, sliceable contrast to the peaches, or go with goat cheese for creaminess.

RIFF
Shred the chicken and stuff it into sandwich rolls with the salad and arugula. Add a swipe of mayo for more creaminess. • Make BBQ chicken sandwiches! Place the shredded chicken in a saucepan with a good glug of barbecue sauce, enough to make it really saucy. Warm over medium heat. Make a slaw (see page 77), toast up some sandwich buns, and make sandwiches piled high with BBQ chicken and slaw! • If you love crispy chicken, just broil it for a few minutes at the end!

BULK IT UP
Serve the chicken over buttery herby couscous! Stir together 1¼ cups hot low-sodium stock, 1 cup couscous, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, and ½ teaspoon salt. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes, then stir in 1 cup finely chopped fresh soft green herbs.

EXTRA EXTRA
Add thinly sliced red onion or a splash of white balsamic to the salad for extra tang.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 200–201

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
