ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) ball burrata or fresh mozzarella cheese
ingredients.name: ball burrata or fresh mozzarella cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft green herbs, such as fresh basil and/or mint
ingredients.name: Soft green herbs, such as fresh basil and/or mint

preparationSteps: Make the chicken. Preheat the oven to 250°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil or parchment paper.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and place them in a large bowl.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat or in the microwave in 20-second bursts. Stir in the brown sugar, paprika, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, and some pepper. Pour the mixture over the chicken and toss well to coat evenly. (It’s okay if the butter hardens as you toss; it’ll soften again.)

Arrange the thighs in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 2½ to 3 hours, until deeply browned and tender. Baste the chicken with the pan juices once or twice during cooking, if you remember to.

Toward the end of the chicken cooking time, make the caprese. Halve the lemon and squeeze the juice from 1 half into a shallow serving bowl. Add the balsamic, 2 tablespoons olive oil, a pinch of kosher salt, and a little bit of pepper and swirl the bowl to combine.

Slice the peaches into thin wedges and the big tomatoes into thick wedges, and halve the cherry tomatoes. Add all of them to the bowl. Tear the burrata or slice the mozzarella and add that, too. Toss gently to coat. Let stand at room temperature for a few minutes or until the chicken is ready. Roughly chop enough herbs to make about ½ cup and add them to the salad along with a pinch of flaky salt and stir gently. Taste and add more lemon juice, olive oil, or whatever else you think it needs.

Let the chicken rest at room temperature for 10 minutes before serving. Divide the warm chicken thighs among plates and spoon over some buttery juices from the pan. Spoon the salad on the side, letting the juices mingle with the meat.

name: Cheddar Chipotle Skillet Meatloaf with Cheesy Grits
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 1¼ hours

As a mom of four kids, I rarely find myself alone with my own parents. But I wound up in my hometown of Winston-Salem, North Carolina, for work recently and got to spend a couple of nights with my parents, totally child-free. It was . . . incredible. My mom and I got our nails and hair done, and I grabbed lunch with my dad at Mozelle’s—a wonderful restaurant that has mastered the art of Southern cooking. I ordered the shrimp and grits as I always do, but my dad ordered the meatloaf, which came with cheesy grits—a combo that absolutely blew my mind. Now I only want to eat my meatloaf served over cheesy grits.

TIP
To speed this up, skip the grits—just serve the meatloaf with roasted sweet potatoes! Broil the potatoes to crisp them up at the same time you broil the meatloaf.

SWAP
Any ground meat would work here—try it with ground chicken, the leanest ground beef you can find (in order to limit the grease), or Impossible brand ground “meat.” • Instead of panko, you can use Italian breadcrumbs—or just chop up stale bread.

RIFF
Instead of making the meatloaf, serve chicken thighs with the grits. Trust me. Toss 2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs in 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1½ teaspoons salt, some pepper, and a few shakes of smoked paprika. Throw them on a baking sheet and roast and broil as directed above. To make it spicy, add another 2 chipotle peppers and do not seed them.

BULK IT UP
If you want something green on your plate, arugula tossed with olive oil, a squirt of lemon juice, and a pinch of salt will fit right in. Or serve with a seasonal salad (see Swap, page 68).
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 203–204

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 2 tablespoons adobo from the can
ingredients.name: chipotle pepper (from a can of chipotles in adobo sauce), plus 2 tablespoons adobo from the can

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of soft green herbs, such as fresh cilantro and/or parsley, for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: Handful of soft green herbs, such as fresh cilantro and/or parsley, for serving (optional)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.

Make the meatloaf. Mince the onion and garlic. Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet (preferably nonstick) over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion, garlic, and a little pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, 4 to 5 minutes. Turn off the heat. Add the breadcrumbs and the milk and stir until the breadcrumbs absorb the milk, about 30 seconds.

Add the ground turkey, eggs, chipotle (smash it with a fork against the side of the skillet to break it up) and adobo, cheddar, ½ cup of the ketchup, the paprika, garlic powder, and 2 teaspoons salt and stir to combine. Use a spatula to smoosh it all flat into the skillet, being sure to get the sides down. Slather the remaining 2 tablespoons ketchup over the meatloaf.

Bake the meatloaf for 1¼ hours, or until a thermometer inserted into the center reads 165°F. Turn the broiler to high. If there is a lot of liquid in your skillet, pour it off into the sink, then broil the meatloaf for 2 to 4 minutes, until browned. Remove from the oven and let stand while you make the grits.

Make the grits. Bring 6 cups water and 1½ teaspoons salt to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat. Whisk in the grits and turn down the heat to low. Cook, whisking occasionally, until thickened, about 5 minutes (or per package instructions). Turn off the heat and stir in the cheddar and butter. If the grits get too thick, stir in a splash of water or milk. I like my grits quite thick—like loose mashed potatoes—but everyone likes theirs differently!
Chop the herbs, if you’re using them. Spoon the grits onto plates. Cut slices of meatloaf and lay one on top of the grits on each plate. Garnish with the herbs and serve.

name: Country Captain Casserole
note:
Hands on for: 25 minutes
Walk away for: 1½ hours

My entire childhood, my mom’s go-to entertaining dish was Country Captain, an Indian curry–inspired dish that, lore has it, was introduced to the American South via trade routes with the East India Company. My mom would bust out her silver chafing dishes and make a huge pot of rice, tons of curry chicken, and some plain chicken for us kids, and set out one million little bowls filled with different toppings. She’d set up a huge buffet in our dining room and let everyone go to town. The whole thing took her ALL DAY. But why should this deliciousness be reserved for special occasions that warrant tons of prep time and silver serving dishes?! It shouldn’t! I repackaged Country Captain into a one-pan dish we can all enjoy even when we really don’t feel like cooking (or hosting). But really, don’t skimp on the toppings!

SWAP
You can use boneless thighs or drumsticks; just reduce the cooking time by about 20 minutes. • Use chopped dried apricots or dates instead of golden raisins.

EXTRA EXTRA
For deeper tomato flavor, add a spoonful of tomato paste along with the rice and cook until they begin to stick to the bottom of the pan, then add the tomatoes, raisins, and stock. • Pump up the flavor and toast the coconut flakes in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes before serving. Same for the nuts!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 206

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (14.5-ounce) can diced tomatoes, with their juices
ingredients.name: diced tomatoes, with their juices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Plain full-fat Greek yogurt, mango chutney, sweetened coconut flakes, chopped peanuts or cashews, chopped soft green herbs (such as fresh cilantro), lime wedges
ingredients.name: Plain full-fat Greek yogurt, mango chutney, sweetened coconut flakes, chopped peanuts or cashews, chopped soft green herbs (such as fresh cilantro), lime wedges

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and season both sides with a big pinch of salt and some black pepper. Chop the onion, celery, and bell pepper. Mince the garlic.

Warm the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the chicken thighs skin side down and cook, undisturbed, until they are nicely browned on the bottom and release easily from the pan, about 5 minutes. Flip and cook until browned on the second side, 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a plate and pour off all but 1 tablespoon of the fat from the pot.

Turn down the heat to medium and add the onion, celery, and bell pepper. Cook, stirring with a wooden spoon and scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot, until the vegetables are softened and beginning to brown, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, curry powder, ginger, and 1 teaspoon salt. Cook just until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the rice and stir to coat it in the spices, then add the tomatoes with their juices, the raisins, and the stock. Nestle the chicken thighs on top, skin side up. Turn up the heat to high and bring the mixture to a simmer. Cover and transfer to the oven.
Bake for about 1½ hours, until the rice is tender and the chicken is very soft. If the mixture seems dry, add a splash more stock toward the end of baking. Let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, put out your toppings of choice in serving bowls.
Spoon the chicken and rice into shallow bowls and let everyone pile on whatever toppings they’d like.

name: Fall-Apart Sesame Ginger Beef and Rice with Smashed Cukes
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 3½ to 4 hours

Chuck roast is a big ol’ budget-friendly cut of meat that, when cooked low and slow, turns into a rich and succulent delicacy. Though you can infuse it with any flavors you choose, I keep coming back to this Asian-inspired sesame-ginger version because it’s a home run with—wait for it—every single child in my family. To further solidify this dinner’s place in my kids’ hearts, I typically enlist their help with smashing the cucumbers for the salad. Fun for the whole fam!

LEARN
Salting the cucumbers draws out their moisture and helps prevent the salad from becoming watery. You can skip this step, but the salad won’t be as tasty!

SWAP
Use brisket in place of chuck roast. Cut it into 2-inch pieces and check for doneness beginning at about 3 hours. • Use 1 to 2 English cucumbers in place of the Persian cukes; halve them lengthwise and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds before smashing them as directed.

BULK IT UP
Before adding the beef to the bowls, top the rice with steamed broccoli or sautéed bok choy. Top the whole bowl with a spoonful of chili crisp or pickled jalapeños.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 208–209

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2½ to 3 pounds chuck roast or boneless short ribs
ingredients.name: chuck roast or boneless short ribs

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup packed brown sugar (light or dark)
ingredients.name: packed brown sugar (light or dark)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Make the beef. Preheat the oven to 275°F.
Cut the beef into roughly 2-inch pieces. Pat it dry, then toss in a bowl with the cornstarch to coat.

Slice 2 of the scallions and reserve them for serving. Slice the 4 remaining scallions and place them in a Dutch oven. Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, vinegar, red pepper flakes (if using), sesame seeds, and ⅓ cup water. Use a Microplane to grate the ginger (no need to peel it!) and garlic (yes, peel it) into the pot. Stir well, then add the beef and turn to coat. Cover the pot and transfer to the oven. Bake for 3½ to 4 hours, until the beef is deeply tender and pulls apart easily with a fork. If it’s not shredding easily after 4 hours, keep cooking it! It’s counterintuitive, but I promise you haven’t overcooked it, it needs more time!

Meanwhile, make the smashed cukes. Lay the cucumbers on a cutting board and gently smash them with the flat side of a large knife or a rolling pin until they crack and split. Cut them into bite-size pieces and transfer to a colander set in the sink or over a bowl. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and toss to coat. Let stand to release their liquid while you prepare the rest of the salad.
Finely chop the garlic and chop enough cilantro to make ¼ cup. In a large bowl, stir together the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, granulated sugar, garlic, and red pepper flakes (if using).
Pat the cucumbers dry, then add them to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and cilantro. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

About 30 minutes before the beef is done cooking, make the rice. In a medium saucepan, combine the rice, neutral oil, sesame oil, salt, and 2½ cups water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down the heat to low, cover, and cook until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender, 15 to 18 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for at least 10 minutes or until ready to serve. Fluff with a fork before serving.
Cut the limes into 8 wedges each.

When the beef is done, use a slotted spoon to skim any fat from the surface of the sauce. Use two forks to shred the meat into large pieces and stir them into the sauce in the pan. Remove the cukes from the fridge and give them a stir.

Scoop the rice into shallow bowls and spoon over the beef. Add a generous serving of smashed cukes on the side. Top everything with the reserved sliced scallions and sprinkle with more sesame seeds. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Beef Bourguignon Stew
note:
Hands on for: 20 minutes
Walk away for: 2 to 3 hours

Boeuf bourguignon is one of the many French classics Julia Child put on the radar of American home chefs in the 1960s and ’70s via her cookbook Mastering the Art of French Cooking and her TV show The French Chef. In fact, she cooked boeuf bourguignon in the show’s very first episode! Julia is a role model to everyone who works in food on some level, but I’ve been chipping away at a more streamlined recipe for this iconic stew for years—and it’s finally ready for you. You’ll achieve that classic French stew flavor with much, much less effort, and I’m also giving you the green light to use whatever dry red wine you want (although authentic boeuf bourguignon “requires” pinot noir from Burgundy). Voilà!

EXTRA EXTRA
Instead of stirring the mushrooms into the pot, cook them separately in a pan with 2 tablespoons of butter over medium-high heat. When they’re tender, stir in 1 minced garlic clove before serving.

SWAP
Instead of wine, you can use really good-quality vinegar + water in these proportions: ½ cup red wine, sherry, or apple cider vinegar + 1½ cups water, or ¼ cup balsamic vinegar + 1¾ cups water.

BULK IT UP
I like this stew with crusty bread or garlic bread (see Extra Extra, page 219), but to make it more classically beef bourguignon, serve it over mashed potatoes or buttered noodles.

SHORTCUT
If you think roasting the onions and mushrooms separately is kind of annoying, you can just add them both to the pot for the final hour of cook time. It’ll totally work, but the flavor and texture will not be quite as good.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 212

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup all-purpose flour, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: all-purpose flour, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups low-sodium beef stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium beef stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ cups pinot noir or other dry red wine
ingredients.name: pinot noir or other dry red wine

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 thyme sprigs, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
ingredients.name: thyme sprigs, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces cremini (baby bella) or white mushrooms
ingredients.name: cremini (baby bella) or white mushrooms

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Cut the beef into 2-inch cubes and place it in a large Dutch oven. Sprinkle with the flour, 2 teaspoons salt, and a lot of pepper. Toss to coat the beef well.

Roughly chop the onion and finely chop the garlic and add them, too. Add the tomato paste, stock, wine, Worcestershire, mustard, thyme, and bay leaves. Stir everything to combine, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven. Cook the stew, undisturbed, for 2 hours.

Meanwhile, halve the potatoes and mushrooms. Cut the carrots into 1-inch pieces. Stir the potatoes, mushrooms, carrots, and pearl onions into the stew, then return the pot, covered, to the oven and cook for another hour, until the beef and potatoes are fork-tender.
Meanwhile, chop the parsley leaves and tender stems.

Remove the pot from the oven. Use tongs to fish out and discard the bay leaves and thyme stems from the stew. Stir in a big handful of chopped parsley. Taste and adjust the seasoning, if needed. If you want your stew to be brothier, stir in more beef stock. If you want it to be thicker, stir together 2 tablespoons flour and 2 tablespoons cold water until smooth; stir this into the soup and simmer over medium-low heat until thickened to your liking.
Spoon the stew into bowls and generously sprinkle each serving with parsley.

name: Braised Short Ribs with Creamy Mashed Potatoes
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 4 hours

Short ribs are the ultimate easy-enough-for-a-weeknight, but impressive-enough-for-company meal. You throw everything in a pot for a low and slow braise (basically a long bath in a flavorful liquid), and they become a melt-in-your-mouth, ridiculously flavorful piece of meat. Bonus ease: In this recipe, the mashed potatoes cook in the oven at the same time!

LEARN
The most important step in this entire recipe is picking good short ribs. This is not a job for a delivery shopper—you need to handpick the best, meatiest short ribs. You also want 1½ to 2 inches of meat (1 inch = roughly the size of the top knuckle of your thumb!) with nice marbling (aka white lines of fat!) running throughout. Even the perfect short ribs sometimes have a tough membrane between the bone and the meat—no worries, just discard it after you eat the meat.

SWAP
Replace the short ribs with 2½ to 3 pounds chuck roast, cut into 3-inch pieces. Since there are no bones, which add a ton of flavor, bump up the tomato paste to 2 tablespoons and the low-sodium soy sauce to 3 tablespoons.

BULK IT UP
Serve with Smashed Cukes Salad (page 208) or Cilantro Lime Slaw (page 93).
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 215–216

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2½ cups low-sodium beef stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium beef stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 pounds Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, scrubbed
ingredients.name: Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, scrubbed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2½ cups whole milk, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: whole milk, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Make the short ribs. Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Dice the onion.

Add the onion, garlic, crushed tomatoes, stock, soy sauce, tomato paste, fish sauce, cumin, paprika, 1 teaspoon salt, ½ teaspoon pepper, and the zest of the lime into a Dutch oven and stir to combine.
Season the short ribs with 2 teaspoons salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper. Nestle the ribs down into the tomato sauce bone side up so that the meat is totally submerged.
Cover the pan with a lid or foil and braise for 4 hours.

Make the mashed potatoes. Once the short ribs are in the oven, start prepping your mashed potatoes immediately—they’re also going in the oven to slow roast. Quarter the potatoes (peeled or unpeeled! I like the peels!). Add them, along with the milk, butter, garlic, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, and ½ teaspoon pepper to a wide ovenproof pot or 9 × 13-inch baking dish. The milk should cover the potatoes at least halfway—if it doesn’t, add a little more.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and add the potatoes to the oven to roast with the short ribs for the remaining 3½-ish hours.
When 1 hour remains, remove the lid from the short ribs and flip them over so that the meat side is up and exposed. Return to the oven, uncovered.

Remove the short ribs and potatoes from the oven. Carefully uncover the potatoes and use a measuring cup or ladle to remove most of the excess liquid from the pot, but don’t throw it away. There might be a bit of a milky film on top—that’s okay, it will soften and mash right in. Mash the potatoes and garlic, ideally using a potato masher, but a wooden spoon or the back of a ladle will do the trick. Add some of the liquid back as needed until you reach your perfect mashed potato consistency. Season to taste with more salt and pepper. Potatoes like a lot of salt!
Carefully spoon off and discard the oily fat layer from the top of the short ribs. Cut the zested lime in half and squeeze the juice on top of the ribs.

Thinly slice the scallions (if using). Divide the mashed potatoes among shallow bowls. Use tongs to place the short ribs on top (the bones might slip out; just discard them if they do). Spoon some of the sauce over the top. Sprinkle with the scallions and enjoy.

name: Life-Changing Beef Ragù
note:
Hands on for: 15 minutes
Walk away for: 2½ to 3 hours

While I was in final edits on this book, my family was also in the middle of a move/renovation, and we had a very small baby. I really, really, really didn’t feel like cooking. Thus, this recipe was born. It’s a riff on the famous Marcella Hazan tomato sauce where you simmer canned tomatoes with a halved onion and a stick of butter and somehow it transforms into the most delicious thing you’ve ever tasted. Instead of butter, we’re simmering chuck roast right in the tomatoes, then blending all the delicious fat and juices from the beef into the tomato sauce at the end. This dish debuted in the newsletter and instantly took the internet by storm, so we decided it just had to be in here. We literally inserted it into the already laid-out book, which is why it’s the only recipe that doesn’t have a photo, but I promise it’s worth your while. Just close your eyes and picture perfectly shredded, tender beef swimming in a sea of deeply flavorful tomato sauce, all wrapped around your favorite pasta, with tons of Parm on top. Okay, now go make it.

LEARN
Tomato sauce is sometimes sold as tomato puree. You know you’re picking up the right thing when the only ingredient in it is tomatoes. • If your beef is still tough after 3 hours, it’s not overcooked—it just needs more time for the fat and tendons to break down. Trust the process and keep cooking!

SHORTCUT
Dump 2 (24-ounce) jars of marinara into a large Dutch oven, nestle in the beef, and proceed straight to the oven.

RIFF
Serve it over oven polenta (page 160), or make a lasagna by layering the sauce with no-boil noodles, ricotta, and mozzarella.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 217

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (28-ounce) can whole or diced tomatoes, with their juices
ingredients.name: whole or diced tomatoes, with their juices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound of your favorite pasta (I like mezze rigatoni)
ingredients.name: of your favorite pasta (I like mezze rigatoni)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, for serving
ingredients.name: Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Chopped fresh parsley and/or basil, for serving
ingredients.name: Chopped fresh parsley and/or basil, for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Cut the beef into 6 pieces. Halve the onion. Trim the root end and fronds (the branchy arms) off the fennel bulb and discard, then cut the bulb in half.
In a large Dutch oven, combine the can of tomatoes with their juices, tomato sauce, and vinegar. Nestle in the beef, onion, and fennel. Sprinkle 2 teaspoons salt and the pepper over everything.

Cover the pot, transfer to the oven, and cook for 2½ hours. Pull at the beef with a fork—if it shreds easily, it’s ready. If it doesn’t, cook for another 30 minutes or until it’s fall-apart tender. It might take up to 3 hours depending on your oven, pot, and/or beef.
During the last 20 minutes or so of cooking, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook to al dente according to the package instructions.
Transfer all the beef to a bowl and use tongs or two forks to shred it. Discard any fat that doesn’t shred.

Use an immersion blender to blend the sauce until smooth, tilting the pot as needed to ensure that the blades are submerged at all times—it usually takes me a minute or two to get it really smooth. (Alternatively, transfer everything—except the beef—to a blender and blend on low speed, gradually increasing to high, until smooth, about 45 seconds, or discard the onion and fennel and whisk the tomato sauce until smooth and combined.)
Return the shredded beef to the sauce and toss in your pasta. Stir to combine well. Serve the ragù in low bowls with lots of Parm and fresh parsley on top.

name: Simple Ricotta Meatballs in Red Sauce
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2 hours

My cousin Marlea has made the baked meatball recipe from my first book, Just Married, so many times and for so many of her friends that she designed and printed out recipe cards to send with the meal for when her meal train recipients inevitably ask for the recipe. She’s been begging me to write her a quicker and easier What to Cook-ified version now that we all have a billion kids and a whole lot less time on our hands. I finally nailed the perfect “walk away” version, where the sauce and meatballs cook at the same time in a low oven. The result is a filling, cozy, and ridiculously tasty dinner with very minimal effort.

LEARN
Using ricotta in the meatballs keeps them tender and light, even without eggs or milk, and using butter does something similar in the red sauce, giving it a silky softness that olive oil alone doesn’t. Plus, it gives the sauce a milder flavor than using olive oil alone. • Removing the lid for the final 30 minutes allows the sauce to thicken up more—when the lid is closed it keeps all of the steam trapped in the pot so the sauce can’t evaporate and thicken! Whenever you want to thicken up a soup or sauce: lid off!

SWAP
Use all beef or all pork, or try ground turkey and increase the salt slightly.

BULK IT UP
Serve over cooked spaghetti or cauliflower rice.

EXTRA EXTRA
To make the best garlic bread to serve alongside, halve a baguette or crusty loaf lengthwise and lay it cut side up on a baking sheet. Melt 4 tablespoons (½ stick) unsalted butter with 2 tablespoons olive oil in a small pan over low heat. Add 2 finely chopped garlic cloves and let them sizzle gently for 1 to 2 minutes, then remove from the heat. Brush or spoon the garlic butter over the bread, sprinkle with a little salt, and toast in a 425°F oven for about 10 minutes, until golden and crisp at the edges. Add chopped parsley for a pop of color.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 219

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (28-ounce) cans tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes, with their juices
ingredients.name: tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes, with their juices

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into 8 little slices
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces (1 cup) whole-milk ricotta cheese, plus more for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: whole-milk ricotta cheese, plus more for serving (optional)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup panko or plain breadcrumbs
ingredients.name: panko or plain breadcrumbs

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Focaccia or other crusty bread, for serving
ingredients.name: Focaccia or other crusty bread, for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Mince the garlic and add it, along with the tomato sauce, butter, 1½ teaspoons salt, and ¼ teaspoon pepper into a large Dutch oven and stir to combine.

In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground pork, ricotta, panko, Parm, onion powder, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, 2 teaspoons salt, and some pepper. Use your hands to mix everything together until just combined. Scoop 2 tablespoon–sized portions (like a ping-pong ball!) of the mixture and roll together between your palms to create roughly 2-inch balls.

Drop the meatballs into the tomato mixture, submerging them as much as possible. Use a wooden spoon to really push them down into the mixture to get them all in there and covered! Yes, they’re still totally raw and I know this seems weird!
Cover the pot and transfer to the oven for 1½ hours. Remove the lid and cook for an additional 30 minutes.

Use a spoon or measuring cup to skim some of the fat off the top of the sauce and discard. Gently stir the meatballs and sauce to bring the sauce together—there will still be some fat on top, and we want that to become part of the sauce! Serve the meatballs in bowls with plenty of sauce, slices of bread for scooping, and perhaps an extra dollop of ricotta.

name: Super Simple Carnitas
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2½ hours

Carnitas tacos were and will always be my solution for feeding a big crowd a really impressive-feeling meal with very minimal effort. While you go about your day, the citrusy pork morphs into the most amazing taco filling you’ve ever tasted. Slap it on a table along with a bunch of delicious taco toppings, and dinner—a knockout dinner, to be exact!—is served.

LEARN
Life hack: When you’re at the store, politely ask the butcher to cut your pork (or any kind of meat you need cubed!) for you. If they have the time, I bet they’ll do it! • If you have a gas stove, use tongs to hold the tortillas directly over a medium flame (no pan needed!) for a smoky, charred flavor. Stack them under a clean kitchen towel to keep them warm.

RIFF
If you need or want to skip cutting the meat into pieces, keep it whole: Roast a whole boneless 4-pound butt for about 4 hours, or a bone-in 4-pound butt for about 5 hours. To test for doneness, stick a fork deep into the pork and twist. When it twists easily and pulls out tender meat, you’re done. • Make Cuban sliders! Horizontally halve a 12-pack of King’s Hawaiian Original rolls and slather the bottom halves with mayo and Dijon mustard. Layer on ½ pound thinly sliced ham, 2 cups of carnitas, pickles, and cheese. Close it all up, spritz with cooking spray, and bake in a 350°F oven for 12 to 15 minutes, until warm and melty. Or riff on the riff and use 8 thick slices of any good bread and make 4 separate sandwiches the same way!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 226

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 pounds boneless pork shoulder or butt
ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder or butt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 (6-inch) flour or corn tortillas, or 3 cups warm cooked rice
ingredients.name: flour or corn tortillas, or 3 cups warm cooked rice

ingredients.rawIngredient: Salsa, sour cream, crumbled Cotija or shredded cheddar cheese, pickled red onion, diced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro, diced white onion
ingredients.name: Salsa, sour cream, crumbled Cotija or shredded cheddar cheese, pickled red onion, diced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro, diced white onion

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Cut the pork into 2-inch pieces and place in a Dutch oven or large roasting pan. Season all over with salt. Halve the oranges and the limes and squeeze the juice into the pan. Add the bay leaves and garlic, cover with the lid or tightly with foil, and roast until the meat easily shreds when prodded with a fork, 1½ to 2 hours. Uncover the dish and cook for an additional 30 minutes. If it’s not shredding easily, keep cooking until it is! You’re not going to overcook it, trust me—it actually needs more time to become tender and shreddable.
If using tortillas, 15 minutes before the pork is finished, wrap them in aluminum foil and place in the oven to warm up.
Transfer the Dutch oven to the stovetop over medium-high heat. Break the meat into pieces and stir every few minutes to crisp it up a bit.
Build your tacos or rice bowls with your desired toppings.

name: Sausage, Egg, and Cheese Breakfast Sandwich Casserole
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 75 minutes, plus chilling time

George is a BIG breakfast sandwich guy. Specifically, a toasted buttery English muffin, cheesy scrambled egg, and sausage patty kind of breakfast sandwich guy. We inherited ten chickens when we bought our first home together in Carmel Valley, and the overabundance of eggs during the chickens’ laying months in the spring and summer meant that we were constantly baking frittatas, stratas, and egg casseroles. This breakfast sandwich–inspired casserole was a 2020 pandemic lockdown creation that has stood the test of time in our home. This reheats well—we make it to have for breakfast all week!

SWAP
You can use any kind of cooked breakfast sausage, including patties you’ve chopped up. Turkey sausage or vegetarian sausage crumbles work, too. • Sharp cheddar gives the most flavor, but Monterey Jack, pepper Jack, or crumbled feta are all good.

BULK IT UP
Add chopped fresh spinach to the egg mixture.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 229

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ bunch soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley and/or cilantro
ingredients.name: soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley and/or cilantro

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 pound breakfast sausage or Mexican (fresh) chorizo, casings removed
ingredients.name: breakfast sausage or Mexican (fresh) chorizo, casings removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces grated sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: grated sharp cheddar cheese (2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Hot sauce or ketchup, for serving
ingredients.name: Hot sauce or ketchup, for serving

preparationSteps: Grease a 9 × 13-inch baking dish with olive oil.
Dice the bell peppers and the onion. Coarsely chop enough herbs to make ½ cup.

Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the sausage and cook, breaking it up into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until it has lost most of its pink color, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the peppers and onion along with a pinch of salt and a grind or two of black pepper. Cook until the sausage is browned and the vegetables are tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the chopped herbs.

Meanwhile, tear half the English muffins into bite-size pieces and scatter them across the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Top with half the cooked sausage mixture and about half the cheese. Repeat with the remaining English muffins, sausage mixture, and cheese.

In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, 1½ teaspoons salt, and some black pepper. Pour the egg mixture evenly over the baking dish, then use a spatula to press lightly on the top to help everything submerge. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight and up to 24 hours.
The next morning, preheat the oven to 325°F. Remove the casserole from the fridge and set it on the counter.
Uncover the strata and bake for about 75 minutes, until puffed, golden brown, and bubbling at the edges. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

Cut into slices and serve warm, with hot sauce on the side. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days; warm the slices in a 375°F oven for 10 minutes or microwave in 30-second increments until hot before serving.

name: Pineapple Jerk Ribs with Cheddar Corn Muffins
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 3 to 3¼ hours

PSA: Ribs are weeknight-friendly! Another PSA: Not all “jerk” dishes are spicy! Though many store-bought jerk seasonings are indeed quite hot, we’re skipping store-bought tonight and instead are using a well-rounded mix of spices from Jamaica’s traditional seasoning blend—allspice, ginger, sugar, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper—so that the sweet and earthy elements temper the heat. The muffins are easy to whip up—and they use a hack to avoid dirtying two bowls like most baked goods typically require. They also allow us to make the most of a can of pineapple bits, which we’ll pull from for both the glaze and muffins.

TIP
Double the cayenne on the ribs if you’d like these to be spicy.

LEARN
Removing the membrane—the thin, silvery skin on the bone side of the ribs—makes all the difference for tender ribs! If the bone side is more white than silvery, your store or butcher already did this. Otherwise, use a knife to loosen one corner, then grab it with a paper towel and pull it off completely. (The membrane might break into multiple strips—that’s normal!)

SHORTCUT
If the muffins are too much for tonight, serve your ribs with boiled corn on the cob slathered with butter, and whip up boxed cornbread (Jiffy is my go-to).

RIFF
Add some tang to the muffins by using ½ cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt and ½ cup whole milk in place of the cup of milk. (If using yogurt, also add ½ teaspoon baking soda to the dry ingredients.)

EXTRA EXTRA
Make some lime butter to serve with the corn muffins: In a small bowl, mash together 1 stick softened or room-temperature unsalted butter with the zest of 1 lime, the juice of ½ lime, ½ teaspoon honey, and a pinch of salt.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 232–233

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 (2-pound) racks baby back pork ribs, membrane removed
ingredients.name: racks baby back pork ribs, membrane removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper or red pepper flakes
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper or red pepper flakes

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup barbecue sauce (I like Stubb’s)
ingredients.name: barbecue sauce (I like Stubb’s)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 tablespoons pineapple juice, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: pineapple juice, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon light brown sugar or honey
ingredients.name: light brown sugar or honey

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup drained canned pineapple chunks in juice
ingredients.name: drained canned pineapple chunks in juice

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 ounces shredded sharp cheddar cheese (¾ cup)
ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese (¾ cup)

preparationSteps: Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and preheat to 275°F.
Make the ribs. Place each rack on its own large (large enough to enclose around the ribs) piece of heavy-duty foil. Pat the ribs completely dry.

In a small bowl, stir together the brown sugar, allspice, ginger, paprika, cayenne, 1½ teaspoons salt, and some black pepper. Generously coat both sides of the rib racks with the rub, massaging it in and pressing to adhere. Arrange the ribs meat side up on their foil and wrap each up tightly to form 3 sealed packages and place on a baking sheet.
Bake the ribs on the lower rack for 2½ to 3 hours, until the meat is tender and pulls away from the bones easily.

Meanwhile, make the glaze. In a small saucepan, stir together the barbecue sauce, pineapple juice, and brown sugar. Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 3 to 5 minutes. Taste and add the vinegar if you’d like some tang in there. And if it’s not pineapple-y enough, add another splash or two of pineapple juice. Remove the pan from the heat and let cool.

A few minutes before the ribs are ready to come out of the oven, get started on the muffins. Break up any larger pieces of pineapple and pat it all dry. Mince the jalapeño, removing and discarding the seeds if you want less heat. Coat a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray.

When the ribs are tender, remove them from the oven and carefully unwrap them (watch out for hot steam!). You can leave them on the foil; just make sure they’re fully uncovered. Turn up the oven temperature to 450°F.

Make the muffins. In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, and melted butter. Add the cornmeal, flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt in a pile right on top, and use your fingers to thoroughly pinch all of the dry ingredients together, then stir them into the wet ingredients until just combined. Gently stir in the pineapple, jalapeño, and cheese.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each one about three-quarters of the way. Bake on the lower rack for 12 to 15 minutes, until the muffins are golden and a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.

Before serving, stir the glaze and spoon it all over the meaty side of the ribs. Roast on the upper rack until caramelized, 10 to 15 minutes. Cut the racks into individual ribs by slicing between the bones. Serve a big platter of the ribs with another big platter of the warm muffins.

name: Slow-Baked Skillet Lasagna
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2 hours

If you’re surprised to find a lasagna recipe in a book about what to cook when you don’t feel like cooking, I get it. Traditional recipes for lasagna are quite involved—you’ve got to boil noodles, cook a meat sauce, make a cheese layer, then methodically assemble it all. That said, I do think every home cook should have a lasagna recipe in their repertoire. It’s such a home run for any occasion when you’re entertaining, and always makes for a very special, cozy dinner at home. So let’s do this! But we’ll do it the WTC way, using no-bake noodles, assembling in the same cast-iron skillet we cook the meat in to eliminate an unnecessary dirty dish, and utilizing sausage’s built-in flavor to keep the ingredient list short.

SHORTCUT
Skip step 4 (where you make a homemade tomato sauce) entirely—just use 2 (24-ounce) jars of marinara sauce in place of the canned tomatoes and seasonings.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 235

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces white or cremini (baby bella) mushrooms
ingredients.name: white or cremini (baby bella) mushrooms

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup fresh basil, plus more for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: fresh basil, plus more for serving (optional)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 ounces mild or hot Italian sausage, casings removed
ingredients.name: mild or hot Italian sausage, casings removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¾ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (3 ounces)
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (3 ounces)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 275°F.
Finely chop the mushrooms and onion. Mince the garlic. Finely chop the basil (if using).

Warm the olive oil in a high-sided 12-inch cast-iron skillet or a shallow Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the mushrooms, onion, and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have softened and all the liquid has evaporated, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until no longer pink, about 5 minutes.

Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, oregano, red pepper flakes, and 1½ teaspoons salt. Turn up the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil. Turn down the heat to medium and cook until the sauce has thickened and has only about ¼ cup of “watery” liquid on top, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove the skillet from the heat. Transfer the tomato sauce to a medium bowl, leaving a very thin layer to coat the bottom of the skillet.
Meanwhile, in a separate medium bowl, stir together the ricotta, 1 cup of the mozzarella, ½ cup of the Parm, basil (if using), ½ teaspoon salt, and some black pepper.

Place 4 or 5 noodles over the thin layer of sauce in the skillet, breaking them and overlapping them as needed to form an evenish layer. Spread one-third of the ricotta mixture over the noodles. Repeat the layering with about 2 cups of the tomato sauce, 4 noodles, and half the remaining ricotta; and then once more, using another 2 cups tomato sauce, 3 or 4 noodles, and all the remaining ricotta. Top with the remaining tomato sauce. Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup mozzarella and ¼ cup Parm over top. Cover the dish with foil so that it is loose enough on top that it does not touch the cheese, but is tightly secured all around the edge of the pan.

Bake for about 2 hours, until the noodles are tender and the lasagna is bubbling all the way through. Remove the foil for the last 20 minutes to lightly brown the top. Let it rest for 20 to 30 minutes. Thinly slice some more basil, if using, and sprinkle over the top, then slice and serve.

name: Fisherman’s Stew with Smoky Garlic Mayonnaise
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 1¼ to 1½ hours

This recipe is my take on bouillabaisse, a French fish-and-veggie stew that sounds intimidating both to cook and to pronounce, but is truly so doable for any home chef, even if you’re a newbie in the kitchen. The hardest part of this whole shebang is scrubbing and debearding the mussels, but if you’re buying your seafood from a specialty fish shop, they will very likely do that for you, if you ask! (And if not, no worries, I’ve got you in the Learn note.) Other than that, you’re just cooking a simple veggie stew then plopping in some fish and mussels toward the end—they will poach and steam, respectively, in and on top of your stewy base until they’re cooked to perfection. And don’t even think about skipping the smoky garlic mayo! It really adds to the flavor and experience here. Now say it with me: boo-yuh-BESS. Yes!

TIP
Most grocery stores carry clam juice; it’s usually near the canned tuna and sardines or in the soup and stock aisle. You can find shelf-stable cartons of seafood stock near the other stocks or in freezer packs.

LEARN
To debeard mussels, cover them with cold water in a bowl for several minutes to make them spit out any grit. Then grab a mussel in one hand with a kitchen towel to keep it from slipping, and with another kitchen towel, clean it off. If you see a little hairy “beard” poking out of the shell, grab it with the towel and yank it out.

SHORTCUT
If you don’t have a full hour-plus to simmer the soup base, cut the potatoes into ¼-inch dice. Simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes, then proceed as written. The soup flavor won’t be as deep, but it’ll still be delicious!

EXTRA EXTRA
At the start, stir 1 pinch saffron threads (about 10 threads) into 2 tablespoons warm water and set aside. Just before adding the fish to the stew, stir in the saffron with its soaking water. • Use a vegetable peeler to remove a long strip of orange zest and add it to the pot with the spices; remove it from the stew before serving. • To make the quick garlic mayo into a quick rouille, which is traditional with classic bouillabaisse, add a few threads of saffron to the mayonnaise.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 236–237

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups clam juice or low-sodium seafood stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: clam juice or low-sodium seafood stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 12 ounces fresh or thawed frozen white fish (cod, tilapia, or haddock)
ingredients.name: fresh or thawed frozen white fish (cod, tilapia, or haddock)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 large loaf sourdough bread or baguette (or any good bread), sliced
ingredients.name: sourdough bread or baguette (or any good bread)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Handful of fresh parsley, for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: Handful of fresh parsley, for serving (optional)

preparationSteps: Finely chop the shallots. Mince the garlic. Cut the potatoes into ½-inch pieces.

Warm 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the shallots and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in all but 1 teaspoon of the garlic, the thyme, ½ teaspoon of the paprika, the turmeric, ½ teaspoon salt, and the red pepper flakes (if using) and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the potatoes, crushed tomatoes, and clam juice. Increase the heat to medium-high, bring to a gentle boil, then stir and partially cover the pot. Turn down the heat to low to maintain a very gentle simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender and the flavors are well combined, 60 to 75 minutes.
Just before the soup is ready, cut the fish into 1-inch pieces.

Nestle the fish into the liquid and scatter the mussels over the top. Cover the pot and cook over medium heat until the fish is flaky and the mussels have opened, 8 to 10 minutes. Discard any mussels that don’t open. Taste and add more salt if needed.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, reserved 1 teaspoon garlic, remaining ½ teaspoon paprika, and ¼ teaspoon salt. Halve 1 lemon and squeeze in the juice from 1 half. Taste and add more salt and/or lemon juice if it needs it.
Position a rack 6 inches from the broiler heat source and turn the broiler to high.
Arrange the bread slices in an even layer on a rimmed baking sheet and brush both sides with a decent amount of olive oil. Broil until golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, cut the remaining lemon into 8 wedges and chop the parsley (if using).

To serve, ladle the stew into bowls (make sure you get a little bit of everything!), plop on a spoonful of the garlic mayo, and sprinkle with the chopped parsley (if using). Serve with the toasted bread on the side for dipping and the lemon wedges for squeezing. Don’t forget to place a big bowl or a few smaller bowls on the table for the empty shells!

name: Risotto alla Vodka with Herby Roast Shrimp
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 80 to 100 minutes

Man, is there anything quite as universally loved as a really good vodka sauce? Once when I had some vodka left over in the fridge, I stirred it into the risotto I was eating on a whim, and George and I both lost our minds over it. Rich and creamy risotto coated with rich and creamy and tangy vodka sauce?! Honestly, I can’t believe I hadn’t thought of it sooner. I knew I’d want to re-create it, so I turned it into a one-pot baked risotto that requires zero standing over the stove and stirring. While it roasts, we also roast shrimp to serve on top for a truly stunning meal with very little effort.

LEARN
Don’t rinse the rice when you’re making risotto! The starch on the surface is what gives risotto its creamy goodness as the grains rub together during cooking.

RIFF
Have pesto in the fridge? Toss the shrimp in a few tablespoons of that to make roasted pesto shrimp.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 239

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
ingredients.name: plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: red pepper flakes, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (4- to 6-ounce) tube or can tomato paste
ingredients.name: or can tomato paste

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 cups low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds peeled and deveined extra-large (21/30) shrimp (tails on or off)
ingredients.name: peeled and deveined extra-large shrimp (tails on or off)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)
ingredients.name: Italian seasoning, store-bought or homemade (see page 20)

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Position one rack 4 inches from the broiler heat source and another rack in the lower third of the oven and preheat to 275°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, and chop enough parsley to make ⅓ cup, plus more for serving.

Warm ¼ cup of the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or braiser over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion and ½ teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add the tomato paste and rice and stir until they start to stick to the skillet, 1 to 2 minutes, then pour in the vodka and use a wooden spoon to scrape up all the stuck-on bits from the bottom of the pan. When the vodka has evaporated, about 1 minute, stir in the half-and-half and 3 cups of the stock. Turn up the heat to high, then stir again to scrape up anything that’s sticking to the pan.
Cover the pot and bake on the lower rack of the oven for 75 to 90 minutes, until the rice is very tender and the mixture looks thick and creamy when stirred.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, toss together the shrimp, the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, the Italian seasoning, and ½ teaspoon salt. Set aside to marinate at room temperature while the risotto cooks. When the risotto is ready, remove the pot from the oven. Turn the broiler to high.
Spread the shrimp on the prepared baking sheet in an even layer. Place under the broiler until the shrimp are pink and opaque throughout, 5 to 7 minutes, flipping them once during cooking.

Meanwhile, uncover the risotto and return the pot to the stovetop over medium-low heat. Stir in 1 cup stock along with the Parm and ⅓ cup parsley. Cook, stirring, until the stock is completely absorbed, about 1 minute. Add more stock as needed, ¼ cup at a time, until you’ve achieved your perfect risotto. Taste and add more salt if you’d like.
Spoon the risotto into bowls, placing a few shrimp on top. Sprinkle with parsley, Parm, and more red pepper flakes if you’d like a little more heat.

name: Red Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk and Lime
note:
Hands on for: 20 minutes
Walk away for: 1½ to 2 hours

Oooh, this soup. It’s an inauthentic take on dal (a spiced Indian dish made from lentils) that’s filling in a satisfying stick-to-your-ribs kind of way, and yet because it’s vegetarian and filled with bright flavors—soul-warming spices like turmeric and cumin, lots of zesty ginger and lime juice, and sweet, creamy coconut milk—it doesn’t feel heavy. I’d be as happy to eat this in August as I would be in the depths of winter! The first time I ever cooked this meal, I repeatedly burned my mouth because I simply could not wait for it to cool down. Don’t be surprised if your willpower (and brain) bow down to its flavor! Also don’t be surprised when your lentils fall apart during cooking. Unlike green or brown lentils, which keep their shape when cooked, red lentils break down, giving whatever dish they’re in a soft, thick, and creamy bite.

BULK IT UP
Stir in chopped kale, baby spinach, or a cup of cooked rice at the end.

EXTRA EXTRA
Top with basil (Thai or sweet!), chili crisp, or toasted coconut flakes. • For an extra-silky texture, blend part of the soup and stir it back in.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 240

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 cups low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt
ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: Crushed pita chips, bagel chips, corn chips, or croutons, for serving
ingredients.name: Crushed pita chips, bagel chips, corn chips, or croutons, for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Dice the onion and finely chop the carrots.

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion, carrots, and ½ teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring, until softened but not browned, about 8 minutes. Use a Microplane to grate in the garlic and ginger (no need to peel it!), then add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne (if using). Cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the lentils, coconut milk, and stock. Turn up the heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to the oven.

Bake for 1½ to 2 hours, until the lentils are fully broken down and the soup is thick and creamy when stirred together. Stir it once or twice while it’s cooking if you think of it; if the mixture gets too thick, add a little more stock or water.

Meanwhile, chop enough cilantro to make ¼ cup, plus more for serving. In a small bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, ¼ cup chopped herbs, and a pinch of salt. Using a Microplane, zest 1 lime directly into the bowl, then halve the lime and squeeze in the juice from 1 half. Taste and add more salt or lime juice to taste.

Remove the pot from the oven. Using a Microplane, grate the zest of 1 lime into the pot, then halve the lime and squeeze in the juice of 1 half. Stir well to blend. Taste and add more lime juice or salt if you think it needs it. Cut the remaining lime into 8 wedges.

Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Top each bowl with a dollop of herbed lime yogurt and a small handful of crushed pita chips. Sprinkle some more chopped cilantro on top if you’d like. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Triple Tomato Oven Orzo
note:
Hands on for: 15 minutes
Walk away for: 1½ hours

This is the best kind of weeknight dinner: almost no chopping required. Cherry tomatoes go in whole, sun-dried tomatoes come straight from the jar, and everything bakes together into a bright, savory one-pot meal. The result tastes like you put in way more effort than you did—which is exactly the point.

BULK IT UP
Stir in two big handfuls of chopped spinach or kale when you add the orzo. • I love adding precooked Italian chicken sausage when I want to incorporate protein. You can either slice it, brown it in a pan with a little bit of oil, and serve it over top; or just slice it and stir it in with the Parm in step 4 to warm through.

RIFF
Add 6 minced garlic cloves. • Give it an olive-y spin: Stir in ½ cup tapenade and omit half the salt from the orzo.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 243

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium vegetable stock, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup drained jarred julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes
ingredients.name: drained jarred julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan (2 ounces), plus more for serving

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.

Add the stock, orzo, cherry tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste, garlic powder, 1½ teaspoons salt, and some black pepper to a 9 × 13-inch baking dish or Dutch oven. Nestle the block of feta and the stick of butter right down in there. Cover.
Bake for 1 hour. While the orzo bakes, finely chop the parsley and basil.

Remove the dish from the oven and stir in the Parm and half the chopped herbs and use your spoon to smash the cherry tomatoes (if they haven’t already burst). Add a splash of water or stock if needed to loosen things up—this will just depend on your oven.
Scoop the orzo into bowls and garnish with the remaining chopped herbs and more Parm.

name: Farro Fazool with Herby-Garlicky Croutons
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2 hours

Pasta e fagioli—which translates to “pasta and beans”—is a warming and delicious Italian soup made from modest pantry ingredients, and it’s what inspired this meal. While that dish typically uses a short pasta shape like ditalini, I wanted a version with farro to give it some extra fiber, protein, and bulk (all that’s to say . . . it helps keep you full for longer). I named it “farro fazool” because pasta e fagioli is sometimes called “pasta fazool” in a very specific Italian New Yorker accent, and I just find it so endearing. Promise me you won’t sleep on those croutons!

SWAP
You can use any kind of dried beans here. • If you don’t have (or don’t like) rosemary, dried oregano or dried Italian seasoning are great choices.

BULK IT UP
Stir in a few handfuls of chopped kale or escarole during the fazool’s last 20 minutes in the oven.

EXTRA EXTRA
Cut the rind off a big chunk of Parm and toss it in, then discard it with the bay leaf.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 244

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup dried cannellini, great northern, or red kidney beans
ingredients.name: dried cannellini, great northern, or red kidney beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 rosemary or sage sprig, or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
ingredients.name: rosemary or sage sprig, or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 cups low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Make the fazool. Place the beans in a colander. Rake your fingers through them and pick out any pebbles or shriveled beans. Rinse thoroughly. (You don’t need to soak the beans, truly.)
Dice the onion, carrots, and celery. Mince the garlic.

Warm 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion, carrots, celery, and a big pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and beginning to turn golden, about 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until the garlic is fragrant and the tomato paste is darker in color and sticking to the bottom of the pan, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the beans, farro, rosemary, and bay leaf. Pour in the stock. Turn up the heat to high and bring the soup to a rolling boil. Cover the pot and transfer to the oven.

Bake the fazool until the beans and farro are very soft and tender when you bite into them (this is the only way to tell if they’re ready), about 2 hours, stirring once or twice if you think of it. Add more stock or water if it gets too thick—it should be stew-like and scoopable, not dry.

Meanwhile, make the croutons. Tear or cut the bread into chunky cubes (you should have about 4 cups cubed bread). Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the bread and cook, flipping the pieces often, until golden and crispy, 6 to 8 minutes; drizzle more olive oil in if the bread looks thirsty. During the last minute of cooking, sprinkle over the rosemary, garlic powder, and a big pinch of salt and toss to coat.
Remove the fazool from the oven and immediately stir in the Parm and some black pepper. Use tongs to fish out and discard the bay leaf. Taste and add more salt and pepper if it needs it.
Spoon the fazool into bowls, pile the croutons on top, and grate lots of Parm over top, then serve!

name: Creamy White Beans with Fennel, Greens, and Smoky Toasts
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2½ to 3 hours

Jillian, a dear friend who helps me run the What to Cook ship, is a bean queen—whenever we go out to eat, if there’s a black bean burger, bean quesadilla, or fancy bean anything on the menu, she’s getting it. So it was no surprise—yet the most delightful treat—when she showed up at my door with an iteration of these creamy, dreamy white beans days after I gave birth to Tavish. Cooking dried beans takes time, sure, but it’s beyond easy and, with the right aromatics (like we have here), will make you an enthusiastic member of Team Bean.

TIP
If you like a creamier consistency, mash a few beans against the side of the pot before adding the greens.

LEARN
Canned beans are a gift to busy people everywhere. That said, if you’ve never cooked with dried beans, you should know: There really is a difference. Cooked dried beans have a firmer, non-mushy texture, they can take on a richer flavor if cooked in a tasty broth like we’re doing here, they are totally free of any additives, and they are so much cheaper (which is saying a lot, since canned beans are already cheap!).

SHORTCUT
No time to wait? Canned beans were made for that! Like, literally. Only use 5 cups of stock, add it to the pot with the Parm rind and bay leaf, and bring to a boil as directed. Turn down the heat, partially cover the pot, and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes. When you stir in the chopped greens, add 2 (15-ounce) cans cannellini or great northern beans, drained and rinsed, and continue with the recipe as written.

SWAP
Any kind of dried white bean will work here, including chickpeas.

BULK IT UP
Add diced potatoes or a handful of small pasta noodles during the last 30 minutes of cooking to turn it into a bean stew.

EXTRA EXTRA
At the start, stir 1 pinch of saffron threads (about 10 threads) into 2 tablespoons warm water and set aside. Stir the saffron with its soaking water into the beans when you add the greens.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 246–247

ingredients.rawIngredient: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ cups dried cannellini or great northern beans
ingredients.name: dried cannellini or great northern beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 cups low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 baguette or loaf of crusty bread, cut into ½-inch-thick slices
ingredients.name: baguette or loaf of crusty bread

preparationSteps: Make the beans. Preheat the oven to 325°F.

Cut the fennel in half lengthwise. Use a small knife to cut out and discard the triangular core at the base of each half. Dice the fennel (save the wispy fronds if you want to be fancy with your garnish) and the onion. Mince the garlic. Stem and roughly chop the chard and set aside. Cut the rind off the Parm. Grate (or grind—see Shortcut, page 78) ¾ cup Parm; reserve the cheese and the rind separately.

Warm the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the fennel, onion, and a pinch of kosher salt. Cook, stirring, until softened and beginning to brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until fragrant, 1 minute more.

Rinse the beans and pluck out and discard anything non-bean-looking. Add the beans to the pot along with the thyme, bay leaf, Parm rind, and stock. Turn up the heat to high and bring to a boil. Cover and transfer to the oven.

Bake the beans for 2 to 2½ hours, until tender (taste them to check!). Remove the pot from the oven and use tongs to fish out and discard the bay leaf and Parm rind. Stir in the chopped chard. Return the uncovered pot to the oven, and cook until the greens are wilted and tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove the beans from the oven and turn the broiler to high.

Make the smoky toasts. Arrange the sliced bread on a rimmed baking sheet in an even layer and coat both sides with a decent layer of olive oil. Sprinkle one side lightly with paprika and a pinch of flaky salt. Broil until golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes per side.

Meanwhile, grate the zest of 1 lemon directly into the pot of beans, then halve it and squeeze in the juice. Stir in the Parm and some black pepper. Taste and season with more kosher salt and lemon juice.
Ladle the beans into bowls and grate some more Parm over the top. Serve with the smoky toast.

name: Farrotto with Roasted Summer Vegetables
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 1¼ to 1½ hours

Cool, crisp, no-cook salads tend to be the stars of summer, but this meal, I promise, is worth turning your oven on for. With time and heat, summer vegetables—even mild-tasting ones like zucchini and yellow squash—transform into sweet and jammy, buttery and umami-rich bites of heaven. We’re combining those with farro cooked like risotto (hence “farrotto”) and some dairy for good measure, for the meatless Monday summer supper of my dreams. Eat this for dinner on the patio, or prep it for a week of lunches, reheated or served cold!

LEARN
Semi-pearled farro works best here because it softens gently without getting mushy.

SWAP
Swap the Parmesan for 4 ounces goat cheese or 8 ounces brine-packed feta (but add the feta before you transfer the pot to the oven so it can get creamy). • Don’t feel like opening a whole bottle of wine just to use ½ cup? Pour 2 tablespoons light vinegar (champagne or aged sherry vinegar would be great here) into a ½-cup measure, fill it the rest of the way with water, and use that instead.

EXTRA EXTRA
Drizzle each serving with balsamic glaze or a spoonful of pesto.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 251

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup dry white wine (I like sauvignon blanc)
ingredients.name: dry white wine (I like sauvignon blanc)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 5 cups low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: low-sodium vegetable stock or chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 tablespoons (½ stick) unsalted butter, at room temperature
ingredients.name: unsalted butter, at room temperature

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan cheese (2 ounces), plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Chopped soft green herbs, for serving
ingredients.name: Chopped soft green herbs, for serving

preparationSteps: Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and preheat to 325°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Finely chop the small yellow onion and the garlic. Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in the farro and cook, stirring, until slightly toasted, 1 to 2 minutes.

Pour in the white wine and cook until mostly evaporated, 3 to 4 minutes. Add 4 cups of the stock, 1 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Turn up the heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer. Cover with the lid and transfer to the lower rack of the oven.
Bake the farrotto until the farro is tender and the liquid has been absorbed, 1 hour and 15 minutes to 1½ hours total.

Immediately after you put the farro in the oven, prep the vegetables, placing them on the prepared baking sheet as you go. Cut the zucchini and yellow squash in half lengthwise and then crosswise into ½-inch-thick half circles. Slice the bell pepper into ½-inch-thick strips. Cut the red onion into 1-inch-thick wedges. Add the whole cherry tomatoes and drizzle over 2 tablespoons olive oil, a couple of generous pinches of salt, and some black pepper. Toss to coat everything evenly.
Transfer to the upper rack of the oven and bake for about 75 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and lightly browned in spots and the tomatoes have collapsed.

When the farrotto is done, remove the pot from the oven. Carefully remove the lid and stir in the butter, Parm, and ½ cup stock. Add the rest of the stock as needed until the farrotto is really creamy. Halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice from 1 half. Stir, then taste and add more salt or lemon juice as desired.
Scoop the farrotto into bowls and top each serving with a spoonful of roasted vegetables. Sprinkle with more Parm and chopped herbs.

name: Chilled Summer Tomato Soup with Garlicky Toast
note:
Hands on for: 30 minutes
Walk away for: 2 hours

When I was eighteen, I nannied in the mountains of North Carolina for the Bassett family, my wonderful neighbors from Winston-Salem, North Carolina. It was a dream job: While the kids went to camp, Bartlett (their mother) and I would cook lengthy recipes and sneak in hikes. After long, fun family dinners, I’d go out all night, Dirty Dancing–style, with the other staff members on the mountain—but that’s a story for another time. Bartlett and I would make a massive batch of gazpacho every week and have it for lunch, snack, appetizers, literally all day every day, all summer long. A few years later, I studied abroad in Spain and learned about salmorejo, a chilled tomato soup that is a cousin to gazpacho—the key difference being that you blend bread into salmorejo to thicken it. Over the years I’ve also started blending in a little Greek yogurt, too, which is customary absolutely nowhere, but very delicious. This is the easiest soup of all time to make, and the most craveable thing to eat on a hot summer day. The base recipe starts with the bare minimum of everything so you can adjust based on how flavorful your tomatoes and peppers are. Add, blend, taste. Add more, blend more, taste more.

TIP
Don’t overcrowd the blender. You can certainly do this in more than two batches if necessary; just combine it in one place after it’s all blended.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 252

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 to 5 slices of good crusty bread (such as sourdough or a baguette), plus more if needed
ingredients.name: of good crusty bread (such as sourdough or a baguette), plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ⅔ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt
ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons aged sherry vinegar or apple cider vinegar, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: aged sherry vinegar or apple cider vinegar, plus more if needed

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 thick slices crusty bread, such as sourdough
ingredients.name: thick slices crusty bread, such as sourdough

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 teaspoons dried rosemary, sage, or oregano
ingredients.name: dried rosemary, sage, or oregano

preparationSteps: Make the soup. Roughly chop the tomatoes and add half of them to a blender. Roughly chop the bell peppers and add half of them, too. Tear or chop the bread (you want just shy of 5 cups) and add half to the blender. Cut the onion into 2 equalish pieces and add 1 piece to the blender. Add a garlic clove. Pour in ⅓ cup of the olive oil, ¼ cup of the Greek yogurt, 1 teaspoon of the vinegar, ½ teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Blend on high speed until smooth, about a minute.
Pour the soup into a large airtight container and repeat with the remaining ingredients. Whisk the batches together thoroughly. Taste and add more salt, pepper, vinegar, or garlic.
Chill the soup in the refrigerator, right in the container, for at least 2 hours before serving. Store for up to 5 days.

When you’re ready to serve, make the garlicky toast. Warm ¼ cup of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add half the bread and cook, flipping the pieces often, until golden and crisp, 6 to 8 minutes; drizzle more olive oil in if the bread looks thirsty. During the last minute of cooking, sprinkle over half the rosemary, garlic powder, and a big pinch of salt. Transfer the toast to a cooling rack or baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining oil, bread, and seasonings.
Taste the soup again (things taste different when they’re chilled) and add more salt, pepper, or vinegar to pump up the flavor.
Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish each serving with a slice of toast, a drizzle of olive oil, and a sprinkle of black pepper.

name: One-Pot Lentils and Rice with Sausage
note:
Hands on for: 20 minutes
Walk away for: 1½ hours

There are two kinds of people in this world: those who see lentils and think “yum,” and those who see lentils and think “meh.” If you’re the latter, I’d bet it’s because you haven’t had a perfectly cooked and properly seasoned version of the legume, and this meal will teach you how to do just that. It’s inspired in part by mujaddara, a Middle Eastern comfort food made with rice (or another grain), lentils, cumin, coriander, and fried onion, plus lots and lots of creamy, delicious labneh or yogurt.
