We’re tapping store-bought fried onions (a gift to home cooks everywhere) and harissa (it’s not traditional, but trust me, it works!), and adding sausage (this is also atypical—mujaddara’s almost always vegetarian!) for extra flavor and bulk.

RIFF
Make the rice and lentils kinda slutty by adding 8 ounces of cream cheese or 1 cup heavy cream when you remove the pot from the oven.

BULK IT UP
About 10 minutes before the rice is ready in the oven, uncover and add a pound of frozen green beans, peas, or mixed vegetables. Don’t stir! Proceed as directed, incorporating the vegetables with the onions when you fluff the rice.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 255

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1½ pounds mild or spicy Italian sausage, casings removed
ingredients.name: mild or spicy Italian sausage, casings removed

ingredients.rawIngredient: ½ cup dried French green lentils, rinsed
ingredients.name: dried French green lentils

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups store-bought crispy fried onions (about 5 ounces)
ingredients.name: store-bought crispy fried onions (about 5 ounces)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Labneh or plain full-fat Greek yogurt
ingredients.name: Labneh or plain full-fat Greek yogurt

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.

Warm the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the sausage and cook, breaking it up into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until browned and just cooked through, about 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, onion powder, garlic powder, and paprika. Cook until very fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add the rice and lentils to the pot and stir to coat in the spices. Stir in 1½ teaspoons salt and some pepper. Stir in the stock and harissa. Turn up the heat to high to bring to a boil, then cover the pot.
Bake for about 75 minutes, until the rice and lentils are very tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Let the pot stand, still covered, for 10 minutes before serving.
Meanwhile, chop the parsley leaves and tender stems and cut the lemon into 8 wedges.

Scatter half the crispy onions on top of the rice and lentils, then use a fork to fluff the rice and incorporate the onions. Serve warm, topping each serving with the remaining crispy onions, parsley, and a giant dollop of labneh. Pass around the lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: grilled bbq chicken and peach chop
note:
Cook time: 30 minutes active + 30 minutes to 4 hours for marinating the chicken

• I don’t have a grill: You can cook the chicken, peaches, and corn inside using a grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat instead. Or, use the following instructions…

• What to cook when you really don’t feel like cooking/store-bought shortcut: Do what we do in the cookbook version! Skip grilling altogether. Use precooked chicken (see the headnote above the recipe for ideas!), a can of rinsed and drained white corn (or thawed frozen corn) in place of the fresh corn, and skip grilling the peaches.

• Feeding kids: I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again — salads are a very family-friendly meal! Just serve it deconstructed for the kids. Before you toss the salad, pull out some chopped chicken, peach, corn kernels, avocado, etc. for their plates. Serve BBQ sauce (or ketchup if they prefer it) for dipping the chicken.

• Feeding a crowd/take it to a party: This recipe is very easy to double (though you will need to use two bowls!). If you haven’t watched it yet, I share my favorite trick for taking salads to a party in this episode of What to Cook the show.

• Make ahead: This recipe can be totally cooked a few hours ahead of time. You can keep the dressing at the bottom of the bowl with the beans, add the greens on top, then the chicken, corn, and peaches (once they’ve all cooled!) and other veg, tightly wrap the bowl with plastic wrap, and store it in the fridge. When you’re ready to eat, add the chips and toss.

• Love your leftovers: Leftovers of each component will keep for up to 4 days stored in airtight containers. Dressed salad greens would get mushy though, so only dress as much as you plan to eat. Alternatively, you could swap the mixed greens out for thinly sliced cabbage or kale, which can hold up dressed in the fridge for days. Only add the avocado and chips to portions you plan to eat immediately, or else they would brown and/or turn mushy.

• Vegetarian: Double the black beans! Or use a can of black and a can of pinto beans for variety. You could also marinate big slabs of tofu in this dressing and grill them or cook them in a cast-iron skillet on the stove.

• Dairy-free: Use a dairy-free cheddar or just skip it.

• Gluten-free: This recipe is inherently gluten-free if you double check that the ingredients you’re buying are certified gluten-free. Check labels for the BBQ sauce and tortilla chips especially!

• BBQ sauce: Homemade BBQ sauce , smoky ketchup, Carolina-style BBQ, chipotle sauce mixed with ketchup, steak sauce with a little honey

• Avocado oil: Olive oil or another neutral oil like grapeseed or canola oil

• Apple cider vinegar: I like ACV best in this recipe, but another light-colored vinegar like white wine or red wine vinegar would work! Lime juice would also be great here.

• Honey: Brown, white, or coconut sugar, whisked until dissolved. Or swap for maple syrup, date syrup, or agave

• Black beans: Pinto beans, white beans, or omit the beans altogether

• Chicken breasts: Use boneless, skinless chicken thighs instead — they take 5 to 7 minutes per side (or until 165°F). You could also grill pork tenderloin. See the “how to grill everything” cheat sheet here for pork tenderloin grill method and timing. Another option is to use ground turkey or chicken or vegan “ground meat.” Brown it in a skillet with a little oil and add a big pinch each of kosher salt, garlic powder, chili powder, and smoked paprika and a splash of the BBQ vinaigrette at the very end.

• Peaches: Plums, pineapple (it’s easy to grill long strips of pineapple and it’s so good!), or mango (but I’d skip the grilling). A berry like blueberries would be summery and delicious, too!

• Fresh corn: A can of corn (drained) or thawed frozen corn. If you hate/can’t eat corn, you could grill zucchini or squash planks or some red onion wedges instead.

• Scallions: Thinly sliced red onion or shallot (you can soak the slices in water for a few minutes to take the bite off) or pickled red onions.

• Avocado: Omit if you don’t have one.

• Mixed greens: Thinly sliced romaine, kale, cabbage, or a combo would be great instead of mixed greens.

• White cheddar: Any cheddar! Or Monterey Jack, pepper Jack, or Gouda. Freshly grated is ideal here. Crumbled cotija would work too!

• Tortilla chips: Homemade croutons, Fritos, toasted pita chips, crispy fried onions, toasted pepitas

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup neutral oil (I like avocado oil)
ingredients.name: neutral oil (I like avocado oil)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black beans

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 scallions, thinly sliced, root tip ends discarded
ingredients.name: scallions, thinly sliced, root tip ends discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces shredded white cheddar cheese (2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded white cheddar cheese (2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Large handful of tortilla chips, crushed
ingredients.name: Large handful of tortilla chips

preparationSteps: Make the vinaigrette: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 2/3 cup barbecue sauce, 1/4 cup neutral oil, 6 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper . Taste for sweetness and add a little honey or sugar if needed (this will depend on how sweet the BBQ sauce you’re using is — they’re all different!) .
Scoop half of the dressing out of the serving bowl and into a zip-top bag or shallow dish (this half will be used as a marinade — the half still in the serving bowl is your salad dressing) .

Marinate the chicken: Add 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts to the zip-top bag or shallow dish with the reserved vinaigrette and flip them over a few times to coat. Marinate the chicken in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
When you’re ready to grill, preheat the grill to medium-high heat (450°F).
Add 1 can of drained and rinsed black beans to the dressing that’s still in the serving bowl. Use a fork or whisk to lightly smash the beans so they better absorb the dressing.
Add 1 (5-ounce) container mixed greens on top of the beans, and season the greens with a big pinch each of kosher salt and black pepper.
Thinly slice 3 scallions (only discard the root tip at the end) and dice 1 avocado — set them aside.
Shuck 2 ears of corn and halve and pit 2 peaches . Drizzle them with a little neutral oil .

Grill everything: Once the grill is hot, scrape the grill grates clean. Remove the chicken from the marinade and grill for 6 to 7 minutes per side, or until cooked through to an internal temperature of 165°F in the thickest part of the breast. At the same time, grill the peaches (cut-side down) and corn, rotating the corn every few minutes, until they release easily and have nice grill marks.
Let everything rest until cool enough to handle, then dice the chicken, slice the peaches, and cut the corn off the cob.
Scatter the chicken over the greens along with the peaches, corn, scallions, avocado, and 2 cups of shredded white cheddar cheese . Toss well. Crunch a handful of tortilla chips over top.
Enjoy immediately!

name: one-pan green chile chicken and corn rice bake 2.0
note:
Cook time: 1 hour 25 minutes (20 minutes active; 1 hour 5 minutes inactive)

• I don’t have a 9-by-13-inch baking dish: You can use another large baking dish like an oval-shaped Dutch oven as long as the rice mixture isn’t packed in too deeply. The important thing is that the rice, liquid, and chicken have plenty of room to cook evenly. Cook time may vary though!

• My baking dish is VERY full: Everyone’s baking dishes vary a litte. If yours is filled to the brim, put it on a baking sheet to catch any potential drops that spill out.

• Can I use foil instead of the baking sheet? If you can’t cover it with a baking sheet, yes, use foil! We are specifying using a sheet pan as a lid to minimize variables that may affect the casserole’s cook time, but tightly wrapped foil can work, too.

• What to cook when you really, really do not feel like cooking: While this is truly such an easy recipe, we can make it even more dump and go! Sub fresh corn for thawed frozen or canned corn (see below for exact measurements). You could also skip the chopped green onions or use pre-chopped if you can find them.

• A note about salt : As a reminder, I use Diamond Crystal kosher salt. If you use Morton or another brand you’ll want to cut the amount by about half so it’s not too salty!

• Can I use chicken breasts instead of thighs? Yes, but I really prefer thighs here! They stay juicy during the long, covered bake and shred beautifully into the rice. That said, if you want to use chicken breasts, use boneless, skinless breasts of a similar total weight and check them for doneness starting at 1 hour of cook time. If they’ve reached 165°F internally, pull them out, recover the dish, and let the rice keep cooking the full time.

• What if I don’t have taco seasoning? You can easily make your own! Use 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano, and a pinch of cayenne in place of the 2 teaspoons taco seasoning. Many taco seasonings come with salt added (salt levels can vary a lot here!!), so make sure to salt to taste at the end!

• Can I make this with brown rice? Stick with long-grain white rice here so it cooks properly! The cooking time and amount of liquid needed are really different, and I don’t want you ending up with crunchy rice and sad chicken.

• Is this spicy? Not really! The mild green chiles and salsa verde give this tons of flavor without making it particularly spicy. If you want more heat, use hot green chiles and/or hot salsa verde, or add sliced jalapeños to the toppings.

• Feeding kids: This is a very kid-friendly dinner, especially if your kids like rice, chicken, corn, and cheese! If they’re suspicious of green things, you can leave out the green chile and green onions. Sour cream and avocado toppings are also excellent ways to get a kid excited about the meal.

• Got a pickled red onion recipe? I love a lime juice one like this ! You don’t have to dice the onion, you can slice it instead. Or just buy store-bought!

• Prep ahead: Earlier in the day, dump the rice, green chiles, salsa verde, corn, green onions, and seasonings into your baking dish, cover, and refrigerate. Season the chicken and stash it in the fridge, too. When it’s time for dinner, add the chicken stock, crumble the feta over top, add the butter and chicken, cover, and bake. The important part: wait to add the stock until you’re ready to cook so the rice doesn’t start soaking it up.

• Take it on the road/make ahead: This casserole is a great one to make ahead and bring with you! Cook it all the way through at home, let it cool, then cover and refrigerate. When you get to your friend’s house (or your vacation house, lake house, etc.), sprinkle the top with shredded Mexican cheese and pop it into a 350°F oven, uncovered, until warmed through and the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 20 to 30 minutes. Basically, you get to show up with a fully cooked casserole and still get the glory of pulling a hot, cheesy casserole out of the oven.

• Freezer friendly: Alternatively, you could cook the whole thing, let it cool, then either cover the dish tightly with foil or plastic wrap and freeze it whole or portion it out and freeze individual servings (I like to do it that way!). Let it thaw overnight in the fridge then follow the “make ahead” instructions above.

• Love your leftovers: Reheat individual portions in the microwave with a splash of chicken stock or water if the rice seems dry. Or turn the leftovers into something totally new: tuck them into tortillas with avocado, sour cream, and salsa for burritos, or sauté the cold rice and chicken in a hot skillet until crispy, scramble an egg in the center, and stir it all together with some soy sauce and other seasonings for an easy fried rice.

• Why is there so much melted butter on top?! Don’t panic. You may pull this out of the oven and see a little pool of melted butter on top. That’s normal! Once you shred the chicken and stir everything together, the butter gets absorbed into the rice and makes the whole thing rich and delicious.

• Can I use water instead of chicken stock? Yep! If you don’t have chicken stock, use 4 cups water + 4 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon. I wouldn’t use plain water without seasoning it though because you’ll lose a lot of the flavor.

• Vegetarian: Swap the chicken stock for vegetable stock and skip the chicken. Add a can of drained black beans or pinto beans to the rice mixture for some protein. For another vegetarian protein boost, dice tofu and stir into the rice mixture before baking. Jillian did that riff and enjoyed it, but says it definitely didn’t add the same rich flavor that chicken does!

• Dairy-free: Use dairy-free butter (or 4 tablespoons olive or avocado oil in place of butter) and one 5.2-ounce package of dairy-free Boursin-style cheese in place of the feta. It won’t be quite as rich as the original, but you’ll still get that creamy, cheesy rice situation!

• Gluten-free: Check the labels when buying your taco seasoning and stock or Better Than Bouillon — look for brands that are certified gluten free.

• Corn: Fresh, frozen, or canned corn will all work! If using canned, drain 2 (15-ounce) cans. If using frozen, use about 2 1/2 cups and thaw it first. If you’re corn-averse, white cannellini beans, chickpeas, or cherry tomatoes are great subs.

• Scallions: Diced yellow or white onion, shallot, thinly sliced chives, or skip them.

• Long-grain white rice: Any long-grain white rice should work here. I don’t recommend swapping in brown rice or a short-grain rice without adjusting the liquid and cooking time, since this recipe was specifically developed for long-grain white rice! We have only tested it with long-grain white rice, but report back on how it goes, if you swap another in!

• Chicken stock: Reduced-sodium vegetable stock, water + 2 teaspoons Better Than Bouillon, or plain water. If using plain water, you’ll want to add a little extra salt to taste.

• Diced green chiles: Cherry tomatoes, diced poblano pepper, or roasted red peppers. The cherry tomatoes will add little bursts of sweetness and acidity rather than heat, but they work nicely with the salsa verde.

• Salsa verde: Any jarred salsa works! If you don’t have salsa verde, you could use green enchilada sauce, though it will be a little smoother and less fresh-tasting.

• Taco seasoning: Use your favorite taco seasoning blend, or make your own with chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, and a pinch of cayenne.

• Garlic powder: Fresh garlic! Use 2 cloves, finely minced. You could also use 1 teaspoon garlic paste or a cube or 2 of frozen crushed garlic.

• Kosher salt: If using table salt or fine sea salt, start with less and add more to taste since the crystals are smaller. Same for non Diamond Crystal brand kosher salt!

• Feta: Boursin would be my first swap! It melts into the rice and makes the whole dish extra creamy. You could also use goat cheese or cream cheese, though both will give you a slightly different flavor. If using cream cheese, I’d cut it into small pieces before scattering it over the rice.

• Unsalted butter: Olive oil or avocado oil. Use 4 tablespoons oil in place of the 8 tablespoons butter. We haven’t tested this substitution, but 4 tablespoons should provide enough fat and richness without making the finished rice greasy.

• Boneless, skinless chicken thighs: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts work. I strongly prefer thighs here because they stay juicy during the long bake. Or swap in 1 pound large peeled and deveined shrimp! Toss the shrimp with 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, then nestle them into the rice during the final 5 to 8 minutes of cooking. Cover and continue baking until the shrimp are opaque and cooked through. See above for vegetarian substitutions.

• Black pepper: Freshly ground or pre-ground black pepper — or skip it!

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ears corn (ideally white), shucked and kernels cut off
ingredients.name: corn (ideally white), shucked and kernels cut off

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 bunch scallions (aka green onions), thinly sliced, root tip ends discarded
ingredients.name: scallions (aka green onions), thinly sliced, root tip ends discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 cups (1 quart) low-sodium chicken stock (or 4 cups water plus 4 teaspoons reduced-sodium Better Than Bouillon)
ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken stock (or 4 cups water plus 4 teaspoons reduced-sodium Better Than Bouillon)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (8-ounce) block feta, broken into about 8 pieces
ingredients.name: feta, broken into about 8 pieces

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 stick (8 tablespoons) unsalted butter, cut into about 8 pieces
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, fat trimmed off and discarded
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, fat trimmed off and discarded

ingredients.rawIngredient: Optional toppings: Sour cream, diced or sliced avocado, cilantro, pickled red onions, pickled jalapeños, lime wedges, hot sauce
ingredients.name: Optional toppings: Sour cream, diced or sliced avocado, cilantro, pickled red onions, pickled jalapeños, lime wedges, hot sauce

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.

Shuck then cut the kernels off of 4 ears of corn (to do this without corn flying all over your kitchen, lay the corn flat on your cutting board and cut down). Thinly slice 1 bunch scallions (use both the white and green parts, only discard the root tip end) and reserve about 1/4 of them for using as a garnish when serving.

To a 9-by-13-inch ceramic or baking dish, add 2 cups long-grain white rice (I don’t rinse it for this!), 4 cups low-sodium chicken stock , 2 (4-ounce) cans diced green chiles , 1 (7-ounce) can salsa verde , the corn kernels, the sliced scallions (except for the reserved garnish), 2 teaspoons taco seasoning, 1 teaspoon garlic powder , and 1 teaspoon of kosher salt . Stir to combine.
Break 1 (8-ounce) block of feta into about 8 pieces and scatter evenly over the top. Cut 1 stick of unsalted butter into about 8 pieces and scatter them evenly over top, too.

Trim any large pieces of white fat from 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs (I use kitchen shears!). Arrange the chicken in an even layer over the rice mixture then season it all over with 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder , and several grinds of black pepper .
Cover the baking dish with a sheet pan and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for another 20 minutes uncovered.

Is the rice tender, the liquid absorbed, and the chicken cooked through to an internal temperature of 165°F? If so, proceed with the recipe! (You may see a layer of melted butter and/or a bit of liquid on the top, and that’s normal!) If your chicken and rice are not ready yet, return the dish to the oven and cook until they are (check every 5 minutes so they don’t overcook).

Use 2 forks to shred the chicken right there in the dish. Stir everything together until well combined. Taste and add more kosher salt, if needed. If the flavors don’t pop, stir in a pinch more salt and taste again. Keep going until it tastes amazing!

Take out and prepare any toppings you’d like to serve with it, such as sour cream , diced avocado , cilantro , pickled red onions , pickled jalapeños , and/or lime wedges . It can be fun to add these to a tray that you bring to the table so everyone can add their own toppings. See notes below for a pickled onion recipe — if making, start right when the chicken and rice dish goes into the oven!
Spoon into bowls and top with the reserved scallions and any additional toppings. Dig in!

name: calabrian chili cherry tomato alla vodka
note: Cook time: 25 minutes

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 tablespoon Calabrian chili paste (OR WAY LESS if you don’t like spice!)
ingredients.name: Calabrian chili paste (OR WAY LESS if you don’t like spice!)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan (ideally Parmigiano-Reggiano) cheese, plus more for serving
ingredients.name: freshly grated Parmesan (ideally Parmigiano-Reggiano) cheese, plus more for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Freshly ground black pepper, for serving
ingredients.name: Freshly ground black pepper, for serving

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water (2 tablespoons of kosher salt in the water is my general rule) to a boil and cook 1 pound rigatoni until al dente (read the box to find your pasta’s ideal cook time). SCOOP OUT ABOUT 1 CUP OF THE PASTA COOKING WATER BEFORE YOU DRAIN THE PASTA!! Set the pasta water aside.
While the water comes to a boil and the pasta cooks, make the sauce.
Mince 1 large shallot and 4 garlic cloves .

Melt 2 tablespoons unsalted butter in a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the minced shallot and garlic and a big pinch of kosher salt . Cook until they’re soft and translucent, about 4 minutes. Add 3 tablespoons tomato paste and stir constantly until it becomes dark red, about 3 minutes.

Stir in 1/4 cup vodka and 1 tablespoon Calabrian chili paste (OR LESS, if you don’t want it to be a bit spicy!) and crank the heat up to medium-high. Stir for about 30 seconds, until the mixture is thick and pasty.
Stir in 2 pounds whole cherry tomatoes and a big pinch of kosher salt . Lower the heat to medium, cover the saucepan, and cook for 7 to 10 minutes, until the tomatoes start to burst.

Now is a good time to grate 1 cup of Parmesan . You can grate it using a box grater, microplane, or your blender. To use the blender, throw chunks of Parm in and pulse until it reaches a grated consistency.
Uncover and stir for several more minutes until the tomatoes are really starting to burst and get saucy. Use your spatula or the back of a spoon to lightly press and release their juices, if needed.

Stir in 1 cup heavy cream . Once it’s warm (but not bubbling, just warm!), very slowly sprinkle and stir in 1 cup of grated Parmesan a little at a time, only adding more Parm once the previous bit has had time to melt into the sauce. It’s important to go slow and that the sauce isn’t too hot when you add your cheese, or the cheese will clump up instead of melting.

Add the drained cooked pasta into the sauce. Stir to coat. If it’s too thick, loosen with a splash of pasta cooking water (you will have pasta water left over — just throw out whatever you don’t use!) . Taste and add more kosher salt if needed.
Serve in low bowls with more grated Parm and some freshly cracked black pepper on top.

name: Easiest-Ever Shredded Beef
note:
Hands on for: 15 minutes
Walk away for: 4½ hours

Chuck roast is too often associated with pot roast—a stewy dish consisting of braised beef and tender veggies—but there are so many other delicious things you can do with this cheap cut of meat! Roast it, slice it, or shred it, then check out my five favorite ways to make it dinner.

Shortcut: If you have zero time, just season the beef with salt and pepper and add a splash of water to the pot. Cover and cook. It’ll still be delicious without the onion and garlic!

Extra extra: For some added flavor and to make your kitchen smell even more incredible while the roast roasts, before adding the onion to the pot, stick 3 or 4 whole cloves into it like you’re pushing tacks into a corkboard.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 222

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup red wine or low-sodium beef stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)
ingredients.name: red wine or low-sodium beef stock (or BTB + water—see page 21)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Pat the beef dry. Cut the onion in half. Smash the garlic cloves with the side of your knife.

Rub the roast all over with 1 tablespoon salt and some pepper. Place it in a Dutch oven or high-sided baking dish that fits the meat pretty tightly, without a lot of free space around it. Add the onion and garlic, then pour in the wine. Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil and roast for about 4 hours, until the meat is deeply tender and pulls apart easily with a fork. If it’s not shredding easily after 4 hours, keep cooking it! It feels counterintuitive, but I promise you haven’t overcooked it, it needs more time. For a more browned, slightly crusty exterior, uncover the pot for the last 30 minutes of roasting.
Remove the pot from the oven, uncover (if necessary), and let rest for 15 to 20 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to skim off any fat from the surface of the liquid.

If you plan to shred the beef, it’s easiest to do so while it’s still warm, right in the pot: Use two forks to pull and shred the meat, then stir it together with the liquid in the pot. (I leave the onion right in the mix, but you can pull it out and discard it if you prefer.) If you’d prefer to slice the roast thinly, separate the meat from the liquid and chill in the refrigerator for about 1 hour (it’s easier to slice when it’s cold), then cut clean slices and return the meat to the liquid. If you want it both ways, cut the roast in half; shred one half now and chill the other half to slice later. Store the shredded or sliced meat in the liquid in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days; store whole meat and the liquid in separate containers for up to 5 days.
servings: About 8 cups, depending on the cut of meat

name: Crispy Beef Tacos with Lime-Pickled Red Onion
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 223

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): crumbled Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese, sour cream, chopped fresh cilantro, pico de gallo or salsa, sliced avocado
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): crumbled Cotija or brine-packed feta cheese, sour cream, chopped fresh cilantro, pico de gallo or salsa, sliced avocado

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Wrap the tortillas in aluminum foil and warm them in the oven for 10 to 15 minutes. Keep them wrapped until ready to serve.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion and place it in a small bowl. Halve the lime and squeeze in the juice. Add the sugar and a pinch of salt. Stir it and let it stand while you crisp the beef.

Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, spread the shredded beef in the skillet and cook, undisturbed, until it’s crispy on the bottom, 3 to 5 minutes. Flip the meat and warm the other side, 3 to 5 minutes more.
Fill the warm tortillas with the crispy beef, pickled onions, and any other desired toppings.

name: Garlic-Soy Beef Bowls
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 223

ingredients.rawIngredient: 3 cups warm cooked white rice, brown rice, or quinoa
ingredients.name: warm cooked white rice, brown rice, or quinoa

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): fried eggs, kimchi, sliced cucumber, chopped cilantro, toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): fried eggs, kimchi, sliced cucumber, chopped cilantro, toasted sesame seeds

preparationSteps: Finely chop the garlic and chop the scallions. Warm the sesame oil in a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the garlic and scallions and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the shredded beef and cook, stirring frequently, until warmed through, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar and cook until the beef is slightly glazed, 1 to 2 minutes.
Scoop the rice into bowls, spoon the beef on top, and finish with any additional toppings.

name: Pasta with Meat Sauce
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 224

ingredients.rawIngredient: 8 ounces short or long pasta noodles, such as rigatoni, penne, or pappardelle
ingredients.name: short or long pasta noodles, such as rigatoni, penne, or pappardelle

ingredients.rawIngredient: Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, for serving
ingredients.name: Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, for serving

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the pasta and cook until just shy of al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out 1 1/4 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.

In the same pot you just boiled the pasta in, combine the marinara, shredded beef, and 1/4 cup of the pasta cooking water. Cook over medium-high heat until the sauce begins to bubble, 7 to 10 minutes.
Toss in the pasta and sprinkle in the Parm at the same time so it doesn’t clump. Stir to coat and combine well, then taste and add salt and pepper as needed.
Divide among plates, top with more Parm, and serve.

name: Cheese Steaks
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 224
preparationSteps: Turn on the broiler.
Thinly slice the bell pepper and onion.

Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the pepper and onion and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Add the shredded beef and cook just until heated through.

Split the hoagie rolls lengthwise and stuff with the hot beef mixture, dividing it evenly, and arrange the stuffed rolls on a baking sheet. Top each with 2 slices of the cheese and broil until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the rolls are lightly toasted, 2 to 4 minutes. Serve warm.

name: Loaded Beefy Pitas
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 225

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup labneh or plain full-fat Greek yogurt
ingredients.name: labneh or plain full-fat Greek yogurt

ingredients.rawIngredient: Pickled red onion (store-bought or see page 223)
ingredients.name: Pickled red onion (store-bought or see page 223)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Stack the pitas, wrap them in aluminum foil, and put them in the oven for 10 to 15 minutes, until warm, soft, and pliable. If they feel stiff or dry before you warm them, sprinkle a tiny bit of water between a couple of them before you wrap them. Meanwhile, dice the cucumbers and finely chop the parsley leaves and tender stems to make 1/2 cup.

Warm the olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the shredded beef and a splash of water and cook, stirring, until the meat is heated through and well coated in the spices, 3 to 4 minutes.
Spread the labneh inside the warm pitas, then divide the seasoned meat among them. Stuff with the cucumbers, pickled red onion, and parsley, and serve.

name: Smoky Black Beans
note: My pantry is never without multiple cans of black beans—they’re one of my very favorite panic purchases. Everyone has their own favorite panic purchase—you know, the item you buy every time you’re at the store because you think “do I have this at home . . .?” They’re a reliable yet humble vessel for impressive flavor—all it takes are a few shakes of spices and you have a delicious protein to build dinner around. I’m no short-order cook, but on smoky black bean nights, I don’t mind customizing plates. For the baby? Black beans straight up. For my pickiest eaters? Black bean flautas they can dunk into sour cream. For George and me? Most often some sort of bowl like these Mediterranean bowls, but I definitely dabble in crunchy tacos and loaded sweet potatoes. There’s no wrong way to down these beans!
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 74
preparationSteps: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, and chili powder and cook, stirring, until fragrant, for 15 seconds.

Drain and rinse 1 can of black beans, then add them to the pan along with the (undrained) beans from the second can. Add 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and the cilantro. Turn down the heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the beans thicken and are no longer watery, about 10 minutes. Use a wooden spoon to lightly smash about half the beans against the side of the pan. Pluck out and discard the cilantro sprigs. Halve the lime and squeeze in the juice of 1 half. Stir, then taste and add more salt and/or lime juice as needed.

If you’re not using the beans right away, let them cool, then store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. When ready to use, warm them gently in a saucepan over medium-low heat or in the microwave. If they’re very thick, stir in some water to loosen them up.

name: Crunchy Black Bean Tacos
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 75

ingredients.rawIngredient: Toppings (optional): shredded iceberg lettuce, chopped fresh cilantro, sour cream, diced avocado or guacamole, pickled red onions, hot sauce, salsa, shredded pepper Jack or cheddar or crumbled Cotija cheese
ingredients.name: Toppings (optional): shredded iceberg lettuce, chopped fresh cilantro, sour cream, diced avocado or guacamole, pickled red onions, hot sauce, salsa, shredded pepper Jack or cheddar or crumbled Cotija cheese

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Place the taco shells on a baking sheet and warm them in the oven for 10 minutes.
Fill the warm taco shells with the smoky black beans and add any desired toppings. Serve.

name: Loaded Sweet Potatoes with Creamy Herby Sauce
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 75

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt or sour cream
ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt or sour cream

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 ounces Cotija, brine-packed feta, or shredded Mexican blend cheese (1 cup)
ingredients.name: Cotija, brine-packed feta, or shredded Mexican blend cheese (1 cup)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash and scrub the sweet potatoes. Halve them lengthwise and place them cut side down on the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender inside.

While the potatoes bake, roughly chop enough cilantro to make 1/2 cup, plus more for serving, if desired. Halve the lime and squeeze the juice of 1 half into a blender or food processor. Add the yogurt, cilantro, and a big pinch of salt and blend on high speed until well incorporated, about 1 minute. (Alternatively, finely chop the cilantro and stir it all together in a small bowl.)

Use a fork to mash the insides of the baked sweet potatoes and season with a big pinch each of salt and pepper, then fill them with smoky black beans, a big scoop of pico de gallo, and a nice drizzle of the creamy herby sauce. Crumble over a hefty serving of Cotija and garnish with more chopped cilantro if you’re feeling fancy.

name: Mediterranean Black Beans
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 76
preparationSteps: Finely chop the parsley. Using a Microplane, grate the lemon zest directly into the quinoa. Add half the parsley and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Stir and fluff to incorporate.
Dice the bell pepper and cucumbers and add them to the quinoa.

Assemble bowls with the quinoa salad as the base, topping each with a big spoonful of smoky black beans and a dollop of tzatziki. Garnish with the remaining parsley. Cut the zested lemon into wedges and serve one with each bowl for squeezing.

name: Tamale Bowls
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 76

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

preparationSteps: Cook the cornmeal per package instructions. Stir in the cheese until it melts, about 1 minute. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and some pepper. These should be quite thick—keep stirring over low heat until they are.
Dice the avocado and chop enough cilantro to make 1/2 cup.
Assemble bowls with the cheesy polenta as the base, topping each with a big spoonful of smoky black beans, pico de gallo, avocado, cilantro, and eggs, if you like.

name: Black Bean Flautas with Avo Slaw
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 77

ingredients.rawIngredient: 6 ounces shredded Mexican blend, cheddar, or pepper Jack cheese (1 1/2 cups)
ingredients.name: shredded Mexican blend, cheddar, or pepper Jack cheese (1 1/2 cups)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley, chives, and/or cilantro
ingredients.name: Soft green herbs, such as fresh parsley, chives, and/or cilantro

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 (10-ounce) bag coleslaw mix or shredded green cabbage
ingredients.name: coleslaw mix or shredded green cabbage

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

If your smoky black beans are still hot, let them cool for about 10 minutes, then stir in the cheese. Spread 3 tablespoons of the bean mixture down the center of 1 tortilla, then roll it up tightly and place it seam side down on a baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, spacing them at least 1 inch apart on the pan. Spritz with cooking spray and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the tortillas are golden brown all over.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the bell pepper and chop enough herbs to make about 1/4 cup. Dice the avocado and place it in a large bowl. Halve the lime and squeeze the juice into the bowl with the avocado. Add a generous pinch of salt and some black pepper. Mash until well combined and mostly smooth. Add the bell pepper, coleslaw mix, and herbs and toss to coat. Taste and add more lime, salt, and/or black pepper as needed.
Serve your flautas with the avo slaw alongside and a big dollop of sour cream!

name: Lemony Herby Chicken Thighs
note: Meet your new favorite protein. Cook these bright and aromatic chicken thighs, then—using the recipes that follow—serve them day after day (for up to 4 days), never repeating the same meal twice. While the chicken roasts, toss some veggies on a baking sheet to cook alongside it, or save that step for another night when you need a quick side.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 120

ingredients.rawIngredient: 4 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 12 thighs)
ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 12 thighs)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F or heat an outdoor grill to medium-high (400° to 450°F).

Using a Microplane, grate the lemon zest into a large bowl, then halve the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Add the olive oil, salt, garlic powder, oregano, onion, thyme, and some pepper and whisk to combine. Add the chicken and turn to coat.
Arrange the chicken in an even layer on two rimmed baking sheets and bake for 25 minutes, or until it reaches 165°F internally, or place it on the hot grill for 6 to 7 minutes per side.
Serve immediately, or let the chicken cool, then transfer it to an airtight container and store in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

name: Curry Chicken Salad
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 121
preparationSteps: In a large bowl, stir together the mayo, curry powder, and cumin. Halve the lime and squeeze in the juice.

Finely chop the chicken thighs until they’re in tiny, shredded pieces. Dice the celery stalks and quarter the grapes. Add the chicken, celery, grapes, and raisins to the bowl of dressing and stir to combine and coat well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or up to 4 days before eating for tastiest results.

name: Chicken Alfredo-ish
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 121

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 (5.3-ounce) blocks Garlic and Fine Herbs Boursin cheese
ingredients.name: Garlic and Fine Herbs Boursin cheese

preparationSteps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the spaghetti and cook until al dente according to the package directions.
Meanwhile, chop the chicken thighs—you want about 2 cups chopped chicken.

Two minutes before the spaghetti is done, add the broccoli, breaking up any large florets as you drop them into the pot. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain everything and return the spaghetti and broccoli to the hot pot over very low heat. Stir in the Boursin, 1/2 cup of the reserved pasta cooking water (see Learn, page 60), and the chicken. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Add more pasta water as needed until a silky-smooth sauce forms, then serve.

name: Pesto Chicken Flatbread
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 122

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup drained jarred julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes
ingredients.name: drained jarred julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Chop the chicken thighs—you want about 1 cup chopped chicken.

Place the naan on the prepared baking sheet and spread the pesto over the top. Sprinkle evenly with the mozzarella and sun-dried tomatoes, then crumble over the goat cheese. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the naan is slightly crisp.

name: Italian Chick Sliders
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 122

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/2 cup drained jarred roasted red peppers
ingredients.name: drained jarred roasted red peppers

preparationSteps: Using a serrated knife, slice the rolls in half horizontally, leaving them all connected, to make one giant top sheet and one giant bottom sheet. Work slowly to make the top and bottom as even in thickness as possible. Smear the mayo on the cut side of the bottom sheet and the mustard on the cut side of the top sheet.

Thinly slice the chicken thighs. Start layering the ingredients onto the bottom sheet, totally covering the surface, in this order: provolone, spinach, chicken, roasted peppers, banana peppers. Sandwich with the top sheet, slice into individual sliders, and serve.

name: Roasted Veggie and Chicken Orzo
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, p. 123

ingredients.rawIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 to 3 warmed Lemony Herby Chicken Thighs
ingredients.name: warmed Lemony Herby Chicken Thighs

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 450°F.

Chop the bell peppers and onion into roughly 1-inch pieces. Toss on a rimmed baking sheet with the tomatoes, 1/4 cup of the olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, some black pepper, and the garlic powder. Spread out into an even layer.
Roast the vegetables (alongside the chicken, if you’re cooking them at the same time) until golden brown and tender, 25 to 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a medium pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the orzo and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Drain in a fine-mesh strainer.

Use a Microplane to grate the lemon zest into a serving bowl, then cut the zested lemon in half and squeeze in the juice. Add the remaining 1/4 cup olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and some black pepper. Whisk to combine.

Chop the chicken thighs and add them to the bowl of dressing. Roughly chop the parsley leaves and tender stems and add them to the bowl. Add the roasted veggies and orzo. Crumble in the feta and toss to combine and coat with the dressing. Taste and season with more salt and black pepper as needed before serving.

name: Sheet Pan Breakfast Burritos
note: There's no need to prep a million components for breakfast burritos; cook everything on one sheet tray (including the eggs!). This high protein version features our staple scrambled egg mixture with cottage cheese while keeping the mixins basics, so it's family-friendly and totally customizable. Get creative and add bell peppers, mushrooms, and more to this meal prep breakfast with 38 grams of protein that takes just 15 minutes of work.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1 cup cottage cheese (low fat, small curd)
ingredients.name: cottage cheese (low fat, small curd)

preparationSteps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.

Dice the 2 russet potatoes (peeling optional) and toss in 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp smoked paprika, and 1/4 tsp garlic powder. Place on a quarter sheet tray or 9x13 dish (and then nestle in the uncooked 1 lb spicy sausage. I tear it up to have small blobs of sausage spread throughout, no larger than 2" diameter. Bake for 30 minutes or until the potatoes are fork-tender.

Blend the 8 eggs, 1 cup cottage cheese, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, and 1/4 tsp smoked paprika in a blender and pour this mixture over the potatoes and sausage in the sheet tray. Sprinkle with 1 cup white cheddar. Return to the oven for 10 minutes to cook until the eggs are set.
Remove burrito filling from the oven and slice into 6 even rectangles, then wrap in 6 burrito tortillas with optional 1 avocado and freeze or store in the fridge. Enjoy with pico de gallo.

name: Winner Winner (Marinated) Chicken Dinner
note:
Recipe family: winner-winner-marinated-chicken
Planner role: template; do not recommend directly.

Chicken options: boneless skinless thighs (most forgiving), boneless skinless breasts, or bone-in skin-on pieces.

Make-ahead strategy: Combine chicken and marinade in freezer bags and freeze flat. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use your cooking method of choice. Marinate and cook extra chicken for salads, wraps, or grain bowls; the cooked chicken can also be frozen.

Kid-friendly hacks: Skip the spice and herbs if needed, use precut chicken tenders or cut chicken into strips, and serve ranch dressing or ketchup on the side.

Flavor presets:
Mediterranean: 2 tablespoons olive oil + 1 tablespoon plain yogurt + Juice of 1 large lemon + 3 garlic cloves, minced + 1 tablespoon dried oregano + 1 teaspoon dried thyme + 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons kosher salt Serve with Roasted vegetables, rice pilaf, and tzatziki.
Asian-Inspired: 2 tablespoons sesame oil (toasted or not) + 1 tablespoon neutral oil + 2 tablespoons soy sauce + 2 tablespoons rice vinegar + 1 tablespoon honey + 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger + 2 garlic cloves, minced Serve with Steamed rice and stir-fried vegetables.
Mexican-Inspired: 2 tablespoons olive oil + Juice of 2 limes + 2 teaspoons ground cumin + 1 teaspoon chili powder + 1 teaspoon sweet paprika + 2 garlic cloves, minced + 1 teaspoon kosher salt Serve with Rice or tortillas, black beans, and your favorite toppings.
Italian Herb: 3 tablespoons olive oil + 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar + 2 tablespoons fresh basil + 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary + 3 garlic cloves, minced + 1 teaspoon kosher salt Serve with A caprese salad.
Indian-Inspired: 3 tablespoons plain yogurt + Juice of 1 lemon + 1 tablespoon garam masala + 1 teaspoon ground turmeric + 2 garlic cloves, minced + 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger + 1 teaspoon kosher salt Serve with Long-grain rice, naan, and cucumber raita.
Honey Mustard: 2 tablespoons olive oil + 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar + 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard + 2 tablespoons honey + 1 tablespoon fresh thyme + 1 teaspoon kosher salt Serve with Roasted potatoes and green beans.
Teriyaki: 2 tablespoons neutral oil + 1 tablespoon sesame oil (toasted or not) + 3 tablespoons soy sauce + 1 tablespoon rice vinegar + 2 tablespoons brown sugar (light or dark) + 1-inch piece fresh ginger, grated + 2 garlic cloves, grated Serve with Steamed broccoli or snap peas and jasmine rice.
sourceName: What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking — Caro Chambers, pp. 196–199

ingredients.name: Kosher salt (1 teaspoon per pound of meat unless using a salty flavor, such as soy sauce)

ingredients.rawIngredient: Boneless skinless thighs; boneless skinless chicken breasts; or bone-in skin-on pieces of chicken
ingredients.name: Boneless skinless thighs; boneless skinless chicken breasts; or bone-in skin-on pieces of chicken

ingredients.rawIngredient: Extra-virgin olive oil; sesame oil; peanut oil; neutral oil; plain yogurt; or mayonnaise
ingredients.name: Extra-virgin olive oil; sesame oil; peanut oil; neutral oil; plain yogurt; or mayonnaise

ingredients.rawIngredient: Lemon or lime juice; any vinegar; or wine
ingredients.name: Lemon or lime juice; any vinegar; or wine

ingredients.rawIngredient: Garlic; ginger; fresh or dried herbs; spices; mustard; soy sauce; oyster sauce; hoisin; gochujang; or harissa
ingredients.name: Garlic; ginger; fresh or dried herbs; spices; mustard; soy sauce; oyster sauce; hoisin; gochujang; or harissa

ingredients.rawIngredient: Honey; maple syrup; or brown sugar
ingredients.name: Honey; maple syrup; or brown sugar

preparationSteps: Mix the marinade: Whisk together the salt, fat, acid, aromatics, and sweetener (if using) in a big bowl or combine in a zip-top bag.

Marinate: Add the chicken, make sure it is coated well, and marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, ideally 4 hours in the fridge, and up to 24 hours. If marinating longer than a couple of hours, reduce or omit the acid so the chicken does not become mushy.
Grill: Cook over medium-high heat on oiled grates for 6 to 8 minutes per side for boneless pieces or 10 to 12 minutes per side for bone-in pieces.

Stove to oven: Cook over medium-high heat in a skillet with oil for 5 to 7 minutes per side for boneless pieces or 8 to 10 minutes per side for bone-in pieces, then transfer to a 375°F oven if not cooked through.
Oven only: Bake at 400°F for boneless pieces for 18 to 25 minutes or at 425°F for bone-in pieces for 35 to 45 minutes.
Check for doneness: The internal temperature should reach 165°F. Let the cooked chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing, then serve.

name: Fried Rice Is Always Nice (and Other Grains, Too)
note:
Recipe family: fried-rice-always-nice
Planner role: template; do not recommend directly.

Cook twice as much grain as needed for an earlier recipe, then turn the extra into fried rice a night or two later. The formula can be halved or doubled and can use more vegetables and less grain.

Vegetable options: frozen broccoli, corn and peas, or blends; fresh carrots, mushrooms, broccoli, bell peppers, snap peas, bok choy, or zucchini; or leafy greens such as spinach, kale, or Swiss chard.

Cooked protein options: chicken, pork, steak, lamb, shrimp, salmon, crab, tofu, tempeh, or edamame—or omit and use only the eggs.

Grain options: white rice, quinoa, farro, brown rice, cauliflower rice, or a mix. Use cold, day-old grains whenever possible.

Pro tips: Chop vegetables to a similar size. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if needed. Stir frequently, use high heat, and add sauces gradually so the fried rice stays crisp rather than soggy.

Make-ahead strategy: Prep and refrigerate chopped vegetables. Cook grains in bulk for the week. Cooked fried rice freezes in an airtight container for up to 3 months.

Kid-friendly hacks: Let kids choose their mix-ins, hold the heat for the table, chop vegetables extra small, use familiar proteins, or serve the rice, vegetables, meat, and eggs in separate piles.

name: high protein pumpkin baked oatmeal
note: All made in the same dish it's baked in, this high-protein pumpkin baked oatmeal is packed with 25 grams of protein. It's also rich in fiber and always a hit with the family. Enjoy some for Sunday breakfast and have plenty left over for meal prep throughout the week.

ingredients.rawIngredient: 2 cups rolled oats (quick or old-fashioned work)
ingredients.name: rolled oats (quick or old-fashioned work)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1.5 cups pure pumpkin puree (not pie filling)
ingredients.name: pure pumpkin puree (not pie filling)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1/4 cup chocolate chips (optional to add nuts for crunch)
ingredients.name: chocolate chips (optional to add nuts for crunch)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1.5 cups Greek yogurt (plain, non-fat, for mixing into the oats)
ingredients.name: Greek yogurt (plain, non-fat, for mixing into the oats)

ingredients.rawIngredient: 1.5 cups Greek yogurt (plain, non-fat, for topping slices when eating)
ingredients.name: Greek yogurt (plain, non-fat, for topping slices when eating)

preparationSteps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees and grease a 9x13 baking dish.

In the baking dish, mix together the 2 cups rolled oats, 1 cup egg whites, 1.5 cups Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup chia seeds, 1/4 cup hemp seeds, 1.5 cups pure pumpkin puree, 1 cup milk, 1/4 cup coconut sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 tsp cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp salt. Once combined, sprinkle the 1/4 cup chocolate chips on top and gently press them into the mixture.
Bake for 30-35 minutes or until all the liquid has absorbed. Check it at 25 minutes to see how it's doing. Overbaking the oats can result in ones that are dry and tough.
Let it cool, then cut into 6 large slices (I know, big beautiful servings). Enjoy with a dollop of Greek yogurt and a drizzle of maple syrup.

name: air fryer high protein pumpkin bagel bites
note: Why eat a regular bagel when you can eat high protein pumpkin bagel bites dipped in a high protein, creamy dip? These bagel bites are ready in just 10 minutes in the air fryer, and blended cottage cheese is used to boost protein. Rolled in cinnamon and sugar, I know you're going to love this snickerdoodle-style bagel bite!
preparationSteps: Blend together the 3/4 cup cottage cheese, 2 tbsp pumpkin puree, and ½ tsp vanilla extract until totally smooth and no curds remain.

Mix together the 1 cup all purpose flour, 3 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp pumpkin pie spice, and ½ tsp cinnamon in a large bowl. Then add the cottage cheese mixture and mix together, pressing the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until fully absorbed.
Transfer to a floured surface and form a circle. If it's too wet, knead a bit more flour into it.
Cut into 16 even triangles and form each one into a ball. Place on the air fryer tray or in the basket. Mix 1 egg and then brush each bagel bite with the egg wash.
Air fry for 8-10 minutes at 350 degrees or until golden brown and cooked through. It should sound hollow when tapped on. Meanwhile, mix together the 2 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 cup cane sugar.
Drop each bite into the ¼ c melted butter briefly and then roll in cinnamon and sugar. To reduce the sugar, you can just brush the tops with butter and sprinkle cinnamon sugar on top.
Serve them up hot with the spiced yogurt dip!To make the dip, just mix together the 1/2 cup pumpkin cream cheese and 1/2 cup plain greek yogurt.
